[[smc-vplan]]
== SMC OCAH Open-Source Verification Plan

=== Overview

This plan covers the SMC subsystem as it is verified in the open-source
harness: the `smc_wrapper` DUT driven over SEP_IN AXI and AXI-Lite, with
cocotb/PyUVM as the primary framework and an SV-UVM view for the scenarios
that carry one. The cocotb checkers
alone carry a card's Pass Criteria; rows marked `SV-UVM shape only` describe
that view and close nothing here, so a card whose checkers were all SV-UVM
would be unclosed. The enrolled testcases and the membership of the `all`
sign-off group are defined in `testlists/all.toml`; `all` is every test this
plan grades, and its `expected_count` is the membership gate. The `hosted`,
`fw` and `sanity` classes select by what a leaf needs to build and do not
between them cover `all`. Non-ROM leaves outside `all` are in
`testlists/holdout.toml`; ROM/OCCP leaves are in `testlists/smc_rom.toml` and
selected through `occp_rom`. Sign-off holdouts have cards under
<<smc-held-out-testcases>>; where the reason is a defect, Known Limitations
records the hole.

Every card under Test Procedures names a testcase that exists and is a member
of `all`, and says which groups enrol it. Where the harness
cannot reach a feature, the testcase is not listed here as enrolled; it is
recorded under Known Limitations with the reason, so this plan states what
is verified rather than what was once intended.

[[smc-vplan-strategy]]
=== Verification Strategy

* *Frontdoor stimulus, frontdoor proof.* Stimulus is driven through product
  ports -- SEP_IN AXI, AXI-Lite, JTAG, and the pad-level protocol VIPs -- and
  every claim is proven by what the DUT returns or drives at those ports and
  on its own outputs. Where the DUT offers no frontdoor way to create the
  condition a testcase verifies -- a corrupted ECC codeword in a scratch
  macro, an unused encoding in a state flop, an error from the eFuse bank
  model -- the testcase may create it with a testbench hook: a backdoor write
  into the macro array, a force on the flop, or an inject pin on the bound DV
  memory collateral. Such a card names the hook on its *BFM / Model* line and
  in its Test Procedure, and the DUT's reaction is still observed frontdoor,
  on the DUT's outputs and registers, never on the poked or forced signal
  itself. Passive hierarchical taps read state and never write it. The rule
  holds for the `all` sign-off sweep and for every card that claims sign-off
  PASS; a leaf whose checks still read the forced signal is held out of `all`
  and recorded under Known Limitations until its checks move to the registers.
* *Checked, not observed.* A read that is printed but not compared is not
  evidence. Expectations come from the generated RDL reset values, the
  preloaded assets, or the specification -- never from a value the DUT
  returned earlier in the same run.
* *Negative checks carry a positive control.* A claim that a signal stays
  low is only meaningful if the same run shows it going high.
* *Evidence tokens.* Each testcase emits `CHK-*` lines that name what was
  compared and against what, so a kept log can be read without the source.

[[smc-vplan-scope-tiers]]
==== Scope tiers

One DUT. Three phases on cocotb over Verilator, plus the SV-UVM realizations
of the scenarios that carry one (`--framework uvm`, `SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc`).

[cols="1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Phase |Environment |Job

|Phase 1
|cocotb / PyUVM on Verilator: the SEP_IN AXI sequencer, the TB responders and the `tb_top` pins and plusargs
|Smoke plus per-area representatives: the three leaves of `smoke`; the sanity, smoke, precheck, observability and bring-up leaves of each area (the SAMPLE-only names among them; `smc_occp_sanity_secure_error_test` injects a fault and is Phase 2); and the bring-up representatives the Matrix (<<smc-traceability-matrix>>) names: `smc_avsbus_sanity_test`, `smc_canonical_smoke_test`, `smc_clk_running_test`, `smc_cold_reset_test`, `smc_cpu_to_sep_axi_test`, `smc_dbs_idle_test`, `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test`, `smc_efuse_otp_clock_test`, `smc_flr_sanity_test`, `smc_gpio_irq_active_test`, `smc_gpio_observe_test`, `smc_i2c_cg_sanity_test`, `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test`, `smc_input_fabric_axi_wr_rd_test`, `smc_irq_observe_test`, `smc_mailbox_idle_test`, `smc_register_sanity_test`, `smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test`, `smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test`. Fewest tests that carry the most real datapath behaviour.

|Phase 2
|Same cocotb environment
|Iconic feature coverage by area: the other Matrix tests (`smc_default_reg_rd_test`, `smc_i2c_master_target_test`, `smc_ijtag_basic_test`, `smc_input_output_fabric_wr_rd_test`, `smc_mailbox_irq_test`, `smc_multi_reset_csr_persistence_test`, `smc_output_filter_remap_security_test`, `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test`), the owning tests of the feature denominator rows and the per-area tests that prove a documented mode, command or path end to end, plus the cross-area edges a per-block bench cannot see. Randomize when there is a legal matrix (`RAND-REP` / `RANDCFG`); keep directed (`RAND-NONE`) when there is not.

|Phase 3
|Same cocotb environment. A test whose evidence needs a four-state value carries `tools = ["vcs"]` on its testlist entry and runs on demand; no Phase 3 entry carries it today.
|Residual contracts: the contracts of the specification and the register description that no Phase 1 or Phase 2 check grades. Corner and illegal cells, past-extent and gap responses, fault or error injection, reset, lock and retention behaviour, sticky status, timing and ratio matrices, register sweeps and islands, concurrency and contention, the fixed-cell variants, and every test whose Objective says it proves what no other test grades. A Phase 3 test never overlaps a Phase 1 or Phase 2 test. A test that extends an open test names that test in its Objective. Randomize when there is a legal matrix (`RAND-REP` / `RANDCFG`); keep directed (`RAND-NONE`) when there is not. Every expected value comes from the specification and the register description, never from the RTL and never from another test. A check that rests on a PROPOSED internal drive is blocked and takes no credit. A read-only observation tap, an error inject and a drive of an `smc_wrapper` port are not PROPOSED. A test with no executable check is parked (<<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>).
|===

Phase 1, Phase 2 and Phase 3 are scope tiers, not a schedule. Phase 1 is the
bring-up and representative set. Phase 2 is the dense, breadth and fault set.
Phase 3 is the residual set. Each test entry names its phase in its `*Phase*`
field and its area in its `*Area*` field; the four cards of
<<smc-held-out-testcases>> are outside `all`, take no credit and carry neither
field. `SMC_FCOV.adoc` keeps its own
organisation by collector module; a cover point does not follow the phase of
its owning test. A tier says what a test is asked to prove. It does not say
when the test is written. A Phase 3 entry takes credit under the rules of
<<smc-credit-rules>> and <<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>. The behaviours this
plan does not claim are in <<smc-vplan-scope,Verification Scope>>. The Phase 3
tests of each area are listed in <<smc-vplan-phase3-overview>>. The Phase 3
contracts that no test can grade are in <<smc-vplan-phase3-lists>>. The
observation taps, the bench hooks and the PROPOSED drives of the Phase 3 tests
are in <<smc-vplan-phase3-proposed>>. The parked-test rule of Phase 3 is in
<<smc-vplan-phase3-parked>>, and the randomization class of every Phase 3 test
is in <<smc-vplan-phase3-random>>.

Randomization contract: the *same* configuration object programs the DUT and
the golden. Pin the datapath directed first, then upgrade that test to
randomized; do not ship a one-point stand-in for a matrix. Skip randomization
only when the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake). The class of every test is one of:

* `RAND-REP`: the seed draws points from a legal matrix, and every point has a stated outcome.
* `RANDCFG`: the seed draws a configuration, the test runs one scenario under it, and the expected outcome is a function of the configuration.
* `RAND-NONE`: the stimulus is directed, for the reason the entry states.

[[smc-vplan-drawn-cells]]
*Drawn cells.* This is the contract for a new test. Regression seeds are
random per leaf, and a leaf does not know its run index, so no seed and no
testlist entry pins a cell. A leaf draws its cells from its seed
(`random.Random(seed)` with `RANDOM_SEED`, weighted toward the corners where
the entry says so, with the constraint filters of the entry), and
`--seed N` replays the leaf. The stream is not a CSPRNG and no drawn value is
a key, a token or a nonce. No document quotes a per-seed value as evidence. A
leaf walks a cell set in every run only when the set is cheap and
contract-critical: a legal minimum or maximum, one representative of each leg,
or the error-injection case itself. A test has one testlist entry; a second
entry exists only when the run mode differs in a way that one entry cannot
carry (a time-0 bench plusarg, a different target, a firmware image), never to
pin a cell. The existing exception is the fixed-cell variant modules: the
clock-cell families of `smc_ref_reset_cycles_test`,
`smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_test`, `smc_octs_clk_rate_test` and
`smc_clk_relation_regxbar_test` (fourteen variant modules, each pinned by a
`+smc_cell` entry) and the image-kind family of
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` (five variant modules, each pinned by a
`+smc_efuse_image` entry), nineteen modules in all, plus the sixteen
`smc_clk_*` modules that pin the three clock periods as module constants:
fifteen Phase 3 cells and the owning leaf of the family,
`smc_clk_smc_slower_than_ref_test`, which is Phase 2. Thirty-four of these
thirty-five modules are directed (`RAND-NONE`) cells, and their entries say so.
The one exception is `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test`, `RANDCFG` in its
entry: the cell pins the image kind, and the module draws the image words and
the write-lock bits of that kind from the seed
(`cocotb/tests/smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test.py`).

[[smc-vplan-audit]]
Checker contracts in this plan are written against these known ways a check
can pass while the DUT is unable to fail it.

*An expectation that shares a source with the thing it measures.* A golden
must not be a value the DUT returned earlier in the same run, and the
agreement of the RTL with a document is corroboration rather than the source.
This plan's rule is the second bullet of the
<<smc-vplan-strategy,Verification Strategy>>: expectations come from the
generated RDL reset values, the preloaded assets or the specification. Where an entry writes back the value it
has just read (the identity write of `smc_reg_island_boundary_sweep_test`),
the entry says that the write is a no-change control and not a golden.

*Golden compared against golden.* An assert between a result already pinned
to its golden and another output of the same model holds with the simulator
switched off. The memory-model goldens of the DMA and zeroer leaves are
TB-local and are compared against the SYS_OUT responder's memory, never
against another field of the same model.

*A guard whose own constructor makes it unfalsifiable.* Non-vacuity must not
rest on a relation the configuration builder or the simulator already
guarantees. `smc_5agent_observability_test` states the case: a SAMPLE gated
only on `item.resolvable` has no FAIL path, because `resolvable` cannot be
false under the 2-state simulator every retained run uses, so the GPIO leg is
a pair of SAMPLEs whose expectation is stated on the raw pad-bus vectors.

*A stimulus with no fan-out.* Driving a pin that nothing reads in the
configuration under test and asserting that an observable did not move is a
DV-invented scenario, not a specification claim. `feat_ctrl` bit 37
`SMC_FUSE_TEST` is not consumed by SMC, so the lifecycle-gated JTAG eFuse
matrix cannot observe it and Known Limitations keeps it as a negative item;
the bench tie-offs of <<smc-bench-tie-offs>> record every constant input in
the same way.

*A tolerance wider than the signal.* A post-event bound above the count the
window actually reaches passes when the event is ignored. The hang-detector
window entries (`smc_hang_sep_timeout_window_test`,
`smc_hang_sys_timeout_window_test`, `smc_hang_data_timeout_window_test`)
stall below, at and beyond the threshold, so the bound is tight on both sides.

*A check that reads back nothing.* Walking a register through several
encodings without reading it back cannot distinguish a register stuck at its
reset value. The rule is the second bullet of the Verification Strategy: a
read that is printed but not compared is not evidence; a write-only leg reads
back through the register or through an output the write must move.

*Entailed guards.* The absence of a complementary-arm marker, or a deferred
line, is not a checker; the owning test already fails if a forbidden marker
appears. A negative check carries a positive control in the same run (third
bullet of the Verification Strategy), and an aggregate the bench cannot back
stays observed-only, as the `tb_gpio_*_any` aggregates of
`smc_5agent_observability_test` do.

[[smc-vplan-reserved-bits]]
*Reserved bits.* Every graded register compare (an expected value from the
RDL or a model, a read-back, a before-and-after compare, or a compare of two
reads) uses the RDL field bits of the register only. A reserved bit is graded
only where the RDL or the specification states its value. A reserved bit with
no stated value is masked out of the compare. The entries that mask reserved
bits today name the mask in their Test Coverage; a new entry also logs the
masked bits and the mask on the PASS or FAIL line.

[[smc-vplan-evidence-gate]]
==== Evidence gate

Per-run logs land under the runner's run tree (git-ignored). PASS/FAIL
requires positive evidence from `results.xml`; a clean simulator exit alone is
not enough (`SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc`, House rules). A test passing is the entry
condition for reading its checkers, never a substitute for them. A checker row
exists only if a run can prove it. A log tag is not the proof.

Every graded contract is reported as a `CHK-<ID>:` line at the start of a log
message. `smc_base_test` reads the IDs from the log records of the whole run
(`_EvidenceRecorder`), and when the scenario returns it prints one line per
test:

----
EVIDENCE_SUMMARY test=<name> observed=N own=N required=N missing=N ids=...
----

`own` is the observed set less the IDs the base class emits itself
(`CHK-BUILD-MODEL-IDENTITY` and the `CHK-PROBE-` positive controls of
bring-up). A leaf whose `own` count is zero fails, unless
`_EvidenceRecorder.NO_OWN_EVIDENCE` names it; that map is empty and held under
a ceiling that never grows. A leaf declares `required_evidence = ("CHK-A",
...)`, a sorted tuple of the IDs that must appear, and may set
`min_evidence = N` as a floor on `own`. A run that never emits a required ID
fails with `EVIDENCE FAIL`. A plain cocotb leaf over `SmcDualHarness` is
registered through the `dual_test` decorator with the module's
`REQUIRED_EVIDENCE`, and the decorator runs the same gate when the leaf
returns.

The tuple is the plan's list. `tools/dv/tests/test_smc_required_evidence.py`,
run by CI with the other DV unit tests, reads every Test Procedures card of
this file, imports every member of the `all` group, and requires that every
member is a module attribute with a card of its own, that `required_evidence`
is a sorted tuple of `CHK-` tokens, that every required token is declared in
the card's Checkers table, and that every cocotb token the card declares is
required by the leaf (a row marked `SV-UVM shape only` is the UVM shape's
checker and is not expected from cocotb; a `<placeholder>` in a declared name
makes it a template that concrete required names instantiate). No mismatch is
tolerated today: the test's `PLAN_CODE_MISMATCH` map is empty, under a one-name
ceiling that can only shrink.

The gate proves that a check ran. It does not prove that the check was right.

[[smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy]]
==== Blocked taxonomy

The Phase 3 entries and the Phase 3 lists use four class words and four terms
for bench items, with these meanings:

* *PROPOSED*: a hook that drives, forces or deposits into a net or a state
  inside `smc` (the `smc_wrapper` DUT and everything it instantiates) for a
  purpose other than error injection, and that `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`
  and `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` do not already have.
* *Observation tap*: a read-only observation that drives nothing: a `tb_*`
  observation signal of the signal list `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/smc_tb_signal_list.svh`,
  a public-scope line of `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/smc_public_scope.vlt`, an observation
  `bind` or a hierarchical read reference of a DUT net. An observation tap is not
  PROPOSED and blocks no check or leg. A tap that
  `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list is an observation tap the
  test adds to the SMC_TB_ARCH signal list.
* *Added hook*: an error inject or a top-port drive that
  `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list and that `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` does not have. An error
  inject is an inject or a force that puts a fault or an illegal condition into
  the DUT, at a net inside `smc` or outside it. A top-port drive is a drive of
  a port of `smc_wrapper` by the bench: a pad, a strap, a reset or power-good
  pin, a SEP, SYS or JTAG port, an external interrupt lane, a memory-macro
  response, or a port value that a plusarg sets. An added hook is not PROPOSED
  and blocks no check or leg. The test adds it to the HDL Top section of
  `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc`.
* *Existing bench hook*: a drive, a force, an inject or a time-0 plusarg that
  `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` has: the inject and poke hooks
  (`tb_cpu_ecc_inject_*`, `tb_cpu_ecc_poke_*`, `tb_cpu_scratch0_inject_fire`,
  `tb_efuse_read_error_inject`, `tb_efuse_read_state_inject*`,
  `tb_efuse_program_state_inject*`, `tb_zeroer_state_inject*`,
  `tb_dfd_fault_inject`), the responder and channel holds
  (`tb_output_axi_resp_hold`, `tb_sep_axi_b_hold`, `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`,
  `tb_sys_axi_r_hold`), the pad and pin drives (`tb_pad_drive_*`,
  `tb_gpio_ext_drive_*`, `tb_uart0_rx_ext_drive`, `tb_boot_stall_jtag_ovrd_i`,
  `tb_plic_threshold0`, `tb_hold_cpu_boot`, `tb_hold_ext_boot`) and the plusargs
  (`+smc_hold_cpu_boot`, `+smc_hold_ext_boot`, `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`,
  `+smc_i2c1_pads`, `+smc_uart_cross_3to0`, `+smc_front_port_r_arb_assertoff`,
  `+bfm_rom_hex`, `+bfm_rom_bin64`). It is existing DV infrastructure and is
  approved, whatever net it drives and whatever its purpose: it is not
  PROPOSED, it is not an added hook, and it blocks no check or leg. When
  `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list it, the test that uses it
  adds its row there.
* *Preload*: the content of a memory outside the checked path that the
  approved t=0 image load of `tb_top.sv` puts in place before it is read: the
  eFuse bank image (`+smc_efuse_hex`; the testlist arg `+smc_efuse_image` names
  an image kind to the cocotb leaf, which renders it at the path `+smc_efuse_hex`
  names), a ROM image (`+rom_hex`, `+rom_bin64`) or a scratch-RAM firmware image
  (`+smc_scratch_ram_hex`). A preload is part of the approved t=0 image load.
  It is not a hook, it is not PROPOSED, and it blocks no check or leg.
* *Blocked*: a check or leg that needs a PROPOSED item, or a value that the
  specification or the register description does not state. An entry writes
  `Blocked: <item or value>` at the check or leg: "Blocked: needs the PROPOSED
  drive `x`", or "Blocked: the specification does not state X". A blocked
  feature is a feature whose checks all need such a value. A blocked check or
  leg takes no credit and is not in an executable total.
* *Executable*: a Phase 3 test with at least one graded check that is not
  blocked.
* *Parked*: a Phase 3 test with no executable check. The entry of a parked
  test has the field `*Needs*: <PROPOSED items or unstated values>`, its
  summary row reads "3, parked", and it takes no credit and is not in an
  executable total.

=== Naming Rules

* Testcases are `smc_<feature>_<scenario>_test`, lower snake case.
* The cocotb module and the testlist entry share that name.
* Sequences are `<testcase>_seq`, in `cocotb/seq_lib/`.
* Evidence tokens are `CHK-<AREA>-<CLAIM>`, upper kebab case.

=== BFM Policy

Shared and vendored components are used where they exist. A local model is
written only where none fits, and every one carries a README beside it
naming what it replaces and why -- see `dv/models/README.md`.

Bus terminators answer a port that a real integration fills with the
adopter's CSRs. They are declared as terminators, never presented as
verifying the block behind the port.

[[smc-vplan-scope]]
=== Verification Scope

This plan claims SMC behaviour at the `smc_wrapper` boundary and over the
SEP_IN AXI and JTAG-AXI ports, with the DUT elaborated at the open-source
integration's parameter defaults (four CPU cores, 256 external interrupts,
32 mailbox pairs, the 1 KiB eFuse map). The behaviours below sit behind
that boundary or belong to another level's plan; a green SMC regression says
nothing about them, and Known Limitations records the disposition of each.

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Behaviour |Why it is out of scope here
|The adopter's PLL and PVT blocks |Placeholder RTL in this harness; there is no design behind the register interface
|Everything behind the mandatory external AXI-Lite window (per-pad controls, clock-observation and pad-bias blocks) |Adopter implementation; this plan proves only the decode into the window
|The DTP CSR window and the raw OTP window |No responder on `smc_wrapper`; the boundary is left idle rather than answered by a placeholder
|The cluster PLIC register file from the external port |The aperture accepts no writes from SEP_IN; PLIC programming is proven only by the firmware leaves that run on the CPU
|I3C CCC and IBI scenarios needing device-address-table state |No DAT/DCT RAM in `tb_top`; the I3C leaf is decode-only
|The eFuse macro and the SEP lifecycle policy behind `lc_state_i` |An `efuse_bank_model` answers the sense; the lifecycle policy is SEP-level verification and the bench drives the resolved state
|The SMU integration of the SMC (`smu_wrapper` straps, cool-reset pin, boundary I/O) |The SMU plan (`hw/sys/smu/dv/docs/SMU_VPLAN.adoc`)
|===

[[smc-scope-traceability-candidate]]
=== Scope and Traceability

This section is the requirement-to-test-to-coverage matrix. Live group
membership is `hw/sys/smc/dv/testlists/all.toml` and the lists it includes;
`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_VPLAN.adoc` states what each testcase verifies. This
file is the reconciliation between the two — which of those testcases count as
feature credit, and which are bring-up or decode-only names that must not be
counted twice.

[cols=",",options="header",]
|===
|Field |Value
|DUT |`--dut smc` → `smc_wrapper` under `smc_uvm_top`
|Spec / plan |`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_VPLAN.adoc` plus the groups
`hw/sys/smc/dv/testlists/all.toml` resolves
|Coverage intent |`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_FCOV.adoc`: the `cov/sv` cover
properties in the `user` family, collected by `run_dv --dut smc --items
hosted fw --tool verilator --cov`
|Checker |The leaf's named `CHK-*` cocotb checkers on its card below + `results.xml`
|CI |`.github/workflows/sim.yml` PR `smoke`; `.github/workflows/regress.yml` nightly and weekly `hosted`
|===

[[smc-live-groups]]
==== Live groups versus credit

Executable membership is resolved from the testlists; the groups and their
`expected_count` guards are in `hw/sys/smc/dv/testlists/`:

[cols="2,3",options="header",]
|===
|Group |Role
|`smoke` |PR gate (`sim.yml`): canonical bring-up, cold reset, and a CSR frontdoor read
|`hosted` |Nightly and weekly (`regress.yml`): `all` minus the twenty leaves that need the RISC-V toolchain (fifteen `fw` leaves, three dual-target leaves that run a ROM or firmware image, and the two `mmio_wedge` leaves of `cpu`)
|`sanity` |The three dual-target leaves, held out of `all`
|`occp_rom` |33 of the 34 BL0/SMC ROM cases (`smc_occp_ring_buffer_stress_test` is left out for runtime), including the hours-long dual-SMC unsecure boot. <<smc-rom-dv-verification-plan>> grades them
|`rtl_issue` |Weekly on its own `regress.yml` row: defect reproducers graded under `expect_fail`; no feature credit
|`all` |The package regression, gated by its `expected_count`; `holdout.toml` defines the non-ROM leaves outside it, `sanity` holds the dual-target leaves, and <<smc-held-out-testcases>> records the sign-off holdouts
|===

`smoke` is the three-leaf PR gate (`smc_canonical_smoke_test`,
`smc_cold_reset_test`, `smc_register_sanity_test`). `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test`
is in `hosted` but not `smoke`, and receives no feature credit.

[[smc-credit-rules]]
==== Credit rules

* Feature credit requires active CSR/fabric/pin stimulus and a named
  `CHK-*` checker that can fail. SAMPLE-only bring-up stays in
  `hosted` (`smc_cold_reset_test` is also in `smoke`) and is not a
  requirement row.
* `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` is HCI_VERSION decode (`proxy=True`). It
  remains runnable by name. It is not
  stub-signature SLVERR, and it is not I3C protocol credit.
* Names in <<smc-deferred-disposition>>, adopter PLL/PVT OKAY+0 wraps, and
  TB-glue DFD tokens are OUT.
* UART loopback and ROM firmware receive no feature credit in this matrix.
* `--dut smc` instantiates `smc_wrapper`. Bring-up and POR credit is
  carried by `smc_canonical_smoke_test` and the reset cluster
  (`smc_cold_reset_test`, `smc_powergood_glitch_test`,
  `smc_multi_reset_csr_persistence_test`).
* A Phase 3 entry takes credit only when its test is in `all`, the named
  evidence that its entry declares (`CHK-<ID>` lines, <<smc-vplan-evidence-gate>>)
  is in the leaf log, and `results.xml` is positive. A blocked check or leg
  and a parked test take no credit (<<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>). A feature
  takes credit once, at the earliest phase that proves it; a later test that
  also reaches the feature does not take the credit again. Every graded
  register compare follows the reserved-bit rule of <<smc-vplan-reserved-bits>>.

[[smc-feature-denominator]]
==== Feature denominator

The denominator is the set of behaviour features in the SMC architecture
chapters: the chapters `hw/sys/smc/doc/index.adoc` lists in its reading order
(clocks and resets, CPU, boot ROM, interconnect, interrupts, peripherals with
the DMA engine, zeroer and watchdog pages, design-for-debug, eFuse scan
protection, memory map), the rows of the peripheral summary table in
`hw/sys/smc/doc/periphs.adoc`, and the TRM and integrator statements that
constrain the SMC (`doc/trm/src/clock_domains.adoc`, `doc/trm/src/reset.adoc`,
`doc/trm/src/memory_map.adoc`, `doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`). Each feature
has one row: its spec source, the live leaves that own it (every name is a
test entry under `hw/sys/smc/dv/testlists/` and is in `all` unless the
cell says otherwise), representative `cov/sv` points from
`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_FCOV.adoc`, and its credit. The feature-credit matrix
that follows is the sign-off subset of this table: it carries only canonical
scenarios, one leaf per row with a cocotb `CHK-*` checker that can fail and a
`cov/sv` point group, so a row there is a claim the regression's PASS proves.
A feature with leaves and points but no credit row is exercised by the
regression and graded by its leaves' cards; it is not a sign-off claim, and
its Credit cell says why.

Credit values:

* `YES`: a feature-credit row below carries it; the cell names the row's leaf.
* `OUT`: a Verification Scope row keeps it out; the cell names the row.
* `NO`: a `NO` row below; runnable by name, not credited.
* `REGRESSION`: enrolled leaves and collected points, no credit row; the cell
  states why the scenario is not a canonical credit row.
* `DECODE-ONLY`: the collected points reach only the feature's CSR decode.
* `NO POINT`: enrolled leaves, no `cov/sv` point.

[[smc-traceability-matrix]]
==== Matrix (feature-credit subset)

Requirement IDs are the VPLAN TC rows or the canonical scenario those
tests actually run. Coverage intent names the `cov/sv` collector modules and
representative `user` cover points that measure the feature
(`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_FCOV.adoc`); which leaf reaches each point is the
measured table in `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_FCOV_OWNERS.adoc`. The covergroups
under `ifndef VERILATOR` are the VCS `group` metric and are not part of it.
Checker evidence names the cocotb `CHK-*` checkers on the leaf's card.

The Groups column is resolved membership, not intent. Every feature-credit row
below is in `all` and `hosted`; the column names the feature groups that also
carry it, so a reviewer can run one feature without the whole regression.

|Testcase |Phase |Objective
|`smc_avsbus_clock_config_proxy_test` |3 |AVS_CFG answers OKAY with AVS_CG_EN cleared and SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E when set, then answers its recorded words again once cleared.
|`smc_avsbus_frame_transaction_test` |2 |Three queued AVS_CMD words walk the AVSBus command path against a responding pad and land one readback entry each.
|`smc_avsbus_interrupt_sources_test` |2 |Each AVSBus FIFO interrupt source raised, observed, cleared through the write-only clear register and observed gone.
|`smc_avsbus_retry_exhaust_test` |2 |Two unanswered AVS_CMD words walk the AVSBus retry states and exhaust the programmed retry budget.
|`smc_avsbus_sanity_test` |1 |Run the AVSBus sideband CSR precheck (alias of `smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq`).
|`smc_avsbus_status_depth_test` |3 |Run AVSBus status-side decode checks.
|`smc_dma_reg_byte_enable_error_test` |3 |Every writable DMA register refuses a two-byte write that omits lanes its PERMIT mask requires, and reads back unchanged.
|`smc_dma_reserved_stream_banks_test` |3 |All sixteen DMA stream banks decode with `NUM_CTRL_STREAMS = 1`; reserved banks read their `dma.adoc` value and launch nothing.
|`smc_dma_sanity_test` |1 |Run DMA copy over output-fabric payload bytes and check the model.
|`smc_octs_dual_sync_test` |2 |SECONDARY pad inject + PRIMARY sync/credit pad edges.
|`smc_octs_sanity_test` |1 |AVSBus status-CSR decode plus the sideband observability probe, a recorded SUBSTITUTE for a pad-level OCTS checker; touches no OCTS register or pad.
|`smc_periph_cg_access_error_test` |3 |Each CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL peripheral enable (AVSBus, I2C, UART, telemetry, I3C) set in turn: the gated window answers SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E on read and SLVERR on write, and its recorded word again once ungated.
|`smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test` |1 |Run the AVSBus sideband CSR representative precheck.
|`smc_telemetry_atb_capture_test` |3 |One ATB message captured on telemetry receiver 0, read back through its registers, then the receiver and transmitter flush paths.
|`smc_telemetry_receiver_csr_test` |2 |TELEMETRY CSR reset + INTR_TEST -> tb_telemetry_irq_any.
|`smc_wdt_key_csr_test` |2 |WDT writes are gated by the KEY magic value, COUNT_HI re-locks, and narrow writes are dropped, proven per core.
|`smc_wdt_timeout_pin_test` |2 |A programmed first timeout raises `smc_wdt_first_timeout_o`; uncleared, the second timeout raises `smc_wdt_second_timeout_o` and the warm reset follows.
|`smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test` |2 |Run zeroer over output-fabric payload bytes and check the model.
|`smc_zeroer_multi_burst_test` |2 |Clear a region larger than one AXI burst and check the first and last word of each half, with a witness word past the end.
|`smc_zeroer_unaligned_test` |3 |Run two in-page jobs that start partway into a word and check that exactly their bytes are zeroed, with the rest of each edge word and the guard words either side keeping their poison.
|`smc_zeroer_sanity_test` |1 |Run zeroer over output-fabric payload bytes and check the model.
|`smc_avsbus_pad_enable_test` |3 |The `avs_clock` pad output enable follows
`AVS_CONFIG.AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` through its reset value, a 0 write and a 1 write, and with the enable
at 1 one AVS_CMD frame appears on `avs_mdata` and its reply reaches AVS_READBACK.
|`smc_avsbus_resync_force_test` |3 |A forced slave resync (`AVS_CFG_1.FORCE_SLAVE_RESYNC_OPERATION`)
from idle gives one resync episode, lets in-flight frames and replies complete, launches queued
commands once each in write order, and survives two back-to-back requests.
|`smc_avsbus_resync_timing_test` |3 |After a cold reset the AVSBus controller resyncs on its own, the
resync lasts 35 `avs_clock_o` periods with `avs_mdata` high, the status flags track the probe, the
probe stays one-hot, and the resync interval follows `AVS_CFG_0.RESYNC_INTERVAL`.
|`smc_octs_csr_access_test` |3 |The nine OCTS registers decode at their own offsets, reset to their
`system_timer_octs.rdl` values, read back their writable fields, ignore writes to the read-only
registers, and the dwords past the map are recorded.
|`smc_octs_primary_count_test` |2 |The PRIMARY count on `timer_count_o` starts from the preset, steps

==== OCCP

Two-instance and production-ROM scenarios. These build a different DUT from the
rest of the plan -- `target = "dual"` elaborates `SMC_DUAL`, and the OCCP family
runs `hw/sys/smc/bootrom/prod` instead of a DV stub image -- so they are

|`smc_i2c_controller_stretch_test` |2 |The DUT's I2C controller must wait out a held clock and still deliver the transfer.
|`smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test` |3 |An SDA edge inside an SCL high window is a START or a STOP; in a pulse the controller receives it
must report `SDA_UNSTABLE`, in a pulse the controller drives high it must report `SDA_INTERFERENCE`,
and the transfer is dropped.
|`smc_uart_rbr_error_path_test` |3 |A character that arrives broken while the receive FIFO is off must carry its flags through the
receiver buffer register.
|`smc_i2c_controller_exits_test` |3 |Two endings of a controller transaction no other leaf produces, and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` as a
register rather than a flag.
|`smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test` |3 |How one AVSBus frame follows another, which the command mix decides.
|`smc_i2c1_target_addr_stretch_test` |3 |The address-phase hold of card 232, on I2C1. Extends `smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test` on I2C1.
|`smc_i2c2_target_addr_stretch_test` |3 |The address-phase hold of card 232, on I2C2. Extends `smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test` on I2C2.
|`smc_i2c1_target_fast_controller_test` |3 |The abandon of card 236, on I2C1. Extends `smc_i2c0_target_fast_controller_test` on I2C1.
|`smc_i2c2_target_fast_controller_test` |3 |The abandon of card 236, on I2C2. Extends `smc_i2c0_target_fast_controller_test` on I2C2.
|`smc_i2c_target_read_abort_test` |3 |A target read ended by something other than the controller must raise the flag `i2c.rdl` gives it,
and that flag must behave as a register.
|`smc_i2c_controller_scl_events_test` |3 |Another device on SCL, at each point of a controller transfer where the controller has released it,
must be answered the way `i2c_controller_fsm` specifies for that point.
|`smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test` |3 |A controller that has started a transaction owns the bus until it gives a STOP; if software clears
`CTRL.ENABLEHOST` with the transaction still open, the controller gives that STOP itself.
|`smc_telemetry_buffer_overflow_test` |3 |Drive telemetry receiver 0 past each of its two bounded stores, the message buffer and the assembly
buffer, and check what the register documentation says happens at each bound.
|`smc_i2c_controller_queue_shapes_test` |3 |Six shapes of the controller's format queue that no other leaf writes. Every other controller leaf
queues one transaction at a time, gives it a STOP, and drains the receive FIFO while the read runs.
|`smc_i2c_controller_edge_timing_test` |3 |Test the controller's decisions that depend on how SCL and SDA move relative to each other. It
samples the two lines through matching synchronisers, so some decisions arise only when both lines
move on the same clock, or when SCL falls after the controller has already seen a stretch.
|`smc_i2c_target_loopback_test` |3 |`CTRL.LLPBK` in target mode, which `i2c.rdl` describes as a target that "sends all received SDA data
back out", driven against a transmit FIFO with one free entry.
|`smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test` |2 |Give the controller the slave replies that a level held on sdata cannot give. A held level only ever
produces all-zero or all-one replies.
|`smc_i2c_event_retain_test` |3 |I2C0 event and counter fields held to what `i2c.rdl` says a write may and may not do to them. Leaves
that raise these events clear them at once, so for most of them no other leaf makes the write that
must not clear a set bit.
|`smc_uart_thr_paths_test` |3 |UART0 transmit-holding and receive paths that only unusual programming reaches. Every other UART
leaf sets a non-zero divisor before writing `THR`, writes whole words, and uses a documented trigger
level.
|`smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test` |3 |Make a log fetch come back with an error. The other log-engine leaves raise `LOG_FETCH_ERR` only
through `INTR_TEST`.
|`smc_octs_credit_expired_test` |3 |`system_timer_octs.rdl` describes `CREDIT_EXPIRED.MAX_CYCLES_EXPIRED` as the largest number of
cycles since a count credit was due, on a secondary. It says: "To reset the value of this register,
write anything to it." No other leaf writes it.
|`smc_efuse_guard_target_test` |3 |The eFuse guard applying a field's hardware locks to the read and program interfaces. Every other
leaf that uses those interfaces targets bit 0, which lies in `LOCKS` itself, a field whose locks the
guard never applies. So no other leaf makes the guard look up a target and find a field.
|`smc_i2c_bus_corners_test` |3 |Five edges around the I2C0 target that the target leaves never reach.
|`smc_octs_primary_start_test` |3 |Start a PRIMARY OCTS timer that has never run. Every other OCTS leaf starts the timer only after a
secondary phase has already enabled it.
|`smc_decode_hole_test` |3 |Write and read the unmapped tail of three block apertures. The RDL address map reserves misc_wrap a
2 KiB aperture, the GPIO interfaces 4 KiB and the DMA controller 512 B (`ocah_aperture_size`), each
with a smaller decoded extent. The crossbars decode each block to its extent, so an address in the
tail reaches no block and the fabric's error slave answers it with the response the RDL gives an
access past the decoded extent (`ocah_past_extent_resp`: a DECERR read for all three).
|`smc_zeroer_size_corners_test` |3 |Run a zeroer job of zero bytes, and one that starts four bytes below a 4 KB boundary and ends
mid-word. Every other zeroer leaf starts on a word, ends on a word and stays inside one page.
|`smc_hang_detector_disable_test` |3 |Clear the SEP hang detector's `enable` while the detector has fired, and drive `irq_test` with
`enable` clear. The other hang detector leaves clear `enable` only while the detector is quiet, and
drive `irq_test` only with `enable` set.
|`smc_cpu_uncore_reset_test` |3 |Request the CPU cluster's uncore reset on its own with every core released. The other CPU reset
leaves request core level resets and core pulses, never the uncore reset alone.
|`smc_dma_backpressure_test` |3 |Queue DMA descriptors behind a destination that stops answering, and read a burst the responder
errors part-way through. The other DMA leaves launch one descriptor of at most eight bytes and wait
for it, so the DMA never has more than one burst in flight, never reads more than one beat per
burst, and never has a descriptor waiting behind another.
|`smc_i3c_private_write_test` |2 |Queue an I3C transfer on I3C0 and I3C1. The other single-build I3C leaves read the CSR window and
set `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE`, but none queues a command, so those controllers never drive their
buses.
|`smc_jtag_axi_shape_test` |3 |The third inbound manager of the input fabric carries the same burst and error-response shapes the
SEP_IN and SYS_IN shape leaves establish.
|`smc_i2c_window_landing_test` |3 |Place I2C0 `CTRL` writes, and a second timeout, on I2C clocks where a bus-monitor or target decision
rests on a one- or two-clock condition. No other leaf times a register write to the I2C clock.
|`smc_uart_window_landing_test` |3 |Place UART0 register writes on the clock the transmit FIFO empties and on the clock the receive
timeout fires. No other leaf times a register write to the UART clock.
|`smc_fw_i3c5_csr_access_test` |held out |The SMC CPU reads `HCI_VERSION` and `HC_CONTROL` in the CSR window of I3C instance 5 and sets and
restores `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE`; the accesses are counted at the I3C cores' CSR ports.
|===

=== Test Procedures

[[smc-vplan-area-misc]]
==== MISC

[[sec-001-smc_5agent_observability_test]]
===== 1 `smc_5agent_observability_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_5agent_observability_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/combined.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `combined`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `combined`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SMC OSS PyUVM 5-agent full observability test.

*Test Coverage*:

* A bare idle IRQ sample, whose `sync_irq` / `gpio_irq_any` / `uart_irq_any` == 0 compares also pass on a stuck-at-0 or mis-bound probe, proves nothing on its own. The SAMPLE is therefore preceded by a **positive control**: GPIO0 is armed over the real SEP_IN AXI frontdoor and driven low at the pad until `tb_gpio_irq_any` is observed at 1, and an IRQ item carrying `expect_gpio_irq_any = 1` is sampled inside that window (`[NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL]`).
* A single SAMPLE gated only on `item.resolvable` gives `CHK-5AGENT-GPIO` no FAIL-ON path, because `resolvable` cannot be False under the 2-state simulator every retained run uses. The GPIO leg is therefore a *pair* of SAMPLEs whose expectation is stated on the **raw pad-bus vectors** (`tb_core2pad_o` / `tb_core2pad_en_o`), backed in the same run by `ensure_gpio_pad_bus_control`. The three `tb_gpio_*_any` aggregates are unbackable in this TB and stay OBSERVED-ONLY -- the scoreboard refuses a stated expectation on them (`[EVIDENCE-TOKEN-CONDITIONAL]`, `[NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL]`).
* The 5-agent composition claim is gated on the **per-type** scoreboard counters, not on the aggregate `total > 0` gate, so a missing item type is a composition failure instead of an invisible hole (`[EXACT-EXPECTATION]`).

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-5AGENT-CLK` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-COMPOSITION` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-GPIO` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-I2C` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-IRQ-IDLE` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-IRQ-POSITIVE` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-5AGENT-RESET` |Named compare in `smc_5agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-5AGENT-CLK`, `CHK-5AGENT-COMPOSITION`, `CHK-5AGENT-GPIO`, `CHK-5AGENT-I2C`, `CHK-5AGENT-IRQ-IDLE`, `CHK-5AGENT-IRQ-POSITIVE` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `combined`.

*Scope limit*: The three `tb_gpio_*_any` aggregates cannot be backed in this bench and stay
observed-only; the scoreboard refuses a stated expectation on them.
'''''

[[sec-002-smc_6agent_observability_test]]
===== 2 `smc_6agent_observability_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_6agent_observability_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/combined.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `combined`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SMC OSS PyUVM 6-agent full observability test.

*Test Coverage*:

* All six agents (reset / i2c / clk / irq / gpio / axil) sampled in one scenario.
* Each agent's mapped expectation is asserted here and only then does the body emit that agent's `CHK-6AGENT-<AGENT>:` evidence token, so no token can be printed from the setup path or from an item whose compare did not run (`[EVIDENCE-TOKEN-CONDITIONAL]`).
* The composition claim is gated on the **scoreboard's typed counters** (`EXPECTED_SAMPLES`), which are incremented on the analysis path: a mis-bound agent, a dropped item type or a monitor that never published fails the gate.
* The ordered `chk_seen` list is a log record of which legs ran, not a compare: `_chk` appends to it in the same straight-line body, so the composition check is the scoreboard's typed counters (`[NO-ALWAYS-PASS-CHECKER]`).

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-6AGENT-AXIL` |AXIL compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-6AGENT-CLK` |CLK compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-6AGENT-COMPOSITION` |Named compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-6AGENT-GPIO` |GPIO compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-6AGENT-I2C` |I2C compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-6AGENT-IRQ` |IRQ compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-6AGENT-RESET` |RESET compare in `smc_6agent_observability_test_seq.py`
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-6AGENT-AXIL`, `CHK-6AGENT-CLK`, `CHK-6AGENT-COMPOSITION`, `CHK-6AGENT-GPIO`, `CHK-6AGENT-I2C`, `CHK-6AGENT-IRQ` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `combined`.

*Scope limit*: The ordered `chk_seen` list is a log record of which legs ran, not a compare; the
composition check is the scoreboard's typed counters.
'''''

[[sec-003-smc_canonical_smoke_test]]
===== 3 `smc_canonical_smoke_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_canonical_smoke_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/combined.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `smoke`,
`combined`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `smoke`, `ci`, `combined`, `canonical`;
seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run six-agent observability across the reset recovery matrix.

*Test Coverage*:

* Canonical high-density SMC smoke sequence.
* This sequence combines the six-agent observability smoke with the reset recovery matrix in one canonical test.
* Synchronization contract: no step waits a magic number of `clk_ref_i` cycles and then samples.
* Every one is a bounded poll on the real reset observables via `SmcResetOp.WAIT_STATE` -- the driver polls until the exact expected state appears and the scoreboard converts bound expiry into a testcase failure with the last observed state (`[NO-BLIND-DELAY-SYNC]`, `[TIMEOUT-MUST-FAIL]`).
* Mid-window `RAW_SAMPLE` snapshots carry the exact asserted expectation they are taken for, so they are checked evidence instead of observations (`[EXACT-EXPECTATION]`).
* The remaining fixed `ClockCycles` are *driven stimulus widths* (how long a pin is held low), which is the quantity the sequence owns, never a stand-in for a completion handshake.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CANONICAL-SMOKE` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-COLD_PRIMARY_ASSERTED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-COLD_RELEASED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-COOL_PRIMARY_ASSERTED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-COOL_RELEASED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-PG_ASSERTED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-RESET-WAIT-PG_RELEASED` |Named compare in `smc_canonical_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CANONICAL-SMOKE`, `CHK-RESET-WAIT-COLD_PRIMARY_ASSERTED`, `CHK-RESET-WAIT-COLD_RELEASED`, `CHK-RESET-WAIT-COOL_PRIMARY_ASSERTED`, `CHK-RESET-WAIT-COOL_RELEASED`, `CHK-RESET-WAIT-PG_ASSERTED` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `combined`, `smoke`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-005-smc_default_reg_rd_test]]
===== 5 `smc_default_reg_rd_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_default_reg_rd_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/register.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `axil`, `canonical`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb module
`smc_default_reg_rd_test`); the SV-UVM half is the class `smc_default_reg_rd_test` of the same name,
selected with `+UVM_TESTNAME` (`--framework uvm`).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Run a compact OSS-safe default-register read sweep.

*Test Coverage*:

* Default register read smoke over the real SEP_IN AXI ingress port.
* The sweep reads side-effect-free internal SMC CSRs through `sep_axi_in_req_i` and checks that every selected address returns an OKAY AXI response **and** — wherever the generated register map defines one — the exact reset value for that register.
* Access-port identity: the test starts this sequence on `env.sys_axi_agent`, whose driver declares `bus_prefix = "s_axi"` / `bus_name = "SEP_IN AXI"` (`env/smc_sys_axi_agent.py`), and `tb_top.sv` wires the top-level `s_axi_*` pins into `smc.sep_axi_in_req_i`.
* The SYS_IN port (`sys_axi_*` -> `sys_axi_in_req_i`) is driven by the separate `env.sys_in_axi_agent`, which this test never starts; despite its name, `env.sys_axi_agent` drives SEP_IN.
* What that does and does not prove: every register read below lives inside `smc_misc_wrap` and is reached over the same internal register fabric from either ingress port, so the reset-default proof holds regardless of which port carried it.
* It gives NO coverage of the SYS_IN ingress port itself.
* Addresses come from the generated PeakRDL map only (indexed `SCRATCH_BASE_ADDR(idx)` macros and per-register `*_BASE_ADDR` symbols in `hw/sys/smc/regs/gen/c/smc_addr.h`); expected values come from `smc_csr_field_catalog` so the address and the value share one source.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_default_reg_rd_test_seq`. The scenario has two implementations that share this
claim: the cocotb `smc_default_reg_rd_test_seq.py` and the SV-UVM
`smc_default_reg_rd_test_seq.svh` (`--framework uvm`). Each checker below is a named compare
the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds. The SV-UVM view reads only
-- it writes nothing -- which is what lets it claim the registers still hold their reset value.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DEFAULT-REG-SWEEP` |Named compare in `smc_default_reg_rd_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DEFAULT-REG-VALUE` |Named compare in `smc_default_reg_rd_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DEFAULT-REG-VALUE-COMPARE-FLOOR` |Named compare in `smc_default_reg_rd_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-REG-DEFAULT` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): each catalogued register reads back its generated `*_REG_DEFAULT`. Two expectations are non-zero (`CHIP_CONFIG.VERSION_LO` = 0x000100A0, `RESET_UNIT.SS_WARM_RESET_N` = 0xFFFFFFFF), so a read path stuck at zero cannot satisfy the catalogue. One compared entry, `NDM_RESET.NDMRESET_REQUEST`, is `sw=r; hw=w` and its value arrives from the harness tie-off `tb_ndmreset_request = '0` at a DUT primary input -- the specified source for such a field, so the register block's decode and read path are in the loop, but the value is not register storage
|(decode-only entries) |SV-UVM: registers whose read value this bench does not establish carry no checker of their own -- the OKAY claim on the access is `CHK-CSR-RESP`, and the observed word is logged as an `OBSERVED-ONLY` observation rather than a check. `CHIP_CONFIG.LC_STATE` is driven by the harness, `NDM_RESET.NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` by a design-side count; both read something other than their RDL default, so comparing against it would be an invented claim
|`CHK-CSR-RESP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): every SEP_IN CSR access completes with an OKAY response
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): warm-reset domain release after fuse sense completes
|`CHK-NONVAC` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): reconciles the accesses the body issued against its own loop bounds -- a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated pass, not a DUT-failable compare. `CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` is the observed-side counterpart
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the `default_reg` feature's comparison count, taken from the always-on scoreboard fed by the PASSIVE monitor, is at or above the floor the completed passes imply (one predicted read per catalogue entry carrying a default)
|`CHK-SB-DEFAULT-REG` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): always-on scoreboard, feature `default_reg`: `smc_default_reg_ref_model` predicts every catalogued read from the generated defaults plus the writes it observed. A required feature with zero comparisons fails the run
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DEFAULT-REG-SWEEP`, `CHK-DEFAULT-REG-VALUE`, `CHK-DEFAULT-REG-VALUE-COMPARE-FLOOR` hold after their compares. Under `--framework uvm` the governing checker set is the SV-UVM one in the table above (the cocotb ids named at the head of this Pass Criteria do not run there), and `+SMC_DEFAULT_REG_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must fail the run. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The SYS_IN ingress port itself gets no coverage; every read is carried over SEP_IN.
In the SV-UVM shape, registers whose read value this bench does not establish
(`CHIP_CONFIG.LC_STATE`, driven by the harness, and `NDM_RESET.NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT`, a
design-side count) carry no checker of their own: only the OKAY response is claimed and the observed
word is logged as observed-only, not compared against the RDL default.
'''''

[[sec-006-smc_ext_interrupts_pin_test]]
===== 6 `smc_ext_interrupts_pin_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_ext_interrupts_pin_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `irq`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `ext`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: ext_interrupts_i[0] after prim_sync3.

* Does not claim PLIC or bits 1..255.

Drive `smc_ext_interrupts_pin_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[[sec-007-smc_fw_plic_claim_test]]
===== 7 `smc_fw_plic_claim_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_fw_plic_claim_test`

*BFM / Model*: the SMC C image `fw/tests/plic_sanity`, executed by the CPU cluster; stimulus on `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i`, `tb_temp_interrupt_i` and `tb_ext_interrupts_hi_i` (`ext_interrupts_i[16:0]`), verdict read over SEP_IN AXI

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fw.toml`; groups `all`, `fw`; not in `hosted` (needs
the RISC-V toolchain of the `c_compile` stage); `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags
`firmware`, `cpu`, `interrupt`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_cpu_boot`,
`+smc_scratch_ram_hex=plic_sanity.ecc.hex`; firmware image `plic_sanity`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Firmware programs the cluster PLIC and claims a real external interrupt through it.

*Test Coverage*:

* The cluster PLIC's enable, priority, threshold and claim-complete path, which **no cocotb sequence in this package can reach**. The 0xC400_0000 aperture answers SEP_IN AXI reads but takes no writes from it -- Known Limitations records that measurement. The CPU is the only master that can program it.
* The loop `smc_ext_interrupts_pin_test` states in its own docstring that it leaves open: that testcase follows `ext_interrupts_i[0]` through `prim_sync3` and "does not claim PLIC". `smc_hang_detector_plic_route_test` checks a route with testbench probes and reads no PLIC register either. This closes it end to end: pin -> synchroniser -> gateway -> enable and priority against threshold -> MEIP -> trap -> claim -> the ID the CPU reads back -> complete.
* PLIC source 1, which is `cpu_interrupts[0]` and therefore `ext_interrupts_i[0]`: the SMC interrupt-vector map (`doc/interrupts.adoc`, "SMC CPU Interrupt Vector Map") places the external interrupts at the bottom of the vector and defines the PLIC source ID as the bit index plus one because ID 0 is reserved; `tt_smc_interrupts.h` transcribes that chapter. It is source 1 and not another because `tb_top.sv` drives `ext_interrupts_i[16:0]` -- bit 0 from `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i`, bit 1 from `tb_temp_interrupt_i`, bits [16:2] from `tb_ext_interrupts_hi_i` -- and ties every bit above 16 to zero, and source 1 is the only source enabled when the first claim runs: a claim of any other ID would leave the verdict unposted and the testcase would time out instead of measuring anything.
* No forced internal state: the stimulus is a DUT input pin and everything between it and the verdict is the DUT ([NO-FORCED-INTERNAL-STATE]).
* Sources 2-17 (`ext_interrupts_i[16:1]`) and the I2C controller 0 source (280, raised by the firmware through `INTR_TEST`) are each registered, enabled at distinct priorities and required to arrive exactly once under their own ID; then each threshold 1-6 is set with each source alone above it and that source alone must be claimed, and an idle claim read at every threshold 0-7 must return source 0. A claim of an unregistered or unexpected ID fails the image.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Build `plic_sanity` through `[c_build.default]`, stage `plic_sanity.ecc.hex`, hold `boot_stall` from t=0, clear CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0 and read the clear back.
. Program the reset vector and release. The image clears every context's enable words, gives the eight contexts distinct thresholds, registers a handler for source 1, enables it, publishes the arm word 0xAAAA_AAAA and parks in `wfi`. The handler masks the source through the context threshold (not the enable bit, which the PLIC requires set for a completion to count) and returns, so the driver's claim-complete write executes; main then lowers the threshold with the pin still high and requires a second delivery before it posts the verdict, because the gateway forwards a source again only after its previous claim was completed.
. Require the arm word before any verdict. A PASS not preceded by it is failed: the image would have reached its verdict without passing through the state the stimulus acts on.
. Hold the pin low for 2000 further `clk_smc_i` cycles and require SCRATCH_0 to still read the arm word.
. Drive `ext_interrupts_i[16:0]` high and poll for the verdict: the image claims and re-delivers source 1, then sources 2-17 and 280 once each, then each source alone at thresholds 1-6 plus an idle claim at every threshold, and posts PASS only after all of them.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FW-PLIC-QUIET` |With the PLIC armed and the pin still low, SCRATCH_0 does not move. Without this the PASS could have come from any interrupt already pending, and the testcase would be satisfied by a DUT that traps on something else
|`CHK-FW-PLIC-STIMULUS` |The pins rise only after the quiet window, so the verdict below is ordered after the stimulus rather than merely coincident with it
|`CHK-FW-PLIC-CLAIM` |The firmware's own PASS word reaches CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0, and only two completed claims of the registered source can put it there: the verdict is posted after the source, unmasked with the pin still high, is delivered a second time, which the PLIC gateway does only once the first claim has been completed. `riscv_plic0.c` dispatches `metal_exint_table[idx]` on the index the claim register returned, and the image registers a handler at one index only -- every other source reaches `__metal_plic0_default_handler`, which posts no verdict. The handler's own ID compare is unreachable for that reason and is not credited here
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold. The verdict poll is bounded at 6000 iterations of 100 `clk_smc_i` cycles; the image spends most of the boot in `__metal_driver_riscv_plic0_init`, which walks all 336 sources over MMIO. No `ci` tag: the hosted runners have no RISC-V toolchain. Enrolled in: `all`, `fw`.

*Scope limit*: The handler's own ID compare is unreachable (a claim of any other ID leaves the
verdict unposted and the run times out) and is not credited.

'''''

* write distinct patterns,

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CSR-SCRATCH-RW-RESTORE` |Each of the 3 scratch CSRs reads its generated RDL reset, reads back its written pattern, and reads back the reset again after the restore write, over 15 SEP_IN AXI accesses (cocotb shape). |`CHK-CSR-RESTORE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): restore write of zero reads back
|`CHK-CSR-RESP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): every SEP_IN CSR access completes with an OKAY response
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): warm-reset domain release after fuse sense completes
|`CHK-NONVAC` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): non-vacuity count of real SEP_IN CSR accesses in `smc_register_sanity_test_seq.svh`
|===

The seven `SV-UVM shape only` rows are that shape's checkers and are listed for it; they do not close this card's Pass Criteria. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `smoke`.

*Scope limit*: The seven SV-UVM-shape-only checker rows are listed for that shape and do not close
this card's Pass Criteria.
'''''

[[sec-327-smc_reg_island_boundary_sweep_test]]
===== 327 `smc_reg_island_boundary_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MISC

*Source Module*: `smc_reg_island_boundary_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcDecodeProbeSeq` / `SmcSysAxiItem` 4-byte reads and writes with
errors allowed, 64-bit reads of `REGION_SIZE` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`) at the local aperture base
(`LOCAL_BASE` reset) plus the island offsets, for the 24 register islands that declare a past-extent
response: `C0_WDT` to `C3_WDT`, `DFX`, `MAILBOX`, `DMA`, `ZEROER`, `CPUCTRL`, `RESET`, `MISC`,
`GPIO`, `AVS`, `I2C`, `EFUSE_MAP`, `EFUSE_IF`, `TELEM`, `OCTS`, `BASECFG`, `ALIAS`, `MREMAP_OUT`,
`XREMAP_OUT`, `INFLT` and `OUTFLT`; the four setup registers `REGION_SIZE`, `LOCAL_BASE`,
`GLOBAL_BASE` (`smc_base_config`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; window, decoded extent and past-extent
response of each island from the generated memory map; the sys-AXI monitor is told that the 48
past-extent and aperture-end addresses expect DECERR; a CSR protocol-VIP record is booked against
the access floor; no probe is sampled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/register.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `axil`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Each of 24 register islands answers OKAY inside its decoded
extent and its declared error response past it.

*Test Coverage*:

* Setup: `REGION_SIZE` (16 MiB reset), `LOCAL_BASE`, `GLOBAL_BASE` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (every
  peripheral clock-gate enable clear) read OKAY and equal their reset values in
  `smc_base_config.rdl`, so the probe table is exercised at the aperture and gate state it assumes;
  the probe table built from the generated memory map must equal the sweep's own table of first,
  last decoded, past-extent and aperture-end offsets and of each island's declared past-extent write
  response (`smc.rdl` `ocah_past_extent_resp`).
* First word of each island: reads answer OKAY, a declared hole (`RESET` first word) reads 0; every
  first word that is read-write or a hole takes a write of the value just read with an OKAY write
  response and reads it back unchanged; read-only first words (`DFX`, `MAILBOX`, `AVS`, `I2C`,
  `EFUSE_MAP`, `EFUSE_IF`, `TELEM`, `OCTS`, `INFLT`, `OUTFLT`) are read only.
* Last decoded word of each island (last word of the last instance for arrays): reads answer OKAY,
  declared holes (`GPIO`, `ALIAS`, `INFLT`, `OUTFLT`) read 0, and read-write or hole words take the
  identity write and read back unchanged; read-only or side-effect words (`MAILBOX`, `ZEROER`,
  `MISC`, `I2C`, `TELEM`) are read only; the watchdog state after the write is printed.
* First past-extent word and aperture-end word of every island: reads answer DECERR with data
  0xBADCAB1E, 48 of 48 words (`smc.rdl`, `memmap.adoc` decode response codes).
* The same words written: the nine islands whose RDL declares a DECERR write response (four
  watchdogs, `DFX`, `MAILBOX`, `DMA`, `ZEROER`, `CPUCTRL`) answer DECERR on 18 of 18 words; the
  fifteen islands whose RDL declares SLVERR answer SLVERR or DECERR on 30 words, counted per island
  as match (SLVERR) or recorded as a mismatch (the DUT answers DECERR where the generated map declares SLVERR; the mismatch count is printed, the code is not compared) rather than failed; any other response
  fails.
* A refused write takes no effect: after all writes every past-extent and aperture-end word still
  reads DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and every read-write last decoded word equals its earlier value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done; read the four setup registers requiring OKAY and their reset values;
  require `LOCAL_BASE` to equal the sweep base; derive the 24-island table from the generated memory
  map, require it to equal the sweep's table and require nine DECERR-class and fifteen SLVERR-class
  islands; register the past-extent and aperture-end addresses as expecting DECERR; stamp S1 and
  print the setup line.
. Read the first word of each island requiring OKAY and 0 from declared holes; stamp S2.
. Write the value read back to each read-write or hole first word, requiring OKAY, and read back
  requiring the same value; stamp S3 and print the first-word line with the per-island values.
. Read the last decoded word of each island requiring OKAY and 0 from declared holes; stamp S4.
. Write the value read back to each read-write or hole last decoded word, requiring OKAY, and read
  back requiring the same value; stamp S5 and print the last-word line.
. Error injection. Point: the first past-extent word and the aperture-end word of every island over
  SEP_IN AXI. Kind: a past-extent read of each of the 48 words. Expected response: DECERR with data
  0xBADCAB1E on every word. Stamp S6.
. Error injection. Point: the first past-extent word and the aperture-end word of the nine
  DECERR-class islands. Kind: a write of the value read to each of the 18 words. Expected response:
  DECERR on each. Stamp S7.
. Error injection. Point: the first past-extent word and the aperture-end word of the fifteen
  SLVERR-class islands. Kind: a write of the value read to each of the 30 words. Expected response:
  SLVERR or DECERR on each, counted as matches and mismatches, requiring 30 words in all. Stamp S8.
. Read every past-extent and aperture-end word again requiring DECERR and 0xBADCAB1E, and every
  read-write last decoded word again requiring OKAY and its earlier value; stamp S9.
. Print the 24-row table of first, last, past-extent and aperture-end responses and data with each
  island's declared class and match or mismatch; require 24 rows with every probe word measured;
  stamp S10, then S11, and require the access count to equal the floor of the table, the checker
  lines in order and the stamps strictly increasing.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ISL-SETUP-GOLDENS` |`REGION_SIZE`, `LOCAL_BASE`, `GLOBAL_BASE` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` read
OKAY and equal their RDL reset values, the 24-island probe table equals the generated memory map,
and the island split is nine DECERR-write and fifteen SLVERR-write.
|`CHK-ISL-FIRST-WORD-WRITE-OKAY` |The first word of all 24 islands answers OKAY (the `RESET` hole reads 0),
and every read-write or hole first word takes the identity write with an OKAY write response and
reads back the value read; read-only words are listed as read-only, with a reason column that
reads not specified for some islands.
|`CHK-ISL-LAST-DECODED-WORD-WRITE-OKAY` |The last decoded word of all 24 islands answers OKAY (declared
holes read 0), and every read-write or hole word takes the identity write with an OKAY write
response and reads back the value read; read-only words are listed as read-only, with a reason
column that reads not specified for some islands, and the
watchdog state is printed without a compare.
|`CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-READ-DECERR` |The first past-extent word and the aperture-end word of all 24
islands read DECERR with data 0xBADCAB1E, 48 of 48 words.
|`CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-WRITE-DECERR-CLASS` |The first past-extent word and the aperture-end word of the
nine DECERR-declared islands answer a write with DECERR, 18 of 18 words.
|`CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-WRITE-SLVERR-CLASS` |The 30 past-extent and aperture-end words of the fifteen
SLVERR-declared islands answer a write with SLVERR or DECERR (any other response fails); the count
of SLVERR matches and of DECERR answers (mismatches with the declared SLVERR) is printed per island.
|`CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-NOCHANGE` |After the refused writes every past-extent and aperture-end word still
reads DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and every read-write last decoded word equals its earlier value.
|`CHK-ISL-TABLE` |The per-island table has 24 rows, each with its four probe words measured, and
each row is counted as match or mismatch so that the two counts sum to 24.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The access count equals the floor derived from the table, the checker lines print in
order each after its step, every checker line covers at least one access, and the stamps S1 to S11
are strictly increasing.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ISL-SETUP-GOLDENS`, `CHK-ISL-FIRST-WORD-WRITE-OKAY`, `CHK-ISL-LAST-DECODED-WORD-WRITE-OKAY`,
`CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-READ-DECERR`, `CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-WRITE-DECERR-CLASS`, `CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-NOCHANGE` and
`CHK-ISL-TABLE` hold after their compares; `CHK-ISL-PASTEXT-WRITE-SLVERR-CLASS` holds when each of
the 30 words answers SLVERR or DECERR, DECERR answers being recorded as mismatches and not as a
match to the declared SLVERR; `CHK-NONVAC` is printed at the end. Enrolled in: `all`; also listed
in `register.toml`.

*Scope limit*: The watchdog state after the last-decoded-word write is printed without a compare.
For the fifteen SLVERR-declared islands a DECERR write answer is recorded and counted as a mismatch
against the declared SLVERR; the mismatch count is printed and the code is not compared. Read-only
first and last words are read only, and their reason column reads not specified for some islands.

'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-power]]
==== POWER

[[sec-010-smc_avsbus_clock_config_proxy_test]]
===== 10 `smc_avsbus_clock_config_proxy_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_clock_config_proxy_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: AVS_CFG answers OKAY with AVS_CG_EN cleared and SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E when set, then answers its recorded words again once cleared.

*Test Coverage*:

* **Positive control** -- with the gate CLEARED, all three AVS_CFG windows must complete OKAY, and the word each returns is recorded ([NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL]).
* **Negative leg** -- with the gate SET, the same three reads must complete SLVERR carrying the error-slave word `0xBADCAB1E`, and a write into AVS_CFG_0 must complete SLVERR. The access gate in front of the AVSBus controller answers these on the SMC clock, so a no-response is a failure of this leg, never a pass: the driver raises on a timeout ([TIMEOUT-MUST-FAIL]).
* **Recovery** -- with the gate CLEARED again, the three windows answer OKAY with the words the positive control recorded, so the refused write took no effect and the AVSBus controller is reachable again.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_avsbus_clock_config_proxy_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVSBUS-CG` |All three AVS_CFG windows answered OKAY with AVS_CG_EN cleared, all three answered SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E and the write into AVS_CFG_0 was refused with SLVERR while it was set, and all three returned the recorded word once it was cleared; the scoreboard booked the three CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL readbacks and the three recovery compares. A timeout, an OKAY while gated, a DECERR, another data word or a changed word after recovery fails it
|`CHK-SIDEBAND-OBSERVABILITY` |Named compare in `smc_sideband_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-AVSBUS-CG`, `CHK-SIDEBAND-OBSERVABILITY` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

*Test Coverage*:

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_avsbus_sanity_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-DEBUG-READBACK-NONDESTRUCTIVE` |Named compare in `smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-AVS-FIFOS-STATUS` |`AVS_FIFOS_STATUS` reads OKAY over SEP_IN with rdata equal to the empty-FIFO word from the generated `avsbus_controller.h` (`smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq.py`); the scoreboard fails the run on a mismatch
|`CHK-AVS-INTERRUPT-MASK` |Named compare in `smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-AVS-INTERRUPT-W1C` |Named compare in `smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-AVS-NORMAL-STATUS` |`AVS_NORMAL_STATUS` reads OKAY with rdata equal to the generated idle word (`smc_sideband_protocol_smoke_test_seq.py`); the scoreboard fails the run on a mismatch

[[sec-013-smc_dma_sanity_test]]
===== 13 `smc_dma_sanity_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_sanity_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcJtagAxiAgent` (JTAG-AXI bench agent over the `tb_top` JTAG-AXI bridge)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run DMA copy over output-fabric payload bytes and check the model.

*Test Coverage*:

* DMA source-to-destination payload check through the output-fabric responder.
* A second descriptor with LENGTH = 1 separates "the programmed length was honoured" from "a whole 64-bit beat was copied": the destination word's upper seven bytes must still read the poison this leg wrote.
* A third descriptor with LENGTH = 32 moves four full-width beats as one burst per direction: the destination is poisoned beat by beat with bytes that differ from the source in every lane, so a burst that repeats, drops or misplaces a beat fails on the bytes, and the address-channel tally requires exactly one read burst and one write burst.
* The SYS_OUT responder is shared, and the pass-all outbound filter this sequence programs lets other masters' traffic complete on it, so each leg's traffic is counted per address from the address-channel handshake of its own transaction rather than from the responder's global transaction counters.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dma_sanity_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-OUTPUT-FABRIC-TRAFFIC` |Per leg and per address: exactly one read transaction at the source, one write transaction at the destination and one verification read at the destination reached the SYS_OUT responder. A transaction sent to the wrong address, or a second one at the same address, fails. The number of transactions other masters completed on the same responder is printed on the same line as reported, not asserted
|===


*Pass Criteria*: all three copies match their expected destination bytes, the LENGTH = 1 leg leaves the destination's upper seven bytes at the poison, and each leg addressed the SYS_OUT responder exactly once per direction. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The number of transactions other masters completed on the shared SYS_OUT responder
is reported on the traffic line and not asserted.
'''''

|===

[[sec-018-smc_wdt_key_csr_test]]
===== 18 `smc_wdt_key_csr_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_key_csr_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).
