draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: WDT writes are gated by the KEY magic value, COUNT_HI re-locks, and narrow writes are dropped, proven per core.

*Test Coverage*:

* **negative leg** -- write `CMP` with the block LOCKED; `CMP` must still read its generated reset `0x1000`;
* **positive leg** -- write `KEY = 0x51F15E`, confirm `KEY` reads 1, write the same `CMP` probe, and require the exact probe back.
* **COUNT_HI leg** -- `COUNT_HI` at 0xC reads 0. With the block unlocked, a 32-bit write to it leaves `COUNT` at 0 and makes `KEY` read 0.
* **write-width leg** -- with the block unlocked, a 1-byte write to `CMP` answers OKAY, leaves `CMP` at reset and `KEY` at 1; a 2-byte write of the probe then reads back exactly and re-locks. A 1-byte write to `CTRL` byte 0 sets `wdogscale` and re-locks.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_wdt_key_csr_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-KEY-PROTOCOL` |Named compare in `smc_wdt_key_csr_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-WDT-COUNTHI-RELOCK` |Named compare in `smc_wdt_key_csr_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-WDT-WRITE-WIDTH` |Named compare in `smc_wdt_key_csr_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-WDT-KEY-PROTOCOL`, `CHK-WDT-COUNTHI-RELOCK` and `CHK-WDT-WRITE-WIDTH` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

'''''

[[sec-019-smc_wdt_timeout_pin_test]]
===== 19 `smc_wdt_timeout_pin_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_timeout_pin_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); `tb_top.sv` sticky latches `tb_wdt_first_timeout_seen` / `tb_wdt_second_timeout_seen` on the `smc_wrapper` timeout outputs

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A programmed first timeout raises `smc_wdt_first_timeout_o` at the DUT boundary; left uncleared, the stage-2 count in `CPU_CTRL.WDT_TIMEOUT` raises `smc_wdt_second_timeout_o`, and the reset unit turns that into the warm reset.

*Test Coverage*:

* core-0 WDT armed over SEP_IN with the magic-key protocol of `wdt.rdl` (`KEY` before each of `CMP`, `COUNT`, `CTRL`; `CTRL.wdogrsten | wdogenalways`);
* `smc_wdt_first_timeout_o` latched within a bound of arming, with `smc_wdt_second_timeout_o` still 0 on that cycle;
* `smc_wdt_second_timeout_o` latched `WDT_TIMEOUT` (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` reset `0x4000`) cycles after the first, within a stated slack;
* `rst_warm` still released on the cycle the first timeout latches, asserted after the second timeout, then released; both live pins read 0 afterwards while both sticky latches still read 1.
* The stage-2 count is kept per core (`smc_cpu_ctrl_wrap.sv`), so after core 0's pass the same sequence runs on cores 1, 2 and 3 in turn, each after the previous warm reset has released. The sticky latches are already set by then, so each of those passes observes the live pins, which the warm reset clears again.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_wdt_timeout_pin_test_seq`. Each checker below is a bounded observation of a `tb_top` pin the DUT can fail to drive; a token is emitted only after that observation holds. `+smc_wdt_timeout_negative` inverts the second-timeout expectation (demands it on the cycle the first one latches) and must FAIL; it is the control for the second-timeout observer.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-FIRST` |`tb_wdt_first_timeout_seen` reaches 1 within `FIRST_TIMEOUT_BOUND_CYCLES` of the arming readback, `tb_wdt_second_timeout_seen` still 0 on that cycle
|`CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-SECOND` |`tb_wdt_second_timeout_seen` reaches 1 between `WDT_TIMEOUT` and `WDT_TIMEOUT + SECOND_TIMEOUT_SLACK_CYCLES` cycles after the first
|`CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-RESET` |`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` reads 1 on the cycle the first timeout latches, falls within `WARM_RESET_BOUND_CYCLES` of the second timeout and rises again; live pins then 0, sticky latches 1
|`CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-CORES` |For each of cores 1, 2 and 3: `tb_wdt_first_timeout` rises within the bound of arming with `tb_wdt_second_timeout` still 0, the second rises `WDT_TIMEOUT` cycles later within the slack, and the warm reset asserts, releases and leaves both live pins 0
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-CORES`, `CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-FIRST`, `CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-SECOND`, `CHK-WDT-TIMEOUT-RESET` hold after their observations. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-020-smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test]]
===== 20 `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcJtagAxiAgent` (JTAG-AXI bench agent over the `tb_top` JTAG-AXI bridge)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run zeroer over output-fabric payload bytes and check the model.

*Test Coverage*:

* Zeroer datapath payload check through the output-fabric responder.
* CTRL_STATUS is read back after the payload is proven cleared and compared exactly with STATUS masked: INT_EN latched, reserved bits zero (`CHK-ZEROER-CTRL-STATUS`). No level is asserted for STATUS itself: the RDL describes the field as "completed" while the implemented field reads the opposite way round, so its resting level is recorded instead and the positive control in the next bullet proves the bit moves.
* A second, longer zeroing is run purely as the positive control for STATUS: the field must leave its resting level while that zeroing is in flight (`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-BUSY-ASSERTED`) and return to it once the zeroing completes (`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-LIFECYCLE`), so a tied or unconnected bit fails without the test taking a side on which level means busy.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Non-vacuity count in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-ZEROER-CMD-READBACK` |DEST_ADDR and SIZE read back the values the trigger step wrote, in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the assert fails the run on a mismatch
|`CHK-ZEROER-CTRL-STATUS` |CTRL_STATUS with STATUS masked equals the packed INT_EN=1 word exactly, in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; STATUS's resting level is recorded, not asserted
|`CHK-ZEROER-REGION-DECODE` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-ZEROER-REGION-ZEROED` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-BUSY-ASSERTED` |STATUS read away from its resting level within a bounded poll while the long zeroing is in flight; expiry fails
|`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-LIFECYCLE` |STATUS back at its resting level within a bounded poll after that zeroing retires, and the rest of the word again equals the INT_EN=1 word exactly; expiry or a mismatch fails
|`CHK-ZEROER-TRIGGER-STARTS` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-ZEROER-CTRL-STATUS`, `CHK-ZEROER-REGION-DECODE`, `CHK-ZEROER-REGION-ZEROED`, `CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-BUSY-ASSERTED`, `CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-LIFECYCLE` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: No level is asserted for the STATUS field of `CTRL_STATUS` itself: its resting level is recorded,
not asserted, because the RDL describes the field as "completed" while the implemented field reads
the opposite way round; the positive control proves only that the bit moves.
'''''

|`CHK-ZEROER-REGION-DECODE` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-ZEROER-REGION-ZEROED` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-BUSY-ASSERTED` |STATUS read away from its resting level within a bounded poll while the long zeroing is in flight; expiry fails
|`CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-LIFECYCLE` |STATUS back at its resting level within a bounded poll after that zeroing retires, and the rest of the word again equals the INT_EN=1 word exactly; expiry or a mismatch fails
|`CHK-ZEROER-TRIGGER-STARTS` |Named compare in `smc_zeroer_dma_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-ZEROER-CTRL-STATUS`, `CHK-ZEROER-REGION-DECODE`, `CHK-ZEROER-REGION-ZEROED`, `CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-BUSY-ASSERTED`, `CHK-ZEROER-STATUS-LIFECYCLE` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: No level is asserted for the STATUS field of `CTRL_STATUS` itself: its resting level is recorded,
not asserted, because the RDL describes the field as "completed" while the implemented field reads
the opposite way round; the positive control proves only that the bit moves.
'''''

[[sec-184-smc_dma_reserved_stream_banks_test]]
===== 184 `smc_dma_reserved_stream_banks_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_reserved_stream_banks_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP); `tb_dma_busy` sampled on every `clk_smc_i` edge across the sweep

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: All sixteen DMA stream banks decode with `NUM_CTRL_STREAMS = 1`: the reserved `STATUS`, `DONE` and `NEXT_ID` registers complete OKAY and read the value `dma.adoc` gives a reserved bank, and no reserved `NEXT_ID` read launches a transfer. A 32-bit read of the unused word at `0x4C`, the other half of `NEXT_ID_0`'s 8-byte word, answers the map's hole response and launches nothing either.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeros are given teeth: `DST_ADDRESS_LO` in the same block takes and returns a pattern before the sweep and is restored after it, so a bank reading 0 is reading from a block that answers rather than from a dead bus.
* `tb_dma_busy` is required resolvable and 0 at every sampled `clk_smc_i` edge across the whole sweep, and the watcher is required to have sampled at least one edge, so "no transfer started" is a per-sample compare and not an untaken branch.
* Bank 0 is the functional stream: its `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` are hardware status the specification pins to no value, so they are read for an OKAY response only and their values are reported, not compared. `NEXT_ID_0` is not read here, because reading it launches a transfer.
* A 32-bit read of `0x4C` must answer OKAY with `0xFFFFFFFF`, the hole response the generated map gives the DMA block, while `tb_dma_busy` stays 0: the access reaches only its own half of the 8-byte word and not `NEXT_ID_0` at `0x48`.
* The DMA clock gate is saved, ungated for the sweep, and restored with an exact readback.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dma_reserved_stream_banks_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer: ungate the DMA clock, start the busy watcher, write and read back the liveness pattern, read `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` for a response, sweep `STATUS_1..15`, `DONE_1..15` and `NEXT_ID_1..15` against an exact 0, read `0x4C` against the hole data, restore the pattern and the clock gate, then require the busy count to be 0 and the access count to have reached its floor. The leaf re-checks the scoreboard compare count and books a protocol-VIP record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-STREAM-BANKS` |The cell ledger: the `all-16-banks-decode` cell with the measured evidence that closed it -- the reserved sweep's exact zeros, bank 0's reported status, the liveness pattern and the sampled busy count. Entered only after those compares passed
|`CHK-DMA-RESERVED-STREAM-BANKS` |Summary line: banks decoded, SEP_IN accesses issued, and the busy-high count out of the sampled cycles. Logged after the busy compare and the stimulus floor have held
|`CHK-DMA-STREAM-BANKS-FLOOR` |The leaf requires the scoreboard's `sys_axi_value_checks_seen` to have reached `EXPECTED_VALUE_CHECKS` before this token is logged
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every reserved `STATUS`, `DONE` and `NEXT_ID` register reads exactly 0 over an OKAY response, the liveness pattern reads back exactly, `tb_dma_busy` is 0 at all sampled cycles, and the scoreboard books at least `EXPECTED_VALUE_CHECKS` compares. Bank 0's status values are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Bank 0's `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` are hardware status the specification pins to no
value, so they are read for an OKAY response only and their values are reported, not compared.
`NEXT_ID_0` is not read, because reading it launches a transfer.

'''''

[[sec-320-smc_periph_cg_access_error_test]]
===== 320 `smc_periph_cg_access_error_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_periph_cg_access_error_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Each CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL peripheral enable (AVSBus, I2C, UART, telemetry, I3C) set in turn: the gated window answers SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E on read and SLVERR on write, and its recorded word again once ungated.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` stops the AVSBus, I2C, UART, telemetry and I3C clocks with one enable each. In front of each of those peripherals an access gate on the SMC clock steers the crossbar leg into an error slave while the enable is set, so software reads an error instead of waiting on a register block whose clock has stopped.
* For each peripheral the same three-step experiment runs on its own enable, with the other four enables cleared: gate CLEARED -- a probe register answers OKAY and its word is recorded ([NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL]); gate SET -- a read of the probe completes SLVERR with `0xBADCAB1E` and a write of the complemented word completes SLVERR, and a no-response raises in the driver ([TIMEOUT-MUST-FAIL]); gate CLEARED -- the probe answers OKAY with the recorded word, so the refused write took no effect and the peripheral is reachable again.
* The probes are AVS_CFG_0, I2C_CTRL_0, UART0 LOG_ENGINE_CTRL, telemetry receiver 0 CTRL and I3C0 HCI_VERSION, each from the generated map; where the register is writable the recovery read also shows the refused write landed nowhere.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_periph_cg_access_error_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer: save CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL, clear all five peripheral enables, run the three-step experiment on each peripheral, restore CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL and reconcile the access count and the value-compare count against the scoreboard. The leaf then requires every peripheral to appear in the positive-control, refused and recovered sets.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PERIPH-CG-ACCESS-ERROR-<periph>` |One line per peripheral (AVSBUS, I2C, UART, TELEMETRY, I3C): its probe answered OKAY ungated, SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E on read and SLVERR on write while its enable was set, and OKAY with the recorded word once the enable was cleared; a timeout, an OKAY while gated, a DECERR, another data word or a changed word after recovery fails it
|`CHK-PERIPH-CG-ACCESS-ERROR-SWEEP` |Summary line: all five peripherals passed the three steps, CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL was restored and read back, and the scoreboard booked at least the expected number of value compares
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-328-smc_avsbus_pad_enable_test]]
===== 328 `smc_avsbus_pad_enable_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_pad_enable_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; pad enable probes `tb_core2pad_en_o` and
`tb_pad2core_en_o` at bits 49 (`avs_clock`), 50 (`avs_mdata`) and 51 (`avs_sdata`); AVSBus pins
`tb_avs_clk_from_dut` and `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut` observed, and `tb_avs_sdata_ext` driven by a bench
reply driver clocked on `tb_avs_clk_from_dut`; bench clock `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The `avs_clock` pad output enable follows
`AVS_CONFIG.AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` through its reset value, a 0 write and a 1 write, and with the enable
at 1 one AVS_CMD frame appears on `avs_mdata` and its reply reaches AVS_READBACK.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CONFIG.AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` drives `avs_gpio_enable_o`, which enables the pads carrying the
  AVSBus signals: output enable for `avs_clock` and `avs_mdata`, input enable for `avs_sdata`
  (`hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/interface.adoc`, Pad Enable Interface). The field resets to 1
  (`avsbus_controller.rdl`).
* The `avs_clock` pad is GPIO 49 (`hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`). Its output enable is compared
  exactly: 1 after reset, 0 after the field is written 0, 1 after it is written 1. The 0 and 1
  writes are read-modify-writes of `AVS_CONFIG` and are read back exactly.
* The output and input enable bits of the `avs_mdata` (50) and `avs_sdata` (51) pads are sampled
  through the same sequence and printed, not compared: their pad numbers and polarity are not stated by the specification.
* With the enable at 1 and `AVS_CFG_0.MAX_RETRIES` cleared, one read AVS_CMD is written. The master
  subframe of that command, with its CRC-3 bits excluded, must appear on `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut`,
  and a good reply driven on `tb_avs_sdata_ext` must reach AVS_READBACK intact on the fields the
  leaf compares (bits 31:30, 29, 28:24 and 23:8 and the CRC bits 2:0), as laid out in
  `interface.adoc` (AVSBus Frame Format).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check that the pad enable probes and the AVSBus pins are visible, sample the three pad enables,
  read `AVS_CONFIG` and require `AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` at its reset value, then start the reply driver
  (default reply idle).
. Wait (bounded) for the `avs_clock` output enable to read 1 and record the three pads.
  Read-modify-write `AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` to 0, read `AVS_CONFIG` back exactly, and wait for the
  `avs_clock` output enable to read 0. Write the field back to 1, read back exactly, and wait for
  the enable to read 1.
. Save `AVS_CFG_0`, clear `MAX_RETRIES` and read it back, queue one good reply, write one read
  command to AVS_CMD, wait (bounded) for a master subframe on `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut`, poll
  `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS.READBACK_HAS_DATA`, pop AVS_READBACK and compare the reply fields. Require the
  expected master subframe among the captured ones, restore `AVS_CFG_0` and stop the reply driver.
. Report the bounded waits taken, require the step stamps and checker lines to be in order, and
  print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-PAD-ENABLE-FOLLOWS` |The `avs_clock` pad output enable reads 1 after reset, 0 after
  `AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` is written 0 and 1 after it is written 1, each within its bounded wait; the
  mdata and sdata pad enables are measured and printed without a compare
|`CHK-AVS-PAD-PROTOCOL` |With `AVS_GPIO_ENABLE` at 1 the command's master subframe appears on
  `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut` and the bench reply reaches AVS_READBACK equal on the compared fields,
  with an OKAY response on each access
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence PADS_SAMPLED < ENABLE_SEQUENCE < PROTOCOL_ON_PADS: the step stamps S1
  to S4 are strictly increasing and the checker lines were logged in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every wait (enable wait, frame wait, reply wait) is bounded in `clk_smc_i`
  cycles and raises with the last sampled pad enables on expiry; the line lists the bounded waits
  taken
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-AVS-PAD-ENABLE-FOLLOWS`, `CHK-AVS-PAD-PROTOCOL`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. The `avs_mdata` and `avs_sdata` pad
enables are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The output and input enable bits of the `avs_mdata` (50) and `avs_sdata` (51) pads
are sampled and printed, not compared, because their pad numbers and polarity are not stated by the
specification.

'''''

[[sec-329-smc_avsbus_resync_force_test]]
===== 329 `smc_avsbus_resync_force_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_resync_force_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; FSM debug probe `tb_avsbus_cur_state_debug` sampled on
every `clk_periph_i` edge (a state counts once it holds over two consecutive samples);
`tb_avs_clk_from_dut` and `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut` observed to count master subframes;
`tb_avs_sdata_ext` held low by the bench (all-zero replies); bench clock `clk_smc_i` for polls

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A forced slave resync (`AVS_CFG_1.FORCE_SLAVE_RESYNC_OPERATION`)
from idle gives one resync episode, lets in-flight frames and replies complete, launches queued
commands once each in write order, and survives two back-to-back requests.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CFG_1.FORCE_SLAVE_RESYNC_OPERATION` requests one slave resync (`avsbus_controller.rdl`);
  `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/architecture.adoc` (AVS Protocol Engine) says the master stops
  launching new commands once it sees the request and starts the resync from idle after the frame in
  flight and its reply complete.
* From AVS_IDLE one force write gives exactly one `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC` episode on the probe, the field
  reads 0 again within a bounded poll and `AVS_CFG_1` returns to its pre-write value.
* Mid-frame: two read commands are queued and the force is written when the probe first shows a
  shift state. Both commands launch once each in order, both replies are pushed to the readback
  FIFO, exactly one resync episode follows and it begins from a state that is not a shift or retry
  state. When the probe shows `AVS_SHIFT_1ST_SUBFRAME` as the force write completes, no master
  subframe may start between the write and the episode. The count of subframes launched before the request is timing dependent and
  is printed.
* With a queue: a force write followed at once by three read commands on distinct rails; the three
  master subframes appear once each in write order and three replies are pushed.
* Twice: two force writes back to back give one or two episodes (the specification does not state
  whether a second request while one is pending gives one resync or two; the count is printed), the
  bus returns to AVS_IDLE and a command queued afterwards launches once and is answered.
* `AVS_CFG_0.RESYNC_INTERVAL` is set to its maximum for the run so no periodic resync falls in the
  windows, and restored with an exact readback.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Hold `tb_avs_sdata_ext` low, save `AVS_CFG_0`, write `RESYNC_INTERVAL` to its maximum and read
  back, start the probe and subframe recorders, drain the readback FIFO, wait (bounded) for
  `AVS_IDLE`, and require the force bit clear in `AVS_CFG_1`.
. Force from idle: read-modify-write the force bit, poll `AVS_CFG_1` (bounded) until the field reads
  0 with the register equal to its base value, wait for an episode and `AVS_IDLE`, and require
  exactly one episode.
. Force mid-frame: write two commands to AVS_CMD, wait for a shift state on the probe, write the
  force bit without a prior register read and record the probe state when the write completes, poll
  the field clear, wait for the episode and `AVS_IDLE`, wait for two readback
  entries, and compare the launched subframes, reply count and the state before the episode. Drain
  the readback FIFO.
. Force with a queue: write the force bit, write three read commands, poll the field clear, wait for
  the episode, three launched subframes and `AVS_IDLE`, wait for three readback entries and compare
  the subframes with the write order. Drain the readback FIFO.
. Force twice: write the force bit twice with no read between, poll the field clear, wait for the
  episode and `AVS_IDLE`, require one or two episodes, write one command, wait for its reply and
  `AVS_IDLE`, and compare its subframe. Drain the readback FIFO.
. Restore `AVS_CFG_0` and read it back, stop the recorders, report the bounded waits, require the
  step stamps and checker lines in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-FORCE-ONE-RESYNC` |One force write from `AVS_IDLE` gave exactly one `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC`
  episode, the force field read 0 within the bounded poll with `AVS_CFG_1` equal to its base value,
  and the bus returned to `AVS_IDLE`
|`CHK-AVS-FORCE-FRAME-COMPLETES` |With the force written mid-frame both queued commands launched
  once each in order, both replies were pushed, one episode followed and began from a non-shift,
  non-retry state, and no subframe started between the write and the episode when the force landed
  in `AVS_SHIFT_1ST_SUBFRAME`
|`CHK-AVS-FORCE-INFLIGHT-INT` |Records the probe state order from the mid-frame force write (frame
  in flight, its reply, resync from idle) together with the replies pushed; the
  launched-before-request count is printed and not compared, and the compares are the ones of the
  previous checker
|`CHK-AVS-FORCE-QUEUE-ORDER` |After a force write followed at once by three commands, the three
  master subframes seen on `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut` match the write order once each and three
  replies are pushed, and a resync episode is recorded; the count of subframes started before the
  episode is printed and not compared
|`CHK-AVS-FORCE-TWICE` |Two back-to-back force writes gave one or two episodes (count printed), the
  bus returned to `AVS_IDLE`, and the command queued afterwards launched once and was answered
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence IDLE_REACHED < FORCE_FROM_IDLE < FORCE_MID_FRAME < FORCE_WITH_QUEUE <
  FORCE_TWICE: step stamps S1 to S6 strictly increasing and the checker lines logged in order, each
  after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every probe wait is bounded in `clk_periph_i` cycles and every register poll
  in `clk_smc_i` cycles; each raises with the episode count and last probe state on expiry, and the
  line lists the bounded waits taken
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The subframes launched
before the request and the episode count after the double force are reported only (the double force
is limited to one or two episodes). Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The count of master subframes launched before a force request is timing dependent
and is printed, not compared. After two back-to-back force writes the episode count is printed,
because the specification does not state whether a second request while one is pending gives one
resync or two; only one or two episodes is required.

'''''

[[sec-330-smc_avsbus_resync_timing_test]]
===== 330 `smc_avsbus_resync_timing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_resync_timing_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; reset agent (`SmcResetOp.COLD_RST_LO` / `COLD_RST_HI`
on `rst_cold_ni`); FSM debug probe `tb_avsbus_cur_state_debug` (17-bit one-hot, sampled on every
`clk_periph_i` edge, a state counts once it holds over two consecutive samples);
`tb_avs_clk_from_dut` (`avs_clock_o` rising edges) and `tb_avs_mdata_from_dut` sampled with the
probe; `tb_avs_sdata_ext` held low by the bench; bench clocks `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: After a cold reset the AVSBus controller resyncs on its own, the
resync lasts 35 `avs_clock_o` periods with `avs_mdata` high, the status flags track the probe, the
probe stays one-hot, and the resync interval follows `AVS_CFG_0.RESYNC_INTERVAL`.

*Test Coverage*:

* Cold reset: with no AVS_CMD written the probe shows `AVS_RESET` (bit 0), then `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC`
  (bit 1), then `AVS_IDLE` (bit 3) in that order and no command-path state
  (`hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/architecture.adoc`, AVS Protocol Engine and Protocol State Machine).
  `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE` reads clear and `RESYNC_INTERVAL` reads its reset value 0x1000
  (`avsbus_controller.rdl`).
* Resync shape: `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC` lasts 35 `avs_clock_o` cycles with `avs_mdata_o` high throughout
  (`architecture.adoc`; `interface.adoc`, Timing). The probe span must equal 34 to 36 `avs_clock_o`
  periods, `avs_mdata` must read 1 at every probe sample inside it, and the `avs_mdata` high run on
  the pin must be longer than the state span.
* Status flags: `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS.AVS_SLAVE_IS_IN_RESYNC` (bit 22) and `AVS_BUS_IS_IDLE` (bit 21)
  are polled across one episode. Polls taken at least three `avs_clock_o` periods away from any
  probe edge must read the flag 1 in the span and 0 in idle (in-resync), and 1 in idle and 0 in the
  span (bus-idle). Polls near an edge are printed.
* One-hot: every probe sample out of reset has exactly one of 17 bits set (`architecture.adoc`,
  Protocol State Machine), over at least 1000 out-of-reset samples; the all-zero samples of the
  in-reset run ending in `AVS_RESET` are counted and printed.
* Interval: for `RESYNC_INTERVAL` 0x1000, 0x0040 and 0x0400 the time from the end of one resync to
  the start of the next, with no frame in flight, is measured. The residual over (interval + 1)
  `clk_reg_i` cycles plus three `avs_clock_o` periods must be at least 0 and the period must grow
  with the interval. Whether that residual is constant across intervals is not stated by the specification; it is printed.
* Interval 0: the period is measured and printed (the specification gives no behaviour for it) and a
  command queued afterwards must be answered.
* Rewrite: 0x0040 is written at half the elapsed 0x1000 interval; a next and a following resync must
  each occur within the bounded wait, and no resync may begin before the rewrite completes. The
  times from the previous end, from the write, and from the first resync's end, next to the periods
  measured earlier, are printed; whether a rewrite restarts or retargets the running interval is not stated by the specification.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Hold `tb_avs_sdata_ext` low, start the probe and clock recorders, and wait (bounded) for
  `AVS_IDLE`.
. Assert `rst_cold_ni` low through the reset agent and wait for the cold-assert state, release it
  and wait for the released state, then wait for a resync episode and `AVS_IDLE`. Require
  `AVS_RESET`, `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC`, `AVS_IDLE` in that order with no command-path state,
  `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE` clear in `AVS_CFG_1`, and `RESYNC_INTERVAL` at 0x1000 in `AVS_CFG_0`.
. Derive the `clk_periph_i` and `avs_clock_o` periods from the recorders, take the first resync
  episode after the reset and compare its span in `avs_clock_o` periods, the `avs_mdata` level at
  every sample inside it and the pin-high run length.
. Poll `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS` back to back across the next episode until six polls have been taken in
  idle after it, classify each poll against the probe window and compare the flags on the polls deep
  inside the span and deep inside idle.
. Require the probe to have shown no sample other than one-hot, and at least 1000 out-of-reset
  samples.
. Measure the period after the default interval, write 0x0040 and measure, write 0x0400 and measure
  (discarding one episode after each write), compute the residuals and require them non-negative and
  the periods ordered 0x0040 < 0x0400 < 0x1000.
. Write `RESYNC_INTERVAL` 0, measure the period, write one read command to AVS_CMD, wait for a
  readback entry and drain the readback FIFO.
. Restore 0x1000 and wait one episode, wait half the interval, write 0x0040, require no resync began
  meanwhile, wait for the next and following resync, measure and print the times and restore 0x1000.
. Stop the recorders, require the probe to end without an open all-zero run, report the bounded
  waits (including the reset agent and SEP_IN access bounds), require step stamps and checker lines
  in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-STARTUP` |After the cold reset, with no AVS_CMD written, the probe held
  `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC` before any command-path state and before `AVS_IDLE`
|`CHK-AVS-FSM-RESET-SEQUENCE` |The probe held `AVS_RESET`, then `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC`, then `AVS_IDLE`
  in that order after `rst_cold_ni` was released, with nothing queued; `AVS_RESET` never being seen
  fails the run
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-LEN35` |`avs_mdata` read 1 at every probe sample inside the first resync span and
  the span was 34 to 36 `avs_clock_o` periods
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-PIN-HIGH` |The `avs_mdata` high run on the pin around the same episode lasted more
  `avs_clock_o` periods than the `AVS_SLAVE_RESYNC` span
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-FLAG` |`AVS_SLAVE_IS_IN_RESYNC` read 1 at every poll deep inside the span and 0 at
  every poll deep in `AVS_IDLE`, with at least one poll in the span and in idle before and after it;
  polls near an edge are printed only
|`CHK-AVS-FSM-IDLE-FLAG` |`AVS_BUS_IS_IDLE` read 1 at every poll deep in `AVS_IDLE` and 0 at every
  poll deep inside the resync span; the mapping at the edges is printed only
|`CHK-AVS-FSM-ONEHOT` |Every resolvable probe sample out of reset had exactly one of 17 bits set,
  over at least 1000 out-of-reset samples; the all-zero samples of the in-reset run are counted and
  printed
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-INTERVAL` |For intervals 0x1000, 0x0040 and 0x0400 the residual period was at least
  0 and the period grew with the interval; the periods and residuals are printed, and their
  constancy across intervals is printed and not compared
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-INTERVAL-ZERO` |With `RESYNC_INTERVAL` 0 the bus kept resyncing and a command
  queued afterwards was answered with a readback entry; the measured period is printed without a
  compare
|`CHK-AVS-RESYNC-REWRITE` |After 0x0040 was written at half of the 0x1000 interval a next and a
  following resync were each observed within their bounded waits and none began before the write
  completed; the measured times are printed without a compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence MONITORS_RUNNING < COLD_RESET_SEQUENCE < RESYNC_SHAPE < FLAGS_POLLED <
  ONEHOT_COUNTED < INTERVALS_MEASURED < INTERVAL_ZERO < REWRITE: step stamps S1 to S9 strictly
  increasing and the checker lines logged in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every probe wait, resync wait, reply wait and flag poll is bounded and raises
  with the episode count and last probe state on expiry, as do the reset-agent and SEP_IN access
  bounds; the line lists the bounded waits taken
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twelve checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The interval constancy,
the interval 0 period, the rewrite times and the near-edge flag polls are reported only.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Status-flag polls taken near a probe edge are printed only. The all-zero probe
samples of the in-reset run are counted and printed. Whether the interval residual is constant
across intervals, the period at `RESYNC_INTERVAL` 0, and whether a rewrite restarts or retargets the
running interval are not stated by the specification, so those periods and times are printed and
not compared.

'''''

[[sec-331-smc_octs_csr_access_test]]
===== 331 `smc_octs_csr_access_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_octs_csr_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (4-byte reads and writes, the raw access items accept
error responses); the system timer OCTS register block at `SMC_TOP_SMC_SYSTEM_TIMER_OCTS_BASE_ADDR`
with `TIMER_START` (0x00), `CTRL` (0x04), `STATUS` (0x08), `TIMER_PRESET_LO` (0x0C),
`TIMER_PRESET_HI` (0x10), `TIMER_COUNT_LO` (0x14), `TIMER_COUNT_HI` (0x18), `CREDIT_EXPIRED` (0x1C)
and `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` (0x20); the dwords at offsets 0x24 and 0x28; the count output net
`tb_top.timer_count` (`timer_count_o`) sampled on `clk_smc_i` rises; the OCTS role is PRIMARY
(`is_primary_i` high, `STATUS.MODE` 0)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: The nine OCTS registers decode at their own offsets, reset to their
`system_timer_octs.rdl` values, read back their writable fields, ignore writes to the read-only
registers, and the dwords past the map are recorded.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset values before any write: `CTRL` reads 0x0001_020A (`CREDIT_VAL` 0xA, `PULSE_WIDTH` 0x2,
  `STEP` 0x1) and `TIMER_START`, `STATUS`, `TIMER_PRESET_LO`, `TIMER_PRESET_HI`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`,
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `CREDIT_EXPIRED` and `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` read 0 (`system_timer_octs.rdl`;
  `STATUS.MODE` 0 and `RUNNING` 0). `tb_top.timer_count` is 0 at 64 of 64 consecutive `clk_smc_i`
  rises.
* `CTRL` field storage: a write of 0xFFA5_5AC3 reads back 0x00A5_5AC3 (bits 31:24 read 0), and a
  write with `PULSE_WIDTH` 0 (0x0001_0010) reads back 0x0001_0010.
* Preset halves: `TIMER_PRESET_LO` written 0xDEAD_BEEF reads back exactly with `TIMER_PRESET_HI`
  still 0; `TIMER_PRESET_HI` written 0x1234_5678 reads back exactly with `TIMER_PRESET_LO`
  unchanged.
* `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` reads 1 after a write of 1 and 0 after a write of 0.
* Decode (`system_timer_octs.rdl` address map, `hw/ip/system_timer_octs/doc/memmap.adoc`): none of
  the written `CTRL` and preset patterns is readable at any other register offset, `STATUS` at 0x08
  reads `RUNNING` 1 with `MODE` 0 and nothing else set after `TIMER_START` is written,
  `TIMER_COUNT_LO` at 0x14 is nonzero and `TIMER_COUNT_HI` at 0x18 reads 0.
* Read-only behaviour on the running timer: `TIMER_START` reads 0 after a write of 1; after writes
  of 0xFFFF_FFFF to `STATUS`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `STATUS` still reads 0x10,
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 0 and `TIMER_COUNT_LO` stays between its earlier reading and that reading plus 0x1000 and is not
  0xFFFF_FFFF. The response codes of those three writes are printed, not compared.
* The reads of the dwords at offsets 0x24 and 0x28 and a write at 0x24 are recorded with their
  response codes and read data; their expected behaviour is not stated by the specification, so
  nothing about the values is compared and the access must only complete with a response.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CTRL` and compare with 0x0001_020A, read the other eight registers and compare each with 0,
  and sample `tb_top.timer_count` at 64 consecutive `clk_smc_i` rises requiring it resolvable and 0
  at each.
. Write `CTRL` 0xFFA5_5AC3 and read back 0x00A5_5AC3; write `TIMER_PRESET_LO` 0xDEAD_BEEF, read both
  presets, write `TIMER_PRESET_HI` 0x1234_5678 and read both presets; read the six other registers
  and require none to hold one of the three patterns.
. Write `CTRL` 0x0001_0010 and read back 0x0001_0010.
. Write `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 1 and read 1, write 0 and read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only registers `STATUS`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and `TIMER_COUNT_HI`
  of the running timer. Kind: a write of 0xFFFF_FFFF to each, recording each response. Expected
  response: `STATUS` still reads 0x10, `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 0 and `TIMER_COUNT_LO` stays between
  its earlier reading and that reading plus 0x1000 and is not 0xFFFF_FFFF; the response codes are
  recorded, not compared. Setup before the writes: restore `CTRL` to 0x0001_020A and both presets
  to 0, write `TIMER_START` 1 and read 0, wait 100 `clk_smc_i` cycles and read `TIMER_COUNT_LO`;
  after the writes read `STATUS`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI` and `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and compare as above.
. Error injection. Point: the dwords at offsets 0x24 and 0x28 past the OCTS register map. Kind: a
  read of each and a write of 0xA5A5_5A5A at offset 0x24. Expected response: each access completes
  with a response; the response and data word of each are recorded and not compared. Require the
  step stamps and checker lines in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCTS-RESET-VALUES` |Before any write `CTRL` reads 0x0001_020A, the other eight registers read
  0, and `tb_top.timer_count` is 0 at 64 of 64 rises; the zero reset values are bench-limited
  (2-state zero init)
|`CHK-OCTS-CTRL-PRESET-READBACK` |`CTRL` written 0xFFA5_5AC3 reads 0x00A5_5AC3 and written
  0x0001_0010 reads 0x0001_0010, and each preset half reads back its written value with the other
  half unchanged
|`CHK-OCTS-GPIO-ENABLE-RW` |`TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` reads 1 after a write of 1 and 0 after a write of 0
|`CHK-OCTS-DECODE-OFFSETS` |The nine registers answer at their own offsets: the written patterns
  appear only at 0x04, 0x0C and 0x10, `STATUS` reads 0x10 after `TIMER_START`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO` is
  no lower than its earlier reading and within 0x1000 of it, is not 0xFFFF_FFFF and is nonzero, and
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 0
|`CHK-OCTS-READONLY-START` |`TIMER_START` reads 0 after a write of 1, and after writes of
  0xFFFF_FFFF to the read-only registers on a running timer `STATUS` still reads 0x10,
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 0 and `TIMER_COUNT_LO` is no lower than its earlier reading and within 0x1000 of it; the
  response codes are printed
|`CHK-OCTS-APERTURE-PAST` |Records the response and read data of the reads at 0x24 and 0x28 and of
  the write at 0x24 without comparing them; each access must complete with a response
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S6 strictly increasing and the six checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The response codes of the
read-only writes and the data and responses past the map are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The response codes of the writes to the read-only registers are printed, not
compared. The reads of the dwords at offsets 0x24 and 0x28 and the write at 0x24 are recorded with
their responses and data; nothing about the values is compared and each access must only complete
with a response, because their expected behaviour is not stated by the specification. The zero
reset values are bench-limited (2-state zero init).

'''''

[[sec-332-smc_octs_primary_count_test]]
===== 332 `smc_octs_primary_count_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_octs_primary_count_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; the OCTS registers `TIMER_START`, `CTRL`, `STATUS`,
`TIMER_PRESET_LO`, `TIMER_PRESET_HI`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` and
`CREDIT_EXPIRED`; the count output net `tb_top.timer_count` (`timer_count_o`) recorded at every
`clk_smc_i` rise by a background monitor (X/Z fails); the OCTS role is PRIMARY
(`is_primary_i` high, `STATUS.MODE` 0)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The PRIMARY count on `timer_count_o` starts from the preset, steps
by one per `clk_smc_i` rise, never stops on any register write, and COUNT_HI/COUNT_LO read back the
carry and the 64-bit wrap.

*Test Coverage*:

* Never-run state (`hw/ip/system_timer_octs/doc/architecture.adoc`, Counting and Synchronization):
  with no `TIMER_START` written both halves of `COUNT` read 0 twice 100 cycles apart,
  `STATUS.RUNNING` reads 0 and the count net is 0 at 64 of 64 rises.
* Start from preset 0: after `TIMER_START` the count net leaves 0, every consecutive pair from the
  first nonzero sample differs by exactly 1, and `STATUS.RUNNING` reads 1 at the 64th rise.
  `RUNNING` read at the first rise is printed (when the first nonzero sample appears is not specified, but
  it must be no higher than 0x40).
* Reload on a running timer: `TIMER_PRESET_LO` 0x1000 then `TIMER_START` 1; the count net must enter
  [0x1000, 0x1040] within 64 rises and then step by exactly 1 at every following rise
  (`architecture.adoc`; `interface.adoc`, Timer Count). The index of the reload sample is printed.
* `TIMER_COUNT_LO` reads are bracketed by two count net samples taken just before and just after
  each of 8 reads; each read lies between the low 32 bits of the two samples. Three
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI` triples have equal high halves and a
  composite between the bracketing samples (`interface.adoc`, Timer Count; `system_timer_octs.rdl`).
* No stop: after `TIMER_START` 0, a `CTRL` write of 0x0001_0210, `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 1,
  `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 0 and a `TIMER_PRESET_LO` write of 0x9999, the count net steps by exactly 1 at
  each of 32 consecutive rises with no hold and no jump to the preset (`architecture.adoc`, Reset;
  `system_timer_octs.rdl`, `TIMER_START`).
* Carry: from preset 0x0000_0000_FFFF_FFF0 the count net reaches 0x1_0000_0000 within 48 rises with
  every difference exactly 1, and `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 1 in both reads after the crossing with the
  composite between 0x1_0000_0000 and the latest net sample.
* Wrap: from preset 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFF0 the count net passes 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF to 0 with every
  difference exactly 1 modulo 2^64 over 48 rises. `STATUS` is read repeatedly during the run and the
  reads taken around the 0 and 1 samples are printed with `RUNNING`, because the value `RUNNING`
  takes at the wrap is not stated by the specification.
* `STATUS.MODE` reads 0 after each of the four starts (`system_timer_octs.rdl`, `STATUS.MODE`), and
  `CREDIT_EXPIRED` reads 0 on the PRIMARY at the end.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Start the count net monitor. With no START written, read `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and `TIMER_COUNT_HI`,
  wait 100 `clk_smc_i` cycles, read both again and `STATUS`, and compare against 0 over the next 64
  samples.
. Write both presets 0 and `TIMER_START` 1, read `STATUS`, wait for 64 samples, read `STATUS` again,
  find the first nonzero sample and require it to be at most 0x40, require every following
  difference to be 1 and `RUNNING` set at the 64th rise, then read `STATUS` for `MODE`.
. Write `TIMER_PRESET_LO` 0x1000 and `TIMER_START` 1, collect 64 samples, find the sample inside
  [0x1000, 0x1040], require every following difference to be 1, then read `STATUS` for `MODE`.
. Read `TIMER_COUNT_LO` eight times, each bracketed by the latest net sample before and after, and
  require each reading inside its bracket.
. Write `TIMER_START` 0 and require the net to step by 1 for 32 rises.
. Write `CTRL` 0x0001_0210, `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 1, `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 0 and `TIMER_PRESET_LO`
  0x9999 in turn, requiring a step of 1 over 32 rises after each.
. Read `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI` three times and compare the halves and
  bracket.
. Write `TIMER_PRESET_LO` 0xFFFF_FFF0, `TIMER_PRESET_HI` 0 and `TIMER_START` 1, collect 48 samples,
  find the reload sample and the crossing of 0x1_0000_0000, require every difference 1, read
  `TIMER_COUNT_HI`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI` after the crossing and `STATUS` for `MODE`.
. Write `TIMER_PRESET_LO` 0xFFFF_FFF0, `TIMER_PRESET_HI` 0xFFFF_FFFF and `TIMER_START` 1; read
  `STATUS` repeatedly until 48 samples exist, within a bound of 112 rises, find the reload sample
  and the sample of 0, require every difference to be 1 modulo 2^64, read `STATUS` for `MODE`.
. Read `STATUS` and require `MODE` 0 at all four recorded points.
. Read `CREDIT_EXPIRED` and require 0; require step stamps and checker lines in order and print the
  ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCTS-NEVER-RUN` |With no START written both `COUNT` reads are 0 twice, `STATUS.RUNNING` reads
  0 and the count net is 0 at 64 of 64 rises
|`CHK-OCTS-PRESET-LOAD-COUNT` |After preset 0x1000 and `TIMER_START` on a running timer the count
  net enters [0x1000, 0x1040] within 64 rises and every later consecutive difference is exactly 1;
  the reload index is printed
|`CHK-OCTS-NO-STOP` |After `TIMER_START` 0, the `CTRL` write, `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` 1 and 0 and the
  preset write, the count net steps by exactly 1 at 32 of 32 consecutive rises for each of the 5
  events
|`CHK-OCTS-COUNT-PORT-REGISTER` |Each of 8 `TIMER_COUNT_LO` reads lies between the low 32 bits of
  its bracketing net samples, and each of 3 HI, LO, HI triples has equal high halves and a composite
  between its bracketing samples
|`CHK-OCTS-COUNT-CARRY` |From preset 0xFFFF_FFF0 the net crosses 0x1_0000_0000 with every difference
  exactly 1, and `TIMER_COUNT_HI` reads 1 after the crossing with a composite between 0x1_0000_0000
  and the latest net sample
|`CHK-OCTS-COUNT-WRAP` |From preset 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFF0 the net passes to 0 with every difference
  exactly 1 modulo 2^64; the `STATUS` reads around the wrap and `RUNNING` afterwards are printed
  without a compare
|`CHK-OCTS-ZERO-PRESET-START` |After START with preset 0 the first nonzero sample is at most 0x40,
  every difference from it is exactly 1 and `STATUS.RUNNING` reads 1 at the 64th rise; the first sample, its rise
  index and `RUNNING` at the first rise are printed
|`CHK-OCTS-ROLE-PERSISTS` |`STATUS.MODE` reads 0 after each of the four starts and reloads
|`CHK-OCTS-EXPIRED-PRIMARY-ZERO` |`CREDIT_EXPIRED` reads 0 on the PRIMARY after the whole sequence
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S11 strictly increasing and the nine checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all ten checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The reload index, the
first-rise `RUNNING` value and the `STATUS` reads at the wrap are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `RUNNING` read at the first rise and the first nonzero sample with its rise index are
printed, because when the first nonzero sample appears is not specified (it must only be no higher
than 0x40). The reload sample index is printed. The `STATUS` reads around the wrap are printed with
`RUNNING`, because the value `RUNNING` takes at the wrap is not stated by the specification.

'''''

[[sec-333-smc_telemetry_address_map_test]]
===== 333 `smc_telemetry_address_map_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_address_map_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (4-byte reads and writes; the raw access items accept
error responses); the telemetry receiver wrapper window at
`SMC_TOP_SMC_TELEMETRY_RECEIVER_WRAP_BASE_ADDR` with three receiver apertures at the generated
stride and per-receiver registers `CTRL`, `STATUS`, `INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST`,
`TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS` and the 32 `TELEMETRY_COUNTER` registers; the bench
ATB beat driver on `tb_telemetry0_*`, `tb_telemetry1_*` and `tb_telemetry2_*` (`atdata`, `atid`
0x00, 0x11 and 0x22, `atvalid`, `atready`) on `clk_smc_i`; `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The three telemetry receiver apertures decode their registers and
counter windows separately, and accesses past the third aperture or at unbacked offsets complete
with recorded responses and disturb no receiver.

*Test Coverage*:

* Register offsets: for receivers 0, 1 and 2 each of the seven register types answers OKAY at its
  offset inside the aperture and reads its reset value (`hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/memmap.adoc`,
  256 bytes per receiver; `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc`, Memory Map; `smc.rdl`). `CTRL` reads 0 and
  `STATUS` reads `BUFFER_EMPTY` set after the flush.
* Isolation of the three apertures: distinct `INTR_ENABLE` (0x01, 0x10, 0x11) and
  `CTRL.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` (0x111, 0x222, 0x333) patterns written to receivers 0, 1 and 2 before any
  read each read back as their own, then are restored to 0.
* Counter window (`telemetry_receiver/doc/memmap.adoc`, 32 counter registers at offsets 0x80 to
  0xFC): an all-valid one-packet message sent to receiver i shows `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` 0xFFFF_FFFF
  and `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[1]` 0 in receiver i's aperture and 0 and 0 in the other two; all 32
  counters of receiver 1 answer OKAY in four-byte steps.
* Past the third receiver (`hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc`, Decode Response Codes): reads and writes at
  window offsets 0x300, 0x304, 0x380 and 0xFFC are measured. Their expected responses are not stated by the specification, so the response and data are printed and not compared, except that a read
  must not answer OKAY with data equal to receiver 0's `STATUS`.
* Unbacked offsets inside an aperture (0x1C, 0x20 and 0x7C of receiver 0 and 0x1C of receiver 2):
  reads and writes are measured and printed (expected response is not stated by the specification);
  the `STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL` words of all three receivers must read
  unchanged afterwards.
* No fourth receiver (`hw/sys/smc/doc/periphs.adoc`, Telemetry Receiver, three receivers): a write
  of 0x11 at window offset 0x30C and a read at 0x304 answer with the same responses as the
  past-extent accesses of the earlier step, and the register words of receivers 0 to 2 stay
  unchanged.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and
  read it back exactly, then flush each receiver and poll `STATUS.BUFFER_EMPTY` to 1.
. For receivers 0 to 2 read the seven register types and compare each with its reset value, write
  the distinct `INTR_ENABLE` and `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` patterns to all three, read all six back and
  compare, restore all six to 0 and read the restore back.
. For each receiver in turn send an all-valid single-packet message over the ATB pins, poll
  `STATUS.BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, read `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` and `[1]` in all three apertures and
  compare; for receiver 1 also read all 32 counters; pop with `CTRL.BUFFER_POP` and poll
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` back to 1.
. Error injection. Point: window offsets 0x300, 0x304, 0x380 and 0xFFC past the third receiver
  aperture. Kind: a read and a write at each. Expected response: each access completes and its
  response and data word are recorded and not compared; a read answering OKAY with data equal to
  receiver 0's `STATUS` fails. Before the accesses snapshot `STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_STATUS`
  and `CTRL` of the three receivers.
. Error injection. Point: the four unbacked offsets inside the apertures (0x1C, 0x20 and 0x7C of
  receiver 0 and 0x1C of receiver 2). Kind: a read and a write at each. Expected response: the
  responses are recorded, and a second snapshot of the three receivers compares equal with the
  first.
. Error injection. Point: window offsets 0x30C and 0x304, where no fourth receiver exists. Kind: a
  write of 0x11 at 0x30C and a read at 0x304. Expected response: the same response codes as the
  past-extent accesses, and a third snapshot compares equal with the first. Restore
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and read it back exactly, print the bounded waits, require the step stamps
  and checker lines in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-APERTURE-REGS` |All seven register types answer OKAY with their reset values in each
  of the three apertures, and the three distinct `INTR_ENABLE` and `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` patterns each
  read back as their own and restore to 0; the zero reset values are bench-limited (2-state zero
  init)
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-COUNTER-WINDOW` |A message in receiver i reads `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` 0xFFFF_FFFF
  and `[1]` 0 in receiver i's aperture and 0 and 0 in the others, and all 32 counters of receiver 1
  answer OKAY at four-byte steps
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-PAST-EXTENT` |Measures and prints the read response, read data and write response at
  window offsets 0x300, 0x304, 0x380 and 0xFFC without comparing the values; a read answering OKAY
  with receiver `STATUS` data fails
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-UNBACKED-OFFSETS` |Measures and prints the responses and data at the four unbacked
  offsets without comparing them; the `STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL` words of all
  three receivers must read unchanged afterwards
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-NO-FOURTH-RECEIVER` |A write at window offset 0x30C and a read at 0x304 answer with
  the same response codes as the past-extent accesses, and the register words of receivers 0 to 2
  stay unchanged
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < OFFSETS_AND_PATTERNS < COUNTER_WINDOWS <
  PAST_EXTENT_MEASURED < UNBACKED_MEASURED < NO_FOURTH_RECEIVER: step stamps S1 to S6 strictly
  increasing and the checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense, buffer-empty polls, ATB beat
  acceptance and the SEP_IN access bound); expiry of any of them raises with the last observed state
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The past-extent and
unbacked responses and data are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The responses and data of the reads and writes past the third receiver (window
offsets 0x300, 0x304, 0x380 and 0xFFC) and at the unbacked offsets (0x1C, 0x20 and 0x7C of receiver
0 and 0x1C of receiver 2) are printed and not compared, because the specification does not state
them; only a read answering OKAY with receiver 0's `STATUS` data fails. The zero reset values are
bench-limited (2-state zero init).

'''''

[[sec-334-smc_telemetry_ctrl_access_test]]
===== 334 `smc_telemetry_ctrl_access_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_ctrl_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (4-byte accesses; raw write items accept error
responses); telemetry receiver 0 registers `CTRL`, `STATUS`, `INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`,
`INTR_TEST`, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` and
`TELEMETRY_COUNTER[31]`; the bench ATB beat driver on `tb_telemetry0_atdata`, `tb_telemetry0_atid`
(0x21), `tb_telemetry0_atvalid` and `tb_telemetry0_atready`; `tb_telemetry0_afready` driven by the
bench (high except in the full-word step); `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Telemetry receiver 0 CTRL, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST fields read
back as written, a full-word CTRL write overwrites the threshold, and writes to the read-only
registers change nothing.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CTRL.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` (bits 23:12, read-write, `telemetry_receiver.rdl`) written 0x000, 0x001,
  0xFFF and 0x555 reads back exactly as the whole `CTRL` word with no other bit set.
* `CTRL.BUFFER_POP` and `CTRL.TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` are write pulses (`telemetry_receiver.rdl`); each
  alone and both together are written on an empty queue and on a queue holding a message, and `CTRL`
  is read after each. Both are `sw=w` in the RDL, so bits 0 and 4 must read 0 after every write; a
  queued message must leave the queue after every write.
* Full-word write (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, Buffer Management): with
  `tb_telemetry0_afready` low `CTRL` is written with `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 5 and `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`
  and the threshold is read back as 5; a following full-word write of only `BUFFER_POP` must leave
  `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` at 0. Whether the pending transmitter flush request is cancelled (bit 8) is not
  specified and is printed.
* `INTR_ENABLE` (`MISSING_LAST` bit 0, `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` bit 4, read-write) written 0x1, 0x10, 0x11
  and 0x0 reads back each exactly.
* `INTR_TEST` (`BUFFER_THRESHOLD` read-write, `MISSING_LAST` write pulse): a write of 0x10 reads
  back 0x10 and a write of 0 reads back 0. The read of bit 0 after a write of 1 must be 0, as
  `MISSING_LAST` is `sw=w` in the RDL; the resulting `INTR_STATUS` is printed.
* Read-only registers (`telemetry_receiver.rdl`, sw = r): writes of 0xFFFF_FFFF and 0 to `STATUS`,
  `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` and `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[31]`
  leave all five reading exactly their pre-write words, on an empty queue (`STATUS` showing
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` set and `BUFFER_FULL` clear) and with one message of probe id 0x0B queued (neither
  flag set, probe id 0x0B). The write responses are printed (the expected response is not
  specified).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and
  read it back exactly, hold `tb_telemetry0_afready` high, flush receiver 0 and poll
  `STATUS.BUFFER_EMPTY`, clear `INTR_ENABLE` and write both clear bits of `INTR_STATUS`.
. Write `CTRL` with only `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 0x000, 0x001, 0xFFF and 0x555 and compare each read-back
  word exactly.
. For `BUFFER_POP`, `TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` and both together, first with an empty queue and then after
  sending a message over the ATB pins and polling `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, write `CTRL`, read it back
  and print bits 0 and 4; on the filled legs poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` back to 1.
. Hold `tb_telemetry0_afready` low, write `CTRL` with threshold 5 and `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`, require
  threshold 5 on read-back, write `CTRL` 0x1, read `CTRL`, release `tb_telemetry0_afready` and
  require `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 0.
. Write `INTR_ENABLE` 0x1, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x0 and compare each read-back exactly.
. Write `INTR_TEST` 0x10 and compare, write 0 and compare, write 0x1 and read `INTR_TEST` and
  `INTR_STATUS` for printing, then write 0 and clear `INTR_STATUS`.
. Error injection. Point: the five read-only registers of receiver 0 (`STATUS`,
  `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0]` and
  `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[31]`). Kind: writes of 0xFFFF_FFFF and 0 to each, first with the queue empty
  and again with one message of probe id 0x0B queued. Expected response: all five read exactly their
  pre-write words after every write; each write response is recorded and printed, not compared.
  Between the two rounds send a message of probe id 0x0B and poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0; afterwards
  flush and write `CTRL` 0.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and read it back exactly, require step stamps and checker lines in
  order, print the ordered fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-THRESHOLD-FIELD-RW` |`BUFFER_THRESHOLD` written 0x000, 0x001, 0xFFF and 0x555 reads
  back as the exact `CTRL` word with no other bit set
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-CTRL-PULSE-READ` |After each pulse write on an empty and on a filled queue `CTRL`
  bits 0 and 4 read 0 (`sw=w` in the RDL), and a queued message leaves the queue after every write
  within the poll bound
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-CTRL-FULL-WORD` |After a full-word write of only `BUFFER_POP`,
  `CTRL.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` reads 0 although it read 5 before; the bit 8 outcome is printed
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-INTR-ENABLE-BITS` |`INTR_ENABLE` reads back 0x1, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x0 exactly as
  written
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-INTR-TEST-ACCESS` |`INTR_TEST` reads 0x10 after a write of 0x10 and 0 after a write
  of 0; bit 0 reads 0 after a write of 1 (`sw=w` in the RDL) and `INTR_STATUS` is measured and
  printed without a compare
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RO-WRITE-IGNORED` |Writes of 0xFFFF_FFFF and 0 to the five read-only registers leave
  every one reading its pre-write word on an empty queue and with one message queued; the write
  responses are printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < THRESHOLD_FIELD_DONE < PULSE_READS_DONE < FULL_WORD_DONE <
  INTR_ENABLE_DONE < INTR_TEST_DONE < RO_WRITES_DONE: step stamps S1 to S7 strictly increasing and
  the six checker lines printed in step order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (SEP_IN access, fuse sense, buffer polls and ATB
  beat acceptance) with the last observed state of each; expiry of any raises
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The pulse-bit read values,
the bit 8 outcome, the `INTR_TEST` bit 0 read and the read-only write responses are reported only.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Whether a full-word `BUFFER_POP` write cancels the pending transmitter flush request
(bit 8) is not specified and is printed. The pulse-bit reads of `CTRL` bits 0 and 4 are reported
only, and `INTR_STATUS` after the `INTR_TEST` bit 0 write is measured and printed without a
compare. The responses of the writes to the read-only registers are printed, because the expected
response is not specified.

'''''

[[sec-335-smc_telemetry_irq_aggregate_test]]
===== 335 `smc_telemetry_irq_aggregate_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_irq_aggregate_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; telemetry receivers 0, 1 and 2 `CTRL`, `STATUS`,
`INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE` and `INTR_TEST`; interrupt outputs `tb_telemetry_irq` (3 bits, bit i
for receiver i) and `tb_telemetry_irq_any` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; the bench ATB beat driver on
`tb_telemetry1_atdata`, `tb_telemetry1_atid` (0x11), `tb_telemetry1_atvalid` and
`tb_telemetry1_atready` (and the matching pins of receivers 0 and 2 for the ATB IDs 0x00 and 0x22);
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Each telemetry receiver interrupt raises its own bit of
`tb_telemetry_irq` and the aggregate `tb_telemetry_irq_any` holds until the last source clears, with
each source working alone and masked sources staying quiet.

*Test Coverage*:

* One receiver at a time: `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` and `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` set on
  receiver i drive `tb_telemetry_irq` to the one-hot value with bit i set and `tb_telemetry_irq_any`
  to 1 within a 64-cycle bound, and clearing `INTR_TEST` returns both to 0
  (`hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc`, telemetry interrupt 0; `hw/sys/smc/doc/periphs.adoc`, Telemetry
  Receiver; `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc`, Interrupts). Platform interrupt
  identifiers and PLIC delivery are not observable here and are not stated by the specification.
* Two receivers: with the source raised on receivers 0 and 2 the vector is 0b101; clearing receiver
  0 leaves 0b100 with the aggregate at 1; clearing receiver 2 returns both to 0.
* Each source alone on receiver 1: with only `INTR_ENABLE.MISSING_LAST` set, unflagged packets
  (last-packet flag clear, at most 16) are sent until `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` sets; the vector
  must read 0b010 with the aggregate at 1, and a write of one to `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` returns
  both to 0. With only `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` set, `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` drives 0b010
  and clearing it releases (`architecture.adoc`, Interrupts: the interrupt output is the masked OR
  of the two sources). The packet count to `MISSING_LAST` is measured and printed.
* Masked sources: with every `INTR_ENABLE` 0, `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` forced on all three
  receivers and `MISSING_LAST` set on receiver 1 must show those sources in each `INTR_STATUS` while
  the vector and the aggregate stay 0 for 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles (masking does not acknowledge a
  source).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and
  read it back exactly, flush each receiver and poll `BUFFER_EMPTY`, write `INTR_ENABLE` 0 and a one
  to `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` on each, and require the vector and aggregate at 0.
. For receivers 0, 1 and 2 in turn write `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` and
  `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD`, wait for the one-hot vector with the aggregate at 1, write
  `INTR_TEST` 0, wait for both at 0, and disable.
. Enable and test-raise receivers 0 and 2, wait for 0b101 with the aggregate at 1, release receiver
  0 and wait for 0b100 with the aggregate at 1, release receiver 2 and wait for both at 0, and
  disable.
. Error injection. Point: the ATB beat pins of receiver 1, with only `INTR_ENABLE.MISSING_LAST`
  enabled. Kind: unflagged packets (last-packet flag clear) sent until `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST`
  is set. Expected response: the vector reads 0b010 with the aggregate at 1, and a write of one to
  clear returns both to 0. Then enable `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` only, set `INTR_TEST`, wait for 0b010,
  clear `INTR_TEST`, wait for both at 0.
. Error injection. Point: `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` of all three receivers and the ATB beat pins
  of receiver 1, with all enables 0. Kind: the test bit written on all three receivers and unflagged
  packets sent to receiver 1 until `MISSING_LAST` is set. Expected response: each `INTR_STATUS`
  shows its sources set while the vector and aggregate stay 0 on each of 64 consecutive `clk_smc_i`
  rises. Then clear every source and require both at 0.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, report the bounded waits, require the step stamps and checker lines
  in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-IRQ-ANY-OF-THREE` |A source on receiver i alone sets exactly bit i of
  `tb_telemetry_irq` and `tb_telemetry_irq_any` for i = 0, 1 and 2, and both read 0 after release,
  each within the 64-cycle bound
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-IRQ-LAST-RELEASE` |With receivers 0 and 2 asserting, clearing receiver 0 leaves
  `tb_telemetry_irq` at 0b100 with the aggregate at 1, and clearing receiver 2 releases both to 0
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-IRQ-EACH-SOURCE` |On receiver 1 the `MISSING_LAST` source alone and the
  `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` source alone each drive 0b010 with the aggregate at 1 and release on their own
  clear; the unflagged packet count is measured and printed
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-IRQ-MASKED-QUIET` |With every `INTR_ENABLE` 0 and sources set on all receivers
  (shown in `INTR_STATUS`), the vector and aggregate stay 0 for 64 cycles
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < ONE_RECEIVER_DONE < TWO_RECEIVERS_DONE < EACH_SOURCE_DONE
  < MASKED_QUIET_DONE: step stamps S1 to S5 strictly increasing and the checker lines printed in
  step order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense, interrupt polls of 64 cycles,
  buffer polls, ATB beat acceptance and the SEP_IN access bound) with the last state of each; expiry
  raises
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The cycle counts to each
vector change and the packet count to `MISSING_LAST` are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Platform interrupt identifiers and PLIC delivery are not observable here and are not
stated by the specification. The packet count to `MISSING_LAST` and the cycle counts to each vector
change are measured and reported only.

'''''

[[sec-336-smc_telemetry_receiver_isolation_test]]
===== 336 `smc_telemetry_receiver_isolation_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_receiver_isolation_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; telemetry receivers 0, 1 and 2 registers `STATUS`,
`TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`, `INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE` and `CTRL`; the bench
ATB beat drivers on `tb_telemetry0_*`, `tb_telemetry1_*` and `tb_telemetry2_*` (`atdata`, `atid`
0x00, 0x11 and 0x22, `atvalid`, `atready`) on `clk_smc_i`, run as three concurrent bench processes
in the simultaneous step; `tb_telemetry_irq_any` sampled; presence of `tb_telemetry1_afvalid`,
`tb_telemetry1_afready`, `tb_telemetry2_afvalid` and `tb_telemetry2_afready` queried;
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Traffic and register operations on one telemetry receiver,
alone or while the other two receive beats, leave the registers of the other receivers unchanged.

*Test Coverage*:

* Single-receiver traffic (`hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc`, Message Queue and
  Readout; `interface.adoc`, Subsystem Wrapper): one single-packet message with probe id 0x0A, 0x0B
  and 0x0C sent to receivers 0, 1 and 2 in turn; the addressed receiver reads non-empty with its own
  probe id and the other two receivers read their pre-message `STATUS`, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`,
  `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`, `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL` words exactly, with `BUFFER_EMPTY` set before
  the message. The receiver is then popped to empty.
* Simultaneous traffic (`interface.adoc`, Subsystem Wrapper; `architecture.adoc`, Assembly and
  Decode): three bench processes drive beats on all three receivers in the same `clk_smc_i` cycles,
  two single-packet messages each (probe ids 0x05 and 0x06, 0x0A and 0x0B, 0x13 and 0x14). At least
  one cycle must accept beats on all three receivers, and each receiver must return its own two
  probe ids in order and none from another receiver.
* Operations (`architecture.adoc`, Reset and Flush; `telemetry_receiver.rdl`, `CTRL`): with
  `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 and receivers holding 1, 2 and 3 messages, a pop on receiver 0, a flush on
  receiver 1 and a rewrite of threshold (2) and `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` on receiver 2 each
  leave the two untouched receivers at the `STATUS`, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL`
  words taken before the operation. The transmitter-flush pin presence on receivers 1 and 2 and
  `tb_telemetry_irq_any` before and after are printed; whether those receivers expose the
  transmitter flush pins is not stated by the specification.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the ATB pins, wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear
  `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and read it back exactly, then flush each receiver, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY`, write
  `INTR_ENABLE` 0 and read it back.
. For each receiver i in turn, take a stable snapshot (two equal consecutive reads) of the other two
  receivers, send one single-packet message, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, read `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` and
  compare it with the sent probe id, compare the other receivers' words with the snapshot, pop and
  poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` back to 1.
. Start three ATB sender processes together, wait for all, require at least one common accepted
  cycle, then for each receiver poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, read and compare the probe id of each
  message in order and pop after each; poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 1.
. Write `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 to every receiver and read it back, send 1, 2 and 3 messages to
  receivers 0, 1 and 2 and require the first probe id of each.
. Snapshot receivers 1 and 2, pop receiver 0 and compare; snapshot receivers 0 and 2, flush receiver
  1 and compare; snapshot receivers 0 and 1, write threshold 2 and `INTR_ENABLE` to receiver 2, read
  both back and compare; flush receiver 2.
. Report the bounded waits, require the step stamps and checker lines in order and print the ordered
  fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-ISOLATION-TRAFFIC` |Traffic on receiver i changes only receiver i: the other two
  receivers read their pre-message `STATUS`, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS`,
  `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL` words, and receiver i reads non-empty with its own probe id
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-ISOLATION-SIMULTANEOUS` |With three ATB sources accepted in at least one common
  cycle, each receiver returns its own two probe ids in order and none from another receiver
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-ISOLATION-OPS` |A pop on receiver 0, a flush on receiver 1 and a threshold and
  enable rewrite on receiver 2 leave the untouched receivers at the words taken before each
  operation; the interrupt aggregate and pin presence are printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < SINGLE_RECEIVER_TRAFFIC < SIMULTANEOUS_TRAFFIC <
  ISOLATED_OPERATIONS: step stamps S1 to S5 strictly increasing and the four checker lines printed
  in step order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense, stable snapshot rounds, buffer
  polls, ATB beat acceptance and the SEP_IN access bound) with the last state of each; expiry raises
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The interrupt aggregate
values and the transmitter flush pin presence are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The transmitter-flush pin presence on receivers 1 and 2 and `tb_telemetry_irq_any`
before and after each operation are printed, not compared; whether those receivers expose the
transmitter flush pins is not stated by the specification.

'''''

[[sec-337-smc_telemetry_rx_flush_test]]
===== 337 `smc_telemetry_rx_flush_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_rx_flush_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; telemetry receiver 0 registers `CTRL`, `STATUS`,
`INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS` and
`TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0..3]`; the bench ATB beat driver on `tb_telemetry0_atdata`, `tb_telemetry0_atid`
(0x21), `tb_telemetry0_atvalid` and `tb_telemetry0_atready`; `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` sampled on
`clk_smc_i`; `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `CTRL.TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` on receiver 0 empties a populated queue
and clears its threshold interrupt, acts once, restarts message assembly, and leaves a pending
MISSING_LAST interrupt untouched.
