*Test Coverage*:

* Populated flush (`hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc`, Reset and Flush and Message
  Queue and Readout; `telemetry_receiver.rdl`, `CTRL`): with `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 and
  `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` set, three messages (probe ids 0x01, 0x02, 0x03) give
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` 0, `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 and `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` 1. After one flush
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` must read 1 within 200 polls, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS` and
  `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0..3]` read 0, `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` reads 0 and `tb_telemetry_irq[0]`
  falls. The head words are shown live before the flush, so zero is not a reset artefact.
* One-shot: `CTRL` bit 4 (`TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH`) reads 0 after the flush and after two further
  flushes on the empty receiver, each leaving `BUFFER_EMPTY` 1, the head words 0 and no interrupt
  source raised. `TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` is `sw=w` in `telemetry_receiver.rdl`, so the bit 4 read of 0
  holds whatever the hardware does with the pulse. A message sent after the repeated flushes must
  then be kept (`BUFFER_EMPTY` 0 and `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` equal to the sent id 0x1B), which a flush
  that stayed asserted would discard; it is popped before the next step.
* Restart: a message sent after the flush clears `BUFFER_EMPTY` and reads `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x1A.
* Mid-message flush: five of the eight beats of a packet (data 0x2A, last-packet flag clear)
  followed by one flush and no second flush, then one complete message with probe id 0x15;
  `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` must read 0x15 and one pop must empty the queue. The probe latch rule for the
  partial packet is not stated by the specification.
* Beats around the pulse (`architecture.adoc`, Assembly and Decode): eight beats of a message with
  probe id 0x13 are streamed while `CTRL.TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` is written once two beats are in; the
  accepted-beat and stalled-cycle counts and `STATUS` after 64 quiet cycles are printed, not
  compared (whether in-flight beats are held or dropped is not stated by the specification), and
  every beat must be accepted within 64 cycles. After one quiet flush a message with probe id 0x14
  must read `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x14 and one pop must empty the queue.
* Flush against `MISSING_LAST` (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, Interrupt Handling;
  `architecture.adoc`, Interrupts): with `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` set by unflagged packets (at
  most 16) and enabled, `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` is 1; after a flush `MISSING_LAST` must still read 1
  and `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` stay 1 for 64 cycles until a write of one clears it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the bench pins, wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear
  `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and read it back exactly, flush receiver 0 and poll `BUFFER_EMPTY`, write
  `INTR_ENABLE` 0 and clear `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST`.
. Write `CTRL` threshold 1 and `INTR_ENABLE.BUFFER_THRESHOLD`, send three messages polling
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0 after each, read the head words and `INTR_STATUS`, wait for
  `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` 1, write the flush, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 1, read the head words and
  `INTR_STATUS`, and wait for `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` 0.
. Read `CTRL`, flush twice more (holding `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` at 0 for 64 cycles before the third),
  and after each poll `BUFFER_EMPTY`, read the head words, `INTR_STATUS` and `CTRL`; then send a
  message with probe id 0x1B, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, require that probe id and pop to empty.
. Send a message with probe id 0x1A, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0, read the probe id, pop and poll
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 1.
. Send five partial beats, write one flush, send a complete message with probe id 0x15, poll, read
  the probe id, pop to empty.
. Stream a message with probe id 0x13 as a background process, wait for two accepted beats, write
  one flush, wait for the stream to finish and 64 quiet cycles, read `STATUS` and the probe id,
  flush, send a message with probe id 0x14, read its probe id and pop to empty.
. Clear `MISSING_LAST`, send unflagged packets until it sets, enable it and wait for
  `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` 1, write the flush, read `INTR_STATUS`, hold `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` at 1 for
  64 cycles, read `INTR_STATUS`, write a one to clear, read `INTR_STATUS` and wait for
  `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` 0, then disable the interrupt, flush and write `CTRL` 0.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, require step stamps and checker lines in order, print the ordered
  fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-EMPTIES` |After a flush of a three-message queue `BUFFER_EMPTY` reads 1
  within the poll bound, `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, `TELEMETRY_COUNTER_VLDS` and
  `TELEMETRY_COUNTER[0..3]` read 0, `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` reads 0 and `tb_telemetry_irq[0]`
  falls
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-ONE-SHOT` |`CTRL` bit 4 reads 0 after the flush and after two repeats on
  the empty receiver (`sw=w` in the RDL), each leaving `BUFFER_EMPTY` 1, the head words 0 and no
  interrupt source raised, and a message sent afterwards is kept with its probe id 0x1B
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-RESTART` |A message sent after a flush clears `BUFFER_EMPTY` within the
  poll bound and reads `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x1A
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-MID-MESSAGE` |After five beats of an unfinished packet and one flush the
  next complete message reads `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x15 and one pop empties the queue
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-BEATS-AROUND` |The beats streamed around the flush are all accepted within
  the bound; the accepted and stalled beat counts and the `STATUS` after quiet cycles are measured
  and printed; after one quiet flush the next message reads `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x14 and one pop
  empties the queue
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-RX-FLUSH-KEEPS-MISSING-LAST` |After a flush with `MISSING_LAST` pending and enabled
  `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` still reads 1 and `tb_telemetry_irq[0]` stays 1 for 64 cycles, then a
  write of one clears the source and the line falls
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < POPULATED_FLUSH_DONE < ONE_SHOT_DONE < RESTART_DONE <
  MID_MESSAGE_DONE < BEATS_AROUND_DONE < MISSING_LAST_KEPT: step stamps S1 to S7 strictly increasing
  and the six checker lines printed in step order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense, buffer polls of 200 reads,
  interrupt waits of 64 cycles, ATB beat acceptance, the unflagged packet count and the SEP_IN
  access bound) with the last state of each; expiry raises
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The beat counts and
`STATUS` in the beats-around step are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The accepted-beat and stalled-cycle counts and `STATUS` after the 64 quiet cycles of
the beats-around step are printed and not compared, because the specification does not state whether
in-flight beats are held or dropped. The probe latch rule for the partial packet of the mid-message
flush is not stated by the specification, so only the next complete message is compared.

'''''

[[sec-338-smc_telemetry_tx_flush_test]]
===== 338 `smc_telemetry_tx_flush_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_tx_flush_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; telemetry receiver 0 registers `CTRL`, `STATUS` and
`TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`; the transmitter flush handshake pins `tb_telemetry0_afvalid` (observed,
sampled by a monitor on every `clk_smc_i` rise) and `tb_telemetry0_afready` (driven by the bench);
the bench ATB beat driver on `tb_telemetry0_atdata`, `tb_telemetry0_atid` (0x33),
`tb_telemetry0_atvalid` and `tb_telemetry0_atready`; `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.TELEMETRY_CG_EN`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` on receiver 0 raises `afvalid_o`, holds
while `afready_i` is low, clears when it rises, keeps `BUFFER_THRESHOLD`, and is separate from the
receiver flush.

*Test Coverage*:

* Ready high (`hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc`, Reset and Flush: hardware clears the
  request after `afvalid_o` and `afready_i`; `interface.adoc`, Subsystem Wrapper): with `afready_i`
  high a write of `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` raises `afvalid_o` within 64 cycles, `afvalid_o` falls
  within 64 cycles of rising, and `CTRL` bit 8 reads 0 afterwards. The cycle counts are ceilings,
  printed and not expected values (the latency is not stated by the specification).
* Pending hold: with `afready_i` low the request holds `afvalid_o` at 1 on every sample for 2048
  `clk_smc_i` cycles and `CTRL` bit 8 at 1 on reads taken about every 64 cycles; once `afready_i`
  rises both clear within 64 cycles.
* Rewrite while pending: a second write of `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` while the request is pending ends in
  one completion within 64 cycles of `afready_i` rising, with `afvalid_o` 0 and `CTRL` bit 8 0. The
  number of `afvalid_o` rising edges is printed and not compared (not stated by the specification).
* Threshold kept (`telemetry_receiver.rdl`, `CTRL`): with `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 3 written together with
  `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` and `afready_i` low `CTRL` reads exactly 0x3100, and exactly 0x3000 after
  `afready_i` rises and the hardware clears the request.
* Path separation (`architecture.adoc`, Reset and Flush): the two messages (probe ids 0x0B and
  0x0C) are sent eight idle cycles apart, as the other telemetry tests send them (sent back to back
  the second message did not enter the queue; the documents do not state a spacing), and with
  `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 the `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` bit shows that both are queued
  (`telemetry_receiver.rdl`); a transmitter flush then leaves `BUFFER_EMPTY` 0 and
  `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x0B, and after one pop `BUFFER_EMPTY` is still 0 with `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`
  0x0C, so neither queued message was dropped; a receiver flush with `afready_i` low then empties
  the queue while `afvalid_o` stays 0 for 64 cycles.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the bench pins, wait (bounded) for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear
  `TELEMETRY_CG_EN` and read it back exactly, drive `afready_i` high and require `afvalid_o` 0.
. Start the `afvalid_o` monitor, write `CTRL` with only `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`, wait for the monitor
  to see a rise and then a fall within 64 samples each, and read `CTRL` requiring bit 8 clear.
. Drive `afready_i` low, write `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`, wait for `afvalid_o` 1, then for 2048 monitored
  cycles read `CTRL` every 64 cycles requiring bit 8 set and `afvalid_o` never 0; drive `afready_i`
  high, wait for `afvalid_o` 0 and read `CTRL` requiring bit 8 clear.
. Drive `afready_i` low, write `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`, wait for `afvalid_o` 1, write it again, read
  `CTRL`, drive `afready_i` high, wait for `afvalid_o` 0 and read `CTRL` requiring bit 8 clear;
  print the rise count.
. Drive `afready_i` low, write `CTRL` 0x3100, wait for `afvalid_o` 1 and read back 0x3100, drive
  `afready_i` high, wait for `afvalid_o` 0 and read back 0x3000.
. Write `BUFFER_THRESHOLD` 1 and clear `INTR_STATUS`, drive `afready_i` low, send messages with
  probe ids 0x0B and 0x0C eight idle cycles apart, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0 and `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` to 1, clear
  it, write `TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`, release `afready_i` after `afvalid_o` rises, wait
  for it to fall, read `CTRL` requiring 0, require `BUFFER_EMPTY` 0 and probe id 0x0B, pop once, print `STATUS` and the probe id, send a message with probe id 0x0C again and poll
  `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 0; with `afready_i` low write `TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH`, poll `BUFFER_EMPTY` to 1, and require `afvalid_o` to
  have stayed 0 for 64 samples with no rise.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, require step stamps and checker lines in order, print the ordered
  fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-TX-FLUSH-READY-HIGH` |With `afready_i` high the request raises `afvalid_o`, retires
  it and leaves `CTRL` bit 8 at 0, each within 64 cycles; the two cycle counts are printed
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-TX-FLUSH-PENDING-HOLD` |For 2048 cycles with `afready_i` low `afvalid_o` stays 1 and
  `CTRL` bit 8 stays 1, and both clear within 64 cycles after `afready_i` rises
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-TX-FLUSH-REWRITE` |A second write of one while pending ends in one completion with
  `afvalid_o` 0 and `CTRL` bit 8 0 within 64 cycles of `afready_i` rising; the number of `afvalid_o`
  rises is printed and not compared
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-TX-FLUSH-THRESHOLD-KEPT` |`CTRL` reads 0x3100 while the request is pending and
  exactly 0x3000 after the hardware clears it
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-FLUSH-PATH-SEPARATION` |A transmitter flush leaves both queued messages
  (`BUFFER_EMPTY` 0 with `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x0B, and after one pop `BUFFER_EMPTY` 0 with
  `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` 0x0C) and a receiver flush empties the queue without a
  rise of `afvalid_o` over 64 samples
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence SETUP_DONE < READY_HIGH_DONE < LONG_HOLD_DONE < REWRITE_DONE <
  THRESHOLD_KEPT < PATHS_SEPARATED: step stamps S1 to S6 strictly increasing and the five checker
  lines printed in step order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense, handshake bounds of 64 cycles, the
  2048-cycle hold window, buffer polls, ATB beat acceptance and the SEP_IN access bound) with the
  last state of each; expiry raises
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The handshake cycle counts
and the rewrite rise count are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The handshake cycle counts of the ready-high step are ceilings, printed and not
expected values, because the specification does not state the latency. The number of `afvalid_o`
rising edges in the rewrite step is printed and not compared, because the specification does not
state it. The two path-separation messages are sent eight idle cycles apart because the documents do
not state a spacing.

'''''

[[sec-339-smc_wdt_count_feed_test]]
===== 339 `smc_wdt_count_feed_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_count_feed_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (core 0 and core 1 watchdog blocks
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*` and `SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE1_WDT_*`: `CTRL`, `COUNT`,
`COUNT_HI`, `FEED`, `KEY`); the CPU control registers `RESET_CTRL` and `RESET_TIMEOUT` (8-byte
accesses) for the core 1 level reset; `tb_top.tb_cpu_core_resets_n` bit 1 sampled on `clk_smc_i`; a
bounded SEP_IN read through the driver's tolerated-timeout path for the access made while core 1 is
held in reset

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Watchdog COUNT counts under `wdogenalways` or `wdogcoreawake`, takes
keyed writes, reads COUNT_HI as 0, restarts on the feed word only, and counts again after a core 1
level reset is released; the reads taken while that reset is held are measured.

*Test Coverage*:

* Enable matrix (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, `CTRL.wdogenalways` and `wdogcoreawake`;
  `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, watchdog): three consecutive `COUNT` reads are strictly
  increasing with `wdogenalways` alone and with `wdogenalways` plus `wdogcoreawake`. With both
  enables clear the three reads and their increase are printed (whether the counter holds or counts
  is not stated by the specification), and after `wdogenalways` is cleared again the three reads
  must show the same behaviour as that earlier both-clear window.
* COUNT write: with `wdogenalways` set, a keyed write of 0x100 makes the next reads at least 0x100
  and strictly increasing, with the first read below the `COUNT` read taken right before the write
  (which must exceed 0x100 plus twice the largest per-read increase measured in the window, so the
  leg is not vacuous) and must not exceed 0x100 plus twice that increase. Whether the first read
  is the written value or the written value plus one is not stated by the specification and is
  printed. With both enables clear a write of 0x8000_0010
  reads bit 31 as 0 and bits 30:0 between 0x10 and 0x10 plus that increase (`wdt.rdl`,
  `COUNT.wdogcount` is 31 bits).
* `COUNT_HI` reads 0 (`wdt.rdl`) while `COUNT` reads nonzero after a keyed write of 0x1234_5678.
* Rollover: eight consecutive `COUNT` reads from 0x7FFF_FFF0 never have bit 31 set; the first read
  below 0x7FFF_FFF0 is printed with its value (the value after 0x7FFF_FFFF is not stated by the
  specification).
* Feed (`wdt.rdl`, `FEED`): after a keyed `COUNT` write of 0x0010_0000 and a keyed `FEED` write of
  0x0D09F00D the first `COUNT` read is below 0x0010_0000 and at most four times the largest
  per-read increase measured earlier, and the second is larger. A keyed `FEED`
  write of 0x0D09F00C and a `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D with the watchdog locked each leave `COUNT`
  at or above 0x0010_0000 (`hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc`, Register Access); `KEY` read after the
  non-feed word is printed (whether that write locks is not stated by the specification), and `KEY`
  must read 0 before the locked write.
* `wdogcoreawake` on core 1: with only `wdogcoreawake` set, three `COUNT` reads increase while core
  1 is out of reset. `RESET_TIMEOUT` is written to forced mode with value 32 and `RESET_CTRL` with
  core 1's level reset low and every other level field unchanged, and `tb_cpu_core_resets_n[1]` must
  read 0 within 256 rises. During the hold one bounded `CTRL` read is made and, if it completes,
  three bounded `COUNT` reads; their values, or the absence of a completion within the driver bound,
  are printed and nothing about them is asserted. After the release `tb_cpu_core_resets_n[1]` must
  read 1 within 256 rises, `CTRL` must still have `wdogcoreawake` set (the watchdog registers are
  not reset by the core reset) and three `COUNT` reads must increase again. Which reset exactly
  defines the condition is not stated by the specification.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0 and `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x0010_0000 on core 0 and take three `COUNT`
  reads (both enables clear).
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x1000 and take three `COUNT` reads, requiring them strictly increasing.
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x3000 and take three `COUNT` reads, requiring them strictly increasing.
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0 and take three `COUNT` reads, requiring them equal when the first window
  held and strictly increasing when it counted.
. With `CTRL` 0x1000 read `COUNT`, write `COUNT` 0x100 and read three times, then compare as above;
  clear `CTRL`, write `COUNT` 0x8000_0010, read `COUNT` and compare bit 31 and bits 30:0.
. Write `COUNT` 0x1234_5678 and read `COUNT_HI` and `COUNT`.
. With `CTRL` 0x1000 write `COUNT` 0x7FFF_FFF0 and take eight `COUNT` reads, requiring bit 31 clear
  in each.
. Write `COUNT` 0x0010_0000, then `FEED` 0x0D09F00D, and read `COUNT` twice.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `FEED` register. Kind: a keyed `FEED` write of the non-feed
  word 0x0D09F00C, then a `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D with the watchdog locked. Expected response:
  each leaves `COUNT` at or above 0x0010_0000. Write `COUNT` 0x0010_0000 first, read `COUNT` and
  `KEY` after the non-feed word; re-lock with a `CTRL` write when `KEY` reads set, require `KEY` 0,
  then make the locked write and read `COUNT`.
. On core 1 write `CTRL` 0x2000 and `COUNT` 0x0010_0000 and take three `COUNT` reads; read
  `RESET_CTRL`, write `RESET_TIMEOUT` forced 32, clear core 1's level reset, wait for
  `tb_cpu_core_resets_n[1]` 0, make the bounded hold-phase reads, require it still 0, restore
  `RESET_CTRL`, wait for 1, read `CTRL` and take three more `COUNT` reads. Restore `RESET_TIMEOUT`
  and clear `CTRL` on both cores, then require the step stamps and checker lines in order and print
  the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-COUNT-ENABLE-MATRIX` |Three `COUNT` reads are strictly increasing with `wdogenalways`
  alone and with `wdogenalways` plus `wdogcoreawake`, and after `wdogenalways` is cleared the
  progression equals the both-clear window; the both-clear increase is printed
|`CHK-WDT-COUNT-WRITE` |After a `COUNT` write of 0x100 with `wdogenalways` set the reads are at
  least 0x100, strictly increasing and the first is below the pre-write read, and a write of
  0x8000_0010 with both enables clear reads bit 31 as 0 and bits 30:0 within 0x10 and 0x10 plus the
  measured increase; the written-value offset is printed
|`CHK-WDT-COUNTHI-ZERO` |`COUNT_HI` reads 0 while `COUNT` reads nonzero after a `COUNT` write of
  0x1234_5678
|`CHK-WDT-COUNT-ROLLOVER` |No bit 31 is set in eight `COUNT` reads from 0x7FFF_FFF0; the first read
  below the start is printed and not compared
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-RESET` |After `KEY` and `FEED` 0x0D09F00D the `COUNT` read is below 0x0010_0000 and
  the next read is larger
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-NONMAGIC` |A keyed `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00C and a locked `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D
  each leave `COUNT` at or above 0x0010_0000; `KEY` after the non-feed write is printed
|`CHK-WDT-COREAWAKE` |With `wdogcoreawake` alone core 1 `COUNT` reads increase before the level
  reset and again after its release, `tb_cpu_core_resets_n[1]` reaches 0 and returns to 1 within 256
  rises and `CTRL` keeps `wdogcoreawake`; the hold-phase accesses are printed and not asserted
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S10 strictly increasing and the seven checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The both-clear behaviour,
the written-value offset, the rollover value, the `KEY` read after the non-feed word and the
hold-phase accesses are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: With both enables clear the three `COUNT` reads and their increase are printed,
because the specification does not state whether the counter holds or counts. Whether the first read
after a `COUNT` write is the written value or the written value plus one, the first read below
0x7FFF_FFF0 at rollover and the `KEY` read after the non-feed word are printed and not compared,
because the specification does not state them. The accesses made while core 1 is held in reset are
printed and nothing about them is asserted; which reset exactly defines the `wdogcoreawake`
condition is not stated by the specification.

'''''

[[sec-340-smc_wdt_ip0_clear_test]]
===== 340 `smc_wdt_ip0_clear_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_ip0_clear_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN; core 0 watchdog block `SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*`
registers `KEY`, `CTRL`, `CMP`, `COUNT` and `FEED`; `CTRL` bit 28 (`wdogip0`) read back

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the stimulus is the named frame, command or sequence the
specification states.

*Objective*: `CTRL.wdogip0` sets while the scaled count is at or above `CMP`, holds
against a clear in that window, and clears only through `KEY` and a `CTRL` write with bit 28 low
once the count is below `CMP`.

*Test Coverage*:

* Set and hold (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, `CTRL.wdogip0`;
  `hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc`, Operation): `CTRL` bit 28 reads 0 at reset; with `CMP` 0x40, scale
  8 and `COUNT` 0x1000 (scaled 0x10) it reads 0; with `COUNT` 0x4400 (scaled 0x44) it reads 1; a
  keyed `CTRL` write of 0x0008 (bit 28 low) while above `CMP` leaves `CTRL` at 0x1000_0008.
* Raising `CMP` to 0x100 and rewriting `CTRL` 0x0008 reads `CTRL` 0x0008. Lowering `CMP` to 0x10
  sets bit 28 within four `CTRL` reads (the read at which it first reads 1 is printed; the latency
  is not specified) and `CTRL` then reads 0x1000_0008.
* Clear sequence (`wdt.rdl`, `FEED` and `CTRL.wdogip0`; `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`,
  watchdog): with `CTRL` 0x1008 (`wdogenalways`, scale 8) and bit 28 set from `COUNT` 0x4400 at
  `CMP` 0x40, a keyed `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D leaves `CTRL` at 0x1000_1008, and a keyed `CTRL`
  write of 0x1008 then reads `CTRL` 0x1008. The same clear works after a keyed `COUNT` write of
  0x1000 (below `CMP`).
* Unlock consumed (`watchdog.adoc`, Register Access): after `KEY` and `FEED`, or `KEY` and a `COUNT`
  write of 0x1000, a `CTRL` write of 0x1008 without a second `KEY` is dropped and `CTRL` still reads
  0x1000_1008; the feed alone does not clear bit 28.
* No clear above `CMP`: with a fresh `KEY` and `COUNT` 0x4400 above `CMP`, a `CTRL` write of 0x1008
  leaves `CTRL` at 0x1000_1008.
* Re-arm: after a successful clear, `COUNT` 0x4400 with `CMP` 0x40 sets bit 28 again within four
  reads.
* Write one: with the scaled count below `CMP` a keyed `CTRL` write of 0x1000_1008 is followed by a
  `CTRL` read whose bit 28 must read 1, because `wdogip0` is `sw=rw` in `wdt.rdl` and the write
  stores 1.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CTRL` and require 0.
. Write `KEY` then `CMP` 0x40, `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x0008, `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x1000 and require
  `CTRL` 0x0008; write `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x4400 and require `CTRL` 0x1000_0008.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL` register. Kind: a keyed `CTRL` write of 0x0008 with bit
  28 low while the scaled count is above `CMP`. Expected response: `CTRL` still reads 0x1000_0008.
. Write `KEY` then `CMP` 0x100, `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x0008 and require `CTRL` 0x0008.
. Write `KEY` then `CMP` 0x10 and poll `CTRL` up to four reads for bit 28, requiring `CTRL`
  0x1000_0008 on the read that sees it.
. Write `CMP` 0x40, `CTRL` 0x1008 and `COUNT` 0x4400 (each after `KEY`), poll for bit 28, write
  `FEED` 0x0D09F00D and require `CTRL` 0x1000_1008, write `CTRL` 0x1008 and require 0x1008.
. Set bit 28 again with `COUNT` 0x4400, write `COUNT` 0x1000 and then `CTRL` 0x1008, and require
  `CTRL` 0x1008.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL` register. Kind: a `CTRL` write of 0x1008 without a
  second `KEY`, once after `KEY` and `FEED` and once after `KEY` and a `COUNT` write of 0x1000.
  Expected response: the write is dropped and `CTRL` still reads 0x1000_1008 both times. Set bit 28
  again before the first pair.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL` register. Kind: a keyed `CTRL` write of 0x1008 with bit
  28 low while `COUNT` 0x4400 keeps the scaled count above `CMP`. Expected response: `CTRL` still
  reads 0x1000_1008. Write `COUNT` 0x4400 after `KEY` first.
. Write `FEED` 0x0D09F00D and `CTRL` 0x1008 and require 0x1008, write `COUNT` 0x4400 and poll for
  bit 28 again within four reads.
. Write `FEED` 0x0D09F00D and `CTRL` 0x1008 and require 0x1008, write `CTRL` 0x1000_1008 (after
  `KEY`), read `CTRL` and require bit 28 to read 1; require step stamps and checker lines in order and print the
  ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-SET` |`CTRL` bit 28 reads 0 at reset and below `CMP`, 1 above it, stays 1 after a
  keyed clear write above `CMP`, reads 0 after `CMP` is raised and the clear sequence is written,
  and reads 1 within four reads after `CMP` is lowered; the first-read latency is printed; the zero
  reset value is bench-limited (2-state zero init)
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-CLEAR-SEQUENCE` |A keyed `FEED` leaves `CTRL` at 0x1000_1008 and a following keyed
  `CTRL` write of 0x1008 clears bit 28 with `wdogenalways` and the scale kept; the same clear works
  after a `COUNT` write below `CMP`
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-UNLOCK-CONSUMED` |After `KEY` and `FEED`, or `KEY` and a `COUNT` write, a `CTRL` write
  without a second `KEY` is dropped and bit 28 stays 1
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-NO-CLEAR-ABOVE` |With a fresh `KEY` and the scaled count above `CMP` a `CTRL` write
  with bit 28 low leaves `CTRL` at 0x1000_1008
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-RESET-AFTER-CLEAR` |After a successful clear, `COUNT` 0x4400 with `CMP` 0x40 sets bit
  28 again within four reads
|`CHK-WDT-IP0-WRITE-ONE` |Bit 28 reads 1 after a keyed `CTRL` write with bit 28 high below `CMP`,
  as `wdogip0` is `sw=rw`
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S11 strictly increasing and the six checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The set latency
is reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The read at which `CTRL` bit 28 first reads 1 after `CMP` is lowered is printed,
because the latency is not specified. The zero reset value of bit 28 is bench-limited: a 2-state
zero init also reads 0.

'''''

[[sec-341-smc_wdt_irq_source_ids_test]]
===== 341 `smc_wdt_irq_source_ids_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_irq_source_ids_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (core 2 watchdog block
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE2_WDT_*`: `KEY`, `CMP`, `CTRL`, `COUNT`); bench pin `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n`
(driven low and high); observation points `tb_cpu_interrupts` (raw vector, 328 bits, bit 282
sampled), `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync`, `tb_plic_pending_331` (PLIC source ID 331, core 2 watchdog) and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, all sampled on `clk_smc_i`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The raw interrupt vector is 328 bits wide, bit 282 follows the SEP
watchdog reset indication, and the core 2 watchdog pending bit at PLIC ID 331 is independent of the
raw vector.

*Test Coverage*:

* Vector width (`hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc`, Raw Vector and PLIC Numbering):
  `tb_cpu_interrupts` is 328 bits wide, and the watchdog IDs 329 to 332 are not additional bits of
  it.
* Level of the SEP watchdog indication (`interrupts.adoc`, raw bit 282;
  `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`, Reset): with `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` high, raw bit 282 and
  `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` read 0 at 64 of 64 rises and `tb_plic_pending_331` reads 0 at every one.
  After `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` falls both read 1 within 64 rises and are equal at every one of the 192
  samples across the whole window. The rises at which they return to 0 after the release are printed
  (latency and level-or-latch are not stated by the specification), and the warm reset must release
  within 200000 rises.
* While the SEP indication is asserted the number of rises at which `tb_plic_pending_331` reads 1 is
  printed and not compared, because the warm reset that the indication causes holds the cluster
  PLIC.
* Independence: with the SEP indication released and the warm reset released, `tb_plic_pending_331`
  reads 0 just before the core 2 watchdog is armed (`CMP` 0x40, `CTRL` 0x0008, `COUNT` 0x4400).
  After arming it must read 1 within 64 rises while every bit of `tb_cpu_interrupts` stays at its
  entry value. The interrupt is then cleared (`CMP` 0x100, `CTRL` 0x0008) and the watchdog disarmed;
  core 2 `CTRL.wdogip0` and the `tb_plic_pending_331` level after the clear are printed (whether the
  PLIC pending bit is level or latch is not stated by the specification).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the bench pins, wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, require `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` 1, raw bit 282,
  `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` and `tb_plic_pending_331` all 0, and the raw vector 328 bits wide.
. Sample the four observation points on 64 consecutive `clk_smc_i` rises and require bit 282 and
  `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` at 0 and `tb_plic_pending_331` at 0 on each.
. Error injection. Point: the bench pin `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n`. Kind: the SEP watchdog reset
  indication driven low. Expected response: raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` read 1 within 64
  rises. Sample for 64 rises and print the `tb_plic_pending_331` count.
. Drive `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` high, sample 64 rises, require bit 282 equal to `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync`
  at every sample of the three windows, print the rise at which each returns to 0, and wait
  (bounded) for `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` 1.
. Write `KEY` then `CMP` 0x40 and `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x0008 on core 2, sample `tb_plic_pending_331`
  once and require 0, write `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x4400, sample 64 rises requiring
  `tb_plic_pending_331` 1 at some rise and the raw vector constant, then clear and disarm, read core
  2 `CTRL` and sample 64 more rises for printing; require step stamps and checker lines in order and
  print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SEP-WDT-IRQ-DISTINCT` |The raw vector is 328 bits wide, `tb_plic_pending_331` reads 0 just
  before the core 2 arming and 1 within 64 rises after it while no bit of `tb_cpu_interrupts`
  changes; the SEP-indication window count, `wdogip0` after the clear and the `tb_plic_pending_331`
  level after the clear are printed without a compare
|`CHK-SEP-WDT-IRQ-LEVEL` |With `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` high raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` read
  0 at 64 of 64 rises; after it falls both read 1 within 64 rises and are equal at every sample; the
  return-to-0 rises after the release are printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S5 strictly increasing and the two checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The `tb_plic_pending_331`
count during the SEP indication and the post-clear levels are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The rises at which raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` return to 0 after the
release are printed, because the latency and level-or-latch behaviour are not stated by the
specification. The `tb_plic_pending_331` count while the SEP indication is asserted is printed and
not compared, because the warm reset that the indication causes holds the cluster PLIC. Core 2
`CTRL.wdogip0` and the `tb_plic_pending_331` level after the clear are printed, because the
specification does not state whether the PLIC pending bit is level or latch.

'''''

[[sec-342-smc_wdt_key_relock_test]]
===== 342 `smc_wdt_key_relock_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_key_relock_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (core 0 watchdog block
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*`: `KEY`, `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `COUNT_HI`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `FEED`,
`CMP`; 4-byte accesses and one 8-byte write at `FEED`)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the stimulus is the named frame, command or sequence the
specification states.

*Objective*: The core 0 watchdog stays locked for any key other than 0x51F15E, a key
write unlocks exactly one register write, and every register write re-locks it.

*Test Coverage*:

* Locked reset state (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, `KEY` and `CMP`): `KEY` reads 0 and
  `CMP` reads its reset value 0x1000. Two back-to-back `COUNT` reads fix a hold allowance A = 4 *
  (second - first) used for the locked-write compare below.
* Non-magic keys (`hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc`, Register Access): `KEY` writes of 0x0051_F15F,
  0xFFFF_FFFF and 0x0000_0000 from the locked state each leave `KEY` reading 0 and a following `CMP`
  write of 0x2222 dropped (`CMP` still 0x1000).
* Repeated magic: two writes of 0x51F15E in a row, then a `CMP` write of 0x3333, which must read
  back 0x3333, after which `KEY` reads 0 and a further `CMP` write of 0x4444 without a key is
  dropped. The `KEY` value read between the second magic write and the register write is printed
  (whether it reads 1 is not stated by the specification).
* Read while unlocked: after one magic write `KEY` reads 1; reads of `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `CMP`,
  `SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT_HI` leave `KEY` reading 1, the next `CMP` write of 0x1000 is accepted
  and `KEY` then reads 0 (`watchdog.adoc`, Register Access: KEY reads 1 while unlocked).
* Re-lock after `CMP`: after a keyed `CMP` write of 0x1234 `KEY` reads 0 and a `CMP` write of 0x4321
  without a key leaves `CMP` at 0x1234.
* Re-lock after each register (`wdt.rdl`, addrmap description: each effective write other than `KEY`
  locks the watchdog): after `KEY` and a 32-bit write of `CTRL` 0x2, `COUNT` 0x0010_0000, `FEED`
  0x0D09F00D and `SCALED_COUNT` 0x1234, `KEY` reads 0 and a `CMP` write of 0x2468 is dropped (`CMP`
  stays 0x1234). `SCALED_COUNT` must not read the written 0x1234 and must not exceed `COUNT` shifted
  right by `CTRL.wdogscale`.
* Locked writes dropped: with the watchdog locked, writes of `CTRL` 0x330, `COUNT` 0x0020_0000 and
  `CMP` 0x1357 leave `CTRL` at 0x0002 and `CMP` at 0x1234, `COUNT` is not above its previous read by
  more than twice A, and `KEY` reads 0.
* 64-bit write at `FEED` (`wdt.rdl`, addrmap description: a 64-bit write at 0x18 writes `FEED` and
  `KEY` together and leaves the watchdog locked): with the `KEY` half carrying 0x51F15E and the
  `FEED` half 0x0D09F00D, issued once from the locked state and once from the unlocked state, `KEY`
  reads 0 afterwards. `COUNT` after each write is printed to show whether the `FEED` half acted (the
  ordering inside the write is not stated by the specification).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `KEY` and require 0, read `CMP` and require 0x1000, take two `COUNT` reads and compute the
  allowance.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `KEY` register. Kind: the non-magic key values 0x0051_F15F,
  0xFFFF_FFFF and 0x0000_0000 written from the locked state, each followed by a `CMP` write of
  0x2222. Expected response: `KEY` reads 0 after each key write and the `CMP` write is dropped,
  `CMP` still reading 0x1000.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` register. Kind: a `CMP` write of 0x4444 without a key
  after the unlock has been spent. Expected response: the write is dropped and `CMP` still reads
  0x3333. Before it, write `KEY` 0x51F15E twice, read `KEY` for printing, write `CMP` 0x3333 and
  read it back, and require `KEY` 0.
. Write `KEY`, require `KEY` 1, read `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `CMP`, `SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT_HI`, require
  `KEY` 1, write `CMP` 0x1000 and require `KEY` 0.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` register. Kind: a `CMP` write of 0x4321 without a key
  after a keyed `CMP` write of 0x1234. Expected response: `KEY` reads 0 after the keyed write and
  the unkeyed write is dropped, `CMP` still reading 0x1234.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` register. Kind: a `CMP` write of 0x2468 without a key
  after each of a keyed `CTRL` 0x2, `COUNT` 0x0010_0000 and `FEED` 0x0D09F00D write. Expected
  response: `KEY` reads 0 after each register write and the `CMP` write is dropped, `CMP` still
  reading 0x1234.
. Write `KEY` and `SCALED_COUNT` 0x1234, read `SCALED_COUNT`, `CTRL` (requiring 0x2), `COUNT` and
  `KEY` (requiring 0) and compare `SCALED_COUNT` against 0x1234 and the shifted `COUNT`.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL`, `COUNT` and `CMP` registers. Kind: writes of `CTRL`
  0x330, `COUNT` 0x0020_0000 and `CMP` 0x1357 with the watchdog locked. Expected response: `CTRL`
  reads 0x2, `CMP` reads 0x1234, `COUNT` is not above the earlier read plus twice A and `KEY`
  reads 0. Read `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `CMP` and `KEY` after the writes and compare `COUNT` with the earlier
  read plus twice A.
. Write `KEY` and `COUNT` 0x0030_0000, then write 0x0051_F15E_0D09_F00D as one 8-byte write at
  `FEED`, require `KEY` 0 and read `COUNT`; write `KEY` again, repeat the 8-byte write, require
  `KEY` 0 and read `COUNT`; require every access reachable, the step stamps and checker lines in
  order, and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-KEY-NONMAGIC` |With the watchdog locked, `KEY` writes of 0x0051_F15F, 0xFFFF_FFFF and
  0x0000_0000 each leave `KEY` at 0 and the following `CMP` write dropped, 3 of 3 values
|`CHK-WDT-KEY-REPEATED-MAGIC` |After two magic writes the next register write is accepted (`CMP`
  reads 0x3333), `KEY` then reads 0 and a further write without a key is dropped; the `KEY` value
  between the magic writes and the register write is printed
|`CHK-WDT-KEY-READ-UNLOCKED` |With the watchdog unlocked, reads of `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `CMP`,
  `SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT_HI` leave `KEY` reading 1 before and after them, and the next `CMP`
  write is accepted and leaves `KEY` at 0
|`CHK-WDT-RELOCK-CMP` |After `KEY` and a `CMP` write `KEY` reads 0 and a second `CMP` write without
  a key leaves `CMP` at the first written value 0x1234
|`CHK-WDT-RELOCK-REGISTERS` |After `KEY` and a 32-bit write to each of `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `FEED` and
  `SCALED_COUNT`, `KEY` reads 0 and a `CMP` write without a key is dropped, and `SCALED_COUNT`
  neither reads 0x1234 nor exceeds the shifted `COUNT`, 4 of 4 registers
|`CHK-WDT-LOCKED-WRITE-DROP` |Locked writes to `CTRL`, `COUNT` and `CMP` change nothing: `CTRL`
  reads 0x2, `CMP` reads 0x1234, `COUNT` is within twice the allowance of its previous read and
  `KEY` reads 0
|`CHK-WDT-WIDE-WRITE-LOCK` |After the 64-bit write at `FEED` carrying the magic in the `KEY` half,
  from the locked and from the unlocked state, `KEY` reads 0; `COUNT` after each write is printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S9 strictly increasing and the seven checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its own step, with every access reachable
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The `KEY` read between
repeated magic writes and the `COUNT` values after the 64-bit writes are reported only.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The `KEY` value read between the second magic write and the register write is
printed, because the specification does not state whether it reads 1. `COUNT` after each 64-bit
write at `FEED` is printed to show whether the `FEED` half acted, because the ordering inside the
write is not stated by the specification.

'''''

[[sec-343-smc_wdt_register_map_test]]
===== 343 `smc_wdt_register_map_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_register_map_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (watchdog blocks `SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*` to
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE3_WDT_*`: `KEY`, `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `COUNT_HI`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `FEED`,
`CMP`; 4-byte accesses)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: The four per-core watchdog apertures decode their registers at the
right offsets, stay independent of each other, and the CTRL fields and the CMP width read back as
`wdt.rdl` defines them.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, `CTRL`): `CTRL` reads 0 on each of the four cores
  before any write.
* Offset decode (`wdt.rdl`, address map): on each core `CTRL` written 0x2 reads back 0x2; `COUNT`
  written 0x0001_0000 with both enables clear reads at or above that value, and `SCALED_COUNT` at
  offset 0x10 lies between the two `COUNT` reads shifted right by 2 (inside the 16-bit
  `SCALED_COUNT` field); a `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D makes the next `COUNT` read fall below
  0x0001_0000; `COUNT_HI` and `KEY` read 0. How `COUNT` behaves with both enables clear is not stated by the specification, and the bracket holds for either.
* Aperture isolation (`hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc`, Operation; `wdt.rdl`, `KEY`): a `CMP` write of
  0x1111 * (N + 1) to core N changes core N only, so the four `CMP` registers read that value for
  cores up to N and 0x1000 above. For each of the 12 ordered pairs of cores N and M, after unlocking
  N, `KEY` of M reads 0, a `CMP` write of 0x5555 to M is dropped and M's `CMP` reads its earlier
  value, `KEY` of N reads 1, and the unlock is spent on a `CMP` write of N that reads back.
* Interleave (`watchdog.adoc`, Register Access) on core pairs (0, 3) and (1, 2): `KEY` of A, `KEY`
  of B, `CMP` of A 0x2AAA and `CMP` of B 0x2BBB read back; then `KEY` of A, a `CMP` write of B
  0x5555 dropped and `CMP` of A 0x2CCC reads back with B unchanged.
* CTRL fields (`wdt.rdl`, `CTRL`): on core 0 with `CMP` 0xFFFF, each of `wdogscale` 0 to 15,
  `wdogrsten` (0x100), `wdogzerocmp` (0x200), `wdogenalways` (0x1000) and `wdogcoreawake` (0x2000)
  written alone reads back exactly, 20 cells. `wdogenalways` and `wdogcoreawake` are cleared again
  after their read.
* Reserved bits: a `CTRL` write of 0xEFFF_CCF0 (reserved bits 7:4, 11:10, 27:14 and 31:29 only)
  reads back 0.
* Locked and all-ones write: an all-ones `CTRL` write while locked reads back 0; after `KEY` it
  reads 0x0000_330F with bit 28 masked (`wdogscale` 0xF, `wdogrsten`, `wdogzerocmp`, `wdogenalways`,
  `wdogcoreawake`). Bit 28 (`wdogip0`) is printed and not compared (its value after an all-ones
  write is not stated by the specification).
* `CMP` width (`wdt.rdl`, `CMP.wdogcmp0[15:0]`): a 32-bit `CMP` write of 0xDEAD_A5A5 reads back
  0x0000_A5A5.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CTRL` of cores 0 to 3 and require 0.
. For each core in turn write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0x2 and read it back; `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x0001_0000
  and read `COUNT`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `COUNT`; compare the bracket; `KEY` then `FEED` and require the
  next `COUNT` below 0x0001_0000; read `COUNT_HI` and `KEY` requiring 0; restore `CTRL` and `COUNT`
  to 0.
. For N = 0 to 3 write `KEY` then `CMP` 0x1111 * (N + 1) to core N and read the four `CMP` registers
  after each write, requiring the written values for cores up to N and the previous values above.
. Error injection. Point: the `CMP` register of core M. Kind: a `CMP` write of 0x5555 to core M
  while only core N is unlocked, for each of the 12 ordered pairs. Expected response: `KEY` of M
  reads 0, the write is dropped and M's `CMP` reads its earlier value. Then read `KEY` of N (1),
  write `CMP` of N and read it back.
. Error injection. Point: the `CMP` register of core B in pairs (0, 3) and (1, 2). Kind: a `CMP`
  write of B 0x5555 after `KEY` of A alone, inside the interleaved key and write sequences. Expected
  response: the write to B is dropped while `CMP` of A 0x2CCC reads back with B unchanged. Run the
  two interleaved sequences and read both `CMP` registers after each.
. On core 0 write `CMP` 0xFFFF, then for each of the 20 field cells write `KEY` and `CTRL` alone,
  read `CTRL` requiring the same value, and clear `wdogenalways` and `wdogcoreawake` afterwards;
  restore `CMP` 0x1000.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL` register. Kind: a keyed `CTRL` write of 0xEFFF_CCF0, the
  reserved bits 7:4, 11:10, 27:14 and 31:29 only. Expected response: `CTRL` reads back 0.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CTRL` register. Kind: an all-ones `CTRL` write while locked,
  then an all-ones `CTRL` write after `KEY`. Expected response: the locked write reads back 0 and
  the keyed write reads 0x0000_330F under the bit 28 mask. Restore `CTRL` 0.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` register. Kind: a keyed 32-bit `CMP` write of
  0xDEAD_A5A5, wider than the 16-bit field. Expected response: `CMP` reads back 0x0000_A5A5. Restore
  `CMP` 0x1000 and require it; require every access reachable, the step stamps and checker lines in
  order, and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-CTRL-RESET` |`CTRL` reads 0 on each of the four cores before any write (bench limit:
  2-state zero init, a missing reset also reads 0)
|`CHK-WDT-OFFSET-DECODE` |On each of the four cores `CTRL` at 0x00, `COUNT` at 0x08, `SCALED_COUNT`
  at 0x10 (within its `COUNT` bracket shifted right by 2), `FEED` at 0x18 (`COUNT` below 0x0001_0000
  afterwards), `COUNT_HI` at 0x0C (0) and `KEY` at 0x1C (0) answer as `wdt.rdl` defines them
|`CHK-WDT-APERTURE-ISOLATION` |A `CMP` write to core N changes core N only, and after unlocking core
  N the `KEY` of every other core reads 0 and a `CMP` write to it is dropped, 12 of 12 ordered pairs
|`CHK-WDT-APERTURE-INTERLEAVE` |After `KEY` of A and B both `CMP` registers read the values written
  to them, and after `KEY` of A alone a write to B is dropped while A's write reads back, 2 of 2
  pairs
|`CHK-WDT-CTRL-FIELD-READBACK` |Each of `wdogscale` 0 to 15, `wdogrsten`, `wdogzerocmp`,
  `wdogenalways` and `wdogcoreawake` written alone reads back exactly, 20 of 20 cells
|`CHK-WDT-CTRL-RESERVED` |A `CTRL` write of 0xEFFF_CCF0 leaves `CTRL` reading 0
|`CHK-WDT-CTRL-LOCKED-WRITE` |An all-ones `CTRL` write while locked reads back 0, and after `KEY` it
  reads 0x0000_330F with bit 28 masked; bit 28 is printed and not compared
|`CHK-WDT-CMP-WIDE-WRITE` |A 32-bit `CMP` write of 0xDEAD_A5A5 reads back 0x0000_A5A5
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S9 strictly increasing and the eight checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its own step, with every access reachable
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nine checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. Bit 28 after the all-ones
write is reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Bit 28 (`wdogip0`) after the all-ones `CTRL` write is printed and not compared,
because its value is not stated by the specification. How `COUNT` behaves with both enables clear
is not stated by the specification, so the `SCALED_COUNT` bracket accepts either. The `CTRL` reset
read of 0 is bench-limited: a 2-state zero init also reads 0.

'''''

[[sec-344-smc_wdt_scale_zerocmp_test]]
===== 344 `smc_wdt_scale_zerocmp_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_scale_zerocmp_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (core 0 watchdog block
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*`: `KEY`, `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `CMP`; 4-byte accesses);
`CTRL` bit 28 (`wdogip0`) read back

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: `SCALED_COUNT` follows `COUNT` shifted right by `CTRL.wdogscale`, and
with `wdogzerocmp` set `COUNT` falls back toward 0 at the compare while with it clear `COUNT` keeps
rising.

*Test Coverage*:

* Shift relation held (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, `SCALED_COUNT`;
  `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, watchdog): with both enables clear and `COUNT` 0x5A5A,
  for each `wdogscale` 0 to 15 `SCALED_COUNT` lies between the `COUNT` reads taken just before and
  after it, each shifted right by the scale (16 of 16 scales).
* Small counts: with `COUNT` written 2^s - 1 for s = 1 to 15 and `wdogscale` s, `SCALED_COUNT` must
  lie between the `COUNT` reads taken just before and after it, each shifted right by s (15 of 15),
  so it reads 0 when `COUNT` holds.
* Wide counts: `SCALED_COUNT` after `COUNT` 0x0001_2345 at scale 0 and `COUNT` 0x0002_4690 at scale
  1 is printed next to `COUNT` shifted by the scale. The field is 16 bits wide (`wdt.rdl`,
  `wdogs[15:0]`) and the specification does not state whether a larger value truncates or
  saturates, so nothing is compared.
* Running counter: with `CMP` 0xFFFF, `wdogenalways` set and `COUNT` running from 0x0008_0000, after
  `wdogscale` changes to 4 `SCALED_COUNT` lies between the two bracketing `COUNT` reads shifted
  right by 4; every bracket value in the test stays below 0x10000 by construction.
* `wdogzerocmp` set (`wdt.rdl`, `CTRL.wdogzerocmp`; `smc-programming.adoc`, watchdog): with `CMP`
  0x40, `COUNT` 0 and scale 0, 16 consecutive `COUNT` reads contain a read below its predecessor and
  `CTRL` bit 28 reads 1 afterwards; with `CMP` 4 and scale 3 the same holds. The maximum read
  against `CMP` shifted by the scale is printed (the count value at the clear is not stated by the specification).
* `wdogzerocmp` clear: with `wdogenalways` set, `CMP` 0x40 and `COUNT` 0, 16 consecutive reads
  strictly increase and the last exceeds 0x40.
* `CMP` 0: after `CMP` 0xFFFF, `COUNT` 0 and `wdogenalways` set, a keyed `CTRL` write with bit 28
  low leaves `CTRL` bit 28 at 0; then with `CMP` 0 and `wdogzerocmp` set, bit 28 reads 1 and the
  next 8 `COUNT` reads are printed.
* Setting `wdogzerocmp` while `COUNT` is already above 0x100 and `CMP` is 0x40 makes a read within
  the next 8 fall below its predecessor.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0 and `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x5A5A; for scale 0 to 15 write `KEY` then `CTRL`
  with the scale, read `COUNT`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `COUNT` and compare the bracket.
. For s = 1 to 15 write `COUNT` 2^s - 1 and `CTRL` s (each after `KEY`), read `COUNT`,
  `SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT` and compare the bracket.
. Write `COUNT` 0x0001_2345 with `CTRL` 0 and `COUNT` 0x0002_4690 with `CTRL` 1, reading
  `SCALED_COUNT` after each, and print both.
. Write `CMP` 0xFFFF, `COUNT` 0x0008_0000, `CTRL` 0x1000 then 0x1004, read `COUNT`, `SCALED_COUNT`,
  `COUNT` and compare the bracket shifted by 4.
. Write `CMP` 0x40, `COUNT` 0 and `CTRL` 0x1200, take 16 `COUNT` reads, require a drop and `CTRL`
  bit 28 at 1.
. Write `CTRL` 0x1000 and `COUNT` 0, take 16 `COUNT` reads, require strictly increasing and the last
  above 0x40.
. Write `CMP` 0xFFFF, `COUNT` 0 and `CTRL` 0x1000, require bit 28 at 0; write `CMP` 0 and `CTRL`
  0x1200, take 8 `COUNT` reads, require bit 28 at 1.
. Write `CMP` 4, `COUNT` 0 and `CTRL` 0x1203, take 16 `COUNT` reads, require a drop and `CTRL` bit
  28 at 1.
. Write `CMP` 0x40 and `CTRL` 0x1000, read `COUNT` until it exceeds 0x100 (bounded at 400 reads),
  write `CTRL` 0x1200, take 8 `COUNT` reads and require a drop; require step stamps and checker
  lines in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-SCALED-COUNT-WIDE` |Prints `SCALED_COUNT` after `COUNT` 0x0001_2345 at scale 0 and
  0x0002_4690 at scale 1 next to `COUNT` shifted by the scale without comparing; every read must
  complete
|`CHK-WDT-SCALED-COUNT-SHIFT` |`SCALED_COUNT` lies within the shifted `COUNT` bracket for scales 0
  to 15, lies within the shifted `COUNT` bracket for the 2^s - 1 writes, and lies within the bracket
  shifted by 4 on the running counter
|`CHK-WDT-ZEROCMP-OFF` |With `wdogzerocmp` clear and `wdogenalways` set, 16 consecutive `COUNT`
  reads strictly increase and the last exceeds `CMP` 0x40
|`CHK-WDT-ZEROCMP-CMP0` |After `CMP` 0xFFFF and a keyed clear write bit 28 reads 0, and with `CMP` 0
  and `wdogzerocmp` set bit 28 reads 1; the 8 `COUNT` reads are printed
|`CHK-WDT-ZEROCMP-CLEAR` |With `wdogzerocmp` set, 16 `COUNT` reads contain a drop and bit 28 reads 1
  for scale 0 with `CMP` 0x40 and for scale 3 with `CMP` 4, and setting `wdogzerocmp` on a counter
  already above 0x100 gives a drop within 8 reads; the maxima against `CMP` shifted by the scale are
  printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S9 strictly increasing and the five checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The wide `SCALED_COUNT`
values, the `COUNT` maxima and the reads after `CMP` 0 are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `SCALED_COUNT` after the wide `COUNT` writes is printed next to the shifted `COUNT`
and nothing is compared, because the specification does not state whether a value wider than the
16-bit field truncates or saturates. The maximum `COUNT` read against `CMP` shifted by the scale is
printed, because the count value at the `wdogzerocmp` clear is not stated by the specification. The
8 `COUNT` reads after `CMP` 0 are printed without a compare.

'''''

[[sec-345-smc_wdt_write_width_test]]
===== 345 `smc_wdt_write_width_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_write_width_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (core 0 watchdog block
`SMC_TOP_SMC_CLUSTER_CORE0_WDT_*`: `KEY`, `CTRL`, `COUNT`, `COUNT_HI`, `SCALED_COUNT`, `FEED`,
`CMP`; 4-byte reads, 4-byte writes and writes with explicit byte-enable masks through the strobed
write item)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `wdt`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Each watchdog register write takes effect only when its byte enables
cover the width `wdt.rdl` requires, narrow writes answer OKAY and change nothing, and CTRL accepts
single-byte writes.

*Test Coverage*:

* Rule under test (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl`, addrmap description;
  `hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc`, Register Access): a write takes effect only if its byte enables
  cover all four bytes of `COUNT`, `COUNT_HI`, `FEED` or `KEY`, or bytes 0 and 1 of `SCALED_COUNT`
  or `CMP`; each `CTRL` byte is written on its own; any other write returns OKAY and changes
  nothing, not even the lock.
* Narrow `COUNT`: after `KEY`, writes of 0x0000_00FF (mask 0b0001), 0x0000_FFFF (0b0011),
  0x00FF_FFFF (0b0111) and 0xFFFF_FF00 (0b1110) each answer OKAY, leave `COUNT` within a hold
  allowance A of 0x0010_0000 (A is the difference of two back-to-back `COUNT` reads taken with both
  enables clear) and leave `KEY` reading 1.
* Narrow `KEY` and `FEED`: `KEY` writes of 0x0051_F15E with masks 0b0011 and 0b0111 from the locked
  state leave `KEY` reading 0 and a following `CMP` write of 0x3333 dropped (`CMP` still 0x1000).
  With the watchdog unlocked a `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D with mask 0b0011 does not reset `COUNT`
  (it stays within A of its previous read and above 0x1000) and `KEY` still reads 1. What `FEED` and
  `KEY` read afterwards is not compared.
* Halfword `CMP` and `SCALED_COUNT`: `CMP` writes with masks 0b0001 (0x00FF) and 0b0010 (0xFF00) are
  dropped (`CMP` reads 0x1000, `KEY` reads 1), while mask 0b0011 (0xA5A5) reads back 0xA5A5 and
  `KEY` reads 0. After a new `KEY`, a `SCALED_COUNT` write with mask 0b0001 leaves `KEY` at 1 and
  with mask 0b0011 leaves `KEY` at 0. A `COUNT_HI` write of 0xFFFF_FFFF with mask 0b0011 answers
  OKAY and leaves `KEY` at 1.
* `CTRL` byte lanes: after `KEY`, single-byte writes with masks 0b0001 (0x05, `wdogscale` 5), 0b0010
  (0x03, `wdogrsten` and `wdogzerocmp`), 0b0010 (0x30, `wdogenalways` and `wdogcoreawake`, with
  `CMP` first raised to 0xFFFF and the fields cleared again afterwards) and 0b1000 (0x10, bit 28)
  each change only the fields of the written lane when `CTRL` is read with bit 28 masked. Two byte
  writes after one `KEY` leave `CTRL` at 0x0000_0003 (the second is dropped as the first re-locked),
  and byte writes each preceded by a `KEY` give 0x0000_0103.
* Narrow `COUNT` does not consume the unlock: after `KEY`, a byte-0 write of 0x7F is dropped with
  `KEY` still 1, and a following 32-bit `COUNT` write of 0x40 is accepted (`COUNT` within A of 0x40)
  with `KEY` reading 0.
* Zero strobe: after `KEY`, a `CMP` write of 0x5555 with byte-enable mask 0b0000 answers OKAY,
  leaves `CMP` at 0x1000 and `KEY` at 1.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `KEY` then `CTRL` 0 with both enables clear, take two back-to-back `COUNT` reads to fix A,
  write `KEY` then `COUNT` 0x0010_0000.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `COUNT` register. Kind: after `KEY`, the four narrow `COUNT`
  writes 0x0000_00FF (mask 0b0001), 0x0000_FFFF (0b0011), 0x00FF_FFFF (0b0111) and 0xFFFF_FF00
  (0b1110) in turn. Expected response: each answers OKAY, `COUNT` stays within A of 0x0010_0000
  and `KEY` reads 1 after each.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `KEY` register. Kind: `KEY` writes of 0x0051_F15E with masks
  0b0011 and 0b0111 from the locked state, each followed by a `CMP` write of 0x3333. Expected
  response: `KEY` reads 0 and the `CMP` write is dropped, `CMP` still reading 0x1000. Write `COUNT`
  0x0010_0000 to re-lock and require `KEY` 0 first.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `FEED` register. Kind: a `FEED` write of 0x0D09F00D with mask
  0b0011 while unlocked. Expected response: `COUNT` is not reset, staying within A of the previous
  read and above 0x1000, and `KEY` still reads 1. Write `KEY` and read `COUNT` first.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` and `SCALED_COUNT` registers. Kind: `CMP` writes with the
  single-byte masks 0b0001 (0x00FF) and 0b0010 (0xFF00), then, after the halfword `CMP` write and a
  new `KEY`, a `SCALED_COUNT` write with mask 0b0001. Expected response: the `CMP` byte writes are
  dropped with `CMP` 0x1000 and `KEY` 1 after each, and the `SCALED_COUNT` byte write leaves `KEY`
  at 1. Between them write `CMP` 0xA5A5 with mask 0b0011 requiring `CMP` 0xA5A5 and `KEY` 0; after
  the byte write, write `SCALED_COUNT` with mask 0b0011 requiring `KEY` 0.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `COUNT_HI` register. Kind: after `KEY`, a `COUNT_HI` write of
  0xFFFF_FFFF with mask 0b0011. Expected response: the write answers OKAY and `KEY` still reads 1.
. Read `CTRL`; for the four lane writes write `KEY` (and for the third also `CMP` 0xFFFF), write the
  byte, read `CTRL` with bit 28 masked and require only that lane to differ, clearing lane 1
  afterwards; restore `CMP`, zero `COUNT` and clear bit 28.
. Write `KEY`, `CTRL` byte 0 (0x03) and byte 1 (0x01) and require `CTRL` 0x0000_0003; write `KEY`,
  byte 0, `KEY`, byte 1 and require 0x0000_0103; restore `CTRL` 0.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `COUNT` register. Kind: after `KEY`, a byte-0 write of `COUNT`
  0x7F. Expected response: the write is dropped with `KEY` still 1 and the unlock is not consumed; a
  following 32-bit `COUNT` write of 0x40 is accepted with `COUNT` within A of 0x40 and `KEY` 0. Make
  the 32-bit write and read `COUNT` and `KEY`.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 `CMP` register. Kind: after `KEY`, a `CMP` write of 0x5555 with
  byte-enable mask 0b0000. Expected response: the write answers OKAY, `CMP` stays 0x1000 and `KEY`
  reads 1. Require step stamps and checker lines in order and print the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-NARROW-KEY-FEED` |Narrow `KEY` writes carrying the magic low bytes (2 masks) leave `KEY`
  at 0 and the following `CMP` write dropped, and a narrow `FEED` write while unlocked does not
  reset `COUNT` and leaves `KEY` at 1
|`CHK-WDT-HALFWORD-CMP-SCALED` |`CMP` single-byte writes leave `CMP` at 0x1000 with `KEY` 1 and the
  halfword write reads back 0xA5A5 with `KEY` 0; a `SCALED_COUNT` byte write leaves `KEY` at 1 and a
  halfword write locks it; a narrow `COUNT_HI` write is dropped without locking
|`CHK-WDT-CTRL-BYTELANES` |A single-byte write to each of the four `CTRL` lanes changes only the
  fields in that lane, and each effective byte write re-locks: `CTRL` reads 0x3 after `KEY`, byte 0,
  byte 1, and 0x103 after `KEY`, byte 0, `KEY`, byte 1
|`CHK-WDT-NARROW-COUNT` |Every narrow `COUNT` write (4 masks) answers OKAY, leaves `COUNT` within A
  of 0x0010_0000 and `KEY` at 1, and a narrow write between `KEY` and a 32-bit write does not
  consume the unlock so the 32-bit write is accepted and `KEY` reads 0
|`CHK-WDT-ZERO-STROBE` |A `CMP` write with byte-enable mask 0 answers OKAY, leaves `CMP` at 0x1000
  and `KEY` at 1
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence: step stamps S1 to S10 strictly increasing and the five checker lines
  printed in step order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds. The `FEED`, `KEY`,
`SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT_HI` read values after narrow writes are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: What `FEED`, `KEY`, `SCALED_COUNT` and `COUNT_HI` read after the narrow writes is
reported only and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-346-smc_accel_egress_attrs_test]]
===== 346 `smc_accel_egress_attrs_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_accel_egress_attrs_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP); the TB SYS_OUT
output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`); the packed SYS_OUT request
`tb_top.output_axi_req` sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise, cross-checked against
`tb_output_axi_araddr` / `tb_output_axi_awaddr` and gated by `tb_output_axi_arready` /
`tb_output_axi_awready`; AR members ARBURST, ARCACHE, ARPROT, ARUSER and AW members AWBURST,
AWCACHE, AWPROT, AWUSER

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: DMA and zeroer egress requests are INCR with constant attributes.

*Test Coverage*:

* The DMA frontend requests incrementing AXI bursts and sets the cache attribute to modifiable
  (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies). The leaf samples the DMA read (AR) and DMA write
  (AW) requests and the zeroer write (AW) requests on the SYS_OUT request, keeping only handshakes
  whose address lies inside the leaf's own source, destination and zeroer buffers.
* ARBURST and AWBURST of every kept DMA AR, DMA AW and zeroer AW request must be INCR (1), and each
  of the three request kinds must have been sampled at least once.
* Bit 1 (modifiable) of ARCACHE and AWCACHE must be set on every kept DMA request with the alias
  remap at its reset state (`dma.adoc`; `fabric.adoc`, Alias Remapping). The full ARCACHE and
  AWCACHE encodings are measured and printed, not compared; the alias-hit replacement of AxCACHE is
  not driven. The specification does not state the full encoding.
* ARPROT, AWPROT and AxUSER of the DMA requests and of the zeroer requests are each required to be
  one constant value over the run (`fabric.adoc`, Non-Secure Bit Filtering and the source ID by
  traffic path). AxUSER must also be the same on the DMA read, DMA write and zeroer write requests,
  as one source ID covers the direct path they all take. The numeric values are measured and
  printed, not compared against an expected value; the specification does not state them.
* The packed request layout is cross-checked on every sample: the address slice must equal the
  exported address probe, and the width of `output_axi_req` must match the layout, so a wrong member
  offset fails instead of reading a neighbouring field.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `tb_top` to expose `output_axi_req` at the layout width and the SYS_OUT responder to be
  bound; program the inbound filter window and the outbound filter window to pass all.
. Seed the DMA source with a poison word per eight bytes, clear the DMA destination, poison the
  zeroer region, and start the SYS_OUT sampler with three windows: DMA AR, DMA AW and zeroer AW.
. Run the DMA copy: enable `CONFIG.ENABLED_ND`, write source, destination, length 256, strides 0 and
  one repetition, read `DONE_0` as the baseline, read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, poll `DONE_0` until it
  moves past the baseline, require it to equal the launched id and require every destination word to
  equal its seed.
. Run the zeroer job: write `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` (256), write `CTRL_STATUS` with the start bit,
  poll `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` to leave and then return to its idle level, require every region word to
  read 0, and clear `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR`.
. Stop the sampler, require at least one sample of each kind, and require ARBURST and AWBURST of
  every kept request to be INCR; record the INCR checker.
. Require bit 1 of ARCACHE and AWCACHE of every kept DMA request to be set and print the encodings
  seen; record the cache checker.
. Require ARPROT, AWPROT and AxUSER of each kept kind to be one value over the run and print the
  values; record the protection and user checker.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase in order and each checker line to follow its own
  compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ACCEL-EGRESS-INCR` |Every kept DMA AR, DMA AW and zeroer AW request on SYS_OUT carries burst
  type INCR (1), with at least one request of each kind sampled
|`CHK-ACCEL-EGRESS-CACHE` |Bit 1 of ARCACHE and of AWCACHE is set on every kept DMA request; the
  full encodings are measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-ACCEL-EGRESS-PROT-USER` |ARPROT, AWPROT and AxUSER of the DMA and of the zeroer requests are
  each constant over the run and AxUSER is the same on all three request kinds; the values are
  measured and printed without comparing them to an expected value
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The four step stamps are strictly increasing and each checker line was emitted after
  its own compare, so the sampler saw real traffic before any checker was logged
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: the DMA copy and the zeroer
job complete with the destination matching its seed and the region reading zero, every kept request
is INCR, bit 1 of the DMA AxCACHE is set, each protection and user member is constant, and AxUSER is the same on all three kinds. The cache
encodings and the protection and user values are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The full ARCACHE and AWCACHE encodings and the numeric ARPROT, AWPROT and AxUSER
values are measured and printed, not compared against an expected value, because the specification
does not state them. The alias-hit replacement of AxCACHE is not driven.

'''''

[[sec-347-smc_accel_window_decode_test]]
===== 347 `smc_accel_window_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_accel_window_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) with the AXI monitor's
expected-DECERR address set (`env.axi_monitor`); DMA register window at `BASE + 0x38000`, zeroer
register window at `BASE + 0x38200`; SMC_BASE_CONFIG `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`DMA_CG_EN`,
`ZEROER_CG_EN`) and `REGION_SIZE`; no bench signal or interrupt line is driven

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: DMA and zeroer windows decode alone, at their ends and past them.

*Test Coverage*:

* The DMA control aperture is `0xC003_8000` to `0xC003_81FF` and the zeroer aperture starts at
  `0xC003_8200` (`dma.adoc`, SMC DMA integration; `zeroer.adoc`, SMC Memory Zeroer Integration;
  `memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization). The leaf first clears `DMA_CG_EN` and `ZEROER_CG_EN`
  in `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and reads them back clear, reads `REGION_SIZE` at its reset value
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`, 0x100_0000) and saves the registers it will disturb.
* No aliasing: `DST_ADDRESS_LO` of the DMA and `DEST_ADDR` of the zeroer are each written with their
  own pattern in both write orders and must read back only their own pattern.
* First and last registers: the DMA `CONFIG` and `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` and the zeroer `DEST_ADDR` and
  `CTRL_STATUS` answer OKAY with their own content; the DMA word at `0xC003_81FC`, past the
  decoded extent of the DMA map, answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, and the read at `0xC003_8200`
  returns the zeroer `DEST_ADDR` pattern.
* Holes and past-extent words inside the apertures are read and written, with the windows taken
  from the generated memory map. The DMA holes inside its decoded extent (`0x44` and `0x4C` plus 8n
  for sixteen steps) must answer OKAY with 0xFFFFFFFF on reads and OKAY on writes, as the map gives
  for a hole. The DMA words past the decoded extent (`0x138` to `0x1FC`) and every eight-byte
  zeroer word past its decoded extent (`0x18` to `0xF8`, the zeroer aperture being 256 bytes) must
  answer DECERR on reads and writes, the DMA reads carrying 0xBADCAB1E and the low word of the
  zeroer reads carrying 0xBADCAB1E, as the map gives for a past-extent access.
* Neighbours: a read just below the DMA window and a read and a write at `0xC003_8300`, above the
  zeroer window, answer DECERR with data 0xBADCAB1E on the reads (`memmap.adoc`, Address Space
  Organization).
* `REGION_SIZE`: with the size reduced to 0x2_0000, below the end of both apertures, both windows
  must answer DECERR on reads and writes (the read data is measured and printed, not compared),
  and with the reset value restored both must again return the patterns written before the
  reduction, so the writes during the reduction did not land (`memmap.adoc`: a unit is reached only
  while its whole aperture lies below `BASE + REGION_SIZE`).
* Writes to the read-only `STATUS_0`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0` and `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` are issued and
  their response and the register value before and after are measured and printed without comparing
  them; `NEXT_ID_0` is written and never read.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, clear `DMA_CG_EN` and `ZEROER_CG_EN` and read them back clear,
  read `REGION_SIZE` and require its reset value, and save `REGION_SIZE`, DMA `CONFIG`,
  `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI`, `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and the zeroer `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` (the saved `SIZE`
  must be 0).
. Write a DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO` pattern and a zeroer `DEST_ADDR` pattern DMA first, read both back
  against their own pattern, then repeat with the zeroer written first and different patterns.
. Error injection. Point: the DMA word at `0xC003_81FC`, past the decoded extent of the DMA map.
  Kind: a read past the extent. Expected response: DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E. Before it, write DMA
  `CONFIG` with 0x5A5 and `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` with 0x123456 and read them back; read zeroer
  `DEST_ADDR` against its pattern, zeroer `CTRL_STATUS` against 0, and `DST_ADDRESS_LO` against its
  pattern; after it read the zeroer base `0xC003_8200` against its pattern; restore the four saved
  registers.
. Error injection. Point: every DMA hole word and past-extent word (four bytes) and every zeroer
  past-extent word (eight bytes). Kind: a read and a write of 0 to each, the past-extent addresses
  first marked as expected DECERR for the monitor. Expected response: the response and read data
  the generated map gives, OKAY with 0xFFFFFFFF on hole reads and OKAY on hole writes, DECERR on
  past-extent reads and writes with 0xBADCAB1E on the read data. Record the runs.
. Error injection. Point: the addresses `0xC003_7FFC`, just below the DMA window, and `0xC003_8300`,
  above the zeroer window. Kind: a read of each and a write of `0xC003_8300`. Expected response:
  DECERR on all three, with read data 0xBADCAB1E on both reads.
. Error injection. Point: the `REGION_SIZE` register. Kind: `REGION_SIZE` written 0x2_0000, below
  the end of both apertures, then a read and a write of each window. Expected response: DECERR on
  the reads and writes of both windows. Before it, write patterns to `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and zeroer
  `DEST_ADDR` and read `REGION_SIZE` back; after it restore `REGION_SIZE` and read it back, require
  both patterns to read back and restore the saved registers.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only `STATUS_0`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0` and zeroer `CTRL_STATUS`
  registers. Kind: a write to each. Expected response: each write completes without a hang; the
  responses and the register values before and after are printed and not compared. Read
  `STATUS_0`, `DONE_0` and zeroer `CTRL_STATUS` before and again after the writes.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase and the checker lines to appear in step order, each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-NO-ALIAS` |The DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and the zeroer `DEST_ADDR` each read back only
  their own pattern after being written in both orders, so neither window aliases onto the other
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-FIRST-LAST` |The first and last registers of both windows answer OKAY with their own
  content, and the DMA word at `0xC003_81FC` answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E while the read at
  `0xC003_8200` returns the zeroer `DEST_ADDR` pattern
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-HOLES` |Every DMA hole inside its decoded extent answers OKAY with 0xFFFFFFFF on
  reads and OKAY on writes, and every DMA and zeroer word past the decoded extent answers DECERR on
  reads and writes with 0xBADCAB1E on the read data, as the generated map gives
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-DECERR-NEIGHBOURS` |Reads just below the DMA window and just above the zeroer window
  answer DECERR with data 0xBADCAB1E, and a write above the zeroer window answers DECERR
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-REGION-SIZE` |With `REGION_SIZE` at 0x2_0000 both windows answer
  DECERR on reads and writes, the read data being measured and printed without comparing it; with
  the reset value restored both return the patterns written before the reduction
|`CHK-ACCEL-WIN-RO-WRITES` |Writes to `STATUS_0`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0` and `CTRL_STATUS` complete
  without a hang; their responses and the register values before and after are measured and printed
  without comparing them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven step stamps are strictly increasing and the six checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: windows do not alias,
first and last registers answer with their own content, hole and past-extent words answer as the
generated map gives, neighbour reads answer DECERR
with 0xBADCAB1E, the reduced `REGION_SIZE` answers DECERR on reads and writes with the read data
measured and printed without a compare, and the patterns survive the reduction. The read-only
write effects are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The read data returned while `REGION_SIZE` is reduced is measured and printed
without a compare. The responses to the writes of the read-only `STATUS_0`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`
and `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` and the register values before and after them are measured and printed
without comparing them; `NEXT_ID_0` is written and never read.

'''''

[[sec-348-smc_dma_2d_copy_test]]
===== 348 `smc_dma_2d_copy_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_2d_copy_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; passive probes `tb_top.tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`,
`tb_output_axi_araddr`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr` and
`tb_dma_busy` sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise; `u_output_axi_if.arlen`, `arsize`, `awlen`,
`awsize` required to exist; DMA registers `CONFIG`, `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`,
`SRC_STRIDE`, `DST_STRIDE`, `NUM_REPETITIONS`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0` and `STATUS_0`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.
