*Objective*: Two-dimensional copies land row by row for each stride and row count.

*Test Coverage*:

* A two-dimensional copy is a linear copy plus source and destination strides and a repetition
  count, the strides being independent address increments between row starts and `NUM_REPETITIONS`
  the number of rows including the first (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies and DMA
  register storage and effective field widths).
* Independent strides: five 24-byte rows with source stride 0x50 and destination stride 0x38 must
  arrive at the destination base plus n times 0x38, with the sentinel bytes between the rows and the
  source rows unchanged.
* Row counts: 1, 2, 3 and 16 repetitions must copy exactly that many 20-byte rows, the first
  included, and the destination of the following row must still hold the sentinel.
* Unaligned rows: four 13-byte rows from a source three bytes into a word to a destination five
  bytes into a word, stride 0x20, must arrive byte for byte with every byte between and around the
  rows unchanged.
* One command, one id: an eight-row command must take exactly one `NEXT_ID_0` read, `DONE_0` must
  equal the returned id on retirement and must have advanced by one over its baseline, not by eight
  (`dma.adoc`, Submission and Completion).
* Stride edges: zero source stride, zero destination stride, both zero, both strides 8 and an
  overlapping source and destination must each retire within the poll bound with `tb_dma_busy` low.
  Row n reads from the source plus n times the source stride and writes to the destination plus n
  times the destination stride (`dma.adoc`), so with zero source stride three destination rows must
  each hold the one source row, and with both strides zero the destination must hold the source
  row; both are compared exactly. The destination bytes of the other three cases depend on the row
  order and are measured and printed, not compared (the specification does not state the order).
* Stepping near 2^56: four 16-byte rows with source base 2^56 - 0x80 and destination base 2^56 -
  0x1C0, strides 0x80 and 0x100, must retire within the poll bound with at least one AR and one AW
  handshake observed; whether the row addresses wrap within 56 bits is measured and printed, not
  compared (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the exported SYS_OUT probes, `tb_dma_busy` and the four `u_output_axi_if` members to
  exist, program the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, start the AR and AW handshake
  sampler, read `DONE_0` as the baseline and wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Seed five source rows and fill the destination span with the sentinel, program a 24-byte, five-row
  job with source stride 0x50 and destination stride 0x38, read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch it (the
  returned id must be the retired id plus one), poll `DONE_0` to that id, and compare the whole
  destination span and the source rows.
. For 1, 2, 3 and 16 rows of 20 bytes with strides 0x40 and 0x30, run the same sequence, compare the
  destination span and require the next row's destination to hold only the sentinel.
. Run four 13-byte rows from an unaligned source and destination, stride 0x20, and compare the
  destination span byte for byte.
. Read `DONE_0` as the baseline, run an eight-row job, require exactly one `NEXT_ID_0` read,
  `DONE_0` equal to the returned id and advanced by one, and compare the image.
. For each of five stride cases (both strides 0, source stride 0 with destination stride 0x20,
  source stride 0x20 with destination stride 0, both strides 8, and both strides 16 with the
  destination 8 bytes above the source) write a pattern region, run the three-row 16-byte job, wait
  one cycle, require `tb_dma_busy` low, compare the destination of the two cases with a zero source
  stride exactly and print the source and destination bytes.
. Place source and destination rows below 2^56 so that later rows lie beyond it, run the four-row
  job, require AR and AW handshakes to have been seen, and print the addresses issued and the
  low-range destination bytes.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-2D-INDEP-STRIDES` |Every row n of the five-row copy lies at the destination base plus n
  times its own destination stride and equals its source row, with the bytes between the rows and
  the source rows unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-2D-ROW-COUNTS` |For 1, 2, 3 and 16 repetitions exactly that many rows are copied, the
  first included, and the destination of the next row still holds the sentinel
|`CHK-DMA-2D-UNALIGNED-ROWS` |Thirteen-byte rows from an unaligned source to an unaligned
  destination arrive byte for byte and the bytes between and around them are unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-2D-SINGLE-ID` |The eight-row command takes exactly one `NEXT_ID_0` read and one id, and
  `DONE_0` after retirement equals that id and is one above its baseline
|`CHK-DMA-2D-STRIDE-EDGES` |Each zero-stride and short-stride command retires within the poll bound
  with `tb_dma_busy` low; the destination of the both-zero and zero-source-stride cases equals the
  expected row image, and the destination bytes of the other cases are measured and printed
  without comparing them
|`CHK-DMA-2D-WRAP-2POW56` |The command whose rows pass 2^56 retires within the poll bound with AR
  and AW handshakes observed; the addresses issued and whether they wrap are measured and printed
  without comparing them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven step stamps are strictly increasing and the six checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: each row of the
independent-stride, row-count, unaligned and single-id jobs matches its source, the sentinel and
source bytes are unchanged, and every job retires with its id. The destination bytes of the zero-destination-stride,
short-stride and overlap cases and the 2^56 address behaviour are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The destination bytes of the zero-destination-stride, short-stride and overlap
cases are measured and printed, not compared, because the specification does not state the row
order. Whether the row addresses of the command near 2^56 wrap within 56 bits is measured and
printed, not compared, because the specification does not state the value.

'''''

[[sec-349-smc_dma_backpressure_breadth_test]]
===== 349 `smc_dma_backpressure_breadth_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_backpressure_breadth_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) with its AR, AW and W channel stall
controls, its read and write response delay controls and its backdoor memory; TB input pin
`tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` driven 0 and 1 to hold the R and B responses; passive probes
`tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`,
`tb_output_axi_wvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wready`, `tb_output_axi_bvalid`, `tb_output_axi_bready` and
`u_output_axi_if.rvalid`, `rready`, `rlast` sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise; DMA registers
`CONFIG`, `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, `SRC_STRIDE`, `DST_STRIDE`, `NUM_REPETITIONS`,
`NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`, `STATUS_0` (bit 9)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only timing: the stall lengths of the held
SYS_OUT channels and the AR, AW, W and R delays; the copies must land exact whatever the timing.

*Objective*: DMA copies stay exact under stalled and held SYS_OUT channels.

*Test Coverage*:

* The backend performs the AXI reads and writes with an in-flight limit of 32 (`dma.adoc`, SMC DMA
  elaboration settings) and handles alignment and burst splitting (`dma.adoc`, Linear and
  Two-Dimensional Copies), so a responder that stalls, delays and holds its channels must change the
  timing of a copy and nothing else.
* Random stalls: six copies of 8, 40, 96, 200, 512 and 1000 bytes each run with a random AW stall
  and W stall, a random AR hold, and random R and B response delays of one to eight cycles. The seed
  is printed. Every copy must deliver its exact payload with `DONE_0` equal to its id, and every
  stall and delay kind must have been applied at least once.
* Outstanding cap: with the R and B responses held, a 128-row copy of 8-byte rows must reach an
  outstanding AR count that is stable for 256 rises and no higher than 32, AR issue must resume
  after the release and the copy must complete exactly. The outstanding AW maximum with only B
  delayed by 24 cycles is measured and printed, not compared (the specification does not state the value).
* Long stall: with R and B held for 4096 rises after launch, every `DONE_0` read must equal the
  baseline id, so the new id stays unretired, and `STATUS_0` bit 9, which `dma.adoc` (DMA status and
  notification) gives as zero, must read 0; after the release `DONE_0` must reach the new id.
* Realignment: a 200-byte copy from a source three bytes into a word to a destination five bytes
  into a word, with a one to three cycle hold before every R beat, must deliver its exact payload
  with the eight guard bytes either side unchanged and at least 25 hold episodes.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the nine `tb_top` probes and the three `u_output_axi_if` members to exist, program the
  inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, seed the random generator from `RANDOM_SEED` and
  print the seed, start the handshake tally, read `DONE_0` as the baseline and wait two `clk_smc_i`
  cycles.
. For each of the six lengths, draw the stalls, apply the AW and W stalls and the response delays,
  seed the source with a pattern, the destination with poison and the guard bytes, program a one-row
  job, hold the AR channel, read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, wait until an ARVALID without ARREADY has
  been seen and the drawn number of rises has passed, release the AR hold, poll `DONE_0` to the id
  and compare the destination, the guards and the source. Require that every stall and delay kind
  was applied.
. Hold R and B with `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`, launch the 128-row job, wait for the outstanding AR
  count to stay unchanged for 256 rises, require it and the running maximum not to exceed 32,
  release the hold, require further ARs to issue, poll `DONE_0` and compare the image. Then delay
  the B responses by 24 cycles on a second 128-row job, complete it, compare its image and print the
  outstanding AW maximum.
. Hold R and B, launch a 64-byte copy and read `DONE_0` and `STATUS_0` repeatedly until 4096
  `clk_smc_i` rises have passed, requiring `DONE_0` to equal the baseline and `STATUS_0` bit 9 to be
  0 on every read; release the hold, poll `DONE_0` to the new id and compare the destination.
. Start a process that holds the responses for one to three cycles whenever an R beat is valid, run
  the 200-byte unaligned copy, stop the process, require at least 25 hold episodes and compare the
  destination, the guard bytes and the source.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-BP-RANDOM` |All six copies deliver their exact payload with `DONE_0` equal to each id, the
  seed is printed, and the AR, AW and W stall counts and the R and B delay counts are each above 0
|`CHK-DMA-BP-OUTSTANDING-CAP` |With R and B held the outstanding AR count settles at a plateau
  stable for 256 rises that never exceeds 32, AR issue resumes after the release and the copy
  completes exactly; the plateau value and the outstanding AW maximum under a B delay are measured
  and printed without comparing the AW maximum
|`CHK-DMA-BP-LONG-STALL` |Throughout the 4096-rise hold every `DONE_0` read equals the baseline and
  `STATUS_0` bit 9 is 0, and after the release `DONE_0` reaches the new id and the destination
  matches
|`CHK-DMA-BP-REALIGN` |The unaligned 200-byte copy with a delay before every R beat delivers its
  exact payload with the guard bytes either side and the source unchanged
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The five step stamps are strictly increasing and the four checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every payload matches byte
for byte, every `DONE_0` poll reaches its id inside the poll bound, the outstanding AR count never
exceeds 32 and `DONE_0` never advances during the hold. The plateau value and the outstanding AW
maximum are reported. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The outstanding AW maximum with only B delayed by 24 cycles is measured and printed,
not compared, because the specification does not state the value. The outstanding AR plateau value
is reported next to its bound of 32.

'''''

[[sec-350-smc_dma_burst_shaping_test]]
===== 350 `smc_dma_burst_shaping_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_burst_shaping_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; TB input pin `tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` driven 0 and 1 to hold the R channel;
passive probes `tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`, `tb_output_axi_araddr`,
`tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr`, `tb_output_axi_rvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_rready` and `u_output_axi_if.arlen`, `arsize`, `awlen`, `awsize` sampled at every
`clk_smc_i` rise; DMA `CONFIG` bits `DECOUPLE_AW`, `DECOUPLE_RW`, `SRC_REDUCE_LEN`,
`DST_REDUCE_LEN`, `SRC_MAX_LLEN`, `DST_MAX_LLEN`, `ENABLED_ND`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: CONFIG burst bits shape AR and AW bursts of a 4 KiB copy.

*Test Coverage*:

* The `CONFIG` register description (`dma_ctrl.rdl`) gives `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` and `DST_REDUCE_LEN`
  clear as bursts of at most 256 beats that do not cross a 2 KiB-aligned boundary, set as bursts
  limited by `SRC_MAX_LLEN` and `DST_MAX_LLEN` as a base-2 logarithm of the beat count with no
  crossing of a 2^(n+3)-byte boundary, and the `MAX_LLEN` fields as ignored while their reduce bit
  is clear; `DECOUPLE_AW` clear holds each write address until the first read data beat returns.
  `dma.adoc` (Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies) points to `CONFIG` for these options.
* Reduction off: a 4 KiB copy whose source and destination each cross a 2 KiB boundary must deliver
  its exact payload with every AR and AW burst at most 256 beats and inside one 2 KiB block.
* Source limit: with `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` set, for each `SRC_MAX_LLEN` n from 0 to 7 every AR burst must
  have at most 2^n beats inside one 2^(n+3)-byte block, and the longest AR burst must have exactly
  2^n beats (single-beat bursts at n = 0).
* Destination limit: the same for `DST_REDUCE_LEN` and `DST_MAX_LLEN` on the AW bursts.
* Ignored and independent limits: with both reduce bits clear and both `MAX_LLEN` fields at 0,
  bursts must still reach 256 beats; with the reduce bit set on one side only, every burst of both
  directions must stay within the reduced cap of 2 beats and the AR and AW burst counts must be
  equal.
* AW after the first R beat: with `DECOUPLE_AW` clear and the R channel held for 256 cycles after
  the first AR, no AW handshake and no R beat may occur, and no AW burst may precede the first R
  beat after the release.
* AW before the first R beat: with `DECOUPLE_AW` set and R held, at least one AW handshake must
  occur and at least one AW burst must precede the first R beat.
* All bits: with `DECOUPLE_AW`, `DECOUPLE_RW`, both reduce bits set and both `MAX_LLEN` at 2, the
  copy must complete with its exact payload and every burst of both directions must have at most 4
  beats inside one 32-byte block. `CONFIG` is restored to 0 and read back.
* Every copy also compares the guard bytes either side of the destination and requires the AR and AW
  bursts to cover at least 4096 bytes each.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the nine `tb_top` probes and the four `u_output_axi_if` members to exist, wait for the
  fuse sense, release the R hold, program the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, start
  the burst sampler, read `DONE_0` as the baseline and wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Run the 4 KiB copy with `CONFIG` at `ENABLED_ND` only (both ends 1 KiB into a 2 KiB block): write
  and read back `CONFIG`, program source, destination, length 4096, strides 0 and one repetition,
  read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, poll `DONE_0` to the id, compare the destination and the guards, and
  check every AR and AW burst against the 256-beat and 2 KiB limits.
. For n from 0 to 7 run the copy with `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` and `SRC_MAX_LLEN` = n and check every AR
  burst against 2^n beats and a 2^(n+3)-byte block and the longest burst against exactly 2^n beats.
. For n from 0 to 7 run the copy with `DST_REDUCE_LEN` and `DST_MAX_LLEN` = n and check every AW
  burst the same way, including the longest AW burst being exactly 2^n beats.
. On 4 KiB-aligned buffers run three copies: both `MAX_LLEN` fields at 0 with reduction clear,
  `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` with `SRC_MAX_LLEN` 1, and `DST_REDUCE_LEN` with `DST_MAX_LLEN` 1; require the
  longest bursts of 256 beats for the first and the cap of 2 beats with equal AR and AW counts for
  the others.
. Run an aligned copy with `DECOUPLE_AW` clear, hold R after the launch until the first AR is seen,
  wait 256 cycles, then require no AW handshake and no R beat while held, release R, poll `DONE_0`,
  compare the destination and require no AW burst before the first R beat.
. Run an aligned copy with `DECOUPLE_AW` set, hold R until the first AR and then the first AW are
  seen, then require no R beat while held and at least one AW burst before the first R beat after
  the release.
. Run the copy with all four shaping bits set and both limits at 2, check the 4-beat and 32-byte
  limits, write `CONFIG` 0 and read it back.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-BURST-REDUCE-OFF` |With both reduce bits clear the unaligned 4 KiB copy delivers its exact
  payload and every AR and AW burst has at most 256 beats and stays inside one 2 KiB block
|`CHK-DMA-BURST-SRC-LLEN` |With `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` set, for each `SRC_MAX_LLEN` n from 0 to 7 the copy
  is exact and every AR burst has at most 2^n beats inside one 2^(n+3)-byte block, the longest
  being exactly 2^n beats
|`CHK-DMA-BURST-DST-LLEN` |With `DST_REDUCE_LEN` set, for each `DST_MAX_LLEN` n from 0 to 7 the copy
  is exact and every AW burst has at most 2^n beats inside one 2^(n+3)-byte block, the longest
  being exactly 2^n beats
|`CHK-DMA-BURST-IGNORED-INDEPENDENT` |A `MAX_LLEN` field of 0 with its reduce bit clear is ignored
  and bursts reach 256 beats, and with one reduce bit set every burst stays within the reduced 2
  beats with equal AR and AW burst counts; the copies run with `DECOUPLE_RW` clear, so read and
  write bursts are formed in lockstep (`dma_ctrl.rdl`, `DECOUPLE_RW`) and the cap applies to both
  directions
|`CHK-DMA-AW-AFTER-FIRST-R` |With `DECOUPLE_AW` clear and R held, no AW handshake and no R beat
  occurs while held, and no AW burst precedes the first R beat; the copy is exact after the release
|`CHK-DMA-AW-BEFORE-FIRST-R` |With `DECOUPLE_AW` set and R held, at least one AW handshake occurs
  with no R beat returned and at least one AW burst precedes the first R beat; the copy is exact
  after the release
|`CHK-DMA-BURST-ALL-BITS` |With all four shaping bits set and both limits at 2 the copy completes
  within the poll bound with its exact payload and every burst has at most 4 beats inside one
  32-byte block
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eight step stamps are strictly increasing and the seven checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every copy delivers its
4096 bytes exactly with the guard bytes unchanged and every `DONE_0` poll reaches its id, and every
AR and AW burst obeys the limit of its `CONFIG` mode. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-351-smc_dma_completion_status_test]]
===== 351 `smc_dma_completion_status_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_completion_status_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; TB input pin `tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` driven 0 and 1 to hold the R and B
responses; passive probes `tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`, `tb_output_axi_araddr`,
`tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr` sampled at every
`clk_smc_i` rise; DMA registers `DONE_0`, `STATUS_0` (bits [7:0], 8 and 9), `NEXT_ID_0`, `CONFIG`,
`NUM_REPETITIONS`, `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, `SRC_STRIDE`, `DST_STRIDE`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: DONE_0 and STATUS_0 report reset, idle, no-data and held; the busy indication is measured.

*Test Coverage*:

* The transfer-ID generator resets `DONE` to 1 and `NEXT_ID` to 2 (`dma.adoc`, Submission and
  Completion), so `DONE_0` must read 1 before any transfer and the first launched id must be 2.
* `STATUS_0[7:0]` is eight copies of frontend request readiness, `0xFF` meaning room to accept a
  command, and bit 9 is zero (`dma.adoc`, status and notification table): two idle reads must both
  have bits [7:0] equal to 0xFF, bit 9 clear, and be equal to each other.
* `STATUS_0` bit 8 is the midend activity indication (`dma.adoc`). It must read 0 at the two idle
  reads before the copy (a compare a bit stuck at 0 also passes). While an eight-row copy runs,
  bit 8 is sampled with its time since submission on every poll and the samples, the polls with
  bit 8 high and the transitions are printed; when and for how long it rises is measured, not
  compared (the specification does not state the value). The copy must still retire with its id,
  move its data and produce AR and AW handshakes.
* No-data commands: clearing `CONFIG.ENABLED_ND` forces the repetition count to zero, and a command
  with a zero repetition count also moves no data, yet each still retires its transfer id
  (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies; `dma_ctrl.rdl`, `CONFIG.ENABLED_ND`). For each,
  `NEXT_ID_0` must return the next id, `DONE_0` must reach it, no AR or AW handshake may occur
  during the command, and the destination must keep its poison; the preceding eight-row copy proves
  the tally counts real traffic.
* Polling in flight: with the R and B responses held after launch, six `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` reads
  must complete and every `DONE_0` read must equal the previous id, at least one AR must be issued
  while held, and after the release `DONE_0` must reach the new id and the data must match. Frontend
  readiness and a zero status do not indicate completion (`dma.adoc`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the seven `tb_top` probes to exist, release the R and B hold, program the inbound and
  outbound filter windows to pass all, start the AR and AW handshake sampler and wait two
  `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Read `DONE_0` and require 1.
. Read `STATUS_0` twice and require bits [7:0] to be 0xFF, bit 9 clear and the two reads equal.
. Seed an eight-row, 16-byte-row job (source stride 0x30, destination stride 0x28), program it, read
  `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, then read `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` in pairs, recording bit 8 and the time
  since submission, until `DONE_0` equals the id; read `STATUS_0` once more, compare the destination
  with the source rows and require AR and AW handshakes.
. Program the same job with `CONFIG` 0 (`ENABLED_ND` clear), launch it, poll `DONE_0` to the id,
  require no AR or AW handshake and the destination poison unchanged.
. Program the job with `ENABLED_ND` set and `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO` 0, launch it and check the same.
. Program a 64-byte one-row job, hold R and B with `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`, launch it, read
  `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` six times requiring `DONE_0` to equal the previous id, require an AR to
  have been issued, release the hold, poll `DONE_0` to the new id and compare the destination.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-DONE-RESET` |`DONE_0` reads 1 after reset and before any transfer
|`CHK-DMA-STATUS-IDLE` |Two idle `STATUS_0` reads are equal, have bits [7:0] equal to 0xFF and bit 9
  clear; bit 8 is printed
|`CHK-DMA-STATUS-BIT8` |`STATUS_0` bit 8 reads 0 at the idle reads before the eight-row copy; its
  samples and transitions during the copy are measured and printed without comparing them, and the
  copy retires its id with the destination equal to the source rows and AR and AW handshakes seen
|`CHK-DMA-NO-DATA-ND-CLEAR` |With `ENABLED_ND` clear the command returns the next id, `DONE_0`
  reaches it, no AR or AW handshake occurs and the destination keeps its poison
|`CHK-DMA-NO-DATA-REPS-ZERO` |With `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO` 0 the command returns the next id, `DONE_0`
  reaches it, no AR or AW handshake occurs and the destination keeps its poison
|`CHK-DMA-POLL-IN-FLIGHT` |With R and B held, six `STATUS_0` and `DONE_0` reads complete with
  `DONE_0` equal to the previous id and an AR issued; after the release `DONE_0` equals the new id
  and the destination equals the source
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven step stamps are strictly increasing and the six checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: `DONE_0` resets to 1, idle
`STATUS_0` bits [7:0] are 0xFF with bit 9 clear, both no-data commands retire their id with no bus
traffic and no byte moved, and `DONE_0` does not advance during the hold. The bit 8 timing is
reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: When and for how long `STATUS_0` bit 8 rises during the eight-row copy is measured
and printed, not compared, because the specification does not state the value.

'''''

[[sec-352-smc_dma_csr_config_test]]
===== 352 `smc_dma_csr_config_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_csr_config_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers and
the SMC_BASE_CONFIG `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`DMA_CG_EN`), `LOCAL_BASE` and `GLOBAL_BASE` registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; the thirteen shared DMA registers `CONFIG`, `DST_ADDRESS_LO/HI`, `SRC_ADDRESS_LO/HI`,
`LENGTH_LO/HI`, `DST_STRIDE_LO/HI`, `SRC_STRIDE_LO/HI`, `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO/HI`, plus `NEXT_ID_0`
and `DONE_0`; `CONFIG` bits [10:0] including `SRC_MAX_LLEN` [6:4] and `DST_MAX_LLEN` [9:7]; reserved
`CONFIG` bits [31:11]; no bench signal is driven

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: DMA descriptor registers and CONFIG hold, keep and alias their values.

*Test Coverage*:

* Software supplies one shared configuration through these registers and submits it by reading
  `NEXT_ID_0`; source, destination, length, strides, repetitions and `CONFIG` are shared by all
  software contexts with no lock register (`dma.adoc`, Stream and Register Ownership). Each register
  in `dma_ctrl.rdl` is a 32-bit data field and `CONFIG` defines bits [10:0].
* Own value: after all thirteen registers are written with distinct patterns (`CONFIG` with 0x5A5),
  each must read back only its own pattern, so no register aliases or shares storage with another.
* Full 32 bits of the high halves: each `_HI` register must read back all 32 bits written, including
  bits [31:24], although the effective address and length widths are narrower (`dma.adoc`, DMA
  register storage and effective field widths).
* `CONFIG` fields: writes of each of bits 0 to 10 alone, of `SRC_MAX_LLEN` 0 to 7 and of
  `DST_MAX_LLEN` 0 to 7 must read back exactly in bits [10:0]. A write of 0xFFFF_FDA5 (0x5A5 with
  the reserved bits [31:11] set) must read back with bits [31:11] equal to 0, since `dma_ctrl.rdl`
  defines `CONFIG` [10:0] only.
* Retention: a one-row linear copy and a two-row copy with strides 0x10 and 0x20 must each retire
  with `DONE_0` equal to the launched id and deliver their rows with the guard bytes either side
  unchanged, and afterwards all thirteen registers must still read the programmed values, so
  launching a copy does not consume or alter the configuration.
* Global alias: a pattern written to `LENGTH_LO` at its local address must read back at its address
  under `GLOBAL_BASE`, and a pattern written to `SRC_STRIDE_HI` under `GLOBAL_BASE` must read back
  at its local address (`memmap.adoc`: the fabric routes SMC resources identically through
  `LOCAL_BASE` or `GLOBAL_BASE`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense, clear `DMA_CG_EN` in `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and read it back clear, program
  the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, read `DONE_0` as the baseline and wait two
  `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Write a distinct pattern to each of the thirteen registers (`CONFIG` 0x5A5), then read all of them
  back and compare each with its own pattern.
. For each `_HI` register write a pattern with bits [31:24] set and read it back in full.
. Error injection. Point: the DMA `CONFIG` register. Kind: a write of 0xFFFF_FDA5, 0x5A5 with the
  reserved bits [31:11] set. Expected response: bits [31:11] of the read-back are 0. Before it,
  write `CONFIG` with each of bits 0 to 10 alone, each `SRC_MAX_LLEN` value 0 to 7 and each
  `DST_MAX_LLEN` value 0 to 7, reading back and comparing bits [10:0] each time.
. Run the linear copy and then the two-row copy: seed the rows and guard bytes, write all thirteen
  registers, read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, poll `DONE_0` to the id, compare the destination rows and
  the guards, and read all thirteen registers back against what was programmed.
. Read `GLOBAL_BASE` and `LOCAL_BASE`, write `LENGTH_LO` locally and read it at the global address,
  write `SRC_STRIDE_HI` at the global address and read it locally.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-CSR-OWN-VALUE` |All thirteen registers each read back their own distinct pattern after all
  were written
|`CHK-DMA-CSR-HI-FULL32` |Each `_HI` register reads back all 32 bits written, including bits [31:24]
|`CHK-DMA-CSR-CONFIG-FIELDS` |Writes of each `CONFIG` bit 0 to 10 alone and of `SRC_MAX_LLEN` and
  `DST_MAX_LLEN` 0 to 7 read back exactly in bits [10:0], and a write with the reserved bits
  [31:11] set reads back 0 in them
|`CHK-DMA-CSR-RETAIN-AFTER-COPY` |The linear and two-row copies retire with `DONE_0` equal to their
  ids and deliver their rows, and all thirteen registers read the programmed values after each copy
|`CHK-DMA-CSR-GLOBAL-ALIAS` |A `LENGTH_LO` pattern written locally reads back at the `GLOBAL_BASE`
  address and a `SRC_STRIDE_HI` pattern written at the `GLOBAL_BASE` address reads back locally
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The six step stamps are strictly increasing and the five checker lines appear in step
  order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every register reads back
exactly what was written in all 32 bits ([10:0] for `CONFIG`), both copies retire and match, the
configuration survives them, and the global alias reads and writes reach the same registers. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-353-smc_dma_field_widths_test]]
===== 353 `smc_dma_field_widths_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_field_widths_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; passive probes `tb_top.tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`,
`tb_output_axi_araddr` (required to be 56 bits wide), `tb_output_axi_awvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr`, `tb_output_axi_bvalid`, `tb_output_axi_bready`,
`tb_output_axi_bresp`, `tb_output_axi_rvalid`, `tb_output_axi_rready`, `tb_output_axi_rresp` sampled
at every `clk_smc_i` rise; DMA registers `SRC_ADDRESS_HI`, `DST_ADDRESS_HI`, `LENGTH_HI`,
`SRC_STRIDE_HI`, `DST_STRIDE_HI`, `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` and their `_LO` halves, `NEXT_ID_0`,
`DONE_0`; HI bits [31:24] (register bits [63:56]) and the HI bits that make up address bits [55:32]

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: DMA fields drop bits above their effective widths and keep bits 55:32.

*Test Coverage*:

* The frontend casts register values to the effective widths of `dma.adoc` (DMA register storage and
  effective field widths): addresses, lengths and strides 56 bits, repetitions 32 bits; upper bits
  are discarded, not validated as an out-of-range access.
* Address top byte: `SRC_ADDRESS_HI` and `DST_ADDRESS_HI` with bits [31:24] set must give a first AR
  at the source and a first AW at the destination programmed without those bits, an exact 64-byte
  copy and only OKAY responses on the 56-bit address bus.
* Length top byte: `LENGTH_HI` with bits [31:24] set and `LENGTH_LO` 64 must copy exactly 64 bytes
  and leave the 16 bytes after the span at poison.
* Stride top byte: `SRC_STRIDE_HI` and `DST_STRIDE_HI` with bits [31:24] set and `_LO` 0x40 must
  land each of four 16-byte rows at base plus n times 0x40, with the first AR and AW addresses at
  the row addresses and the gaps untouched.
* Repetitions high word: `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` 1 with `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO` 3 must copy three rows,
  issue three AW bursts and leave the fourth row untouched, as the effective repetition width is 32
  bits.
* Address bits 55:32: source and destination addresses with bits [55:32] nonzero
  (`0x00A5_5A01_0000_1000` and `0x0012_C3D4_0000_2000`) must be issued unchanged as the first AR and
  AW and the destination must equal the source.
* Every copy compares the whole destination image including a 16-byte guard of poison either side,
  and requires every B and R response to be OKAY.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the twelve SYS_OUT probes to exist and `tb_output_axi_araddr` to be 56 bits wide, program
  the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, start the egress log, read `DONE_0` as the
  baseline and wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Error injection. Point: the `SRC_ADDRESS_HI` and `DST_ADDRESS_HI` registers. Kind: bits [31:24]
  set above the 56-bit effective address width on a 64-byte one-row copy. Expected response: the
  first AR and AW are at the addresses programmed without those bits, the destination image is exact
  and every response is OKAY. Seed source and destination, write `CONFIG` with `ENABLED_ND` and all
  twelve descriptor registers, read `NEXT_ID_0` to launch, poll `DONE_0` to the id, wait two cycles,
  then compare the image and the first AR and AW addresses.
. Error injection. Point: the `LENGTH_HI` register. Kind: bits [31:24] set above the 56-bit
  effective length width with `LENGTH_LO` 64. Expected response: exactly 64 bytes are copied and the
  16 bytes after the span keep their poison. Compare the image.
. Error injection. Point: the `SRC_STRIDE_HI` and `DST_STRIDE_HI` registers. Kind: bits [31:24] set
  above the 56-bit effective stride width with `_LO` 0x40 on a four-row, 16-byte-row copy. Expected
  response: each row lands at base plus n times 0x40 with the AR and AW at the row addresses and
  the gaps untouched. Compare the image and require the row addresses.
. Error injection. Point: the `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` register. Kind: `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` 1 above the
  32-bit effective repetition width with `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO` 3. Expected response: three rows are
  copied with exactly three AW bursts and the fourth row is untouched. Compare the image.
. Run a 64-byte copy between the two addresses with bits [55:32] nonzero, compare the image and
  require the first AR and AW at those addresses.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-FW-ADDR-TOP-BYTE` |With the top byte of the address HI registers set, the first AR and AW
  are at the programmed 56-bit addresses, the 64 bytes arrive exactly and every response is OKAY
|`CHK-DMA-FW-LENGTH-TOP-BYTE` |With the top byte of `LENGTH_HI` set, exactly `LENGTH_LO` bytes are
  copied and the guard bytes after the span keep their poison
|`CHK-DMA-FW-STRIDE-TOP-BYTE` |With the top byte of both stride HI registers set, each row lands at
  its base plus n times the low stride, with AR and AW at those row addresses and the gaps unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-FW-REPS-HI` |With `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` nonzero the copy still performs
  `NUM_REPETITIONS_LO` rows with that many AW bursts and the next row is unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-FW-ADDR-55-32` |Source and destination addresses with bits [55:32] nonzero are issued
  unchanged as the first AR and AW and the destination equals the source
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The six step stamps are strictly increasing and the five checker lines appear in step
  order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: each copy retires with its
id, each destination image equals the expected image including the guards, every B and R response is
OKAY, and the issued AR and AW addresses equal the programmed effective addresses. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-354-smc_dma_linear_copy_test]]
===== 354 `smc_dma_linear_copy_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_linear_copy_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) for the DMA registers;
the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) preloaded and read back through
its backdoor; passive probes `tb_top.tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`,
`tb_output_axi_araddr`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr`,
`tb_dma_busy` and `u_output_axi_if.arlen`, `arsize`, `awlen`, `awsize` sampled at every `clk_smc_i`
rise; DMA registers `CONFIG` (`ENABLED_ND`), `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, `SRC_STRIDE`,
`DST_STRIDE`, `NUM_REPETITIONS`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`, `STATUS_0`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the copy lengths inside each length bucket, the offsets
and the payload bytes.

*Objective*: Linear DMA copies match byte for byte across offsets and sizes.

*Test Coverage*:

* A linear copy is one repetition with `CONFIG.ENABLED_ND` set; the backend handles alignment and
  burst splitting (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies). Every copy here compares the
  destination with the source, requires eight guard bytes either side of the destination and the
  source itself to be unchanged, and retires with `DONE_0` equal to the launched id.
* Unaligned starts: 21 copies of 40 bytes, with source offsets 1 to 7, destination offsets 1 to 7
  and unequal offset pairs inside a word, must all arrive exactly.
* 2 KiB boundary: with `SRC_REDUCE_LEN` and `DST_REDUCE_LEN` clear, two 3000-byte copies, one whose
  source and one whose destination crosses a 2 KiB boundary, must arrive exactly with every observed
  AR and AW burst at most 256 beats and inside one 2 KiB block (`dma_ctrl.rdl`,
  `CONFIG.SRC_REDUCE_LEN`).
* Large copies: 8 KiB and 64 KiB copies must retire and match.
* 56-bit addresses: a 200-byte copy from `0x0012_3456_0000_1000` to `0x0034_5678_0000_2000` must
  issue the first AR and AW at exactly those addresses, bits [55:32] preserved (`dma.adoc`, DMA
  register storage and effective field widths).
* Overlap: copies with the destination 16 bytes above the source, 16 bytes below it, and equal to it
  must each retire with `tb_dma_busy` low. The region of the copy whose destination equals its
  source must read unchanged; the resulting bytes of the other two are measured and printed, not
  compared (the specification does not state the copy order).
* Random mix: 20 copies with lengths in the small (1 to 64), mid (65 to 1024) and large (1025 to
  4000) buckets and source and destination offsets in the aligned, 1 to 3 and 4 to 7 buckets must
  all arrive exactly, the buckets being assigned round-robin so each is used, and the seed is
  printed before the first copy.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the seven `tb_top` probes and the four `u_output_axi_if` members to exist, program the
  inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, read `RANDOM_SEED`, print it and seed the random
  generator, start the burst sampler, read `DONE_0` as the baseline and wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. For each of the 21 offset pairs, seed a 40-byte source and the guarded destination, write `CONFIG`
  with `ENABLED_ND` and the descriptor registers (strides 0, one repetition), read `NEXT_ID_0` to
  launch, poll `DONE_0` to the id and compare the destination, the guards and the source.
. Run the source-crossing and the destination-crossing 3000-byte copies and check the burst limits
  of every observed AR and AW.
. Run the 8 KiB copy and the 64 KiB copy and compare each.
. Run the 200-byte copy between the high addresses, compare it and require the first AR and AW
  addresses to equal the programmed ones.
. For each of the three overlap cases write the pattern region, run the copy, wait one cycle,
  require `tb_dma_busy` low, require the equal-address copy to leave the region unchanged and
  print the original source and the result.
. Run the 20 random copies, bucketed round-robin by length and by source and destination offset,
  comparing each.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase, the checker lines to appear in step order and each
  after its own compare; record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-UNALIGNED` |All 21 copies with source, destination and unequal word offsets deliver
  the exact payload with the guard bytes and the source unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-2KIB-BOUNDARY` |Both 3000-byte copies are exact and every observed AR and AW burst has
  at most 256 beats and stays inside one 2 KiB block
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-LARGE` |The 8 KiB and 64 KiB copies retire with `DONE_0` equal to the id and every
  destination byte equals its source byte
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-HI-ADDR` |The first AR and AW addresses equal the programmed addresses with bits
  [55:32] preserved and the 200 destination bytes equal the source
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-OVERLAP` |Each overlapping copy retires with `DONE_0` equal to its id and
  `tb_dma_busy` low; the equal-address copy leaves the region unchanged and the resulting bytes of
  the other two are measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-DMA-LIN-RANDOM` |The seed is printed and all 20 random copies deliver their exact payload with
  intact guards, the length and offset buckets assigned round-robin so each is used
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven step stamps are strictly increasing and the six checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every compared copy is
exact with guards and source unchanged, every `DONE_0` poll reaches its id inside the poll bound,
the burst limits hold and the high addresses are issued unchanged. The overlap result bytes of the
non-equal-address copies are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The resulting bytes of the two overlapping copies whose destination differs from
the source are measured and printed, not compared, because the specification does not state the
copy order.

'''''

[[sec-355-smc_zeroer_busy_outstanding_test]]
===== 355 `smc_zeroer_busy_outstanding_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_busy_outstanding_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP); a ZEROER_DMA
protocol-VIP record booked for the run; the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`)
with its AW and W stall controls, its write response delay control and its backdoor memory; TB input
pin `tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` driven 0 and 1 to hold the B responses; passive probes sampled
at every `clk_smc_i` rise: `tb_zeroer_busy`, `tb_zeroer_outstanding`, `tb_zeroer_intp`,
`tb_zeroer_state`, `tb_zeroer_awvalid`, `tb_zeroer_awready`, `tb_zeroer_awlen`, `tb_zeroer_wvalid`,
`tb_zeroer_wready`, `tb_zeroer_wlast`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_awready`,
`tb_output_axi_wvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wready`, `tb_output_axi_bvalid`, `tb_output_axi_bready`;
zeroer registers `DEST_ADDR`, `SIZE` and `CTRL_STATUS` (`INT_EN` bit 0, `STATUS` bit 32)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only timing: the AW and W stall lengths and
the per-beat stalls; the busy and ordering contracts hold whatever the timing.

*Objective*: Zeroer stays busy to the last B; over 32 bursts; AW/W in order.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeroer counts accepted write addresses and consumed write responses in a 32-bit outstanding
  counter that decides when it stops being busy; the counter is not a 32-transaction limit and does
  not throttle address issuance, and `AWREADY` and `WREADY` provide the downstream back-pressure
  (`zeroer.adoc`, Outstanding Transaction Management and the integration table).
  `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` is a read-only busy bit at bit 32 (`zeroer_ctrl.rdl`).
* Busy lifecycle: `STATUS` must read 0 while idle and before the start write, 1 after the start
  write and while the job issues, and 0 again with `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0 and the range zero
  after completion.
* Busy until the last B: with the B responses held after the last W beat, `STATUS` must stay 1 and
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding` at least 1 for 16 polls with no B handshake; after the release
  `tb_zeroer_busy` must fall only after the last B handshake, and the B handshake count must equal
  the AW handshake count.
* Random stalls: with random AW and W stalls (4 to 8 and 1 to 5 cycles) and per-beat B delays of 1
  to 8 cycles, a 4 KiB job must complete with the range exactly zero, the guard bytes unchanged,
  `STATUS` 0 and `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0, and each stall kind must have been applied. The seed is
  printed.
* Long stall: with B held for 4096 rises, `STATUS` must read 1 at every read, and no interrupt
  pulse may occur, `CTRL_STATUS` outside `STATUS` must hold only `INT_EN`, and after
  the release the job completes with at least one completion interrupt pulse. The zeroer state
  transitions and outstanding count at the end of the hold are printed; the zeroer gives no
  software-visible timeout or error report (`zeroer.adoc`, Status Features; the specification does not state the value).
* More than 32 bursts: a 96 KiB job issues more than 32 bursts. With all B held it must go quiet on
  AW and W for at least 1024 rises with at least one write outstanding, `STATUS` must read 1 and no
  B may complete; after the release the B count must equal the burst count, `STATUS` must fall to 0
  and the range must be exactly zero. What stops the issue is printed from the channel state.
* Outstanding cap: at every sampled rise the SYS_OUT outstanding AW count must not exceed
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding`; the maximum counts and the responder depth are measured and printed, and
  the cap value is not compared (the specification does not state the value).
* AW and W order: a 4 KiB job of at least two bursts must show every AW handshake before the first W
  beat of its burst, each burst carrying AWLEN + 1 W beats with `WLAST` on the last, and 512 W beats
  of 8 bytes in all.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the seventeen `tb_top` probes to exist, release the B hold, program the inbound and
  outbound filter windows to pass all, read `RANDOM_SEED` and print it, start the passive sampler
  and read `STATUS`, requiring 0.
. Poison a 2 KiB range with guard bytes, read `STATUS` (0), write `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` and write
  `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set; poll `STATUS` until it reads 0, requiring the first read to be 1
  and at least one read of 1 while AW handshakes were issued; read it once more (0), require
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0, the range zero and `tb_zeroer_busy` to have fallen.
. Hold B, start a 2 KiB job, wait for its last W beat, then read `STATUS` and
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 16 times, requiring 1 and at least 1 and no B handshake; release the hold,
  poll to idle, and require the B count to equal the burst count and `tb_zeroer_busy` to fall after
  the last B handshake.
. Draw the stalls from the seed, enable the AW and W stalls and the B delays, run a 4 KiB job, poll
  to idle and compare the zeroed range and the guards, require `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0 and every
  stall kind to have been applied.
. Hold B, start a 2 KiB job and read `CTRL_STATUS` for 4096 rises, requiring `STATUS` 1 on every
  read and only `INT_EN` outside it; assert the test issued no register write itself and see no
  interrupt pulse during the hold;
  release it, poll to idle, compare the range and require at least one interrupt pulse.
. Hold B, start a 96 KiB job and wait for 1024 quiet rises with a write outstanding, read `STATUS`
  (1), require no B handshake and record the channel state; release, poll to idle, and require more
  than 32 bursts, the B count equal to the burst count and the range zero.
. Read `STATUS` (0) and require at least one sampled rise; print the maximum outstanding counts and
  the responder depth.
. Run a 4 KiB job and, from the sampled handshakes, require at least two bursts, each AW before its
  first W beat, each burst's W beat count equal to AWLEN + 1 with `WLAST` on the last, and 512 beats
  in all.
. Require the step stamps to strictly increase and the checker lines to appear in step order, each
  after its own compare and after a clean passive-sampler check; record the non-vacuity checker; the
  leaf books the ZEROER_DMA protocol-VIP record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-BUSY-LIFECYCLE` |`STATUS` reads 0 idle and before the start write, 1 after it and while
  the job issues, then 0 twice with `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0, the range zero and `tb_zeroer_busy`
  fallen
|`CHK-ZEROER-BUSY-UNTIL-LAST-B` |With B held after the last W beat `STATUS` stays 1 and
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding` stays at least 1 for 16 polls with no B handshake, and after the release
  `tb_zeroer_busy` falls after the last B handshake with the B count equal to the AW count
|`CHK-ZEROER-RANDOM-STALL` |Under random AW and W stalls and B delays a 4 KiB job ends with the
  range exactly zero, guards unchanged, `STATUS` 0 and `tb_zeroer_outstanding` 0, with each stall
  kind applied
|`CHK-ZEROER-LONG-STALL` |Through the 4096-rise hold `STATUS` reads 1 and `tb_zeroer_intp` stays
  low; after the release the job completes with the range zero and at least
  one completion interrupt pulse
|`CHK-ZEROER-NO-TIMEOUT-INDICATION` |During the hold `CTRL_STATUS` outside `STATUS` holds only
  `INT_EN` and no interrupt pulse occurs; the zeroer state transitions and outstanding count at the
  end of the hold are measured and printed
|`CHK-ZEROER-GT32-BURSTS` |The 96 KiB job issues more than 32 bursts, goes quiet for at least 1024
  rises with all B held and `STATUS` 1, and after the release every response is consumed, `STATUS`
  falls to 0 and the range is exactly zero
|`CHK-ZEROER-AW-CAP` |At every sampled rise the SYS_OUT outstanding AW count is not above
  `tb_zeroer_outstanding` and `STATUS` reads 0 after the held job; the maximum counts are measured
  and printed without comparing the cap value
|`CHK-ZEROER-AW-W-ORDER` |Every AW handshake precedes the first W beat of its burst, each burst has
  AWLEN + 1 W beats with `WLAST` on the last, and 512 beats cover the 4 KiB job
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eight step stamps are strictly increasing and the eight checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nine checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: `STATUS` and
`tb_zeroer_busy` follow the outstanding responses in every job, every range reads zero with its
guards unchanged, the 96 KiB job exceeds 32 bursts and drains, and the AW and W channels stay in
order. The maximum outstanding counts and the timeout indication fields are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The zeroer state transitions and outstanding count at the end of the 4096-rise hold
are printed; the zeroer gives no software-visible timeout or error report and the specification does
not state the value. What stops the issue in the 96 KiB job is printed from the channel state. The
maximum outstanding counts and the responder depth are measured and printed, and the cap value is
not compared, because the specification does not state it.

'''''

[[sec-356-smc_zeroer_irq_test]]
===== 356 `smc_zeroer_irq_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_irq_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP); a ZEROER_DMA
protocol-VIP record booked for the run; the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`)
with its backdoor memory; TB input pin `tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` driven 0 and 1 to hold the B
responses; passive probes sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise: `tb_zeroer_intp` (the zeroer completion
interrupt), `tb_plic_pending_324` (PLIC source 324, raw vector bit 323), `tb_dma_intp`,
`tb_output_axi_bvalid`, `tb_output_axi_bready`, `tb_zeroer_wvalid`, `tb_zeroer_wready`,
`tb_zeroer_wlast`, `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`; zeroer registers `DEST_ADDR`, `SIZE` and `CTRL_STATUS`
(`INT_EN` bit 0, `STATUS` bit 32)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Zeroer completion pulse comes once, after the last B, only with INT_EN.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeroer interrupt is a one-cycle pulse on the falling edge of zeroer busy, routed to raw CPU
  vector bit 323 (PLIC source 324), and is not a counted queue; `CTRL_STATUS.INT_EN` enables it
  (`interrupts.adoc`, `zeroer.adoc` Status Features, `zeroer_ctrl.rdl`). The sampler stamps every
  pulse, B handshake, last W beat and PLIC pending rise by `clk_smc_i` rise.
* One pulse: a 2 KiB job with `INT_EN` set must raise exactly one `tb_zeroer_intp` pulse, after the
  last B handshake, with `tb_plic_pending_324` rising at or after the pulse and still set
  afterwards, `tb_dma_intp` never high, the range zero and the pulse falling inside the quiet window
  of 64 rises.
* No pulse when disabled: the same job with `INT_EN` clear must leave `STATUS` 0 at completion,
  raise no pulse through completion and the quiet window and keep `tb_dma_intp` low.
* After the last B: with the B responses held from the job start through 200 rises past the last W
  beat, `STATUS` must read 1, no B handshake and no pulse may occur while held, and after the
  release the single pulse must rise at or after the last B handshake and not on the last W beat.
* Two jobs: two back-to-back `INT_EN` jobs must give two pulses.
* Zero size and the pulse width: a trigger with `SIZE` 0 and `INT_EN` set must raise no pulse over
  400 rises; the pulse widths of the earlier jobs are measured and printed, and the effect of
  clearing `INT_EN` while a held job is busy, with the `CTRL_STATUS` words and pulse counts, is
  measured and printed without comparing it (the specification does not state the value).
* The PLIC pending probe is the observation point for the PLIC source; the specification does not
  state the value for that observation point.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the nine probes to exist and the responder to be bound, program the inbound and outbound
  filter windows to pass all, write `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` (2 KiB) and read both back, read `STATUS`
  (0), start the sampler, wait four cycles and require at least three rises sampled and
  `tb_plic_pending_324` clear.
. Poison the range, write `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set, wait for `STATUS` to rise and fall, wait
  for the pulse, then a quiet window of 64 rises; require the range zero, one pulse after the last B
  handshake, the PLIC pending rise at or after it with the bit set, `tb_dma_intp` low and the pulse
  width at least 1.
. Poison the range, write `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` clear, wait for `STATUS` to rise and fall and
  the quiet window; require the range zero, `STATUS` 0 and no pulse.
. Poison the range, hold B, write `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set, wait for the last W beat and 200
  more rises, read `STATUS` (1), release the hold, wait for `STATUS` to fall, the pulse and the
  quiet window; require no B handshake or pulse while held, the last B after the release, one pulse
  at or after the last B and not at the last W beat.
. Poison the range, start a job with `INT_EN` set, wait for it to finish, start a second job at once
  and require two pulses.
. Write `SIZE` 0, read it back, write `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set, read `STATUS` every eight
  cycles for 400 rises and require no pulse; write `SIZE` 2 KiB, hold B, start a job, write
  `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` clear once `STATUS` is 1, read the word, release and wait for
  completion, and print the word, pulses and widths.
. Clear `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR`, read `SIZE` back, stop the sampler and require the step stamps to
  strictly increase and the checker lines to appear in step order, each after its own compare;
  record the non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-IRQ-ONE-PULSE` |A job with `INT_EN` set raises exactly one `tb_zeroer_intp` pulse after
  the last B handshake, `tb_plic_pending_324` is set at or after the pulse and stays set,
  `tb_dma_intp` stays low and the range is zero
|`CHK-ZEROER-IRQ-NONE-WHEN-DISABLED` |The same job with `INT_EN` clear ends with `STATUS` 0, the
  range zero and no pulse through completion and the quiet window, `tb_dma_intp` low
|`CHK-ZEROER-IRQ-AFTER-LAST-B` |With B held past the last W beat `STATUS` reads 1 with no B
  handshake and no pulse while held, and after the release the single pulse rises at or after the
  last B handshake and not on the last W beat
|`CHK-ZEROER-IRQ-TWO-JOBS` |Two back-to-back jobs with `INT_EN` set raise two pulses and the range
  is zero
|`CHK-ZEROER-IRQ-ZERO-SIZE-WIDTH` |A `SIZE` 0 trigger with `INT_EN` set raises no pulse over 400
  rises; the earlier pulse widths and the effect of an `INT_EN` write while a held job is busy are
  measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The six step stamps are strictly increasing and the five checker lines appear in step
  order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: one pulse per job with
`INT_EN` set and never earlier than the last B handshake, none with `INT_EN` clear, none for `SIZE`
0, and every compared range reads zero. The pulse widths and the `INT_EN` write while busy are
reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The pulse widths of the earlier jobs are measured and printed. The effect of
clearing `INT_EN` while a held job is busy, with the `CTRL_STATUS` words and pulse counts, is
measured and printed without comparing it, because the specification does not state the value. The
PLIC pending probe is the observation point for the PLIC source, for which the specification does
not state the value.

'''''

[[sec-357-smc_zeroer_job_breadth_test]]
===== 357 `smc_zeroer_job_breadth_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_job_breadth_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP); a ZEROER_DMA
protocol-VIP record booked for the run; the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder memory
(`cfg.sys_out_mem`) poisoned and read back through its backdoor; passive probes on the zeroer master
port sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise: `tb_top.tb_zeroer_awvalid`, `tb_zeroer_awready`,
`tb_zeroer_awaddr`, `tb_zeroer_awlen`, `tb_zeroer_wvalid`, `tb_zeroer_wready`, `tb_zeroer_wdata`,
`tb_zeroer_wstrb`, `tb_zeroer_wlast`; zeroer registers `DEST_ADDR`, `SIZE` and `CTRL_STATUS`
(`STATUS` bit 32)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the bucket order, the alignment order, the job sizes, the
offsets and the poison pattern.

*Objective*: Zeroer jobs clear exactly their range: aligned, high, random.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeroer streams zero data for all beats with correct byte strobes and `w_last`, and handles
  unaligned start addresses (`zeroer.adoc`, Operation Details and AXI Master Interface); `DEST_ADDR`
  is a byte address and `SIZE` a byte count, and a write to `CTRL_STATUS` triggers the job
  (`zeroer_ctrl.rdl`). Every region is pre-filled with a non-zero pattern and flanked by an 8-byte
  guard of the same pattern either side.
* Aligned beats: a 64-byte job at an aligned destination must show exactly one zeroer AW with that
  address and `AWLEN` 7, eight W beats each with zero data and strobe 0xFF, `WLAST` only on the
  eighth, the 64 bytes zero and both guards intact.
* Restart: a second job of 0x58 bytes on a new region must clear it with its first AW at that
  address and leave the first region at its pattern; a bare re-trigger of the same `DEST_ADDR` and
  `SIZE` after re-poisoning the region must clear it again and again leave the first region
  unchanged.
* High destination: a 0x40-byte job with the destination `0x00A5_5A12_0000_1000`, bits [55:32] set,
  must issue its first AW at exactly that address and clear the bytes there with the guards intact.
  `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` are 64-bit `sw=rw` fields (`zeroer_ctrl.rdl`) and must read back the
  programmed values exactly.
* Random mix: 20 seeded jobs over three size buckets (1 to 64, 65 to 0x7FF and 0x801 to 0x1800
  bytes) and aligned and unaligned start offsets must each clear exactly `[DEST, DEST+SIZE)` with
  both guards intact, the size and offset kinds being assigned round-robin so each is used, and the
  seed is printed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the nine zeroer master-port probes to exist and the responder to be bound, program the
  inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all and read `STATUS`, requiring 0.
. Fill the aligned region and its guards with 0xA5, write `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` (64) and read both
  back, start a passive AW and W sampler, write `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set, wait for the first
  AW and poll `STATUS` to 0; require one AW at the destination with `AWLEN` 7, eight W beats of zero
  data, strobe 0xFF and `WLAST` on the last, and compare the region and the guards.
. Fill the first region with 0x5A and the second with 0xC3, program the second job, trigger it,
  require its first AW at the new destination, compare it and require the first region unchanged;
  re-poison the second region with 0x3C, trigger again without reprogramming, and compare both
  regions again.
. Fill the high-address region with 0x96, program it, require `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` to read back as
  programmed, trigger the
  job, require the first AW at the programmed address and compare the region and the guards.
. Read `RANDOM_SEED`, print it, shuffle the size and offset buckets, and for each of 20 jobs poison
  the region with its own pattern, program it, trigger it, poll `STATUS` to 0 and compare the range
  and the guards.
. Clear `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR`, read `SIZE` back as 0, then require the step stamps to strictly
  increase and the checker lines to appear in step order, each after its own compare; record the
  non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-JOB-ALIGNED-BEATS` |The aligned 64-byte job issues one AW at the destination with
  `AWLEN` 7 and eight W beats of zero data and strobe 0xFF with `WLAST` on the last beat only,
  zeroes the 64 bytes and keeps both guards
|`CHK-ZEROER-JOB-RESTART` |A second job on a new region clears it, and a bare re-trigger of the same
  settings clears the re-poisoned region again, while the first region keeps its pattern after each
|`CHK-ZEROER-JOB-HIGH-ADDR` |The job with bits [55:32] of the destination set issues its first AW at
  the programmed address and clears the bytes there with the guards intact; `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE`
  read back as programmed
|`CHK-ZEROER-JOB-RANDOM` |Each of the 20 seeded jobs clears exactly `[DEST, DEST+SIZE)` with both
  guards intact, the size and offset kinds assigned round-robin so each is used, and the seed
  printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The five step stamps are strictly increasing and the four checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every job completes with
`STATUS` back at 0, its range reads zero, its guards and the other regions keep their pattern, and
the aligned job shows the expected AW and W beats. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-358-smc_zeroer_resp_unchecked_test]]
===== 358 `smc_zeroer_resp_unchecked_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_resp_unchecked_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP); a ZEROER_DMA
protocol-VIP record booked for the run; the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`)
with its backdoor memory and its per-burst write error injection (SLVERR and DECERR on chosen
bursts, cleared after each job); the SYS_OUT output AXI monitor (`env.output_axi_monitor`, SLVERR
and DECERR allowed, B-response counters `b_slverr` and `b_decerr` read before and after each job);
passive probes sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise: `tb_top.tb_zeroer_awvalid`, `tb_zeroer_awready`,
`tb_zeroer_awaddr`, `tb_zeroer_awlen`, `tb_zeroer_intp`; zeroer registers `DEST_ADDR`, `SIZE` and
`CTRL_STATUS` (`INT_EN` bit 0, `STATUS` bit 32)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Zeroer jobs complete despite SLVERR and DECERR write responses.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeroer consumes the write response channel without checking `BRESP`: completion means all
  responses have arrived, not that every write succeeded; there is no software-visible AXI error
  report and failed responses are not distinguished from successful ones (`zeroer.adoc`, Outstanding
  Transaction Management and Status Features).
* Baseline: an uninjected 6 KiB job gives the reference burst list (address and `AWLEN` of each AW),
  at least two bursts, exactly one completion interrupt pulse, `STATUS` polled to 0 and read 0
  again, `CTRL_STATUS` outside `STATUS` equal to `INT_EN` alone, no SLVERR or DECERR response seen
  by the monitor, and the bursts cover exactly 6 KiB.
* SLVERR: with the SLVERR response injected on the first, the middle and the last burst in turn, the
  job must finish with `STATUS` 0 on two reads, the baseline burst list, `CTRL_STATUS` outside
  `STATUS` equal to `INT_EN` alone, the monitor counting exactly the injected SLVERR responses, and
  every non-errored burst zero; the bytes left in the errored burst are measured and printed, not
  compared.
* DECERR on every burst: the job must finish with `STATUS` 0, the baseline burst list and the
  baseline interrupt count, the monitor counting every injected DECERR, with the bytes left in the
  errored bursts measured and printed.
* Mixed responses: on a 12 KiB job of at least six bursts, OKAY, SLVERR and DECERR responses
  alternating across the bursts must give `STATUS` 0 on three reads, the baseline burst list, the
  injected response counts and zero in every non-errored burst; the interrupt count against its
  baseline and the bytes left in the errored bursts are measured and printed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the five zeroer probes to exist and the responder to be bound, allow SLVERR and DECERR in
  the output monitor, program the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, write `DEST_ADDR`
  and read it back, read `STATUS` (0).
. Write `SIZE` 6 KiB and read it back, poison the region and run an uninjected job: write
  `CTRL_STATUS` with `INT_EN` set, wait for the first AW, poll `STATUS` to 0 and read `CTRL_STATUS`
  once more; record the AW list as the baseline and require two or more bursts, one interrupt pulse,
  `STATUS` 0 twice, no SLVERR or DECERR response counted by the monitor, `INT_EN` alone outside
  `STATUS`, burst coverage of 6 KiB and a zeroed region.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder's per-burst write error injection. Kind: SLVERR on
  the first, the middle and the last burst in turn, the region re-poisoned before each job.
  Expected response: the monitor counts that response, the job shows the baseline completion and
  every other burst reads zero; the bytes left in the errored burst are printed.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder's per-burst write error injection. Kind: DECERR on
  every burst, the region re-poisoned first. Expected response: the monitor tally matches and the
  job shows the baseline completion with the baseline interrupt count; the bytes left in the
  errored bursts are printed without comparing them.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder's per-burst write error injection. Kind: OKAY,
  SLVERR and DECERR in rotation across the bursts of a 12 KiB job. Expected response: the monitor
  tally matches, the job shows the baseline completion, every non-errored burst reads zero and a
  further `STATUS` read is 0; the interrupt count and the bytes left in errored bursts are printed.
  Before it, write `SIZE` 12 KiB, run a new uninjected baseline and require at least six bursts.
. Clear `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR`, read `SIZE` back as 0, then require the step stamps to strictly
  increase and the checker lines to appear in step order, each after its own compare; record the
  non-vacuity checker.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-SLVERR-COMPLETES` |With SLVERR injected on the first, middle and last burst in turn,
  each job ends with `STATUS` 0, the baseline burst list, only `INT_EN` outside `STATUS`, the
  injected responses counted by the monitor and every non-errored burst zero; the bytes left in the
  errored burst are measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-ZEROER-DECERR-ALL-COMPLETES` |With DECERR on every burst the job ends with `STATUS` 0, the
  baseline burst list and the baseline interrupt pulse count and every DECERR counted by the
  monitor; the bytes left in the errored bursts are measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-ZEROER-MIXED-RESP` |With OKAY, SLVERR and DECERR alternating over at least six bursts the job
  ends with `STATUS` 0 on three reads, the baseline burst list, the injected responses counted and
  every non-errored burst zero; the interrupt count and the bytes left in the errored bursts are
  measured and printed without comparing them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The four step stamps are strictly increasing and the three checker lines appear in
  step order, each after its own compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold and every sequence assert holds: every injected-response job
completes with `STATUS` 0 and the same burst list as the uninjected baseline, the monitor counts
exactly the injected responses, and every burst that was not errored reads zero. The bytes left in
errored bursts and the mixed-job interrupt count are reported only. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The bytes left in the errored bursts of every injected job and the interrupt count of
the mixed job against its baseline are measured and printed, not compared; the zeroer does not check
`BRESP` and does not distinguish failed responses from successful ones.

'''''

[[sec-359-smc_zeroer_sram_init_test]]
===== 359 `smc_zeroer_sram_init_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: POWER

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_sram_init_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer (`env.sys_axi_agent`, no protocol VIP) with bursts of up to 2048
bytes for the SRAM fill and read-back; the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`)
with its backdoor memory and its write count (`output_responder_counts`); the SYS_OUT output AXI
monitor (`env.output_axi_monitor`, SLVERR and DECERR allowed); the outbound filter registers
`OUTBOUND0_START`, `OUTBOUND0_END` and `OUTBOUND0_FILTER_CONFIG`; passive probes sampled at every
`clk_smc_i` rise: `tb_top.tb_zeroer_awvalid`, `tb_zeroer_awready`, `tb_zeroer_awaddr`,
`tb_zeroer_bvalid`, `tb_zeroer_intp`, `tb_dma_busy`, `tb_dma_mst_awvalid`, `tb_dma_mst_awready`,
`tb_dma_mst_awaddr`, `tb_dma_mst_bvalid`, `tb_dma_trans_complete`; the 128 KiB scratch SRAM window
at `0xC006_0000`, the unmapped local address `0xC080_0000`; zeroer registers `DEST_ADDR`, `SIZE` and
`CTRL_STATUS` (`INT_EN` bit 0, `STATUS` bit 32); DMA registers `CONFIG`, `SRC_ADDRESS`,
`DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, strides, `NUM_REPETITIONS`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`, `STATUS_0`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Zeroer clears SRAM and egress ranges; odd local targets are probed.

*Test Coverage*:

* The zeroer clears any region it can reach, performs no check of the destination, length or target
  permissions, and completion means every write response arrived, not that every write succeeded;
  `INT_EN` in the start write requests a completion pulse (`smc-programming.adoc` Memory Zeroer
  procedure; `zeroer.adoc`). Reads of the scratch SRAM go over SEP_IN. The SRAM window is `BASE +
  0x60000` (`memmap.adoc`, generated memory map).
* Full clear: after the 128 KiB window is filled with a non-zero pattern, sampled back to prove the
  fill, one zeroer job of 0x2_0000 bytes with `CTRL_STATUS` written 0 must end with `STATUS` 0 twice
  and every word of a SEP_IN read of the whole window zero.
* Partial ranges: after refilling the window, an unaligned job (0x25 bytes from offset 3 of a word),
  a one-beat job (8 bytes) and a one-burst job (0x800 bytes) must each clear exactly their range,
  with the bytes either side, including an 8-byte guard, keeping the pattern.
* Egress region: a 0x800-byte job in the SYS_OUT output window with `INT_EN` set must end with
  `STATUS` 0, the range and only the range zero with the 8-byte guards unchanged, and exactly one
  `tb_zeroer_intp` pulse with the line low after a 200-cycle quiet window.
* Unmapped and denied targets: a 0x100-byte job aimed at the unmapped local address, and a
  0x400-byte job whose destination lies under an outbound-filter entry that blocks writes, must each
  end with `STATUS` 0 twice; the denied job must leave the egress window and its guards unchanged.
  CTRL_STATUS bits outside `STATUS`, interrupt pulses, AW handshakes, B cycles and the SYS_OUT write
  count change are measured and printed, not compared; the response codes are not on a bench probe
  (the specification does not state the value).
* Local targets of the DMA: a 64-byte DMA copy from the egress source to the SRAM must retire with
  `DONE_0` above its baseline, wait for `tb_dma_busy` to go idle for 64 cycles and leave the SRAM
  equal to the source. A copy to the unmapped address must go quiet within the bound; its `DONE_0`,
  `STATUS_0`, AW handshakes, B cycles and completion cycles are measured and printed, not compared.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the eleven probes to exist and the responder to be bound, allow SLVERR and DECERR in the
  output monitor, program the inbound and outbound filter windows to pass all, write `SIZE` 0 and
  read `STATUS` (0), fill the 128 KiB SRAM window over SEP_IN with a non-zero pattern and read back
  three 2 KiB samples against it, and poison the egress and denied regions with guards.
. Run the full-window clear: write `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE` and read both back, write `CTRL_STATUS` 0,
  wait for the first AW, poll `STATUS` to 0 and read it again; read the whole window over SEP_IN and
  require every 8-byte word zero.
. Refill the window with a second pattern; for each of the three partial legs run the job, read the
  range with an 8-byte guard each side over SEP_IN and compare with the pattern having only the
  range zeroed.
. Run the 0x800-byte egress job with `INT_EN` set, wait for `STATUS` 0 and a 200-cycle quiet window
  and require the range zero, both guard words 0xA5, one `tb_zeroer_intp` pulse and the line low.
. Error injection. Point: the zeroer `DEST_ADDR`, aimed at the unmapped local address `0xC080_0000`
  and then at a region under an outbound filter entry that allows reads and blocks writes. Kind: a
  0x100-byte job at the unmapped address and a 0x400-byte job at the denied region, each with
  `INT_EN` set. Expected response: `STATUS` reads 0 twice after each job and the denied region and
