The DTP control window and the bus error units are named as cells not closed and are not claimed: the bench leaves the DTP AXI-Lite response idle, so an access there would never complete, and the bus error units lie outside the local and global apertures at the reset `REGION_SIZE`.

'''''

[[sec-360-smc_filter_lock_scope_test]]
===== 360 `smc_filter_lock_scope_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_lock_scope_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) through the SEP_IN sequencer, single accesses and one
outstanding group (`SmcSysAxiGroupItem`), with the monitor's expected-DECERR address list;
`ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, JTAG) for the outbound traffic; SYS_OUT responder memory (`sys_out_mem`
backdoor) and the `tb_top` probes `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_write_count`, `tb_output_axi_read_count`,
`tb_output_axi_last_addr`, `tb_output_axi_last_wdata`, `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; the `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR`
registers of the inbound and outbound filter banks

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A locked filter entry refuses writes to all three of its registers,
even writes queued right behind the locking write, still reads back its locked configuration, and
keeps its permit or deny decision on JTAG traffic.

*Test Coverage*:

* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`FILTER_CONFIG.locked`, bit 63, write-once) and `index.adoc` (Locking a Filter
Entry): once `locked` is set, every write to the entry's `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and
`END_ADDR` terminates with DECERR, and reads still return the locked configuration. Entry 14 of the
inbound and of the outbound bank is locked and then written on all three registers; the locking
write is answered OKAY and each refused write DECERR.
* Locked entries read OKAY with the locked configuration: `FILTER_CONFIG` reads the reset word
0x3000 plus `locked`, i.e. 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, `START_ADDR` reads its reset value 0x0 and
`END_ADDR` its reset value 0x7 (`filter_ctrl.rdl` reset values), so a refused write changed nothing.
* Queued writes: on entry 13 of each bank the locking write and the three writes behind it are
issued as one outstanding group without awaiting a response. The three queued writes must still be
answered DECERR, each group inside the 50 us per-access bound, and the entry reads the locked
configuration afterwards.
* Match Then Permit (`index.adoc`): a locked outbound entry keeps its decision. Entries 5 and 6
cover range R1 (0x0200_8000 to 0x0200_8FFF) and entries 3 and 4 cover R2 (0x0200_9000 to
0x0200_9FFF); entry 5 (permit) and entry 3 (deny) are the lower-numbered, so they win over the
unlocked entries 6 (deny) and 4 (permit) on the same range. After the lock, an attempt to clear
`entry_enabled` is answered DECERR, JTAG writes into R1 still land in SYS_OUT memory and JTAG writes
into R2 are still answered DECERR with SYS_OUT memory unchanged.
* Locking together with other fields: one 8-byte write of 0x8000_0000_0023_0003 (`locked`,
`read_allowed`, `write_allowed`, `src_id` 3, `group_id` 2) to outbound entry 12 is observed only.
Whether the fields other than `locked` are applied by a lock write is not stated in
`filter_ctrl.rdl` or `index.adoc`, so the leaf prints the BRESP and the two
reads and asserts only that they agree.
* Entry 0 of either bank is never locked, and every locked entry is used by no later step.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound) and sample `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for the wait record.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of inbound 14, outbound 14, inbound 13, outbound 13 and outbound 5, 6, 3, 4
and 12 and require `locked` and `entry_enabled` clear on each.
. Error injection. Point: entry 14 of the inbound and then the outbound bank, after the locking
word 0x8000_0000_0000_3000 is written (OKAY). Kind: writes to the locked entry's `FILTER_CONFIG`
(`src_id` 5), `START_ADDR` (0x0200_1000) and `END_ADDR` (0x0200_1FFF), each registered as an
expected DECERR address. Expected response: each write is answered DECERR; the three registers read
back 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, 0x0 and 0x7.
. Error injection. Point: entry 13 of each bank, through the SEP_IN sequencer as one outstanding
group. Kind: the locking write with the three writes to the entry's registers queued directly behind
it, issued without awaiting a response. Expected response: the locking write OKAY and the three
others DECERR; the three registers then read back the locked configuration.
. Program outbound entries 5, 6 over R1 and 3, 4 over R2 (`START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`, then
`FILTER_CONFIG` with the permit word 0x0000_0000_0100_0013 or the deny word 0x0000_0000_0100_0010,
and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back with the read-only `data_bus_width` bits set). Take the SYS_OUT write
and read counts.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 5 `FILTER_CONFIG`, after the entry is locked. Kind: a
write clearing `entry_enabled` on the locked permit entry. Expected response: DECERR, and the locked
word reads back. Then a JTAG write of 0x1111_2222_3333_4444 to 0x0200_8100 must answer OKAY, raise
the SYS_OUT write count by exactly one with that address and data, and land in SYS_OUT memory.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 3 `FILTER_CONFIG`, after the entry is locked. Kind: a
write clearing `entry_enabled` on the locked deny entry. Expected response: DECERR, and the locked
word reads back. Then a JTAG write of 0x5555_6666_7777_8888 to 0x0200_8108 must land the same way,
and the two R1 words are read back over JTAG and compared, each read raising the SYS_OUT read count
by one.
. Error injection. Point: the JTAG-AXI manager, writing to 0x0200_9100 and 0x0200_9108 over R2,
which the locked deny entry 3 covers, with the SYS_OUT memory words preset to a sentinel. Kind:
outbound writes into a denied range. Expected response: both writes answer DECERR; the SYS_OUT write
count must stay unchanged for 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles, the memory must keep the sentinel, and
`tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid` and `tb_output_axi_arvalid` must read 0.
. Write 0x8000_0000_0023_0003 to outbound entry 12 `FILTER_CONFIG`, read it twice, print the BRESP
and both words, and require the two reads equal and bit 63 set exactly when the BRESP was OKAY.
. Restore outbound entries 4 and 6 to the reset words 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7; the locked entries stay
locked until reset. Print the ordered-fence line and the wait record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOCK-WRITES-REFUSED` |Entry 14 of each bank accepts the locking write with OKAY and answers
the `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` writes with DECERR (six refused writes), and the
entry reads the locked configuration afterwards
|`CHK-LOCK-READS-OKAY` |Reads of `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of the locked entry 14
answer OKAY with 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, 0x0 and 0x7 on both banks; each is an exact scoreboard
compare
|`CHK-LOCK-QUEUED-WRITES` |On entry 13 of each bank the locking write is answered OKAY and the three
writes queued directly behind it are answered DECERR inside the 50 us per-access bound, leaving the
entry reading 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, 0x0 and 0x7
|`CHK-LOCK-FROZEN-PERMIT` |The locked permit entry 5 keeps admitting: the disable write is answered
DECERR, both JTAG writes into R1 answer OKAY, raise the SYS_OUT write count by one each and land in
SYS_OUT memory, although unlocked deny entry 6 covers the same range, and both read back
|`CHK-LOCK-FROZEN-DENY` |The locked deny entry 3 keeps blocking: the disable write is answered
DECERR, both JTAG writes into R2 are answered DECERR, the SYS_OUT write count does not advance, the
memory keeps its sentinel and the SYS_OUT AW, W and AR valids stay low, although unlocked permit
entry 4 covers the same range
|`CHK-LOCK-WITH-FIELDS-OBSERVE` |Measures and prints the BRESP of the combined lock write and the
two `FILTER_CONFIG` reads; the only compares are that the two reads are equal and that bit 63 is set
exactly when the BRESP is OKAY, and it does not require the other fields to be applied or refused
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S6 are recorded in order with strictly increasing time, each
checker line is printed after its step in the fixed order, and the SEP_IN plus JTAG access count
reaches the floor of 79; a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated run, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounds of the waits the run took -- fuse-sense wait, per-access
bound, SYS_OUT responder delta bound and blocked-write hold -- as a line; the compares are the
bounded polls themselves, so an expired bound raises before this line
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-LOCK-WRITES-REFUSED`, `CHK-LOCK-READS-OKAY`, `CHK-LOCK-QUEUED-WRITES`,
`CHK-LOCK-FROZEN-PERMIT` and `CHK-LOCK-FROZEN-DENY` hold: the six refused entry-14 writes and the
six queued entry-13 writes answer DECERR, locked entries read 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, 0x0 and 0x7,
JTAG writes to R1 land and writes to R2 answer DECERR with the sentinel kept.
`CHK-LOCK-WITH-FIELDS-OBSERVE` reports the combined write and is held only to its two consistency
compares. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after the access floor of 79. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Whether a lock write also applies the fields other than `locked` is not stated in
`filter_ctrl.rdl` or `index.adoc`, so the combined write 0x8000_0000_0023_0003 to outbound entry 12
is observed only: the BRESP and the two `FILTER_CONFIG` reads are printed, and the only compares are
that the two reads agree and that bit 63 is set exactly when the BRESP was OKAY.

'''''

[[sec-361-smc_filter_range_granule_test]]
===== 361 `smc_filter_range_granule_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_range_granule_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) through the SEP_IN sequencer, 8-byte reads and writes of
the `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` registers of entries 2 and 3 of the inbound and
outbound filter banks (entries stay disabled); `tb_top` probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` sampled after the fuse-sense wait; no other VIP, pad
or IRQ line

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Programming a filter range on a disabled entry reads back widened
to the granule selected by allow_burst, identically in both banks, and the data_bus_width field
cannot be written.

*Test Coverage*:

* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`FILTER_CONFIG.data_bus_width`, `sw = r`, reset 3): the field reads 3
(`FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000) at reset and after a write of 0x0 and a write of 0x7000 on entry 2 of each
bank. The write responses are printed, not compared, because no document fixes the response to a
write of a read-only field.
* `index.adoc` (Address Range Granule, granule widening examples): with `allow_burst` 0 the range
0x1001..0x1002 reads back `START_ADDR` 0x1000 and `END_ADDR` 0x1007 (one 8-byte granule); with
`allow_burst` 1 the same range reads back 0x1000 and 0x1FFF (one 4 KB granule).
* `index.adoc`: with `allow_burst` 1 an already aligned range 0x2000..0x2FFF reads back unchanged.
* Bank parity: entry 2 of the inbound and of the outbound bank (same `filter_ctrl` register block)
return the same read-back pairs for the three programmed ranges.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`START_ADDR` write-back): the write-back fires when both values land in the
same granule. On entry 3 the leaf writes `START_ADDR` alone after `FILTER_CONFIG` 0, then the
`allow_burst` 1 pair, then clears `allow_burst`, and prints the pair read after the START-only write
and after the clear. Neither document states what triggers the write-back or whether clearing
`allow_burst` re-evaluates it, so those two reads are printed and not
compared; the `allow_burst` 1 pair is compared with 0x1000 and 0x1FFF.
* Entries 2 and 3 of both banks are restored to the reset words 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7 and read back;
`entry_enabled` stays clear and nothing is locked throughout.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound) and require `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to be resolvable.
. Error injection. Point: `FILTER_CONFIG` of entry 2 of the inbound and then the outbound bank.
Kind: writes of 0x0 and 0x7000 to the read-only `data_bus_width` field. Expected response: bits
[14:12] of the readback after each write still read 3; both BRESP values are printed, not compared.
Read `FILTER_CONFIG` and compare it with 0x3000 before the writes, and require bits [14:12] of all
three reads to be 3.
. For each bank on entry 2: write `FILTER_CONFIG` 0, `START_ADDR` 0x1001, `END_ADDR` 0x1002 and
compare the pair read back with (0x1000, 0x1007).
. For each bank on entry 2: write `FILTER_CONFIG` with `allow_burst` set (0x0100_0000), `START_ADDR`
0x1001, `END_ADDR` 0x1002 and compare the pair with (0x1000, 0x1FFF).
. For each bank on entry 2: write `FILTER_CONFIG` with `allow_burst` set, `START_ADDR` 0x2000,
`END_ADDR` 0x2FFF and compare the pair with (0x2000, 0x2FFF); then require the inbound and outbound
pairs of the three ranges to be identical.
. For each bank on entry 3: read `FILTER_CONFIG` (0x3000) and the pair (0x0, 0x7); write
`FILTER_CONFIG` 0 and `START_ADDR` 0x1001 only and read the pair; write `FILTER_CONFIG` with
`allow_burst` set, `START_ADDR` 0x1001 and `END_ADDR` 0x1002 and compare the pair with (0x1000,
0x1FFF); write `FILTER_CONFIG` 0 and read the pair. Print the START-only and the cleared pairs.
. Restore `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of entries 2 and 3 of both banks to 0x3000,
0x0 and 0x7 and compare them back; require the 94 SEP_IN accesses of the sequence to have been
issued, then print the wait record and the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DBW-READ-ONLY` |`data_bus_width` (bits [14:12] of `FILTER_CONFIG`) reads 3 at reset and after
writes of 0x0 and 0x7000 on entry 2 of both banks; the write responses are printed and not compared
|`CHK-GRANULE-BURST0` |With `allow_burst` 0 the range 0x1001..0x1002 reads back `START_ADDR` 0x1000
and `END_ADDR` 0x1007 on both banks, an exact compare of each word
|`CHK-GRANULE-ALIGNED` |With `allow_burst` 1 the aligned range 0x2000..0x2FFF reads back
`START_ADDR` 0x2000 and `END_ADDR` 0x2FFF on both banks, unchanged
|`CHK-GRANULE-BANK-PARITY` |The inbound and outbound banks return identical pairs for the three
ranges, (0x1000, 0x1007), (0x1000, 0x1FFF) and (0x2000, 0x2FFF); the `allow_burst` 1 pair (0x1000,
0x1FFF) is an exact compare on both banks, so the parity follows from the exact compares
|`CHK-GRANULE-WRITEBACK-OBSERVE` |Measures and prints the `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` read after the
START-only write and after the `allow_burst` clear, without comparing them; the entry-3 reset words
and the `allow_burst` 1 pair (0x1000, 0x1FFF) are the only compares of the leg
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms DBW_READS, BURST0_PAIR, BURST1_PAIR, ALIGNED_PAIR, OBSERVE_LEG and
RESTORED are stamped in order with strictly increasing time and each checker line is printed after
its term; a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated run, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the three fuse-sense sub-waits (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles each), the
50 us SEP_IN access bound and the access count; the compares are the bounded waits and the 94-access
assert, so an expired bound raises before this line
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DBW-READ-ONLY`, `CHK-GRANULE-BURST0`, `CHK-GRANULE-ALIGNED` and
`CHK-GRANULE-BANK-PARITY` hold: `data_bus_width` reads 3, the three ranges read back (0x1000,
0x1007), (0x1000, 0x1FFF) and (0x2000, 0x2FFF) on both banks, and the entries read the reset words
after the restore. `CHK-GRANULE-WRITEBACK-OBSERVE` reports the START-only and cleared readings and
is held only to its reset and `allow_burst` 1 compares. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are
printed after all 94 accesses. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The responses to the writes of 0x0 and 0x7000 on `FILTER_CONFIG` are printed, not
compared, because no document fixes the response to a write of a read-only field. The `START_ADDR` /
`END_ADDR` pair read after the START-only write and after the `allow_burst` clear on entry 3 is
printed and not compared, because neither document states what triggers the write-back or whether
clearing `allow_burst` re-evaluates it.

'''''

[[sec-362-smc_filter_reset_word_test]]
===== 362 `smc_filter_reset_word_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_reset_word_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) through the SEP_IN sequencer, all accesses 8 bytes,
reading and writing the `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` registers of the inbound and
outbound filter banks (entries 0, 7, 12 and 15), the alias remap `REGION_START`, `REGION_END` and
`REGION_ATTRS` registers and the M-mode and Xvisor output remap `REGION_ATTRS` registers (regions 0
and 7); the reset agent (`COLD_RST_LO`, `COLD_RST_HI`, `WAIT_STATE` and raw-sample hold on
`powergood_stable`, `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_n`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_n`, `rst_primary_smc_clk_n`
and `rst_wdt_smc_clk_n`, counted in `clk_ref_i` cycles); `tb_top` probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after each fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The filter, alias remap and output remap registers read their reset
words, a cold reset returns programmed non-reset values to those words, and it clears a filter lock
so the entry can be written again.

*Test Coverage*:

* `filter_ctrl.rdl` reset values: `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000 (read-only `data_bus_width` 3),
`START_ADDR` 0x0 and `END_ADDR` 0x7. Entries 0, 7 and 15 of both banks are read over SEP_IN before
anything is programmed and compared with those words (18 reads).
* `alias_remap.rdl` (`REGION_START`, `REGION_END`, `REGION_ATTRS`) and `output_remap.rdl`
(`REGION_ATTRS`) reset to 0. A reset word of 0 cannot be told from an unwritten register, so alias
regions 0 and 7 and the M-mode and Xvisor output remap regions 0 and 7 are first programmed with
non-zero values and read back, and the post-reset 0 is compared against that prior value.
* Filter entry 7 of both banks is programmed (`START_ADDR` 0x0200_1000, `END_ADDR` 0x0200_1FFF,
`FILTER_CONFIG` 0x0105_0013, read back 0x0105_3013) and must read the reset words after the cold
reset.
* `index.adoc` (Locking a Filter Entry) and `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`FILTER_CONFIG.locked`, reset 0):
entry 12 of both banks is locked with the write 0x8000_0000_0000_3000, reads back that word, and
after the cold reset reads 0x3000 with bit 63 clear. The documents do not say which reset clears
filter entries; the leaf applies the cold reset and compares only the values
above.
* After the reset the formerly locked entry 12 accepts a `FILTER_CONFIG` write with `src_id` 3
(0x3_0000), answered OKAY and read back 0x3_3000, then is restored to 0x3000.
* Entry 0 of either bank is never locked and entry 12 is touched by no other step before the reset.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound) and record `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of entries 0, 7 and 15 of the inbound and then
the outbound bank over SEP_IN, each answered OKAY and compared with 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7.
. For both banks write entry 7 `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR` and `FILTER_CONFIG` and write
0x8000_0000_0000_3000 to entry 12; for regions 0 and 7 write the alias remap `REGION_START`
0x0200_2000, `REGION_END` 0x0200_3000 and `REGION_ATTRS` 0x8F00_0000_0000_1000 and the M-mode and
Xvisor `REGION_ATTRS` 0x8000_0000_0240_0000 (region 0) and 0x8000_0000_0250_0000 (region 7).
. Read every programmed register back and compare it with the programmed word (entry 7
`FILTER_CONFIG` reads 0x0105_3013, entry 12 reads 0x8000_0000_0000_3000).
. Drive `COLD_RST_LO`, wait (bound 400 `clk_ref_i` cycles) for `powergood_stable` 1 and the cold and
primary resets asserted, hold those levels over 32 raw samples, drive `COLD_RST_HI`, wait (bound
2000 `clk_ref_i` cycles) for all five reset observables released, then wait for the fuse-sense
sub-waits again (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles each).
. Read entry 7 of both banks and compare with 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7; read entry 12 of both banks and
compare with 0x3000, requiring bit 63 clear; read the alias remap `REGION_START`, `REGION_END` and
`REGION_ATTRS` and the M-mode and Xvisor `REGION_ATTRS` of regions 0 and 7 and compare each with 0.
. For each bank write 0x3_0000 to entry 12 `FILTER_CONFIG` (OKAY), read it back and compare with
0x3_3000, write 0 and read back 0x3000.
. Read entry 12 of both banks once more and compare with 0x3000, require at least 82 SEP_IN
accesses, then print the wait record and the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RESET-WORD-INBOUND` |Inbound entries 0, 7 and 15 read `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000, `START_ADDR` 0x0
and `END_ADDR` 0x7 before anything is programmed, every access OKAY; the START_ADDR 0x0 legs cannot fail on X/Z on this two-state bench, FILTER_CONFIG 0x3000 and END_ADDR 0x7 carry the compare
|`CHK-RESET-WORD-OUTBOUND` |Outbound entries 0, 7 and 15 read `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000, `START_ADDR`
0x0 and `END_ADDR` 0x7 before anything is programmed, every access OKAY; the START_ADDR 0x0 legs cannot fail on X/Z on this two-state bench, FILTER_CONFIG 0x3000 and END_ADDR 0x7 carry the compare
|`CHK-RESET-ALIAS-REMAP` |Alias regions 0 and 7 read back the programmed `REGION_START`,
`REGION_END` and `REGION_ATTRS` words before the cold reset and read 0x0 in all three registers
after it
|`CHK-RESET-OUTPUT-REMAP` |The M-mode and Xvisor output remap `REGION_ATTRS` of regions 0 and 7 read
back their programmed non-zero words before the cold reset and 0x0 after it
|`CHK-RESET-FILTER-PROGRAMMED` |Entry 7 of each bank reads 0x0105_3013, 0x0200_1000 and 0x0200_1FFF
before the cold reset and the reset words 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7 after it
|`CHK-RESET-CLEARS-LOCK` |Entry 12 of each bank reads 0x8000_0000_0000_3000 after the locking write
and 0x3000 with bit 63 clear after the cold reset
|`CHK-LOCK-WRITABLE-AFTER-RESET` |After the reset a `FILTER_CONFIG` write with `src_id` 3 to the
formerly locked entry 12 of each bank is answered OKAY, reads back 0x3_3000, and the restore write
reads back 0x3000
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms RESET_STATE_READS, PROGRAMMED_READBACKS, COLD_RESET_ASSERT,
COLD_RESET_RELEASE, POST_RESET_READS and LOCKED_ENTRY_WRITE are stamped in order with strictly
increasing time and each checker line is printed after its term; a control-flow invariant, not a DUT
compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One line per bounded wait the run took -- the two fuse-sense waits, the
cold-reset assert and release waits and the 50 us SEP_IN access bound; the compares are the bounded
waits themselves, so an expired bound raises before this line
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-RESET-WORD-INBOUND`, `CHK-RESET-WORD-OUTBOUND`, `CHK-RESET-ALIAS-REMAP`,
`CHK-RESET-OUTPUT-REMAP`, `CHK-RESET-FILTER-PROGRAMMED`, `CHK-RESET-CLEARS-LOCK` and
`CHK-LOCK-WRITABLE-AFTER-RESET` hold: every reset word reads 0x3000 / 0x0 / 0x7 for the filter
entries and 0 for the remap registers, each programmed non-zero value reads back before the cold
reset and the reset word after it, entry 12 reads locked before and unlocked after, and its
post-reset write is OKAY. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after at least 82
accesses. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The documents do not say which reset clears the filter entries, so the leaf applies
the cold reset and compares only the listed values. The `START_ADDR` 0x0 reset legs cannot fail on
X/Z on this two-state bench; `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000 and `END_ADDR` 0x7 carry the reset-word compare.

'''''

[[sec-363-smc_infilt_addr_burst_match_test]]
===== 363 `smc_infilt_addr_burst_match_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_infilt_addr_burst_match_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SYS_IN) for the 8-byte reads around each programmed range and
`ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) for the programming, seeding and cleanup; `tb_top` signals
`sys_axi_arvalid` and `sys_axi_awvalid` with the inbound filter probes `tb_inb_read_hit`,
`tb_inb_write_hit`, `tb_inb_isolate_read` and `tb_inb_isolate_write`, sampled at every `clk_smc_i`
rise (bit i of a hit vector is inbound entry i); the scratchpad memory (SPM) at its base plus
0x4_0000 (P0) as the probe target and `CHIP_CONFIG.VERSION_LO` through its global alias 0x4000_2900;
the output AXI monitor's DECERR and SLVERR allowances for the 56-bit leg; `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after the fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Inbound filter entries admit only the addresses inside their
widened range, none when disabled, whole 56-bit addresses, and bursts only when allow_burst is set,
with a refused burst falling through to the next entry.

*Test Coverage*:

* `index.adoc` (Address Range Granule, Match Then Permit): an entry admits the whole granule of its
range and nothing outside it. With `allow_burst` 1 the range P0+0x1000..P0+0x1FFF admits a read at
P0+0x1800 (OKAY, the seeded word, hit bit 2) and refuses reads one 4 KB granule below (P0+0x0FF8)
and above (P0+0x2000) with DECERR and a zero hit vector; with `allow_burst` 0 the range
P0+0x3040..P0+0x3047 admits P0+0x3040 and refuses P0+0x3038 and P0+0x3048 the same way. The
`START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` read-backs of the 8-byte case are printed, not compared.
* `index.adoc` (`entry_enabled`): the same range with `entry_enabled` clear answers DECERR with a
zero hit vector, although the range and permissions would admit the read.
* `fabric.adoc` (Filtering and Protection, input fabric): the system AXI input is filtered and the
SMC window is reached at the local or the global base. An entry over 0x4000_2000..0x4000_2FFF admits
a 4-byte read of `CHIP_CONFIG.VERSION_LO` at 0x4000_2900 returning its reset 0x000100A0
(`chip_config.rdl`) with hit bit 2. An entry over 0x00AB_C006_5000..0x00AB_C006_5FFF has hit bit 2
at 0x00AB_C006_5800 and a zero hit vector with DECERR at 0x0000_C006_5800, whose address bits
[55:32] differ; the downstream response of the first read is printed, not compared.
* `index.adoc`: a range spanning three granules (P0+0x8000..P0+0xAFFF) admits reads at P0+0x8000,
P0+0x9FF8 and P0+0xAFF8 and refuses P0+0x7FF8 and P0+0xB000; `START_ADDR` equal to `END_ADDR`
(P0+0xC123) admits the whole 4 KB granule (P0+0xC000 and P0+0xCFF8) and refuses P0+0xBFF8 and
P0+0xD000.
* `index.adoc` (`allow_burst`): with `allow_burst` 0 on entry 2 a single-beat read at P0+0xE000 is
admitted (hit bit 2) and a 2-beat INCR read (AxLEN 1) is refused with DECERR and a zero hit vector;
with entry 3 added over P0+0xE000..P0+0xEFFF at `allow_burst` 1 the same 2-beat read is admitted by
entry 3 with the 16 seeded bytes, hit bit 3 set and bit 2 clear. A match failure falls through to
the next entry (Match Then Permit).
* The inbound filter blocks unmatched traffic (`fabric.adoc`, `index.adoc` instance table), so every
refusal above is a DECERR; entry 0 and every lock stay untouched and entries 2 and 3 return to their
reset words.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), sample the three fuse and reset
probes, and start the hit watcher on the SYS_IN valids and the inbound hit probes.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of inbound entries 2 and 3 over SEP_IN
(`entry_enabled` clear, 0x7 and 0x0 as reset words), write a distinct seed word to each of the 17
probe addresses and read each back.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed with the permit word `allow_burst` 1
(0x0000_0000_0100_0013) over P0+0x1000..P0+0x1FFF and then reprogrammed with `allow_burst` 0 (0x13)
over P0+0x3040..P0+0x3047, driven by SYS_IN reads. Kind: reads one granule below and above each
programmed range, at P0+0x0FF8 and P0+0x2000 and then at P0+0x3038 and P0+0x3048. Expected response:
each refused read answers DECERR with a zero hit vector, while the reads inside each range, at
P0+0x1800 and at P0+0x3040, answer OKAY with the seeded word and hit bit 2; each read's response,
data and hit vector is compared.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, reprogrammed with `entry_enabled` clear over
P0+0x1000..P0+0x1FFF. Kind: a SYS_IN read at P0+0x1800 against the disabled entry. Expected
response: DECERR with a zero hit vector.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed over 0x00AB_C006_5000..0x00AB_C006_5FFF.
Kind: a SYS_IN read at 0x0000_C006_5800, whose address bits [55:32] differ from the programmed
range. Expected response: DECERR with a zero hit vector. Before it, program entry 2 over
0x4000_2000..0x4000_2FFF and read `VERSION_LO` at 0x4000_2900, then program it over the 56-bit range
and read 0x00AB_C006_5800 with the output monitor allowing DECERR and SLVERR.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed over P0+0x8000..P0+0xAFFF. Kind: SYS_IN
reads at P0+0x7FF8 and P0+0xB000, outside the three-granule span. Expected response: DECERR with a
zero hit vector. Also read P0+0x8000, P0+0x9FF8 and P0+0xAFF8 inside the span.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed with `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` both
P0+0xC123. Kind: SYS_IN reads at P0+0xBFF8 and P0+0xD000, in the neighbouring granules. Expected
response: DECERR with a zero hit vector. Also read P0+0xC000 and P0+0xCFF8 inside the granule.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed with `allow_burst` 0 over
P0+0xE000..P0+0xE007. Kind: a 2-beat INCR read (AxLEN 1) at P0+0xE000. Expected response: DECERR
with a zero hit vector. Also issue the single-beat read at P0+0xE000.
. Program entry 3 with `allow_burst` 1 over P0+0xE000..P0+0xEFFF and repeat the 2-beat read,
comparing the 16 bytes and the hit vector.
. Restore `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of entries 2 and 3 to 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7,
read `FILTER_CONFIG` back, stop the watcher, require at least 96 SEP_IN and SYS_IN accesses and
print the ordered-fence line and the wait record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-INB-ADDR-GRANULE` |With `allow_burst` 1 the read inside the 4 KB granule is OKAY with the
seeded word and hit bit 2, the reads one granule below and above are DECERR with a zero hit vector,
and the same holds for the 8-byte granule with `allow_burst` 0
|`CHK-INB-DISABLED-NO-MATCH` |With `entry_enabled` clear the read at P0+0x1800 is answered DECERR
with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-ADDR-HIGH-BITS-GLOBAL` |`VERSION_LO` through the global alias 0x4000_2900 returns
0x000100A0 with hit bit 2, the 56-bit entry has hit bit 2 at 0x00AB_C006_5800 (response printed, not
compared), and the read with differing bits [55:32] is DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-SPAN-WHOLE` |The three reads inside the three-granule span are OKAY with the seeded words
and hit bit 2, and the two reads outside are DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-START-EQ-END` |`START_ADDR` equal to `END_ADDR` admits the reads at both edges of the 4 KB
granule (OKAY, hit bit 2) and the neighbouring granules are DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-BURST0-SINGLE-ONLY` |With `allow_burst` 0 the single-beat read is OKAY with hit bit 2 and
the 2-beat INCR read is DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-BURST-FALLTHROUGH` |The 2-beat read refused by entry 2 is OKAY with the 16 seeded bytes
through entry 3, with hit bit 3 set and bit 2 clear
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 are recorded in order with strictly increasing time, each
checker line is printed after its step in the fixed order, and the SEP_IN plus SYS_IN access count
reaches the floor of 96; a control-flow invariant, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the fuse-sense bounds and the 50 us per-access bound of the SEP_IN and
SYS_IN accesses as a line; the compares are the bounded accesses themselves, so an expired bound
raises before this line, and the hit watcher is a passive sampler with no wait
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-INB-ADDR-GRANULE`, `CHK-INB-DISABLED-NO-MATCH`,
`CHK-INB-ADDR-HIGH-BITS-GLOBAL`, `CHK-INB-SPAN-WHOLE`, `CHK-INB-START-EQ-END`,
`CHK-INB-BURST0-SINGLE-ONLY` and `CHK-INB-BURST-FALLTHROUGH` hold: every admitted read is OKAY with
its seeded word and the programmed entry's hit bit, every refused read is DECERR with a zero hit
vector, and the fall-through read sets bit 3 and not bit 2. The isolate probes are printed with each
read and not compared. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after the access floor of
96. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` read-backs of the 8-byte granule case are printed,
not compared. The downstream response of the read at 0x00AB_C006_5800 is printed, not compared. The
isolate probes are printed with each read and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-364-smc_infilt_attr_match_test]]
===== 364 `smc_infilt_attr_match_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_infilt_attr_match_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SYS_IN) for the reads and writes with a chosen AxPROT, every
SYS_IN master presenting AxUSER 0, and `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) for the programming, seeding,
readbacks and cleanup; `tb_top` signals `sys_axi_arvalid` and `sys_axi_awvalid` with the inbound
filter probes `tb_inb_read_hit`, `tb_inb_write_hit`, `tb_inb_isolate_read` and
`tb_inb_isolate_write`, sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise (bit i of a hit vector is inbound entry
i); the scratchpad memory (SPM) page at its base plus 0x5_0000 (nine 8-byte words);
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after the fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Inbound filter entries match on AxPROT[1] equality in both
polarities, fall through on a mismatch, decide each channel by its own AxPROT, match source ID 0
against AxUSER 0 and not against 5, and ignore group_id.

*Test Coverage*:

* `index.adoc` (Match, Then Permit) and `fabric.adoc` (Non-Secure Bit Filtering): `allow_ns` is an
equality test on `prot[1]`, not a permission. Entry 2 with `allow_ns` 0 admits a read with prot 0
(OKAY, the seeded word, hit bit 2) and refuses prot 0b010 with DECERR and a zero hit vector; with
`allow_ns` 1 the polarity reverses.
* Fall-through (`index.adoc`): with a deny entry 2 at `allow_ns` 0 and a permit entry 3 at
`allow_ns` 1, a prot 0b010 read does not select entry 2 and is admitted by entry 3 (hit bit 3 set,
bit 2 clear); a prot 0 read matches the deny entry 2 and is answered DECERR, its hit vector printed
and not compared.
* `fabric.adoc` (AXI Protection Bit Encoding): only `prot[1]` decides. With entry 2 at `allow_ns` 0
and entry 3 disabled, reads with prot 0, 1, 4 and 5 are OKAY with hit bit 2 and reads with prot 2,
3, 6 and 7 are DECERR with a zero hit vector.
* `index.adoc` (AW and AR decoded independently): with entry 2 at `allow_ns` 0 a prot 0 read and
write are admitted and a prot 0b010 read and write are refused; the refused write leaves the seeded
word and the admitted write lands 0xC0DE_0000_0000_5A5A, read back over SEP_IN.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`src_id`): `src_id` 0 is a wildcard and a non-zero value must equal the
transaction's source ID. An entry with `src_id` 0 admits the SYS_IN read presenting AxUSER 0 and an
entry with `src_id` 5 does not (DECERR, zero hit vector). Matching a non-zero source ID against a
wildcard entry is not reachable here because every SYS_IN master presents AxUSER 0, so it is not
claimed.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` and `index.adoc` (instance table): `group_id` matching is not built, so an entry
with `group_id` 10 still admits the read (OKAY, hit bit 2).
* Entry 0 and every lock stay untouched, and entries 2 and 3 return to their reset words.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), sample the three fuse and reset
probes, and start the hit watcher.
. Read inbound entries 2 and 3 over SEP_IN (`entry_enabled` clear, `START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR`
0x7), write a distinct seed word to each of the nine page words and read each back.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, programmed over the page with `allow_ns` 0
(0x0000_0000_0100_0013) and then with `allow_ns` 1 (0x0000_0000_0100_0113). Kind: a SYS_IN read
whose AxPROT[1] mismatches `allow_ns`, prot 0b010 in the first polarity and prot 0 in the second.
Expected response: DECERR with a zero hit vector, while the matching read in each polarity is OKAY.
Read prot 0 and prot 0b010 under `allow_ns` 0, then prot 0b010 and prot 0 under `allow_ns` 1.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2 programmed as the deny word 0x0000_0000_0100_0010 and
entry 3 as the permit word with `allow_ns` 1, both over the page. Kind: a prot 0 SYS_IN read that
matches the deny entry 2. Expected response: DECERR. Also read prot 0b010, whose hit vector must be
0x8.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2 programmed as `allow_ns` 0 permit, with entry 3
disabled. Kind: SYS_IN reads of word p of the page with prot p for p = 2, 3, 6 and 7, which carry
prot[1] set. Expected response: DECERR with a zero hit vector, while the reads with prot 0, 1, 4 and
5 are OKAY with hit bit 2. Read word p with prot p for p = 0 to 7 and compare each decision and hit
vector.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_IN write and read channels, with entry 2 at `allow_ns` 0. Kind:
a write and a read with prot 0b010. Expected response: both DECERR, with a SEP_IN readback of the
unchanged seed after the write. Also read prot 0 (admitted) and write prot 0 (OKAY) with a SEP_IN
readback of the new word.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2 programmed with `src_id` 5 (0x0000_0000_0105_0013).
Kind: a SYS_IN read presenting AxUSER 0 against the non-zero `src_id`. Expected response: DECERR
with a zero hit vector. Before it, program entry 2 with `src_id` 0 and read with AxUSER 0; after it,
program entry 2 with `group_id` 10 (0x0000_0000_01A0_0013) and read again.
. Restore `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of entries 2 and 3 to 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7,
stop the watcher, require at least 83 SEP_IN and SYS_IN accesses and print the ordered-fence line
and the wait record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-INB-NS0-EQUALITY` |With `allow_ns` 0 the prot 0 read is OKAY with the seeded word and hit bit
2 and the prot 0b010 read is DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-NS1-EQUALITY` |With `allow_ns` 1 the prot 0b010 read is OKAY with the seeded word and hit
bit 2 and the prot 0 read is DECERR with a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-NS-FALLTHROUGH` |The prot 0b010 read passes the `allow_ns` 0 deny entry 2 and is OKAY
through entry 3 with hit vector 0x8; the prot 0 read matches entry 2 and is DECERR, its hit vector
printed and not compared
|`CHK-INB-PROT-BITS-IGNORED` |Reads with prot 0, 1, 4 and 5 are OKAY with the seeded word and hit
bit 2, and reads with prot 2, 3, 6 and 7 are DECERR with a zero hit vector, so only `prot[1]`
decides
|`CHK-INB-NS-PER-CHANNEL` |The prot 0 read and write are OKAY with hit bit 2 of their own channel,
the prot 0b010 read and write are DECERR with a zero hit vector, the refused write leaves the seed
and the admitted write lands its word
|`CHK-INB-SRCID-WILDCARD-ZERO` |An entry with `src_id` 0 admits the read presenting AxUSER 0 (OKAY,
hit bit 2); the wildcard against a non-zero source ID is not exercised and not claimed
|`CHK-INB-SRCID-NONZERO-VS-ZERO` |An entry with `src_id` 5 does not match the read presenting AxUSER
0: DECERR and a zero hit vector
|`CHK-INB-GROUPID-INERT` |An entry with `group_id` 10 still admits the read: OKAY with hit bit 2
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 are recorded in order with strictly increasing time, each
checker line is printed after its step in the fixed order, and the SEP_IN plus SYS_IN access count
reaches the floor of 83; a control-flow invariant, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the fuse-sense bounds and the 50 us per-access bound of the SEP_IN and
SYS_IN accesses as a line; the compares are the bounded accesses themselves, so an expired bound
raises before this line, and the hit watcher is a passive sampler with no wait
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-INB-NS0-EQUALITY`, `CHK-INB-NS1-EQUALITY`, `CHK-INB-NS-FALLTHROUGH`,
`CHK-INB-PROT-BITS-IGNORED`, `CHK-INB-NS-PER-CHANNEL`, `CHK-INB-SRCID-WILDCARD-ZERO`,
`CHK-INB-SRCID-NONZERO-VS-ZERO` and `CHK-INB-GROUPID-INERT` hold: every admitted access is OKAY with
the seeded word and the programmed entry's hit bit, every refused access is DECERR with a zero hit
vector, and the admitted write lands. The isolate probes are printed with each access and not
compared. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after the access floor of 83. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The hit vector of the prot 0 read that matches the deny entry 2 is printed and not
compared. Matching a non-zero source ID against a wildcard `src_id` 0 entry is not reachable here,
because every SYS_IN master presents AxUSER 0, so it is not claimed. The isolate probes are printed
with each access and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-365-smc_infilt_default_liveness_test]]
===== 365 `smc_infilt_default_liveness_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_infilt_default_liveness_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SYS_IN) for the filtered traffic, singly and as outstanding
groups (`SmcSysAxiGroupItem`), the flood and reconfiguration groups under an `AxiTimingProfile` with
`b_ready_delay` 64, and `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) for programming, seeding and readbacks;
`tb_top` signals `sys_axi_arvalid`, `sys_axi_awvalid`, `sys_axi_awready`, `sys_axi_bvalid` and
`sys_axi_bready` with the inbound filter probes `tb_inb_read_hit`, `tb_inb_write_hit`,
`tb_inb_isolate_read` and `tb_inb_isolate_write`, sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise (bit i of a hit
vector is inbound entry i); targets `CHIP_CONFIG.VERSION_LO`, `SCRATCH_COLD` registers 1 to 6, the
scratchpad memory (SPM) pages at its base plus 0x1_0000 (page A) and plus 0x2_0000 (page D), and
inbound entries 1 to 4 and 7; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`
after the fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: With no entry programmed the inbound filter refuses SYS_IN and
leaves SEP_IN alone, and once an entry admits it stays live across enable and disable, simultaneous
ports, denied writes and a reconfiguration under load.

*Test Coverage*:

* `fabric.adoc` (Filtering and Protection, Fabric Topology) and `index.adoc` (instance table): the
SMC inbound filter blocks traffic that matches no entry and the SEP input is not filtered. At reset
a SYS_IN 4-byte read of `VERSION_LO` and a write to `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 are answered DECERR, the
scratch register keeps its seed, and SEP_IN reads `VERSION_LO` at its reset 0x000100A0 and the
seeded scratch word. Every blocked access has hit vector 0, and the read has the isolate probe set;
the readings are graded once an admitted access has set its entry's bit.
* Match Then Permit (`index.adoc`): an enabled entry that does not cover the registers (entry 3) and
an enabled entry whose `allow_ns` mismatches AxPROT[1] (entry 4) leave SYS_IN blocked with no hit
bit.
* Enable lifecycle (`fabric.adoc` Inbound Filtering, `index.adoc` `entry_enabled`): enabling entry 2
over 0xC000_0000..0xC0FF_FFFF admits SYS_IN (hit bit 2): the 8-byte read of entry 7 `FILTER_CONFIG`
returns its reset 0x3000 (`filter_ctrl.rdl`) and a scratch write and read round-trip 0x5A5A_2222;
clearing `entry_enabled` blocks the next read again with DECERR.
* Simultaneous ports (`fabric.adoc` Fabric Topology): eight SYS_IN reads of `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 to 4 in
one outstanding group run while eight SEP_IN accesses are issued; the two time windows must overlap
and all sixteen accesses complete OKAY with exact data inside the 50 us bound.
* Blocked transactions (`index.adoc`): with deny entry 1 over page D ahead of admitting entry 2, one
outstanding group [write D, write A, read D, read A, write A, write D] is answered DECERR, OKAY,
DECERR, OKAY, OKAY, DECERR, the page A read returns its seed, the page A writes read back over
SEP_IN and the page D words are unchanged.
* Forty denied writes to page D are issued outstanding under a delayed `bready`. Each error
subordinate holds 32 outstanding transactions (`fabric.adoc` transaction-limit table); all forty are
answered DECERR, the AW and B handshake counts are 40 each, the peak of AW minus B handshakes is at
least 2 and page D is unchanged.
* A SEP_IN write clearing `write_allowed` of entry 2 lands while twelve SYS_IN writes are
outstanding. The documents do not say from which point the new entry governs transactions already in
flight, so the leaf requires only consistency: each response is OKAY or
DECERR, each OKAY changed its word and each DECERR left it, there is at most one OKAY-to-DECERR
transition in issue order and none the other way, and at least one write was still outstanding when
the reconfiguration completed.
* Entries 1 to 4 and scratch registers 1 to 6 return to their reset words; entry 0 and every lock
stay untouched.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), sample the three fuse and reset
probes and start the watcher on the hit, isolate and `sys_axi` handshake signals.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of inbound entries 1 to 4 (`entry_enabled` clear), seed `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 to
6, four page A words, twelve reconfiguration words and eight page D words over SEP_IN.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_IN port, with no inbound entry programmed. Kind: a SYS_IN read of
`VERSION_LO` and a write to `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 that match no entry. Expected response: both must be
DECERR. Then read `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 and `VERSION_LO` over SEP_IN and compare.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entries 3 and 4, with entry 3 (0x0000_0000_0100_0013) programmed
over 0x0200_0000..0x0200_0FFF and entry 4 programmed with `allow_ns` 1 (0x0000_0000_0100_0113) over
the window. Kind: the SYS_IN read and write against an entry that does not cover the registers and
an entry whose `allow_ns` mismatches AxPROT[1]. Expected response: both must be DECERR.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 2, after it has admitted SYS_IN. Kind: the disabled word
0x0000_0000_0100_0003 written to entry 2, then a SYS_IN read of `VERSION_LO`. Expected response:
DECERR with hit vector 0. Before it, disable entries 3 and 4; program entry 2 over
0xC000_0000..0xC0FF_FFFF; SYS_IN read of entry 7 `FILTER_CONFIG` (0x3000, hit bit 2), write and read
`SCRATCH_COLD` 2 (0x5A5A_2222); grade the blocked readings; restore the scratch seed.
. Re-enable entry 2 and run the eight-read SYS_IN group against the SEP_IN write and read sequence
on `SCRATCH_COLD` 5 and 6, requiring overlap and exact data.
. Error injection. Point: inbound deny entry 1 (0x0000_0000_0100_0010), programmed over page D
ahead of admitting entry 2. Kind: the six-member outstanding group [write D, write A, read D, read A,
write A, write D], whose page D members match the deny entry. Expected response: the responses
[3, 0, 3, 0, 0, 3], the page D members DECERR and the page A members OKAY. Then read the page A and
page D words over SEP_IN.
. Error injection. Point: page D behind deny entry 1, driven from the SYS_IN port under the
64-cycle `bready` delay. Kind: forty denied writes issued outstanding. Expected response: forty DECERR
responses, 40 AW and 40 B handshakes and an overlap of at least 2. Then read the eight page D words
back.
. Re-enable entry 2, start twelve SYS_IN writes outstanding, write `FILTER_CONFIG` of entry 2 with
`write_allowed` clear (0x0000_0000_0100_0011) over SEP_IN, wait for the group, read the entry back,
read the twelve words and compare each with its response.
. Restore entries 1 to 4 and `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 to 6 to their reset words, read the entries back,
require no X/Z watcher sample and print the ordered-fence line and the wait record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-INB-RESET-BLOCKS-SYS-IN` |At reset the SYS_IN read of `VERSION_LO` and write to `SCRATCH_COLD`
1 are answered DECERR with hit vector 0 and the read has the isolate probe set, and `SCRATCH_COLD` 1
still reads its seed over SEP_IN
|`CHK-INB-UNMATCHED-STAYS-BLOCKED` |With entry 3 enabled over another range and entry 4 enabled with
a mismatching `allow_ns`, the SYS_IN read and write are still answered DECERR with no hit bit
|`CHK-INB-SEP-NOT-FILTERED` |While every SYS_IN access is refused, SEP_IN reads `VERSION_LO` as
0x000100A0 and `SCRATCH_COLD` 1 as its seeded word, both OKAY
|`CHK-INB-READ-FILTER-CONFIG` |Once entry 2 admits, the SYS_IN 8-byte read of inbound entry 7
`FILTER_CONFIG` returns 0x3000 with OKAY and hit bit 2
|`CHK-INB-ENABLE-LIFECYCLE` |SYS_IN is blocked before programming, admitted after entry 2 is enabled
over SEP_IN (the `SCRATCH_COLD` 2 round trip of 0x5A5A_2222 is exact with hit bit 2) and blocked
again, DECERR with hit vector 0, after `entry_enabled` is cleared
|`CHK-INB-SIMULTANEOUS-PORTS` |The eight SYS_IN reads and the eight SEP_IN accesses overlap in time
and all sixteen are OKAY with exact data inside the 50 us bound
|`CHK-INB-ADMIT-AFTER-DENY` |In the outstanding group the page D members are DECERR and the page A
members OKAY, in both orders, with the page A read returning its seed, the page A writes readable
and page D unchanged, all inside the bound
|`CHK-INB-DENY-FLOOD` |All forty denied writes are answered DECERR inside the per-access bound with
forty AW and forty B handshakes and an overlap of at least 2, and the page D words are unchanged
|`CHK-INB-RECONFIG-OUTSTANDING` |All twelve writes complete with OKAY or DECERR, each OKAY changed
its word and each DECERR left it, there is at most one OKAY-to-DECERR transition and no
DECERR-to-OKAY one, and a write was still outstanding at the reconfiguration; which writes the new
entry governs is not required
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 and the fence terms RESET_BLOCKED to RECONFIG are recorded
in order with strictly increasing time and each checker line is printed after its step; a
control-flow invariant, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the fuse-sense bounds, each group's join bound and the 50 us
per-access bound as a line; the compares are the bounded joins themselves, so an expired bound
raises before this line, and the watcher is a passive sampler with no wait
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-INB-RESET-BLOCKS-SYS-IN`, `CHK-INB-UNMATCHED-STAYS-BLOCKED`,
`CHK-INB-SEP-NOT-FILTERED`, `CHK-INB-READ-FILTER-CONFIG`, `CHK-INB-ENABLE-LIFECYCLE`,
`CHK-INB-SIMULTANEOUS-PORTS`, `CHK-INB-ADMIT-AFTER-DENY`, `CHK-INB-DENY-FLOOD` and
`CHK-INB-RECONFIG-OUTSTANDING` hold: SYS_IN is DECERR with a zero hit vector until an entry admits,
SEP_IN is never refused, the admitted accesses carry exact data and hit bit 2, the 74 SYS_IN
accesses of the run are all issued and every group completes inside its bound. `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after the last compare. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The documents do not say from which point a reconfigured entry governs transactions
already in flight, so which of the twelve outstanding writes the new entry governs is not required;
the leaf requires only that each response is OKAY or DECERR consistent with its word, with at most
one OKAY-to-DECERR transition in issue order and none the other way.

'''''

[[sec-366-smc_infilt_priority_deny_test]]
===== 366 `smc_infilt_priority_deny_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_infilt_priority_deny_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SYS_IN) for the reads, writes, 2-beat and 4-beat bursts, and
`ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) for the programming, seeding and word readbacks; `tb_top` signals
`sys_axi_arvalid`, `sys_axi_awvalid`, `sys_axi_rvalid`, `sys_axi_rready`, `sys_axi_rresp`,
`sys_axi_rlast`, `sys_axi_wvalid`, `sys_axi_wready`, `sys_axi_bvalid` and `sys_axi_bready` with the
inbound filter probes `tb_inb_read_hit`, `tb_inb_write_hit`, `tb_inb_isolate_read` and
`tb_inb_isolate_write`, sampled at every `clk_smc_i` rise (bit i of a hit vector is inbound entry
i); inbound entries 0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 14 and 15 and the scratchpad memory (SPM) pages at its base plus
0x6_0000 (page A), 0x7_0000 (page D) and 0x8_0000 onward (one page per entry pair);
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after the fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the overlap offsets and the channel (read or write) of the
overlapping-entry probes.

*Objective*: The lowest-numbered matching inbound entry alone decides a
transaction, each channel uses its own permission and entry, and every denied read and write
completes with DECERR on its response channel.

*Test Coverage*:

* `index.adoc` (Match, Then Permit): the lowest-numbered matching entry decides and its permission
bit alone is consulted. Deny entry 1 over permit entry 2 on page A answers a SYS_IN read and write
DECERR and the word keeps its seed; swapped to permit entry 1 over deny entry 2 the read returns the
seed and the write lands 0xC0DE_0000_..., both OKAY, with hit bits 1 and 2 both set.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`read_allowed`, `write_allowed`): with entry 1 read-only the read is OKAY and
the write to the same address DECERR with the word unchanged; with entry 1 write-only the write
lands and the read is DECERR.
* `index.adoc` (AW and AR decoded independently): at one address a prot 0b010 read selects deny
entry 1 (`allow_ns` 1, DECERR, read hit bit 1) while a prot 0 write selects permit entry 2 (OKAY,
write hit bit 2 set and bit 1 clear, word changed).
* Strict priority on the entry pairs (0, 1), (7, 8) and (14, 15): each pair is programmed with
overlapping ranges and probed in the overlap twice, once with the lower entry denying (DECERR) and
once permitting (OKAY); the offset in the overlap and the channel of each probe are drawn from the
run's seed and printed, and all six cells must be visited.
* `index.adoc` (Blocked Transactions): a denied transaction is steered to the error subordinate and
answered DECERR. A denied single-beat and 4-beat read on page D return DECERR on every returned beat
with RLAST on the last (the beat count is compared exactly, 1 and 4, and `rdata` is printed); a denied single-beat
and 2-beat write answer BRESP DECERR and the three target words still read their seeds over SEP_IN
(the W beats accepted before B are printed, not compared).
* The three denial classes (`fabric.adoc` Inbound Filtering, `index.adoc` instance table): no match
(entry disabled, DECERR, hit vector 0), a matching deny entry (DECERR, hit vector printed and not
compared) and a burst mismatch (an `allow_burst` 0 entry admits the single-beat read with hit bit 1
and refuses the 2-beat read with DECERR and hit vector 0).
* Entries 0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 14 and 15 return to their reset words; entry 0 is never locked and no entry
is locked.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), sample the three fuse and reset
probes and start the watcher on the SYS_IN handshakes and the hit and isolate probes.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of the seven entries (`entry_enabled` clear) and seed three page A words,
eight page D words and three words in each entry pair's overlap page over SEP_IN.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entries 1 (deny) and 2 (permit) over page A, probed from SYS_IN at
page A + 0x100. Kind: a read and a write through a denying entry ranked above a permitting one.
Expected response: both DECERR and the word keeps its seed. Then swap the two words (permit on 1,
deny on 2): read must return the seed and write must land, with hit bits 1 and 2 set; zero both
entries.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 1, programmed read-only (0x0000_0000_0100_0011) and then
write-only (0x0000_0000_0100_0012). Kind: a write through the read-only entry and a read through the
write-only entry. Expected response: read-only gives read OKAY and write DECERR with the word
unchanged; write-only gives write OKAY with the word changed and read DECERR. Zero the entry.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 1 deny with `allow_ns` 1 (0x0000_0000_0100_0110) above
permit entry 2, one address. Kind: a SYS_IN read with prot 0b010 that selects the deny entry.
Expected response: DECERR with hit bit 1, while the write with prot 0 at the same address must be
OKAY with hit bit 2 and not bit 1. Read the written word back over SEP_IN; zero both entries.
. Error injection. Point: each entry pair (0, 1), (7, 8) and (14, 15), lower entry deny and higher
entry permit over overlapping ranges. Kind: one probe at a seeded offset and channel in the overlap.
Expected response: DECERR. Swap the two decisions, probe again and require OKAY; zero the pair.
Require all six cells visited.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 1 programmed deny over page D. Kind: a SYS_IN single-beat
read and a 4-beat read through the deny entry. Expected response: DECERR on every returned beat with
RLAST on the last.
. Error injection. Point: the same deny entry 1 over page D. Kind: a SYS_IN single-beat write and a
2-beat write through the deny entry. Expected response: DECERR on both. Read the three words back
over SEP_IN and compare them with their seeds.
. Error injection. Point: inbound entry 1 over page D, disabled, then deny, then `allow_burst` 0
permit (0x13). Kind: a no-match read, a matching-deny read and a 2-beat read through the
single-beat-only entry. Expected response: DECERR with hit vector 0 for the no-match read, DECERR for
the deny read, and after the single-beat read is OKAY with hit bit 1 the 2-beat read is DECERR with
hit vector 0.
. Restore all seven entries to 0x3000, 0x0 and 0x7 and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back, stop the watcher,
require exactly 24 SYS_IN accesses and at least 150 accesses in total, and print the ordered-fence
line and the wait record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-INB-PRIO-DENY-OVER-PERMIT` |With deny entry 1 over permit entry 2 the SYS_IN read and write
are both answered DECERR and the word still reads its seed over SEP_IN
|`CHK-INB-PRIO-PERMIT-OVER-DENY` |With permit entry 1 over deny entry 2 the SYS_IN read returns the
seed and the write lands its word, both OKAY, and both entries' hit bits are set on each channel
|`CHK-INB-PER-CHANNEL` |With a read-only entry the read is OKAY with the seed and the write DECERR
with the word unchanged; with a write-only entry the write is OKAY with the word changed and the
read DECERR
|`CHK-INB-RD-WR-DIFF-ENTRY` |At one address the prot 0b010 read selects deny entry 1 (DECERR, read
hit bit 1) and the prot 0 write selects permit entry 2 (OKAY, write hit bit 2 set and bit 1 clear)
|`CHK-INB-PRIO-PAIRS` |In each of the pairs (0, 1), (7, 8) and (14, 15) the overlap probe is DECERR
when the lower entry denies and OKAY when it permits, a write probe leaving the seed or landing its
word accordingly, and all six cells are visited
|`CHK-INB-DENY-READ-RRESP` |The denied single-beat and 4-beat reads return exactly 1 and 4 R beats,
every returned beat carries RRESP DECERR and the last carries RLAST; the beat count is compared exactly
and the read data is printed
|`CHK-INB-DENY-WRITE-BRESP` |The denied single-beat and 2-beat writes are answered BRESP DECERR and
the three target words still read their seeds; the W beats accepted before B are printed and not
compared
|`CHK-INB-DENY-CLASSES` |The no-match read, the matching-deny read and the burst-mismatch read are
each answered DECERR, the no-match and burst-mismatch reads with hit vector 0 and the single-beat
read through the `allow_burst` 0 entry OKAY with hit bit 1; the hit vector of the deny class is
printed and not compared
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 are recorded in order with strictly increasing time, each
checker line is printed after its step in the fixed order, exactly 24 SYS_IN accesses were issued
and the total reaches the floor of 150; a control-flow invariant, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the fuse-sense bounds and the 50 us per-access bound of the SEP_IN and
SYS_IN accesses as a line; the compares are the bounded accesses themselves, so an expired bound
raises before this line, and the watcher is a passive sampler with no wait
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-INB-PRIO-DENY-OVER-PERMIT`, `CHK-INB-PRIO-PERMIT-OVER-DENY`,
`CHK-INB-PER-CHANNEL`, `CHK-INB-RD-WR-DIFF-ENTRY`, `CHK-INB-PRIO-PAIRS`, `CHK-INB-DENY-READ-RRESP`,
`CHK-INB-DENY-WRITE-BRESP` and `CHK-INB-DENY-CLASSES` hold: the lower-numbered entry decides every
overlap, each channel follows its own permission bit and entry, every denied access ends in DECERR
with the denied words unchanged, and the admitted accesses return their seeds. `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed after the access floor of 150. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The read data of the denied single-beat and 4-beat reads, the W beats accepted
before B on the denied writes, and the hit vector of the matching-deny class are printed and not
compared.

'''''

[[sec-367-smc_outfilt_addr_match_test]]
===== 367 `smc_outfilt_addr_match_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_outfilt_addr_match_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, JTAG) for the 8-byte probe writes and `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI,
SEP_IN) for programming outbound entry 1 and reading entries 0 and 1; SYS_OUT responder memory
(`sys_out_mem` backdoor, a sentinel preset at every probe address) and the `tb_top` probes
`tb_output_axi_write_count`, `tb_output_axi_read_count`, `tb_output_axi_last_addr`,
`tb_output_axi_last_wdata`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid` and
`tb_output_axi_arvalid`, with the three valids counted at every `clk_smc_i` rise; outbound
`FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of entry 1; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after the fuse-sense wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: An outbound deny entry catches exactly its widened address range
when enabled, at 56 bits and across granules, and nothing when disabled.

*Test Coverage*:

* `fabric.adoc` (Outbound Filtering) and `index.adoc` (instance table): the SMC outbound filter
permits traffic that matches no entry, so entry 1 is programmed as a deny entry (`entry_enabled`
set, `read_allowed` and `write_allowed` clear). A match is DECERR, leaves the SYS_OUT word at its
sentinel and leaves the SYS_OUT write count and the SYS_OUT AW and W valids unchanged; a miss is
OKAY, lands the word and raises the write count by one.
* `index.adoc` (Address Range Granule): with `allow_burst` 1 the range 0x0200_4000..0x0200_4FFF
denies 0x0200_4800 and admits 0x0200_3FF8 and 0x0200_5000; with `allow_burst` 0 the range
0x0200_6040..0x0200_6047 denies 0x0200_6040 and admits 0x0200_6038 and 0x0200_6048.
* `index.adoc` (`entry_enabled`): with `entry_enabled` clear the same range admits 0x0200_4800
although its permissions would deny it.
* `fabric.adoc` (Filtering and Protection, 56-bit addresses): an entry over
0x00AB_0200_4000..0x00AB_0200_4FFF denies 0x00AB_0200_4800 and admits 0x0000_0200_4800 and
0x00CD_0200_4800, which differ in bits [55:32].
* `index.adoc`: a four-granule span 0x0200_8000..0x0200_BFFF denies 0x0200_8000, 0x0200_9FF8 and
0x0200_BFF8 and admits 0x0200_7FF8 and 0x0200_C000; `START_ADDR` equal to `END_ADDR` admits the
whole granule, 8 bytes with `allow_burst` 0 (0x0200_C008 denied, 0x0200_C000 and 0x0200_C010
admitted) and 4 KB with `allow_burst` 1 (0x0200_D123 denies 0x0200_D000 and 0x0200_DFF8 and admits
0x0200_CFF8 and 0x0200_E000).
* `index.adoc` (granule widening example, `START_ADDR` 0x0FFF and `END_ADDR` 0x1000 on two
granules): `START_ADDR` 0x0200_0FFF and `END_ADDR` 0x0200_1000 read back unchanged, and the entry
denies 0x0200_0000 and 0x0200_1FF8 and admits 0x01FF_FFF8 and 0x0200_2000.
* Every case disables entry 1 again, entries 0 and 1 read their reset words and are not enabled at
the start, and the cleanup writes the entry's reset words back.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), require the three fuse and reset
probes resolvable and start the SYS_OUT valid counters.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` of outbound entries 0 and 1, compare them with
the reset words and require both entries not enabled; preset the sentinel 0x5A5A_5A5A_5A5A_5A5A in
SYS_OUT memory at all 26 probe addresses and read it back.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 over 0x0200_4000..0x0200_4FFF with `allow_burst` 1
(case 1) and over 0x0200_6040..0x0200_6047 with `allow_burst` 0 (case 2). Kind: JTAG writes at the
three probes of each case, one inside the widened range and two just outside it. Expected response:
the inside probe (0x0200_4800, then 0x0200_6040) is DECERR and the outside probes (0x0200_3FF8 and
0x0200_5000, then 0x0200_6038 and 0x0200_6048) are OKAY. For each case disable entry 1, write
`START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR` and `FILTER_CONFIG` and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back before the probes, and
disable the entry after the case.
. Case 3: program the 4 KB range with `entry_enabled` clear and JTAG-write 0x0200_4800.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 over the 56-bit range
0x00AB_0200_4000..0x00AB_0200_4FFF (case 4). Kind: JTAG writes at 0x00AB_0200_4800, 0x0000_0200_4800
and 0x00CD_0200_4800. Expected response: the first is DECERR and the two that differ in bits [55:32]
are OKAY.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 over the four-granule span 0x0200_8000..0x0200_BFFF
(case 5). Kind: JTAG writes at its five probes. Expected response: 0x0200_8000, 0x0200_9FF8 and
0x0200_BFF8 DECERR; 0x0200_7FF8 and 0x0200_C000 OKAY.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 with `START_ADDR` equal to `END_ADDR`, at
0x0200_C008 (`allow_burst` 0) and then at 0x0200_D123 (`allow_burst` 1) (case 6). Kind: JTAG writes
at three, then four, probe addresses around the single granule. Expected response: 0x0200_C008 DECERR with
0x0200_C000 and 0x0200_C010 OKAY for the 8-byte granule; 0x0200_D000 and 0x0200_DFF8 DECERR with
0x0200_CFF8 and 0x0200_E000 OKAY for the 4 KB granule.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 with `START_ADDR` 0x0200_0FFF and `END_ADDR`
0x0200_1000, which widen onto two granules (case 7). Kind: JTAG writes at four probe addresses
around the widened pair of granules. Expected response: 0x0200_0000 and 0x0200_1FF8 DECERR;
0x01FF_FFF8 and 0x0200_2000 OKAY. First write `FILTER_CONFIG` with `allow_burst` set and
`entry_enabled` clear, write the two addresses, read both back and require them unchanged, then
enable the deny entry before the probes.
. For each probe: a denied write must answer DECERR, hold the SYS_OUT write count for 64 `clk_smc_i`
cycles, keep the sentinel and raise no SYS_OUT AW or W valid; an admitted write must answer OKAY,
raise the write count by exactly one with the probe address and data (bounded poll of 200
`clk_smc_i` cycles), land the word and raise the SYS_OUT AW and W valids.
. Write the reset words back to entry 1 (`FILTER_CONFIG` disabled), read each back and compare,
require at least 52 SEP_IN accesses and exactly 26 JTAG writes, then print the wait record and the
ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OUT-ADDR-GRANULE` |With `allow_burst` 1 the write at 0x0200_4800 is DECERR and those at
0x0200_3FF8 and 0x0200_5000 are OKAY and land, and with `allow_burst` 0 the write at 0x0200_6040 is
DECERR and those at 0x0200_6038 and 0x0200_6048 are OKAY and land; a denied write keeps the sentinel
and leaves the write count unchanged
|`CHK-OUT-DISABLED-NO-MATCH` |With `entry_enabled` clear the write at 0x0200_4800 is OKAY and lands
although the range and the clear permissions would deny it
|`CHK-OUT-HIGH-ADDRESS-BITS` |The write at 0x00AB_0200_4800 is DECERR and the writes at
0x0000_0200_4800 and 0x00CD_0200_4800, which differ in bits [55:32], are OKAY and land
|`CHK-OUT-SPAN-WHOLE` |The writes at 0x0200_8000, 0x0200_9FF8 and 0x0200_BFF8 are DECERR and the
writes at 0x0200_7FF8 and 0x0200_C000 are OKAY and land
|`CHK-OUT-START-EQ-END` |`START_ADDR` equal to `END_ADDR` matches the whole granule: 0x0200_C008 is
DECERR and 0x0200_C000 and 0x0200_C010 OKAY for the 8-byte granule; 0x0200_D000 and 0x0200_DFF8 are
DECERR and 0x0200_CFF8 and 0x0200_E000 OKAY for the 4 KB granule
|`CHK-GRANULE-MULTI-ADMIT` |`START_ADDR` 0x0200_0FFF and `END_ADDR` 0x0200_1000 read back unchanged,
writes at 0x0200_0000 and 0x0200_1FF8 are DECERR and writes at 0x01FF_FFF8 and 0x0200_2000 are OKAY
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms SENTINELS_SEEDED, C1_C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7 and CLEANED are stamped
in order with strictly increasing time, each checker line is printed after its term, and the SEP_IN
and JTAG access counts reach their floors of 52 and 26; a control-flow invariant, not a DUT compare
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One entry per bounded wait the run took -- fuse-sense, JTAG and SEP_IN access
bounds, the 64-cycle write-count hold and the 200-cycle responder poll; the compares are the bounded
waits themselves, so an expired bound raises before this line
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-OUT-ADDR-GRANULE`, `CHK-OUT-DISABLED-NO-MATCH`, `CHK-OUT-HIGH-ADDRESS-BITS`,
`CHK-OUT-SPAN-WHOLE`, `CHK-OUT-START-EQ-END` and `CHK-GRANULE-MULTI-ADMIT` hold: every probe inside
a widened range is DECERR with the sentinel kept and the write count unchanged, every probe outside
it or with the entry disabled is OKAY with its word landed, and the unaligned `START_ADDR` and
`END_ADDR` of the last case read back unchanged. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed
after both access floors. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-368-smc_outfilt_attr_match_test]]
===== 368 `smc_outfilt_attr_match_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_outfilt_attr_match_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, JTAG) for the 8-byte probe writes with a chosen AxPROT and beat
count and `ocah_axi_vip` (AXI, SEP_IN) for programming outbound entries 1 to 3, the M-mode and
Xvisor output remap `REGION_ATTRS` of region 0 and the cleanup; SYS_OUT responder memory
(`sys_out_mem` backdoor, a sentinel preset at every probe address) and the `tb_top` probes
`tb_output_axi_write_count`, `tb_output_axi_read_count`, `tb_output_axi_last_addr`,
`tb_output_axi_last_wdata`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid` and
`tb_output_axi_arvalid`, with the three valids counted at every `clk_smc_i` rise, and
`u_output_axi_if` members `awvalid`, `awready`, `awaddr`, `awprot` and `awlen` sampled at the AW
handshake; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` after the fuse-sense
wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Outbound deny entries match on AxPROT[1] equality and on burst
length, fall through on a mismatch, match source ID 0 on every output path, and ignore group_id.

*Test Coverage*:

* `fabric.adoc` (Non-Secure Bit Filtering) and `index.adoc` (Match, Then Permit): `allow_ns` is an
equality test on `prot[1]`. The SMC outbound filter permits traffic that matches no entry, so entry
1 is a deny entry (`entry_enabled` set, permissions clear). With `allow_ns` 0 a prot 0 write is
DECERR and a prot 0b010 write is OKAY and lands; with `allow_ns` 1 the polarity reverses. A match
leaves the SYS_OUT sentinel and the SYS_OUT write count unchanged and raises no AW or W valid.
* Fall-through (`index.adoc`): with permit entry 1 at `allow_ns` 0 and deny entry 2 at `allow_ns` 1
over the same range, a prot 0b010 write does not select entry 1 and is refused by entry 2 (DECERR),
and a prot 0 write matches permit entry 1 and lands.
* `fabric.adoc` (AXI Protection Bit Encoding): only `prot[1]` decides. With an `allow_ns` 0 deny
entry and entry 2 disabled, writes with prot 0, 1, 4 and 5 are DECERR and writes with prot 2, 3, 6
and 7 are OKAY and land, and the `awprot` seen at the SYS_OUT AW handshake equals the prot driven.
* `index.adoc` (`allow_burst`): an `allow_burst` 0 deny entry matches only single beats, so over
0x0200_6000..0x0200_6007 a single-beat write is DECERR and a 2-beat INCR write matches no entry and
lands both beats with `awlen` 1; an `allow_burst` 1 deny entry over 0x0200_7000..0x0200_7FFF refuses
a single-beat write and a 2-beat write. A 2-beat write that the `allow_burst` 0 entry 1 does not
select falls through to the `allow_burst` 1 entry 2 and is DECERR.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` (`src_id` 0 is a wildcard) and `fabric.adoc` (output remaps; source ID by
traffic path): deny entries 1 to 3 with `src_id` 0 over the direct path (0x0200_A000..0x0200_AFFF)
and over the post-remap addresses of the M-mode window (0xC100_0100 into 0x0240_0000..0x0240_0FFF)
and the Xvisor window (0xC180_0100 into 0x0260_0000..0x0260_0FFF) refuse writes on all three paths,
each of which carries a different source ID, and the three sentinels are kept. With the deny
entries disabled, the same writes through the M-mode and Xvisor windows are first shown to land at
their remapped addresses, so the refusal is the filter's. The remap
`REGION_ATTRS` words 0x8000_0000_0240_0000 and 0x8000_0000_0260_0000 (`output_remap.rdl`) are
written and read back first.
* `filter_ctrl.rdl` and `index.adoc` (instance table): `group_id` matching is not built, so an entry
with `group_id` 7 still matches and refuses the write.
* Entries 1 to 3 and both remap regions are restored to their reset words and read back.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles bound), require the three fuse and reset
probes resolvable and start the SYS_OUT valid and AW-handshake watcher.
. Read `FILTER_CONFIG` of outbound entries 1 to 3 (reset word, not enabled) and preset the sentinel
0x5A5A_5A5A_5A5A_5A5A in SYS_OUT memory at every probe address and read it back.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 1 as an `allow_ns` 0 deny (0x0000_0000_0100_0010) over
0x0200_4000..0x0200_4FFF, then reprogrammed `allow_ns` 1 (0x0000_0000_0100_0110). Kind: JTAG writes
whose prot[1] equals the entry's `allow_ns`, beside writes whose prot[1] differs. Expected response:
with `allow_ns` 0 the prot 0 write at 0x0200_4800 is DECERR and the prot 0b010 write at 0x0200_4808
OKAY; with `allow_ns` 1 the prot 0b010 write at 0x0200_4810 is DECERR and the prot 0 write at
0x0200_4818 OKAY.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 1 as the permit word 0x0000_0000_0100_0013 and entry 2 as
the `allow_ns` 1 deny over the same range. Kind: a prot 0b010 JTAG write at 0x0200_4820 that permit
entry 1 does not select. Expected response: DECERR from entry 2, while the prot 0 write at
0x0200_4828 matches entry 1 and is OKAY.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 1 as an `allow_ns` 0 deny with entry 2 disabled. Kind: JTAG
writes at 0x0200_4830 + 8 * p with prot p for p = 0 to 7. Expected response: DECERR for p = 0, 1, 4,
5 and OKAY with the driven `awprot` for the rest.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 with `allow_burst` 0 over 0x0200_6000..0x0200_6007,
then `allow_burst` 1 over 0x0200_7000..0x0200_7FFF. Kind: a single-beat and a 2-beat JTAG write at
0x0200_6000, then a single-beat write at 0x0200_7000 and a 2-beat write at 0x0200_7100. Expected
response: with `allow_burst` 0 the single beat is DECERR and the 2-beat write matches no entry and
lands; with `allow_burst` 1 both writes are DECERR.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entry 1 `allow_burst` 0 over 0x0200_7000..0x0200_7007 and entry 2
`allow_burst` 1 over 0x0200_7000..0x0200_7FFF. Kind: a 2-beat JTAG write at 0x0200_7000 that entry
1 does not select. Expected response: DECERR from entry 2.
. Error injection. Point: outbound entries 1 to 3 as `src_id` 0 deny entries over the direct range
and the post-remap ranges of the M-mode and Xvisor windows. Kind: JTAG writes at 0x0200_A800,
0xC100_0100 and 0xC180_0100, one per output path. Expected response: each DECERR with the sentinels
at 0x0200_A800, 0x0240_0100 and 0x0260_0100 unchanged. Before the deny entries are programmed, write
and read back the M-mode and Xvisor `REGION_ATTRS` and JTAG-write 0xC100_0100 and 0xC180_0100 with
no deny entry programmed, requiring OKAY with the words landed at 0x0240_0100 and 0x0260_0100.
. Error injection. Point: outbound deny entry 1 with `group_id` 7 (0x0000_0000_0170_0010) over
0x0200_B000..0x0200_BFFF. Kind: a JTAG write at 0x0200_B800. Expected response: DECERR, the entry
still matching.
. For each probe: a denied write must hold the SYS_OUT write count for 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles, keep
every sentinel and raise no AW or W valid; an admitted write must raise the write count by exactly
one with the last address and data (200-cycle poll), land every beat and present exactly one AW
handshake of the driven address, prot and `awlen`.
. Write the reset words back to entries 1 to 3 and the two remap regions, read each back, require at
least 90 SEP_IN accesses and exactly 23 JTAG writes, then print the wait record and the
ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
