  the four `CHIP_CONFIG` words, requiring OKAY, the seeded words and the values read in step 1.
. In one `clk_smc_i` cycle start a SEP_IN group of 4 `SCRATCH_COLD` reads and a JTAG group of 4
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM` reads, join both within 50 000 ns and require OKAY and each word.
. Issue 8 outstanding reads of SPM words 0 to 7, requiring OKAY and each word.
. Issue 9 and then 16 outstanding reads of SPM words, requiring OKAY and each word.
. Issue 24 interleaved reads over SPM words 0 to 7, `SCRATCH_COLD` words 0 to 7 and
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM` words 0 to 7, requiring OKAY and the word of each address.
. Issue one group of 8 reads of SPM words 0 to 7 interleaved with 8 writes of new words to SPM words
  8 to 15, requiring OKAY, then read the 8 written words back singly with exact compares.
. Write 0 to the scratch and warm scratch words, stop the stall watcher and print the stall totals;
  log the bounded waits and require the ten step stamps in increasing order, the eight checker lines
  in order, at least 170 accesses and at least 110 scoreboard exact-value compares.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-XLIM-LITE-N4` |The 4 outstanding SEP_IN reads of `SCRATCH_COLD` words 0 to 3 complete OKAY
within the guard, each returning 0xC0DE_0500 + i; the stall cycles are printed
|`CHK-XLIM-LITE-OVER` |The 5-read and the 8-read `SCRATCH_COLD` groups complete OKAY, each
read returning its own register's word; the limit of 4 is not asserted and the stall
cycles are printed, not compared
|`CHK-XLIM-LITE-MULTI` |The 12 interleaved reads over `SCRATCH_COLD`, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM`
and `CHIP_CONFIG` complete OKAY with 0xC0DE_0500 + i, 0xC0DE_0600 + i and the
`CHIP_CONFIG` values read at the start (`VERSION_LO`, `VERSION_HI` and `CHIP_ID` equal their
`chip_config.rdl` resets; only `LC_STATE` is compared with its first reading)
|`CHK-XLIM-LITE-TWO-MGR` |The SEP_IN group of 4 and the JTAG group of 4 started in one
cycle both complete OKAY within the guard, each read returning its own word; the
SEP_IN stall cycles are printed
|`CHK-XLIM-LOCAL-N8` |The 8 outstanding SPM reads complete OKAY within the guard, each returning the
word seeded at its address; the stall cycles are printed
|`CHK-XLIM-LOCAL-OVER` |The 9-read and the 16-read SPM groups complete OKAY, each read returning the
word of its address; the limit of 8 is not asserted and the stall cycles are printed, not compared
|`CHK-XLIM-LOCAL-MULTI` |The 24 interleaved reads over the SPM, `SCRATCH_COLD`
and `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM` complete OKAY, each returning the word of its own
address; the stall cycles are printed
|`CHK-XLIM-LOCAL-MIXED` |The 16-member group of 8 SPM reads and 8 SPM writes completes
OKAY, the reads return the seeded words and the 8 written words read back exactly as
written; the stall cycles are printed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ten steps were stamped in strictly increasing time, each checker line was printed
in order and no earlier than its step, and the access floor of 170 and the scoreboard's floor of 110
exact-value compares were reached; a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated run
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits of the run (the three fuse and reset waits at
200 000 `clk_smc_i` cycles, each AXI access at 50 000 ns with no timeout allowed, the
two-manager joins at 50 000 ns and the watcher join at 1 000 ns); the expiry of any raises, so
the line is a record and not a compare
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every read in every group, at and above the limits, completes OKAY with the word of
its own address, the `CHIP_CONFIG` reads equal their first values, the mixed group's written words
read back exactly, and at least 110 exact-value compares are booked over at least 170 accesses. The
stall cycles around each limit are recorded without an expected count. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The stall cycles around each crossbar limit are printed and not asserted, because
the document gives the limits but not whether an access past a limit stalls or errors.

'''''

[[sec-387-smc_axi_channel_timing_ports_test]]
===== 387 `smc_axi_channel_timing_ports_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_axi_channel_timing_ports_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` managers on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`), SYS_IN
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) and JTAG (`env.jtag_axi_agent`), each item carrying an `AxiTimingProfile`
(`aw_delay`, `w_delay`, `ar_delay`, `b_ready_delay`, `r_ready_delay`); a clocked port watch
sampled on the falling edge of `clk_smc_i` over the `s_axi_*`, `sys_axi_*` and `jtag_axi_*` AW, W,
AR, B and R valid/ready lines and `rlast`; the R-hold drives `tb_sep_axi_r_hold` and
`tb_sys_axi_r_hold` with the raw R valid probes `tb_sep_axi_r_raw_valid` and
`tb_sys_axi_r_raw_valid` (JTAG has no hold drive); the inbound filter probes `tb_inb_write_hit`,
`tb_inb_read_hit`, `tb_inb_isolate_write` and `tb_inb_isolate_read` sampled on SYS_IN;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for the fuse-sense wait; the
scoreboard's per-bus access counts and exact-value compare count

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only timing: the AW-to-W skew and the AR
delays of the random step on each port; every access must complete once with its data whatever the
timing.

*Objective*: On SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG the AW and W channels are skewed
in both orders, BREADY and RREADY are held and AW, W and AR are randomly delayed, and every access
still completes OKAY with the word of its own address.

*Test Coverage*:

* A write whose W reaches the port four cycles ahead of AW completes on every port: a 4-byte write
  to `SCRATCH_COLD(k)` (`scratch.rdl`, `SCRATCH` is `sw=rw`, 32 bits, reset 0) reads back
  0xC0DE_1000+k, and on SEP_IN an 8-beat INCR write of 8-byte beats in the SPM reads back beat by
  beat in order (`fabric.adoc`, Topology). The watch requires W to be presented before AW on each
  of these writes.
* A write whose AW leads W by four cycles completes the same way, 0xC0DE_2000+k at
  `SCRATCH_COLD(k+3)` and, on SEP_IN, an 8-beat INCR burst, so both channel orders are accepted
  (`fabric.adoc`, Topology). The watch requires AW to be presented before W on each of these
  writes.
* Four single writes queued as one group with W held back 16 cycles are all accepted: at least two
  AW handshakes are seen before the first W handshake and `SCRATCH_COLD(4..7)` reads
  0xC0DE_3004..0xC0DE_3007.
* Eight outstanding 8-byte writes per port under a 64-cycle BREADY hold all complete OKAY, the
  port watch sees at least one B stall cycle and at least eight B handshakes, and each word reads
  back as written (`fabric.adoc`, Configuration Parameters, transaction limits).
* A 4-beat 8-byte read per port under a 32-cycle RREADY hold returns the four words in order with
  RLAST on the fourth beat only; on SEP_IN and SYS_IN the R-hold drive additionally pulses for
  eight cycles after each beat; at least one R stall cycle is seen (`fabric.adoc`, Configuration
  Parameters).
* Per port two groups of eight writes and eight reads at distinct addresses, once with a random
  `aw_delay` (1 to 8) and once with a random `w_delay` (1 to 8), each also with a random
  `ar_delay` (0 to 8), return for every read the word its own address was seeded with; the run's
  seed and the drawn delays are printed.
* The inbound filter entry 0 is opened for pass-all over SEP_IN as setup and returned to its
  `filter_ctrl.rdl` reset values (`FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000, `START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR` 0x7) at the
  end.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to be high, each
within 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, and record their values; over SEP_IN write inbound filter entry 0
with 8-byte writes of `START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR` 0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF and a `FILTER_CONFIG`
that allows reads and writes, enabled, data bus width 3 and burst allowed; start one port watch
per port.
. For each port k in SEP_IN, SYS_IN, JTAG: write 0xC0DE_1000+k to `SCRATCH_COLD(k)` with
`aw_delay`=4, print the AW-to-W lead measured by the watch, and read the register back and
compare.
. On SEP_IN write an 8-beat INCR burst of 8-byte beats at the SPM base plus 0x7_0000 with
`aw_delay`=4 (beat i is 0xC2 in the top byte, i in bits 32 up, 0xC0DE_0000 and i in the low word)
and read it back as one 8-beat burst; print `CHK-CTP-W-FIRST`.
. For each port k write 0xC0DE_2000+k to `SCRATCH_COLD(k+3)` with `w_delay`=4 and read it back.
. On SEP_IN write and read back an 8-beat INCR burst at the SPM base plus 0x7_0400 with
`w_delay`=4 and prefix 0xC3; print `CHK-CTP-AW-FIRST`.
. On SEP_IN issue one group of four single writes of 0xC0DE_3000+i to `SCRATCH_COLD(i)`, i = 4..7,
with `w_delay`=16, read the four registers back, and require at least two AW handshakes before the
first W handshake; print `CHK-CTP-AW-QUEUE`.
. For each port k issue one group of eight 8-byte writes of distinct words at the SPM base plus
0x7_0000 plus 0x1000*(k+1) with `b_ready_delay`=64, read the eight words back singly, and require
at least eight B handshakes and at least one B stall cycle on the port; print
`CHK-CTP-BREADY-PORTS`.
. For each port k read four 8-byte beats at the same address with `r_ready_delay`=32 and compare
the four words in order; on SEP_IN and SYS_IN run the R-hold pulse driver for the four beats, each
pulse eight `clk_smc_i` cycles long once a beat's raw R valid is seen, each wait bounded at 2000
rises; require RLAST to be 0, 0, 0, 1 and at least one R stall cycle; print
`CHK-CTP-RREADY-BEATS`.
. Print the run's random seed. For each port k seed eight words, then run two groups of eight
writes and eight reads with random AW-lead or W-lead delay and a random `ar_delay`, read the eight
written words back after each group, and require the drawn AW, W and AR delays to be non-zero in
total; print `CHK-CTP-RANDOM-STALLS` with the seed and the drawn delays.
. Write `SCRATCH_COLD(0..7)` to 0 and restore inbound filter entry 0 `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR`
and `END_ADDR` to their reset values; stop the watches and require no X/Z probe sample on any of
them.
. Require 257 accesses against the sequence's own count, the scoreboard to have checked at least
that many SYS_IN items, then print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CTP-W-FIRST` |On each port the W-first register write answers OKAY within the per-access
guard and the read returns 0xC0DE_1000+k, and the SEP_IN W-first 8-beat burst answers OKAY and every
beat reads back in order; on each of these writes W is presented before AW and the AW-to-W lead is
printed.
|`CHK-CTP-AW-FIRST` |On each port the AW-first register write answers OKAY and reads back
0xC0DE_2000+k, and the SEP_IN AW-first 8-beat burst answers OKAY and every beat reads back in
order; on each of these writes AW is presented before W and the lead is printed.
|`CHK-CTP-AW-QUEUE` |The watch counts at least two AW handshakes before the first W handshake of
the group, all four writes answer OKAY and `SCRATCH_COLD(4..7)` reads 0xC0DE_3004..0xC0DE_3007;
fewer AW handshakes fail the run.
|`CHK-CTP-BREADY-PORTS` |On each port the eight writes answer OKAY under the 64-cycle BREADY hold,
the watch counts at least eight B handshakes and at least one B stall cycle, and every word reads
back equal to the word written.
|`CHK-CTP-RREADY-BEATS` |On each port the 4-beat read returns the four words written in the BREADY
step in order with RLAST on the fourth beat only, and the watch counts at least one R stall cycle;
the R-hold pulses on SEP_IN and SYS_IN each end with the beat accepted within its bound.
|`CHK-CTP-RANDOM-STALLS` |On each port all accesses of both groups answer OKAY, every read returns
the word its own address was seeded with and every written word reads back, and the delays drawn
for AW, W and AR are each non-zero in total; the seed and the drawn delays are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S10 are in increasing time order, the six checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, at least 257 accesses were issued, the
scoreboard's per-bus access counts equal the issued counts on SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG, and its
exact-value compare count covers every read that carried an expectation.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports the bound of every wait the leaf makes (the three fuse-sense waits
of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, the R-hold pulse waits of 2000 rises per beat, the two-rise watch
stop and the 50 us per-access guard) together with the last observed values; it is a printed
report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CTP-W-FIRST`, `CHK-CTP-AW-FIRST`, `CHK-CTP-AW-QUEUE`,
`CHK-CTP-BREADY-PORTS`, `CHK-CTP-RREADY-BEATS`, `CHK-CTP-RANDOM-STALLS`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; every access on the three ports answers OKAY with the exact
expected word, the AW-queue step shows at least two AW handshakes ahead of the first W, each port
stalls B and R at least once, no watch sample is X/Z, and 257 accesses are booked by the
scoreboard. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The AW-to-W lead measured on each skewed write is printed without a compare.

'''''

[[sec-388-smc_axi_contested_ports_test]]
===== 388 `smc_axi_contested_ports_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_axi_contested_ports_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` managers on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`), SYS_IN
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) and JTAG (`env.jtag_axi_agent`); one cocotb task per port released from
the same `clk_smc_i` rising edge; `AxiTimingProfile` `r_ready_delay` and `w_delay`; sampled
`s_axi_*`, `sys_axi_*` and `jtag_axi_*` `arvalid`, and for SEP_IN `arready`, `awvalid`, `wvalid`,
`rvalid`, `rready`; SYS_IN filter probes `tb_inb_read_hit` and `tb_inb_isolate_read`; the reset
agent (`env.reset_agent`, `SmcResetOp.COOL_RST_LO` and `COOL_RST_HI`) with
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no` sampled on `clk_ref_i`; `env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Reads released from one clock edge on two and three inbound
ports, a held read with requests behind it, a local and a global window read, and a cool reset
during an access all leave every port answering correctly.

*Test Coverage*:

* A SEP_IN and a SYS_IN read of `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` (`scratch.rdl`, `SCRATCH` is `sw=rw`, reset 0)
  released from one `clk_smc_i` edge both answer OKAY with the written word 0xC0DE_0A00 in each of
  16 rounds, and the ARVALID of the two ports rises in the same cycle (`fabric.adoc`, Topology).
* The same read from SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG together answers OKAY with 0xC0DE_0A00 on every port
  in each of 16 rounds, with zero ARVALID skew (`fabric.adoc`, Topology; `port_table.adoc`, AXI
  port rows).
* A SEP_IN read held by `r_ready_delay`=32 does not block the read of `SCRATCH_COLD(1)` and the
  write of 0xC0DE_0A01 presented behind it: all three answer, the reads with 0xC0DE_0A00 and
  0xC0DE_0A01 and the write OKAY, while the first read's R channel is observed stalled and
  requests are observed presented during that wait.
* A local-address read on SEP_IN and a read of the same register at its global address 0x4000_2800
  on SYS_IN, released together for four rounds, both complete; the local read returns 0xC0DE_0A00
  OKAY, and the global read also answers OKAY with 0xC0DE_0A00
  (`memmap.adoc`, Memory Map: the fabric routes `LOCAL_BASE` and `GLOBAL_BASE` accesses
  identically inside the aperture; `LOCAL_BASE` is 0xC000_0000 and `GLOBAL_BASE` resets to
  0x4000_0000).
* On each port, for a write with AW accepted and W pending and for a read with R held, a cool
  reset that takes effect while the access is in flight does not leave the port wedged: after
  release the read of `VERSION_LO` answers OKAY with its `chip_config.rdl` reset 0x000100A0. What
  the interrupted access itself returns is printed and not graded.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises; over SEP_IN write inbound filter entry 0 pass-all with 8-byte writes of
`START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR` 0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF and then `FILTER_CONFIG`; write
`SCRATCH_COLD(0)` = 0xC0DE_0A00 and `SCRATCH_COLD(1)` = 0xC0DE_0A01, each answered OKAY, and read
`VERSION_LO` to confirm 0x000100A0.
. Sixteen rounds: release a SEP_IN and a SYS_IN read of `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` from one `clk_smc_i`
rising edge, require each to answer OKAY with 0xC0DE_0A00 and the first ARVALID cycle of the two
ports to be the same; record whether `tb_inb_read_hit` and `tb_inb_isolate_read` were seen; print
`CHK-CONT-SYS-SEP`.
. Sixteen rounds of the same read released together on SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG, each required OKAY
with 0xC0DE_0A00 and zero ARVALID skew; print `CHK-CONT-THREE-PORTS`.
. On SEP_IN issue one group: a read of `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` with `r_ready_delay`=32, a read of
`SCRATCH_COLD(1)` and a write of 0xC0DE_0A01 to `SCRATCH_COLD(1)`; require 0xC0DE_0A00,
0xC0DE_0A01 and OKAY, and require the watch to have seen R stalled and requests presented while
the first read was pending; print `CHK-CONT-PENDING-NEW`.
. Add 0x4000_2800 to the monitor's expected-DECERR addresses; in four rounds release a SEP_IN read
of `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` and a SYS_IN read of 0x4000_2800 together; require the local read OKAY with
0xC0DE_0A00, both reads completed, the global read OKAY with 0xC0DE_0A00, and zero ARVALID skew;
print both responses as `CHK-CONT-LOCAL-GLOBAL`.
. Error injection. Point: the reset agent (`COOL_RST_LO`, `COOL_RST_HI`), for each port in SEP_IN,
SYS_IN, JTAG and each direction, write then read. Kind: a cool reset that takes effect while a
write with `w_delay`=16 (AW accepted, W pending) or a read with `r_ready_delay`=64 (R held) is in
flight. Expected response: the access is still pending when `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` falls, its
outcome is printed and not graded, and after release the read of `VERSION_LO` on the same port
answers OKAY with 0x000100A0. For each leg apply `COOL_RST_LO`, wait 28 `clk_ref_i` cycles, start
the access, wait up to 200 `clk_smc_i` samples for its AWVALID or ARVALID and up to 400 `clk_ref_i`
samples for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` to fall; release with `COOL_RST_HI`, wait for release, repeat
the fuse-sense waits, reprogram filter entry 0 pass-all, collect the interrupted access, then read
`VERSION_LO`; print `CHK-CONT-RESET-MID`.
. Write `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` and `SCRATCH_COLD(1)` to 0 and restore inbound filter entry 0
`FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000, `START_ADDR` 0x0 and `END_ADDR` 0x7 over SEP_IN.
. Require exactly 132 accesses, print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, then run the fence that prints
`CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CONT-SYS-SEP` |In all 16 rounds the SEP_IN and SYS_IN reads released together answer OKAY
within the 50 us per-access guard with 0xC0DE_0A00 and show zero ARVALID skew; the filter hit and
isolate probes are recorded and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-CONT-THREE-PORTS` |In all 16 rounds the SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG reads answer OKAY with
0xC0DE_0A00 within the guard and show zero ARVALID skew.
|`CHK-CONT-PENDING-NEW` |The held read returns 0xC0DE_0A00, the read of `SCRATCH_COLD(1)` behind
it returns 0xC0DE_0A01 and the write answers OKAY, all within the guard, and the held read's R
stall and the requests presented during it are both observed non-zero.
|`CHK-CONT-LOCAL-GLOBAL` |In all four rounds both reads complete within the guard, the local read
returns 0xC0DE_0A00 with OKAY, the global read returns 0xC0DE_0A00 with OKAY, and zero ARVALID skew
is seen.
|`CHK-CONT-RESET-MID` |On each of the six legs the access was in flight when the port reset took
effect and, after release, the read of `VERSION_LO` answers OKAY with 0x000100A0 within the guard;
the interrupted access's outcome (completed, error or abandoned) is printed and not graded.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S7 are in increasing time order and the five checker lines
above were printed in step order, each after its own step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports every bounded wait with its bound and last observed state (the
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, the 200-sample request waits, the reset assertion
and release waits in `clk_ref_i` cycles, the 50 us guard and the 100 us join per access); it is a
printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CONT-SYS-SEP`, `CHK-CONT-THREE-PORTS`, `CHK-CONT-PENDING-NEW`,
`CHK-CONT-LOCAL-GLOBAL`, `CHK-CONT-RESET-MID`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all
printed; every same-edge round answers OKAY with 0xC0DE_0A00 and zero ARVALID skew, the held read
and the requests behind it all answer, the local read of the local-and-global pair returns
0xC0DE_0A00, each of the six reset legs reads `VERSION_LO` 0x000100A0 OKAY afterwards, and exactly
132 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The inbound filter hit and isolate probes seen during the same-edge rounds are
recorded and printed, not compared. The outcome of each access interrupted by the cool reset
(completed, error or abandoned) is printed and not graded.

'''''

[[sec-389-smc_axil_write_side_test]]
===== 389 `smc_axil_write_side_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_axil_write_side_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) issuing single
items and `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` groups; the eFuse-bank model behind the eFuse-shim window
(`EFUSE_SHIM_CTRL_BASE_ADDR`), the external windows `SMC_PLL_WRAP_BASE_ADDR` and
`GPIO_EXTRA_CTRL_BASE_ADDR`, and the reset-unit `SS_CONFIG`; activity probes
`tb_axil_external_active`, `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and `tb_axil_any_master_active` sampled on
`clk_smc_i` (`tb_axil_dtp_csr_active` is sampled and reported only); SEP_IN `s_axi_rvalid`,
`s_axi_rready` and `s_axi_rlast` for the burst end; `env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/axil.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `axil`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The downstream AXI-Lite manager ports stay idle after reset and after
a burst, and eFuse-shim and external-window writes interleaved on SEP_IN keep each window's own
value.

*Test Coverage*:

* After the fuse-sense wait and before any access, none of the three AXI-Lite activity probes
  reads 1 in any of 2000 consecutive `clk_smc_i` cycles, so no downstream manager port asserts a
  request while idle (`fabric.adoc`, Topology, AXI-Lite network; the AMBA rule that VALID is not
  asserted when there is nothing to send).
* The idle checks are backed by positive controls in the same run: a SEP_IN read of the eFuse-shim
  window (reset value 0x20, `efuse_shim_ctrl.rdl` `EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME.init_time`, `sw=rw`)
  drives `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and `tb_axil_any_master_active` to 1 in flight, and a read of
  the PLL-wrap external window drives `tb_axil_external_active` to 1, each back to 0 within 32
  cycles.
* Sixteen writes in one SEP_IN group alternate eight to the eFuse-shim register (0xE0+i) and eight
  to an external window (0xA5A5_0000+i): all eight eFuse-shim writes answer OKAY, the register
  then reads 0xE7 (the last write wins), and at least one cycle has the eFuse-shim and external
  ports active together. The external window's answer is adopter-defined, so its response codes
  are printed and not compared.
* A mixed group of reads and writes to the two windows leaves each eFuse-shim read returning the
  value last written and each eFuse-shim write OKAY, again with at least one cycle of both ports
  active.
* Writes to the reset-unit `SS_CONFIG` (`reset_unit.rdl`, `sw=rw`, reset 0) in one outstanding
  group with a read, each answered whatever the code, leave the register at the value read before
  them (`regblock_udps.rdl`, external register semantics).
* A 4-beat INCR read at the eFuse-shim window is followed by 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles with all three
  probes at 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises; add the four window addresses to the monitor's expected-DECERR addresses; then
for 2000 consecutive `clk_smc_i` cycles sample the three probes and require every one to be 0 in
every cycle (the DTP probe is sampled and reported).
. Positive controls: require the three probes to be 0, read the eFuse-shim register on SEP_IN
expecting 0x20 and require `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and `tb_axil_any_master_active` to have
read 1 during the read; read the PLL-wrap window (any response accepted) and require
`tb_axil_external_active` to have read 1; after each, wait for all probes to fall to 0 within 32
samples; print `CHK-AXLWS-PROBE-ALIVE` and `CHK-AXLWS-IDLE-AFTER-RESET`.
. Issue one group of 16 four-byte writes alternating eFuse-shim 0xE0+i and external-window
0xA5A5_0000+i for i = 0..7 while counting cycles with the eFuse-shim and external probes high
together; read the eFuse-shim register back; require all eight eFuse-shim writes OKAY, at least
one concurrent cycle and a readback of 0xE7.
. Issue one group of eight members: two pairs of an eFuse-shim read (expecting 0xE7) with an
external-window write of 0xA5A5_1000+i, then two pairs of an external-window read with an
eFuse-shim write of 0xF0+i; require every eFuse-shim response OKAY, each eFuse-shim read to return
0xE7 and at least one concurrent cycle.
. Read `SS_CONFIG` as H; issue one group of three writes of H to `SS_CONFIG` followed by a read,
any response code accepted; read `SS_CONFIG` once more and require H.
. Issue a 4-beat INCR read (AxLEN=3, AxSIZE=2) at the eFuse-shim window, wait 64 more cycles,
locate the last R handshake with RLAST, and require all three probes to be 0 in each of the 64
cycles after it; the response code is accepted.
. Write the eFuse-shim register back to its reset value 0x20 and read it back, requiring 0x20.
. Require 36 accesses with the scoreboard having checked at least as many SEP_IN items, print the
step 3 to 6 checker lines, then `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AXLWS-PROBE-ALIVE` |Each backable probe reads 1 while its positive-control read is in flight
and returns to 0 afterwards, and the eFuse-shim read returns the 0x20 reset value; a probe that
never rises or stays high fails the run.
|`CHK-AXLWS-IDLE-AFTER-RESET` |`tb_axil_external_active`, `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and
`tb_axil_any_master_active` all read 0 in each of 2000 consecutive `clk_smc_i` cycles after the
fuse-sense wait and before any access; the DTP probe's high-cycle count is reported, not compared.
|`CHK-AXLWS-WRITE-INTERLEAVE` |All 16 writes complete within the 50 us guard, all eight eFuse-shim
writes answer OKAY, at least one cycle has the eFuse-shim and external ports active together and
the eFuse-shim register then reads 0xE7; the eight external-window response codes are printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-AXLWS-MIXED-RDWR` |All eight members complete within the guard, each eFuse-shim read returns
0xE7, each eFuse-shim write answers OKAY and at least one cycle has two downstream ports active;
the external-window responses and data are printed, not compared.
|`CHK-AXLWS-EXT-WRITE-PENDING` |All four requests of the `SS_CONFIG` group complete within the
guard whatever their response code, and `SS_CONFIG` then reads the value H it held before the
writes; the group's response codes are printed, not compared.
|`CHK-AXLWS-IDLE-AFTER-BURST` |The 4-beat read completes within the guard and the three probes
read 0 in each of the 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles after its last R beat; the burst's response code is
printed, not compared.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S7 are in increasing time order, the six checker lines above
were printed in step order (`CHK-AXLWS-PROBE-ALIVE` ahead of the two idle checkers) each after its
own step, and the scoreboard checked at least as many SEP_IN items as the 36 accesses issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, the 32-sample probe fall waits, the fixed 2000-cycle
and 64-cycle idle windows and the 50 us guard of every SEP_IN access); it is a printed report with
no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-AXLWS-PROBE-ALIVE`, `CHK-AXLWS-IDLE-AFTER-RESET`,
`CHK-AXLWS-WRITE-INTERLEAVE`, `CHK-AXLWS-MIXED-RDWR`, `CHK-AXLWS-EXT-WRITE-PENDING`,
`CHK-AXLWS-IDLE-AFTER-BURST`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; the probes are
0 for 2000 cycles after reset and 64 cycles after the burst, the eFuse-shim register reads 0xE7
after the interleaved writes and 0x20 after the restore, `SS_CONFIG` is unchanged by the pending
writes, and exactly 36 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The DTP activity probe is sampled and reported only. The response codes of the
external-window writes, the external-window responses and data of the mixed group, the response
codes of the `SS_CONFIG` group and the response code of the 4-beat read are printed and not
compared; the external window's answer is adopter-defined.

'''''

[[sec-390-smc_clock_gated_window_slverr_test]]
===== 390 `smc_clock_gated_window_slverr_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_clock_gated_window_slverr_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) for every
access except one; SYS_IN driver (`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) for the read issued during the enable
write; `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (SMC_BASE_CONFIG) enables `i3c_cg_en` [9], `avs_cg_en` [10],
`i2c_cg_en` [11], `uart_cg_en` [12] and `telemetry_cg_en` [13]; the five window registers read and
written (I3C `HCI_VERSION`, AVSBus `AVS_CFG_0`, I2C `I2C_CTRL`, UART log engine `CTRL`, telemetry
receiver `CTRL`); the fabric error slave's data word 0xBADCAB1E; a counter of `clk_smc_i` rising
edges; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Setting a peripheral's clock-gate enable alone turns its
window into an SLVERR responder returning 0xBADCAB1E, leaves the other windows reachable, and
clearing the enable restores the window's reset word.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `i3c_cg_en`, `avs_cg_en`, `i2c_cg_en`, `uart_cg_en` or `telemetry_cg_en` set on its own,
  every access to the matching window answers SLVERR and reads 0xBADCAB1E; the leaf polls a read
  every four `clk_smc_i` cycles and requires that response within 400 cycles (`memmap.adoc`,
  Address Space Organization; `smc_base_config.rdl`, `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` field descriptions).
* A write of the complemented reset word to each gated window answers SLVERR; the response code is
  the compare; the write step does not read the window back.
* After the enable clears, the window answers OKAY within the same 400-cycle bound and reads the
  RDL reset word of its register (`smc_base_config.rdl`, the enable bits are `sw=rw`).
* With one peripheral gated, the other four windows each read OKAY with their RDL reset words and
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads back the value written (`memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization).
* A SYS_IN read of the I2C window issued while the SEP_IN write that sets `i2c_cg_en` is in flight
  completes within the 50 us per-access guard with some response; the code is printed and not
  compared, since no document fixes the outcome of an access that overlaps the enable write.
* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` is read at the start, written back at the end and read again; its other
  fields, including `cg_hysteresis` (reset 0x1F, so the register resets to 0x1F00_0000), are left
  as found.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and keep it; the value with the five peripheral
enable bits cleared is the base for every later write.
. Error injection. Point: `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, for each of I3C, AVS, I2C, UART and TELEMETRY in
turn, written base plus that peripheral's enable and read back to compare. Kind: reads of the
peripheral's window while its clock gate is enabled, polled every four `clk_smc_i` cycles.
Expected response: SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E within 400 cycles, and again on one more read; then
write base to clear the enable, read back, and poll the window until it answers OKAY. Print
`CHK-CG-READ-SLVERR` with each window's poll count and elapsed cycles.
. Error injection. Point: each peripheral's window register, with its clock-gate enable set and the
window polled to SLVERR as above. Kind: a write of the complement of the register's reset word into
the gated window. Expected response: a SLVERR write response. Clear the enable and poll to OKAY.
Print `CHK-CG-WRITE-SLVERR`.
. For each peripheral: set the enable, poll to SLVERR, clear the enable, poll to OKAY and require
the data read to equal the register's reset word. Print `CHK-CG-RESTORED`.
. For each peripheral: set the enable and poll to SLVERR; read each of the other four windows with
its reset word as the expected value; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` expecting base plus the enable;
clear the enable and poll to OKAY. Print `CHK-CG-ISOLATION`.
. Error injection. Point: `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, written base plus `i2c_cg_en` on SEP_IN while a
SYS_IN read of the I2C window is outstanding. Kind: the enable write overlapping an access to the
window it gates. Expected response: the SYS_IN read completes with some response within the 50 us
guard; its code and data are kept and printed, not compared. Read the enable back, poll the I2C
window to SLVERR, then clear the enable and poll to OKAY. Print `CHK-CG-TRANSITION-BOUNDED`.
. Write the saved `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` value back and read it back to compare; print
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and then run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CG-READ-SLVERR` |For each of the five peripherals the window read answers SLVERR with
0xBADCAB1E within 400 `clk_smc_i` cycles of the enable write and again on a second read; the poll
count and elapsed cycles are measured and printed, not compared against a figure.
|`CHK-CG-WRITE-SLVERR` |For each of the five peripherals a write to the gated window is refused
with a SLVERR write response; the scoreboard enforces that exact code.
|`CHK-CG-RESTORED` |After the enable clears, each window answers OKAY within the 400-cycle bound
and reads its register's RDL reset word exactly; SLVERR persisting past the bound or a different
word fails the run.
|`CHK-CG-ISOLATION` |With each peripheral gated in turn, the other four windows read OKAY with
their RDL reset words and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads the value just written, all as exact
compares.
|`CHK-CG-TRANSITION-BOUNDED` |The SYS_IN read issued during the enable write completes with a
response within the 50 us guard; its response code and data are printed and not compared.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps for saving, read, write, restored, isolation, transition and the
final `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` restore are in increasing time order, the five checker lines above were
printed in step order each after its own step, and the access count reaches the floor of 130.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last state (the five 400-cycle
gated and restored polls, the 200000-cycle fuse-sense waits and the 50 us guard of each SEP_IN and
SYS_IN access); it is a printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its
bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CG-READ-SLVERR`, `CHK-CG-WRITE-SLVERR`, `CHK-CG-RESTORED`,
`CHK-CG-ISOLATION`, `CHK-CG-TRANSITION-BOUNDED`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all
printed; each of the five gated windows answers SLVERR (code 2) with 0xBADCAB1E on reads and
SLVERR on writes within the 400-cycle bound, each reads its reset word with OKAY after the enable
clears, the four other windows and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` stay reachable, `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` is
restored to the value read at the start, and at least 130 SEP_IN accesses are issued.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The poll count and elapsed cycles until each gated window answers SLVERR are
measured and printed, not compared against a figure. The response code and data of the SYS_IN read
that overlaps the enable write are printed and not compared, because no document fixes the outcome
of an access that overlaps the enable write.

'''''

[[sec-391-smc_cpuif_ro_wo_edge_test]]
===== 391 `smc_cpuif_ro_wo_edge_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_cpuif_ro_wo_edge_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) issuing 4-byte
reads and writes, with a write-strobe override on three writes; `CHIP_CONFIG` `VERSION_LO`
(read-only), the write-only log engine `INTR_TEST` (UART log engine) and the `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR`
register of the AVSBus controller (no readable field), the control register `SCRATCH_COLD(7)`, and
the first address past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block; `env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A partial-strobe write at a read-only register leaves it unchanged,
write-only, unreadable and past-extent accesses complete without wedging the port, and a control
register reads its value after each.

*Test Coverage*:

* Three 4-byte writes of 0xFFFF_FFFF at `VERSION_LO` with `wstrb` 0x3, 0xC and 0x1 leave the
  register reading its baseline value after each (`smc.rdl`, `chip_config` `VERSION_LO` is
  `sw=r`); the write response of each is printed and not compared, because no document pins it.
* A write of 0 and a read at the write-only `INTR_TEST` of the UART log engine (`log_engine.rdl`,
  fields `sw=w`) complete within the 50 us guard; the read response and data are measured and
  printed, not compared, since no document states what a read of a write-only register returns.
* A read of `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` (`avsbus_controller.rdl`, every field `sw=w`) completes within
  the guard; its response and data are measured and printed, not compared.
* A read and a write at the first address past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block complete within the guard;
  their responses and the read data are measured and printed, not compared (`memmap.adoc`, Address
  Space Organization, and `smc.rdl` `ocah_gap_resp` both describe a gap answer, and they are not
  required to agree here).
* After each of the four edge accesses `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` (`scratch.rdl`, `SCRATCH` is `sw=rw`),
  written 0xC0DE_0007 at setup, reads 0xC0DE_0007 with OKAY, which shows the port still serves a
  register access.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises, and record their values; read `VERSION_LO` as the baseline V0 and require OKAY;
write `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` = 0xC0DE_0007 and require OKAY.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the read-only `VERSION_LO`. Kind: a 4-byte write of 0xFFFF_FFFF
with the partial strobe 0x3, 0xC and 0x1 in turn. Expected response: `VERSION_LO` then reads OKAY
with the baseline value V0; the three write responses are printed, not compared. Print
`CHK-EDGE-RO-PARTIAL` with them.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the write-only log engine `INTR_TEST`. Kind: a write of 0 and then
a read of the write-only register. Expected response: both complete within the guard; the
responses and data are printed, not compared. Then read `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` expecting OKAY and
0xC0DE_0007; print `CHK-EDGE-WO-WRITE-READ-OBS`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR`, which has no readable field. Kind: a read
of the unreadable register. Expected response: completes within the guard; the response and data
are printed, not compared. Then read `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` expecting OKAY and 0xC0DE_0007; print
`CHK-EDGE-UNREADABLE-OBS`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the first address past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block, added to the
monitor's expected-DECERR addresses. Kind: a 4-byte read past the block extent. Expected response:
completes within the guard; the response and data are printed, not compared. Then read
`SCRATCH_COLD(7)` expecting OKAY and 0xC0DE_0007.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the same address past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block. Kind: a 4-byte
write of 0 past the block extent. Expected response: completes within the guard; the response is
printed, not compared. Read `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` expecting OKAY and 0xC0DE_0007, then write
`SCRATCH_COLD(7)` = 0 and require OKAY; print `CHK-EDGE-PAST-EXTENT-OBS` and `CHK-EDGE-RECOVERY`.
. Require 18 accesses against the sequence's own count and the scoreboard's checked count, print
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, then run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EDGE-RO-PARTIAL` |After each of the three partial-strobe writes `VERSION_LO` reads OKAY with
its baseline value V0, an exact compare; the three write responses are measured and printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-EDGE-WO-WRITE-READ-OBS` |The write of 0 and the read of the write-only `INTR_TEST` both
complete within the guard; the leaf measures and prints the read response and data without
comparing them.
|`CHK-EDGE-UNREADABLE-OBS` |The read of `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` completes within the guard; the leaf
records the response and data without comparing them.
|`CHK-EDGE-PAST-EXTENT-OBS` |The read and the write at the first address past `SCRATCH_COLD` both
complete within the guard; the leaf prints the read response and data and the write response
without comparing them.
|`CHK-EDGE-RECOVERY` |After each of the four edge accesses (the `INTR_TEST` read, the
`AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` read, the past-extent read and the past-extent write) `SCRATCH_COLD(7)`
reads OKAY with 0xC0DE_0007.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S6 are in increasing time order, the five checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least 18 accesses were issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises and the 50 us guard of each SEP_IN access); it is a
printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EDGE-RO-PARTIAL`, `CHK-EDGE-WO-WRITE-READ-OBS`, `CHK-EDGE-UNREADABLE-OBS`,
`CHK-EDGE-PAST-EXTENT-OBS`, `CHK-EDGE-RECOVERY`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all
printed; `VERSION_LO` reads V0 after each of the three partial-strobe writes, every edge access
completes within the guard, `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` reads 0xC0DE_0007 with OKAY after each of the four
edge accesses, and exactly 18 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The write responses of the three partial-strobe writes at `VERSION_LO` are printed
and not compared, because no document pins them. The read response and data of the write-only
`INTR_TEST` and of `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` are printed, not compared, since no document states what
a read of a write-only register returns. The responses and read data of the read and write past the
`SCRATCH_COLD` block are printed, not compared; the memory map and the register description both
describe a gap answer and are not required to agree here.

'''''

[[sec-392-smc_dma_traffic_shape_test]]
===== 392 `smc_dma_traffic_shape_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_traffic_shape_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) programming
the DMA control registers (`CONFIG`, `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, `SRC_STRIDE`,
`DST_STRIDE`, `NUM_REPETITIONS`, `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`, `STATUS_0`); the SYS_OUT responder memory
(`cfg.sys_out_mem`) seeded and read back through its backdoor, with the model region
`dma_traffic_shape` at 0x0200_0000 (size 0x1_0000) added to `env.memory_model`; output-port probes
`tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`, `tb_output_axi_awvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wready`, `tb_output_axi_araddr`
and `tb_output_axi_awaddr` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: With DECOUPLE_RW and DECOUPLE_AW clear, a 2D copy, a linear copy,
four queued descriptors and a copy starting on a 4 KiB boundary each land byte for byte in the
SYS_OUT responder.

*Test Coverage*:

* A 2D copy of four 8-byte rows, source contiguous at 0x0200_0000 and destination rows 0x40 apart
  from 0x0200_1000, lands every row equal to its source: `NEXT_ID_0` returns a non-zero id above
  the previous one and `DONE_0` advances by exactly one (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional
  Copies; `dma_ctrl.rdl`, `CONFIG` reset 0, `NEXT_ID` read launches the transfer).
* A linear copy (`NUM_REPETITIONS`=1) of 64 bytes from 0x0200_2000 to 0x0200_3000 lands all 64
  bytes (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies: one repetition with `CONFIG.ENABLED_ND`
  set).
* Four descriptors of one 8-byte row each (sources 0x0200_4000+0x100*i, destinations
  0x0200_5000+0x100*i) are programmed and launched back to back with no `DONE_0` poll between
  them; the request FIFO between the frontend and the 2D midend is four deep (`dma.adoc`,
  Architecture and Configuration). The ids rise and `DONE_0` advances by exactly four, each
  destination equal to its own source.
* A 256-byte copy whose source starts on the 4 KiB boundary 0x0200_8000, to 0x0200_A000, lands all
  256 bytes. The backend splits bursts itself (`dma.adoc`, Linear and Two-Dimensional Copies); the
  first AR address and every AR and AW address seen at the output port are printed, not compared.
* The ordering of AR, AW and W valid at the output port, the burst counts, and the order of the
  four queued transfers are measured and printed: no document fixes them.
* `CONFIG` is left at 0 at the end and reads back 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises; add the `dma_traffic_shape` model region if absent; require the eight
`tb_output_axi_*` probes to exist and start the output-port sampler.
. Read DMA `CONFIG` and require 0; write `CONFIG` with `ENABLED_ND` only (the two DECOUPLE bits
stay 0); read `DONE_0` as the baseline.
. Seed four 8-byte source rows at 0x0200_0000 and a sentinel (0xEE) over the destination rows;
program source, destination, `LENGTH`=8, destination stride 0x40, source stride 8 and
`NUM_REPETITIONS`=4; read `NEXT_ID_0`, require a non-zero id above the last; poll `DONE_0` up to
2000 reads until it equals baseline+1; compare each of the four destination rows with its source;
print `CHK-DTS-COUPLED-COPY` with the output-port shape.
. Seed 64 source bytes at 0x0200_2000 and a sentinel at 0x0200_3000; program a single 64-byte
linear copy, read `NEXT_ID_0`, poll `DONE_0` to +1 and compare all 64 bytes; print
`CHK-DTS-LINEAR` with the burst counts.
. Seed four sources and sentinels; for i = 0..3 program and launch a descriptor by reading
`NEXT_ID_0` without polling `DONE_0`; then poll `DONE_0` until it has advanced by four and compare
each destination with its own source; print `CHK-DTS-QUEUE-FOUR` with the transfer order seen.
. Seed 256 source bytes at 0x0200_8000 and a sentinel at 0x0200_A000; program the copy, read
`NEXT_ID_0`, poll `DONE_0` to +1 and compare all 256 bytes; print `CHK-DTS-PAGE-ALIGNED` with the
first AR address and the burst addresses.
. Write `CONFIG` back to 0 and read it back requiring 0; require at least seven descriptors
submitted, print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DTS-COUPLED-COPY` |`NEXT_ID_0` returns a non-zero id above the previous one, `DONE_0`
reaches exactly one more than its baseline within 2000 polls, and all four destination rows equal
their sources byte for byte (a sentinel byte or a wrong row fails); the AR, AW and W valid order
and burst addresses at the output port are measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-DTS-LINEAR` |The id rises, `DONE_0` advances by exactly one within 2000 polls and all 64
destination bytes equal the source; the numbers of AR and AW bursts at the output port are
measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-DTS-QUEUE-FOUR` |The four `NEXT_ID_0` reads return non-zero rising ids, `DONE_0` advances by
exactly four within 2000 polls and each destination equals its own source; the order of the four
transfers at the output port is measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-DTS-PAGE-ALIGNED` |The id rises, `DONE_0` advances by exactly one within 2000 polls and all
256 destination bytes equal the source that starts on the 4 KiB boundary; the first AR address and
the burst addresses are measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S6 are in increasing time order, the four checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least seven descriptors were submitted
with the SEP_IN access count reaching its floor of 96.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, each `DONE_0` poll of 2000 reads and the 50 us guard
of every SEP_IN access); it is a printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure
when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DTS-COUPLED-COPY`, `CHK-DTS-LINEAR`, `CHK-DTS-QUEUE-FOUR`,
`CHK-DTS-PAGE-ALIGNED`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; every copy lands
byte for byte in the responder with a non-zero rising id and an exact `DONE_0` advance (one per
single copy, four for the queue), `CONFIG` reads 0 after teardown, and at least 96 SEP_IN accesses
are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The order of AR, AW and W valid at the output port, the burst counts, the order of
the four queued transfers, and the first AR address and burst addresses of the page-aligned copy
are measured and printed, not compared, because no document fixes them.

'''''

[[sec-393-smc_past_extent_decerr_units_test]]
===== 393 `smc_past_extent_decerr_units_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_past_extent_decerr_units_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) issuing 4-byte
reads and writes at `LOCAL_BASE` (0xC000_0000) plus the unit's generated window;
`env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs` carrying every probed address; the live registers read
before and after each write: core 0 watchdog `CMP`, outbound mailbox 0 `ERROR_FLAGS`, DMA control
`DST_ADDRESS_LO`, zeroer control `DEST_ADDR`, DFX control `STATUS`, and CPU control `SCRATCH_0`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: For six units whose past-extent write response is declared
DECERR, a read at the first address past the decoded extent and at the last word of the aperture
answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, and the unit's live registers are unchanged by the writes.

*Test Coverage*:

* For the core 0 watchdog (aperture 0x400, extent 0x24), the mailbox (aperture 0x20000), the DMA
  control (aperture 0x200, extent 0x138), the zeroer control (aperture 0x100, extent 0x18), the
  DFX control (aperture 0x800) and the CPU control (aperture 0x1000), the address just past the
  unit's register extent and the last word of its aperture are each read: the response must be
  DECERR with read data 0xBADCAB1E (`smc.rdl`, `ocah_past_extent_resp` of each unit declares rresp
  DECERR and rdata 0xBADCAB1E; `memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization).
* A 4-byte write of 0xA5A5_5A5A to the same two addresses of each unit is issued; `smc.rdl`
  declares its response DECERR (`ocah_past_extent_resp` bresp), and the observed code must equal
  the declaration.
* The live register of each unit, read before the probes and again after each write, holds the
  same value, so a past-extent write did not land in a neighbouring register.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises, and record their values.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the core 0 watchdog's first address past its decoded extent and
the last word of its aperture, both added to the monitor's expected-DECERR addresses. Kind: a read
and then a 4-byte write of 0xA5A5_5A5A at each of the two addresses. Expected response: the read
answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, the write response equals the declared DECERR (printed), and `CMP`,
read before the probes, re-reads the earlier value after each write; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-WDT`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the mailbox's first address past its extent and the last word of
its aperture. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2,
with outbound mailbox 0 `ERROR_FLAGS` as the live register; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-MAILBOX`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the DMA
control, then of the zeroer control. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected
response: as in step 2, with `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and `DEST_ADDR` both read before and after every
write; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DMA-ZEROER` with both units.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the DFX
control. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2, with
`STATUS` as the live register; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DFX`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the CPU
control. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2, with
`SCRATCH_0` as the live register; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CPU-CTRL`.
. Require 48 accesses against the sequence's own count and the scoreboard's checked count, print
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, then run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-WDT` |The reads at the first address past the core 0 watchdog's extent and at
the last word of its 0x400 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, exact compares, and `CMP` reads
the same value before and after each write; the write responses must equal the declared DECERR.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-MAILBOX` |The reads past the mailbox register extent and at the last word of its
0x20000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and outbound mailbox 0 `ERROR_FLAGS` is unchanged
after each write; the write responses equal the declared DECERR.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DMA-ZEROER` |For the DMA control (0x200 aperture) and the zeroer control (0x100
aperture) the reads past the extent and at the aperture's last word answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E
and both `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and `DEST_ADDR` are unchanged after each write; the write responses are
equal the declared DECERR.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DFX` |The reads past the DFX control extent and at the last word of its 0x800
aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and `STATUS` is unchanged after each write; the write
responses equal the declared DECERR.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CPU-CTRL` |The reads past the CPU control extent and at the last word of its
0x1000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and `SCRATCH_0` is unchanged after each write; the
write responses equal the declared DECERR.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S6 are in increasing time order, the five checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least 48 accesses were issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises and the 50 us guard of every SEP_IN access); it is a
printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-WDT`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-MAILBOX`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DMA-ZEROER`,
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-DFX`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CPU-CTRL`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all
printed; every past-extent and last-word read answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, every live register
holds its value across the writes, and exactly 48 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-394-smc_past_extent_slverr_units_test]]
===== 394 `smc_past_extent_slverr_units_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_past_extent_slverr_units_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.sys_axi_agent`) issuing 4-byte
reads and writes at `LOCAL_BASE` (0xC000_0000) plus each unit's generated window;
`env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs` carrying every probed address; the live registers read
before and after each write: reset unit `SS_CONFIG`, eFuse map `SMC_CONFIG`, eFuse interface
control `EFUSE_READ_CTRL`, system timer `OCTS_CTRL`, base config `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, instance 0
of the alias, M-mode, Xvisor, inbound-filter and outbound-filter control arrays, `SCRATCH_COLD(0)`
for the spare wrapper, and GPIO `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE`, AVSBus `AVS_CFG_0`, I2C `INTR_ENABLE` and
telemetry receiver `INTR_ENABLE`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: For the units whose past-extent write response is declared
SLVERR, the spare-block gaps, the peripheral windows and the CLA window, a read past the decoded
extent answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and the live registers are unchanged by the writes.

*Test Coverage*:

* For the reset unit (aperture 0x800), the eFuse map and eFuse interface control (0x1000 each),
  the system timer (0x1000), the base config (0x2000) and the five fabric control arrays (0x1000
  each), a read at the first address past the register extent and at the last word of the aperture
  answers DECERR with read data 0xBADCAB1E (`smc.rdl`, `ocah_past_extent_resp` rresp DECERR and
  rdata 0xBADCAB1E; `memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization). The base config adds a third read
  at the next 8-byte boundary after its last register.
* The spare wrapper's three gaps between its sub-blocks (first and last word of each), the address
  just past the `ndm_reset` extent and the last word of its 0x800 aperture answer the same DECERR
  and 0xBADCAB1E (`misc_wrap.rdl`, `ocah_gap_resp`; `smc.rdl`, `smc_misc_wrap` past-extent
  response).
* The GPIO, AVSBus, I2C and telemetry receiver windows answer the same DECERR and 0xBADCAB1E at
  the first address past their register extent and at the last word of their 0x1000 aperture. The
  UART and I3C windows declare no past-extent response, so only their aperture-end word is read
  and written and the answers are printed, not compared.
* A write of 0xA5A5_5A5A to every probed address completes; `smc.rdl` declares SLVERR for these
  units, and the observed code is printed beside the declared one and not compared.
* The live register of each unit, read before its probes and after every write, holds the same
  value, so a write past the extent did not land in a neighbouring register.
* The CLA window's last word reads OKAY and the first address past the window reads DECERR with
  0xBADCAB1E; the write response there is printed, not compared (`smc.rdl`, `smc_cla` placement).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises, and record their values.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the reset unit's first address past its extent and the last word
of its aperture, added to the monitor's expected-DECERR addresses. Kind: a read and then a 4-byte
write of 0xA5A5_5A5A at each address. Expected response: the read answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E,
the write completes with its declared and observed response printed and not compared, and
`SS_CONFIG`, read before the probes, re-reads the earlier value after each write; print
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-RESET-UNIT`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the eFuse
map, then of the eFuse interface control. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address.
Expected response: as in step 2, with their live registers; print both units in
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-EFUSE`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the system
timer. Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2, with
`OCTS_CTRL` as the live register; print `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-TIMER`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, three base config addresses (past the last register, the next
8-byte boundary, the last aperture word). Kind: the same read and write pair at each address.
Expected response: as in step 2, with `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` as the live register; print
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-BASE-CONFIG`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of each fabric
control array (alias remap, M-mode remap, Xvisor remap, inbound filter, outbound filter). Kind: the
same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2, with the first register
of the array as live register; print all five in `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-FABRIC-CTRL`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, eight spare wrapper addresses (first and last word of each of the
three gaps, just past `ndm_reset`, last aperture word). Kind: the same read, write and live re-read
at each address. Expected response: as in step 2, with `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` as live register; print
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-SPARE`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the past-extent address and the last aperture word of the GPIO,
AVSBus, I2C and telemetry receiver windows, and the aperture-end word of the UART and I3C windows.
Kind: the same read and write pair at each address. Expected response: as in step 2 for the first
four windows; for UART and I3C the read and write complete and the responses are printed without
comparing them; print all six in `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-PERIPH`.
. Error injection. Point: SEP_IN, the first address past the CLA window. Kind: a read and a write
past the window. Expected response: the read answers DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and the write response
is printed, not compared. Before it, read the last word of the window requiring OKAY; print
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CLA`.
. Require 133 accesses against the sequence's own count and the scoreboard's checked count, print
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, then run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-RESET-UNIT` |The reads at the first address past the reset unit extent and at
the last word of its 0x800 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, exact compares, and `SS_CONFIG`
reads the same value after each write; the write responses are measured and printed against the
declared SLVERR, not compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-EFUSE` |For the eFuse map and the eFuse interface control the reads past the
extent and at the last word of the 0x1000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and each unit's
live register is unchanged after each write; the write responses are measured and printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-TIMER` |The reads past the system timer extent and at the last word of its
0x1000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and `OCTS_CTRL` is unchanged after each write; the
write responses are measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-BASE-CONFIG` |The reads past the last base config register, at the next 8-byte
boundary and at the last word of the 0x2000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` is unchanged after each write; the write responses are measured and printed,
not compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-FABRIC-CTRL` |For each of the five fabric control arrays the reads past the
array extent and at the last word of its 0x1000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and the
array's live register is unchanged after each write; the write responses are measured and printed,
not compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-SPARE` |The reads at the first and last word of each spare gap, just past
`ndm_reset` and at the last word of the 0x800 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and
`SCRATCH_COLD(0)` is unchanged after each write; the write responses are measured and printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-PERIPH` |For GPIO, AVSBus, I2C and telemetry the reads past the extent and at
the last word of the 0x1000 aperture answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and the live register is
unchanged after each write; for UART and I3C the aperture-end read and write complete and the leaf
records the responses without comparing them; the write responses are measured and printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CLA` |The last word of the CLA window reads OKAY and the first address past the
window reads DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, exact compares; the write response past the window is
measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 are in increasing time order, the eight checker lines
above were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least 133 accesses were issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises and the 50 us guard of every SEP_IN access); it is a
printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-RESET-UNIT`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-EFUSE`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-TIMER`,
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-BASE-CONFIG`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-FABRIC-CTRL`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-SPARE`,
`CHK-PAST-EXTENT-PERIPH`, `CHK-PAST-EXTENT-CLA`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all
printed; every past-extent, gap and last-word read of a unit with a declared response answers
DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, every live register holds its value across the writes, the CLA last word
reads OKAY, and exactly 133 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The write responses at every probed address are printed beside the SLVERR the
register description declares and not compared. The UART and I3C windows declare no past-extent
response, so only their aperture-end word is read and written and the answers are printed, not
compared. The write response past the CLA window is printed, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-395-smc_sys_out_path_responder_control_test]]
===== 395 `smc_sys_out_path_responder_control_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_sys_out_path_responder_control_test`

*BFM / Model*: JTAG AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` master, `env.jtag_axi_agent`) for the
outbound accesses, SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`) and SYS_IN (`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) drivers for
the local accesses; the SYS_OUT responder memory (`cfg.sys_out_mem`) with its backdoor `read64`,
`write64` and `read_int`, channel backpressure (`enable_backpressure`, `disable_backpressure`),
`arm_w_before_aw`, `inject_error` and `clear_response_delay`; the output-port monitor
`env.output_axi_monitor` with its SLVERR and DECERR tallies; bench probes `tb_output_axi_awvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_awready`, `tb_output_axi_wvalid`, `tb_output_axi_wready`, `tb_output_axi_bvalid`,
`tb_output_axi_bready`, `tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `tb_output_axi_arready`, `tb_output_axi_awaddr`,
`tb_output_axi_araddr`, `tb_output_axi_wdata`, `tb_output_axi_bresp`, `tb_output_axi_write_count`
and `tb_output_axi_read_count`; the response hold `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`; `jtag_axi_awvalid`,
`jtag_axi_wvalid`, `jtag_axi_bvalid` and `jtag_axi_rvalid`; sampled on `clk_smc_i`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: JTAG accesses leave through SYS_OUT with address and
data intact, tolerate split and stalled channels and injected error responses, and local accesses
are still answered while an outbound read is held.

*Test Coverage*:

* A JTAG 64-bit write then read at four address classes (below both windows 0x0200_0000, between
  them 0x8000_1000, above both 0xD000_0000, and the 56-bit address 0x0000_0123_4567_8000) appears
  at SYS_OUT with the issued AW and AR address and the issued write data, once each, the memory
  holds the word and the read returns it with OKAY (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric Topology: the demux
  sends every other address to the output fabric; Alias Remapping: transparent at reset).
* A 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF write with `wstrb` 0x0F over a zero word leaves the upper four bytes 0
  in the responder memory.
* With the SYS_OUT response held by `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`, a JTAG read produces no
  `jtag_axi_rvalid` or `jtag_axi_bvalid` for 200 `clk_smc_i` cycles after its AR handshake; the
  response that follows the release is measured and printed, not compared (`fabric.adoc`, Outbound
  Traffic Flow; `smc-programming.adoc`, Address Map, the `ext_out` catch-all statement).
* With the responder's W channel stalled in 40-cycle windows the AW handshake precedes the W
  handshake and the write completes OKAY after W; with W presented first and the AW channel
  stalled the W handshake precedes AW and the write completes OKAY after AW (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric
  Topology). In both, wvalid or awvalid is seen high while the channel's ready is low, so the
  stall reached the bus.
* A write with no backpressure completes OKAY and its word is stored; how often AW and W handshake
  in the same cycle, and the first-valid cycle offsets, are measured and printed, not compared.
* After a read answered SLVERR, a read answered DECERR and an OKAY read, the next plain read
  returns OKAY with the seeded word; after the same three write responses the next plain write
  returns OKAY and the responder memory holds its word. Each injected code is seen exactly once on
  the SYS_OUT wire; the response the manager receives for the injected access is measured and
  printed, not compared (`fabric.adoc`, Outbound Traffic Flow).
* While a JTAG read is held at SYS_OUT, a SYS_IN read and a SEP_IN read of `REGION_SIZE` (reset
  0x0100_0000, `fabric.adoc`, Local and Remote Resource Access) and a SEP_IN write and read of
  `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` (`scratch.rdl`, `SCRATCH` is `sw=rw`) are answered while the JTAG read stays
  pending.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; start the
handshake watch on the SYS_OUT and JTAG probes; sample `tb_output_axi_write_count` and
`tb_output_axi_read_count`.
. For each of the four address classes: JTAG write of a distinct 64-bit pattern, require OKAY,
exactly one AW and one W handshake whose address and data equal the issued ones and the stored
word equal; then a JTAG read, require OKAY, the pattern and exactly one AR handshake at the issued
address. Then zero a word, write 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF with `wstrb` 0x0F and require the lower
four bytes 0xFFFF_FFFF and the upper four bytes 0; print `CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-ROUTE`.
. Set `tb_output_axi_resp_hold` to 1, start a JTAG read at 0x0200_0000, wait up to 2000 cycles for
the AR handshake, then for 200 cycles require `jtag_axi_rvalid` and `jtag_axi_bvalid` to be 0 and
the read still pending; clear the hold, wait up to 2000 cycles for completion and print the
response and data as `CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-SILENT`.
. Enable W-channel backpressure (40-cycle stall), JTAG write at 0x0200_0000 with a distinct word;
require OKAY, at least one stalled W cycle, the AW handshake before the W handshake, the B
handshake after W and the stored word equal; disable the backpressure; print
`CHK-WSPLIT-AW-FIRST`.
. Arm W-before-AW and enable AW-channel backpressure (40-cycle stall), JTAG write; require OKAY,
at least one stalled AW cycle, the W handshake before the AW handshake, the B handshake after AW
and the stored word equal; print `CHK-WSPLIT-W-FIRST`.
. Clear backpressure and response delay, JTAG write at 0x0200_0000; require OKAY and the stored
word; print the count of cycles with AW and W handshakes together and the first-valid offsets as
`CHK-WSPLIT-SAME-CYCLE`.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder (`inject_error`), for a JTAG read at 0x0200_0008.
Kind: a one-shot read SLVERR, then a one-shot read DECERR. Expected response: each injected code is
seen exactly once on the SYS_OUT wire, the manager's response to the injected read is printed and
not compared, and the plain read that follows each answers OKAY with the seeded word; then two
plain reads; print `CHK-OUT-READ-RECOVERY`.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder (`inject_error`), for a JTAG write at 0x0200_0008.
Kind: a one-shot write SLVERR, then a one-shot write DECERR. Expected response: each injected code
is seen exactly once on the wire, the manager's response to the injected write is printed and not
compared, and the plain write that follows each answers OKAY with the stored word; then two plain
writes; print `CHK-OUT-WRITE-RECOVERY`.
. Program inbound filter entry 0 pass-all over SEP_IN and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back; set
`tb_output_axi_resp_hold` to 1 and start a JTAG read at 0x0200_0000; after its AR handshake read
`REGION_SIZE` on SYS_IN and on SEP_IN requiring 0x0100_0000, write 0x5A5A_C0DE to
`SCRATCH_COLD(0)` and read it back; require the JTAG read still pending, clear the hold and wait
up to 2000 cycles for it; write `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` to 0, restore filter entry 0 to its
`filter_ctrl.rdl` reset values and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back; print
`CHK-STALLED-OUTBOUND-LOCAL-ANSWERED`.
. Require 26 JTAG, 1 SYS_IN and 12 SEP_IN accesses at the scoreboard, print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`,
then run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed state (the
2000-cycle request and release waits, the 200-cycle silence window, the 200000-cycle fuse-sense
waits and the 50 us guard of every access); it is a printed report with no compare, each wait
raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|`CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-ROUTE` |For each of the four address classes the SYS_OUT AW and AR address and
the write data equal the issued values with one handshake each, the read returns the written word
with OKAY, and the `wstrb` 0x0F write leaves bytes 4 to 7 of the seeded word at 0 in the responder
memory.
|`CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-SILENT` |`jtag_axi_rvalid` and `jtag_axi_bvalid` stay 0 and the read stays
pending for 200 cycles of `tb_output_axi_resp_hold` after the AR handshake and the read completes
after release; the response code and data that arrive are measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-WSPLIT-AW-FIRST` |With the W channel stalled for 40-cycle windows the AW handshake comes
before the W handshake, the B handshake after W, the write answers OKAY, the stored word matches
and the stall reached the bus.
|`CHK-WSPLIT-W-FIRST` |With W presented first and the AW channel stalled the W handshake comes
before the AW handshake, the B handshake after AW, the write answers OKAY, the stored word matches
and the stall reached the bus.
|`CHK-WSPLIT-SAME-CYCLE` |The write released from the stall answers OKAY and its stored word matches; the number
of cycles with AW and W handshakes together and the first-valid offsets are measured and printed,
not compared.
|`CHK-OUT-READ-RECOVERY` |After the SLVERR read, the DECERR read and the OKAY read each plain read
returns OKAY with the seeded word, and each injected code is counted once on the SYS_OUT wire; the
manager's response to an injected read is measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-OUT-WRITE-RECOVERY` |After the SLVERR write, the DECERR write and the OKAY write each plain
write answers OKAY and the responder memory holds its word, and each injected code is counted once
on the SYS_OUT wire; the manager's response to an injected write is measured and printed, not
compared.
|`CHK-STALLED-OUTBOUND-LOCAL-ANSWERED` |While the JTAG read is held, `REGION_SIZE` reads
0x0100_0000 OKAY on SYS_IN and on SEP_IN, `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` reads back 0x5A5A_C0DE and the JTAG
read is still pending; its response after release and the local access times are measured and
printed, not compared.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S9 are in increasing time order, the eight checker lines
above were printed in step order each after its own step, and the scoreboard booked exactly 26
JTAG, 1 SYS_IN and 12 SEP_IN accesses, at least 39 in all.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, `CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-ROUTE`, `CHK-JTAG-OUTBOUND-SILENT`,
`CHK-WSPLIT-AW-FIRST`, `CHK-WSPLIT-W-FIRST`, `CHK-WSPLIT-SAME-CYCLE`, `CHK-OUT-READ-RECOVERY`,
`CHK-OUT-WRITE-RECOVERY`, `CHK-STALLED-OUTBOUND-LOCAL-ANSWERED` and `CHK-NONVAC` are all printed;
JTAG addresses and data reach SYS_OUT unchanged, no response appears during the 200-cycle hold,
the split writes keep their handshake order and answer OKAY, every plain access after an injected
error answers OKAY, the local accesses are answered during the hold, no handshake probe sample is
