X/Z, and 26 JTAG, 1 SYS_IN and 12 SEP_IN accesses are booked. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The response and data that follow the release of the held JTAG read, the number of
cycles with AW and W handshakes together and the first-valid offsets, the manager's response to
each injected SLVERR or DECERR access, and the local access times during the hold are measured and
printed, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-396-smc_unit_base_register_port_matrix_test]]
===== 396 `smc_unit_base_register_port_matrix_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_unit_base_register_port_matrix_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` managers on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`), SYS_IN
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) and JTAG (`env.jtag_axi_agent`, items on its sequencer), issuing 4-byte
and 8-byte reads at `LOCAL_BASE` (0xC000_0000) and `GLOBAL_BASE` (0x4000_0000) plus each
register's offset; inbound filter entry 0 programmed over SEP_IN, with `tb_inb_read_hit` sampled
on `clk_smc_i` as the hit probe; the registers read: core 0 to 3 watchdog `CTRL`, reset unit
`SS_WARM_RESET_N`, `SCRATCH_COLD(0)`, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0)`, `CHIP_CONFIG` `VERSION_LO`,
`NDM_RESET` `NDMRESET_REQUEST`, `GLOBAL_BASE`, `LOCAL_BASE` and `REGION_SIZE`, the three
hang-detector `CTRL` and `TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` registers, DFX `STATUS`, `DEBUG_CTRL` and
`DEBUG_BUS_MUX`, the first and last instance of the alias, M-mode, Xvisor, inbound-filter and
outbound-filter arrays, DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO`, zeroer `DEST_ADDR` and CPU control `RESET_VECTOR_0`;
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: The base register of each system and configuration
unit aperture and the last instance of each fabric control array read their RDL reset word from
SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG at both LOCAL_BASE and GLOBAL_BASE.

*Test Coverage*:

* The `CTRL` register of each of the four core watchdogs (apertures at offsets 0x0, 0x400, 0x800
  and 0xC00) reads its reset 0 with OKAY from all three ports at both bases (`wdt.rdl`; `smc.rdl`
  placements; `memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization: the fabric routes `LOCAL_BASE` and
  `GLOBAL_BASE` accesses identically).
* The reset unit `SS_WARM_RESET_N` reads its reset 0xFFFF_FFFF (`reset_unit.rdl`); whether the
  specification pins this readback is an open question and the leaf compares it to the RDL reset.
* The first register of each spare sub-block reads its reset: `SCRATCH_COLD(0)` and
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0)` 0 (`scratch.rdl`), `VERSION_LO` 0x000100A0 (`chip_config.rdl`) and
  `NDMRESET_REQUEST` 0 (`ndm_reset.rdl`). Only `VERSION_LO` is a non-zero compare; a 0 compare
  cannot tell a decoded register from an undecoded window on a simulator that initialises to zero.
* `GLOBAL_BASE` reads 0x4000_0000, `LOCAL_BASE` 0xC000_0000 and `REGION_SIZE` 0x0100_0000 from all
  ports at both bases (`smc_base_config.rdl`; `fabric.adoc`, Local and Remote Resource Access:
  `REGION_SIZE` resets to 0x0100_0000).
* The three hang-detector `CTRL` registers (offsets 0x20, 0x30, 0x40 of the base config) read 0
  and the three `TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` registers (0x28, 0x38, 0x48) read 0x1000, over SEP_IN at
  `LOCAL_BASE` (`smc_base_config.rdl`).
* DFX `DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read their reset 0 from all ports at both bases, and
  `STATUS` answers OKAY from all ports at both bases with its value measured and printed against
  the reset 0, not compared (`dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`).
* The first register of the alias, M-mode, Xvisor, inbound-filter and outbound-filter arrays reads
  its reset (`REGION_START` and `REGION_ATTRS` 0, `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000) before any setup from
  SEP_IN and JTAG at both bases, and from SYS_IN at both bases after inbound entry 0 is programmed
  pass-all, where that entry returns the pass-all `FILTER_CONFIG` word and `tb_inb_read_hit` is
  seen high (`fabric.adoc`, Alias Remap Registers; `filter_ctrl.rdl`).
* The last instance of each array (alias 7, M-mode 7, Xvisor 7, inbound 15, outbound 15) at the
  generated stride reads the same reset from all ports at both bases.
* DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and zeroer `DEST_ADDR` read their reset 0 from all ports at both bases;
  distinct patterns written over SEP_IN then read back from SYS_IN at `GLOBAL_BASE` and from JTAG
  at `LOCAL_BASE`, so a decoded register is told from an undecoded one; `NEXT_ID_0`, which
  launches a transfer, is never read.
* CPU control `RESET_VECTOR_0` reads its reset 0xC004_0000 over SEP_IN at `LOCAL_BASE` and from
  SYS_IN and JTAG at both bases (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises.
. Read the base register of the five fabric arrays (8-byte) from SEP_IN and JTAG at both bases,
expecting `REGION_START` or `REGION_ATTRS` 0 and `FILTER_CONFIG` 0x3000, before anything is
programmed (20 reads).
. Over SEP_IN write inbound filter entry 0 with 8-byte writes of `START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR`
0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF and a pass-all `FILTER_CONFIG`.
. Read the four watchdog `CTRL` registers from the three ports at both bases expecting 0 (24
reads); print `CHK-WDT-BASE-PORTS`.
. Read `SS_WARM_RESET_N` from the three ports at both bases expecting 0xFFFF_FFFF; print
`CHK-RESET-UNIT-BASE-PORTS`.
. Read `SCRATCH_COLD(0)`, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0)`, `VERSION_LO` and `NDMRESET_REQUEST` from the
three ports at both bases expecting 0, 0, 0x000100A0 and 0 (24 reads); print
`CHK-SPARE-FIRST-REGS-PORTS`.
. Read `GLOBAL_BASE`, `LOCAL_BASE` and `REGION_SIZE` (8-byte) from the three ports at both bases
expecting 0x4000_0000, 0xC000_0000 and 0x0100_0000; print `CHK-BASE-CONFIG-RESETS-PORTS`.
. Read the three hang-detector `CTRL` registers (expecting 0) and the three `TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`
registers (expecting 0x1000) over SEP_IN at `LOCAL_BASE`; print `CHK-HANG-DET-RESETS`.
. Read DFX `STATUS` (8-byte, no expected value), `DEBUG_CTRL` (4-byte, expecting 0) and
`DEBUG_BUS_MUX` (8-byte, expecting 0) from the three ports at both bases; print
`CHK-DFX-REGS-PORTS` with the `STATUS` values and whether they equal 0.
. With a watcher on `tb_inb_read_hit`, read the base register of the five arrays from SYS_IN at
both bases expecting the reset words, except inbound entry 0 expecting the pass-all
`FILTER_CONFIG`; require `tb_inb_read_hit` high in at least one sample; print
`CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-BASES-PORTS` with the step 2 reads.
. Read the last instance of each array from the three ports at both bases expecting the reset
words (30 reads); print `CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-LAST-INSTANCE`.
. Read DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and zeroer `DEST_ADDR` from the three ports at both bases expecting 0;
write 0xDA7A_0028 and 0x2E20_0028 over SEP_IN, read them back from SYS_IN at `GLOBAL_BASE` and
from JTAG at `LOCAL_BASE` expecting those patterns, write both back to 0 and read 0 over SEP_IN;
print `CHK-DMA-ZEROER-BASE-PORTS`.
. Read `RESET_VECTOR_0` over SEP_IN at `LOCAL_BASE`, then from SYS_IN and JTAG at both bases,
expecting 0xC004_0000; print `CHK-CPU-CTRL-FIRST-REG-PORTS`.
. Restore inbound entry 0 `FILTER_CONFIG`, `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` to their reset values and
read `FILTER_CONFIG` back expecting 0x3000; require 190 accesses, print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and
run the fence that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-BASE-PORTS` |All 24 reads of the four watchdog `CTRL` registers answer OKAY with 0
from SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG at both bases; the data compares cannot fail on this two-state bench
and the OKAY response is the decode evidence.
|`CHK-RESET-UNIT-BASE-PORTS` |`SS_WARM_RESET_N` answers OKAY with 0xFFFF_FFFF from the three ports
at both bases, an exact compare against the RDL reset.
|`CHK-SPARE-FIRST-REGS-PORTS` |`SCRATCH_COLD(0)`, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0)`, `VERSION_LO` and
`NDMRESET_REQUEST` answer OKAY with 0, 0, 0x000100A0 and 0 from the three ports at both bases;
`VERSION_LO` is the compare that carries the decode.
|`CHK-BASE-CONFIG-RESETS-PORTS` |`GLOBAL_BASE` reads 0x4000_0000, `LOCAL_BASE` 0xC000_0000 and
`REGION_SIZE` 0x0100_0000 with OKAY from the three ports at both bases.
|`CHK-HANG-DET-RESETS` |The three hang-detector `CTRL` registers read 0 and the three
`TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` registers read 0x1000 with OKAY over SEP_IN at `LOCAL_BASE`; the thresholds
are the non-zero compare.
|`CHK-DFX-REGS-PORTS` |`DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read their reset 0 and `STATUS` answers
OKAY from the three ports at both bases; the `STATUS` values are measured and printed with whether
they equal the reset 0, without comparing them.
|`CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-BASES-PORTS` |Before setup the five array base registers read their reset words
with OKAY from SEP_IN and JTAG at both bases, and from SYS_IN at both bases after setup, inbound
entry 0 returning the pass-all `FILTER_CONFIG` word, with `tb_inb_read_hit` high in at least one
sample of the SYS_IN reads.
|`CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-LAST-INSTANCE` |The last instance of each of the five arrays, at the offset the
generated map gives, reads its reset word (0 for the remap regions, 0x3000 for the filters) with
OKAY from the three ports at both bases.
|`CHK-DMA-ZEROER-BASE-PORTS` |`DST_ADDRESS_LO` and `DEST_ADDR` read 0 with OKAY from the three
ports at both bases, the two distinct patterns written over SEP_IN read back exactly from SYS_IN
and JTAG, and both registers read 0 again after being restored.
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-FIRST-REG-PORTS` |`RESET_VECTOR_0` reads 0xC004_0000 with OKAY over SEP_IN at
`LOCAL_BASE` and from SYS_IN and JTAG at both bases.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S12 are in increasing time order, the ten checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least 190 accesses were issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises, the `tb_inb_read_hit` watcher that stops after the
last SYS_IN read and the 50 us guard of every access); it is a printed report with no compare,
each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-WDT-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-RESET-UNIT-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-SPARE-FIRST-REGS-PORTS`,
`CHK-BASE-CONFIG-RESETS-PORTS`, `CHK-HANG-DET-RESETS`, `CHK-DFX-REGS-PORTS`,
`CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-BASES-PORTS`, `CHK-FABRIC-ARRAY-LAST-INSTANCE`, `CHK-DMA-ZEROER-BASE-PORTS`,
`CHK-CPU-CTRL-FIRST-REG-PORTS`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; every
register answers OKAY with its RDL reset word from each port and base the step names, the
co-resident DMA and zeroer patterns read back, the DFX `STATUS` word is reported only, and at
least 190 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The DFX `STATUS` values are measured and printed with whether they equal the reset
0, not compared. The watchdog `CTRL` and other 0 compares cannot fail on this two-state bench, so
the OKAY response is the decode evidence; `VERSION_LO` and the thresholds carry the non-zero
compares. Whether the specification pins the `SS_WARM_RESET_N` readback is an open question; the
leaf compares it to the RDL reset.

'''''

[[sec-397-smc_unit_extent_register_decode_test]]
===== 397 `smc_unit_extent_register_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_unit_extent_register_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` managers on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`), SYS_IN
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) and JTAG (`env.jtag_axi_agent`, items on its sequencer) at `LOCAL_BASE`
(0xC000_0000) and `GLOBAL_BASE` (0x4000_0000) plus each register's offset, with 4-byte and 8-byte
accesses; inbound filter entry 0 programmed pass-all over SEP_IN; the registers and memories
accessed: outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA`, eFuse map word 0, eFuse interface control `STATUS`,
`EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` and `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT`, system timer (OCTS) `TIMER_START`,
`CTRL` and `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE`, CLA `TRDSTRAMIMPL`, the first and last 64-bit words of the ROM and
SPM apertures, `SCRATCH_COLD(7)`, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(7)`, `LC_STATE`, `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT`,
inbound mailbox 31 `CTRL`, DMA control `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI`, zeroer control
`DEST_ADDR` and `CTRL_STATUS`; `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: The base register of the mailbox, eFuse, timer and CLA
apertures and the ROM and SPM words decode and answer OKAY from SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG at both
bases, and the last register of five units answers over SEP_IN at `LOCAL_BASE`.

*Test Coverage*:

* The first register of the mailbox, the eFuse map and eFuse interface control, the system timer
  and the CLA each answers OKAY from the three ports at both bases and the six reads agree. Where
  the register has a declared reset the read equals it: `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` 0x0080_0000, OCTS
  `TIMER_START` 0 and OCTS `CTRL` 0x0001_020A (`smc.rdl` placements and the units' RDL;
  `memmap.adoc`, Address Space Organization), and the CLA `TRDSTRAMIMPL` reset of the DFD block's
  CLA map, read through the 32-bit APB path (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric Topology, local fabric).
* Registers that no document gives a stable readback for are only required to answer OKAY and to
  agree across ports and bases: the write-only outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA`, the
  hardware-driven eFuse interface control `STATUS`. The eFuse map word 0 is compared with the word
  the eFuse bank model was preloaded with, since no document gives its value.
* The first and last 64-bit words of the 128 KiB ROM aperture (`rom.adoc`: 0xC004_0000 to
  0xC005_FFFF) answer OKAY with identical data from all ports and both bases; the data is printed
  and is required to differ from the SPM patterns.
* The first and last 64-bit words of the SPM aperture take a pattern written through `LOCAL_BASE`
  on SEP_IN and return it through `GLOBAL_BASE` on SYS_IN, and take a second pattern written
  through `GLOBAL_BASE` on JTAG and return it through `GLOBAL_BASE` on JTAG and through
  `LOCAL_BASE` on SEP_IN, then read back 0 after being restored (`fabric.adoc`, Fabric Topology:
  the local fabric rebases a global-window request onto the local window).
* `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` and `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(7)` read their reset 0 and round-trip 0x5AC3_A53C
  (`scratch.rdl`, `SCRATCH` is `sw=rw`); `LC_STATE` and `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` are hardware
  driven, answer OKAY and are printed with their RDL resets (0xF and 0) without being compared.
* The last declared register of the eFuse interface control (`EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT`, reset
  0x0080_0000) and of the system timer (`TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE`, reset 0) read their resets, and
  inbound mailbox 31 `CTRL` answers OKAY and is printed; the last register of the DMA control
  (`NUM_REPETITIONS_HI`, reset 0) and of the zeroer control (`CTRL_STATUS`, reset 0) read their
  resets while distinct patterns written to `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and `DEST_ADDR` stay in place, so a
  decode that collapsed onto the first register would show.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each within 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises; over SEP_IN write inbound filter entry 0 pass-all (8-byte `FILTER_CONFIG`,
`START_ADDR` 0x0, `END_ADDR` 0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF) and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back to compare.
. Read seven base registers (outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA`, eFuse map word 0, eFuse `STATUS`,
`EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT`, OCTS `TIMER_START`, OCTS `CTRL`, CLA `TRDSTRAMIMPL`) from the three
ports at both bases (42 reads), each with its expected value where one exists and requiring all
six reads of a register to be equal; print `CHK-MAILBOX-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-EFUSE-BASE-PORTS`,
`CHK-TIMER-BASE-PORTS` and `CHK-CLA-BASE-PORTS`.
. Read the first and last 64-bit ROM words from the three ports at both bases (12 reads), require
the six reads of each to be equal and different from the SPM patterns; print
`CHK-ROM-WORDS-PORTS`.
. Write distinct 64-bit patterns to the first and last SPM words through `LOCAL_BASE` on SEP_IN;
read them back through `LOCAL_BASE` on SEP_IN and through `GLOBAL_BASE` on SYS_IN; write a second
pair through `GLOBAL_BASE` on JTAG; read it back on JTAG at `GLOBAL_BASE` and on SEP_IN at
`LOCAL_BASE`; write both words to 0 and read 0 back; print `CHK-SPM-WORDS-BASES`.
. Over SEP_IN, for `SCRATCH_COLD(7)` and `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(7)` read the reset 0, write and read
back 0x5AC3_A53C and restore 0; read `LC_STATE` and `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT`; print
`CHK-SPARE-LAST-REGS`.
. Over SEP_IN read inbound mailbox 31 `CTRL`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` (expecting 0x0080_0000)
and OCTS `TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` (expecting 0); print `CHK-LAST-REG-MAILBOX-EFUSE-TIMER`.
. Over SEP_IN write and read back 0xDA7A_0001 at DMA `DST_ADDRESS_LO` and 0x2E20_0002 at zeroer
`DEST_ADDR`; read DMA `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` (expecting 0), `DST_ADDRESS_LO` (expecting its
pattern), zeroer `CTRL_STATUS` (expecting 0) and `DEST_ADDR` (expecting its pattern); restore both
patterns to 0 with readback; print `CHK-LAST-REG-DMA-ZEROER`.
. Restore inbound filter entry 0 to its reset values and read `FILTER_CONFIG` back expecting
0x3000; require 105 accesses, print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and run the fence that prints
`CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MAILBOX-BASE-PORTS` |Outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA` answers OKAY from the three ports at
both bases with the same word on all six reads; the word is a write-only register's readback,
printed and not compared with the RDL default.
|`CHK-EFUSE-BASE-PORTS` |The eFuse map word 0 reads the preloaded word, the interface control
`STATUS` answers OKAY with the same value on all six reads (value printed, not compared with a
reset) and `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` reads 0x0080_0000, each from the three ports at both bases.
|`CHK-TIMER-BASE-PORTS` |OCTS `TIMER_START` reads 0 and OCTS `CTRL` reads 0x0001_020A with OKAY
from the three ports at both bases, all six reads of each equal.
|`CHK-CLA-BASE-PORTS` |`TRDSTRAMIMPL` reads its CLA-map reset with OKAY from the three ports at
both bases through the 32-bit APB path, all six reads equal.
|`CHK-ROM-WORDS-PORTS` |The first and last ROM words answer OKAY with the same 64-bit data on
every port and base and differ from the SPM patterns; the data is printed, since no document gives
its value.
|`CHK-SPM-WORDS-BASES` |The first and last SPM words read back exactly the written pattern through
the base used for the write, through the other base and from another port, and read 0 after the
restore.
|`CHK-SPARE-LAST-REGS` |`SCRATCH_COLD(7)` and `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(7)` read 0 and round-trip
0x5AC3_A53C; `LC_STATE` and `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` answer OKAY and the leaf records their values
without comparing them.
|`CHK-LAST-REG-MAILBOX-EFUSE-TIMER` |`EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` reads 0x0080_0000 and OCTS
`TIMER_GPIO_ENABLE` reads 0 with OKAY; inbound mailbox 31 `CTRL` answers OKAY and the leaf records
its word without comparing it.
|`CHK-LAST-REG-DMA-ZEROER` |DMA `NUM_REPETITIONS_HI` and zeroer `CTRL_STATUS` read 0 with OKAY
while `DST_ADDRESS_LO` still reads 0xDA7A_0001 and `DEST_ADDR` still reads 0x2E20_0002.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S7 are in increasing time order, the nine checker lines above
were printed in step order each after its own step, and at least 105 accesses were issued.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports each bounded wait with its bound and last observed value (the three
fuse-sense waits of 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises and the 50 us guard of every SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG
access); it is a printed report with no compare, each wait raising its own failure when its bound
expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MAILBOX-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-EFUSE-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-TIMER-BASE-PORTS`,
`CHK-CLA-BASE-PORTS`, `CHK-ROM-WORDS-PORTS`, `CHK-SPM-WORDS-BASES`, `CHK-SPARE-LAST-REGS`,
`CHK-LAST-REG-MAILBOX-EFUSE-TIMER`, `CHK-LAST-REG-DMA-ZEROER`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; every base-register read answers OKAY with one value across
the three ports and two bases (the declared reset where there is one), the ROM words match across
ports, the SPM patterns round-trip across bases and ports, the DMA and zeroer patterns survive the
last-register reads, and at least 105 accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The outbound mailbox 0 `WRITE_DATA` readback, the eFuse interface control `STATUS`,
inbound mailbox 31 `CTRL`, `LC_STATE` and `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` are required only to answer
OKAY (and, where read from several ports, to agree) and are printed, not compared, because no
document gives them a stable readback. The ROM words are printed since no document gives their
value, and the eFuse map word 0 is compared with the eFuse bank model's preloaded word for the
same reason.

'''''

[[sec-540-smc_axi_random_stress_test]]
===== 540 `smc_axi_random_stress_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_axi_random_stress_test`

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip (AXI)` managers on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`), SYS_IN
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) and JTAG (`env.jtag_axi_agent`) driving AxID, AxLOCK, AxCACHE, AxQOS,
AxREGION, AxUSER and AxPROT per access, as single accesses and as `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` groups
under a per-group `AxiTimingProfile`; the VIP response-ID capture (`capture_resp_id`); passive
`SmcAxiPortResponseRecorder` on the B and R handshakes of `s_axi_*`, `sys_axi_*` and
`jtag_axi_*`, `SmcRawRStallWatch` on the raw R valid probes and `SmcOutputHandshakeSampler` on
the AW, AR, B and RLAST handshakes and the AW and AR READY stalls of `u_output_axi_if`; the
SYS_OUT responder (`cfg.sys_out_mem`, depth 8
through `sys_out_max_outstanding`) with `set_response_delay`, `enable_backpressure` and
`inject_error`; `env.output_axi_monitor` `allow_slverr` and `allow_decerr` and
`env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs`; a per-port golden model keyed by byte address; every draw
from a `random.Random` stream per step seeded from `RANDOM_SEED`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the AXI attributes, burst shapes, outstanding depths,
transaction IDs, payload words and the SYS_OUT responder timing and error faults on SEP_IN, SYS_IN
and JTAG; every drawn point has a stated response.

*Objective*: Seeded random AXI attributes, burst shapes, outstanding depths and SYS_OUT responder
timing and error faults on SEP_IN, SYS_IN and JTAG all leave every access completing at its own
port with its own ID and, where answered OKAY, returning the word of its own address.

*Test Coverage*:

* Response IDs: on SYS_IN and SEP_IN 12 AxIDs (0x00, 0x3F, each single bit and four draws) and on
  JTAG IDs 0 to 3 twice, every write answers OKAY with BID equal to its AWID and every read OKAY
  with RID equal to its ARID and the word written (`fabric.adoc`, Interfaces / AXI ID Widths by
  Fabric Stage).
* Sideband attributes: 16 write-then-read pairs per port over AxCACHE 0 to 15 and drawn AxQOS,
  AxREGION and AxUSER, half at the port's SPM window and half at its registers; every read after
  an OKAY write answers OKAY and returns the word of its own address; the write code per knob
  value is observed (`fabric.adoc`, Interfaces / AXI Interface Widths and Address Remapping).
* AxLOCK: an exclusive read and an exclusive write per port are observed and the ordinary
  write-then-read after each returns the fresh word.
* Carriage to output_axi: eight JTAG writes and eight reads at OUT2 reach the responder at their
  own address with the driven AxCACHE and with one AxUSER value whatever was driven; SYS_IN and
  SEP_IN accesses at OUT0 and OUT1, inside neither the local nor the global aperture, answer
  DECERR and never reach the responder (`fabric.adoc`, Routing / Outbound Traffic Flow;
  `memmap.adoc`, Memory Map).
* Shapes: AxSIZE 1 to 8 at SPM words and registers, INCR bursts of 2, 16, 256 and drawn lengths,
  FIXED and WRAP bursts and narrow register bursts, then a mixed stream of 40 accesses per port
  with every attribute, size, burst, length, direction and target drawn and up to 4 outstanding,
  followed by the full-width reads of KNOWN words (after one aligned write when the stream left
  none) that bring the stream's compare reads to two when the drawn ones fall short;
  every OKAY read at a KNOWN byte returns the golden byte of that address, every read issued at
  KNOWN bytes with AxPROT[1] clear answers OKAY, each beat count equals AxLEN+1 (`fabric.adoc`,
  Interfaces / AXI Interface Widths and Topology).
* Local concurrency: groups of depth 4, 8, 9, 16 and 24 per port, the AxID set {1, 2} on all three
  ports at once and manager-side BREADY and RREADY holds; per port and AxID the recorded responses
  equal the requests (`fabric.adoc`, Configuration Parameters / SMC Fabric Transaction Limits).
* Output concurrency: JTAG groups of depth 1, 8 and 16 at OUT2, SYS_IN and SEP_IN accesses outside
  the window while a JTAG group is outstanding, and a JTAG split between SPM2 and OUT2 with local
  SYS_IN and SEP_IN traffic; the OUT2 handshakes equal the JTAG accesses issued (`fabric.adoc`,
  Topology).
* Responder timing and errors: response delays, AW and AR ready stalls and depth-8 reordering at
  the responder, each profile shown on the wire; injected SLVERR and DECERR on writes and reads
  alone, in a group of 24 and under delay and stall with local traffic outstanding, each code
  answered unchanged at the JTAG port (`smu-smc.adoc`, AXI Interface Configuration).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within 200000 `clk_smc_i` rises; print `RAND-SEED`; bind the
SYS_OUT responder and require depth 8; require the ID space of each port to equal its BID width
and the output windows to lie outside the local and global apertures of `SMC_BASE_CONFIG`; start
the three port recorders and the output sampler; over
SEP_IN program inbound and outbound filter entry 0 pass-all; write the four registers of each port
(`SCRATCH_COLD(0..3)` for SYS_IN, `SCRATCH_COLD(4..7)` for SEP_IN, `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0..3)` for
JTAG) with 4-byte words by address; preload each port's output window in the responder.
. Per port, for each AxID of the list, write then read one SPM word with `capture_resp_id`; require
OKAY, BID and RID equal to the request ID both through the VIP capture and the port recorder, and
the read word equal to the write; print `CHK-RAND-ID-ECHO`.
. Per port, 16 write-then-read pairs with AxCACHE k, drawn AxQOS, AxREGION, AxUSER and AxID, even
k at the SPM window with 8 bytes and odd k at a register with 4 bytes, `allow_error` set; require
every read after an OKAY write to answer OKAY and return the word written, with at least one such
pair per port; print the OKAY and non-OKAY counts per port and `CHK-RAND-ATTR-OWN-WORD`.
. Per port at one SPM word: write, exclusive read, write, read, exclusive write, write, read;
require the two ordinary reads OKAY with the fresh word; print the exclusive responses and
`CHK-RAND-LOCK-OBS`.
. Error injection. Point: SYS_IN and SEP_IN at OUT0 and OUT1, inside neither the local nor the
global aperture. Kind: two write-then-read pairs per port at each window with `allow_error`.
Expected response: DECERR on each with no AW or AR sampled at the responder. Alongside, on JTAG,
eight writes then reads at OUT2 with AxCACHE 0x0, 0xF, 0x3 and five draws and AxUSER draws; require
one AW and one AR at the responder per access with the driven AxCACHE, the read word equal to the
write, one `awuser` across the writes and one `aruser` across the reads; print
`CHK-RAND-OUT-SIDEBAND`.
. Per port, 51 accesses: SPM write-then-read at AxSIZE 1, 2, 4, 8; register pairs at each size
with the 4-byte pair compared and the others observed, each followed by a 4-byte re-arm; INCR
bursts of 2, 16, 256 and two drawn lengths of 8-byte beats compared beat by beat; FIXED x4, x16 and
WRAP x2, x4, x8, x16 observed and then a fresh word; four narrow INCR register reads each followed
by a register read; require exactly 51 accesses per port and every compare read of the step to
have compared.
. Three tasks, one per port, each 10 groups of 4 disjoint accesses with every attribute, AxPROT,
size, burst, length, direction and target drawn; observed where FIXED, WRAP, AxLOCK 1 or a narrow
register access; require every read issued at KNOWN bytes with AxPROT[1] clear on each port to
have answered OKAY and compared; print one `OBS-SHAPE` line per observed access, the
`OBS-SHAPE-PROT` DECERR view and `CHK-RAND-SHAPE-BY-ADDR` with the compared byte count.
. Groups of depth 4, 8, 9, 16 and 24 on the three ports together, a group of 8 per port under the
AxID set {1, 2}, and a group of 16 per port under a seeded `AxiTimingProfile` run one port at a
time; require per port and AxID the recorded B responses, R beats and R words to equal the
requests and the b and r stall counts above 0 on every port; print `CHK-RAND-LOCAL-DEEP`.
. Error injection. Point: SYS_IN and SEP_IN at OUT0 and OUT1 while a JTAG depth-8 read group at
OUT2 is outstanding. Kind: 8 accesses per port outside both apertures presented during the group.
Expected response: DECERR with no handshake at the responder, the responder counters advancing by
the JTAG reads only. Around it, JTAG groups of depth 1, 8 and 16 of reads then of writes at OUT2,
then a three-task group of JTAG split between SPM2 and OUT2 with 16 local accesses on SYS_IN and
SEP_IN; require the OUT2 AW and AR handshakes and the responder counters to advance by exactly the
JTAG accesses issued; print `CHK-RAND-OUT-DEEP` and `CHK-RAND-OUT-OTHER-PORTS-DECERR`.
. Four responder profiles (delay 1 to 8, delay 32 to 64, AW and AR stall 16, delay 0 to 64 with
depth 8), each a JTAG group of 12 writes and 12 reads at OUT2; require the AW and AR address sets
at the responder to equal the sets issued, the counters to advance by 12 and 12, the stall profile
to have held AWREADY and ARREADY low with a request valid, and each delay profile's shortest
AW-to-B and AR-to-RLAST at the responder to be at least its fewest delay cycles; print
`CHK-RAND-RESP-TIMING`.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT responder (`inject_error`), with `allow_slverr` and
`allow_decerr` set on the output monitor. Kind: three rounds of one-shot SLVERR and DECERR
injections on a JTAG write and on a read with `capture_resp_id`, each followed by an ordinary
write-then-read; a JTAG group of 24 with a seeded third injected; the same under delay, ready stall
and reorder with 12 local accesses outstanding on each of SYS_IN and SEP_IN. Expected response: the
response ID and the injected code of each one-shot at the JTAG port, the injected code on each
injected group member and OKAY on the others, the monitor tally equal to the injected codes, the
ordinary pairs OKAY with the word written and every local access OKAY; print
`CHK-RAND-RESP-ERRORS-ECHO` and `CHK-RAND-RESP-COMBINED`.
. Clear the monitor opt-ins, responder errors, backpressure and delays; restore inbound and
outbound filter entry 0 to the RDL reset over SEP_IN; write `SCRATCH_COLD(0..7)` and
`SCRATCH_COLD_WARM(0..3)` to 0; stop the recorders; print `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, then run the fence
that prints `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RAND-ID-ECHO` |On every port each write of the AxID list answered OKAY with BID equal to its
AWID and each read OKAY with RID equal to its ARID and the word written, the IDs read both through
the VIP capture and the passive port recorder.
|`CHK-RAND-ATTR-OWN-WORD` |All 48 attribute pairs completed within the guard, every read after an
OKAY write answered OKAY and returned the word of its own address, and on every port at least one
such pair was issued; the write code per knob value is printed, not asserted.
|`CHK-RAND-LOCK-OBS` |All 21 lock-leg accesses completed within the guard and on every port the
ordinary write-then-read after the exclusive read and after the exclusive write answered OKAY with
the fresh word; the exclusive responses are printed, not asserted.
|`CHK-RAND-OUT-SIDEBAND` |All eight JTAG writes and reads reached the responder at their own OUT2
address with `awcache` and `arcache` equal to the driven AxCACHE, the read word equal to the
write, one `awuser` across the writes and one `aruser` across the reads; the SYS_IN and SEP_IN
pairs at OUT0 and OUT1 answered DECERR with no AW or AR at the responder.
|`CHK-RAND-SHAPE-BY-ADDR` |Every access of steps 6 and 7 completed within the guard, each beat
count equals AxLEN+1, every OKAY read at a KNOWN byte returned the golden byte of its own address,
every read of steps 6 and 7 issued at KNOWN bytes with AxPROT[1] clear answered OKAY and compared
with at least one such read per port and step, and the recovery write-then-reads returned the
fresh word; FIXED, WRAP, narrow register, AxLOCK 1 and AxPROT[1] responses are printed, not
asserted.
|`CHK-RAND-LOCAL-DEEP` |For depths 4, 8, 9, 16 and 24, the AxID set {1, 2} on all three ports and
the manager stall profiles, per port and AxID the recorded B responses, R beats and R words equal
the requests, and the b and r stall counts are above 0 on every port; the DUT-side stall counts
and the response order are printed, not asserted.
|`CHK-RAND-OUT-DEEP` |For the JTAG groups of depth 1, 8 and 16 and the JTAG split between SPM2 and
OUT2 with local SYS_IN and SEP_IN traffic, per AxID the B count and returned words match the
requests, every OKAY read word equals the responder word of its address, and the OUT2 handshakes
and responder counters advanced by exactly the JTAG accesses issued.
|`CHK-RAND-OUT-OTHER-PORTS-DECERR` |All 16 SYS_IN and SEP_IN accesses at OUT0 and OUT1 presented
while the JTAG depth-8 group was outstanding answered DECERR within the guard at their own port
with no AW or AR at the responder, the responder counters advanced by the 8 JTAG reads only, and
the JTAG group still returned its own words and IDs.
|`CHK-RAND-RESP-TIMING` |Under the four responder profiles all 96 JTAG accesses completed within the
guard, per AxID the B count and returned words match the requests, the AW and AR address sets at
the responder equal the sets issued, the counters advanced by 24 per profile, the stall profile
held AWREADY and ARREADY low with a request valid, and each delay profile's shortest AW-to-B and
AR-to-RLAST at the responder is at least its fewest delay cycles; the response order is printed,
not asserted.
|`CHK-RAND-RESP-ERRORS-ECHO` |The 12 one-shot injections and the injected third of the group of 24
each completed at the JTAG port with its own ID and the injected code, the other members of the
group answered OKAY, the responder monitor counted exactly the injected codes, and each ordinary
write-then-read after an injection answered OKAY with the word written.
|`CHK-RAND-RESP-COMBINED` |With delay, ready stall, reorder and injected errors on the JTAG group of
24, all 24 SYS_IN and SEP_IN local accesses answered OKAY at their own port with the golden word of
their own address, every JTAG access completed with its own ID and the code the responder
returned, and every OKAY JTAG read word equals the responder word of its address.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S12 are in increasing time order, the eleven checker lines
above were printed in step order each after its own step, each port recorder saw at least one
response and at least one AW handshake was sampled at the responder.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Reports every bounded wait with its bound (the fuse-sense wait of 200000
`clk_smc_i` rises and the 50 us driver guard per access); it is a printed report with no compare,
each wait raising its own failure when its bound expires.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-RAND-ID-ECHO`, `CHK-RAND-ATTR-OWN-WORD`, `CHK-RAND-LOCK-OBS`,
`CHK-RAND-OUT-SIDEBAND`, `CHK-RAND-SHAPE-BY-ADDR`, `CHK-RAND-LOCAL-DEEP`, `CHK-RAND-OUT-DEEP`,
`CHK-RAND-OUT-OTHER-PORTS-DECERR`, `CHK-RAND-RESP-TIMING`, `CHK-RAND-RESP-ERRORS-ECHO`,
`CHK-RAND-RESP-COMBINED`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are all printed; every access
completes within the guard at its own port and answers OKAY unless it is allowed to error, every
OKAY read of a KNOWN or responder address returns the word of that address, every read of steps
3, 6 and 7 issued at KNOWN bytes with AxPROT[1] clear answers OKAY and compares, the response IDs
echo the request IDs, SYS_IN and SEP_IN outside both apertures answer DECERR without reaching the
responder, each injected code is answered unchanged at JTAG, each responder profile shows on the
wire, and the OUT2 handshakes and responder counters match the JTAG accesses issued. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The write code per sideband knob value, the exclusive (AxLOCK) responses, the
responses of the FIXED, WRAP, narrow register, AxLOCK 1 and AxPROT[1] accesses, the DUT-side stall
counts and response order of the deep local groups, and the response order under the responder
profiles are printed, not asserted.

'''''




[[sec-541-smc_axil_endpoint_prot_sweep_test]]
===== 541 `smc_axil_endpoint_prot_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_axil_endpoint_prot_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN and JTAG AXI), `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` outstanding groups, `SmcAxiPortResponseRecorder` on the SEP_IN response channels

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/axil.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `axil`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Present every request attribute, non-zero then zero, to every internal AXI-Lite register endpoint and show that no value changes the endpoint's response or content.

*Test Coverage*:

* `fabric.adoc` (Protection Bit Pass-Through) passes every protection bit through the fabric unmodified, and `memory_map.adoc` gives each endpoint its window and response, so an endpoint answers a request the same whatever AxPROT, AxUSER, AxREGION, AxQOS, AxLOCK, AxCACHE, AxLEN or AxID it carries.
* **Check set.** One register per endpoint, 59 endpoints in eight classes: the internal-crossbar targets (GPIO interface 0, DFX, base configuration, cpu_ctrl), each of the 32 filter entries (inbound and outbound 0..15, `START_ADDR`), the alias, M-mode and Xvisor remaps (instance 0), mailbox port 0 (`WIRQT`), every peripheral-crossbar target (reset unit `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE`, misc scratch, AVSBus, I2C 0..2, UART, log engines 0..3, telemetry receiver 0, OCTS, I3C 0), the eFuse shadow and interface-control windows, the zeroer and iDMA control windows and the DFD/CLA window. Every probe is held against the generated contract before any access: no field may carry a read action, a modified write or write-only access, so a write-back of the value it holds changes nothing.
* **Seed and reference.** `memory_map.adoc` answers an in-extent hole of most of these blocks with OKAY and 0x0, and almost every probe resets to 0x0, so a misdecode into a hole would pass a data compare against the reset word. Before the sweep, a zero-attribute write therefore seeds a distinct non-zero word into every probe whose seeded bits have no effect while its block is idle (52 endpoints: plain read-write fields, the filter `START_ADDR` entries with `entry_enabled` clear, the remap offsets with `valid` clear, the reserved byte of `DEBUG_BUS_MUX`, the `MISSING_LAST` interrupt enable, and `WIRQT` = 1, since `axil_mailbox.adoc` reduces a threshold at or above the mailbox depth to depth - 1). Each endpoint then takes a read with every attribute zero (AxCACHE included). That word is the only expected value the leaf uses, and on every compared endpoint it must be non-zero; a seeded plain read-write probe must read back its seed exactly. The four unseeded compared probes (AVSBus `AVS_CFG_0`, eFuse `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT`, GPIO `ACCESS_FILTER`, base configuration) hold non-zero reset words. Every seeded probe is written back to its pre-seed word, and read back, at the end of the run. Each attribute checker line reports `nonzero-reference=<k>/<n>`.
* **Per attribute value.** A read with the value, a write-back of the reference with the same value, and a zero-attribute read. On a compared endpoint the read must answer OKAY with the reference, the write OKAY, and the zero-attribute read OKAY with the reference. AxPROT 0x1..0x7 then 0x0, followed by a zero-attribute read per endpoint; AxUSER 0xFFF, a walking one over the twelve bits (which bits carry the source ID is open, SF-005) and 0x000; AxREGION and AxQOS 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0xF, 0x0; AxLOCK 1 then 0; AxCACHE 0x1, 0x2, 0x3, 0x6, 0x7, 0xA, 0xB, 0xE, 0xF, 0x0; AxLEN 0; AxID 0x01, 0x15, 0x2A, 0x3F, 0x00 with RID and BID required to equal AxID.
* **Debug manager.** The JTAG AXI input reads the reset unit's seeded `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE` with AxPROT 0x3 then 0x0; each word must equal the SEP_IN reference, and both RRESPs are logged (which inbound managers carry the attribute is open, SF-007).
* **AxLEN > 0** only on the burst set whose footprint lies in side-effect-free read-write registers: the M-mode and Xvisor output remaps from `region_attrs` of instance 0 with AxLEN 1, 3 and 7, the alias remap from `region_start` of instance 0 with AxLEN 1, and the reset unit from `SS_CONFIG_HOLD` with AxLEN 1. Each takes an INCR read and a write of the footprint's reference words in 8-byte beats; every beat's response and data, the B response and the footprint read before and after are logged, not compared (SF-003). A footprint register that moved is written back to its reference before the AxLEN 0 sweep.
* **Outstanding IDs.** Per endpoint class, four reads with AxID 0x01..0x04 are outstanding at once; the RIDs the recorder sees must be exactly that set, and on a compared class each read must answer OKAY with the reference. The number of ARs accepted up to the first R beat is logged per class (acceptance depth is open, SF-010).
* **Not reachable at this level.** The DTP CSR target (BASE + 0xB000) is a forwarded port with no responder on the subsystem bench, so it is outside the check set (SF-040).
* **Measure-and-log legs (LINKED-ISSUE).** Every access to the zeroer and iDMA control windows (SF-008) and the DFD/CLA window (SF-038); the two eFuse windows on the AxPROT leg (SF-012); and the response code of every AxLOCK = 1 access (SF-002). These log the response and word as `MEASURE` lines and compare nothing on that leg; the AxLOCK = 1 read word is still compared.
* The SEP_IN monitor's DECERR excuse covers the measure-and-log endpoints for the whole run, the two eFuse windows only during the AxPROT leg, and the burst start addresses only during the burst legs.
* Every response wait is bounded at 20 us and fails with the outstanding request list; recorder beat waits are bounded at 16 clocks.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_axil_endpoint_prot_sweep_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ATTR-PROT` |Every compared endpoint answered each AxPROT 0x1..0x7 and 0x0 read with OKAY and its non-zero reference, each write-back OKAY, and the following zero-attribute read with the reference; the eFuse windows were logged
|`CHK-ATTR-DEBUG-MANAGER` |The JTAG AXI reads of the seeded `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE` with AxPROT 0x3 and 0x0 each returned the non-zero SEP_IN reference; both RRESPs logged
|`CHK-ATTR-USER` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxUSER 0xFFF, the twelve single-bit values and 0x000
|`CHK-ATTR-REGION` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxREGION 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0xF, 0x0
|`CHK-ATTR-QOS` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxQOS 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0xF, 0x0
|`CHK-ATTR-LOCK` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxLOCK 1 and 0, with the AxLOCK = 1 response codes logged rather than compared
|`CHK-ATTR-CACHE` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxCACHE 0x1, 0x2, 0x3, 0x6, 0x7, 0xA, 0xB, 0xE, 0xF, 0x0
|`CHK-ATTR-LEN` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxLEN 0 on every endpoint; the burst set's beats and footprint logged
|`CHK-ATTR-ID` |As `CHK-ATTR-PROT` for AxID 0x01, 0x15, 0x2A, 0x3F, 0x00, with RID and BID equal to AxID
|`CHK-ATTR-ID-OUTSTANDING` |Per endpoint class, four outstanding reads with AxID 0x01..0x04 returned exactly that RID set, and on a compared class each OKAY with the reference; AR acceptance depth logged
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence REFERENCE < PROT < DEBUG-MGR < USER < REGION < QOS < LOCK < CACHE < LEN < ID < OUTSTANDING, every term with a non-zero count and its own sim time
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every response and recorder wait was bounded, with its bound and last state reported, and none expired
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twelve checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.
'''''

*Scope limit*: The DTP CSR target (`BASE + 0xB000`) is a forwarded port with no responder on the subsystem bench and is outside the check set; the zeroer, iDMA, DFD/CLA and eFuse windows and the AxLOCK = 1 and burst-start response codes are measured and logged, not compared.
'''''

[[sec-542-smc_cpuif_handshake_instances_test]]
===== 542 `smc_cpuif_handshake_instances_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FABRIC

*Source Module*: `smc_cpuif_handshake_instances_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` outstanding groups, `AxiTimingProfile` AR delay, the VIP's AW source and B and R response sinks held and released by the sequence, and a passive per-clock monitor of the SEP_IN AW, W, AR, B and R channels

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive the AXI-Lite front end of every generated register-block instance -- every instance of the multi-instance blocks and instance 0 of the single-instance ones -- with pipelined, back-to-back, W-ahead and ready-held traffic.

*Test Coverage*:

* **Instance set.** 225 instances, one at a time. Every instance of the multi-instance families: GPIO interfaces 0..64, inbound and outbound filter entries 0..15, M-mode, Xvisor and alias remaps 0..7, I2C 0..2, the UART/log wraps 0..3 (log-engine control, main UART, divisor latch and log engine), telemetry receivers 0..2 and the cold and warm scratch banks. Instance 0 of every single-instance family: reset unit, cpu_ctrl, the `IRQEN` register of each of the 64 mailbox apertures, AVSBus, I2C control, OCTS, DFX, base configuration, eFuse interface control, the eFuse shadow, zeroer and iDMA control, I3C 0, the DFD/CLA sink, chip_config, ndm_reset and the straps window. 187 are pinned-map instances (GPIO interface, filter entries, remaps, reset unit, cpu_ctrl, mailbox) and 38 are plain. Instance addresses come from `smc_addr.h` through `smc_indexed_addr` where the block is indexed and must equal the IP-XACT map's address. The DTP CSR target has no responder on this bench and is never accessed (NOT-REACHABLE-AT-THIS-LEVEL, SF-040). `uart_16550_main_wo` has no read side and is not in the set. The mailbox clock enable in `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` is set for the run and restored at the end.
* **Reference register.** Each instance has one register, and its first isolated read is the reference. On the pinned-map families it is a register whose fields the generated documentation makes inert while the entry is disabled, so it also takes distinct values: GPIO `ACCESS_FILTER` (only the AxPROT requirement fields move; both filter enables must read clear), filter `START_ADDR` (4 KiB multiples, with `FILTER_CONFIG.entry_enabled`, `allow_burst` and `locked` reading clear first, so the granule rounding `filter_ctrl.adoc` describes leaves each value unchanged), alias `region_start` (with `region_attrs.valid` clear) and M-mode / Xvisor `region_attrs` (offset bits 55:20 only, `valid` held clear). The second register of a pinned-map instance is GPIO `DATA_CTRL` (only `interrupt_type`, with `interrupt_enable` clear, compared on its read-write bits), filter `END_ADDR`, alias `region_end`, and for a remap, which has one register, the next instance's `region_attrs`. The reset unit uses its two FLR counter value registers and cpu_ctrl `SCRATCH[15]` / `SCRATCH[14]`. A mailbox aperture uses `IRQEN`, with `IRQS` of the aperture and of its neighbour required to read clear first so that no enabled interrupt is pending (`IRQP` is `IRQS` gated by `IRQEN`); its second register is the next aperture's `IRQEN`, and its three enable bits repeat once exhausted. The plain instances use the instance-0 leaf's probe: a register whose every field is plain read-write in the generated contract, or a read-only one (chip_config, ndm_reset, straps) (`HOST_FIFO_CONFIG`, `CTRL`, `SCR`, `DLL` with `LCR.DLAB` set and restored, `LOG_REGION_SIZE`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `SCRATCH[0]`) and write only the value it holds.
* **Pipelined.** On every pinned-map instance an interleaved group of 4 writes of distinct values and 4 reads is outstanding at once; every access must answer OKAY, and the requests the port accepted before the first response (the achieved outstanding depth, 4 requested) must be at least 2 and are logged per instance. Each read is classified: equal to the last write whose B preceded its AR (compared), equal to a write of the group whose AW handshake is at or before the read's R handshake and whose B is not before its AR (logged with the AR, R, AW and B cycles of each match; AXI orders no read against writes on the write channel, SF-010), or a value no write of the group produced (must be none). On every instance 4 reads of the reference register are outstanding at once, each returns the reference, and the achieved depth must be at least 2.
* **Back to back.** Every instance takes two reads of its reference register in one group (the AR handshake gap is logged), each returning the reference; every pinned-map instance writes distinct values to its two registers and reads both in one group, each returning its own written value.
* **W ahead of AW.** Every pinned-map instance takes a write with W presented 1, 2 and 4 cycles before AW, each answered OKAY and read back. The sequence holds the VIP's AW source and releases it so that AW VALID rises exactly that many cycles after W VALID; the monitor measures the lead and the run fails unless it equals the driven one. Every instance then takes a write-back of its reference with W exactly 2 cycles ahead: on a pinned-map instance the following read must equal the reference, and on a plain instance the B response and the following read are logged (check set open, SF-001, SF-009). The same write-back value then goes out in a pair of writes followed by a read, and in a single write followed by a read, with the read's AR held back 0 to 11 cycles, which lines a read accept up with a write's acknowledge on each path; on a pinned-map instance every such read must equal the reference, and on a plain instance the reads are logged.
* **Held ready.** Every instance takes a read with RREADY held 16 cycles after RVALID is first seen, and every pinned-map instance a write with BREADY held the same way: VALID must stay high and RID/RRESP/RDATA or BID/BRESP unchanged on every held cycle, with exactly one handshake, the read returning the reference and the write read back.
* **Held groups.** Every instance takes 16 reads, then 8 writes alternating with 8 reads (distinct values on a pinned-map instance, write-backs of the reference on a plain one), then 16 writes, each group queued behind its held ready and released 16 cycles after the first response VALID. Every request of a group carries the same ID on its channel, so AXI requires the responses in issue order; every response must arrive once and is matched to its request by position. Each read must return the reference or, on the mixed group of a pinned-map instance, is classified as in the pipelined group: last acknowledged write (compared), a write of the group overlapping the read as in the pipelined group (logged with its AR, R, AW and B cycles, SF-010), a value no write of the group produced (must be none). The register must read the last write afterwards. Same-ID requests are serialised in front of some blocks, so every instance then also takes 16 reads and 16 write-backs of its reference with one ID each behind the same held ready; AXI leaves their response order free, so each read must return the reference, every write answer OKAY and the register read the reference afterwards.
* **Coverage intent.** The stimulus targets the accept-while-acknowledged rows of every regblock instance, the held BVALID / RVALID arms of `gpio_intf_reg` 1..64 and the read-after-read dispatch arm of the output remaps 1..6; these are stimulus criteria, not expected values.
* Every register a leg writes is restored to its reference and read back before the next leg compares against the reference. Every SEP_IN record must be resolvable on a VALID cycle, and no response may drop VALID or change while held.
* Every group wait is bounded at 40 us and fails with the outstanding count and the last SEP_IN record; every held ready and every held AW waits at most 4000 clk_smc_i cycles for VALID and fails with the last VALID level.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpuif_handshake_instances_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPUIF-PIPELINED-RW` |Every pinned-map instance answered its interleaved group of 4 writes and 4 reads OKAY with an achieved outstanding depth of at least 2 (min/max logged); reads equal to the last acknowledged write compared, reads equal to an overlapping write of the group logged with their AR/R/AW/B cycles (SF-010), and no read returned a value no write of the group produced; per-channel AR and AW depth logged
|`CHK-CPUIF-PIPELINED-READ` |Every instance answered 4 outstanding reads OKAY with the reference, with an achieved outstanding depth of at least 2 (min/max logged)
|`CHK-CPUIF-B2B-SAME` |Every instance answered two back-to-back reads OKAY with the reference
|`CHK-CPUIF-B2B-DIFF` |Every pinned-map instance returned each of two distinct written values from its own register on back-to-back reads
|`CHK-CPUIF-W-AHEAD` |Every pinned-map instance answered writes with W VALID measured exactly 1, 2 and 4 cycles ahead of AW VALID OKAY and read each value back
|`CHK-CPUIF-W-AHEAD-WRITEBACK` |Every pinned-map instance read its reference after a write-back of it with W measured exactly 2 cycles ahead and on every read of the AR-offset write-back sweep; the plain instances' responses and reads logged
|`CHK-CPUIF-RREADY-HOLD` |Every instance held RVALID with unchanged RID/RRESP/RDATA for at least 16 cycles against a low RREADY, completed once, and returned the reference
|`CHK-CPUIF-BREADY-HOLD` |Every pinned-map instance held BVALID with an unchanged BID/BRESP for at least 16 cycles against a low BREADY, completed once, and read back the written value
|`CHK-CPUIF-HELD-GROUP` |Every instance completed each 16-deep held group in issue order with none lost or duplicated; reads equal to the reference or the last acknowledged write compared, reads equal to an overlapping write of the group logged with their AR/R/AW/B cycles (SF-010), and no read returned a value no write of the group produced
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence per instance REFERENCE < PIPELINED-RW < PIPELINED-READ < B2B-SAME < B2B-DIFF < W-AHEAD < W-AHEAD-WB < RREADY-HOLD < BREADY-HOLD < HELD-GROUP (pinned-map terms on pinned-map instances), every term with its count and its first and last sim time
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every group wait and held-ready wait was bounded, with its bound and last state reported, and none expired
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eleven checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.
'''''

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[smc-vplan-area-reset]]
==== RESET

[[sec-038-smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test]]
===== 38 `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `clock`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`, `dft_cg`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: LIVE/CONNECTIVITY DFT test_en_i bypass, and the Zeroer clocks free-running under the primary reset with the gating enable at its reset value.

*Test Coverage*:

* `test_en_i` bypass A-B-A on the DMA and Zeroer gaters. `test_en_i` is static in the functional mission and changes only while the reset is asserted, so each change is made with `rst_cold_ni` held low: gated off while idle with `test_en_i` = 0; `test_en_i` set to 1 under a cold reset, gating programmed on after release, and every cycle enabled across a window at least as long as the gaters took to gate off; `test_en_i` cleared under a second cold reset, gating programmed on after release, and gated off again. With `test_en_i` = 1 the reset synchronisers take `scan_rst_ni`, which the bench ties high, so the second cold reset reaches `rst_primary_smc_clk_n` only once `test_en_i` is cleared.
* Zeroer clocks under reset: while `rst_primary_smc_clk_n` is asserted in the second cold reset, with `test_en_i` = 0, both Zeroer gated clocks run every cycle of the window. The cold reset returns `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` to its generated reset, so `tb_zeroer_cg_en` reads 0 across that window and is recorded in the token; an enabled gate held in reset cannot be produced from the frontdoor on this bench and is not claimed. What is claimed is the clock behaviour under reset with the enable at its reset value.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DFT-BYPASS-FREE-RUN` |With `test_en_i` = 1 set under a cold reset and gating programmed on after release, the DMA and both Zeroer gated clocks show an enabled edge on every cycle of a window at least as long as the gate-off latency measured with `test_en_i` = 0
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Non-vacuity count in `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-RESET-OVERRIDE-FREE-RUN` |With `rst_primary_smc_clk_n` = 0 both Zeroer gated clocks show an enabled edge on every cycle of the window, and `tb_zeroer_cg_en` reads 0 before and after it (`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` at its reset), carried in the token; a gated-off edge or an enable that did not reset fails the run (`smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test_seq.py`)
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DFT-BYPASS-FREE-RUN`, `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-RESET-OVERRIDE-FREE-RUN` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `clock`.

*Scope limit*: An enabled gate held in reset cannot be produced from the frontdoor on this bench and
is not claimed; the claim is the clock behaviour under reset with the gating enable at its reset
value, `tb_zeroer_cg_en` reading 0 across the window.

'''''

[[sec-039-smc_reset_unit_lock_test]]
===== 39 `smc_reset_unit_lock_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_reset_unit_lock_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb module
`smc_reset_unit_lock_test`); the SV-UVM half is the class `smc_reset_unit_lock_test` of the same
name, selected with `+UVM_TESTNAME` (`--framework uvm`).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK and SS_CONFIG_LOCK are write-one-to-set over all 32 bits, mask the registers they guard in both directions, and clear on the primary (cool) reset.

*Test Coverage*:

* `RESET_UNIT.SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK`, which no other cocotb testcase reads; `fw/tests/cold_reset_lock_sanity` exercises the same two properties from firmware, and this testcase covers them without a firmware dependency.
* `RESET_UNIT.SS_CONFIG_LOCK`, which no other testcase names or drives.
* `reset_unit.rdl` declares both lock fields (`SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK`, `SS_CONFIG_LOCK`) as `sw = rw; hw = r; onwrite = woset;` reset 0, so a taken lock cannot be released by software.
* Each lock's RDL description names the register it guards and the per-bit hold: `SS_CONFIG_LOCK` "lock[s] down SS config. If bit 0 is written, then bit 0 of other SS config cannot be written to again" (`reset_unit.rdl`), and `SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK` the same for SS cold reset. The RDL does not state the bus response to a write that hits locked bits; `CHK-CSR-RESP` requires OKAY there as the bench's working assumption. `cool_reset_isolate_cfg` records the cold-reset half from the other side, as its reason for *not* comparing that register, so the masking is asserted here and nowhere else.
* One testcase rather than two: the registers have the same declaration and the same gate, so a second would differ only in two addresses. The three checkers run once per pair and are tagged with it, and the sequence requires all six tokens, so a pair silently dropped from the list fails rather than shrinking the test.
* cocotb, testcase contract `SMC_COV_B1_002` revision 2: every bit of both locks is set by its own write and kept through an all-zeroes write and a repeated write, so each lock bit toggles 0->1 and the lock reads 0xFFFFFFFF at the end of its walk (bits [31:2] included).
* cocotb: every bit of `SS_CONFIG` and `SS_COLD_RESET_N` is attempted against its lock in one direction (1->0 on even bits, 0->1 on odd bits) while the unlocked bits of the same write must follow it; the response code of each such write is logged and must be uniform, since the register documentation does not state it (SF-014).
* cocotb: a cool-reset pulse with the cold reset inactive takes both locks 1->0 on every bit and both targets back to 0x00000000; the targets then accept 0xA5A5A5A5. The first-access latency after release is measured and logged (no stated bound; SF-016 waived by proxy). Expected values: `reset_unit.adoc` (RW / RW1S, reset 0x0), `register-field-access.adoc` (1S), `clk_rst.adoc` (the register interface and both targets are reset by the primary reset, which includes the stable cool reset).

*Test Procedure*:

The scenario has two implementations that share this claim: the cocotb
`smc_reset_unit_lock_test_seq.py` and the SV-UVM `smc_reset_unit_lock_test_seq.svh`
(`--framework uvm`).

cocotb (`SMC_COV_B1_002`):

[arabic]
. SETUP: cold reset, wait for fuse sense done.
. UNLOCKED: read both locks (0x00000000), then write each target with 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x00000000, reading back after each.
. CONFIG WALK and MASKING: for i = 0..31, write `SS_CONFIG` so bit i is 1 for even i and 0 for odd i (the first iteration is `CHK-RESET-LOCK-ARM`); write `SS_CONFIG_LOCK` = 1<<i, 0x00000000, 1<<i, reading back mask(0..i) after each (`CHK-RESET-LOCK-WOSET` at i = 1); write `SS_CONFIG` with every bit inverted from its readback and require the locked bits to hold the even/odd pattern and the unlocked bits to equal the write (`CHK-RESET-LOCK-MASKS-WRITE` at i = 1), logging the response code.
. COLD-RESET WALK and MASKING: the same on `SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK` / `SS_COLD_RESET_N`.
. PRIMARY RESET: with both locks at 0xFFFFFFFF and both targets at 0x55555555, pulse the cool-reset pin with the cold reset inactive; bounded waits on the asserted and released reset levels, the warm release and the first reset-unit read.
. POST RESET: both locks and both targets read 0x00000000; each target takes 0xA5A5A5A5 and reads it back.

SV-UVM, for each of the two (target, lock) pairs:

[arabic]
. Write bit 0 to the target with nothing locked and read it back, proving the register is writable before any lock exists.
. Write bit 1 to the lock and require it to set, then write all zeroes and require it to remain set. The SV-UVM sequence performs no lock pre-read: it locks a fresh bit per pass and expects the accumulated `bits 1..1+loop_index` back, so from pass 1 onward a lock that ignored writes or reset to the wrong value fails on the accumulation instead.
. Write bits 0 and 1 to the target in one access. Require bit 1 to stay clear and bit 0 to follow the write.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RESET-LOCK-ARM` |Once per pair, the proof opens with `[<pair>]`. The target accepts a write with the lock clear, so "unchanged" later cannot be explained by a register that never changes
|`CHK-RESET-LOCK-WOSET` |Once per pair, the proof opens with `[<pair>]`. A set lock bit survives an all-zeroes write, per `onwrite = woset`
|`CHK-RESET-LOCK-MASKS-WRITE` |Once per pair, the proof opens with `[<pair>]`. In one inverting write, the locked bits do not follow software while the unlocked bits do -- so the write demonstrably reached the register
|`CHK-LOCK-CONFIG-UNLOCKED` |`SS_CONFIG_LOCK` reads 0x00000000 after cold reset and `SS_CONFIG` reads back 0xFFFFFFFF then 0x00000000, all OKAY
|`CHK-LOCK-COLD-UNLOCKED` |`SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK` reads 0x00000000 after cold reset and `SS_COLD_RESET_N` reads back 0xFFFFFFFF then 0x00000000, all OKAY
|`CHK-LOCK-CONFIG-W1S` |After each write of 1<<i, and after the following 0x00000000 and repeated 1<<i writes, `SS_CONFIG_LOCK` reads exactly mask(0..i), for all 32 i (96 readbacks); the lifecycle closes when the lock reads 0 after the cool reset
|`CHK-LOCK-COLD-W1S` |The same 96 readbacks on `SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK`, closed by its post-cool-reset 0 readback
|`CHK-LOCK-CONFIG-MASKS` |After each of the 32 inverting writes, every locked bit of `SS_CONFIG` keeps its pre-write value (16 attempts 1->0, 16 attempts 0->1) and every unlocked bit equals the written value
|`CHK-LOCK-COLD-MASKS` |The same on `SS_COLD_RESET_N` under `SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK`
|`CHK-LOCK-CONFIG-MASKED-RESP` |Measure and log: the response code of the 32 masked `SS_CONFIG` writes, required to be uniform and resolvable; the code itself is not compared (LINKED-ISSUE SF-014)
|`CHK-LOCK-COLD-MASKED-RESP` |Measure and log: the same for the 32 masked `SS_COLD_RESET_N` writes (LINKED-ISSUE SF-014)
|`CHK-LOCK-CONFIG-PRIMARY-RESET` |After the cool-reset pulse with the cold reset inactive, `SS_CONFIG_LOCK` reads 0x00000000 (was 0xFFFFFFFF), `SS_CONFIG` reads 0x00000000 and then accepts 0xA5A5A5A5; the first-access latency is logged
|`CHK-LOCK-COLD-PRIMARY-RESET` |The same for `SS_COLD_RESET_LOCK` and `SS_COLD_RESET_N`
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |cocotb: the cool assert and release waits, the warm release and the first post-reset access each carry a finite bound that fails the run with the last state on expiry; the line lists bound and last state per wait
|`CHK-LOCK-TARGET-WRITABLE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): positive control: the target accepts a write at this pass's bit while the lock is still clear, so "unchanged" later cannot be satisfied by a register that never changes
|`CHK-LOCK-SET` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the written bit appears in the lock register, which accumulates the bits earlier passes locked
|`CHK-LOCK-STICKY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): an all-zeroes write does not release any set lock bit, per `onwrite = woset`
|`CHK-LOCK-MASKS-TARGET` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): after the lock is taken, a write clearing the locked bit leaves it set -- per the lock's RDL description in `reset_unit.rdl`, the same bit of the guarded register "cannot be written to again"
|`CHK-LOCK-FREE-BIT-MOVED` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the same write carries never-locked bit 0, and that bit is required to change in both directions -- so "unchanged" cannot be explained by the write being dropped
|`CHK-CSR-RESP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): every SEP_IN CSR access completes with an OKAY response
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): warm-reset domain release after fuse sense completes
|`CHK-NONVAC` |cocotb: ordered fence SETUP < UNLOCKED < CONFIG-WALK < CONFIG-MASK < COLD-WALK < COLD-MASK < PRIMARY-RESET < POST-RESET-WRITE, each term with its own sim time and a non-zero compare count. SV-UVM (`--framework uvm`): reconciles the accesses the body issued against its own loop bounds -- a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated pass, not a DUT-failable compare. `CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` is the observed-side counterpart
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the `lock_csr` feature's comparison count, taken from the always-on scoreboard fed by the PASSIVE monitor, is at or above the floor the completed passes imply (five predicted reads per lock pair per pass)
|`CHK-SB-LOCK-CSR` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): always-on scoreboard, feature `lock_csr`: `smc_lock_csr_ref_model` applies `woset` to the lock and lock-filtered bit-enables to the guarded register, rebuilt from the traffic the passive monitor saw rather than from the sequence's own bookkeeping. Both rules are RDL-sourced: `woset` from the two lock field declarations in `reset_unit.rdl` and the per-bit hold from the same lock descriptions ("bit 0 of other SS config cannot be written to again"). It corroborates; the primary proof of masking is the sequence-side `CHK-LOCK-MASKS-TARGET`, whose expectation comes from the bench's own accumulation
|===

*Pass Criteria*: under cocotb, every checker above that is not marked SV-UVM shape only holds after its compares: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`, the three `CHK-RESET-LOCK-*` checkers per pair and the ten `CHK-LOCK-*` checkers. Each lock ends its walk at 0xFFFFFFFF with its target at 0x55555555, and the cool reset returns all four registers to 0x00000000.

A taken lock is irreversible for the rest of the simulation it was taken in, which is what
`woset` means. The two implementations of this scenario handle that differently, and the
difference is part of the claim:

* the cocotb testcase owns its simulation, locks every bit, and releases them with a cool reset;
* the SV-UVM testcase runs at least 16 scenario passes back to back in ONE simulation with no
  reset between them (`ocah_test.MinDefaultLoops`), so each pass locks a FRESH bit --
  bit 1 + `loop_index` -- while bit 0 is never locked in any pass and stays the writability
  control. After sixteen passes each lock holds 0x1FFFE and a write of 0x00000001 to its
  target reads back 0x0001FFFF. A loop knob that would run past the
  lockable bits fails the run rather than aliasing silently.

Under `--framework uvm` the governing checker set is the SV-UVM one in the table above (the cocotb ids named at the head of this Pass Criteria do not run there), and
`+SMC_LOCK_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must fail the run. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The register description does not state the bus response to a write that hits locked
bits; the SV-UVM `CHK-CSR-RESP` requires OKAY there as the bench's working assumption, not as a
specified value.

'''''

[[sec-040-smc_cold_reset_repeated_test]]
===== 40 `smc_cold_reset_repeated_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cold_reset_repeated_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run the SMC OSS repeated cold-reset re-assert scenario.

*Test Coverage*:

* assert half: a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on the asserted levels. It doubles as the stimulus hold -- `smc_reset_ctrl` de-glitches `rst_cold_ni` / `rst_cool_ni` over 32 `clk_ref_i` samples, so a fixed hold shorter than that window is silently rejected and resets nothing. Holding until the reset is *observed* cannot be short.
* hold half: after the wait matched, the pin stays low across a further `MID_ASSERT_HOLD_REF_CYCLES` `clk_ref_i` edges and EVERY one of those samples must still read the asserted levels. This is a separate observation in time from the wait (the wait's match and a RAW_SAMPLE dispatched straight after it land in the same delta region, so such a snapshot could not fail unless the wait already had -- [NO-ALWAYS-PASS-CHECKER]). A DUT that releases the cold/cool path early, anywhere inside the window, fails here.
* release half: a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on the released levels followed by the post-release `SAMPLE` (the checked_cleared leg). No fixed `ClockCycles` wait stands in for completion on the reassert / between / recover path ([NO-BLIND-DELAY-SYNC] / [TIMEOUT-MUST-FAIL]).
* `skip_mem_repair_o` against the isolate-request pin: the pad is the one the DV-owned pad table (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`) names "Isolate Request", and `clk_rst.adoc` ("Function Level Reset", "Memory Test Bypass") defines pin-based isolation as that pin gated by `ISOLATE_REQ_PINEN_REG` and makes it an isolation source that activates the bypass. The testcase module first programs `ISOLATE_REQ_PINEN_REG` to all ones over SEP_IN and reads it back (`smc_isolate_req_pinen_seq`); then, with no FLR signalled and `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` at its reset 0, the output must read 0 with the pin driven low and 1 with it driven high, each within a bounded poll (`CHK-SKIP-MEM-REPAIR-PIN`), and 0 again when fuse sense completes after the last reset with the pin held low (`CHK-SENSE-DONE-REPAIR-ENABLED`; the resets have returned the enable to 0, and a low pin is no isolation source under either enable value). The level the output shows with the pad undriven is reported, not asserted. The pad table recommends a pull-down for this pad, so a board idles the pin low; the bench pad model reads it as 1 when undriven, so the sequence drives the pin and does not rely on the undriven level.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cold_reset_repeated_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MID-ASSERT-HOLD` |Every `clk_ref_i` sample across the `MID_ASSERT_HOLD_REF_CYCLES` window after the assert handshake matched carries the asserted levels (`_hold_raw` in `smc_reset_seq_base.py`); each sample carries the expectation, so the scoreboard fails the run at the first sample that leaves them, one token per held window
|`CHK-SKIP-MEM-REPAIR-PIN` |`skip_mem_repair_o` 0 within a bounded poll of driving the isolate-request pad low and 1 within a bounded poll of driving it high, with no FLR signalled and `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` at 0; expiry or a wrong level fails
|`CHK-SENSE-DONE-REPAIR-ENABLED` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` reads 0 on at least the first sample after the last reset release and then rises within a bounded wait, and `skip_mem_repair_o` reads 0 at that point with the pin held low; already 1, expiry, or a 1 on `skip_mem_repair_o` fails
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MID-ASSERT-HOLD`, `CHK-SKIP-MEM-REPAIR-PIN` and `CHK-SENSE-DONE-REPAIR-ENABLED` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The level `skip_mem_repair_o` shows with the isolate-request pad undriven is
reported, not asserted: the bench pad model reads the undriven pin as 1 while the pad table
recommends a pull-down, so the sequence drives the pin and does not rely on the undriven level.

'''''

[[sec-041-smc_cold_reset_test]]
===== 41 `smc_cold_reset_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cold_reset_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `smoke`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `smoke`, `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator
(cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run the SMC OSS cold-reset / POR / cool scenario.

*Test Coverage*:

* every reset step is a bounded `WAIT_STATE` handshake carrying the exact expected levels, so the scoreboard owns the verdict and expiry raises with the last observed state ([TIMEOUT-MUST-FAIL]). No fixed settle sits on the proof path -- recovery is a wait for the released levels, not a delay ([NO-BLIND-DELAY-SYNC]).
* the POR/cold interaction fence (S7) is a *hold* monitor, not a first-match poll: with `powergood_stable_o==0` every sample across a window wider than the DUT's 32-sample cold de-glitch must still show the cold-stable and primary resets asserted. A delayed incorrect release inside the window fails, which a return-on-first-match poll could not see ([NO-ALWAYS-PASS-CHECKER]).
* the non-vacuity fence (S9) counts the scoreboard's *fail-capable* reset checks (`reset_samples_seen` + `reset_raw_checks_seen` + `reset_wait_checks_seen`) at every step boundary and requires each of S3..S8 to have advanced that total **with checks of its own**: the shared `_recover_sample()` tail's contribution is tracked separately and subtracted, so a step is not credited for the recovery every step ends with and dropping that step's own assert leg fails the fence. Expectation-free `RAW_SAMPLE` observations are booked in a separate counter and cannot satisfy it either, so a step whose expectations were dropped (or which never ran) fails instead of being papered over ([NO-ZERO-ACTIVITY-PASS] / [NO-DUMMY-DEAD-CODE]).

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cold_reset_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BRINGUP-LEVELS` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-COLD-ASSERT-PRIMARY` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-COOL-PRIMARY` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-INT-COOL-SEQ` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-INT-POR-COLD` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MID-ASSERT-HOLD` |The cold-reset levels hold at every `clk_ref_i` sample of the `POR_HOLD_REF_CYCLES` window while `powergood_i` is low (`_hold_raw` in `smc_reset_seq_base.py`); the scoreboard fails the run at the first sample that leaves them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Non-vacuity count in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-POWERGOOD-GATES` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Named compare in `smc_cold_reset_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===
