[[sec-183-smc_cold_boot_chain_order_test]]
===== 183 `smc_cold_boot_chain_order_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cold_boot_chain_order_test`

*BFM / Model*: reset agent driving `powergood_i` and `rst_cold_ni` (no external VIP); the boundary observables and the hart-0 retire trace sampled on every `clk_smc_i` edge in `tb_top`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `boot`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: On a second cold reset, power-good is stable before fuse sense completes, fuse sense completes before the core reset releases, the first retired instruction sits at the specified ROM vector, and cluster isolation is held past both `smc_init_mem_done_o` and the core reset release.

*Test Coverage*:

* Every observable -- `powergood_stable_o`, `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`, `smc_init_mem_done_o`, core 0 `tb_cpu_core_reset_n`, cluster `tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` -- is first required at its reset level while the cold pin is held, within a bound. Each recorded rise is therefore a bring-up event of this reset and not a stale level left from the initial bring-up.
* All stamps come from one `clk_smc_i` timeline taken by a single monitor, and the ordering claims are strict inequalities between those stamps; each observable is required resolvable at every sample.
* The first retired PC is compared against the vector `rom.adoc` pins, not against the `CPU_CTRL` reset value the DUT reads back.
* The two bounded reset legs are scoreboard `WAIT_STATE` handshakes carrying exact expected levels, and the leaf requires the scoreboard to have booked at least two of them, so an expired bound raises there with the last observed state.
* What this bench cannot show is named and left open: the automatic SRAM zeroing never runs (`smc_disable_sram_auto_init_i` is tied high in `tb_top`, so `smc_init_mem_done_o` rises as soon as the cluster reset releases), the repair and MBIST done inputs are tied high so there is no engine to observe, and the uncore reset has no separate probe.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Sample the entry state, drop `powergood_i` and assert `rst_cold_ni`, and match a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on power-good low with the cold-stable and both primary resets asserted and left stable.
. Require every boot observable to reach its reset level while the pin is held.
. Start the per-edge monitor, restore `powergood_i`, hold the cold pin ten `clk_ref_i` cycles, release it, and match the bounded released handshake.
. Wait, bounded, for every observable to reach its boot level and for hart 0 to retire its first instruction.
. Assert the ordering inequalities and the ROM vector, then emit the tokens.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-COLD-BOOT-ORDER` |`powergood_stable` < `fuse_sense_done` < `core_reset_release` <= first retired instruction, as strict inequalities between cycle stamps on one `clk_smc_i` timeline. The retire stamp is taken from `tb_cpu_trace_valid_unmasked`, the retire record without the core-reset mask, so a retire during reset would be stamped before the release and fail the compare; any observable that never reached its boot level inside the bound raises first
|`CHK-COLD-BOOT-FIRST-FETCH-AT-ROM-VECTOR` |The first retired hart-0 PC (`tb_cpu_trace_pc_unmasked`) equals the cold-reset ROM vector `rom.adoc` pins, and the retire, stamped from the unmasked probe, happened no earlier than the core reset release
|`CHK-CLUSTER-SELF-ISOLATED-AT-COLD-BOOT` |`tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` read 1 while the cold pin was held and released strictly after both `smc_init_mem_done_o` rose and the core reset released
|`CHK-COLD-BOOT-NOT-CLOSED` |A recorded gap, not a compare: sram-auto-init-runs, repair-triggered-by-fuse-sense-done and the repair/MBIST steps, and release-requires-uncore-out-of-reset, each with the tie-off or missing probe that prevents it. Logged unconditionally
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One line per bounded reset leg the run took, naming the bound and the `clk_ref_i` cycle at which the expected levels matched. The compare is the scoreboard's -- an expired bound raises there -- so these lines are the record of the bounded legs, not a separate compare
|`CHK-COLD-BOOT-CHAIN` |Ledger line in the leaf: the stamp dictionary, the first-fetch cycle and PC, and the scoreboard's reset `WAIT_STATE` count. Logged after the leaf requires at least two booked wait checks and requires the sequence to have observed both the reset levels and a first fetch
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every boot observable reaches its reset level and then its boot level inside the bounds, the three ordering inequalities and the two isolation inequalities hold, the first retired PC is the ROM vector, and the scoreboard books at least two reset `WAIT_STATE` checks. The memory-repair and SRAM-init steps are recorded as not closed and are not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The memory-repair and SRAM-init steps are recorded as not closed and are not part of
the claim: the automatic SRAM zeroing never runs because `smc_disable_sram_auto_init_i` is tied high
in `tb_top`, the repair and MBIST done inputs are tied high so there is no engine to observe, and
the uncore reset has no separate probe.

'''''

[[sec-189-smc_primary_reset_scope_test]]
===== 189 `smc_primary_reset_scope_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_primary_reset_scope_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR legs, with the reset items dispatched to the reset agent through a one-shot; `tb_cpu_core_reset_n`, `tb_cpu_rom_read_count`, the SEP_IN request and response channels and the UART0 TX pad output enable sampled every clock edge of the held window

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: With a core fetching ROM and UART0 mid-frame, the cool pin asserts the primary reset and the cores and the peripheral controllers are held across the whole asserted window; an outbound filter register holding a pattern before the reset reads its generated reset after it, which is how far the fabric half is taken in this bench.

*Test Coverage*:

* Each consumer is first put into a state a reset would visibly end -- the ROM read counter advancing, a pattern resident in `OUTBOUND_FILTER_CTRL[0].END_ADDR`, UART0 enabled and driving a start bit -- so the held observation is not trivially satisfied by an idle DUT.
* Every held claim is a per-sample compare across the window rather than one instant: the core reset must read 0 at every sample and the UART TX pad output enable must read 0 at every sample after a stated settle. A consumer released anywhere inside the window fails.
* The fabric is **not** claimed held, and the four SEP_IN tallies the run records say why rather than standing in as a check. `arready`/`awready` read 1 just before the cool pin drops and 1 at every sample of the window, so ready is not withdrawn under primary reset. `arvalid` reads 0 at every sample because the SEP_IN AXI master takes `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` as its own reset and parks its request lines there, so no request can be presented inside the window and a no-response would be the bench's reset rather than the DUT's refusal. `rvalid`/`bvalid` read 0 for the same reason the window is idle -- on any RTL. None of the four is asserted on.
* The pad *value* probe cannot carry the peripheral claim: `tb_uart0_tx_from_dut` mirrors `core2pad_o`, which a GPIO wrap in reset parks at 0 with its driver off. The pad's output enable is the observable that distinguishes "transmitter stopped driving" from "wrap parked the pin".
* A ROM fetch counted inside the window must sit at its head, before the cores' reset had propagated; an advance later in the window fails as a fetch by a core that was not held.
* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` is armed before the reset with `I3C_CG_EN` set -- a field the RDL resets to 0 whose effect (the I3C clock stopped, its window answering SLVERR) touches nothing this leaf observes -- and the armed word is read back, so the post-reset read can tell a reverted register from an untouched one.
* After release, the outbound filter register, UART0 `CTRL` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` are required to read their generated resets, and core 0's reset release is bounded.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Sample the entry state; prove the cores are fetching by measuring `tb_cpu_rom_read_count` advancing over a window.
. Write and read back the filter pattern; write `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` with `I3C_CG_EN` set and read the armed word back; arm UART0 mid-frame at the slowest divisor so the de-glitched reset assertion lands inside the frame.
. Assert `rst_cool_ni` and match a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on power-good and cold-stable released with both primary resets asserted and left stable.
. Sample the held window every clock edge and assert the two per-sample held claims plus the frozen ROM counter, recording the four SEP_IN tallies.
. Release the pin, match the bounded released handshake, bound core 0's reset release, and read the three registers against their generated resets.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PRIMARY-RESET-CORES-HELD` |`tb_cpu_core_reset_n` read 0 at every sample of the held window, the ROM read counter stopped advancing after the reset propagated, and core 0 released inside its bound after `rst_cool_ni` returned. The pre-reset fetch count is reported as the precondition
|`CHK-PRIMARY-RESET-FABRIC-REVERTED` |The outbound filter register went from the resident pattern to its generated reset across the reset and answered a read again afterwards, so the primary reset reached the fabric configuration registers. The line also carries the four recorded SEP_IN tallies and states that held-state is not claimed and why
|`CHK-PRIMARY-RESET-PERIPHERALS-HELD` |UART0 was mid-frame with its TX pad output enable asserted when the reset landed; the output enable read 0 at every sample after the stated settle; UART0 `CTRL` read its generated reset afterwards, and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, read back with `I3C_CG_EN` set before the reset, read its generated reset
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One line per bounded reset leg the run took, naming the bound and the `clk_ref_i` cycle at which the expected levels matched. The compare is the scoreboard's -- an expired bound raises there -- so these lines are the record of the bounded legs, not a separate compare
|`CHK-PRIMARY-RESET-SCOPE` |Ledger line in the leaf: the held-window sample count, the two per-sample held tallies and the four recorded SEP_IN tallies. Logged after the leaf requires at least two booked reset `WAIT_STATE` checks, the SEP_IN exact-value compare floor, a non-empty held window and a non-zero pre-reset fetch delta
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both per-sample held claims hold across the whole window, the ROM counter freezes at its head, the three registers read their generated resets after release, core 0 releases inside its bound, and the scoreboard books at least two reset `WAIT_STATE` checks and the SEP_IN value-compare floor. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The fabric is not claimed held. The four SEP_IN tallies (`arready`/`awready`,
`arvalid`, `rvalid`/`bvalid`) are recorded, not asserted on, because the SEP_IN AXI master takes
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no` as its own reset and can present no request inside the window, so a
no-response would be the bench's reset rather than the DUT's refusal. The pre-reset fetch count is
reported as the precondition.

'''''

[[sec-191-smc_reset_sync_edge_test]]
===== 191 `smc_reset_sync_edge_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_reset_sync_edge_test`

*BFM / Model*: reset agent for the bounded handshakes, with `rst_cool_ni` driven directly at a controlled sub-cycle phase; `clk_ref_i` and `clk_smc_i` rising-edge timestamps and both synchronized reset outputs read at simulation-time resolution

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Assertion of the synchronized primary resets is asynchronous and anchored on `clk_ref_i`, deassertion is synchronous to each output's own target clock, and more than one target-clock edge separates the release anchor from each output's rise.

*Test Coverage*:

* The pin is driven one third into a clock period on both the assert and the release, so none of the timestamp coincidences below can be an artefact of the stimulus landing on a clock edge.
* Assertion: `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` is required to read 0 at the very instant `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` falls, and that instant is required to equal the most recent recorded `clk_ref_i` rising edge. A synchronous assertion in the SMC domain would have waited for the next `clk_smc_i` edge and could not coincide.
* Deassertion: each output's rise is required to fall exactly on a recorded rising edge of its own clock, and the reference output's rise is required to be a whole number of `clk_ref_i` periods after the release anchor -- the first `clk_ref_i` edge after the pin was released.
* Stages: `clk_rst.adoc` pins no stage count, so only "at least two target-clock edges" is asserted, in both domains, and the measured counts are reported.
* The cool pin is the source because its de-glitch path has no release extender. Both bounded legs are scoreboard `WAIT_STATE` handshakes with exact expected levels, and the leaf requires at least two of them.
* `rst_primary_periph_clk_no` is unconnected in `tb_top` and is not claimed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Start the two edge logs, sample the entry state with every reset observable released.
. Assert `rst_cool_ni` one third into a `clk_smc_i` period; timestamp the reference output's fall, inspect the SMC output at that instant, and check the instant against the `clk_ref_i` edge log. Match the bounded asserted handshake and hold the pin low past the de-glitch window.
. Release `rst_cool_ni` one third into a `clk_ref_i` period; timestamp each output's rise against its own clock's edge log. Match the bounded released handshake.
. Compute the release anchor and the per-domain edge counts, and assert the period relation and the stage minimums.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RESET-SYNC-ASYNC-ASSERT` |`rst_primary_ref_clk_no` and `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` were both asserted at the same simulation instant, and that instant is a recorded `clk_ref_i` rising edge, so the SMC-domain output asserted without waiting for its own clock
|`CHK-RESET-SYNC-SYNC-DEASSERT` |Each output rose exactly at a recorded rising edge of its own target clock, and the reference output's rise is a whole number of `clk_ref_i` periods after the release anchor
|`CHK-RESET-SYNC-MULTI-STAGE` |At least two `clk_ref_i` edges and at least two `clk_smc_i` edges separate the release anchor from the corresponding output's rise. The measured counts are reported; the specification pins no exact stage count
|`CHK-RESET-SYNC-REF-ANCHOR` |Both the assertion instant and the release anchor are `clk_ref_i` rising edges, which is what makes the reference domain the synchronization anchor for these crossings
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One line per bounded reset leg the run took, naming the bound and the `clk_ref_i` cycle at which the expected levels matched. The compare is the scoreboard's -- an expired bound raises there -- so these lines are the record of the bounded legs, not a separate compare
|`CHK-RESET-SYNC-EDGE` |Ledger line in the leaf: the assert instant, both release timestamps and both stage counts. Logged after the leaf requires at least two booked reset `WAIT_STATE` checks and requires the sequence to have timestamped every edge it claims
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the two outputs assert in the same `clk_ref_i`-anchored instant, each releases on a rising edge of its own clock, the reference release is a whole number of reference periods after the anchor, both stage counts are at least two, and the scoreboard books at least two reset `WAIT_STATE` checks. `rst_primary_periph_clk_no` is not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The specification pins no synchronizer stage count, so only the at-least-two-edge
minimum is asserted in each domain and the measured counts are reported. `rst_primary_periph_clk_no`
is unconnected in `tb_top` and is not claimed.

'''''

[[sec-326-smc_jtag_reset_ovrd_walk_test]]
===== 326 `smc_jtag_reset_ovrd_walk_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_reset_ovrd_walk_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN); `tb_jtag_reset_ctrl` drives the packed `jtag_reset_ctrl_i`; `tb_ss_cold_reset_n` / `tb_ss_warm_reset_n` publish every subsystem's `ss_reset_ctrl_o` cold and warm reset

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `jtag_reset_ctrl`; seed 1; tool
Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Every override mux smc_jtag_reset_ctrl_test leaves idle, through its reset pin.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_jtag_reset_ctrl_test` drives the cool override, the warm override released and the subsystem-0 warm override of `jtag_reset_ctrl_i`. The other 65 override muxes of the reset unit -- `ss_warm_reset_n[1..31]`, `ss_cold_reset_n[0..31]`, `fuse_reset_n` and `cold_reset_n` -- never see their select active there, and the warm mux never sees val=0. This leaf takes each one through ovrd=1/val=0, ovrd=1/val=1, ovrd=0/val=1 and idle with the overridden reset released by its source, and through ovrd=1/val=1 with the source asserting it where the bench can arrange that, so each mux input and the select exercise the mux in every combination the override can reach.
* Per-subsystem legs are observed on `ss_reset_ctrl_o[i]` after the mux. The walked pin must move while the other 31 pins of the same vector hold their level, which fails on a wrong bit position in the DV-owned slice table, a swapped ovrd/val half or an override that reaches a neighbour. `SS_WARM_RESET_N` resets released, so the warm walk runs first against the reset value and then with the register asserting one subsystem at a time; `SS_COLD_RESET_N` resets asserted, so the cold walk runs first against the reset value and then with the register written all ones. Both registers are read unchanged across each walk, so the overrides do not write them, and both are restored.
* The warm and fuse legs assert the warm reset alone: `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` drops while `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `rst_cool_no` and the delayed `fuse_reset_n` from the eFuse controller stay released, so the override acts downstream of fuse sensing. `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` clears and `SCRATCH_COLD_0` keeps its pattern after each.
* The cold leg comes last because it resets the whole SMC: `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, the primary and the warm reset assert with `powergood_stable_o` held and every reset source idle (`rst_cold_ni`, `rst_cool_ni`, `powergood_i`, `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, `sep_wdt_reset_n_i`). After the override releases, the eFuse controller re-senses and holds the warm reset; the fuse override at val=1 releases the warm reset while `tb_fuse_sense_done` and the delayed `fuse_reset_n` are still 0, and is dropped once the sense completes. `SS_COLD_RESET_N` returns to its reset value on the pins, and `SCRATCH_COLD_0` reads 0 and takes a pattern again.
* The cold mux is not asked to release a cold reset the pin asserts: the bench models clocked from `rst_cold_ni` would reset while the SMC kept running. Not DTP `IC_RESET`, the boot-stall JTAG override or any reset the pins drive.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense, drive the packed override to 0 and require both subsystem vectors at their register reset values, the top-level resets released and every reset source idle.
. For `ss_warm_reset_n[1..31]`: ovrd=1/val=0 drops that pin with the other 31 held 1; ovrd=1/val=1 returns it; ovrd=0/val=1 and then 0 hold the vector released. Then for `ss_warm_reset_n[0..31]`: write `SS_WARM_RESET_N` with that bit clear, require the pin low, ovrd=1/val=1 must raise it, ovrd=0 must drop it again; restore the register.
. For `ss_cold_reset_n[0..31]` at the register reset: ovrd=1/val=1 raises only that pin and ovrd=0 drops it. Write `SS_COLD_RESET_N` all ones and repeat the released walk of step 2 over `ss_cold_reset_n[0..31]`; read the register unchanged and restore it, requiring the pins to follow.
. Write patterns to `SCRATCH_COLD_0` and `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`. Warm ovrd=1/val=0 must drop the SMC-clock warm reset with the primary reset, `rst_cool_no` and the delayed `fuse_reset_n` held 1; val=1 and the release must return it. Read the warm scratch cleared and the cold scratch kept. Rewrite the warm scratch and repeat with the fuse override.
. Cold ovrd=1/val=0 must take `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, the primary and the warm reset low with `powergood_stable_o` held 1; val=1 must release the chain and the override is then dropped. Once the primary reset returns, fuse ovrd=1/val=1 must release the warm reset before the sense completes; wait for the sense, drop the override, then read both scratch registers cleared and write the cold scratch again.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-IDLE` |Packed override 0: both subsystem vectors read their register resets, the primary, warm and cool resets are released and every reset source is idle
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-SS-WARM` |Each `ss_warm_reset_n[1..31]` went 1→0→1 through its own override with the other 31 pins held 1 and `SS_WARM_RESET_N` unchanged; with the register asserting one subsystem at a time, each `ss_warm_reset_n[0..31]` went 0→1→0 through ovrd=1/val=1; the register was restored and the pins followed
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-SS-COLD` |At the register reset each `ss_cold_reset_n[0..31]` went 0→1→0 through ovrd=1/val=1 alone; with `SS_COLD_RESET_N` written all ones each went 1→0→1 through its own override with the other 31 pins held 1; the register read unchanged and the pins followed its restore
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-WARM` |The warm override asserted and released only the warm reset; `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` cleared and `SCRATCH_COLD_0` kept its pattern
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-FUSE` |The fuse override asserted and released only the warm reset; `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` cleared and `SCRATCH_COLD_0` kept its pattern
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-COLD` |The cold override took the cold chain, primary and warm resets low with `powergood_stable_o` and every source idle; after release the fuse override released the warm reset before the fuse sense finished, the chain, sense and subsystem cold pins recovered, `SCRATCH_COLD_0` read 0 and accepted a pattern again
|`CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-BASIC` |Ledger line: all five legs completed
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-BASIC`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-COLD`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-FUSE`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-IDLE`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-SS-COLD`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-SS-WARM`, `CHK-JTAG-OVRD-WALK-WARM` hold after their compares; every bounded poll expires into a failure naming the pin and its last level. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The cold mux is not asked to release a cold reset the pin asserts, because the bench
models clocked from `rst_cold_ni` would reset while the SMC kept running. DTP `IC_RESET`, the
boot-stall JTAG override and any reset the pins drive are not claimed.

'''''

[[sec-398-smc_ndm_process_extra_bits_test]]
===== 398 `smc_ndm_process_extra_bits_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_ndm_process_extra_bits_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` and
`NDMRESET_PROCESS` accesses; `tb_top` probe `tb_ndmreset_process` (the 4-bit process output, one bit per connected cluster)
read on `clk_smc_i` edges; `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` wait before the first access

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `ndm_extra`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: PROCESS bits above the cluster count are stored, not driven.

*Test Coverage*:

* `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` reads 4 on this harness (`smc-programming.adoc`, External CPU Cluster
  NDM Reset); the leaf derives the bits at and above the count from the value it reads.
* `NDMRESET_PROCESS` bits at and above the count are stored: the register reads back the full
  written pattern, 0xFFFFFFF0 for a count of 4 (`ndm_reset.rdl` `NDMRESET_PROCESS`,
  `smc-programming.adoc`).
* The same bits do not reach the driven bits: the 4-bit `tb_ndmreset_process` reads 0x0 at idle,
  at every one of 64 `clk_smc_i` samples taken after the write, and after the register is
  restored to 0; bits at and above the count have no output pin on this harness (`ndm_reset.rdl`:
  bits below the count are driven, bits at and above it are stored and not driven). Each sample
  is required resolvable, so an X or Z output fails.
* Positive control: writing the below-count mask (0xF for a count of 4) reads back 0xF and
  `tb_ndmreset_process` reaches 0xF within 64 `clk_smc_i` samples, so the probe is live. Writing
  0xFFFFFFFF then reads back 0xFFFFFFFF and `tb_ndmreset_process` reads 0xF at each of 64
  samples, so the bits above the count neither drive nor clear the driven bits.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`, read `NDMRESET_CLUSTER_COUNT` against 4, and require
  `tb_ndmreset_process` to idle at 0x0; stamp step S1.
. Write the above-count mask (0xFFFFFFF0) to `NDMRESET_PROCESS` and read it back against the
  same value.
. Sample `tb_ndmreset_process` on 64 consecutive `clk_smc_i` rising edges and require 0x0 at
  each.
. Positive control: write the below-count mask (0xF), read it back against the same value and
  poll `tb_ndmreset_process` to 0xF within 64 `clk_smc_i` samples; write 0xFFFFFFFF, read it back
  against the same value and require 0xF at each of 64 consecutive samples; stamp step S2 and
  print the checker line.
. Restore `NDMRESET_PROCESS` to 0 (write, then read back 0) and require `tb_ndmreset_process`
  to read 0x0.
. Check the ordered fence: step stamps S1 < S2 strictly increasing, and the checker line printed
  after the S2 stamp, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-NDM-PROCESS-ABOVE-COUNT` |`NDMRESET_PROCESS` reads back exactly the above-count pattern
  that was written, and `tb_ndmreset_process` reads 0x0 at all 64 post-write samples (and idle and
  restore samples), so the stored bits drive no output on the 4-bit probe; the below-count mask
  drives 0xF, and the all-ones write holds 0xF at 64 samples
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: the step ids are S1 then S2 with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, exactly one checker line was printed, and it came after the S2 stamp
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NDM-PROCESS-ABOVE-COUNT` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold; the readback is 0xFFFFFFF0,
`tb_ndmreset_process` is 0x0 at every sample of the above-count leg, 0xF at every sample of the
all-ones leg, and the leaf takes exactly 64 samples in each. Enrolled in:
`all`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-399-smc_reset_pin_deglitch_test]]
===== 399 `smc_reset_pin_deglitch_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_reset_pin_deglitch_test`

*BFM / Model*: reset agent (no external VIP) driving `rst_cold_ni` and `rst_cool_ni` directly
at a third of a `clk_ref_i` period after a rising edge, and sampling the DUT outputs
`powergood_stable_o`, `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`,
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no` and `rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` on `clk_ref_i`; a rising-edge log of
`clk_ref_i` that counts the pulse length

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `deglitch`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A 31-sample low pulse on the cold or cool pin is filtered out.

*Test Coverage*:

* The cold and cool reset inputs each pass a low-sample filter once released: assertion needs 32
  consecutive low samples (`clk_rst.adoc`, Power-Good and Cold Reset; pins in `port_table.adoc`,
  SMC Port Declaration). A pulse one sample short must therefore leave the outputs released.
* The pulse length is measured, not assumed: the leaf counts the `clk_ref_i` rising edges between
  the pin falling and rising and requires exactly 31 for both pins.
* Cold pin: with `rst_cold_ni` low for 31 samples, `powergood_stable_o`,
  `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` and `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` must read 1
  at every one of 400 consecutive `clk_ref_i` samples. A single instant would pass a DUT that
  asserts at some other point of the window, so every sample carries the expectation.
* Cool pin: with `rst_cool_ni` low for 31 samples, `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`,
  `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` and `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` must read 1 at every one of 100 samples.
* Positive controls show the monitored outputs do move in this run and that each pin reaches its
  de-glitcher: a held `rst_cool_ni` low asserts both primary reset outputs inside a bound and
  releases again, and a held `rst_cold_ni` low asserts `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` and both
  primary reset outputs inside a bound and releases again after the cold-reset extension. The four
  bounded legs are scoreboard `WAIT_STATE` handshakes with exact levels, and the leaf requires at
  least four to have been booked.
* The sample count each hold window reports is the number of samples the window sent, and the
  leaf compares it with the window width.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Sample the entry state and require all five reset observables released and resolvable; stamp
  step S1.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cold_ni` pin. Kind: a low pulse of exactly 31 `clk_ref_i`
  edges, one sample short of the 32-sample filter. Expected response: `powergood_stable_o`, the
  stable cold reset and both primary resets stay released at every one of the 400 samples of the
  hold window. Start the 400-sample hold monitor that requires the cold-pin levels before the
  pulse, measure the pulse, wait for the monitor to finish, stamp step S2 and print the cold
  checker line.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cool_ni` pin. Kind: a low pulse of exactly 31 `clk_ref_i`
  edges, one sample short of the 32-sample filter. Expected response: the stable cold reset and
  both primary resets stay released at every one of the 100 samples of the hold window. Start the
  100-sample hold monitor that requires the cool-pin levels before the pulse, measure the pulse,
  wait for the monitor to finish, stamp step S3 and print the cool checker line.
. Positive control: hold `rst_cool_ni` low, match a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on both primary resets
  asserted and the outputs having left their stable state, release the pin and match the bounded
  released handshake. Then hold `rst_cold_ni` low, match a bounded `WAIT_STATE` on the stable
  cold reset and both primary resets asserted, release the pin and match the bounded released
  handshake.
. Check the ordered fence: step stamps S1 < S2 < S3 strictly increasing and each checker line
  printed after its step stamp, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-COLD-31-IGNORED` |With `rst_cold_ni` low for exactly 31 `clk_ref_i` samples, the stable
  cold reset and both primary resets stay released and `powergood_stable_o` stays 1 at all 400
  samples of the window
|`CHK-COOL-31-IGNORED` |With `rst_cool_ni` low for exactly 31 `clk_ref_i` samples, both primary
  resets and the stable cold reset stay released at all 100 samples of the window
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1, S2 and S3 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the two checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-COLD-31-IGNORED`, `CHK-COOL-31-IGNORED` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold; both pulses
measure 31 samples, the hold windows check 400 and 100 samples, and the scoreboard books at least
four reset `WAIT_STATE` checks. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-400-smc_reset_sync_async_assert_test]]
===== 400 `smc_reset_sync_async_assert_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_reset_sync_async_assert_test`

*BFM / Model*: reset agent (no external VIP) for the bounded `WAIT_STATE` handshakes, with
`powergood_i` and the `tb_top` pin `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` driven directly one third into a clock
period; DUT outputs `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`,
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` and the `tb_top` probes
`rst_primary_periph_clk_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, read at simulation-time resolution;
rising-edge logs of `clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i`; `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` wait

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `sync`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Resets assert asynchronously, release on their own clock.

*Test Coverage*:

* `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` and `rst_primary_periph_clk_n` assert
  without waiting for a clock edge; every synchronized reset output releases synchronously to its
  own destination clock after a four-stage synchronizer (`clk_rst.adoc`, Reset Synchronization;
  output names and clocks in its reset synchronization domains table).
* Assertion: `powergood_i` falls one third into a `clk_ref_i` period, so no `clk_ref_i` or
  `clk_periph_i` edge can coincide with the fall. `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` and
  `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` must already read 0 in that same instant, and `rst_primary_periph_clk_n`
  must read 0 in that instant with the last `clk_periph_i` edge elsewhere.
* Release: each output must rise exactly on a rising edge of its own clock, read 1 in that
  instant, and rise no earlier than the fourth own-clock edge after its source released. The
  measured edge counts are reported. `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`,
  `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` and `rst_primary_periph_clk_n` are timed from the `powergood_i`
  release; `rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` from a `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` release.
  Each rise is bounded, so an output that never releases fails with its last observed state.
* Re-assertion: `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` is released, then driven low again two `clk_smc_i` cycles
  later for 16 cycles; `rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` must read 0 at every one
  of those 16 samples, then release on their own edge after the final release. The two cycles
  before the re-assertion are measured and printed without a compare.
* The two bounded handshakes (outputs released after the `powergood_i` release, and after the
  final watchdog release) are scoreboard `WAIT_STATE` checks with exact levels; the leaf requires
  at least two to have been booked and every timestamp it claims to have been taken.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`, sample the entry state and require the five reset observables,
  `rst_primary_periph_clk_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` released and resolvable; stamp step S1.
. Start the three clock edge logs. Drop `powergood_i` one third into a `clk_ref_i` period, read the
  reference outputs in the same instant and require 0 with no `clk_ref_i` edge at that instant;
  stamp step S2 and print the reference-output line.
. Require `rst_primary_periph_clk_n` to read 0 in that instant with no `clk_periph_i` edge at it;
  stamp step S3 and print the periphery line, then hold `powergood_i` low for 64 `clk_ref_i` cycles.
. Release `powergood_i` one third into a `clk_ref_i` period after requiring the four outputs low,
  and require each of the four outputs to rise on its own clock edge, no earlier than the fourth
  edge; match the bounded released handshake. Pulse `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` low (held low until both
  outputs read 0, at least 16 `clk_smc_i` cycles), release it one third into a `clk_smc_i` period and
  require `rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to rise on their own edge; stamp step S4
  and print the release-edge line.
. Drive `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` low for 16 cycles and release it, count the two following
  `clk_smc_i` cycles, drive it low again, and require both outputs 0 at each of 16 samples.
  Release it, require both outputs to rise on their own edge inside the bound, and match the
  bounded released handshake; stamp step S5 and print the re-assertion line.
. Check the ordered fence: step stamps S1 < S2 < S3 < S4 < S5 strictly increasing and each checker
  line printed after its step, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REF-OUTPUTS-ASSERT-ASYNC` |`rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` read 0
  in the same simulation instant as the `powergood_i` fall, with no `clk_ref_i` rising edge at
  that instant
|`CHK-PERIPH-OUTPUT-ASSERTS-ASYNC` |`rst_primary_periph_clk_n` reads 0 in the same simulation
  instant as the `powergood_i` fall, with no `clk_periph_i` rising edge at that instant
|`CHK-EACH-OUTPUT-RELEASES-ON-OWN-EDGE` |Each of the six outputs rises exactly on a rising edge
  of its own clock, reads 1 in that instant and rises no earlier than the fourth own-clock edge
  after its source released; the measured edge counts are reported
|`CHK-SOURCE-REASSERTS-IN-LATENCY` |`rst_wdt_smc_clk_no` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` read 0 at all
  16 `clk_smc_i` samples while the re-asserted `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` is low and then rise on their
  own edge inside the bound; the two cycles before the re-assertion are recorded without
  comparing
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S5 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the four checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold; the two assertion instants coincide with the
`powergood_i` fall, every release lands on its own clock edge at or after the fourth edge, the
re-asserted watchdog source holds both outputs at 0 for all 16 samples, and the scoreboard books
at least two reset `WAIT_STATE` checks. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The two `clk_smc_i` cycles between the watchdog release and its re-assertion are
measured and printed without a compare. The edge counts from each source release to each output's
rise are reported; only the at-least-fourth-edge floor is compared.

'''''

[[sec-401-smc_scratch_banks_test]]
===== 401 `smc_scratch_banks_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_scratch_banks_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) reading and writing `scratch_cold[0..7]` and
`scratch_cold_warm[0..7]` (the two `SCRATCH[8]` banks of the misc wrap, word offsets 0 to 7 in each
bank); `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` wait before the first access

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `scratch`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Sixteen scratch registers reset to 0 and hold independent values.

*Test Coverage*:

* Both scratch banks hold eight 32-bit `SCRATCH.data` registers that reset to 0x0 and are
  software read-write (`scratch.rdl`); the misc wrap places them as `scratch_cold` and
  `scratch_cold_warm` (`misc_wrap.rdl`). All sixteen are read before any write and must read
  0x00000000 after the bring-up cold reset; this is a measured leg, not a proven one, because the
  bench zero-initialises flops and the read cannot fail on a 4-state reset value.
* Independence: for each register in turn a distinct pattern, 0xA5000000 + 16*bank + n for
  register n of the bank (bank 0 `scratch_cold`, bank 1 `scratch_cold_warm`), is written and then
  all sixteen registers are read back against a shadow of what was written. A
  write that disturbs a neighbour in either bank, or the same index in the other bank, fails the
  readback of that neighbour. The sweep is repeated with the bitwise complement of each pattern so
  every bit of every register is driven both ways.
* Every readback carries its expected value on the access, so the scoreboard compares it, and the
  leaf compares it again; the leaf requires exactly 592 SEP_IN accesses
  (16 reset reads, 32 writes each followed by 16 readbacks, and 16 restore write and readback
  pairs).
* After the sweeps each register is restored to 0 and read back as 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; stamp step S1.
. Read all sixteen registers (`scratch_cold[0..7]`, then `scratch_cold_warm[0..7]`) against 0;
  stamp step S2 and print the reset-value line.
. For each bank and each register n, write 0xA5000000 + 16*bank + n and read all sixteen registers back
  against the shadow; then repeat the sweep writing the complement of each pattern. Stamp step
  S3 and print the independence line.
. Restore every register to 0 and read it back as 0.
. Check the ordered fence: step stamps S1 < S2 < S3 strictly increasing and each checker line
  printed after its own step stamp, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SCRATCH-RESET-0` |All sixteen scratch registers read 0x00000000 before any write
  (measured, not proven: the bench zero-initialises flops)
|`CHK-SCRATCH-INDEPENDENT-RW` |After each of the 32 writes (the 0xA5000000 + 16*bank + n patterns,
  then their complements) every one of the sixteen registers reads the shadow value, so each register
  holds its own value and no write changes another register in either bank
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1, S2 and S3 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the two checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SCRATCH-RESET-0`, `CHK-SCRATCH-INDEPENDENT-RW` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold; all
sixteen registers read 0 before the first write (measured), every readback of both sweeps matches
its shadow, and the leaf issues exactly 592 SEP_IN accesses. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The reset-value read of the sixteen scratch registers is a measured leg, not a proven
one: the bench zero-initialises flops, so a read of 0 cannot fail on a 4-state reset value.

'''''

[[sec-402-smc_sync_reg_irq_test]]
===== 402 `smc_sync_reg_irq_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_sync_reg_irq_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for `SYNC_REG` accesses; the `tb_top` probe
`tb_sync_irq` (the `sync_irq_o` output) sampled on `clk_smc_i` rising edges, each sample required
resolvable; `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` wait before the first access

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `sync_irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SYNC_REG.sync drives sync_irq_o and only bit 0 is implemented.

*Test Coverage*:

* `SYNC_REG` holds one implemented field, `sync[0:0]`, software read-write with reset value 0
  (`reset_unit.rdl`, `SYNC_REG`), so it reads 0x00000000 after the bring-up reset, and
  `sync_irq_o` reads 0 with it (`port_table.adoc`, SMC Port Declaration: the output is the
  software-controlled global synchronization bit `SYNC_REG.sync`). This is a measured leg, not a
  proven one, because the bench zero-initialises flops and the read cannot fail on a 4-state
  reset value.
* Writing 0x1 reads back 0x1 and `sync_irq_o` rises; writing 0x0 reads back 0x0 and `sync_irq_o`
  falls. Each transition is polled for at most 64 `clk_smc_i` samples, a bench ceiling and not a
  latency claim; the sample count at which the pin changed is printed.
* Only bit 0 is implemented: writing 0xFFFFFFFE reads back 0x00000000 and `sync_irq_o` stays 0 at
  each of 8 samples; writing 0xFFFFFFFF reads back 0x00000001 and `sync_irq_o` rises.
* `SYNC_REG` is restored to 0 and `sync_irq_o` must fall again inside the bound.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; stamp step S1.
. Read `SYNC_REG` against 0 and sample `tb_sync_irq` at 0; stamp step S2 and print the reset
  line.
. Write 0x1 to `SYNC_REG`, read it back against 0x1, poll `tb_sync_irq` to 1; write 0x0, read it
  back against 0x0, poll `tb_sync_irq` to 0; stamp step S3 and print the drives-pin line.
. Error injection. Point: `SYNC_REG`. Kind: a write of 0xFFFFFFFE, every bit except the
  implemented bit 0. Expected response: the register reads back 0x00000000 and `tb_sync_irq`
  holds at 0 for 8 samples. Then write 0xFFFFFFFF, read it back against 0x00000001 and poll
  `tb_sync_irq` to 1; restore `SYNC_REG` to 0 (write, then read back 0) and poll `tb_sync_irq`
  to 0; stamp step S4 and print the bit-0 line.
. Check the ordered fence: step stamps S1 < S2 < S3 < S4 strictly increasing and each checker
  line printed after its own step, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SYNC-RESET-0` |`SYNC_REG` reads 0x00000000 and `sync_irq_o` reads 0 after the bring-up
  reset (measured, not proven: the bench zero-initialises flops)
|`CHK-SYNC-DRIVES-IRQ` |After `SYNC_REG` is written 0x1 and reads 0x1, `sync_irq_o` reaches 1
  inside the bound, and after it is written 0x0 and reads 0x0, `sync_irq_o` reaches 0 inside the
  bound
|`CHK-SYNC-ONLY-BIT-0` |`SYNC_REG` reads 0x00000000 after a write of 0xFFFFFFFE with `sync_irq_o`
  held at 0 for 8 samples, and 0x00000001 after a write of 0xFFFFFFFF with `sync_irq_o` rising,
  so only bit 0 is stored
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S4 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the three checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold; `SYNC_REG` and `sync_irq_o` read 0 after the bring-up reset (measured), the pin
follows bit 0 inside the 64-sample bound in both directions, the upper bits are not stored, and
the leaf issues at least nine SEP_IN accesses. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The reset-value read of `SYNC_REG` and `sync_irq_o` is a measured leg, not a proven
one, because the bench zero-initialises flops. The 64-sample poll is a bench ceiling and not a
latency claim; the sample count at which the pin changed is printed, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-532-smc_cool_reset_deglitch_window_test]]
===== 532 `smc_cool_reset_deglitch_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cool_reset_deglitch_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN programming and reading `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE`,
`ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_RESET_COUNTER_VALUE` and `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`; the pin `rst_cool_ni` driven on
`clk_ref_i` edges; the FLR request `tb_cfg_flr_pf_active` (`cfg_flr_pf_active_i`); the
isolate-request pad held low through `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` and `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`; probes
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`, `tb_rst_cool_from_flr` (the FLR cool-reset
output) and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each sampled on every `clk_ref_i` edge or, for the warm reset,
on `clk_smc_i`; `tb_skip_mem_repair_o`; `clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `flr`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A low pulse on `rst_cool_ni` shorter than 32 reference-clock samples is rejected, a
high sample restarts the count, the release does not depend on the low duration, and pin segments
inside the FLR hold do not shorten or extend it.

*Test Coverage*:

* Positive control: a 40-cycle low on `rst_cool_ni` asserts primary reset; the offsets from the
  first low to the assertion and from the first high to the release are measured on both primary
  outputs.
* A 31-cycle low leaves both primary resets released at every sample from the first low until 64
  cycles after the pin returned high.
* Low 20, high 1, low 40 asserts primary reset at the same offset from the re-assert low as the
  control does from its first low, and not before 32 consecutive lows.
* A 100-cycle low releases at the same offset from the first high as the 40-cycle low, so the
  release carries the filter and synchroniser offset only.
* FLR alone gives the baseline for the cool-reset fall and rise and the primary reset assertion and
  release.
* Inside the FLR hold, three 20-cycle lows separated by single highs leave primary reset asserted at
  every sample of the hold and release at the same offset from the cool-reset rise as FLR alone.
* Inside the FLR hold, a 40-cycle low, a 10-cycle high and a 40-cycle low leave primary reset
  asserted until the later of the two sources ends and release inside a bench bound of 256
  reference-clock cycles afterwards.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense, hold the isolate-request pad low, write the two FLR counters (pre-delay 0x20,
  hold 0xC0), read them back, require both primary resets and the cool-reset output released, and
  allow 64 reference-clock cycles for the counts to cross into the reference domain.
. Drive `rst_cool_ni` low for 40 reference-clock cycles, then high, and wait for primary reset to
  assert and release; record the assertion offset from the first low and the release offset from the
  first high.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cool_ni` pin. Kind: a 31-cycle low, one sample short of the
  32-sample filter. Expected response: both primary resets read released at every sample through
  the 64 cycles after the pin returned high. Sample both primary resets for those 64 further
  cycles.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cool_ni` pin. Kind: a 20-cycle low broken by a single high
  sample, then a 40-cycle low. Expected response: primary reset asserts at the same offset from
  the re-assert low as the step 2 control does from its first low, and not before 32 consecutive
  lows. Wait for assertion and release, then compare the assertion offset with step 2 and
  require it to be at least 32.
. Drive the pin low for 100 cycles, then high; wait for release; compare the release offset from the
  first high with step 2.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, wait for the cool-reset output to fall and rise and both primary
  resets to release, wait for the warm reset and clear the latched request; record the release
  offset from the cool-reset rise.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cool_ni` pin inside the FLR hold. Kind: three 20-cycle lows
  separated by single high samples, driven once the cool-reset output is low. Expected response:
  primary reset is asserted at every sample from the first assertion to the cool-reset rise and
  releases at the same offset from the rise as step 6. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i` first to start
  the hold.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`; once the cool-reset output is low drive low 40, high 10, low 40, then
  high; require no released sample from the first assertion until the later source ends and the
  release inside the bench bound.
. Print each checker after its compare, stamp the ordered fence two reference-clock cycles after the
  last step, and print the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-COOLRST-GLITCH-REJECT` |After a 40-cycle low asserts primary reset, a 31-cycle low leaves
  `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` released at every sample until 64 cycles
  after the pin returned high; any asserted sample, an absent control assertion or an X sample fails
  it
|`CHK-COOLRST-REASSERT-RESTART` |After low 20, high 1, low 40 primary reset asserts at the same
  offset from the re-assert low as in the control, on both outputs, and no earlier than 32 cycles
  after it; a differing offset, an earlier assertion or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-RELEASE-NO-EXTENSION` |The cycles from the first high to primary release are equal for
  the 40-cycle and the 100-cycle low on both outputs, and are printed as measured; a differing
  offset or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-REASSERT-IN-HOLD` |With three sub-32 low segments in the FLR hold primary reset is
  asserted at every sample of the hold and releases at the same offset from the cool-reset rise as
  FLR alone, inside the bench bound; a released sample, a differing offset or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-RELEASE-REASSERT-HOLD` |With a release and a re-assert of the pin inside the FLR hold
  no sample is released before both sources end and release follows inside the bench bound; a
  released sample, a release past the bound or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S8 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps and the five checker lines printed in order after the last step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait (assertion 128, release 512, cool-reset fall 160,
  cool-reset rise 320 reference-clock cycles, warm reset 50000 `clk_smc_i` cycles, latch clear 64
  polls) is named with its bound and raises AssertionError with the last sampled levels on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-COOLRST-GLITCH-REJECT`, `CHK-COOLRST-REASSERT-RESTART`,
`CHK-COOLRST-RELEASE-NO-EXTENSION`, `CHK-COOLRST-REASSERT-IN-HOLD`,
`CHK-COOLRST-RELEASE-REASSERT-HOLD`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares;
the offsets from a pin edge to a probe are measured and only the equalities and orderings above are
compared. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The offsets from a pin edge to a probe (assertion from the first low, release from
the first high, release from the cool-reset rise) are measured and printed; only the equalities and
orderings between them are compared.

'''''

[[sec-533-smc_cool_reset_pin_flr_overlap_test]]
===== 533 `smc_cool_reset_pin_flr_overlap_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cool_reset_pin_flr_overlap_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN programming and reading `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE`,
`ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_RESET_COUNTER_VALUE` and `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`; the pin `rst_cool_ni` driven on
`clk_ref_i` edges; the FLR request `tb_cfg_flr_pf_active` (`cfg_flr_pf_active_i`); the
isolate-request pad held low through `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` and `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`; probes
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`, `tb_rst_cool_from_flr` (the FLR cool-reset
output), `rst_cold_n_o`, `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, each sampled on
every `clk_ref_i` edge or, for the warm reset, on `clk_smc_i`; `tb_skip_mem_repair_o`; `clk_ref_i`,
`clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `flr`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The FLR cool-reset fall and low duration move by exactly the difference of the
programmed counts, the pin alone asserts primary reset while the cool-reset output and the cold
resets stay deasserted, and a pin low inside the pre-reset count, outlasting the hold or released
early combines with the FLR hold without changing its duration.

*Test Coverage*:

* FLR alone with pre-reset count 0x20 and hold 0x60, then with 0x50 and 0xA0: the fall offset from
  the FLR edge differs by exactly the pre-reset count difference and the low duration by exactly the
  hold difference.
* The cool-reset output is low from its fall to its rise in every FLR run and high at every other
  sample, including the pin-alone window.
* FLR alone asserts primary reset after the FLR edge and releases it after the cool-reset rise.
* A 48-cycle low on `rst_cool_ni` asserts primary reset no earlier than 32 cycles after the first
  low, with the cool-reset output high and both cold resets deasserted at every sample.
* A pin low 8 cycles after the FLR edge, held past the end of the pre-reset count, asserts primary
  reset before the cool-reset fall, which keeps its FLR-alone offset.
* A pin low inside the hold and kept low 56 cycles past its end keeps primary reset asserted until
  the pin release and releases at the pin-alone offset from it.
* A pin low for 40 cycles inside the hold keeps primary reset asserted until the cool-reset rise and
  releases at the FLR-alone offset from it.
* The cool-reset low duration of the three overlap runs equals the FLR-alone duration.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense, hold the isolate-request pad low, write the pre-reset count 0x20 and hold
  0x60, read them back, allow 64 reference-clock cycles for the counts to cross into the reference
  domain, and require both primary resets and the cool-reset output released.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, wait for the cool-reset output to fall and rise and both primary
  resets to release, wait for the warm reset and clear the latched request; program 0x50 and 0xA0,
  read them back, wait 64 cycles and run the FLR sequence alone again.
. Drive `rst_cool_ni` low for 48 reference-clock cycles, then high, and wait for primary reset to
  assert and release; sample every probe on every cycle.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, drive the pin low 8 cycles later and high 4 cycles after the
  cool-reset fall; wait for the cool-reset rise, the primary release and the warm reset.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, drive the pin low 4 cycles after the cool-reset fall and high 56
  cycles after the cool-reset rise; wait for the primary release and the warm reset.
. Pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, drive the pin low 4 cycles after the cool-reset fall and high 40
  cycles later; wait for the cool-reset rise, the primary release and the warm reset.
. Print each checker after its compare, stamp the ordered fence two reference-clock cycles after the
  last step, and print the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-COOLRST-BP-LEVEL` |The cool-reset output is low at every sample from its fall to its rise in
  the five FLR runs and high at every other sample, including the pin-alone window; a sample low
  outside the FLR hold, a sample not low inside it or an X sample fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-COLD-STABLE` |`rst_cold_n_o` and `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` read deasserted at every
  sample of the pin-alone window and of the pre-count and hold overlap windows, with primary reset
  asserted in the pin-alone window as the positive control; an asserted cold output, a missing
  primary assertion or an X sample fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-COLLISION-HOLD` |With the pin outlasting the FLR hold primary reset stays asserted at
  every sample until the pin release, after the cool-reset rise, and releases at the same offset
  from the pin release as in the pin-alone run; a released sample, a differing offset or a timeout
  fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-COLLISION-PRE` |With the pin low inside the pre-reset count primary reset asserts
  before the cool-reset fall, the fall keeps the FLR-alone offset from the FLR edge, and release
  follows the cool-reset rise, the later source, at the FLR-alone offset; a late assertion, a
  differing offset or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-FLR-ALONE-PRIMARY` |In the FLR-alone runs primary reset asserts after the FLR edge and
  no later than the cool-reset fall, stays asserted until the cool-reset rise and releases at the
  first released sample at or after it; the release offset from the rise is kept as the baseline of
  the early-release run; a late or missing assertion, a released sample in the hold, a first release
  before the cool-reset rise or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-FLR-HOLD-COUNT` |The cool-reset low duration of the second count pair minus the first
  equals the programmed hold difference exactly in reference-clock cycles, and the durations are
  printed as measured; a differing delta or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-FLR-PRE-COUNT` |The counters read back as written and the cool-reset fall offset from
  the FLR edge of the second pair minus the first equals the programmed pre-reset difference
  exactly; a differing delta, a readback mismatch or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-HOLD-INVARIANT` |The cool-reset low duration of the three overlap runs equals the
  FLR-alone duration exactly, and all four durations are printed; a differing duration fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-PIN-ALONE-PRIMARY` |After a 48-cycle low primary reset asserts no earlier than 32
  cycles after the first low with the cool-reset output high at every sample, and releases after the
  pin release; the offsets are printed as measured; an earlier assertion, a low cool-reset sample, a
  release before the pin or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-PIN-EARLY-RELEASE` |With the pin released at least 16 cycles before the hold ends
  primary reset stays asserted until the cool-reset rise and releases at the same offset from it as
  in the FLR-alone run; a released sample before the rise or a differing offset fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S5 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps and the ten checker lines printed in order after the last step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait (assertion 128, release 512, cool-reset fall 208,
  cool-reset rise 288 reference-clock cycles, warm reset 50000 `clk_smc_i` cycles, latch clear 64
  polls) is named with its bound and raises AssertionError with the last sampled levels on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-COOLRST-BP-LEVEL`, `CHK-COOLRST-COLD-STABLE`, `CHK-COOLRST-COLLISION-HOLD`,
`CHK-COOLRST-COLLISION-PRE`, `CHK-COOLRST-FLR-ALONE-PRIMARY`, `CHK-COOLRST-FLR-HOLD-COUNT`,
`CHK-COOLRST-FLR-PRE-COUNT`, `CHK-COOLRST-HOLD-INVARIANT`, `CHK-COOLRST-PIN-ALONE-PRIMARY`,
`CHK-COOLRST-PIN-EARLY-RELEASE`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares;
offsets from an edge to a probe are measured and only the deltas, equalities and orderings above are
compared. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The offsets from an edge to a probe and the cool-reset low durations are measured and
printed; only the deltas, equalities and orderings between them are compared.

'''''

[[sec-534-smc_cool_reset_recovery_test]]
===== 534 `smc_cool_reset_recovery_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: RESET

*Source Module*: `smc_cool_reset_recovery_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN reading and writing `SS_CONFIG`, `SS_COLD_RESET_N`,
`ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG`, `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`, `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS`, `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE`,
`ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_RESET_COUNTER_VALUE`, `I2C TIMING0` of instance 0, `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` and
`CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]` at the addresses of the generated address map (`smc_addr`,
`reset_unit_u32`, `cpu_ctrl_u32`); the pin `rst_cool_ni` driven on `clk_ref_i` edges; the FLR
request `tb_cfg_flr_pf_active` (`cfg_flr_pf_active_i`); the isolate-request pad held low through
`tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` and `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`; probes `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`,
`rst_primary_ref_clk_no`, `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, `rst_cold_n_o`, `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no`,
`tb_rst_cool_from_flr` (the FLR cool-reset output) and `tb_isolate_req_o`, each sampled on every
`clk_ref_i` edge; `tb_skip_mem_repair_o`; `clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `flr`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: After the `rst_cool_ni` pin collides with the FLR cool-reset hold, both primary resets
release after the last source ends, the warm reset follows the primary reset, the cold resets never
assert, the reset-unit registers split into those the primary reset clears and those the cold reset
retains, `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS` reads its reset levels, and the FLR isolation latch sets, holds, clears
and sets again with a zero hold count.

*Test Coverage*:

* `SS_CONFIG` and `SS_COLD_RESET_N` read back nonzero patterns, `ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG` and both FLR
  counters read back their programmed values, and the I2C timing, scratch and reset-vector words are
  read before the collision.
* The pin goes low 4 cycles after the cool-reset fall and high 56 cycles after its rise, so it is
  low for at least 32 cycles inside the hold and ends after it; primary reset is asserted at every
  sample until the pin release.
* The warm reset is asserted at every sample at which `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` is asserted and
  releases no earlier than it.
* `rst_cold_n_o` and `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` are deasserted at every sample of the collision
  window, with primary reset asserted in the same window as the positive control.
* After recovery `SS_CONFIG` and `SS_COLD_RESET_N` read their reset value 0 while
  `ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG` and both FLR counters read the programmed values.
* `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS.cool_reset_n_i` and `cool_reset_n_o` read their reset value 1 with `rst_cool_ni`
  and the cool-reset output high; the pin bit, the I2C timing field, `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` and
  `CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]` are printed as measured.
* `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` reads 0 before the FLR edge, 1 after it and 1 after the cool reset ended,
  then 0 after a write of 0xFFFFFFFF with byte strobe 0x1.
* With the hold counter at 0 an FLR edge sets the latch while no reset output asserts in a 384-cycle
  window.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense, hold the isolate-request pad low, write the pre-reset count 0x100 and hold
  0x80, allow 64 reference-clock cycles for the counts to cross into the reference domain, write and
  read back `SS_CONFIG` (0xA5A5A5A5), `SS_COLD_RESET_N` (0x5A5A5A5A), `ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG`
  (0xFFFFFFFF), the I2C0 `TIMING0` THIGH field and `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]`, read both counters and
  `CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]`, and require the resets released.
. Read `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`, pulse `cfg_flr_pf_active_i` and poll the latch until it reads 1 before
  the cool reset starts; wait for the cool-reset output to fall, drive `rst_cool_ni` low 4 cycles
  later, wait for the cool-reset rise, drive the pin high 56 cycles after it, and sample every probe
  each cycle until both primary resets release and the warm reset releases.
. Read `SS_CONFIG`, `SS_COLD_RESET_N`, `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS`, `ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG`, both counters,
  `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`, the I2C0 `TIMING0`, `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` and `CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]`.
. Read the latch, write `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` with 0xFFFFFFFF and byte strobe 0x1, and read it back.
. Write `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_RESET_COUNTER_VALUE` = 0 and allow 64 cycles; read the latch, pulse
  `cfg_flr_pf_active_i`, watch every reset output for 384 reference-clock cycles, read the latch,
  clear it and restore the hold counter to 0x80.
. Print each checker after its compare, stamp the ordered fence two reference-clock cycles after the
  last step, and print the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-COOLRST-COLD-STAYS` |`rst_cold_n_o` and `rst_cold_stable_ref_clk_no` read deasserted at every
  sample of the collision window, with both primary outputs asserted at some samples of it as the
  positive control; an asserted cold output, a missing primary assertion or an X sample fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-CSR-RECOVERY` |The pre-collision readbacks match the written values, `SS_CONFIG` and
  `SS_COLD_RESET_N` read 0 after recovery, and `ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG` and both FLR counters read
  the programmed values; a readback mismatch, a nonzero primary-reset register, a changed retained
  register or an X read fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-ISOLATE-VIS` |After recovery with `rst_cool_ni` and the cool-reset output high,
  `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS` bits 4 and 8 read 1, equal to their reset value, and bit 0 is printed as
  measured; a 0 in either bit, a failed read or an X read fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-CLEAR` |With the latch reading 1, a write of 0xFFFFFFFF with byte strobe 0x1
  leaves it reading 0, and both words are printed; a latch reading 0 before the write or 1 after it
  fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-HOLD0` |With the hold counter at 0 the latch reads 0 before the FLR edge and 1
  after it, every sample of the 384-cycle window has both primary outputs and the cool-reset output
  released, and the latch clears and the hold counter restores; a latch reading 1 before or 0 after
  the edge, a reset assertion in the window or a failed restore fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-SET-HOLD` |The latch reads 0 before the FLR edge, 1 after it and 1 after the
  cool reset ended with every reset output released; a latch reading 1 before the edge, 0 after the
  edge or 0 after the cool reset fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-OTHER-CSR-MEASURED` |The I2C0 `TIMING0` and `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` words before and
  after the cool reset are printed as measured and compared with nothing; a missing line fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-PRIMARY-RELEASE` |Both primary outputs assert after the FLR edge, stay asserted at
  every sample until the pin release, and release after both sources end; the release offsets are
  printed as measured; a missing assertion, a released sample inside the collision, a release before
  the pin or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-RESET-VECTOR` |`CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]` read before the collision and after recovery
  is printed next to the reset vector 0xC0040000 as measured and compared with nothing; a missing
  line or a failed read fails it
|`CHK-COOLRST-WARM-FOLLOWS` |`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` is low at every sample at which
  `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` is low, asserts with it and releases no earlier than it; the first
  warm-high sample at or after the primary release is printed as measured; a released warm sample
  while primary is asserted, an early warm release or a timeout fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S5 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps and the ten checker lines printed in order after the last step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait (cool-reset fall 384, cool-reset rise 256, primary release
  512, warm release 50000 reference-clock cycles, latch set 64 polls, zero-hold watch 384
  reference-clock cycles) is named with its bound and raises AssertionError with the last sampled
  levels on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-COOLRST-COLD-STAYS`, `CHK-COOLRST-CSR-RECOVERY`, `CHK-COOLRST-ISOLATE-VIS`,
`CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-CLEAR`, `CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-HOLD0`, `CHK-COOLRST-LATCH-SET-HOLD`,
`CHK-COOLRST-PRIMARY-RELEASE`, `CHK-COOLRST-WARM-FOLLOWS`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold
after their compares, and `CHK-COOLRST-OTHER-CSR-MEASURED` and `CHK-COOLRST-RESET-VECTOR` print
their measured values; release offsets are measured and only the levels, orderings and register
words above are compared. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: The I2C0 `TIMING0` and `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` words before and after the cool reset,
`CPU_CTRL.RESET_VECTOR[0]` next to the reset vector, and `ISOLATE_REQ_VIS` bit 0 are printed as
measured and compared with nothing. The release offsets and the first warm-high sample after the
primary release are measured; only the levels, orderings and register words are compared.

'''''

[[sec-304-smc_clk_smc_slower_than_ref_test]]
===== 304 `smc_clk_smc_slower_than_ref_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_smc_slower_than_ref_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP); the leaf's own period measurement on the three input clocks

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `clock`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the three clock periods are pinned by the module.

*Objective*: SEP_IN register traffic into the SMC and peripheral clock domains completes with the expected words while the input clocks run with the SMC clock slower than the reference clock and the peripheral clock faster than both.

*Test Coverage*:

* `clk_rst.adoc` constrains one input clock: `clk_periph_i` runs at 100 MHz or faster. It states no relation between `clk_smc_i` and `clk_ref_i` or between `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i`, so every ratio between them is legal. The bench drives the `pll_wrap` oscillators at ref / smc / periph 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns by default, so this relation never runs otherwise.
* The leaf pins ref / smc / periph to 10 / 12 / 8 ns after the base test resolves its periods, measures each clock's period over 64 of its own rising edges, and counts the SMC and peripheral rising edges together across 1024 reference edges, one `smc_clk_fcov` ratio window, before any traffic. The measured periods are compared with the leaf's declared constants, not with the bench configuration that drives the clocks, and each count must be within one edge of what those periods give and fall in the `cg_clk_ratio` class the leaf's name states, so the run is known to have the relation it is named for.
* Register traffic crosses into both domains: the generated resets of `GLOBAL_BASE`, core 0 watchdog `CMP`, `AVS_CFG_0` and every UART `LSR`, then distinct patterns written to every UART `SCR` and every I2C `TARGET_ID` before any is read back, each restored and read back.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_clk_ratio_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT or the configuration can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

[[sec-305-smc_clk_smc_equal_ref_test]]

`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the three clock periods are pinned by the module.

*Objective*: SEP_IN register traffic into the SMC and peripheral clock domains completes with the expected words while the input clocks run with all three input clocks at one period.

*Test Coverage*:

* `clk_rst.adoc` constrains one input clock: `clk_periph_i` runs at 100 MHz or faster. It states no relation between `clk_smc_i` and `clk_ref_i` or between `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i`, so every ratio between them is legal. The bench drives the `pll_wrap` oscillators at ref / smc / periph 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns by default, so this relation never runs otherwise.
* The leaf pins ref / smc / periph to 10 / 10 / 10 ns after the base test resolves its periods, measures each clock's period over 64 of its own rising edges, and counts the SMC and peripheral rising edges together across 1024 reference edges, one `smc_clk_fcov` ratio window, before any traffic. The measured periods are compared with the leaf's declared constants, not with the bench configuration that drives the clocks, and each count must be within one edge of what those periods give and fall in the `cg_clk_ratio` class the leaf's name states, so the run is known to have the relation it is named for.

===== 313 `smc_clk_smc_faster_periph_slower_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_smc_faster_periph_slower_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP); the leaf's own period measurement and edge count on the three input clocks

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `clock`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the three clock periods are pinned by the module.

*Objective*: SEP_IN register traffic into the SMC and peripheral clock domains completes with the expected words while the SMC clock runs between one and two times as fast as the reference clock and the peripheral clock runs slower than it.

*Test Coverage*:

* `clk_rst.adoc` constrains one input clock: `clk_periph_i` runs at 100 MHz or faster. It states no frequency for `clk_ref_i` and no relation between the input clocks, so every ratio between them is legal. The bench drives the `pll_wrap` oscillators at ref / smc / periph 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns by default, so this relation never runs otherwise.
* The leaf pins ref / smc / periph to 8 / 5 / 10 ns after the base test resolves its periods, measures each clock's period over 64 of its own rising edges, and counts the SMC and peripheral rising edges together across 1024 reference edges, one `smc_clk_fcov` ratio window, before any traffic. The measured periods are compared with the leaf's declared constants, not with the bench configuration that drives the clocks, and each count must be within one edge of what those periods give and fall in the `cg_clk_ratio` class the leaf's name states, so the run is known to have the relation it is named for.
* Register traffic crosses into both domains: the generated resets of `GLOBAL_BASE`, core 0 watchdog `CMP`, `AVS_CFG_0` and every UART `LSR`, then distinct patterns written to every UART `SCR` and every I2C `TARGET_ID` before any is read back, each restored and read back.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_clk_ratio_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT or the configuration can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CLK-RATIO-PERIODS` |Each input clock measured the period the leaf declares in its own constants, the SMC and peripheral edge counts across 1024 reference edges are within one of what those periods give, and the counts fall in the `cg_clk_ratio` classes the leaf's name states. A stimulus-integrity check, not a DUT property: it proves the bench drove the declared periods and fails when it did not
|`CHK-CLK-RATIO-CSR` |Every reset read returned its generated value and every co-resident pattern read back exactly, with the scoreboard booking at least `EXPECTED_VALUE_CHECKS` exact compares and the leaf issuing exactly `EXPECTED_ACCESSES` accesses
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `clock`.

*Scope limit*: The specification states no frequency for `clk_ref_i` and no relation between the
input clocks, so this ratio is run as a legal one rather than a specified one;
`CHK-CLK-RATIO-PERIODS` is a stimulus-integrity check that the bench drove the declared periods, not
a DUT property.
'''''
