[[sec-063-smc_dma_cg_activity_test]]
===== 63 `smc_dma_cg_activity_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_cg_activity_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcJtagAxiAgent` (JTAG-AXI bench agent over the `tb_top` JTAG-AXI bridge)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `clock`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`, `dma_cg`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RANDCFG: the seed draws the extra hysteresis sweep gaps, the race hysteresis and
the early, back-to-back and late-margin cycle counts; the expected gate activity is a function of
the drawn configuration.

*Objective*: LIVE DMA activity/enable clock-gating check.

*Test Coverage*:

* After the base steps, whose evidence tokens are emitted unchanged, `_p2_extension`, called once at the end of `body()`, adds the full-range hysteresis sweep {0,1,32,63,64} and the activity-reassert race.
* CG_HYSTERESIS_W==6 (hw/sys/smc/doc/dma.adoc) -- gap=64 exercises the field's own truncation (64 & 0x3F == 0), not a TB special case, and its expectation is the truncated value 0, not a `<= 63` bound that no RTL can violate.
* Sweep gaps {0, 1, 32, 63, 64} plus seed extras are all driven and all exactly asserted, but only {32, 63, 64} are BOOKED as covered cells: the 0..8 band is booked UNPROVEN and must not be counted as covered by any closure report -- see `P2_LOW_BAND_EXCLUSION_REASON` in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-GATE-OFF` |After the DMA goes idle the gated clock's last toggle lies inside the hysteresis window and zero toggles follow across the idle observation window; a late or leaking gate fails
|`CHK-DMA-GATING-DISABLED` |With DMA clock gating disabled the clock toggles on every cycle of the observation window
|`CHK-DMA-HYST-RACE` |Named compare in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DMA-HYST-SWEEP` |Named compare in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DMA-WAKEUP-BACKEND` |Named compare in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DMA-WAKEUP-FRONTEND` |A new DMA start wakes the gated clock within one cycle of busy and the clock free-runs for the whole wake-up window; a late resume or a missing edge fails
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Non-vacuity count in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`
|`CHK-NONVAC-P2` |Named compare in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Named compare in `smc_dma_cg_activity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DMA-GATE-OFF`, `CHK-DMA-GATING-DISABLED`, `CHK-DMA-HYST-RACE`, `CHK-DMA-HYST-SWEEP`, `CHK-DMA-WAKEUP-BACKEND`, `CHK-DMA-WAKEUP-FRONTEND` (and 3 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `clock`.

*Scope limit*: Of the hysteresis sweep gaps {0, 1, 32, 63, 64} plus seed extras, all driven and
exactly asserted, only {32, 63, 64} are booked as covered cells; the 0..8 band is booked unproven
and must not be counted as covered by any closure report.
'''''

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run the SMC OSS I2C clock-gate sanity scenario.

*Test Coverage*:

* Dispatches one SmcI2cItem SAMPLE.
* The agent driver reads `tb_i2c_cg_en` / `tb_i2c_debug_lo` and broadcasts the result; the scoreboard exact-compares the post-reset clock-gate default `tb_i2c_cg_en == 0`.
* That compare is a negative check, and the scoreboard *silently* downgrades it to `OBSERVED-ONLY (NOT checked evidence)` when the run holds no liveness credit for `tb_i2c_cg_en` -- it does not fail.
* The sequence-side gate below therefore consumes the retained sample into the property that makes the run evidence at all: the probe carries a same-run credit (so a stuck-at-0 / mis-bound net is excluded) **and** the sample read the gated default.
* The credit is fed by the passive ledger in `env/smc_probe_liveness.py` from a DUT observation of the probe at 1, produced here by the test's `probe_positive_controls = ("i2c_cg_en",)` ([NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL]).
* `tb_i2c_debug_lo` stays observed-only: it has no SPEC/RDL-sourced reset value in this environment, so this sequence states no expectation for it.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_cg_sanity_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CG-SANITY-GATED` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_cg_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-CG-SANITY-GATED` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: `tb_i2c_debug_lo` stays observed-only: it has no specification- or
register-description-sourced reset value in this environment, so the sequence states no expectation
for it.
'''''

[[sec-182-smc_clock_domain_connectivity_test]]
===== 182 `smc_clock_domain_connectivity_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clock_domain_connectivity_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the UART CSRs; `tb_uart0_tx_from_dut` timestamped at simulation-time resolution

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The UART 16550 is clocked from `clk_periph_i`: an all-zero frame holds TX low for nine bit times of 16 x (DIVISOR + 1) peripheral-clock periods, within two peripheral clocks.

*Test Coverage*:

* Before the measurement the sequence requires the run's `clk_periph_i` and `clk_smc_i` periods to differ, and requires the same frame clocked from `clk_smc_i` to fall outside the tolerance. Without that, the compare could not tell the two domains apart on this seed.
* TX is required idle-high after the divisor programming and before `THR` is written; the start of the frame is bounded at three bit times of `THR`, and the low pulse is bounded at twice the expected width. Both bounds raise rather than being absorbed.
* The expected pulse is computed from the programmed divisor and the run's configured peripheral-clock period, not read back from the DUT.
* Only the UART cell of the peripheral-clock scenario is closed. The AVSBus, I2C and I3C cells need their bus protocols in flight, the PLL wrapper is a behavioural model here with no reference-clock consumer to observe, and `rst_telemetry_ni` is tied to the cold reset in `tb_top`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_clock_domain_connectivity_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer: ungate the UART clock, enable UART0, program the divisor through `LCR.DLAB`, confirm TX idle-high, write an all-zero byte to `THR`, timestamp the falling and rising edge of the frame's low pulse, compare it with nine peripheral-clock bit times, and restore the clock-gate register. The leaf then books a protocol-VIP record against a stimulus floor.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-ON-CLK-PERIPH` |The measured low pulse equals nine bit times of the run's `clk_periph_i` period within two peripheral clocks. Logged only after that compare holds; the line also prints what the same frame would have measured on `clk_smc_i`, which the sequence proved lies outside the tolerance
|`CHK-CLOCK-DOMAIN-NOT-CLOSED` |A recorded gap, not a compare. Names the cells of this scenario the bench cannot drive -- avsbus/i2c/i3c-on-clk-periph, clk-ref-reaches-pll-wrapper, telemetry-reset-asserted/released -- each with its reason. Logged unconditionally
|`CHK-CLOCK-DOMAIN-CONNECTIVITY` |Ledger line in the leaf: the measured pulse, the expected pulse and the tolerance, logged after the leaf requires the sequence to have produced a measurement at all. The compare itself is the sequence's; this line carries none of its own
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the UART0 all-zero frame holds TX low for nine `clk_periph_i` bit times within two peripheral clocks, having been proven distinguishable from the `clk_smc_i` alternative on this seed. The other cells of the peripheral-clock scenario are recorded as not closed and are not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Only the UART cell of the peripheral-clock scenario is closed. The AVSBus, I2C and
I3C cells need their bus protocols in flight, the PLL wrapper is a behavioural model with no
reference-clock consumer to observe, and `rst_telemetry_ni` is tied to the cold reset in `tb_top`;
these are recorded as not closed and are not part of the claim.

'''''

[[sec-403-smc_avs_cfg_csr_cdc_test]]
===== 403 `smc_avs_cfg_csr_cdc_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_avs_cfg_csr_cdc_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`env.sys_axi_agent`, `SmcSysAxiItem`, 4-byte accesses, 50 us
access bound, byte strobe on the AVS_CFG_1 lane-2 write) to `AVS_CFG_0`, `AVS_CFG_1` and
`AVS_CONFIG` at AVSBus controller window offsets 0x4050, 0x4054 and 0x4058, crossing the AVSBus
AXI-Lite CDC bridge into the `clk_periph_i` domain; AVS clock observed at the pad on
`tb_top.tb_avs_clk_from_dut` (`core2pad_o[49]`, 100 us edge bound); `tb_top.clk_periph` for the
64-period wait; no protocol VIP is attached

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: AVS_CFG_1 and AVS_CONFIG hold their reset words, field values, byte
strobes, force-bit pulse and write-read order across the AVSBus CDC
bridge.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CFG_1` reads 0x00000003 after reset (`AVS_CLOCK_SELECT[1:0]` reset 3, every other field reset
  0), `AVS_CONFIG` reads 0x00000001 (`AVS_GPIO_ENABLE[0]` reset 1) and `AVS_CFG_0` reads 0x00051000
  (`MAX_RETRIES[23:16]` reset 5, `RESYNC_INTERVAL[15:0]` reset 0x1000), per `avsbus_controller.rdl`.
* Each `AVS_CFG_1` field written alone through the programmer's gated order (set
  `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS[10]`, write the fields, clear it; `interface.adoc` of the AVSBus
  controller) reads back as written with every other field unchanged: `AVS_CLOCK_SELECT` 2'b10 then
  2'b11, `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE[8]` 1 then 0, `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS[10]` 1 then 0,
  `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE[23:16]` 0x08, `CLK_DIVIDER_DUTY_CYCLE_NUMERATOR[31:24]` 0x40.
* A write with only the byte-lane-2 strobe (0x4) changes `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` to 0x10 and leaves
  bytes 0, 1 and 3 at their pre-write values although the write data differs in those lanes.
* `FORCE_SLAVE_RESYNC_OPERATION[9]` is a single-pulse field (`avsbus_controller.rdl`): after a write
  of 1 it reads 0 immediately and 64 `clk_periph_i` periods later.
* Bits of `AVS_CFG_1` that carry no field: their read values before and after a write of ones are
  measured and printed, since the specification does not state the value; the defined fields and the AVS clock
  period over eight periods at the pad are compared unchanged by that write.
* The `AVS_CFG_1` divider value written and read back through the CDC bridge, and write-then-read
  `AVS_CFG_0` / `AVS_CFG_1` writes outstanding together on one AXI ID followed by both reads
  outstanding together, across the bridge (`clk_rst.adoc`, clock-domain responsibilities table).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `AVS_CFG_0` and compare it with the reset word 0x00051000; read `AVS_CFG_1`; keep both words
  for restoring; stamp step S1.
. Read `AVS_CFG_1` and compare it with the reset word 0x00000003; read `AVS_CONFIG` and compare it
  with 0x00000001; require the saved `AVS_CFG_1` to equal the reset read. Log the words and the
  `MAX_RETRIES` / `RESYNC_INTERVAL` fields of the saved `AVS_CFG_0`.
. Through the gated sequence write `AVS_CLOCK_SELECT` = 2'b10 then back to 2'b11 and
  `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE` = 1 then 0, reading `AVS_CFG_1` back after each and comparing it with the
  full word written; write `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS` = 1 then 0 directly and compare each
  readback; then through the gated sequence write `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` = 0x08 and
  `CLK_DIVIDER_DUTY_CYCLE_NUMERATOR` = 0x40 with the same readback compare.
. Read `AVS_CFG_1`, set `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS`, write the word with data 0xA5105AC3 differing
  from the stored bytes in lanes 0, 1 and 3 and strobe 0x4 only (`CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` = 0x10), read
  it back and compare it with the gated pre-write word with only the divider replaced; clear the
  gate and compare the readback.
. Write `FORCE_SLAVE_RESYNC_OPERATION` = 1, read `AVS_CFG_1` immediately, wait 64 `clk_periph_i`
  periods, read again; require bit 9 = 0 and the held word on both reads.
. Read `AVS_CFG_1`, measure eight periods of the pad clock, write ones to every bit outside the
  defined fields, read again and measure again; require the defined fields and the eight-period span
  to be unchanged; write the defined fields back with zeros in the unallocated bits and compare the
  defined fields.
. Write `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` = 0x08 through the gated sequence with the other fields preserved and
  compare the readback at 0x4054.
. Write `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` = 0x06 gated and read it back immediately; then, with the gate set,
  issue `AVS_CFG_0` (one `MAX_RETRIES` bit and one `RESYNC_INTERVAL` bit toggled) and `AVS_CFG_1`
  as one group of two writes on one AXI ID, then `AVS_CFG_0` and `AVS_CFG_1` as one group of two
  reads on that ID, and compare each read with the word written; clear the gate.
. Restore `AVS_CFG_0` and, through the gated sequence, `AVS_CFG_1` to the saved words; log the
  bounded waits and the ordered step fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-CSR-RESET` |`AVS_CFG_1` reads 0x00000003, `AVS_CONFIG` reads 0x00000001 and `AVS_CFG_0`
reads 0x00051000, all with OKAY responses.
|`CHK-AVS-CSR-FIELDS` |After each single-field gated write `AVS_CFG_1` reads back the full word
written, so the written field holds its value and every other field holds what it held before, for
select, stop, turn-off, divider and numerator.
|`CHK-AVS-CSR-BYTE-LANE-2` |After the lane-2-only strobed write `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` reads 0x10 and
bytes 0, 1 and 3 read exactly their pre-write values.
|`CHK-AVS-CSR-FORCE-PULSE` |After a write of 1 to bit 9 `AVS_CFG_1` reads bit 9 = 0 and the held
word, both immediately and 64 `clk_periph_i` periods later.
|`CHK-AVS-CSR-UNALLOCATED` |A write of ones to the bits without a field leaves the defined fields
and the eight-period AVS clock span at the pad unchanged; the unallocated bits' own read values
before and after are measured and printed, not compared.
|`CHK-CDC-AVS-RT` |The read at 0x4054 after the gated write returns `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` = 0x08 with
the other fields as before, through the CDC bridge with OKAY.
|`CHK-CDC-AVS-ORDER` |The read after the immediate write returns the written word, and after the
`AVS_CFG_0` and `AVS_CFG_1` writes issued together as one group the two reads, also issued together
on one AXI ID, return those words in issue order.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered step stamps S1 to S8 are strictly increasing, the seven checker lines
print in the listed order and each after its own step, and the restore completes after the last
step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits: the 50 us SEP_IN access bound and the 100 us AVS
clock edge bound both fail the run on expiry, and the 64-period `clk_periph_i` wait is a counted
wait whose following read is compared; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-AVS-CSR-RESET`, `CHK-AVS-CSR-FIELDS`, `CHK-AVS-CSR-BYTE-LANE-2`,
`CHK-AVS-CSR-FORCE-PULSE`, `CHK-AVS-CSR-UNALLOCATED`, `CHK-CDC-AVS-RT` and `CHK-CDC-AVS-ORDER` hold
after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. The values of
the unallocated `AVS_CFG_1` bits are not claimed. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The read values of the `AVS_CFG_1` bits that carry no field, before and after the
write of ones, are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state
them. The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-404-smc_avs_clock_select_test]]
===== 404 `smc_avs_clock_select_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_avs_clock_select_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` reads and writes of `AVS_CFG_1`, with the driver's
access bound from the bench configuration); AVS clock observed at the pad on
`tb_top.tb_avs_clk_from_dut` (`core2pad_o[49]`, 100 us edge-wait bound, rising and falling edges
timestamped in ps); clock sources `clk_ref_i` (10 ns) and `clk_periph_i` (5 ns) at the default
period triple, the expected table periods formed from the configured clock periods; run seed from `RANDOM_SEED` for the order of the transitions; no protocol VIP

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only the order in which the walk visits the
`AVS_CLOCK_SELECT` settings; every setting is visited and has its table period as the stated
outcome.

*Objective*: Each AVS_CLOCK_SELECT setting and each change between settings puts
its table period on the AVS clock pad.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CLOCK_SELECT[1:0]` of `AVS_CFG_1` selects the AVS clock: 2'b00 the peripheral clock directly,
  2'b01 the peripheral clock divided, 2'b10 the reference clock directly, 2'b11 the reference clock
  divided by `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` (`avsbus_controller.rdl`, `interface.adoc` clock architecture
  table). At the default 10 ns reference and 5 ns peripheral periods with the divider at its
  effective default of 4 (`CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` resets to 0, which keeps the hardware-default
  divisor of 4) the periods are 5 ns, 20 ns, 10 ns and 40 ns.
* Every select value is programmed through the programmer's gated order (set
  `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS[10]`, write the select, clear it) and `AVS_CFG_1` reads back the word
  written.
* All 12 ordered pairs of distinct select values are exercised in a seed-drawn order; each pair
  programs the first value, requires its table period, then programs the second and requires its
  table period.
* A select change written without the gate is measured and printed, since the specification
  does not state the value for that interval; the gated reprogram of the same value afterwards must end at its table
  period.
* The measured high fraction of the pad clock is printed for each window and is not compared.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `AVS_CFG_1`, require `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE[8]` clear, and take the word (gate bit cleared)
  as the starting configuration.
. For select 0, 1, 2 and 3 in turn write the gated sequence, read `AVS_CFG_1` back against the word
  written, align to a low level on the pad clock and measure eight rising-edge periods, repeating
  the window until one has every rise-to-rise gap at the table value; require the mean period to
  equal the table value (5, 20, 10, 40 ns).
. Draw the 12 ordered pairs of distinct select values in the order of the run seed; for each pair
  program and measure the first value against its table period, then program and measure the second
  value and require its table period.
. Write the next select value with `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS` clear, read `AVS_CFG_1` back against
  the word written, measure one window on the pad and print its period and high fraction, or print
  that no edge arrived within the bound; then program the same select through the gated sequence and
  require its table period.
. Log the bounded waits, then require the step stamps strictly increasing, the fence terms in order
  and the three checker lines in order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-SELECT-TABLE` |For each select value the gated write reads back as written and the settled
eight-period mean at the pad equals 5 ns, 20 ns, 10 ns and 40 ns for 2'b00, 2'b01, 2'b10 and 2'b11,
exact at picosecond resolution.
|`CHK-AVS-SELECT-TRANSITIONS` |After each of the 12 gated ordered transitions, in the seed's order,
the pad period equals the new select's table value, and the value before the transition equalled the
old select's table value.
|`CHK-AVS-SELECT-UNGATED-RECOVERY` |The behaviour of the ungated select change is measured and
printed with no value asserted for it, and the gated reprogram of the same select afterwards ends at
that select's table period.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps are strictly increasing, the fence terms SELECT_TABLE_MEASURED,
TRANSITIONS_12_DONE, UNGATED_WRITE and GATED_RECOVERY_MEASURED occur in that order, and the three
checker lines print in the listed order.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits: the 100 us AVS edge wait and the SEP_IN access
bound, each failing the run on expiry with the last pad level; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-AVS-SELECT-TABLE`, `CHK-AVS-SELECT-TRANSITIONS` and
`CHK-AVS-SELECT-UNGATED-RECOVERY` hold after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. The pad behaviour in the ungated interval and the high
fraction are not claimed. `AVS_CFG_1` is not restored at the end of the test. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The pad period in the interval after a select change written without the gate is
measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state the value for that
interval. The measured high fraction of the pad clock is printed for each window and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-405-smc_cg_ctrl_reg_access_test]]
===== 405 `smc_cg_ctrl_reg_access_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_cg_ctrl_reg_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcSysAxiItem`, 64-bit read and write of `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` at
the `smc_base_config` block offset 0x18, 50 us access bound; 32-bit narrow writes at 0x18 and 0x1C
and a strobed 64-bit write); register bits: the fourteen `cg_en` enables in bits 13:0 (`dma_cg_en`
is bit 0, the telemetry enable bit 13) and `cg_hysteresis` in bits 29:24; no protocol VIP and no
probe is sampled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL resets to the documented value and holds its
enables and hysteresis over SEP_IN accesses.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads enables 13:0 = 0 and `cg_hysteresis[29:24]` = 0x1f after reset, with an
  OKAY response (`smc_base_config.rdl`).
* Walking one and walking zero across the fourteen enables: each enable alone set from the base
  value, and each alone cleared from all-ones, reads back the written pattern with `cg_hysteresis`
  still 0x1f, 14 of 14 cells in each direction.
* `cg_hysteresis` values 0x00, 0x01, 0x1f, 0x20 and 0x3f read back as written in bits 29:24 with the
  enables held all clear and then all set.
* Writes of ones to the reserved bits 23:14 and 63:30 are measured and printed; only that the
  defined fields keep their held value is compared, since the specification does not state the
  value reserved bits must show.
* Narrow accesses (32-bit low-word write, 32-bit high-word write, 64-bit write with byte strobe
  0x05) are measured and printed; they must complete, and their responses and resulting values are
  not claimed.
* Repeated writes: the same value written twice, a 1-0-1 sequence on one enable, and two
  successive writes read back as the last value written.
* The register is written back to its reset base value after every step so that no peripheral window
  is accessed while an enable is set.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check that the bench masks place `dma_cg_en` at bit 0, the fourteenth enable at bit 13 and
  `cg_hysteresis` as a six-bit field at bit 24; stamp step S1, which issues no register write.
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; require enables 13:0 equal to 0 and `cg_hysteresis` equal to 0x1f.
. For each enable i from 0 to 13 write the base value with bit i set, read back and require enable
  bits equal to 1 << i and `cg_hysteresis` 0x1f; write the base value back after each.
. Write all fourteen enables set; for each i clear enable i alone, read back and require the enables
  to equal all-ones with bit i clear and `cg_hysteresis` 0x1f; restore all-ones after each cell,
  then write the base value.
. For both enable patterns (all clear, all set) write each hysteresis value of 0x00, 0x01, 0x1f,
  0x20 and 0x3f, read back and require the hysteresis and the enables to match; restore the base
  value after each pattern.
. Write the base value with ones in bits 23:14, then in bits 63:30, tolerating any response; read
  back after each, require the defined fields to equal the base value, print the response and the
  reserved bits; restore.
. Issue the 32-bit low-word write of 0x555, the 32-bit high-word write of 0x2A000000 and the 64-bit
  write of 0x1500000000000A0A with strobe 0x05, each tolerating any response; read back after each
  and print; restore after each.
. Write enable 5 set twice and require the read back to equal the value; write 1, 0, 1 to enable 3
  and require the final read back; write enable 2 then enable 9 successively and require the read
  back to hold enable 9 only; restore after each sequence.
. Require the step stamps strictly increasing and the seven checker lines in order, each after its
  own step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CGC-RESET-VALUE` |After reset enables 13:0 read 0 and `cg_hysteresis` reads 0x1f, with an OKAY
response.
|`CHK-CGC-WALKING-ONE` |In all 14 cells the enable written alone reads back set, the other thirteen
read clear, and `cg_hysteresis` reads 0x1f, with OKAY responses.
|`CHK-CGC-WALKING-ZERO` |In all 14 cells from all-ones the enable cleared alone reads back clear,
the other thirteen read set, and `cg_hysteresis` reads 0x1f, with OKAY responses.
|`CHK-CGC-HYST-RANGE` |Each of the five `cg_hysteresis` values reads back as written in both the
all-clear and all-set enable patterns, and no enable changes from a hysteresis write.
|`CHK-CGC-RESERVED-BITS` |The writes of ones to bits 23:14 and 63:30 complete and the defined fields
read back the held base value; the reserved bits' own response and value are measured and printed
without a compare.
|`CHK-CGC-NARROW-ACCESS` |The narrow writes complete within the bound; their responses and the
resulting register values are recorded without comparing them.
|`CHK-CGC-REWRITE` |After the same-value write twice, the 1-0-1 sequence and the successive pair
the read back equals the last value written, other fields hold the base value, and every response is
OKAY.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps are strictly increasing and the seven checker lines print in the
listed order, each after the step it belongs to.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CGC-RESET-VALUE`, `CHK-CGC-WALKING-ONE`, `CHK-CGC-WALKING-ZERO`,
`CHK-CGC-HYST-RANGE`, `CHK-CGC-RESERVED-BITS` (defined fields only), `CHK-CGC-REWRITE` hold after
their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` printed at the end; `CHK-CGC-NARROW-ACCESS` records the
narrow-access responses and values without claiming them. The specification does not state the
reserved-bit and narrow-access values. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response and the read value of the reserved bits 23:14 and 63:30 after the
writes of ones are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state
the value reserved bits must show. The responses and resulting register values of the narrow
accesses (32-bit low-word and high-word writes, strobed 64-bit write) are recorded and not claimed;
only their completion is required.

'''''

[[sec-406-smc_clk_ratio_base_config_test]]
===== 406 `smc_clk_ratio_base_config_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_ratio_base_config_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` with `SmcSysAxiItem`; 64-bit reads of `GLOBAL_BASE`,
`LOCAL_BASE` and `REGION_SIZE`, 32-bit reads and writes of the three `HANG_DET_*_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`
registers, 64-bit write of `LOCAL_BASE`; 50 us access bound) into the `smc_base_config` block at the
bench-default `clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` periods of 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns; the
fuse-sense-done wait is bounded at 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles; register addresses come from the
generated address map; no protocol VIP and no probe is sampled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: The smc_base_config base, size and hang-detector threshold
registers show their reset values and accept or ignore writes as
documented.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset reads, each with an OKAY response and none sharing an address: `GLOBAL_BASE` 0x40000000,
  `LOCAL_BASE` 0xC0000000, `REGION_SIZE` 0x01000000, and the three `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI`,
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL` timeout thresholds 0x1000 each
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`, `memmap.adoc`).
* `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` is a read-write 20-bit `value[19:0]` field
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`): 0x5A5A5 reads back as written with no bit above bit 19 set, and the reset
  value 0x1000 written back reads as 0x1000.
* `LOCAL_BASE` is a read-only register (`smc_base_config.rdl`): a write of 0xB0000000 leaves it at
  0xC0000000; the write's response code is measured and printed because the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done within 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles and stamp the bring-up step.
. Read `GLOBAL_BASE`, `LOCAL_BASE`, `REGION_SIZE` and the three timeout thresholds, require distinct
  addresses, an OKAY response and the reset values 0x40000000, 0xC0000000, 0x01000000 and 0x1000 for
  each threshold.
. Write 0x5A5A5 to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` and read it back, requiring 0x5A5A5 with
  bits above 19 clear; write 0x1000 back and require the read to return 0x1000.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only `LOCAL_BASE` register of the `smc_base_config` block. Kind:
  a write of 0xB0000000 to a read-only register, with any response tolerated. Expected response:
  `LOCAL_BASE` still reads 0xC0000000, equal to the read taken before the write; the response code
  is recorded. Read `LOCAL_BASE` and require 0xC0000000 before the write; read `LOCAL_BASE` again
  after it and require it equal to the first read.
. Log the bounded waits, then require the fence terms BRINGUP_DONE, BASECFG_RESET_READS,
  THRESHOLD_WRITE_READ, LOCAL_BASE_BEFORE, LOCAL_BASE_WRITE and LOCAL_BASE_AFTER in order with
  strictly increasing stamps, and the three checker lines in order, each after its step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BASECFG-RESET-READ` |The six registers read their reset values (0x40000000, 0xC0000000,
0x01000000 and 0x1000 three times) with OKAY responses.
|`CHK-BASECFG-THRESHOLD-WRITE` |`HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` reads 0x5A5A5 (bits above 19
clear) after the write and 0x1000 after the restore write, with OKAY responses.
|`CHK-BASECFG-RO-IGNORED` |`LOCAL_BASE` reads 0xC0000000 both before and after the write of
0xB0000000; the write response code is measured and printed and is not compared with any value.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms occur in the listed order with strictly increasing stamps and the
three checker lines print in order, each after the step it belongs to.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense done in clock cycles, SEP_IN access at
50 us) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-BASECFG-RESET-READ`, `CHK-BASECFG-THRESHOLD-WRITE` and
`CHK-BASECFG-RO-IGNORED` hold after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`
printed at the end. The response code of the `LOCAL_BASE` write is not claimed. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code of the write to the read-only `LOCAL_BASE` register is measured
and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state it. The bounded waits are
recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-407-smc_clk_ratio_handshake_stall_test]]
===== 407 `smc_clk_ratio_handshake_stall_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_ratio_handshake_stall_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq`, `SmcSysAxiItem` with `AxiTimingProfile` from
`ocah_axi_vip`: `r_ready_delay`, `w_delay` and `b_ready_delay`; 50 us access bound) at the
bench-default 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns `clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` triple, to UART0 `SCR[0]`
(UART per-port AXI-Lite bridge into the `clk_periph_i` domain) and to `SCRATCH[0]` (SMC-domain
scratch path); passive per-`clk_smc` sampling of `tb_top.s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready`,
`s_axi_awvalid`, `s_axi_awready`, `s_axi_wvalid`, `s_axi_wready`, `s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`,
`s_axi_rresp`, `s_axi_bvalid`, `s_axi_bready` and `s_axi_bresp`; fuse-sense-done wait bounded at
200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Stalled R and B handshakes and trailing write data complete
once with correct data on the peripheral and SMC clock
domains.

*Test Coverage*:

* A read to UART0 `SCR[0]` whose RREADY is held 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles returns the preloaded 0x5A
  with OKAY, with R stalled for a positive number of cycles, RVALID held from its first cycle until
  the handshake, and exactly one R beat; the cycles from
  RREADY rising to completion are measured and printed, since the specification gives no bound for
  them (`fabric.adoc` peripheral ports cross to the peripheral clock, `memmap.adoc` register
  interface standards).
* A write of 0xA5 to UART0 `SCR[0]` whose data trails the address by 64 cycles and whose BREADY is
  held 256 cycles draws exactly one OKAY B beat, shows a W trail of at least 64 cycles and a B stall with BVALID held
  from its first cycle until the handshake, and lands: `SCR[0]` reads 0xA5 afterwards.
* The same stalled read and trailing-data stalled write on `SCRATCH[0]` (`clk_rst.adoc` clock-domain
  responsibilities): read returns 0xC3C3C3C3, the 0x3C3C3C3C write lands, each with exactly one OKAY
  beat.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, start the per-cycle sampler of the `s_axi` channels, preload UART0
  `SCR[0]` with 0x5A and `SCRATCH[0]` with 0xC3C3C3C3 with a read back compared against each; stamp
  S1.
. Read UART0 `SCR[0]` with `r_ready_delay` 256; require OKAY, data 0x5A, a positive R stall count equal to the
  cycles from the first RVALID to the R handshake, exactly one R beat with OKAY and no second beat in a 16-cycle quiet window; stamp S2.
. Write 0xA5 to UART0 `SCR[0]` with `w_delay` 64 and `b_ready_delay` 256; require OKAY, a W
  handshake at least 64 cycles after the first AWVALID, a positive B stall count equal to the cycles
  from the first BVALID to the B handshake and exactly one OKAY B beat; read
  `SCR[0]` back and require 0xA5; stamp S3.
. Repeat the stalled read on `SCRATCH[0]` (require 0xC3C3C3C3) and the trailing-data stalled write
  of 0x3C3C3C3C with the same checks, then read back and require 0x3C3C3C3C; stamp S4.
. Stop the sampler, print the three checker lines and the bounded waits (fuse sense done, SEP_IN
  access 50 us, sampler catch-up 256 cycles, quiet window 16 cycles); stamp S5 and require the
  stamps strictly increasing, the checker lines in order and each after its step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-STALL-PERIPH-READ` |The peripheral read held on RREADY returns 0x5A with OKAY, R stalls for a
positive cycle count with RVALID held until the handshake and exactly one R beat arrives; the cycles from RREADY rising to completion are
measured and printed without a bound.
|`CHK-STALL-PERIPH-WRITE` |The peripheral write with trailing data and held BREADY draws exactly one
OKAY B beat after a W trail of at least 64 cycles and a B stall with BVALID held until the
handshake, and lands, with `SCR[0]` reading 0xA5; the
completion cycle counts are measured and printed without a bound.
|`CHK-STALL-SMC` |The SMC-domain stalled read returns 0xC3C3C3C3 and the stalled write lands with
`SCRATCH[0]` reading 0x3C3C3C3C, each with exactly one OKAY beat and a positive stall count.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms PRELOAD_DONE, PERIPH_READ_STALLED, PERIPH_WRITE_STALLED,
SMC_STALLS_DONE and TIMEOUT_BOUNDS_LISTED occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the
four checker lines print in order, each after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 256-cycle sampler
catch-up, 16-cycle quiet window) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a
compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-STALL-PERIPH-READ`, `CHK-STALL-PERIPH-WRITE` and `CHK-STALL-SMC` hold after
their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. No completion-time
bound is claimed for the peripheral accesses; the cycle counts are printed only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The cycles from RREADY rising to completion of the peripheral read and the completion
cycle counts of the peripheral write are measured and printed without a bound, because the
specification gives no bound for them. The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-408-smc_clk_ratio_order_per_id_test]]
===== 408 `smc_clk_ratio_order_per_id_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_ratio_order_per_id_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcSysAxiGroupItem` of `SmcSysAxiItem` members with explicit AXI
IDs 0x21 for the same-ID groups and 0x31 to 0x34 for the different-ID group; 50 us access bound) at
the bench-default 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns `clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` triple, to
`SCRATCH[0]` and `SCRATCH[1]` (SMC domain) and UART0 and UART1 `SCR` (peripheral domain, per-port
AXI-Lite bridge) and to word addresses inside a generated gap between unit apertures; passive
per-`clk_smc` sampling of `tb_top.s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_arid`, `s_axi_awvalid`,
`s_axi_awready`, `s_axi_awid`, `s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_rid`, `s_axi_rdata`,
`s_axi_rresp`, `s_axi_bvalid`, `s_axi_bready`, `s_axi_bid` and `s_axi_bresp`; fuse-sense-done wait
bounded at 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Outstanding same-ID and different-ID accesses across both clock
domains return every response under its own ID with correct
data.

*Test Coverage*:

* Eight outstanding reads under one AXI ID alternate `SCRATCH[0]`, UART0 `SCR`, `SCRATCH[1]`, UART1
  `SCR` twice; the sampler sees eight AR and eight R beats, every ARID and RID equal to the issued
  ID, every RRESP OKAY, and the R data multiset equal to the preload values. Whether the data arrive
  in issue order is measured and printed, not compared (`memmap.adoc` register interface standards,
  `fabric.adoc` peripheral clock crossing).
* Eight outstanding writes under one ID alternate the two domains with distinct values, interleaved
  with eight witness writes into an address gap between unit apertures that answer DECERR
  (`memmap.adoc`); the sampler sees all sixteen AW and B beats under that ID, the BRESP multiset
  equal to the issued pattern, and each register reads back its last written value. The arrival
  order of the responses is measured and printed, not compared.
* Four outstanding reads under four different IDs, two per domain, each return an RID matching one
  request and the data and OKAY response of the register that request addressed, in whatever order
  they arrive (`fabric.adoc` transaction limits).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, start the sampler on the `s_axi` AR, R, AW and B handshakes and wait two
  `clk_smc_i` cycles; stamp S1.
. Write the four preload values (`SCRATCH[0]` 0xA5A50001, `SCRATCH[1]` 0x5A5A0002, UART0 `SCR` 0x5A,
  UART1 `SCR` 0xA5) and read each back against its value; stamp S2.
. Issue the eight same-ID reads as one group and require OKAY for each member; after the sampler
  catches up require eight AR and eight R beats, every ARID and RID the issued ID, every RRESP OKAY,
  and the R data multiset equal to the preload multiset; record the order match; stamp S3.
. Error injection. Point: word addresses inside a generated gap between unit apertures, reached
  over SEP_IN under the same AXI ID as the register writes. Kind: eight witness writes to unmapped
  addresses, interleaved in one outstanding group with the eight same-ID register writes of eight
  distinct values (0xC0DE0000 + n to scratch, 0x10 + n to UART). Expected response: each member
  returns the response issued for it (DECERR for the witness writes), with sixteen AW and B beats
  under the issued ID and the BRESP multiset equal to the issued pattern. Read back each register
  against its last written value; record the order match; stamp S4.
. Issue the four reads under IDs 0x31 to 0x34 as one group; require four AR and R beats, the set of
  ARIDs and of RIDs equal to the four IDs, and for each ID an OKAY response and the data of the
  register it addressed; stamp S5.
. Stop the sampler, print the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 64-cycle sampler
  catch-up), then require the stamps strictly increasing, the four checker lines in order and each
  after its step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ORDER-READS-SAME-ID` |Eight same-ID reads across both domains return eight R beats, each with
the issued RID and an OKAY response, whose data multiset equals the preload multiset; the order
match is measured and printed without a compare.
|`CHK-ORDER-WRITES-SAME-ID` |Sixteen same-ID writes (eight to the registers, eight DECERR witnesses)
return sixteen B beats under the issued BID whose response multiset equals the issued pattern, and
each register reads back its last written value; the arrival order is measured and printed without a
compare.
|`CHK-ORDER-DIFFERENT-IDS` |Four reads under four different IDs return one R beat per ID, each with
OKAY and the data of the register that ID addressed, in any arrival order.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms SAMPLER_ARMED, PRELOAD_DONE, SAME_ID_READS, SAME_ID_WRITES and
DIFFERENT_ID_READS occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the four checker lines print
in order, each after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 64-cycle sampler
catch-up) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ORDER-READS-SAME-ID`, `CHK-ORDER-WRITES-SAME-ID` and `CHK-ORDER-DIFFERENT-IDS`
hold after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. Response
order within one ID is not claimed: it is printed only, and the multiset of responses is what is
compared. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Whether the same-ID read data and the same-ID write responses arrive in issue order
is measured and printed and not compared; only the multiset of responses is compared. The bounded
waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-409-smc_clk_ratio_resp_once_test]]
===== 409 `smc_clk_ratio_resp_once_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_ratio_resp_once_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` single accesses and one `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` of 32
members, 4-byte accesses, 50 us access bound) at the bench-default 10 / 1.25 / 5 ns `clk_ref_i` /
`clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` triple, to `SCRATCH[0..7]` (SMC domain) and the UART `SCR` registers
(peripheral domain, per-port AXI-Lite bridge; the UART instance count is the generated `NUM` value
of the UART log-engine wrapper); passive per-`clk_smc` counting of handshakes on
`tb_top.s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_awvalid`, `s_axi_awready`, `s_axi_wvalid`,
`s_axi_wready`, `s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_rresp`, `s_axi_bvalid`, `s_axi_bready` and
`s_axi_bresp`; `tb_top.clk_ref` for the quiet window; fuse-sense-done wait bounded at 200000
`clk_smc_i` cycles

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Every SEP_IN request on the SMC and peripheral clock domains draws
exactly one OKAY response and no late duplicate.

*Test Coverage*:

* Sixteen counted accesses to the SMC-domain scratch registers (eight writes then eight reads of
  `SCRATCH[0..7]` with distinct patterns 0x11111111 x (k + 1)) draw exactly 8 AR, 8 AW, 8 W, 8 R and
  8 B handshakes, every response OKAY, with every read returning the value written (`memmap.adoc`
  register interface standards, `clk_rst.adoc` clock-domain responsibilities).
* Sixteen counted accesses to the UART `SCR` registers (eight writes, eight reads, spread over the
  UART instances) draw the same 8 / 8 / 8 / 8 / 8 handshake counts through the peripheral-clock
  bridge (`fabric.adoc` peripheral ports cross to the peripheral clock), with each read returning
  the last value written to that UART.
* A 32-member outstanding group interleaving 16 scratch and UART `SCR` writes and 16 reads draws 16
  AR, 16 AW, 16 W, 16 R and 16 B handshakes, every member OKAY, one response per request, and each
  read returning the value held.
* After the last response the sampler keeps counting for 1024 `clk_ref_i` periods and sees no
  further AR, AW, W, R or B handshake, so a late duplicate response would be counted.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, start the handshake sampler and wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles; require all
  five counters 0; stamp S1.
. Write `SCRATCH[0..7]` then read them back, each read compared with its pattern; after the sampler
  catches up require the counter deltas AR 8, AW 8, W 8, R 8, B 8 and every R and B response OKAY;
  stamp S2.
. Write eight patterns (0x5A, 0xA5, 0x3C, 0xC3, 0x96, 0x69, 0x0F, 0xF0) to the UART `SCR` registers
  cycling over the UART instances, then read eight times, each against the last value written to
  that UART; require the same counter deltas and OKAY responses; stamp S3.
. Issue the 32-member mixed group (alternating scratch and UART writes, each followed by a read of
  the other domain) as one outstanding group; require every member response OKAY and the counter
  deltas AR 16, AW 16, W 16, R 16, B 16 with OKAY responses; stamp S4.
. Keep the sampler running for 1024 `clk_ref_i` periods and require zero new handshakes; stamp S5,
  stop the sampler and print the three checker lines, the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN
  access, 64-cycle sampler catch-up, 1024-period quiet window), and require the stamps strictly
  increasing, the checker lines in order and each after S5.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RESP-ONCE-SMC` |The SMC-domain sequence of eight writes and eight reads draws exactly 8 B and
8 R beats (AR, AW and W counts equal the requests), every response OKAY, and no handshake arrives in
the late window.
|`CHK-RESP-ONCE-PERIPH` |The peripheral-domain sequence of eight writes and eight reads draws
exactly 8 B and 8 R beats, every response OKAY, and no handshake arrives in the late window.
|`CHK-RESP-ONCE-MIXED` |The 32-member outstanding group draws exactly 16 B and 16 R beats, one
response per request, every member and every sampled response OKAY, and no handshake arrives in the
late window.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms SAMPLER_ARMED, SMC_SEQUENCE_COUNTED, PERIPH_SEQUENCE_COUNTED,
MIXED_GROUP_COUNTED and QUIET_WINDOW_CLOSED occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the
four checker lines print in order, each after the last step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 64-cycle sampler
catch-up, 1024-period quiet window) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a
compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-RESP-ONCE-SMC`, `CHK-RESP-ONCE-PERIPH` and `CHK-RESP-ONCE-MIXED` hold after
their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-410-smc_clk_ratio_scratch_test]]
===== 410 `smc_clk_ratio_scratch_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_ratio_scratch_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` 4-byte reads and writes, 50 us access bound) to
`SCRATCH[0..7]` in the misc wrapper (address from the generated map), with the leaf pinning
`clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` to 10 / 12 / 6 ns in `build_phase` before bring-up;
fuse-sense-done wait bounded at 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles; no protocol VIP, no probe sampled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The eight scratch registers reset to zero and hold distinct written
values at a 10 / 12 / 6 ns clock triple.

*Test Coverage*:

* `SCRATCH[0..7]` all read 0x00000000 with OKAY before any scratch write (`scratch.rdl`, read-write
  registers with reset 0).
* `SCRATCH[0]` reads 0xA5A5A5A5 after that value is written (`clk_rst.adoc` clock-domain
  responsibilities for the SMC-domain register path).
* Eight pairwise distinct patterns 0x11111111 x (k + 1) are written to `SCRATCH[0..7]` back to back
  before any read; each register then reads its own pattern and the eight words are distinct, so no
  scratch register aliases another.
* All eight registers written with 0 read back 0 after the burst.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Pin the three clock periods to 10 / 12 / 6 ns in `build_phase`, wait for fuse sense done within
  200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles, and stamp BRINGUP_DONE.
. Read `SCRATCH[0..7]` and require 0x00000000 from each; stamp S2.
. Write 0xA5A5A5A5 to `SCRATCH[0]`, read it back and require the same word; stamp S3.
. Write the eight patterns to `SCRATCH[0..7]`, stamp the burst writes, read all eight in order and
  require each equal to its own pattern and the eight words distinct; stamp S4.
. Write 0 to all eight registers and read each back, requiring 0x00000000; stamp S5.
. Print the four checker lines and the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access); require the
  six stamps strictly increasing and the checker lines in order, each after its step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SCRATCH-RESET-READ` |All eight scratch registers read 0x00000000 with OKAY responses before
any scratch write.
|`CHK-SCRATCH-WRITE-READ` |`SCRATCH[0]` reads 0xA5A5A5A5 after that write and all eight registers
read 0x00000000 after the restore writes, each with an OKAY response.
|`CHK-SCRATCH-NO-ALIAS` |After eight back-to-back writes each register reads its own pattern
(0x11111111 to 0x88888888) and the eight read words are distinct.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms BRINGUP_DONE, SCRATCH_RESET_READS, SCRATCH0_WRITE_READ,
SCRATCH_BURST_WRITES, SCRATCH_BURST_READS and SCRATCH_RESTORE_READS occur in order with strictly
increasing stamps and the checker lines print in order, each after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access) and that expiry
raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SCRATCH-RESET-READ`, `CHK-SCRATCH-WRITE-READ` and `CHK-SCRATCH-NO-ALIAS` hold
after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. The zero reset
compare cannot fail on an unknown value under a two-state simulator. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The zero reset compare cannot fail on an unknown value under a two-state simulator,
so an unknown reset state is not observable from this bench. The bounded waits are recorded, not
compared.

'''''

[[sec-411-smc_clk_relation_regxbar_test]]
===== 411 `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcSysAxiItem` 4-byte reads and writes and `SmcSysAxiGroupItem`
for the outstanding case, 50 us access bound) to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`
(`smc_base_config`, clock domain `clk_smc_i`) and to `AVS_CFG_0` (AVSBus controller window, crossing
the AVSBus CDC bridge into `clk_periph_i`); the run argument `+smc_cell` pins the `clk_ref_i` /
`clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` triple in `build_phase`; input clocks timestamped on
`tb_top.clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i` (1 us edge bound); in the slowest-peripheral cell
`tb_top.s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_rid`, `s_axi_rdata`,
`s_axi_bvalid` and `s_axi_bready` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; fuse-sense-done wait bounded at 200000
`clk_smc_i` cycles

*Run mode*: one testlist entry per cell: `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_test` (`+smc_cell=default`, this
module) and the variant entries `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_smc_slower_test` (`+smc_cell=smc_slower`),
`smc_clk_relation_regxbar_smc_equal_test` (`+smc_cell=smc_equal`),
`smc_clk_relation_regxbar_periph_slower_test` (`+smc_cell=periph_slower`),
`smc_clk_relation_regxbar_periph3_test` (`+smc_cell=periph3`), `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_ref8_test`
(`+smc_cell=ref8`), `smc_clk_relation_regxbar_slowest_periph_test` (`+smc_cell=slowest_periph`),
each a module of its own in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; args `+smc_cell=default`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cell of this entry is pinned by its testlist entry; the
other cells run as fixed-cell variant modules.

*Objective*: The hang-detector threshold and AVS_CFG_0 hold written values at
each single-axis clock relation of the run.

*Test Coverage*:

* The cell of a run selects the clock triple in ns: default 10 / 1.25 / 5, smc_slower 10 / 12 / 8,
  smc_equal 10 / 10 / 10, periph_slower 8 / 1.25 / 10, periph3 10 / 1.25 / 3, ref8 8 / 1.25 / 5 and
  slowest_periph 8 / 12 / 10; the other cells are further runs of the same leaf. Each of the three
  input clock periods is measured over 64 rising edges and must equal the cell's period to within 1
  ps (`clk_rst.adoc` peripheral timing requirements).
* In every cell `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` (20-bit `value[19:0]`, reset 0x1000,
  `smc_base_config.rdl`) written with 0xA5A5A reads back 0xA5A5A, and `AVS_CFG_0.MAX_RETRIES`
  written to 0x2A reads back in the written word (`avsbus_controller.rdl`), both with OKAY; both
  registers are then restored to the words saved before the test and read back.
* Default cell only: the threshold first reads its reset value 0x1000, then round-trips 0xA5A5A and
  the restore to 0x1000.
* periph3 and ref8 cells: with `clk_smc_i` at 1.25 ns and only the peripheral or only the reference
  period changed, the threshold round trip repeats and gives the same 0xA5A5A and 0x1000 as the
  default cell (`clk_rst.adoc`, clock-domain responsibilities: register crossbar on `clk_smc_i`).
* slowest_periph cell only: a threshold write and an `AVS_CFG_0` write are issued together, then
  eight reads under one AXI ID alternating the two registers are issued together; all ten responses
  are OKAY within the 50 us bound, the sampler sees eight AR, eight R and two B handshakes, and each
  R beat carries the issued ID and its own expected word in issue order. The drain time is measured
  and printed because the specification gives no bound for the bridge latency. After the last
  response is collected the sampler runs 256 more `clk_smc_i` cycles and no further R or B beat
  appears.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, measure the periods of `clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i` over
  64 rising edges each and require each to equal the cell's period within 1 ps; stamp
  CELL_PERIODS_MEASURED.
. Default cell only: read the threshold and require 0x1000, write 0xA5A5A and read it back against
  the 20-bit pattern, write 0x1000 and read it back; stamp RESET_ROUND_TRIPPED.
. Read and save the threshold and `AVS_CFG_0`; build the `AVS_CFG_0` word with `MAX_RETRIES` = 0x2A
  and require it to differ from the saved word; write the threshold with 0xA5A5A and stamp
  SMC_SIDE_WRITTEN; write `AVS_CFG_0` and stamp AVS_SIDE_WRITTEN; read both back against the written
  words, restore both saved words, read both back against the saved words and stamp BOTH_READ_BACK.
. periph3 and ref8 cells only: write the threshold 0xA5A5A, read it back, write 0x1000, read it back
  against the reset value; stamp SMC_SIDE_REPEATED.
. slowest_periph cell only: start the AXI sampler, issue the threshold write and the `AVS_CFG_0`
  write as one group, then the eight same-ID (0x21) alternating reads as a second group; require
  every response OKAY, the drain within 50 us, two B, eight AR and eight R handshakes, each R beat
  with the issued ID and the expected word in issue order, and no further beat in the 256-cycle
  quiet window after the last response; restore both registers and read them
  back; stamp OUTSTANDING_DRAINED.
. Print the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 1 us clock edge, 50 us outstanding
  drain), require the fence terms of the cell in order with strictly increasing stamps and the
  checker lines in order, each after its term.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CLK-RELATION-ROUNDTRIP` |In the run's cell the threshold reads back 0xA5A5A and `AVS_CFG_0`
reads back the word written with `MAX_RETRIES` 0x2A, both OKAY, and the restores read back the saved
words; the cell name and measured periods are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms of the run's cell (CELL_PERIODS_MEASURED, then RESET_ROUND_TRIPPED,
SMC_SIDE_WRITTEN, AVS_SIDE_WRITTEN, BOTH_READ_BACK, SMC_SIDE_REPEATED, OUTSTANDING_DRAINED as the
cell applies) occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the checker lines print in order,
each after its term.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 1 us clock edge,
50 us outstanding drain) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|`CHK-REGXBAR-RESET-RT` |Default cell: the threshold reads 0x1000 after reset, 0xA5A5A after the
write and 0x1000 after the restore, each with OKAY.
|`CHK-REGXBAR-PERIODS` |periph3 and ref8 cells: the threshold reads 0xA5A5A after the write and
0x1000 after the restore, as in the default cell; the measured periods are printed.
|`CHK-CLK-RELATION-BACKPRESSURE` |slowest_periph cell: the ten outstanding accesses complete OKAY
within 50 us, the sampler sees eight AR, eight R and two B handshakes and no further R or B beat in
the 256-cycle quiet window, and each read returns its own expected word in issue order with the
issued ID.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CLK-RELATION-ROUNDTRIP` holds in every cell, with `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. The extra row depends on the cell: the table above lists the
default cell with `CHK-REGXBAR-RESET-RT`; the smc_slower, smc_equal and periph_slower cells have no
extra row; the periph3 and ref8 cells have `CHK-REGXBAR-PERIODS` (the threshold reads 0xA5A5A after
the write and 0x1000 after the restore, as in the default cell); the slowest_periph cell has
`CHK-CLK-RELATION-BACKPRESSURE` (the ten outstanding accesses complete OKAY within 50 us, each read
returning its own expected word in issue order, with no response lost or duplicated). Enrolled in:
`all`.

*Scope limit*: In the slowest_periph cell the drain time of the outstanding group is measured and
printed and not compared, because the specification gives no bound for the bridge latency. The
bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

reads back the word written with `MAX_RETRIES` 0x2A, both OKAY, and the restores read back the saved
words; the cell name and measured periods are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms of the run's cell (CELL_PERIODS_MEASURED, then RESET_ROUND_TRIPPED,
SMC_SIDE_WRITTEN, AVS_SIDE_WRITTEN, BOTH_READ_BACK, SMC_SIDE_REPEATED, OUTSTANDING_DRAINED as the
cell applies) occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the checker lines print in order,
each after its term.
|`CHK-REGXBAR-PERIODS` |periph3 and ref8 cells: the threshold reads 0xA5A5A after the write and
0x1000 after the restore, as in the default cell; the measured periods are printed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (fuse sense, 50 us SEP_IN access, 1 us clock edge,
50 us outstanding drain) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CLK-RELATION-ROUNDTRIP`, `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-REGXBAR-PERIODS`,
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-418-smc_octs_clk_rate_test]]
===== 418 `smc_octs_clk_rate_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_octs_clk_rate_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcSysAxiItem` 4-byte accesses, 50 us bound) to the OCTS
(`system_timer_octs`) `CTRL`, `TIMER_START`, `STATUS`, `TIMER_COUNT_LO`, `TIMER_COUNT_HI`,
`TIMER_PRESET_LO` and `TIMER_PRESET_HI` registers at their generated addresses; bench rising-edge
counters on `tb_top.clk_smc_i`, `clk_ref_i` and `clk_periph_i` (100 us edge bound for the period
measurement); `tb_top.tb_chiplet_is_primary` required 1; the run argument `+smc_cell` pins the
`clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` / `clk_periph_i` triple in `build_phase`; no protocol VIP

*Run mode*: one testlist entry per cell: `smc_octs_clk_rate_test` (`+smc_cell=default`, this module)
and the variant entries `smc_octs_clk_rate_smc_slower_test` (`+smc_cell=smc_slower`),
`smc_octs_clk_rate_smc_equal_test` (`+smc_cell=smc_equal`), `smc_octs_clk_rate_smc_fast_test`
(`+smc_cell=smc_fast`), `smc_octs_clk_rate_ref8_test` (`+smc_cell=ref8`),
`smc_octs_clk_rate_periph3_test` (`+smc_cell=periph3`), each a module of its own in
`testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags
`clock`; seed 1; args `+smc_cell=default`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cell of this entry is pinned by its testlist entry; the
other cells run as fixed-cell variant modules.

*Objective*: The OCTS counter advances at the clk_smc_i rate in every clock cell and
restarts from its preset on a START after the preset is latched.

*Test Coverage*:

* The cell of a run selects the clock triple in ns: default 10 / 1.25 / 5, smc_slower 10 / 12 / 5,
  smc_equal 10 / 10 / 5, smc_fast 10 / 1 / 5, ref8 8 / 1.25 / 5 and periph3 10 / 1.25 / 3; the other
  cells are further runs of the same leaf. Each input clock period is measured over 64 rising edges
  and must equal the cell's period exactly (`clk_rst.adoc`).
* The OCTS runs from `clk_smc_i` (`clk_rst.adoc` timer and debug timebases; `architecture.adoc` of
  `system_timer_octs`, counting and synchronization). Over two consecutive windows of 4000
  `clk_smc_i` edges the `TIMER_COUNT` delta lies in the interval from E_lo (`clk_smc_i` edges
  between the two read pairs) to E_hi (`clk_smc_i` edges over the whole window and its read pairs),
  widened only by the `CTRL.CREDIT_VAL` count-advance granularity; the specification does not state the
  rule for the count latch, so the tolerance is only that granularity.
* Where the reference or peripheral clock period differs from the `clk_smc_i` period, that clock's
  edge count over the same window lies outside the interval, so the compare tells `clk_smc_i` from
  the other clocks; where the period equals the `clk_smc_i` period the count is printed and not
  discriminating.
* The third `TIMER_START` write, issued while `STATUS.RUNNING` is 1 after the preset is latched and
  after a `TIMER_START` write whose `STATUS` read shows `RUNNING`, restarts the counter from the non-zero
  preset 0x100004000 (`TIMER_PRESET_LO/HI`): the first sample after it is at least the preset and at
  most the preset plus the `clk_smc_i` edges since the write plus the granularity, `STATUS.RUNNING`
  stays 1, and the next window delta again lies in the interval (`architecture.adoc` pulse
  generation and clock crossing).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done; require `tb_chiplet_is_primary` = 1; measure the periods of `clk_ref_i`,
  `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i` over 64 rising edges each and require each to equal the cell's
  period.
. Read `CTRL` and require its reset value; take `CREDIT_VAL` as the granularity and require it
  non-zero; start edge counters on the three clocks.
. Write `TIMER_START` = 1 and poll `STATUS` up to 32 reads until `RUNNING` is set; require `MODE` to
  show primary; stamp FIRST_START_RUNNING.
. Read `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and `TIMER_COUNT_HI` as c0 and stamp COUNT_PAIR_0; wait 4000 `clk_smc_i`
  edges and stamp WINDOW_EDGES_COUNTED; read c1, require the delta within the interval and, for the
  reference and peripheral clocks whose period differs from `clk_smc_i`, an edge count outside it;
  stamp COUNT_PAIR_1.
. Repeat the window from c1 (second window with the same compares); stamp CELL_REWINDOW and print
  the rate line.
. Write `TIMER_PRESET_LO` and `TIMER_PRESET_HI` with 0x100004000 and stamp PRESET_WRITTEN; write
  `TIMER_START` = 1, read `STATUS` and require `RUNNING`, write `TIMER_START` = 1 again (the third `TIMER_START`
  write) and stamp THIRD_START.
. Read the count as c2 and stamp RELOAD_SAMPLE; require the read issued within 16 `clk_smc_i` cycles
  of the third `TIMER_START` write, c2 at least the preset and at most the preset plus the edges since the write
  plus the granularity; read `STATUS` and require `RUNNING`; run a third window from c2 with the
  delta-in-interval compare.
. Print the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 32-read `RUNNING` poll, 4000-edge window, 100 us
  input clock edge), then require the fence terms in order with strictly increasing stamps and the
  rate line before the reload line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCTS-RATE-DEFAULT` |The `TIMER_COUNT` delta of each of the two windows lies within the
`clk_smc_i` edge interval widened by the `CREDIT_VAL` granularity, and the reference and peripheral
edge counts of the window lie outside it; the periods are printed.
|`CHK-OCTS-START-RELOAD` |After the third `TIMER_START` write the first count sample is at least the preset and
at most the preset plus the `clk_smc_i` edges since the write plus the granularity, `STATUS.RUNNING`
reads 1, and the following window delta lies within the `clk_smc_i` interval.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms FIRST_START_RUNNING, COUNT_PAIR_0, WINDOW_EDGES_COUNTED,
COUNT_PAIR_1, CELL_REWINDOW, PRESET_WRITTEN, THIRD_START and RELOAD_SAMPLE occur in order with
strictly increasing stamps, and the rate line prints after CELL_REWINDOW and before the reload line,
which prints after RELOAD_SAMPLE.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 32-read `RUNNING` poll,
4000-edge window, 100 us input clock edge) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a
record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: The rate row varies with the cell: the table lists the default cell
(`CHK-OCTS-RATE-DEFAULT`); the smc_slower, smc_equal and smc_fast cells carry
`CHK-OCTS-RATE-SMC-PERIOD` instead (the delta lies within the interval computed from that cell's
`clk_smc_i` edges and the ref and periph counts lie outside it where their periods differ); the ref8
and periph3 cells carry `CHK-OCTS-RATE-OTHER-CLOCKS` (with `clk_smc_i` at 1.25 ns and only one other
period changed, the delta stays within the `clk_smc_i` interval). In every cell the rate row,
`CHK-OCTS-START-RELOAD`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold or print as described. Enrolled
in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Where the reference or peripheral clock period equals the `clk_smc_i` period, that
clock's edge count over the window is printed and is not discriminating. The specification does not
state the rule for the count latch, so the delta tolerance is only the `CREDIT_VAL` granularity. The
bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

* The `smc_octs_clk_rate_test` procedure runs at the ref8 cell (`clk_ref_i` / `clk_smc_i` /
`clk_periph_i` = 8 / 1.25 / 5 ns), so a scheduled run reaches this cell; its checks are those of the
`smc_octs_clk_rate_test` card with this cell's own checker ids.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. As `smc_octs_clk_rate_test`, with the cell fixed by the module.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms FIRST_START_RUNNING, COUNT_PAIR_0, WINDOW_EDGES_COUNTED,
COUNT_PAIR_1, CELL_REWINDOW, PRESET_WRITTEN, THIRD_START and RELOAD_SAMPLE occur in order with
strictly increasing stamps, and the rate line prints after CELL_REWINDOW and before the reload line,
which prints after RELOAD_SAMPLE.
|`CHK-OCTS-RATE-OTHER-CLOCKS` |In this cell the `TIMER_COUNT` delta of each of the two windows lies
within the `clk_smc_i` edge interval widened by the `CREDIT_VAL` granularity, and the reference and
peripheral edge counts of the window lie outside it; the periods are printed.
|`CHK-OCTS-START-RELOAD` |After the third `TIMER_START` write the first count sample is at least the
preset and at most the preset plus the `clk_smc_i` edges since the write plus the granularity,
`STATUS.RUNNING` reads 1, and the following window delta lies within the `clk_smc_i` interval.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 32-read `RUNNING` poll,
4000-edge window, 100 us input clock edge) and that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a
record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-OCTS-RATE-OTHER-CLOCKS`, `CHK-OCTS-START-RELOAD`,
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''
