[[sec-424-smc_periph_cg_window_extent_test]]
===== 424 `smc_periph_cg_window_extent_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_periph_cg_window_extent_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` reads and writes of `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`,
expected-error reads and writes, 4-byte accesses) to the AVSBus controller (`AVS_CFG_0`), I2C
(`I2C_CTRL_0`), UART (`UART0_LOG_ENGINE_CTRL`), telemetry receiver (`TELEMETRY0_CTRL`) and I3C
(`I3C0_HCI_VERSION` as probe, `I3C0_DEV_CTX_BASE_LO` as writable register) windows, each window's
bounds taken from the generated address map, with the peripheral enables `avs_cg_en`, `i2c_cg_en`,
`uart_cg_en`, `telemetry_cg_en` and `i3c_cg_en` of `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; AVS clock pad on
`tb_top.tb_avs_clk_from_dut` (rises counted over 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles); no protocol VIP

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: With one peripheral clock-gate enable set, that window answers
SLVERR with the error pattern while the other windows stay
reachable.

*Test Coverage*:

* With a peripheral's enable set alone, a read of a registered address and of an unbacked address
  inside that window answers SLVERR with data 0xBADCAB1E, for five of five windows (AVSBus, I2C,
  UART, telemetry, I3C) (`clk_rst.adoc` subsystem controls and clock gating, `memmap.adoc` AXI-Lite
  external windows). The response and data of a read at the last 4-byte address of each window are
  measured and printed; the specification does not state the extent, so they are not compared.
* With each enable set alone, a probe register of each of the other four windows reads OKAY with the
  value it read when all five enables were clear, and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads back the value
  written.
* With the enable set, a write of the inverted word to a writable register of that window completes
  with SLVERR; the register's value before the write and after the enable is cleared is measured and
  printed, and whether a refused write may change peripheral state is not claimed.
* The rises of the AVSBus clock pad over 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles with `avs_cg_en` clear and with it
  set are measured and printed; the level and activity that the pad must show while the enable is
  set are not claimed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read and save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, clear the five peripheral enables and read back; read one
  probe register per window with all enables clear and keep the words; stamp S1.
. Error injection. Point: the window of each of the five peripherals, with that peripheral's
  clock-gate enable in `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` set alone. Kind: a read of a registered address and a
  read of an unbacked address (window start plus 0x10, 0x100, 0x300, 0x40 and 0x70 for the five
  windows in turn) inside the gated window. Expected response: SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E on each of the
  two reads. For each of the five peripherals set its enable alone and read back before the two
  reads; read the window-end address and print its response and data; clear the enable and read
  back; stamp S2 and print one line per window.
. For each peripheral set its enable alone, read the probe register of each of the other four
  windows and require OKAY and the clear-state word, clear the enable; stamp S3 and print one line
  per window.
. Error injection. Point: the writable register of each peripheral's window, with that
  peripheral's enable set. Kind: a write of the inverted word into the gated window. Expected
  response: SLVERR on the write. For each peripheral read the writable register before setting the
  enable; after the write clear the enable, read the register again and print the words before and
  after; stamp S4.
. Count rises of the AVS clock pad over 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles with `avs_cg_en` clear, set the
  enable, count again and print the level at the end; clear the enable; stamp S5.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` to the saved word and read it back; stamp S6; require the six stamps
  strictly increasing and the checker lines in order, each after its own step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WINDOW-EXTENT` |With the enable set, the registered and the unbacked address of each of the
five windows answer SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E on a read; the window-end response and data are measured
and printed without a compare.
|`CHK-WINDOW-ISOLATION` |With each enable set alone, the probe registers of the other four windows
answer OKAY with their clear-state values and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads back what was written, five
of five windows.
|`CHK-WINDOW-WRITE-DELIVERY-PRINT` |The write to a gated window completes with SLVERR; the
register's words before the write and after the enable is cleared are measured and printed, and
whether they match is not compared.
|`CHK-AVS-CLOCK-PRINT` |The `tb_avs_clk_from_dut` rise counts over 256 cycles with `avs_cg_en` clear
and set are measured and printed without a compare; the probe must be resolvable and the enable
writes must complete.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step stamps S1 to S6 are strictly increasing, the checker lines print in step
order (five lines of the first three kinds, one of the last) and each after its own step stamp.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-WINDOW-EXTENT` (registered and unbacked addresses only) and
`CHK-WINDOW-ISOLATION` hold after their compares; `CHK-WINDOW-WRITE-DELIVERY-PRINT` holds for the
SLVERR response of the refused write and prints the register words without claiming them;
`CHK-AVS-CLOCK-PRINT` records the pad rise counts without claiming them; `CHK-NONVAC` is printed at
the end. The specification does not state the window extent, whether a refused write changes state or the
AVSBus pad activity. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response and data of the read at the last 4-byte address of each gated window
are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state the window
extent. The writable register's words before the refused write and after the enable is cleared are
printed and not compared; whether a refused write may change peripheral state is not claimed. The
AVS clock pad rise counts with `avs_cg_en` clear and set are measured and printed without a
compare; the level and activity the pad must show while the enable is set are not claimed, because
the specification does not state them.

'''''

[[sec-425-smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_test]]
===== 425 `smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcSysAxiItem` 4-byte read and write of `AVS_CFG_0`, 50 us access
bound) through the AVSBus AXI-Lite CDC bridge into the `clk_periph_i` domain; bench input clocks
timestamped on `tb_top.clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i` (100 us edge bound); the run
argument `+smc_cell` selects the peripheral period (periph10, periph5 or periph3) in `build_phase`
while `clk_ref_i` stays 10 ns and `clk_smc_i` 1.25 ns; AVS register fields `MAX_RETRIES` and
`RESYNC_INTERVAL` of `AVS_CFG_0`; no protocol VIP

*Run mode*: one testlist entry per cell: `smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_test` (`+smc_cell=periph10`,
this module) and the variant entries `smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_periph5_test`
(`+smc_cell=periph5`), `smc_periph_floor_roundtrip_periph3_test` (`+smc_cell=periph3`), each a
module of its own in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; args `+smc_cell=periph10`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cell of this entry is pinned by its testlist entry; the
other cells run as fixed-cell variant modules.

*Objective*: AVS_CFG_0 round-trips a written value through the AVSBus bridge
at peripheral clock periods of 10, 5 and 3 ns.

*Test Coverage*:

* The run's cell sets only the peripheral clock period to 10 ns (periph10, the 100 MHz minimum of
  `clk_rst.adoc` peripheral timing requirements), 5 ns (periph5, the default) or 3 ns (periph3); the
  other cells are further runs of the same leaf. The reference, SMC and peripheral periods are each
  measured over 64 rising edges and must equal the cell's period exactly.
* `AVS_CFG_0` (`avsbus_controller.rdl`, `memmap.adoc` of the AVSBus controller) written with
  `MAX_RETRIES` = 0x2A and `RESYNC_INTERVAL` unchanged reads back exactly the written word with
  OKAY, so `RESYNC_INTERVAL` keeps its pre-write value; restoring the saved word reads back the
  saved word.
* The test issues exactly five SEP_IN accesses: save read, write, read back, restore write, restore
  read.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Measure the periods of `clk_ref_i`, `clk_smc_i` and `clk_periph_i` over 64 rising edges each and
  require each to equal the cell's period; stamp CELL_PERIODS_MEASURED.
. Read `AVS_CFG_0` and keep the saved word; stamp AVS_CFG_0_SAVED.
. Write the saved word with `MAX_RETRIES` replaced by 0x2A; stamp AVS_CFG_0_WRITTEN.
. Read `AVS_CFG_0` back; stamp AVS_CFG_0_READ_BACK; require the word to equal the written word,
  `MAX_RETRIES` 0x2A and `RESYNC_INTERVAL` equal to its pre-write value.
. Write the saved word back and read it; stamp AVS_CFG_0_RESTORED; require the read to equal the
  saved word.
. Print the checker line, the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 100 us input clock edge) and
  require the fence terms in order with strictly increasing stamps and the checker line after the
  restore; the test requires exactly five accesses.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PERIPH-FLOOR-ROUNDTRIP` |In the run's peripheral cell (periods measured as the cell's)
`AVS_CFG_0` reads back the written word with `MAX_RETRIES` 0x2A and `RESYNC_INTERVAL` equal to its
pre-write value, every response OKAY, and the restore write reads back the saved word.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms CELL_PERIODS_MEASURED, AVS_CFG_0_SAVED, AVS_CFG_0_WRITTEN,
AVS_CFG_0_READ_BACK and AVS_CFG_0_RESTORED occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the
checker line prints after the restore.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 100 us input clock edge) and
that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-PERIPH-FLOOR-ROUNDTRIP` holds in the run's cell after its compares, with
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end; the checker is the same for the periph10,
periph5 and periph3 cells. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (50 us SEP_IN access, 100 us input clock edge) and
that expiry raises an assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-PERIPH-FLOOR-ROUNDTRIP`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their
compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-428-smc_ref_reset_cycles_test]]
===== 428 `smc_ref_reset_cycles_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CLOCK

*Source Module*: `smc_ref_reset_cycles_test`

*BFM / Model*: Reset agent sequencer (`SmcResetOp` `SAMPLE`, `COLD_RST_LO` and `COLD_RST_HI` driving
the `rst_cold_ni` pin, reset-chain release wait with a 600 `clk_ref_i` cycle bound);
`tb_top.rst_primary_ref_clk_no` read on `clk_ref_i` rising edges; `tb_top.clk_ref_i` rising edges
logged in ps; the run argument `+smc_cell` selects the reference period (ref10 = 10 ns or ref4 = 4
ns) in `build_phase` with `clk_smc_i` at 1.25 ns and `clk_periph_i` at 5 ns; pin changes are placed
a third of a reference period after a `clk_ref_i` edge; no CSR access and no protocol VIP

*Run mode*: one testlist entry per cell: `smc_ref_reset_cycles_test` (`+smc_cell=ref10`, this
module) and the variant entries `smc_ref_reset_cycles_ref4_test` (`+smc_cell=ref4`), each a module
of its own in `testlists/clock.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec`
1800; tags `clock`; seed 1; args `+smc_cell=ref10`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cell of this entry is pinned by its testlist entry; the
other cells run as fixed-cell variant modules.

*Objective*: The cold-reset release hold and assertion de-glitch are counted in
clk_ref_i cycles at two reference periods.

*Test Coverage*:

* The cell of a run sets the reference period to 10 ns (ref10) or 4 ns (ref4); the other cell is a
  further run of the same leaf. The reset conditions are clock-cycle counts in the reference-clock
  domain, not nanosecond delays (`clk_rst.adoc` power-good and cold reset; `port_table.adoc`).
* After `rst_cold_ni` has been held low for 64 `clk_ref_i` cycles (the pin low is checked to span
  exactly 64 edges and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` to read 0), the count of `clk_ref_i` rising edges
  from the release to `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` reading 1 is at least 255, the 255-cycle
  reference-clock extension of the cold-reset release (`clk_rst.adoc`); the exact count is measured
  and printed, since the specification does not state the value.
* After the reset chain is released `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` still reads 1.
* The cold-reset input is de-glitched: a 31-cycle low pulse leaves `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` high at
  every sample during the pulse and for 100 samples after it, and a 32-cycle low pulse drives it to
  0 (`clk_rst.adoc`: assertion requires 32 consecutive low samples); the cycle count from the first
  low sample to the assertion is measured and printed, since the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Sample the reset agent and require `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` = 1; stamp BRINGUP_DONE.
. Drive `rst_cold_ni` low a third of a period after a `clk_ref_i` edge, wait 64 `clk_ref_i` edges,
  release it, and require the logged edges in the low interval to be 64 and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`
  to read 0; stamp COLD_LOW_64.
. Count `clk_ref_i` rising edges from the release until `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` reads 1, within 600
  cycles; require the count to be at least 255; stamp RELEASE_COUNTED; wait for the reset chain
  release and require the output still 1; print the count.
. Error injection. Point: the `rst_cold_ni` pin, driven by the reset agent. Kind: a 31-cycle low
  pulse on `rst_cold_ni`, one `clk_ref_i` cycle short of the 32 consecutive low samples that
  assertion requires. Expected response: `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` stays high at each of the 31
  samples during the pulse and at 100 further samples after the release. Require the logged edges
  in the pulse to be 31; stamp GLITCH_31_IGNORED.
. Drive `rst_cold_ni` low and release it after 32 `clk_ref_i` cycles; count the cycles from the
  first low sample until the output reads 0 within 600 cycles; stamp PULSE_32_ASSERTED and print the
  count; wait for the reset chain release within 600 cycles; stamp CHAIN_RELEASED.
. Print the bounded waits (600-cycle release, assertion, glitch-hold and chain-release waits) and
  require the fence terms in order with strictly increasing stamps, the two checker lines in order
  and each after its step; the test also requires the release count at least 255 and the assertion
  count at least 1.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REF-RESET-RELEASE-CYCLES` |The release-to-high count in `clk_ref_i` cycles is at least 255
after the 64-cycle cold-reset low, and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` still reads 1 after the reset chain
release; the exact count is printed without a compare, the specification not stating the value.
|`CHK-REF-RESET-DEGLITCH` |A 31-cycle low pulse on `rst_cold_ni` leaves `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`
high at every sample and a 32-cycle pulse drives it to 0; the cycle count of the assertion is
printed without a compare, the specification not stating the value.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms BRINGUP_DONE, COLD_LOW_64, RELEASE_COUNTED, GLITCH_31_IGNORED,
PULSE_32_ASSERTED and CHAIN_RELEASED occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the two
checker lines print in order, each after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (600 `clk_ref_i` cycles for the release count, the
assertion count and each chain release, and the glitch-hold sample count) and that expiry raises an
assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-REF-RESET-RELEASE-CYCLES` and `CHK-REF-RESET-DEGLITCH` hold after their
compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` printed at the end. Whether the counts agree
between the ref10 and ref4 runs is not compared inside one run; each run compares the cycle-count
conditions above. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The exact count of `clk_ref_i` edges from the cold-reset release to
`rst_primary_ref_clk_no` reading 1 (only its minimum of 255 is compared) and the cycle count from
the first low sample of the 32-cycle pulse to the assertion (only that it is at least 1 is compared)
are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state the values.
Whether the counts agree between the ref10 and ref4 runs is not compared inside one run. The
bounded waits are recorded, not compared.

'''''

PULSE_32_ASSERTED and CHAIN_RELEASED occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and the two
checker lines print in order, each after its step.
|`CHK-REF-RESET-DEGLITCH` |A 31-cycle low pulse on `rst_cold_ni` leaves `rst_primary_ref_clk_no`
high at every sample and a 32-cycle pulse drives it to 0; the cycle count of the assertion is
printed without a compare, the specification not stating the value.
|`CHK-REF-RESET-RELEASE-CYCLES` |The release-to-high count in `clk_ref_i` cycles is at least 255
after the 64-cycle cold-reset low, and `rst_primary_ref_clk_no` still reads 1 after the reset chain
release; the exact count is printed without a compare, the specification not stating the value.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (600 `clk_ref_i` cycles for the release count, the
assertion count and each chain release, and the glitch-hold sample count) and that expiry raises an
assertion; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-REF-RESET-DEGLITCH`, `CHK-REF-RESET-RELEASE-CYCLES`,
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The exact release-to-high count and the cycle count of the assertion are printed
and not compared, because the specification does not state the values. The bounded waits are
recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-069-smc_cluster_beu_test]]
===== 69 `smc_cluster_beu_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cluster_beu_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SEP_IN reads and writes at the documented BEU addresses answer DECERR at the reset aperture and change no register below.

*Test Coverage*:

* The address map places one Bus Error Unit per core at `0xC801_0000 + core * 0x1000`. At the generated resets (`LOCAL_BASE` `0xC000_0000`, `GLOBAL_BASE` `0x4000_0000`, `REGION_SIZE` 16 MiB) those addresses lie outside both the local and the global aperture (`fabric.adoc`, Local and Remote Resource Access). The input fabric answers an inbound access there with DECERR. No access reaches a BEU, so no BEU property is claimed; the BEU registers themselves are `smc_region_size_plic_clint_beu_decode_test`'s subject.
* Each core's BEU base and core 0's `PLIC_ENABLE` word (`0xC801_0018`) take a read and a write, and every access must answer DECERR. Each address is declared an expected DECERR to the SEP_IN monitor. The written word is `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`'s reset with the hysteresis field changed, which differs from every reset checked below.
* Afterwards, the `0xC001_xxxx` registers that share those addresses' low bits must read their generated resets: `SMC_BASE_CONFIG` `GLOBAL_BASE`, `REGION_SIZE` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, alias-remap region 0 `region_start` and `region_attrs`, and M-mode remap entry 0 `region_attrs`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cluster_beu_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BEU-WINDOW-DECERR` |The five BEU addresses each answered DECERR on a read and on a write, and the six registers sharing their low address bits read their generated resets afterwards
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-BEU-WINDOW-DECERR` holds after its compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: No BEU property is claimed: at the reset aperture no access reaches a bus-error unit,
and the BEU registers themselves are the subject of `smc_region_size_plic_clint_beu_decode_test`.

'''''

[[sec-070-smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test]]
===== 70 `smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `cpu`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Run CPU-control address-map CSR depth checks.

*Test Coverage*:

* SMC_BASE_CONFIG (CPU address-map + hang-detector) reset-value precheck.
* The block at `smc_addr("SMC_TOP_SMC_BASE_CONFIG_BASE_ADDR")` is SMC_BASE_CONFIG (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl`), reached over real SEP_IN AXI.
* Every row of :data:`CPU_MAP_READS` addresses a **real register that exists in the generated map**, by its own generated `SMC_TOP_SMC_BASE_CONFIG_*_BASE_ADDR` symbol, and expects that register's **generated RDL reset constant**, imported by symbol from `hw/sys/smc/regs/gen/c/blocks/smc_base_config.h` -- never a hand literal and never an address computed as `BASE_ADDR + <offset>`.
* So every read verifies decode *and* spec-defined reset content.
* No row addresses `0xC001_0050`.
* `0xC001_0050` lies past the block: `SMC_TOP_SMC_BASE_CONFIG_BASE_ADDR` is `0xC0010000` and `SMC_TOP_SMC_BASE_CONFIG_SIZE` is `0x0000004C` (generated `smc_addr.h`), so the block ends at `0xC001004B` and the fabric refuses the access.
* A row there would log a register-shaped name that names no register (`[ADDRESS-FROM-AUTHORITATIVE-MAP]`).
* `LOCAL_BASE` (`sw=r` in the RDL) is written with a non-reset word and read back: the write completes and the readback still carries the generated reset, so the base-config alias the CPU uses cannot be moved from the bus.
* The sweep reads `REGION_SIZE` instead: a real register of the same block with a non-zero generated reset, so the row fails if the fabric ever stops decoding it.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPU-BFM-OBSERVABILITY` |Named compare in `smc_cpu_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-DEPTH` |Named compare in `smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-LIVE` |Named compare in `smc_cpu_ctrl_map_depth_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-LOCAL-BASE-RO` |`LOCAL_BASE` accepts a write of a non-reset word and its readback is an exact scoreboard compare against the generated reset, so the field is read-only on the single-base bench
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CPU-BFM-OBSERVABILITY`, `CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-DEPTH`, `CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-LIVE`, `CHK-CPU-CTRL-MAP-LOCAL-BASE-RO` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

'''''

'''''

[[sec-075-smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test]]
===== 75 `smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the codeword corruption is a backdoor write
through the `tb_cpu_ecc_poke_*` pins of the bound `smc_cpu_mem_dv` collateral

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_cpu_boot`,
`+smc_scratch_ram_hex={repo_root}/hw/sys/smc/dv/assets/min_pass.ecc.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Two flipped codeword bits: the CPU raises cluster_ded_o.

*Test Coverage*:

* Scratch ECC codeword corrupted in the macro array: two flipped bits raise DED.

*Test Procedure*:

The DUT offers no frontdoor way to corrupt a stored codeword, so the sequence
XORs two bits into scratch bank0 entry 0 through `tb_cpu_ecc_poke_en` /
`tb_cpu_ecc_poke_entry` / `tb_cpu_ecc_poke_mask` before the CPU boot release;
that pulse is the only write this leaf makes into DUT state. The reaction is
observed frontdoor: `smc_cluster_ded_o` on the wrapper (held sticky in
`tb_cluster_ded_seen`) must assert after the reset-vector fetch, and the bound
module's scratch read counter must have advanced, so the DED came from a read
of the poked word and not from a bench that never fetched.

Drive `smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ECC-CODEWORD-DED` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_codeword_corrupt_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ECC-CODEWORD-DED` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The DUT offers no frontdoor way to corrupt a stored codeword, so the two-bit flip is
a backdoor write through the bench poke pins of the bound memory collateral; the reaction is
observed frontdoor only.

'''''

[[sec-078-smc_ecc_fault_inject_test]]
===== 78 `smc_ecc_fault_inject_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_ecc_fault_inject_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); `tb_cpu_ecc_inject_sbe` / `tb_cpu_ecc_inject_dbe`
are testbench pins into the bound `smc_cpu_mem_dv` collateral, not product ports

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_cpu_boot`,
`+smc_scratch_ram_hex={repo_root}/hw/sys/smc/dv/assets/min_pass.ecc.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The scratch bank0 ECC inject hook is reached during FW boot and is gated by its enable pins.

*Test Coverage*:

* ECC SBE/DBE inject hooks on scratch bank0.
* DEFENDS: with inject armed, a real scratch bank0 read advances tb_cpu_ecc_inject_fire_count via DUT cpu_scratch0_inject_fire; clearing inject holds that counter while further scratch reads are still arriving. The claim is the contrast between those two halves of the run -- the hold on its own is true for every DUT state, because both inject pins are TB inputs and both are 0.
* DOES NOT DEFEND: Rocket ECC syndrome CSR / precise RAS recovery FW policy. Nor any DUT SECDED behaviour: the hook counts qualifying reads and corrupts no data -- there is no force on the macro response in this bench.

*Test Procedure*:

The inject pins arm a hook in the bound DV memory collateral that counts
qualifying bank0 reads; the hook writes nothing into DUT state and forces no
DUT signal. The claim is scored on the hook's own fire counter against the
CPU's real scratch reads, so no DUT SECDED behaviour is claimed here -- the
stored-codeword vehicles `smc_ecc_codeword_sec_test` and
`smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test` carry that.

Drive `smc_ecc_fault_inject_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ECC-INJECT` |Emitted only after three asserted compares on `tb_cpu_ecc_inject_fire_count`: it advanced while SBE inject was armed, held while both inject pins were clear across further scratch reads, and advanced again while DBE inject was armed (`smc_ecc_fault_inject_test_seq.py`); any of the three failing fails the run before the token
|`CHK-ECC-INJECT-NO-DUT-SECDED` |Carries no compare of its own: a scope statement that this leaf proves the inject hook and its enable gating, not the DUT's SECDED detector, which `smc_ecc_codeword_corrupt_test` covers
|`CHK-ECC-INJECT-RECOVERY` |Reports both halves of the contrast: the armed advance and the cleared hold, with the scratch-read counts they were taken over
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ECC-INJECT`, `CHK-ECC-INJECT-NO-DUT-SECDED`, `CHK-ECC-INJECT-RECOVERY` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: No DUT SECDED behaviour is claimed: the inject hook counts qualifying bank0 reads and
corrupts no data, there is no force on the macro response in this bench, and the ECC syndrome CSR
and precise RAS recovery firmware policy are not defended. The SECDED claim is carried by
`smc_ecc_codeword_sec_test` and `smc_ecc_codeword_ded_test`. The hold half of the contrast is true
for every DUT state on its own; only the contrast with the armed half is claimed.

'''''

[[sec-079-smc_mutex_semaphore_test]]
===== 79 `smc_mutex_semaphore_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_mutex_semaphore_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `cpu`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb module
`smc_mutex_semaphore_test`); the SV-UVM half is the class `smc_mutex_semaphore_test` of the same
name, selected with `+UVM_TESTNAME` (`--framework uvm`).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CPU_CTRL MUTEX/SEMA over SEP_IN AXI (expectations from cpu_ctrl.rdl).

*Test Coverage*:

* `reg MUTEX` (rdl:270-281), `field ... mutex[0:0] = 0x1`, desc: "HW mutex. Reads will attempt to acquire mutex, 1 on success. If the mutex is already acquired, the read will return 0. To release the mutex, write any value to the register." `MUTEX[4] @ 0x240` (rdl:378) -- four *independent* locks.
* `reg SEMA` (rdl:283-293), `field ... sema[15:0] = 0x0`, desc: "16-bit semaphore value to inc/dec. Writing to this register will inc/dec the semaphore value. The written value is treated as a signed number using 2s compliment." `SEMA[4] @ 0x260` (rdl:379).

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq`. The scenario has two implementations that share this
claim: the cocotb `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py` and the SV-UVM
`smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.svh` (`--framework uvm`). Each checker below is a named compare
the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MUTEX-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-HELD` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-NEIGHBOUR-FREE` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-NEIGHBOUR-HOLD` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-REL` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-TAKE` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-SEMA-ACCUMULATE` |Named compare in `smc_mutex_semaphore_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MUTEX-DENY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the second read of a held `MUTEX[0]` returns 0. Only meaningful because the first read expected the available encoding and got it -- a mutex stuck at 0 fails the take leg, one stuck at 1 fails this one
|`CHK-MUTEX-INDEP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): `MUTEX[1]` still reports available while `MUTEX[0]` is held, so "acquired" is a property of one lock rather than of the block
|`CHK-MUTEX-RELEASE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): after a write, `MUTEX[0]` reports available again. The RDL permits *any* value to release; both implementations write zero, so the property is proved for that value and the wider claim is not exercised
|`CHK-SEMA-ACCUM` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): `SEMA[0]` accumulates a signed 16-bit increment; +N then -N returns it to its baseline, and the baseline expectation of zero is also the check that the previous pass restored it
|`CHK-CSR-RESP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): every SEP_IN CSR access completes with an OKAY response
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): warm-reset domain release after fuse sense completes
|`CHK-NONVAC` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): reconciles the accesses the body issued against its own loop bounds -- twelve per pass, seven reads and five writes. A control-flow invariant, not a DUT-failable compare: it catches a truncated pass, and `CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` is the observed-side counterpart
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the `mutex_sema` feature's comparison count, taken from the always-on scoreboard fed by the PASSIVE monitor, is at or above the floor the completed passes imply (seven predicted reads per pass)
|`CHK-SB-MUTEX-SEMA` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): always-on scoreboard, feature `mutex_sema`: `smc_mutex_sema_ref_model` models acquire-on-read and the signed accumulator, computing each expected value BEFORE the state advances, and compares under the RDL field mask
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MUTEX-BASIC`, `CHK-MUTEX-HELD`, `CHK-MUTEX-NEIGHBOUR-FREE`, `CHK-MUTEX-NEIGHBOUR-HOLD`, `CHK-MUTEX-REL`, `CHK-MUTEX-TAKE` (and 1 more) hold after their compares.

Both registers are declared regwidth 64 with their live field inside the low 32 bits, so only
the RDL field bits are compared -- the bits above the field hold no field and are masked out
rather than given an invented expectation.

A mutex read acquires, so the SV-UVM view -- 16 scenario passes in one simulation -- hands the
block back as it found it: `MUTEX[0]` is released again after the read that proves the release,
`MUTEX[1]` is released, and `SEMA[0]` is returned to its baseline. Under `--framework uvm` the
SV-UVM checkers above hold instead, and `+SMC_MUTEX_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must fail the run.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The bits of MUTEX and SEMA above the live field hold no field and are masked out of
the compare rather than given an expectation. The release is proved only for a written value of
zero; the wider any-value release the register description permits is not exercised.

'''''


[[sec-081-smc_reference_counter_test]]
===== 81 `smc_reference_counter_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_reference_counter_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: 64-bit refclk counter rate check; not the OCTS timer.

*Test Coverage*:

* CPU_CTRL REFERENCE_COUNTER is a refclk CDC counter, not the OCTS timer.
* EXPECT-SOURCE (SPEC, not RTL): `doc/trm/src/architecture.adoc:256-265` -- the `REFERENCE_COUNTER` CSR is a free-running 64-bit counter "clocked by the always-on reference clock (`clk_ref_i`)", advancing "continuously from reset, independent of the system clock (`clk_smu_i`) frequency or PLL state", synchronised into the CPU clock domain for software reads.
* One count per `clk_ref_i` rising edge is therefore a SPEC-derived rate, not a transcription of `smc_cpu_ctrl_wrap.sv` / `prim_refclk_count_w_cdc` ([INDEPENDENT-EXPECTED-MODEL]).
* The check below turns that rate into a two-sided bound on the observed delta, measured over the very interval the two CSR samples bracket -- so a counter clocked by `clk_smc_i` (faster), by `clk_periph_i`, or at half rate fails, which a bare `c1 > c0` floor would pass.
* Load protocol (contract `SMC_COV_B1_003` revision 3), EXPECT-SOURCE `hw/sys/smc/regs/gen/adoc/blocks/cpu_ctrl.adoc:118-128`: write the counter once, then poll until the readback reflects the written value, at or just above it. Full-strobe 64-bit loads of V1 = `0x0000000000100000`, V2 = `0x0000000100000000`, V3 = `0xFFFFFFFF00000000`, V4 = `0x5A5A5A5AA5A5A5A5`, then the lower V5 = `0x0000000000001000`, the higher V6 = `0x0000000200000000`, V7 = `0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA` and V8 = `0x0000000000000000`.
* A poll converges when the readback has crossed the load: at or above the written value for a load above the previous readback, below the previous readback for a load under it. The bound is 256 polls per load; the poll count, the convergence time (SF-019) and the post-load excess (SF-020) are measured and logged, not compared.
* Coverage target (stimulus only): loading values with the upper bits set and then lower values toggles the upper bits of the Gray-coded reference-count synchroniser in the CPU-domain counter crossing; V7 and V8 have the Gray images all ones and all zeros, so every synchroniser bit sees both edges.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_reference_counter_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

. S1: run the existing rate legs unchanged (`CHK-REF-COUNT`, `CHK-REF-COUNT-BASIC`).
. S2: load V1 and poll `REFERENCE_COUNTER` until it converges; every poll read answers OKAY.
. S3: issue 8 further 64-bit reads and record each value and its excess over V1.
. S4: load and converge V2, V3 and V4 in turn; record each converged readback.
. S5: load V5 (below the V4 readback) and converge, then load V6 (above) and converge.
. S6: every convergence poll fails with the last readback when the 256-poll bound expires.
. S7: after S5, load V7 (above the V6 readback) and converge, then load V8 and converge below the V7 readback.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REF-COUNT` |Named compare in `smc_reference_counter_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-REF-COUNT-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_reference_counter_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-REFCNT-LOAD` |After the V1 load a readback R >= V1 is reached within the poll bound with every poll OKAY; polls and time to convergence logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-019)
|`CHK-REFCNT-MONOTONIC` |The 8 post-load readbacks are non-decreasing and each >= V1; the minimum and maximum excess over V1 are logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-020)
|`CHK-REFCNT-UPPER-HALF` |For V2, V3, V4 and V7 the converged readback R >= V and R[63:32] equals V[63:32], or V[63:32] + 1 only when R[31:0] < V[31:0]; V7 polls and time logged
|`CHK-REFCNT-RELOAD` |After the V5 load the readback converges to R5 with V5 <= R5 < the V4 readback, and after the V6 load to R6 >= V6; after the V8 load the readback R8 falls below the V7 readback; polls and time per reload logged
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence RATE-LEGS < LOAD-V1 < POST-LOAD-READS < UPPER-HALF-V2-V3-V4 < RELOAD-LOWER < RELOAD-HIGHER < LOAD-V7 < LOAD-V8, each term with its own sim time and a non-zero compare count
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Eight bounded convergence polls, each logging its bound, fail path and converged state; none expires on a passing run
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-REF-COUNT`, `CHK-REF-COUNT-BASIC`, `CHK-REFCNT-LOAD`, `CHK-REFCNT-MONOTONIC`, `CHK-REFCNT-UPPER-HALF`, `CHK-REFCNT-RELOAD`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-082-smc_spm_mem_boundary_test]]
===== 82 `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `cpu`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `mem`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb module
`smc_spm_mem_boundary_test`); the SV-UVM half is the class `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test` of the same
name, selected with `+UVM_TESTNAME` (`--framework uvm`).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SPM first/next/last 64-bit word write/readback via SEP_IN AXI.

*Test Coverage*:

* SPM window edges via SEP_IN AXI.
* Real-stall / multi-hart traffic is not claimed.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq`. The scenario has two implementations that share this
claim: the cocotb `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.py` and the SV-UVM
`smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.svh` (`--framework uvm`). Both write ALL the edge patterns
before reading any of them back: writing and reading one address at a time cannot see aliasing,
because each write would be followed immediately by its own read and every pair would still
match. With the writes batched, a decode that collapsed the edges onto one location returns the
last pattern written and the first readback fails. Each checker below is a named compare the
DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SPM-MEM-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_HI` |Named compare in `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_LO` |Named compare in `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_LO_NEXT` |Named compare in `smc_spm_mem_boundary_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-SPM-MEM-EDGE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): each window edge reads back the 64-bit word written to it while the other two edge patterns are still resident
|`CHK-SPM-CO-RESIDENT` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): each edge's readback is required NOT to equal any other edge's pattern -- the shape a collapsed decode would produce. Addresses and patterns are asserted pairwise distinct before the legs run, since identical patterns would make aliasing indistinguishable from correctness
|`CHK-MEM-RESP` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): every SEP_IN full-width access completes with an OKAY response
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): warm-reset domain release after fuse sense completes
|`CHK-NONVAC` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): reconciles the accesses the body issued against its own loop bounds -- a control-flow invariant that catches a truncated pass, not a DUT-failable compare. `CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` is the observed-side counterpart
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): the `spm_mem` feature's comparison count, taken from the always-on scoreboard fed by the PASSIVE monitor, is at or above the floor the completed passes imply (one predicted readback per window edge per pass)
|`CHK-SB-SPM-MEM` |SV-UVM shape only (`--framework uvm`): always-on scoreboard, feature `spm_mem`: `smc_spm_mem_ref_model` shadows the window per 64-bit word address, so an aliased decode disagrees with the model that keeps the edges apart
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SPM-MEM-BASIC`, `CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_HI`, `CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_LO`, `CHK-SPM-MEM-SPM_LO_NEXT` hold after their compares.

Accesses are full-width 64-bit single beats (AxSIZE = 3, every byte lane strobed): a 32-bit
CSR-shaped access would leave half of each word untouched and could not discriminate the
addresses. The SV-UVM view draws a fresh pattern set per pass from the scenario seed, so its 16
passes exercise different data and each pass also re-proves that the previous pass's words were
replaced rather than merely re-read. Under `--framework uvm` the governing checker set is the SV-UVM one in the table above (the cocotb ids named at the head of this Pass Criteria do not run there), and `+SMC_SPM_MEM_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must fail the run. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Real-stall and multi-hart traffic are not claimed.

'''''

[[sec-080-smc_occp_sanity_secure_error_test]]
===== 80 `smc_occp_sanity_secure_error_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_occp_sanity_secure_error_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex={repo_root}/hw/sys/smc/dv/assets/smc_efuse_default.hex`,
`+smc_efuse_prog_fail_count=1`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Secure program-fail completes and reports done; recovery burn programs bit0; signature positive gate.

*Test Coverage*:

* OTP PROGRAM failure injection (secure programming error), via `+smc_efuse_prog_fail_count`.
* DEFENDS: on the injected-failure burn the eFuse controller still reaches PROGRAM_DONE (bounded poll, expiry fails), and the subsequent recovery burn really does sticky-OR bit0 of word0 through the unmodified data path. The signature positive gate reads CHIP_CONFIG / EFUSE_MAP word0 against their expected values.
* DOES NOT DEFEND, model-backed: "the failing burn left the OTP word unchanged" is *not DUT-earned*. `hw/ip/efuse/dv/models/efuse_bank_model.sv` drives the macro as `.s_apb_pwdata(prog_fail_act ? 32'h0 : apb_req_i.pwdata)`, so on the failing write the DV model substitutes 0 for whatever the controller put on the bus and the word cannot change whatever the controller does. The compare stands as a consistency check on the injection hook only. Same tap as testcase 95, which already carries this disclaimer.
* GAP: the fail path is DUT-observable only if the model rejects the burn at the APB handshake (`pslverr`, macro write suppressed) instead of rewriting the data; the model is shared between the SEP and SMC benches.
* No mismatched signature is injected -- no write, plusarg, image variant or force on the proof path produces one, and the only `+smc_efuse_hex` image's word 0 *is* the golden. The positive gate is what runs.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_occp_sanity_secure_error_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCCP-SECURE-ERROR-RECOVERY` |EFUSE_MAP word0 matches the preload marker and CHIP_CONFIG_VERSION_LO its constant; the injected program failure reaches PROGRAM_DONE within the poll bound with word0 unchanged; the recovery burn reaches PROGRAM_DONE and sticky-ORs bit0 of word0. Fails on any mismatch, a poll that expires, or a non-OKAY SEP_IN response
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-OCCP-SECURE-ERROR-RECOVERY` holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: That the failing burn left the OTP word unchanged is not DUT-earned: the eFuse bank
model substitutes zero for the write data on the failing burn, so the word cannot change whatever
the controller does, and the compare stands as a consistency check on the injection hook only. No
mismatched signature is injected; the signature check runs only as its positive gate.

'''''

[[sec-430-smc_beu_csr_access_test]]
===== 430 `smc_beu_csr_access_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_beu_csr_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`, 8-byte reads and writes, 4-byte
REGION_SIZE accesses); the SEP_IN grouped-access item that issues a read and a write as one
outstanding group; `env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs` (the core 0 BEU base, the core 3 BEU
base and the core 0 ENABLE address are registered as expected DECERR); bench probes
`tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`, `clk_smc` and the passive `s_axi_arvalid`/`s_axi_arready`,
`s_axi_awvalid`/`s_axi_awready`, `s_axi_rvalid`/`s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_bvalid`/`s_axi_bready`
handshakes sampled per `clk_smc` cycle; the SMC `REGION_SIZE` CSR and the six registers of each of
the four per-core BEU blocks (CAUSE, PHYS_ADDR, ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE, ACCRUED_ENABLE,
LOCAL_ENABLE); ENABLE bits 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 (defined) and bits 0, 3, 4 (reserved).

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: BEU CSRs answer DECERR at the reset aperture, exact once widened.

*Test Coverage*:

* REGION_SIZE aperture: `fabric.adoc` makes `REGION_SIZE` reset to `0x0100_0000` (16 MiB) and
  `memmap.adoc` places the bus-error units beyond that reset aperture, so a BEU access answers
  DECERR until `REGION_SIZE` is widened to `0x1000_0000`.
* BEU registers at `0xC801_0000 + N * 0x1000` for cores 0 to 3 (`cpu.adoc` "Bus Error Reporting";
  `bus_error_unit.rdl`): ENABLE reset `0xE6`, PLIC_ENABLE and LOCAL_ENABLE storage on bits 1, 2, 5,
  6, 7, 3-bit CAUSE, 56-bit PHYS_ADDR, ACCRUED_ENABLE set and clear.
* Per-core independence: a pattern written to every register of core 0, then of core 3, leaves the
  other three cores' registers unchanged.
* Reserved ENABLE-family bits 0, 3, 4: the RDL declares them software-writable; the read-back is
  printed against that expectation and not compared (the specification does not state the value).
* Back-to-back ENABLE writes and a BEU access in flight together with a REGION_SIZE write back to
  its reset value: the overlap is measured, the REGION_SIZE write must answer OKAY and the access
  after each group is required to answer DECERR.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc` cycles), register the DECERR addresses with
  the AXI monitor, read `REGION_SIZE` and compare with its reset `0x0100_0000`.
. Error injection. Point: the BEU base addresses of core 0 and of core 3, registered as expected
  DECERR with the AXI monitor. Kind: a read of each BEU base while `REGION_SIZE` is at its reset
  aperture, beyond which the bus-error units lie. Expected response: both reads answer DECERR.
. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000`, read it back, then read ENABLE of cores 0 to 3; all four
  must answer OKAY.
. Read ENABLE of each core and compare with `0xE6`; read every register of every core as the base
  value; on core 0 write a walking one over bits 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 of PLIC_ENABLE and of LOCAL_ENABLE,
  read each back under the defined-bit mask, and restore both registers to 0.
. Write each CAUSE value 0 to 7 on core 0 and read it back under the 3-bit mask; write PHYS_ADDR
  all ones (56 bits) and each of the 56 walking ones and require an exact read-back; write CAUSE 0
  and restore PHYS_ADDR to its base value.
. Write ACCRUED_ENABLE with all defined bits set and read them back; write 0 and read 0.
. Write a distinct pattern to all six registers of core 0, read it back under each register's
  mask, read all registers of cores 1 to 3 and compare with their base values, then restore core 0
  and read the restore back; repeat with core 3 written and cores 0 to 2 read.
. Write ones to reserved bits 0, 3, 4 of ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE, ACCRUED_ENABLE and LOCAL_ENABLE of
  core 0, read each register and print it against the expected pattern without comparing it, then
  restore each register to its reset value and compare the restore read.
. Write ENABLE of core 0 as `0x00` then `0xE6` with no read between and read `0xE6`; write `0xE6`
  then `0x00` and read `0x00`; restore `0xE6` and read it.
. Error injection. Point: the core 0 BEU ENABLE register, with `REGION_SIZE` written back to its
  reset value while a BEU access is outstanding. Kind: a BEU ENABLE read, and in a second group a
  BEU ENABLE write, each issued together with a `REGION_SIZE` write of the reset value as one
  outstanding group, followed by an ENABLE read at the reset aperture. Expected response: at least
  two accesses outstanding at once in each group, and the ENABLE read after each group answers
  DECERR. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000` before the first group and widen again before the
  second; read `REGION_SIZE` at the end and compare with the reset value.
. Read `REGION_SIZE` and compare with its reset value, print the bounded waits and require the
  steps to complete in order with strictly increasing time stamps and the checker lines in order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BEU-DECERR-RESET` |With REGION_SIZE at its reset, the core 0 and core 3 BEU base reads must
  answer DECERR.
|`CHK-BEU-WIDENED-REACH` |With REGION_SIZE widened to `0x1000_0000`, the ENABLE register of cores 0
  to 3 must answer OKAY.
|`CHK-BEU-ENABLE-RESET` |ENABLE must read `0xE6` in each of the four BEUs, and PLIC_ENABLE and
  LOCAL_ENABLE of core 0 must read back each walking one written on bits 1, 2, 5, 6, 7.
|`CHK-BEU-CAUSE-PHYS` |CAUSE of core 0 must read back every value 0 to 7 written, and PHYS_ADDR
  must read back all ones and each of the 56 walking ones exactly.
|`CHK-BEU-ACCRUED` |ACCRUED_ENABLE of core 0 must read the defined bits written as ones and 0 after
  a write of 0.
|`CHK-BEU-INDEPENDENT` |A pattern written to all six registers of core 0, then of core 3, must read
  back on the written core and leave every register of the other three cores unchanged.
|`CHK-BEU-RESERVED-BITS` |Measures and prints the read-back of reserved bits 0, 3, 4 of the four
  ENABLE-family registers against the all-ones expectation without comparing it.
|`CHK-BEU-ENABLE-B2B` |ENABLE of core 0 must read `0xE6` after back-to-back writes `0x00` then
  `0xE6`, `0x00` after `0xE6` then `0x00`, and `0xE6` after the restore.
|`CHK-BEU-INFLIGHT` |A BEU read and then a BEU write issued together with a REGION_SIZE write must
  overlap with at least two accesses outstanding, and the BEU access after each group must answer
  DECERR; the responses of the grouped accesses themselves (OKAY or DECERR) are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eleven steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the ten
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access and
  group bounds) with the last access of each; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: DECERR at the reset
aperture, OKAY and exact read-back once widened, ENABLE reset `0xE6`, other cores unchanged,
overlap of at least two outstanding accesses, DECERR after each group, `REGION_SIZE` back to
`0x0100_0000`. `CHK-BEU-RESERVED-BITS` records the reserved-bit read-back without comparing it.

*Scope limit*: The read-back of the reserved ENABLE-family bits 0, 3, 4 after a write of ones is
printed against the all-ones expectation and not compared, because the specification does not state
the value. The responses of the grouped accesses themselves in the in-flight step (OKAY or DECERR)
are printed.

'''''

[[sec-431-smc_beu_register_test]]
===== 431 `smc_beu_register_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_beu_register_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`, 8-byte BEU accesses, 4-byte
REGION_SIZE accesses); bench probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; the SMC `REGION_SIZE` CSR widened to
`0x1000_0000`; the six registers (CAUSE, PHYS_ADDR, ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE, ACCRUED_ENABLE,
LOCAL_ENABLE) of each of the four per-core BEU blocks; ENABLE-family bits 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 (defined)
and 0, 3, 4 (reserved); CAUSE values 0 to 7; PHYS_ADDR bits [55:0].

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: BEU reset values, bit storage, CAUSE and PHYS_ADDR on four instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset values of the four BEU instances (`bus_error_unit.rdl`): ENABLE `0xE6`, PLIC_ENABLE,
  LOCAL_ENABLE, ACCRUED_ENABLE and CAUSE 0; PHYS_ADDR has no reset value and is printed.
* Defined bits 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 of ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE and LOCAL_ENABLE store a written one, per
  instance, with the other three instances unchanged (`bus_error_unit.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc`
  "Bus Error Unit Interrupts").
* ACCRUED_ENABLE replaces its value on each write and clears on a write of 0.
* CAUSE reads back the written values 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 on every instance (3-bit field in
  `bus_error_unit.rdl`); the read-back after writing 4 is printed.
* PHYS_ADDR (56-bit field) stores a distinct value per instance, each walking one over bits
  [55:0] and all ones, with the other instances unchanged.
* The BEUs are reached only after `REGION_SIZE` is widened to `0x1000_0000` (`fabric.adoc`,
  `memmap.adoc`); `REGION_SIZE` is restored to `0x0100_0000` at the end.
* Reserved bits and the CAUSE value 4 read-back are measured and printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000` and read it back.
. For each of the four BEUs read ENABLE and compare with `0xE6`; read PLIC_ENABLE, LOCAL_ENABLE,
  ACCRUED_ENABLE and CAUSE and compare with 0; read and save PHYS_ADDR without comparing it.
. For ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE and LOCAL_ENABLE of each BEU, write each defined bit alone and compare
  the read-back under the defined-bit mask, after each write reading the same register of the
  other three BEUs and comparing with their last values; write all ones, require the defined bits
  set and record the reserved-bit read-back; restore ENABLE to `0xE6` and the others to 0.
. Write `0x22` to ACCRUED_ENABLE of BEU 0 and read `0x22`; write `0x84` and read `0x84`; write 0
  and read 0.
. Write each CAUSE value 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 to every BEU and compare the read-back; write 4 to
  every BEU and print the read-back; write 0 to every BEU and read 0.
. Write a distinct 56-bit value (`0x0012_3456_789A_BC00` OR the BEU index) to PHYS_ADDR of each
  BEU and read all four back; then on each BEU write each of the 56 walking ones and all ones
  (`0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF`), compare the read-back, and compare the PHYS_ADDR of the other three
  BEUs with their last values.
. Restore each saved PHYS_ADDR word and compare the read-back; write `REGION_SIZE` back to its
  reset and compare the read-back; print the bounded waits and require the steps and checker lines
  in order with strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BEUREG-RESET` |ENABLE must read `0xE6` and PLIC_ENABLE, LOCAL_ENABLE, ACCRUED_ENABLE and CAUSE
  must read 0 on each of the four BEUs (the 0 reads cannot tell a reset value from a bench that
  initializes to zero under 2-state simulation); the PHYS_ADDR reset read is measured and printed
  only.
|`CHK-BEUREG-BITS` |Each defined bit (1, 2, 5, 6, 7) written alone to ENABLE, PLIC_ENABLE and
  LOCAL_ENABLE must read back as written on each BEU with the other three unchanged; the
  reserved-bit read-back is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-BEUREG-ACCRUED` |BEU 0 ACCRUED_ENABLE must read `0x22` after writing `0x22`, `0x84` after
  writing `0x84` (replaced, not merged) and 0 after writing 0.
|`CHK-BEUREG-CAUSE` |CAUSE must read back each written value 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 on every BEU and 0
  after the re-arm write; the read-back of 4 is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-BEUREG-PHYS` |PHYS_ADDR of each BEU must read back its distinct value, all 56 walking ones
  and `0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF` exactly, with the other instances unchanged.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eight steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the six
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access of each; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: ENABLE reset
`0xE6`, other registers 0, defined bits and PHYS_ADDR patterns exact, CAUSE values exact,
ACCRUED_ENABLE replaced, `REGION_SIZE` back to `0x0100_0000`. The reserved-bit, CAUSE 4 and
PHYS_ADDR reset reads are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The PHYS_ADDR reset read, the reserved-bit read-back after a write of all ones and
the CAUSE read-back after writing 4 are measured and printed and not compared, because the
specification does not state the values. The 0 reads of the reset check cannot tell a reset value
from a bench that initializes to zero under 2-state simulation.

'''''

[[sec-432-smc_clint_register_test]]
===== 432 `smc_clint_register_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_clint_register_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte MSIP and REGION_SIZE
accesses, 8-byte MTIMECMP and MTIME accesses); bench probes `tb_top.tb_clint_msip` (bit n is
core n), `tb_top.tb_clint_mtimecmp0`, `tb_top.tb_clint_mtimecmp1`, `tb_top.tb_clint_mtime`,
`tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done` and `clk_smc_i`; the SMC `REGION_SIZE` CSR widened to `0x1000_0000`;
CLINT MSIP[0..3], MTIMECMP[0..3] and MTIME.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CLINT MSIP, MTIMECMP and MTIME register behaviour with probe checks.

*Test Coverage*:

* MSIP[n] bit 0 stores a written one, bits [31:1] are reserved and read 0, and the register
  drives `tb_clint_msip` bit n with the other cores' MSIP registers unchanged (`clint.rdl`).
* MTIMECMP[n] stores a full 64-bit value per core, independently of the other cores
  (`clint.rdl`); `tb_clint_mtimecmp0` and `tb_clint_mtimecmp1` follow cores 0 and 1.
* MTIME advances and never reads smaller than an earlier read, and `tb_clint_mtime` changes
  within a bounded number of `clk_smc_i` cycles (`clint.rdl`, `clk_rst.adoc` tick description).
* A write to MTIME is reflected: a later read is at or above the written `0x0000_0001_0000_0000`
  and lies between the two samples of `tb_clint_mtime` around the read.
* The CLINT is reached only after `REGION_SIZE` is widened to `0x1000_0000` (`memmap.adoc`,
  `fabric.adoc`); all touched registers and `REGION_SIZE` are restored.
* The reset values of MSIP and MTIMECMP, the tick-to-clock relation and the exact
  reflected-minus-written MTIME difference are measured and printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000` and read it back; save MSIP[0..3] and MTIMECMP[0..3]; write
  0 to every MSIP.
. For each core write all ones to MSIP[n]; require the read-back 1, require `tb_clint_msip` bit n
  set and the other three MSIP registers reading 0, require `tb_clint_msip` equal to `1 << n`, write
  0 and require MSIP[n] and `tb_clint_msip` to read 0.
. Write the distinct value `0x0123_4567_89AB_CD00 | n` to MTIMECMP[n] of each core and read all
  four back, comparing `tb_clint_mtimecmp0` and `tb_clint_mtimecmp1` with cores 0 and 1; then for
  each core write all ones, read all four MTIMECMP registers and probes expecting only that core
  changed, and write the distinct value back.
. Read MTIME, wait up to 20000 `clk_smc_i` cycles for `tb_clint_mtime` to change, read MTIME three
  more times; require the second read above the first and no read smaller than the previous one.
. Write MTIME = `0x0000_0001_0000_0000`; poll MTIME up to 200 reads for a value at or above it,
  sampling `tb_clint_mtime` before and after each read; require the hit to lie between the two
  samples.
. Restore each saved MSIP and MTIMECMP and compare the read-back, restore `REGION_SIZE` and compare
  the read-back, print the bounded waits and require the steps and checker lines in order with
  strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CLINT-MSIP` |Ones written to each MSIP[n] must read bit 0 set with bits [31:1] clear, the
  other three MSIP registers must read 0 and `tb_clint_msip` must equal `1 << n`, then 0 after the
  clear; the saved reset values are measured and printed.
|`CHK-CLINT-MTIMECMP` |Four distinct 64-bit values and an all-ones value must read back
  independently per core with `tb_clint_mtimecmp0` and `tb_clint_mtimecmp1` agreeing for cores 0
  and 1; the saved reset values are measured and printed.
|`CHK-CLINT-MTIME-ADV` |MTIME reads must never decrease, the second read must exceed the first, and
  `tb_clint_mtime` must change within 20000 `clk_smc_i` cycles; the tick-to-clock relation is
  measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-CLINT-MTIME-LOAD` |After a write of `0x0000_0001_0000_0000` an MTIME read within 200
  polls must be at or above it and between the two `tb_clint_mtime` samples; the
  reflected-minus-written difference is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the five
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done, MTIME change, MTIME load poll
  and the SEP_IN access bound) with the last observed state of each; an expiry fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: MSIP bit 0 and
`tb_clint_msip` follow each write, MTIMECMP values are exact per core, MTIME advances monotonically
and reflects a write, and `REGION_SIZE` returns to `0x0100_0000`. The reset-value, tick-ratio and
reflected-offset figures are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The reset values of MSIP and MTIMECMP, the tick-to-clock relation of MTIME and the
reflected-minus-written MTIME difference are measured and printed and not compared, because the
specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-433-smc_cpu_boot_regs_read_test]]
===== 433 `smc_cpu_boot_regs_read_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_boot_regs_read_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 8-byte reads and writes, 4-byte
STRAPS and chip-configuration reads, one 8-beat 8-byte burst read); no firmware image and no
preload; CPU_CTRL RESET_VECTOR[0..3], RESET_CTRL (bit 24 `debug_reset_n`), DUMMY_ROM_0..3,
DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3] and SCRATCH[0]; STRAPS_LO and STRAPS_HI; chip configuration VERSION_LO,
VERSION_HI and CHIP_ID; SMC base configuration GLOBAL_BASE, LOCAL_BASE and REGION_SIZE.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Boot-time register reads against reset values over SEP_IN.

*Test Coverage*:

* RESET_VECTOR[0..3] reset value `0x0000_0000_C004_0000` (`cpu.adoc` "Reset and Boot";
  `cpu_ctrl.rdl`).
* RESET_CTRL reads its reset word `0x10F` before any write, with `debug_reset_n` (bit 24) 0
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`); the 0 bit is reset-equal under 2-state Verilator.
* STRAPS_LO and STRAPS_HI: the 64-bit read at the STRAPS_LO address is compared with the two 32-bit
  reads combined (`straps.rdl`); the bench ties the straps to zero, so the compare does not
  discriminate lane order (measured); the strap levels are printed.
* VERSION_LO `0x0001_00A0`, VERSION_HI 0 and CHIP_ID 0 (`chip_config.rdl`).
* GLOBAL_BASE `0x4000_0000`, LOCAL_BASE `0xC000_0000` and REGION_SIZE `0x0100_0000`
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`, `fabric.adoc`); LOCAL_BASE is read-only (`smc_base_config.rdl`), the
  response to a write is printed and not compared.
* DUMMY_ROM_0..3 hold the four boot-stub words and DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3] read 0 (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`);
  the zero words are reset-equal under 2-state Verilator;
  an 8-beat burst read at DUMMY_ROM_0 is checked against those words when it answers OKAY or EXOKAY.
* SCRATCH[0] is 32 bits wide: a 64-bit all-ones write reads back `0x0000_0000_FFFF_FFFF`
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Stamp the start of the run after bring-up; no register has been written.
. Read RESET_VECTOR[0..3] as 64-bit reads and compare each with `0x0000_0000_C004_0000`.
. Read RESET_CTRL as a 64-bit read and compare the whole word with its reset word `0x10F`.
. Read STRAPS_LO and STRAPS_HI as 32-bit reads, then the 64-bit word at the STRAPS_LO address; the
  64-bit word is compared with `(HI << 32) | LO`; with the straps tied to zero the compare is
  non-discriminating (measured).
. Read VERSION_LO, VERSION_HI and CHIP_ID and compare with `0x0001_00A0`, 0 and 0.
. Read GLOBAL_BASE, LOCAL_BASE and REGION_SIZE and compare with `0x4000_0000`, `0xC000_0000` and
  `0x0100_0000`.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only LOCAL_BASE register of the SMC base configuration. Kind: a
  write of `0xD000_0000` to a read-only register. Expected response: LOCAL_BASE still reads
  `0xC000_0000`; the write response is printed and not compared.
. Read DUMMY_ROM_0..3 and DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3] as single 64-bit reads and compare with the stub
  words `0x0145_0513_0000_0517`, `0xFFF0_0693_3055_1073`, `0x1050_0073_3046_B073`,
  `0x0000_0000_FFDF_F06F` and four zero words.
. Issue one 8-beat 64-bit burst read at DUMMY_ROM_0; print the response; require no more than
  eight beats; when the response is OKAY or EXOKAY require the beats to equal DUMMY_ROM_0..3 then
  DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3].
. Write all ones (64-bit) to SCRATCH[0] and compare the read-back with `0x0000_0000_FFFF_FFFF`;
  write `0xA5C3_9E71` and compare the read-back; check that the ten steps stamped in order with
  strictly increasing time and the checker lines printed in step order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BOOT-RESET-VECTOR-RESET` |All four RESET_VECTOR registers must read `0x0000_0000_C004_0000`.
|`CHK-BOOT-DEBUG-RESET-N` |RESET_CTRL must read its reset word `0x10F` before any write, so bit 24
  (`debug_reset_n`) reads 0 (the 0 bit is reset-equal under 2-state Verilator).
|`CHK-BOOT-STRAP-WORD` |The 64-bit read at STRAPS_LO is compared with `(STRAPS_HI << 32) | STRAPS_LO`
  from the two 32-bit reads; the straps are tied to zero, so the compare is non-discriminating
  (measured); the three values are printed.
|`CHK-BOOT-CHIPCFG-RESET` |VERSION_LO must read `0x0001_00A0`, VERSION_HI 0 and CHIP_ID 0.
|`CHK-BOOT-APERTURE-RESET` |GLOBAL_BASE must read `0x4000_0000`, LOCAL_BASE `0xC000_0000` and
  REGION_SIZE `0x0100_0000`.
|`CHK-BOOT-LOCALBASE-RO` |LOCAL_BASE must still read `0xC000_0000` after a write of `0xD000_0000`;
  the response of the write is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-BOOT-DUMMY-WORDS` |DUMMY_ROM_0..3 must read the four stub words and DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3] must
  read 0 (the zero words are reset-equal under 2-state Verilator).
|`CHK-BOOT-DUMMY-BURST` |The 8-beat burst read response is measured and printed; only when it is
  OKAY or EXOKAY must the beats equal DUMMY_ROM_0..3 then DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3] in address order.
|`CHK-BOOT-SCRATCH-WIDTH` |SCRATCH[0] must read `0x0000_0000_FFFF_FFFF` after a 64-bit all-ones
  write and `0x0000_0000_A5C3_9E71` after a write of that pattern.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ten steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the nine
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold with the values
named in the table. The strap levels, the LOCAL_BASE write response and, on a burst
response other than OKAY or EXOKAY, the burst data are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The bench ties the straps to zero, so the STRAPS word compare does not discriminate
lane order; the strap levels are printed. The response of the LOCAL_BASE write and the response of
the 8-beat burst read are printed and not compared, and the burst data are compared only when the
response is OKAY or EXOKAY. The zero RESET_CTRL bit and the DUMMY_ROM_NULL zero words are
reset-equal under 2-state Verilator.

'''''

[[sec-434-smc_cpu_boot_release_sequence_test]]
===== 434 `smc_cpu_boot_release_sequence_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_boot_release_sequence_test`

*BFM / Model*: reset agent (`env.reset_agent`: `COLD_RST_LO` and `COLD_RST_HI` operations) on two
cold resets, with the `+smc_hold_ext_boot` run option holding `tb_top.tb_hold_ext_boot` at 1 from
time 0 and the sequence driving it to 0 and back to 1; a passive sampler of these probes on every
`clk_smc_i` rising edge: `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n`,
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, `tb_hold_ext_boot` and `ext_boot_seq_done` (`ext_boot_seq_done` is the bench assign
`~tb_hold_ext_boot`: stimulus, not a DUT probe; the sequence samples `1 - tb_hold_ext_boot`), `tb_cpu_core_resets_n` (all core
bits), `tb_cpu_uncore_reset_n`, `smc_init_mem_done_o`, `tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` and
`tb_cpu_isolate_req`; `smc_disable_sram_auto_init_i` is held 1 by the bench. No AXI VIP and no
firmware image.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_ext_boot`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CPU reset release against fuse sense, ext boot and isolate.

*Test Coverage*:

* The CPU core and uncore resets stay asserted from the cold reset release until fuse sense is
  done, and stay asserted with sense done while the external boot sequence is not done
  (`cpu.adoc` "Memory Repair": the qualified `ext_boot_seq_done_i` gates fuse-reset release
  together with fuse sensing; `clk_rst.adoc`).
* The CPU resets release only after both sense done and external boot done have risen.
* `smc_init_mem_done_o` reports completion or bypass and is 1 whenever a CPU reset output is 1
  (`cpu.adoc` "Reset and Boot": the scratchpad zero-fill holds the cores in reset until
  initialization completes or is bypassed).
* The cluster boundary self-isolates after a cold reset: `tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` stays 1 from the
  release of the primary reset and falls only after init-done and both CPU resets have released
  (`cpu.adoc` "CPU AXI Isolation").
* External boot done rising while fuse sensing is still running after a second cold reset: no CPU
  reset releases before sense done.
* The release latencies and the four-cycle isolate release count are measured and printed; the
  specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `tb_hold_ext_boot` = 1; wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles);
  start the per-edge sampler; assert a cold reset, wait for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low, release
  the cold reset and wait for it to rise.
. Require `tb_fuse_sense_done` still 0 at the release edge; wait for it to rise (bound 200000
  cycles); require every sampled CPU core and uncore reset output 0 from the release edge to the
  sense-done edge.
. Over a window of 64 edges from the sense-done edge require `tb_fuse_sense_done` 1, external boot
  done 0 and every CPU reset output 0 on all of them; the levels of `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
  `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` in the window are printed.
. Drive `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 0; wait for external boot done to rise (bound 16 cycles) and for all
  core and uncore reset outputs to read 1 (bound 20000 cycles); require the release after both
  the sense-done and the external boot edges; require no earlier edge from the sense-done edge to
  read fully released.
. Wait for `smc_init_mem_done_o` to read 1 (bound 20000 cycles from the first cold reset assert);
  require it to read 1 on every recorded edge on which a CPU reset output reads 1.
. Require `tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` 1 at the first edge after `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` released and
  on every edge until it falls (bound 2000 cycles); require the fall after the latest of init-done,
  core release and uncore release.
. Drive `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 1; repeat the cold reset assert and release; require
  `tb_fuse_sense_done` 0 at the release edge and at the next drive; drive `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 0
  while sensing; wait for sense done and for the CPU release (bounds 200000 and 20000 cycles);
  require no CPU reset output 1 before sense done, the CPU release after sense done and the reset
  agent to settle released; require the eight fence edges increasing and print the checker lines
  in order after the last step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FUSE-CORES-HELD-UNTIL-SENSE` |Every core reset output and the uncore reset output must read 0
  on every recorded edge from the cold reset release to the first edge with `tb_fuse_sense_done`
  1, and sense must read 0 at the release edge.
|`CHK-FUSE-HELD-WITHOUT-EXT-BOOT` |With `tb_fuse_sense_done` 1 and external boot done 0 for 64
  consecutive edges, every core reset output and the uncore reset output must stay 0; the
  `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` levels are measured and printed.
|`CHK-FUSE-RELEASE-BOTH-TERMS` |All core and uncore reset outputs must first read 1 after both the
  sense-done rise and the external-boot rise; the edge counts after each rise are measured and
  printed without comparing them.
|`CHK-FUSE-EXT-BOOT-MID-SENSE` |With external boot done raised while `tb_fuse_sense_done` is still 0
  after the second cold reset, no CPU reset output may read 1 before sense done and the full
  release must follow sense done; the latency is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-INIT-MEM-DONE-BYPASS` |`smc_init_mem_done_o` must read 1 on every recorded edge on which a CPU
  reset output reads 1, with initialization bypassed; the first edge it reads 1 is printed.
|`CHK-COLD-SELF-ISOLATE-HELD` |`tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` must read 1 from the first edge after the
  primary reset releases until it falls; the `tb_cpu_isolate_req` values around the fall are
  printed.
|`CHK-COLD-SELF-ISOLATE-RELEASE` |`tb_cpu_cluster_isolate` must fall after the latest of init-done,
  core release and uncore release; the delay in `clk_smc_i` rises is measured and printed against
  the documented four cycles without comparing it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time, the seven checker
  lines must print in step order and the fence edges must increase, so a truncated run fails.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: CPU resets held
until both fuse sense and external boot are done, `smc_init_mem_done_o` 1 whenever a CPU reset
