output is 1, isolate held then released after the latest of init-done and the CPU releases, and the
same hold in the second cold reset with external boot raised mid-sense. The release latencies and
the isolate delay are recorded without comparison. The run requires `+smc_hold_ext_boot`.

*Scope limit*: The release latencies after the sense-done and external-boot rises, the latency of
the mid-sense release and the isolate release delay against the documented four cycles are measured
and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state the values. The levels of
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` in the hold window, the first edge on which
`smc_init_mem_done_o` reads 1 and the `tb_cpu_isolate_req` values around the isolate fall are
printed.

'''''

[[sec-435-smc_cpu_ctrl_access_rules_test]]
===== 435 `smc_cpu_ctrl_access_rules_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_access_rules_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 8-byte accesses, `prot` = `0b000` secure and `0b010` non-secure on SCRATCH[1]); bench
probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL registers CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT (pre_reset_count
[15:0], post_reset_count [31:16], core_resets_done [35:32]), RESET_TIMEOUT (timeout_value [15:0],
timeout_mode bit 16, reset_applied bit 32, reset_timeout bit 36), TEST_CTRL,
WB_PC_CORE0[0], SMC_ATTRIBUTES, SCRATCH[1], RESET_VECTOR[1], RESET_CTRL, WDT_TIMEOUT; SMC base
configuration LOCAL_BASE.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CPU_CTRL zero, read-only, reserved-bit and AxPROT rules.

*Test Coverage*:

* A full-width write of 0 clears the read-write fields of CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT and
  RESET_TIMEOUT while the read-only core_resets_done keeps 0xF and reset_applied and
  reset_timeout stay 0 (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`).
* A write of all ones to read-only registers (TEST_CTRL, WB_PC_CORE0[0], SMC_ATTRIBUTES,
  LOCAL_BASE) and to the read-only core_resets_done field leaves the read value unchanged
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` `sw=r`, `smc_base_config.rdl`); the write response is measured and printed
  (the specification does not state the value).
* A write of ones over bits outside any declared field (SCRATCH[1], RESET_VECTOR[1], RESET_CTRL,
  WDT_TIMEOUT, WB_PC_CORE0[0]) leaves every named field unchanged (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`); the reserved
  bits as read back are printed (the specification does not state the value).
* Secure and non-secure (AxPROT) reads and writes of SCRATCH[1] complete (`memmap.adoc`
  "Protection, Access Control"); the effect of AxPROT on CPU_CTRL is measured and printed
  (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Write CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT with pre_reset_count `0x0123` and post_reset_count `0x0456`, and
  RESET_TIMEOUT with timeout_value `0xBEEF` and timeout_mode 1; read both back (the pulse count
  with core_resets_done 0xF); write a full-width 0 to CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT and RESET_TIMEOUT and
  read the pulse count expecting core_resets_done only and RESET_TIMEOUT expecting 0; restore CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT to its reset value and read it back.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only registers TEST_CTRL, WB_PC_CORE0[0], SMC_ATTRIBUTES and
  LOCAL_BASE, and the read-only core_resets_done field of CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT. Kind: a write of
  all ones to each read-only register, and a write of CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT with the
  core_resets_done bits clear. Expected response: each register reads the word it held before the
  write; the write response of each is printed and not compared. Read each register before its
  write to take the word compared against.
. For SCRATCH[1], RESET_VECTOR[1], RESET_CTRL and WDT_TIMEOUT write ones over the bits outside the
  declared fields with the named fields held at their read values, read back, require the named
  fields unchanged, print the reserved bits, restore the register and compare the restore read;
  do the same without a restore for WB_PC_CORE0[0] bits [63:58].
. Read SCRATCH[1]; write and read it with AxPROT secure and again with AxPROT non-secure, printing
  data and response of each; restore SCRATCH[1] and compare the restore read; print the bounded
  waits and require the steps and checker lines in order with strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ACCR-ZERO` |After a full-width 0, the read-write fields of CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT and
  RESET_TIMEOUT must read 0 with core_resets_done 0xF and reset_applied and reset_timeout 0.
|`CHK-ACCR-RO-RESP` |Each read-only register or field must read the word it held before a write of
  all ones; the write response of each is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-ACCR-RESERVED` |After ones over the undeclared bits every named field must read its earlier
  value; the undeclared bits as read are measured and printed without comparing them.
|`CHK-ACCR-PROT` |Secure and non-secure SCRATCH[1] accesses must complete and SCRATCH[1] must
  restore; the data and response of each AxPROT access are measured and printed without comparing
  them.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The five steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the four
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access of each; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: zero writes clear
only the read-write fields, read-only registers keep their read value, named fields survive ones
over reserved bits, and SCRATCH[1] restores. The read-only write responses, the reserved-bit
read-back and the AxPROT responses are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The write responses of the read-only registers and field, the reserved bits as read
back after a write of ones, and the data and response of the secure and non-secure AxPROT accesses
are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state them.

'''''

[[sec-436-smc_cpu_ctrl_dummy_rom_test]]
===== 436 `smc_cpu_ctrl_dummy_rom_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_dummy_rom_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 8-byte reads and writes); bench
probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL DUMMY_ROM_0..3 and DUMMY_ROM_NULL[0..3], eight
consecutive 64-bit registers.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: DUMMY_ROM line read and read-write storage with restore.

*Test Coverage*:

* The eight consecutive 64-bit words from DUMMY_ROM_0 read the four boot-stub words
  `0x0145_0513_0000_0517`, `0xFFF0_0693_3055_1073`, `0x1050_0073_3046_B073` and
  `0x0000_0000_FFDF_F06F`, then four zero words that pad the 64-byte cache line
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` DUMMY_ROM_0..3 and DUMMY_ROM_NULL reset values).
* Each of the eight registers is software read-write (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` `sw=rw`): a distinct pattern
  written to each reads back in address order and in reverse order with no aliasing between
  registers, and the original words are restored.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Read the eight words at DUMMY_ROM_0 to DUMMY_ROM_NULL[3] and compare each with the stub word or
  zero listed above.
. Write the pattern `0x5A5A_0000_0000_0000 | (index << 32) | 0x1111_1111` to each of the eight
  registers (every write must answer OKAY), read all eight back in order and then in reverse
  order and compare each with its own pattern.
. Write each original word back, read all eight and compare each with the original; print the
  bounded waits, require the four steps and the two checker lines in order with strictly
  increasing time stamps and a count of at least 48 accesses.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DROM-LINE` |The eight consecutive 64-bit words from DUMMY_ROM_0 must read the four stub words
  then four zero words (the zero words are reset-equal under 2-state Verilator).
|`CHK-DROM-RW` |Each of the eight registers must read back its own distinct pattern in address
  order and in reverse order, and the restore must return the words read in step 2.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The four steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the two
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access of each; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: stub words and
zeros on the first read, every pattern read back exactly in both orders, the original words
restored, and all accesses answered OKAY.

*Scope limit*: The four DUMMY_ROM_NULL zero words are reset-equal under 2-state Verilator, so the
zero compare cannot tell a reset value from a bench that initializes to zero.

'''''

[[sec-437-smc_cpu_ctrl_mutex_all_test]]
===== 437 `smc_cpu_ctrl_mutex_all_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_mutex_all_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte MUTEX reads, 8-byte MUTEX
writes; a two-read group item sharing AXI ID 5; a single read with the R-channel ready delayed by
32 cycles through the VIP timing profile); bench probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL
MUTEX[0..3], bit 0 of the read data; the write data of the release writes includes a value drawn
from the run seed.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the 64-bit value of the fourth release write.

*Objective*: MUTEX[0..3] hold, release, independence, back-to-back, stalled R.

*Test Coverage*:

* MUTEX[n] is a hardware mutex: a read acquires it and returns 1, a read while it is held returns
  0, and a write of any value releases it (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` MUTEX field description; reset value 1).
* The release works for the written values 0, 1, all ones and a seeded 64-bit value, on all four
  instances.
* The four mutexes are independent: holding MUTEX[n] leaves the other three acquirable.
* Two reads issued as one group item under one AXI ID return acquire (1) then held (0) in order
  (overlap not measured).
* A read whose R response is held off for 32 cycles still delivers the acquire value and the next
  read sees the mutex held.
* All four mutexes are free again at the end of the test.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. For each instance read MUTEX[n] and require bit 0 = 1, then read it three more times and require
  bit 0 = 0 each time.
. For each instance and each written value 0, 1, all ones and the seeded value: when the value is
  not the first, re-acquire and require 1; require a read to return 0 while held; write the value
  and require the next read to return 1; write 0 to release.
. For each instance acquire it, require the other three to read 1 (each then held), require the
  instance itself to read 0 and write 0 to all four to release.
. For each instance issue two reads under AXI ID 5 as one group item (overlap not measured) and require bit 0 of
  the data to be 1 then 0; release with a write of 0.
. For each instance issue one read with `r_ready_delay` = 32 cycles and require bit 0 = 1; read
  again and require 0; release with a write of 0.
. Read every MUTEX, require 1 on each, release; require the six steps and five checker lines in
  order with strictly increasing time stamps; print the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MUTEX-HELD-READS` |On each of the four instances the acquire read must return bit 0 = 1 and
  the three following reads must return bit 0 = 0.
|`CHK-MUTEX-RELEASE-VALUES` |A write of 0, 1, all ones and the seeded value must each release the
  mutex so the next read returns bit 0 = 1, on all four instances.
|`CHK-MUTEX-INDEP` |With MUTEX[n] held the other three must read bit 0 = 1 and MUTEX[n] must read
  bit 0 = 0, for each n.
|`CHK-MUTEX-BACK2BACK` |Two reads issued as one group item under AXI ID 5 must return bit 0 = 1
  then 0 on each instance (overlap not measured).
|`CHK-MUTEX-RSTALL` |A read with the R ready delayed 32 cycles must deliver bit 0 = 1 and the next
  read must return 0, on each instance.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The six steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the five
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access state; an access that never completes fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: the acquire read
returns 1, held reads return 0, every written value releases, instances are independent, the
grouped and stalled reads keep their order, and every mutex ends free.

*Scope limit*: The overlap of the two reads issued as one group item under AXI ID 5 is not measured;
only their order of return is compared.

'''''

[[sec-438-smc_cpu_ctrl_scratch_all_test]]
===== 438 `smc_cpu_ctrl_scratch_all_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_scratch_all_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes); bench
probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL SCRATCH[0..15], the 32-bit `data` field of each entry.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: SCRATCH[0..15] isolation, walking entry and 32-bit storage.

*Test Coverage*:

* All sixteen SCRATCH entries are software read-write 32-bit registers with reset 0
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` SCRATCH; `smc-programming.adoc`): a distinct pattern per entry reads back in
  order and in reverse order with no aliasing.
* Walking entry: a pattern written to entry k alone leaves the other fifteen entries at 0.
* Width: `0xFFFF_FFFF`, `0x0000_0001` and `0x8000_0000` written to every entry read back exactly.
* Every entry is restored to its value read before the sweep. Which entries the bench and the
  firmware use is not identified, so all sixteen are swept and restored.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles); require the sixteen entry
  addresses to be distinct.
. Read and save all sixteen entries.
. Write `0xA5A5_0000 | (index << 8) | index` to each entry; read all back in order and then in
  reverse order and compare each with its own pattern; require the sixteen patterns read in order
  to be distinct.
. Write 0 to all entries; for each k write `0xDEAD_BE00 | k` to entry k, read all sixteen and
  compare entry k with the pattern and the other fifteen with 0, then write 0 to entry k.
. For each of `0xFFFF_FFFF`, `0x0000_0001` and `0x8000_0000` write it to every entry and read
  every entry back comparing exactly.
. Write each saved value back and compare the read-back of every entry; require the total access
  count to match the steps; print the bounded waits and require the six steps and the checker
  lines in order with strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SCRATCH-UNIQUE` |Each of the sixteen entries must read its own distinct pattern in order and
  in reverse order, and the restore must return the saved words.
|`CHK-SCRATCH-WALK` |With one entry written alone it must hold its pattern and the fifteen idle
  entries must read 0, for each of the sixteen entries.
|`CHK-SCRATCH-BITS` |All sixteen entries must read back `0xFFFF_FFFF`, `0x0000_0001` and
  `0x8000_0000` exactly as written.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The six steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the checker
  lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: sixteen distinct
patterns read back in both orders, only the written entry changes during the walk, the three width
patterns are exact and every entry is restored.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-439-smc_cpu_ctrl_sema_test]]
===== 439 `smc_cpu_ctrl_sema_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_sema_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes; a group
item of eight writes to SEMA[1]); bench probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL
SEMA[0..3], the 16-bit signed `sema` field of each entry.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SEMA[0..3] signed accumulate, independence, wrap and pipelined writes.

*Test Coverage*:

* A write to SEMA[n] adds the written value, treated as a 2s-complement signed number, to the
  semaphore (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` SEMA field description; reset 0): +5, +3, -2 and -6 accumulate to 5,
  8, 6 and 0 on SEMA[0].
* The four instances accumulate independently: +1, +2, +3, +4 written to SEMA[0..3] read back as
  written and negating each returns every instance to 0.
* Behaviour below 0 and for write data above bit 15 is not defined by the register description;
  the results are measured and printed (the specification does not state the value), and only the
  stability of two consecutive reads is required. After the -1 write, a restore write of +1 must
  return SEMA[0] to 0.
* The 16-bit maximum is inside the signed range: 16383, 16383 and 1 accumulate to `0x7FFF`. The
  reads after one more +1, after the restore and after -32768 and -1 are measured and printed.
* Eight +1 writes issued as one group item to SEMA[1] sum to 8 and a write of -8 returns it to 0
  (overlap not measured).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. On SEMA[0] write +5, +3, -2 reading after each and comparing with 5, 8, 6; write -6 and compare
  the read with 0.
. Write +1, +2, +3, +4 to SEMA[0], SEMA[1], SEMA[2], SEMA[3] and compare each read with its
  value; write the negations and compare each read with 0.
. Write -1 to SEMA[0] and read it twice requiring the two reads equal; restore by writing +1 and
  compare the read with 0.
. Write 16383, 16383 and 1 to SEMA[0] and compare the read with `0x7FFF`; write 1 more and
  read twice requiring equal reads; restore; write -32768 and -1 and read twice requiring equal
  reads; restore and read twice requiring equal reads.
. Write `0x0001_0005` to SEMA[0], read twice requiring equal reads, restore by writing the
  negation of the read value and read twice requiring equal reads.
. Read SEMA[1] and require 0; issue eight +1 writes to SEMA[1] as one group item (overlap not measured); read and
  compare with 8; write -8 and compare the read with 0; print the bounded waits and require the
  seven steps and six checker lines in order with strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SEMA-SEQ` |SEMA[0] must read 5, 8 and 6 after +5, +3 and -2 and 0 after -6.
|`CHK-SEMA-INDEP` |SEMA[0..3] must read 1, 2, 3, 4 after +1, +2, +3, +4 and 0 after the negations.
|`CHK-SEMA-NEG` |Measures and prints SEMA[0] after -1 from 0; only the equality of two
  consecutive reads is required, the value is not compared; after the restore write of +1 SEMA[0]
  must read 0.
|`CHK-SEMA-WRAP` |SEMA[0] must read `0x7FFF` at the 16-bit maximum; the values after one more +1,
  after the restore and after -32768 and -1 are measured and printed; only the equality of two
  consecutive reads is required, those values are not compared.
|`CHK-SEMA-UPPER` |Measures and prints SEMA[0] after a write with bits above bit 15 set; only the
  equality of two consecutive reads is required, the value is not compared.
|`CHK-SEMA-PIPELINED` |Eight +1 writes issued as one group item to SEMA[1] (overlap not measured) must complete within the access bound
  and SEMA[1] must then read 8 and, after -8, 0.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the six
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access state; an access that never completes fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: the signed running
sum, four independent instances and the eight grouped writes and the 16-bit maximum compare exactly. The below-zero,
over-maximum and upper-bit results are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The SEMA value below 0, after the +1 past the 16-bit maximum, after the restore,
after -32768 and -1, and after a write with bits above bit 15 set is measured and printed and not
compared, because the register description does not define it; only the equality of two consecutive
reads is required. The overlap of the eight grouped writes to SEMA[1] is not measured.

'''''

[[sec-440-smc_cpu_ctrl_wb_pc_test]]
===== 440 `smc_cpu_ctrl_wb_pc_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_wb_pc_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 8-byte reads); bench probes
`tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done` and `tb_top.tb_cpu_wb_pc0` to `tb_top.tb_cpu_wb_pc3` (one per core);
CPU_CTRL WB_PC_CORE0..3, eight 64-bit entries each (32 words).

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: WB_PC_CORE0..3[0..7] read decode and idle values beside probes.

*Test Coverage*:

* All 32 WB_PC words (four cores of eight entries, `cpu_ctrl.rdl` WB_PC_CORE0..3 at `0x100`,
  `0x140`, `0x180`, `0x1C0`) answer OKAY at the generated addresses.
* The WB_PC value is a read-only writeback PC field `pc[57:0]` (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`); two reads of the
  idle cluster agree for every entry.
* The meaning and the idle value of each entry are measured and printed beside the per-core
  `tb_cpu_wb_pc` probe; the specification does not state the value; the probe is sampled and printed, not compared.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles); require the four
  `tb_cpu_wb_pc` probes to exist.
. Read every entry of WB_PC_CORE0..3 once (each must answer OKAY).
. Read each entry twice, sampling `tb_cpu_wb_pc<n>` after each read, and require the two reads of
  each entry to agree; print the values and probes; require the access count to match the steps,
  print the bounded waits and require the three steps and two checker lines in order with strictly
  increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WBPC-DECODE` |All 32 WB_PC words must answer OKAY at the generated addresses, none DECERR.
|`CHK-WBPC-IDLE` |Two reads of each of the 32 entries must agree; the idle value and its
  relation to `tb_cpu_wb_pc<n>` are measured and printed without comparing them.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The three steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the two
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: 32 words
answered OKAY and agreeing double reads. The idle WB_PC values and the probe values are
recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The meaning and the idle value of each WB_PC entry and its relation to the per-core
`tb_cpu_wb_pc` probe are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not
state the value; the probe is sampled and printed, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-441-smc_cpu_ctrl_wdt_regs_test]]
===== 441 `smc_cpu_ctrl_wdt_regs_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_wdt_regs_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes); bench
probe `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; CPU_CTRL WDT_TIMEOUT (`data` [31:0]), WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET
(`reset_cycle_count_0` to `reset_cycle_count_3`, bits [3:0]) and TEST_CTRL (`data` [31:0]).

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: WDT_TIMEOUT, WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET pulse bits and TEST_CTRL read-only.

*Test Coverage*:

* WDT_TIMEOUT resets to `0x4000` (16384 cycles) and is read-write over all 32 bits
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`; `smc-programming.adoc`).
* WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET bits [3:0] are single-pulse write-one fields (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`
  `singlepulse`): after a write the register reads 0; the immediate read-back is measured and
  printed (the specification does not state the value).
* TEST_CTRL is read-only (`cpu_ctrl.rdl` `sw=r`): writes leave the value read before; that value
  is measured and printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Read WDT_TIMEOUT and compare with its reset `0x4000`.
. Write each of `0x0000_FFFF`, `0xFFFF_0000`, `0xA5A5_5A5A` and `0xFFFF_FFFF` to WDT_TIMEOUT and
  compare each read-back with the pattern; write the reset value back and compare the read-back.
. Write each of the four WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET bits alone and then all four together; after each write
  read the register once immediately (printed) and once more, requiring the second read to be 0.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only TEST_CTRL register. Kind: writes of `0xFFFF_FFFF` and
  `0xAAAA_AAAA` to a read-only register. Expected response: after each write TEST_CTRL reads the
  word of the first read. Read TEST_CTRL before the writes; require the access count to match the
  steps; print the bounded waits and require the five steps and four checker lines in order with
  strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-RESET` |WDT_TIMEOUT must read its reset value `0x4000` before any write.
|`CHK-WDT-RW` |WDT_TIMEOUT must read back each of the four 32-bit patterns exactly and its reset
  value after the restore.
|`CHK-WDTRST-PULSE` |WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET must read 0 after each write of one bit and of all four
  bits; the immediate read-back is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-TESTCTRL-RO` |TEST_CTRL must read the same word after each write as before it; the first
  read value is measured and printed without comparing it to a constant.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The five steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the four
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: WDT_TIMEOUT reset
`0x4000` and exact storage, WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET reading 0 after each write, TEST_CTRL unchanged by
writes. The immediate pulse read-back and the TEST_CTRL value are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The immediate read-back of WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET after each write and the value TEST_CTRL
holds are measured and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state them.

'''''

[[sec-442-smc_ext_window_aperture_test]]
===== 442 `smc_ext_window_aperture_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_ext_window_aperture_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes, a
two-access group item, write strobes `0xF` and `0x3`); `env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs`
(the supplementary window address registered as expected DECERR); a per-`clk_smc_i` passive
sampler of `tb_top.tb_axil_external_arvalid`, `tb_axil_external_araddr`, `tb_axil_external_awvalid`,
`tb_axil_external_awaddr`, `tb_axil_external_active`, `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and the SEP_IN
handshakes `s_axi_arvalid`/`s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_awvalid`/`s_axi_awready`,
`s_axi_rvalid`/`s_axi_rready`/`s_axi_rlast`, `s_axi_bvalid`/`s_axi_bready`; bench probe
`tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; the adopter external AXI-Lite port window (supplementary region at
BASE + `0x40_4000`), the eFuse SHIM control window (BASE + `0x40_0000`) and the SMC `REGION_SIZE`
CSR.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: External window requests and REGION_SIZE aperture limit.

*Test Coverage*:

* A SEP_IN read of the supplementary window reaches the external port as exactly one AR request,
  and each of two writes (full and partial strobe) as exactly one AW request with the same
  address as the read's AR (`memmap.adoc` "AXI-Lite External Window": the supplementary region
  is passed through; `fabric.adoc`).
* An access at the eFuse SHIM control window never appears on the external port
  (`tb_axil_external_active` stays 0) and drives `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` (`memmap.adoc`: the
  SHIM request "never appears on the external port").
* With `REGION_SIZE` programmed to `0x40_0000` and then `0x20_0000` the window read and write
  answer DECERR with no external request; with the reset size `0x0100_0000` restored the read
  reaches the external port again (`memmap.adoc` apertures sized by `REGION_SIZE`; `fabric.adoc`).
* A window access outstanding together with a `REGION_SIZE` shrink completes with OKAY or DECERR, the
  `REGION_SIZE` write answers OKAY, and the next window read answers DECERR without reaching the external port.
* The external AR address encoding, the response and data of the reference terminator, and the
  write data and strobes (not exported) are measured and printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles); start the per-cycle sampler and
  register the window address with the AXI monitor; read `REGION_SIZE` and compare with its reset.
. Read the window; require exactly one external AR rising edge and no AW edge; print the AR
  address, response and data.
. Write the window with strobe `0xF` and then `0x3`; require exactly one external AW rising edge
  per write, no AR edge, and the AW address equal to the read's AR address.
. Read and write the eFuse SHIM control window; require `tb_axil_external_active` low for every
  cycle and `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` to rise at least once.
. Error injection. Point: the supplementary external window, with `REGION_SIZE` programmed to
  `0x40_0000` and then `0x20_0000`. Kind: a read and a write of the window beyond the reduced
  aperture, at each size. Expected response: DECERR on the read and the write with no external
  request. Write and read back each size before its accesses; restore `REGION_SIZE`, then read the
  window and require exactly one external AR edge at the earlier address.
. Error injection. Point: the supplementary external window, with a `REGION_SIZE` = `0x20_0000`
  shrink issued while a window access is outstanding. Kind: a window read, and in a second group a
  window write, each issued together with the `REGION_SIZE` shrink as one outstanding group,
  followed by a window read beyond the reduced aperture. Expected response: the grouped window
  access completes OKAY or DECERR, the `REGION_SIZE` write completes OKAY with at least one cycle of
  two SEP_IN accesses outstanding, and the following window read answers DECERR with no external
  request. Restore `REGION_SIZE` after each group.
. Print the bounded waits and require the ten fence terms in order with strictly increasing time
  stamps and the five checker lines in order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EXT-READ-REQ` |A window read must produce exactly one external AR rising edge and no AW edge
  and complete; the AR address, response and data are measured and printed without comparing them.
|`CHK-EXT-WRITE-REQ` |Each of the full-strobe and partial-strobe window writes must produce exactly
  one external AW rising edge with the AR address of the read leg; the write data and strobes
  are not exported.
|`CHK-EXT-SHIM-ISOLATION` |Accesses at the eFuse SHIM control window must leave
  `tb_axil_external_active` low on every cycle and raise `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` at least
  once; the response and data are measured and printed without comparing them.
|`CHK-EXT-REGION-DECERR` |At `REGION_SIZE` `0x40_0000` and `0x20_0000` the window read and write
  must answer DECERR with no external request, and at the restored reset size the read must drive
  exactly one external AR edge at the earlier address.
|`CHK-EXT-INFLIGHT` |A window read and a window write each outstanding with a `REGION_SIZE` shrink
  must complete OKAY or DECERR, with the `REGION_SIZE` write answering OKAY, and with at least one overlap cycle, and the next window read must
  answer DECERR with no external request; the grouped responses and handshake cycles are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ten fence terms must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the five
  checker lines must print in order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done, the SEP_IN access and group
  bounds) with the last access; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: one AR and one AW
edge per window access with matching address, no external activity at the SHIM or beyond the
reduced aperture, DECERR at both reduced sizes, an overlap of at least one cycle in each in-flight
group, DECERR after each group and `REGION_SIZE` back to `0x0100_0000`. The AR address encoding,
terminator response and data are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The external AR address encoding, the response and data of the reference terminator,
and the specific response code and the handshake cycles of the grouped in-flight accesses are
printed; the window access is held to OKAY or DECERR and the `REGION_SIZE` write to OKAY. The write
data and strobes are not exported to the external port.

'''''

[[sec-443-smc_flr_isolation_sources_test]]
===== 443 `smc_flr_isolation_sources_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_flr_isolation_sources_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes); reset
unit registers ISOLATE_REQ_REG, ISOLATE_REQ_PINEN_REG, ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG and
ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG (bit 3 used); bench probes `tb_top.tb_isolate_req_o` (bit 3),
`tb_top.tb_skip_mem_repair_o`, `tb_top.tb_rst_cool_from_flr` (must stay 1),
`tb_top.tb_flr_sync_ref` and `clk_smc_i`; bench drives `tb_top.tb_cfg_flr_pf_active` (the FLR
input) and the isolate-request pad pin through `tb_top.tb_gpio_ext_drive_value` and
`tb_top.tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` (the pad bit is the Isolate Request index of the integrator GPIO
pad table); `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Isolation sources, FLR latch set and clear, skip_mem_repair_o.

*Test Coverage*:

* `isolate_req_o[3]` is `ISOLATE_REQ_REG[3]` OR (`ISOLATE_REQ_PINEN_REG[3]` AND the synchronized
  isolate-request pin) OR (`ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG[3]` AND `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`); clearing one
  source does not cancel a request held by another (`clk_rst.adoc` "Isolation Controls").
* The synchronized FLR rising edge sets `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`; a write to that register clears the
  latch with write data ignored; an FLR edge in the same cycle takes priority (`clk_rst.adoc`
  "Function Level Reset and Isolation"). The flow does not assert the cool reset because the FLR
  counters stay at their reset value.
* `skip_mem_repair_o` is asserted by the synchronized isolation pin or the FLR-set
  `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` latch, not by a request through `ISOLATE_REQ_REG` (`cpu.adoc` "Memory
  Repair").
* Latencies in `clk_smc_i` rises are measured and printed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`; hold the FLR input low and the pin low; read ISOLATE_REQ_REG,
  ISOLATE_REQ_PINEN_REG, ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG and ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG expecting 0; require
  `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` and `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` 0 on 8 consecutive rises.
. Write ISOLATE_REQ_REG = bit 3 and wait for `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1 (bound 128 rises); write 0
  and wait for it to read 0.
. Drive the pin high; wait for `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` = 1; require `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` 0 on 32
  rises with PINEN[3] clear; set PINEN[3] and wait for `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1; drop the pin and
  wait for 0.
. Drive the pin high, wait for `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` = 1, set ISOLATE_REQ_REG[3] and wait for
  `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1; clear ISOLATE_REQ_REG and require it to stay 1 on 32 rises; drop the
  pin and wait for 0.
. Clear PINEN, set SMCEN[3]; require both outputs 0 on 8 rises; raise the FLR input; wait for
  `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` = 1 and `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1 and for `tb_flr_sync_ref` = 1; require
  both outputs to hold on 32 rises.
. Drop the FLR input, require both outputs to stay 1 until `tb_flr_sync_ref` falls; write `0xFFFF_FFFF` to
  ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG while sampling the outputs and measure the rises until each reads 0
  (`tb_skip_mem_repair_o` must fall no later than `tb_isolate_req_o[3]`); require
  `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` 0 on 32 rises; then sweep the FLR rise from 0 to 96 rises after the
  clearing write launch and stop two delays after the first one that leaves the latch set (or at
  96), requiring the two outputs equal on every trial, the latch cleared at delay 0, a delay that
  leaves the latch set to occur, the first such delay to equal the clear latency minus the set
  latency, and that delay and the sampled delays after it to leave it set; clear the latch.
. Write ISOLATE_REQ_REG = bit 3 with no FLR edge, wait for `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1 and require
  `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` = 1 and `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` = 0 on 64 consecutive rises; restore
  ISOLATE_REQ_REG and ISOLATE_REQ_SMCEN_REG to 0 and require the seven steps and six checker lines
  in order with strictly increasing time stamps.
. Throughout every wait and hold require `tb_rst_cool_from_flr` to stay 1; each wait is bounded by
  128 `clk_smc_i` rises and its expiry fails the run.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FLR-REG-SOURCE` |`tb_isolate_req_o[3]` must read 1 after ISOLATE_REQ_REG[3] is set and 0 after
  it is cleared, within 128 rises, with `tb_rst_cool_from_flr` staying 1.
|`CHK-FLR-PIN-SOURCE` |With the pin high and PINEN[3] clear `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` must read 0 on 32
  rises and it must read 1 after PINEN[3] is set; the rises for the pin to reach
  `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` are measured and printed.
|`CHK-FLR-SOURCE-OR` |With the pin active and ISOLATE_REQ_REG[3] cleared `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` must
  stay 1 on 32 rises and read 0 after the pin drops.
|`CHK-FLR-LATCH-SET` |Both outputs must read 0 before the FLR edge and, after it,
  `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` and `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` must read 1 and hold on 32 rises; the rise
  counts are measured and printed.
|`CHK-FLR-LATCH-CLEAR` |A write of 0 to ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG must clear both outputs, and in the
  sweep the latch must end cleared at delay 0 and a delay that leaves it set must occur; the first
  such delay must equal the clear latency minus the set latency and it and the two sampled
  delays after it must leave the latch set; the delays between 0 and it are recorded without
  comparison.
|`CHK-FLR-SW-NO-SKIP` |With only ISOLATE_REQ_REG[3] set `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` must read 1 and
  `tb_skip_mem_repair_o` must read 0 on 64 consecutive rises.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The seven steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the six
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: each source
raises `tb_isolate_req_o[3]` independently and the OR holds while any source is active, the FLR
edge sets the latch and a write clears it with the FLR-edge priority, the software request never
asserts `tb_skip_mem_repair_o`, and `tb_rst_cool_from_flr` never falls. The latencies are recorded
without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The latencies in `clk_smc_i` rises (pin to `tb_skip_mem_repair_o`, FLR edge to the
outputs, clearing write to each output falling) and the sweep delays between 0 and the first delay
that leaves the latch set are measured and printed and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-444-smc_plic_register_test]]
===== 444 `smc_plic_register_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_plic_register_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 4-byte reads and writes); bench
probes `tb_top.tb_plic_priority_low`, `tb_top.tb_plic_pending_low`, `tb_top.tb_plic_enables0_w0`,
`tb_top.tb_plic_threshold0`, `tb_top.tb_plic_claim0` (bit n of the vector probes is source n + 1)
and `tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; the SMC `REGION_SIZE` CSR widened to `0x1000_0000`; PLIC
PRIORITY[1, 2, 328, 329, 332, 333, 336], PENDING[0..10], ENABLE words 0 and 10 of contexts 0, 3,
4 and 7 (CORE0_MEIP, CORE3_MEIP, CORE0_SEIP, CORE3_SEIP), THRESHOLD of those four contexts and
CLAIM_COMPLETE of contexts 0 to 7.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: PLIC PRIORITY, PENDING, ENABLE, THRESHOLD and CLAIM register behaviour.

*Test Coverage*:

* PRIORITY[k] is a 3-bit read-write field (`plic.rdl`): every value 0 to 7 reads back for the
  probed sources, and `tb_plic_priority_low` bit (k - 1) follows PRIORITY[k] bit 0 for sources 1
  and 2.
* PENDING is read-only (`plic.rdl` `sw=r`): a write of all ones leaves PENDING[0] and PENDING[10]
  unchanged, and PENDING[0] shifted right by one equals `tb_plic_pending_low`.
* ENABLE words hold only the bits for source IDs 1 to 336 (`plic.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc` "PLIC
  Sources and Contexts"): distinct masked patterns across four contexts and two words read back
  without aliasing, and `tb_plic_enables0_w0` equals context 0 word 0 shifted right by one.
* THRESHOLD is a 3-bit read-write field with maximum value 7 (`plic.rdl`): each value reads back
  per context with the other contexts unchanged, and `tb_plic_threshold0` follows context 0.
* With no source pending every CLAIM_COMPLETE reads 0 and `tb_plic_claim0` is 0.
* The PLIC is reached only after `REGION_SIZE` is widened to `0x1000_0000` (`memmap.adoc`,
  `fabric.adoc`); `REGION_SIZE` and all touched registers are restored.
* The reset values of PRIORITY and THRESHOLD and the live pending content are measured and
  printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles).
. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x1000_0000` and read it back.
. For each probed source save PRIORITY[k]; write each value 0 to 7 and compare the read-back;
  for sources 1 and 2 require `tb_plic_priority_low` bit (k - 1) to equal bit 0 of the value;
  restore and compare.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only PENDING[0] and PENDING[10] registers. Kind: a write of all
  ones to each read-only register. Expected response: each register reads the value of its first
  read, unchanged by the write. Read PENDING[0] and PENDING[10] before the writes; require
  `tb_plic_pending_low` to equal PENDING[0] shifted right by one.
. Save ENABLE words 0 and 10 of contexts 0, 3, 4 and 7; require the eight patterns distinct; write
  all eight patterns (masked to source-ID bits), then read all eight back; require
  `tb_plic_enables0_w0` to equal context 0 word 0 shifted right by one; restore and compare.
. Save THRESHOLD of contexts 0, 3, 4 and 7; for each context write each value 0 to 7, compare the
  read-back, compare the other three contexts with their saved values and, for context 0, compare
  `tb_plic_threshold0`; restore and compare.
. Read PENDING[0..10] and require all 0 and `tb_plic_pending_low` 0; read CLAIM_COMPLETE of
  contexts 0 to 7 and require 0 for each and `tb_plic_claim0` 0.
. Restore `REGION_SIZE` and compare the read-back; print the bounded waits and require the eight
  steps and six checker lines in order with strictly increasing time stamps.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PLICREG-PRIORITY` |PRIORITY[k] must read back every value 0 to 7 for the seven probed
  sources, and `tb_plic_priority_low` bit (k - 1) must equal PRIORITY[k] bit 0 for sources 1 and 2;
  the saved reset values are measured and printed.
|`CHK-PLICREG-PENDING` |PENDING[0] and PENDING[10] must be unchanged by a write of all ones and
  `tb_plic_pending_low` must equal PENDING[0] shifted right by one; the content is measured and
  printed.
|`CHK-PLICREG-ENABLE` |The eight distinct masked ENABLE patterns must read back exactly and
  `tb_plic_enables0_w0` must equal context 0 word 0 shifted right by one.
|`CHK-PLICREG-THRESHOLD` |THRESHOLD of each of the four contexts must read back every value 0 to 7
  with the other three unchanged and `tb_plic_threshold0` must follow context 0; the saved reset
  values are measured and printed.
|`CHK-PLICREG-CLAIM` |With PENDING[0..10] all 0 and `tb_plic_pending_low` 0, CLAIM_COMPLETE of all
  eight contexts must read 0 and `tb_plic_claim0` must be 0 (the 0 reads cannot tell a reset value
  from a bench that initializes to zero under 2-state simulation).
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eight steps must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the six
  checker lines must print in step order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done and the SEP_IN access bound)
  with the last access; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: exact read-back of
PRIORITY, ENABLE and THRESHOLD, PENDING read-only, the probes agreeing with the registers, CLAIM
reading 0 with nothing pending, and `REGION_SIZE` back to `0x0100_0000`. The reset values of
PRIORITY and THRESHOLD and the pending content are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The reset values of PRIORITY and THRESHOLD and the live pending content are measured
and printed and not compared, because the specification does not state them. The CLAIM_COMPLETE 0
reads cannot tell a reset value from a bench that initializes to zero under 2-state simulation.

'''''

[[sec-445-smc_spm_aperture_region_size_test]]
===== 445 `smc_spm_aperture_region_size_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: CPU

*Source Module*: `smc_spm_aperture_region_size_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN (`env.sys_axi_agent`; 8-byte window accesses, 4-byte
REGION_SIZE and GLOBAL_BASE accesses, a two-access group item);
`env.axi_monitor.expected_decerr_addrs` (the window address registered as expected DECERR); a
passive per-`clk_smc_i` sampler of the
SEP_IN handshakes `s_axi_arvalid`/`s_axi_arready`/`s_axi_araddr`,
`s_axi_awvalid`/`s_axi_awready`/`s_axi_awaddr`, `s_axi_rvalid`/`s_axi_rready` and
`s_axi_bvalid`/`s_axi_bready`; the scoreboard exact-value compare count; bench probe
`tb_top.tb_fuse_sense_done`; the SMC `REGION_SIZE` and GLOBAL_BASE CSRs; one scratchpad word,
the last 64-bit word of the scratchpad window at offset `0x15_FFF8` from LOCAL_BASE, addressed
through both the local alias (`0xC000_0000` base) and the global aperture (`0x4000_0000` base).

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SPM window alias and REGION_SIZE reach and limit over SEP_IN.

*Test Coverage*:

* The local alias and the global aperture reach the same scratchpad word: a write through one
  reads back identically through the other, both OKAY (`fabric.adoc`: a request for the global
  window reaches the same register as one for the local window; `memmap.adoc`).
* The word is reachable at `REGION_SIZE` = `0x0100_0000` (reset, `fabric.adoc`) and at `0x20_0000`,
  and unreachable at `0x10_0000`, where the window lies beyond the aperture and reads and writes
  answer DECERR (`memmap.adoc`: a unit is reached only while its whole aperture lies below
  `BASE + REGION_SIZE`; an address outside the window answers DECERR); the refused write stores
  nothing.
* Two `REGION_SIZE` writes with no access between them: the second governs the next access, in
  both orders.
* A window access outstanding together with a `REGION_SIZE` write completes with OKAY or DECERR,
  the `REGION_SIZE` write answers OKAY and is accepted while the access is outstanding, and the next access
  answers DECERR.
* The DECERR read data is measured and printed (the specification does not state the value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bound 200000 `clk_smc_i` cycles); register the window address
  with the AXI monitor; read `REGION_SIZE` and compare with `0x0100_0000`; read GLOBAL_BASE and
  compare with `0x4000_0000`.
. Write `0x1111_2222_3333_4444` at the local window address and read the global address
  expecting the same; write `0x5555_6666_7777_8888` at the global address and read the local
  address expecting the same.
. Read the window at the reset size; write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x20_0000`, read it back, read the
  window expecting the same word; restore `REGION_SIZE` to its reset and compare the read-back.
. Error injection. Point: the scratchpad window word, registered as expected DECERR with the AXI
  monitor, with `REGION_SIZE` written to `0x10_0000`. Kind: a read of the window and a write of
  `0x9999_AAAA_BBBB_CCCC` to it while the window lies beyond the aperture. Expected response: both
  answer DECERR, the refused write stores nothing, and after the restore the window reads the word
  held before the refused write; the DECERR read data is printed. Restore `REGION_SIZE` after the
  two accesses; then write `0xDDDD_EEEE_FFFF_0123` and read it back.
. Write `REGION_SIZE` = `0x10_0000` then `0x0100_0000` with no access between and read the window
  expecting the word; write `0x0100_0000` then `0x10_0000` with no access between and read the
  window requiring DECERR; restore.
. Error injection. Point: the scratchpad window word, with a `REGION_SIZE` = `0x10_0000` write
  issued while a window access is outstanding. Kind: a window read, and in a second group a window
  write of `0x0F0F_1E1E_2D2D_3C3C`, each issued together with the `REGION_SIZE` write as one
  outstanding group, followed by a window read beyond the aperture. Expected response: the grouped
  window access answers OKAY or DECERR and the `REGION_SIZE` write answers OKAY, the window request
  cycle is no later than the `REGION_SIZE` AW cycle and that AW precedes the first R beat (the
  first B beat for the write group), and the following window read answers DECERR. Restore
  `REGION_SIZE` after each group.
. Require the scoreboard to have booked at least as many exact-value compares as the sequence
  issued; print the bounded waits and require the eleven fence terms in order with strictly
  increasing time stamps and the five checker lines each after its own step.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SPM-ALIAS` |A word written through the local alias must read identically through the global
  aperture, and the reverse, both OKAY.
|`CHK-SPM-REGION-REACH` |The window word must read OKAY with its written value at `REGION_SIZE`
  `0x0100_0000` and at `0x20_0000`.
|`CHK-SPM-REGION-DECERR` |At `REGION_SIZE` `0x10_0000` the window read and write must answer DECERR,
  the refused write must store nothing, and after the restore a fresh write must read back; the
  DECERR read data is measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-SPM-REGION-B2B` |After `0x10_0000` then `0x0100_0000` the next window read must be OKAY with
  the word, and after `0x0100_0000` then `0x10_0000` it must answer DECERR; the DECERR read data is
  measured and printed without comparing it.
|`CHK-SPM-REGION-INFLIGHT` |A window read and a window write each outstanding with a `REGION_SIZE`
  write must complete with the window access OKAY or DECERR, the `REGION_SIZE` write OKAY, and the window request no later than the `REGION_SIZE`
  AW and that AW before the first response beat, and the following window read must answer
  DECERR; the cycles and DECERR read data are printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The eleven fence terms must stamp in order with strictly increasing time and the
  five checker lines must print in order, so a truncated run fails.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits taken (fuse sense done, the SEP_IN access and group
  member bounds) with the last observed state; an access that exceeds its bound fails the run.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker above is emitted and the sequence asserts hold: alias reads exact,
reach exact at both sizes, DECERR at `0x10_0000` with no stored write, the second of two
`REGION_SIZE` writes governing the next access, the in-flight overlap order observed with DECERR
after each group, and `REGION_SIZE` back to `0x0100_0000`. The DECERR read data and the
in-flight window response are recorded without comparison.

*Scope limit*: The DECERR read data and the response (OKAY or DECERR) of the window access that is
outstanding with a `REGION_SIZE` write are measured and printed and not compared, because the
specification does not state them.

'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-jtag]]
==== JTAG

[[sec-083-smc_dbs_idle_test]]
===== 83 `smc_dbs_idle_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dbs_idle_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run the DBS/DFD/ECC diagnostic CSR precheck.

*Test Coverage*:

* Alias of the DBS/DFD/ECC diagnostic precheck; drives `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dbs_idle_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DIAG-AXIL-ACTIVE` |Named compare in `smc_diagnostic_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-AXIL-IDLE` |Named compare in `smc_diagnostic_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-CSR-COUNT` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-CSR-DFX_DEBUG_BUS_MUX` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-CSR-DFX_DEBUG_CTRL` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-CSR-NDMRESET_PROCESS` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-DIAG-NDMRESET-CLUSTER-COUNT-BOUNDS` |Bounds check in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`: the count is nonzero, inside the generated 8-bit field with reserved bits 0, and at most the 32 `ndmreset_request` bits the RDL has it mask; the run fails outside those bounds. The count itself is reported, not compared. The programmer's guide states this harness reads 4
|`CHK-DIAG-NDMRESET-CLUSTER-COUNT-RO` |Named compare in `smc_ecc_dfd_dbs_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-BANK-AXIL-ACTIVE` |Positive control in `smc_efuse_vip_utils.py`, reached through `prove_axil_any_master_activity`: `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` samples 1 while a strict SEP_IN read of the eFuse-shim window (expected its generated reset) is in flight; the run fails if the probe never rises
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DIAG-AXIL-ACTIVE`, `CHK-DIAG-AXIL-IDLE`, `CHK-DIAG-CSR-COUNT`, `CHK-DIAG-CSR-DFX_DEBUG_BUS_MUX`, `CHK-DIAG-CSR-DFX_DEBUG_CTRL`, `CHK-DIAG-CSR-NDMRESET_PROCESS` (and 3 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The `ndmreset` cluster count is held to its bounds only; the count itself is reported, not compared.
'''''

[[sec-084-smc_dfd_sanity_test]]
===== 84 `smc_dfd_sanity_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfd_sanity_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run diagnostic CSR reads as the public DFD bounded checker.

*Test Coverage*:

* SMC OSS DFD sanity bounded diagnostic test.

*Test Procedure*:

The count itself is reported, not compared. The programmer's guide states this harness reads 4
