  drives; log the two bounded waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound).
. Require the step terms in order with increasing simulation times and the checker lines in order,
  then print the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DST-RW-PATTERNS` |Every plain read-write DST field other than `Trdstformat` reads back
the all-ones and the all-zeros value written to it alone; any other value fails it, and
`Trdstformat` and the fields the hardware drives are printed
|`CHK-DST-FIELD-ISOLATION` |Writing one field to the complement of its baseline leaves every other
non-hardware-driven field of the DST block unchanged; any other bit that moves fails it
|`CHK-DST-UNDEFINED-BITS` |Writes and reads of the bit positions no DST field covers complete
inside the bound; it prints the stored value of each position and compares none
|`CHK-DST-INST-FIELDS-RW` |Writes and reads of `Trdstinsttracing` and `Trdstinsttriggerenable`
with the trace inactive and active complete; it prints the read values and compares none
|`CHK-SCRATCH-PATTERNS` |Each of the six scratch registers reads back exactly every one of the 36
patterns written; any other value fails it
|`CHK-SCRATCH-NO-ALIAS` |Six distinct values written before any read each read back from their own
register; a register returning another register's value fails it
|`CHK-APERTURE-OFFSET-ISOLATION` |Three values written to the same offset of `dst_sink`, `funnel`
and `dst` read back each from its own block while the other two keep theirs; a block returning
another block's value fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The step terms appear in order with increasing simulation times and every checker
line follows its step; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The two waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound) are bounded and raise
with the last observed signal or register on expiry
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DST-RW-PATTERNS`, `CHK-DST-FIELD-ISOLATION`, `CHK-SCRATCH-PATTERNS`,
`CHK-SCRATCH-NO-ALIAS` and `CHK-APERTURE-OFFSET-ISOLATION` hold after their compares;
`CHK-DST-UNDEFINED-BITS` and `CHK-DST-INST-FIELDS-RW` hold once their accesses completed, their
values printed (the specification does not state the values); `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every
sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `Trdstformat`, whose supported value set the specification does not state, and the
fields the hardware also writes (`Trdstinsttracing`) are printed, not compared. The bit positions no
DST field covers are written with ones and zeros and their stored values printed, with no value
compared, because `dfd_dst.rdl` declares no field there. The reads of `Trdstinsttracing` and
`Trdstinsttriggerenable` with the trace inactive and active, and whether hardware changed
`Trdstinsttracing`, are printed without a compare.

'''''

[[sec-447-smc_dfx_aperture_extent_test]]
===== 447 `smc_dfx_aperture_extent_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfx_aperture_extent_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN, reads and writes of the `dfx_ctrl` block at
`STATUS_SMU` (0xC000_B800, 8 bytes), `DEBUG_CTRL` (0xC000_B808) and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` (0xC000_B810,
8 bytes), past the register extent at 0xC000_B818, 0xC000_B900 and 0xC000_BFFC, at the first
address after the 0x800 aperture (0xC000_C000) and at offset 0xC (0xC000_B80C); the AXI
response code and read data seen by the SEP_IN scoreboard; bench signals `tb_fuse_sense_done` and
`clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `dfx`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `dfx_ctrl` addresses, DECERR past the extent and the gap at 0xC.

*Test Coverage*:

* `STATUS_SMU`, `DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` answer OKAY at the addresses of the
  `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl` address map placed by `smc.rdl` at 0xC000_B800 (`memory_map.adoc`, DFX
  Control and Status Address Map). `STATUS_SMU` reads the idle word and the other two read 0. The
  idle word is a property of this bench: the bench drives the memory repair done and success and
  the MBIST done and pass inputs high, which sets bits 0, 1, 4 and 8 of `STATUS`, and no abort
  bit is set. `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl` gives the bit positions, a reset value of 0 and sticky
  semantics, and no idle word. The expected word is built from the four done and pass bit masks
  of the RDL, with both abort pins required to read 0.
* `DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` each read back a distinct non-zero word written to them
  (0x2A5A_5A5A with bit 31 clear, and 0x0123_4567_89AB_CDEF), then read 0 again after 0 is
  written, so a register that is not decoded at its address fails.
* Reads past the three registers, inside the 0x800 aperture that `smc.rdl` gives the block, answer
  DECERR with the word 0xBADCAB1E that `smc.rdl` names as the past-extent read data; the
  response and the word are taken from the generated map row of `dfx_ctrl`
  (`memory_map.adoc`, Past Extent: DECERR, 0xBADCAB1E).
* Writes past the register extent answer DECERR and leave the three registers as they were.
* The first address after the aperture, 0xC000_C000, lies between the `dfx_ctrl` aperture and
  `smc_base_config` at BASE + 0x1_0000, so it reaches no unit; `memmap.adoc` states that a read
  or write between unit apertures answers DECERR, and a read returns 0xBADCAB1E.
* The offset 0xC between `DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX`, inside the register extent, holds no
  register; `memory_map.adoc` (Hole in Extent) documents OKAY with data 0x0 for it. The leaf
  compares the response and data with the generated Hole in Extent answer.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, bounded to 200000 cycles; stamp step 1.
. Read `STATUS_SMU` (8 bytes, expected the idle word), `DEBUG_CTRL` (expected 0) and
  `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` (8 bytes, expected 0), and require the idle word, 0 and 0. Write 0x2A5A5A5A to
  `DEBUG_CTRL` and 0x0123456789ABCDEF to `DEBUG_BUS_MUX`, require each to read back exactly, then
  write 0 to each and require 0 on reading it back.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN AXI read address, at 0xC000_B818, 0xC000_B900 and
  0xC000_BFFC, past the `dfx_ctrl` register extent. Kind: past-extent reads. Expected response:
  each answers the generated past-extent response (DECERR) and returns the generated past-extent
  word 0xBADCAB1E.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN AXI write address, at 0xC000_B818 and 0xC000_BFFC, past the
  `dfx_ctrl` register extent. Kind: all-ones past-extent writes. Expected response: each answers
  the generated past-extent write response (DECERR). Read the three registers again and require
  them equal to their step 2 values.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN AXI read address, at 0xC000_C000, the first address after
  the `dfx_ctrl` aperture, which lies between unit apertures and reaches no unit. Kind: read of
  an address between unit apertures. Expected response: DECERR carrying 0xBADCAB1E.
. Read 0xC000_B80C and require OKAY with data 0x0.
. Wait one rising edge of `clk_smc_i`, log the two bounded waits (the SEP_IN access bound and
  fuse sense), then require the step stamps in order and increasing and print the ordered-fence
  line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-APERTURE-REGISTERS` |`STATUS_SMU` reads the idle word, `DEBUG_CTRL` reads 0 and
`DEBUG_BUS_MUX` reads 0, all OKAY, at their generated addresses, and `DEBUG_CTRL` and
`DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read back a distinct non-zero word written to them; any other word or a
non-OKAY response fails it
|`CHK-APERTURE-PAST-READ` |Reads at 0xC000_B818, 0xC000_B900 and 0xC000_BFFC answer DECERR
carrying 0xBADCAB1E; any other response or data fails it
|`CHK-APERTURE-PAST-WRITE` |Writes at 0xC000_B818 and 0xC000_BFFC answer DECERR and `STATUS_SMU`,
`DEBUG_CTRL` and `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read the values they held before; an OKAY response or a changed
register fails it
|`CHK-APERTURE-NEXT-BLOCK` |The read at 0xC000_C000 answers DECERR carrying 0xBADCAB1E; any other
response or data fails it
|`CHK-APERTURE-HOLE` |The read at offset 0xC compares OKAY, 0x0; any other response or data
fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The two waits (the SEP_IN access bound and fuse sense) are bounded and fail
on expiry with the last observed response or signal
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-APERTURE-REGISTERS`, `CHK-APERTURE-PAST-READ`, `CHK-APERTURE-PAST-WRITE` and
`CHK-APERTURE-NEXT-BLOCK` hold after their compares; `CHK-APERTURE-HOLE` holds once its read
compares OKAY, 0x0 (`memory_map.adoc`); `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-448-smc_dfx_debug_bus_mux_storage_test]]
===== 448 `smc_dfx_debug_bus_mux_storage_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfx_debug_bus_mux_storage_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN, 8-byte writes and reads of `DEBUG_BUS_MUX`
(`dfx_ctrl` at 0xC000_B810; fields `Dbmmode` 1:0, `Dbmid` 7:2, `Rsvd158` 15:8 and `Muxselseg0` to
`Muxselseg7` at 21:16, 27:22, 33:28, 39:34, 45:40, 51:46, 57:52 and 63:58); bench signal
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Every `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` field stored and read back exactly.

*Test Coverage*:

* `Dbmmode` takes each of 0 (off), 1 (normal debug), 2 (identifier output) and 3 (toggle) with
  every other field 0, per the `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` description in `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`.
* `Dbmid` takes the identifiers 3, 6, 7 and 14 of the twelve debug-bus muxes (level-2 muxes 3 to
  6, level-3 muxes 7 to 14, `dfd.adoc` and `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`) and reads them back; 0 and 63,
  which address no mux, are written and read back exactly, as `Dbmid` is a plain read-write
  field.
* `Muxselseg0` to `Muxselseg3`, the lane selects the RDL describes, take the six-bit patterns 0, 1,
  2, 3, 4, 5, 42 and 63; `Muxselseg4` to `Muxselseg7`, which the RDL says have no effect in the
  SMC, store 63. `Rsvd158`, a plain read-write field, is written with 63 and reads back exactly.
* A one walked through each of the 64 bits, `Rsvd158` included, reads back as exactly that bit.
* Each of the mux identifiers 3 to 14 is programmed in turn in normal mode with its own
  `Muxselseg0` to `Muxselseg3` patterns and reads back exactly.
* Two writes with no read between show the second value in both orders, and the register is
  restored to 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, bounded to 200000 cycles; stamp step 1.
. Write `Dbmmode` 0, 1, 2 and 3 alone, each time reading the register and comparing all 64 bits.
. Write `Dbmid` 3, 6, 7, 14, 0 and 63 alone and compare the full register.
. For each of `Muxselseg0` to `Muxselseg3` write the patterns 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 42 and 63 alone and
  compare the full register (32 cells).
. Write 63 alone to each of `Muxselseg4` to `Muxselseg7` and compare the full register; write 63
  alone to `Rsvd158` and compare the full register.
. Write a one at each of the 64 bit positions and compare the full register.
. For `Dbmid` 3 to 14 write normal mode, the identifier and the four lane-select patterns
  ((identifier x 5 + lane x 11 + 1) masked to six bits) and compare the full register.
. Write pattern A (mode 1, `Dbmid` 5, `Muxselseg0` 42, `Muxselseg3` 21) then pattern B (mode 2,
  `Dbmid` 9, `Muxselseg1` 21, `Muxselseg2` 42) and read B; write B then A and read A; write 0 and
  compare 0.
. Log the two bounded waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound), then require the step stamps
  in order and increasing and the checker lines in order, and print the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-MODE` |`Dbmmode` reads back 0, 1, 2 and 3 with every other field 0; any other value
or a changed field fails it
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-ID` |`Dbmid` reads back 3, 6, 7, 14, 0 and 63 exactly with every other field 0; any
other word fails it
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-SEL03` |`Muxselseg0` to `Muxselseg3` each read back all eight patterns exactly with
every other field 0; a differing pattern or a neighbouring field that moves fails it
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-SEL47` |`Muxselseg4` to `Muxselseg7` each hold the 63 written with no other field
changing, and `Rsvd158` reads back the 63 written to it exactly with every other field 0
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-WALK1` |A one at each of the 64 bit positions, `Rsvd158` included, reads back as
exactly that bit; any other word fails it
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-ONEATATIME` |Each `Dbmid` from 3 to 14 reads back exactly with its own mode and
`Muxselseg0` to `Muxselseg3` patterns; any differing word fails it
|`CHK-DFX-MUX-B2B` |After two back-to-back writes the second value reads back in both orders, and
the register restored to 0 reads 0; the first value or a mix fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The two waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound) are bounded and fail
on expiry with the last observed access
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DFX-MUX-MODE`, `CHK-DFX-MUX-ID`, `CHK-DFX-MUX-SEL03`, `CHK-DFX-MUX-SEL47`,
`CHK-DFX-MUX-WALK1`, `CHK-DFX-MUX-ONEATATIME` and `CHK-DFX-MUX-B2B` hold after their compares, including the
`Dbmid` readbacks of 0 and 63 and the `Rsvd158` readbacks; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-449-smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_noeffect_gate_test]]
===== 449 `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_noeffect_gate_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_noeffect_gate_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN, 4-byte accesses to `DEBUG_CTRL` (`dfx_ctrl` at
0xC000_B808), an 8-byte `STATUS_SMU` read (0xC000_B800) and an 8-byte `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read
(0xC000_B810) issued with a `DEBUG_CTRL` write as one outstanding group; SMC reset agent driving
`rst_cold_ni` (cold reset, observed on the powergood, cold, primary and fuse-sense signals);
bench probes `tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; SEP_IN
handshake signals `s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_awvalid`, `s_axi_awready`,
`s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_rlast`, `s_axi_bvalid` and `s_axi_bready`; bench signal
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `dfx`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `DEBUG_CTRL` no-effect fields, bit 31 and `cg_en` access.

*Test Coverage*:

* `chiplet_enable`, `gpio_en`, `dtb_ns_en`, `dtb_ew_en`, `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` bits 15:1 (register
  bits 22:8) and `debug_marker` hold the written value alone and together, as the
  `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl` descriptions and `dfd.adoc` say these fields have no effect in the SMC.
* With every no-effect field set, `cg_en`, `force_clk_en` and bit 0 of `xtrig_clk_halt_mask`
  (register bit 7), the fields with an effect, read 0.
* After a cold reset `DEBUG_CTRL` reads 0, and after a write of all ones register bit 31, which
  no `DEBUG_CTRL` field covers in `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`, reads 0 because no field stores it. The
  documents state no value for that bit, and the leaf requires 0; the `DEBUG_CTRL` storage leaf
  (card 429) writes the same bit and only prints the readback.
* With every no-effect field set, `tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` stay 0 for
  256 `clk_smc_i` cycles. This leg is measured: the CLA is not programmed in the leaf, so the
  probes are not shown to rise, and the cross-trigger output lanes are not exported to the
  bench, so the leaf cannot observe them.
* A `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read and a `DEBUG_CTRL` write of `cg_en` issued together overlap on the SEP_IN
  channels and both answer OKAY, as both registers lie inside the decoded extent of `dfx_ctrl`.
  Any effect of `cg_en` on the DFD
  clock cannot be observed on this bench (`dfd.adoc`, Design-for-Debug).
* With `cg_en` set and `force_clk_en` clear, `STATUS_SMU` still reads the idle word (bits 0, 1, 4
  and 8, set because the bench drives the done and pass inputs high;
  `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl` gives only the bit positions and a reset value of 0) and
  `DEBUG_CTRL` still stores a write (`memmap.adoc`, Base Config and DFX Status).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, read `DEBUG_CTRL` and require 0, and print the two probes as the
  baseline.
. Write each no-effect field alone (`chiplet_enable` 3, `gpio_en`, `dtb_ns_en`, `dtb_ew_en`,
  `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` bits 15:1, `debug_marker` 0xA5) and then all together, reading `DEBUG_CTRL`
  back after each and comparing it exactly.
. Read `DEBUG_CTRL` with every no-effect field set, require it equal to the written word and
  require `cg_en`, `force_clk_en` and `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` bit 0 to read 0.
. Drive `rst_cold_ni` low, wait (bounded) for the powergood, cold and primary levels to show the
  assertion and require `tb_fuse_sense_done` to read 0; release `rst_cold_ni`, wait (bounded) for
  all resets to release and the fuse sense to finish; read `DEBUG_CTRL` and require 0; write
  0xFFFFFFFF, read it back and require bit 31 to read 0; write 0 and compare.
. Write every no-effect field again, sample `tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` on
  256 consecutive rising edges of `clk_smc_i` and require both to stay 0.
. Write 0, then issue the `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` 8-byte read and the `DEBUG_CTRL` `cg_en` write as one
  group while watching the SEP_IN read and write handshakes; require OKAY for each and a
  positive number of cycles with both admitted and neither answered; write `cg_en` back to 0
  and compare.
. Write `cg_en`, read `STATUS_SMU` and require the idle word, write `cg_en` with `debug_marker`
  0xA5 and compare the readback, then write 0 and compare.
. Log the bounded waits, wait one rising edge of `clk_smc_i`, require the steps in order with
  increasing stamps and the checker lines in order, and print the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DEBUGCTRL-FIELD-HOLD` |Each no-effect field alone and all together read back the written
value exactly with every other field 0; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DEBUGCTRL-EFFECT-CLEAR` |With every no-effect field set, `DEBUG_CTRL` reads the written word
and `cg_en`, `force_clk_en` and `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` bit 0 read 0; any of them reading 1 fails it
|`CHK-DEBUGCTRL-RESET-BIT31` |`DEBUG_CTRL` reads 0 after the cold reset and register bit 31 reads
0 after 0xFFFFFFFF is written; a non-zero reset read or bit 31 reading 1 fails it
|`CHK-DEBUGCTRL-NO-OBSERVABLE` |`tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` stay 0 for 256
`clk_smc_i` cycles with every no-effect field set; either probe rising fails it. The leg is
measured: no positive control shows that either probe can rise
|`CHK-CLKGATE-INFLIGHT` |The `DEBUG_BUS_MUX` read and the `cg_en` write both answer OKAY, with
the two overlapping on the SEP_IN channels; any other response or no overlap fails it
|`CHK-CLKGATE-STATUS-ACCESS` |With `cg_en` set and `force_clk_en` clear `STATUS_SMU` reads the
idle word and `DEBUG_CTRL` reads back the word written; a different word fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every wait (fuse sense, the cold reset assert and release, the 256-cycle
probe window, the in-flight group and the SEP_IN access bound) has a finite bound and fails on
expiry with the last observed state
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DEBUGCTRL-FIELD-HOLD`, `CHK-DEBUGCTRL-EFFECT-CLEAR`,
`CHK-DEBUGCTRL-RESET-BIT31`, `CHK-DEBUGCTRL-NO-OBSERVABLE`, `CHK-CLKGATE-INFLIGHT` and
`CHK-CLKGATE-STATUS-ACCESS` hold after their compares, `CHK-DEBUGCTRL-NO-OBSERVABLE` being a
measured leg; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The probe leg is measured: the CLA is not programmed in the leaf, so
`tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` are not shown to rise, and the cross-trigger
output lanes are not exported to the bench, so the leaf cannot observe them. Any effect of `cg_en`
on the DFD clock cannot be observed on this bench; only the register accesses around it are checked.
The documents state no value for register bit 31; the leaf requires 0.

'''''

[[sec-450-smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_storage_test]]
===== 450 `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_storage_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_storage_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN, 4-byte and 8-byte writes and reads of `DEBUG_CTRL`
(`dfx_ctrl` at 0xC000_B808; fields `chiplet_enable` 1:0, `gpio_en` 2, `cg_en` 3, `force_clk_en` 4,
`dtb_ns_en` 5, `dtb_ew_en` 6, `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` 22:7, `debug_marker` 30:23, bit 31 not in
any field); bench signal `tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/cpu.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Every `DEBUG_CTRL` field stored and read back exactly.

*Test Coverage*:

* `chiplet_enable`, `gpio_en`, `dtb_ns_en`, `dtb_ew_en` and `debug_marker`, the fields whose
  `dfx_ctrl_status.rdl` description says they hold the written value for software to read back,
  take all ones and alternating patterns with every other field 0.
* `cg_en` and `force_clk_en`, the DFD clock stop and force bits, are written alone and together
  and restored to 0 at once; only their storage is checked, not any clock effect.
* `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` takes all ones and a one at each of its 16 bit positions 7 to 22; the
  RDL says only its bit 0 has an effect and the others hold the written value.
* A one at each of register bits 0 to 30 reads back as exactly that bit.
* Register bit 31 is covered by no field: a 4-byte write of it and an 8-byte write with the upper
  half set are read back and printed, not compared; the documents state no value for it (the
  `DEBUG_CTRL` no-effect leaf, card 428, requires bit 31 to read 0 after an all-ones write).
* Of two back-to-back writes the second reads back, in both orders.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, bounded to 200000 cycles; stamp step 1.
. For `chiplet_enable` (3, 2, 1), `gpio_en` (1, 0), `dtb_ns_en` (1, 0), `dtb_ew_en` (1, 0) and
  `debug_marker` (0xFF, 0xAA, 0x55) write the pattern alone and compare the full register
  (12 cells).
. Write `cg_en`, then `force_clk_en`, then both, each followed by a write of 0; compare the
  register after every write.
. Write `xtrig_clk_halt_mask` all ones and then a one at each of its 16 positions, comparing the
  register after each write.
. Write a one at each of bits 0 to 30 and compare the register with that single bit (31 cells).
. Write bit 31 with a 4-byte access and read; write 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 with an 8-byte access and
  read the 8-byte slot; print both words.
. Write all ones in bits 0 to 30 then 0 with no read between and require 0; write 0 then all ones in
  bits 0 to 30 with no read between and require the all-ones word.
. Write 0 and compare 0, log the bounded waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound), require
  the step stamps in order and increasing and the checker lines in order, and print the
  ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-FIELDS` |`chiplet_enable`, `gpio_en`, `dtb_ns_en`, `dtb_ew_en` and `debug_marker`
each read back every pattern written with every other bit 0; a differing word fails it
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-CLK-BITS` |`cg_en`, `force_clk_en` and both read back exactly and each restore to 0
reads 0; the DFD clock effect is not checked
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-XTRIG` |`xtrig_clk_halt_mask` reads back all ones and each of its 16 walking-one
positions exactly; a differing word fails it
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-WALK1` |A one at each of bits 0 to 30 reads back as exactly that bit; any other bit
set or the written bit clear fails it
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-BIT31` |The 4-byte write of bit 31 and the 8-byte write with the upper half set
complete and the readbacks are printed; no value is compared
|`CHK-DFX-CTRL-B2B` |Of two writes with no read between, the second value reads back: 0 after all
ones then 0, and all ones in bits 0 to 30 after 0 then all ones; the first value or a mix fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The two waits (fuse sense and the SEP_IN access bound) are bounded and fail
on expiry with the last observed access
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DFX-CTRL-FIELDS`, `CHK-DFX-CTRL-CLK-BITS`, `CHK-DFX-CTRL-XTRIG`,
`CHK-DFX-CTRL-WALK1` and `CHK-DFX-CTRL-B2B` hold after their compares; `CHK-DFX-CTRL-BIT31` holds
once its accesses completed, the readbacks printed (the specification does not state the values); `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Register bit 31 is covered by no field and the documents state no value for it, so
the 4-byte write of it and the 8-byte write with the upper half set are read back and printed, not
compared. Only the storage of `cg_en` and `force_clk_en` is checked, not any clock effect.

'''''

[[sec-451-smc_dfx_status_smu_pulse_reset_test]]
===== 451 `smc_dfx_status_smu_pulse_reset_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_dfx_status_smu_pulse_reset_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN, 8-byte reads and writes of `STATUS_SMU` (`dfx_ctrl` at
0xC000_B800; `mem_repair_abort` bit 2, `mbist_abort` bit 12; the idle word is bits 0, 1, 4 and 8,
set because the bench drives the done and pass inputs high), writes with
byte strobes 0x01 and 0x10, 4-byte accesses to `SS_WARM_RESET_N` (`smc_reset_unit`) bit 0; bench
abort inputs `tb_mem_repair_abort` and `tb_mbist_abort`; SMC reset agent driving `rst_cold_ni` and
`rst_cool_ni` and observing the powergood, cold and primary reset levels; SEP_IN read channel
signals `s_axi_arvalid`, `s_axi_arready` and `s_axi_rvalid`; bench signals `clk_smc_i` and
`tb_fuse_sense_done`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `dfx`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `STATUS_SMU` abort bits alone, pulsed and through resets.

*Test Coverage*:

* On the clean status an 8-byte write of all ones leaves `STATUS_SMU` at the idle word; the
  `STATUS` bits are read-only to software (`dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`, `sw = r`). The RDL gives the
  bit positions, a reset value of 0 and sticky semantics; the idle word itself comes from the
  bench driving the done and pass inputs high.
* The bench holds those four inputs high and cannot drive done, success and pass individually, so
  only the two abort bits are exercised alone and in sequence.
* `tb_mbist_abort` alone sets `mbist_abort` (bit 12) and no other abort bit; adding
  `tb_mem_repair_abort` sets `mem_repair_abort` (bit 2) too, each within four reads of the
  register, the bits sticky as the `STATUS` descriptions say.
* With both aborts set and both pins back at 0, bits 3, 5 to 7, 9 to 11 and 13 to 63, which no
  `STATUS` field covers, read 0.
* A write of zero and writes of all ones with byte strobes 0x01 and 0x10 leave the word at the idle
  bits plus bits 12 and 2; the AXI write responses are printed, not compared, as the documents
  state no response for a write to the read-only register.
* A one-`clk_smc_i` pulse on `tb_mem_repair_abort` after a cold reset sets bit 2 within four reads
  and the bit holds, including when the pulse starts after the address handshake of a `STATUS_SMU`
  read whose data has not yet returned.
* With both abort bits set, a cold reset, a warm reset through `SS_WARM_RESET_N` bit 0 and a primary
  reset through `rst_cool_ni` are each followed by a read of `STATUS_SMU`; the cold reset clears
  bits 2 and 12 (the idle word is required), and the warm and primary results are printed, not
  compared (`clk_rst.adoc` states no per-bit clearing). The idle word is built from the four done and
  pass bit masks of the RDL, with both abort pins required to read 0.
* `tb_mem_repair_abort` held high through a cold reset: whether bit 2 is set after the release is
  printed, not compared (the documents state no expected value).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, bounded to 200000 cycles, set both abort pins to 0, read
  `STATUS_SMU` and require the idle word.
. Error injection. Point: `STATUS_SMU` over SEP_IN AXI. Kind: an 8-byte all-ones write to the
  read-only register on the clean status. Expected response: the register reads the idle word on
  reading it back.
. Drive `tb_mbist_abort` to 1 and read up to four times for the idle word plus bit 12, requiring
  bit 2 clear; also drive `tb_mem_repair_abort` to 1 and read up to four times for the idle word
  plus bits 12 and 2.
. Set both pins to 0, read `STATUS_SMU` and require the idle word plus bits 12 and 2 with bits 3,
  5 to 7, 9 to 11 and 13 to 63 clear.
. Error injection. Point: `STATUS_SMU` over SEP_IN AXI, with both abort bits set. Kind: a write
  of zero, then all ones with byte strobe 0x01, then all ones with byte strobe 0x10, to the
  read-only register. Expected response: after each write `STATUS_SMU` reads the idle word plus
  bits 12 and 2. After each write print the AXI response.
. Apply a cold reset (`rst_cold_ni` low until the cold and primary levels assert, then high until
  all resets release, then the fuse sense wait) and require the idle word; pulse
  `tb_mem_repair_abort` for one `clk_smc_i` period and read up to four times for the idle word plus
  bit 2, accepting only the idle word or that word on the way, then read once more and require bit
  2 held. Apply a second cold reset and require the idle word. Start a `STATUS_SMU` read, wait up
  to 64 cycles for its address handshake, require the read data phase not started, pulse
  `tb_mem_repair_abort` for one period, require the read data to be the idle word or that word plus
  bit 2, read up to four times for bit 2 set and read once more to require it held.
. Three times (cold reset, warm reset, primary reset): set both pins to 1 and read up to four
  times for the idle word plus bits 12 and 2, set the pins to 0, apply the reset, read
  `STATUS_SMU`, print the state of bits 2 and 12 and, after the cold reset, require the idle word.
. Drive `tb_mem_repair_abort` to 1, apply a cold reset with it held, read `STATUS_SMU`, set the
  pin to 0 and print whether bit 2 is set.
. Log the bounded waits, wait one rising edge of `clk_smc_i`, require the step stamps in order and
  increasing and the checker lines in order, and print the ordered-fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-RO-CLEAN` |After an 8-byte all-ones write on the clean status `STATUS_SMU` reads
the idle word; any bit that changes, an abort bit rising included, fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-MBIST-ALONE` |`tb_mbist_abort` alone gives the idle word plus bit 12 within four
reads with bit 2 clear; any other word or no change within four reads fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-STAGGER` |After `tb_mbist_abort` and then `tb_mem_repair_abort` the word is the
idle word plus bit 12 and then plus bits 12 and 2, each within four reads; any other word or no
change fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-RESERVED` |With both aborts set and both pins at 0 the word is the idle word plus
bits 12 and 2 and every reserved bit reads 0; any reserved bit set fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-RO-SET` |After a zero write and all-ones writes with strobes 0x01 and 0x10 the
word stays the idle word plus bits 12 and 2; any bit that changes fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-WRITE-RESP` |The AXI response of each of the three writes is printed without
comparing it; only a missing response fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-PULSE` |A one-`clk_smc_i` pulse on `tb_mem_repair_abort` gives the idle word plus
bit 2 within four reads and the bit holds, also when the pulse starts with a read outstanding,
whose data must be the word before or after the pulse; bit 2 not set, dropping, or a torn word
fails it
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-RESET-CLEARS` |Both abort bits read set before each of the cold, warm and primary
resets; the cold reset clears bits 2 and 12 (asserted), and the leaf prints bits 2 and 12 and the
word read after the warm and primary resets without comparing them
|`CHK-DFX-STATUS-HIGH-THROUGH-RESET` |The cold reset taken with `tb_mem_repair_abort` held at 1
completes and the following read is printed without comparing bit 2
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every wait (fuse sense, each reset assert and release, the four-read polls,
the 64-cycle address handshake and the SEP_IN access bound) has a finite bound and fails on expiry
with the last observed word
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DFX-STATUS-RO-CLEAN`, `CHK-DFX-STATUS-MBIST-ALONE`, `CHK-DFX-STATUS-STAGGER`,
`CHK-DFX-STATUS-RESERVED`, `CHK-DFX-STATUS-RO-SET` and `CHK-DFX-STATUS-PULSE` hold after their
compares; `CHK-DFX-STATUS-RESET-CLEARS` holds after the cold reset compare, its warm and primary
results printed, not compared; `CHK-DFX-STATUS-WRITE-RESP` and
`CHK-DFX-STATUS-HIGH-THROUGH-RESET` hold once their accesses and resets completed, their values
printed, not compared; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert
holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The AXI responses to the writes to the read-only `STATUS_SMU` are printed, not
compared, because the documents state no response for a write to the read-only register. The
`STATUS_SMU` words read after the warm and primary resets are printed, not compared, because
`clk_rst.adoc` states no per-bit clearing; only the cold reset is required to clear the abort bits.
Whether bit 2 is set after a cold reset taken with `tb_mem_repair_abort` held high is printed, not
compared, because the documents state no expected value. The bench holds the done, success and pass
inputs high and cannot drive them individually, so only the two abort bits are exercised.

'''''

[[sec-452-smc_jtag_dm_sbcs_haltsum_test]]
===== 452 `smc_jtag_dm_sbcs_haltsum_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_dm_sbcs_haltsum_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_jtag_vip bit-banging the CPU TAP pins `tb_cpu_jtag_tck`, `tb_cpu_jtag_tms`,
`tb_cpu_jtag_tdi` and `tb_cpu_jtag_tdo` with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` pulsed while TCK runs; DMI
addresses `sbcs` 0x38, `haltsum1` 0x13, `haltsum0` 0x40 and `dmcontrol` 0x10 (`dmactive`), with
`dtmcs` giving `abits` and the idle count; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN writing and reading
`CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` (8 bytes, `debug_reset_n` at bit 24); `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `sbcs` capabilities fixed under writes and `haltsum` idle at 0.

*Test Coverage*:

* `sbcs` reads `sbversion` 1, `sbasize` 56, `sbaccess8`, `sbaccess16`, `sbaccess32` and
  `sbaccess64` 1 and `sbaccess128` 0, the capability values in the SMC Debug Module capability
  readbacks table of `cpu.adoc`.
* After a write of all ones to `sbcs` the capability fields read as before; `sbcs` is then written
  back to 0 and both words are printed. No system bus access is started.
* `haltsum0` (DMI 0x40, implemented for bits 3:0 only) and `haltsum1` (DMI 0x13, bit 0 only), per
  the DMI register inventory table of `cpu.adoc`, read 0 with no hart halted: the Debug Module
  implements Debug Specification 0.13 (`cpu.adoc`, Debug Module Configuration), whose haltsum
  registers carry one bit per halted hart.
* An all-ones write to each leaves both reading 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` with `debug_reset_n` set (the Debug Module is held in reset by the
  register's default), wait 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles, read `RESET_CTRL` back and require bit 24 set.
. Create the TAP, drive the pins idle, reset the TAP with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` while TCK steps,
  read IDCODE, activate the Debug Module (`dmcontrol.dmactive` over the DMI) and read `dmstatus`,
  read `dtmcs`, and take `abits` (7 if 0) and the idle count (at least 5) from it.
. Read `sbcs` over the DMI and require `sbversion` (bits 31:29) to be 1.
. Read `sbcs` again and require `sbasize` (bits 11:5) to be 56.
. Read `sbcs` again and require `sbaccess` (bits 4:0) to be 01111, that is `sbaccess8`,
  `sbaccess16`, `sbaccess32` and `sbaccess64` set and `sbaccess128` clear.
. Error injection. Point: `sbcs` over the DMI. Kind: a write of 0xFFFFFFFF covering the read-only
  capability fields. Expected response: the capability fields of the all-ones readback equal
  those of the first read. Then write 0 and read it; print both words and the restored word.
. Read `haltsum0` and require 0.
. Read `haltsum1` and require 0.
. Error injection. Point: `haltsum0` and `haltsum1` over the DMI. Kind: a write of 0xFFFFFFFF to
  each halt summary register with no hart halted. Expected response: both read 0 afterwards.
. Require the steps in order with increasing stamps and the checker lines in order, print the
  ordered-fence line and the two bounded waits (the DMI busy retries, four at most, and the
  sixteen-poll `dmactive` wait).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SBCS-VERSION` |`sbcs.sbversion` reads 1; any other value or a stalled scan fails it
|`CHK-SBCS-ASIZE` |`sbcs.sbasize` reads 56; any other value fails it
|`CHK-SBCS-ACCESS-CAPS` |`sbaccess8`, `sbaccess16`, `sbaccess32` and `sbaccess64` read 1 and
`sbaccess128` reads 0; any other combination fails it
|`CHK-SBCS-CAPS-WRITE-ALL-ONES` |After an all-ones write `sbversion`, `sbasize` and the five
`sbaccess` bits read as they did before it; any change fails it, and the words read are printed
|`CHK-HALTSUM0-IDLE` |`haltsum0` reads 0 with no hart halted; any non-zero value fails it
|`CHK-HALTSUM1-IDLE` |`haltsum1` reads 0 with no hart halted; any non-zero value fails it
|`CHK-HALTSUM-WRITE-IGNORED` |After all-ones writes to `haltsum0` and `haltsum1` both read 0;
either reading non-zero fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The DMI busy retries (four at most) and the sixteen-poll `dmactive` wait are
bounded and fail on expiry with the last readback
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SBCS-VERSION`, `CHK-SBCS-ASIZE`, `CHK-SBCS-ACCESS-CAPS`,
`CHK-SBCS-CAPS-WRITE-ALL-ONES`, `CHK-HALTSUM0-IDLE`, `CHK-HALTSUM1-IDLE` and
`CHK-HALTSUM-WRITE-IGNORED` hold after their compares with `sbversion` 1, `sbasize` 56, `sbaccess`
01111 and both halt summaries 0; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert
holds. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The `sbcs` words read after the all-ones write and after the restore are printed;
only the capability fields are compared. No system bus access is started.

'''''

[[sec-535-smc_jtag_dm_halt_progbuf_test]]
===== 535 `smc_jtag_dm_halt_progbuf_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_dm_halt_progbuf_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_jtag_vip bit-banging the CPU TAP pins `tb_cpu_jtag_tck`, `tb_cpu_jtag_tms`,
`tb_cpu_jtag_tdi` and `tb_cpu_jtag_tdo` with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` pulsed while TCK runs; DMI
addresses `data0`..`data3` 0x04..0x07, `dmcontrol` 0x10, `dmstatus` 0x11, `abstractcs` 0x16,
`command` 0x17, `progbuf0`..`progbuf15` 0x20..0x2F and `haltsum0` 0x40, with `dtmcs` giving
`abits` and the idle count; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN reading and writing `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL`
(8 bytes, `debug_reset_n` at bit 24) and `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` (8 bytes, address from the generated
address map accessor `smc_indexed_addr("SMC_TOP_SMC_CPU_CTRL_SCRATCH_BASE_ADDR", 0)`, the local
alias a hart store uses); hart 0 running from its reset vector; `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A halted hart runs a program-buffer store through the Debug Module and the stored word
reads back in `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]`.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` `debug_reset_n` reads 0 before the release and is compared, with the
  release readback of 1 as the paired positive control.
* After the release and `dmcontrol.dmactive` = 1, `dmstatus` reads `version` 2 and `impebreak` 1,
  `abstractcs` reads `progbufsize` 16 and `datacount` 4, `dmcontrol.hartsello` written 3 reads back
  3 and a nonzero `hartselhi` reads back 0.
* Positive control: before `haltreq` hart 0 runs (`allrunning` 1, `anyhalted` 0); after `haltreq`
  within sixteen polls `dmstatus` has `allhalted` 1 and `anyrunning` 0, and `haltsum0` bits 3:0 read
  0b0001. `dpc` is not compared.
* With `hartsello` = 1 the other hart still runs (`allrunning` 1, `anyhalted` 0).
* `data0`..`data3` read back four distinct patterns; an Access Register write of `x8` (64-bit) and
  `x9` followed by an Access Register read of `x8` returns the pattern in `data0` and `data1`, with
  `abstractcs.busy` 0 and `cmderr` 0 after each command.
* `progbuf0`..`progbuf15` read back sixteen distinct words. `progbuf0` is then set to `sw x8, 0(x9)`
  (0x0084A023) and the Access Register command with `transfer` 0 and `postexec` 1 runs the program
  buffer with no explicit `ebreak`: `busy` returns to 0 and `cmderr` reads 0, so the implicit
  `ebreak` returned the hart to the Debug ROM. The other fifteen words are `addi x0, x0, k`.
* `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` reads a sentinel before the run and the low 32 bits of `x8` after it; the
  sentinel differs from that value and from the register reset value 0, so only the hart store can
  change it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` over AXI-Lite and take `debug_reset_n` (bit 24), which holds the Debug
  Module in reset; require 0 and print the word.
. Write `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` with `debug_reset_n` set, wait 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles, read it back and
  require bit 24 set. Create the TAP, reset it with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` while TCK steps, read
  IDCODE, activate the Debug Module (`dmactive` plus a bounded wait on `dmstatus`), read `dtmcs`
  for `abits` and the idle count, then read `dmstatus` (require `version` 2, `impebreak` 1) and
  `abstractcs` (require `progbufsize` 16, `datacount` 4). Write `dmcontrol` with `hartsello` 3 and
  require it to read back 3, write a nonzero `hartselhi` and require it to read back 0, then write
  `dmcontrol` with `dmactive` only.
. Read `dmstatus` and require `allrunning` 1 and `anyhalted` 0.
. Write `dmcontrol.haltreq`, poll `dmstatus` until `allhalted` is 1 (sixteen reads at most), clear
  `haltreq`, read `dmstatus` and `haltsum0`; require `allhalted` 1, `anyrunning` 0 and `haltsum0`
  bits 3:0 equal to 0b0001.
. Select `hartsello` 1, read `dmstatus` and require `allrunning` 1 and `anyhalted` 0; restore
  `hartsello` 0.
. Write `data0`..`data3` with four distinct patterns and read all four back. Write `x8` (64-bit
  pattern) and `x9` (the `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` address) with Access Register commands, clear
  `data0` and `data1`, read `x8` back with an Access Register command and require the pattern in
  `data0` and `data1`; each command waits for `busy` 0 (sixteen reads at most) and requires
  `cmderr` 0.
. Write `progbuf0`..`progbuf15` with sixteen distinct words and read all sixteen back, then write
  `progbuf0` with 0x0084A023. Write the sentinel to `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` over AXI-Lite and read
  it back.
. Write `command` with `transfer` 0 and `postexec` 1, read `abstractcs` until `busy` is 0 (sixteen
  reads at most) and require `cmderr` 0.
. Read `CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` over AXI-Lite and require the low 32 bits of the `x8` pattern.
. Write `dmcontrol.resumereq`, poll `dmstatus` until `allresumeack` and `allrunning` are 1
  (sixteen reads at most), clear `resumereq`, wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles.
. Require the steps in order with increasing stamps and each checker line after its step, print the
  ordered-fence line and the bounded waits (DMI busy retries, four at most; `dmactive` wait, `halt`
  wait, `busy` wait and `resume` wait, sixteen reads each).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DM-ACT-RESET-HELD` |`debug_reset_n` reads 0 before the release, compared, with the release
readback of 1 as the positive control; a nonzero read before the release, a clear bit after it or
a failed read fails it
|`CHK-DM-ACT-DMSTATUS` |After the release and `dmactive` = 1, `dmstatus.version` reads 2 and
`impebreak` reads 1; any other value, a stalled scan or a busy response beyond the retry bound fails
it
|`CHK-DM-CAP-READBACK` |`abstractcs.progbufsize` reads 16 and `datacount` 4, `hartsello` written 3
reads back 3 and a nonzero `hartselhi` reads back 0; any difference fails it
|`CHK-DM-HART-HALT` |Before `haltreq` `dmstatus` has `allrunning` 1 and `anyhalted` 0, within the
bound after it `allhalted` 1 and `anyrunning` 0; a failed control, a missing halt or a timeout fails
it
|`CHK-DM-HALTSUM0` |With hart 0 halted `haltsum0` bits 3:0 read 0b0001; bit 0 clear or any of bits
3:1 set fails it
|`CHK-DM-OTHER-HART-RUNS` |With `hartsello` 1 `dmstatus` has `allrunning` 1 and `anyhalted` 0 while
hart 0 is halted; a halted or absent hart fails it
|`CHK-DM-GPR-DATA` |`data0`..`data3` read back the four patterns and the 64-bit `x8` read returns
the written pattern with `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 0 after each command; any difference or a nonzero
`cmderr` fails it
|`CHK-DM-PROGBUF-REGS` |`progbuf0`..`progbuf15` read back the sixteen distinct words written; any
difference fails it
|`CHK-DM-PROGBUF-STORE` |`CPU_CTRL.SCRATCH[0]` reads the sentinel before the program buffer runs and
the low 32 bits of `x8` after it; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-PROGBUF-IMPEBREAK` |With no explicit `ebreak` `abstractcs.busy` returns to 0 within the
bound and `cmderr` reads 0 after the `postexec` command; busy at the bound or a nonzero `cmderr`
fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The DMI busy retries (four at most) and the sixteen-read `dmactive`, halt,
busy and resume waits are bounded and fail on expiry with the last `dmstatus`, `abstractcs` and DMI
response
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DM-ACT-RESET-HELD`, `CHK-DM-ACT-DMSTATUS`, `CHK-DM-CAP-READBACK`,
`CHK-DM-HART-HALT`, `CHK-DM-HALTSUM0`, `CHK-DM-OTHER-HART-RUNS`, `CHK-DM-GPR-DATA`,
`CHK-DM-PROGBUF-REGS`, `CHK-DM-PROGBUF-STORE` and `CHK-DM-PROGBUF-IMPEBREAK` hold after their
compares; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `dpc` is not compared.

'''''

[[sec-536-smc_jtag_dm_sba_scratchpad_test]]
===== 536 `smc_jtag_dm_sba_scratchpad_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_dm_sba_scratchpad_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_jtag_vip bit-banging the CPU TAP pins `tb_cpu_jtag_tck`, `tb_cpu_jtag_tms`,
`tb_cpu_jtag_tdi` and `tb_cpu_jtag_tdo` with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` pulsed while TCK runs; DMI
addresses `data0` 0x04, `sbcs` 0x38, `sbaddress0` 0x39, `sbaddress1` 0x3A, `sbdata0` 0x3C and
`sbdata1` 0x3D, the not-implemented `data4` 0x08, `hartinfo` 0x12, `confstrptr0` 0x19, `nextdm`
0x1D, `authdata` 0x30, `haltsum2` 0x34, `sbaddress2` 0x3B and `sbdata2` 0x3E, with `dtmcs` giving
`abits` and the idle count; `sbcs` layout `sbversion` bits 31:29, `sbbusy` bit 21, `sbreadonaddr`
bit 20, `sbaccess` bits 19:17, `sberror` bits 14:12 (write 1 to clear), `sbasize` bits 11:5 and
`sbaccess128`..`sbaccess8` bits 4:0; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN reading and writing
`CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` (8 bytes, `debug_reset_n` at bit 24) and the scratchpad words (4 and 8 bytes,
addresses from the generated address map accessor `SPM_MEMORY_BASE`, the local alias); `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The Debug Module system bus writes and reads the scratchpad at 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits
and the SEP_IN AXI driver sees the same words.

*Test Coverage*:

* After the debug reset release and `dmcontrol.dmactive` = 1, `sbcs` reads `sbversion` 1, `sbasize`
  56, `sbaccess8`, `sbaccess16`, `sbaccess32` and `sbaccess64` 1 and `sbaccess128` 0.
* The not-implemented DMI registers `data4`, `hartinfo`, `confstrptr0`, `nextdm`, `authdata`,
  `haltsum2`, `sbaddress2` and `sbdata2` read 0 before and after a write of 0xFFFFFFFF; `data0`
  reads back its written pattern as the positive control.
* Two 32-bit system bus writes at distinct scratchpad word addresses end with `sbbusy` 0 and
  `sberror` 0 and `sbaddress0` reads back each address; `sbaddress1` (written 0 by the sequence)
  is printed and not compared.
* System bus reads with `sbreadonaddr` of both words return the two distinct patterns.
* Width-specific writes at 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits into four distinct doublewords with a known
  background read back at the same width, and the 64-bit read of the doubleword equals the
  background with only the written bytes replaced.
* A 64-bit write with `sbdata1` loaded before `sbdata0` reads back with `sbdata0` the low word and
  `sbdata1` the high word.
* The AXI driver reads the words the system bus wrote, and the system bus reads a word the AXI
  driver wrote.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` with `debug_reset_n` set, wait 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles, read it back and
  require bit 24 set. Create the TAP, reset it with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` while TCK steps, read
  IDCODE, activate the Debug Module (`dmactive` plus a bounded wait on `dmstatus`), read `dtmcs`
  for `abits` and the idle count, then read `sbcs` and require `sbversion`, `sbasize` and the
  `sbaccess` capability bits listed above.
. Error injection. Point: the not-implemented DMI registers `data4`, `hartinfo`, `confstrptr0`,
  `nextdm`, `authdata`, `haltsum2`, `sbaddress2` and `sbdata2`. Kind: a read, a write of
  0xFFFFFFFF and a second read of each. Expected response: each reads 0 both times. Write `data0`
  with a pattern and require it to read back as the positive control.
. Write `sbcs` with `sbaccess` 2 and `sberror` cleared, write `sbaddress1` 0 and `sbaddress0` with
  the first word address, write `sbdata0` to start the access, read `sbcs` until `sbbusy` is 0
  (sixteen reads at most) and require `sberror` 0; read `sbaddress0` back. Repeat at the second
  word address with a different pattern and read `sbaddress0` and `sbaddress1`.
. Write `sbcs` with `sbreadonaddr` and `sbaccess` 2, write `sbaddress0` with each word address in
  turn, wait for `sbbusy` 0 and `sberror` 0, read `sbdata0` and require the written pattern.
. For each of `sbaccess` 0, 1, 2 and 3 write a known 64-bit background into a doubleword, write
  the width-specific pattern at a byte lane inside it, read it at the same width and read the
  doubleword at 64 bits; require the pattern at the width and the background with only the written
  bytes replaced.
. Write `sbcs` with `sbaccess` 3, `sbaddress0`, `sbdata1` and then `sbdata0`; wait for `sbbusy` 0
  and `sberror` 0, read the location back with `sbreadonaddr` and read `sbdata0` and `sbdata1`;
  require the low and high words as written.
. Read the words of steps 3 and 5 and the 64-bit location of step 6 with the SEP_IN AXI driver and
  require each to equal the system bus value; write a new pattern at a fresh word with the AXI
  driver, wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles and read it with a system bus read.
. Require the steps in order with increasing stamps and each checker line after its step, print the
  ordered-fence line and the bounded waits (DMI busy retries, four at most; `dmactive` wait and
  `sbbusy` wait, sixteen reads each).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DM-SBCS-CAPS` |`sbcs` reads `sbversion` 1, `sbasize` 56, `sbaccess8`..`sbaccess64` 1 and
`sbaccess128` 0; any other field value or a stalled scan fails it
|`CHK-DM-NOT-IMPL-DMI` |Each listed not-implemented DMI register reads 0 before and after a write
of 0xFFFFFFFF and `data0` reads back its pattern; a nonzero read or a failed control fails it
|`CHK-DM-SBA-WRITE` |After each 32-bit system bus write `sbbusy` reads 0 within the bound and
`sberror` 0 and `sbaddress0` reads back the written address, and `sbaddress1` (written 0 by the
sequence) is printed and not compared; a busy bit at the bound, a nonzero `sberror` or an address
difference fails it
|`CHK-DM-SBA-READ` |A system bus read of each written word returns its own pattern with `sbbusy` 0
and `sberror` 0; a different word, an aliased word or a nonzero `sberror` fails it
|`CHK-DM-SBA-WIDTHS` |Each of the 8-, 16-, 32- and 64-bit writes reads back its pattern at its width
and the doubleword keeps its background outside the written bytes; any difference fails it
|`CHK-DM-SBA-64BIT` |A 64-bit write started by `sbdata0` with `sbdata1` loaded first reads back
`sbdata0` as the low word and `sbdata1` as the high word; a difference or swapped words fails it
|`CHK-DM-SBA-VISIBLE` |The AXI reads of the words the system bus wrote equal the written values and
the system bus read of the word the AXI driver wrote equals it; any difference fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The DMI busy retries (four at most), the sixteen-read `dmactive` wait and the
sixteen-read `sbbusy` wait are bounded and fail on expiry with the last `sbcs` and DMI response
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DM-SBCS-CAPS`, `CHK-DM-NOT-IMPL-DMI`, `CHK-DM-SBA-WRITE`, `CHK-DM-SBA-READ`,
`CHK-DM-SBA-WIDTHS`, `CHK-DM-SBA-64BIT` and `CHK-DM-SBA-VISIBLE` hold after their compares;
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `sbaddress1`, written 0 by the sequence, is printed and not compared.

'''''

[[sec-537-smc_jtag_dm_abstractcs_lifecycle_test]]
===== 537 `smc_jtag_dm_abstractcs_lifecycle_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: JTAG

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_dm_abstractcs_lifecycle_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_jtag_vip bit-banging the CPU TAP pins `tb_cpu_jtag_tck`, `tb_cpu_jtag_tms`,
`tb_cpu_jtag_tdi` and `tb_cpu_jtag_tdo` with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` pulsed while TCK runs (10 ns
period); DMI addresses `data0` 0x04, `data1` 0x05, `dmcontrol` 0x10, `dmstatus` 0x11, `abstractcs`
0x16, `command` 0x17 and `progbuf0`..`progbuf15` 0x20..0x2F, with `dtmcs` giving `abits` and the
idle count; `abstractcs` fields `busy` bit 12 and `cmderr` bits 10:8 (write 1 to clear); Access
Register fields `aarsize`, `postexec`, `transfer`, `write` and `regno` 0x1000..0x101F for
`x0`..`x31` and the Quick Access command type 1; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN reading and writing
`CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` (8 bytes, `debug_reset_n` at bit 24); hart 0 halted by `haltreq` and running
the program-buffer loop; `clk_smc_i` measured by the leaf to size the loop count

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/jtag.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `abstractcs.busy` is observed while a program-buffer loop runs, and command misuse sets
`cmderr` 1 and 2 without executing anything and clears on a write of 1s.

*Test Coverage*:

* Before any command `abstractcs` reads `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 0; after a postexec command with
  `transfer` clear, `busy` reads 1 at least once while the loop runs (positive control that busy is
  observable) and later 0 with `cmderr` 0.
* A command written while `busy` is 1 does not execute (`x6` unchanged) and leaves `cmderr` 1; the
  wait for `busy` 0 is a bench bound, not a specification value.
* With `cmderr` 1 held and `busy` 0, a Quick Access write replaces the held code with 2; a write of
  1s then reads `cmderr` 0.
* With `cmderr` 0, a Quick Access command, an Access Register command with `transfer` set,
  `aarsize` 3 and `regno` 0x1020, and one with `transfer` set, `aarsize` 1 and `regno` 0x1008 each
  leave `cmderr` 2; the same operands with `transfer` clear leave `cmderr` 0.
* A command written with `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 2 replaces the stored command and leaves `cmderr` 2;
  it does not execute, so `x8` still reads its earlier pattern after the clear.
* After the clear a 32-bit Access Register write and read of `x8` execute with `cmderr` 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Write `CPU_CTRL.RESET_CTRL` with `debug_reset_n` set, wait 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles and read it back.
  Create the TAP, reset it with `tb_cpu_jtag_reset` while TCK steps, read IDCODE and `dtmcs`, write
  `dmcontrol.dmactive` and wait (sixteen reads at most) for `dmstatus` to answer, set `haltreq` and
  wait (sixteen reads at most) for `allhalted`. Read `abstractcs` and require `busy` 0 and `cmderr`
  0, then write `x8` with pattern A.
. Measure the `clk_smc_i` period, compute the loop count from the TCK period, the DMI access cost
  and two clocks per iteration, print it, and write `x5` with it. Write `progbuf0` `addi x5, x5, -1`
  (0xFFF28293), `progbuf1` `bne x5, x0, -4` (0xFE029EE3) and `nop` into `progbuf2`..`progbuf15`,
  printing each word.
. Write the postexec command with `transfer` clear and read `abstractcs` until `busy` reads 0
  (sixty-four reads at most); require a `busy` 1 read, then `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 0.
. Error injection. Point: the Debug Module `command` register over the DMI. Kind: the `x6` Access
  Register command written while `abstractcs.busy` reads 1 with the program-buffer loop running,
  then a Quick Access command written with `cmderr` 1 held. Expected response: `cmderr` 1 once
  `busy` reads 0 (sixty-four reads at most), then `cmderr` 2 after the Quick Access write; after
  1s are written to `cmderr` it reads 0 and `x6` reads its earlier value. Setup before the
  injection: write `x6`, re-arm `x5`, load the `x6` busy-write data, write the postexec command
  and read `abstractcs` until `busy` reads 1.
. Error injection. Point: the Debug Module `command` register over the DMI, with `cmderr` 0. Kind:
  command misuse, issued in turn: the Quick Access command, the `transfer` set `aarsize` 3 `regno`
  0x1020 command and the `transfer` set `aarsize` 1 `regno` 0x1008 command. Expected response:
  each rejected leg leaves `cmderr` 2, read from `abstractcs` after each, and `cmderr` is cleared
  after each rejected leg. Then issue the `transfer` clear `aarsize` 1 `regno` 0x1020 command and
  read `abstractcs` after it.
. Error injection. Point: the Debug Module `command` register over the DMI. Kind: a Quick Access
  command that makes `cmderr` 2, then the Access Register command that writes `x8` issued with
  `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 2 held. Expected response: `command` reads back the stored write and
  `abstractcs` still reads `cmderr` 2; the command does not execute, and after 1s are written to
  `cmderr` a command read of `x8` returns pattern A. Setup before the injection: load pattern B in
  `data0` and `data1`.
. Wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles, write a 32-bit Access Register write of `x8` with pattern C and a
  32-bit read, reading `abstractcs` after each and `data0` after the read.
. Require the steps in order with increasing stamps and each checker line after its step, print the
  ordered-fence line and the bounded waits (DMI busy retries, four at most; the `dmactive`, halt and
  idle waits of sixteen reads; the loop, busy-observe and busy-write waits of sixty-four reads).

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DM-BUSY-LIFECYCLE` |`abstractcs` reads `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 0 before any command, `busy` 1 at
least once during the loop and `busy` 0 with `cmderr` 0 after it; no busy read, a busy read at the
bound or a nonzero `cmderr` fails it
|`CHK-DM-BUSY-WRITE` |A command written while `busy` is 1 leaves `cmderr` 1 with `busy` 0 within the
bench bound, `x6` unchanged and `cmderr` 0 after a write of 1s; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-CMDTYPE` |A Quick Access command leaves `cmderr` 2 and `busy` 0; any other value
fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-REGNO` |An Access Register command with `transfer` set, `aarsize` 3 and `regno`
0x1020 leaves `cmderr` 2; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-AARSIZE` |An Access Register command with `transfer` set, `regno` 0x1008 and
`aarsize` 1 leaves `cmderr` 2; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-NOTRANSFER` |The operands rejected with `transfer` set leave `cmderr` 0 and `busy` 0
with `transfer` clear, and the two rejected legs read `cmderr` 2; any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-STORE` |A command written with `busy` 0 and `cmderr` 2 reads back from `command` as
written and leaves `cmderr` 2; the earlier value or another `cmderr` fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-REPLACE` |With `cmderr` 1 held and `busy` 0 a Quick Access write leaves `cmderr` 2;
`cmderr` 1 or any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-NOEXEC` |`x8` reads pattern A after the pattern-B write command issued with `cmderr`
2; pattern B or any other value fails it
|`CHK-DM-CMDERR-RECOVER-GPR32` |After the clear a 32-bit write of `x8` and a 32-bit read return
`cmderr` 0 and `busy` 0 and the read returns pattern C; any other value fails it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow their steps; a missing or misordered term fails it
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Seven bounded waits: the DMI busy retries (four at most), the sixteen-read
`dmactive` and halt waits on `dmstatus`, the sixteen-read idle wait on `abstractcs` that every
command (the GPR writes and reads, the rejected-command legs, the replace and store waits) and
every `cmderr` clear use, and the sixty-four-read loop, busy-observe and busy-write waits; each
fails on expiry with the last `dmstatus`, `abstractcs`, `command` and DMI response
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DM-BUSY-LIFECYCLE`, `CHK-DM-BUSY-WRITE`, `CHK-DM-CMDERR-CMDTYPE`,
`CHK-DM-CMDERR-REGNO`, `CHK-DM-CMDERR-AARSIZE`, `CHK-DM-CMDERR-NOTRANSFER`,
`CHK-DM-CMDERR-STORE`, `CHK-DM-CMDERR-REPLACE`, `CHK-DM-CMDERR-NOEXEC` and
`CHK-DM-CMDERR-RECOVER-GPR32` hold after their compares; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold
and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The wait for `busy` to return to 0 after the command written while `busy` was 1 is a
bench bound, not a specification value.

'''''

[[sec-090-smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test]]
===== 90 `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test`

*BFM / Model*: SPI pad BFM, ocah_axi_vip (AXI), ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite), ocah_jtag_vip

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive lc_state_i + JTAG eFuse accesses; assert the block/allow matrix.

*Test Coverage*:

* `tb_lc_state` drives `lc_state_i` = {diff_n, diff_p} directly, and
* the `ej_axi` AXI-Lite master drives `axil_smc_otp_jtag_req_i`.
* The expected matrix is taken from the specification, not the RTL: `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, section "Lifecycle State (LC_STATE) Effects", cited below by line.
* lifecycle encodings, :265-282 -- `TEST_DEV 0x0 | PROD 0x1 | RMA_SOP 0x2, 0x3 | RMA_CHIPLET 0x6-0x7 | PROD_END 0x8 | INVALID all others`;
* the restricted set, :286 -- "When lifecycle state is PROD (0x1) or RMA_SOP (0x2, 0x3), JTAG access to eFuse registers is restricted";
* the access table, :289-295 -- JTAG Write *Blocked* / JTAG Read *Blocked* except Chiplet ID / JTAG Read Chiplet ID Allowed, in both columns;
* the Chiplet ID exception, :301-305 -- "Even in PROD or RMA_SOP states, JTAG read access to the chiplet ID and package ID registers is permitted";
* the blocked response, :297-299 -- "the error slave returns an error response with data value `0xbadcab1e`".

The matrix below is the specification's outcome per raw `lc_state_i`
encoding; the encodings and state names are the specification's
(`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc:265-282`). The checkers drive one
encoding per state -- `0x0`, `0x1`, `0x2`, `0x6`, `0x8` -- plus the
integrity-error case; `0x3` and `0x7`, the specification's second encodings
of RMA_SOP and RMA_CHIPLET, are not driven. The integrity-error row is not a
specification table row: it is the `INVALID ... (error fallback)` class
(`:281`) applied fail-closed, with no identity exception.
`smc_efuse_wrapper` gates JTAG-to-eFuse access on `lc_state_i`; a blocked
transaction returns DECERR with data `0xBADCAB1E`. `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_negative_test`
covers the CSR-observable subset (`CHIP_CONFIG_LC_STATE` plus the always-allowed
JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY reads).

[cols="2,2,2,3",options="header",]
|===
|SMC LC state (raw) |JTAG eFuse write |JTAG eFuse read (non-ID) |JTAG read JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY
|TEST_DEV `0x0` |allow |allow |allow
|PROD `0x1` |BLOCK (DECERR/`0xBADCAB1E`) |BLOCK |allow
|RMA_SOP `0x2`,`0x3` |BLOCK |BLOCK |allow
|RMA_CHIPLET `0x6`,`0x7` |allow |allow |allow
|PROD_END `0x8` |allow |allow |allow
|differential-decode integrity error |BLOCK |BLOCK |BLOCK (no ID exception)
|===

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-PROD` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-PROD_END` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-RMA_CHIPLET` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-RMA_SOP` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-SIGINT` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-TEST_DEV` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-PROD`, `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-PROD_END`, `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-RMA_CHIPLET`, `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-RMA_SOP`, `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-SIGINT`, `CHK-EFUSE-JTAG-LC-TEST_DEV` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: One encoding per lifecycle state is driven (`0x0`, `0x1`, `0x2`, `0x6`, `0x8`) plus
the integrity-error case; `0x3` and `0x7`, the specification's second encodings of RMA_SOP and
RMA_CHIPLET, are not driven.
'''''

[[sec-098-smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test]]
===== 98 `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: timeout_enable|0 aborts; default timeout recovers OTP bit0.

*Test Coverage*:

* PROGRAM/READ timeout CSRs.
* timeout_enable|0 fires in ST_WAIT_RESP on this shim.
* **The claim is split, and only one half is a DUT-path claim.** *DUT path (reportable).* `EFUSE_PROGRAM_REQ_TIMEOUT` / `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` with `timeout_enable=1, cycles=0` must abort the outstanding request and raise `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL.PROGRAM_STATUS` / leave `EFUSE_READ_INTERFACE_READ_DATA` empty; re-programming the RDL-default cycle count must let the same operation complete.
* That FSM is real `efuse_interface_controller` RTL and every address, field mask and reset used here is imported by generated symbol from `efuse_interface_ctrl.h`.
* *Model-backed (NOT silicon-path coverage).* `tb_efuse_programmed_word0` is a TB tap on `u_dut.u_smc_ip_integration.u_efuse_bank_model.u_efuse_bank_reg` (`tb/tb_top.sv`).
* SPEC declares that block a stand-in: "The eFuse bank model (`efuse_bank_model.sv`) is a reference, simulation-only stand-in for the real foundry OTP macro ...
* In a production integration it is replaced by the actual foundry macro driven by the SHIM" (`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`), and its set-once semantics are `onwrite = woset` in the DV RDL `hw/ip/efuse/dv/models/regs/efuse_bank.rdl`.
* The `OTP=...` observations below therefore show that the controller's command did or did not reach the bank model -- they are **not** proof that a fuse burns in silicon ([BEHAVIORAL-STUB-DECLARED]).

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EFUSE-READ-STATUS-SET-ON-NO-ENABLE` |Positive control for the `READ_STATUS == 0` compares: with `STATUS.EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` read clear first, the recovery read's command word minus `READ_ENABLE` sets `READ_STATUS` in `EFUSE_READ_CTRL`, the cause `efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl` names for the field; `READ_DATA` is logged, not asserted (`smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG-REC` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG-SET` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD-REC` |Named compare in `smc_efuse_read_program_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EFUSE-READ-STATUS-SET-ON-NO-ENABLE`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-BASIC`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG-REC`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-PROG-SET`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD` (and 1 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The OTP word observations through the bank-model tap show that the controller's
command did or did not reach the simulation-only bank model; they are not proof that a fuse burns in
silicon. `READ_DATA` on the positive-control read is logged, not asserted.
'''''

[[sec-099-smc_efuse_read_timeout_status_test]]
===== 99 `smc_efuse_read_timeout_status_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_read_timeout_status_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) against the eFuse bank model

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A read that hits `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` completes with `EFUSE_READ_CTRL.READ_STATUS` set, after a successful read shows it clear.

*Test Coverage*:

* `hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl` defines `EFUSE_READ_CTRL.READ_STATUS` as the read interface's error report (`read_done` says the read completed, `read_status` says how) and `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` as a bound on the cycles the interface waits for a SHIM response; the Programmer's Guide eFuse read sequence (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`) has software check `read_status` after every completion. A read that hits the bound is a completed read with an error: `read_done=1` and `read_status=1`.
* The arming leg makes the check real: `READ_STATUS` holds until the next completion, so a stale 1 would satisfy the timeout leg on its own. A successful read at the RDL-default cycle count comes first and must show `READ_STATUS` 0; `STATUS.EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` is required clear beforehand because a sticky request error also reports through `READ_STATUS`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Issue a successful read at the RDL default READ_TMO and record READ_CTRL with READ_STATUS clear.
. Require STATUS.EFUSE_REQ_ERROR clear, so a sticky req-err cannot be mistaken for the timeout path.
. Error injection. Point: `EFUSE_READ_REQ_TIMEOUT`, the bound on the cycles the read interface waits
  for a SHIM response. Kind: a read forced to hit the programmed timeout. Expected response: the read
  completes as an error, with `READ_DONE` set and `READ_STATUS` set. Read READ_CTRL again.
. Require READ_STATUS to be set.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD-STATUS-ARM` |A successful read at the RDL-default timeout completes with `READ_DONE` set and `READ_STATUS` clear, with `STATUS.EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` clear, arming the leg below (`smc_efuse_read_timeout_status_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD-STATUS-SET` |The read that hits the programmed timeout completes with `READ_DONE` set and `READ_STATUS` set (`smc_efuse_read_timeout_status_test_seq.py`)
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD-STATUS-ARM`, `CHK-EFUSE-TMO-RD-STATUS-SET` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''
