[[sec-453-smc_efuse_bank_ctrl_window_test]]
===== 453 `smc_efuse_bank_ctrl_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_bank_ctrl_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (strict reads and writes with the full strobe 0xF); the reset agent
(cold reset assert and release); the passive per-cycle sampler on `clk_smc_i` over
`tb_efuse_bank_awvalid`, `tb_efuse_bank_wvalid`, `tb_efuse_bank_arvalid`, `tb_efuse_bank_bvalid`,
`tb_efuse_bank_rvalid`, `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` and `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`; the wait probes
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the eFuse bank is the DV model
behind `efuse_bank_ctrl`; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SHIM window accesses show exact bank handshake counts.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SHIM control window at the SMC-local 0xC040_0000 forwards every access to `efuse_bank_ctrl`
  unchanged, and the controller's own register blocks do not use that path
  (`doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface, SHIM control address window;
  `hw/ip/efuse/doc/interface.adoc`, Fuse Bank Control Interface).
* The window holds the `EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME` register of the reference register block
  `efuse_shim_ctrl` (`doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface). The 0x20 reset value
  comes from the reference block's own RDL (`hw/ip/efuse/dv/models/regs/efuse_shim_ctrl.rdl`),
  a DV model of the SHIM control map; the integrator guide names the block and the register but
  states no reset value, so 0x20 has no standing beyond that model.
* A window read is one `ar` and one `r` handshake, and a window write is one `aw`, one `w` and one
  `b` handshake. Traffic to the controller's own `STATUS` and `READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` registers
  (`hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl`) and to the SMC_EFUSE_MAP `LOCKS` register
  (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`) produces no bank-control edge.
* Back-to-back serialized window accesses (read, read; write, read; read, write) return the
  expected data, each with an OKAY response.
* The write of a non-reset init time followed by a cold reset is measured against the baseline
  delay from reset release to the first `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid`; the delay difference and whether
  the register survives the reset are recorded; the specification does not state whether it survives.
* The strobe content that reaches the port and the address presented on the port are not
  observable here and are not claimed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the first fuse sense to finish, start the edge sampler (rising edges of the five channel
  valids, cycles with any valid high, release and first `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` cycles), and mark
  the step.
. Run a cold reset through the reset agent (assert, check the reset state, require
  `tb_fuse_sense_done` to be 0, release, wait for the sense and for the first
  `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` within 2000 clocks). Read `STATUS` three times, write 0x1000 to
  `READ_REQ_TIMEOUT`, read it back, restore its reset value and read it back, and read `LOCKS`;
  every one of these accesses must add no edge on any channel. Require all five edge counters and
  the busy-cycle count to be 0 and record the baseline reset-release-to-first-command delay.
. Read the window and require 0x20, an OKAY response and exactly one `ar` and one `r` edge.
. Write 0x15 and then 0x3A to the window with strobe 0xF; each write must give exactly one `aw`,
  one `w` and one `b` edge, and each read-back must equal the written value with one `ar` and one
  `r` edge. Restore 0x20 and read it back. Require every channel counter to have moved.
. Issue read, read; write, read; read, write; then a restoring write and read, all through the
  window, each access awaited before the next. Require the expected data for each access, all
  responses OKAY and no channel valid high for 16 cycles afterwards.
. Write 0x40, read it back and require 0x40; run a second cold reset and wait for the sense and the
  first command; read the window once more and, when 0x40 survived, restore 0x20 and read it back.
  Record the second release-to-first-command delay and its difference from the baseline.
. Require the six steps in order with increasing time stamps and strictly increasing cumulative edge
  totals, the checker lines in the order printed, and the SEP_IN access count at or above the
  computed floor; print the fence and the list of bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-BANKCTRL-IDLE` |Across the cold reset, the sense, three `STATUS` reads, the
`READ_REQ_TIMEOUT` write, read and restore and the `LOCKS` read, the edges of `aw`, `w`, `ar`, `b`
and `r` are all 0 with 0 busy cycles, while the same counters later move in the window steps
(positive control).
|`CHK-WINDOW-READ` |A window read returns the `EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME` reset value 0x20 with an
OKAY response and exactly one `ar` and one `r` edge, and no `aw`, `w` or `b` edge.
|`CHK-WINDOW-WRITE` |Two window writes of distinct values with strobe 0xF each give one `aw`, one
`w` and one `b` edge and read back equal with one `ar` and one `r` edge; 0x20 is restored and
re-read.
|`CHK-BANKCTRL-ORDER` |Back-to-back serialized window accesses (read-read, write-read and
read-write) return the expected data with OKAY responses, and all five valids stay 0 for 16 cycles
afterwards.
|`CHK-INITTIME-RESENSE` |Records the init time 0x40 read back through the window before the reset,
the release-to-first-command delay with the reset value and with 0x40, their difference and whether
the register survived the reset, without comparing the delay or the survival to an expected value.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (idle leg with zero edges, then window read, window write,
sequences and re-sense, with strictly increasing cumulative edge totals) and every checker line
printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every window access and every sense wait is bounded and fails with an
assertion on expiry; the bounds and the last observed states are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold: zero bank-control edges for the idle traffic, one `ar` and
one `r` edge for each window read, one `aw`, one `w` and one `b` edge for each window write, 0x20
read at reset and after each restore, expected data for the serialized window sequences, and every bounded wait finishing
inside its bound. The re-sense delay is recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The release-to-first-command delay with the reset init time and with 0x40, their
difference and whether `EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME` survives the cold reset are recorded without a
compare, because the specification does not state whether the register survives. The 0x20 reset
value comes from the DV model's own RDL and has no standing beyond that model, the integrator guide
stating no reset value. The strobe content that reaches the bank port and the address presented on
it are not observable here and are not claimed.

'''''

[[sec-454-smc_efuse_fuse_reset_gate_test]]
===== 454 `smc_efuse_fuse_reset_gate_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_fuse_reset_gate_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (a continuous `STATUS` read stream); the reset agent (three cold
reset assert/release pairs); the bench boot-gate control `tb_hold_ext_boot` (the bench's own
`ext_boot_seq_done_i` control, held 1 from time 0 so `ext_boot_seq_done` reads 0); a passive sampler
on every `clk_smc_i` edge of `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n`
(the `smc_fuse_reset_n_delayed_o` path), `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` and `ext_boot_seq_done`; the eFuse
bank is the DV model; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_ext_boot`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: Delayed fuse reset waits for sense done and boot release.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_fuse_reset_n_delayed_o` is the fuse reset after 16 pipeline stages, and `ext_boot_seq_done_i`
  is the external boot completion that pauses reset release until it is raised
  (`hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc`, port rows; `doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface).
* The fuse reset is one term of the warm reset equation and holds warm reset until the fuse-control
  path releases it (`hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`, reset sources table and reset equations).
* With the boot gate held low the delayed fuse reset stays 0 through sense done and 64 further
  edges, while `STATUS.efuse_sense_done` reads 1 and then stays 1
  (`hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl`).
* After the boot gate is raised the delayed fuse reset rises at least 16 edges later and not before;
  the exact edge count is measured and printed, because the documented stage count is not stated
  as an exact latency including the input synchroniser.
* With the boot gate already high at the cold-reset release the delayed fuse reset waits for sense
  done and then rises at least 16 edges later.
* The level of the delayed fuse reset after the boot gate drops again is recorded only; the
  specification does not state the value and nothing is asserted about it.
* A further cold reset returns the delayed fuse reset to 0 and it rises again only after the second
  sense done and the raised boot gate.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `tb_hold_ext_boot` to be 1, wait up to 200000 clocks for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, and start
  the per-edge sampler.
. Collect 8 samples and require `tb_fuse_reset_n` and the boot gate to read 0 on all of them and
  sense done to be 1.
. Run cold reset 1 (assert, check the reset state, wait for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low, release,
  wait for the release), start the `STATUS` read stream, wait for sense done, collect 64 more edges,
  and require `tb_fuse_reset_n` and the boot gate to read 0 on every edge from the assertion to the
  end of that window. Stop the stream after a `STATUS` read of 1 and require every later read to
  be 1.
. Set `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 0, wait up to 16 edges for the boot gate to read 1 and up to 2000 edges
  for `tb_fuse_reset_n` to rise; require it to read 0 from the edge before the write up to the rise
  and the rise to come at least 16 edges after the boot gate. Record the warm reset edge.
. Run cold reset 2 with the boot gate still high, wait for sense done and for the rise of
  `tb_fuse_reset_n`; require the boot gate to read 1 from the release to the rise, the fuse reset to
  read 0 before it, the rise to come after sense done and at least 16 edges later; print the count
  next to the earlier one without comparing them.
. Set `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 1, wait up to 16 edges for the boot gate to read 0, collect 64 edges
  with the boot gate low and record the levels of `tb_fuse_reset_n` and the first change edge.
. Run cold reset 3 and require `tb_fuse_reset_n` to read 0 within 256 edges of the assertion and
  on every edge until the release; wait for sense done, collect 32 quiet edges with the fuse reset
  and boot gate both 0, set `tb_hold_ext_boot` to 0 and wait for the boot gate to rise and then the
  fuse reset to rise; require the rise to be after both sense done and the boot gate and the fuse
  reset to read 0 before it.
. Require the six steps in order with increasing time stamps, increasing fence edges, the checker
  lines in the order printed, and the SEP_IN access count at or above the number of `STATUS` reads;
  print the fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FRST-HELD-LOW` |`tb_fuse_reset_n` reads 0 on every sampled edge from the cold reset
assertion through sense done and 64 further edges with the boot gate held low, and
`STATUS.efuse_sense_done` reads 1 in that window and never returns to 0.
|`CHK-FRST-16-STAGE` |After the boot gate rises, `tb_fuse_reset_n` is 0 on every earlier edge
and rises at least 16 edges later (the 16 pipeline stages of `smc_fuse_reset_n_delayed_o`); the
exact edge count and the warm reset edge are measured and printed.
|`CHK-FRST-EARLY-BOOT` |With the boot gate high from the cold-reset release, `tb_fuse_reset_n`
stays 0 until sense done and rises at least 16 edges after it; the count is printed beside the
count after the boot gate without being compared with it.
|`CHK-FRST-BOOT-DROP` |After `tb_hold_ext_boot` is set to 1 the boot gate reads 0 and stays 0 for
64 edges; the level of `tb_fuse_reset_n` over that window is recorded without comparing it to an
expected level, because the specification does not state the value.
|`CHK-FRST-COLD-REARM` |Under the third cold reset `tb_fuse_reset_n` reads 0 and stays 0 to the
release, through sense done and 32 quiet edges with the boot gate low, and rises again only after
the second sense done and the raised boot gate.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (cold assert, sense done with boot low, boot rise, fuse reset
release, early-boot run, boot drop, second cold reset, second release) as strictly increasing
measured edges, with each checker line printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every sampler wait, reset wait and read-stream wait is bounded and fails
with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last samples are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold: `tb_fuse_reset_n` is 0 while the boot gate is low and
before sense done, rises at least 16 edges after the later of the two, returns to 0 under a cold
reset and rises only after the second sense done and boot gate, and `STATUS.efuse_sense_done`
reads 1 and stays 1 once seen. The exact stage count and the level after the boot drop are recorded
only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The exact edge count from the boot-gate rise, and from sense done, to the rise of the
delayed fuse reset is measured and printed without a compare, because the documented 16-stage count
is not stated as an exact latency including the input synchroniser; the two counts are printed
beside each other without being compared. The level of the delayed fuse reset after the boot gate
drops again is recorded only, because the specification does not state the value.

'''''

[[sec-455-smc_efuse_map_concurrency_test]]
===== 455 `smc_efuse_map_concurrency_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_concurrency_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`s_axi`, single items and outstanding groups); the JTAG AXI-Lite
master `ej_axi` on `axil_smc_otp_jtag_req_i` / `axil_smc_otp_jtag_resp_o` (bounded at 400 ns per
access); a passive bus monitor on the falling edge of `clk_smc_i` over `s_axi_arvalid`,
`s_axi_arready`, `s_axi_arid`, `s_axi_araddr`, `s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_rready`, `s_axi_rid`,
`s_axi_rdata`, `s_axi_awvalid`, `s_axi_awready`, `s_axi_awaddr` and the matching `ej_axi_*` read
signals; the wait probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the
eFuse bank is the DV model, loaded from the image the leaf writes into the run directory under
`+smc_efuse_hex` (`LOCKS` 0, every other word a distinct marker word); an EFUSE protocol-VIP record
is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_concurrency_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Overlapping SEP_IN and JTAG map accesses return exact data.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SMC_EFUSE_MAP shadow window is reachable from the SEP_IN path and from the eFuse OTP/JTAG
  AXI-Lite port (`hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc`, `axil_smc_otp_jtag_req_i` row;
  `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`).
* SPARE[0] word 0 (map word 32) and SPARE[1] word 0 (map word 40) are the addresses used; the
  shadow holds the loaded image word until written
  (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`).
* Two reads of one word started on the same clock edge from SEP_IN and JTAG both complete and both
  return the image word; the arbitration order between the two ports is not specified and is only
  printed.
* A SEP_IN write and a JTAG read of the same word started together both complete, the JTAG read
  returns the image word or the written pattern and no other value, and a later SEP_IN read returns
  the written pattern.
* `LOCKS.spare0_write_lock` (bit 8, write-one-to-set) locks SPARE[0] against writes, and the
  hardware-and-software lock rules apply (`smc_efuse_map.rdl`, reg `LOCKS`; `architecture.adoc`,
  Hardware vs. Software Locks): sixteen back-to-back SEP_IN writes alternating between the locked
  SPARE[0] word 0 and the unlocked SPARE[1] word 0 leave the locked word unchanged and keep the last
  write of the unlocked word. The response code of the dropped writes is reported, not asserted (OKAY in the kept run).
* Eight SEP_IN reads of eight distinct SPARE words issued as one outstanding group return their
  eight responses in request order, each equal to its image word, with a measured outstanding depth
  above one; the depth the interconnect accepts is not specified.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Before the run the image is generated into the run directory; require its `LOCKS` words and
  image shape (distinct marker words, fresh test patterns), wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within
  200000 clocks, idle the `ej_axi` inputs, create the JTAG master and start the bus monitor.
. On one `clk_smc_i` edge start a SEP_IN read and a JTAG read of SPARE[0] word 0; require both to
  complete OKAY with the image word, the two start times to be equal and both address handshakes
  to be seen; print the handshake offset in cycles.
. On one edge start a SEP_IN write of pattern X (0xC3A5_1E7B) to SPARE[0] word 0 and a JTAG read of
  the same word; require the SEP_IN write to complete OKAY, the JTAG read to return the image word
  or X, and a later SEP_IN read to return X.
. Error injection. Point: SPARE[0] word 0 over SEP_IN, after `LOCKS.spare0_write_lock` is written
  with a 64-bit write and both `LOCKS` words are read back (low word equal to the bit, high word 0).
  Kind: sixteen writes issued as one SEP_IN group, alternating between the write-locked SPARE[0]
  word 0 (errors allowed) and the unlocked SPARE[1] word 0. Expected response: the AW handshake
  addresses alternate in order, the unlocked writes complete OKAY, SPARE[0] word 0 still reads X and
  SPARE[1] word 0 reads the last pattern written to it. Print the AW gaps, the AW sampler counts and
  the locked-write responses.
. Issue eight SEP_IN reads of SPARE[2] to SPARE[9] word 0 as one group; require the AR handshake
  addresses in request order, eight OKAY responses in request order with each image word and a measured peak outstanding depth above one.
. Require the five steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the floor; print the fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-CONC-SAME-READ` |Simultaneous SEP_IN and JTAG reads of SPARE[0] word 0 both complete
with OKAY and both return the image word; the offset between their address handshakes is printed.
|`CHK-EMAP-CONC-WR-RD` |A SEP_IN write of X racing a JTAG read of the same word completes on both
paths, the JTAG read returns the image word or X, and a later SEP_IN read returns X; which of the
two the JTAG read saw is printed.
|`CHK-EMAP-CONC-ALTERNATE` |After `LOCKS.spare0_write_lock` is set, sixteen alternating back-to-back
writes leave the locked SPARE[0] word 0 at X and the unlocked SPARE[1] word 0 at the last value
written; the response code of the dropped writes is printed without being compared (OKAY in the kept run).
|`CHK-EMAP-CONC-OUTSTANDING` |Eight outstanding SEP_IN reads return eight OKAY responses in
request order, each equal to its image word, with a measured peak depth above one.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (same-edge reads, write racing read, alternating writes,
outstanding reads) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step
completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every sense wait, SEP_IN access and JTAG read is bounded and fails with an
assertion on expiry; the bounds and the last bus states are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold: both ports return the image word for the same-edge reads,
the racing JTAG read returns only the image word or X and the final value is X, the locked word
keeps X while the unlocked word keeps its last write across sixteen alternating writes, and the
eight outstanding reads return in order with their image words. Arbitration order, error codes and
the accepted depth are recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The arbitration order between the SEP_IN and JTAG ports for the same-edge reads is
only printed, because it is not specified. The response code of the writes dropped by the write lock
is reported, not asserted (OKAY in the kept run). The outstanding depth the interconnect accepts is
not specified; the peak depth is measured and only a depth above one is required.

'''''

[[sec-456-smc_efuse_map_layout_decode_test]]
===== 456 `smc_efuse_map_layout_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_layout_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (32-bit and 64-bit reads, one item inspected for beats and
transfer bytes, read and write error-response items); the wait probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the eFuse bank is the DV model, loaded from the
256-word marker image the leaf writes into the run directory under `+smc_efuse_hex` (every word
distinct, `LOCKS` 0x4000_0000_0000_0000); the generated SMC address map symbols for the map base,
size, region bases and SPARE and I2C_I3C_ID strides; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the
end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_layout_decode_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Map layout, read widths and past-extent decode match.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SMC_EFUSE_MAP register layout: `LOCKS` at 0x0, `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` at 0x8 (eight words),
  nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements at 0x28 plus 8 per element, `SMC_CONFIG` at 0x70,
  `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` at 0x78 and 28 `SPARE` elements at 0x80 with a 0x20 stride, tiling the
  0x400-byte map (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`).
* Every one of the 256 words reads its own marker word with no gap or alias between adjacent
  regions, region-edge words included.
* The 64-bit registers read correctly as separate 32-bit halves and as one 64-bit access, with the
  high word above the low word, and `SMC_CONFIG` is read as one 32-bit access in a single beat
  (`smc_efuse_map.rdl`, reg `SMC_CONFIG`).
* Reads past the 0x400-byte map inside the 0x1000-byte aperture are answered by the past-extent
  responder with a read response of DECERR and data 0xBADCAB1E (`hw/sys/smc/regs/smc.rdl`,
  `smc_efuse_map` past-extent response). The specification does not state the extent of the range.
* Writes past the map are refused with an error response; `smc.rdl` declares SLVERR for them, and
  the leaf accepts either error code (the response must be above OKAY) and prints both response
  codes beside the declared name and code, so the printed codes show which one was returned. The
  read response and data are taken from the generated memory map.
* The past-extent accesses change no word and no lock bit.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the generated map symbols (size 0x400, region offsets and strides) and the marker image
  (256 distinct words, `LOCKS` words 0 and 0x4000_0000), then wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within
  200000 clocks.
. Read the eight `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` words at 0x08 to 0x24 and both words of the nine
  `I2C_I3C_ID` elements and require marker words 2 to 9 and 10 to 27, all 26 values distinct.
. Read `SMC_CONFIG` (0x70, 0x74) and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` (0x78, 0x7C) and require marker words
  28 to 31 and the two registers to differ.
. Read the first word of each of the 28 `SPARE` elements and the last words of `SPARE[0]` (0x9C) and
  `SPARE[27]` (0x3FC); require their marker words and all 30 values distinct.
. Read all 256 words at 4 times the word number and require each marker word.
. Read `LOCKS`, the nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements, `SMC_CONFIG` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` as
  separate 32-bit halves; require the marker halves and the two halves of each register to differ.
. Read `LOCKS` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` as single 64-bit accesses and require the high and low
  marker words in order.
. Read 0x70 as one 32-bit item and require one beat, four transfer bytes, OKAY and marker word 28.
. Error injection. Point: offsets 0x400 and 0xFFC over SEP_IN, past the 0x400-byte map inside the
  0x1000-byte aperture. Kind: past-extent reads. Expected response: DECERR with data 0xBADCAB1E on
  each. Before them, read 0x3FC and require marker word 255.
. Error injection. Point: offsets 0x400 and 0xFFC over SEP_IN. Kind: past-extent writes of
  0xFFFF_FFFF. Expected response: an error response on each (SLVERR or DECERR).
. Read all 256 words again and require the marker words, then read `LOCKS` and require 0x0 and
  0x4000_0000.
. Require the eleven steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the call count; print the fence and the waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-LAYOUT-JPI-I2C` |The eight `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` words at 0x08 to 0x24 read marker
words 2 to 9 and the nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements at 0x28 plus 8 per element (first 0x28, last 0x68)
read marker words 10 to 27, all 26 values pairwise distinct.
|`CHK-EMAP-LAYOUT-CFG-OCCP` |Offsets 0x70 to 0x7C read marker words 28 to 31 and the `SMC_CONFIG`
and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` values differ, so the two registers do not alias.
|`CHK-EMAP-LAYOUT-SPARE` |The first word of each `SPARE[k]` at 0x80 plus 0x20 per element reads its
marker word, `SPARE[0]` word 7 (0x9C) and the last mapped word 0x3FC read their marker words, and
the 30 values are distinct.
|`CHK-EMAP-LAYOUT-SWEEP` |All 256 words read their marker words, region-edge offsets included, so no
gap or alias exists.
|`CHK-EMAP-WIDTH-32` |Each 32-bit read of the low and high half of `LOCKS`, the nine
`I2C_I3C_ID` elements, `SMC_CONFIG` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` equals the matching marker half
and the two halves differ.
|`CHK-EMAP-WIDTH-64` |The 64-bit read of `LOCKS` returns marker word 1 above word 0 and the 64-bit
read of `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` returns word 31 above word 30.
|`CHK-EMAP-WIDTH-CFG` |The 32-bit read of 0x70 completes as one item with one beat, four transfer
bytes, OKAY and marker word 28.
|`CHK-EMAP-PAST-READ` |0x3FC reads marker word 255 with OKAY, and 0x400 and 0xFFC each answer with
a DECERR read response and data 0xBADCAB1E.
|`CHK-EMAP-PAST-WRITE` |A write of 0xFFFF_FFFF to 0x400 and to 0xFFC completes with an error
response (SLVERR or DECERR, any response above OKAY); the leaf prints the two response codes
beside the declared response name and code from the generated memory map, so the printed codes
show which one was returned; the exact code is not compared.
|`CHK-EMAP-PAST-NOCHANGE` |After the past-extent reads and writes all 256 words read their marker
words again and `LOCKS` reads 0x0000_0000 and 0x4000_0000, so no word and no lock bit changed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (sense done, layout, widths, past-extent read, past-extent
write, no-change sweep) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step
completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The post-image sense wait is bounded and fails with an assertion on expiry;
the bound and the last sense state are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twelve checkers hold: every word of the 256-word map reads its marker word at
32-bit and 64-bit width, the past-extent reads answer DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, the past-extent writes
get an error response, and no word or lock bit changes. The exact write error code and the extent of
the past-extent range are not asserted. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The exact error code of a past-extent write is not compared: `smc.rdl` declares
SLVERR, either error code above OKAY is accepted, and both response codes are printed beside the
declared name and code. The extent of the past-extent range is not stated by the specification and
is not asserted.

'''''

[[sec-457-smc_efuse_map_lock_field_enforce_test]]
===== 457 `smc_efuse_map_lock_field_enforce_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_lock_field_enforce_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (word reads and writes, 64-bit `LOCKS` writes, items that allow an
error response for rejected writes and read-locked reads); the shadow-register output port
`shadow_regs` (`shadow_regs_o`), or `efuse_shadow_probe_o` with `tb_efuse_locks` when the packed
struct cannot be read as one value; the word probe `efuse_shadow_probe_o` (32 bits per map word);
the wait probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the eFuse bank
is the DV model, loaded from an all-zero image the leaf writes into the run directory under
`+smc_efuse_hex`; the per-word software model of the shadow held by the sequence; an EFUSE
protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_lock_field_enforce_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the 32-bit field values written.

*Objective*: Each field's write and read locks are enforced.

*Test Coverage*:

* `LOCKS` holds a write lock and a read lock for each lockable field, set by writing 1 and never
  cleared by software (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`, reg `LOCKS`,
  `onwrite = woset`; `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, Hardware vs. Software Locks).
* A write lock holds the whole field against writes: all eight words of SPARE[0], SPARE[27] and
  `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` and all 18 words of `I2C_I3C_ID` keep their value after a write
  (`smc_efuse_map.rdl`: one lock bit covers the whole field).
* Neighbouring fields (SPARE[1], SPARE[26]) stay writable while their neighbours are locked.
* A read lock hides the whole field: reads of a read-locked word return neither the stored value
  nor its complement. The response code of a read-locked read is not asserted.
* A read lock alone does not reject a write: the write lands in the shadow, and a write lock plus
  read lock together leave the shadow unchanged.
* The shadow-register output port does not change across rejected writes or hidden reads
  (`hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc`, `shadow_regs_o` row); what the port is specified to show for
  a locked field is not specified and only its stability is checked.
* The response code of a rejected write is not asserted; only its effect on the shadow is.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the lock bit masks against the named `LOCKS` bits (SPARE[0] bits 8 and 9, SPARE[1] bit 11,
  SPARE[27] bit 62, `I2C_I3C_ID` bits 2 and 3, `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` bits 0 and 1) and the field
  sizes, wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within 200000 clocks and read both `LOCKS` words as 0.
. Positive control: write a fresh distinct random word to every word of SPARE[0], SPARE[1],
  SPARE[27], `I2C_I3C_ID` and `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` and read each back.
. Error injection. Point: every word of SPARE[0] and SPARE[27] over SEP_IN, after their write locks
  are set and `LOCKS` is read back. Kind: a new pattern written to all words of both write-locked
  fields, with the shadow port sampled before and after. Expected response: the shadow port is
  unchanged and the locked words read back at their S2 values. Write and read back new patterns in
  SPARE[1] and SPARE[26].
. Error injection. Point: the 18 words of `I2C_I3C_ID` over SEP_IN, after its write lock is set.
  Kind: a new pattern written to all 18 words of the write-locked field. Expected response: the
  words read back at their earlier values.
. Error injection. Point: the eight words of `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` over SEP_IN, after its write
  lock is set. Kind: a new pattern written to all eight words of the write-locked field. Expected
  response: the words read back at their earlier values.
. Error injection. Point: the words of SPARE[1], then the 18 words of `I2C_I3C_ID`, over SEP_IN,
  with only the read lock of each set in turn. Kind: reads of read-locked words, and a write of a
  new pattern to SPARE[1] under its read lock alone. Expected response: each SPARE[1] word reads
  neither the stored value nor its complement with `efuse_shadow_probe_o` equal to the model, the
  SPARE[1] write lands (probe equals the pattern), and the 18 `I2C_I3C_ID` words read as hidden with
  the shadow port, sampled before those reads, unchanged.
. Error injection. Point: `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` and SPARE[0] over SEP_IN, after their read locks
  are set on top of their write locks. Kind: reads of both doubly locked fields, a new pattern
  written to each, then reads again. Expected response: both fields read hidden with the probe
  equal to the model, the probe is unchanged by the writes, and both fields read hidden again.
. Require the seven steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the call count; print the fence and the waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-ENF-WR-SPARE` |With the SPARE[0] and SPARE[27] write locks set, all 16 words of the two
fields reject a new pattern and read their earlier value.
|`CHK-EMAP-ENF-NEIGHBOUR` |SPARE[1] and SPARE[26], the neighbours of the locked fields, accept a new
pattern and read it back on all 16 words.
|`CHK-EMAP-ENF-PORT` |The shadow output port is bit-identical before and after the rejected writes
and across the hidden reads; the port mode, value count and digests are printed.
|`CHK-EMAP-WHOLE-I2C-WR` |With the single `I2C_I3C_ID` write lock set, all 18 words keep their
earlier value after a write.
|`CHK-EMAP-WHOLE-I2C-RD` |With the single `I2C_I3C_ID` read lock set, all 18 words read neither
their stored value nor its complement.
|`CHK-EMAP-WHOLE-JPI` |The `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` write lock holds all eight words against a write
and its read lock hides all eight words.
|`CHK-EMAP-WHOLE-SPARE` |The SPARE[0] write lock holds all eight words against a write and its read
lock hides all eight words.
|`CHK-EMAP-PAIR-RDONLY` |With only the SPARE[1] read lock set, reads hide the stored value and
complement, and a write is not rejected: `efuse_shadow_probe_o` shows the new pattern.
|`CHK-EMAP-PAIR-BOTH` |With write and read locks both set on `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` and SPARE[0],
reads hide the value before and after a further write and `efuse_shadow_probe_o` does not change.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (baseline, write locks, read-only locks, both locks) with
increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The post-image sense wait is bounded and fails with an assertion on expiry;
the bound and the last sense state are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eleven checkers hold: a write-locked field keeps all its words, an unlocked
neighbour accepts its write, a read-locked field discloses neither value nor complement, a read lock
alone leaves writes landing, both locks together leave the probe unchanged, and the shadow port is
stable across rejected writes and hidden reads. Response codes of rejected and hidden accesses are
not asserted. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code of a rejected write and of a read-locked read is not asserted; only
the effect on the shadow is. What the shadow-register output port is specified to show for a locked
field is not specified, so only its stability across rejected writes and hidden reads is checked.

'''''

[[sec-458-smc_efuse_map_locks_register_test]]
===== 458 `smc_efuse_map_locks_register_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_locks_register_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (32-bit and 64-bit `LOCKS` accesses, field word reads and writes,
items that allow an error response for rejected writes and read-locked reads); the reset agent
(cold reset assert and release); `efuse_shadow_probe_o` read as 32 bits per map word; the wait
probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the eFuse bank is the DV
model, loaded from an image the leaf writes into the run directory under `+smc_efuse_hex` (every
field 0, `LOCKS` 0x4000_0000_0000_0000); the sequence's 64-bit `LOCKS` model and per-word shadow
model; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_locks_register_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the slot order and the fresh field values written before
each lock.

*Objective*: LOCKS sets by write-one and each slot locks its field.

*Test Coverage*:

* `LOCKS` is a 64-bit register of write-one-to-set bits: slot n holds a write lock at bit 2n and a
  read lock at bit 2n+1, for 32 slots, slots 0 to 3 for `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY`, `I2C_I3C_ID`,
  `SMC_CONFIG` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` and slots 4 to 31 for SPARE[0] to SPARE[27]
  (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`, reg `LOCKS`).
* The sensed value of `LOCKS` is the image value, and a cold reset restores it
  (`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, Hardware vs. Software Locks: software locks are set by
  writing 1 and cannot be loosened without a reset).
* The low and high 32-bit halves can be set by separate 32-bit writes, a repeated write of a set bit
  changes nothing, and one 64-bit write sets several bits across both halves.
* All 64 bits are set one lock at a time in a seeded random slot order; each write lock rejects
  writes to its own field only, and each read lock hides the first word of its own field.
* Fields not yet locked keep accepting writes after another slot's lock is set.
* With every lock set, a write to a field is still rejected as seen on `efuse_shadow_probe_o`.
* The response codes of rejected writes and hidden reads are not asserted.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the 32 regions against the lock bit masks (write lock 2n, read lock 2n+1) and the image
  (`LOCKS` words 0 and 0x4000_0000, every other word 0), then wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within
  200000 clocks.
. Read both `LOCKS` words and require the image values.
. Error injection. Point: every word of every field over SEP_IN, SPARE[27] included, whose write
  lock the image sets. Kind: a fresh random word written to every word, the write-locked SPARE[27]
  among them. Expected response: every unlocked word reads back against the model and SPARE[27]
  keeps its value.
. Write 1 to the low `LOCKS` word with a 32-bit write and read both words back; write 1 to the high
  word and read both words back; each compare is against the model that ORs in the written bits.
. Repeat the write of 1 to the low word and require `LOCKS` unchanged.
. Write 0x0000_0002_0000_0010 as one 64-bit write; read both words and read the register as 64 bits;
  require the model.
. Run a cold reset, wait for the sense, require `LOCKS` to read the image values, and re-apply the
  random patterns to every field.
. Error injection. Point: each slot's own field over SEP_IN, in a seeded shuffled slot order, after
  the slot's write lock and later its read lock are set with 64-bit `LOCKS` writes, `LOCKS` being
  read against the model after each. Kind: fresh words written to the write-locked field, then a
  read of the field's first word under its read lock. Expected response: the locked field's words
  keep their value (read back over SEP_IN, or compared with `efuse_shadow_probe_o` when its read
  lock is already set), and the first word reads neither its value nor its complement. Between the
  two locks, write and read back every field that is still unlocked, and check once that the probe
  word equals the field and differs from its mirror word. Finish with `LOCKS` reading all ones.
. Error injection. Point: `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` word 0 over SEP_IN, with every lock set. Kind: a
  fresh word written to the locked word. Expected response: its `efuse_shadow_probe_o` word,
  required beforehand to equal the model and be non-zero, is unchanged.
. Run a cold reset, wait for the sense and require `LOCKS` to read the image values.
. Require the nine steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the floor; print the fence and the waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCKS-SENSED` |After the sense, `LOCKS` reads the image words 0x0000_0000 and
0x4000_0000.
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCKS-HALVES` |A 32-bit write of 1 to the low word and one to the high word each set only
the written bit, and both halves read the model value after each write.
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCKS-IDEMPOTENT` |Repeating the write of 1 to the low word leaves both halves unchanged.
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCKS-WIDE` |One 64-bit write of 0x0000_0002_0000_0010 sets exactly those bits on top of
the earlier ones, and the two 32-bit reads and the 64-bit read all return the model value.
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCKS-BITWISE` |All 64 bits (the bit the image presets being a no-op write) are set one
at a time in the printed seeded order and `LOCKS` equals the model after every write, ending at all
ones; after the cold reset `LOCKS` reads the image words again.
|`CHK-EMAP-SLOT-MAP` |For each of the 32 slots the write lock at bit 2n makes its own field reject
writes (read back unchanged, or unchanged on `efuse_shadow_probe_o` when the read lock is already
set) and the read lock at bit 2n+1 makes the first word of its field read neither value nor
complement.
|`CHK-EMAP-SLOT-ISOLATION` |After each lock is set, the fields that are not yet locked still accept
a write and read it back.
|`CHK-EMAP-LOCK-PERSIST` |With every lock set, a write to `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` word 0 leaves its
`efuse_shadow_probe_o` word unchanged.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (sensed, halves, idempotent, wide, re-sense, bitwise; slot map,
persistence, reset) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step
completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every sense wait is bounded and fails with an assertion on expiry; the bounds
and the last sense states are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all ten checkers hold: `LOCKS` follows the write-one-to-set model after every
32-bit, 64-bit and per-slot write, each slot's write and read lock affect only its own field, the
unlocked fields keep accepting writes, a locked field stays unchanged on the probe, and a cold reset
restores the image value of `LOCKS`. Response codes of rejected writes and hidden reads are not
asserted. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response codes of rejected writes and hidden reads are not asserted; only their
effect on the field, read back over SEP_IN or seen on `efuse_shadow_probe_o`, is.

'''''

[[sec-459-smc_efuse_map_reset_persistence_test]]
===== 459 `smc_efuse_map_reset_persistence_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_reset_persistence_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (word and `LOCKS` reads and writes, items that allow an error
response, and mid-reset reads bounded at 50000 ns that may end without a response); the reset
agent (cold reset assert and release); the bench JTAG reset-control override `tb_jtag_reset_ctrl`
(the `warm_reset_n_ovrd` and `warm_reset_n_val` bits drive the warm reset); passive probes
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`, `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n`, `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`,
`s_axi_rvalid`, `s_axi_arvalid` and `s_axi_arready` sampled on `clk_smc_i`; the eFuse bank is the DV
model, loaded from an image the leaf writes into the run directory under `+smc_efuse_hex` (every
word 0 except SPARE[5] word 0, which holds the marker 0x5A5A_1234);
an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_reset_persistence_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Shadow words and locks survive warm reset, not cold.

*Test Coverage*:

* The eFuse bank is sensed once per cold boot, when the primary reset is released; CPU and warm
  resets do not repeat the sense (`doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface, sensing once
  per cold boot).
* A warm reset (`rst_warm_n` is a term of the warm reset equation, `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`)
  leaves the shadow words and the `LOCKS` bits unchanged: SPARE[3] keeps its pattern under its
  write lock and SPARE[4] word 0 stays hidden under its read lock
  (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`, reg `LOCKS`).
* `tb_fuse_sense_done` stays 1 on every sample from 100 edges before to 2000 edges after the warm
  reset, so the bank is not re-sensed.
* A cold reset clears the lock bits and the written patterns and re-senses the image, so the word
  holding the marker reads the marker again after the reset although a different pattern was
  written to it, and writes to the same fields land again.
* A SEP_IN read outstanding when a warm reset or a cold reset reaches the DUT either completes with
  OKAY or is aborted by the reset flush without a response, within a bound and without a driver
  timeout; the next `LOCKS` read after release returns the expected value, and no read data beat
  appears after a cold reset until the next read is accepted. Which of the two outcomes occurs is
  recorded, and the controller's handling of a request withdrawn mid-command is outside this test.
* The response code of the rejected write and of the hidden read is not asserted.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the SPARE[3] words 56 to 63, SPARE[4] word 64, the lock masks (SPARE[3] write lock bit 14,
  SPARE[4] read lock bit 17), the override width and the image (all words 0 except the SPARE[5]
  marker word), wait for
  `tb_fuse_sense_done` within 200000 clocks and read `LOCKS` as 0.
. Write P1 (0xA5C3_1E71) to the eight SPARE[3] words and P2 (0x3C69_D2B4) to SPARE[4] word 0, read
  them back, read SPARE[5] word 0 and require the marker, write 0xE2B4_6D09 to it and read it
  back, write `LOCKS` bits 14 and 17 as one 64-bit write and require `LOCKS` to read 0x24000
  and 0.
. Start the `tb_fuse_sense_done` sampler and wait for 100 samples. Assert the warm reset by
  setting the override bits (bounded at 64 edges for `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to fall), clear the
  override and wait up to 50000 edges for it to rise; read all eight SPARE[3] words and require P1.
. Error injection. Point: SPARE[3] word 0 (write-locked) and SPARE[4] word 0 (read-locked) over
  SEP_IN, after the warm reset. Kind: a write of P3 (0x5AE1_7C93) to the write-locked word and a
  read of the read-locked word. Expected response: SPARE[3] word 0 still reads P1 and SPARE[4]
  word 0 reads neither P2 nor its complement. Read `LOCKS` and require 0x24000 and 0.
. Wait for the sampler to cover 2000 edges after the release; require no 1-to-0 transition and no
  sample of 0 across the window, and SPARE[3] word 0 still P1.
. Start a SEP_IN `LOCKS` read, assert the warm reset two edges later through the override and
  release it; require the read to be outstanding at the fall, whether it then completes with OKAY or
  is aborted by the reset flush, within 200000 edges and with no driver timeout; read `LOCKS` and
  require 0x24000 and 0.
. Run a cold reset (assert, release, wait for the sense); require `LOCKS` to read 0 and 0 and all
  eight SPARE[3] words to read 0 and SPARE[5] word 0 to read the marker 0x5A5A_1234; write P3 to SPARE[3] word 0 and P4 (0xC7D2_0B58) to SPARE[4] word
  0 and read both back.
. Write the SPARE[3] write lock again and read `LOCKS` back, send the cold reset assertion, and
  re-issue SEP_IN `LOCKS` reads back to back until one is aborted or the primary reset falls; watch
  `s_axi_rvalid` from the fall to the next accepted read request. Release the reset, wait for the
  sense and require `LOCKS` to read 0 and 0, no `s_axi_rvalid` sample in the watch window and an
  accepted read request after the release.
. Require the eight steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the floor; print the fence and the waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-WARM-VALUES` |After the warm reset through the JTAG override all eight SPARE[3] words
still read P1; the edges to the fall and the rise of `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` are printed.
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-WARM-LOCKS` |After the warm reset `LOCKS` reads 0x00024000, the SPARE[3] write lock
rejects P3 (the word still reads P1) and SPARE[4] word 0 reads neither P2 nor its complement; the
write response code is printed without being compared.
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-WARM-NORESENSE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` reads 1 on every sample from 100 edges before
to 2000 edges after the warm reset with no 1-to-0 transition, and SPARE[3] word 0 still reads P1.
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-WARM-MID` |A SEP_IN `LOCKS` read with the warm reset asserted two edges later is
outstanding at the fall and then either completes with OKAY or is aborted by the reset flush,
within 200000 edges and with no driver timeout, and `LOCKS` reads 0x00024000 after the release;
which outcome occurred is printed, and the line always carries the fixed text `orphan_r=n/a`
whatever the outcome.
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-COLD-LOCKS` |After the cold reset and sense done `LOCKS` reads 0 on both words, all
eight SPARE[3] words read 0, SPARE[5] word 0 reads the sensed marker, and P3 and P4 written to SPARE[3] word 0 and SPARE[4] word 0 read back.
|`CHK-EMAP-RST-COLD-MID` |Back-to-back SEP_IN `LOCKS` reads over a cold reset each complete or are
aborted by the reset flush within 200000 edges with no driver timeout, no read data beat is
presented between the primary reset fall and the next accepted read request, and `LOCKS` reads 0
and 0 after the release and sense; which outcome occurred is printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (setup, warm values, warm locks, warm no re-sense, warm mid-read,
cold locks, cold mid-read) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step
completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every sense wait, warm reset edge wait, mid-reset read bound and the
sampler window is bounded and fails with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last states are
logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eight checkers hold: SPARE[3] keeps P1, `LOCKS` keeps 0x00024000 and SPARE[4]
word 0 stays hidden across the warm reset with `tb_fuse_sense_done` never dropping; after the cold
reset `LOCKS` and SPARE[3] read 0, SPARE[5] word 0 reads the marker again and writes land; and each mid-reset read ends within its bound
with no driver timeout and no stray data beat. The write response code and the completed-or-aborted
outcome are recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code of the rejected write and of the hidden read is not asserted; the
write response code is printed. Whether a SEP_IN read outstanding at the warm or the cold reset
completes with OKAY or is aborted by the reset flush is recorded, not asserted, and the controller's
handling of a request withdrawn mid-command is outside this test.

'''''

[[sec-460-smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test]]
===== 460 `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (word reads compared with the image); the reset agent (cold reset
assert and release); a passive sampler on every `clk_smc_i` edge of `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` and
`tb_fuse_sense_done` that captures `efuse_shadow_probe_o` (256 words of 32 bits) on each 0 to 1
edge of sense done; the shadow-register output port `shadow_regs` (`shadow_regs_o`) read as one
8192-bit integer; the eFuse bank is the DV model, loaded from the image file the run senses (the
bench default asset by default, or an image the leaf writes into the run directory under
`+smc_efuse_hex` when `+smc_efuse_image` names the zero, ones, walking, random or unique pattern);
an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry per cell: `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` (this module, the default
cell) and the variant entries `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_zero_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=zero`),
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_ones_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=ones`),
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_walking_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=walking`),
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=random`),
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=unique`), each a module of its own in
`testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`,
`efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the default eFuse image; the other image kinds run as
fixed-cell variant modules.

*Objective*: Sensed image words match the loaded file on every path.

*Test Coverage*:

* After a cold reset, `tb_fuse_sense_done` (`smc_fuse_sense_done_o`) stays 0 until the sense
  finishes and rises once; on that first rise `efuse_shadow_probe_o` already holds the whole image
  (`doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface, sensing once per cold boot;
  `hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc`, `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` row).
* All 256 words of the SMC_EFUSE_MAP shadow, including the `LOCKS` words, read over SEP_IN as the
  image words, and the probe still equals the image after the sweep
  (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`).
* The sense-done signal does not drop and does not rise a second time over a window of 2000 edges
  that contains 64 reads spread over the unlocked words.
* The shadow-register output port carries the sensed words, word n at bits 32n to 32n+31
  (`port_table.adoc`, `shadow_regs_o` row). What the port is specified to show for read-locked
  words is not specified: those words are observed and not compared.
* The pattern kinds select the image: the default asset, zero, ones, walking one, random and
  pairwise-distinct (unique) words; the zero kind carries 0 in every data word and the lowest
  write-lock bit in `LOCKS` word 0, so the `LOCKS` compares tell a sensed image from a reset value.
  Only write-lock bits are ever set in the generated `LOCKS` words, so no word is read-locked in a
  generated image.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the image to hold 256 words (pairwise distinct for the unique kind), wait for
  `tb_fuse_sense_done` within 200000 clocks, start the sampler and let it take 4 samples.
. Print the image name, kind, seed and `LOCKS`; send the cold reset assertion, check the reset
  state, wait for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low, require 8 samples with the reset low and sense done
  0, release the reset and wait for the release.
. Wait for the first rise of `tb_fuse_sense_done` (bounded at 200000 edges), require sense done 0
  on every sample from the reset to that rise and the 256 captured probe words to equal the image;
  then wait for the warm domain to be released.
. Read every word that is not read-locked over SEP_IN and require the image word; require words 0
  and 255 to be read; require the probe to equal the image again.
. For the unique kind only: after one more edge require all 256 probe words to equal the image.
. Issue 64 reads spread over the unlocked words inside a 2000-edge window, wait for the window to
  end, and require sense done 1 on every sample of the window and from the first rise onward and
  exactly one 0 to 1 transition since the release.
. Read `shadow_regs` and require every word that is not read-locked to equal the image; when no word
  is read-locked, require the whole port to equal the packed image; print the port value of any
  read-locked word.
. Require the steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order printed
  and the SEP_IN access count at or above the call count; print the fence and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-FIRST-DONE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` is 0 on every sample from the cold reset to the
edge before its first rise, rises after the release, and all 256 words of `efuse_shadow_probe_o`
captured on that rise equal the image.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DEFAULT` |For the default image, every SEP_IN read of a non-read-locked word
equals the image word with words 0 and 255 included, and all 256 probe words equal the image again
after the sweep. The id varies with the configuration: `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-UNIQUE` for the unique kind
and `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-PATTERNS` for the zero, ones, walking and random kinds.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DONE-ONCE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` reads 1 on all 2000 samples of the window with 64
reads issued and on every sample from its first rise, with exactly one 0 to 1 transition since the
release.
|`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-SENSED` |The `shadow_regs` port equals the image word for word on every word
that is not read-locked, and as a whole when none is read-locked; read-locked words are printed
without a compare.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (image name, first done, sense image, done once, shadow output)
with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every reset wait, sense wait, window wait and SEP_IN read is bounded and
fails with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last samples are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: with the default image the six listed checkers hold (the sense-image checker is
`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DEFAULT`; the unique kind replaces it with `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-UNIQUE` and an extra
probe compare, and the other pattern kinds with `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-PATTERNS`): the probe, every SEP_IN
read and the `shadow_regs` port equal the image, and sense done rises once and never drops.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: What the shadow-register output port is specified to show for read-locked words is
not specified; those words are printed and not compared.

'''''
[[sec-461-smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test]]
===== 461 `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test`

*BFM / Model*: as `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`; the module fixes the image kind;
`+smc_efuse_image=unique` and `+smc_efuse_hex` in the testlist entry name the image and its file.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry, `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=unique`),
a fixed-cell variant entry of `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups
`all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_image=unique`, `+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_sense_image_unique_test.hex`; tool
Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, a fixed-cell variant; the eFuse image kind is pinned by the
module and its testlist entry.

*Objective*: Sensed image words match the loaded file on every path, in the unique eFuse image. Extends `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` with the unique image kind.

*Test Coverage*:

* The `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` procedure runs at the unique eFuse image, so a scheduled run
reaches this cell; its checks are those of the `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` card with this
cell's own checker ids.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. As `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`, with the cell fixed by the module.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DONE-ONCE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` reads 1 on all 2000 samples of the window with 64
reads issued and on every sample from its first rise, with exactly one 0 to 1 transition since the
release.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-FIRST-DONE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` is 0 on every sample from the cold reset to the
edge before its first rise, rises after the release, and all 256 words of `efuse_shadow_probe_o`
captured on that rise equal the image.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-UNIQUE` |For the unique image every SEP_IN read of a non-read-locked word equals
the image word with words 0 and 255 included, and all 256 probe words equal the image again after
the sweep.
|`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-SENSED` |The `shadow_regs` port equals the image word for word on every word
that is not read-locked, and as a whole when none is read-locked; read-locked words are printed
without a compare.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (image name, first done, sense image, done once, shadow output)
with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every reset wait, sense wait, window wait and SEP_IN read is bounded and fails
with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last samples are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DONE-ONCE`, `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-FIRST-DONE`, `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-UNIQUE`,
`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-SENSED`, `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled
in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Read-locked words on the `shadow_regs` port are printed without a compare, as in
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`.

'''''

[[sec-462-smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test]]
===== 462 `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test`

*BFM / Model*: as `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`; the module fixes the image kind;
`+smc_efuse_image=random` and `+smc_efuse_hex` in the testlist entry name the image and its file.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry, `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test` (`+smc_efuse_image=random`),
a fixed-cell variant entry of `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups
`all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_image=random`, `+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_sense_image_random_test.hex`; tool
Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RANDCFG: the seed draws the field words of the sensed image and the write-lock bits
of its `LOCKS` words; a fixed-cell variant whose cell is the `random` image kind.

*Objective*: Sensed image words match the loaded file on every path, in the random eFuse image. Extends `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` with the random image kind.

*Test Coverage*:

* The `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` procedure runs at the random eFuse image, so a scheduled run
reaches this cell; its checks are those of the `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` card with this
cell's own checker ids.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. As `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`, with the cell fixed by the module.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DONE-ONCE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` reads 1 on all 2000 samples of the window with 64
reads issued and on every sample from its first rise, with exactly one 0 to 1 transition since the
release.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-FIRST-DONE` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` is 0 on every sample from the cold reset to the
edge before its first rise, rises after the release, and all 256 words of `efuse_shadow_probe_o`
captured on that rise equal the image.
|`CHK-EMAP-SENSE-PATTERNS` |For this image every SEP_IN read of a non-read-locked word equals the
image word with words 0 and 255 included, and all 256 probe words equal the image again after the
sweep.
|`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-SENSED` |The `shadow_regs` port equals the image word for word on every word
that is not read-locked, and as a whole when none is read-locked; read-locked words are printed
without a compare.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (image name, first done, sense image, done once, shadow output)
with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every reset wait, sense wait, window wait and SEP_IN read is bounded and fails
with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last samples are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-DONE-ONCE`, `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-FIRST-DONE`, `CHK-EMAP-SENSE-PATTERNS`,
`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-SENSED`, `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled
in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Read-locked words on the `shadow_regs` port are printed without a compare, as in
`smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test`.

'''''

[[sec-466-smc_efuse_map_sep_write_test]]
===== 466 `smc_efuse_map_sep_write_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_map_sep_write_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (32-bit and 64-bit reads and writes, one read that must be answered
with an error response); the shadow-register output port `shadow_regs` (`shadow_regs_o`) read as
one 8192-bit integer; `efuse_shadow_probe_o` read as 32 bits per map word; `tb_efuse_locks`; the
wait probes `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; the eFuse bank is
the DV model, loaded from an all-zero image the leaf writes into the run directory under
`+smc_efuse_hex`; the sequence's per-word shadow model; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at
the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; args
`+smc_efuse_hex=smc_efuse_map_sep_write_test.hex`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the 32-bit values written, the 256-bit patterns and the
element order of the map walk.

*Objective*: Unlocked SEP_IN map writes read back and reach the shadow port.

*Test Coverage*:

* With no lock set, every writable class of SMC_EFUSE_MAP accepts SEP_IN writes and reads them
  back: `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` (eight words from 0x08), nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements (64-bit
  writes from 0x28), `SMC_CONFIG` (0x70), `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` (0x78) and 28 `SPARE` elements
  (eight words each from 0x80) (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl`).
* The reserved bits of `SMC_CONFIG` (bits 6:1, 14:8 and 63:16) and the upper word of
  `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` are software read-write fields and read back as written
  (`smc_efuse_map.rdl`, regs `SMC_CONFIG` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT`).
* A write changes only its own words: the word below and the word above every written range keep
  their model value, and the word past the last `SPARE` element is answered with the DECERR read response and the
  data 0xBADCAB1E that the generated memory map gives `smc_efuse_map`.
* Separate 32-bit writes to the two halves of a 64-bit register change only the half written.
* The shadow-register output port equals the written shadow, word n at bits 32n to 32n+31
  (`hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc`, `shadow_regs_o` row), with `efuse_shadow_probe_o` equal word
  for word and `tb_efuse_locks` 0. What the port is specified to show beyond the stored words is an
  not specified.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check the field sizes and offsets and the all-zero image, wait for `tb_fuse_sense_done` within
  200000 clocks, then read both `LOCKS` words, `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY`, `I2C_I3C_ID`, `SMC_CONFIG`,
  `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` and every `SPARE` word and require 0.
. For each of the eight `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` words write a fresh distinct pattern, read the word
  below and the word above (the high `LOCKS` word and the first `I2C_I3C_ID` word), and read the
  word back.
. For each of the nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements write a 64-bit pattern with bits 63:7 non-zero, read
  the neighbours (the last `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` word and `SMC_CONFIG`), read both halves and read
  the element as 64 bits.
. Write 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_7F7E to `SMC_CONFIG` and 0xA5A5_A5A5_5A5A_5A5A to `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT`
  as 64-bit writes, read both back as 64 bits and require the reserved bits and the whole values
  as written.
. Error injection. Point: the word past the map, directly after `SPARE[27]`, over SEP_IN. Kind: a
  past-extent read. Expected response: the DECERR read response and the data 0xBADCAB1E from the
  generated memory map. Before it, in a seeded shuffled order write a 256-bit pattern to each
  `SPARE` element as eight 32-bit writes, read each word back, and read the word below and above
  the element.
. Write 0x1234_5678 to the low word of `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` and require the high word unchanged;
  write 0x9ABC_DEF0 to the high word and require the low word unchanged.
. Read both `LOCKS` words, require the `shadow_regs` port to equal the packed model, require every
  `efuse_shadow_probe_o` word to equal the model and require `tb_efuse_locks` to be 0.
. Require the seven steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the call count; print the fence and the waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-JPI` |The eight `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` words each read back their own distinct
pattern.
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-I2C` |The nine `I2C_I3C_ID` elements accept 64-bit writes and read back both halves
and the 64-bit value, bits 63:7 included.
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-CFG-OCCP` |`SMC_CONFIG` and `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` read back as written, as 64-bit
values.
|`CHK-EMAP-RSVD-BITS` |The `SMC_CONFIG` reserved bits (6:1, 14:8 and 63:16) read back as written,
and the upper word of `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` is printed.
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-SPARE` |All 28 `SPARE` elements read back their 256-bit patterns after eight 32-bit
writes each, in the printed seeded order.
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-NEIGHBOUR` |Every word read below and above a written range keeps its model value
across the `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY`, `I2C_I3C_ID` and `SPARE` writes, and the read past the last
`SPARE` element returns the DECERR read response with the data 0xBADCAB1E.
|`CHK-EMAP-WR-HALVES` |A 32-bit write to one half of `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` changes that half and
leaves the other half unchanged, for each half in turn.
|`CHK-EMAP-SHADOW-OUT-WRITE` |The `shadow_regs` port equals the model word for word,
`efuse_shadow_probe_o` equals the model, and `tb_efuse_locks` is 0.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (zero image, `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY`, `I2C_I3C_ID`, config and
timeout, `SPARE`, halves, shadow output) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed
after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The post-image sense wait is bounded and fails with an assertion on expiry;
the bound and the last sense state are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all ten checkers hold: every written word reads back as written, no neighbour
word changes, the half writes touch only their half, the word past the map returns DECERR
with 0xBADCAB1E, and the shadow port, the word probe and `tb_efuse_locks` agree with the model.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: What the shadow-register output port is specified to show beyond the stored words is
not specified. The upper word of `OCCP_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT` is printed by the reserved-bits checker.

'''''

[[sec-467-smc_efuse_sense_sequence_test]]
===== 467 `smc_efuse_sense_sequence_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: EFUSE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_sense_sequence_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (a continuous `STATUS` read stream); the reset agent (one cold
reset assert/release); a passive sampler on every `clk_smc_i` edge of `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`,
`tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid`, `tb_efuse_shim_resp_valid` and `tb_fuse_sense_done`; the eFuse bank
behind the SHIM interface is the DV model; an EFUSE protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: Sense request, 256 strobes and hand-over follow the interface.

*Test Coverage*:

* After the primary reset is released the eFuse controller issues one sense request that reads the
  whole 256-word bank, and the SHIM answers with one `valid` strobe per word
  (`doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc`, eFuse Interface, SHIM read rules and sensing once per cold
  boot). The latency from the reset release to the first request is measured; no bound is asserted.
* `tb_fuse_sense_done` stays 0 from the cold reset through the last strobe, and
  `STATUS.efuse_sense_done` reads 0 on every read that completes before the port rises and 1 on
  every read issued after it (`hw/ip/efuse/regs/efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl`).
* The offset between the last strobe and the sense-done rise is measured and printed; the offset
  visible at the port is not specified.
* After sensing, the request `valid` stays high until the sense-done hand-over to the firmware path
  and falls two cycles after the last strobe, with no further request or strobe afterwards
  (`smu-smc.adoc`, When `valid` falls).
* The strobe spacing is logged only.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait up to 200000 clocks for `tb_fuse_sense_done`, start the sampler and let it take 4 samples.
. Send the cold reset assertion, check the reset state, wait for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low and
  require 8 samples with the reset low and `tb_fuse_sense_done` 0.
. Send the release, start the `STATUS` read stream, wait for the release, for the first
  `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` and for the first `tb_efuse_shim_resp_valid`; require exactly one rising
  edge of the request valid before the first strobe and record the release-to-request latency.
. Count `tb_efuse_shim_resp_valid` strobes until 256 are seen, requiring sense done 0 on every
  edge on the way, then wait for the rise of `tb_fuse_sense_done`; require the rise after the last
  strobe and exactly 256 strobes before it, and record the strobe gaps.
. Wait for a `STATUS` read to complete after the rise; require sense done 0 from the reset to the
  last strobe, every read completed before the rise to read `efuse_sense_done` 0 with at least one
  completed during the stream, and the first read after the release to read 0.
. Require the rise at least one cycle after the last strobe, wait for four `STATUS` reads issued
  after the rise, stop the stream and require all of them to read 1; record the reads straddling the
  rise.
. Wait for `tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` to fall and require it exactly two cycles after the last
  strobe; require the request valid and the strobe both 0 for 64 edges, and no strobe after the
  rise.
. Require the six steps in order with increasing time stamps, strictly ordered fence edges (the
  sense-done rise and the request-valid fall may be equal edges), the checker lines in the order
  printed and the SEP_IN access count at or above the number of `STATUS` reads; print the fence and
  the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SENSE-REQ-LATENCY` |`tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` rises exactly once between the reset release
and the first strobe; the number of cycles from the release to the first request is measured and
printed without a bound.
|`CHK-SENSE-STROBE-COUNT` |Exactly 256 `tb_efuse_shim_resp_valid` strobes occur before
`tb_fuse_sense_done` rises, and sense done is 0 on the cycle of the 256th strobe; the strobe gap
is logged only.
|`CHK-SENSE-DONE-LOW` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` is 0 on every sampled edge from the cold reset
assertion to the last strobe, and every `STATUS` read that completes before the rise reads
`efuse_sense_done` 0, with at least one read completing during the strobe stream.
|`CHK-SENSE-DONE-OFFSET` |`tb_fuse_sense_done` rises at least one cycle after the 256th strobe, the
offset is measured and printed, and four or more `STATUS` reads issued after the rise all read
`efuse_sense_done` 1; reads straddling the rise are printed without a compare.
|`CHK-SENSE-REQ-HANDOVER` |`tb_efuse_shim_cmd_valid` falls exactly two cycles after the last strobe
(`smu-smc.adoc`), stays 0 with `tb_efuse_shim_resp_valid` 0 for 64 edges while no command is issued,
and no strobe follows the sense-done rise.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (cold reset asserted, release, first request, first strobe, last
strobe, sense done, request valid low, quiet window) as measured edges, with each checker line
printed after its step completed.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every reset, request, strobe, sense-done and read wait is bounded and fails
with an assertion on expiry; the bounds and last samples are logged.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold: one request after the release, exactly 256 strobes
before sense done, `STATUS.efuse_sense_done` 0 before the rise and 1 after it, and the request
valid falling two cycles after the last strobe with a quiet interface afterwards. The
release-to-request latency, the strobe gaps and the sense-done offset are recorded only. Enrolled
in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The latency from the reset release to the first sense request is measured and printed
without a bound. The offset between the last strobe and the sense-done rise is measured and printed,
because the offset visible at the port is not specified. The strobe spacing is logged only, and the
`STATUS` reads straddling the rise are printed without a compare.

'''''
