[[sec-103-smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test]]
===== 103 `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `gpio`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: GPIO0/1 ACCESS_FILTER: only the AxPROT equal to the programmed requirement passes (read + write).

*Test Coverage*:

* READ half -- an unprivileged read is refused with DECERR, the code the GPIO programming guide specifies for a blocked transaction, and the error-slave signature 0xBADCAB1E, while the privileged read returns the programmed word.
* WRITE half -- an unprivileged write of the value that would DISARM the filter is refused with DECERR, the code the Programmer's Guide GPIO section (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, "Configuring Access Filtering") specifies for a blocked transaction, and a privileged read afterwards shows the register unchanged.
* SWEEP -- each of the eight AxPROT requirement values is programmed into GPIO0 in turn and every AxPROT value is driven against it on both halves; only the value equal to the requirement is admitted, every other one is refused. Each refused write carries the filter word for its own AxPROT value, the word the register would hold had the write landed, so the readback with the admitted value that closes each requirement shows the refused writes left the register unchanged.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]

|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-GPIO1` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-PRE` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-PRIV` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-SCOREBOARD` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-SWEEP` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_filter_access_sep_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches

[[sec-111-smc_gpio_p0_mux_test]]
===== 111 `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test`

*BFM / Model*: SPI pad BFM, ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `gpio`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: GPIO0 interface_enable vs a live lsio_select competitor.

*Test Coverage*:

* The pad is wrap 0, which the integrator pad table (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`) assigns SPI.DATA[0]; the bench drives that data lane through its `tb_spi_dq_oe_n` / `tb_spi_txd` pins with the SPI enable pin held low. The expectations are the GPIO ownership table (`hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Data and Direction Ownership"): the register interface outranks a software-forced `lsio_select`, and a software-forced `lsio_select` routes the LSIO inputs to the pad.
* `DATA_CTRL.lsio_enable`, which the RDL says reports the hardware LSIO request after the disable gate, is read back clear in every leg, so the first row of the ownership table is shown not to be in play and the routing the LSIO leg measures is the software-forced one.
* `lsio_select` alone is shown to ROUTE the LSIO function to the pad -- the positive control that separates a live select bit from one tied to 0, since with the source parked both produce `core2pad_en[0] = 0`; and
* the priority leg runs against a competitor that is actually contributing a different value, so "interface_enable wins" is a distinguishable outcome rather than one both hypotheses satisfy.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-P0-MUX-LSIO` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-P0-MUX-PATTERN` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-P0-MUX-PRIO` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-GPIO-P0-MUX-REG` |Named compare in `smc_gpio_p0_mux_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-186-smc_external_window_pad_ctrl_decode_test]]
===== 186 `smc_external_window_pad_ctrl_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_external_window_pad_ctrl_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver; the request valids and addresses of `smc_external_req_o`, sampled on every `clk_smc_i` edge while each access is in flight; nothing in this bench answers behind the window

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The five mandatory external-window control blocks and the first, second and last of the 65 per-pad control blocks decode into the adopter external AXI-Lite window.

*Test Coverage*:

* Addresses come from the generated bootrom register header, the same map the boot ROM is built against.
* The adopter's implementation of these blocks is outside this repository, so nothing behind the window is specified or credited here. What the SMC side owns, and what is measured here, is the decode into the window: every access must drive the external port while it is in flight and must complete with a decode error (DECERR, the AMBA code for an address nobody decodes) carrying the error-slave word 0xBADCAB1E that every error slave in the design returns, so another word means a live block answered in the window's place. An access that wedges or is answered by another block fails.
* The activity sampler keeps running for a few cycles after the access completes, so a request still being drained is not missed; a zero active-cycle count fails.
* The per-pad instance list and stride are checked against the chapter's 65 instances and 0x20 stride, and the last instance's address is checked to equal base plus index times stride, before the first, second and last instance are probed.
* Every probe is credited only for cycles on which the external port presents a request on the matching channel carrying the probed address, so activity from another master or at another address in the same window does not count. A write into the first per-pad block must likewise reach the port as a write request for that address and be refused, so the terminator's write channel is shown as its read channel is. The error code is reported, not asserted.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_external_window_pad_ctrl_decode_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer: probe the five control blocks, check the generated per-pad geometry against the chapter, probe per-pad instances 0, 1 and 64, require the access count to have reached its floor and print the cell ledger. The leaf then requires an external-port activity record for every probe with a non-zero active-cycle count, and books a protocol-VIP record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EXTWIN-PAD-CTRL` |The cell ledger: one line per control block and per-pad instance closed, naming the number of `clk_smc_i` cycles `smc_external_req_o` presented a read request carrying the probed address and the DECERR/0xBADCAB1E answer it received. A cell is entered only after both of those held
|`CHK-EXTERNAL-WINDOW-PAD-CTRL-DECODE` |Summary line: the control-block and per-pad probe counts, the per-probe active-cycle counts, the measured per-pad stride and the instance count, and the refused per-pad write with its active cycles and response. Logged after every probe's routing and response compare and the stimulus floor have held
|`CHK-EXTWIN-PAD-CTRL-FLOOR` |The leaf requires one external-port activity record per expected probe and a non-zero active-cycle count on every one of them before this token is logged, so a run that stopped probing part-way fails
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nine probes drive the adopter external AXI-Lite port for at least one cycle while in flight and complete DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E, the generated per-pad geometry matches the chapter, and the leaf's per-probe activity check holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Nothing behind the external window is specified or credited here, the adopter's
implementation of these blocks being outside this repository; only the decode into the window is
measured. The error code of the refused per-pad write is reported, not asserted.

'''''

[[sec-187-smc_gpio_pad_input_readback_test]]
===== 187 `smc_gpio_pad_input_readback_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_pad_input_readback_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the GPIO CSRs; the bench external-pin path `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` / `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`; `tb_core2pad_en_o`, a mirror of the `core2pad_en_o` port

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: On six bonded GPIO wraps a pad input transition is captured in `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` in both directions, and TX enable raises and releases only that wrap's `core2pad_en_o` bit.

*Test Coverage*:

* The six wraps are taken from the integrator pad table (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`): three SPI data lanes and the SPI chip select, whose function the bench leaves disabled, the thermal-emergency input and a pad the table reserves. Whether a wrap is free is measured: each must read its enable bit clear before it is programmed and follow the bench drive on `pad2core`.
* Each wrap's `core2pad_en_o` bit is required to read 0 before it is programmed, so the bit that later moves is the one this test caused to move; a wrap already enabled fails rather than being skipped.
* The pad is driven 0, then 1, then 0, and `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` is polled to follow each level within a bounded number of reads; the bound raises, and the number of reads each level needed is reported.
* While a wrap's output enable is programmed, exactly one bit of `tb_core2pad_en_o` may move: any other bit moving raises, which is what attributes the change to that wrap rather than to the write itself.
* `pad2core_en_o` has no vector probe in `tb_top` and `lsio_interface_select_o` is unconnected, so the RX direction enable and the interface-select output are not claimed.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_gpio_pad_input_readback_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer. Per wrap: require the enable bit clear, program the wrap as a register-controlled input, drive the pad 0/1/0 and poll `pad2core` to each level, release the bench drive, program the wrap as a register-controlled output and require its own enable bit to rise, restore `DATA_CTRL` and require the bit to clear. Afterwards require the access count and the scoreboard's SEP_IN item count to cover every access. The leaf requires every wrap to have completed both legs and books a protocol-VIP record.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-PAD-INPUT-WRAP<wrap>` |Per wrap: the pad 0 -> 1 -> 0 sequence was followed in `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` inside the read bound at each level, and the wrap's own `core2pad_en_o` bit rose under TX enable and cleared on the restore without any other bit of the vector moving. One token per member of `WRAPS`, so the recorded name carries the wrap number
|`CHK-GPIO-PAD-INPUT-READBACK` |Summary line: the wraps that completed both legs and the SEP_IN access count, restating that `pad2core_en_o` and `lsio_interface_select_o` are not probed. Logged after every wrap's compares and the access floors have held
|`CHK-GPIO-PAD-INPUT-FLOOR` |The leaf requires every wrap in `WRAPS` to have completed both legs before this token is logged; the line prints the SEP_IN access count against the stimulus floor the sequence already asserted
|===

*Pass Criteria*: on every wrap, `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` follows the driven pad at all three levels inside the read bound, and the wrap's own `core2pad_en_o` bit rises and falls with the register while no other bit of the vector moves. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `pad2core_en_o` has no vector probe in the bench and `lsio_interface_select_o` is
unconnected, so the RX direction enable and the interface-select output are not claimed. The number
of reads each pad level needed before `pad2core` followed it is reported, not compared.

'''''


[[sec-163-smc_gpio_irq_mask_deassert_test]]
===== 163 `smc_gpio_irq_mask_deassert_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_irq_mask_deassert_test`

*BFM / Model*: GPIO pad drive via `tb_gpio_ext_drive_*`; observation on `tb_gpio_irq_any`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `gpio`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Clearing DATA_CTRL.interrupt_enable must de-assert interrupt_o.

*Test Coverage*:

* The mask half of `hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc:122`'s `interrupt_o = interrupt_enable && interrupt_trigger`, which no other GPIO test drives.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Program DATA_CTRL armed (RX enable, interface enable, interrupt enable, active-high) and prove the IRQ is low with the pad low.
. Drive the pad high, require the IRQ to assert, and hold it for 32 cycles.
. Clear only `interrupt_enable`, leaving the pad high and touching nothing else.
. Require the IRQ to fall and stay low.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-IRQ-MASK-ARM` |Pad high with the enable set asserts the IRQ and holds it, so the mask leg's stimulus is the enable write alone
|`CHK-GPIO-IRQ-MASK-DEASSERT` |Clearing the enable de-asserts the IRQ and holds it de-asserted for the same span the arm leg holds it asserted
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-GPIO-IRQ-MASK-ARM` and `CHK-GPIO-IRQ-MASK-DEASSERT` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `gpio`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-468-smc_gpio_data_ctrl_enable_fields_test]]
===== 468 `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_enable_fields_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_enable_fields_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses; `DATA_CTRL` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` of GPIO
interface instance 60 (the generated SMC address symbols for the `gpio_intf` register arrays, 32-bit
accesses); no pad pin is driven and no output is probed; a GPIO protocol-VIP record is booked at
the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of the
register description.

*Objective*: Each DATA_CTRL_ENABLE bit and DATA_CTRL stay independent.

*Test Coverage*:

* `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` holds three software-writable per-field overrides, `use_reg_core2pad` (bit 0),
  `use_reg_tx` (bit 4) and `use_reg_rx` (bit 5), which reset to 0 (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`,
  reg `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE`; `hw/ip/gpio/doc/memmap.adoc`).
* Each override bit is written alone and reads back exactly itself with the other two bits clear,
  and reads 0 after being cleared.
* `DATA_CTRL` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` are separate registers: a write of `DATA_CTRL.core2pad` and a
  write of `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` = 0x31 do not disturb each other in either write order.
* Instance 60 is the pad the integrator pad table marks Reserved
  (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`), so the test changes no pad that another function
  uses.
* Only the register fields are compared; the effect of the overrides on the pad is not driven or
  probed here.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, require the integrator pad table to give pad 60 the function
  Reserved, and require the three override masks to be 0x1, 0x10 and 0x20.
. Read `DATA_CTRL` (writable bits) and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` of instance 60 and require their reset
  values.
. For each of `use_reg_core2pad`, `use_reg_tx` and `use_reg_rx`: write the bit alone to
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE`, require the read-back to equal that bit, write 0 and require 0.
. Order one: write `DATA_CTRL.core2pad` = 1, read it back (writable bits 0x1), write
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` = 0x31, read it back; read both registers again and require `DATA_CTRL`
  writable bits 0x1 and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` 0x31; restore both registers to their reset values and
  read them back.
. Order two: the same with `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` = 0x31 written first and `DATA_CTRL.core2pad` second.
. Read both registers once more and require their reset values; require the five steps in order
  with increasing time stamps and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-ENABLE-BITS-ALONE` |Each `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` bit written alone (0x1, 0x10, 0x20) reads
back exactly itself with the other two bits clear and 0 after the restore, for all three bits.
|`CHK-GPIO-ENABLE-CROSS-REGISTER` |In both write orders `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` reads exactly 0x31 and
the writable bits of `DATA_CTRL` read exactly 0x1, neither disturbed by the write to the other, and
both restore to their reset values.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, single-bit read-backs, first order, second order,
restore read-back) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold: the three override bits read back one at a time as 0x1,
0x10 and 0x20 and clear to 0, and `DATA_CTRL` (0x1) and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` (0x31) keep their written
values in both write orders. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Only the register fields are compared; the effect of the override bits on the pad is
not driven or probed here.

'''''

[[sec-469-smc_gpio_data_ctrl_ro_status_test]]
===== 469 `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_ro_status_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_ro_status_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses; `DATA_CTRL` of all 65 GPIO interface
instances (read scan) and `DATA_CTRL` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` of instance 60 (the generated SMC
address symbols for the `gpio_intf` register arrays, 32-bit accesses); the pad of instance 60 is
driven through the bench external-pin path `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` / `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`, bit
60, for the `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` (bit 31) leg; bit 25 is `DATA_CTRL.lsio_enable`; a GPIO
protocol-VIP record is booked at the end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of the
register description.

*Objective*: Software writes do not change the hardware status bits.

*Test Coverage*:

* `DATA_CTRL.lsio_enable` (bit 25) and `DATA_CTRL.pad2core` (bit 31) are software read-only,
  hardware-written fields, and the software-writable bits of the register are 0x003F_0031
  (`core2pad` bit 0, `enable_rx_tx` bits 5:4, `interface_enable` bit 16, `lsio_select` bit 17,
  `interrupt_enable` bit 18, `lsio_disable` bit 19 and `interrupt_type` bits 21:20)
  (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, reg `DATA_CTRL`).
* A software write of 1 to bit 25 on instance 60 does not set it; on any pad whose bit 25 reads 1
  (a hardware LSIO request, set while `lsio_interface_select_i` is asserted and `lsio_disable` is
  clear), a software write of 0 does not clear it. The response code of those writes is printed,
  not asserted.
* A software write of 1 to bit 31 does not make `pad2core` read 1 while the receive path is not
  selected; with `enable_rx_tx` = 2'b10 and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE.use_reg_rx` set the bit follows the
  driven pad level 0 then 1, and the test asserts that it reads 0 and then 1 while the pad is
  driven; the drive is then released; it reads 0 again once both are cleared.
* A write of 0xFFFF_FFFF sets exactly the software-writable bits, leaves bit 25 as the hardware
  presents it, and sets no undeclared bit; a write of 0 clears the writable bits and again leaves
  bit 25 unchanged.
* Which pads see a hardware LSIO request is read from the scan and printed; the specification does
  not state whether any pad does, and when none does, the write-zero leg has nothing to test.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done and check the register shape: 65 `DATA_CTRL` instances, writable mask
  0x003F_0031, declared mask equal to the writable mask plus bits 25 and 31, reset word 0 and the
  `use_reg_rx` mask 0x20.
. Read `DATA_CTRL` of all 65 instances, record the pads whose bit 25 reads 1 and require the
  writable bits of instance 60 to read the reset value.
. Error injection. Point: `DATA_CTRL` bit 25 (`lsio_enable`, software read-only) of instance 60,
  and of each pad whose bit 25 read 1 in the scan. Kind: a software write of 0x0200_0000 (bit 25
  set) to instance 60, and a write of 0 to the writable bits of each pad whose bit 25 read 1.
  Expected response: bit 25 of instance 60 reads as before (0) with the writable bits 0 and no bit
  other than 25 and 31 set; bit 25 of each such pad still reads 1. For each such pad print the
  write response, restore the reset value, read it back and require the writable bits at reset.
. Error injection. Point: `DATA_CTRL` bit 31 (`pad2core`, software read-only) of instance 60, with
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` read first and `use_reg_rx` required clear. Kind: a software write of bit 31
  while the receive path is not selected. Expected response: bit 31 reads 0. Then write
  `enable_rx_tx` = 2'b10, set `use_reg_rx`, read `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` back and require `use_reg_rx`
  set; drive pad 60 to 0 and require bit 31 to read 0, drive it to 1 and require bit 31 to read 1,
  then release the drive; clear `use_reg_rx` and `DATA_CTRL` and require bit 31 to read 0.
. Write 0xFFFF_FFFF and require the writable bits to read 0x003F_0031, bit 25 as before and no
  undeclared bit set; write 0 and require the writable bits to read 0 and bit 25 as before.
. Restore the reset value, require the writable bits at reset and bit 25 as before, require
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` at its reset value; require the six steps in order with increasing time stamps
  and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-LSIO-ENABLE-RO` |A software write of 1 to bit 25 of instance 60 leaves bit 25
reading as before, and on every pad whose bit 25 reads 1 a software write of 0 leaves it 1; the
write response is printed without being compared.
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-PAD2CORE-RO` |A software write of 1 to bit 31 leaves `pad2core` reading 0 with
the receive path unselected; with `enable_rx_tx` = 2'b10 and `use_reg_rx` set it follows the driven pad level, reading 0 with
the pad driven 0 and 1 with the pad driven 1; after both are cleared it reads 0.
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-WRITE-ALL-ONES` |After a write of 0xFFFF_FFFF the writable bits read
0x003F_0031 with bit 25 unchanged and no undeclared bit set, and after a write of 0 the writable
bits read 0; the bit 31 level is printed.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, pad scan, lsio_enable write, pad2core write, all-ones
write, restore read-back) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step
ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold: bits 25 and 31 of `DATA_CTRL` never change because of a
software write, the writable bits read exactly 0x003F_0031 after all ones and 0 after zeros, and no
undeclared bit sets. The write response codes and the set of pads with a hardware LSIO request are
recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code of the software writes to the read-only bits is printed, not
asserted. Which pads see a hardware LSIO request is read from the scan and printed, because the
specification does not state whether any pad does; when none does, the write-zero leg has nothing to
test. The bit 31 level after the all-ones write is printed.

'''''

[[sec-470-smc_gpio_data_ctrl_rw_values_test]]
===== 470 `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_rw_values_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_rw_values_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses; `DATA_CTRL` of GPIO interface instance 60
(the generated SMC address symbols for the `gpio_intf` register array, whole-word 32-bit writes of
the software-writable bits); `tb_core2pad_en_o` (a mirror of the `core2pad_en_o` port), bit 60,
sampled and printed once after the `enable_rx_tx` leg; a GPIO protocol-VIP record is booked at the
end

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: DATA_CTRL fields hold written values with no cross-talk.

*Test Coverage*:

* The software-writable fields of `DATA_CTRL` are `core2pad` (bit 0), `enable_rx_tx` (bits 5:4),
  `interface_enable` (bit 16), `lsio_select` (bit 17), `interrupt_enable` (bit 18), `lsio_disable`
  (bit 19) and `interrupt_type` (bits 21:20), all resetting to 0
  (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, reg `DATA_CTRL`).
* Each of the four values of `enable_rx_tx` (2'b00 neither, 2'b01 TX, 2'b10 RX, 2'b11 both) and of
  `interrupt_type` (0 active-high level, 1 active-low level, 2 rising edge, 3 falling edge) reads
  back exactly as written with no other writable bit set.
* A read-modify-write that changes one field leaves the other six fields at their base values, for
  all seven fields.
* The six constants of the Programmer's Guide GPIO example (0x1 `core2pad`, 0x10 and 0x20 the two
  `enable_rx_tx` bits, 0x10000 `interface_enable`, 0x40000 `interrupt_enable`, 0x200000 the rising
  edge `interrupt_type`) each read back as exactly themselves, setting only the named field
  (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, GPIO).
* Instance 60 is the pad the integrator pad table marks Reserved
  (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`). The `core2pad_en_o` bit is sampled and printed after
  the `enable_rx_tx` leg without being compared.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done; require the integrator pad table to give pad 60 the function Reserved,
  the field masks to add up to the writable mask, `tb_core2pad_en_o` to exist, and `DATA_CTRL` of
  instance 60 to read the reset value.
. For each `enable_rx_tx` value 0 to 3 write it alone, read back and require the whole writable word
  and the field to equal the value; restore the reset value and require it. Sample
  `tb_core2pad_en_o[60]`.
. Do the same for each `interrupt_type` value 0 to 3.
. Write a base pattern (every one-bit field 1, `enable_rx_tx` 1, `interrupt_type` 2) and require it.
  For each of the seven fields: read the register and require the base pattern, write it with only
  that field changed (`core2pad` 0, `enable_rx_tx` 2, `interface_enable` 0, `lsio_select` 0,
  `interrupt_enable` 0, `lsio_disable` 0, `interrupt_type` 1), read back and require the new value
  in that field and the six other fields unchanged; rewrite the base pattern. Restore the reset
  value.
. Write each of the six Programmer's Guide constants, require it to read back as exactly itself with
  only the named field set, and restore the reset value after each.
. Read `DATA_CTRL` and require the reset value; require the six steps in order with increasing time
  stamps and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-RX-TX-VALUES` |`enable_rx_tx` reads back exactly the written value for all four
values with no other writable bit set; the `core2pad_en_o` bit 60 level is printed.
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-INTERRUPT-TYPE-VALUES` |`interrupt_type` reads back exactly the written value
for all four values with no other writable bit set.
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-RMW-ISOLATION` |Each of the seven fields changes alone from the base pattern
in a read-modify-write while the other six read unchanged.
|`CHK-GPIO-DATA-CTRL-PG-CONSTANTS` |Each of the six Programmer's Guide constants reads back as
exactly itself inside its named field and sets no other field.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, `enable_rx_tx` values, `interrupt_type` values,
read-modify-write isolation, constants, restore read-back) with increasing time stamps and each
checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold: every field value, read-modify-write and Programmer's Guide
constant reads back exactly as written on instance 60 with no other writable bit changed, and the
register returns to its reset value after each phase. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The `core2pad_en_o` bit of instance 60 is sampled and printed after the
`enable_rx_tx` leg without being compared.

'''''

[[sec-471-smc_gpio_ext_extra_decode_test]]
===== 471 `smc_gpio_ext_extra_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_ext_extra_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (reads and writes at the supplementary GPIO blocks, a read at the
eFuse SHIM base and a read above the SHIM block); the request valids and addresses of the adopter
external AXI-Lite port, `tb_axil_external_arvalid` / `tb_axil_external_araddr` and
`tb_axil_external_awvalid` / `tb_axil_external_awaddr`, sampled on every `clk_smc_i` edge while
each access is in flight and for 8 cycles after it; the eFuse bank activity probe
`tb_axil_efuse_bank_active`; the AXI monitor's expected-DECERR address set; nothing in this bench
answers behind the window

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Extra GPIO blocks decode into the external window.

*Test Coverage*:

* The supplementary region of the external window starts at the window base plus 0x40_4000 and holds
  the optional blocks `gpio_extra_intf` (three words at region offset 0x1000) and `gpio_extra_ctrl`
  (one word at 0x100C) (`hw/sys/smc/regs/include/smc_external_supplementary.rdl`;
  `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc`, AXI-Lite External Window).
* The supplementary region is passed through to the SMC external port; hardware treats it like the
  mandatory region, and an adopter may implement it or terminate it with an error response. The
  adopter's implementation is outside this repository, so only the decode is measured: every read
  and write must present a request on the matching channel of the external port with its own
  address.
* With no adopter block present, the access must complete with DECERR (the AMBA code for an address
  nobody decodes), the response the reference integration gives an unclaimed access in this region
  (`memmap.adoc`). The read data returned with that DECERR is printed; its expected value is an
  open question.
* The eFuse SHIM control block sits at the window base and is routed to the eFuse controller and
  never to the external port: a read of its base raises the eFuse bank activity probe and produces
  no external-port read request, while the first address above the SHIM block does reach the
  external port (`memmap.adoc`).
* Each probe is credited only for cycles on which the external port presents a request on the
  matching channel carrying the probed word address, so activity from another master or another
  address does not count.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, require the three `gpio_extra_intf` word addresses to be followed by
  the `gpio_extra_ctrl` address and the first per-pad control address to lie above the SHIM block,
  and add the nine probed addresses to the monitor's expected-DECERR set.
. Error injection. Point: each of the three `gpio_extra_intf` words in the supplementary region of
  the external window, which nothing in this bench answers. Kind: a read of the word and a write of
  0xA5A5_5A5A to it. Expected response: each access presents a request on the external port with
  its address for at least one cycle and completes with DECERR.
. Error injection. Point: the `gpio_extra_ctrl` word in the same region. Kind: a read and a write
  of the word. Expected response: the same requirement, a request on the external port with its
  address for at least one cycle and a DECERR completion.
. Require all eight accesses to have completed with DECERR (3) and print each read's data.
. Read the SHIM base while sampling `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active` and the external-port read channel;
  require the activity probe to be low before the read and high for at least one cycle during it,
  and zero external-port read requests for that address. Read the first address above the SHIM block
  and require at least one external-port read request for it and a DECERR response.
. Require the five steps in order with increasing time stamps and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-EXT-EXTRA-INTF-ROUTED` |Each of the three reads and three writes of `gpio_extra_intf` is
presented on the matching external-port channel carrying its own address for at least one cycle.
|`CHK-GPIO-EXT-EXTRA-CTRL-ROUTED` |The read and the write of the `gpio_extra_ctrl` word are
presented on the matching external-port channel carrying that address for at least one cycle.
|`CHK-GPIO-EXT-EXTRA-RESPONSE` |All eight accesses complete with DECERR; the response codes and read
data are printed, and the read data is not compared with an expected value.
|`CHK-GPIO-EXT-EXTRA-SHIM-BOUNDARY` |The read of the SHIM base raises `tb_axil_efuse_bank_active`
and produces no external-port read request for its address, and the first address above the SHIM
block produces at least one external-port read request.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, interface routed, control routed, responses printed,
SHIM boundary) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold: all eight supplementary-block accesses reach the external
port with their own address and complete with DECERR, the SHIM base never reaches the external port
while the eFuse bank activity probe moves, and the first address above the SHIM does reach it. The
read data returned with DECERR is recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The adopter's implementation of the supplementary blocks is outside this repository,
so only the decode into the external port is measured. The read data returned with the DECERR is
printed and not compared, its expected value being an open question.

'''''

[[sec-472-smc_gpio_filter_reg_fields_test]]
===== 472 `smc_gpio_filter_reg_fields_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_filter_reg_fields_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses, with the AXI write protection value
(`AWPROT`) and read protection value (`ARPROT`) of selected accesses set by the test;
`ACCESS_FILTER` of GPIO interface instance 60 (the generated SMC address symbols for the
`gpio_intf` register array and its field masks, bit positions and reset values, 32-bit accesses);
no pad pin is driven and no output is probed

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of the
register description.

*Objective*: ACCESS_FILTER requirement fields and enable bits read back.

*Test Coverage*:

* `ACCESS_FILTER` holds `write_filter_enable` (bit 0), `read_filter_enable` (bit 1),
  `awprot_requirement` (bits 10:8) and `arprot_requirement` (bits 18:16); both requirement fields
  reset to 1 and both enables reset to 0 (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, reg `ACCESS_FILTER`).
* With both enables clear, each requirement field takes every value 0 to 7 and reads back exactly as
  written, without disturbing the other requirement field or the enables.
* When an enable is set, the matching direction accepts only an access whose protection value equals
  the requirement field, so the writes and reads that change an enable bit are issued with the
  protection value that satisfies the filter they arm (1, the reset value of both requirements);
  `write_filter_enable`, `read_filter_enable` and both together can each be set and cleared and read
  back exactly. The register description requires reading the register back after writing it.
* Instance 60 is the pad the integrator pad table marks Reserved
  (`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`).
* The effect of an armed filter on accesses with another protection value is not driven here.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, require the integrator pad table to give pad 60 the function Reserved,
  and read `ACCESS_FILTER` of instance 60 and require the reset word (both requirements 1, both
  enables 0).
. For `awprot_requirement` and then `arprot_requirement`, write each value 0 to 7 with the other
  requirement at its reset value and both enables clear, read back after each write and require the
  written word; restore the reset word and require it (16 values in all).
. Set `write_filter_enable` with a write issued with `AWPROT` 0 (the filter is not yet armed) and
  read back with `ARPROT` 0; clear it with a write issued with `AWPROT` 1; set `read_filter_enable`
  with `AWPROT` 0 and read back with `ARPROT` 1; clear it with `AWPROT` 0 and read back with
  `ARPROT` 0; set both enables with `AWPROT` 0 and read back with `ARPROT` 1; clear both with
  `AWPROT` 1 and read back with `ARPROT` 0; require the expected word after every step.
. Read `ACCESS_FILTER` and require the reset word; require the four steps in order with increasing
  time stamps and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-REG-REQ-VALUES` |With both enables clear, all 16 requirement values (0 to 7 in
each field) read back exactly as written with the other requirement and the enables unchanged.
|`CHK-GPIO-FILTER-REG-ENABLE-BITS` |`write_filter_enable`, `read_filter_enable` and both together
set and clear individually, each read-back equals the reset word with exactly the armed enable bits
set, and the restoring access reads the reset word.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, requirement values, enable-bit legs, restore read-back)
with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold: every requirement value 0 to 7 of both fields and every
set and clear of the two enable bits reads back exactly, and the register ends at its reset word
0x0001_0100. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The effect of an armed filter on accesses with another protection value is not driven
here; the accesses that change an enable bit are issued with the protection value that satisfies the
filter they arm.

'''''

[[sec-473-smc_gpio_intf_decode_map_test]]
===== 473 `smc_gpio_intf_decode_map_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_intf_decode_map_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses; `DATA_CTRL`, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and
`ACCESS_FILTER` of all 65 GPIO interface instances (the generated SMC address symbols for the
`gpio_intf` register arrays and their field masks and bit positions, 32-bit accesses); the
scoreboard's SEP_IN value-check count; no pad pin is driven and no output is probed

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: GPIO interface instances decode without aliasing.

*Test Coverage*:

* The GPIO block holds one interface instance per pad, 65 in all, each with `DATA_CTRL` at offset
  0x0, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` at 0x4 and `ACCESS_FILTER` at 0x8, at the base 0xC000_3000 plus 0x10 per
  pin (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, GPIO; `hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`).
* The first and last instances (0 and 64) answer at the three offsets, and a different pattern
  written to each register reads back at its own offset.
* A distinct pattern written to the `ACCESS_FILTER` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` of every instance reads
  back from the same instance after all 130 writes, so no instance aliases another;
  `ACCESS_FILTER` carries the instance number modulo 64 over its two requirement fields and
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` carries the instance number modulo 8 over its three bits (instance 64 adds one
  to its number, so the pair for instance 64 differs from the pair for instance 0); the
  `DATA_CTRL` of every instance is unchanged by those writes.
* On one instance, a write to any one of the three registers leaves the other two at their earlier
  values, so the three registers do not alias each other.
* The Programmer's Guide address formula, base plus pin times 0x10 plus the register offset, equals
  the generated address of each register for pins 0, 32 and 64, and `ACCESS_FILTER` read at the
  formula address returns its reset word 0x0001_0100 (both requirement fields reset to 1,
  `gpio_intf.rdl`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, require 65 instances of each of the three registers in the generated
  map, and snapshot all three registers of every instance.
. For instances 0 and 64: require the three offsets 0x0, 0x4 and 0x8; read `ACCESS_FILTER` and
  require its reset word; write `core2pad` to `DATA_CTRL`, `use_reg_core2pad` plus `use_reg_rx` to
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and `awprot_requirement` 3 plus `arprot_requirement` 5 to `ACCESS_FILTER`;
  read all three and require the written patterns; restore the snapshot values and require them.
. Write to every instance an `ACCESS_FILTER` pattern derived from the instance number modulo 64
  (`awprot_requirement` from its low three bits, `arprot_requirement` from the next three) and a
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` pattern in which `use_reg_core2pad`, `use_reg_tx` and `use_reg_rx` carry the
  bits of (instance number plus instance number divided by 64) modulo 8. Read back
  every instance's `ACCESS_FILTER` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` against its pattern and its `DATA_CTRL`
  against the snapshot; require all 65 read-back pairs to be pairwise distinct and the scoreboard's
  value-check count to have grown by at least 130; restore and re-read every instance.
. On instance 60 write a pattern to all three registers and read them back; then write a new value
  to `DATA_CTRL`, then to `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE`, then to `ACCESS_FILTER`, each alone, and after each
  write require all three registers to read the held values with only the written register changed;
  restore the snapshot values and require them.
. For pins 0, 32 and 64 require the formula address of each register to equal the generated address,
  and read `ACCESS_FILTER` at the formula address and require the reset word.
. Require the steps in order with increasing time stamps and the checker line order; print the
  fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-DECODE-ENDPOINTS` |Instances 0 and 64 answer OKAY at offsets 0x0, 0x4 and 0x8, and each
pattern written to a register reads back at its own offset, with `ACCESS_FILTER` first reading its
reset word.
|`CHK-GPIO-DECODE-NO-ALIAS` |After all writes every one of the 65 instances reads back its own
`ACCESS_FILTER` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` pattern, its `DATA_CTRL` is unchanged, all 65 read-back pairs
differ, and all registers restore.
|`CHK-GPIO-DECODE-REG-DISTINCT` |On instance 60, writing any one of `DATA_CTRL`, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE`
and `ACCESS_FILTER` leaves the other two at their earlier values.
|`CHK-GPIO-DECODE-PG-FORMULA` |The Programmer's Guide formula 0xC000_3000 plus 0x10 per pin plus
0x0, 0x4 or 0x8 equals the generated address of `DATA_CTRL`, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and `ACCESS_FILTER`
for pins 0, 32 and 64, and `ACCESS_FILTER` read at the formula address returns its reset word.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (snapshot, endpoint patterns, co-resident writes, co-resident
read-backs, register distinct, formula compare) with increasing time stamps and each checker line
printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold: every instance keeps the `ACCESS_FILTER` and
`DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` pattern written to it and reads back distinct from its neighbours, the three
registers of an instance do not alias, and the Programmer's Guide formula matches the generated
addresses. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-474-smc_gpio_intf_reset_writeback_test]]
===== 474 `smc_gpio_intf_reset_writeback_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_intf_reset_writeback_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the CSR accesses; `ACCESS_FILTER`, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and
`DATA_CTRL` of all 65 GPIO interface instances (the generated SMC address symbols for the
`gpio_intf` register arrays, 32-bit accesses); the scoreboard's SEP_IN value-check count; no pad pin
is driven and no output is probed

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of the
register description.

*Objective*: Reset words written back read as reset on all instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* `ACCESS_FILTER` resets to 0x0001_0100 (`awprot_requirement` and `arprot_requirement` both 1,
  enables 0), and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and the software-writable bits of `DATA_CTRL` reset to 0
  (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, regs `ACCESS_FILTER`, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and `DATA_CTRL`); the
  reset word of `ACCESS_FILTER` in the generated map equals 0x0001_0100.
* A non-reset pattern is written and read back first on each of the three registers of each of the
  65 instances (`ACCESS_FILTER` 0x0006_0500, `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` 0x20 and `DATA_CTRL` 0x0030_0000);
  writing the reset word back to each register is then accepted and reads back as the reset word,
  so a write of the reset word takes effect and the writable bits of `DATA_CTRL` return to 0.
* The first reads of the registers are taken as a snapshot only and are not compared; the pad state
  they reflect is not specified here.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, require 65 instances of each of the three registers in the generated
  map and the `ACCESS_FILTER` reset word 0x0001_0100.
. Read all three registers of every instance as an uncompared snapshot.
. For each instance in turn write the non-reset pattern to the three registers and require it on
  read-back; then write 0x0001_0100 to `ACCESS_FILTER` and 0 to `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and
  `DATA_CTRL`, then read each back and require 0x0001_0100, 0 and 0 on the software-writable bits of
  `DATA_CTRL`; require the scoreboard to have counted at least 260 value checks and all accesses to
  have completed.
. Require the steps and fence terms in order with increasing time stamps; print the fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GPIO-RESET-WRITEBACK` |On all 65 instances `ACCESS_FILTER` reads 0x0001_0100,
`DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` reads 0 and the software-writable bits of `DATA_CTRL` read 0 after the reset
words are written back.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (bring-up, initial reads, reset-word writes, write-back reads) with
increasing time stamps and the checker line printed after the write-back reads.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold: all 65 instances read back the reset words of the three
registers after the write-back. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The first reads of the three registers of every instance are taken as a snapshot only
and are not compared, because the pad state they reflect is not specified here.

'''''

[[sec-475-smc_gpio_irq_or_test]]
===== 475 `smc_gpio_irq_or_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_irq_or_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver for the `DATA_CTRL` accesses of GPIO interface instances 4, 31, 32
and 60 (the generated SMC address symbols for the `gpio_intf` register array and the `DATA_CTRL`
field masks); the bench external-pin path `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` / `tb_gpio_ext_drive_value` (one
bit per pad, bits 4, 31, 32 and 60); the raw per-wrap interrupt vector `tb_gpio_interrupt`; the
peripheral interrupt vector `tb_peripheral_interrupts`, bit 28 (lower half, PLIC source 284) and bit
29 (upper half, PLIC source 285), sampled once per `clk_smc_i` cycle; `tb_spi_enable` (required
low); no firmware image

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: GPIO interrupt OR halves drive PLIC sources 284 and 285.

*Test Coverage*:

* The GPIO interrupt sources are OR-reduced into two lines: sources 0 to 31 raise PLIC source 284
  (`tb_peripheral_interrupts[28]`) and sources 32 to 64 raise PLIC source 285
  (`tb_peripheral_interrupts[29]`) (`hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc`, the 284 and 285 rows).
* A pad interrupt on wrap 4 or 31 asserts only the lower line, and on wrap 32 or 60 only the upper
  line, within a bound of 64 cycles and while the pad is held.
* A line stays asserted while any contributing wrap is asserted and drops only after the last
  contributor clears, in the clearing order 4, 32, 31, 60.
* With no wrap interrupt-enabled and the pads low, both lines and the raw vector stay 0.
* An edge-type interrupt (`interrupt_type` 2, rising edge) is a one clock-cycle pulse per detected
  edge, and the OR line carries the pulse for as many cycles as the raw bit without stretching it
  (`hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc`, Interrupts). The absolute pulse width is an open question and
  is printed.
* `DATA_CTRL.interrupt_enable` gates the interrupt, and the level types 0 (active-high) and 2
  (rising edge) are the types used (`hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, reg `DATA_CTRL`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require the probes and `tb_spi_enable` low, clear both bench drive vectors, and for each of wraps
  4, 31, 32 and 60 drive the pad low, write `DATA_CTRL` 0 and read it back; when `lsio_enable` reads
  1 set `lsio_disable` and require `lsio_enable` to clear. Require `tb_peripheral_interrupts[29:28]`
  and the raw vector `tb_gpio_interrupt` to be 0.
. For wraps 4 and 31 in turn: program `DATA_CTRL` with RX enabled (`enable_rx_tx` 2'b10),
  `interface_enable` and `interrupt_enable` set and `interrupt_type` 0, drive the pad high, wait up
  to 64 cycles for the wrap's raw bit and for line 28, hold 16 cycles requiring line 28 high and
  line 29 low, drive the pad low, wait for line 28 to clear, require both lines 0, and disarm the
  wrap.
. Do the same for wraps 32 and 60 with line 29 as the asserted line and line 28 as the line that
  must stay 0.
. Arm and drive all four wraps high and wait for both lines. Clear the wraps in the order 4, 32,
  31, 60; after each clear wait for its raw bit to drop, require the line of the half that still has
  a contributor to stay high for 16 cycles, wait for a half whose last contributor cleared to drop,
  require the other half to stay high while it has a contributor, and finally require both lines 0;
  disarm all four.
. Arm and release wraps 4 and 60 once as a positive control; then with `interrupt_enable` clear on
  all four wraps and the pads low require the raw vector 0 and `tb_peripheral_interrupts[29:28]` 0
  on each of 64 cycles.
. For wraps 4 and 60: program `interrupt_type` 2 with the interrupt enabled, require the raw bit and
  its line 0, drive the pad high, sample every cycle until the raw bit and the line have each pulsed
  and returned to 0 (bound 64 cycles) and then for 32 more cycles; require exactly one pulse on the
  raw bit and on the line, the line pulse width equal to the raw pulse width, the other line 0
  throughout and the line 0 for the last 32 cycles; print the width. Release the pad and disarm.
. Clear both bench drive vectors, write `DATA_CTRL` 0 on the four wraps and require the writable
  bits to read 0.
. Require the seven steps in order with increasing time stamps, the checker lines in order and every
  access to have completed; print the fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OR-LOWER` |An interrupt on wrap 4 and on wrap 31 asserts `tb_peripheral_interrupts[28]` within
64 cycles, holds it for 16 cycles with `[29]` low, and releases it when the pad is released.
|`CHK-OR-UPPER` |An interrupt on wrap 32 and on wrap 60 asserts `tb_peripheral_interrupts[29]`
within 64 cycles, holds it for 16 cycles with `[28]` low, and releases it when the pad is released.
|`CHK-OR-HOLD-UNTIL-ALL-CLEAR` |Each line stays 1 while any contributing wrap is asserted and drops
within 64 cycles only after the last contributor clears, with the other line unaffected, in the
clearing order 4, 32, 31, 60.
|`CHK-OR-IDLE` |With every wrap's `interrupt_enable` clear, a pad driven high on wrap 4 and then
on wrap 60 leaves its line 0 for 32 cycles each, and with the pads low both lines and the raw vector
read 0 on all 64 cycles, after positive controls on wraps 4 and 60 set and released the lines.
|`CHK-OR-EDGE-PULSE` |A rising-edge interrupt on wrap 4 and on wrap 60 pulses the OR line exactly
once with a width equal to the raw bit's width, never wider, and the line is 0 afterwards; the
width in cycles is printed without comparing it to an absolute value.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (baseline, lower, upper, hold, idle, edge pulse, restore) with
increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold: each half asserts only for its own wraps, holds until the
last contributor clears, stays 0 when idle, and carries an edge pulse once with the raw width, all
within the 64-cycle bounds. The absolute edge pulse width is recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The absolute width of the rising-edge interrupt pulse is an open question and is
printed without being compared to an absolute value; only equality with the raw bit's width is
required.

'''''

[[sec-476-smc_gpio_rst_primary_test]]
===== 476 `smc_gpio_rst_primary_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: GPIO

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_rst_primary_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (the `DATA_CTRL` programming, the pad-level polling reads and one
write that is left in flight across the reset); the reset agent, which asserts and releases
`rst_cold_ni` on a `clk_ref_i` edge; the bench external-pin path `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` /
`tb_gpio_ext_drive_value`, bit 60 (the pad of GPIO interface instance 60); a passive sampler on
every `clk_smc_i` edge of `tb_gpio_interrupt[60]` and `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`; the write-address
valid `s_axi_awvalid`; the SEP_IN driver's reset-abort flag, which is set only when the driver saw
`rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low at a no-response completion; `DATA_CTRL` and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` of
instance 60; no firmware image

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/gpio.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `gpio`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Primary reset clears GPIO interrupt state; an in-flight access is recorded.

*Test Coverage*:

* The interface and control registers are reset asynchronously by `rst_primary_ni`, so a cold reset
  returns `DATA_CTRL` (including `interrupt_enable`) and `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` (written 0x31 and read
  back before the reset) to 0 and a level
  interrupt that was asserted drops and stays low with the pad still high and the register not
  re-programmed (`hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc`, Reset and Strap Capture;
  `hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl`, reg `DATA_CTRL`, `interrupt_enable` reset 0). The reset is driven
  through `rst_cold_ni`; the cold-only reset is not separable from the primary reset at the SMC
  boundary, and the specification does not state it.
* The cold reset reaches `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` after a de-glitch measured as L `clk_smc_i`
  cycles, so a pad edge or an access that must land inside the reset is timed against
  `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`, not against the pin.
* A rising edge on the pad raises `tb_gpio_interrupt[60]` in a control run, which makes the probe
  live; an edge that lands inside the input synchroniser when the effective reset arrives is
  set up (the reset reads released on the cycle the pad rises and low within 4 cycles after), and
  the number of interrupt samples that follow is recorded without comparing it, because the
  specification does not state the edge detector state at reset release.
* An access in flight when the primary reset takes effect was outstanding when the reset fell; its
  completion kind (the DUT's own response of OKAY, SLVERR or DECERR, or the bench master's reset
  flush) and latency are recorded, not asserted, and after the reset `DATA_CTRL` and
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` read OKAY and 0 apart from `pad2core` (bit 31) and `lsio_enable` (bit 25).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, start the sampler, drive the pad high, program `DATA_CTRL` for an
  active-high level interrupt (RX enabled, `interface_enable`, `interrupt_enable`, `interrupt_type`
  0) and wait up to 64 cycles for `tb_gpio_interrupt[60]` to read 1.
. Assert `rst_cold_ni` on a `clk_ref_i` edge, wait up to 1024 cycles for `rst_primary_smc_clk_no`
  to fall and record L, hold the reset 64 cycles, release it, wait up to 8192 cycles for
  `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` to rise and sample 64 more cycles. Require the interrupt to have read 1
  on the last sample before the reset and 0 on every sample from the reset assertion on, with the
  pad still high; print L and the release-to-rise time; wait for sense done.
. Control run: write `DATA_CTRL` 0, drive the pad low, program a rising-edge interrupt
  (`interrupt_type` 2), poll `pad2core` to 0 within 64 reads, require the interrupt 0 for 8 samples,
  drive the pad high, wait up to 64 cycles for the interrupt, drive the pad low and poll `pad2core`
  to 0; require at least one interrupt sample. Reset run: re-program the edge type, poll the pad
  low, assert `rst_cold_ni`, wait L minus 2 cycles, require `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` still 1, drive
  the pad high and require `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` to read 0 within 4 cycles; hold, release, sample
  64 cycles, and print the interrupt samples before the fall, between the fall and the rise, and
  after the rise.
. Assert `rst_cold_ni` and launch a write of `DATA_CTRL` (RX enabled, `interface_enable`,
  `interrupt_enable`, `interrupt_type` 1) L minus 4 cycles later; require the write address valid
  to be seen no later than the reset fall and the fall no later than the completion, and a DUT
  response or a reset flush (credited only with `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` low and booked by the
  scoreboard as a reset abort). Release the reset, wait for sense done, read `DATA_CTRL` and
  `DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` and require 0 outside `pad2core` and `lsio_enable`; print the
  launch-to-address, launch-to-fall and launch-to-completion cycle counts and the completion kind.
. Release the pad drive, write `DATA_CTRL` 0 and read it back as 0; require the five steps in order
  with increasing time stamps and the checker line order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RST-PRIMARY-LEVEL-IRQ` |`tb_gpio_interrupt[60]` reads 1 before the reset and 0 on every sample
from the reset assertion through the reset window and the 64 samples after release, with the pad
still high and `DATA_CTRL` not re-programmed; L and the release-to-rise time are printed.
|`CHK-RST-PRIMARY-EDGE` |The control run raises at least one interrupt sample for a rising pad edge;
in the reset run `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` reads 1 on the cycle the pad rises and 0 within 4 cycles
after; the interrupt samples before, during and after the reset are printed without being compared.
|`CHK-RST-PRIMARY-AXI-BOUNDED` |A `DATA_CTRL` write launched L minus 4 cycles after the reset
assertion is outstanding when `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` falls; its completion kind (DUT response or
bench reset flush) and latency are recorded, and after the release `DATA_CTRL` and
`DATA_CTRL_ENABLE` read OKAY and 0 outside bits 31 and 25.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence (interrupt asserted, level reset, edge reset, access reset,
restore) with increasing time stamps and each checker line printed after its step ended.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold: the level interrupt reads 0 from the reset assertion on,
the edge is timed inside the reset window with a live control pulse, the in-flight write is
outstanding across the reset fall, and the registers read 0 after the reset. The interrupt samples around the reset edge and the completion kind of the in-flight write
are recorded only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The cold-only reset is not separable from the primary reset at the SMC boundary and
the specification does not state it, so the reset is driven through `rst_cold_ni`. The number of
interrupt samples around a pad edge that lands inside the input synchroniser as the effective reset
arrives is recorded without a compare, because the specification does not state the edge detector
state at reset release. The completion kind and latency of the access in flight when the primary
reset takes effect are recorded, not asserted.

'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-irq]]
==== IRQ

[[sec-112-smc_hang_detector_data_timeout_test]]
===== 112 `smc_hang_detector_data_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

[[sec-114-smc_hang_detector_sanity_test]]
===== 114 `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `irq`; `run_modes`

draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: irq_test fire/clear on sys/sep/data hang detectors + OR.

*Test Coverage*:

* Hang-detector CTRL.irq_test on each lifted IRQ.
* Real bus-stall timeout is not claimed.
* The `irq_test` gating poison runs three ways: `irq_test` alone, `enable` with `irq_test`, and `irq_en` with `irq_test`. `smc_base_config.rdl` says `irq_test` "is gated by enable and irq_en", so none of them may raise `irq_o`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-HANG-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-HANG-DATA-CLR` |Clearing `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` drops `tb_axi_hang_irq_data` and the OR to 0 inside the bounded handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-HANG-DATA-FIRE` |A fire write to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` raises `tb_axi_hang_irq_data` and the OR `tb_axi_hang_irq` while the other two detector pins stay 0, inside the bounded `_await_irqs` handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-HANG-OR-ALL` |Named compare in `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-HANG-OR-CLR` |Named compare in `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-HANG-OR-HOLD` |Named compare in `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-HANG-POISON` |Named compare in `smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-HANG-SEP-CLR` |Clearing `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` drops `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` and the OR to 0 inside the bounded handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-HANG-SEP-FIRE` |A fire write to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` raises `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` and the OR `tb_axi_hang_irq` while the other two detector pins stay 0, inside the bounded `_await_irqs` handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-HANG-STATUS-GATED` |Every `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` reads 0 at idle and on each `irq_test` poison leg, matching the gated `irq_o`
|`CHK-HANG-STATUS-MAP` |Firing each detector alone sets its own `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` and no other, and clearing it returns all three to 0; all three are read each time, so a status bit wired to the wrong detector fails
|`CHK-HANG-STATUS-OR` |With all three detectors fired every `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` reads 1; after SYS and SEP clear only DATA reads 1; after DATA clears none does
|`CHK-HANG-SYS-CLR` |Clearing `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` drops `tb_axi_hang_irq_sys` and the OR to 0 inside the bounded handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-HANG-SYS-FIRE` |A fire write to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` raises `tb_axi_hang_irq_sys` and the OR `tb_axi_hang_irq` while the other two detector pins stay 0, inside the bounded `_await_irqs` handshake (`smc_hang_detector_sanity_test_seq.py`)
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-HANG-BASIC`, `CHK-HANG-DATA-CLR`, `CHK-HANG-DATA-FIRE`, `CHK-HANG-OR-ALL`, `CHK-HANG-OR-CLR`, `CHK-HANG-OR-HOLD` (and 8 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `irq`.

*Scope limit*: A real bus-stall timeout is not claimed; only the `irq_test` fire and clear path of each detector is covered.
'''''

[[sec-118-smc_irq_observe_test]]
===== 118 `smc_irq_observe_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_irq_observe_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `irq`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SMC OSS PyUVM interrupt-observe test.

*Test Coverage*:

* One IRQ SAMPLE of the three `tb_top` interrupt aggregates, consumed into the only property this leaf can honestly claim: **every aggregate reads its idle 0 and every one of the three probes carries a same-run liveness credit**, so the scoreboard exact-compared all three legs instead of booking them OBSERVED-ONLY.
* An idle `== 0` is a pure negative check, and the scoreboard silently downgrades an uncredited leg to `OBSERVED-ONLY (NOT checked evidence)` rather than failing, so the liveness credit is part of the assertion.
* Without the gate below, dropping `probe_positive_controls` from the test would turn this testcase into an all-observed-only run that still passes.
* The credits come from the passive ledger in `env/smc_probe_liveness.py`, which is fed by a DUT observation (the probe seen at 1), so requiring them is DUT-sensitive: a stuck-at-0 / undriven / mis-bound aggregate fails here.
* `item.resolvable` is **not** presented as this testcase's check: every retained run is Verilator (2-state), where `value.is_resolvable` cannot be False, so it has no FAIL-ON path in the evidence that exists.
* Three unrelated sources asserted together: `SYNC_REG.sync` (`reset_unit.rdl`) raises `tb_sync_irq`; while it is held, UART0 `IER.ETBEI` with `ITR.TTBEI` raises `tb_uart_irq_any`; while both are held, GPIO0 armed as an active-low level interrupt raises `tb_gpio_irq_any` when its pad is driven low. All three must read 1 in one `clk_smc_i` sample, and releasing them in reverse order must drop only each one's own output. A shared or cross-wired output fails one of those samples. The UART clock gate, both UART registers and GPIO0's `DATA_CTRL` are restored and the pad drive released.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_irq_observe_test_seq` on the IRQ sequencer, then `smc_irq_concurrent_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-IRQ-CONCURRENT-SOURCES` |Each output rose with the earlier ones still 1, all three read 1 together, each release dropped only its own output, and each level held for four cycles, all within a bounded poll
|`CHK-IRQ-OBSERVE-IDLE-CHECKED` |Named compare in `smc_irq_observe_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-IRQ-CONCURRENT-SOURCES` and `CHK-IRQ-OBSERVE-IDLE-CHECKED` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `irq`.

*Scope limit*: Resolvability of the sampled aggregates (`item.resolvable`) is not presented as this testcase's check, because every retained run uses a two-state simulator where it cannot be false.
'''''

[[sec-477-smc_ext_irq_hold_release_test]]
===== 477 `smc_ext_irq_hold_release_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_ext_irq_hold_release_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench inputs
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (raw bit 0), `tb_top.tb_ext_interrupts_hi_i` (the [16:2] bus: bit 0 of
the bus is raw bit 2, bit 14 of the bus is raw bit 16) and `tb_top.tb_temp_interrupt_i` (raw bit 1,
read only, must be 0); inputs 17..255 are tied 0 by the bench (SF-039); observed
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` sampled on each `clk_smc_i` rise; the PLIC `pending_N` registers (source
N + 1) read passively under `u_dut.u_smc.u_smc_cpu_wrapper.u_smc_cpu.u_digital_top.plic_domain.plic`
and only logged; scratch register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `ext`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Walk external inputs 0 and 2..16: hold each high 256 rises alone, then release.

*Test Coverage*:

* External interrupt inputs 0 and 2..16 reach raw bits 0 and 2..16 of `cpu_interrupts` through the
  three-flop synchroniser into `clk_smc`, as level signals (`interrupts.adoc`,
  `smc-interrupts-risc-v-plic`; `smu-smc.adoc`, `interrupt-integration`); raw bit N is PLIC source
  ID N + 1 (`interrupts.adoc`, `cpu-interrupt-vector-map`).
* The gateways are active-high and level-sensitive with no selectable edge mode (`interrupts.adoc`),
  so a held input keeps its raw bit at 1 for the whole hold.
* Each pin-to-raw-bit transition takes at least 3 `clk_smc_i` rises, the depth of the three-flop
  synchroniser (`interrupts.adoc`); a faster path fails.
* While one input is high, every other raw external bit (0..255, including the temperature bit 1
  and the tied-off 17..255) reads 0 at each hold sample.
* A released input drops its raw bit to 0 and the vector returns to the baseline, so nothing
  latches.
* The PLIC pending bit of ID i + 1 during the hold and after the release, and any other external
  pending bit during the hold, are logged without a compare: the PLIC map, route, bound and
  retention before claim are open (SF-025, SF-026, SF-027, SF-028).
* Every wait for a pin-to-raw-bit transition is bounded at 64 `clk_smc_i` rises and raises with the
  last vector on expiry.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i`, `tb_temp_interrupt_i` and
  `tb_ext_interrupts_hi_i` to read 0, sample `tb_cpu_interrupts` as the baseline vector, require its
  bits [255:0] to read 0 and the whole vector to stay equal to the baseline for 16 consecutive rises.
. For each i in 0, 2, 3, ..., 16 in that order: drive input i = 1 alone, wait up to 64 rises for raw
  bit i to read 1 with no other bit moved, require that wait to be at least 3 rises, then require the
  vector to equal the baseline XOR `1 << i` and bits [255:0] to equal `1 << i` at each of 256
  consecutive rises; log the PLIC pending bit of ID i + 1 and every other external pending bit set.
. Drive input i = 0, wait up to 64 rises for raw bit i to read 0, require that wait to be at least
  3 rises, then require the vector to equal the baseline at each of the next 64 rises; log the PLIC
  pending bit of ID i + 1. The temperature pin must still read 0.
. After iterations i = 0, 2 and 16 print the matching `CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT<i>` line; after the walk print
  the assert, isolation and release lines.
. Read `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access, log the 32 bounded waits taken,
  then check the ordered terms BASELINE < ASSERT-i < HOLD-i < RELEASE-i for each i and the six
  checker lines.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT0` |Raw bit 0 rises, holds 256 rises with only that bit moved, falls, no latch
|`CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT2` |Raw bit 2 rises, holds 256 rises with only that bit moved, falls, no latch
|`CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT16` |Raw bit 16 rises, holds 256 rises with only that bit moved, falls, no latch
|`CHK-EXTIRQ-ASSERT` |16/16 inputs: raw bit i rises in at least 3 and at most 64 rises and holds 256; pending of ID i + 1 logged only
|`CHK-EXTIRQ-ISOLATION` |16 walks x 256 samples: every other raw external bit reads 0; other pending logged only
|`CHK-EXTIRQ-RELEASE` |16/16 raw bits fall within 64 rises and the vector returns to baseline; pending after release logged only
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered terms BASELINE < ASSERT-i < HOLD-i < RELEASE-i for all 16 inputs and the six checker lines, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the 32 bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: for every i in 0, 2, 3, ..., 16, raw bit i reads 1 at least 3 and within 64 rises
of its input rising, the vector equals the baseline XOR the bit at each of 256 rises with every other
raw external bit 0, and after release the bit reads 0 at least 3 and within 64 rises and the vector
equals the baseline for 64 rises (`CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT0`, `CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT2`, `CHK-EXTHOLD-BIT16`,
`CHK-EXTIRQ-ASSERT`, `CHK-EXTIRQ-ISOLATION`, `CHK-EXTIRQ-RELEASE`). The PLIC pending values are
measured only (LINKED-ISSUE SF-025, SF-026, SF-027, SF-028). `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all 49 terms
and the six checker lines appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Exactly
one SEP_IN access, the scratch read, is issued and answers OKAY. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-478-smc_ext_irq_low_bits_test]]
===== 478 `smc_ext_irq_low_bits_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_ext_irq_low_bits_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench inputs
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (raw bit 0) and `tb_top.tb_temp_interrupt_i` (raw bit 1); observed
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` (whole vector, compared against the baseline), the synchroniser outputs
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_sync` and `tb_top.tb_temp_interrupt_irq`, and `clk_smc_i`; scratch
register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `ext`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive external inputs 0 and 1 alone and together; compare vector.

*Test Coverage*:

* External interrupt inputs 0 and 1 map to raw `cpu_interrupts_o` bits 0 and 1 and are the only bits
  that move when those pins change (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt map table, bits
  `[255:0]`, and `smc-interrupts-risc-v-plic`).
* Each pin alone sets and clears exactly its own raw bit, and the probe of the matching
  synchroniser output agrees with the XOR of the vector and the baseline (probe consistency, not an
  independent check).
* Each transition takes at least 3 `clk_smc_i` rises, the depth of the three-flop synchroniser
  (`interrupts.adoc`); a faster path fails.
* With both pins high the XOR reads 3; releasing either pin first leaves exactly the other bit set,
  and releasing the second returns the vector to the baseline, so the two bits are independent.
* Every pin-to-raw-bit wait is bounded at 64 `clk_smc_i` rises and raises with the last XOR vector
  on expiry; each reached level must then be held for 64 rises.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the five bench signals to exist, read
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access.
. Drive both pins 0, sample `tb_cpu_interrupts` one rise later as the baseline, and require raw bits
  1:0 of the baseline and both synchroniser outputs to read 0.
. Bit 1 alone: drive `tb_temp_interrupt_i` = 1, wait up to 64 rises for the XOR to equal 0x2 and
  hold it for 64 rises; drive it 0, wait up to 64 rises for the XOR to equal 0 and hold it for 64
  rises. In every sample no bit outside the expected pair differs and the synchroniser outputs match
  the XOR.
. Bit 0 alone: the same rise and fall on `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` with XOR 0x1. Every single-pin and release transition
  must take at least 3 rises.
. Both pins, bit 0 released first: raise `tb_temp_interrupt_i` (XOR 0x2), then
  `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (XOR 0x3), hold 64 rises, release `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (XOR 0x2, hold 64
  rises), then release `tb_temp_interrupt_i` (XOR 0, hold 64 rises).
. Both pins, bit 1 released first: the same raise order, then release `tb_temp_interrupt_i` (XOR
  0x1) before `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (XOR 0).
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the four checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOW2-BIT1` |Input 1 alone sets then clears only raw bit 1, held 64 rises each way
|`CHK-LOW2-BIT0` |Input 0 alone sets then clears only raw bit 0, held 64 rises each way
|`CHK-LOW2-BOTH-BIT0-FIRST` |Both set (XOR 3); releasing input 0 first leaves bit 1, then baseline
|`CHK-LOW2-BOTH-BIT1-FIRST` |Both set (XOR 3); releasing input 1 first leaves bit 0, then baseline
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===
