*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-LOW2-BIT1`, `CHK-LOW2-BIT0`, `CHK-LOW2-BOTH-BIT0-FIRST` and
`CHK-LOW2-BOTH-BIT1-FIRST` hold: every transition reaches its XOR value at least 3 and within 64 rises
and holds it for 64 rises (0x2, 0x1, then 0x3 followed by 0x2 or 0x1 and 0), with the synchroniser
output probes agreeing with the vector. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the four checker lines appear in order;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Ten hold phases complete and at least one SEP_IN
access is issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The synchroniser output probes are compared for consistency with the vector only, not
as an independent check. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of
its own.

'''''

[[sec-479-smc_ext_irq_pulse_sampling_test]]
===== 479 `smc_ext_irq_pulse_sampling_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_ext_irq_pulse_sampling_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench input
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` driven with timed pulses (raw bit 0); observed
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` sampled on each `clk_smc_i` rise (bit 0 and the rest of the vector
against the baseline); scratch register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`; `clk_smc_i` period measured from two
consecutive rises.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `ext`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Pulse external input 0 at set widths and phases; read bit 0.

*Test Coverage*:

* External pins pass through a three-flop synchroniser before the raw vector, and a short pulse can
  be missed if it is not sampled (`interrupts.adoc`, `smc-interrupts-risc-v-plic`;
  `port_table.adoc`, `smc_ext_interrupts_i`); pulse capture is therefore not assumed.
* Wide pulses (4, 8 and 16 `clk_smc_i` periods at four quarter-period phases) are sampled: each
  reads as a single run of at least width minus one high samples on raw bit 0, leaves raw bit 0 at 0
  by the end of the window and moves no other raw bit (`smu-smc.adoc`: a pulse that stays high long
  enough to be sampled on `clk_smc` is captured).
* Sub-period pulses (1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a period at four phases) never latch: raw bit 0 is 0 at the
  64-rise ceiling, rises at most once, and the vector equals the baseline for 64 further rises.
* Whether each sub-period pulse was seen is measured and printed without a compare.
* The rise and fall delay of a held input is at least 3 `clk_smc_i` rises, the depth of the
  three-flop synchroniser, and within the 64-rise wait bound; the delay values are printed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` and `tb_cpu_interrupts` to
  exist, read `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access.
. Drive `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` = 0, measure the `clk_smc_i` period, sample the baseline vector and
  require raw bit 0 to read 0.
. For each wide width and each quarter-period phase (12 runs) drive one pulse after a rise, sample
  the vector at each of width plus 64 rises, require no other raw bit to differ from the baseline
  and raw bit 0 to read 0 at the last sample, require at least width minus one high samples in a
  single run, and log the high sample count.
. Error injection. Point: the `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` bench input. Kind: one sub-period pulse (1/4,
  2/4 or 3/4 of a `clk_smc_i` period) at each of four quarter-period phases, 12 runs, each sampled
  for 128 rises. Expected response: raw bit 0 reads 0 at rise 64 and rises at most once, no other
  raw bit moves in the first 64 rises, and the vector equals the baseline at each of the last 64
  rises; log what was seen.
. Eight times drive `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` = 1, count the rises until raw bit 0 reads 1 (bound 64),
  hold to 32 rises, drive 0, count the rises until raw bit 0 reads 0 (bound 64), hold to 32 rises,
  require every count to be at least 3, and log the minimum and maximum counts.
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S4 and the four checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EXTPULSE-WIDE` |12 wide pulses each read as one run of at least width minus one high samples
|`CHK-EXTPULSE-SHORT-NOLATCH` |12 short pulses: bit 0 at 0 by 64 rises, vector at baseline after
|`CHK-EXTPULSE-SHORT-SEEN-LOG` |Records which short pulses were seen, without comparing the result
|`CHK-EXTPULSE-LATENCY-LOG` |Prints 8 rise and fall delays; each is at least 3 and within the bound
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EXTPULSE-SHORT-NOLATCH` holds: all 12 sub-period pulses leave raw bit 0 at 0
by the 64-rise ceiling and the vector at the baseline for 64 further rises. `CHK-EXTPULSE-WIDE`
holds: every wide pulse reads as one run of at least width minus one high samples, leaves raw bit 0
low at the window end and moves no other raw bit. `CHK-EXTPULSE-SHORT-SEEN-LOG` records a
measurement and is not compared with an expected value. `CHK-EXTPULSE-LATENCY-LOG` holds when
every rise and fall delay is at least 3 rises.
`CHK-NONVAC` holds when all four step stamps and the four checker lines appear in order;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Exactly 12 wide, 12 short and 8 latency runs
complete and at least one SEP_IN access is issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Whether each sub-period pulse was seen is measured and printed without a compare
(`CHK-EXTPULSE-SHORT-SEEN-LOG`), and the rise and fall delay values are printed. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`
only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-480-smc_hang_data_timeout_window_test]]
===== 480 `smc_hang_data_timeout_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_data_timeout_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the register accesses; DMA jobs programmed
through `DMA_CTRL` (`CONFIG`, `SRC_ADDRESS`, `DST_ADDRESS`, `LENGTH`, strides, `NUM_REPETITIONS`,
`NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0`) with pass-all `INBOUND0` and `OUTBOUND0` filter entries; bench stall control
`tb_top.tb_output_axi_resp_hold` and handshake signals `tb_top.tb_output_axi_arvalid`, `_arready`,
`_awvalid`, `_awready` on SYS_OUT; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_data`,
`tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sys`, `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` and raw bit 286 of
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` on `clk_smc_i`; registers `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`,
`HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`; fuse
sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Stall a data-accelerator job below, beyond, at 0x40.

*Test Coverage*:

* The data-accelerator hang detector fires after the programmed count of consecutive cycles with
  outstanding transactions and no completion (`smc_base_config.rdl`,
  `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value`, `HANG_DET_CTRL.enable` and `irq_en`).
* A 16-rise stall against a 0x40 threshold keeps the data interrupt and raw bit 286 at 0.
* A stall held past the threshold raises the data interrupt and raw bit 286 within 128 rises of the
  handshake, `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL.irq` reads 1, the SYS and SEP detector interrupts stay 0
  while both of those detectors are armed with the same 0x40 threshold, and everything drops after
  the stall is released and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` is cleared.
* The programmed count sets the rise: a second stall held past a 0x80 threshold raises the data
  interrupt exactly 0x40 rises after the 0x40-threshold stall did (`smc_base_config.rdl`:
  threshold in clock cycles).
* Raw bit 286 carries the OR of the three hang detectors (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt
  map table, bit 286).
* A stall of exactly 0x40 rises is measured: the rise at which the data interrupt first reads 1 is
  printed without a compare, because the document does not say whether a stall equal to the
  threshold fires; the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the nine bench signals to exist and drive
  `tb_output_axi_resp_hold` = 0.
. Write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, program the `INBOUND0` and
  `OUTBOUND0` filters to pass all, write 0x40 to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` and read it
  back, write `enable | irq_en` to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` and read it back, read `DMA_CTRL`
  `DONE_0` as the baseline, and require the data, SYS and SEP interrupts and raw bit 286 to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT response hold `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`. Kind: a response
  stall of 16 rises, below the 0x40 threshold, on one 8-byte DMA job. Expected response: the data
  interrupt and raw bit 286 read 0 at each of 256 rises. Drive the hold to 1, program the job and
  require a non-zero `NEXT_ID_0`, wait up to 4096 rises for an AR or AW handshake on SYS_OUT,
  release the hold at rise 16, then poll `DONE_0` up to 50 times until it increments.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT response hold `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`. Kind: a response
  stall held beyond the 0x40 threshold on a second DMA job, with the SYS and SEP detectors armed at
  the same 0x40 threshold, then a stall held beyond a 0x80 threshold on a third job. Expected
  response: within 128 rises of the SYS_OUT handshake the data interrupt and raw bit 286 both rise
  with the SYS and SEP interrupts 0 at every rise and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL.irq` reads 1; after
  the release and a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` both read 0 within 128 rises; with
  threshold 0x80 both rise within 192 rises, again with the SYS and SEP interrupts 0 at every rise,
  and the data interrupt rise is exactly 0x40 rises later than in the second job. Setup and
  remaining actions: write 0x40 to the SYS and SEP threshold registers and `enable | irq_en` to
  both control registers before the second job; poll `DONE_0` until it increments after each
  release; write 0x80 to the data threshold with readback and re-arm before the third job; after it
  release, write 0, poll `DONE_0`, wait for both to read 0, write 0 to the SYS and SEP control
  registers and restore the data threshold to 0x40.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_OUT response hold `tb_output_axi_resp_hold`. Kind: a response
  stall of exactly 0x40 rises after the handshake, equal to the threshold, on a fourth DMA job.
  Expected response: none is required; the first rise at which the data interrupt reads 1 over 0x48
  sampled rises is recorded, and after a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` the data
  interrupt and raw bit 286 read 0 within 128 rises. Re-arm `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` and read it
  back before the job, poll `DONE_0` after the clear, then log the result.
. Release the hold, write 0 to `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`, restore the threshold to 0x1000, check
  the ordered step stamps S1 to S5, the three checker lines and four jobs started, then log the
  bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DATAWIN-BELOW` |A 16-rise stall below 0x40 keeps data irq and bit 286 at 0 for 256 rises
|`CHK-DATAWIN-BEYOND` |Stall past 0x40 raises data irq and bit 286, armed sys, sep 0, CTRL.irq 1; 0x80 shifts the rise by 0x40
|`CHK-DATAWIN-AT-LOG` |Records the first data irq rise for a stall of 0x40 rises; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps, the three checker lines and four DMA jobs all occurred
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DATAWIN-BELOW` and `CHK-DATAWIN-BEYOND` hold: the data interrupt and raw bit
286 stay 0 for the whole sub-threshold window, rise within 128 rises of the handshake for the
past-threshold stall with `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL.irq` = 1 and the armed SYS and SEP interrupts
0, read 0 again within 128 rises of the release, and rise exactly 0x40 rises later when the
threshold is 0x80. `CHK-DATAWIN-AT-LOG` records the measured rise without
a compare. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the three checker lines appear in order
and four DMA jobs were started; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Five phases
complete and at least 60 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The rise at which the data interrupt first reads 1 for a stall of exactly 0x40 rises
is printed without a compare, because the document does not say whether a stall equal to the
threshold fires. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its
own.

'''''

[[sec-481-smc_hang_irq_or_matrix_test]]
===== 481 `smc_hang_irq_or_matrix_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_irq_or_matrix_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for every register access; no bench pin is
driven; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sys`, `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`,
`tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_data` and raw bits 285, 286 and 287 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` on
`clk_smc_i`; registers `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`
(`enable`, `irq_en`, `irq_test`, `irq`) and the three `HANG_DET_*_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` registers; fuse
sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Fire hang irq_test in pairs and orders; check bit 286 OR.

*Test Coverage*:

* Raw bit 286 asserts while any of the three AXI hang detectors asserts and drops only when the last
  one drops (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt map table, bit 286).
* `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq_test` asserts a detector interrupt without a bus stall when `enable` and
  `irq_en` are set, and `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq` reads that detector's live level
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`).
* With threshold 0 written and read back, `irq_test` still asserts the detector interrupt, raw bit
  286 and `CTRL.irq` (`smc_base_config.rdl`, `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value`); threshold 0 on a
  stalled bus is not exercised.
* The neighbouring raw bits 285 and 287 stay at their baseline 0 while bit 286 toggles.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the three hang nets and `tb_cpu_interrupts` to exist,
  sample the baseline and require raw bits 285, 286 and 287, the three nets and the three
  `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` reads to be 0.
. Start a monitor that samples the vector each rise and records any deviation of raw bits 285 and
  287 from the baseline. For each of the three detector pairs write `enable | irq_en | irq_test` to
  both control registers, wait up to 64 rises for the nets of that pair and raw bit 286 to read 1,
  read both `irq` bits, clear the first control register, require raw bit 286 to hold 1 for 64 rises
  with only the second `irq` reading 1, clear the second, and wait up to 64 rises for raw bit 286
  and all nets to read 0 with every `irq` 0.
. For each of the six clear orders fire all three detectors, wait for all nets and raw bit 286 to
  read 1 with every `irq` 1, then clear them in order; after each clear that leaves a detector
  asserted hold raw bit 286 at 1 for 16 rises and require the `irq` bits and nets to equal the
  remaining set, and after the last clear wait up to 64 rises for raw bit 286 to read 0.
. Stop the monitor and require at least one sample and no deviation of raw bits 285 and 287.
. For each detector write 0 to its threshold register and read it back as 0, write `enable`,
  `irq_en` and `irq_test` together to its control register, wait for its own net and raw bit 286 to
  read 1 with only its `irq` set, write 0 to the control register, wait for raw bit 286 and all nets
  to read 0, and restore the threshold to 0x1000 with a readback.
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the four checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-HANGOR-PAIRS` |In 3 pairs raw 286 is 1 while either fires, 0 after both clear
|`CHK-HANGOR-ORDERS` |In 6 clear orders raw 286 equals any detector remaining; each CTRL.irq follows
|`CHK-HANGOR-NEIGHBOURS` |Raw bits 285 and 287 stay at baseline 0 at every sampled rise
|`CHK-HANGOR-THR0-TEST` |With threshold 0 irq_test still raises net, raw 286, CTRL.irq
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-HANGOR-PAIRS`, `CHK-HANGOR-ORDERS`, `CHK-HANGOR-NEIGHBOURS` and
`CHK-HANGOR-THR0-TEST` hold: raw bit 286 equals the OR of the three hang nets within 64 rises of
each change, each `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` equals its own detector's state, raw bits 285 and 287 read 0
at every sampled rise, and threshold 0 does not prevent the `irq_test` assertion. `CHK-NONVAC` holds
when all five step stamps and the four checker lines appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs
the bounded waits. Five phases complete and at least 150 SEP_IN accesses are issued.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Threshold 0 on a stalled bus is not exercised. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the
bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-482-smc_hang_sep_drop_controls_test]]
===== 482 `smc_hang_sep_drop_controls_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_sep_drop_controls_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the held read of `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` and
the setup accesses; JTAG AXI agent (`env.jtag_axi_agent`) for every `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` write
and read during the stall; bench stall control `tb_top.tb_sep_axi_r_hold`; SEP_IN AR handshake
signals `tb_top.s_axi_arvalid` and `tb_top.s_axi_arready`; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` and
raw bit 286 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` on `clk_smc_i`; registers `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`
(`enable`, `irq_en`, `irq_test`, `irq`), `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`,
`HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`; fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`,
`tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the control value written at each toggle of the held-read
phase.

*Objective*: Change SEP hang controls during a held read; observe.

*Test Coverage*:

* Clearing `irq_en` while the read stays held drops the SEP detector interrupt and raw bit 286, and
  `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq` reads 0 (`smc_base_config.rdl`: `irq_o` follows the detector only while
  `irq_en` and `enable` are set, `irq` is a live level and not a latch).
* The interrupt stays at 0 for 128 further rises and across three control reads while `irq_en`
  stays clear.
* With `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` armed (`enable | irq_en`) and the SEP interrupt live, clearing
  `enable` while `irq_en` stays set drops the interrupt and raw bit 286 within one rise of the
  readback and `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq` reads 0 (`smc_base_config.rdl`: `enable` 0 forces `irq_o` low;
  `interrupts.adoc`, bit 286).
* Control values with `enable` or `irq_en` clear force the interrupt and raw bit 286 to 0 on a live
  stall (`HANG_DET_CTRL.enable` and `irq_en` descriptions); eight seeded toggles are applied.
* How soon the interrupt returns after `irq_en` is set late, and the interplay of `irq_test` with a
  persisting timeout, are measured and printed without a compare because the documents do not give
  expected values; the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the five bench signals to exist, drive
  `tb_sep_axi_r_hold` = 0, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`, write
  0x40 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` and read it back, write `enable | irq_en` to
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and read it back, and require `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` and raw bit 286 to
  read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a SEP_IN read of
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` held past the 0x40 threshold, then `enable` written over JTAG with `irq_en`
  cleared while the read stays held. Expected response: `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` rises within 128 rises
  of the AR handshake; after the write, whose readback must equal it, both probes read 0 at each of
  the next 65 rises with the read still held and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL.irq` reads 0. Drive the
  hold to 1 before the read and wait up to 256 rises for the AR handshake.
. Require both probes 0 at each of 128 more rises with no write, then read `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`
  three times over JTAG and require `irq` 0 and both probes 0 each time with the read still held.
. Write `enable | irq_en` and wait up to 128 rises for `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`, write `irq_en` alone
  (`enable` cleared) and read it back, require both probes 0 one rise later and
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL.irq` 0 with the read still held, then write `enable` and require both
  probes 0 at each of the next 65 rises.
. Write `enable | irq_en` and wait up to 128 rises for `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`, write `irq_en` alone,
  write `enable | irq_en` again and wait up to 128 rises for the interrupt, release the hold and
  wait up to 256 rises for the read to complete, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, and log the
  rises counted.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` over JTAG. Kind:
  a second held read and, from 60 rises after the AR handshake, eight JTAG control writes with
  readback (the first `enable | irq_en`, the rest chosen by the run seed from 0, `enable`, `irq_en`
  and `enable | irq_en`). Expected response: sampled one rise after each write, both probes read 0
  whenever the value was not `enable | irq_en`, and at least one such value must have been applied
  while the interrupt was live. Re-arm before the read; afterwards release the hold, write 0 to
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and wait up to 128 rises for both probes to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`. Kind: a third
  held read with `irq_test` written together with `enable` and `irq_en` while the timeout persists.
  Expected response: none is required; the samples are logged. Re-arm before the read, wait for
  `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`, write all three of `enable`, `irq_en` and `irq_test`, write
  `enable | irq_en` (stall persists, sample logged), write all three again, release the hold and
  sample, write `enable | irq_en` and sample, and log the three samples.
. Release the hold, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, restore the threshold to 0x1000 and wait up
  to 128 rises for both probes to read 0; check the ordered step stamps S1 to S7, the seven checker
  lines and three held reads started, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DROPCTL-IRQEN-CLEAR` |Clearing irq_en on a held stall drops sep irq, raw 286 and CTRL.irq to 0
|`CHK-DROPCTL-GATE-HOLD` |Irq stays 0 for 128 rises and three CTRL reads while irq_en stays clear, read held
|`CHK-DROPCTL-ENABLE-CLEAR` |Clearing enable with irq_en set on a live stall drops sep irq, raw 286, CTRL.irq
|`CHK-DROPCTL-REENABLE-LOG` |Measures and prints rises to sep irq after a late irq_en, no compare
|`CHK-DROPCTL-TOGGLE-GATING` |Eight toggles: enable or irq_en clear reads sep irq and raw 286 at 0
|`CHK-DROPCTL-TOGGLE-LOG` |Records the seeded toggle values and samples, without comparing them
|`CHK-DROPCTL-BOTH-CAUSES-LOG` |Records irq_test with a persisting stall, no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps, the seven checker lines and three held reads all occurred
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DROPCTL-IRQEN-CLEAR`, `CHK-DROPCTL-GATE-HOLD`,
`CHK-DROPCTL-ENABLE-CLEAR` and `CHK-DROPCTL-TOGGLE-GATING` hold: the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286
read 0 after `irq_en` is cleared on a live stall for 65 and then 128 rises, and one rise after
`enable` is cleared with `irq_en` set, with `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL.irq` 0 and the read still held,
and every toggle readback matches the written value. `CHK-DROPCTL-REENABLE-LOG`,
`CHK-DROPCTL-TOGGLE-LOG` and `CHK-DROPCTL-BOTH-CAUSES-LOG` record measurements and are not compared
with expected values. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all seven step stamps and the seven checker lines appear
in order and three held reads were started; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Seven
phases complete and at least 11 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: How soon the interrupt returns after `irq_en` is set late, and the interplay of
`irq_test` with a persisting timeout, are measured and printed without a compare, because the
documents give no expected values; the seeded toggle values and samples are recorded without
comparing them. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-483-smc_hang_sep_threshold_test]]
===== 483 `smc_hang_sep_threshold_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_sep_threshold_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the held reads of `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` and
the setup accesses; JTAG AXI agent (`env.jtag_axi_agent`) for the threshold and control writes made
during a stall; bench stall control `tb_top.tb_sep_axi_r_hold`; SEP_IN AR handshake signals
`tb_top.s_axi_arvalid` and `tb_top.s_axi_arready`; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` on
`clk_smc_i`, counted in rises from the AR handshake; registers `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`,
`HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`; fuse
sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only the order of the small-threshold walk;
every threshold is walked.

*Objective*: Update SEP hang threshold in held reads; measure irq rise.

*Test Coverage*:

* A threshold write takes effect when the stall count next restarts, so it does not change a stall
  already being timed (`smc_base_config.rdl`, `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value`).
* Raising the threshold from 0x40 to 0x400 after 16 rises does not stop the running stall from
  raising the interrupt from rise 0x40 (the original threshold) to rise 128 of the AR handshake.
* Lowering the threshold from 0x400 to 0x40 after 32 rises leaves the interrupt at 0 through rise
  512 and raises it before rise 1088; the threshold then reads back 0x40.
* The stored threshold 0x40 applies to the next stall: the interrupt rises from rise 0x40 to rise
  128.
* Threshold 0x1000, written with readback, raises the interrupt from rise 0x1000 to 0x1000 plus 64
  rises, and small values 1, 2 and 16 (shuffled by the run seed) each raise it from the value to
  the value plus 64 rises; the threshold is the count of consecutive cycles before a timeout fires
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`, `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`). The threshold's reset value is not
  exercised.
* The exact rise relative to each threshold, and the rise after a threshold write combined with an
  `irq_en` clear and set, are measured and printed without a compare; the specification does not
  state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the four bench signals to exist, shuffle the small
  thresholds with the run seed, drive `tb_sep_axi_r_hold` = 0, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`,
  `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, and require `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep` to read
  0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold and `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`
  over JTAG. Kind: a SEP_IN read of `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` held past the 0x40 threshold, with the
  threshold raised to 0x400 16 rises after the AR handshake. Expected response: the interrupt rises
  from rise 0x40 to rise 128 of the AR handshake. Before the read write 0x40 to the threshold with
  readback and `enable | irq_en` to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`; afterwards release the hold, write 0 to
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and wait up to 128 rises for the interrupt to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold and the threshold register over JTAG. Kind:
  a read held with threshold 0x400 armed, with the threshold lowered to 0x40 after 32 rises.
  Expected response: the interrupt reads 0 through rise 512 and rises by rise 1088, and the
  threshold then reads back 0x40. Afterwards release the hold, read the threshold, and wait up to
  128 rises for the interrupt to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold. Kind: a new held read with the threshold
  0x40 still stored from the previous step. Expected response: the interrupt rises from rise 0x40
  to rise 128. Afterwards release, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and wait for it to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold, the threshold and control registers over
  JTAG. Kind: a read held with threshold 0x400 armed; after 32 rises the threshold is written 0x40,
  then `irq_en` alone and then `enable | irq_en`. Expected response: the interrupt rises within
  1232 rises. Afterwards release, write 0 and wait for the interrupt to read 0; log the rises from
  the re-enable.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold. Kind: a read held past threshold 0x1000,
  written with readback and armed. Expected response: the interrupt rises from rise 0x1000 to rise
  0x1000 plus 64. Afterwards release and write 0; log the rise offset.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold. Kind: for each of the thresholds 1, 2 and
  16 in shuffled order, written with readback and armed, a read held past the value. Expected
  response: the interrupt rises from the rise equal to the value to the value plus 64. After each,
  release and write 0; log the offsets.
. Release the hold, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, restore the threshold to 0x1000, check the
  ordered step stamps S1 to S8, the eight checker lines and eight held reads started, then log the
  bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-THR-RAISE-DURING` |Raise to 0x400 mid-stall: sep irq still rises from rise 0x40 to 128, then clears
|`CHK-THR-LOWER-DURING` |Lower to 0x40 mid-stall: irq 0 through rise 512, rises by 1088, reads 0x40
|`CHK-THR-AFTER-COMPLETION` |Next stall uses stored 0x40: sep irq from rise 0x40 to 128
|`CHK-THR-AFTER-ENABLE-CLEAR-LOG` |Prints the rise after the threshold write; only the bound fails
|`CHK-THR-DEFAULT-BEYOND` |With threshold 0x1000 the sep irq rises from rise 0x1000 to 0x1000 plus 64
|`CHK-THR-DEFAULT-EXACT-LOG` |Records the rise offset from 0x1000, without comparing it
|`CHK-THR-SMALL-RISE` |Thresholds 1, 2 and 16 each raise sep irq from the value to the value plus 64
|`CHK-THR-SMALL-LOG` |Records each small threshold's rise offset, without comparing it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps, the eight checker lines and eight held reads all occurred
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-THR-RAISE-DURING`, `CHK-THR-LOWER-DURING`, `CHK-THR-AFTER-COMPLETION`,
`CHK-THR-DEFAULT-BEYOND` and `CHK-THR-SMALL-RISE` hold: the interrupt rises at or after the programmed
count (0x40 in the raise and after-completion stalls) and within the stated ceiling of the AR
handshake in every stall, stays 0 through rise 512 after the lowering write, the
lowered threshold reads back 0x40, and the interrupt reads 0 within 128 rises of the release.
`CHK-THR-AFTER-ENABLE-CLEAR-LOG`, `CHK-THR-DEFAULT-EXACT-LOG` and `CHK-THR-SMALL-LOG` record
measurements and are not compared with expected values. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all eight step
stamps and the eight checker lines appear in order and eight held reads were started;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Eight phases complete and at least 40 SEP_IN
accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The exact rise relative to each threshold, and the rise after a threshold write
combined with an `irq_en` clear and set, are measured and printed without a compare, because the
specification does not state them; only the wait bound can fail. The threshold's reset value is not
exercised. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-484-smc_hang_sep_timeout_window_test]]
===== 484 `smc_hang_sep_timeout_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_sep_timeout_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the held reads of `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` and
the register accesses; JTAG AXI agent (`env.jtag_axi_agent`) for the `HANG_DET_*_CTRL` status reads;
bench stall control `tb_top.tb_sep_axi_r_hold`; SEP_IN AR handshake signals `tb_top.s_axi_arvalid`
and `tb_top.s_axi_arready`; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`, `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sys`,
`tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_data` and raw bit 286 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` on `clk_smc_i`;
registers `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and
`HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`; fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Stall a SEP_IN read below, beyond, at threshold 0x40.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SEP_AXI hang detector fires after the programmed count of consecutive cycles with an
  outstanding transaction and no completion (`smc_base_config.rdl`,
  `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value`, `HANG_DET_CTRL.enable` and `irq_en`; `overview.adoc` lists the
  SEP inbound link among the watched links).
* A 16-rise stall against a 0x40 threshold keeps the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286 at 0 for 256
  rises from the AR handshake.
* A stall held past the threshold raises the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286 within 128 rises, the SYS
  and data interrupts stay 0 while both of those detectors are armed with the same 0x40 threshold,
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL.irq` reads 1 while the other two `irq` bits read 0, and everything drops
  after the release and a write of 0 to the control register.
* Raw bit 286 carries the OR of the three hang detectors (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt
  map table, bit 286).
* The rise for a stall of exactly 0x40 rises is measured and printed without a compare; the
  specification does not state the value.
* The programmed count sets the rise: the SEP interrupt rises exactly 0x1000 minus 0x40 rises later
  with threshold 0x1000 than with threshold 0x40 (`smc_base_config.rdl`: threshold in clock cycles).
  The rises from the AR handshake to the SEP interrupt and to raw bit 286 are printed; the waits are
  bounded.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the seven bench signals to exist, drive
  `tb_sep_axi_r_hold` = 0, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`, write
  0x40 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` with readback, write `enable | irq_en` to
  `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and read it back, and require the SEP, SYS and data interrupts and raw bit
  286 to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a SEP_IN read
  stalled for 16 rises, below the 0x40 threshold. Expected response: the SEP interrupt and raw bit
  286 read 0 at each of 256 rises. Wait up to 256 rises for the AR handshake before releasing the
  hold at rise 16, then wait up to 256 rises for the read to complete.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a second SEP_IN
  read held past the 0x40 threshold, with the SYS and data detectors armed at the same 0x40
  threshold. Expected response: within 128 rises of the AR handshake the SEP interrupt and raw bit
  286 both rise with the SYS and data interrupts 0 at every rise, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` read over
  JTAG shows `irq` = 1 and of the three `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` bits only the SEP one is set; after
  the release and a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286 read 0
  within 128 rises. Before the read write 0x40 to the SYS and data threshold registers and
  `enable | irq_en` to both control registers; after the release wait for the read, and at the end
  write 0 to the SYS and data control registers.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a third read
  stalled for exactly 0x40 rises after the AR handshake, equal to the threshold. Expected response:
  none is required; the first rise of the SEP interrupt and of raw bit 286 over 0x48 sampled rises
  is recorded, and after a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` the interrupt clears within 128
  rises. Re-arm `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` before the read, then log the result.
. Error injection. Point: the SEP_IN read response hold `tb_sep_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a fourth held
  read with threshold 0x40 and a fifth with threshold 0x1000, written with readback, each re-armed.
  Expected response: in each measurement the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286 both rise within the
  threshold plus 256 rises, and the SEP interrupt rise with threshold 0x1000 exceeds the rise with
  threshold 0x40 by exactly 0x1000 minus 0x40. After each measurement release the hold, write 0 and
  wait for both to clear; log both rises and their difference for each threshold.
. Release the hold, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and restore the threshold to 0x1000; check
  the ordered step stamps S1 to S6, the four checker lines and five held reads started, then log the
  bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SEPWIN-BELOW` |A 16-rise stall below 0x40 keeps the sep irq and raw bit 286 at 0 for 256 rises
|`CHK-SEPWIN-BEYOND` |Stall past 0x40 raises sep irq, bit 286; armed sys, data 0; only SEP CTRL.irq
|`CHK-SEPWIN-AT-LOG` |Records the first sep irq rise for a stall of 0x40 rises; no compare
|`CHK-SEPWIN-EXACT-DELTA` |Sep irq rise at 0x1000 minus rise at 0x40 equals 0x1000 minus 0x40
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps, the four checker lines and five held reads all occurred
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SEPWIN-BELOW` and `CHK-SEPWIN-BEYOND` hold: the SEP interrupt and raw bit 286
stay 0 for the whole sub-threshold window, rise within 128 rises of the AR handshake for the
past-threshold stall with the armed SYS and data interrupts 0 and only `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL.irq`
set, and read 0 again within 128 rises of the release. `CHK-SEPWIN-EXACT-DELTA` holds when the SEP
interrupt rise moves by exactly the threshold difference. `CHK-SEPWIN-AT-LOG` records a measurement
and is not compared with an expected value. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all six step
stamps and the four checker lines appear in order and five held reads were started;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Six phases complete and at least 22 SEP_IN accesses
are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The rise for a stall of exactly 0x40 rises is measured and printed without a compare,
because the specification does not state it; the rises from the AR handshake to the SEP interrupt
and to raw bit 286 are printed. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no
compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-485-smc_hang_sys_timeout_window_test]]
===== 485 `smc_hang_sys_timeout_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_sys_timeout_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the register accesses; SYS_IN AXI agent
(`env.sys_in_axi_agent`) for the held reads of `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`, which must answer OKAY; bench
stall control `tb_top.tb_sys_axi_r_hold`; SYS_IN AR handshake signals `tb_top.sys_axi_arvalid` and
`tb_top.sys_axi_arready`; observed `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sys`, `tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`,
`tb_top.tb_axi_hang_irq_data` and raw bit 286 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` on `clk_smc_i`;
registers `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`,
`HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL` and the `INBOUND0` filter `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR` and `FILTER_CONFIG`
registers; fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Stall a SYS_IN read below, beyond, at threshold 0x40.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SYS_AXI hang detector fires after the programmed count of consecutive cycles with an
  outstanding transaction and no completion (`smc_base_config.rdl`,
  `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value`, `HANG_DET_CTRL.enable` and `irq_en`; `overview.adoc` lists the
  system inbound link among the watched links).
* A 16-rise stall against a 0x40 threshold keeps the SYS interrupt and raw bit 286 at 0 for 256
  rises from the AR handshake.
* A stall held past the threshold raises the SYS interrupt and raw bit 286 within 128 rises, the SEP
  and data interrupts stay 0 while both of those detectors are armed with the same 0x40 threshold,
  `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL.irq` reads 1, and everything drops after the release and a write of 0 to
  the control register.
* The programmed count sets the rise: a second stall held past a 0x80 threshold raises the SYS
  interrupt exactly 0x40 rises after the 0x40-threshold stall did (`smc_base_config.rdl`:
  threshold in clock cycles).
* Raw bit 286 carries the OR of the three hang detectors (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt
  map table, bit 286).
* The rise for a stall of exactly 0x40 rises is measured and printed without a compare, because the
  document does not say whether a stall equal to the threshold fires; the specification does not
  state the value.
* The `INBOUND0` filter is set to pass all for the test and restored to its register defaults.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the seven bench signals to exist and drive
  `tb_sys_axi_r_hold` = 0.
. Program `INBOUND0` to pass all (start 0, end 0x00FF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF, pass-all configuration) and
  read the configuration back, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL` and `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`,
  write 0x40 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` with readback, write `enable | irq_en` to
  `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` with readback, and require the SYS, SEP and data interrupts and raw bit
  286 to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_IN read response hold `tb_sys_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a SYS_IN read
  stalled for 16 rises, below the 0x40 threshold. Expected response: the SYS interrupt and raw bit
  286 read 0 at each of 256 rises. Wait up to 256 rises for the AR handshake before releasing the
  hold at rise 16, then wait up to 256 rises for the read to complete.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_IN read response hold `tb_sys_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a second SYS_IN
  read held past the 0x40 threshold, with the SEP and data detectors armed at the same 0x40
  threshold, then another read held past a 0x80 threshold. Expected response: within 128 rises of
  the AR handshake the SYS interrupt and raw bit 286 both rise with the SEP and data interrupts 0 at
  every rise and `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` read through SEP_IN shows `irq` = 1; after the release and
  a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` both read 0 within 128 rises; with threshold 0x80 both
  rise within 192 rises, again with the SEP and data interrupts 0 at every rise, and the SYS
  interrupt rise is exactly 0x40 rises later than in the 0x40-threshold stall. Before the second
  read write 0x40 to the SEP and data threshold registers and `enable | irq_en` to both control
  registers; after each release wait for the read; write 0x80 to the SYS threshold with readback
  and re-arm before the third read; after it release, write 0, wait for both to read 0, write 0 to
  the SEP and data control registers and restore the SYS threshold to 0x40.
. Error injection. Point: the SYS_IN read response hold `tb_sys_axi_r_hold`. Kind: a fourth read
  stalled for exactly 0x40 rises after the AR handshake, equal to the threshold. Expected response:
  none is required; the first rise of the SYS interrupt over 0x48 sampled rises is recorded, and
  after a write of 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` the interrupt clears within 128 rises. Wait for the
  read after the release, then log the result.
. Release the hold, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, restore the threshold to 0x1000, restore the
  `INBOUND0` configuration, start and end registers to their register defaults and read the
  configuration back; check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5, the three checker lines and four held
  reads started, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SYSWIN-BELOW` |A 16-rise stall below 0x40 keeps the sys irq and raw bit 286 at 0 for 256 rises
|`CHK-SYSWIN-BEYOND` |Stall past 0x40 raises sys irq, bit 286; armed sep, data 0; 0x80 shifts rise by 0x40
|`CHK-SYSWIN-AT-LOG` |Records the first sys irq rise for a stall of 0x40 rises; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps, the three checker lines and four held reads all occurred
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SYSWIN-BELOW` and `CHK-SYSWIN-BEYOND` hold: the SYS interrupt and raw bit 286
stay 0 for the whole sub-threshold window, rise within 128 rises of the AR handshake for the
past-threshold stall with the armed SEP and data interrupts 0 and `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL.irq` = 1,
read 0 again within 128 rises of the release, and rise exactly 0x40 rises later when the threshold
is 0x80. `CHK-SYSWIN-AT-LOG` records the measured rise without
a compare. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the three checker lines appear in order
and four held reads were started; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Five phases
complete and at least 19 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The rise for a stall of exactly 0x40 rises is measured and printed without a compare,
because the document does not say whether a stall equal to the threshold fires. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`
only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-486-smc_irq_csr_readback_test]]
===== 486 `smc_irq_csr_readback_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_irq_csr_readback_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), frontdoor accesses only, no bench pin or probe;
registers `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`,
`HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`, `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`,
`HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` (`smc_base_config.rdl`) and `SMC_ATTRIBUTES`
(`cpu_ctrl.rdl`, 64-bit access); fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Read back hang detector registers; check isolation; log counts.

*Test Coverage*:

* `HANG_DET_CTRL.enable`, `irq_en` and `irq_test` are read-write and each reads back as written with
  `irq` 0 when written alone (`smc_base_config.rdl`).
* `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq` is read-only: writing bit 12 alone leaves every defined bit at 0
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`: "Writes are ignored").
* `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value` holds the full 20-bit range, read back for 0, 1, 0x1000 and
  0xFFFFF on each of the three detectors (`smc_base_config.rdl`).
* Writing one detector's control and threshold registers changes none of the other five registers,
  and restoring the written detector returns all six registers to their saved values.
* `SMC_ATTRIBUTES.num_ext_interrupts` and `num_cpu_interrupts` are read and printed; the document
  gives 256 external and 328 CPU interrupts (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC CPU Interrupt Vector Map) but
  the leaf only records the values without comparing them.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish and save the control and threshold registers of the SYS_AXI,
  SEP_AXI and DATA_ACCEL detectors.
. For each detector and each of `enable`, `irq_en` and `irq_test` write that bit alone, read the
  control register and require the defined bits to equal the value written with `irq` 0, then write
  0 and require the defined bits to read 0 (nine writes).
. Error injection. Point: the control register of each of the three detectors. Kind: a write of the
  read-only `HANG_DET_CTRL.irq` bit (bit 12) alone. Expected response: the defined bits read 0, and
  after a write of 0 they read 0 again.
. For each detector write 0 to the control register and then write each threshold 0, 1, 0x1000 and
  0xFFFFF, requiring bits 19:0 to read back equal (twelve writes).
. For each detector as the written one: read all six registers, write `enable | irq_en` to its
  control register and 0x123 to its threshold, read all six again and require the written detector
  to read those values and the other two to read unchanged, write 0 and the saved threshold back,
  and require the written detector to read 0 and the saved threshold and the others to read as
  before.
. Read `SMC_ATTRIBUTES` (64-bit) and log `num_ext_interrupts` and `num_cpu_interrupts`.
. Write 0 and the saved threshold to every detector and require each control register to read 0 on
  the defined bits and each threshold to read its saved value; check the ordered step stamps S1 to
  S7 and the five checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-HANGREG-CTRL-RW` |enable, irq_en and irq_test each read back as written with irq 0, then clear
|`CHK-HANGREG-IRQ-RO` |Writing the irq bit alone leaves every defined CTRL bit at 0 on all three
|`CHK-HANGREG-THR-RANGE` |Thresholds 0, 1, 0x1000 and 0xFFFFF read back equal in bits 19:0, restored
|`CHK-HANGREG-ISOLATION` |Writing one detector leaves the other five registers unchanged
|`CHK-ATTR-COUNTS-LOG` |Records num_ext_interrupts and num_cpu_interrupts without comparing them
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all five checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-HANGREG-CTRL-RW`, `CHK-HANGREG-IRQ-RO`, `CHK-HANGREG-THR-RANGE` and
`CHK-HANGREG-ISOLATION` hold: each control field reads back as written with `irq` 0, a write of the
`irq` bit alone reads 0, each of the four thresholds reads back equal over bits 19:0, a write to one
detector changes none of the other five registers, and the final restore returns control registers
to 0 and thresholds to their saved values. `CHK-ATTR-COUNTS-LOG` records the two counts and is not
compared with 256 or 328. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all seven step stamps and the five checker lines
appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Seven phases complete and at least
80 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `SMC_ATTRIBUTES.num_ext_interrupts` and `num_cpu_interrupts` are recorded and not
compared with the 256 and 328 the document gives. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits
taken and has no compare of its own.
'''''

[[sec-487-smc_irq_reserved_idle_zero_test]]
===== 487 `smc_irq_reserved_idle_zero_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_irq_reserved_idle_zero_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench input
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (raw bit 0, liveness control only); observed the whole of
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` (328 bits, raw bits 287, 327 to 324, 323 to 320, 264 to 266, 268 to 281
and 283 to 285 in particular) on each `clk_smc_i` rise; scratch register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`; fuse
sense signal `tb_fuse_sense_done`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Sample the idle raw vector; reserved bits read 0.

*Test Coverage*:

* Raw bit 287 and the tail bits 327 to 324 are reserved and tied to zero (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC
  indexed interrupt map table, rows 287 and `[327:324]`), so they read 0 at every idle rise.
* The vector is shown to be live first: raising `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` moves raw bit 0 and the
  vector returns to the baseline when it is released, so an all-zero window is not a stuck probe.
* The internal bits 323 to 320 (CLA clock stop, CLA interrupt, DMA complete and Zeroer complete) and
  the peripheral-owned bits 264 to 266, 268 to 281 and 283 to 285 are sampled over the same window
  and printed without a compare, because the specification does not state their idle
  value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` to exist and `tb_cpu_interrupts`
  to be at least 328 bits wide, read `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access, drive
  `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` = 0 and sample the baseline vector one rise later.
. Drive `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` = 1 and wait up to 64 rises for the whole vector to equal the
  baseline with bit 0 set, then drive 0 and wait up to 64 rises for the vector to equal the
  baseline.
. Sample 258 consecutive rises with every source idle and require raw bits 287 and 327 to 324 to
  read 0 at every rise.
. Log the distinct values of raw bits 323 to 320 over the window.
. Log the distinct values of the peripheral-owned raw bits over the window, then check the ordered
  step stamps S1 to S5 and the four checker lines and log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-RSVDIDLE-287` |Raw bit 287 reads 0 at each of the 258 idle rises
|`CHK-RSVDIDLE-TAIL` |Raw bits 327 to 324 read 0 at each of the 258 idle rises
|`CHK-RSVDIDLE-INTERNAL-LOG` |Records the distinct values of raw bits 323 to 320; no compare
|`CHK-RSVDIDLE-PERIPH-LOG` |Records the distinct values of the peripheral-owned raw bits; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-RSVDIDLE-287` and `CHK-RSVDIDLE-TAIL` hold: raw bit 287 and raw bits 327 to
324 read 0 at each of 258 consecutive idle rises after the bit-0 liveness control moved the vector
and returned it to the baseline. `CHK-RSVDIDLE-INTERNAL-LOG` and `CHK-RSVDIDLE-PERIPH-LOG` record
values and are not compared with an expected value. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and
the four checker lines appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Five phases
complete and at least one SEP_IN access is issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The internal raw bits 323 to 320 and the peripheral-owned raw bits 264 to 266, 268 to
281 and 283 to 285 are sampled and printed without a compare, because the specification does not
state their idle value. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of
its own.

'''''

[[sec-488-smc_irq_vector_assembly_test]]
===== 488 `smc_irq_vector_assembly_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_irq_vector_assembly_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for the register accesses, with the output fabric
filters programmed to pass all; bench inputs `tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (raw bit 0),
`tb_top.tb_ext_interrupts_hi_i` (bit 14 of the [16:2] bus, raw bit 16),
`tb_top.tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts` (bits 0 and 7, raw bits 256 and 263) and
`tb_top.tb_ndmreset_request` (raw bit 267); register-driven sources `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` (raw bit
286), inbound mailboxes 0 and 31 (`IRQEN`, `WRITE_DATA`, `CTRL`, `IRQS`; raw bits 288 and 319) and
the zeroer (`ZEROER_CTRL` destination, size and status; raw bit 323); `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` for the
mailbox clock enable; observed `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` (328 bits),
`tb_top.tb_peripheral_interrupts`, `tb_top.tb_mailbox_interrupts` and `tb_top.tb_zeroer_intp` on
each `clk_smc_i` rise; fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and
`tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Assert sources in every vector region; compare to baseline.

*Test Coverage*:

* The raw `cpu_interrupts_o` vector is assembled from external inputs, SEP mailbox interrupts, the
  NDM reset request, the hang detector OR and the internal sources at the bit positions of the
  indexed map (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt map table and SMC CPU Interrupt Vector Map):
  raw bits 0, 16, 256, 263, 267 and 286 each appear at their own position.
* All sources together read the cumulative mask, hold it for 256 rises with
  `tb_peripheral_interrupts` unchanged, and dropping them in reverse order removes one bit at a
  time.
* Raw bit 287 and raw bits 327 to 324 are reserved and read 0 at every sampled rise
  (`interrupts.adoc`, rows 287 and `[327:324]`).
* Region edges stay clean: raw bit 255 reads 0 while raw bit 256 is high, raw bit 287 reads 0 while
  raw bit 286 is high, and raw bit 320 stays at its baseline while inbound mailbox 31 is pushed.
* The zeroer completion appears as a pulse on raw bit 323 (`interrupts.adoc`, row 323).
* Raw bits 319 to 288 are excluded from the compare; the levels of raw bits 288 and 319 after the
  mailbox 0 and mailbox 31 pushes are printed, because the table places those mailbox channels there
  and the leaf does not compare them; the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require `tb_cpu_interrupts` to be at least 328 bits wide,
  sample the baseline vector, read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and set the mailbox clock enable, and
  program the inbound and outbound filters to pass all.
. Assert the sources one at a time in the order ext0, ext16, sep0, sep7, ndm, hang, inbound mailbox
  0 and inbound mailbox 31; after each, wait up to 64 rises (128 for a mailbox) for the vector XOR
  the baseline, with raw bits 319 to 288 masked, to equal the cumulative mask and the mailbox output
  bit to be set.
. Hold all sources and require the masked XOR to equal the full mask and `tb_peripheral_interrupts`
  to stay constant at each of 256 consecutive rises.
. Drop the sources in reverse order and wait after each for the masked XOR to equal the remaining
  mask, ending at 0.
. With the edge checks on, clear both inbound mailboxes, raise and drop `tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts`
  bit 0 (XOR `1 << 256`), fire the SYS hang detector (XOR `1 << 286`), push inbound mailbox 0 on top
  of it and print raw bits 288 and 319, drop both, then push inbound mailbox 31 (masked XOR 0),
  print raw bits 288 and 319, drop it and clear it.
. Program one zeroer job (destination 0x0200_3000, 256 bytes, interrupt enabled) and sample every
  rise until raw bit 323 has pulsed and fallen, within 4096 rises.
. Disable and clear both mailboxes, write 0 to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, restore
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, check the ordered step stamps S1 to S7 and the seven checker lines, then log
  the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-VECASM-ALL-REGIONS` |Each source asserted adds exactly its own raw bit; final mask is set
|`CHK-VECASM-DROP-EACH` |Dropping sources in reverse order removes one bit each, ending at baseline
|`CHK-VECASM-HOLD` |Masked XOR and tb_peripheral_interrupts stay constant for 256 rises
|`CHK-VECASM-RSVD-287` |Raw bit 287 reads 0 at every sampled rise, including with bit 286 high
|`CHK-VECASM-TAIL-ZERO` |Raw bits 327 to 324 read 0 at every sampled rise; raw 323 pulses and falls
|`CHK-VECASM-EDGES` |Raw 255, 287 and 320 stay quiet beside raw 256, 286 and a mailbox 31 push
|`CHK-VECASM-INBOUND-LOG` |Records raw 288 and 319 after mailbox pushes; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Stamps S1 to S7 increase; seven checker lines print once each after their stamp
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-VECASM-ALL-REGIONS`, `CHK-VECASM-DROP-EACH`, `CHK-VECASM-HOLD`,
`CHK-VECASM-RSVD-287`, `CHK-VECASM-TAIL-ZERO` and `CHK-VECASM-EDGES` hold: the masked vector XOR the
baseline equals the cumulative mask after each assertion and each drop, stays at the full mask for
256 rises, raw bits 287 and 327 to 324 read 0 at every sampled rise, raw bit 255 reads 0 while raw
bit 256 is high and raw bit 320 stays at its baseline, and raw bit 323 pulses and falls within 4096
rises of the zeroer job. `CHK-VECASM-INBOUND-LOG` records the mailbox raw bits and is not compared
with an expected value. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when the seven step stamps increase and the seven
checker lines each print once, after their step stamp; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded
waits. At least 27 SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Raw bits 319 to 288 are excluded from the compare; the levels of raw bits 288 and 319
after the mailbox 0 and mailbox 31 pushes are printed without a compare, because the specification
does not state the value. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare
of its own.

'''''

[[sec-489-smc_mbx_inbound_irq_vector_test]]
===== 489 `smc_mbx_inbound_irq_vector_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_mbx_inbound_irq_vector_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), 8-byte accesses to the 32 inbound mailbox
instances (`IRQEN` bit `wtirq`, `WRITE_DATA`, `CTRL` bits `wflush` and `rflush`, `IRQS` bits
`wtirq`, `rtirq` and `eirq`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`mailbox_cg_en`); observed raw bits 319 to
288 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` and `tb_top.tb_mailbox_interrupts` on `clk_smc_i`; fuse sense
signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`; no bench pin is driven.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Push inbound mailboxes; print observed raw bits 319:288.

*Test Coverage*:

* Inbound SMC mailbox interrupt channels 31 to 0 appear at raw bits 319 to 288 of the CPU interrupt
  vector (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC CPU Interrupt Vector Map and SMC indexed interrupt map table, row
  `[319:288]`).
* A push with `IRQEN.wtirq` set raises the channel's interrupt; the leaf measures which raw bits
  rise for mailboxes 0, 1, 15, 16, 30 and 31 alone, the pairs (0, 1) and (0, 31) and all 32
  together, and prints expected against observed bits and any extra bits without comparing them
  because the specification does not state the value; only the bounded wait for the expected bits
  can fail.
* Clearing `IRQEN.wtirq` on mailbox 5 while all 32 are asserted is observed for which bit falls, and
  flushing and acknowledging all 32 returns raw bits 319 to 288 and `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to 0
  (`axil_mailbox.rdl`, `IRQS` and `CTRL`).
* The baseline reads 0 on raw bits 319 to 288 and on `tb_mailbox_interrupts`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require raw bits 319 to 288 and `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to read
  0, read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, set the mailbox clock enable and read it back.
. For each of mailboxes 0, 1, 15, 16, 30 and 31 write `IRQEN.wtirq`, write `WRITE_DATA`, wait up to
  128 rises for the expected raw bit, print expected and observed bits, then write `IRQEN` 0, flush
  both FIFOs, acknowledge `IRQS` and wait up to 128 rises for raw bits 319 to 288 and
  `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to return to 0.
. Repeat for the pairs (0, 1) and (0, 31), then arm and push all 32 mailboxes and wait up to 128
  rises for all 32 raw bits; print expected and observed bits for each group.
. Write `IRQEN` 0 on mailbox 5, watch up to 128 rises for the first change of raw bits 319 to 288
  and print whether only raw bit 293 fell, flush and acknowledge all 32 mailboxes, and wait up to
  128 rises for raw bits 319 to 288 and `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to read 0.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and read it back, check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the
  three checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MBXIN-POSITION-LOG` |Prints expected vs observed raw bits per push; only the wait fails
|`CHK-MBXIN-MULTI-LOG` |Prints expected vs observed bits for pairs and all 32; wait can fail
|`CHK-MBXIN-CLEAR-LOG` |Prints which bit fell when mailbox 5 IRQEN cleared; final 0 is waited
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all three checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits; they raise on expiry except the clear window
|===

*Pass Criteria*: Every bounded wait completes: the expected raw bits rise within 128 rises of each
push, the vector returns to 0 within 128 rises after each clear, and the clock-gate readbacks match.
`CHK-MBXIN-POSITION-LOG`, `CHK-MBXIN-MULTI-LOG` and `CHK-MBXIN-CLEAR-LOG` record observed bits and
are not compared with expected bit positions. `CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the
three checker lines appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. At least 200
SEP_IN accesses are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The raw bits that rise for each push, for the pairs and for all 32 mailboxes, and
which bit falls when `IRQEN.wtirq` of mailbox 5 is cleared, are printed against the expected bits
without comparing them, because the specification does not state the value; only the bounded waits
for the expected bits can fail. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits, which raise on
expiry except the clear window.

'''''

[[sec-490-smc_ndm_irq_or_test]]
===== 490 `smc_ndm_irq_or_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_ndm_irq_or_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench input
`tb_top.tb_ndmreset_request` (4 bits, one per external CPU cluster); observed
`tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` (whole vector against the baseline, raw bit 267),
`tb_top.tb_ndmreset_irq` and `tb_top.tb_ndmreset_request_sync` on `clk_smc_i`; scratch register
`SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive NDM request bits alone, in OR and held; compare vector.

*Test Coverage*:

* The NDM reset request is synchronised onto `clk_smc` and OR-reduced onto raw bit 267
  (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt map table, row 267; `port_table.adoc`,
  `smc_ndmreset_request_i`: request of external CPU cluster `i` on bit `i`).
* Each of the four request bits alone sets raw bit 267 and no other raw bit, holds it for 64 rises
  and returns the vector to the baseline on release; the `tb_ndmreset_irq` probe agrees with the raw bit
  level (probe consistency, not an independent check).
* With two or four request bits set, dropping them one at a time keeps raw bit 267 at 1 until the
  last request drops.
* A single request held for 256 rises keeps raw bit 267 at 1 for the whole hold.
* Every pin-to-raw-bit wait is bounded at 64 `clk_smc_i` rises and raises with the last XOR vector
  on expiry.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the four bench signals to exist and
  `tb_ndmreset_request` to be 4 bits wide, read `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a
  liveness access, drive `tb_ndmreset_request` = 0, sample the baseline one rise later and require raw bit 267 and
  `tb_ndmreset_irq` to read 0.
. For each request bit 0 to 3 drive it alone to 1, wait up to 64 rises for raw bit 267 to read 1
  with no other bit differing from the baseline and `tb_ndmreset_irq` = 1, hold 64 rises with the
  vector XOR baseline equal to `1 << 267`, then drive 0, wait for the vector to equal the baseline
  and hold 64 rises.
. Drive 0b0011, then 0b0010, then 0, and drive 0b1111, then 0b1110, 0b1100, 0b1000 and 0, requiring
  raw bit 267 to read 1 for 64 rises after each non-final drop and 0 after the last, with each level
  held 64 rises.
. Drive request bit 0 to 1, require raw bit 267 to read 1 at each of 256 consecutive rises, then
  drive 0 and require the baseline for 64 rises.
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S4 and the three checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-NDM-EACH-ALONE` |Each request bit alone sets only raw bit 267 for 64 rises, then baseline
|`CHK-NDM-OR-DROP` |Raw bit 267 stays 1 after each non-final drop of 2 or 4 requests, 0 after last
|`CHK-NDM-HOLD` |A held request keeps raw bit 267 at 1 for 256 rises, then returns to baseline
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all three checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NDM-EACH-ALONE`, `CHK-NDM-OR-DROP` and `CHK-NDM-HOLD` hold: raw bit 267 reads
1 within 64 rises of a request, the vector XOR the baseline equals `1 << 267` and the
`tb_ndmreset_irq` probe agrees for every held rise (64, or 256 in the hold), the bit stays 1 after each drop that leaves a
request set, and after the last drop the vector equals the baseline for 64 rises. `CHK-NONVAC` holds
when all four step stamps and the three checker lines appear in order; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs
the bounded waits. Eighteen phases complete and at least one SEP_IN access is issued.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The `tb_ndmreset_irq` probe is compared for consistency with the raw bit only, not as
an independent check. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of
its own.

'''''

[[sec-491-smc_sep_mbx_irq_vector_test]]
===== 491 `smc_sep_mbx_irq_vector_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_sep_mbx_irq_vector_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench input
`tb_top.tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts[7:0]` (raw bits 263 to 256); observed `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts`
(whole vector against the baseline), `tb_top.tb_peripheral_interrupts` (bits 7 to 0) and
`tb_top.tb_mailbox_irq_any` on `clk_smc_i`; scratch register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Walk, hold and group SEP mailbox inputs; compare vector.

*Test Coverage*:

* The eight SEP mailbox interrupt inputs appear at raw bits 256 to 263 of the CPU interrupt vector
  and at peripheral interrupt bits 0 to 7 (`interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed interrupt map table, rows
  256 to 263; `port_table.adoc`, `sep_mailbox_interrupts_i`: eight channels routed to internal
  interrupts of the SMC CPU).
* Each input driven alone sets exactly its own raw bit, holds for 64 rises and returns to the
  baseline on release; the probes of its peripheral bit and `tb_mailbox_irq_any` agree with the raw
  bit (probe consistency, not an independent check).
* Inputs 0 and 7 held for 256 rises keep their raw bit at 1 for the whole hold.
* The subsets 0xFF, 0x55 and 0xAA and eight single drops from 0xFF each produce the expected raw XOR
  baseline, so the channels are independent.
* The delay in `clk_smc_i` rises from an input edge to raw bit 256, rising and falling over eight
  repeats, is measured and printed without a compare because the specification does not state the
  value; the 64-rise wait bound still raises on expiry.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the four bench signals to exist, read
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access, drive `tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts` = 0, sample
  the baseline one rise later and require raw bits 263 to 256 and `tb_mailbox_irq_any` to read 0.
. Walk: for each input k from 0 to 7 drive bit k to 1, wait up to 64 rises for the raw XOR baseline
  to equal `1 << (256 + k)` with no other bit moved, hold 64 rises requiring peripheral bit k and
  `tb_mailbox_irq_any` to match, then drive 0, wait for the baseline and hold 64 rises.
. Hold: drive input 0, then input 7, to 1 for 256 rises each with the same match at every rise, then
  release and hold the baseline for 64 rises.
. Subsets: drive 0xFF, 0x55 and 0xAA, each cleared to 0 afterwards, then drive 0xFF and clear inputs
  0 to 7 one at a time, requiring the raw XOR to equal the subset shifted by 256 at each step and
  each level to hold 64 rises.
. Latency: eight times drive input 0 to 1 and count the rises until raw bit 256 changes (bound 64),
  settle 4 rises, drive 0 and count again, settle 4 rises; print the minimum and maximum.
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the four checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SEPMBX-WALK` |Each of 8 inputs alone sets only raw bit 256+k and peripheral bit k, then clears
|`CHK-SEPMBX-HOLD` |Inputs 0 and 7 held 256 rises keep their raw bit at 1, then release to baseline
|`CHK-SEPMBX-SUBSETS` |Subsets 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA and eight single drops give the expected raw XOR
|`CHK-SEPMBX-LATENCY-LOG` |Measures and prints input-to-raw-bit rises over 8 repeats; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SEPMBX-WALK`, `CHK-SEPMBX-HOLD` and `CHK-SEPMBX-SUBSETS` hold: the raw vector
XOR the baseline equals the driven inputs shifted by 256 within 64 rises of each change and at every
held rise (64, or 256 in the hold), the peripheral bit and `tb_mailbox_irq_any` probes agree with
the raw bits (probe consistency, not an independent check), and each release returns the vector to
the baseline.
`CHK-SEPMBX-LATENCY-LOG` records the measured delays and is not compared with an expected value.
`CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the four checker lines appear in order;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Fifty-one phases complete and at least one SEP_IN
access is issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The delay from an input edge to raw bit 256, rising and falling over eight repeats,
is measured and printed without a compare, because the specification does not state it; the
peripheral bit and `tb_mailbox_irq_any` probes are compared for consistency only, not as an
independent check. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its
own.

'''''

[[sec-492-smc_sep_wdt_irq_level_test]]
===== 492 `smc_sep_wdt_irq_level_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_sep_wdt_irq_level_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP, one scratch read); bench input
`tb_top.tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` (active low); observed raw bit 282 of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts`,
`tb_top.tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` and `tb_top.tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` on each `clk_smc_i` rise; scratch
register `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: Drive the SEP watchdog reset pin; check raw bit 282.

*Test Coverage*:

* The SEP watchdog reset input is active low, inverted and synchronised onto `clk_smc`, and appears
  as a level on raw bit 282 (`port_table.adoc`, `sep_wdt_reset_n_i`; `interrupts.adoc`, SMC indexed
  interrupt map table, row 282).
* With the pin high, raw bit 282 reads 0 for 64 consecutive rises and the `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync`
  probe agrees.
* After the pin falls, raw bit 282 reads 1 within 64 rises and the `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` probe
  agrees.
* After the pin is released and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` returns to 1, raw bit 282 reads 0 for 64
  consecutive rises and the synchroniser probe agrees (probe consistency, not an independent check); the warm reset release is bounded at 200000
  rises.
* The value of raw bit 282 while the pin is held low through the warm reset, the delay from the pin
  fall to raw bit 282 and the delay from the release to raw bit 282 reading 0 are measured and
  printed without a compare; the specification does not state the value.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require the four bench signals to exist, read
  `SCRATCH_COLD_WARM_0` through SEP_IN as a liveness access, drive `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` = 1, sample the
  baseline one rise later and require the pin to read 1 and raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` to
  read 0.
. Sample 64 consecutive rises and require raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` to read 0.
. Drive `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` = 0 and wait up to 64 rises for raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync`
  to both read 1, then print raw bit 282, the synchroniser and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for 64 more
  rises without comparing them.
. Drive `tb_sep_wdt_reset_n` = 1 and wait up to 200000 rises for `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to read 1,
