  recording the first rise at which raw bit 282 read 0, then require raw bit 282 and
  `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` to read 0 at each of the next 64 rises.
. Sample one more rise and require raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` to read 0, print the two
  delays, check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the four checker lines, then log the bounded
  waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SEPWDT-IDLE-ZERO` |With the pin high, raw bit 282 and the synchroniser read 0 for 64 rises
|`CHK-SEPWDT-ASSERT-HIGH` |After the pin falls, raw 282 and the synchroniser read 1 in 64 rises
|`CHK-SEPWDT-RELEASE-ZERO` |After release and warm reset release, both read 0 for 64 rises
|`CHK-SEPWDT-LATENCY-LOG` |Records fall-to-high and release-to-low rises; no compare
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all four checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SEPWDT-IDLE-ZERO`, `CHK-SEPWDT-ASSERT-HIGH` and `CHK-SEPWDT-RELEASE-ZERO`
hold: raw bit 282 and `tb_sep_wdt_irq_sync` read 0 for 64 rises at idle, both read 1 within 64 rises
of the pin falling, and after the pin release and the return of `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` to 1 both
read 0 for 64 rises. `CHK-SEPWDT-LATENCY-LOG` records the measured delays and is not compared with
an expected value; the level while the pin is held low through the warm reset is printed only.
`CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the four checker lines appear in order;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Four phases complete and at least one SEP_IN access
is issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The level of raw bit 282 while the pin is held low through the warm reset, the delay
from the pin fall to raw bit 282 and the delay from the release to raw bit 282 reading 0 are
measured and printed without a compare, because the specification does not state them; the
synchroniser probe is compared for consistency only, not as an independent check.
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.

'''''

[[sec-493-smc_sync_irq_isolation_test]]
===== 493 `smc_sync_irq_isolation_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: IRQ

*Source Module*: `smc_sync_irq_isolation_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for `SYNC_REG` (`reset_unit.rdl`) and
`HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`; bench inputs `tb_top.tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` (raw bit 0) and
`tb_top.tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts` (bit 0, raw bit 256); the hang detector `irq_test` source (raw
bit 286); observed `tb_top.tb_sync_irq` and the whole of `tb_top.tb_cpu_interrupts` (328 bits) on
`clk_smc_i`; fuse sense signals `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: Toggle SYNC_REG.sync; tb_sync_irq follows, sources do not.

*Test Coverage*:

* `sync_irq_o` is the software-controlled global synchronisation bit `SYNC_REG.sync` and is not an
  interrupt aggregate output (`port_table.adoc`, `sync_irq_o`; `reset_unit.rdl`, `SYNC_REG.sync`,
  reset value 0).
* Writing 1 to `SYNC_REG.sync` raises `tb_sync_irq` within 64 rises and leaves the raw vector equal
  to the baseline for 64 rises; writing 0 lowers it with the vector still at the baseline.
* With raw bits 0, 256 and 286 asserted and `SYNC_REG.sync` at 0, `tb_sync_irq` reads 0 at each of
  64 consecutive rises, so interrupt sources do not drive it.
* Setting `SYNC_REG.sync` with the sources still asserted raises `tb_sync_irq` and none of the three
  source bits drops, so the output is live in that state and the zero above is not a stuck probe.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for the fuse sense to finish, require `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` and `tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts`
  to exist and `tb_cpu_interrupts` to be at least 328 bits wide, drive both pins to 0, sample the
  baseline vector one rise later and require `tb_sync_irq` to read 0.
. Write 1 to `SYNC_REG` over SEP_IN and read it back, wait up to 64 rises for `tb_sync_irq` to read
  1 with the vector equal to the baseline, then require both at each of 64 consecutive rises.
. Write 0 to `SYNC_REG` and read it back, wait up to 64 rises for `tb_sync_irq` to read 0 with the
  vector equal to the baseline, then require both at each of 64 consecutive rises.
. Drive `tb_ext_interrupt_0_i` = 1 and `tb_sep_mailbox_interrupts` = 1, write all three of `enable`,
  `irq_en` and `irq_test` to `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, wait up to 64 rises for raw bits 0, 256 and
  286 to read 1 with `tb_sync_irq` at 0, then require raw bits 0, 256 and 286 at 1 and `tb_sync_irq`
  at 0 at each of 64 consecutive rises.
. Write 1 to `SYNC_REG` and read it back, wait up to 64 rises for `tb_sync_irq` to read 1 and
  require raw bits 0, 256 and 286 still at 1; drive both pins to 0, write 0 to
  `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL` and to `SYNC_REG`, and wait up to 64 rises for `tb_sync_irq` to read 0
  with the vector equal to the baseline.
. Check the ordered step stamps S1 to S5 and the three checker lines, then log the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SYNCIRQ-SET-CLR` |SYNC_REG.sync set and clear drive tb_sync_irq 1 and 0, vector at baseline
|`CHK-SYNCIRQ-SOURCES-ZERO` |Raw bits 0, 256 and 286 high leave tb_sync_irq at 0 for 64 rises
|`CHK-SYNCIRQ-POSCTRL` |SYNC_REG set with sources high raises tb_sync_irq; sources stay; clears
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered step stamps and all three checker lines occurred, in order
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Logs the bounded waits taken; no compare of its own, the waits raise on expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SYNCIRQ-SET-CLR`, `CHK-SYNCIRQ-SOURCES-ZERO` and `CHK-SYNCIRQ-POSCTRL` hold:
`SYNC_REG` reads back as written, `tb_sync_irq` follows `SYNC_REG.sync` within 64 rises with the raw
vector at its baseline for 64 rises, `tb_sync_irq` reads 0 at each of 64 rises while raw bits 0, 256
and 286 are high with `SYNC_REG.sync` at 0, and with `SYNC_REG.sync` set the output reads 1 with the
three source bits still high and returns to 0 with the vector at the baseline after the clears.
`CHK-NONVAC` holds when all five step stamps and the three checker lines appear in order;
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits. Five phases complete and at least 9 SEP_IN accesses
are issued. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` only logs the bounded waits taken and has no compare of its own.
'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-i2c]]
==== I2C

[[sec-120-smc_i2c_error_fifo_depth_test]]
===== 120 `smc_i2c_error_fifo_depth_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_error_fifo_depth_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: PROXY -- run I2C CSR decode plus SCL/SDA pin override depth checks. Extends
`smc_i2c_master_target_test` with the same `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq` body.

*Test Coverage*:

* DEFENDS: I2C0 host/target CSR decode, and LSIO SCL/SDA release and pull-low behaviour at the pads.
* DOES NOT DEFEND: I2C error conditions or FIFO depth. This testcase runs the same `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq` body as testcase 117 -- `FIFO_STATUS` is never read, the only `FIFO_CTRL` accesses are `RXRST | FMTRST` resets, and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` is only written W1C to clear and read to decorate failure messages, so no event bit is ever asserted.
* FIFO-depth and error-injection coverage is not this testcase's: `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test` covers the full-FIFO case and `smc_i2c_p0_nack_test` the NACK case.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_error_fifo_depth_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-HOST-WRITE` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C0-HOST-REPEATED-START` |Two DUT-host write frames joined by a repeated START: the EEPROM VIP frames exactly two STARTs against one STOP on `tb_i2c0_*`, in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails otherwise
|`CHK-I2C0-OVRD-PAD` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C0-SMBUS-ARA` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C0-SMBUS-PEC` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C0-U4-2-SMBUS` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_master_target_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C0-HOST-WRITE`, `CHK-I2C0-OVRD-PAD`, `CHK-I2C0-SMBUS-ARA`, `CHK-I2C0-SMBUS-PEC`, `CHK-I2C0-U4-2-SMBUS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: I2C error conditions and FIFO depth are not defended: `FIFO_STATUS` is never read,
the only `FIFO_CTRL` accesses are resets and no `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` bit is ever asserted; the
full-FIFO case belongs to `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test` and the NACK case to `smc_i2c_p0_nack_test`.
'''''

[[sec-121-smc_i2c_fifo_full_test]]
===== 121 `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test`

* ACQ: DUT I2C0 as target accepts a VIP-master write, and the leg requires `ACQLVL` to reach the acquired-word count before `ACQRST` is applied.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]

|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-ACQ` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches

|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-FMT` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-RX` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-TX` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_fifo_full_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-ACQ`, `CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-BASIC`, `CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-FMT`, `CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-RX`, `CHK-I2C-FIFO-FULL-TX` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-122-smc_i2c_master_target_test]]
===== 122 `smc_i2c_master_target_test`

[[sec-123-smc_i2c_multi_instance_test]]
===== 123 `smc_i2c_multi_instance_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_multi_instance_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: I2C_1/2 + I2C_CTRL reset sweep and per-instance TARGET_ID co-resident patterns.

*Test Coverage*:

* I2C multi-instance CSR precheck over the three controllers (I2C_0/1/2) and the top-level I2C_CTRL block the generated map declares.
* Reset content: the I2C_1 and I2C_2 INTR_STATE bases and the I2C_CTRL base read their generated reset word as scoreboard value compares.
* Per-instance decode: every controller's `TARGET_ID` (plain rw storage, reset 0) holds a distinct target-address pattern at the same time and reads back its own before being restored, so a stride that aliases two controllers or an undecoded window answering OKAY with zeros fails the readback. The reset reads alone cannot make that distinction, since their reset word is zero.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_multi_instance_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-CORESIDENT` |`TARGET_ID` of I2C_0, I2C_1 and I2C_2 hold three distinct patterns written before any is read back, each reads back its own and then its reset after the restore write, every readback a scoreboard value compare; an aliased pair or an OKAY-zero hole fails the first readback of the pair
|`CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-RESET-DECODE` |The I2C_1 and I2C_2 INTR_STATE bases and the I2C_CTRL base each returned OKAY and matched the reset word 0x0 in a scoreboard value compare, with the scoreboard checking all 3 accesses and booking exactly 3 value compares; a non-OKAY response, a non-zero word or a compare that never ran fails it
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-CORESIDENT` and `CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-RESET-DECODE` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds, including the exact access and value-compare counts. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-132-smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test]]
===== 132 `smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator
(cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: I2C1 stretch timeout measured against an I2C0 target proven live on the same shared bus.

*Test Coverage*:

* Allow leg first: the I2C0 target's TX FIFO is preloaded and the I2C1 host reads the byte back through RDATA while I2C0's ACQ FIFO shows the START word for the read address, so the two controllers are demonstrably on one bus before anything is timed.
* Timeout leg: the same read with the I2C0 TX FIFO empty. I2C1 raises `INTR_STATE.STRETCH_TIMEOUT` after the programmed count while I2C0 reports `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` and holds the START word for that address, so the timeout is the host's measurement of the target's stretch and not of a stuck-low SCL with no target in the loop.
* Release leg: a byte written to I2C0 TXDATA ends the stretch; the host leaves its busy state and reads that byte back.
* Requires +smc_i2c_shared_bus.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT` |I2C1 `INTR_STATE.STRETCH_TIMEOUT` set within the bounded poll while I2C0 `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` is set and I2C0's ACQ FIFO holds the START word carrying the read address (`smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test_seq.py`); any of the three missing fails the run
|`CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT-RELEASE` |After the timeout, a byte written to I2C0 TXDATA lets the I2C1 host leave its busy state and read exactly that byte (`smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT-TARGET-LIVE` |Positive control run first: with the I2C0 TX FIFO preloaded, the I2C1 host reads exactly that byte and I2C0's ACQ FIFO holds the START word for the read address (`smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-I2C-TIMEOUT-CSR-SWEEP` |Named compare in `smc_i2c_p0_timeout_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT`, `CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT-RELEASE`, `CHK-I2C-P0-TIMEOUT-TARGET-LIVE`, `CHK-I2C-TIMEOUT-CSR-SWEEP` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-165-smc_i2c_intr_mask_test]]
===== 165 `smc_i2c_intr_mask_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_intr_mask_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); observation on `tb_i2c_irq[0]`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: The same interrupt-enable placement, on I2C: INTR_ENABLE must mask the output, not the set path.

*Test Coverage*:

* The contract is the OpenTitan interrupt register convention the block carries (comportability specification: `INTR_ENABLE` "enables/masks the output of INTR_STATE", `INTR_STATE` is "not qualified by INTR_ENABLE", an Event interrupt is cleared only by a W1C and a Status interrupt follows its input), as `i2c.rdl` declares it per field. `CMD_COMPLETE`, an Event source raised by `INTR_TEST` on the same line as the real event, is the vehicle.
* Both the held and the dropped consequence, as for the log engine.
* Every one of the twenty sources in the `irq_o` reduction, each raised as the only enabled source so the output move belongs to that term and no other. The Event/Status split is read from the generated IP-XACT export of `i2c.rdl`: an Event source has a write-only (`singlepulse`) `INTR_TEST` field and a write-one-to-clear `INTR_STATE` field and is released by a W1C; a Status source has a read-write `INTR_TEST` field and a read-only `INTR_STATE` field and is released by writing that field back to 0; the two registers must agree on every field. A source the bench holds asserted cannot be swept from a measured clear, so it is named in the evidence and skipped, and the leg states the minimum number of sources it still requires.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock and require instance 0's PLIC bit to read 0.
. Set INTR_ENABLE.CMD_COMPLETE, pulse INTR_TEST, require INTR_STATE to latch and the IRQ to assert, held 32 cycles.
. Clear INTR_ENABLE only and sample the IRQ.
. W1C the status, prove it cleared, then pulse INTR_TEST with INTR_ENABLE=0 and set the enable afterwards.
. Require INTR_STATE to hold the event.
. Sweep every source: clear it, enable it alone, raise it through INTR_TEST, require the IRQ to rise, release it and require the IRQ to fall with INTR_STATE clear.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-ARM` |The set path, the status register and the probe are all alive
|`CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-DEASSERT` |Clearing the enable de-asserts the IRQ, holds it de-asserted for the same span the arm leg holds it asserted, and leaves INTR_STATE still carrying the bit -- the last is what separates an output mask from a DUT that simply clears the state
|`CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-EVERY-SOURCE` |At least 16 of the twenty interrupt sources each raised the IRQ while it was the only enabled source, and released it again with `INTR_STATE` clear
|`CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-LATCH` |An event arriving while masked is still latched and surfaces once the enable is set
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-ARM`, `CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-DEASSERT`, `CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-EVERY-SOURCE` and `CHK-I2C-INTR-MASK-LATCH` hold after their compares; the last three are measured before any raises, so none hides another. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: A source the bench holds asserted cannot be swept from a measured clear; it is named
in the evidence and skipped, and the sweep states the minimum number of sources it still requires.

'''''

[[sec-494-smc_i2c_clock_gate_response_test]]
===== 494 `smc_i2c_clock_gate_response_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_clock_gate_response_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor, error responses allowed where the
step expects them); `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en` (bit 11); probes `tb_i2c_cg_en`,
`tb_i2c_irq[1]`, `tb_peripheral_interrupts[24]`, `tb_cpu_interrupts[280]`; clock `clk_smc_i`; the
`SMC_I2C_WRAP` window (STATUS, TARGET_ID, TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, INTR_STATE,
HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT of instances 0-2, and the `I2C_CTRL` registers 0-2); no I2C protocol VIP
drives the bus.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: While `i2c_cg_en` is set every I2C window read answers SLVERR
with 0xBADCAB1E, and after it is cleared the window answers OKAY with every register and event kept.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en` resets to 0 and, while set, every access to the `SMC_I2C_WRAP`
  window answers SLVERR with read data 0xBADCAB1E (`smc_base_config.rdl` `i2c_cg_en`,
  `clk_rst.adoc`, `memmap.adoc`).
* A write under the gate completes with SLVERR (`clk_rst.adoc`). The response and read data at the
  gap and past-extent addresses, the interrupt levels while gated, and whether a gated write lands
  are only measured and printed, because the specification does not state the values.
* After the gate is cleared the window answers OKAY (`STATUS` reads its reset value 0x33C,
  `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL[2]` is read-write) and `TARGET_ID`, `I2C_CTRL`, `INTR_ENABLE` and a latched
  `INTR_STATE.RX_OVERFLOW` read back unchanged (`i2c.rdl`, `smc_base_config.rdl`), also across three
  further set/clear cycles.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, the `TARGET_ID`, `I2C_CTRL`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_STATE` words of
  instances 0-2 and `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL[2]`; require `tb_i2c_cg_en` to be 0.
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` again and require `i2c_cg_en` and `tb_i2c_cg_en` to be 0.
. Write distinct `TARGET_ID` words (address 0x21+n, mask 0x7F) to instances 0-2, `I2C_CTRL[0]` =
  SMBUS_EN and `I2C_CTRL[1]` = I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN, `INTR_ENABLE[0]` = SCL_INTERFERENCE |
  SDA_INTERFERENCE | HOST_TIMEOUT; raise `INTR_STATE[0].RX_OVERFLOW` through `INTR_TEST` and require
  it to read 1; enable and raise `CMD_COMPLETE` on instance 1 and poll `tb_i2c_irq[1]` to 1.
. Error injection. Point: the `SMC_I2C_WRAP` window (`STATUS` of instances 0-2 and `I2C_CTRL[0..2]`)
  with `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en` set. Kind: reads of a clock-gated window. Expected response:
  each read completes with SLVERR and read data 0xBADCAB1E. Set `i2c_cg_en` and poll `tb_i2c_cg_en`
  to 1 before the reads.
. Error injection. Point: `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]` while gated. Kind: writes
  (0x321 and SMBUS_EN) to a clock-gated window. Expected response: SLVERR on each.
. Error injection. Point: the gap words (`SMC_I2C_WRAP` base + 0x600 and the last word below
  `I2C_CTRL`) and the first and last word past the window extent for reads, the gap word and the
  last aperture word for writes, while gated. Kind: gap and past-extent reads and writes under the
  clock gate. Expected response: an error response on each; the code and data are recorded.
. While gated, sample `tb_i2c_irq[1]`, `tb_peripheral_interrupts[24]` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[280]`,
  wait 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles and sample them again; record the levels.
. Clear `i2c_cg_en`, poll `tb_i2c_cg_en` to 0, read `STATUS` of instances 0-2 (0x33C), write
  `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL[2]` = 0x1234 and read it back, read back every retained word
  (`TARGET_ID[0..2]`, `I2C_CTRL[0..1]`, `INTR_ENABLE[0]`) and require `INTR_STATE[0].RX_OVERFLOW`
  still 1; sample `tb_i2c_irq[1]`.
. Repeat set and clear of the gate three more times, comparing every retained word after each clear
  and `INTR_STATE[0].RX_OVERFLOW` still 1; then W1C `RX_OVERFLOW` and require it to read 0.
. Read back `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]` and record whether the gated writes
  landed; restore every saved word, zero the two probe registers and restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`;
  check the ordered step fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-GATE-READ-SLVERR` |`i2c_cg_en` and `tb_i2c_cg_en` read 0 before the write, `tb_i2c_cg_en`
reads 1 within the poll bound after it, and the six window reads (`STATUS` 0-2, `I2C_CTRL` 0-2) each
complete with SLVERR and 0xBADCAB1E.
|`CHK-I2C-GATE-WRITE-SLVERR` |Both gated writes (`HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]`)
complete with SLVERR (`clk_rst.adoc`).
|`CHK-I2C-GATE-GAP-OBS` |All four gated reads and two gated writes at the gap and past-extent
addresses must complete with an error response; the code and read data are measured and printed
without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-GATE-UNGATE-OKAY` |After the clear `tb_i2c_cg_en` reads 0, `STATUS` of instances 0-2 reads
0x33C, and `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL[2]` reads back the written 0x1234; the `tb_i2c_irq[1]` level is
printed.
|`CHK-I2C-GATE-IRQ-OBS` |`tb_i2c_irq[1]` must reach 1 before the gate is set; the three interrupt
levels while gated and 256 cycles later are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-REGS` |After the gate cycle `TARGET_ID[0..2]`, `I2C_CTRL[0]` (SMBUS_EN) and
`I2C_CTRL[1]` (I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN) read back equal to the words written before the gate.
|`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-INTR` |`INTR_ENABLE[0]` reads back its written value, `INTR_STATE[0].RX_OVERFLOW`
still reads 1 after the gate was set and cleared, and reads 0 after its W1C.
|`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-GATED-WRITE-OBS` |Whether `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]` kept the
gated write (landed) or read 0 (dropped) is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-CYCLES` |After each of three further set/clear cycles `TARGET_ID[0..2]`,
`I2C_CTRL[0..1]` and `INTR_ENABLE[0]` read back equal to the words written before the gate.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints its ten checkpoints in order with increasing time stamps, each
checker line printed only after the checkpoints it depends on completed.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-GATE-READ-SLVERR`, `CHK-I2C-GATE-WRITE-SLVERR`,
`CHK-I2C-GATE-UNGATE-OKAY`, `CHK-I2C-RETAIN-REGS`,
`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-INTR`, `CHK-I2C-RETAIN-CYCLES` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares, the
gap accesses all return an error response, and `tb_i2c_irq[1]` reaches 1 before
gating; `CHK-I2C-GATE-GAP-OBS`, `CHK-I2C-GATE-IRQ-OBS` (gated levels) and
`CHK-I2C-RETAIN-GATED-WRITE-OBS` record measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code and read data at the gap and past-extent addresses, the three
interrupt levels while gated and 256 cycles later, and whether the gated writes to
`HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]` landed or were dropped are measured and printed
without comparing, because the specification does not state the values; the `tb_i2c_irq[1]` level
after the clear is printed.

'''''

[[sec-495-smc_i2c_ctrl_intr_w1c_test]]
===== 495 `smc_i2c_ctrl_intr_w1c_test`

*Phase*: 3

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`, which joins

`clk_smc_i`; registers CTRL, TIMING0-4, OVRD, FDATA, FIFO_CTRL, STATUS, RDATA, TXDATA, ACQDATA,
TARGET_ID, TIMEOUT_CTRL, HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, TARGET_EVENTS, INTR_STATE,
INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, SMBUS_CTRL, SMBUS_STATUS of instances 0-2 and their wrapper control registers;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0-I2C2 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the
sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Instance 0 `CMD_COMPLETE`, `SDA_UNSTABLE` and `SCL_INTERFERENCE` are
set by their bus event, cleared by a written 1, and `SCL_INTERFERENCE` reaches `tb_i2c_irq` only
once enabled; on instances 1 and 2 the `INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `TARGET_EVENTS` flags
are set and cleared per written 1, `CMD_COMPLETE` is gated onto `tb_i2c_irq`, and `SMBUS_CTRL`
drives and `SMBUS_STATUS` follows the shared SMBus suspend and alert lines.

*Test Coverage*:

* `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` of I2C0 reads 0 before a write transaction, sets after the target
  frames the STOP, is cleared by a written 1 and sets again after a second identical transaction
  (`i2c.rdl`).
* A write, repeated START, read transaction records the wire monitor START, STOP and data byte
  counts at the first read that shows `CMD_COMPLETE`; the expected set point is not compared.
* `INTR_STATE.SDA_UNSTABLE` sets when a second master pulls SDA low inside the acknowledge SCL high
  pulse and is cleared by a written 1; `INTR_STATE.SCL_INTERFERENCE` sets when SCL is pulled low
  inside the controller high pulse and is cleared by a written 1 (`i2c.rdl`).
* `INTR_ENABLE.SCL_INTERFERENCE` gates the flag onto the instance 0 interrupt line: `tb_i2c_irq`
  stays 0b000 while the flag is set and the enable is clear, reads 0b001 once enabled and 0b000
  after the clear (`i2c.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc`).
* On I2C1 and I2C2, `INTR_TEST` 0x000FE3E8 sets every write 1 pulse field of `INTR_STATE`, and the
  partial writes 0x000AA2A0 and 0x00054148 clear only the written bits; each RW `INTR_TEST` field
  (`FMT_THRESHOLD`, `RX_THRESHOLD`, `ACQ_THRESHOLD`, `CONTROLLER_HALT`, `TX_STRETCH`,
  `TX_THRESHOLD`, `ACQ_STRETCH`) holds its status bit through a written 1 and releases it at
  `INTR_TEST` 0 (`i2c.adoc`).
* `INTR_ENABLE.CMD_COMPLETE` gates a forced `CMD_COMPLETE` of instance k onto `tb_i2c_irq` bit k
  only (`i2c.adoc`, `interrupts.adoc`).
* As controller each of I2C1 and I2C2 sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and `CONTROLLER_HALT` on an
  absent-address NACK without issuing the next entry, passes the same byte with `FDATA.NAKOK`, and
  after an unserviced NACK past `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` reads `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0x3 and STOPs
  the bus; the two flags clear one written 1 at a time, `CONTROLLER_HALT` holding until both are 0.
* As target with `CTRL.TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` each instance sets `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING`,
  `START_DETECT` and `TX_STRETCH` on a READ from the other instance and sends its byte only after
  the written 1; `STOP_DETECT` records the STOP; a bench SCL hold of twice `TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` sets
  `TARGET_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT`, cleared by a written 1 (`i2c.adoc`); `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` with the
  flag set and after the clear is logged without an expected value.
* `TARGET_EVENTS.ARBITRATION_LOST` after a lost arbitration between I2C0 and the other instance, and
  `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` with the ACQ entries after a STOP sent before the target NACK, are logged
  without an expected value; a written 1 clears each when it reads 1, and a normally terminated read
  leaves `UNEXP_STOP` 0.
* `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBSUS` of the controller-direction instance pulls the shared suspend line low and the
  target-direction I2C1 reads `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBSUS` while it is held; `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` of a
  target pulls the shared alert line low and clears itself when the other instance addresses it;
  with `SMBUS_EN` the I2C1 controller sets `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` and `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT`, and
  without it `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` stays 0 (`i2c.adoc`, `i2c_ctrl.adoc`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the I2C0 wrapper control register (enable, controller
  mode), arm the I2C0 pads and poll `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i` to 1; program
  TIMING0-4 (THIGH 0x1A, TLOW 0x32), OVRD off, `INTR_ENABLE` 0, reset the FIFOs, clear
  `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE`, set `CTRL` 0 and require ENABLEHOST, the three watched
  flags and `INTR_ENABLE` to read 0; create the EEPROM target, the injector and the wire monitor.
. Re-enable the host with every enable, event and flag cleared, require `CMD_COMPLETE` 0, queue a
  write of 0x5C at offset 0x20 to 0x50 with STOP, wait for the target's STOP, poll `CMD_COMPLETE` to
  1, require it to read 1 before a written 1 and 0 after it.
. Re-enable the host, require `CMD_COMPLETE` 0, repeat the identical write and poll `CMD_COMPLETE`
  to 1.
. Write 1 to `CMD_COMPLETE` and require 0; re-enable the host, queue a write of the offset, a
  repeated START and an 8 byte read with STOP; at the first `INTR_STATE` read showing `CMD_COMPLETE`
  record the monitor START, STOP and data byte counts; wait for the target STOP and STATUS HOSTIDLE.
. Error injection. Point: the SDA pad, pulled low by the injector 20 ns after the ninth SCL rise,
  inside the acknowledge SCL high pulse, for half of THIGH times the peripheral clock period, during
  an address-only write queued to the absent address 0x51. Kind: a second-master SDA pull inside the
  acknowledge pulse. Expected response: `SDA_UNSTABLE` polls to 1, reads 1 before and 0 after a
  written 1. Re-enable the host and require `SDA_UNSTABLE` 0 before starting the injector (it waits
  for a START and the ninth SCL rise); then set `CTRL` 0 and clock the bus back to idle (SCL and SDA
  1).
. Error injection. Point: the SCL pad, pulled low by the injector for 100 ns, 60 ns after the ninth
  rise, during a write queued to 0x50. Kind: SCL pulled low inside the controller high pulse.
  Expected response: `SCL_INTERFERENCE` polls to 1 and, after HOSTIDLE, reads 1 before and 0 after a
  written 1. Re-enable the host and require `SCL_INTERFERENCE` 0 first; then halt and recover the
  bus.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL pad, the same injector pull repeated with `INTR_ENABLE` 0. Kind:
  SCL pulled low inside the controller high pulse with the interrupt masked. Expected response: the
  flag still 1 after HOSTIDLE and `tb_i2c_irq` 0b000 at two samples 200 `clk_smc_i` cycles apart.
  Then write `INTR_ENABLE.SCL_INTERFERENCE` and read it back; poll `tb_i2c_irq` bit 0 to 1 with bits
  2:1 at 0; write 1 to the flag, require it 0 and poll `tb_i2c_irq` to 0b000; halt and recover the
  bus.
. Require `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; clear the I2C0 `INTR_ENABLE`, arm the I2C1 and I2C2 pads, poll the
  bus idle, program their TIMING0-4 as for I2C0, OVRD off, `INTR_ENABLE` 0, clear their FIFOs,
  `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `TARGET_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE`, and require `INTR_STATE` 0 and
  `tb_i2c_irq[2:1]` 0b00.
. For k = 1, 2 write `INTR_TEST` 0x000FE3E8 and read `INTR_STATE` of k and of the other instance,
  then write `INTR_STATE` 0x000AA2A0 and 0x00054148, reading after each.
. For k = 1, 2 and each RW `INTR_TEST` field f write `INTR_TEST` 1<<f, read, write `INTR_STATE`
  1<<f, read, write `INTR_TEST` 0, read.
. For k = 1, 2 write `INTR_TEST` 0x200, sample `tb_i2c_irq` twice 200 cycles apart, write
  `INTR_ENABLE` 0x200 and poll `tb_i2c_irq` to 1<<k, write `INTR_STATE` 0x200 and poll it to 0b000.
. For controller k = 1, 2 queue START + 0x51 write and a data byte, poll `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, read
  `INTR_STATE` and STATUS; reset the format FIFO and write `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0x1, read both; clear
  `CMD_COMPLETE`, queue 0x51 with START, STOP and `NAKOK`, poll `CMD_COMPLETE` and HOSTIDLE and read
  `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE`.
. For controller k = 1, 2 with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` EN and VAL 256 queue the same write,
  poll `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and the wire monitor for `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` and a STOP within VAL
  peripheral clocks plus 5 us; reset the format FIFO, write 0x1 and read, write 0x2 and read.
. For target k = 1, 2 with `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` and TXDATA 0xA7, the other instance reads one byte
  with STOP; poll `TARGET_EVENTS`, read `TX_STRETCH` and the controller RX FIFO state, write 0x1,
  poll and pop RDATA, poll the wire STOP, read `TARGET_EVENTS`, write 0x18 and read both.
. For target k = 1, 2 with `TIMEOUT_CTRL` EN, MODE 1 and VAL of 8 us the bench controller reads
  from k, clears `TX_PENDING` and clocks data bit 7, then holds SCL low for 2 VAL; poll
  `TARGET_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT`, log `TX_STRETCH`, write 0x2 and read both, recover the bus. Then
  queue a READ of 0x3C / 0x3F (k's second address) on the other instance and of k's first address on
  I2C0, enable both, release `TX_PENDING`, poll until each controller is idle or halted and log
  `TARGET_EVENTS.ARBITRATION_LOST` and which controller lost; write 0x4 when it reads 1.
. For target k = 1, 2 with `ACQ_START_STOP_EN` the other instance reads one byte with `RCONT` and
  STOP; log `UNEXP_STOP` and drain ACQDATA, write `INTR_STATE` 0x2000 and read; repeat with a
  normally terminated read and read `UNEXP_STOP`.
. I2C1 controller: write `SMBSUS` 1 and 0, polling the shared suspend line to 0 and 1; I2C1 target
  with I2C0 holding the suspend line: poll `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBSUS` to 1, release, poll to 0; I2C2
  controller: write `SMBSUS` 1 and 0, reading back each and polling the line.
. I2C1 target with `SMBALERT` 1: poll the alert line to 0, let I2C2 address I2C1, read `SMBUS_CTRL`
  and poll the line to 1; I2C1 controller with `SMBUS_EN` and I2C0 holding the alert line: poll
  `SMBUS_STATUS` and `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT`, release the line by I2C1 addressing the I2C0 target at
  0x2A, write 0x8000 and read; repeat without
  `SMBUS_EN`; I2C2 target with `SMBALERT` 1 addressed by I2C1: read `SMBUS_CTRL`.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CMDC-STOP` |`CMD_COMPLETE` reads 0 before the write, reads 1 within the poll bound after the
target frames the STOP, and reads 0 after a written 1.
|`CHK-CMDC-REASSERT` |After the written 1 cleared `CMD_COMPLETE`, a second identical write sets it
again within the poll bound and a written 1 clears it again.
|`CHK-CMDC-RS-OBS` |`CMD_COMPLETE` must set within the poll bound during the write, repeated START,
read transaction; the START, STOP and data byte counts at that read are measured and printed without
comparing.
|`CHK-SDAU-W1C` |The SDA pull inside the acknowledge SCL high pulse sets `SDA_UNSTABLE` within the
poll bound and a written 1 clears it.
|`CHK-SCLI-W1C` |The SCL pull inside the controller high pulse sets `SCL_INTERFERENCE` within the
poll bound and a written 1 clears it.
|`CHK-SCLI-GATE` |With `INTR_ENABLE.SCL_INTERFERENCE` clear and the flag set `tb_i2c_irq` reads
0b000 at both samples, after the enable it reads 0b001 within the poll bound with bits 2:1 at 0, and
after the written 1 it reads 0b000 within the poll bound.
|`CHK-I2C12-INTR-TEST-W1C` |On I2C1 and I2C2 `INTR_STATE` & 0x000FE3E8 reads 0x000FE3E8 after the
`INTR_TEST` write with the other instance at 0, 0x00054148 after the written 0x000AA2A0, and 0 after
the written 0x00054148.
|`CHK-I2C12-INTR-TEST-RW-HOLD` |For each RW `INTR_TEST` field f and k = 1, 2 `INTR_STATE` bit f
reads 1 after `INTR_TEST` 1<<f, still 1 after a written 1, and 0 after `INTR_TEST` 0.
|`CHK-I2C12-IRQ-LINE-GATE` |With `CMD_COMPLETE` set on instance k, `tb_i2c_irq` reads 0b000 at both
samples while `INTR_ENABLE` is 0, exactly 1<<k within the poll bound after `INTR_ENABLE` 0x200, and
0b000 within the poll bound after the written 0x200.
|`CHK-I2C12-CTRL-NACK-HALT` |On controller k = 1, 2 the unanswered address sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`
0x1 and `CONTROLLER_HALT` with FMTEMPTY 0; both read 0 after the written 0x1; the byte with `NAKOK`
leaves `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0 and `CONTROLLER_HALT` 0 and reaches `CMD_COMPLETE` and HOSTIDLE.
|`CHK-I2C12-CTRL-EVENTS-PARTIAL` |The unserviced NACK yields `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0x3 and a wire STOP
within the bound (the elapsed time is logged); after the written 0x1 it reads 0x2 with
`CONTROLLER_HALT` 1, after the written 0x2 it reads 0 with `CONTROLLER_HALT` 0.
|`CHK-I2C12-TGT-TX-PENDING` |On target k the READ address sets `TARGET_EVENTS` 0x09 and `TX_STRETCH`
with the controller RX FIFO empty; after the written 0x1 the controller pops 0xA7; after the STOP
`STOP_DETECT` reads 1; after the written 0x18 `TARGET_EVENTS` reads 0 and `TX_STRETCH` 0.
|`CHK-I2C12-TGT-ABNORMAL-END` |SCL held low for 2 VAL during the READ sets `TARGET_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT`,
which reads 0 after the written 0x2; `TX_STRETCH` in both states is logged (LINKED-ISSUE gate
T_impl_i2c_w1c-s8-dut, SF-040); `TARGET_EVENTS.ARBITRATION_LOST` after the lost
arbitration is logged with the losing controller (LINKED-ISSUE SF-017) and, when 1, reads 0 after
the written 0x4.
|`CHK-I2C12-UNEXP-STOP` |`UNEXP_STOP` and the ACQ entries after the early STOP are logged
(LINKED-ISSUE SF-007); when the bit reads 1 the written 0x2000 returns it to 0, and after the
normally terminated read `UNEXP_STOP` reads 0.
|`CHK-I2C12-SMBSUS` |The shared suspend line reads 0 with only I2C1 pulling while I2C1
`SMBSUS` is 1 and 1 after the written 0; the I2C1 target reads `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBSUS` 1 while the line
is held and 0 after release; I2C2 `SMBSUS` reads back as written and its line reads 0 with only I2C2
pulling, then 1.
|`CHK-I2C12-SMBALERT` |The I2C1 target with `SMBALERT` 1 pulls the alert line to 0 and after I2C2
addresses it `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` reads 0 and the line 1; the I2C1 controller with `SMBUS_EN` and
the line held by the I2C0 target reads `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` 1 and `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` 1,
cleared by a written 0x8000 after I2C1 addresses the I2C0 target; without `SMBUS_EN` `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` stays 0 (`SMBUS_STATUS` logged, SF-012); the I2C2
target `SMBALERT` reads 0 after I2C1 addresses it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints BRINGUP, CMDC_STOP, CMDC_REASSERT, CMDC_RS_OBS, SDAU_W1C, SCLI_W1C,
SCLI_GATE, I2C12_INTR_TEST_W1C, I2C12_RW_HOLD, I2C12_IRQ_GATE, I2C12_CTRL_NACK, I2C12_CTRL_PARTIAL,
I2C12_TGT_TX_PENDING, I2C12_TGT_ABNORMAL, I2C12_UNEXP_STOP, I2C12_SMBSUS, I2C12_SMBALERT in order
with increasing time stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run (reset release, clock measure, bus release,
flag, STOP, HOSTIDLE, injector edge and interrupt level polls, bus recovery, event and status polls,
RDATA pops, ACQ drains, SMBus line samples) is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run fails
with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every checker above holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-CMDC-RS-OBS` records the counts without an expected value, and the arbitration value and
`TX_STRETCH` of `CHK-I2C12-TGT-ABNORMAL-END` and the early-STOP values of `CHK-I2C12-UNEXP-STOP` are
logged without one. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The wire monitor START, STOP and data byte counts at the first read that shows
`CMD_COMPLETE` during the write, repeated START, read transaction are measured and printed without
comparing; the expected set point is not compared.

'''''

[[sec-496-smc_i2c_ctrl_nack_modes_test]]
===== 496 `smc_i2c_ctrl_nack_modes_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_ctrl_nack_modes_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); bench targets on the I2C0 pads: an
I2C protocol VIP NACK target at 0x10 (NACKs its address), a bench target at 0x12 that NACKs one
chosen data byte index; the I2C wire monitor on the same pads;
probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i`, `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`;
`clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL, FDATA, FIFO_CTRL, STATUS, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, INTR_STATE,
HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT, TIMING0-4, OVRD and the I2C0 wrapper control register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The I2C0 controller sets `NACK` and `CONTROLLER_HALT` on address
and later data NACKs, honours `NAKOK` and the `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` enable, and every leg ends
with the events cleared.

*Test Coverage*:

* A NACKed read address sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT`; the halt
  flag stays set as a level while `NACK` is set; both clear after the controller is disabled and a 1
  is written to `NACK` (`i2c.rdl`).
* A NACK on a later data byte of a write sets `NACK`; the wire frame shows the address and the first
  data byte acknowledged and the second not.
* `FDATA.NAKOK` on a NACKed data byte suppresses `NACK` and the halt, the transfer completes
  (HOSTIDLE, FMTEMPTY) and the remaining bytes go out; the same pattern without `NAKOK` sets both
  (`i2c.rdl`).
* `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT.EN` makes an unhandled NACK set
  `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` and end the transfer with one STOP; with the register
  at 0 neither happens over four times the measured latency (`i2c.rdl`).
* Measured and printed only: `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` while halted, and the events, STOP count and pad
  levels after a `NACK` clear that arrives before the timeout expires.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the I2C0 wrapper control register (enable, controller
  mode), arm the I2C0 pads, poll `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i` to 1, program
  TIMING0-4 and OVRD off, set `CTRL` 0, and create the wire monitor, the 0x10 and 0x12 targets and
  the EEPROM.
. Error injection. Point: the bench NACK target at 0x10 on the I2C0 pads. Kind: a queued read of
  0x10 whose address is not acknowledged. Expected response: `NACK` polls to 1, `CONTROLLER_HALT`
  reads 1 and the wire frame for 0x10 is a read with the address not acknowledged. Start each leg
  with `CTRL` 0, FIFO reset, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE` cleared and ENABLEHOST set.
. Read `CONTROLLER_HALT` and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` three more times at least 300 cycles apart and
  require halt 1 and `NACK` 1 each time; set `CTRL` 0, wait for SCL to stop toggling, write 1 to
  `NACK` and require `NACK` and halt 0.
. Error injection. Point: the bench target at 0x12, made to NACK data byte index 1. Kind: a NACK on
  a later data byte of the write 0xC1, 0xC2, 0xC3. Expected response: `NACK` polls to 1 and the wire
  frame shows the address acknowledged, 0xC1 acknowledged, 0xC2 not acknowledged. Then set `CTRL` 0,
  clear `NACK` and require it 0.
. Error injection. Point: the bench target at 0x12, made to NACK data byte index 0. Kind: a NACK on
  the first data byte of the write 0xD1 with NAKOK, 0xD2, 0xD3. Expected response: STATUS HOSTIDLE
  and FMTEMPTY and a wire STOP, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0, halt 0 and a frame with 0xD1 not acknowledged
  followed by 0xD2 and 0xD3.
. Error injection. Point: the bench target at 0x12, still NACKing data byte index 0. Kind: the same
  pattern without NAKOK. Expected response: `NACK` polls to 1 and halt reads 1. Then set `CTRL` 0,
  clear `NACK` and require both 0.
. Error injection. Point: the bench NACK target at 0x10, with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` = EN | 256
  written first. Kind: a queued write whose address NACK is left unhandled. Expected response:
  polling every cycle shows `NACK` then `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT`, and exactly one wire STOP. Record
  the cycle gap L; set `CTRL` 0, clear both events and require 0.
. Error injection. Point: the bench NACK target at 0x10, with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` = 0
  written first. Kind: the same unhandled address NACK with the handler disabled. Expected response:
  over the events read every 200 cycles for 4 x L cycles after the `NACK` poll, `NACK` set,
  `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` clear and no wire STOP. Clean up as above.
. Error injection. Point: the bench NACK target at 0x10, with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` = EN |
  4096 written first. Kind: an address NACK whose `NACK` is cleared by a written 1 within 400 cycles
  and before the timeout expires. Expected response: the written 1 lands inside its cycle limit;
  STATUS, events, STOP count and pad levels sampled every 1024 cycles over 8192 cycles are printed.
  Read STATUS after the `NACK` poll; clean up as above.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ADDR-NACK-READ` |A read to 0x10 whose address is NACKed sets `NACK` and `CONTROLLER_HALT`, the
wire frame is a read with the address not acknowledged, and both flags read 0 after `CTRL` 0 and a
written 1 to `NACK`.
|`CHK-HALT-LEVEL` |`CONTROLLER_HALT` reads 1 on all three further reads at least 300 cycles apart
while `NACK` still reads 1 and nothing has been written, and reads 0 after the clear.
|`CHK-DATA-NACK-LATER` |A NACK on data byte index 1 of a three byte write sets `NACK` within the
poll bound; the wire frame shows the address and 0xC1 acknowledged and 0xC2 not acknowledged, and
`NACK` reads 0 after the clear; nothing is asserted about 0xC3.
|`CHK-NAKOK-DATA` |With NAKOK on the NACKed first data byte `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and halt read 0,
HOSTIDLE and FMTEMPTY reach 1 within the poll bound, and the wire frame shows 0xD1 not acknowledged
followed by 0xD2 and 0xD3.
|`CHK-NAKOK-CONTROL` |The same pattern without NAKOK sets `NACK` and halt within the poll bound and
both read 0 after `CTRL` 0 and a written 1 to `NACK`.
|`CHK-NTO-ENABLED` |With `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` = EN | 256 and the NACK unhandled,
`UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` sets within the poll bound after `NACK`, the wire monitor counts exactly
one STOP, and the events read 0 after the clear; `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` must set after `NACK`
(the measured latency is the window of the disabled-timeout leg).
|`CHK-NTO-DISABLED` |With `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` = 0, over at least four times the measured
latency `NACK` stays 1, `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` stays 0 and no STOP appears on the wire.
|`CHK-NTO-CLEAR-OBS` |The written 1 to `NACK` must complete within 400 cycles of the NACK and before
the timeout expires; the events, STOP count and pad levels over the following 8192 cycles are
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-STATUS-HALT-OBS` |`STATUS` (HOSTIDLE) read while the controller is halted by the NACK is
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints BRINGUP, ADDR_NACK_READ, HALT_LEVEL, DATA_NACK_LATER, NAKOK_DATA,
NAKOK_CONTROL, NTO_ENABLED, NTO_DISABLED, NTO_CLEAR_OBS in order with increasing time stamps, each
checker line printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ADDR-NACK-READ`, `CHK-HALT-LEVEL`, `CHK-DATA-NACK-LATER`, `CHK-NAKOK-DATA`,
`CHK-NAKOK-CONTROL`, `CHK-NTO-ENABLED`, `CHK-NTO-DISABLED`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`
hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds; `CHK-NTO-CLEAR-OBS` additionally requires
the clear to land inside its cycle limit, and `CHK-STATUS-HALT-OBS` records a measurement only.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` while the controller is halted by the NACK, and the events, STOP
count and pad levels over the 8192 cycles after a `NACK` clear that arrives before the timeout
expires, are measured and printed without comparing; nothing is asserted about 0xC3 in the
later-data-byte leg.

'''''

[[sec-497-smc_i2c_ctrl_role_gate_test]]
===== 497 `smc_i2c_ctrl_role_gate_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_ctrl_role_gate_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP EEPROM target at
0x50 on the instance 0 pads; a second I2C protocol VIP master used to pull SCL and SDA low; probes
`tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i`, `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`,
`tb_i2c_host_enable[0]`, `tb_i2c_target_enable[0]`; `clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL, FDATA, STATUS,
VAL, FIFO_CTRL, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, INTR_STATE, TIMING0-4, OVRD; the I2C0 `I2C_CTRL` wrapper register
(`I2C_EN`, controller mode); `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad
routing armed by the sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Three FDATA entries queued with `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` clear stay idle on
the pads until the host role is enabled, and `I2C_CTRL.I2C_EN` leaves the core role enables
unchanged.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and `ENABLETARGET` clear and three FDATA entries queued the pads stay
  released, the target sees no START and `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` stays 0 (`i2c.rdl`).
* Setting `ENABLEHOST` runs the queued stream: one START, one STOP, one data byte at the EEPROM,
  `FMTEMPTY` returns to 1, and the start latency is measured against the idle window length.
* Writing `I2C_CTRL.I2C_EN` 0 then 1 reads back and leaves `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` 1, `ENABLETARGET` 0 and
  the core enable probes unchanged (`i2c_ctrl.rdl`).
* `VAL` is read with the lines released and pulled low and printed without a compare, because the
  specification does not state the oversampling rate.
* Clearing `CTRL` stops the host: `ENABLEHOST` reads 0 and, with three further FDATA entries
  queued, the `dut_low` probes stay 0 and the target counters stop moving.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the I2C0 wrapper control register (enable, controller
  mode), arm the I2C0 pads, poll `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i` to 1, program
  TIMING0-4, OVRD off, reset the FIFOs, clear events and flags, set `CTRL` 0, require `ENABLEHOST`
  and `ENABLETARGET` to read 0 and create the EEPROM target.
. Queue three FDATA entries: address 0x50 write with START, offset 0x10, data 0xA7 with STOP;
  require `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` 0 after the first and after the third.
. For 4000 `clk_smc_i` cycles sample the pads every 16 cycles and require scl 1, sda 1,
  `scl_dut_low` 0, `sda_dut_low` 0; require the target START count 0 and `FMTEMPTY` 0 at the end.
. Write `CTRL.ENABLEHOST`; poll for SDA low or a target START and record the latency L; require the
  4000 cycle window to be at least 4 x L.
. Poll the target STOP and poll `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` to 1; require exactly one START, one STOP, one
  data byte and 0xA7 at memory offset 0x10.
. Write `I2C_CTRL.I2C_EN` 0 and then 1 (controller mode kept); after each, read back `I2C_EN`,
  `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` (1), `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` (0), `tb_i2c_host_enable[0]` (1) and
  `tb_i2c_target_enable[0]` (0).
. Read `VAL` until two successive reads agree with the lines released; pull SCL low for 2000
  cycles and read `VAL`, release it; repeat for SDA; read `VAL` released again; print the four words
  with the pad levels.
. Write `CTRL` 0, require `ENABLEHOST` 0, queue three FDATA entries (address 0x50 write with START,
  offset 0x10, data 0xA7 with STOP) and require `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` 0, sample the `dut_low` probes
  every 16 cycles over the 4000 cycle window and require 0, and require the target counters
  unchanged.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ROLE-OFF-IDLE` |With `ENABLEHOST` and `ENABLETARGET` clear and three entries queued every pad
sample over the 4000 cycle window reads scl 1, sda 1, both `dut_low` probes 0 and the target START
count is 0, and the window is at least four times the measured start latency.
|`CHK-ROLE-ON-RUNS` |Setting `ENABLEHOST` with the entries queued makes the target frame exactly one
START, one STOP and one data byte with 0xA7 at offset 0x10, the latency is finite, and after `CTRL`
0 with three entries queued the `dut_low` probes stay 0 over 250 samples and the target counters
do not move.
|`CHK-FMTEMPTY-TRACK` |`STATUS.FMTEMPTY` reads 0 after the first FDATA write, after the third and at
the end of the idle window, and reads 1 within the poll bound after the target frames its STOP.
|`CHK-IEN-ROLE-INDEP` |After each `I2C_EN` write (0 then 1) `I2C_EN` reads back the written value,
`CTRL.ENABLEHOST` reads 1, `ENABLETARGET` reads 0, `tb_i2c_host_enable[0]` is 1 and
`tb_i2c_target_enable[0]` is 0.
|`CHK-VAL-OBS` |The four `VAL` words (released, SCL low, SDA low, released) are measured and printed
with the pad levels, without comparing; the first released read is polled until two successive
reads agree and the second released read is a single read.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints BRINGUP, QUEUE_DISABLED, DISABLED_WINDOW, ENABLE, TARGET_STOP,
IEN_TOGGLE, VAL_OBS in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ROLE-OFF-IDLE`, `CHK-ROLE-ON-RUNS`, `CHK-FMTEMPTY-TRACK`,
`CHK-IEN-ROLE-INDEP`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every
sequence assert holds; `CHK-VAL-OBS` records the `VAL` words without an expected value. Enrolled
in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `VAL` read with the lines released and pulled low is printed without a compare,
because the specification does not state the oversampling rate.

'''''

[[sec-498-smc_i2c_ctrl_wire_frames_test]]
===== 498 `smc_i2c_ctrl_wire_frames_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_ctrl_wire_frames_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); three I2C protocol VIP EEPROM
targets at 0x50, 0x29 and 0x6B on the I2C0 pads; the I2C wire monitor that decodes every frame
(address, direction, per-byte ACK, START and STOP counts); probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`,
`tb_i2c0_scl_i`, `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`; `clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL,
FDATA, RDATA, STATUS, FIFO_CTRL, TIMING0-4, OVRD and the I2C0 wrapper control register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Transactions queued in the I2C0 FDATA FIFO appear on the wire with
one START and one STOP each, the queued address, data and read counts, and the RX FIFO returns the
bytes read.

*Test Coverage*:

* `FDATA.START` and `FDATA.STOP` frame a write as one START and one STOP, with the STOP after the
  flagged entry whatever the number of data bytes (`i2c.rdl`).
* The address byte on the wire equals the `FDATA` byte written for three target addresses.
* A write of six data bytes covering 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA, 0x01 and 0x80 lands in target memory.
* A read with `FDATA.READB` acknowledges every byte but the last (`RCONT` clear), for a count of one
  and of four; `RDATA` returns the bytes in order and `STATUS.RXEMPTY` tracks the pops.
* A second transaction queued while the first is open is sent after it; `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` reads 0
  right after the push. `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` during and after a transaction is only measured and
  printed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the I2C0 wrapper control register (enable, controller
  mode), arm the I2C0 pads, poll `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i` to 1, program
  TIMING0-4 and OVRD off, set `CTRL` 0, create the wire monitor and the three EEPROM targets.
. Twice queue (with `CTRL` 0 and the FIFOs reset) a write of one offset byte and one data byte to
  0x50 with START and STOP, set ENABLEHOST, wait for the wire STOP and require the monitor counts
  1/1/1 then 2/2/2 (STARTs, STOPs, frames) and the frame to be an acknowledged write.
. Queue a one data byte write (0x20) and a two data byte write (0x21, 0x5C) to 0x50; require one
  STOP each and acknowledged frames with exactly those bytes.
. Write one data byte to each of 0x50, 0x29, 0x6B; require the decoded address, a write direction,
  an acknowledged address and a wire byte equal to the FDATA byte written.
. Write offset 0x30 and the six pattern bytes with STOP on the last; require the acknowledged frame
  and target memory 0x30..0x35 to hold the pattern.
. Preload target memory at 0x40 with 0xF1..0xF4; run a write of the offset, a repeated START and a
  read of one byte with STOP; require the read frame with the last byte not acknowledged and the
  `RDATA` pop to be 0xF1.
. Reset the FIFOs, require `STATUS.RXEMPTY` 1, run the same sequence with a read count of four, wait
  for the wire STOP and poll `RXEMPTY` to 0; require 0xF1, 0xF2, 0xF3 acknowledged and 0xF4 not
  acknowledged; pop `RDATA` four times reading `STATUS` after each; require the bytes 0xF1..0xF4 and
  `RXEMPTY` 0, 0, 0, 1.
. Queue a three data byte write, set ENABLEHOST, wait for a wire START with no STOP, push a second
  write (offset 0x58, data 0x63), read `STATUS` and require `FMTEMPTY` 0 with the first transaction
  still open; read `STATUS` after each STOP and print `HOSTIDLE`; require frames 0x50, 0x61, 0x62
  then 0x58, 0x63 and two STARTs and two STOPs.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ONE-START-PER-STOP` |After the first write the monitor counts one START, one STOP and one
frame, after the second two of each, and holds exactly two frames.
|`CHK-STOP-POSITION` |The one data byte frame holds the acknowledged address and the single
acknowledged byte 0x20 before one STOP, and the two data byte frame holds 0x21 and 0x5C, both
acknowledged, before one STOP.
|`CHK-ADDR-VALUES` |The three frames carry addresses 0x50, 0x29 and 0x6B in the order written as
acknowledged writes, and the byte on the wire equals the address byte written to `FDATA`.
|`CHK-WRITE-PATTERN` |The frame data list is 0x30, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA, 0x01, 0x80 each
acknowledged, and target memory 0x30..0x35 equals 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA, 0x01, 0x80.
|`CHK-READ-LAST-NACK` |With `RCONT` clear every read byte is acknowledged except the last: the
single byte 0xF1 is not acknowledged, and for a count of four 0xF1, 0xF2, 0xF3 are acknowledged and
0xF4 is not.
|`CHK-READ-COUNTS` |The `RDATA` pop of the count one read returns 0xF1 and the four pops of the
count four read return 0xF1, 0xF2, 0xF3, 0xF4 in order.
|`CHK-RX-POP` |`STATUS.RXEMPTY` reads 1 before the count four read, reads 0 within the poll bound
after the transaction, reads 0 after pops 1 to 3 and reads 1 after pop 4.
|`CHK-QUEUE-WHILE-BUSY` |`STATUS.FMTEMPTY` reads 0 right after the second transaction is pushed
while the monitor shows the first open, and both appear on the wire in order (0x50, 0x61, 0x62 then
0x58, 0x63) with two STARTs and two STOPs in total.
|`CHK-HOSTIDLE-OBS` |`STATUS.HOSTIDLE` read after the push and after each STOP is measured and
printed together with the wire monitor state, without comparing.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints BRINGUP, ONE_START_PER_STOP, STOP_POSITION, ADDR_VALUES,
WRITE_PATTERN, READ_LAST_NACK, READ_COUNTS, RX_POP, QUEUE_WHILE_BUSY in order with increasing time
stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ONE-START-PER-STOP`, `CHK-STOP-POSITION`, `CHK-ADDR-VALUES`,
`CHK-WRITE-PATTERN`, `CHK-READ-LAST-NACK`, `CHK-READ-COUNTS`, `CHK-RX-POP`, `CHK-QUEUE-WHILE-BUSY`,
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-HOSTIDLE-OBS` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` during and after a transaction, read after the push and after each
STOP, is measured and printed with the wire monitor state without comparing.

'''''

[[sec-499-smc_i2c_ctrl_xinst_events_test]]
===== 499 `smc_i2c_ctrl_xinst_events_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_ctrl_xinst_events_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); the three I2C instances on one
shared open-drain bus (plusarg `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`), one enabled as controller at a time; I2C
protocol VIP EEPROM target at 0x50 and the absent address 0x51; the I2C wire monitor; probes
`tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]` (instance k on bit k); `clk_smc_i`; per instance
registers CTRL, FDATA, RDATA, TXDATA, STATUS, FIFO_CTRL, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE,
TARGET_ID, OVRD, TIMING0-4 and the `I2C_CTRL` wrapper register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; GPIO/LSIO pad routing of the three instances armed
by the sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Instance 1 reads the bytes that instance 2 transmits over the
shared bus, and each instance raises its own `tb_i2c_irq` bit for `CMD_COMPLETE` and
`CONTROLLER_HALT` only when enabled.

*Test Coverage*:

* An instance 1 controller read of an instance 2 target at 0x36 returns the `TXDATA` bytes 0x9E,
  0x71 in order through `RDATA` (`i2c.rdl` FDATA.READB, RDATA.DATA).
* Measured and printed only: the NACK and halt state after a write to an unconfigured address
  (0x6E), and `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` of the target instance after a controller STOP straight after
  the address, after a written 1, and after a normally terminated write, because the specification does not state
  the values.
* For each instance k, `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` and `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` reach `tb_i2c_irq`
  as `1 << k` only after the matching `INTR_ENABLE` bit is set, and the line falls after the clear
  (`i2c.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc` I2C interrupts 0-2).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; ungate the I2C peripheral clock, arm the pads of instances 0-2,
  poll `tb_i2c0_scl` and `tb_i2c0_sda` to 1; for each instance program TIMING0-4, `INTR_ENABLE` 0,
  OVRD 0 and disable `CTRL` and the wrapper register; create the wire monitor and the EEPROM at
  0x50.
. Make instance 2 a target at 0x36 (wrapper target mode, `TARGET_ID`, FIFO reset, ENABLETARGET and
  ACQ_START_STOP_EN) with `TXDATA` 0x9E, 0x71; make instance 1 a controller, queue a read of two
  bytes with STOP, poll `RDATA` until two bytes are popped and require 0x9E then 0x71; wait for
  HOSTIDLE, FMTEMPTY and a wire STOP, then disable the instance.
. Error injection. Point: the shared bus, driven by instance 0 as controller. Kind: a one data byte
  write to the unconfigured address 0x6E. Expected response: the leg ends in `NACK` or a wire STOP
  within the poll bound; `INTR_STATE` is read, the wire frame recorded and the state printed. Then
  recover the bus.
. Error injection. Point: the instance 1 target at 0x44, driven by instance 0 as controller with
  instance 2 disabled. Kind: START, address and STOP with no data. Expected response: instance 1
  `INTR_STATE` is read every 100 cycles for 4000 cycles and the `UNEXP_STOP` bit printed.
. Read instance 1 `INTR_STATE`, write 1 to `UNEXP_STOP`, read it again and print both.
. Send a normal write (0xA5, 0x5A, STOP) from instance 0 to the instance 1 target, poll `INTR_STATE`
  for 4000 cycles and print the `UNEXP_STOP` bit.
. For k = 0, 1, 2 (the other instances disabled): write 0x20, 0x5C to the EEPROM with STOP, poll
  `CMD_COMPLETE` to 1, require the EEPROM address acknowledged, require `tb_i2c_irq` 0b000 at two
  samples 200 cycles apart, set `INTR_ENABLE.CMD_COMPLETE`, poll `tb_i2c_irq` to `1 << k`, write 1
  to `CMD_COMPLETE` and poll `tb_i2c_irq` to 0b000.
. Error injection. Point: the shared bus, driven by each instance k = 0, 1, 2 as controller in turn.
  Kind: a write to the absent address 0x51. Expected response: `NACK` polls to 1, `CONTROLLER_HALT`
  reads 1, the frame address is not acknowledged and `tb_i2c_irq` reads 0b000 at two samples; after
  `INTR_ENABLE.CONTROLLER_HALT` is set `tb_i2c_irq` polls to `1 << k`; after `CTRL` 0 and a written
  1 to `NACK` it polls to 0b000 with `NACK` and halt 0.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-XINST-READ-1-2` |The two `RDATA` pops of instance 1 return 0x9E then 0x71, the `TXDATA` bytes
of instance 2, in order, within the poll bound.
|`CHK-XINST-UNCFG-OBS` |The wire frame for 0x6E, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and
`INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` of instance 0 are measured and printed without comparing; the leg must
end in a `NACK` or a STOP within the poll bound.
|`CHK-UNEXP-STOP-OBS` |`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` of instance 1 at every poll after a controller STOP
sent straight after the address is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-UNEXP-CLEAR-OBS` |`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` of instance 1 before and after a written 1 is
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-UNEXP-NORMAL-OBS` |`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` of instance 1 after a normally terminated write is
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-IRQ-CMDC-LINES` |For each instance with `CMD_COMPLETE` set and its enable clear `tb_i2c_irq`
reads 0b000 at both samples, after the enable it reads exactly `1 << k` within the poll bound, and
after the written 1 it reads 0b000 within the poll bound.
|`CHK-IRQ-HALT-LINES` |For each instance with `NACK` and `CONTROLLER_HALT` set and its enable clear
`tb_i2c_irq` reads 0b000 at both samples, after the enable it reads exactly `1 << k`, and after
`CTRL` 0 and a written 1 to `NACK` it reads 0b000 with `NACK` and halt 0.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints BRINGUP, XINST_READ_1_2, XINST_UNCFG_OBS, UNEXP_STOP_OBS,
UNEXP_CLEAR_OBS, UNEXP_NORMAL_OBS, IRQ_CMDC_LINES, IRQ_HALT_LINES in order with increasing time
stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-XINST-READ-1-2`, `CHK-IRQ-CMDC-LINES`, `CHK-IRQ-HALT-LINES`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-XINST-UNCFG-OBS`, `CHK-UNEXP-STOP-OBS`, `CHK-UNEXP-CLEAR-OBS` and `CHK-UNEXP-NORMAL-OBS` record
measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The NACK and halt state after a write to the unconfigured address 0x6E, and
`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` of the target instance after a controller STOP straight after the address,
before and after a written 1, and after a normally terminated write, are measured and printed
without comparing, because the specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-500-smc_i2c_fmtrst_repro_test]]
===== 500 `smc_i2c_fmtrst_repro_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_fmtrst_repro_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP EEPROM target at
0x50 on the I2C0 pads; a second I2C protocol VIP master used as the SCL holder
(`tb_i2c0_scl_ext_low`); a bench pad decoder sampling `tb_i2c0_scl` and `tb_i2c0_sda` every
`clk_smc_i` cycle; probes `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`; `clk_periph_i` for the hold
and window counts; I2C0 registers CTRL, FDATA, FIFO_CTRL, STATUS, HOST_FIFO_STATUS (FMTLVL),
CONTROLLER_EVENTS, INTR_STATE, TIMEOUT_CTRL, OVRD, TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper control register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `i2c`, `repro`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: After a bus-timeout halt of the I2C0 controller, a recovery with
`FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST` and a written 1 to `BUS_TIMEOUT` is run with and without an `ENABLEHOST` toggle,
and the START, `CMD_COMPLETE` and FDATA consumption that follow are recorded.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `TIMEOUT_CTRL` in bus mode and `VAL` set to four times TLOW, an external SCL hold of three
  times that value at the address acknowledge sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT` within twice that
  value, `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` reads 1 and `INTR_STATE.STRETCH_TIMEOUT` stays 0 (`i2c.rdl`
  TIMEOUT_CTRL, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, INTR_STATE).
* While halted the controller consumes no format FIFO entry and sends no data byte.
* Recovery arm A writes `FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST` and a written 1 to `BUS_TIMEOUT` with `CTRL.ENABLEHOST`
  left set; arm B clears `ENABLEHOST` first, writes both, then sets it (`i2c.rdl` FIFO_CTRL).
* After each arm one START-flagged write is queued and a bounded window records whether a START
  reaches the pads, whether `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` sets and whether the FMTLVL entries are
  consumed. A recorded value of 0 is a valid outcome; no expected value is compared.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Prove the I2C0 pins, ungate the I2C peripheral clock, enable the I2C0 wrapper as controller, wait
  for the I2C0 pad routing, create the EEPROM target, the SCL holder and the pad decoder; program
  OVRD off, TIMING0-4 (THIGH 0x1A, TLOW 0x32), reset the FIFOs, set `TIMEOUT_CTRL` 0, clear events
  and `INTR_STATE`, set `ENABLEHOST`; require `TIMEOUT_CTRL` 0, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` 0 and the
  `CONTROLLER_HALT`, `SCL_INTERFERENCE`, `STRETCH_TIMEOUT`, `CMD_COMPLETE` flags clear; wait for
  HOSTIDLE.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL pad, held low by the SCL holder once the pad decoder has followed
  the START, nine SCL rises and the fall of the acknowledge. Kind: an external SCL hold of three
  times VAL peripheral cycles at the address acknowledge. Expected response:
  `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT` within two times VAL cycles of the hold start, as polled in
  step 3. Halt A: first write `TIMEOUT_CTRL` = EN | bus mode | VAL and read it back, clear EEPROM memory
  at offset 1, and queue START with 0xA0, 0x01 and 0x02 with STOP.
. Poll `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` until `BUS_TIMEOUT` is set within two times VAL cycles of the hold start;
  require `CONTROLLER_HALT` 1 and `STRETCH_TIMEOUT` 0; release the hold, read FMTLVL twice 2 x TLOW
  apart and require equal values, the EEPROM data byte count and offset 1 unchanged and exactly one
  START seen by the EEPROM.
. Repro A: write 1 to `CMD_COMPLETE` and read `INTR_STATE`, write `FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST`, write 1 to
  `BUS_TIMEOUT`, snapshot STATUS, FMTLVL, `INTR_STATE`, events; open the pad window (40 x VAL
  peripheral cycles by default), queue START with 0xA0 and 0x33 with STOP and read FMTLVL; at the
  window end read `INTR_STATE`, FMTLVL, STATUS and events and print the START, `CMD_COMPLETE` and
  FDATA facts.
. Cleanup: set `CTRL` 0, reset the FIFOs, clear every event and flag, poll HOSTIDLE, wait for the
  pads to release, set `ENABLEHOST`, wait for HOSTIDLE and snapshot.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL pad, held low by the SCL holder as in step 2. Kind: halt B, the
  same external SCL hold at the address acknowledge. Expected response: as in step 3, `BUS_TIMEOUT`
  within two times VAL cycles, `CONTROLLER_HALT` 1, `STRETCH_TIMEOUT` 0, FMTLVL steady, offset 1
  unchanged and exactly one START seen by the EEPROM.
. Repro B: set `CTRL` 0, write `FIFO_CTRL.FMTRST`, write 1 to `BUS_TIMEOUT` and to `CMD_COMPLETE`,
  wait for HOSTIDLE, set `ENABLEHOST`, then repeat the window, queue and fact lines of step 4.
. Check the ordered fence of the six stages SETUP, HALT-A, REPRO-A, CLEANUP, HALT-B and
  REPRO-B in that order.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-START-SEEN` |Arm A: whether a START is decoded on the pads inside the window is
measured and printed with its time, the SCL and STOP counts and the EEPROM START count, without
comparing.
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-CMD-COMPLETE` |Arm A: `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` at the window end, with
`CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and STATUS (HOSTIDLE), is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-FDATA-CONSUMED` |Arm A: whether FMTLVL fell between the queued and the end
reading, with the EEPROM byte, ACK and STOP counts, is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-START-SEEN-CTRL` |Arm B (`ENABLEHOST` toggled first): the same START observation
is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-CMD-COMPLETE-CTRL` |Arm B: `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` at the window end is
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-FDATA-CONSUMED-CTRL` |Arm B: whether the queued format entries were consumed is
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints SETUP, HALT-A, REPRO-A, CLEANUP, HALT-B, REPRO-B in order with
increasing time stamps before the final PASS mark.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-NONVAC` holds after its compares, and every sequence assert holds: the setup
reads, `BUS_TIMEOUT` within twice VAL, `CONTROLLER_HALT` 1, `STRETCH_TIMEOUT` 0, FMTLVL steady, and
no EEPROM data byte while halted, in both halts. The six `CHK-FMTRST-REPRO-*` ids record
measurements only and carry no pass or fail from their values. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Whether a START reaches the pads, whether `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` sets and whether
the FMTLVL entries are consumed after each recovery arm are measured and printed without comparing;
a recorded value of 0 is a valid outcome and the six repro ids carry no pass or fail from their
values.

'''''

[[sec-501-smc_i2c_intr_output_path_test]]
===== 501 `smc_i2c_intr_output_path_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_intr_output_path_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor only, no bus traffic and no I2C
protocol VIP); `INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST` of I2C instances 0-2;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; probes `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]` (instance n on bit n),
`tb_peripheral_interrupts` (I2C on bits 23-25, neighbours on bits 22 and 26) and
`tb_cpu_interrupts` (I2C on IDs 279-281, neighbours on IDs 278 and 282, whole vector scanned);
clock `clk_smc_i`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `INTR_ENABLE` qualifies `INTR_STATE` into each instance's
`tb_i2c_irq` bit, the three instances stay independent, and the neighbouring peripheral and CPU
interrupt bits do not move.

*Test Coverage*:

* `INTR_ENABLE` and `INTR_STATE` reset to 0, `INTR_ENABLE` reads back an all-ones write on all
  three instances, and `tb_i2c_irq` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` read 0 before any write
  (`i2c.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc` I2C interrupts 0-2).
* An enabled `INTR_TEST.CMD_COMPLETE` of instance n raises `tb_i2c_irq[n]` alone within 512 cycles
  and a W1C with the enable cleared drops it (`interrupts.adoc`, I2C `index.adoc`).
* A pending bit B stays invisible while only a different bit A is enabled and appears once B is
  enabled, for three bit pairs (`i2c.rdl` per-field `INTR_ENABLE`).
* Three instances forced together read 0b111 and clearing them in either order steps down 0b110,
  0b100, 0b000 and 0b011, 0b001, 0b000; the other instances' `INTR_STATE`/`INTR_ENABLE` words do not
  move when one instance is driven.
* The CPU vector bits 279-281 follow the instance outputs with a bounded latency; IDs 278 and 282
  belong to other sources and stay at their baseline.
* Measured and printed only: which CPU vector bits are high while an output is high, and the output
  level when a state is pending with the enable clear, after the enable, after the enable is cleared
  again and after each one-by-one clear of three pending enabled bits.
