*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock and sample the neighbour bits (peripheral 22 and 26, CPU 278 and
  282) as the baseline.
. Require `tb_i2c_irq` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` 0 and `INTR_ENABLE` 0 on all instances; for
  each instance write the all-ones enable, read it back, record `tb_i2c_irq`, write 0 and read 0;
  wait for `tb_i2c_irq` 0.
. For n = 0, 1, 2: enable `CMD_COMPLETE`, raise it through `INTR_TEST`, poll `tb_i2c_irq[n]` to 1
  within 512 cycles, require the other two bits 0 and the peripheral neighbours at baseline, record
  the CPU vector bits that are high, W1C `CMD_COMPLETE`, clear the enable, poll the bit to 0 and
  require `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` 0.
. Raise `CMD_COMPLETE` of instance 0 with its enable 0, sample `tb_i2c_irq[0]` for 64 cycles and
  read `INTR_STATE`; set the enable and observe the rise; clear the enable and observe the level
  after 512 cycles; W1C and require `CMD_COMPLETE` 0.
. For the pairs (`CMD_COMPLETE`, `TX_STRETCH`), (`RX_OVERFLOW`, `TARGET_RX_FIFO_ERROR`) and
  (`TX_STRETCH`, `SMBALERT`): enable A, force B through `INTR_TEST`, require B in `INTR_STATE` and
  `tb_i2c_irq[0]` 0 on 64 consecutive samples, enable A and B, poll `tb_i2c_irq[0]` to 1, release B
  (W1C for an event bit, `INTR_TEST` 0 for a status bit), poll it to 0 and require B clear.
. Enable and force `CMD_COMPLETE` on all three instances, poll `tb_i2c_irq` to 0b111, clear
  instances in the order 0, 1, 2 polling 0b110, 0b100, 0b000, raise all again and clear in the order
  2, 1, 0 polling 0b011, 0b001, 0b000.
. For each writer n snapshot the other two instances' `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` and their
  `tb_i2c_irq` bits, enable and force `CMD_COMPLETE` on n, require the other words and bits
  unchanged and 0, W1C, clear the enable, require the other words still unchanged.
. For n = 0, 1, 2: enable and force `CMD_COMPLETE`, poll `tb_cpu_interrupts[279+n]` to 1 within 2000
  cycles, W1C, poll it to 0 within 2000 cycles, clear the enable.
. Read `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` 0 on all instances and require every neighbour sample taken in
  steps 3, 6 and 8 to equal the baseline.
. Enable `CMD_COMPLETE`, `SDA_UNSTABLE` and `RX_OVERFLOW` on instance 0, force all three, observe
  the rise of `tb_i2c_irq[0]`, W1C them one at a time observing the level and `INTR_STATE` after
  each, clear the enable and restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`.
. Check the ordered fence S1 to S10.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-IRQ-RESET-LOW` |`tb_i2c_irq` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` read 0 before any write,
`INTR_ENABLE` reads 0 at reset and reads back the all-ones write on all three instances and then 0,
and each `tb_i2c_irq` bit later rises in step 3, so the zero is fail-capable.
|`CHK-I2C-IRQ-PERIPH-ONEHOT` |After an enabled `INTR_TEST.CMD_COMPLETE` of instance n only
`tb_i2c_irq[n]` reads 1 within 512 cycles, the other two bits read 0 and peripheral bits 22 and 26
equal the baseline; after the W1C and the enable cleared `tb_i2c_irq[n]` reads 0 with `CMD_COMPLETE`
clear.
|`CHK-I2C-CPU-VEC-RAISE-OBS` |The `tb_cpu_interrupts` bit indices that read 1 while instance n's
output is high are measured and printed for n = 0, 1, 2 without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-ENABLE-MASK-OBS` |The `tb_i2c_irq[0]` level with the state pending and the enable 0, after
the enable, after the enable is cleared, and after each of three one-by-one clears, with the
matching `INTR_STATE` words, is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-PAIR-MASK` |For each of the three bit pairs `tb_i2c_irq[0]` reads 0 on 64 consecutive
samples with only A enabled, reads 1 within 512 cycles once B is enabled, reads 0 after B is
released and B reads clear in `INTR_STATE`.
|`CHK-I2C-IRQ-THREE-INDEPENDENT` |With all three instances forced and enabled `tb_i2c_irq` reads
0b111; clearing 0, 1, 2 gives 0b110, 0b100, 0b000 and clearing 2, 1, 0 gives 0b011, 0b001, 0b000,
each within 512 cycles.
|`CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-INTR-ISOLATION` |For each writer n the other two instances' `INTR_STATE` and
`INTR_ENABLE` words equal the snapshot after the raise and after the clear, and their `tb_i2c_irq`
bits read 0.
|`CHK-I2C-CPU-VEC-FALL-OBS` |The rise latency of `tb_cpu_interrupts[279+n]` and its fall latency
after the W1C are measured and printed in `clk_smc_i` cycles; each wait must end within 2000 cycles.
|`CHK-I2C-CPU-NEIGHBOURS` |Every sample of peripheral bits 22 and 26 and CPU bits 278 and 282 taken
in steps 3, 6 and 8 equals the step 1 baseline, and `CMD_COMPLETE` reads clear on all instances.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S10 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
printed after its steps.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-IRQ-RESET-LOW`, `CHK-I2C-IRQ-PERIPH-ONEHOT`, `CHK-I2C-PAIR-MASK`,
`CHK-I2C-IRQ-THREE-INDEPENDENT`, `CHK-I2C-INSTANCE-INTR-ISOLATION`, `CHK-I2C-CPU-NEIGHBOURS` and
`CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds; `CHK-I2C-CPU-VEC-RAISE-OBS`,
`CHK-I2C-ENABLE-MASK-OBS` and the latency values of `CHK-I2C-CPU-VEC-FALL-OBS` record measurements
only, the last also requiring the CPU bit to rise and fall within its bound. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Which CPU vector bits are high while an output is high, the `tb_i2c_irq[0]` level
with a state pending and the enable clear, after the enable, after the enable is cleared again and
after each one-by-one clear of three pending enabled bits, and the rise and fall latency of
`tb_cpu_interrupts[279+n]` are measured and printed without comparing; the latency waits must still
end within 2000 cycles.

'''''

[[sec-502-smc_i2c_intr_test_state_test]]
===== 502 `smc_i2c_intr_test_state_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_intr_test_state_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor, register reads and writes only, no
bus traffic and no I2C protocol VIP); `INTR_TEST`, `INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE` of I2C instances 0-2
(every `INTR_ENABLE` left at reset, so no interrupt output is observed);
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`. Status bits: FMT_THRESHOLD, RX_THRESHOLD,
ACQ_THRESHOLD, CONTROLLER_HALT, TX_STRETCH, TX_THRESHOLD, ACQ_STRETCH. Event bits: the thirteen
other `INTR_STATE` fields from RX_OVERFLOW to TARGET_RX_FIFO_ERROR.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: `INTR_TEST` forces and releases the seven status bits, latches the
thirteen event bits until a written 1 clears them, and a clear on one instance leaves the others
alone.

*Test Coverage*:

* `INTR_TEST` is read-write on the status bits ("Writing 1 forces the interrupt", "Writing 0
  releases it") and `INTR_STATE` is read-only there: a software write of the bit or of 0 leaves a
  forced bit set (`i2c.rdl`).
* `INTR_TEST` is write-only single-pulse on the event bits and `INTR_STATE` is write-one-to-clear:
  `INTR_TEST` 0 or an `INTR_STATE` write of 0 does not release a latched event; contiguous and
  alternating partial clears remove exactly the written bits; a zero write changes nothing.
* An event can be re-armed after its clear, a repeated `INTR_TEST` while it is set keeps it set and
  one clear removes it.
* A written 1 to `RX_OVERFLOW` clears only that instance of the three (`i2c_wrap.rdl` instance
  spacing).
* Status bits that are live at baseline are not measured; the `INTR_TEST` read-back and the effect
  of `INTR_TEST` on a live status bit are only measured and printed because the specification does not state
  the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, read `INTR_ENABLE` and `INTR_STATE` of all instances and note the
  status bits of instance 0 that are live.
. For each status bit that is not live and reads 0, write its `INTR_TEST` bit, require it to read 1
  in `INTR_STATE`, record the `INTR_TEST` read-back; write `INTR_TEST` 0; require all seven
  status bits measured and none live at baseline.
. For each measured bit force it, read `INTR_STATE`, write `INTR_TEST` 0 and require it to read 0.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only `INTR_STATE` status bits, while `INTR_TEST` holds each
  measured bit forced. Kind: a software write of 1 to the bit and then a write of 0. Expected
  response: the bit reads 1 after each write; the write responses are recorded. Then release it and
  require 0.
. Write `INTR_TEST` 1 and then 0 on each status bit that was live or already set and print the
  `INTR_STATE` words, or print the idle words when no status bit was live.
. Clear all 13 event bits with a W1C and require 0; write `INTR_TEST` with all 13 event bits and
  require all set; write `INTR_TEST` 0 and `INTR_STATE` 0 and require all still set.
. Clear the first six event bits and require the other seven set, clear the other seven and require
  0; re-raise all 13 and clear alternating halves A then B and then B then A, requiring the
  complement after the first write and 0 after the second; require a zero write to leave a cleared
  word and a partly set word unchanged; clear all.
. Require `RX_OVERFLOW` 0, force it, W1C it, force it again, force it once more while set, and W1C
  once requiring 0.
. Force `RX_OVERFLOW` on all three instances, require it set on all; for n = 0, 1, 2 write 1 to
  instance n and require that instance 0 and the others 1, re-raise it; clear all and require 0.
. Check the ordered fence S1 to S9.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-STATUS-FORCE` |None of the seven status bits is live at baseline, all seven are measured
and every measured status bit reads 1 in `INTR_STATE` after its `INTR_TEST`
write; the `INTR_TEST` read-back and the list of unmeasured bits are measured and printed without
comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-STATUS-RELEASE` |After `INTR_TEST` is written 0 every measured status bit reads 0 in
`INTR_STATE`.
|`CHK-I2C-STATUS-SW-RO` |While `INTR_TEST` holds a status bit an `INTR_STATE` write of the bit and a
write of 0 each leave it reading 1, and `INTR_TEST` 0 then releases it; the write responses are
printed.
|`CHK-I2C-STATUS-LIVE-OBS` |The `INTR_STATE` words read after `INTR_TEST` 1 and after `INTR_TEST` 0
on each live status bit are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-EVENT-NO-RELEASE` |After `INTR_TEST` writes the 13 event bits `INTR_STATE` reads them all
set, and after `INTR_TEST` 0 and `INTR_STATE` 0 they still read set.
|`CHK-I2C-EVENT-PARTIAL-CLEAR` |From 13 set bits the low-half write leaves exactly the seven high
bits, the high-half write leaves 0, each alternating write leaves exactly its complement and the
second leaves 0, and a zero write changes nothing.
|`CHK-I2C-EVENT-REARM` |`RX_OVERFLOW` reads 0 after its W1C, 1 after a second `INTR_TEST` write,
still 1 after a further `INTR_TEST` write while set, and 0 after one W1C.
|`CHK-I2C-W1C-ISOLATION` |With `RX_OVERFLOW` set on all three instances a W1C on instance n leaves
instance n at 0 and the other two at 1, for n = 0, 1, 2, and the final clear leaves all 0.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S9 in order with increasing time stamps and the eight checker
lines have been printed.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-STATUS-FORCE`, `CHK-I2C-STATUS-RELEASE`, `CHK-I2C-STATUS-SW-RO`,
`CHK-I2C-EVENT-NO-RELEASE`, `CHK-I2C-EVENT-PARTIAL-CLEAR`, `CHK-I2C-EVENT-REARM`,
`CHK-I2C-W1C-ISOLATION` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-I2C-STATUS-LIVE-OBS` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Status bits that are live at baseline are not measured; the `INTR_TEST` read-back,
the list of unmeasured bits, the write responses of the `INTR_STATE` writes on a forced status bit,
and the `INTR_STATE` words read after `INTR_TEST` 1 and 0 on each live status bit are measured and
printed without comparing, because the specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-503-smc_i2c_pad_override_test]]
===== 503 `smc_i2c_pad_override_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_pad_override_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); no I2C protocol VIP on the bus;
resolved pad probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`; per-instance pull probes `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`,
`tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`, `tb_i2c1_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c1_sda_dut_low`, `tb_i2c2_scl_dut_low`,
`tb_i2c2_sda_dut_low`; clock `clk_smc_i`; registers `OVRD` (TXOVRDEN, SCLVAL, SDAVAL) of instances
0-2, `VAL` (SCL_RX bits 15:0, SDA_RX bits 31:16) of instance 0 and the `I2C_CTRL` wrapper register
of instance 0; `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 pad routing readiness.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `OVRD.TXOVRDEN` makes an instance pull its own SCL and SDA probes,
other instances stay unaffected, and the pad levels and `VAL` words under `OVRD` are recorded.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `OVRD.TXOVRDEN` clear, `SCLVAL` and `SDAVAL` have no pull effect; the pad nets are
  sampled and printed and both pull probes read 0 (`i2c.rdl` OVRD, "enables control of the SDA and
  SCL lines").
* With `TXOVRDEN` set, `SCLVAL` or `SDAVAL` of 0 pulls the line low and 1 releases it
  (`i2c.rdl` OVRD); the settled pad levels are measured and printed together with the
  line level the register description implies, because the specification does not state the pad
  pull-up model; the pull probes `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low` and `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low` read 1 for a value
  of 0 and 0 for a value of 1.
* `OVRD[n]` = `TXOVRDEN` raises both `tb_i2cn_*_dut_low` probes of instance n and none of the other
  two instances' probes, and `OVRD[n]` = 0 lowers them again (`i2c/doc/index.adoc` per-instance
  ports, `i2c.rdl` OVRD).
* `VAL` is read released, with SCL held low, with SDA held low and in a burst after the release, and
  printed without a compare, because the specification does not state the sampling cadence and reset history.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the I2C0 wrapper register in target mode, wait for the I2C0
  pad routing and for the bus to release, and require `tb_i2c0_scl` and `tb_i2c0_sda` to read 1.
. Write four `OVRD` words with `TXOVRDEN` clear (0, `SCLVAL`, `SDAVAL`, both) on instance 0 and
  sample the two pads and two probes for 16 cycles after each; print the samples and require both
  probes 0.
. Write `OVRD` = `TXOVRDEN` | `SDAVAL`, `TXOVRDEN` | `SCLVAL` and `TXOVRDEN` alone; after each wait
  until the four levels are stable for 8 samples within 400 cycles, print the settle cycle and
  levels and require each probe to equal 1 minus the written value of its line.
. Write `OVRD` = `TXOVRDEN` | `SCLVAL` | `SDAVAL`, `TXOVRDEN` | `SDAVAL`, `TXOVRDEN` | `SCLVAL`;
  wait, print the settled levels and require the probes as in step 3.
. For each instance n write `OVRD[n]` = `TXOVRDEN`; for 8 samples require its own two probes 1 and
  the other instances' four probes 0; write `OVRD[n]` = 0 and require its own probes 0 for 8
  samples.
. Release the lines through `OVRD` on instance 0, read `VAL`; pull SCL low for 64 cycles and read
  `VAL`; release and read `VAL` 16 times 8 cycles apart; repeat for SDA; write `OVRD` 0; print the
  `SCL_RX` and `SDA_RX` halves of every word.
. Check the ordered fence S1 to S6.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-OVRD-DISABLED-OBS` |For the four `OVRD` words with `TXOVRDEN` clear both pull probes read
0 on all 16 samples; the pad levels are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-OVRD-PULL-OBS` |For each of the three pull words the levels must settle within 400
cycles and each pull probe equals 1 minus the written line value; the settle cycle and pad levels
are measured and printed, and the implied line level is shown without comparing the pads.
|`CHK-I2C-OVRD-RELEASE-OBS` |For each of the three release words the levels must settle within 400
cycles and each pull probe equals 1 minus the written line value; the settle cycle and pad levels
are measured and printed without comparing the pads.
|`CHK-I2C-OVRD-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` |With `OVRD[n]` = `TXOVRDEN` both probes of instance n read 1 on
all 8 samples and the other two instances' probes read 0 on every sample, and after `OVRD[n]` = 0
the probes of instance n read 0, for n = 0, 1, 2.
|`CHK-I2C-VAL-SENSE-OBS` |Every `VAL` word read in the released, SCL low, SDA low and release again
phases is measured and printed as `SCL_RX` and `SDA_RX` without comparing.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S6 in order with increasing time stamps and the five checker
lines cover S2 to S6.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-OVRD-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares, the
pads read 1 after bring-up, the pull and release legs settle within their bound and their pull
probes and the disabled-leg pull probes match the compares above; the pad levels of
`CHK-I2C-OVRD-DISABLED-OBS`, `CHK-I2C-OVRD-PULL-OBS` and `CHK-I2C-OVRD-RELEASE-OBS` and
`CHK-I2C-VAL-SENSE-OBS` record measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The pad levels under every `OVRD` word, the settle cycle and the implied line level
are measured and printed without comparing the pads, because the specification does not state the
pad pull-up model; every `VAL` word read released, with SCL or SDA held low and in the burst after
release is printed without a compare, because the specification does not state the sampling cadence
and reset history.

'''''

[[sec-504-smc_i2c_reg_access_class_test]]
===== 504 `smc_i2c_reg_access_class_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_reg_access_class_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor word accesses, error responses allowed
on the observation steps); no I2C bus traffic and no protocol VIP, `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and
`ENABLETARGET` held at 0; registers of I2C instances 0-2 (INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST,
SMBUS_CTRL, CTRL, STATUS, RDATA, FDATA, FIFO_CTRL, HOST_FIFO_CONFIG, TARGET_FIFO_CONFIG,
HOST_FIFO_STATUS, TARGET_FIFO_STATUS, OVRD, VAL, TIMING0-4, TIMEOUT_CTRL, TARGET_ID, ACQDATA,
TXDATA, HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL, TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL, TARGET_ACK_CTRL, ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA,
HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, TARGET_EVENTS, SMBUS_STATUS, TARGET_NACK_COUNT) and
the `I2C_CTRL` wrapper registers 0-2 (`I2C_EN` bit 0, `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN` bit 4, `SMBUS_EN` bit
8); probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c_host_enable`, `tb_i2c_target_enable`;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the sequence;
the `RANDOM_SEED` environment value (default 1) picks the instance walked per register.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the seed selects only which instance is walked per leg; the
access classes and the expected words are the same on every instance.

*Objective*: The I2C registers keep what is written under their declared access
class on every instance, read-only and write-only registers have no side effect, and the three
`I2C_CTRL` registers and instances stay isolated.

*Test Coverage*:

* The 16 software-writable register families read back all-ones, all-zero, every walking-one and
  walking-zero word under the writable-bit mask (role bits of `CTRL`, `SMBALERT` and a half-driven
  `OVRD` excluded; `TIMING0` THIGH/TLOW below 2 printed without a compare) (`i2c.rdl`).
* Each field of `TARGET_ID`, `HOST_FIFO_CONFIG`, `TIMEOUT_CTRL` and `TIMING0` changes alone against
  a background word; patterns persist across unrelated accesses and `STATUS` polls reading 0x33C.
* Read-only registers keep their reset value after the write of all-ones and after the write of 0
  (`STATUS` 0x33C; the four zero-reset ones read 0); write-only registers read without side effect
  on `STATUS` or the `INTR_STATE` event bits (`i2c.rdl` access classes).
* `I2C_CTRL` bits 0, 4 and 8 read back as written and do not enable either engine (`i2c_ctrl.rdl`,
  I2C `index.adoc`); a write to one `I2C_CTRL` or one instance's register leaves the other two alone
  (`i2c_wrap.rdl` instance spacing).
* Measured and printed only: write response codes of read-only registers, read values and response
  codes of write-only registers, reserved-bit residue, `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES`, `SMBALERT` and
  threshold readbacks, `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` reads and the host/target enable probes.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, require `STATUS` 0x33C on all instances and arm the I2C0 pads.
. For each of the 16 families write all-ones and all-zero on instances 0-2 and read back under the
  mask; on the seeded instance walk a one and a zero through every writable bit; restore reset
  values.
. For `TARGET_ID`, `HOST_FIFO_CONFIG`, `TIMEOUT_CTRL` and `TIMING0` write a background word, change
  each field in turn to two other values and require the background with only that field replaced.
. Write a distinct pattern to every family on a seeded instance, run 8 rounds of an unrelated read
  and a `STATUS` read (0x33C) with `tb_i2c0_scl` and `tb_i2c0_sda` at 1, then require every pattern
  unchanged; restore.
. On instance 0 write `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES` 0x5, `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT`, and the thresholds 0x40,
  0x41, 0x100, 0xFFF to `ACQ_THRESH` and the host `RX_THRESH`/`FMT_THRESH`; print each readback;
  restore.
. Error injection. Point: the read-only registers `STATUS`, `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`,
  `TARGET_FIFO_STATUS`, `VAL`, `SMBUS_STATUS` and `ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA` of instance 0. Kind: writes
  of all-ones and of 0 to read-only registers. Expected response: the responses are recorded, the
  register read after the all-ones write holds its reset value (`STATUS` 0x33C, the four zero-reset
  registers 0), `STATUS` reads 0x33C after each, and finally `STATUS` 0x33C and the four zero-reset
  registers 0.
. Error injection. Point: the write-only registers `FIFO_CTRL`, `FDATA`, `TXDATA` and `INTR_TEST` of
  instance 1, then every register of the instance. Kind: reads of write-only registers, then an
  all-ones write to every register. Expected response: the read responses and values are recorded,
  `STATUS` reads 0x33C and the `INTR_STATE` event bits are unchanged; every register is read back
  and the reserved residue printed. Then clear events and flags, restore, reset the FIFOs, read
  `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` twice, write it, read it twice, and require `STATUS` and the event bits
  unchanged.
. Write the five patterns (`I2C_EN`, `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN`, `SMBUS_EN`, all three, none) to each
  `I2C_CTRL` register and require bits 0, 4, 8 to read as written; print the reserved residue.
. Write distinct patterns to `I2C_CTRL[0]`, `[1]`, `[2]` in turn and require the other two registers
  to hold their previous words.
. For `TARGET_ID`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `TIMING0` write a distinct pattern at the same offset of each
  instance in turn and require that instance at its pattern and the other two unchanged.
. Set each `I2C_CTRL` field on each instance, require `CTRL` role bits 0 and `STATUS` 0x33C and
  print the host and target enable probes.
. Check the ordered fence S1 to S11.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-RW-PATTERNS` |Every readback of the 16 families equals the written word under the
writable-bit mask for all-ones, all-zero and every walking step; the seed, the instances walked and
the `TIMING0` THIGH/TLOW below 2 points are printed, the last without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RW-FIELD-INDEP` |After each single-field change `TARGET_ID`, `HOST_FIFO_CONFIG`,
`TIMEOUT_CTRL` and `TIMING0` read the background word with only that field replaced.
|`CHK-I2C-RW-PERSIST` |Each pattern written with the engines disabled reads back unchanged after 8
unrelated accesses and 8 `STATUS` polls, each `STATUS` reading 0x33C with the pads at 1.
|`CHK-I2C-RW-OBSERVED` |The readbacks of `NBYTES`, `SMBALERT`, `ACQ_THRESH` and the host thresholds
for 0x5, 0x40, 0x41, 0x100, 0xFFF are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RO-IGNORED` |After the write of all-ones and after the write of 0 `STATUS` reads 0x33C and
`HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `TARGET_FIFO_STATUS`, `SMBUS_STATUS`, `ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA` read 0; the
write response codes and `VAL` are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-ROWO-OBSERVED` |After the write-only reads and the all-ones sweep `STATUS` reads 0x33C and
the `INTR_STATE` event bits are unchanged; the read values, response codes, reserved residue and
`TARGET_NACK_COUNT` reads are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-FIELDS` |For the five patterns and the three `I2C_CTRL` registers bits 0, 4 and 8
read back equal to the written bits; the reserved residue is printed.
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NEIGHBOURS` |After each write of one `I2C_CTRL` register the other two read their
previous word, for n = 0, 1, 2.
|`CHK-I2C-ISOLATION-MATRIX` |After a distinct pattern is written at the same offset of instance n
only, instance n reads it under the mask and the other two read the word they held before, for the
three families and n = 0, 1, 2.
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NO-ENGINE` |With each `I2C_CTRL` field set `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and `ENABLETARGET` read
0, `STATUS` reads 0x33C, and the core's `host_enable` and `target_enable` probes read 0
(`i2c_ctrl.rdl`: the field does not enable the I2C core).
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S11 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
printed after its step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-RW-PATTERNS`, `CHK-I2C-RW-FIELD-INDEP`, `CHK-I2C-RW-PERSIST`,
`CHK-I2C-RO-IGNORED`, `CHK-I2C-ROWO-OBSERVED` (its `STATUS` and event-bit compares),
`CHK-I2C-CTRL-FIELDS`, `CHK-I2C-CTRL-NEIGHBOURS`, `CHK-I2C-ISOLATION-MATRIX`,
`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NO-ENGINE` (its compares) and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every
sequence assert holds; `CHK-I2C-RW-OBSERVED` and the printed legs named above record measurements
only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Write response codes of read-only registers, read values and response codes of
write-only registers, reserved-bit residue, the `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES`, `SMBALERT` and threshold
readbacks, `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` reads, `VAL`, the host and target enable probes and the `TIMING0`
THIGH/TLOW points below 2 are measured and printed without comparing.

'''''

[[sec-505-smc_i2c_target_addr_gate_test]]
===== 505 `smc_i2c_target_addr_gate_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_addr_gate_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP master (2 MHz) on
the I2C0 pads, one VIP per leg, acting as the bench controller; probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`,
`tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`; clock `clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL, TARGET_ID,
STATUS, INTR_STATE, FIFO_CTRL, TARGET_FIFO_STATUS (ACQLVL), TXDATA, ACQDATA (SIGNAL, ABYTE),
TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper control register; `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`;
I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the sequence. Addresses used: pair 0 = 0x23, pair 1 = 0x35,
non-matching 0x2A and 0x3C.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The I2C0 target ACKs an address only when `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` is
set and the address matches `TARGET_ID` under a non-zero mask, and records each ACKed address in the
ACQ FIFO.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `ENABLETARGET` set, both address bytes of pair 0 (write 0x46, read 0x47) and of pair 1 (0x6A,
  0x6B) are ACKed, and the ACQ FIFO holds the START entry with the address byte, the data entry and
  the STOP entry; a read returns the `TXDATA` byte (`i2c.rdl` TARGET_ID, CTRL, ACQDATA).
* Addresses that match neither pair are NACKed and leave the ACQ FIFO empty.
* A mask of 0 disables its address and a rewritten `ADDRESS0` moves the match (`i2c.rdl` TARGET_ID).
* `CTRL` = 0 and `CTRL` = `ENABLEHOST` alone NACK the target address with `I2C_CTRL.I2C_EN` set; the
  hybrid role (`ENABLEHOST` | `ENABLETARGET`) ACKs it (`i2c.rdl` CTRL, `i2c_ctrl.rdl`).
* A repeated START to pair 1 is ACKed and recorded as a restart entry; one to a non-match is NACKed.
* Measured and printed only: the ACQ entries after an address-only write, `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP`,
  and the bus, `STATUS.TARGETIDLE` and ACQ state when `ENABLETARGET` is cleared and set again
  mid-transfer, because the specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, arm the I2C0 pads, write the I2C0 wrapper register in target
  mode, wait for the pads to release, program TIMING0-4, reset the ACQ and TX FIFOs, write
  `TARGET_ID` (ADDRESS0 0x23, ADDRESS1 0x35, masks 0x7F), write `CTRL` = `ENABLETARGET` | ACQ
  start/stop enable; require `STATUS.ACQEMPTY` and `TXEMPTY` set, both pads 1 and `sda_dut_low` 0.
. Write 0x11 to 0x23, then read it with `TXDATA` 0x6E; require ACK bits 0 for 0x46, 0x11 and 0x47,
  the write entries (START, 0x46), (none, 0x11), STOP, the read byte 0x6E and a first read entry
  (START, 0x47).
. Repeat for pair 1 (0x35, data 0x12, `TXDATA` 0x6F) and require pair 0 to still ACK 0x46.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target, addressed by the bench controller. Kind: transfers to the
  non-matching addresses 0x2A and 0x3C. Expected response: the NACK and five `ACQLVL` reads of 0
  with `ACQEMPTY` set.
. Write `TARGET_ID` with MASK0 = 0, then MASK1 = 0, then both 0; require the address with a zero
  mask NACKed and the other ACKed, and both NACKed in the last case.
. Restore the masks, require 0x23 ACKed with data 0x15; rewrite `ADDRESS0` to 0x3C; require 0x23
  NACKed with `ACQLVL` 0 on five reads and 0x3C ACKed with entries (START, 0x78), a data entry and
  STOP.
. Restore `TARGET_ID`; write `CTRL` = 0 and then `ENABLEHOST` only; each time require 0x46 NACKed
  and `ACQLVL` 0 on five reads with `ACQEMPTY` set.
. Write `CTRL` = `ENABLEHOST` | `ENABLETARGET`; require 0x46 and 0x13 ACKed and entries (START,
  0x46), (none, 0x13), STOP.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target with the target role set, addressed by the bench
  controller. Kind: an address-only write to 0x46, and a repeated START to the non-matching address
  0x54 inside START, 0x46, 0x23, repeated START, 0x54, STOP. Expected response: the address-only
  write's first entry is (START, 0x46), with all entries and `INTR_STATE` printed; the last byte
  0x54 is NACKed and no restart entry for 0x54 appears. Between them send START, 0x46, 0x21,
  repeated START, 0x6A, 0x22, STOP and require ACKs and entries (START, 0x46), (none, 0x21),
  (restart, 0x6A), (none, 0x22) ending in STOP.
. Error injection. Point: `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` of I2C0, cleared and set again in the middle of an
  address byte, in the middle of a data byte, and after an address while the role is off. Kind: the
  target role dropped mid-transfer. Expected response: after the bus is released the bus levels,
  `TARGETIDLE`, `ACQLVL` and entries are printed; after a FIFO reset and restored `CTRL`, START,
  0x46, 0x14, STOP is ACKed with entries (START, 0x46), (none, 0x14), STOP and `TARGETIDLE` within
  its poll bound.
. Print the list of bounded waits (including the VIP clock-stretch bounds) and check the ordered
  fence S1 to S10.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-PAIR0` |With `ENABLETARGET` set 0x46 and 0x47 are ACKed, the write pops (START,
0x46), (none, 0x11) and a STOP entry, the read returns 0x6E, and the first read entry is (START,
0x47).
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-PAIR1` |For pair 1 = 0x35 mask 0x7F 0x6A and 0x6B are ACKed, the write pops
(START, 0x6A), (none, 0x12), STOP, the read returns 0x6F with first entry (START, 0x6B), and pair 0
still ACKs 0x46 in the same run.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-NONMATCH` |Addresses 0x2A and 0x3C get a NACK and every `ACQLVL` read is 0 with
`ACQEMPTY` set, while the same bench ACKed 0x23 in the pair 0 leg.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-MASKZERO` |With MASK0 = 0 0x23 is NACKed and 0x35 ACKed; with MASK1 = 0 0x35 is
NACKed and 0x23 ACKed; with both 0 both are NACKed and `ACQLVL` stays 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-REWRITE` |Before the rewrite 0x23 is ACKed; after `ADDRESS0` is 0x3C, 0x23 is
NACKed with `ACQLVL` 0 and 0x3C is ACKed with entries (START, 0x78), a data entry and STOP.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-GATE` |With `I2C_EN` set, `CTRL` = 0 and `CTRL` = `ENABLEHOST` NACK 0x46 with
`ACQLVL` 0, and `ENABLEHOST` | `ENABLETARGET` ACKs 0x46 and 0x13 and pops (START, 0x46), (none,
0x13), STOP; the pair 0 ACK is the positive control.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ADDR-ONLY` |The address-only write 0x46 is ACKed and its first entry is (START, 0x46);
the remaining entries and `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-RESTART-ADDRESS` |The repeated START to pair 1 gets ACKs and the entries begin (START,
0x46), (none, 0x21), (restart, 0x6A), (none, 0x22) and end with STOP; the repeated START to 0x2A
gets a NACK and no (restart, 0x54) entry.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-MIDTRANSFER-LOG` |The bus levels after release, `STATUS.TARGETIDLE`, `ACQLVL` and
the entries after `ENABLETARGET` is cleared and set mid-address, mid-data and after an address with
the role off are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-MIDTRANSFER-RECOVER` |After the FIFO reset and the restored `CTRL` the write
START, 0x46, 0x14, STOP is ACKed, pops (START, 0x46), (none, 0x14), STOP, and `TARGETIDLE` reads 1
within the poll bound.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S10 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
recorded after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-PAIR0`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-PAIR1`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-NONMATCH`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-MASKZERO`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-GATE-REWRITE`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-GATE`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-RESTART-ADDRESS`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-MIDTRANSFER-RECOVER`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-I2C-TGT-ADDR-ONLY` compares only the ACK and the first entry, and
`CHK-I2C-TGT-ROLE-MIDTRANSFER-LOG` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The ACQ entries after the first entry of an address-only write and
`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP`, and the bus levels, `STATUS.TARGETIDLE`, `ACQLVL` and entries when
`ENABLETARGET` is cleared and set again mid-transfer, are measured and printed without comparing,
because the specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-506-smc_i2c_target_bus_symbol_test]]
===== 506 `smc_i2c_target_bus_symbol_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_bus_symbol_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP master (2 MHz) on
the I2C0 pads acting as the bench controller, with its SCL and SDA pull controls used to time bare
START and STOP symbols; probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c0_scl_i`, `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`,
`tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`, `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]` (instance 0 on bit 0), `tb_cpu_interrupts[279]`; clock
`clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL, TARGET_ID, STATUS, FIFO_CTRL, TARGET_FIFO_STATUS (ACQLVL, TXLVL),
TXDATA, ACQDATA (SIGNAL, ABYTE), TARGET_EVENTS (START_DETECT bit 3, STOP_DETECT bit 4), INTR_STATE,
INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST (UNEXP_STOP), TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the sequence.
Target address 0x23 (write byte 0x46, read byte 0x47); non-matching address 0x2A.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The I2C0 target records a repeated START, recovers cleanly after
every early-ended transaction, delivers `UNEXP_STOP` through `INTR_TEST` and `INTR_ENABLE`, and
keeps the START and STOP detect flags sticky until written 1.

*Test Coverage*:

* A write, repeated START, read transaction pops the START, data and restart entries with the
  address byte and the read returns the `TXDATA` byte (`i2c.rdl` ACQDATA.SIGNAL, ABYTE, TXDATA).
* A read followed by a controller NACK and STOP returns the first `TXDATA` byte before the NACK.
* After each of five early-ended cases (STOP in the address byte, STOP in a data byte, repeated
  START in a data byte, read NACK, STOP right after the address ACK) a clean write is ACKed and pops
  exactly START 0x46, 0x31, 0x32 and a STOP entry, so the target is usable again (`i2c.rdl`
  FIFO_CTRL.ACQRST, STATUS.TARGETIDLE).
* `INTR_TEST` sets `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP`; `INTR_ENABLE.UNEXP_STOP` gates it onto `tb_i2c_irq[0]`
  and `tb_cpu_interrupts[279]`; a written 1 clears it; instances 1 and 2 stay quiet (`i2c.rdl`,
  `interrupts.adoc`).
* With `ENABLETARGET` set and the ACQ start/stop entries off, `TARGET_EVENTS.START_DETECT` and
  `STOP_DETECT` set on a transaction, stay set over further transactions until written 1,
  `START_DETECT` sets again on a repeated START, and neither sets with `ENABLETARGET` clear
  (`i2c.rdl` TARGET_EVENTS).
* Measured and printed only: the ACQ entry list, TARGETIDLE and TXLVL after each early end, the bus
  positions that raise `UNEXP_STOP`, and the flag state when a clear is issued at counted offsets
  around a bench-timed STOP, because the specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, arm the I2C0 pads, write the I2C0 wrapper register in target
  mode, wait for the pads to release, program TIMING0-4, reset the ACQ and TX FIFOs, write
  `TARGET_ID` (0x23, mask 0x7F), set `CTRL` = `ENABLETARGET` | ACQ start/stop enable, clear
  `UNEXP_STOP` and the detect flags; require them clear, `ACQEMPTY` and `TXEMPTY` set, pads 1 and
  `sda_dut_low` 0.
. Load `TXDATA` 0x5C; run START, 0x46, 0x21, repeated START, 0x47, read one byte with NACK, STOP
  while draining the ACQ FIFO; require ACKs and 0x5C and the first three entries (START, 0x46),
  (none, 0x21), (restart, 0x47).
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target, driven by the bench controller's SCL and SDA pull
  controls. Kind: case A, a STOP driven in the address byte. Expected response: `TARGETIDLE` is
  reached, the entries are popped and the recovery write is ACKed with exactly START 0x46, 0x31,
  0x32 and a STOP entry. Clear `UNEXP_STOP` and reset the FIFOs first.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target, driven by the bench controller. Kind: case B, a STOP in a
  data byte, and case C, a repeated START in a data byte followed by the address and STOP. Expected
  response: the same recovery as case A after each.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target with `TXDATA` 0x61, 0x62, 0x63 loaded. Kind: case D, a
  read ended by a controller NACK on the first byte and STOP. Expected response: the read address
  ACKed and the byte 0x61; then the same recovery.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target, driven by the bench controller. Kind: case E, START,
  address ACK and STOP. Expected response: the same recovery; the entries, TARGETIDLE and TXLVL of
  cases A to E and the recovery results are printed.
. Clear the enable, clear `UNEXP_STOP`, write `INTR_TEST.UNEXP_STOP`; require `INTR_STATE` 1 and
  both lines 0; set `INTR_ENABLE.UNEXP_STOP` and poll both lines to 1; write 1 to `INTR_STATE` and
  require 0 and both lines polled to 0; require `tb_i2c_irq[1]` and `[2]` 0 at every step; repeat
  the case A STOP with the enable clear and print `UNEXP_STOP` and the lines; restore.
. With `CTRL` = `ENABLETARGET` only, clear the flags, run one write to 0x23 and require both detect
  flags set; run two more writes and require both still set; write 1 to both and require 0; set
  `CTRL` 0, run a write and require both 0.
. With `ENABLETARGET` set, clear the flags, start a write to 0x23 and leave it open, require
  `START_DETECT`, write 1 to it and require 0, send a second write inside the open transaction
  (repeated START) and require `START_DETECT` set again.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 target with `CTRL` restored, driven by the bench controller.
  Kind: START and the non-matching address 0x2A followed by STOP, then a written 1 to `STOP_DETECT`
  and to `UNEXP_STOP` issued at 0 cycles and at 2, 4, 8, 16 cycles before and after a bench-timed
  STOP. Expected response: `TARGETIDLE` is reached each time within its bound; the flags are printed
  after each case.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence S1 to S10.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-REPSTART-ENTRIES` |The write, repeated START, read transaction gets ACKs on both
address bytes and the data byte, the read returns 0x5C, and the first three entries are (START,
0x46), (none, 0x21), (restart, 0x47).
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-READ-NACK` |The read address is ACKed and the first byte read is 0x61 before
the controller NACKs and sends STOP.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-LOG` |For cases A to E the ordered ACQ entry list, `STATUS.TARGETIDLE` and
`TXLVL` after the early end are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-RECOVER` |After each of cases A to E, once `ACQRST` is written and
`TARGETIDLE` reads 1, the recovery write is ACKed and pops exactly (START, 0x46), (none, 0x31),
(none, 0x32) and a STOP entry.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-UNEXP-STOP-LOG` |`INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` after each early STOP of cases A to E, after
each recovery write and after a second case A STOP following a written 1 is measured and printed
without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-UNEXP-STOP-REG` |`INTR_TEST` sets `UNEXP_STOP`; with the enable clear `tb_i2c_irq[0]`
and `tb_cpu_interrupts[279]` read 0 and with it set they read 1 within the poll bound; a written 1
clears the bit and both lines fall within the poll bound; `tb_i2c_irq[1]` and `[2]` stay 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-DETECT-FLAGS` |With `ENABLETARGET` set both detect flags read 1 after one write, still
1 after two more, 0 after a written 1, `START_DETECT` reads 1 again after a repeated START, and both
read 0 with `ENABLETARGET` clear.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-DETECT-RACE-LOG` |The detect flags and `UNEXP_STOP` after a no-match START and after a
written 1 at counted offsets around a bench-timed STOP are measured and printed without comparing;
each case must reach `TARGETIDLE` within its bound.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S10 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
recorded after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-TGT-REPSTART-ENTRIES`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-READ-NACK`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-RECOVER`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-UNEXP-STOP-REG`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-DETECT-FLAGS`,
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-I2C-TGT-ABANDON-LOG`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-UNEXP-STOP-LOG` and `CHK-I2C-TGT-DETECT-RACE-LOG` record
measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The ordered ACQ entry list, `STATUS.TARGETIDLE` and `TXLVL` after each early-ended
case, `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` after each early STOP, recovery write and second case A STOP, and the
detect flags and `UNEXP_STOP` after a no-match START and after a written 1 at counted offsets around
a bench-timed STOP are measured and printed without comparing, because the specification does not
state the values.

'''''

[[sec-507-smc_i2c_target_event_flags_test]]
===== 507 `smc_i2c_target_event_flags_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_event_flags_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP master (2 MHz) on
the I2C0 pads sending START, address 0x2C, one data byte 0x4D and STOP; clock `clk_smc_i`; I2C0
registers CTRL (`ENABLETARGET`), TARGET_ID, TARGET_EVENTS (START_DETECT, STOP_DETECT), INTR_STATE
(`TX_STRETCH`), FIFO_CTRL (`ACQRST`), OVRD, TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 pad routing readiness.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `TARGET_EVENTS.START_DETECT` and `STOP_DETECT` stay clear while
`CTRL.ENABLETARGET` is clear, set on a transfer once it is set, and each clears only on its own
written 1.

*Test Coverage*:

* The detect flags are set by hardware only while `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` is 1: a transfer to 0x2C with
  the target disabled is NACKed and leaves both flags 0, while the same transfer with it enabled
  sets both (`i2c.rdl` TARGET_EVENTS, CTRL.ENABLETARGET).
* The flags are sticky and write-one-to-clear: repeated reads with unrelated reads between keep both
  set, a written 1 to `START_DETECT` clears only it, then `STOP_DETECT` clears on its own written 1
  (`i2c.rdl` TARGET_EVENTS).
* Measured and printed only: `TARGET_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` after `CTRL` is cleared
  with the flags set, immediately, 256 cycles later and after the written ones, because the specification
  does not state which disable keeps the record.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, set `CTRL` 0, write the I2C0 wrapper register in target mode,
  wait for the I2C0 pad routing, set OVRD off, program TIMING0-4, reset the FIFOs, write `TARGET_ID`
  (0x2C, mask 0x7F), write 1 to both detect flags and require them clear; create the bench master.
. With `ENABLETARGET` clear send START, 0x2C, 0x4D, STOP and require the write NACKed; wait for the
  bus to release; read `TARGET_EVENTS`, make 8 unrelated reads, read it again and require both flags
  0 both times.
. Set `CTRL.ENABLETARGET`, repeat the transfer, wait for the bus to release and poll `TARGET_EVENTS`
  (up to 40 reads) until both flags read 1.
. Read `TARGET_EVENTS` twice around 8 unrelated reads and require both flags set; write 1 to
  `START_DETECT` and require it 0 with `STOP_DETECT` still 1; write 1 to `STOP_DETECT` and require
  both 0.
. Repeat the transfer and wait for both flags; set `CTRL` 0; read `TARGET_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE`,
  wait 256 `clk_smc_i` cycles, read them again, write 1 to both flags, read `TARGET_EVENTS`, write
  `ACQRST`; print the values.
. Check the ordered fence S1 to S5.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-DISABLED-NOSET` |With `ENABLETARGET` clear and a START, address and STOP on the
bus `START_DETECT` and `STOP_DETECT` read 0 on both reads, the write having been NACKed.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-SET` |After one START, address 0x2C, data 0x4D and STOP with `ENABLETARGET` set
both `START_DETECT` and `STOP_DETECT` read 1 within the 40 read poll bound.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-STICKY-W1C` |Two reads around 8 unrelated reads show both flags set; a written 1
to `START_DETECT` leaves it 0 and `STOP_DETECT` 1; a written 1 to `STOP_DETECT` leaves both 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-DISABLE-RETAIN-OBS` |`TARGET_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` after
`ENABLETARGET` is cleared, read immediately, 256 cycles later and after the written ones, are
measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S5 in order with increasing time stamps and the four checker
lines were printed in step order.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-DISABLED-NOSET`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-SET`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-STICKY-W1C` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every sequence assert
holds; `CHK-I2C-TGT-FLAG-DISABLE-RETAIN-OBS` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: `TARGET_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` after `CTRL` is cleared with the flags
set, read immediately, 256 cycles later and after the written ones, are measured and printed without
comparing, because the specification does not state which disable keeps the record.

'''''

[[sec-508-smc_i2c_target_instance_pair_test]]
===== 508 `smc_i2c_target_instance_pair_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_instance_pair_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor, SLVERR expected under the gate); the
three I2C instances on one shared open-drain bus (plusarg `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`); I2C protocol VIP
master (2 MHz, SCL wait bound 2 ms) as the bench controller; an I2C bus monitor and the I2C wire
monitor on the bus; probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`, `tb_i2c_cg_en`, `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]`,
`tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]`; clock `clk_smc_i`; per instance registers CTRL, TARGET_ID, STATUS,
FIFO_CTRL, ACQDATA, TXDATA, FDATA, RDATA, CONTROLLER_EVENTS, TARGET_EVENTS, INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE,
INTR_TEST, HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT, HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL, TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL, TIMING0-4, OVRD, the
`I2C_CTRL` wrapper registers; `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en` (bit 11); GPIO/LSIO pad
routing of the three instances armed by the sequence.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Instance pairs on the shared bus keep their interrupts,
addresses and ACQ FIFOs separate, every controller-target pairing transfers data, the I2C clock gate
answers SLVERR, and the NACK handler enable decides whether an unhandled NACK ends with a STOP.

*Test Coverage*:

* `INTR_TEST.TX_STRETCH` with its enable set raises `tb_i2c_irq` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` as
  exactly `1 << i` for instance i and both fall when it is released (`i2c.rdl`, `interrupts.adoc`
  I2C interrupts 0-2).
* With targets at 0x23, 0x35 and 0x40, a write reaches only the owning instance's ACQ FIFO and an
  address without an enabled owner is NACKed; enabling instance 2 does not change the other results.
* For each of the six ordered controller-target pairs the target pops START, data, data and restart
  entries and the controller reads the two `TXDATA` bytes through `RDATA` (`i2c.rdl` ACQDATA,
  TXDATA, RDATA, FDATA).
* While `i2c_cg_en` is set every window read answers SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E and every write answers
  SLVERR; after it is cleared the window answers OKAY (`clk_rst.adoc`, `memmap.adoc`); a transaction
  left open by the gate leaves the target usable after reprogramming.
* With `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT.EN` set a NACKed address leaves `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and
  `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` set and a STOP on the bus within the window; with it clear no STOP and no
  timeout flag appear (`i2c.rdl`).
* Measured and printed only: two targets on the same address, two simultaneous controllers, register
  the bus behaviour across the gate, and the NACK handler against a software STOP
  placed around the expiry, because the specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; ungate the I2C peripheral clock, arm the pads of instances 0-2,
  disable `CTRL`, enable the wrapper in target mode, program TIMING0-4, interrupt enables 0, OVRD 0
  and reset the FIFOs on each instance, wait for the bus to release and require `ACQEMPTY`; create
  the bus and wire monitors.
. For each instance i: enable `TX_STRETCH`, write `INTR_TEST.TX_STRETCH`; poll `tb_i2c_irq` and
  `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` to `1 << i`, require `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH`, hold 200 cycles and
  require the lines unchanged; write `INTR_TEST` 0, poll both to 0, clear the enable.
. Make instance 0 a target at 0x23 and instance 1 at 0x35 (instance 2 with `ENABLETARGET` clear);
  write 0x77 to 0x23, 0x35, 0x40; require ACKs and entries only in the owner and a NACK with empty
  FIFOs for 0x40; enable instance 2 at 0x40, repeat and require 0x40 ACKed with entries only in
  instance 2 and the 0x23 and 0x35 results unchanged.
. Error injection. Point: instances 0 and 1 as targets on the shared bus. Kind: two targets at the
  same address 0x23, written one byte and read one byte with `TXDATA` 0x91 and 0x92. Expected
  response: the leg completes within its bound; the ACK bits, read byte, entries and `TARGET_EVENTS`
  of both are printed.
. Error injection. Point: instances 0 and 1 as controllers on the shared bus with the
  multi-controller monitor and a host timeout, against instance 2 as a target at 0x40. Kind: two
  simultaneous controllers each queuing a write to 0x40. Expected response: both become idle or
  report NACK or arbitration loss within the bound; the events, instance 2 entries and STOP count
  are printed.
. For each ordered pair (c, t) with c different from t: make t a target at 0x50+t with `TXDATA`
  0x71, 0x72 and c a controller; queue START write, 0x61, 0x62, START read, a 2 byte read with STOP;
  drain t's ACQ FIFO while c goes idle; require entries (START, W), (none, 0x61), (none, 0x62),
  (restart, R), `RDATA` 0x71, 0x72, and no `NACK`.
. Error injection. Point: `CTRL` of the three instances and the `I2C_CTRL[0]` wrapper register with
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en` set. Kind: reads and writes of a clock-gated window. Expected
  response: every read completes with SLVERR and 0xBADCAB1E and every write with SLVERR. First
  program instance 0 as a target and `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL`, read the programmed words, set
  `i2c_cg_en` and poll `tb_i2c_cg_en` to 1.
. Clear `i2c_cg_en`, poll `tb_i2c_cg_en` to 0, read `TARGET_ID`, `CTRL`, `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL`,
  require none to be the error signature and each to equal its programmed word, write 0x41 to 0x23 and print the ACKs and entries.
. Error injection. Point: `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`, set while a write to 0x23 is parked after
  the address ACK. Kind: the clock gate applied mid-transaction. Expected response: the pads are
  printed, the bus released and the pads sampled for 64 x 200 cycles; after the gate is cleared and
  instance 0 disabled and reprogrammed, a write of 0x44 to 0x23 from a new master is ACKed with
  entries (START, 0x46), (none, 0x44), STOP.
. Error injection. Point: instance 1 as controller on the shared bus, with instance 0 a target at
  0x23. Kind: a write to the absent address 0x2A, first with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` EN | 4000
  and then with EN clear over the full window. Expected response: with EN set `NACK`,
  `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` and a bus STOP within 8 x 4000 peripheral cycles, both flags reading 0
  after the clear; with EN clear `NACK` set, `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` clear and no STOP.
. Error injection. Point: `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and the bus, with VAL 20000. Kind: the NACK
  cleared before the expiry, then a sweep of a software STOP sent from -8 to +8 cycles around the
  expiry. Expected response: each case completes within its poll bound; the STOP counts, events and
  final STATUS of each are printed.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence S1 to S11.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-IRQ` |For each instance i with `TX_STRETCH` enabled, `INTR_TEST` makes
`tb_i2c_irq` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[281:279]` read exactly `1 << i`, unchanged over 200 cycles, and
releasing the test bit makes both read 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` |A write to 0x23 is ACKed with entries only in instance 0, to 0x35
only in instance 1, to 0x40 NACKed with every ACQ FIFO empty; after instance 2 is enabled 0x40 is
ACKed with entries only in instance 2 and the 0x23 and 0x35 results are unchanged.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-CONTENTION-LOG` |For two targets on one address the ACK bits, read byte and
ACQ entries of both, and for two simultaneous controllers the events, instance 2 entries and STOP
count, are measured and printed without comparing; each leg must complete within its bound.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-LOOP-PAIRS` |For each of the six ordered pairs the target pops (START, write address),
(none, 0x61), (none, 0x62), (restart, read address) first, the controller `RDATA` returns 0x71 then
0x72, `NACK` stays clear and the controller returns to HOSTIDLE with FMTEMPTY.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-GATED` |With `i2c_cg_en` set every read of the four I2C windows completes with
SLVERR and 0xBADCAB1E and every write completes with SLVERR.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-UNGATE` |After the clear the reads of `TARGET_ID`, `CTRL` and `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL`
complete OKAY, are not the error signature and equal the programmed words; the ACK bits and
entries of the following write are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-MIDXFER` |The bus levels while the gate is set mid-transaction and after release
are measured and printed without comparing; after ungating and reprogramming the write START, 0x46,
0x44, STOP is ACKed and pops (START, 0x46), (none, 0x44), STOP.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACKH-STOP` |With the enable set the NACKed controller reports `NACK`, a STOP appears
within the window, `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` reads 1 and clears with a written 1; with the enable
clear no STOP appears over the same window and `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` reads 0; the STOP delay is
printed.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACKH-LOG` |The STOP count and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` after the NACK is cleared before
expiry and after a software STOP at counted offsets around the expiry are measured and printed
without comparing; each case must complete within its poll bound.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S11 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
printed after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state, except the listed observation windows; the line lists each
bound.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-IRQ`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-ISOLATION`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-LOOP-PAIRS`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-GATED`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-NACKH-STOP`, `CHK-NONVAC` and
`CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-UNGATE` (its OKAY reads and retained words) hold after their compares, the recovery write of
`CHK-I2C-TGT-CG-MIDXFER` matches, and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-I2C-TGT-INSTANCE-CONTENTION-LOG`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-NACKH-LOG` and the printed legs of the gate
checkers record measurements only; `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the bounded waits. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Two targets on one address, two simultaneous controllers, the bus levels while the
gate is set mid-transaction and after release, the ACK bits and entries of the write after ungating,
the STOP delay of the NACK handler, and the STOP count and events after a NACK cleared before expiry
or a software STOP at counted offsets around the expiry are measured and printed without comparing,
because the specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-509-smc_i2c_target_tx_read_test]]
===== 509 `smc_i2c_target_tx_read_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_tx_read_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP master (2 MHz) on
the I2C0 pads as the bench controller, one VIP per read; an SCL hold monitor on `tb_i2c0_scl` and
`tb_i2c0_scl_ext_low` that counts `clk_smc_i` cycles in which SCL is low while the bench has
released it (a run of n held samples counts n - 1); probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`,
`tb_i2c0_scl_i`, `tb_i2c0_scl_dut_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_dut_low`, `tb_i2c_irq[0]`; clock `clk_smc_i`;
I2C0 registers CTRL (`ENABLETARGET`, `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN`), TARGET_ID, TXDATA, STATUS (`TXEMPTY`,
`ACQEMPTY`), TARGET_FIFO_STATUS (`TXLVL`), TARGET_EVENTS (`TX_PENDING`), INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE
(`TX_STRETCH`), FIFO_CTRL (`TXRST`, `ACQRST`), TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper register;
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 pad routing armed by the sequence; the
`RANDOM_SEED` environment value (default 1) picks the payload length and bytes.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the length (2 to 12) and the byte values of the target
transmit payload.

*Objective*: The I2C0 target returns the `TXDATA` bytes in order, holds SCL on an
empty TX FIFO, and with `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` set holds every read until software clears
`TX_PENDING`.

*Test Coverage*:

* Bytes written to `TXDATA` are returned in order on reads of target addresses 0x23 and 0x35,
  including bytes written while the read is in progress (`i2c.rdl` TXDATA, TARGET_ID).
* After a two byte read of six loaded bytes the TX FIFO is not empty (`STATUS.TXEMPTY` 0, `TXLVL` 1
  to 4; the exact residue is printed), and `FIFO_CTRL.TXRST` empties it (`i2c.rdl`
  TARGET_FIFO_STATUS, FIFO_CTRL).
* With `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` clear the target stretches a read only while the TX FIFO is empty and
  sets no `TARGET_EVENTS` flag (`i2c.rdl` CTRL.TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN).
* With `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` set a READ address is always held and sets `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING`
  and `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH`; the clear releases the hold and the line falls (`i2c.rdl`).
* `FIFO_CTRL.TXRST` while `TX_PENDING` is set discards the loaded byte, so the next load is the byte
  read.
* Measured and printed only: the hold after the first byte of a read that empties the FIFO, the
  outcome of `TXRST` during an empty-FIFO hold, and the `TX_PENDING` clear placed around a repeated
  READ address, because the specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Pick the seed, ungate the I2C peripheral clock, arm the I2C0 pads, write the I2C0 wrapper register
  in target mode, wait for the pads to release, program TIMING0-4, reset the ACQ and TX FIFOs, write
  `TARGET_ID` (0x23 and 0x35, masks 0x7F), set `CTRL` = `ENABLETARGET` | ACQ start/stop enable;
  require `TARGET_EVENTS` bits 2:0 0, `ACQEMPTY` and `TXEMPTY` set, pads 1 and `sda_dut_low` 0.
. Write 0xA5 to `TXDATA` and read one byte from 0x23; write a seeded payload of 2 to 12 bytes and
  read them all; write 0x3C and read one byte from 0x35; require 0xA5, the payload in order and
  0x3C.
. Load 0x10 to 0x15 and read two bytes from 0x23; require 0x10, 0x11, `TXEMPTY` 0 and `TXLVL` 1
  to 4; write `TXRST` and require `TXEMPTY` 1 and `TXLVL` 0.
. Load 0x71, 0x72, start a four byte read, poll `TXLVL` below 2 while the read is incomplete, write
  0x73 and 0x74, and require the bytes 0x71, 0x72, 0x73, 0x74 with the address ACKed.
. Start the hold monitor; read one byte with the TX FIFO empty and require at least 16 hold samples
  and the read incomplete; write 0x3C and require the byte 0x3C; write 0x3D and read once more and
  require 0x3D with fewer than 16 hold samples and `TARGET_EVENTS` bits 2:0 0.
. Load 0x41, start a two byte read, wait for the first byte, wait 64 x 200 cycles, count the hold
  samples, write 0x42 and finish the read; print the hold, the bytes and whether the read finished
  first.
. Error injection. Point: `FIFO_CTRL.TXRST` of I2C0, written once a one byte read on an empty TX
  FIFO shows the hold. Kind: a TX FIFO reset during an empty-FIFO hold, followed by `TXDATA` 0x55 to
  finish the read. Expected response: the read completes within its bound; the outcome and the bus
  levels are printed. Then write `TXRST`, write 0x56, read one byte and require 0x56.
. Set `CTRL.TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN`, enable `INTR_ENABLE.TX_STRETCH`, write 0x5D, start a read and poll
  `TX_PENDING`; require `TX_PENDING` 1, `INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` 1, `tb_i2c_irq[0]` 1, at least 16
  hold samples and the read incomplete; write 1 to `TX_PENDING`, finish the read and require 0x5D,
  `TX_PENDING` 0, `TX_STRETCH` 0 and `tb_i2c_irq[0]` 0.
. Write 0x11, start a read, poll `TX_PENDING`, write `TXRST` and require `TXEMPTY` 1 and `TXLVL` 0;
  write 0x22, write 1 to `TX_PENDING` and require the byte 0x22.
. Error injection. Point: `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING` of I2C0, cleared while a repeated READ address
  is parked inside the address byte, at the address ACK, or inside a data byte. Kind: the software
  clear placed around a parked repeated READ, for the three parked cases, each with 0x61, 0x62
  loaded and one byte read first, then the bus released. Expected response: each case completes
  within its bound; the bytes read, the flag and the completion are printed.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence S1 to S10.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-READ-ORDER` |The single byte read equals 0xA5, the payload read equals the seeded
bytes in order, the pair 1 read returns 0x3C, and a four byte read with `TXDATA` written during the
read returns 0x71, 0x72, 0x73, 0x74, with every address ACK bit 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-READ-RESIDUE` |After a two byte read of six loaded bytes the bytes are 0x10, 0x11,
`TXEMPTY` reads 0 and `TXLVL` 1 to 4 (the exact residue is printed), and after `TXRST` `TXEMPTY`
reads 1 and `TXLVL` 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-AUTO-STRETCH` |With `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` clear the read against an empty TX FIFO
shows at least 16 hold samples, is not complete before `TXDATA` is written and returns 0x3C; the
read with 0x3D loaded shows fewer than 16 hold samples, returns 0x3D, and `TARGET_EVENTS` bits 2:0
read 0.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-AUTO-MIDREAD-LOG` |The hold samples after the first byte, the bytes read and
whether the read waited for the second `TXDATA` write are measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-TXRST-STRETCH-LOG` |The completion, bytes read and final bus levels after `TXRST`
written during an empty-FIFO hold are measured and printed without comparing; the read must complete
within its bound.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-TXRST-RECOVER` |After `TXRST`, `TXDATA` 0x56 and a one byte read the byte is 0x56
with the address ACKed.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-STRETCH` |With `TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN` set a READ address leaves `TX_PENDING` 1,
`INTR_STATE.TX_STRETCH` 1 and `tb_i2c_irq[0]` 1, with at least 16 hold samples and the read
incomplete; after the written 1 both flags and the line read 0 and the byte is 0x5D.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-RESET-RELOAD` |After `TXRST` while `TX_PENDING` is set `TXEMPTY` reads 1 and
`TXLVL` 0, and after `TXDATA` 0x22 and the written 1 to `TX_PENDING` the byte read is 0x22, not
0x11.
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-RACE-LOG` |For the three parked cases `TX_PENDING` before and after the clear,
the bytes read and the completion are measured and printed without comparing; each case must
complete within its bound.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S10 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
recorded after its step.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last observed state; the line lists each bound and last state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-READ-ORDER`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-READ-RESIDUE`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-AUTO-STRETCH`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-TXRST-RECOVER`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-STRETCH`,
`CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-RESET-RELOAD`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and
every sequence assert holds; `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-AUTO-MIDREAD-LOG`, `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-TXRST-STRETCH-LOG`
and `CHK-I2C-TGT-TX-SW-RACE-LOG` record measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The exact TX FIFO residue after the two byte read, the hold after the first byte of a
read that empties the FIFO, the outcome of `TXRST` during an empty-FIFO hold, and `TX_PENDING`, the
bytes read and the completion when the clear is placed around a parked repeated READ address are
measured and printed without comparing, because the specification does not state the values.

'''''

[[sec-510-smc_i2c_window_decode_test]]
===== 510 `smc_i2c_window_decode_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_window_decode_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor, 32-bit aligned accesses, error
responses allowed on the gap accesses, full-strobe writes in step 10); probe `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]`;
clock `clk_smc_i`; the `SMC_I2C_WRAP` window with the three instance register blocks at a stride of
0x200 (STATUS, INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, SMBUS_CTRL, CTRL, FIFO configuration and status,
OVRD, TIMING0-4, TIMEOUT_CTRL, TARGET_ID and the other registers of `i2c.rdl`), the `I2C_CTRL`
wrapper registers 0-2 and the unclaimed gap between the last instance block and the `I2C_CTRL`
registers; GPIO/LSIO pad routing of the three instances armed by the sequence so `SMBUS_STATUS`
senses idle pads.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: The I2C window decodes the three instance blocks, the `I2C_CTRL`
registers and the gap at 32-bit aligned addresses, with the documented reset state and a DECERR
answer in the gap.

*Test Coverage*:

* `STATUS` of the three instances reads its non-zero reset value 0x33C, so a decoded register is
  told from an OKAY-zero hole; the other registers read their `i2c.rdl` reset literals and the
  `INTR_STATE` event bits read 0 (`i2c.rdl`, `i2c_wrap.rdl`).
* `I2C_CTRL[0..2]` read their reset value at the generated addresses (`i2c_ctrl.rdl`).
* Reads in the gap between the instance blocks and `I2C_CTRL` complete with DECERR and 0xBADCAB1E
  between OKAY reads of `STATUS[2]` and `I2C_CTRL[0]` (`i2c_wrap.rdl` gap response).
* A unique pattern written to every read-write register of instance n reads back there and nowhere
  else, and restoring returns the reset; alternating reads between blocks return the addressed
  block's pattern.
* A burst of gap reads and writes mixed with valid accesses changes no register and raises no
  interrupt.
* A full-strobe aligned write, `INTR_TEST` and `INTR_STATE` write-one-to-clear work (`memmap.adoc`).
* Measured and printed only: reserved-bit residue, the read response and value of the FIFO read
  ports, `VAL` and `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`, the `I2C_CTRL` element spacing, the gap write responses and
  the maximum access time, because the specification does not state the values.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `tb_i2c_irq` 0b000, measure the `clk_smc_i` period against the configured value, arm the
  pads of instances 0-2 and register the four gap addresses as expected DECERR addresses.
. Read `STATUS` of each instance and require 0x33C; for each instance read the listed reset
  registers and require the declared fields to equal the reset word and the `INTR_STATE` event bits
  0.
. Read every register again, compute the reserved-bit residue and read the `I2C_CTRL` reserved bits;
  print.
. For each instance read `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `RDATA`, `ACQDATA`, `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` and `VAL`,
  record response and value, then read `STATUS` and require 0x33C.
. Read `I2C_CTRL[0..2]` and require the reset value; print the element spacing.
. Error injection. Point: the first, middle and last word of the unclaimed gap between the last
  instance block and `I2C_CTRL`. Kind: a read of an unmapped gap word, each between a read of
  `STATUS[2]` (0x33C) and a read of `I2C_CTRL[0]`. Expected response: OKAY on the controls and
  DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E on the gap read.
. For each instance write a unique pattern to every read-write register, read every register and
  require the pattern under the writable mask, the unwritten registers at reset, and the other
  instances' `TARGET_ID`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `TIMING0` unchanged; restore the reset and read everything
  back.
. Write distinct `TARGET_ID` patterns and `I2C_CTRL[0]`; alternate 32 reads between instances 0 and
  1 and 32 between instance 2 and `I2C_CTRL[0]`, requiring the addressed block's pattern; record the
  maximum access time.
. Error injection. Point: the gap words, in 8 rounds of a gap read and a `STATUS` read with, on odd
  rounds, a gap write and a `TARGET_ID` write and read back. Kind: a burst of unmapped gap reads and
  writes mixed with valid accesses. Expected response: the snapshot of `STATUS`, `TARGET_ID`,
  `INTR_STATE`, `CTRL` and `I2C_CTRL` of every instance taken before the rounds is unchanged and
  `tb_i2c_irq` reads 0 on every sample.
. Write `TARGET_ID[0]` with strobe 0xF and require the read back; require `STATUS[0]` 0x33C; write
  `INTR_TEST` `RX_OVERFLOW` with strobe 0xF and require `INTR_STATE` bit 3 set; write 1 to it and
  require 0; require that no gap read deviated from DECERR with 0xBADCAB1E and check the ordered
  fence S1 to S10.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-RESET-STATUS` |`STATUS` of instances 0, 1 and 2 each reads OKAY with 0x33C, a non-zero
value that tells a decoded register from an OKAY-zero hole.
|`CHK-I2C-RESET-LITERALS` |Each listed register of each instance reads OKAY with the `i2c.rdl` reset
value in every declared field and the `INTR_STATE` event bits read 0 (reset-value-only evidence);
the status-type `INTR_STATE` bits are printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RESERVED-OBS` |The reserved-bit residue of every register read at reset and of
`I2C_CTRL[0..2]` is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-RESET-SIDE-OBS` |The response and value of the five FIFO-port and sense reads on each
instance are measured and printed without comparing; the `STATUS` re-read must be 0x33C after them.
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-RESET` |`I2C_CTRL[0..2]` at their generated addresses each read OKAY with the
`i2c_ctrl.rdl` reset value (reset-value-only evidence); the element spacing is printed.
|`CHK-I2C-GAP-READ-DECERR` |Three gap reads (first, middle, last word before `I2C_CTRL`) each
complete with DECERR (3) and 0xBADCAB1E, between OKAY reads of `STATUS[2]` and `I2C_CTRL[0]`.
|`CHK-I2C-DECODE-IDENTITY` |After a unique pattern is written to every read-write register of
instance n every register of the instance reads its own pattern under the writable mask, unwritten
registers read their reset, the other instances are unchanged, and after the restore all read their
reset, for n = 0, 1, 2.
|`CHK-I2C-DECODE-ALTERNATE` |All 64 alternating reads return the pattern of the addressed block; the
maximum access time in `clk_smc_i` cycles is measured and printed without comparing.
|`CHK-I2C-GAP-NO-SIDE-EFFECT` |After 8 gap reads and 4 gap writes mixed with valid accesses every
snapshot word equals its pre-burst value, each valid access is OKAY and `tb_i2c_irq` reads 0b000 on
every sample; the gap write responses are printed.
|`CHK-I2C-ACCESS-ALIGNED` |The full-strobe write of `TARGET_ID[0]` reads back, `STATUS[0]` reads
0x33C, the `INTR_TEST` write sets `INTR_STATE` bit 3 and the written 1 clears it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints S1 to S10 in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line
printed after its step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-RESET-STATUS`, `CHK-I2C-RESET-LITERALS`, `CHK-I2C-CTRL-RESET`,
`CHK-I2C-GAP-READ-DECERR`, `CHK-I2C-DECODE-IDENTITY`, `CHK-I2C-DECODE-ALTERNATE` (its compares),
`CHK-I2C-GAP-NO-SIDE-EFFECT`, `CHK-I2C-ACCESS-ALIGNED` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares
and every sequence assert holds; `CHK-I2C-RESERVED-OBS` and the printed legs of
`CHK-I2C-RESET-SIDE-OBS` record measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The reserved-bit residue of every register and of `I2C_CTRL[0..2]`, the status-type
`INTR_STATE` bits at reset, the response and value of the FIFO-port and sense reads
(`HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `RDATA`, `ACQDATA`, `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`, `VAL`), the `I2C_CTRL` element
spacing, the gap write responses and the maximum access time are measured and printed without
comparing, because the specification does not state the values; the reset reads are reset-value-only
evidence.

'''''

[[sec-511-smc_smbus_alert_instance_isolation_test]]
===== 511 `smc_smbus_alert_instance_isolation_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_smbus_alert_instance_isolation_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); the three SMBALERT# pads `I2C[0]`,
`I2C[1]` and `I2C[2]` `SMB_A` driven through the bench external pad drive `tb_gpio_ext_drive_en` and
`tb_gpio_ext_drive_value` (bits from the pad table); no I2C protocol VIP; per instance registers
`SMBUS_STATUS` (SMBALERT), `INTR_STATE` (SMBALERT), `SMBUS_CTRL`, `CTRL` (`ENABLEHOST`) and the
`I2C_CTRL` wrapper registers (`SMBUS_EN`, host mode);
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: With the three alert pads driven low, clearing
`SMBUS_EN` on one instance leaves `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` of the other two instances at 1.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `SMBUS_EN` set on all three instances and the alert pads low, `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` reads 1
  on every instance and falls back to 0 when the pads are released (`i2c.rdl` SMBUS_STATUS,
  `i2c_ctrl.rdl` SMBUS_EN).
* `SMBUS_EN` is one register per instance: clearing it on instance k leaves the other two instances'
  `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` at 1 on all polls, for k = 0, 1, 2 (I2C `index.adoc` OCAH modifications,
  `i2c_ctrl.rdl` register array).
* The cleared instance's own `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` reads 0, because `SMBUS_EN` low masks
  `smbalert_ni` (I2C `index.adoc`); its `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` is printed without a compare.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock; for each instance write the wrapper register (host mode with
  `SMBUS_EN`), `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and a written 1 to `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT`; release the three alert
  pads.
. For each k in 0, 1, 2: drive the three alert pads low and poll `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` of all
  three to 1 (500 polls of 10 us); clear `SMBUS_EN` on instance k only; read the other two
  instances' status 16 times each and require 1 every time; read the cleared instance's
  `SMBUS_STATUS` and `INTR_STATE`; restore the wrapper register, release the pads and poll all three
  to 0.
. Clear `SMBUS_CTRL`, the wrapper register and `CTRL` on all instances, release the pads and restore
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`.
. Print the list of bounded waits and check the ordered fence SETUP, GATE_ROUNDS, TEARDOWN.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-GATE-ALL-SEE-ALERT` |With the three alert pads low and `SMBUS_EN` set on all three,
`SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` reads 1 on instances 0, 1 and 2 within the poll bound in each round, and
reads 0 on all three within the poll bound after the pads are released.
|`CHK-GATE-OTHERS-UNMASKED` |With `SMBUS_EN` cleared on instance k only, `SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` of
the other two instances reads 1 in 16 of 16 polls and the cleared instance's own
`SMBUS_STATUS.SMBALERT` reads 0, for k = 0, 1, 2; its `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` is measured and printed
without comparing.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded poll of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
