fails with the last readings; the line lists each bound and last state.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints SETUP, GATE_ROUNDS, TEARDOWN in order with increasing time stamps.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-GATE-ALL-SEE-ALERT`, `CHK-GATE-OTHERS-UNMASKED` (its 1 reads and the 0 read of the cleared instance),
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds; the
cleared instance's `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` reading records a measurement only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The cleared instance's `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` is measured and printed without
comparing.

'''''

[[sec-512-smc_smbus_alert_irq_route_test]]
===== 512 `smc_smbus_alert_irq_route_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_smbus_alert_irq_route_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); no I2C protocol VIP and the alert
pads left idle; shared I2C bus (plusarg `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`); registers `INTR_TEST`, `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` (SMBALERT field) of I2C
instances 0-2; `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; probe `tb_i2c_irq[2:0]` (instance i
on bit i, peripheral interrupt bits 23 to 25); clock `clk_smc_i`.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `INTR_TEST.SMBALERT` latches `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` with the pad
idle, and the latched bit reaches only its own `tb_i2c_irq` bit while `INTR_ENABLE.SMBALERT` is set,
follows the enable and clears with a written 1.

*Test Coverage*:

* `INTR_TEST.SMBALERT` makes `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` read 1 on each instance with the alert pad idle
  (`i2c.rdl` INTR_TEST, INTR_STATE).
* With `INTR_ENABLE.SMBALERT` clear the pending bit does not reach `tb_i2c_irq` (`i2c.rdl`
  INTR_ENABLE).
* With the enable set on instance i only, `tb_i2c_irq` reads exactly `1 << i` and returns to 0b000
  when the enable is cleared (`interrupts.adoc` I2C interrupts 0, 1, 2).
* The output follows the enable written 1, 0, 1 with the interrupt pending, and a written 1 to
  `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` clears the state and drops the output (`i2c.rdl` woclr).
* Measured and printed only: the number of polls and `clk_smc_i` cycles from the enable write to the
  output rising, because the specification does not state the synchroniser latency.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock; for each instance write `INTR_ENABLE` 0 and a written 1 to
  `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT`; require `tb_i2c_irq` 0b000.
. For each instance write `INTR_TEST.SMBALERT`, read `INTR_STATE` (up to 500 reads) until the bit is
  1, then sample `tb_i2c_irq` 16 times 4 cycles apart and require 0b000.
. For each instance write `INTR_ENABLE.SMBALERT` 1, poll `tb_i2c_irq` to `1 << i` (up to 2000 polls
  of 4 cycles) with no other bit rising, record the polls, write the enable 0 and poll `tb_i2c_irq`
  to 0b000.
. For each instance write the enable 1, 0, 1 and poll `tb_i2c_irq` to `1 << i`, 0b000, `1 << i`
  after each write; write the enable 0 and poll to 0b000.
. For each instance write the enable 1, poll `tb_i2c_irq` to `1 << i`, write 1 to
  `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT`, require `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` 0, poll `tb_i2c_irq` to 0b000, write the
  enable 0.
. Clear every enable and state bit, restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, print the list of bounded waits
  and check the ordered fence SETUP, PENDING_MASKED, ROUTED, TOGGLED, CLEARED, TEARDOWN.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-IRQ-MASKED` |For instances 0, 1, 2 `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` reads 1 after the `INTR_TEST` write
and `tb_i2c_irq` reads 0b000 in all 16 samples while `INTR_ENABLE.SMBALERT` is 0.
|`CHK-IRQ-TEST-STATE` |With the alert pad idle a written 1 to `INTR_TEST.SMBALERT` makes
`INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` read 1 within the read bound on each instance.
|`CHK-IRQ-ROUTE` |With the interrupt pending and the enable set on instance i only `tb_i2c_irq`
reads exactly `1 << i` within the poll bound and reads 0b000 within the bound after the enable is
cleared.
|`CHK-IRQ-ENABLE-TOGGLE` |With the interrupt pending `tb_i2c_irq` follows the enable written 1, 0, 1
as `1 << i`, 0b000, `1 << i`, each within the poll bound.
|`CHK-IRQ-CLEAR` |A written 1 to `INTR_STATE.SMBALERT` with the enable set makes the bit read 0 and
`tb_i2c_irq` read 0b000 within the poll bound.
|`CHK-IRQ-LATENCY-LOG` |The polls, `clk_smc_i` cycles and picoseconds from the enable write to the
output rising are measured and printed per instance without comparing.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded poll of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last readings; the line lists each bound and last state.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints SETUP, PENDING_MASKED, ROUTED, TOGGLED, CLEARED, TEARDOWN in order
with increasing time stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-IRQ-MASKED`, `CHK-IRQ-TEST-STATE`, `CHK-IRQ-ROUTE`, `CHK-IRQ-ENABLE-TOGGLE`,
`CHK-IRQ-CLEAR`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and every sequence
assert holds; `CHK-IRQ-LATENCY-LOG` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The number of polls, `clk_smc_i` cycles and picoseconds from the enable write to the
output rising are measured and printed per instance without comparing, because the specification
does not state the synchroniser latency.

'''''

[[sec-513-smc_smbus_alert_self_clear_test]]
===== 513 `smc_smbus_alert_self_clear_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_smbus_alert_self_clear_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP master (100 kHz) on
the I2C0 pads as the bench controller and an I2C bus monitor counting START conditions; the I2C0
SMBALERT# pad probe `tb_i2c0_smbalert` (0 = asserted low); I2C0 registers `SMBUS_CTRL` (SMBALERT),
CTRL (`ENABLETARGET`), TARGET_ID, FIFO_CTRL, OVRD, TIMING0-4 and the I2C0 wrapper register in target
SMBus mode; `SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 GPIO/LSIO pad routing armed by the
sequence. Own address 0x10; non-matching address 0x55.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A transfer to a non-matching address leaves
`SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` set and the alert pad low, while a transfer to the own address 0x10 clears the
bit and releases the pad.

*Test Coverage*:

* `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` is cleared by hardware when the controller addresses this target (`i2c.rdl`
  SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT hwclr): a read of 0x55, which matches no `TARGET_ID` address, leaves the bit
  at 1 and `tb_i2c0_smbalert` at 0 and returns 0xFF, with at least one START on the bus.
* In the same run a write to 0x10 makes the bit read 0 and the pad read 1.
* Measured and printed only: the settled value of the bit and the pad when a software write of 1
  lands while a transfer to 0x10 is in flight, because the specification does not state the outcome of
  the race between the software write and the hardware clear.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C peripheral clock, set `CTRL` 0, write the I2C0 wrapper register (target, SMBus),
  wait for the I2C0 pad routing and arm the pads, set OVRD off, program TIMING0-4, reset the FIFOs,
  write `TARGET_ID` (0x10, mask 0x7F), set `CTRL.ENABLETARGET`; create the bus monitor and the
  master.
. Error injection. Point: the I2C0 SMBus target, addressed by the bench controller after
  `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` is written 1 and `tb_i2c0_smbalert` polled to 0 (500 polls of 10 us). Kind:
  a one byte read of 0x55, which matches no `TARGET_ID` address. Expected response: at least one new
  START, the byte 0xFF, `SMBALERT` still 1 and the pad still 0.
. Write the own address 0x10 with no data; poll `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` to 0, then poll
  `tb_i2c0_smbalert` to 1.
. Error injection. Point: `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT`, written 1 again while a write to 0x10 is in flight
  after its START. Kind: a software write of 1 racing the hardware clear. Expected response: after
  the transfer returns the bit and pad pair is unchanged on 8 consecutive polls within the poll
  bound; the pair is printed. First write 1 to `SMBALERT` and start the write to 0x10.
. Clear `SMBUS_CTRL`, `CTRL` and the wrapper register, restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, print the list
  of bounded waits and check the ordered fence SETUP, OTHER_ADDR, OWN_ADDR_CONTROL, RACE, TEARDOWN.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-SELFCLEAR-OTHER-ADDR` |After a read of 0x55 `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` reads 1 and
`tb_i2c0_smbalert` reads 0 with at least one START witnessed and the byte 0xFF returned; after a
write to the own address 0x10 the bit reads 0 and the pad reads 1, each within the poll bound.
|`CHK-SELFCLEAR-RACE-LOG` |The bit and pad pair that settles on 8 consecutive polls after a software
write lands during a transfer to 0x10 is measured and printed without comparing; the pair must
settle within the poll bound.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded poll of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last readings; the line lists each bound and last state.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints SETUP, OTHER_ADDR, OWN_ADDR_CONTROL, RACE, TEARDOWN in order with
increasing time stamps, each checker line printed after its step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-SELFCLEAR-OTHER-ADDR`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their
compares and every sequence assert holds; `CHK-SELFCLEAR-RACE-LOG` records a measurement only.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The settled value of `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` and the alert pad when a software write of
1 lands while a transfer to 0x10 is in flight is measured and printed without comparing, because the
specification does not state the outcome of the race between the software write and the hardware
clear.

'''''

[[sec-514-smc_smbus_pmbus_linear11_read_test]]
===== 514 `smc_smbus_pmbus_linear11_read_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_smbus_pmbus_linear11_read_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SYS_IN (SEP_IN frontdoor); I2C protocol VIP EEPROM target at
0x50 on the I2C0 pads holding the words 0xF4 0xF1 at command 0x88 and 0xD4 0xEE at command 0x8B,
with its START, STOP and ACK counters; probes `tb_i2c0_scl`, `tb_i2c0_sda`,
`tb_i2c0_smbsus_dut_low`; clock `clk_smc_i`; I2C0 registers CTRL (`ENABLEHOST`), FDATA, RDATA,
STATUS (`HOSTIDLE`, `RXEMPTY`), FIFO_CTRL, SMBUS_CTRL (`SMBSUS`), OVRD, TIMING0-4 and the I2C0
`I2C_CTRL` wrapper register (`I2C_EN`, `SMBUS_EN`, `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN`);
`SMC_BASE_CONFIG.CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i2c_cg_en`; I2C0 pad routing readiness.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The I2C0 controller reads a two-byte word with a repeated
START, delivering the bytes through `RDATA` in wire order, unchanged by `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBSUS` written
mid-transfer and by a clear `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN`.

*Test Coverage*:

* A write of the command byte, repeated START and a two byte read return the target's bytes in the
  order sent, for a positive and a negative Linear11 word, and the target counts advance by two
  STARTs, one STOP and two ACKs (`i2c.rdl` FDATA, RDATA, `memmap.adoc` endianness: bytes are
  compared as bytes).
* `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBSUS` written while the transfer is on the wire does not disturb it and drives
  `tb_i2c0_smbsus_dut_low` away from its earlier level until it is written 0 again (`i2c.rdl`
  SMBUS_CTRL).
* With `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN` clear the same read returns the same bytes and counts and releases
  SCL and SDA afterwards (`i2c_ctrl.rdl`).
* Measured and printed only: the Linear11 decode (exponent, mantissa, value) of both words, because
  the specification does not state the expected decode.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Create the EEPROM target and preload the two words; ungate the I2C peripheral clock, write the
  I2C0 wrapper register (host, SMBus), wait for the I2C0 pad routing, set OVRD off, program
  TIMING0-4, reset the FIFOs and set `CTRL.ENABLEHOST`.
. Queue START write address 0x50, command 0x88, START read address, a 2 byte read with STOP; poll
  STATUS until `HOSTIDLE` is set and `RXEMPTY` clear; read `RDATA` twice and require 0xF4 then 0xF1
  and the target counters up by 2 STARTs, 1 STOP, 2 ACKs.
. Repeat with command 0x8B and require 0xD4 then 0xEE with the same counter deltas; print the
  Linear11 decode of both words.
. Sample `tb_i2c0_smbsus_dut_low`, queue the 0x88 read, wait until the target sees its first START
  with no STOP, write 1 to `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBSUS`, poll `tb_i2c0_smbsus_dut_low` until it differs from
  the earlier sample, wait for completion and require 0xF4, 0xF1 and the counter deltas; write
  `SMBSUS` 0 and poll the probe back to the earlier level; require SCL 1.
. Write the wrapper register with `I2C_EN` and `SMBUS_EN` only, repeat the 0x88 read and require
  0xF4, 0xF1 and the counter deltas; wait for SCL and SDA to read 1.
. Clear `CTRL`, the wrapper register and restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; print the list of bounded
  waits and check the ordered fence TARGET_ARMED, WORD_READ, NEG_WORD_READ, SUS_DURING_XFER,
  FIELD_CLEARED, TEARDOWN.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PMBUS-WORD-BYTES` |`RDATA` returns 0xF4 then 0xF1 in the order the target sent them for
command 0x88, and the target counters advance by 2 STARTs, 1 STOP and 2 ACKs.
|`CHK-PMBUS-NEG-WORD-BYTES` |`RDATA` returns 0xD4 then 0xEE in wire order for command 0x8B with the
same counter deltas.
|`CHK-PMBUS-DECODE-LOG` |The Linear11 decode of both received words is measured and printed without
comparing.
|`CHK-SUS-DURING-XFER` |With `SMBSUS` written 1 while the transfer is on the wire the transfer
completes with 0xF4 then 0xF1 and the same counter deltas, `tb_i2c0_smbsus_dut_low` differs from its
earlier sample within the poll bound and returns to it after `SMBSUS` is written 0.
|`CHK-SCL-SDA-FIELD-INVARIANT` |With `I2C_CONTROLLER_MODE_EN` clear the 0x88 read returns 0xF4 then
0xF1 with the same counter deltas and SCL and SDA read 1 after the stop.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded poll of the run is satisfied within its bound, otherwise the run
fails with the last readings; the line lists each bound and last state.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence prints TARGET_ARMED, WORD_READ, NEG_WORD_READ, SUS_DURING_XFER,
FIELD_CLEARED, TEARDOWN in order with increasing time stamps, each checker line printed after its
step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-PMBUS-WORD-BYTES`, `CHK-PMBUS-NEG-WORD-BYTES`, `CHK-SUS-DURING-XFER`,
`CHK-SCL-SDA-FIELD-INVARIANT`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and `CHK-NONVAC` hold after their compares and
every sequence assert holds; `CHK-PMBUS-DECODE-LOG` records measurements only. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The Linear11 decode (exponent, mantissa, value) of both words is measured and printed
without comparing, because the specification does not state the expected decode.

'''''

[[sec-538-smc_i2c_wire_timing_test]]
===== 538 `smc_i2c_wire_timing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_wire_timing_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` (0x50) on `tb_i2c0_scl` / `tb_i2c0_sda`; a clock-sampled measurer
in the sequence that reads both pad nets on every `clk_periph_i` rising edge and keeps each edge
as a cycle count; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN writing and reading `TIMING0` to `TIMING4`,
`FDATA`, `STATUS`, `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `RDATA`, `INTR_STATE`, `CTRL`, `OVRD`, `FIFO_CTRL` and
`CONTROLLER_EVENTS` of I2C0, the I2C0 wrapper control register and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`;
`clk_periph_i` (the clock `clk_i` of the I2C core is gated from) and `clk_smc_i`; the peripheral
clock period is read from the environment configuration

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The difference in the I2C0 controller's SCL, SDA, START, STOP and bus-free timing on
the pads between two programming sets equals the difference in the `TIMING0` to `TIMING4` counts
that were changed.

*Test Coverage*:

* All ten `TIMING0` to `TIMING4` fields read back the distinct nonzero value written at their
  width, and a halfword-strobed rewrite of one field leaves its neighbour unchanged; the reset
  readback is logged only (a stuck-at-zero reset cannot be told apart on a 2-state bench).
* Set A is the Fast-mode-plus minimums of UM10204 Table 11 in `clk_i` cycles (`THD_DAT` at 1);
  set B scales `THIGH`, `TLOW`, `TSU_DAT` and `THD_DAT` by 4 and set C by 10; the SCL high, low
  and period differences between B or C and A equal the programmed differences on every clock
  pulse of a write, repeated-START read and STOP transfer.
* The SDA hold after an SCL fall of the bits the controller transmits, and the hold after the SCL
  fall of the bit it not-acknowledges, change with `THD_DAT` by the programmed difference. The SDA
  setup before the SCL rise of those bits is measured and printed next to `TSU_DAT` and
  `TLOW` minus `THD_DAT` of each set, with no expectation.
* With `TSU_STA`, `THD_STA` and `TSU_STO` each raised (set A3) the repeated-START setup and hold
  and the STOP setup change by the programmed differences; with only `T_BUF` raised (set A4) the
  bus-free time between a STOP and the next START changes by the programmed difference. The
  measured bus-free time of each set is printed next to its programmed `T_BUF`, which `i2c.rdl`
  states as the time between a STOP and START condition; a value below it is printed, not compared.
* Raising `T_R` and `T_F`, and the hold of the first START, are measured and printed with no
  expectation. Full-rate Standard-mode SCL is not run.
* With `THIGH` and `TLOW` at 2 and every other field at 1 a transfer of START, address write and
  STOP completes with one acknowledge and one STOP.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a controller with the EEPROM target on the pads, read `TIMING0` to `TIMING4`
  before any write, write every field with a distinct value at its width and read the five
  registers back, then rewrite each low and each high field with a halfword strobe and read back
  the register.
. Program set A. Queue transfer X (START, address write, one byte, repeated START, address read,
  one byte with the controller not-acknowledging, STOP) and transfer Y (START, address write,
  STOP) behind it, wait for the second STOP on the pads and `STATUS.HOSTIDLE`, and require the
  byte read and the target's START, STOP and acknowledge counts. Reduce the pad edges to the
  intervals under test.
. Program set B and repeat.
. Program set C and repeat.
. Program set A2 (`T_R` and `T_F` raised by 6) and repeat.
. Program set A3 (`TSU_STA`, `THD_STA` and `TSU_STO` raised by 8) and repeat, then program set A4
  (only `T_BUF` raised by 8) and repeat.
. Program the minimum set, clear `INTR_STATE`, run transfer Y alone and require the START, the
  acknowledge, exactly one STOP, `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` and `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE`.
. Compare the deltas against set A in order, print the checker lines, the ordered-fence line and
  the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-TIMING-FIELDS` |Each of the ten fields reads back its distinct written value and a
rewrite of one field leaves its neighbour unchanged; a differing readback fails it, and the reset
leg is printed only.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-HIGH-DELTA` |The change in measured SCL high time on every clock pulse, B minus A
and C minus A, equals the change in `THIGH` exactly in cycles; any other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-LOW-DELTA` |The change in measured SCL low time on every low phase between clock
pulses, B minus A and C minus A, equals the change in `TLOW` exactly; any other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-PERIOD-DELTA` |The change in measured SCL period, B minus A and C minus A, equals
the change in `THIGH` plus `TLOW` with `T_R` and `T_F` equal in all three sets; any other delta
fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-MEASURED-ONLY` |Measured only: the period change with `T_R` and `T_F` raised, the
first-START hold in A and A3 and the STOP-to-next-START time are printed; nothing is compared.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-DATA-SETUP-MEASURED` |Measured only: the SDA setup before the SCL rise of the
transmitted bits in sets A, B and C is printed with the programmed `TSU_DAT` and `TLOW` minus
`THD_DAT`; nothing is compared and only a missing line or edge fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-DATA-HOLD-DELTA` |The change in SDA hold after the SCL fall of each transmitted bit,
B minus A and C minus A, equals the change in `THD_DAT`; any other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-NACK-HOLD-DELTA` |With SDA high in the controller's not-acknowledge pulse, the change
in SDA hold after that pulse's SCL fall, B minus A and C minus A, equals the change in `THD_DAT`;
a low SDA or any other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-RSTART-DELTA` |The change in repeated-START setup (SCL rise to SDA fall) and hold
(SDA fall to the next SCL fall), A3 minus A, equals the change in `TSU_STA` and `THD_STA`; any
other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-STOP-SETUP-DELTA` |The change in STOP setup (SCL rise to SDA rise), A3 minus A,
equals the change in `TSU_STO`; any other delta fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-BUS-FREE-DELTA` |The change in time from the SDA rise of the STOP of X to the SDA
fall of the START of Y, A4 minus A, equals the change in `T_BUF`; any other delta fails it. The
measured bus-free time of each set is printed next to its programmed `T_BUF` (the time between a
STOP and START condition per `i2c.rdl`); a value below it is printed, not compared.
|`CHK-I2C-WIRE-MIN-SET-RUN` |With `THIGH` and `TLOW` at 2 and the other fields at 1 transfer Y
shows a START, an acknowledged address, one STOP, `HOSTIDLE` and `CMD_COMPLETE`; a missing START
or acknowledge, another STOP count or either flag clear fails it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow them in order; a missing or misordered term fails it.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The wait for the STOP edges, the `HOSTIDLE` poll, the LSIO ready poll and the
AXI access are bounded and fail on expiry with the last `STATUS`, `HOST_FIFO_STATUS` and measurer
state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-WIRE-TIMING-FIELDS`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-HIGH-DELTA`,
`CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-LOW-DELTA`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-SCL-PERIOD-DELTA`,
`CHK-I2C-WIRE-DATA-HOLD-DELTA`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-NACK-HOLD-DELTA`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-RSTART-DELTA`,
`CHK-I2C-WIRE-STOP-SETUP-DELTA`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-BUS-FREE-DELTA`, `CHK-I2C-WIRE-MIN-SET-RUN`,
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds;
`CHK-I2C-WIRE-MEASURED-ONLY` and `CHK-I2C-WIRE-DATA-SETUP-MEASURED` record measurements only.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: The reset readback of `TIMING0` to `TIMING4` is logged only, because a stuck-at-zero
reset cannot be told apart on a 2-state bench; the SDA setup before the SCL rise of the transmitted
bits is printed next to `TSU_DAT` and `TLOW` minus `THD_DAT` with no expectation; the measured
bus-free time of each set is printed next to its programmed `T_BUF` and a value below it is printed,
not compared; the period change with `T_R` and `T_F` raised, the hold of the first START and the
STOP-to-next-START time are measured and printed with no expectation; full-rate Standard-mode SCL is
not run.

'''''

[[sec-539-smc_i2c_dual_concurrent_transfer_test]]
===== 539 `smc_i2c_dual_concurrent_transfer_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I2C

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_dual_concurrent_transfer_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` (0x50) and `SmcI2cBusMonitor` on `tb_i2c0_scl` / `tb_i2c0_sda`
(`tb_i2c0_scl_ext_low`, `tb_i2c0_sda_ext_low`) and `SmcI2cEepromSlave` (0x2A) and
`SmcI2cBusMonitor` on `tb_i2c1_scl` / `tb_i2c1_sda` (`tb_i2c1_scl_ext_low`,
`tb_i2c1_sda_ext_low`), with `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` not passed and `+smc_i2c1_pads` passed, which
makes the bench drive the resolved open-drain value onto pads 41 and 42; `tb_i2c1_scl` and
`tb_i2c1_sda` are read from the padring outputs of those pads (`core2pad_en_o` and `core2pad_o`),
that is after the `I2C_CTRL[1].I2C_EN` pad-function select; a clock-sampled recorder in the
sequence that reads all four pad nets on every `clk_periph_i` rising edge and keeps each edge as a
cycle count; ocah_axi_vip (AXI) on SEP_IN writing and reading `TIMING0` to `TIMING4`, `FDATA`,
`STATUS`, `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `CTRL`, `OVRD`, `FIFO_CTRL` and
`TARGET_ID` of I2C0 and I2C1 at the generated map's instance stride, `I2C_CTRL` of each instance
and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; the GPIO `DATA_CTRL.LSIO_SELECT` of the I2C1 pads; `clk_periph_i` (the
clock `clk_i` of the I2C cores is gated from) and `clk_smc_i`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c1_pads`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Two I2C controllers, instances 0 and 1, run write transfers at the same time on
separate pad pairs, each pad pair carries only its own instance's bytes with the programmed timing
difference, and the register windows, FIFO levels, `CMD_COMPLETE` and NACK state stay per
instance.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `I2C_CTRL[1].I2C_EN` clear a write on instance 0 shows its START on the instance-0 pads,
  and a write queued on instance 1 with its host enabled gives no edge on the instance-1 padring
  outputs over a bounded window; with `I2C_EN` set the instance-1 write shows its START on the
  instance-1 pads and no further edge on the instance-0 pads. The pad level with `I2C_EN` clear is
  not compared.
* One register written in the instance-1 window reads back there while the same register of the
  instance-0 window keeps its value, and the reverse.
* Instance 0 runs a write of an address byte, a pointer byte and four data bytes and instance 1,
  programmed with `THIGH` and `TLOW` four times those of instance 0, a write of an address byte, a
  pointer byte and two data bytes; the instance-1 START falls after the instance-0 START and
  before the instance-0 STOP. Each pad pair shows START, the address byte with write, the data in
  push order, an acknowledge per byte and a STOP, and only its own bytes.
* The SCL high and low phases of the two instances differ by the programmed difference of `THIGH`
  and `TLOW` on every phase index both transfers have whose edges lie inside the overlap window,
  from the instance-1 START to the instance-0 STOP; the compared phase count is printed and must
  be nonzero. The overlap and the absolute phases are printed as measured.
* `HOST_FIFO_STATUS.FMTLVL` of an instance rises with its pushes while the other instance's
  levels stay, in both orders; both format levels return to 0 with `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` and
  `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` set. The levels are printed as measured.
* `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` of each instance is set after its STOP and a write of 1 to one
  instance leaves the other instance's bit set. Each pad pair counts one STOP.
* An address on instance 1 that no target acknowledges sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and
  `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` on instance 1 only while instance 0 completes its write; writing 1
  to the instance-1 NACK event clears both.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the I2C clock, enable I2C0 as a controller, start a target and a monitor on each pad
  pair, start the recorder, program the same five timing registers on both instances and clear
  `I2C_CTRL[1]`. Enable the instance-0 host, push a write and wait for its STOP. Require one START
  on the instance-0 pads. With `I2C_CTRL[1].I2C_EN` still clear, enable the instance-1 host, push a
  write and require no edge on the instance-1 padring outputs for 4000 `clk_periph_i` cycles. Set
  `I2C_CTRL[1].I2C_EN`, require a START on the instance-1 pads within 4000 cycles, with no LSIO
  select made; wait for the STOP, require an unchanged instance-0 edge count, then select the I2C1
  pads for LSIO for the later steps.
. Read `TARGET_ID` of both instances, write a distinct value to instance 1, read both, write a
  different value to instance 0 and read both.
. Program instance 0 with the base timing set and instance 1 with the same set and `THIGH` and
  `TLOW` multiplied by 4, and read every register back.
. With both hosts disabled and the FIFOs reset, read `HOST_FIFO_STATUS` of both instances, push
  the instance-0 write words and read both, push the instance-1 write words and read both. Enable
  the instance-0 host, then two cycles later the instance-1 host, and poll `HOST_FIFO_STATUS` of
  both until both pad pairs show a START.
. Wait, bounded, until both instances show `STATUS.HOSTIDLE`, `STATUS.FMTEMPTY`,
  `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` and one more STOP on their pad pairs. Read `STATUS`,
  `HOST_FIFO_STATUS` and `INTR_STATE` of both, write 1 to `CMD_COMPLETE` of instance 0 and read
  both, write 1 to `CMD_COMPLETE` of instance 1 and read both.
. Error injection. Point: instance 1 as controller on its own pad pair, while instance 0 runs a
  normal write. Kind: a write to an address nobody answers. Expected response: instance 0 completes
  and the instance-1 NACK event arrives; `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE` of both are read, a 1
  is written to the instance-1 NACK event, and both are read again.
. Reduce the overlapped-transfer pad edges of each instance to bytes, acknowledges and SCL phases
  and compare the phase differences of the phases inside the overlap window with the programmed
  `THIGH` and `TLOW` differences.
. Compare and print the checker lines in order, then the ordered-fence line and the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-PAD-ROUTE` |On the padring outputs of the instance pads, with `I2C_EN[1]` clear and
an instance-1 write queued and its host enabled there is no edge on the instance-1 pads over the
bounded window while the instance-0 write gives one START on the instance-0 pads; with `I2C_EN[1]`
set the instance-1 write gives one START on the instance-1 pads and no edge on the instance-0
pads. An edge on the clear pair, a START that does not follow `I2C_EN` alone within the window,
or an X fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-REG-WINDOW` |A value written in one instance window reads back there and the other
window keeps its value, in both directions, at the generated-map addresses; a changed other
window, a differing readback or an X fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-WIRE-ORDER` |Each pad pair shows START, the address byte with write, the data in
push order, an acknowledge per byte and a STOP, with only its own bytes, and the instance-1 START
lies between the instance-0 START and STOP with a nonzero overlap printed; a missing, reordered or
foreign byte, no overlap or a timeout fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-LIVENESS` |Both transfers reach `CMD_COMPLETE`, and the NACKed instance reports its
event, within the bench bound; the elapsed cycles and the bound are printed, and an instance that
does neither within the bound fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-TIMING-DIFF` |The difference in measured SCL high and low time, instance 1 minus
instance 0, equals the difference in `THIGH` and `TLOW` exactly on every common phase index whose
edges lie inside the overlap window, from the instance-1 START to the instance-0 STOP; any other
difference, a programmed difference of 0 or no phase inside the window fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-FIFO-LEVELS` |`FMTLVL` of an instance rises with its pushes while the other
instance's `FMTLVL` and both `RXLVL` stay, and both `FMTLVL` return to 0 with `FMTEMPTY` and
`HOSTIDLE` set and `FMTFULL` clear; a moved level of the idle instance, a nonzero final level or
a missing flag fails it, and the levels are printed.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-CMD-COMPLETE` |`INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` of each instance is 1 after its STOP and 0
after a write of 1 to it, and the other instance's bit survives the clear; a bit not set, still
set after the clear or cleared by the other write fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-STOP-COUNT` |The bus monitor of each pad pair counts exactly 1 STOP in the
overlapped transfers; any other count fails it.
|`CHK-I2C-DUAL-NACK-ISOLATION` |The unanswered address sets `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and
`INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` on instance 1 only, instance 0 completes with `CMD_COMPLETE` and no
event, and writing 1 to the instance-1 NACK event clears both; a flag on instance 0, a flag not
set on instance 1 or one that stays set fails it.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The steps are stamped in order with increasing simulation times and the checker
lines follow them in order; a missing or misordered term fails it.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The transfer wait, the START wait, the NACK wait, the pad release wait, the
LSIO ready poll and the AXI access are bounded and fail on expiry with the last register and
recorder state.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-DUAL-PAD-ROUTE`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-REG-WINDOW`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-WIRE-ORDER`,
`CHK-I2C-DUAL-LIVENESS`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-TIMING-DIFF`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-FIFO-LEVELS`,
`CHK-I2C-DUAL-CMD-COMPLETE`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-STOP-COUNT`, `CHK-I2C-DUAL-NACK-ISOLATION`,
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: The pad level with `I2C_CTRL[1].I2C_EN` clear is not compared; the overlap window and
the absolute SCL phases, the FIFO levels and the elapsed cycles against the liveness bound are
printed as measured.

'''''

[[sec-543-smc_i2c1_target_ack_ctrl_test]]
===== 543 `smc_i2c1_target_ack_ctrl_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c1_target_ack_ctrl_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN); I2C1 and I2C2 on one open-drain bus (`+smc_i2c_shared_bus`), one the target and the other the controller; `SmcFwI2cWireMonitor` on `tb_i2c0_scl` / `tb_i2c0_sda`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A DUT target in ACK Control Mode must ACK exactly the bytes software grants through `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES` and NACK when software writes `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK`, on instances 1 and 2.

*Test Coverage*:

* The instance-1 and instance-2 targets, driven by the other DUT instance as the controller; `smc_i2c_target_ack_ctrl_test` covers instance 0 against a bench controller.
* The count is a counter: reloads of 3, 2 and 1 at successive holds each release exactly that many bytes, counted from the ACK bits on the wire, and `ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA` names the pending byte at the hold.
* The field range on I2C1: N = 1 and N = 64 each release exactly N bytes before the next hold, and 0x1FF reads back as written. The NBYTES read-backs between bytes and the ACK count of the 0x1FF leg are logged, not compared (SF-005).
* The software NACK: the pending byte is NACKed on the wire, the controller halts with `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK`, the acquisition FIFO ends with an error entry and `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` counts the transaction once.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Disable I2C0, make I2C1 a target at 0x26 with `CTRL.ACK_CTRL_EN` and `CTRL.ACQ_START_STOP_EN` and I2C2 a controller, require `STATUS.ACK_CTRL_STRETCH` clear and read `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` twice on both instances.
. For target I2C1 (controller I2C2), then target I2C2 (controller I2C1): the controller writes 0xD0..0xD5; at the first hold write `NBYTES` = 3; at the second hold read `STATUS`, `INTR_STATE` and `ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA`.
. Read `NBYTES` after each byte the wire shows ACKed and count the ACKed bytes between consecutive holds.
. At the second hold write `NBYTES` = 2, at the third `NBYTES` = 1, wait for the STOP and drain `ACQDATA`.
. On target I2C1 for N = 1, 64 and 0x1FF: the controller writes N + 1 bytes while software feeds the format FIFO and drains `ACQDATA`; at the first hold write `NBYTES` = N and read it back; count the ACKed bytes before the next hold and log any `ACQFULL` polls.
. For each target: the controller writes 0xE0..0xE3; at the first hold write `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK`; read the wire ACK bits, poll `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `INTR_STATE`, end the transaction with `CTRL` = 0, write `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` = 0x1, drain `ACQDATA` and read `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` twice.
. Every wait is a bounded poll that fails with its last state.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NBYTES3` |After `NBYTES` = 3 bytes 0xD0..0xD2 are ACKed and the target holds with `STATUS.ACK_CTRL_STRETCH` = 1, `INTR_STATE.ACQ_STRETCH` = 1, `STATUS.ACQFULL` = 0 and `ACQ_FIFO_NEXT_DATA` = 0xD3, on both targets
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-DECREMENT` |The bytes ACKed between consecutive holds equal the reloads 3, 2, 1; the `NBYTES` read-backs between bytes are logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-005)
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-RELOAD` |Each reload releases the hold and the pending byte is ACKed; the acquired stream is START/address, 0xD0..0xD5 in order, STOP
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NBYTES-RANGE` |`NBYTES` written 0x1FF reads back 0x1FF; N = 1 and N = 64 release exactly N bytes; the 0x1FF ACK count and `ACQFULL` polls are logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-005)
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-SW-NACK` |After the NACK write 0xE0 is NACKed on the wire, the controller reads `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` = 0x1 with `CONTROLLER_HALT` = 1, then 0x0 after the written 0x1, and no data entry carries 0xE0..0xE3
|`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NACK-RECORD` |The drained acquisition stream ends with `SIGNAL` = 0x6 and `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` reads 1 then 0, on both targets
|`CHK-NONVAC` |BRINGUP < I2C_ACKCTRL_NBYTES3 < I2C_ACKCTRL_DECREMENT < I2C_ACKCTRL_RELOAD < I2C_ACKCTRL_RANGE < I2C_ACKCTRL_SW_NACK are stamped in order with increasing simulation times, each after its checker lines
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |The hold, release, STOP, transfer, drain, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and bus-release polls and the AXI access are bounded and fail on expiry with the last register and wire state
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NBYTES3`, `CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-DECREMENT`, `CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-RELOAD`,
`CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NBYTES-RANGE`, `CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-SW-NACK`, `CHK-I2C1-ACKCTRL-NACK-RECORD`,
`CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds.
Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: The `NBYTES` read-backs between bytes, the ACK count of the 0x1FF leg and the `ACQFULL` polls are logged, not compared (LINKED-ISSUE SF-005).

'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-i3c]]
==== I3C

[[sec-139-smc_i3c_to_fabric_test]]
===== 139 `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: I3C

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test`

*BFM / Model*: I3C VIP, ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `i3c_decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run the I3C CSR decode smoke through the SMC SEP_IN AXI input.

*Test Coverage*:

* I3C-window → fabric decode smoke (real OCA I3C core).
* Toggles the I3C CSR clock-gate control, restores it, proves the I3C wrapper CSR window is decoded by reading HCI_VERSION and comparing it against the reset declared in the I3C core's SystemRDL source (see below), then enables the core through `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE` and observes the I3C0 pads while it is enabled before restoring the register.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-CLOCK-GATE-RW` |Named compare in `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I3C0-HC-CONTROL-BUS-ENABLE` |Named compare in `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-I3C0-HCI-VERSION` |Named compare in `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I3C-CLOCK-GATE-RW`, `CHK-I3C0-HC-CONTROL-BUS-ENABLE`, `CHK-I3C0-HCI-VERSION` hold after their compares. The four external pull-low steps are driven with the core enabled and their pad levels and resolvability are recorded, not claimed: no positive control exists for the DUT-drive nets in this bench, and resolvability cannot fail on the two-state simulator the `hosted` run uses. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The pad levels and resolvability of the four external pull-low steps driven with the core enabled are recorded and not claimed, because no positive control exists for the DUT-drive nets in this bench and resolvability cannot fail on the two-state simulator the `hosted` run uses.
'''''

[[sec-515-smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test]]
===== 515 `smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I3C

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` single accesses and `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` outstanding
groups with expected-error and tolerant-timeout members; 5 us and 10 us bounds) to
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`smc_base_config`, `i3c_cg_en` in bit 9, `i2c_cg_en`), the six I3C instance
windows (`I3C_CSR` base per instance, offsets 0x000, 0xFFC, 0x400, 0x800 and 0x0B4, `HCI_VERSION` at
its register offset, DAT slot 15 word 0), the first GPIO interface `DATA_CTRL` register and the
first UART log-engine control register, addresses from the generated map; no protocol VIP and no
probe is sampled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `i3c_decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Each I3C window answers SLVERR with the error pattern while
i3c_cg_en is set and decodes again once it is cleared.

*Test Coverage*:

* With `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i3c_cg_en` set, 30 reads (six windows x five offsets) answer SLVERR with
  data 0xBADCAB1E and 30 writes of 0xFFFFFFFF answer SLVERR (`clk_rst.adoc` access gates,
  `smc_base_config.rdl`); with the gate clear, DAT slot 15 word 0 of each instance holds a distinct
  pattern and reads it back with OKAY, the positive control of the error path.
* A write to DAT slot 15 word 0 while gated answers SLVERR; after the gate is cleared each slot read
  answers OKAY, and whether the slot still equals its earlier pattern is measured and printed
  because the specification does not state it.
* Other windows are unaffected (`memmap.adoc`): with `i3c_cg_en` set the GPIO interface and UART
  reads answer OKAY and not 0xBADCAB1E; with only `i2c_cg_en` set `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` answers OKAY
  with 0x00000120.
* Restore: after the first clear and after each of eight further set and clear cycles, all six
  instances answer OKAY with `HCI_VERSION` 0x00000120 (reset value from the I3C core's SystemRDL
  source), and a window read answers SLVERR after each set.
* Timing: the first I3C0 read after the clearing write answers OKAY with 0x00000120 within 5 us, and
  the I3C0 read right after the set write answers SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E within 5 us
  (`clk_rst.adoc`: the leg is redirected as soon as the `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` write completes); the 5
  us bound is a bench choice, the specification states none.
* `i3c_cg_en` written 1 twice reads 1 after each write and written 0 twice reads 0 after each, with
  the window OKAY after the last.
* In-flight accesses around the gate write: a back-to-back group of a set write, two I3C reads, a
  clear write and two I3C reads completes within 10 us with each member OKAY or SLVERR (printed); a
  read issued together with the set write is measured through a tolerant driver item and its
  outcome, including no completion, is printed; the specification gives no rule for them.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done, read and save `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` requiring `i3c_cg_en` and `i2c_cg_en`
  clear; write a distinct pattern to DAT slot 15 word 0 of each instance and read each back; stamp
  GATE_CLEAR_CONTROL.
. Error injection. Point: the five offsets of each of the six I3C instance windows with
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.i3c_cg_en` set. Kind: 30 reads and 30 writes of 0xFFFFFFFF to the clock-gated
  windows. Expected response: every read answers SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E and every write answers
  SLVERR. Set `i3c_cg_en` first; stamp GATED_SLVERR.
. Error injection. Point: DAT slot 15 word 0 of each instance while `i3c_cg_en` is set. Kind: a
  write of 0xFFFFFFFF to the gated slot. Expected response: SLVERR on each of the six writes. Then
  clear `i3c_cg_en`, read each slot requiring OKAY and print whether it equals its pattern; stamp
  GATED_WRITE_RETAINED.
. Set `i3c_cg_en`, read the GPIO and UART probe registers requiring OKAY and not 0xBADCAB1E; clear
  it; set only `i2c_cg_en` and read `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` requiring OKAY 0x00000120; restore
  `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`; stamp OTHER_WINDOWS.
. Set then clear `i3c_cg_en` and read `HCI_VERSION` of all six instances requiring OKAY 0x00000120;
  repeat set, one gated window read (SLVERR), clear and six `HCI_VERSION` reads for eight cycles;
  stamp RESTORE_CYCLES.
. Set the gate, read an I3C window (SLVERR), write the clearing word and read `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION`
  requiring OKAY 0x00000120 within 5 us; stamp FIRST_ACCESS.
. Error injection. Point: the I3C0 window, read right after the `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` set word is
  written. Kind: a read of a window that has just been clock-gated. Expected response: SLVERR with
  0xBADCAB1E within 5 us; stamp POST_WRITE_SLVERR. Then read back `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` equal to the
  set word, write the set word again and read it back, write the clear word twice reading back the
  clear word each time, read `HCI_VERSION` requiring OKAY 0x00000120; stamp IDEMPOTENT.
. Issue the six-member group (set write, `I3C0` and `I3C1` `HCI_VERSION` reads, clear write, the
  same two reads) within 10 us requiring each member OKAY or SLVERR and printing its response and
  data; write the clear word and read `HCI_VERSION` requiring OKAY 0x00000120; issue a tolerant
  `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` read together with a set write requiring the write OKAY and printing the
  read's outcome; write the clear word requiring OKAY; attempt a final tolerant `HCI_VERSION` read
  and print its outcome; stamp INFLIGHT_GROUPS.
. Print the bounded waits and require the nine fence terms and their checker lines in order with
  strictly increasing stamps; restore the saved `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` word and read it back.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-GATED-SLVERR` |With `i3c_cg_en` set all 30 window reads answer SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E and
all 30 window writes answer SLVERR, after the gate-clear DAT slot accesses answered OKAY.
|`CHK-I3C-GATED-WRITE-RETAINED` |The six DAT slot writes while gated answer SLVERR and every slot
read after the gate is cleared answers OKAY; whether each value equals its earlier pattern is
measured and printed without a compare.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-OTHER-WINDOWS` |With `i3c_cg_en` set the GPIO interface and UART reads answer OKAY
and do not return 0xBADCAB1E, and with only `i2c_cg_en` set `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` answers OKAY
0x00000120.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-RESTORE-DECODE` |After the first clear and each of the eight further cycles every one
of the six instances answers OKAY with `HCI_VERSION` 0x00000120, and a gated window read answers
SLVERR after each set.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-FIRST-ACCESS-BOUND` |The first `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` read after the clearing write
answers OKAY with 0x00000120 within 5 us.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-POST-WRITE-SLVERR` |The `I3C0` window read presented after the set write answers
SLVERR with 0xBADCAB1E within 5 us.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-IDEMPOTENT` |`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` reads the set word after each of two set writes and
the clear word after each of two clear writes, and `I3C0` `HCI_VERSION` answers OKAY 0x00000120
after the last.
|`CHK-I3C-GATE-INFLIGHT-GROUPS` |Every member of the back-to-back group completes within 10 us with
OKAY or SLVERR (responses printed, not compared further), `HCI_VERSION` answers OKAY 0x00000120
after the clear, and the set write and the clearing write complete OKAY; the outcome of the
in-flight read and of the final tolerant read, including no completion, is measured and printed
without a compare.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The nine fence terms occur in the listed order, each followed by its checker line
where it has one, with strictly increasing stamps.
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Records the bounded waits (5 us first-access and post-write reads, 10 us group
members, the default SEP_IN bound for other accesses) and that expiry raises an assertion except for
the two tolerant group reads, whose expiry is printed; the line is a record, not a compare.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I3C-GATED-SLVERR`, `CHK-I3C-GATE-OTHER-WINDOWS`,
`CHK-I3C-GATE-RESTORE-DECODE`, `CHK-I3C-GATE-FIRST-ACCESS-BOUND`, `CHK-I3C-GATE-POST-WRITE-SLVERR`
and `CHK-I3C-GATE-IDEMPOTENT` hold after their compares; `CHK-I3C-GATED-WRITE-RETAINED` holds for
the SLVERR writes and OKAY reads and prints the slot values without claiming retention;
`CHK-I3C-GATE-INFLIGHT-GROUPS` holds for the completion and response-class compares and prints the
in-flight outcomes without claiming them; `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` are printed at the
end. Enrolled in: `all`; also listed in `fabric.toml`
(tags `ci`, `fabric`).

*Scope limit*: Whether each DAT slot still equals its earlier pattern after the gate is cleared is
measured and printed without a compare, because the specification does not state it. The responses
of the back-to-back group members are printed and not compared further, and the outcome of the read
issued together with the set write and of the final tolerant read, including no completion, is
printed without a compare, because the specification gives no rule for in-flight accesses around the
gate write. The 5 us and 10 us bounds are bench choices; the specification states none.
`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` is a record of the bounded waits, not a compare.
'''''

[[sec-516-smc_i3c_csr_sweep_core_test]]
===== 516 `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_core_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I3C

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_core_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` 4-byte reads and writes, OKAY required) to the six I3C
instance CSR windows (`I3C_CSR` base per instance from the generated map, instance count from the
generated `NUM` symbol) at the register offsets of the generated I3C wrapper register map; the
register table is parsed at run time from the I3C core's SystemRDL sources `base_registers.rdl`,
`controller_config.rdl`, `pio_registers.rdl` and `standby_controller_mode.rdl`, with the hardware
parameters set in its `registers.rdl`; no protocol VIP, no probe, no pad is read

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Every I3C base, PIO, standby and config register shows its RDL
reset, access type and write-one-to-clear behaviour in each
instance.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset: in each of the six instances every register of the table reads, on every field the hardware
  never writes (hw access na or r), the reset value declared in the I3C core's SystemRDL
  (`base_registers.rdl`, `controller_config.rdl`, `pio_registers.rdl`,
  `standby_controller_mode.rdl`); fields hardware can write (hw w or rw, or hwclr or hwset) are
  read, printed and compared with reset only in the printout. A field declared without a bit range
  is one bit at bit 0.
* Table scope: every register of the four files except the PIO queue ports `COMMAND_PORT`,
  `RESPONSE_PORT`, `TX_DATA_PORT`, `RX_DATA_PORT` and `IBI_PORT`, whose access has side effects, and
  `RESET_CONTROL`, whose soft-reset behaviour the specification does not state; action fields (`BUS_ENABLE`,
  `RESUME`, `ABORT`, `RS`, `ENABLE`, `STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT`, `CR_REQUEST_SEND`, `HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP`)
  are left at reset.
* Read-only: writing the reset word XOR the mask of the sw=r bits leaves every hardware-stable field
  at its reset.
* Read-write: every sw=rw field that is neither an action field nor hardware-updated nor
  write-one-to-clear reads back the 0x55555555 pattern masked to the field, then its complement,
  then its reset after the restore.
* Write-one-to-clear: every interrupt status field with `woclr` that hardware sets, in each register
  that has matching enable and force registers, is set through its force bit with its status enable
  set, reads 1, stays latched after the force is dropped, clears with a write of 1 while a
  neighbouring bit stays set, and the neighbour then clears with its own write of 1.
* Instance isolation: a distinct pattern written to the register of each block with the most
  read-write bits in instance n leaves the stable fields of the same register in the other five
  instances at their
  reset, and is then restored.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done; read the instance count; parse the four RDL files into the table of
  registers and fields and print the register and field counts by access class, the exclusions, the
  action fields and the hardware-updated fields; require the exclusion count and that no block
  parsed empty; stamp TABLE_PARSED.
. For each instance and register read the register and require every hardware-stable field to equal
  its RDL reset; count and print the hardware-updated fields that differ from reset; stamp
  RESET_SWEPT.
. Error injection. Point: every register with sw=r bits, in each instance. Kind: a write of the
  reset word XOR the sw=r mask (each read-only bit written with its inverted value). Expected
  response: the read-back shows every hardware-stable field still at its reset; stamp RO_SWEPT.
. For each instance and each in-scope sw=rw register write the pattern, read back, write the
  complement, read back, write the reset, read back, requiring each in-scope field to match each
  time; stamp RW_SWEPT.
. For each instance, interrupt status register and `woclr` field: enable the field and a neighbour
  in the enable register, force the neighbour and drop the force, force the field, read the status
  (both bits set), drop the force and read again (both latched), write 1 to the field and require
  the neighbour kept and the field clear, write 1 to the neighbour and require the w1c bits all
  clear, restore the force and enable registers; stamp W1C_SWEPT.
. For one register of each of the base, PIO and standby blocks and each instance n write a distinct
  pattern, read it back, require every other instance's stable fields at reset, restore and read
  back; stamp ISOLATION_SWEPT.
. Require the six stamps strictly increasing, the five checker lines printed at their own steps and
  print the fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RESET-READ` |In every instance each hardware-stable field of every table register
reads the reset declared in the I3C core's SystemRDL; the register and field counts per block are
printed and the hardware-updated fields are measured and printed.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RO-IGNORED` |In every instance after the write of reset XOR the sw=r mask every
hardware-stable field reads its reset, so the sw=r bits do not follow the written value;
hardware-updated fields are measured and printed.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RW-ROUNDTRIP` |In every instance each in-scope sw=rw field reads back the masked
0x55555555 pattern, then its complement, then its reset; excluded action and hardware-updated fields
are listed with the reason.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-W1C-CLEAR` |In every instance each `woclr` interrupt field reads 1 after its force
with the status enable set, stays latched after the force is dropped, and reads 0 after a write of 1
with the neighbouring bit kept, which then clears on its own write.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` |After a distinct pattern is written to one register of each
block in instance n, the hardware-stable fields of the same register in each of the other five
instances read their reset, for every n, and the pattern is restored.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms TABLE_PARSED, RESET_SWEPT, RO_SWEPT, RW_SWEPT, W1C_SWEPT and
ISOLATION_SWEPT occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and each checker line prints at its
own step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RESET-READ`, `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RO-IGNORED`,
`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RW-ROUNDTRIP`, `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-W1C-CLEAR` and `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` hold
after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` printed at the end; the values of hardware-updated fields
and the `RESET_CONTROL` soft-reset behaviour are not claimed. Zero reset words cannot fail on an
unknown value under a two-state simulator. Enrolled in: `all`; also listed in `fabric.toml`
(tags `ci`, `fabric`).

*Scope limit*: The values of the fields hardware can write (hw w or rw, hwclr or hwset) are read,
printed and compared with reset only in the printout; they are not claimed. The `RESET_CONTROL`
soft-reset behaviour is not claimed, because the specification does not state it. The PIO queue
ports are excluded because their access has side effects, and the action fields are left at reset.
Zero reset words cannot fail on an unknown value under the two-state simulator.

'''''

[[sec-517-smc_i3c_csr_sweep_ext_test]]
===== 517 `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_ext_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: I3C

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_ext_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (`SmcCsrSeq` 4-byte reads and writes, OKAY required) to the six I3C
instance CSR windows (`I3C_CSR` base per instance from the generated map, instance count from the
generated `NUM` symbol) at the register offsets of the generated I3C wrapper register map; the
register table is parsed at run time from the I3C core's SystemRDL sources
`target_transaction_interface.rdl`, `soc_management_interface.rdl` and
`secure_firmware_recovery_interface.rdl`; no protocol VIP, no probe, no pad is read

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Every I3C TTI, SoC management and recovery register shows its RDL
reset, access type and write-one-to-clear behaviour in each instance.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset: in each of the six instances every register of the table reads, on every field the hardware
  never writes (hw access na or r), the reset declared in the I3C core's SystemRDL; fields hardware
  can write are read and printed, not asserted. A field declared without a bit range is one bit at
  bit 0.
* Table scope: every register of the three files except the TTI queue ports (`RX_DESC_QUEUE_PORT`,
  `RX_DATA_PORT`, `TX_DESC_QUEUE_PORT`, `TX_DATA_PORT`, `IBI_PORT`) and the recovery
  `INDIRECT_FIFO_DATA` port, whose accesses have side effects. `SOC_PAD_CONF` and `SOC_PAD_ATTR` are
  accessed as registers only and their effect on any pad is not observed. Action registers and
  fields (`RESET_CONTROL`, `DEVICE_RESET`, `RECOVERY_CTRL`, `REC_INTF_REG_W1C_ACCESS`,
  `REC_PAYLOAD_DONE`, `INDIRECT_FIFO_CTRL_0.RESET`) are left at reset.
* Read-only: writing the reset word XOR the mask of the sw=r bits leaves every hardware-stable field
  at its reset; sw=r fields hardware can write read what they read before the write.
* Read-write: every sw=rw field that is neither an action field nor hardware-updated nor
  write-one-to-clear nor read-clear reads back the 0x55555555 pattern masked to the field, then its
  complement, then its reset; the recovery block contributes no such field.
* Write-one-to-clear: each `woclr` field that has a status, enable and force register triple is set
  through its force bit with its status enable set; where it sets it reads 1, stays latched after
  the force is dropped, clears on a write of 1 while a second pre-set bit of the same register keeps
  reading 1, and that second bit then clears. A field whose status stays 0 after its force is
  measured and printed per instance and not failed, and no minimum count of fields that set is
  required (the set and not-set counts per block are printed); fields the RDL describes as not
  implemented are
  driven and printed, not asserted; self-clearing `singlepulse` fields read 0 after a write of 1.
* Instance isolation: a distinct pattern written to a read-write register of each block in instance
  n leaves the same register in the other five instances at its reset, and is then restored.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense done; read the instance count; parse the three RDL files into the table of
  registers and fields and print the register and field counts by access class, the exclusions, the
  action fields, the hardware-updated fields and the block base offsets; require the exclusion count
  and that no block parsed empty; stamp TABLE_PARSED.
. For each instance and register read the register and require every hardware-stable field to equal
  its RDL reset; count and print the hardware-updated fields that differ from reset; stamp
  RESET_SWEPT.
. Error injection. Point: every register with sw=r bits, in each instance. Kind: a write of the
  reset word XOR the sw=r mask (each read-only bit written with its inverted value). Expected
  response: the read-back shows every hardware-stable field still at its reset and every
  hardware-updated sw=r field equal to its value read before the write; stamp RO_SWEPT.
. For each instance and each in-scope sw=rw register write the pattern, read back, write the
  complement, read back, write the reset, read back, requiring each in-scope field to match each
  time; stamp RW_SWEPT.
. For each instance, status register and `woclr` field: clear any residual set status bits, require
  the status clear, set the enable, write the force bit, read the status and drop the force; where
  the field sets require it to read 1 and still read 1 after the force drop, pre-set a second bit
  where the register has one, write 1 to the field and require it clear with the second bit kept,
  then clear the second bit and restore the enable; where it stays 0 or is not implemented print it;
  then write 1 to each `singlepulse` field and require 0; stamp W1C_SWEPT.
. For one read-write register of each of the TTI, SoC management and recovery blocks and each
  instance n write a distinct pattern, require it to read back where the register's read-write bits
  are all in scope, require every other instance's stable and writable fields at reset, restore and
  read back; stamp ISOLATION_SWEPT.
. Require the six stamps strictly increasing, the five checker lines printed at their own steps and
  print the fence line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RESET-READ` |In every instance each hardware-stable field of every table register
reads the reset declared in the I3C core's SystemRDL; the register and field counts per block are
printed and the hardware-updated fields are measured and printed.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RO-IGNORED` |In every instance after the write of reset XOR the sw=r mask every
hardware-stable field reads its reset and every hardware-updated sw=r field reads what it read
before the write, so the sw=r bits do not follow the written value.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RW-ROUNDTRIP` |In every instance each in-scope sw=rw field reads back the masked
0x55555555 pattern, then its complement, then its reset; excluded action and hardware-updated fields
are listed with the reason.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-W1C-CLEAR` |In every instance each `woclr` field whose force sets its status reads 1
after the force with the enable set, still 1 after the force drop, and 0 after a write of 1 with the
second pre-set bit kept, which then clears; a status that stays 0 after its force or a field not
implemented is printed per instance without a compare; each `singlepulse` field reads 0 after a
write of 1.
|`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` |After a distinct pattern is written to one register of each
block in instance n, the same register in each of the other five instances reads its reset in the
stable and writable fields, for every n, and the pattern is restored.
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The fence terms TABLE_PARSED, RESET_SWEPT, RO_SWEPT, RW_SWEPT, W1C_SWEPT and
ISOLATION_SWEPT occur in order with strictly increasing stamps and each checker line prints at its
own step.
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RESET-READ`, `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RO-IGNORED`,
`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-RW-ROUNDTRIP`, `CHK-I3C-SWEEP-W1C-CLEAR` (for the fields that set; no minimum count
of them is required) and
`CHK-I3C-SWEEP-INSTANCE-ISOLATION` hold after their compares, with `CHK-NONVAC` printed at the end;
the values of hardware-updated fields, the status fields whose force does not set them, the fields
the RDL marks not implemented, the pad effect of `SOC_PAD_CONF` and `SOC_PAD_ATTR`, and the action
registers are not claimed. Zero reset words cannot fail on an unknown value under a two-state
simulator. Enrolled in: `all`; also listed in `fabric.toml`
(tags `ci`, `fabric`).

*Scope limit*: The values of the fields hardware can write are read and printed, not asserted. A
`woclr` status field that stays 0 after its force is measured and printed per instance and not
failed, no minimum count of fields that set is required, and the fields the RDL describes as not
implemented are driven and printed, not asserted. `SOC_PAD_CONF` and `SOC_PAD_ATTR` are accessed as
registers only and their effect on any pad is not observed. The TTI queue ports and the recovery
`INDIRECT_FIFO_DATA` port are excluded because their accesses have side effects, and the action
registers and fields are left at reset and not claimed. Zero reset words cannot fail on an unknown
value under the two-state simulator.
'''''


[[smc-vplan-area-mailbox]]
==== MAILBOX

[[sec-140-smc_mailbox_data_error_test]]
===== 140 `smc_mailbox_data_error_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_data_error_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `axil`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run mailbox write/read data and illegal access response checks.

*Test Coverage*:

* Mailbox data path and error-response depth test over real SEP_IN AXI.
* Every register address and the clock-gate field mask are imported by generated symbol (`hw/sys/smc/regs/gen/c/smc_addr.h` / `blocks/smc_base_config.h`), as `smc_mailbox_irq_test_seq` does.
* The `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` offset is taken from the generated map, so a regenerated map moves this sequence with it ([ADDRESS-FROM-AUTHORITATIVE-MAP]).
* The DUT-vs-golden compare is the `expected=` on each paired `READ_DATA` read, enforced by `SmcScoreboard` (`env/smc_scoreboard.py`): data written into `OUTBOUND_WRITE_DATA` must come back out of `INBOUND_READ_DATA` in FIFO order, and vice versa.
* There are no synthetic `SmcMemoryModel` regions here: asserting a written literal back out of a TB-local dict at an address no DUT transaction reaches is a `C == C` compare that cannot fail on any RTL ([NO-ALWAYS-PASS-CHECKER]).
* The scoreboard's real `update_golden` / `check_golden` path cannot replace them either: it is keyed by `item.addr`, and a mailbox is a FIFO whose two writes land on the same address, so an address-keyed model cannot represent it.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_mailbox_data_error_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MAILBOX-FIFO-DATA` |Named compare in `smc_mailbox_data_error_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-ASSERT` |Named compare in `smc_mailbox_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-CLEAR` |Named compare in `smc_mailbox_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-IDLE` |Named compare in `smc_mailbox_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-SOURCE` |Named compare in `smc_mailbox_vip_utils.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MAILBOX-FIFO-DATA`, `CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-ASSERT`, `CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-CLEAR`, `CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-IDLE`, `CHK-MAILBOX-IRQ-SOURCE` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-142-smc_mailbox_field_sweep_test]]
===== 142 `smc_mailbox_field_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_field_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Every readable field of mailboxes 0-3 decodes, on the inbound port as well as the outbound one.

*Test Coverage*:

* The seven readable registers of each port, checked against `axil_mailbox.rdl` rather than trusted as a list: STATUS +0x010, ERROR_FLAGS +0x018, WIRQT +0x020, RIRQT +0x028, IRQS +0x030 (write-1-to-clear), IRQEN +0x038, IRQP +0x040 (`irqs_q & irqen_q`, read-only derived).
* Three of the ten registers per port are out, each for a stated reason. WRITE_DATA +0x000 and READ_DATA +0x008 are omitted because a read pops the paired port's FIFO, which is state this sweep must not disturb. CTRL +0x048 is `sw = w` flush strobes with nothing to read; its effect is covered by `smc_mailbox_flush_test`.
* Both ports, and the swept set **derived from the generated map** rather than listed: `_swept_fields` enumerates every `SMC_MAILBOX_<port>_MAILBOX_0_*_REG_OFFSET` symbol in `regs/gen/py/smc_reg.py` and removes the three that cannot be read. A hand-maintained list cannot guard itself -- an access count computed from the list the loop walks matches for any list content -- so deriving it from the map is what makes the anti-shrink claim true rather than circular.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL, set MAILBOX_CG_EN, and restore the original value at the end.
. Read all seven fields of mailboxes 0-3 on the outbound port, then the same on the inbound port.
. Require the access count to equal the number of readable registers the generated map holds, times the mailboxes, times the ports, plus the three clock-gate accesses.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MBOX-FIELD-DECODE` |Every one of the 56 field reads returns OKAY. `csr_read` routes through the scoreboard's `item.resp_ok` assert, so a mis-decoded field answers DECERR or hangs and fails. `csr_read_bounded` is not used: it would tolerate a dead field and make the sweep vacuous
|`CHK-MBOX-FIELD-COUNT` |The access count matches the register count in the generated map, not the length of any list this testcase owns. Dropping a read from the loop fails; so does the map growing a register the sweep does not read. The one remaining way to narrow the sweep is to add a name to the `_UNREADABLE` table, which is pinned at three entries and requires a written reason, so it cannot happen silently
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold and the scoreboard reports zero errors. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `WRITE_DATA` and `READ_DATA` are not read, because a read pops the paired port's FIFO, and `CTRL` is not read because it is write-only flush strobes; its effect is covered by `smc_mailbox_flush_test`.

'''''

[[sec-143-smc_mailbox_flush_test]]
===== 143 `smc_mailbox_flush_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_flush_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the feature has no legal knob space (a strap, a single named
handshake).

*Objective*: CTRL.wflush empties the write FIFO it claims to flush.

*Test Coverage*:

* `OUTBOUND_MAILBOX_0.CTRL` @0x48, which no other testcase reaches. `smc_mailbox_field_sweep_test` covers every other readable register of the port, on both directions, but cannot cover this one: a sweep reads, and CTRL is write-only.
* The register cannot be a readback test. `axil_mailbox.rdl` marks both fields as external, user-defined write effects: they are flush strobes, not storage, so a write/read-back pair would compare against whatever the register file returns for a write-only address and prove nothing. What is testable is the effect, and `STATUS.write_level_above_thresh` @0x10 bit 2 reports it.
* Addresses from `smc_addr.h`, field masks from `axil_mailbox.h`, rather than offsets added to a base ([ADDRESS-FROM-AUTHORITATIVE-MAP]).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Enable the mailbox clock gate, then write WIRQT := 0 and read it back, so "above threshold" has a known meaning and the port is proven writable.
. Require `STATUS.write_level_above_thresh` to read 0 with nothing pushed.
. Push one word into WRITE_DATA and require the same bit to read 1.
. Write CTRL.wflush and require the bit to return to 0.
. Restore the clock-gate register.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MBOX-FLUSH-ARM` |One word pushed with WIRQT=0 raises `STATUS.write_level_above_thresh`. This is the positive control: without it the check below is satisfied by a STATUS that reads zero for every reason including a dead one ([NEGATIVE-NEEDS-POSITIVE-CONTROL])
|`CHK-MBOX-FLUSH` |After CTRL.wflush the bit is clear again. Nothing in this bench drains the outbound write FIFO on its own -- its far side is the paired inbound port's read side, reached only by an explicit INBOUND_READ_DATA access -- so a level that falls between the two checks fell because of the flush
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold: the level bit reads 0, then 0x4 after the push, then 0 after the flush. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-145-smc_mailbox_inbound_test]]
===== 145 `smc_mailbox_inbound_test`

*Phase*: 1

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_inbound_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Inbound mailbox 0 STATUS/ERROR/IRQEN precheck.

*Test Coverage*:

* Inbound mailbox 0 CSR precheck.
* The SMC integration has 32 outbound + 32 inbound mailboxes (`periphs.adoc`, `NumMailboxes`); this test covers the inbound-mailbox 0 STATUS/ERROR/IRQ CSR surface after enabling the mailbox clock-gate.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_mailbox_inbound_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MAILBOX-INBOUND-RESET-SURFACE` |With the mailbox clock gate enabled, inbound mailbox 0 STATUS read 0x1 (FIFO empty), ERROR_FLAGS read 0x0 and IRQEN read 0x0, each in a scoreboard value compare, with all 6 accesses checked by the scoreboard and exactly 3 value compares booked; a non-OKAY response, a mismatched word or a compare that never ran fails it
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MAILBOX-INBOUND-RESET-SURFACE` holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''
