[[sec-147-smc_mailbox_multi_instance_test]]
===== 147 `smc_mailbox_multi_instance_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_multi_instance_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), ocah_axi_vip (AXI-Lite)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the leaf walks the whole cell set in one run.

*Objective*: Mailbox STATUS sweep over every outbound and inbound instance the generated map exports (32 + 32, the `NumMailboxes` value `periphs.adoc` gives the SMC integration), IRQEN storage on instance 0 of each direction, the last inbound instance raising its own bit of `mailbox_interrupts`, and the read-only-write, empty-read and `ERROR_FLAGS` read-to-clear access results of every one of the 64 apertures.

*Test Coverage*:

* The instance count is derived from the `SMC_TOP_SMC_MAILBOX_{OUTBOUND,INBOUND}_MAILBOX_<n>_BASE_ADDR` symbols in `smc_addr.h` and required to equal the `periphs.adoc` value for both directions; a map that gained or lost an instance fails at import.
* Every instance's STATUS is read against the RDL idle word (EMPTY set, nothing else), so a mis-decoded or dead instance fails a scoreboard value compare rather than an OKAY-only read.
* IRQEN is the one register in the block the RDL declares as plain software-owned storage (`sw = rw; hw = r` with no acknowledge semantics), so it is the write/read-back leg; the RDL attributes of the other registers are the reason they are not swept here.
* The last inbound instance is armed for the write-threshold interrupt and one word is pushed; `mailbox_interrupts` must go from 0 to exactly that instance's bit and back to 0 when IRQEN is dropped. The STATUS word expected after the push is built from the RDL field descriptions and the `periphs.adoc` depth (2); the depth the DUT publishes in `CPU_CTRL.SMC_ATTRIBUTES` is compared against that value rather than used as its source, and the threshold rule (a write-threshold IRQ once the usage pointer exceeds WIRQT, which resets to 0) comes from the WIRQT description in `axil_mailbox.rdl`.
* Access results on every one of the 64 apertures (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc`, Access Results): writes to `READ_DATA`, `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQP` answer `SLVERR` and leave `STATUS` at its idle word and `IRQP` at 0; the `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` values after those writes are not stated (SF-030) and are printed, required only to agree across apertures. Each aperture's B and R response paths carry a `SLVERR` in both directions.
* An empty `READ_DATA` read on every aperture answers `SLVERR` with low data word 0xFEEDDEAD (the upper word is not stated, SF-032, and is printed) and sets `IRQS[2]` and the read-error flag, while the next aperture keeps `IRQS` and `ERROR_FLAGS` at 0; writing 0x4 to `IRQS` clears it, and two `ERROR_FLAGS` reads return 0x1 then 0x0.
* Two back-to-back and four pipelined empty reads on outbound and inbound aperture 31 each answer `SLVERR` 0xFEEDDEAD within a bounded group wait, with `STATUS` still empty after; on aperture 0 of each direction an `ERROR_FLAGS` read pipelined behind an empty read and the read after it report the read error exactly once (which of the two is printed, SF-033) and a third read returns 0.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_mailbox_multi_instance_test_seq` (contract `SMC_COV_B1_006`, steps S1-S10): the STATUS sweep, IRQEN and channel-vector legs, then the read-only writes, empty reads, read-to-clear, back-to-back and same-window legs over SEP_IN. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MAILBOX-CHANNEL-VECTOR` |The whole 32-bit `mailbox_interrupts` vector observed 0 before the push and with IRQEN armed, exactly the last instance's bit within a bounded poll after the push, and 0 again after IRQEN is dropped; every STATUS and IRQEN compare is a scoreboard value compare
|`CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-STATUS` |On all 64 apertures the `READ_DATA` and `STATUS` writes answer `SLVERR` (128 of 128) and `STATUS` reads 0x1 before and after
|`CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-FLAGS` |On all 64 apertures the `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQP` writes answer `SLVERR` (128 of 128) and `IRQP` reads 0x0 before and after; the `ERROR_FLAGS` value read after is printed (SF-030)
|`CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-EFFECT` |The `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` values observed after the read-only writes are printed and must be the same on every aperture (SF-030)
|`CHK-MBX-EMPTY-READ` |On all 64 apertures an empty `READ_DATA` read answers `SLVERR` with data[31:0] = 0xFEEDDEAD; data[63:32] is printed (SF-032)
|`CHK-MBX-EMPTY-FLAGS` |After each empty read `IRQS[2]` and `ERROR_FLAGS[0]` read 1, the next aperture reads `IRQS` 0x0 and `ERROR_FLAGS` 0x0, and `IRQS` reads 0x0 after 0x4 is written to it
|`CHK-MBX-ERRFLAGS-RC` |On all 64 apertures the first `ERROR_FLAGS` read after the empty read returns 0x1 and the second 0x0, both `OKAY`
|`CHK-MBX-EMPTY-B2B` |On outbound and inbound aperture 31, 2 back-to-back and 4 pipelined empty reads all answer `SLVERR` 0xFEEDDEAD and `STATUS` reads 0x1 after
|`CHK-MBX-ERRFLAGS-RETAIN` |On outbound and inbound aperture 0, exactly one of the `ERROR_FLAGS` read pipelined behind an empty read and the read after it carries the read error, and a third read returns 0x0; which one is printed (SF-033)
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence IDLE-SWEEP < RO-WRITES < RO-EFFECT < EMPTY-READ < FLAGS < RC per aperture, then B2B < SAME-WINDOW, every term with its count and sim times
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every grouped back-to-back, pipelined and same-window wait is bounded at 40 us and fails with the outstanding read count and the last R record; the line lists each wait
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-MAILBOX-CHANNEL-VECTOR`, `CHK-MBX-EMPTY-B2B`, `CHK-MBX-EMPTY-FLAGS`, `CHK-MBX-EMPTY-READ`, `CHK-MBX-ERRFLAGS-RC`, `CHK-MBX-ERRFLAGS-RETAIN`, `CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-EFFECT`, `CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-FLAGS`, `CHK-MBX-RO-WRITE-STATUS`, `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Only `IRQEN` is swept as write/read-back storage; the other registers of the block are not swept here because of their RDL access attributes.
'''''

[[sec-518-smc_mailbox_access_error_test]]
===== 518 `smc_mailbox_access_error_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_access_error_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including grouped access items, for the
registers of mailbox pair 2: outbound aperture A and inbound aperture B (`WRITE_DATA`, `READ_DATA`,
`STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `IRQP`, `CTRL`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`
(`MAILBOX_CG_EN`); the scoreboard compares every access response and expected read value; the
bench nets `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` are read only for
the bring-up wait and the bounded-wait line; the driver's own 50 microsecond access limit

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Mailbox access errors, ERROR_FLAGS clearing and channel overlap.

*Test Coverage*:

* Access results of the mailbox (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc`, Access Results; the
  SMC mailbox depth is 2, `periphs.adoc`): a `READ_DATA` read while empty answers `SLVERR` with low
  data word 0xFEEDDEAD, sets the read-error flag and `IRQS[2]`; a `WRITE_DATA` write while full
  answers `SLVERR`, discards the data and sets the write-error flag and `IRQS[2]`. The upper data
  half of an empty read is not specified and is printed without a compare.
* Read-to-clear: reading `ERROR_FLAGS` returns and clears both flags (`ERROR`, sticky and clear on
  read, in `axil_mailbox.rdl`); a repeat read returns 0; the read does not acknowledge `IRQS[2]`,
  which clears only by writing 1 to it (`architecture.adoc`, Interrupts). Flags are per
  aperture: aperture B stays 0 while A is exercised.
* `STATUS[3:2]` (write and read level above threshold) read 0 before and after an empty read, and
  traffic in both directions afterwards returns the words written; `STATUS[1:0]` is printed.
* After the FIFO is full and a word is popped by B, the next write answers `OKAY` and words pop in
  write order (`architecture.adoc`, Paired FIFOs).
* `WRITE_DATA` is write-only: reading it answers `OKAY` with low word 0xFEEDC0DE, empty, with one
  word and when full, without changing `IRQS` or `ERROR_FLAGS` and without raising `IRQS[2]` (`interface.adoc`). Writes to
  `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQP` answer `SLVERR` and are ignored: `STATUS[3:2]`, the
  read-error flag and `IRQP[2:0]` (0x1 with `IRQEN` 0x1 and one word queued) are unchanged.
  Whether the ignored writes touch `ERROR_FLAGS[1]` or `IRQS` is measured and printed, not compared.
* Channel coincidence: three grouped accesses are issued together, a `WRITE_DATA` write with a
  `STATUS` read, a `WRITE_DATA` write with a `READ_DATA` read, and a `CTRL` flush write with an
  `IRQS` read. Each member must complete with its response under the driver limit; no cycle
  alignment is claimed (`interface.adoc`, External Interface). The `STATUS` value in the first
  group and the `IRQS` value in the third are printed. In the second group the read returns the
  word B had sent and B later pops the word the group wrote, each on its own FIFO.
* The leaf requires at least 80 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have checked at least as
  many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with `MAILBOX_CG_EN` set and
  read it back; stamp step S1.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` of aperture A and of aperture B. Kind: a read while the FIFO
  is empty. Expected response: `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD on each; stamp S2 and print the
  line with the upper halves.
. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` of A and B and require 0b01 and 0b100 on both; write 0x4 to `IRQS`
  of both and require `IRQS` 0. Stamp S3 and print the line.
. Read `STATUS` of A and B, make an empty read of A, read `STATUS` of A again, and require
  `STATUS[3:2]` 0 each time; B writes a word and A pops it; A writes a word and B pops it. Stamp S4
  and print the line.
. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` and write `IRQS` 0x7 on both apertures; stamp S5.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: a third write after two words have filled the
  two-entry FIFO. Expected response: the third write answers `SLVERR`, `IRQS` of A reads 0b101, and
  `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b10 then 0 on two reads. Stamp S6 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` and `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: an empty read and a further
  write to the full FIFO. Expected response: `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b11 then 0 on two reads, `IRQS`
  bit 2 is set and clears after 0x4 is written. Stamp S7 and print the two lines.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` and `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: two empty reads and two full
  writes, repeated. Expected response: `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b11 then 0 on two reads; stamp S8 and
  print the line.
. B pops the first word, A writes a word with `OKAY`, B pops the other two in write order; stamp S9
  and print the line.
. Read `ERROR_FLAGS` of B twice requiring 0 each; stamp S10 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: a read of the write-only register while the FIFO
  is empty. Expected response: `OKAY` with low word 0xFEEDC0DE; stamp S11 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: a read of the write-only register with one word
  queued and again with the FIFO full. Expected response: `IRQS` is unchanged by each read with
  `IRQS[2]` clear after each read, and `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0 at the end. First write 0x7 to `IRQS`
  of A to acknowledge every bit; A writes a word, read `WRITE_DATA`, A writes a second word, read
  `WRITE_DATA`, reading `IRQS` after each step and `ERROR_FLAGS` at the end; B pops both words.
  Stamp S12 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQP` of A. Kind: a write to each of the
  three read-only registers, with `IRQEN` 0x1, one word queued and the read-error flag set by an
  empty read. Expected response: each write answers `SLVERR` and the read-back shows `STATUS[3:2]`
  unchanged, the read-error flag still set and `IRQP[2:0]` 0x1. Beforehand read `IRQEN`, set
  `IRQEN` 0x1 on A, queue one word, make an empty read, read `ERROR_FLAGS`, make another empty read,
  read `STATUS` and `IRQS`; afterwards read `IRQS`, B pops the word, restore `IRQEN`. Stamp S13 and
  print the two lines.
. Issue the group `WRITE_DATA` write with `STATUS` read, then B pops the written word; stamp S14
  and print the line.
. B writes a word, issue the group `WRITE_DATA` write with `READ_DATA` read (read expected to
  return B's word), then B pops the written word; stamp S15 and print the line.
. Issue the group `CTRL` flush write with `IRQS` read; stamp S16 and print its line, then require
  all six members to have a response and print the completion line. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`.
. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S16 with strictly increasing stamps and the seventeen
  checker lines printed in order at their steps, print the non-vacuity line, then print the
  bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EMPTY-READ-SLVERR-DATA` |`READ_DATA` of A and of B answers `SLVERR` with low data word
  0xFEEDDEAD while empty; the upper half is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-EMPTY-READ-FLAGS` |After the empty read `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b01 and `IRQS` reads 0b100 on A
  and on B, and `IRQS` reads 0 after 0x4 is written
|`CHK-EMPTY-READ-NO-SIDE-EFFECT` |`STATUS[3:2]` reads 0 before and after the empty read, and the
  words written in both directions afterwards pop exactly; `STATUS[1:0]` is recorded without
  comparing
|`CHK-FULL-WRITE-FLAGS` |After two `OKAY` writes and a `SLVERR` third write `IRQS` reads 0b101, the
  first `ERROR_FLAGS` read returns 0b10 and the second returns 0
|`CHK-FULL-WRITE-RECOVERS` |After B pops one word the next write answers `OKAY`, and B pops the
  remaining word and the new word in write order
|`CHK-ERRFLAGS-BOTH-THEN-ZERO` |With an empty read and a full write both made, the first
  `ERROR_FLAGS` read returns 0b11 and the second returns 0
|`CHK-ERRFLAGS-READ-KEEPS-IRQS-ERROR` |`IRQS[2]` is still 1 after two `ERROR_FLAGS` reads and is 0
  only after 0x4 is written to `IRQS`
|`CHK-ERRFLAGS-STICKY-ONE-READ-CLEARS` |After repeated errors the first `ERROR_FLAGS` read returns
  0b11 and the next returns 0
|`CHK-ERRFLAGS-PER-APERTURE` |`ERROR_FLAGS` of B reads 0b00 on two reads although A's flags were
  set and cleared several times
|`CHK-WRITE-DATA-READ-EMPTY` |A `WRITE_DATA` read answers `OKAY` with low word 0xFEEDC0DE; the upper
  half is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-WRITE-DATA-READ-NO-EFFECT` |`WRITE_DATA` reads with one word queued and with a full FIFO
  answer `OKAY`, `ERROR_FLAGS` stays 0, `IRQS` is identical before and after each read with
  `IRQS[2]` clear after each read (`IRQS` is acknowledged before the first write), and B pops the
  two words in order
|`CHK-READ-ONLY-WRITES-REJECTED` |Writes to `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQP` each answer
  `SLVERR`; `STATUS[3:2]` is unchanged, the read-error flag is still set and `IRQP[2:0]` reads 0x1
|`CHK-READ-ONLY-WRITES-NO-SIDE-EFFECT-OBSERVED` |Measures and prints `ERROR_FLAGS[1]` and `IRQS`
  before and after the ignored writes without comparing them
|`CHK-CHANNELS-WRITE-WITH-STATUS` |The grouped `WRITE_DATA` write and `STATUS` read both answer
  `OKAY` with resolvable data, and B pops the written word; the `STATUS` value is recorded
  without comparing
|`CHK-CHANNELS-WRITE-WITH-READ` |The grouped `READ_DATA` read returns the word B sent, the grouped
  write answers `OKAY`, and B pops the written word
|`CHK-CHANNELS-CTRL-WITH-IRQS` |The grouped `CTRL` write and `IRQS` read both answer `OKAY`; the
  `IRQS` value is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-CHANNELS-COMPLETE-BOUNDED` |All six grouped members complete with a response under the
  driver limit, with no cycle count assumed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S16 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the seventeen checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound and the SEP_IN access limit; the compare is each wait's own assertion, which
  fails the leaf on expiry, and the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nineteen checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 80
SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The upper data halves, `STATUS[1:0]`,
the ignored-write side effects and the grouped `STATUS` and `IRQS` values are recorded and are not
part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The upper data half of an empty `READ_DATA` read and of a `WRITE_DATA` read,
`STATUS[1:0]`, whether the ignored writes to the read-only registers touch `ERROR_FLAGS[1]` or
`IRQS`, and the `STATUS` and `IRQS` values returned inside the grouped accesses are recorded and not
compared; the upper half of an empty read is not specified. No cycle alignment of the grouped
accesses is claimed. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the bounded waits as a record; the compare is each
wait's own assertion.

'''''

[[sec-519-smc_mailbox_flush_status_test]]
===== 519 `smc_mailbox_flush_status_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_flush_status_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including grouped access items, for the
registers of mailbox pair 4: outbound aperture A and inbound aperture B (`CTRL`, `WRITE_DATA`,
`READ_DATA`, `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`
(`MAILBOX_CG_EN`); the scoreboard compares every access response and expected read value; the
bench nets `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` are read only for
the bring-up wait and the bounded-wait line; the driver's own 50 microsecond access limit

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CTRL flushes hit one FIFO each; STATUS threshold bits are live.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CTRL` flush bits are write-only strobes that are not stored and read back as zero
  (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc`, Access Results; `CTRL` in `axil_mailbox.rdl`:
  `WFLUSH` bit 0, `RFLUSH` bit 1). `CTRL` bits 1:0 read 0 at reset and after writes of 0x1 and 0x2.
  What a write of 0x3 does is not specified; its response and which FIFOs drained are printed
  without a compare. The zero reset value cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build
  (bench limit); the read-back after writes is the discriminating leg.
* Strict thresholds (`architecture.adoc`, Interrupts): with `WIRQT` 1 `STATUS[2]` reads 0 with one
  queued word and 1 with two; with `RIRQT` 0 `B.STATUS[3]` reads 1 with one received word; with
  `RIRQT` 1 it reads 0 at one word and 1 at two. Both bits fall as the occupancy falls with no
  `IRQS` write issued and `IRQEN` 0, while `IRQS[0]` stays latched: the live `STATUS` bit does
  not depend on the acknowledge or the enable. `STATUS[1:0]` and the empty and full bits are
  printed.
* Write flush: a flush of A's write FIFO discards words its peer B would read
  (`architecture.adoc`, Paired FIFOs): after queuing two words and a flush, B's read answers
  `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD; the next write to the formerly full FIFO answers `OKAY` and B
  pops it; A's own read FIFO is untouched (A pops the word B sent); a flush of an empty write
  FIFO leaves `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` 0.
* Read flush: a flush of A's read FIFO empties it (A's read answers `SLVERR` with low word
  0xFEEDDEAD although B had sent a word); the peer's write to a formerly full FIFO answers `OKAY`
  and A pops it; A's own write FIFO is untouched (B pops the word A queued); a flush of an empty
  read FIFO leaves `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` 0.
* Flush against traffic: three grouped accesses are issued together, `CTRL` write wflush with a
  `WRITE_DATA` write on A, `CTRL` write rflush with a `WRITE_DATA` write by B, and `CTRL` write
  rflush with a `READ_DATA` read on A. All members complete with `OKAY` (the grouped read is
  measured only); the word queued before the flush is never popped; the word written in the same
  group is either kept or discarded, which is printed (the specification does not state which), and the
  FIFO then ends in the empty error and a later word round-trips intact. No cycle alignment is
  claimed.
* The leaf requires at least 100 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have checked at least as
  many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with `MAILBOX_CG_EN` set and
  read it back; stamp step S1.
. Read `CTRL` of A and of B requiring bits 1:0 clear; stamp S2 and print the line.
. Require `IRQEN` of A clear, write `WIRQT` 1, write one word to A reading `STATUS`, write a
  second word reading `STATUS`, B pops one word and A reads `STATUS`, read `IRQS` requiring
  `IRQS[0]` latched, B pops the last word and A reads `STATUS`; require `STATUS[2]` 0, 1, 0, 0;
  no `IRQS` write is issued. Stamp S3 and print the two lines.
. Write `RIRQT` 0 on B, A sends a word, read `B.STATUS`, B pops, write `RIRQT` 1, A sends one word
  and then a second, reading `B.STATUS` each time, B pops one word and reads `STATUS`, B pops the
  last; require `B.STATUS[3]` 1, 0, 1, 0; no `IRQS` write is issued. Stamp S4 and print the two lines.
. Write `CTRL` 0x1 and 0x2 on A, each followed by a `CTRL` read requiring bits 1:0 clear; stamp S5
  and print the line.
. Queue two words in each direction, write `CTRL` 0x3 on A recording the response, and drain both
  `READ_DATA` registers until the empty error, recording each word; stamp S6 and print the line.
. Clear the error state, A writes two words (full), write wflush, B's `READ_DATA` must answer
  `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD, read `STATUS` of both, A writes a third word with `OKAY` and
  B pops it. Stamp S7 and print the two lines.
. B writes a word, write wflush on A, A pops the word; stamp S8 and print the line.
. Establish a zero `ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` baseline, write wflush on A with its write FIFO empty,
  and require both still 0; stamp S9 and print the line.
. B writes a word, write rflush on A, A's `READ_DATA` must answer `SLVERR` with low word
  0xFEEDDEAD, read `STATUS` of A; stamp S10 and print the line.
. B writes two words (A's read FIFO full), write rflush on A, B writes a third word with `OKAY`,
  A pops it, read `STATUS` of B; stamp S11 and print the line.
. A writes a word, write rflush on A, B pops it; stamp S12 and print the line.
. Establish the baseline, write rflush on A with its read FIFO empty, require `ERROR_FLAGS` and
  `IRQS` 0; stamp S13 and print the line.
. A writes V0, issue the group wflush write with a `WRITE_DATA` write of V1, drain B requiring at
  most the one word V1 and the empty error, A writes V2 and B pops it; stamp S14 and print the
  line.
. B writes U0, issue the group rflush write with B's `WRITE_DATA` write of U1, drain A requiring at
  most the one word U1 and the empty error, B writes U2 and A pops it; stamp S15 and print the
  line.
. B writes Z0, issue the group rflush write with an `READ_DATA` read on A and record the read, A's
  `READ_DATA` must answer `SLVERR`, B writes Z1 and A pops it; stamp S16 and print the line.
. Restore `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S16 with
  strictly increasing stamps and the eighteen checker lines printed in order at their steps,
  print the non-vacuity line, then print the bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CTRL-ZERO-AT-RESET` |`CTRL` of A and of B answer `OKAY` with bits 1:0 equal to 0 at reset;
  the reset leg cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit)
|`CHK-WRITE-THRESHOLD-STRICT` |With `WIRQT` 1, `STATUS[2]` reads 0 with one queued word and 1 with
  two queued words, and 0 again after B pops one
|`CHK-STATUS-FOLLOWS-OCCUPANCY-NO-ACK` |`STATUS[2]` falls while `IRQS[0]` still reads 1 and no
  `IRQS` write was made, with `IRQEN` 0
|`CHK-READ-THRESHOLD-STRICT` |`B.STATUS[3]` reads 1 with `RIRQT` 0 and one received word, and with
  `RIRQT` 1 reads 0 at one word and 1 at two words
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-BITS-FALL-LIVE` |`STATUS[2]` and `B.STATUS[3]` fall to 0 as the occupancy falls;
  the procedure issues no `IRQS` write
|`CHK-CTRL-READS-ZERO-AFTER-WRITE` |`CTRL` writes of 0x1 and 0x2 answer `OKAY` and each later
  `CTRL` read answers `OKAY` with bits 1:0 equal to 0
|`CHK-CTRL-BOTH-BITS-OBSERVED` |Measures and prints the response to a `CTRL` write of 0x3 and the
  words drained from each side, requiring only that both drains end in the empty error
|`CHK-WFLUSH-DISCARDS-PEER-WORDS` |After a write flush on A, B's `READ_DATA` answers `SLVERR` with
  low word 0xFEEDDEAD although two words had been queued; `STATUS` is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-WFLUSH-CLEARS-FULL` |After a flush of the full write FIFO the next write answers `OKAY` and B
  pops it; the `STATUS` full bit is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-WFLUSH-KEEPS-OWN-READ-FIFO` |A's `READ_DATA` returns the word B had sent after a write flush
  on A
|`CHK-WFLUSH-EMPTY-HARMLESS` |`ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` read 0 before and after a write flush of an
  empty write FIFO
|`CHK-RFLUSH-EMPTIES-OWN-READ-FIFO` |After a read flush on A, A's `READ_DATA` answers `SLVERR` with
  low word 0xFEEDDEAD although B had sent a word; `STATUS` is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-RFLUSH-FREES-PEER` |After a flush of A's full read FIFO the peer's next write answers `OKAY`
  and A pops it; the `STATUS` full bit of B is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-RFLUSH-KEEPS-OWN-WRITE-FIFO` |B pops the word A had queued after a read flush on A
|`CHK-RFLUSH-EMPTY-HARMLESS` |`ERROR_FLAGS` and `IRQS` read 0 before and after a read flush of an
  empty read FIFO
|`CHK-WFLUSH-VS-PUSH-CONSISTENT` |Both grouped members answer `OKAY`, the word queued before the
  flush is never popped, at most the grouped word is popped, the FIFO ends in the empty error and a
  later word round-trips; whether the grouped word survives is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-RFLUSH-VS-PUSH-CONSISTENT` |Both grouped members answer `OKAY`, the word queued before the
  flush is never popped, at most the grouped word is popped, the FIFO ends in the empty error and a
  later word round-trips; whether the grouped word survives is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-FLUSH-VS-POP-NO-STALE-NO-STUCK` |Both grouped members complete, A's `READ_DATA` then answers
  `SLVERR` (no stale word) and a later word round-trips; the grouped read's result is recorded
  without comparing
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S16 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the eighteen checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound, the six-read drain loops and the SEP_IN access limit; the compare is each
  wait's own assertion, which fails the leaf on expiry, and the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twenty checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 100 SEP_IN
accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The `CTRL` 0x3 outcome, the `STATUS` empty
and full bits, the fate of the grouped words and the grouped read result are recorded and are not
part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: What a write of `CTRL` 0x3 does is not specified; its response and which FIFOs
drained are printed without a compare. `STATUS[1:0]` and the empty and full bits are printed, and
the `STATUS` words after the flushes are recorded without comparing. The grouped read is measured
only, and whether the word written in the same group as a flush is kept or discarded is printed,
because the specification does not state which; no cycle alignment is claimed. The zero reset value
of `CTRL` cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit). `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS`
lists the bounded waits as a record; the compare is each wait's own assertion.

'''''

[[sec-520-smc_mailbox_irq_ack_output_test]]
===== 520 `smc_mailbox_irq_ack_output_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_irq_ack_output_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including grouped access items, for the
registers of the inbound and outbound apertures of mailbox pairs 0, 1, 7, 15, 16 and 31 (`IRQS`,
`IRQEN`, `IRQP`, `RIRQT`, `WRITE_DATA`, `READ_DATA`, `ERROR_FLAGS`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`
(`MAILBOX_CG_EN`); `tb_top` probes `tb_mailbox_interrupts` (the 32 inbound-port interrupts),
`tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` (the same bits as they enter the SMC CPU interrupt vector) and
`tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` (the 32 outbound-port interrupts), sampled on `clk_smc_i` edges and
required resolvable; the scoreboard compares every access response and expected read value; the
bench nets `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for the bring-up
wait; the driver's own 50 microsecond access limit

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: IRQS acknowledge and the per-pair mailbox interrupt outputs.

*Test Coverage*:

* `IRQS` bits latch independently of `IRQEN`, reading does not clear them, and writing a 1 to a
  bit clears it; a written 0 changes nothing (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc`,
  Interrupts; `IRQS` is write-one-to-clear in `axil_mailbox.rdl`). With all three sources latched
  on one aperture `IRQS[2:0]` reads 0b111 twice, stays 0b111 after a write of 0x0 and reads 0b011
  after a write of 0x4. In that state `IRQS[1:0]` relatch while their occupancy conditions hold,
  so only `IRQS[2]` separates the cases there; the selective acknowledge and the read-not-clear
  legs are repeated on `IRQS[1:0]` after the conditions end.
* Threshold status can reassert if the occupancy condition remains true (`architecture.adoc`):
  after acknowledging bits 1:0 while both conditions hold they must read 0b11 again within 16
  reads; the read count is printed, and the timing is not compared. After the conditions end,
  reading twice returns 0b11 both times, a write of 0x1 leaves 0b10, and a further write of 0x2
  clears the bits so they read 0 on the next two reads.
* The error bit is separate: after an empty read `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b01, `IRQS[2]` still reads
  1 afterwards and clears only on the write of 0x4 (`interface.adoc`, Access Results). An
  acknowledge issued together with a write that raises the same bit is measured and printed
  without a compare; both members must answer `OKAY`.
* Interrupt output: each output bit is the OR of `IRQP = IRQS & IRQEN` for its aperture
  (`architecture.adoc`). On the inbound aperture of pair 1 each source alone (write threshold,
  read threshold, access error, one `IRQEN` bit at a time) raises `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to
  exactly 0x00000002 with `IRQP` equal to that source's bit, and the vector returns to 0 after
  the acknowledge. With `IRQEN` 0 each latched source leaves both vectors at 0 for 16 cycles.
  With `IRQP` bits 0 and 2 set the output stays 1 after bit 0 is acknowledged and falls after bit
  2, on the inbound and the outbound aperture.
* Placement: the 32 inbound-port interrupts are SMC CPU interrupts 288 to 319 and the 32
  outbound-port interrupts leave the SMC on `smc_ext_mailbox_interrupts_o`
  (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/index.adoc`, Overview; `interrupts.adoc`, SMC CPU Interrupt Vector
  Map). For pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 an inbound interrupt must raise exactly bit m of
  `tb_mailbox_interrupts` and of `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` with `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` 0,
  and an outbound interrupt exactly bit m of `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` with the inbound
  vector 0. Pair 16 is also driven outbound-only and inbound-only and both whole vectors compared.
* The output is a level: on pairs 15 and 16 both outputs read 1 at each of 16 consecutive cycles
  while `IRQP` is non-zero and fall after the acknowledge. Pairs 0 and 31 together give
  0x80000001 and, as each is acknowledged, 0x80000000 and 0, on both directions. On pair 7 the
  output holds at 0x00000080 across 512 idle cycles without AXI traffic; the idle state of the
  mailbox clock gate is not observed and the specification does not state it.
* Every probe wait is a per-cycle poll capped at 128 `clk_smc_i` cycles, a liveness ceiling and
  not a latency claim. The leaf requires at least 150 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have
  checked at least as many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with `MAILBOX_CG_EN` set and
  read it back; stamp step S1.
. Hold both interrupt vectors at 0 for four cycles; stamp S2.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of A on pair 1 (A outbound, B inbound). Kind: a third write
  after two words have filled the FIFO, with `IRQEN` cleared, `RIRQT` of A 0, every `IRQS` bit of
  both apertures acknowledged beforehand, and B sending a word to A. Expected response: the third
  write answers `SLVERR` and `IRQS` of A reads 0b111 on two reads; then write 0x0 and read, write
  0x4 and read. Stamp S3 and print the two lines.
. Write 0x3 to `IRQS` of A and read `IRQS[1:0]` up to 16 times until 0b11; stamp S4 and print the
  line.
. B pops A's two words and A pops the received word; read `IRQS[1:0]` twice requiring 0b11, write
  0x1 and read requiring 0b10, write 0x2 and read twice requiring 0; stamp S5 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` of A. Kind: an empty read after `ERROR_FLAGS` is drained.
  Expected response: `IRQS` reads 0b100, `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b01, `IRQS` still reads 0b100 after
  that read, and `IRQS` reads 0 after 0x4 is written; stamp S6 and print the line.
. Require `IRQS` 0, issue the group `IRQS` write 0x1 with a `WRITE_DATA` write on A, read `IRQS[0]`,
  B pops the word and both apertures are acknowledged; stamp S7 and print the line.
. For each source in turn, set one `IRQEN` bit on the inbound aperture of pair 1, raise the source,
  poll `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to 0x00000002 with the outbound vector 0, require `IRQP` equal to the
  source bit, end the condition, acknowledge and poll both vectors to 0; stamp S8 and print the
  line.
. With `IRQEN` 0 latch each source in turn, hold both vectors at 0 for 16 cycles, require the
  source bit in `IRQS`, end and acknowledge; stamp S9 and print the line.
. On the inbound and then the outbound aperture of pair 1, set `IRQEN` 0x7, latch `IRQS` bits 0 and
  2, poll the output to 1, require `IRQP` 0b101, end the occupancy condition, acknowledge bit 0,
  hold the output at 1 for 8 cycles and require `IRQP` 0b100, acknowledge bit 2 and poll to 0.
  Stamp S10 and print the line.
. For m = 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31, set `IRQEN` 0x1 on the inbound aperture of pair m, write one word,
  poll `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to bit m with `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` 0 and require
  `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` equal; end the condition, acknowledge and poll to 0. Stamp S11 and
  print the line.
. Repeat on the outbound apertures, polling `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` to bit m with the inbound
  vector 0; stamp S12 and print the line.
. On pairs 15 and 16 raise both apertures, poll both outputs to bit m, require `IRQP` equal to 0x1 on
  both, hold both outputs for 16 cycles, pop the words, acknowledge and poll to 0; stamp S13 and
  print the line.
. On pair 16 raise the outbound aperture only and poll the vectors to (0, bit 16), then the
  inbound aperture only and poll to (bit 16, 0); stamp S14 and print the line.
. Raise the inbound apertures of pairs 0 and 31 and poll to 0x80000001; acknowledge pair 0 and poll
  to 0x80000000, pair 31 and poll to 0; repeat on the outbound apertures. Stamp S15 and print the
  line.
. On pair 7 raise the inbound aperture, poll to 0x00000080, hold it for 512 cycles without AXI
  traffic, end the condition, acknowledge and poll to 0; stamp S16 and print the line.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S16 with strictly increasing
  stamps and the fifteen checker lines printed in order at their steps, print the non-vacuity line,
  then the bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ACK-CLEARS-ONLY-WRITTEN-BITS` |`IRQS[2:0]` of A reads 0b111, stays 0b111 after a write of 0x0
  and reads 0b011 after a write of 0x4; in that state only `IRQS[2]` separates the cases because
  `IRQS[1:0]` relatch while their conditions hold, and the selective acknowledge of bits 1:0 is
  checked after the conditions end
|`CHK-IRQS-READ-DOES-NOT-CLEAR` |Two consecutive `IRQS` reads both return 0b111; only `IRQS[2]` can
  fall on a clearing read there, and two reads of `IRQS[1:0]` after the conditions end both return
  0b11
|`CHK-ACK-REASSERTS-OBSERVED` |After acknowledging bits 1:0 while both occupancy conditions hold,
  `IRQS[1:0]` reads 0b11 again within 16 reads; the number of reads is recorded without comparing
  the timing
|`CHK-ACK-AFTER-CONDITION-STAYS-CLEAR` |`IRQS[1:0]` stays 0b11 on two reads after the pops, reads
  0b10 after a write of 0x1, and reads 0 after a write of 0x2 and 0 again on the next read
|`CHK-ACK-ERROR-BIT-SEPARATELY` |After an empty read `IRQS` reads 0b100, `ERROR_FLAGS` reads 0b01,
  `IRQS[2]` still reads 1 after that read, and reads 0 after the write of 0x4
|`CHK-ACK-VS-EVENT-OBSERVED` |Both members of the grouped `IRQS` acknowledge and `WRITE_DATA` write
  answer `OKAY`; `IRQS[0]` afterwards is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-OR-EACH-SOURCE-ALONE` |Each of the write threshold, read threshold and access error alone,
  with only its `IRQEN` bit set, raises `tb_mailbox_interrupts` to 0x00000002 inside the poll
  bound with `IRQP` equal to the source bit, and the vector returns to 0 after the acknowledge
|`CHK-OR-LATCHED-NOT-ENABLED` |With `IRQEN` 0 each latched source (`IRQS` non-zero, the positive
  control) leaves both vectors at 0 on 16 consecutive cycles
|`CHK-OR-CLEAR-ONE-OF-TWO` |With `IRQP` bits 0 and 2 set the output stays 1 for 8 cycles after bit 0
  is acknowledged and falls to 0 after bit 2, on the inbound and the outbound aperture
|`CHK-INBOUND-RAISES-OWN-BIT` |For pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 an inbound interrupt raises exactly
  bit m of `tb_mailbox_interrupts` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` with
  `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` 0, and the vector returns to 0 after the acknowledge
|`CHK-OUTBOUND-RAISES-OWN-BIT` |For the same five pairs an outbound interrupt raises exactly bit m
  of `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` with `tb_mailbox_interrupts` 0, and returns to 0 after the
  acknowledge
|`CHK-OUTPUT-IS-LEVEL-AND-FALLS` |On pairs 15 and 16 both outputs read 1 on each of 16 consecutive
  cycles while `IRQP` is non-zero and fall to 0 after the acknowledge
|`CHK-CROSS-ISOLATION-INBOUND-OUTBOUND` |On pair 16 an outbound-only interrupt leaves
  `tb_mailbox_interrupts` at 0 and sets only bit 16 of `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts`, and an
  inbound-only interrupt leaves `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` at 0 and sets only bit 16 of
  `tb_mailbox_interrupts`
|`CHK-TWO-PAIRS-INDEPENDENT` |Interrupts on pairs 0 and 31 give 0x80000001, acknowledging pair 0
  leaves 0x80000000 and acknowledging pair 31 leaves 0, on the inbound vector and on the outbound
  vector, with the other vector 0
|`CHK-OUTPUT-HOLDS-ACROSS-IDLE` |`tb_mailbox_interrupts` stays 0x00000080 on each of 512
  consecutive idle cycles after rising and falls to 0 after the acknowledge; the idle state of the
  clock gate is not observed
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound, every per-cycle probe poll with its 128-cycle cap and last vectors, and the
  SEP_IN access limit; the compare is each wait's own assertion, which fails the leaf on expiry,
  and the line is the record
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S16 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the fifteen checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seventeen checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 150
SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The reassertion read count and the
`IRQS[0]` value after the grouped acknowledge are recorded and are not part of the claim.
Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The number of reads until `IRQS[1:0]` reassert is recorded and the timing is not
compared; the `IRQS[0]` value after an acknowledge grouped with a write that raises the same bit is
measured and printed without a compare. The idle state of the mailbox clock gate is not observed and
the specification does not state it. Every probe wait is a liveness ceiling of 128 cycles, not a
latency claim. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the bounded waits as a record; the compare is each wait's
own assertion.

'''''

[[sec-521-smc_mailbox_pair_datapath_test]]
===== 521 `smc_mailbox_pair_datapath_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_pair_datapath_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including strobed writes and grouped access
items, for the `WRITE_DATA`, `READ_DATA` and `STATUS` registers of the outbound and inbound
apertures of mailbox pairs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 15, 16 and 31, and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`
(`MAILBOX_CG_EN`); the data words of the five-pair rounds are drawn from the logged
`RANDOM_SEED` (default 1); the scoreboard compares every access response and expected read value;
the bench nets `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for the
bring-up wait; the driver's own 50 microsecond access limit

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-REP: the seed draws the 64-bit words written through each pair.

*Objective*: Words written to one aperture pop from the peer aperture.

*Test Coverage*:

* Within pair N the outbound aperture writes FIFO A and reads FIFO B and the inbound aperture
  writes FIFO B and reads FIFO A, each FIFO two entries deep
  (`axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc`, Paired FIFOs; `index.adoc`, Overview;
  `periphs.adoc`). A seeded 64-bit word written with `OKAY` to one aperture must read back
  unchanged from the peer aperture on pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31, outbound to inbound and then
  inbound to outbound.
* A writer does not read its own word: after a write to outbound pair 15 its own `READ_DATA`
  answers `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD (empty read, `interface.adoc`, Access Results), and all
  eight `READ_DATA` registers of pairs 0, 1, 16 and 31 answer the same while the word sits in
  pair 15; the peer then returns the word. Writer `STATUS` is printed without a compare.
* With four words queued on pair 1 the outbound read returns the two inbound-written words in
  order and the inbound read returns the two outbound-written words in order.
* Partial writes: inactive byte lanes are stored as zero and a partial write does not merge with
  an existing word (`architecture.adoc`). Strobes 0x0F, 0xF0 and 0x01 of the same non-zero data
  word pop as the active lanes only; a full word followed by a 0x0F-strobed word pops as two
  separate entries and then the empty error; the two entries fill the FIFO so a third write
  answers `SLVERR`. A write with strobe 0x00 is not specified: its response, the peer's following read and any further words are printed and the
  drain must end in the empty error.
* Push with pop on one FIFO: three grouped accesses are issued together. With one word held, a
  write with a read returns the older word and leaves the new one for the next read, so the
  occupancy stays one. With the FIFO full, a write with a read returns the oldest word; the push
  response and the drained words are printed, since the specification does not state the
  outcome. With the FIFO empty, the write and read both complete and their responses and data are
  printed. No cycle alignment is claimed (`interface.adoc`, External Interface).
* The leaf requires at least 80 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have checked at least as
  many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with `MAILBOX_CG_EN` set and
  read it back; log the seed; stamp step S1.
. For pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 draw a word, write it to the outbound aperture and read the inbound
  aperture against it; stamp S2 and print the line.
. Repeat inbound to outbound on the same pairs; stamp S3 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: the writer's own `READ_DATA` of outbound pair 15 and both `READ_DATA`
  registers of pairs 0, 1, 16 and 31. Kind: reads of empty FIFOs while the written word sits in
  pair 15. Expected response: each answers the empty error, and the peer of pair 15 then returns
  the word. Write the word to outbound pair 15 first and read `STATUS` after the own read; stamp S4
  and print the two lines.
. On pair 1 write two words outbound and two inbound, read the outbound `READ_DATA` twice and the
  inbound twice against the words of the other side; stamp S5 and print the line.
. On pair 0 write one data word with strobes 0x0F, 0xF0 and 0x01, popping the peer each time
  against the active lanes; stamp S6 and print the line.
. Write a full word and a 0x0F-strobed word, pop the full word, the lane-masked word and then
  require the empty error; stamp S7 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA`. Kind: a write with strobe 0x00, which is not specified.
  Expected response: none is required beyond a response to each access and a drain that ends in the
  empty error; read the peer and drain until the empty error, recording the responses and data;
  stamp S8 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA`. Kind: a third write after a full word and a 0x0F-strobed
  word have filled the two entries. Expected response: the third write answers `SLVERR` with no
  other error response, and the peer pops both words against their values and then the empty
  error; stamp S9 and print the line.
. On pair 2 write a word, issue the group write with an inbound read against the first word, pop
  the second word and require the empty error; stamp S10 and print the line.
. On pair 3 fill the FIFO, issue the group write with a read against the oldest word, drain
  recording the words; stamp S11 and print the line.
. On pair 4 with empty FIFOs issue the group write with read, drain recording the words; stamp S12
  and print the line.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S12 with strictly increasing
  stamps and the twelve checker lines printed in order at their steps, print the non-vacuity line,
  then print the bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PAIR-FORWARD-PAIRS` |For pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 the word written with `OKAY` to the
  outbound aperture reads back unchanged, 64 bits, from the inbound aperture of the same pair
|`CHK-PAIR-REVERSE-PAIRS` |For the same five pairs the word written with `OKAY` to the inbound
  aperture reads back unchanged from the outbound aperture
|`CHK-PAIR-OWN-READ-FIFO-EMPTY` |The writer's own `READ_DATA` of pair 15 answers `SLVERR` with low
  word 0xFEEDDEAD, and the peer then returns the word; `STATUS` is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-PAIR-ISOLATION` |All eight `READ_DATA` reads of pairs 0, 1, 16 and 31 answer `SLVERR` with
  low word 0xFEEDDEAD while the word sits in pair 15, and pair 15's inbound read returns it
|`CHK-PAIR-BOTH-DIRECTIONS` |With four words queued on pair 1 the outbound `READ_DATA` returns the
  two inbound-written words in order and the inbound `READ_DATA` returns the two
  outbound-written words in order
|`CHK-PARTIAL-LANES-ZERO` |For strobes 0x0F, 0xF0 and 0x01 the peer pops 0x00000000C3C33C3C,
  0xA5A55A5A00000000 and 0x000000000000003C, so every inactive lane is zero and the active lanes
  are intact
|`CHK-PARTIAL-NO-MERGE` |A full word pops intact, the 0x0F-strobed word pops separately as
  0x0000000099AABBCC, and the third read is the empty error
|`CHK-PARTIAL-ZERO-STROBE-OBSERVED` |Measures and prints the response to a write with strobe 0x00,
  the peer's following read and any further words, requiring only a response to each access and
  that the drain ends in the empty error
|`CHK-PARTIAL-FILLS-FIFO` |A full word and a partial word fill the two entries, the third write
  answers `SLVERR`, and the peer pops the full word then 0x0000000055AA55AA and then the empty
  error
|`CHK-PUSHPOP-OCCUPANCY-ONE` |Both grouped members answer `OKAY`, the grouped read returns the
  older word, the next read returns the grouped write's word and the third read is the empty error
|`CHK-PUSHPOP-FULL-OBSERVED` |With the FIFO full the grouped read returns the oldest word; the push
  response and the drained words are recorded without comparing, and the drain ends in the empty
  error
|`CHK-PUSHPOP-EMPTY-OBSERVED` |With empty FIFOs both grouped members complete; their responses and
  data and the drained words are recorded without comparing, and the drain ends in the empty
  error
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S12 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the twelve checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound, the four-read drain loops and the SEP_IN access limit; the compare is each
  wait's own assertion, which fails the leaf on expiry, and the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all fourteen checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 80
SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The writer `STATUS`, the strobe-0x00
outcome, and the full-FIFO and empty-FIFO push-with-pop outcomes are recorded and are not part of
the claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Writer `STATUS` is printed without a compare. A write with strobe 0x00 is not
specified, so its response, the peer's following read and any further words are printed. With the
FIFO full, the push response and the drained words of the grouped write-with-read are printed, and
with the FIFO empty the responses and data of both members are printed, since the specification does
not state the outcome; no cycle alignment is claimed. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the bounded waits as
a record; the compare is each wait's own assertion.

'''''

[[sec-522-smc_mailbox_register_map_reset_test]]
===== 522 `smc_mailbox_register_map_reset_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_register_map_reset_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including grouped access items, for the
registers of the 64 mailbox apertures (outbound and inbound of pairs 0 to 31; `STATUS`,
`ERROR_FLAGS`, `WIRQT`, `RIRQT`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `IRQP`, `CTRL`, `WRITE_DATA`, `READ_DATA`),
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`MAILBOX_CG_EN`) and `SMC_ATTRIBUTES` of the CPU control block; `tb_top`
probes `tb_mailbox_interrupts`, `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` and `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]`
sampled on `clk_smc_i` edges and required resolvable; a `clk_smc_i` edge counter for one access
latency; the logged `RANDOM_SEED`; the scoreboard compares every access response and expected
read value; the bench nets `tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n`
for the bring-up wait; the driver's own 50 microsecond access limit

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: 64 mailbox apertures decode, reset clean and keep state.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.MAILBOX_CG_EN` resets to 0 and reads back 1 after it is set
  (`smc_base_config.rdl`); no mailbox access is made before it is set. The zero reset value cannot
  fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit).
* Reset state (`axil_mailbox.rdl`; `architecture.adoc`, Clock and Reset: reset empties the FIFOs
  and clears thresholds, error flags, interrupt status and enables): on both apertures of pairs 0,
  1, 15, 16 and 31 `STATUS[3:0]` reads 0x1 (empty) and `ERROR_FLAGS[1:0]`, all 64 bits of
  `WIRQT` and of `RIRQT`, `IRQS[2:0]`, `IRQEN[2:0]`, `IRQP[2:0]` and `CTRL[1:0]` read 0 (80 reads);
  masks and reset values come from the generated register header, and bits outside the defined
  fields are printed and not compared. The zero reset values here and in the 64-aperture and
  vector reads cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit); `STATUS[0]` = 1
  is the discriminating reset leg. All 64 apertures read
  `STATUS[3:0]` 0x1 and `IRQS[2:0]` 0 (128 reads). `READ_DATA` of both apertures of pairs 0 and 31
  answers `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD (`interface.adoc`, Access Results). The three interrupt
  vectors read 0 on two consecutive samples before any traffic.
* Aperture decode (`index.adoc`, Overview; `memmap.adoc`, Address Examples; `smc.rdl`, the
  `smc_mailbox` instance at offset 0x001_8000 from the SMC base 0xC000_0000, i.e. 0xC0018000): the
  outbound aperture of pair m is at 0xC0018000 + m x 0x1000 and the inbound aperture 0x800 above
  it. Distinct
  `IRQEN` patterns 1 to 5 written to the outbound apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 read
  back on those apertures and read 0 on the five inbound apertures, and the same for the inbound
  apertures against the outbound ones.
* Register offsets on both apertures of pair 0 (`axil_mailbox.rdl` address map): `WRITE_DATA` reads
  `OKAY` with low word 0xFEEDC0DE, `READ_DATA` reads `SLVERR` with 0xFEEDDEAD, `STATUS[3:0]` reads
  0x1, `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQP` and `CTRL` read 0, and `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` each read
  back only the value written at its own offset. `WIRQT` written on the pair-15 outbound aperture
  reads 1 there and 0 on the pair-15 inbound, pair-14 outbound and pair-16 outbound apertures.
  The pair-0 `READ_DATA` addresses are 0xC0018008 outbound and 0xC0018808 inbound, and a word
  written at one aperture pops at the peer's address.
* `SMC_ATTRIBUTES.mailbox_depth` bits [39:36] and `num_mailboxes` bits [45:40]
  (`cpu_ctrl.rdl`) are read, required resolvable and printed raw. The specification does not state
  how the fields encode the count, so they are not compared. On pair 31 the first two writes
  answer `OKAY` and pop in order and the third answers `SLVERR` (the SMC mailbox depth is 2,
  `periphs.adoc`).
* Interrupt outputs have a positive control: a pair-31 error on the outbound aperture with
  `IRQEN[2]` set raises `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` to bit 31 with the inbound vector and
  `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` 0, and one on the inbound aperture raises `tb_mailbox_interrupts`
  and `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` to bit 31 with the outbound vector 0; each falls after the
  acknowledge and `IRQEN` clear. Each poll is capped at 64 `clk_smc_i` cycles.
* Idle gap (the `OKAY` response and the retained values are the leaf's own requirement; no
  document states a mailbox-specific first-access or retention value): after an idle gap of 512
  `clk_smc_i` cycles the first write answers `OKAY` and pops back intact; its completion latency
  in cycles is measured and printed without a compare. `WIRQT` 1, `IRQEN` 0x5 and a queued word
  survive a second 512-cycle gap. Two grouped writes followed by two grouped reads, issued without
  a gap, complete with `OKAY` and return the words in order.
* The leaf requires at least 300 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have checked at least as
  many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o` and log the seed; stamp step S1.
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` requiring `MAILBOX_CG_EN` 0, write it set and read it back requiring the
  bit set; stamp S2 and print the line.
. Sample the three interrupt vectors, wait one cycle and sample again, requiring 0 on all; stamp
  S3.
. Read the eight registers of both apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 against their reset
  values, recording bits outside the defined fields; stamp S4 and print the line.
. Read `STATUS` and `IRQS` of all 64 apertures; stamp S5 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` of both apertures of pairs 0 and 31. Kind: a read while the
  FIFO is empty after reset. Expected response: `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD, with `IRQS[2]`
  and the read-error flag latched on each; then acknowledge `IRQS[2]`; stamp S6 and print the line.
. Compare the five pairs' aperture addresses with the formula, write `IRQEN` 1 to 5 on the outbound
  apertures, read the five outbound and the five inbound `IRQEN` back, restore 0; repeat on the
  inbound apertures. Stamp S7 and print the two lines.
. On both pair-0 apertures read `WRITE_DATA`, `STATUS`, `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQP` and `CTRL`,
  write and read back `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` checking the other two, restore 0, make the empty
  `READ_DATA` read, read `ERROR_FLAGS` and acknowledge `IRQS[2]`; stamp S8 and print the line.
. Write `WIRQT` 1 on the pair-15 outbound aperture, read `WIRQT` of four apertures, restore 0;
  stamp S9 and print the line.
. Compare the pair-0 `READ_DATA` addresses, then push a word at each side and pop it at the peer's
  address; stamp S10 and print the line.
. Read `SMC_ATTRIBUTES` as 64 bits and require it resolvable; stamp S11 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of the pair-31 outbound aperture, then `READ_DATA` of the
  pair-31 inbound aperture. Kind: a third write to the two-entry FIFO with `IRQEN[2]` set, and an
  empty read on the inbound aperture. Expected response: the third write answers `SLVERR` and the
  outbound vector polls to bit 31, then to 0 after the acknowledge and `IRQEN` clear; the inbound
  repeat does the same on its vector. Write two words and set `IRQEN[2]` first; after the poll pop
  both words, read `ERROR_FLAGS`, acknowledge, clear `IRQEN` and poll to 0; repeat inbound. Stamp
  S12 and print the pair-depth line and the vector line.
. Idle 512 cycles, write a word on pair 5 timing the access in cycles, pop it; stamp S13 and print
  the line.
. On pair 6 write a word, `WIRQT` 1 and `IRQEN` 0x5, idle 512 cycles, read `WIRQT` and `IRQEN`
  requiring 1 and 0x5 and pop the word, then restore; stamp S14 and print the line.
. On pair 8 issue a group of two writes and then a group of two reads against the written words;
  stamp S15 and print the line.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S15 with strictly increasing
  stamps and the fifteen checker lines printed in order at their steps, print the non-vacuity
  line, then print the bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CG-ENABLE-RESET-AND-SET` |`MAILBOX_CG_EN` reads 0 at reset and reads 1 after it is set over
  SEP_IN; the zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit); `STATUS[0]` = 1 is the discriminating reset leg
|`CHK-IRQ-VECTORS-LOW-AT-RESET` |`tb_mailbox_interrupts`, `tb_ext_mailbox_interrupts` and
  `tb_cpu_interrupts[319:288]` read 0 on two consecutive samples before any traffic, and the
  pair-31 positive control raises and then clears the outbound and inbound outputs as stated; the
  zero vector reads cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit)
|`CHK-RESET-REGISTERS-REPRESENTATIVE-PAIRS` |On both apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31,
  `STATUS[3:0]` reads 0x1 and the defined bits of `ERROR_FLAGS`, all 64 bits of `WIRQT` and
  `RIRQT`, and the defined bits of `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `IRQP` and `CTRL` read 0; bits outside the
  defined fields are recorded without comparing; the zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit); `STATUS[0]` = 1 is the discriminating reset leg
|`CHK-RESET-ALL-64-APERTURES` |All 64 apertures read `STATUS[3:0]` 0x1 and `IRQS[2:0]` 0; the zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit); `STATUS[0]` = 1 is the discriminating reset leg
|`CHK-RESET-EMPTY-READ-BOTH-DIRECTIONS` |`READ_DATA` of the outbound and inbound apertures of pairs
  0 and 31 answers `SLVERR` with low word 0xFEEDDEAD after reset
|`CHK-APERTURE-DECODE-OUTBOUND` |The outbound addresses of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31 equal
  0xC0018000 + m x 0x1000, and outbound `IRQEN` patterns 1 to 5 read back while the five inbound
  `IRQEN` read 0
|`CHK-APERTURE-DECODE-INBOUND` |The inbound addresses equal the outbound address + 0x800, and
  inbound `IRQEN` patterns 1 to 5 read back while the five outbound `IRQEN` read 0
|`CHK-REGISTER-OFFSETS-PAIR0` |On both pair-0 apertures `WRITE_DATA` reads `OKAY` with low word
  0xFEEDC0DE, `READ_DATA` reads `SLVERR` with 0xFEEDDEAD, `STATUS[3:0]` reads 0x1,
  `ERROR_FLAGS`, `IRQS`, `IRQP` and `CTRL` read 0, and `WIRQT`, `RIRQT` and `IRQEN` each read back
  only their own written value
|`CHK-REGISTER-STATE-PER-APERTURE` |`WIRQT` of the pair-15 outbound aperture reads 1 after the
  write while the pair-15 inbound, pair-14 outbound and pair-16 outbound apertures read 0
|`CHK-ADDRESS-EXAMPLES-PAIR0` |The pair-0 `READ_DATA` addresses are 0xC0018008 outbound and
  0xC0018808 inbound, the word written at outbound `WRITE_DATA` pops at 0xC0018808, and the word
  written at inbound `WRITE_DATA` pops at 0xC0018008
|`CHK-ATTRIBUTES-OBSERVED` |`SMC_ATTRIBUTES` reads resolvable data; the `mailbox_depth` and
  `num_mailboxes` fields are recorded raw without comparing
|`CHK-PAIR31-DEPTH-TWO` |On pair 31 the first two writes answer `OKAY` and pop in
  order and the third write to the two-entry FIFO answers `SLVERR`
|`CHK-CG-FIRST-ACCESS-AFTER-IDLE` |After the idle gap the write answers `OKAY` and the pop returns
  the written word; the completion latency is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-CG-RETENTION-ACROSS-IDLE` |After the idle gap `WIRQT` reads 1 (all 64 bits compared), `IRQEN[2:0]` reads 0x5 and
  the queued word pops unchanged
|`CHK-CG-BACK-TO-BACK-IN-ORDER` |Two grouped writes and two grouped reads all answer `OKAY` and the
  reads return the written words in order
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S15 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the fifteen checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound, the 64-cycle vector polls, the fixed idle gaps and the SEP_IN access limit;
  the compare is each wait's own assertion, which fails the leaf on expiry, and the line is the
  record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seventeen checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 300
SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The reserved upper bits, the
`SMC_ATTRIBUTES` field values and the first-access latency are recorded and are not part of the
claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Bits outside the defined fields of the reset registers are printed and not compared.
`SMC_ATTRIBUTES.mailbox_depth` and `num_mailboxes` are printed raw and not compared, because the
specification does not state how the fields encode the count. The completion latency of the first
write after the idle gap is measured and printed without a compare; no document states a
mailbox-specific first-access or retention value. The zero reset values and vector reads cannot fail
on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit); `STATUS[0]` = 1 is the discriminating
reset leg. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the bounded waits as a record; the compare is each wait's own
assertion.

'''''

[[sec-523-smc_mailbox_threshold_irqs_test]]
===== 523 `smc_mailbox_threshold_irqs_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: MAILBOX

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_threshold_irqs_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP), including grouped access items, for the
registers of mailbox pair 6, outbound aperture A and inbound aperture B (`WIRQT`, `RIRQT`,
`STATUS`, `IRQS`, `IRQEN`, `IRQP`, `WRITE_DATA`, `READ_DATA`), the `IRQS` of the outbound and
inbound apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16 and 31, and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`MAILBOX_CG_EN`); the
scoreboard compares every access response and expected read value; the bench nets
`tb_fuse_sense_done`, `tb_fuse_reset_n` and `tb_rst_warm_smc_clk_n` for the bring-up wait; the
driver's own 50 microsecond access limit; no interrupt output probe is read

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/mailbox.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Thresholds, IRQS latches and the IRQEN gate into IRQP.

*Test Coverage*:

* Thresholds and `IRQS` after reset (`axil_mailbox.rdl`; `architecture.adoc`, Clock and Reset and
  Interrupts): `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` (all 64 bits compared) of A and B read 0 and read back 0, 1 and 0
  as written; `IRQS[2:0]` reads 0 on the outbound and inbound apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16, 31
  and 6 before any traffic. The zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state
  build (bench limit); the 0, 1, 0 read-back is the discriminating part.
* Strictness and clamp (`architecture.adoc`: the status bits fire when occupancy is strictly
  greater than the threshold, and threshold writes are clamped to the FIFO depth minus one, which
  is 1 for the depth-2 SMC mailbox, `periphs.adoc`): for written values 2, 5 and 0xFF the
  above-threshold bit reads 0 with one queued word and 1 with two words, on `STATUS[2]` with
  `WIRQT` and on `B.STATUS[3]` with `RIRQT`. The read-back of the clamped value is printed, as are
  `STATUS[2]` with one word and the `WIRQT` read-back for the wider values 0x100 and 0x10000; the
  document does not say how values above the byte are held, so neither is compared.
* Threshold 0 detects any word: with `WIRQT` of A 0 one queued word sets `STATUS[2]` and `IRQS[0]`,
  and with `RIRQT` of B 0 one received word sets `B.STATUS[3]` and `IRQS[1]`; the `STATUS` bits fall
  after the pops. The maximum useful threshold, 1, fires only when full: with it one word leaves
  `STATUS` and `IRQS` bits at 0 and two words set both, on both sides.
* The four threshold registers are independent: after `WIRQT` of A 1 and the other three 0,
  writing `RIRQT` of A leaves the other three unchanged.
* `IRQS` latches its own source independently of `IRQEN` and survives the end of the condition
  (`architecture.adoc`): with `IRQEN` 0 a queued word gives `IRQS[2:0]` 0b001 and `IRQP` 0, a
  received word gives 0b010 and `IRQP` 0, an empty read gives 0b100, and a full write with two
  words above `WIRQT` 1 gives 0b101. After B pops the word `IRQS[0]` stays 1 while `STATUS[2]`
  falls. A threshold crossing and a full write issued together as one group leave `IRQS[2:0]` 0b101;
  no cycle alignment is claimed.
* `IRQP` is `IRQS` AND `IRQEN` (`architecture.adoc`; `IRQP` in `axil_mailbox.rdl`): with
  `IRQS[2:0]` latched at 0b111 and `IRQEN` written 0 to 7, `IRQEN` reads back as written, `IRQS`
  stays 0b111 and `IRQP` equals `IRQS` AND `IRQEN`. Enabling `IRQEN` 0x7 raises `IRQP` to 0b111 on
  the first read after the write and writing 0 drops `IRQP` to 0 with `IRQS` still 0b111. After
  each of two grouped `IRQEN` changes (with a `WRITE_DATA` write, and with a `STATUS` read) `IRQP`
  equals `IRQS` AND `IRQEN` on reads made after the group completed.
* The leaf requires at least 150 SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard to have checked at least as
  many.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for `smc_fuse_sense_done_o`, log the seed; read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with
  `MAILBOX_CG_EN` set and read it back; stamp step S1.
. Read `IRQS` of the twelve apertures requiring 0, read `WIRQT` and `RIRQT` of A and B requiring 0,
  write each 0, 1, 0 reading back; stamp S2 and print the two lines.
. Error injection. Point: `WIRQT` of A, then `RIRQT` of B. Kind: threshold writes of 2, 5 and 0xFF,
  above the depth minus one the register clamps to. Expected response: for each value the
  above-threshold `STATUS` bit reads 0 after A writes one word and 1 after a second (`B.STATUS` for
  `RIRQT`); the threshold read-back is recorded. After each value B pops both words and `IRQS` is
  acknowledged; stamp S3 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WIRQT` of A. Kind: the wider values 0x100 and 0x10000, above the byte.
  Expected response: none is required; `STATUS[2]` with one queued word and the threshold read-back
  are printed. Queue one word after each write, read `STATUS[2]` and the threshold, pop and
  acknowledge; stamp S4 and print the line.
. With threshold 0 on `WIRQT` of A queue a word, require `STATUS[2]` and `IRQS[0]` set, pop and
  require `STATUS[2]` clear; repeat for `RIRQT` of B with `STATUS[3]` and `IRQS[1]`; stamp S5 and
  print the line.
. With threshold 1 queue one word then a second on A requiring the `STATUS` and `IRQS` bits clear
  then set, pop both, and repeat for B; stamp S6 and print the line.
. Write the four thresholds 1, 0, 0, 0, read all four, write `RIRQT` of A 1 and read all four again;
  stamp S7 and print the line.
. With `IRQEN` 0 and `WIRQT` of A 0, A writes a word; require `IRQS` 0b001 and `IRQP` 0, B pops, and
  require `IRQS[0]` still set with `STATUS[2]` clear; stamp S8 and print the line.
. With `RIRQT` of B 0, A sends a word; require B's `IRQS` 0b010 and `IRQP` 0, B pops; stamp S9.
. Error injection. Point: `READ_DATA` and then `WRITE_DATA` of A. Kind: an empty read, and after
  the acknowledge a third write above `WIRQT` 1 to the full FIFO. Expected response: `IRQS` reads
  0b100 after the empty read, the third write answers `SLVERR` and `IRQS` then reads 0b101. Set
  `WIRQT` 1 after the acknowledge; drain through B; stamp S10 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: `WRITE_DATA` of A, with one word queued and `WIRQT` 1. Kind: a grouped
  pair of a write that fills the FIFO and a write that overflows it, issued together. Expected
  response: the members answer `OKAY` and `SLVERR` and `IRQS` reads 0b101; drain; stamp S11 and
  print the line.
. Latch `IRQS` 0b111 on A, then for `IRQEN` 0 to 7 write it and require the read-back, `IRQS` 0b111
  and `IRQP` equal to `IRQS` AND `IRQEN`; stamp S12 and print the line.
. With `IRQEN` 0 read `IRQP` requiring 0, write `IRQEN` 0x7 and read `IRQP` requiring 0b111, write 0
  and require `IRQP` 0 with `IRQS` 0b111; drain and acknowledge; stamp S13 and print the two lines.
. With one word queued issue the group `IRQEN` 1 with a `WRITE_DATA` write and then the group
  `IRQEN` 0 with a `STATUS` read, reading `IRQS`, `IRQEN` and `IRQP` after each and requiring `IRQS` 0b001, the `IRQEN` value and
  `IRQP` equal to 0b001 AND `IRQEN`; drain and acknowledge; stamp S14 and print the line.
. Restore `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S14 with strictly increasing
  stamps and the fourteen checker lines printed in order at their steps, print the non-vacuity
  line, then print the bounded-wait line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-RESET-AND-INRANGE` |`WIRQT` and `RIRQT` of A and B read 0 at reset and read back
  exactly 0, 1 and 0 after those writes; the zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under
  the 2-state build (bench limit)
|`CHK-IRQS-ZERO-AFTER-RESET` |`IRQS[2:0]` reads 0 with `OKAY` responses on the outbound and inbound
  apertures of pairs 0, 1, 15, 16, 31 and 6 before any traffic; the zero reset values cannot fail
  on a missing reset under the 2-state build (bench limit)
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-CLAMP-BEHAVIOUR` |For written values 2, 5 and 0xFF the above-threshold `STATUS` bit
  reads 0 with one queued word and 1 with two, on `WIRQT` and on `RIRQT`; the threshold read-back
  is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-WIDE-VALUE-OBSERVED` |Measures and prints `STATUS[2]` with one queued word and the
  `WIRQT` read-back after writing 0x100 and 0x10000, without a compare
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-ZERO-DETECTS-ANY-WORD` |With threshold 0 one queued word sets `STATUS[2]` and
  `IRQS[0]` on A and one received word sets `B.STATUS[3]` and `IRQS[1]` on B, and the `STATUS`
  bits read 0 after the pops
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-MAX-FIRES-ONLY-FULL` |With threshold 1 one word leaves `STATUS[2]` and `IRQS[0]`
  (and `B.STATUS[3]` and `IRQS[1]`) at 0 and a full FIFO sets both to 1
|`CHK-THRESHOLD-INDEPENDENT-PER-REGISTER` |The four threshold registers read 1, 0, 0, 0 as written
  and, after `RIRQT` of A is written 1, read 1, 1, 0, 0
|`CHK-IRQS-LATCHES-OWN-SOURCE` |With `IRQEN` 0 a queued word gives `IRQS[2:0]` 0b001 with `IRQP` 0,
  a received word 0b010 with `IRQP` 0, an empty read 0b100, and a full write above `WIRQT` 1
  0b101
|`CHK-IRQS-STAYS-AFTER-CONDITION-ENDS` |`IRQS[0]` stays 1 after B pops the word while `STATUS[2]`
  falls to 0
|`CHK-IRQS-OVERLAPPING-SOURCES` |A threshold crossing and a full-write error issued together leave
  `IRQS[2:0]` equal to 0b101, with the members answering `OKAY` and `SLVERR`
|`CHK-IRQP-IS-IRQS-AND-IRQEN` |For `IRQEN` 0 to 7 with `IRQS[2:0]` 0b111, `IRQEN` reads back as
  written and `IRQP[2:0]` equals `IRQS` AND `IRQEN`
|`CHK-IRQP-RAISES-ON-ENABLE-AT-ONCE` |With `IRQS` 0b111 latched and `IRQEN` 0, `IRQP` reads 0, and
  the first `IRQP` read after `IRQEN` 0x7 is written returns 0b111
|`CHK-IRQP-FALLS-ON-DISABLE-IRQS-KEEPS` |After `IRQEN` is written 0, `IRQP` reads 0 while `IRQS`
  still reads 0b111
|`CHK-IRQP-FOLLOWS-LIVE-ENABLE-CHANGE` |After each grouped `IRQEN` change, `IRQEN` reads back as
  written, `IRQS[2:0]` is exactly 0b001 and `IRQP[2:0]` equals 0b001 AND `IRQEN` on reads made after
  the group completed
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S14 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the fourteen checker lines printed in order, each after its step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists the bounded waits of the run: the three bring-up net waits with their
  200000-rise bound and the SEP_IN access limit; the compare is each wait's own assertion, which
  fails the leaf on expiry, and the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all sixteen checkers hold after their compares; the leaf issues at least 150
SEP_IN accesses and the scoreboard checks at least that many. The clamped and wide threshold
read-backs are recorded and are not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The read-back of the clamped threshold values 2, 5 and 0xFF, and `STATUS[2]` with one
word and the `WIRQT` read-back for the wider values 0x100 and 0x10000, are printed and not compared,
because the document does not say how values above the byte are held. No cycle alignment of the
grouped accesses is claimed. The zero reset values cannot fail on a missing reset under the 2-state
build (bench limit); the 0, 1, 0 read-back is the discriminating part. `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` lists the
bounded waits as a record; the compare is each wait's own assertion.

'''''
