[[smc-vplan-area-uart]]
==== UART

[[sec-149-smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test]]
===== 149 `smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `uart`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 divisor x frame-format sweep, every axis observed where it is visible: frame timing and content on the TX pad, a driven frame on the RX pad, and the parity and framing detectors shown able to assert.

*Test Coverage*:

* Divisors 1 and 8 x the 16 WLS/STB/PEN/EPS combinations (stick parity excluded), 32 in all, with `MCR.LOOP` clear so the frames leave on pad 12 and enter on pad 11. Under `MCR.LOOP` the transmitter and receiver share one setting and every combination deframes the same byte, so the divisor, stop-bit and parity axes would be unfalsifiable there.
* TX pad: three queued bytes are decoded at simulation-time resolution on `tb_uart0_tx_from_dut` -- start bit, every data bit, parity bit and stop bit sampled at their bit centres -- and the shortest interval between consecutive start bits is compared with `(1 + data + parity + stop) x 16 x (DLL + 1)` `clk_periph_i` periods, with the stop count 1, 2 or 1.5 per `LCR.STB` and the word length and parity polarity per `LCR.WLS`/`LCR.PEN`/`LCR.EPS` (`uart_16550_main.rdl`). Each axis moves that measurement, so a DUT ignoring `DLL`, `STB`, `PEN` or `EPS` fails.
* RX pad: one frame in the same format is driven on `tb_uart0_rx_ext_drive` and read back through `RBR` with `LSR` clear of OE/PE/FE/BI.
* Error detectors: at each divisor a frame with the wrong parity bit raises `LSR.PE` and a frame with a low stop bit raises `LSR.FE`, both cleared again after the character is popped, so the no-error compares rest on detectors shown to fire in the same run.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test_seq`: ungate the UART clock and enable the UART0 pad function, then for each divisor and format program `DLL`/`DLH`/`LCR`, reset both FIFOs, queue three bytes and decode them on the TX pad, drive one frame on the RX pad and read it back, and after the sixteen formats drive the parity-error and framing-error frames. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-BAUD-BASIC` |All 32 combinations completed, each with its frame length measured, and both error controls asserted (`smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-UART-BAUD-FMT` |One per combination: the three TX pad frames decoded to the queued bytes masked to the word length with the parity bit matching `EPS`, the shortest start-to-start interval equals one frame of the programmed format within two baud ticks, no interval is shorter than a frame, and the RX pad frame read back exactly through `RBR` with no LSR error (`smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-UART-FMT-FE-ASSERTS` |At each divisor a frame with a low stop bit sets `LSR.FE` with `DR`, and `FE` is clear after the pop (`smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-UART-FMT-PE-ASSERTS` |At each divisor an 8E1 frame with the parity bit inverted sets `LSR.PE` with `DR`, and `PE` is clear after the pop (`smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test_seq.py`)
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-BAUD-BASIC`, `CHK-UART-BAUD-FMT`, `CHK-UART-FMT-FE-ASSERTS`, `CHK-UART-FMT-PE-ASSERTS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: Stick parity is excluded from the format sweep; the 32 combinations cover divisors 1
and 8 with the 16 WLS/STB/PEN/EPS settings only.
'''''

[[sec-150-smc_uart_error_conditions_test]]
===== 150 `smc_uart_error_conditions_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_error_conditions_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `uart`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; args `+smc_uart_cross_3to0`; tool Verilator
(cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 parity / overrun / break and UART1-3 line status, loopback, THRE and FIFO access.

*Test Coverage*:

* UART0 parity mismatch, RX overrun, and break/framing.
* Requires +smc_uart_cross_3to0; the UART1-3 legs use the cross-wired pairs UART1<->UART2 and UART3<->UART0, so each receiver's frames come from its peer.
* UART1-3 receive break, parity and framing errors with IER.ELSI on and off: LSR BI / PE / FE on the first read and bits 4:2 = 0 once RBR is drained, IIR ID 0x3 only with ELSI=1 (IIR is polled once the sender reads LSR.TEMT=1 and before the receiver's first LSR read; the ELSI=0 legs enable ERBFI only and require IIR=0xC4, so the erroring character is shown received), no error on the instances not receiving. The second LSR read before the drain is logged, not compared (SF-041).
* UART1-3 MCR.LOOP keeps the byte inside the instance and off its peer; with LOOP=0 the byte reaches the peer only.
* UART1-3 IIR THRE lifecycle: set with the TX FIFO empty, cleared by the IIR read with LSR.THRE still 1, re-armed by a drained character, ranked below a pending parity error and reported again once RBR is drained and LSR read. The IIR read right after the first LSR read is logged, not compared (SF-041).
* UART1-3 ITR.TTBEI forces IIR ID 0x1 while the TX FIFO is non-empty and releases it.
* UART1-3 FCR.XMIT_FIFO_RESET discards the queued characters (at most the first leaves the line) and leaves the received byte in place.
* UART1-3 THR writes past the FIFO depth inside one frame and an RBR read with the RX FIFO empty: LSR.DR stays 0; the bus responses, IIR, LSR, the combined interrupt line and the characters the peer receives are logged against SF-018.
* The combined interrupt line `tb_uart_irq_combined` is logged at each error, OUT2, ITR and FIFO-access observation and never compared (SF-001).
* UART1-3 MCR.OUT2 does not gate the interrupt: with ITR.TTBEI forcing, IIR reads 0xC2 after each OUT2 write.
* Not covered: the MCR DTR / OUT1 / OUT2 pad levels (SF-042). `smc_peripherals` leaves `uart_dtr_no`, `uart_out1_no` and `uart_out2_no` unconnected and the bench has no probe for them; MCR=0x0D / 0x00 is written as stimulus only.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-ERR-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-ERR-BI` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-ERR-OE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-ERR-OE-NEG` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-ERR-PE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-ERR-PE-NEG` |Named compare in `smc_uart_error_conditions_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART13-BREAK` |A two-frame break from the peer gives BI=1 on UART1-3, with ERROR_IN_RCVR_FIFO=1 and IIR=0xC6 under ELSI=1 and no ID 0x3 under ELSI=0; the other receivers read LSR bits 4:1 = 0; LSR bits 4:2 = 0 after the RBR drain
|`CHK-UART13-PARITY` |Odd parity into an even-parity receiver gives PE=1, IIR=0xC6 under ELSI=1 and no ID 0x3 under ELSI=0; the other receivers read no line-status error; LSR bits 4:2 = 0 after the RBR drain
|`CHK-UART13-FRAMING` |A 0 at the 5-bit receiver's stop position gives FE=1 with BI=0, IIR=0xC6 under ELSI=1 and no ID 0x3 under ELSI=0; LSR bits 4:2 = 0 after the RBR drain
|`CHK-UART13-LSR-RC` |For every BI, PE and FE leg the first LSR read returns the error and the LSR read after the RBR drain returns bits 4:2 = 0; the second read before the drain is logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-041)
|`CHK-UART13-MCR-LOOP` |LOOP=1: the instance reads its byte back and the peer reads DR=0; LOOP=0: the peer reads the byte and the instance reads DR=0
|`CHK-UART13-OUT2-IIR` |With ITR.TTBEI forcing, IIR reads 0xC2 after each MCR.OUT2 write; the combined line is logged (SF-001)
|`CHK-UART13-IIR-THRE` |IIR 0xC2 then 0xC1 with LSR.THRE=1 on an empty TX FIFO, 0xC2 after a drained character, 0xC6 with a parity error also pending and 0xC2 after the RBR drain and an LSR read; the IIR read right after the first LSR read is logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-041)
|`CHK-UART13-ITR-THRE` |With the TX FIFO non-empty ITR.TTBEI=1 makes IIR read 0xC2 and ITR=0 makes it read 0xC1
|`CHK-UART13-XMIT-RESET` |After FCR.XMIT_FIFO_RESET LSR.THRE=1, the peer receives at most the first queued character, and the received byte 0x6E stays readable
|`CHK-UART13-FIFO-ACCESS-OBS` |LSR.DR=0 after an RBR read with the RX FIFO empty; the THR-overflow and RBR-underflow indications are logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-018)
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence BRINGUP < UART13_BREAK < ... < UART13_FIFO_ACCESS after the UART0 legs, each step stamped after its checker lines
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One entry per bounded wait of the UART1-3 legs with its bound and last observed state (an expiry fails naming the UART and its last LSR, IIR and line), the fixed collection windows listed as windows, and the pre-existing UART0-leg waits with their bounds and expiry messages
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-ERR-BASIC`, `CHK-UART-ERR-BI`, `CHK-UART-ERR-OE`, `CHK-UART-ERR-OE-NEG`, `CHK-UART-ERR-PE`, `CHK-UART-ERR-PE-NEG`, `CHK-UART13-BREAK`, `CHK-UART13-PARITY`, `CHK-UART13-FRAMING`, `CHK-UART13-LSR-RC`, `CHK-UART13-MCR-LOOP`, `CHK-UART13-OUT2-IIR`, `CHK-UART13-IIR-THRE`, `CHK-UART13-ITR-THRE`, `CHK-UART13-XMIT-RESET`, `CHK-UART13-FIFO-ACCESS-OBS`, `CHK-NONVAC`, `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-151-smc_uart_extremes_misc_test]]
===== 151 `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `uart`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 SCR R/W + idle LSR.DR quiet check.

*Test Coverage*:

* UART0 SCR R/W without LCR/MCR/ECR side-effects; idle LSR has no DR.
* DEFENDS: only LSR.DR in the idle window, and only because this sequence has a same-run positive control (`_positive_dr_then_idle`) that drives DR to 1 and back to 0, so a stuck-at-0 DR fails.
* DOES NOT DEFEND: LSR.OE/PE/FE/BI. Nothing in this sequence can drive those bits to 1, so an idle-window check on them would be an unbacked negative that a tied-off bit passes identically. They are claimed by `smc_uart_error_conditions_test`, which raises PE and OE individually and break as FE and BI together, each and back; no testcase in this package raises FE on its own.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-EXT-BASIC` |Named compare in `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-EXT-DR-POS` |Named compare in `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-EXT-IDLE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-EXT-SCR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_extremes_misc_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-EXT-BASIC`, `CHK-UART-EXT-DR-POS`, `CHK-UART-EXT-IDLE`, `CHK-UART-EXT-SCR` hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: `LSR.OE`, `PE`, `FE` and `BI` are not defended in the idle window, because nothing in
this sequence can drive them to 1; they are claimed by `smc_uart_error_conditions_test`. Only
`LSR.DR` is checked idle, backed by the same-run positive control.
'''''

[[sec-152-smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test]]
===== 152 `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `uart`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 IER gating, natural clears, and multi-source IIR priority.

*Test Coverage*:

* UART0 IER/ITR: FIFO_ERROR > LSR > TIMEOUT > RDR > THRE > MODEM. Every adjacent pair of the chain is contested through the Interrupt Test Register (FIFO/LSR, LSR/TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT/RDR, RDR/THRE, THRE/MODEM), plus LSR/RDR; the winner each contest requires comes from the IIR priority ranking in `uart_16550_main.rdl`.
* Each modem-status delta on its own. With `MCR.LOOP` set, the UART programming guide feeds DSR from DTR, RI from OUT1 and DCD from OUT2. The leaf changes one of those outputs at a time and requires the MSR deltas to be exactly DDSR, TERI or DDCD, raising the modem interrupt, which the MSR read clears. TERI marks only RI's trailing edge, so OUT1 is first set, which must raise no delta, and then cleared.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-MSR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-RDR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-THRE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-FIFO` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-LSR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-MODEM` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-RDR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-THRE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-MAP-TIMEOUT` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-FIFO_vs_LSR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-LSR_vs_RDR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-LSR_vs_TO` |Receiver Line Status and Reception Timeout forced together (with `IER.ERBFI`, the timeout's only enable); IIR reports the line-status id, the higher of the two in the RDL ranking
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-RDR_vs_THRE` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-THRE_vs_MODEM` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-IRQ-PRI-TO_vs_RDR` |Named compare in `smc_uart_irq_sources_priority_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-MSR-SINGLE-DELTA` |In loopback, DTR alone raised only DDSR, OUT1's trailing edge alone only TERI (its rising edge none) and OUT2 alone only DDCD; each raised the modem interrupt and the MSR read cleared it
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-MSR`, `CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-RDR`, `CHK-UART-IRQ-CLR-THRE`, `CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-FIFO`, `CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-LSR`, `CHK-UART-IRQ-GATE-MODEM` (and 9 more) hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[sec-153-smc_uart_log_engine_error_boundary_test]]
===== 153 `smc_uart_log_engine_error_boundary_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_log_engine_error_boundary_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`

|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-LOG-COUNT` |Named compare in `smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches
|`CHK-UART-LOG-LOG_ENGINE_CTRL` |Named compare in `smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test_seq.py`; the run fails if it mismatches

|`CHK-UART-MSR-CTS-PAD1` |After this test drives UART0 CTS pad 14 to 1, the same bounded poll of the CTS and DCTS bits reads the pre-change word or exactly CTS=0 with DCTS=1, and the transition word arrives within the bound (`smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test_seq.py`)
|`CHK-UART-MSR-DELTA-CLEAR` |The CTS and DCTS bits of the second back-to-back `UART_MSR` read equal exactly 0x10: CTS still asserted with DCTS cleared by the preceding read, as the delta-since-last-read contract in `uart_16550_main.rdl` requires (`smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test_seq.py`). Every MSR compare in this card is masked to CTS and DCTS, the two bits this test drives through pad 14; DSR, RI, DCD and their delta bits are logged, not compared, because the integrator pin table (`ocah_gpio_table.csv`) pins no pad for them and the bench has no specification for their level

DSR, RI, DCD and their delta bits are outside the compare (see `CHK-UART-MSR-DELTA-CLEAR`)
|===

pin table pins no pad for them and the bench has no specification for their level.

[[sec-164-smc_log_engine_intr_mask_test]]
===== 164 `smc_log_engine_intr_mask_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_log_engine_intr_mask_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); observation on `tb_uart_irq_combined[3:0]`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `uart`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: INTR_ENABLE must mask the log-engine interrupt output, not its set path.

*Test Coverage*:

* The contract is the log engine's documentation: `hw/ip/uart/log_engine/doc/architecture.adoc` (Errors and Interrupts) has the `INTR_STATUS` error bits latch "whether or not their interrupts are enabled", `INTR_ENABLE` mask "the corresponding contributions to `irq_o`" and a written 1 clear a status bit; `interface.adoc` has `irq_o` be "the active-high OR of enabled, latched fetch and write error status"; `log_engine.rdl` declares the status fields `level intr` with `woclr`.
* Both consequences of that contract: an interrupt held after the enable is cleared, and an interrupt dropped because it arrived while masked.
* `INTR_TEST` is `sw = w, singlepulse`, so the stimulus is a one-cycle event on the same line as the real event and needs no bus traffic.
* The IRQ is observed on `tb_uart_irq_combined[0]`, the slice of `peripheral_interrupts[21:18]` that `hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc` (PLIC sources 274-277) gives the combined UART IRQ, UART error and log-engine interrupt of each instance.
* Log engines 1-3 (UART1-3, addresses from the generated SMC map): `INTR_TEST` forcing of `LOG_FETCH_ERR` and `LOG_WRITE_ERR` with `INTR_ENABLE=0`, the written-1 clear and a 64-cycle re-read, with the two other engines required to stay 0x0.
* On engines 1-3, each bit enabled, forced, masked and cleared: `INTR_STATUS` holds the bit while masked and clears on the written 1; the level of `tb_uart_irq_combined[N]` in each state is logged, not compared (LINKED-ISSUE SF-001, the combining function of the instance line is not in the pinned sources).
* A real erroring fetch per engine 1-3 (`LOG_REGION_ADDR` at the I2C0 past-`SIZE` address `smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test` uses, UART in loopback so the write side drains) latches `LOG_FETCH_ERR` alone with `INTR_ENABLE=0`; `LOG_WRITE_ERR` is set through `INTR_TEST=0x10` because a real write-port error is not reachable on this bench (SF-039), and the two bits clear one written 1 at a time.
* One more erroring fetch per engine with only `INTR_ENABLE.LOG_FETCH_ERR` set on that engine: `INTR_STATUS` reads 0x01 there and 0x0 on the other two; `tb_uart_irq_combined[3:0]` before submission, latched and after the clear is logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-001).
* Coverage target (stimulus only): the log-engine register, wrapper and interrupt rows of engines 1-3.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate the UART peripheral clock and require instance 0's PLIC bit to read 0, so nothing below can be credited to the 16550 IRQ or the UART error line.
. Set INTR_ENABLE, pulse INTR_TEST, require INTR_STATUS to latch and the IRQ to assert, held 32 cycles.
. Clear INTR_ENABLE only and sample the IRQ.
. W1C the status, prove it cleared, then pulse INTR_TEST with INTR_ENABLE=0 and set the enable afterwards.
. Require INTR_STATUS to hold the event.
. Engines 1-3: ungate the UART clock, write IER=0 and MCR=0, require INTR_STATUS=0x0, INTR_ENABLE=0x0 and `tb_uart_irq_combined[3:1]=0b000` (bounded poll).
. Per engine: INTR_TEST=0x01 then 0x10, read all three INTR_STATUS after each; write 0x11, read, wait 64 cycles, read.
. Per engine and bit: enable and force, sample the line; clear the enable, sample, read the status; enable, write the bit to INTR_STATUS, sample, read.
. Per engine with INTR_ENABLE=0: LOG_REGION_SIZE=0x80 at the refusing address, LOG_CTRL[0].LOG_LEN=8, poll LOG_LEN to 0, read INTR_STATUS; INTR_TEST=0x10, read; write 0x10, read; write 0x01, read.
. Per engine with INTR_ENABLE=0x01 on that engine only: submit one erroring fetch, poll INTR_STATUS bit 0, sample the line, write 0x01, read, sample again; restore the UARTs and the clock gate.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-ARM` |The set path, the status register and the probe are all alive
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-DEASSERT` |Clearing the enable de-asserts the IRQ, holds it de-asserted for the same span the arm leg holds it asserted, and leaves INTR_STATUS still carrying the bit -- the last is what separates an output mask from a DUT that simply clears the status
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-LATCH` |An event arriving while masked is still latched and surfaces once the enable is set
|`CHK-LOGENG13-TEST-FORCE` |On engines 1-3 INTR_STATUS reads 0x01 after INTR_TEST=0x01 and 0x11 after INTR_TEST=0x10 with INTR_ENABLE=0x0, the other engines read 0x0, a written 0x11 clears it and it still reads 0x0 after 64 cycles
|`CHK-LOGENG13-LINE-MASK` |INTR_STATUS keeps the bit with the enable cleared and reads 0x0 after the written bit; the line level in the enabled, masked and cleared states is logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-001)
|`CHK-LOGENG13-FETCH-ERR` |A fetch from the refusing address returns LOG_LEN to 0 and latches INTR_STATUS=0x01 on that engine only, with INTR_ENABLE=0x0
|`CHK-LOGENG13-WRITE-ERR-TEST` |INTR_TEST=0x10 sets LOG_WRITE_ERR with INTR_ENABLE=0x0 and the written 0x10 clears it; a real write-port error is not reachable here (SF-039)
|`CHK-LOGENG13-PARTIAL-W1C` |With the fetch-latched bit 0 and the test-forced bit 4, INTR_STATUS reads 0x11, then 0x01 after the written 0x10, then 0x0 after the written 0x01
|`CHK-LOGENG13-LINE-REAL` |After an erroring fetch with INTR_ENABLE=0x01, INTR_STATUS reads 0x01 on that engine and 0x0 on the others; `tb_uart_irq_combined[3:0]` before and after the clear is logged (LINKED-ISSUE SF-001)
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the engines 1-3 legs with its bound and last observed state; expiry fails the test
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Ordered fence BRINGUP < LOGENG13_TEST_FORCE < LOGENG13_LINE_MASK < LOGENG13_FETCH_ERR_LATCH < LOGENG13_WRITE_ERR_TEST < LOGENG13_LINE_REAL, each after its step's checker lines with an increasing sim time
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-ARM`, `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-DEASSERT` and `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-INTR-MASK-LATCH` hold after their compares; the last two are measured before either raises, so neither hides the other. Every engines 1-3 checker above prints after its compares hold, followed by `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` and `CHK-NONVAC`. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-524-smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test]]
===== 524 `smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for every UART0 access (`THR`, `RBR`, `IER`,
`IIR`, `FCR`, `LCR`, `LSR`, `ECR`, `DLL`, `DLM`, `MCR`), the UART0 pad-mux control (`UART_EN`) and
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`UART_CG_EN`); UART0 in `MCR.LOOP` system loopback so no pad is driven by
the bench; the `tb_top` probe `tb_uart0_tx_from_dut` (UART0 TX pad) read for failure diagnostics
and required resolvable; the driver's own SEP_IN access timeout

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 FIFO enable change, depth, trigger fields and read order.

*Test Coverage*:

* Changing `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` clears both FIFOs and the holding state, so mode changes can discard
  data; the serializer is not cleared (`uart_16550/doc/architecture.adoc`, Transmit and Receive
  Paths). With data buffered at divisor 8 (`LSR.DR` 1, `THRE` 0), writing `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` 0 then
  1 must leave `DR` 0 and `THRE` 1 at once, `TEMT` must follow, and at most the one frame already
  in the serializer may arrive afterwards: the readable characters are either none or exactly the
  first backlog character.
* Depth: the SMC integration uses 32-entry TX and RX FIFOs (`uart_16550/doc/index.adoc`;
  `periphs.adoc` configuration table, UART 16550 TX and RX FIFO depth 32). Thirty-two `THR` writes
  without polling leave `LSR.THRE` 0, all 32 are received with `LSR.OE` clear in every `LSR` read
  of the fill, and the 32 `RBR` reads equal the written sequence in order. Upper bound
  (`architecture.adoc`, FIFO Protection and Line Errors, and Transmit and Receive Paths: an
  overrun drops the newly received character and sets `LSR.OE`): 33 characters sent with no `RBR`
  read, then `TEMT` plus one frame (divisor + 1) later `LSR.OE` must have been seen, exactly 32
  `RBR` reads must return the first 32 characters, and `LSR.DR` must read 0 after them. A 33rd `THR`
  write while 32 are queued
  is issued and its response, the later `LSR` and the number of characters readable are printed
  without a compare; the document does not state whether the extra write is accepted or refused.
* Writing `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` = 1 a second time with four characters held must complete and leave
  either none or exactly those four readable in order, with `LSR.DR` clear after the last read;
  which of the two happens is measured and printed, since the document does not say.
* `FCR` written with `FIFO_ENABLE` clear and both reset bits set completes; a held character
  that is still readable must read back intact and `LSR.DR` must be consistent with `RBR`, and the
  next character looped must arrive intact. Whether the held character survives is printed, not
  required.
* Trigger fields do not matter without FIFOs: with the FIFOs disabled, `ECR` = 1 and `FCR` trigger
  fields 3 and then 1, one looped character must make `IIR` report pending ID 2 (received data
  ready) and `LSR.DR` read 1 (`architecture.adoc`, interrupt priority and service table).
* Composition of `ECR.RCVR_TRIGGER_MS2B` and `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER` into one 4-bit receive trigger level
  (`smc-programming.adoc`, UART Receive FIFO levels): the occupancy at which `IIR` first reports ID
  2 is measured in four states, A (`ECR` 1, `FCR` field 0), B (`ECR` 1, `FCR` field 1), C (`FCR`
  field back to 0, `ECR` 1) and D (`ECR` 0, `FCR` field 0). The exact onset values are printed
  only, because whether the comparator fires at or above the level and the exact level-32 onset
  are not stated by the document. The compares are relative: A has an onset, B shows none within 32
  characters, C equals A, and D is below A.
* Receive order: five looped characters read from `RBR` in arrival order with `LSR.DR` 1 before
  each read and still 1 after every read except the last; an `RBR` read with the buffer empty is
  issued, its response, data and `LSR` printed without a compare, and the next looped character
  must then arrive intact with `DR` 1.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and write it with `UART_CG_EN` cleared; enable the UART0 pad function,
  program divisor 1, 8N1, `MCR.LOOP` (read back), `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE`, `IER` 0 (require `LSR.DR`
  clear), then `IER.ERBFI`, `ECR` 0 and `FCR` with both resets and `FIFO_ENABLE`; read `LSR`;
  stamp step S1.
. Loop three characters and wait for them. Switch to divisor 8, write eight backlog characters and
  require `LSR` `DR` 1 and `THRE` 0. Write `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` 0 then 1, require `DR` 0 and `THRE` 1,
  wait for `TEMT`, wait one frame time, require `THRE` 1, read `IIR`, and drain `RBR` requiring
  none or only the first backlog character. Stamp S2 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: UART0 `THR` and the receive FIFO in loopback. Kind: 33 characters sent
  with no `RBR` read (a receive overrun), then a 33rd `THR` write while 32 are queued. Expected
  response: after `TEMT` and one frame (divisor + 1) `LSR.OE` has been seen, exactly 32 `RBR`
  reads return the first 32 characters and `DR` reads clear after them; the response to the 33rd
  write, the later `LSR` and the readable count are printed without a compare. Before the
  injection, write 32 characters without polling and require `THRE` 0; wait for `TEMT` and `DR`,
  require `OE` clear in the last `LSR` and in every `LSR` read of the fill, read 32 characters and
  require them equal to the written sequence with `OE` and `DR` clear afterwards and no `OE` seen
  in any `LSR` read. Then send the 33 characters as above, and afterwards write 32 more, issue the
  33rd write, read `LSR`, wait, drain and read `LSR` again, printing the response and counts.
  Stamp S3 and print the line.
. Return to divisor 1, loop four characters, write `FIFO_ENABLE` 1 twice (reading `LSR` between),
  drain `RBR` and require none or the four characters in order, and `DR` clear. Stamp S4 and print the line.
. Write `FCR` with `FIFO_ENABLE` clear, drain, loop one held character, write `FCR` with
  `FIFO_ENABLE` clear and both reset bits set, read `LSR` and, if `DR` is set, require the held
  character; require `DR` clear afterwards, loop the next character and require it intact. Stamp
  S5 and print the line.
. Set `ECR` to 1; for `FCR` trigger fields 3 and 1 with the FIFOs off, loop one character and
  require `IIR` pending ID 2, `LSR.DR` 1 and the character on `RBR`. Stamp S6 and print the line.
. Run the four trigger states A to D in turn: write `ECR` and `FCR`, loop up to 32 characters one
  at a time reading `IIR` after each, record the occupancy of the first pending ID 2, and drain.
  Require the onset of A, none for B, C equal to A, and D below A. Stamp S7 and print the line.
. Error injection. Point: UART0 `RBR`. Kind: an `RBR` read with the receive buffer empty (`LSR.DR`
  clear). Expected response: the read completes within the bound; its response, data and the
  following `LSR` are printed without a compare, and the next looped character arrives intact
  with `DR` 1. Before the injection, loop five characters and read `LSR` then `RBR` for each,
  requiring the arrival order and `DR` 1 before every read and after every read except the last,
  then read `LSR` and require `DR` clear. After the empty read, read `LSR`, loop one more character
  and require `DR` 1 and the character intact. Stamp S8 and print the order line and the
  empty-read line.
. Restore UART0 to its reset configuration and write the saved `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` back; stamp
  S9 and print the bounded-wait line. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S9 with strictly
  increasing stamps and every checker line printed in order at its own step, then print the
  non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-FIFO-ENABLE-CHANGE` |After `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` is written 0 then 1 with data buffered,
  `LSR` reads `DR` 0 and `THRE` 1 at once, `THRE` still reads 1 a frame after `TEMT`, and the
  readable characters are none or only the first backlog character, never an old or queued one
|`CHK-UART-FIFO-DEPTH-32` |32 unpolled `THR` writes leave `THRE` 0, all 32 characters are received
  with `OE` clear in every `LSR` read of the fill, and the 32 `RBR` reads equal the written
  sequence in order; 33 characters sent with no `RBR` read set `OE` and exactly the first 32 are
  read, with `DR` clear after them, so the receive FIFO holds exactly 32; the response to a
  further 33rd write is recorded without comparing
|`CHK-UART-FIFO-ENABLE-SAME` |A second `FIFO_ENABLE` = 1 write with four characters held completes,
  the readable characters are none or the four in order and `LSR.DR` is clear after the last read;
  which of the two occurs is recorded without comparing it to a value
|`CHK-UART-RESET-BITS-NOFIFO` |`FCR` written with `FIFO_ENABLE` clear and both reset bits set
  completes; a held character that remains readable is read back intact, `LSR.DR` is clear after
  it, and the next looped character arrives intact; survival of the held character is recorded
  without comparing
|`CHK-UART-TRIG-NONFIFO` |With the FIFOs disabled and trigger fields 3 and 1 programmed, one
  character makes `IIR` report pending ID 2 and `LSR.DR` read 1, and `RBR` returns it
|`CHK-UART-TRIG-COMPOSE` |State A shows an ID 2 onset, state B shows none within 32 characters,
  state C reproduces the onset of A, and state D's onset is below A's; the onset occupancies are
  printed, and their exact values are not compared
|`CHK-UART-RX-ORDER` |Five looped characters read from `RBR` in arrival order, `LSR.DR` reads 1
  before every read and after every read except the last, after which it reads 0
|`CHK-UART-RBR-EMPTY` |An `RBR` read with the buffer empty completes within the bound and the
  character looped afterwards arrives intact with `DR` 1; the response, data and `LSR` of the
  empty read are recorded without comparing
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S9 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the nine checker lines printed in order, each at its own step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists every bounded wait of the run with its finite bound and the state it
  prints on expiry: `LSR` polls (last `LSR`, `IIR` and pad level), drain loops (characters read)
  and the SEP_IN access bound. The compare is each wait's own assertion, which fails the leaf on
  expiry; the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-FIFO-ENABLE-CHANGE`, `CHK-UART-FIFO-DEPTH-32`,
`CHK-UART-RX-ORDER`, `CHK-UART-TRIG-NONFIFO`, `CHK-UART-TRIG-COMPOSE`,
`CHK-UART-FIFO-ENABLE-SAME`, `CHK-UART-RESET-BITS-NOFIFO` and `CHK-UART-RBR-EMPTY` hold after
their compares; the printed measurements (33rd-write response, surviving counts, onset values,
empty-read data) are not part of the claim. `CHK-NONVAC` and `CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` hold. Enrolled
in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response to a 33rd `THR` write with 32 queued, the later `LSR` and the number
of readable characters are printed without a compare, because the document does not state whether
the extra write is accepted or refused. Whether a second `FIFO_ENABLE` = 1 write keeps or drops the
four held characters, and whether a held character survives the `FCR` reset bits with the FIFOs
disabled, are printed, not required, since the document does not say. The exact trigger onset
occupancies of states A to D are printed only, because whether the comparator fires at or above
the level and the exact level-32 onset are not stated; the compares are relative. The response,
data and `LSR` of the empty `RBR` read are printed without a compare.

'''''

[[sec-525-smc_uart_irq_thre_identify_test]]
===== 525 `smc_uart_irq_thre_identify_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_irq_thre_identify_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) for every UART0 access (`THR`, `RBR`, `IER`,
`IIR`, `LCR`, `MCR`, `LSR`, `MSR`, `ITR`, `DLL`, `DLM`, `FCR`), the UART0 pad-mux control
(`UART_EN`) and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`UART_CG_EN`); UART0 in `MCR.LOOP` loopback at divisor 8 with
8N1, so no pad is driven by the bench; the `tb_top` net `uart_interrupt` (bit 0, the UART0
interrupt output) sampled on `clk_periph` edges and required resolvable; `tb_uart0_tx_from_dut`
(UART0 TX pad) read for failure diagnostics; the driver's own SEP_IN access timeout

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 THRE interrupt lifecycle and IIR service ordering.

*Test Coverage*:

* The transmit-holding-register-empty source (`IIR` ID 1) is controlled by `IER.ETBEI`. It is
  raised when the buffer drains, cleared by a `THR` write or by an `IIR` read while it is the
  selected source, and re-armed by a later transition back to empty
  (`uart_16550/doc/architecture.adoc`, Interrupt Priority and Service; `uart_16550_main.rdl`,
  `IER.ETBEI`).
* Raise: with `ETBEI` set, one looped character that has drained (`LSR` `TEMT`, `THRE` and `DR`
  all set) makes `uart_interrupt` read 1 within 64 `clk_periph` edges and `IIR` report pending
  ID 1.
* Clear by write: with ID 1 pending and `uart_interrupt` high, a `THR` write must drop
  `uart_interrupt` while the new character is still transmitting (`LSR.TEMT` clear when read after
  the fall). The fall is found by sampling every `clk_periph` edge from the write, bounded at 64.
* Clear by `IIR` read: the read that showed ID 1 is followed by a read that reports no interrupt
  pending. With a higher-priority source also pending (`ITR.TRBFI` forced with `IER.ERBFI`), the
  `IIR` read must show ID 2 and ID 1 must still be pending after the forced source is cleared.
* Re-arm: after the clear a new character that drains makes `IIR` report ID 1 again.
* Mask: with `ETBEI` clear and the buffer drained, eight `IIR` samples never report ID 1,
  `uart_interrupt` reads 0 at each, and `LSR.THRE` reads 1.
* `ETBEI` set on an already empty buffer: whether `IIR` then reports ID 1 is not stated in the
  document. The leaf records whether ID 1 appears in up to
  16 reads, and requires only that `LSR.THRE` reads 1 and that the reads are consistent with each
  other (no ID 1 on the read after one that reported it, none at all if none was reported).
* `LSR.THRE` persistence: clearing the interrupt does not clear `LSR.THRE` (`uart_16550_main.rdl`
  `LSR.THRE`); after the `IIR` read that cleared ID 1 both `THRE` and `TEMT` must read 1.
* Priority: with received data (ID 2) and THRE (ID 1) both pending, `IIR` reports ID 2, then,
  after the `RBR` read, ID 1. With modem status (`MCR.DTR` in loopback), a break line status
  (`LCR.SET_BREAK` for two frames, then a further character), received data and THRE all pending,
  `IIR` first reports ID 3 and servicing by reading `IIR` until no interrupt is pending visits IDs
  3, 2, 1 and 0 once each in that order. Two successive `IIR` reads with received data and THRE
  pending both report ID 2, and ID 2 is released by the `RBR` read.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and write it with `UART_CG_EN` cleared; enable the UART0 pad function,
  program divisor 8, 8N1, `MCR.LOOP` (read back), FIFOs on with both resets, `IER` 0; empty `RBR`,
  read `MSR` and require `uart_interrupt` low; stamp step S1.
. Set `IER.ETBEI`, write one character, wait for it to drain, wait for `uart_interrupt` high and
  require `IIR` ID 1; stamp S2 and print the raise line.
. Wait for a second drained character and `uart_interrupt` high, then write `THR` while sampling
  `uart_interrupt` each edge; require the fall and `LSR.TEMT` clear, then wait for the drain.
  Stamp S3 and print the line.
. Require `IIR` ID 1, then a second `IIR` read with no interrupt pending. Write a character, drain,
  empty `RBR`, set `IER` to `ETBEI` and `ERBFI`, force `ITR.TRBFI`, and require `IIR` ID 2;
  clear `ITR` and `ERBFI` and require `IIR` ID 1. Stamp S4 and print the line.
. Write a character, drain, and require `IIR` ID 1. Stamp S5 and print the line.
. Clear `IER`, empty `RBR`, write a character, drain, read `IIR` eight times requiring no ID 1
  and `uart_interrupt` 0 after each, and read `LSR` requiring `THRE`. Stamp S6 and print the line.
. Empty `RBR`, read `LSR` requiring `THRE`, set `ETBEI`, read `IIR` up to 16 times for a pending
  source, read `IIR` and `LSR` again and apply the consistency requirements. Stamp S7 and print
  the line.
. Write a character, wait for the drain, require `IIR` ID 1 and then `LSR` `THRE` and `TEMT`
  both 1. Stamp S8 and print the line.
. Empty `RBR`, set `IER` to `ETBEI` and `ERBFI`, write a character and require `IIR` ID 2, the
  character on `RBR`, then `IIR` ID 1. Empty `RBR`, enable all four sources in `IER`, set
  `MCR.DTR`, loop one character and read it, hold `LCR.SET_BREAK` for two frames, write a further
  character and wait two frames; require `IIR` ID 3 and the service loop to visit IDs 3, 2, 1, 0.
  Stamp S9 and print the order line and the service-loop line.
. Clear `MCR.DTR`, read `MSR`, empty `RBR`, write a character, wait for it, read `IIR` twice
  requiring ID 2 both times, read `RBR` requiring the character, and require that `IIR` no longer
  reports ID 2. Stamp S10 and print the line.
. Clear `IER`, empty `RBR`, clear `MCR`, write the saved `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` back, stamp S11 and
  print the bounded-wait line. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S11 with strictly increasing
  stamps and every checker line printed in order at its own step, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-THRE-RAISE` |With `ETBEI` set, after the transmit buffer drains `uart_interrupt` reads 1
  and `IIR` reports pending ID 1
|`CHK-UART-THRE-WRITE-CLEARS` |A `THR` write while ID 1 is pending drops `uart_interrupt` before the
  new character has drained (`LSR.TEMT` still clear)
|`CHK-UART-THRE-IIR-CLEAR` |An `IIR` read that shows ID 1 as the selected source clears it (the next
  read reports no interrupt pending); with a forced higher-priority source `IIR` shows ID 2, and ID
  1 appears once that source is cleared
|`CHK-UART-THRE-REARM` |After ID 1 was cleared, a new character that drains makes `IIR` report
  ID 1 again
|`CHK-UART-THRE-MASK` |With `ETBEI` clear and the buffer drained, none of eight `IIR` samples
  reports ID 1, `uart_interrupt` reads 0 at each, and `LSR.THRE` reads 1
|`CHK-UART-THRE-ETBEI-EMPTY` |With `ETBEI` set on an empty buffer, `LSR.THRE` reads 1 and the `IIR`
  reads are mutually consistent (no ID 1 after the read that reported it, none if none was
  reported); whether ID 1 appears is recorded without comparing it to a value
|`CHK-UART-LSR-THRE-STICKY` |After the `IIR` read clears ID 1, `LSR.THRE` and `LSR.TEMT` still read
  1 with the buffer empty
|`CHK-UART-ID-ORDER` |With received data and THRE pending, `IIR` reports ID 2 first, and ID 1 after
  the received character is read from `RBR`
|`CHK-UART-ID-SERVICE-LOOP` |With modem, line status, received data and THRE pending, `IIR` first
  reports ID 3 and servicing visits IDs 3, 2, 1 and 0 once each in that order before no interrupt
  is pending, within the loop bound
|`CHK-UART-ID-IIR-SIDE-EFFECT` |Two successive `IIR` reads with received data and THRE pending both
  report ID 2, and ID 2 is no longer reported after the `RBR` read
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S11 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the ten checker lines printed in order, each at its own step
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Lists every bounded wait of the run with its finite bound and the state it
  prints on expiry (`LSR` and `IIR` poll counts, the 64-edge `uart_interrupt` bounds, the drain and
  service loop limits, and the SEP_IN access bound). The compare is each wait's own assertion,
  which fails the leaf on expiry; the line is the record
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twelve checkers hold after their compares; `CHK-UART-THRE-ETBEI-EMPTY` holds
on its consistency requirements, and whether ID 1 appears for an empty buffer is not part of the
claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: Whether `IIR` reports ID 1 when `ETBEI` is set on an already empty buffer is
recorded without a compare, because the document does not state it; only `LSR.THRE` reading 1 and
the mutual consistency of the `IIR` reads are required.

'''''

[[sec-526-smc_uart_log_engine_reg_map_test]]
===== 526 `smc_uart_log_engine_reg_map_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_log_engine_reg_map_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) reading and writing the register window of each
of the four UART and log-engine wrappers (instances 0 to 3): log-engine `CTRL`,
`LOG_REGION_SIZE`, `LOG_REGION_ADDR` (low and high halves), `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`, `INTR_STATUS`,
`INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST` and the sixteen `LOG_CTRL` slots, the wrapper `CTRL` (`UART_EN`), and
the UART `LSR`, `IIR` and `SCR`; no probe and no pad is used

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Log-engine and wrapper registers on all four instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset values: the log-engine registers and the wrapper `CTRL` reset to 0 (`log_engine.rdl`,
  `uart_log_engine_ctrl.rdl`), so the eight registers read 0x0 on every instance (32 reads) and
  all sixteen `LOG_CTRL` slots read 0x0 (64 reads), each with an OKAY response. The UART `LSR`
  reads 0x60 (`THRE` and `TEMT` reset to 1) and `IIR` reads 0x01 (`INTERRUPT_PENDING` reset 1) on
  every instance (`uart_16550_main.rdl`). The 0x0 reset compares carry no reset evidence on the
  2-state build: it zero-initialises every flop, so a missing reset also reads 0x0. Only the
  `LSR` and `IIR` reset words can discriminate.
* Read-write fields and widths: `CTRL.EN` is bit 0 only; `LOG_REGION_SIZE` is `[19:0]`;
  `LOG_REGION_ADDR` is a low word `[31:0]` and a high field `[55:32]` with reserved `[63:56]`;
  `LOG_WRITE_ADDR` is `[31:0]`; `INTR_ENABLE` holds `LOG_FETCH_ERR` bit 0 and `LOG_WRITE_ERR`
  bit 4 only (`log_engine.rdl`). Single-bit walks and an all-ones write must read back exactly
  the written value masked to the field, so bits above a field read 0.
* Instance isolation: each instance is programmed with a distinct signature in four registers and
  every register is read back after all four are written, so a write to one instance that moves
  another is caught. The four wrappers sit at a 0x400 stride (`uart_wrap.rdl`).
* `INTR_TEST` is write-only and single-pulse, and `INTR_STATUS` is write-one-to-clear
  (`log_engine.rdl`). With `INTR_ENABLE` 0, writing `INTR_TEST` 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11 must leave
  `INTR_STATUS` equal to each value; from status 0x11 a write of 0x00, 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11 to
  `INTR_STATUS` must leave 0x11, 0x10, 0x01 and 0x00. What an `INTR_TEST` read returns is not
  specified; its response code and data are measured at
  reset and after a write of 0x11 and printed, and the leaf requires only that each read
  returns a response.
* Unimplemented bits: after a write of 0xFFFFFFFF `INTR_ENABLE` reads 0x00000011 and `INTR_STATUS`
  reads 0x0, both from clear and with 0x11 forced. Partial byte-strobe writes are not exercised;
  the specification does not state their behaviour.
* Wrapper `CTRL` (`UART_EN`, bit 0, reset 0) reads 1 after a write of 1 and 0 after a write of 0
  on every instance. Bank placement follows the wrapper map: control at 0x000, UART at 0x100 and
  log engine at 0x200 of each wrapper (`uart_log_engine_wrap.rdl`). The wrapper offsets of the
  wrapper `CTRL`, the UART `SCR` and `LOG_REGION_SIZE` come from the wrapper's own generated map.
  The address `window_base + n x 0x400 + wrapper offset` must equal the SoC generated-map address
  of instance n, and the signature written there reads back and reads 0 at the same register of
  every other instance.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Error injection. Point: `INTR_TEST` of every instance. Kind: a read of the write-only,
  single-pulse register. Expected response: each read returns a response; its response code and
  data are recorded and not compared to a value. Before it, read `CTRL`, `LOG_REGION_SIZE`,
  `LOG_REGION_ADDR` low and high, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`, `INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE` and the wrapper
  `CTRL` of every instance against 0; stamp step S1.
. Read the sixteen `LOG_CTRL` slots of every instance against 0; stamp S2 and print the reset-zero
  line.
. Read `LSR` against 0x60 and `IIR` against 0x01 on every instance; stamp S3 and print the line.
. On every instance write `CTRL` 1, 0xFFFFFFFE and 0, reading back 1, 0 and 0; stamp S4.
. On instance 0 write each single bit 0 to 19 and 0xFFFFFFFF to `LOG_REGION_SIZE`, reading back the
  value masked to `[19:0]`, then restore 0; stamp S5 and print the line.
. On instance 0 walk each bit of `LOG_REGION_ADDR` low (0 to 31), each bit of the high half (0 to
  23) and 0xFFFFFFFF in the high half (read back masked to 24 bits), restoring 0; stamp S6.
. On instance 0 walk each of the 32 bits of `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`, restore 0; stamp S7 and print the
  address line.
. On instance 0 write `INTR_ENABLE` 0x01, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x00, reading each back; stamp S8 and
  print the line.
. Write a distinct signature to `LOG_REGION_SIZE`, `LOG_REGION_ADDR` low, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR` and
  `INTR_ENABLE` of each instance, read all sixteen back, restore 0; stamp S9 and print the
  isolation line.
. Error injection. Point: `INTR_TEST` of instance 0. Kind: one read of the write-only register
  after the 0x11 write. Expected response: the read returns a response, recorded and not compared
  to a value. Around it, on instance 0 write `INTR_TEST` 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11, reading `INTR_STATUS`
  and clearing it after each; for each of 0x00, 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11 force status 0x11, write the
  value to `INTR_STATUS`, compare the remaining bits, and drain. Stamp S10 and print the
  `INTR_TEST` read line and the pulse and clear line.
. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to `INTR_STATUS` with status clear and with 0x11 forced, requiring 0; write
  0xFFFFFFFF to `INTR_ENABLE` requiring 0x11; restore 0. Stamp S11 and print the line.
. On every instance write the wrapper `CTRL` `UART_EN` 1 then 0 with read-back; then for each
  instance write signatures through `window_base + n x 0x400 + wrapper offset` (offsets from the
  wrapper's generated map) for the wrapper `CTRL`, UART `SCR` and `LOG_REGION_SIZE`, require that
  address to equal the SoC generated-map address, read the signatures there, read the other instances' registers
  against 0, and restore 0. Stamp S12 and print the `UART_EN` and placement lines.
. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S12 with strictly increasing stamps and every checker line
  printed in order at its own step, that every SEP_IN access completed, then print the
  non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOGENG-RESET-ZERO` |All 32 log-engine and wrapper register reads and all 64 `LOG_CTRL` slot
  reads return 0x0 with OKAY responses before any write; the `INTR_TEST` reads are recorded
  without comparing. The 0x0 compares carry no reset evidence on the 2-state build, which
  zero-initialises every flop, so a missing reset also reads 0x0
|`CHK-LOGENG-RESET-UART` |Every instance's UART `LSR` reads 0x60 and `IIR` reads 0x01
|`CHK-LOGENG-RW-EN-SIZE` |`CTRL` reads 0x1, 0x0 and 0x0 after writes of 1, 0xFFFFFFFE and 0 on all
  four instances, and `LOG_REGION_SIZE` returns each single bit 0 to 19 and 0xFFFFFFFF masked to
  `[19:0]`
|`CHK-LOGENG-RW-ADDR` |`LOG_REGION_ADDR` low returns each single bit 0 to 31, its high half returns
  each single bit 0 to 23 and 0xFFFFFFFF masked to 24 bits, and `LOG_WRITE_ADDR` returns each
  single bit 0 to 31
|`CHK-LOGENG-RW-INTR-ENABLE` |`INTR_ENABLE` reads exactly 0x01, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x00 after writes of
  those values
|`CHK-LOGENG-RW-ISOLATION` |After all four instances are programmed with distinct signatures, every
  one of the 16 registers reads its own signature
|`CHK-LOGENG-ACCESS-INTR-TEST-READ` |Each `INTR_TEST` read, at reset and after a write of 0x11,
  completes with a response; the response code and data are printed and not compared to a value
|`CHK-LOGENG-ACCESS-PULSE-W1C` |With `INTR_ENABLE` 0, `INTR_TEST` writes 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11 leave
  `INTR_STATUS` equal to each value, and from status 0x11 write-one-to-clear writes of 0x00,
  0x01, 0x10 and 0x11 leave 0x11, 0x10, 0x01 and 0x00
|`CHK-LOGENG-ACCESS-UNIMPL` |After a write of 0xFFFFFFFF `INTR_ENABLE` reads 0x00000011 and
  `INTR_STATUS` reads 0x0 both from clear and with 0x11 forced
|`CHK-LOGENG-UART-EN-RW` |The wrapper `CTRL` reads 0x0 at reset, 0x1 after a write of 1 and 0x0
  after a write of 0 on every instance; the reset read carries no reset evidence on the 2-state
  build
|`CHK-LOGENG-BANK-PLACEMENT` |`window_base + n x 0x400 + wrapper offset`, with the offsets taken
  from the wrapper's generated map, equals the SoC generated-map `CTRL`, UART `SCR` and
  `LOG_REGION_SIZE` address of instance n; the signature written there reads back and reads 0 at
  every other instance
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S12 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, the eleven checker lines printed in order, each at its own step, and
  the SEP_IN accesses all completed
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all checkers hold after their compares; the 0x0 reset legs of
`CHK-LOGENG-RESET-ZERO` and `CHK-LOGENG-UART-EN-RW` are not part of the claim on the 2-state
bench. The `INTR_TEST` response and data, and partial-strobe writes, are not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`.

*Scope limit*: The response code and data of an `INTR_TEST` read, at reset and after a write of
0x11, are printed and not compared, because what the read returns is not specified. Partial
byte-strobe writes are not exercised, because the specification does not state their behaviour.
The 0x0 reset compares of the log-engine registers and the wrapper `CTRL` carry no reset evidence
on the 2-state build, which zero-initialises every flop; only the `LSR` and `IIR` reset words
discriminate.

'''''

[[sec-527-smc_uart_reg_reset_rw_test]]
===== 527 `smc_uart_reg_reset_rw_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_reg_reset_rw_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP) reading and writing the UART register block of
each of the four wrapper instances (0 to 3, 0x400 stride): `RBR`, `IER`, `IIR`, `LCR`, `MCR`,
`LSR`, `MSR`, `SCR`, `ECR`, `ITR` and the divisor latches `DLL` and `DLM` (behind `LCR.DLAB`);
`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`UART_CG_EN`) for the UART clock; no probe, pad or UART pad-mux write is
used and `UART_EN` is left untouched

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: UART reset values, field read/write and isolation on 4 instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* Reset values (`uart_16550_main.rdl`, `uart_16550_dl.rdl`): `RBR`, `IER`, `LCR`, `MCR`, `SCR`,
  `ECR` and `ITR` read 0x00, `IIR` reads 0x01 (`INTERRUPT_PENDING` reset 1, ID 0, FIFOs disabled)
  and `LSR` reads 0x60 (`THRE` and `TEMT` reset 1), with `DLL` and `DLM` 0x00 behind `LCR.DLAB`,
  on each of the four instances. The 0x00 reset compares are not reset evidence on the 2-state
  bench: zero-initialised flops read 0x00 with or without a reset, so only the `IIR` and `LSR`
  compares can discriminate.
* `MSR` (reset 0x00 in `uart_16550_main.rdl`): on the first read of each instance `DCD`, `RI` and
  `DSR` must read 0. The `CTS` level and the four delta bits of that first read are printed and
  not compared to a value; how the modem input is connected, and why a delta can be set on a
  first read with no input transition since reset, are not stated by the document. A second
  read must return the delta bits clear (the delta bits clear on read) with the level bits equal
  to the first read.
* The twelve-value reset vector (the ten registers read plus `DLL` and `DLM`, with the first `MSR`
  read) of instances 1 to 3 must equal that of instance 0 (`uart_wrap.rdl`: identical wrappers at
  a 0x400 stride).
* Read-write fields on instance 0, each read back after the write and compared under the mask of
  the implemented bits: `IER` bits 4:0 for each of the five bits alone and all five set (bits
  31:5 are printed, since the document does not say they read 0); `LCR` bits 5:0 and 7 for every
  `WLS` value 0 to 3, each of `STB`, `PEN`, `EPS`, `STICK_PARITY` and `DLAB` alone and all
  together, with `SET_BREAK` never written and required to read 0; `MCR` bits 5:0 for each bit
  alone and a combination of all but `LOOP`; `ECR` bits 1:0 for values 0 to 3; `ITR` bits 5:0 for
  each bit alone and for 0.
* With `LCR.DLAB` set, `DLL` and `DLM` each read back 0x00, 0xFF, 0xA5 and 0x5A as written, and a
  write to one leaves the other at 0 (`uart_16550_dl.rdl`).
* Isolation: for each instance k a distinct non-zero pattern is written to `IER`, `LCR`, `MCR`,
  `SCR`, `ECR`, `DLL` and `DLM`; the other three instances must read 0 before and unchanged after,
  instance k must read the pattern exactly, and after restoring k all four read 0.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, write it with `UART_CG_EN` cleared and require the bit to read back
  clear; stamp step S1.
. On each instance read `RBR`, `IER`, `IIR`, `LCR`, `MCR`, `LSR`, `MSR`, `SCR`, `ECR` and `ITR`,
  then read `MSR` again; require the reset values above for every register except `MSR`, stamp
  S2, print the reset-value line, and apply the `MSR` requirements and print the `MSR` line.
. On each instance set `LCR.DLAB`, read `DLL` and `DLM` and clear `DLAB`; require both 0 and the
  twelve-value vectors of all four instances to match; stamp S3 and print the divisor-latch line
  and the instance-vector line.
. On instance 0 write each `IER` bit alone and then all five, reading `IER` back after each;
  clear `IER`; stamp S4 and print the line.
. Write `LCR` with every `WLS` value, each flag alone, `DLAB` alone and a combination, reading
  back each under the defined mask and requiring `SET_BREAK` clear; clear `LCR`; stamp S5 and
  print the line.
. Write `MCR` with each bit alone and a combination, reading back each; clear `MCR`; stamp S6 and
  print the line.
. Write `ECR` 0 to 3 and `ITR` each bit alone and 0, reading both back; clear `ECR`; stamp S7 and
  print the line.
. Set `DLAB`, write `DLL` and `DLM` each with the four patterns, reading back and requiring the
  other latch at 0, clearing each after its test, then clear `DLAB`; stamp S8 and print the line.
. For k = 0 to 3, read the seven registers of the other instances against 0, write instance k's
  pattern and require it back exactly, read the other instances unchanged, restore k and read all
  four against 0; stamp S9 and print the line. Write the saved `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` back.
. Check the ordered fence: steps S1 to S9 with strictly increasing stamps and every checker line
  printed in order at its own step, then print the non-vacuity line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-RESET-VALUES` |On all four instances `RBR`, `IER`, `LCR`, `MCR`, `SCR`, `ECR` and `ITR`
  read 0x00, `IIR` reads 0x01 and `LSR` reads 0x60; the 0x00 reset compares are not reset evidence
  on the 2-state bench (zero-initialised flops read 0x00 with or without a reset)
|`CHK-UART-RESET-MSR` |On the first `MSR` read of each instance `DCD`, `RI` and `DSR` read 0; the
  second read returns the delta bits clear with the level bits equal to the first read; the first
  read's `CTS` level and delta bits are recorded without comparing them to a value
|`CHK-UART-RESET-DL` |With `LCR.DLAB` set, `DLL` and `DLM` read 0x00 on all four instances; the
  0x00 reset compare is not reset evidence on the 2-state bench (zero-initialised flops read 0x00
  with or without a reset)
|`CHK-UART-RESET-INSTANCES` |The twelve-value reset vector of instances 1, 2 and 3 equals that of
  instance 0
|`CHK-UART-RW-IER` |`IER` bits 4:0 read back as written for the five single-bit writes and for all
  five set; bits 31:5 are recorded without comparing
|`CHK-UART-RW-LCR` |`LCR` bits 5:0 and 7 read back as written for every value written, and
  `SET_BREAK` reads 0
|`CHK-UART-RW-MCR` |`MCR` bits 5:0 read back as written for the six single-bit writes and the
  combination
|`CHK-UART-RW-ECR-ITR` |`ECR` bits 1:0 read back 0 to 3 as written and `ITR` bits 5:0 read back each
  single-bit pattern as written; `ITR` reads 0 after a write of 0
|`CHK-UART-RW-DL` |With `DLAB` set, `DLL` and `DLM` read back 0x00, 0xFF, 0xA5 and 0x5A as
  written, and a write to one latch leaves the other at 0
|`CHK-UART-RW-ISOLATION` |After each pattern write to instance k the other three instances read
  the values they held before, instance k reads its own pattern, and all four read reset values
  after restore
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered fence holds: steps S1 to S9 in order with strictly increasing
  simulation-time stamps, and the ten checker lines printed in order, each at its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all eleven checkers hold after their compares, except that the 0x00 reset
legs of `CHK-UART-RESET-VALUES` (all registers but `IIR` and `LSR`) and `CHK-UART-RESET-DL` are
not part of the claim on the 2-state bench. The first-read `MSR` `CTS` and
delta bits and the `IER` bits above 4 are recorded and are not part of the claim. Enrolled in:
`all`.

*Scope limit*: The `CTS` level and the four delta bits of the first `MSR` read are printed and not
compared, because how the modem input is connected, and why a delta can be set on a first read
with no input transition since reset, are not stated by the document. `IER` bits 31:5 are printed,
since the document does not say they read 0. The 0x00 reset compares are not reset evidence on the
2-state bench, where zero-initialised flops read 0x00 with or without a reset; only the `IIR` and
`LSR` compares discriminate.

'''''

[[sec-529-smc_uart_pad_mux_enable_test]]
===== 529 `smc_uart_pad_mux_enable_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_pad_mux_enable_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer writing and reading `CTRL.UART_EN` of wrapper 0, the UART0
`THR`, `LSR.THRE` and `LSR.TEMT`, the pad-12 GPIO `DATA_CTRL` fields `interface_enable`,
`enable_rx_tx` and `core2pad`, and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` (`UART_CG_EN`); the UART0 pad VIP sink on
`tb_uart0_tx_from_dut` (pad 12) decodes 8N1 frames at 115200 baud, and the same signal is also
sampled on every `clk_smc_i` rise; `tb_uart0_rx_ext_drive` (pad 11) is bound by the VIP and left
idle

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `THR` 0xA5 reaches pad 12 as one frame with `UART_EN` set, again after `UART_EN` is
cleared and set, and the UART transmits with `UART_EN` clear while the pad is only measured.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CTRL.UART_EN` of wrapper 0 set: a `THR` write of 0xA5 produces exactly one 8N1 frame on pad 12
  decoded as 0xA5 within the 5000 us capture bound (`uart_log_engine_ctrl.rdl` `CTRL.UART_EN`;
  `ocah_gpio_table` pad 12 = `UART[0].TX`).
* `UART_EN` cleared while idle: `LSR.TEMT` reads 0 after the `THR` write and `LSR.THRE` and
  `LSR.TEMT` read 1 together after the byte is shifted out (`uart_16550_main.rdl` `LSR`), so the
  UART itself transmitted.
* The frames the pad VIP decodes on pad 12 within a window of 3 frame times and the minimum and
  maximum pad level on every `clk_smc_i` rise are measured, not compared; the document does not
  state the pad behaviour with `UART_EN` clear.
* Pad-12 `DATA_CTRL` with `interface_enable` 1, `enable_rx_tx` 1 and `core2pad` 1 then 0: the
  fields read back the written values (compared, `gpio_intf.rdl`); the pad level after each write
  is measured, not compared, for the same reason.
* `UART_EN` set again: the same `THR` write produces exactly one frame decoded as 0xA5, the
  positive control that the stimulus and the pad decoder still work after the clear leg.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Read `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` and clear `UART_CG_EN`; program UART0 for 115200 baud 8N1 through
  `LCR.DLAB`, `DLL` and `DLM`; read `LSR` requiring `TEMT` and `THRE` 1; bind the pad VIP; read
  `CTRL` and the pad-12 `DATA_CTRL` as the restore values; stamp S1.
. Write `UART_EN` 1 and read it back; write `THR` 0xA5; capture the frame within 5000 us; poll
  `LSR` to idle and wait one frame time; require one frame decoded as 0xA5; stamp S2 and print
  `CHK-UART-PADMUX-FRAME-ON`.
. Error injection. Point: wrapper 0 `CTRL.UART_EN` and UART0 `THR`. Kind: a `THR` write of 0xA5 with
  `UART_EN` cleared (read back 0), the pad function off. Expected response: `LSR.TEMT` reads 0 after
  the write and `TEMT` and `THRE` read 1 together within 5000 us (the UART itself transmitted); the
  frames decoded on pad 12 and the minimum and maximum pad level over the 3-frame-time window are
  measured, not compared. Before the write, read `LSR` (both bits 1), write `UART_EN` 0 and read it
  back, read `LSR` again and start the `clk_smc_i` level sampler; after the idle reads complete the
  3-frame-time window; stamp S3, print `CHK-UART-PADMUX-OFF-TX-SHIFTED` after its compare and the
  measured `CHK-UART-PADMUX-OFF-PAD-MEASURED`.
. With `UART_EN` still 0 write pad-12 `DATA_CTRL` with `interface_enable`, `enable_rx_tx` 1 and
  `core2pad` 1, sample the pad after the write and after the read-back, repeat with `core2pad` 0,
  then write the saved `DATA_CTRL` back and read it; stamp S4 and print
  `CHK-UART-PADMUX-GPIO-LEVEL-MEASURED`.
. Write `UART_EN` 1 and read it back; write `THR` 0xA5; capture the frame, poll `LSR` to idle and
  wait one frame time; require one frame decoded as 0xA5; stamp S5 and print
  `CHK-UART-PADMUX-FRAME-RECOVER`.
. Write the saved `CTRL` and `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles, stamp S6, check
  the ordered fence and print `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-PADMUX-FRAME-ON` |With `UART_EN` read back 1 a `THR` write of 0xA5 yields exactly one
  frame on pad 12 decoded as 0xA5 within 5000 us; no frame, another byte, a second frame or a
  `UART_EN` read-back of 0 fails
|`CHK-UART-PADMUX-OFF-TX-SHIFTED` |With `UART_EN` read back 0, `LSR.TEMT` reads 0 after the `THR`
  write and `TEMT` and `THRE` read 1 together before 5000 us, after idle reads of 1 and 1 before
  the write; a `TEMT` that never reads 0 or an idle that never returns fails
|`CHK-UART-PADMUX-OFF-PAD-MEASURED` |Measured, not compared: frames decoded, their bytes and the
  minimum and maximum pad-12 level over the 3-frame-time window; an X/Z sample or no sample fails
|`CHK-UART-PADMUX-GPIO-LEVEL-MEASURED` |Pad-12 `DATA_CTRL` `interface_enable`, `enable_rx_tx` and
  `core2pad` read back the written values (compared) and the saved value after the restore; the
  pad level after each write is measured, not compared, and an X/Z sample fails
|`CHK-UART-PADMUX-FRAME-RECOVER` |With `UART_EN` read back 1 again the same `THR` write yields
  exactly one frame decoded as 0xA5 within 5000 us
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Steps S1 to S6 ran in order with strictly increasing simulation-time stamps and the
  five checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all checkers hold after their compares. The pad behaviour with `UART_EN` clear
is observed and is not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: With `UART_EN` clear, the frames the pad VIP decodes on pad 12 within the
3-frame-time window and the minimum and maximum pad level on every `clk_smc_i` rise are measured,
not compared, because the document does not state the pad behaviour with `UART_EN` clear. The
pad level after each pad-12 `DATA_CTRL` write is measured, not compared, for the same reason.

'''''

[[sec-530-smc_log_engine_region_size_test]]
===== 530 `smc_log_engine_region_size_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_log_engine_region_size_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer writing and reading the SPM log window (tagged bytes, read
back), the wrapper 0 log-engine registers `LOG_REGION_SIZE`, `LOG_REGION_ADDR`, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`,
`LOG_CTRL[i].LOG_LEN`, `CTRL.EN` and `INTR_STATUS`, the wrapper 0 UART `THR`, `RBR`, `LSR` and
`MCR.LOOP`, and `CTRL.UART_EN`; the engine writes `THR` and the bytes return through the same
UART's receiver, so no pad carries them

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Wrapper 0 delivers the bytes the slot-start formula, the capacity clamp and the
zero-capacity rule name, for region sizes other than the one `smc_log_engine_transfer_test` uses.

*Test Coverage*:

* Slot start at the minimum size: `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x80, `LOG_LEN` 8 on each of the 16 slots, the
  delivered bytes equal the window bytes at `LOG_REGION_ADDR + (LOG_REGION_SIZE / 16) * i`
  (`log_engine/doc/architecture.adoc` "Memory Slots and Lengths").
* Slot start at a mid size: `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x200, slots 0, 7 and 15 with `LOG_LEN` 0x20; the
  window bytes differ above offset 0x100 so a start off by 0x100 fails.
* Byte order: every compared message arrives at `RBR` in increasing address order, least
  significant byte first in each fetched word, exactly `LOG_LEN` bytes and none beyond
  (`architecture.adoc` "Arbitration and Data Transfer").
* Resubmission: slot 0 at 0x200 takes `LOG_LEN` 0x20 a second time after hardware cleared it and
  delivers the same 32 bytes (`architecture.adoc` "Memory Slots and Lengths"; `log_engine.rdl`
  `LOG_CTRL`).
* Capacity clamp: `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 135, 143, 144 and 271 on slots 0, 1 and 15; `LOG_LEN` at the
  capacity (8, 8, 8 and 16 bytes) or below delivers 8 bytes, and `LOG_LEN` of capacity + 8 and the
  largest multiple of eight the field holds (0xFFF8) each deliver exactly the capacity
  (`architecture.adoc` "Memory Slots and Lengths"; `log_engine.rdl` `LOG_REGION_SIZE`).
* The slot start of the unaligned sizes is measured, not compared; the compare is that every
  delivered message is made of consecutive window offsets. The window byte names its offset only
  below 0x100 (above it the byte is the offset XOR 0xA5, so a start off by 0x100 fails), so the
  leaf also requires every delivered message of these sizes to end at or below offset 0x100; the
  sizes and slots chosen keep them there (size 271, slot 15 ends exactly at 0x100).
* Zero capacity: `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 127, `LOG_LEN` 8 on slots 0, 1 and 15 clears within 64 reads
  with no byte at `RBR`; the delivering legs of the same leaf are the positive control.
* `LOG_LEN` 9 and 7 at 0x200 is a measured leg: the count and values of the delivered bytes are
  printed, measured, not compared; the hardware clear of `LOG_LEN` within 64 reads is compared, as
  in every other leg.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for fuse sense; arm the wrapper 0 UART (`CTRL.UART_EN` 1, 8N1, divisor 1, `MCR.LOOP`, FIFO
  enable, `IER` 0); disable the engine, clear `INTR_STATUS`, `INTR_ENABLE` 0, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR` =
  the `THR` address, `LOG_REGION_ADDR` = the SPM log window base; write 0x200 tagged bytes and read
  them back; set `CTRL.EN`; stamp S1.
. `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x80; for slots 0 to 15 in turn write `LOG_LEN` 8, drain `RBR` through `LSR.DR`
  polls until the receiver is idle, read `LOG_CTRL[i]` until 0 within 64 reads, read
  `INTR_STATUS`; stamp S2 and print `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-SLOT-START-MIN`.
. `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x200; for slots 0, 7 and 15 write `LOG_LEN` 0x20 and drain 32 bytes; write
  slot 0 again and drain the second delivery; stamp S3 and print
  `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-SLOT-START-MID`, `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-RESUBMIT` and
  `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-BYTE-ORDER`.
. Error injection. Point: `LOG_CTRL[i].LOG_LEN` of slots 0, 1 and 15 at the unaligned
  `LOG_REGION_SIZE` values 135, 143, 144 and 271. Kind: a `LOG_LEN` of capacity + 8 and of 0xFFF8,
  the largest multiple of eight the field holds, both past the slot capacity. Expected response:
  each delivers exactly the capacity and nothing beyond, and `LOG_LEN` reads 0 afterwards; the
  first fetched offset of the slot 1 and 15 messages is measured, not compared. At each size also
  write `LOG_LEN` 8 (delivers exactly 8 bytes), each write after the previous message cleared and
  the receiver idled (`LSR.TEMT` 1 and `LSR.DR` 0 on 32 consecutive polls); record every
  delivered message; stamp S4 and print `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-CAPACITY`,
  `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-BELOW-CAP` and the measured
  `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-START-MEASURED`.
. Error injection. Point: `LOG_REGION_SIZE` and `LOG_CTRL[i].LOG_LEN` of slots 0, 1 and 15. Kind:
  `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 127, below the minimum, giving every slot zero capacity, with `LOG_LEN` 8
  written. Expected response: `LOG_LEN` reads 0 within 64 reads and no byte reaches `RBR`. For
  each slot apply the idle rule, read `LOG_CTRL` until 0 within 64 reads, read `LSR` and
  `INTR_STATUS`; stamp S5 and print `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-ZERO-CAPACITY`.
. Error injection. Point: `LOG_CTRL[0].LOG_LEN` at `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x200. Kind: `LOG_LEN` 9 then
  7, lengths that are not a multiple of 8. Expected response: the hardware clear of `LOG_LEN`
  within 64 reads is compared; the count and values of the delivered bytes are printed, measured,
  not compared. Each write is followed by the idle rule and the clear poll; stamp S6 and print the
  measured `CHK-LOGENG-REGION-LEN-NOT-MULT8-MEASURED`.
. Clear `CTRL.EN`, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`, `LOG_REGION_SIZE` and `LOG_REGION_ADDR`, restore the UART,
  wait two `clk_smc_i` cycles, stamp S7, check the ordered fence and print `CHK-NONVAC`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-SLOT-START-MIN` |At `LOG_REGION_SIZE` 0x80 each of the 16 slots delivers the 8
  window bytes at offset 8 * i and `INTR_STATUS` bits 0 and 4 read 0; a wrong first byte, a wrong
  count or a clear that never comes fails
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-SLOT-START-MID` |At 0x200 slots 0, 7 and 15 deliver the 32 window bytes at offset
  0x20 * i, first bytes 0x00, 0xE0 and 0x45; a start off by any multiple of 8 fails
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-BYTE-ORDER` |Every compared message arrives in increasing address order with
  exactly `LOG_LEN` bytes and `LSR.DR` reads 0 after them; reversed or reordered bytes, a wrong
  count or a trailing byte fails
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-RESUBMIT` |Slot 0 at 0x200 delivers the same 32 bytes a second time after
  `LOG_LEN` 0x20 is written again and `LOG_LEN` reads 0 afterwards
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-CAPACITY` |For sizes 135, 143, 144 and 271 a `LOG_LEN` of capacity + 8
  and of 0xFFF8, the largest multiple of eight the field holds, each deliver exactly the capacity
  and nothing beyond on slots 0, 1 and 15, and `LOG_LEN` reads 0 afterwards
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-BELOW-CAP` |`LOG_LEN` 8 delivers exactly 8 bytes at each of the four
  unaligned sizes on slots 0, 1 and 15
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-UNALIGNED-START-MEASURED` |The first fetched window offset of the slot 1 and 15
  messages is printed, measured, not compared; every delivered message is consecutive window
  offsets ending at or below offset 0x100 and none is empty
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-ZERO-CAPACITY` |At size 127 `LOG_LEN` 8 on slots 0, 1 and 15 reads 0 within 64
  reads, no byte reaches `RBR` and `INTR_STATUS` bits 0 and 4 read 0
|`CHK-LOGENG-REGION-LEN-NOT-MULT8-MEASURED` |`LOG_LEN` 9 and 7 at 0x200: the delivered count and
  values are printed, measured, not compared; the hardware clear of `LOG_LEN` within 64 reads is
  compared
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Steps S1 to S7 ran in order with strictly increasing simulation-time stamps and the
  nine checker lines printed in order, each after its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all checkers hold after their compares; the measured legs are observed and are
not part of the claim. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The slot start of the unaligned sizes (the first fetched window offset of the slot
1 and 15 messages) is measured, not compared; only consecutive window offsets ending at or below
0x100 are required. For `LOG_LEN` 9 and 7 at 0x200 the count and values of the delivered bytes are
printed, measured, not compared; only the hardware clear of `LOG_LEN` within 64 reads is compared.

'''''

[[sec-531-smc_log_engine_round_robin_test]]
===== 531 `smc_log_engine_round_robin_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: UART

*Source Module*: `smc_log_engine_round_robin_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI sequencer writing and reading the SPM log window (0x100 bytes, slot `s`
byte `j` carrying `(s << 4) | j`), the wrapper 0 log-engine registers `LOG_REGION_SIZE`,
`LOG_REGION_ADDR`, `LOG_WRITE_ADDR`, `LOG_CTRL[i].LOG_LEN`, `CTRL.EN` and `INTR_STATUS`, the
wrapper 0 UART `THR`, `RBR`, `LSR` and `MCR.LOOP`, and `CTRL.UART_EN`; the engine writes `THR` and
the bytes return through the same UART's receiver, so no pad carries them

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The wrapper 0 arbiter serves each pending slot as one whole message exactly once,
skips zero lengths, and `LOG_LEN` holds the submitted value until hardware clears it.

*Test Coverage*:

* Atomic messages: with four, sixteen and five slots pending, every message arrives at `RBR` as 16
  consecutive bytes of one slot in order, with no byte of another slot between them
