|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-BYTES` |All 128 log bytes of the run reached the receiver of their own wrapper, every element's bytes arrived in slot order and exactly once, and no byte named another element or another wrapper; a transfer that never started fails on the byte count before the compare is reached
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-HWCLR` |Every driven LOG_CTRL element read a length of 0 after its log arrived, and nothing in the leaf wrote a pending length back, so the clear is the hardware completion the RDL declares
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-CLEAN` |Every LSR read during the transfer showed no overrun, parity, framing or break error, the receiver went quiet after the last expected byte, and INTR_STATUS read clear before and after, so the engine hit neither a fetch nor a write error and sent nothing it was not asked to
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-BYTES`, `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-CLEAN`, `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-TRANSFER-HWCLR` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The order in which the arbiter interleaves the four elements is not predicted; only
each element's own bytes are required to arrive in slot order, exactly once.

'''''

[[sec-203-smc_zeroer_multi_burst_test]]
===== 203 `smc_zeroer_multi_burst_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_multi_burst_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `zeroer`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Clear a region larger than one AXI burst and check both halves.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_zeroer_sanity_test` clears eight bytes and its busy probe clears 0x800, both of which fit one AXI4 burst -- `AxLEN` is eight bits, so a burst carries at most 256 transfers, which on the 64-bit output path is 0x800 bytes. This leaf programs 0x1000, which no single burst can carry, so the zeroer has to return from its data phase to a second address phase.
* Four probe words -- the first and last word of each half of the region -- are poisoned with distinct values beforehand and read back to prove the poison landed, then required to read zero.
* A witness word immediately past the end of the region keeps its own poison, so a job that ran past its size fails.
* The output responder's write-transaction counter has to advance by at least the two bursts the size demands, and `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` has to leave the level it rests at while the zeroer is idle and return to it. Which level means busy is not asserted, as in `smc_zeroer_sanity_test`.
* `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR` are cleared afterwards, so a later write to `CTRL_STATUS` -- the register whose write side effect is the trigger -- cannot start a job over anything.

* `ZEROER_CTRL_STATUS_START` is packed with `int_en = 1`, so the start write leaves `CTRL_STATUS.INT_EN` holding a one. The field is bit 0 of a 64-bit register. A four-byte write of 0 at the upper half leaves INT_EN's byte lane deasserted, so a field that honours the strobe keeps its one, while one that took the zero-filled lower lanes would clear; the whole word outside the STATUS bit then has to read back as the armed word.
* INT_EN is then cleared by a four-byte write of 0 at the low half, which selects its lane, and held clear across a four-byte write of all ones at the upper half. The only upper-half field is `STATUS` (`sw = r`), so that write can change nothing, while a DUT that steered the upper word onto the low lanes or decoded +4 onto the low word would set INT_EN. So INT_EN is held against an unselected write both set and clear, each time against data that would change it.
* Every one of those writes is also the zeroer's trigger -- `INT_EN.wr_swacc` fires on any write of the register, whichever half is written -- and a trigger starts a job even at a size of zero, writing one burst to `DEST_ADDR` before the size is ever tested. That is why these writes happen here, where each one re-runs this leaf's own job over the region it has already zeroed, and not at reset, where `DEST_ADDR` is 0. After each write `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` must leave its idle level and return to it, so the re-run is checked, not assumed. INT_EN ends at its RDL reset of 0, and `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR` are cleared afterwards as before.
* The job then runs again while the output side pushes back. `zeroer.adoc` (Outstanding Transaction Management) has `AWREADY` and `WREADY` provide the zeroer's downstream back-pressure, but the output fabric absorbs a single master's addresses, so a 64-repetition DMA job is started on the same accelerator master port and the SYS_OUT responder stalls AW and W in repeating eight-cycle windows. The zeroer must be seen holding `AWVALID` high against `AWREADY` low for at least one cycle, the re-poisoned probe words must read zero with the witness intact, and every DMA repetition must land at its destination.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_zeroer_multi_burst_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-PRELOAD` |The four probe words spanning both halves of the job and the witness word past its end were poisoned with distinct values and read back exactly, so the zero readbacks that follow can fail
|`CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-STATUS` |`CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` left the level it rests at while the zeroer is idle and returned to it, and the output responder booked at least the two write transactions a 0x1000-byte job needs under AxLEN's 256-transfer cap, so the zeroer took a second address phase after its first data phase
|`CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-ZEROED` |All four probe words read 0 after the job, including the first and last word of each half, and the witness word immediately past the end still holds its poison
|`CHK-ZEROER-BACKPRESSURE` |With the DMA job contending and the responder stalling AW and W, the zeroer held AWVALID high against AWREADY low for a counted, non-zero number of cycles; the re-poisoned probe words, read back as poisoned before the job, read 0 after it, the witness kept its poison, and every DMA repetition read back its seed
|`CHK-ZEROER-INT-EN-HALF-WRITE` |CTRL_STATUS.INT_EN held a one across a four-byte write of 0 at the half of the 64-bit register it does not occupy, with the armed word read back after it; was cleared by a four-byte write of 0 at the half it does occupy; and held a zero across a four-byte write of all ones at the other half. After each write STATUS left its idle level and returned
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ZEROER-BACKPRESSURE`, `CHK-ZEROER-INT-EN-HALF-WRITE`, `CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-PRELOAD`, `CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-STATUS`, `CHK-ZEROER-MULTI-BURST-ZEROED` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Which `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` level means busy is not asserted, as in
`smc_zeroer_sanity_test`; only that the field leaves its idle level and returns to it is required.

[[sec-324-smc_zeroer_unaligned_test]]
===== 324 `smc_zeroer_unaligned_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_unaligned_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the TB SYS_OUT output-fabric responder

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `zeroer`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Zero a byte range that starts partway into a word, inside one 4 KB page, and touch no byte outside it.

*Test Coverage*:

* `hw/sys/smc/doc/zeroer.adoc` lists unaligned start addresses among what the zeroer handles, and the RDL gives `DEST_ADDR` as a byte address and `SIZE` as a byte count. With an unaligned start, the end offset `DEST_ADDR[2:0] + SIZE` sets both the number of beats and the width of the final beat; a design that derives either from `SIZE` alone corrupts the edges. The page-crossing job in `smc_zeroer_size_corners_test` does not reach this case, because the 4 KB split makes each fragment end on a word.
* A 13-byte job from five bytes into a word covers the top three bytes of the first word, the whole second word and the low two bytes of the third. A beat count taken from `SIZE` alone leaves the third word's bytes poisoned; a final-beat width taken from `SIZE` clears too many bytes of it.
* A 4-byte job from six bytes into a word straddles two words by two bytes each. A single beat from `SIZE` alone leaves the second word's bytes poisoned.
* Each covered word and a guard word below and above each job are poisoned and read back first, so the compares after the job can fail. `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR` are cleared afterwards, so a later write to `CTRL_STATUS` cannot start a job.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_zeroer_unaligned_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-UNALIGNED-TAIL` |After the 13-byte job, each of the three words reads its poison with exactly the job's bytes cleared, the guard words below and above keep their poison, `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` returned to idle, and the output responder booked at least one write transaction
|`CHK-ZEROER-UNALIGNED-SPAN` |After the 4-byte job, the two straddled words read their poison with exactly the job's two bytes in each cleared, and the guard words below and above keep their poison
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-ZEROER-UNALIGNED-SPAN`, `CHK-ZEROER-UNALIGNED-TAIL` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-204-smc_cool_reset_zero_delay_test]]
===== 204 `smc_cool_reset_zero_delay_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cool_reset_zero_delay_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); `cfg_flr_pf_active_i` driven as a TB input

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`, `flr`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run an FLR cool reset with no pre-reset delay programmed.

*Test Coverage*:

* `reset_unit.rdl` makes `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_COUNTER_VALUE` the wait before the cool asserts and `ISOLATE_REQ_FLR_RESET_COUNTER_VALUE` the hold, and records that a hold of 0 prevents initiation whatever the pre-delay is. So the hold decides whether a cool happens and the pre-delay only decides when. `smc_cool_reset_from_pcie_test` always programs a non-zero pre-delay.
* Deny leg: with both counters at their reset 0 the FLR request has to latch in `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` and no cool may follow.
* Allow leg: with the same pre-delay of 0 and a non-zero hold the cool has to assert inside the synchroniser allowance -- a reset unit that counted a programmed delay anyway runs past the bound -- and then release.
* A warm-domain scratch register written before the cool reads 0 after it, which is the DUT-side evidence that a cool went through rather than a pin wiggle.
* The isolate-request pad is held low throughout so the FLR path is the only isolation source, `cfg_flr_pf_active_i` is dropped before the recovery wait, the warm reset is waited for before any further CSR access, and the latched request and the hold counter are cleared at the end.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cool_reset_zero_delay_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FLR-ZERO-DELAY-DENY` |The FLR request latched in `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` with both counters at their reset 0 and no cool followed within the watched window, which is the RDL's "a value of 0 will prevent initiation" for the hold counter
|`CHK-FLR-ZERO-DELAY-COOL` |With the pre-delay at 0 and a non-zero hold the cool asserted inside the synchroniser allowance, so no programmed pre-delay was counted, was held and released, and the warm-domain scratch register that carried a pattern beforehand reads 0 afterwards
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-FLR-ZERO-DELAY-COOL`, `CHK-FLR-ZERO-DELAY-DENY` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-205-smc_log_engine_abort_test]]
===== 205 `smc_log_engine_abort_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_log_engine_abort_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the wrapper's own UART in `MCR.LOOP`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Halt a log-engine transfer with CTRL.EN on all four wrapper instances and bring the engine back.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_log_engine_transfer_test` runs transfers to completion. `log_engine.rdl` gives `CTRL.EN` the other half of its contract -- "When cleared, the engine stops fetching and writing, discards buffered log data and resets transfer progress. Configuration and pending LOG_LEN values are retained" -- and this leaf is the one that exercises it.
* Each wrapper is given one log filling its whole slot, which this region makes twice the UART transmit FIFO the `uart_log_engine_disable_during_xfer` firmware image pins and several fetch beats deep, so neither the fetch nor the write side can be finished when the disable lands one register access after the first byte is seen.
* Three legs, an allow followed by a deny followed by an allow, so the deny cannot pass on a dead bus: the transfer starts and bytes reach the receiver; `CTRL.EN` is cleared and, once the UART reports itself idle, fewer than the whole log has arrived, what did arrive is the head of that slot in order, and a second drain finds nothing more; a shorter length written into the same element while the engine is still disabled is delivered in full once `CTRL.EN` is set again.
* Draining until the UART reports transmitter-empty with no received data, for a run of polls longer than a character time, is how the firmware image measures the same thing, and it is what lets the halt be checked without knowing how many bytes the UART had buffered.
* Nothing writes a pending LOG_CTRL length back to 0: the aborted length is replaced by a shorter non-zero one, so the arbiter request the element holds never drops before the hardware clear that ends it.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_log_engine_abort_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-HALTED` |On every wrapper a transfer was in flight -- bytes had reached the receiver -- when `CTRL.EN` was cleared, and once the UART went idle at least one and fewer than the whole log had arrived, each byte the head of that wrapper's own slot in order, with a second drain finding nothing more
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-LENGTH-KEPT` |LOG_CTRL still read the length it was given while the engine was disabled, which is the RDL's reset of the FSMs, flops and FIFOs with the registers preserved
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-RETRIGGER` |A shorter length written into the same element while the engine was disabled delivered exactly its bytes from the head of the slot once `CTRL.EN` was set again, hardware cleared the length, and INTR_STATUS stayed clear across both the halt and the re-trigger
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-HALTED`, `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-LENGTH-KEPT`, `CHK-LOG-ENGINE-ABORT-RETRIGGER` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-206-smc_periph_regblock_sweep_test]]
===== 206 `smc_periph_regblock_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_periph_regblock_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/register.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `register`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Cycle the peripheral register blocks no other leaf writes against their RDL contract.

*Test Coverage*:

* The AVSBus controller, the three telemetry receivers, the OCTS system timer, the eFuse interface controller, the DMA controller configuration and the four log engines' region and enable registers are written by no other leaf in this package. Each takes the cycle the other register sweeps use: read at reset, the all-ones and the all-zeros pattern of the fields the generated contract pins, each half written on its own so the byte lanes over the other half are deasserted, then the RDL reset restored.
* Only fields the contract makes plain read-write are driven, so a `singlepulse` trigger, a `oneToClear` event and a hardware-driven status are never written by the generic cycle.
* `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` additionally holds `efuse_data` and `program_enable` at their reset, on top of the `singlepulse` `efuse_program_go` the contract already excludes, so no combination the sweep writes can arm a fuse burn. Its address and read-back select are driven normally.
* `AVS_CFG_1` carries the AVS clock mux and divider, and `avsbus_controller.rdl` says to gate the clocks entering the mux before changing either and to turn them back on afterwards, which is the order this cycle takes. The gate is on the AVS protocol clock, not the register interface.
* The OCTS system timer's `CTRL` does not take the all-ones and all-zeros patterns. `system_timer_octs.rdl` makes `CREDIT_VAL` "must be greater than PULSE_WIDTH" and `PULSE_WIDTH` "must be less than CREDIT_VAL" a software constraint, and `system_timer_octs_core.sv` holds a run-time assertion to it; all ones makes the two equal and all zeros makes `CREDIT_VAL` zero. The register takes two constrained cycles instead, whose four patterns between them drive every bit of all three fields both ways while every word written keeps `CREDIT_VAL` above the effective `PULSE_WIDTH` -- effective because the RDL rounds a `PULSE_WIDTH` of 0 up to 1. The sequence checks that relation host-side for every word, including the RDL reset it restores, before issuing any access, and both constrained fields sit in the same half of the word so the half-register writes never leave an illegal pair resident.
* The telemetry `INTR_TEST` forces the two INTR_STATUS events, and the generic cycle leaves the level one released and never pulses the other, so each receiver takes an interrupt leg after its three cycles. `telemetry_receiver.rdl` makes `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` plain storage that forces the interrupt on 1 and releases it on 0 over a read-only `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD`; `INTR_TEST.MISSING_LAST` is a write-only `singlepulse` over a `oneToClear` `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST`. With INTR_STATUS read clear, the level test field written to 1 has to set exactly its status bit and written back to 0 has to release it; a pulse of the write-only test field has to set exactly its status bit, which then holds until a write of its own mask clears it. Every INTR_STATUS read of the leg is predicted exactly from the INTR_TEST word driving it, and the field masks and access types come from the generated IP-XACT contract.
* The DMA controller's block answers a sub-word write with an error response, so its configuration takes the same cycle at full width instead of in halves.
* `log_engine/CTRL` is swept last, so the enable is only ever set while the region and write addresses are back at their reset and no LOG_CTRL element holds a length, and no transfer starts.
* `AVS_CMD`, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR`, the telemetry counters, the DMA transfer descriptors and the eFuse read and program data registers are not driven: each is a command, an event clear or a hardware-owned value with a leaf of its own or no written-value expectation.

* `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS` is the one register of the eFuse block no leaf reaches. Four of its fields are `sw = r; hw = w` and its three clears are write-only `singlepulse`, so the half-register cycle has nothing to drive and a sweep of it would assert rather than run. What it can be held to is checked instead: a read reports an idle block with no error bit and no clear bit set, a write of all three clears is accepted, and the register then reads back exactly what it read before -- so no clear stayed set and no `sw = r` state field moved under the write. The masks come from the generated `efuse_interface_ctrl.h`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_periph_regblock_sweep_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PERIPH-REGBLOCK-SINGLE-SWEEP` |Every single-instance peripheral register read its RDL reset, carried the all-ones and all-zeros pattern of its driven fields after each write, drove no bit outside the fields the RDL declares, held the reset of the bits software cannot write, and returned to that reset
|`CHK-PERIPH-TELEMETRY-SWEEP` |All three telemetry receivers cycled INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST and CTRL against their contract and were restored; on each, INTR_STATUS read clear at idle, `INTR_TEST.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` written to 1 set exactly `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` and written back to 0 released it, and a pulse of the write-only `INTR_TEST.MISSING_LAST` set exactly `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST`, which held until a write of its own mask cleared it
|`CHK-PERIPH-LOG-ENGINE-SWEEP` |All four log engines cycled their region size, region address, write address and enable against their contract and were restored, with the enable set only while the addresses were at their reset
|`CHK-PERIPH-REGBLOCK-COMPARES` |The scoreboard booked at least the expected number of exact-value compares of its own for the reads whose whole word the RDL contract predicts, independently of the sequence's counters
|`CHK-PERIPH-EFUSE-STATUS` |EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS read an idle block with no error bit and no clear bit set, took a write of all three of its write-only singlepulse clears, and read back exactly what it read before
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-PERIPH-EFUSE-STATUS`, `CHK-PERIPH-LOG-ENGINE-SWEEP`, `CHK-PERIPH-REGBLOCK-COMPARES`, `CHK-PERIPH-REGBLOCK-SINGLE-SWEEP`, `CHK-PERIPH-TELEMETRY-SWEEP` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Only fields the contract makes plain read-write are driven; `singlepulse` triggers,
`oneToClear` events and hardware-driven status are never written by the generic cycle.
`AVS_CMD`, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR`, the telemetry counters, the DMA transfer descriptors and the
eFuse read and program data registers are not driven, each being a command, an event clear or a
hardware-owned value with a leaf of its own or no written-value expectation. The OCTS `CTRL` does
not take the all-ones and all-zeros patterns, which would break its documented
`CREDIT_VAL`/`PULSE_WIDTH` constraint; it takes two constrained cycles instead.

'''''

[[sec-207-smc_uart_char_loopback_test]]
===== 207 `smc_uart_char_loopback_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_char_loopback_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); each wrapper's own UART in `MCR.LOOP`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Send characters through every UART's own loopback and check the registers they move.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_uart_log_engine_field_sweep_test` writes the UART's software-owned registers and the log-engine leaves read LSR and RBR while the engine feeds the transmitter, but no other leaf drives the UART's own transmit holding register or writes at the addresses the read-only registers occupy. This leaf owns the write side of RBR, IIR, LSR and MSR and the external-register handshake behind RBR.
* FCR is write-only, so its enable is checked where its effect shows: `uart_16550_main.rdl` gives `IIR.FIFOS_ENABLED` the value `0x3` with the FIFOs on and `0x0` with them off, and the leaf drives FCR both ways and requires IIR to follow. `FCR.RCVR_FIFO_RESET` is `singlepulse`, and its effect is `LSR.DR` going away with a character still unread.
* Six distinct bytes are written into THR and compared against what comes back out of RBR on each wrapper, with the transmitter required empty before the first and the receiver quiet after the last. That is also the only access that reaches the external-register interface RBR sits behind.
* With `IER.ERBFI` set and a character waiting, IIR has to report an interrupt pending -- `INTERRUPT_PENDING` is active low -- with the Received Data Ready id `0x2` the RDL names, and no interrupt pending once RBR is drained.
* The Programmer's Guide UART section (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`) fixes the loopback modem mapping: with `MCR.LOOP` set, CTS follows RTS, DSR follows DTR, RI follows OUT1 and DCD follows OUT2. Raising the four outputs must raise exactly those four MSR levels and dropping them must clear them. The sticky deltas separate on the same two legs: DCTS, DDSR and DDCD set on either edge, while TERI sets only on the trailing edge of RI, so the rising leg must leave TERI clear and the falling leg must set it.
* LSR and MSR have no write side, so a write at either address must leave them reading what they read before.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_char_loopback_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-CHAR-LOOPBACK` |Every byte written into the transmit holding register of every UART came back out of the receiver of the same UART unchanged, with the transmitter reported empty before the first and the receiver quiet after the last, and no overrun, parity, framing or break error on any LSR read
|`CHK-UART-FCR-EFFECT` |The write-only FCR was driven both ways and IIR reported the matching `FIFOS_ENABLED` encoding each time, and a write of the singlepulse receive-FIFO reset with a character waiting made LSR stop reporting received data
|`CHK-UART-IIR-RX-READY` |IIR reported an interrupt pending with the Received Data Ready id while a character waited and the received-data interrupt was enabled, and none pending once RBR was drained
|`CHK-UART-MSR-LOOPBACK` |Raising all four MCR outputs raised exactly the four MSR levels the programming guide maps them to with DCTS, DDSR and DDCD set and TERI clear; dropping them cleared the levels and set all four deltas including TERI; and a write at the LSR and MSR addresses left both reading what they read before
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-CHAR-LOOPBACK`, `CHK-UART-FCR-EFFECT`, `CHK-UART-IIR-RX-READY`, `CHK-UART-MSR-LOOPBACK` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-208-smc_efuse_lock_guard_test]]
===== 208 `smc_efuse_lock_guard_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_lock_guard_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the default eFuse image in the adopter bank model

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Establish a software lock on three eFuse shadow fields and check the guard's answer.

*Test Coverage*:

* `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` gives every shadow field a 4-bit `lock` permission reachable two ways, and says the guard (`efuse_guard.sv`) enforces whichever of the hardware and software locks is more restrictive. The software lock is the `LOCKS` CSR, "write-1-to-set", so firmware can tighten access but never loosen it without a reset.
* `smc_efuse_locked_access_interrupt_test` drives that path on `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` with a lock its preload asset already sets; this leaf establishes its locks itself, on fields the default image leaves clear.
* Three fields -- the first two SPARE entries and the OCCP transport timeout, whose locks the default image leaves clear -- each take four steps, the first being the live control for the two denies: a pattern written and read back while unlocked; the write lock set and a different pattern shown not to land; `LOCKS` written again with that bit clear and the bit shown still set; the read lock set and the read shown not to disclose the field.
* The sequence reads `LOCKS` first and fails if any bit it is about to set is already set by the image, so it never mistakes a pre-set lock for one it established.
* The response to a write-locked write is recorded rather than asserted: neither the RDL nor the architecture document fixes whether the guard refuses or ignores it, and the claim is that the write did not land. Likewise the read-locked read claims non-disclosure only, because the document states the permission but not the substituted word.
* `SMC_CONFIG` and `JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` are left alone: the first carries boot configuration other logic reads, the second is the held-out leaf's subject. A software lock is cleared only by reset, so the leaf leaves its six bits set and is terminal for those three fields.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_efuse_lock_guard_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-PRE` |LOCKS read the eFuse image word with every lock bit the sequence goes on to set still clear, so each deny that follows is against a lock the sequence established itself
|`CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-WRITE` |On all three fields a pattern written while unlocked read back exactly, and a different pattern written with the write lock set did not land -- the field still read the first pattern -- and the guard answered the refused write instead of wedging the bus
|`CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-WOSET` |On all three fields a later write of LOCKS with the field's write-lock bit clear left it set, which is the `onwrite = woset` contract the RDL gives every lock
|`CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-READ` |On all three fields a read taken with the read lock set returned something other than the word the field holds, so the guard withheld the content
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-PRE`, `CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-READ`, `CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-WOSET`, `CHK-EFUSE-LOCK-GUARD-WRITE` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The response to a write-locked write is recorded rather than asserted, because
neither the RDL nor the architecture document fixes whether the guard refuses or ignores it; the
claim is only that the write did not land. The read-locked read claims non-disclosure only,
because the document states the permission but not the substituted word. `SMC_CONFIG` and
`JTAG_PUBLIC_IDENTITY` are left alone.

'''''

[[sec-209-smc_cpu_ctrl_read_only_write_test]]
===== 209 `smc_cpu_ctrl_read_only_write_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_ctrl_read_only_write_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/register.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `register`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Write at every CPU_CTRL address the RDL makes read-only, and write 0 into the singlepulse reset fields.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_rdl_field_sweep_test` owns CPU_CTRL and drives every register the RDL makes writable, but never writes at the addresses of the registers it makes `sw = r`; this leaf exercises the decode row those addresses take on a write.
* `TEST_CTRL`, `SMC_ATTRIBUTES` and the head of each of the four per-core writeback program-counter arrays are written with all ones and required to read the same word afterwards as before. The sequence asserts each one's `rw_mask` is zero first, so a register that gained a writable field cannot be written at here by accident.
* `WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET` takes a full-width write of 0, which `smc_rdl_field_sweep_test` never does -- it writes the fields set and then writes 0 only over the half they do not occupy. Its four `reset_cycle_count` fields are `singlepulse`, so nothing is stored either way and the register has to read 0 afterwards. `CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT` is read either side as a second, weaker observation -- it carries the configured pulse durations and a bit that reads low while a core reset is in progress -- and does not catch a pulse that began and ended between the two reads.
* `RESET_CTRL` is not written. It carries the per-core and uncore reset levels and the four core reset-pulse starts, which is why `smc_rdl_field_sweep_test` excludes it, and a write of ones into it would reset the running bench.

* The four `MUTEX` registers are 64 bits wide with the mutex in bit 0, so a four-byte write at the low half selects that byte lane and one at the upper half does not. `cpu_ctrl.rdl` describes the field as "HW mutex. Reads will attempt to acquire mutex, 1 on success. If the mutex is already acquired, the read will return 0. To release the mutex, write any value to the register", so a read is the only way to see it, a read takes it, and any write gives it back whichever half it selects.
* Each mutex is taken through every combination of its bit and its lane. It is read first and has to come back free, which fails if anything else holds it. While held it takes a low-half write and then, once retaken, an upper-half write; each must give it back, which the read after it shows by taking it again. It is then released with a full-width write carrying a one on its lane, which the read after it shows by taking it again; released again, it takes a low-half write carrying a one and an upper-half write while free, neither of which may take it -- the read after them has to find it still free. The leg's last full-width release is read back the same way, so every release it claims is one the DUT showed; that read leaves the mutex taken, and nothing after it uses the register.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpu_ctrl_read_only_write_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-READ-ONLY-WRITE` |All six CPU_CTRL registers every field of which the RDL makes `sw = r` read the same word after a write of all ones at their address as before it
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-WDT-ZERO-WRITE` |A full-width write of 0 into the four singlepulse reset fields of WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET left the register reading 0, so nothing it carried was stored, and CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT read the same word either side with no core reset in progress when the second read landed
|`CHK-CPU-CTRL-MUTEX-HALF-WRITE` |Each of the four CPU_CTRL mutexes took four-byte writes at the half its bit occupies and at the half it does not, both while held and while free, and a full-width write carrying a one on its bit's lane while held; every write while held gave the mutex back, shown by the next read taking it again, the writes while free left it free, and the leg's last release was shown the same way, by the read after it taking the mutex
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CPU-CTRL-MUTEX-HALF-WRITE`, `CHK-CPU-CTRL-READ-ONLY-WRITE`, `CHK-CPU-CTRL-WDT-ZERO-WRITE` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `RESET_CTRL` is not written, since a write of ones into it would reset the running
bench. The `CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT` reads either side of the `WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET` write are a
second, weaker observation that does not catch a pulse that began and ended between the two reads.

'''''

[[sec-210-smc_dma_reg_byte_enable_error_test]]
===== 210 `smc_dma_reg_byte_enable_error_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_reg_byte_enable_error_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `dma`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Refuse a sub-word write at every writable DMA register, and show the refusal takes no effect.

*Test Coverage*:

* This block answers a sub-word write with an error, which is why `smc_periph_regblock_sweep_test` cycles its configuration at full width. The generated block says why: `reg_error = (devmode_i & addrmiss) | wr_err` and `wr_err = reg_we & (addr_hit[N] & |(PERMIT[N] & ~reg_be))`, so a write errors when it omits a byte lane that register's `PERMIT` mask requires -- not merely when it is narrow. Every register update is gated on `!reg_error`.
* That distinction decides where the write lands. `PERMIT` covers the lanes a register's fields occupy and all thirteen writable registers have fields in their low half, so a two-byte write at the register's own address can leave `PERMIT` satisfied and be accepted. The write therefore goes to the upper half, which omits the low lanes of all thirteen.
* Each of the thirteen -- the configuration word and the twelve transfer-descriptor registers -- takes four accesses: a full-width read that records what it holds; a full-width write of that same value, which has to be accepted and is the live control that the address is writable at all; the two-byte write over the upper half, which has to be refused; and a full-width read that has to return the recorded value.
* The last step is also why the leaf is safe against the transfer descriptors: a refused write never reaches the register. The second writes back the value already there. No transfer is started -- in this frontend the launch is a read of a `NEXT_ID` register, which is read-only and outside the set this leaf touches.
* The read-only registers are left alone. Their uncovered rows pair `addr_hit` with `reg_re` and a set `reg_error`, which no stimulus can produce: `reg_re` and `reg_we` are mutually exclusive, `wr_err` is gated on `reg_we`, and `addrmiss` needs no address to hit.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dma_reg_byte_enable_error_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-REG-BYTE-ENABLE-ERROR` |At each of the thirteen writable DMA registers a full-width write of the word it already held was accepted and a two-byte write over its upper half was refused with an error response, so the refusal is the missing byte lanes and not a dead window
|`CHK-DMA-REG-REFUSED-WRITE-NO-EFFECT` |Every one of the thirteen read back the word it held before its refused write, so the byte-enable error gates the register update rather than being reported after it
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DMA-REG-BYTE-ENABLE-ERROR`, `CHK-DMA-REG-REFUSED-WRITE-NO-EFFECT` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The read-only registers are left alone; their uncovered error rows pair a read
enable with a set error, which no stimulus can produce.

'''''

[[sec-211-smc_uart_core_mode_select_test]]
===== 211 `smc_uart_core_mode_select_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_core_mode_select_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); each wrapper's own UART in `MCR.LOOP`, and wrapper 0 in `MCR.LINE_LOOPBACK`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive the three UART mode selectors no other leaf moves, and check what each one is specified to do.

*Test Coverage*:

* Every other UART leaf in the package configures the UART the same way -- the FIFOs enabled, DMA mode 0, the receive trigger at one character and `MCR.LOOP` for the loopback -- so this leaf is the only one that moves three of the core's mode selectors: `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` cleared, `FCR.DMA_MODE_SELECT` set, and `MCR.LINE_LOOPBACK` set.
* `hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/doc/architecture.adoc` describes the two receive paths the 16550 has -- software reads "from RBR or FIFO" -- and `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` resets clear. A character is left unread in the receive FIFO and the FIFOs are then turned off: `IIR.FIFOS_ENABLED` has to report `0x0`, the encoding `uart_16550_main.rdl` gives that state, and `LSR.DR` has to read clear, because the character parked in the FIFO is no longer on the path software reads. Two further characters are then sent one at a time and compared, which is the only traffic in the package that goes through the receiver buffer register rather than the FIFO.
* The Programmer's Guide UART FIFO section (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`) says "Set `FCR.DMA_MODE_SELECT` only to use mode-1 DMA service indications" and `uart_16550_main_wo.rdl` gives FCR a `DMA_MODE_SELECT` bit. With DMA mode 1 selected and `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER` at `0x1`, which that RDL names as four characters, one character is sent and left unread. Its trigger level is not reached, so the only interrupt that can arise is the reception timeout `architecture.adoc` fixes at four character times and `uart_16550_main.rdl` names id `0x6`; IIR has to report exactly that, and none pending once the character is read out. Four characters are then sent and read back in order, which is the same mode with the trigger level reached instead of timed out.
* The Programmer's Guide UART section (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`): "With `MCR.LINE_LOOPBACK` set, the modem inputs are routed straight back out to the modem outputs and all four `MSR` level bits read 0." The leaf sets it and requires those four bits to read 0. The receiver input is held idle in that mode, so a character written into THR has to be transmitted without ever being received: the leaf polls until `LSR.TEMT` reports the transmitter drained and requires `LSR.DR` clear on every read up to that point, which is a bound the DUT sets rather than a fixed wait.
* Still in line loopback, the divisor is slowed and a burst longer than the SMC UARTs' 32-entry transmit FIFO (`hw/sys/smc/doc/periphs.adoc`, peripheral parameter table; `hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/doc/index.adoc`) is written into THR without polling, so the transmit FIFO reaches its full condition while the transmitter is still draining. What the leaf checks is what the register map exposes: `LSR.THRE` clear straight after the burst, so the FIFO is holding characters, and `LSR.TEMT` and `LSR.THRE` both set once it has drained. The full flag is not a register field and is not claimed.
* Line loopback runs on wrapper 0 only. That mode substitutes the receive pin onto the transmit pin, and `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` drives only UART0's receive pad -- idle high -- unless `+smc_uart_cross_3to0` shorts the pairs, so wrapper 0 is the only one where the substituted pin has a defined value. The other two modes use `MCR.LOOP`, which keeps every character inside the UART, and run on all four wrappers.
* Every character the legs send is distinct and the sequence fails if they are not, so a character one leg left behind cannot be read as the character another leg sent. The UART is returned to its reset configuration on each wrapper afterwards.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_uart_core_mode_select_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-RBR-PATH` |On every wrapper FCR.FIFO_ENABLE was written clear with a character unread in the receive FIFO, IIR reported the FIFOs off and LSR stopped reporting received data, and the characters sent with the FIFOs off came back out of the receiver buffer register unchanged before the FIFOs were enabled again and IIR reported them on
|`CHK-UART-DMA-MODE-1` |On every wrapper FCR selected DMA mode 1 with the receive trigger at four characters, and every character sent in that mode came back in order, both below the trigger level and with it reached
|`CHK-UART-RX-TIMEOUT` |On every wrapper a single character left unread below the trigger level made IIR report an interrupt pending with the Reception Timeout id, the only source that can be pending below the trigger, and none pending once that character was read out
|`CHK-UART-LINE-LOOPBACK` |With MCR.LINE_LOOPBACK set on wrapper 0 all four MSR level bits read 0 as the programming guide requires, a character written into THR was transmitted to completion without the receiver ever reporting data, and a burst longer than the transmit FIFO left LSR reporting the holding register non-empty and then drained to both TEMT and THRE set
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-UART-RBR-PATH`, `CHK-UART-DMA-MODE-1`, `CHK-UART-RX-TIMEOUT`, `CHK-UART-LINE-LOOPBACK` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The transmit-FIFO full flag is not a register field and is not claimed; only
`LSR.THRE` clear after the burst and `TEMT` and `THRE` set after the drain are checked. Line
loopback runs on wrapper 0 only, the one wrapper whose receive pad the bench drives to a defined
value.

'''''

[[sec-212-smc_i2c_config_regblock_sweep_test]]
===== 212 `smc_i2c_config_regblock_sweep_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_config_regblock_sweep_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the I2C block left idle, neither engine enabled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Cycle every I2C configuration register on every instance with the block held idle.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_i2c_intr_reg_sweep_test` drives the interrupt and event registers and the protocol leaves drive the bus, but no other leaf writes the block's configuration. This leaf owns the write enables and the read mux behind the control register, the five timing registers, both FIFO threshold registers, the three timeout controls, the NACK handler timeout, the target identity, the bus override and the SMBus control, on all three instances.
* Each is driven to all-ones and all-zeros over the fields the generated contract pins, through half-register writes whose byte lanes over the other half are deasserted, and restored to its RDL reset. Every readback checks the whole register, so each half write also proves the untouched half kept its value.
* **The block stays idle.** `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` are the two fields that start the controller and the target, and both are held at their reset for the whole cycle. Every other CTRL field only shapes how a running block behaves. The bus monitor `CTRL.MULTI_CONTROLLER_MONITOR_EN` selects is a monitor whose outputs are detect and event strobes, nothing that drives SCL or SDA, and CTRL is cycled first so it is back at its reset before the timeout registers are given values.
* **The override never pulls a line down.** `i2c.rdl` gives `OVRD.SCLVAL` and `OVRD.SDAVAL` the sense "0 - Pull the line low, 1 - Release the line", and `TXOVRDEN` enables both. All three sit in one byte, so a single write moves them together: the ones pattern releases both lines while enabling the override, and the zero pattern clears `TXOVRDEN` in the same write that clears the values.
* **No zero the sweep writes is a value the reset does not already hold.** `i2c.rdl` says of `TIMING0.THIGH` and `TIMING0.TLOW` that each "Must be `>= 2`". Every register in the set resets to zero over the fields the cycle drives, so the all-zeros leg only restores what reset already put there; the constraint is a programming rule for a running controller, and this leaf never enables one.
* All three guarantees are checked as assertions over every word the cycle would leave resident -- the halves between the two writes of a leg included -- and they run before the sequence issues a single access, so a contract that changed under the sweep stops it rather than starting an engine or pulling a bus line low.
* `FIFO_CTRL` is not in the set: the generated contract gives it no software-writable field with a pinned readback, because `RXRST`, `FMTRST`, `ACQRST` and `TXRST` are every one of them self-clearing. The FIFO data ports and the status registers are excluded for the same reason, the engine writing only fields the contract pins exactly.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_config_regblock_sweep_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CONFIG-REG-SWEEP` |All three I2C instances drove all fifteen configuration registers to all-ones and all-zeros over the fields their RDL pins, through half-register writes whose byte lanes over the other half were deasserted, and every register was restored to its reset and read back
|`CHK-I2C-CONFIG-IDLE-GUARD` |Every register cycle was checked before any access that the words it would leave resident hold CTRL.ENABLEHOST and CTRL.ENABLETARGET at their reset, never enable the bus override with SCLVAL or SDAVAL clear, and are zero over the driven fields wherever the reset is
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-CONFIG-IDLE-GUARD`, `CHK-I2C-CONFIG-REG-SWEEP` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `FIFO_CTRL` is not in the set, because its four self-clearing fields give the
contract no pinned readback; the FIFO data ports and the status registers are excluded for the
same reason.

'''''

[[sec-213-smc_i2c_fifo_reset_pulse_test]]
===== 213 `smc_i2c_fifo_reset_pulse_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_fifo_reset_pulse_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the I2C block left idle, neither engine enabled

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Pulse each of the four I2C FIFO resets and check it against a measured fill level.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_i2c_config_regblock_sweep_test` cycles the I2C configuration registers but cannot express `FIFO_CTRL`: `i2c.rdl` makes all four of its fields `sw = w` with `singlepulse`, so the generated contract pins no written value to read back and the half-register cycle has nothing to drive. No other leaf writes the register, so this leaf is the only one that pulses the four resets.
* The block is idle throughout -- `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` stay at their reset -- so no engine drains what the sequence puts in and every level read is one the sequence caused.
* **`FMTRST` and `TXRST` carry the strong claim.** `i2c.rdl` maps them to the Controller TX and Target TX FIFOs, and both of those have a software write port, `FDATA` and `TXDATA`, whose push is not gated on either engine enable. The sequence fills each, reads the level out of `HOST_FIFO_STATUS.FMTLVL` and `TARGET_FIFO_STATUS.TXLVL`, pulses the reset and requires that level to have gone to empty. The two fills are different depths -- three bytes and five -- so a status register reporting the other FIFO's level fails the compare before any reset is pulsed.
* **`RXRST` and `ACQRST` carry a weaker claim, stated here rather than implied.** They reset the Controller RX and Target RX FIFOs, and both of those are filled only by traffic on the wire: the controller receiving from a remote target, or a remote controller writing to this block as a target. Neither is reachable from the CSR port alone, and the leaves that drive the bus own the protocol agent and are a different shape. So what this leaf shows for these two is that each is pulsed while the two software-fillable FIFOs hold known, different levels and **neither level moves**. That fails if the reset decode is not one-hot, but it does **not** show that either reset empties the FIFO it names. Closing that needs a directed leaf on the protocol branch that first acquires a byte.
* The same one-hot check covers the other two: `FMTRST` must leave the target transmit level untouched while clearing the controller one, and `TXRST` is pulsed last with the controller FIFO already empty, so each of the four resets is shown to reach its own FIFO and no other.
* `FIFO_CTRL` is read after the four pulses and must read 0, which is the `singlepulse` contract the RDL gives all four fields.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_fifo_reset_pulse_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-RST-EMPTIES` |On every instance FMTRST and TXRST each emptied the FIFO the RDL names for it, from a level the sequence had put there through FDATA and TXDATA and measured in the status registers first
|`CHK-I2C-FIFO-RST-ONE-HOT` |On every instance each of the four resets reached its own FIFO and no other -- RXRST and ACQRST left both measured levels where they were, FMTRST left the target transmit level untouched, TXRST cleared the target level with the controller FIFO already empty -- and FIFO_CTRL read 0 afterwards, which is the singlepulse contract for all four
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-I2C-FIFO-RST-EMPTIES`, `CHK-I2C-FIFO-RST-ONE-HOT` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `RXRST` and `ACQRST` carry only the one-hot claim: the Controller RX and Target RX
FIFOs are filled only by wire traffic, which is not reachable from the CSR port alone, so the leaf
does not show that either reset empties the FIFO it names. Closing that needs a directed leaf on
the protocol branch that first acquires a byte.

'''''

[[sec-214-smc_filter_region_span_test]]
===== 214 `smc_filter_region_span_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_region_span_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN and JTAG); the SMC DMA as the outbound master

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Program a filter region spanning two granules on every outbound entry, and show one of them enforced on the bus.

*Test Coverage*:

* `smc_filter_config_field_sweep_test` cycles `FILTER_CONFIG` on every entry and `smc_filter_multi_entry_test` reads the reset of all of them, but nothing programs `START_ADDR` and `END_ADDR` into a region. A sweep cannot: its ones and zeros patterns give both registers the same value, so the start and the end always land in the same granule. Only `smc_dma_sanity_test_seq` programs a spanning region, and only on entry 0; this leaf gives entries 1 to 15 a start and an end in different granules.
* **The outbound filter carries the region, and the choice is from the document.** `hw/sys/smc/doc/fabric.adoc` separates the two: inbound filtering "protects SMC resources from unauthorized external access", which is the path this sequence's own CSR accesses arrive on, while outbound filtering "manages which external resources the SMC can access, restricting SMC-initiated requests". No access this leaf makes to program or read a filter can therefore be caught by the filter it is programming. The same document records the difference the traffic leg relies on: of traffic matching no entry, "the inbound filter blocks it, and the outbound filter permits it".
* **What the region proves comes from the RDL.** `filter_ctrl.rdl` states the write-back rule for both address registers: "Hardware writes the rounded start_addr and end_addr back into these fields only when both land in the same granule; otherwise readback returns the programmed values even though matching is still granule-aligned." Each of entries 1 to 15 is driven both ways and both readbacks are required -- a single-granule region must read back rounded down to the granule base and up to its top, a spanning one exactly as programmed -- so the leaf fails if hardware rounds a spanning region or leaves a single-granule one alone. `FILTER_CONFIG.allow_burst` is set, which that RDL makes the 4 KiB granule.
* **The enforcement leg uses the DMA, which is the outbound master.** `fabric.adoc` lists the DMA controller among the SMC-initiated paths that run "Alias remap -> filtering -> destination". Entry 1 is enabled over the spanning region with `write_allowed` clear and `read_allowed` set, and the DMA copies a word into the region and a word a granule above it. The copy inside must leave its destination holding the sentinel it was seeded with; the copy outside must land, and that second copy is what shows the first was refused rather than the DMA idle. Both descriptors are required to complete, so neither result can come from a transfer that never ran.
* The observable there is memory rather than the response: the backend is elaborated with `ErrorCap(idma_pkg::NO_ERROR_HANDLING)`, so a refused write raises no error the DMA reports. The JTAG2AXI bridge seeds and reads those addresses and is not the master under test: it enters the fabric on the inbound side rather than the outbound one the entry sits on, so the outbound filter never sees its traffic.
* Entry 1 is the highest-priority entry `smc_dma_sanity_test_seq` leaves alone, the hit index being a leading-zero count over the entries. The leaf reads entry 0 first and fails if it is already enabled, so a rule of somebody else's cannot be what the traffic leg measures.
* Every entry the leaf programs is restored to its RDL reset, the traffic entry's three registers are read back to prove it, and `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` is never written.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_filter_region_span_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FILTER-REGION-SPAN` |Each of outbound entries 1 to 15 took a region whose start and end sit in different 4 KiB granules and read both address registers back exactly as programmed, and a region inside one granule and read it back rounded to the granule base and top, which is the write-back rule filter_ctrl.rdl states
|`CHK-FILTER-REGION-ENFORCED` |With outbound entry 1 enabled over a two-granule region with write_allowed clear, a DMA copy into the region left its destination at the seeded sentinel while a copy a granule above the region landed, both transfers having completed; every entry was restored to its RDL reset and read back and the write-once lock was never written
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-FILTER-REGION-ENFORCED`, `CHK-FILTER-REGION-SPAN` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The refusal is observed in memory rather than as a response: the DMA backend is
elaborated without error handling, so a refused write raises no error the DMA reports.
`FILTER_CONFIG.locked` is never written.

'''''

[[sec-328-smc_filter_remap_bitwalk_test]]
===== 328 `smc_filter_remap_bitwalk_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_remap_bitwalk_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN); the generated IP-XACT register map for every address, field and reset

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Walk a one and a zero across every software-writable bit of the filter and alias-remap address registers and every mailbox write strobe, reading each register back against the contract its RDL states.

*Test Coverage*:

* The filter and remap leaves program a few fixed regions (`smc_filter_region_span_test`, `smc_dma_sanity_test`, `smc_remap_cla_test`), so most bits of `START_ADDR`, `END_ADDR`, `REGION_START` and `REGION_END` only ever hold their reset. This leaf gives every one of those bits a one and a zero on every entry, with a readback after each write.
* **Filter address registers.** `filter_ctrl.rdl` makes both fields `hw = rw` and states the write-back rule: the rounded pair is written back "only when both land in the same granule; otherwise readback returns the programmed values". Every entry is read at its `FILTER_CONFIG` reset first -- disabled, `allow_burst` clear, so the granule is 2^`data_bus_width` bytes -- and the two registers of an entry are walked together, one carrying the one and the other the zero, so the pair never shares a granule and each readback is required to be the programmed word. A disabled entry matches nothing, so the fabric this leaf's own accesses cross stays usable while the range is an arbitrary pair; the rounding case is `smc_filter_region_span_test`.
* **Remap table.** `alias_remap.rdl` gives `start_addr` and `end_addr` bits [55:12] as `sw = rw; hw = r` storage with no side effect, so the expected readback is the written word masked to the field, the low twelve bits and the top byte reading zero. `REGION_ATTRS.valid` is read clear on every region before its bounds move.
* **Mailbox data and strobes.** `axil_mailbox.rdl` makes `WRITE_DATA` `sw = w; onwrite = wuser` and `READ_DATA` `sw = r; onread = ruser`, and `axil_mailbox_smc_wrap.rdl` says the two apertures of a pair share one FIFO, "data written through WRITE_DATA in one aperture is what READ_DATA in the other aperture returns". Each of the 64 apertures takes a walking-one strobe over its eight byte lanes and four of the 256 strobe patterns, so every pattern but the empty one is driven once across the block; the AXI master refuses an empty strobe. The paired readback must carry the written byte on every strobed lane and zero on every other lane, which is what tells a strobe the mailbox honoured from one it ignored.
* Every address comes from the generated maps, each instance cross-checked between `smc_addr.h` and `smc_reg.py`, and every field position, width, reset and access type from the IP-XACT export. Every readback carries its expected word into the scoreboard, and the leaf requires the scoreboard to have booked one exact compare per such read.
* Every filter entry and remap region is restored to its RDL reset and read back. Every mailbox `ERROR_FLAGS` register is read clear, the sticky threshold interrupts the pushes raised are acknowledged through `IRQS` and read clear, and `mailbox_interrupts` must be quiet.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. For each of the 16 inbound and 16 outbound filter entries: read `FILTER_CONFIG` against its reset word; for each of the 56 address bits write `START_ADDR` with that bit alone set and `END_ADDR` with that bit alone clear, read both back exactly, then the other way round and read both back; write both registers' reset words and read them back.
. For each of the 8 alias-remap regions: read `REGION_ATTRS` and require `valid` clear; for each of the 44 writable bits walk `REGION_START` and `REGION_END` the same way, reading each back as the written word masked to the field; restore both and read them back.
. For each of the 64 mailbox apertures: for each walking-one strobe and each of the aperture's four shared patterns, write `WRITE_DATA` with a distinct 64-bit word under that strobe and read the paired aperture's `READ_DATA` against the word masked to the strobed lanes. Then read every `ERROR_FLAGS` as zero, acknowledge every `IRQS` and read it back as zero, and require `mailbox_interrupts` to be zero.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FILTER-ADDR-BITWALK` |On all 32 filter entries a one and a zero walked across all 56 bits of START_ADDR and END_ADDR, each pair reading back as programmed because its two words never share a granule, with FILTER_CONFIG at reset throughout and every entry restored to its RDL reset and read back
|`CHK-REMAP-REGION-BITWALK` |On all 8 alias-remap regions a one and a zero walked across all 44 writable bits of REGION_START and REGION_END, each reading back the written word with the unimplemented bits clear, valid read clear first and both bounds restored and read back
|`CHK-MAILBOX-STROBE-WALK` |Over the 64 mailbox apertures a walking-one byte strobe on each and every non-empty strobe pattern once across the block, every paired READ_DATA returning the written byte on each strobed lane and zero elsewhere, every ERROR_FLAGS read clear and mailbox_interrupts quiet
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The granule rounding case of the filter address registers belongs to
`smc_filter_region_span_test`; every pair walked here never shares a granule. The empty byte
strobe is not driven, because the AXI master refuses it.

'''''

[[sec-215-smc_dma_decouple_rw_test]]
===== 215 `smc_dma_decouple_rw_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_decouple_rw_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN and JTAG); the SMC DMA

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run DMA transfers with the read and write channels decoupled, and queue a second descriptor while the first is in flight.

*Test Coverage*:

* Every other DMA leaf leaves `CONFIG.DECOUPLE_RW` at its reset and runs the backend legalizer's coupled arm, where the read and the write machine advance together. This leaf runs the decoupled arm, where either may advance alone, and is the only leaf that queues a second descriptor while the legalizer is busy.
* The golden for the field is the generated header, not the RTL: `dma_ctrl.h` gives `DMA_CTRL__CONFIG__DECOUPLE_RW_bm` the value `0x2` and its reset `0x0`, and `dma_ctrl.rdl` makes it `sw = rw`. The leaf reads `CONFIG` first and fails if the field is already set, writes it, and requires it to read back before running anything through it.
* **Two transfers whose channels have different work to do.** Decoupling only shows if the two sides are not in step, so each transfer is two-dimensional with a stride on one side only: a scatter, where the source rows are contiguous and the destination rows are a stride apart, so the read side issues one long run and the write side many short ones; and a gather, the other way round, so the fragmented side is the read. Both move the same four distinct rows and every row is compared against its source at the stride that should have placed it, so a transfer that dropped, duplicated or misplaced a row fails rather than passing quietly.
* **Two descriptors back to back.** `dma_ctrl.rdl` says of `NEXT_ID` that "Reading this register starts the DMA transfer. Returns an ID value for the cumulative number of transfers. Returns 0 if command was not set up correctly", and of `DONE` that it "Holds the cumulative number of completed transfers". The second descriptor is therefore programmed and submitted without waiting for the first, and the leaf requires both ids to be non-zero and rising, `DONE` to have advanced by two, and each destination to hold its own payload rather than the other's or the sentinel.
* Every destination is seeded with a sentinel that is none of the payload rows, so a transfer that never ran reads as the sentinel and fails.
* **Transfers into a stalled SYS_OUT.** The legalizer issues a read or write request only while the backend's request ready for that side is high. Those readies come back from SYS_OUT through the AR register, the coupler's AW store, the write last-flag FIFO and the data FIFOs, and an always-ready responder never drops them. The leaf turns on the SYS_OUT responder's `enable_backpressure`, which holds READY low for 64 cycles out of every 65, and runs six 128-row 2D transfers of single-beat rows: the read side stalled (`ar`), the write side (`aw`, `w`), and both, first coupled and then decoupled. `CONFIG.ENABLE_ND` is set, so each row is a burst of its own; with it clear, the midend rejects every request as zero-length.
* The bench counts cycles at the SYS_OUT boundary with VALID high and READY low, and requires a count on every stalled channel. The rows are seeded and compared in the responder's memory directly, each transfer with rows of its own, and every row must match its source.
* A third mode sets `CONFIG.DECOUPLE_AW` (`dma_ctrl.h`: `DMA_CTRL__CONFIG__DECOUPLE_AW_bm`), so the channel coupler sends each AW without waiting for its write data. The same three stall cases run in it, which gives nine backpressured transfers in all.
* **Rows split at a page on one side only.** AXI bursts may not cross a 4 KB page, so the legalizer splits a row that does. Two 256-byte rows cross a page on one side only, first the source and then the destination, so one machine has two bursts to issue against the other's one. Each must arrive intact in the responder's memory and put exactly two AWs on SYS_OUT, both inside its destination.
* **The same splits with the channels decoupled.** With `CONFIG.DECOUPLE_RW` set, reads and writes split only at their own page boundary, so the source-split row becomes two read bursts and one write burst, and the destination-split row one read burst and two write bursts. The source split must put exactly one AW on SYS_OUT and the destination split exactly two, all inside their destinations, and both must arrive intact. A coupled source split runs between them and must put only its own two AWs on SYS_OUT.
* **Partial words, a queue behind a stall, and NEXT_ID writes.**
** A 29-byte row runs from a source 3 bytes into a bus word to a destination 5 bytes in, so both ends of the row are partial. It must arrive intact, and the eight bytes on either side must stay untouched.
** A second descriptor is offered while a 128-row transfer is held up by the stalled responder. It must get a higher id, and both must complete with their own data.
** Writes of 0 to the read-triggered `NEXT_ID_2..14` must leave `DONE` and `STATUS` as they were.
* The read request ready is driven low in the coupled and decoupled modes. The write request ready stays high in all three. The legalizer loads the next row only when both machines are done and both readies are high, and a stalled write fills the backend's three-beat data buffer, which stops the reads. So the read side saturates before 32 writes are outstanding, whatever channel the responder stalls. Driving the write ready low needs a responder that keeps accepting reads while their data waits, and this bench does not have one.
* `CONFIG` is restored to its reset and read back. The leaf writes no other DMA field, and touches no fuse.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_dma_decouple_rw_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-DECOUPLE-RW` |CONFIG.DECOUPLE_RW read back set from the mask the generated header gives it, and both transfers ran with the channels decoupled -- a scatter whose write side was the fragmented one and a gather whose read side was -- with every row landing where its stride puts it and matching its source; CONFIG was restored to its reset and read back
|`CHK-DMA-PAGE-SPLIT` |A 256-byte row whose source crossed a 4 KB page and whose destination did not, and one the other way round, each arrived intact and put exactly two AWs on SYS_OUT, both inside its destination
|`CHK-DMA-DECOUPLE-RW-PAGE-SPLIT` |With `DECOUPLE_RW` set, the source-split row (two read bursts, one write burst) put exactly one AW on SYS_OUT and the destination-split row (one read burst, two write bursts) exactly two, all inside their destinations; both rows arrived intact, and the coupled split run between them put only its own two AWs on SYS_OUT
|`CHK-DMA-QUEUED-DESCRIPTORS` |A second descriptor was programmed and submitted without waiting for the first, both NEXT_ID reads returned a non-zero and rising id rather than the 0 the RDL gives a rejected command, DONE advanced by two, and each destination held its own payload
|`CHK-DMA-UNALIGNED-QUEUED` |The 29-byte partial-word row arrived intact with its neighbours untouched, the descriptor queued behind the stalled transfer got a higher id and both completed with their own data, and the `NEXT_ID_2..14` writes left `DONE` and `STATUS` unchanged
|`CHK-DMA-LEGALIZER-BACKPRESSURE` |Nine 128-row 2D transfers ran into the backpressured SYS_OUT responder -- read side, write side and both, coupled, decoupled and with `DECOUPLE_AW`. Every stalled channel showed VALID high with READY low at the boundary, and every row of every transfer matched its own source
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-DMA-DECOUPLE-RW`, `CHK-DMA-DECOUPLE-RW-PAGE-SPLIT`, `CHK-DMA-LEGALIZER-BACKPRESSURE`, `CHK-DMA-PAGE-SPLIT`, `CHK-DMA-QUEUED-DESCRIPTORS`, `CHK-DMA-UNALIGNED-QUEUED` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The write request ready is never driven low; only the read request ready is, in the
coupled and decoupled modes. Driving the write ready low needs a responder that keeps accepting
reads while their data waits, and this bench does not have one. The leaf writes no other DMA
field.

'''''

[[sec-216-smc_intr_status_partial_clear_test]]
===== 216 `smc_intr_status_partial_clear_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_intr_status_partial_clear_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Clear write-one-to-clear status bits a few at a time and show the rest survive the write.

*Test Coverage*:

* Three blocks carry an interrupt status register whose bits software raises through the matching `INTR_TEST` and clears by writing a one back: the I2C `INTR_STATE`, the log-engine `INTR_STATUS` and the telemetry-receiver `INTR_STATUS`. Every other leaf that touches them raises the whole declared mask and clears the whole declared mask, so this leaf is the only one whose write carries a zero over a set bit and exercises the half of the `oneToClear` contract that says such a bit *stays* set.
* On each of the ten instances the leaf reads the register and requires it clear, so every bit it goes on to see set is one it raised itself; writes the event bits of `INTR_TEST` and requires exactly those raised; writes back half of them and requires precisely that half to have gone and the other half to still be set; then writes the rest and requires the register to read clear again, which is its reset.
* **Only the `read-write` fields take part, and the reason is in the generated map.** A status register mixes two kinds of field. The event bits are `read-write` -- hardware sets them, software clears them with a one, and they hold otherwise. The rest are `read-only` level bits hardware drives from a condition, and on I2C those are the FIFO thresholds and the stretch and halt indications; a write cannot clear one of those while its condition holds, so the leaf excludes them by their access type rather than expecting them to go.
* The two halves are alternating bits of the mask, so neither is a contiguous run a byte-granular decode could clear by accident. Where a register has only one clearable bit the write that has to leave it set carries no bits at all, which puts the same contract to the same test.
* Raising a status bit through `INTR_TEST` is the mechanism `smc_i2c_intr_reg_sweep_test` already uses. Nothing is left raised: every register ends its leg reading clear.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_intr_status_partial_clear_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-INTR-STATUS-PARTIAL-CLEAR` |On all ten write-one-to-clear status registers across the I2C blocks, the log engines and the telemetry receivers, the event mask was raised through INTR_TEST, half of it was written back and went, the bits the write carried a zero over stayed set, and the register read clear again once the rest was written
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-INTR-STATUS-PARTIAL-CLEAR` holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Only the `read-write` event fields take part; the `read-only` level bits hardware
drives from a condition (on I2C the FIFO thresholds and the stretch and halt indications) are
excluded by their access type, since a write cannot clear one while its condition holds.

'''''

[[sec-217-smc_gpio_data_ctrl_field_test]]
===== 217 `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_field_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_gpio_data_ctrl_field_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive each software-writable DATA_CTRL field of one idle GPIO instance on its own.

*Test Coverage*:
