draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: I2C2 driving the shared bus as controller for a write and a two-byte read against I2C1.

*Test Coverage*:

* This leaf makes instance 2 the controller, so its controller state machine acknowledges a byte and clocks one in. Which instance is the controller is set by which one gets `CTRL.ENABLEHOST`.
* The read asks for two bytes rather than one. A controller reading a single byte only ever NACKs it, so the acknowledge phase is entered only when a byte is followed by another.
* Both legs are checked at the far end: the write against the bytes the target acquired, the read against the bytes the target was told to source.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c2_controller_rdwr_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C2-CTRL-WRITE` |Controller I2C2 drove the bus and target I2C1 acquired every payload byte in order, with no NACK reported in `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`
|`CHK-I2C2-CTRL-READ` |Controller I2C2 clocked two bytes out of target I2C1 and read back exactly the bytes written to the target's TXDATA, acknowledging every byte but the last, then returned idle
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''


[[sec-227-smc_i2c_target_bus_timeout_test]]
===== 227 `smc_i2c_target_bus_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_bus_timeout_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the shared open-drain I2C bus

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The programmable bus timeout expiring at every slot of an addressed target transaction, and against the target's own stretch, on all three instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* `hw/ip/i2c/regs/i2c.rdl` describes `TIMEOUT_CTRL.MODE` 1 as a bus timeout that fires "if SCL is LOW for more time than `TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL`", and `doc/architecture.adoc` adds that the count "accumulates across all sources" and that "the counter resets when SCL goes high, so this count only accumulates during a single bit transfer". Parking SCL low is therefore what makes it expire.
* Unlike a STOP or a repeated START, the timeout is a counter rather than a bus event, so it lands in states where no control symbol can be driven -- the acknowledge slots, and the states the target reaches while stretching.
* The timeout value sits well above the VIP's per-bit SCL low time and the deliberate park sits well above the value, so the timeout fires only where this leaf puts it and never on ordinary bit timing.
* The stretch leg drives nothing on the bus at all: the target is holding SCL low itself because its acquisition FIFO is full, and the timeout counts that hold.
* The address-stretch leg then starts a transaction while the acquisition FIFO is still full, so the address cannot be deposited. The filling write is abandoned first: it and the new transaction share one VIP and cannot be in flight together.
* `doc/architecture.adoc` states that a bus timeout while the target was addressed adds an entry to the ACQ FIFO, and the RDL defines `SIGNAL` 6 for a transaction that "ended abnormally, for example, due to ... a Bus or Stretch Timeout". That entry is the observable.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_target_bus_timeout_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSTO-SLOT-SWEEP` |The bus timeout expired at each of nine slots of an addressed transaction on I2C0, every one recorded as an abnormal ending in the acquisition FIFO, with a clean write before and after
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSTO-STRETCH` |With its acquisition FIFO full, I2C0 held SCL low itself and the timeout counted that hold and returned the instance to idle, with nothing driven on the bus
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSTO-ADDR-STRETCH` |A transaction started while I2C0's acquisition FIFO was still full drove the address phase against a target with nowhere to deposit it, and the instance ran a clean write afterwards
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSTO-SLOT-SWEEP` |The slot sweep on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSTO-STRETCH` |The stretch timeout on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSTO-ADDR-STRETCH` |The address-phase stretch on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSTO-SLOT-SWEEP` |The slot sweep on I2C2
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSTO-STRETCH` |The stretch timeout on I2C2
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSTO-ADDR-STRETCH` |The address-phase stretch on I2C2
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nine checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''


[[sec-228-smc_i2c_bus_monitor_idle_test]]
===== 228 `smc_i2c_bus_monitor_idle_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_bus_monitor_idle_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the shared open-drain I2C bus

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The I2C bus monitor's idle-with-SCL-high state entered and left on every instance, witnessed by the host-timeout interrupt.

*Test Coverage*:

* `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` arms the bus monitor's inactive timeout, and the RDL calls the resulting interrupt a "Target Mode interrupt: asserted when the controller stops generating the clock longer than `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL`". Nothing else in this package programs that register.
* `INTR_STATE.HOST_TIMEOUT` is what makes the state observable rather than inferred: only the idling state counts that timeout down, so the interrupt firing is a witness that the monitor was in it. Leaving the state is witnessed the same way: after each exit the cleared interrupt stays clear through a hold as long as the park that raised it, and a further park raises it again, which a counter that never left the state cannot do once cleared.
* `TIMING4.T_BUF` is programmed long for this leaf, so the bus-free window after a STOP is wide enough for the bench to drive the bus low inside it; at the default of a few cycles it is shorter than a round trip from the sequence.
* The enable-with-multi-controller leg drives the monitor's other entry into the idling state, but asserts only that a clean transaction follows: the inactive counter is not reloaded on that path, so the host-timeout witness does not fire there, and no register reports the monitor's state directly. That entry is stimulus, not a claim.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_bus_monitor_idle_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSMON-IDLE-TIMEOUT` |With the bus busy and the bench holding SCL released mid-transaction, I2C0's monitor counted `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` down and raised `INTR_STATE.HOST_TIMEOUT`, with a clean write before and after
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSMON-RESUME` |I2C0's monitor left the idling state both ways. After a park raised `HOST_TIMEOUT`, SCL held low for as long as the park kept the cleared interrupt clear and a second park raised it again; after a STOP, the released bus held for as long as the park kept it clear and a further park raised it again, whose STOP was followed by the bus pulled low inside the bus-free window; the instance ran a clean write after
|`CHK-I2C0-BUSMON-MULTI-ENABLE` |I2C0 enabled with `CTRL.MULTI_CONTROLLER_MONITOR_EN` set on a quiet bus then ran a clean write that was acquired byte for byte
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSMON-IDLE-TIMEOUT` |The idle timeout on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSMON-RESUME` |The resume and stop legs on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C1-BUSMON-MULTI-ENABLE` |The multi-controller enable on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSMON-IDLE-TIMEOUT` |The idle timeout on I2C2
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSMON-RESUME` |The resume and stop legs on I2C2
|`CHK-I2C2-BUSMON-MULTI-ENABLE` |The multi-controller enable on I2C2
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all nine checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The multi-controller enable leg is stimulus, not a claim: it asserts only that a
clean transaction follows, because the inactive counter is not reloaded on that path, so the
host-timeout witness does not fire there, and no register reports the monitor's state directly.

'''''


[[sec-229-smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test]]
===== 229 `smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); one DUT I2C instance as the controller, another as the target, and `SmcI2cMasterVip` pulling SDA low from the pads

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 3600; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: SDA pulled low under a transmitting I2C controller, on all three instances.

*Test Coverage*:

* `doc/architecture.adoc` Bus Arbitration describes the bus monitor detecting a controller that "attempts to transmit a logic high, but another device is pulling SDA low", and the RDL gives `INTR_STATE.SDA_INTERFERENCE` for the controller side. That condition is a global override on the controller state machine, so it returns the controller to idle from whatever state it was in -- unlike clearing the host enable, which is only acted on in particular states.
* Every payload byte is 0xFF, so the controller drives a logic high in every data slot and the pull-down is a genuine conflict rather than a bit that happened to agree.
* The injection is anchored on the bus, not on a poll: the leaf waits for the START on the pads, counts SCL rising edges, and pulls SDA low inside the high window of a chosen one. The pull-down is released inside that same window, since one that outlasts it reaches a bit the controller may be driving low. The level the controller was driving is read immediately before the pull and required to be a high, so the conflict is measured rather than assumed.
* **One injection point per instance, not a sweep.** Where the pull-down lands decides which of two things the controller reports: at this point it reports the interference under test, while at other points the byte is corrupted early enough that the target NACKs first and the controller halts on the NACK instead. The anchor is what makes that choice repeatable -- a delay measured in bit periods from a poll of `STATUS` landed in a different part of the bit loop from seed to seed.
* **Recovery is not asserted.** After an interference event on this DUT the next transaction from the same controller is NACKed even when, measured immediately beforehand, the controller's events read 0 and it reports idle, the interrupted transaction has been ended with a STOP the target acknowledges by reporting itself idle, the target has been through disable and a full re-enable, and the bus reads released. The identical transaction succeeds as the opening control. Both instances are hard reset between injections, and nothing is claimed about the transaction that follows an event.
* The opening clean transaction of each instance is the positive control: it shows the pair works, so an injection that reports nothing is a real absence rather than a bench that never reached the DUT.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-CTRL-SDA-INTERFERENCE` |SDA pulled low under controller I2C0 while it drove a logic high raised `INTR_STATE.SDA_INTERFERENCE` and returned the controller to idle, with a clean write to its target beforehand as the control
|`CHK-I2C1-CTRL-SDA-INTERFERENCE` |The same on I2C1
|`CHK-I2C2-CTRL-SDA-INTERFERENCE` |The same on I2C2
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Recovery is not asserted: nothing is claimed about the transaction that follows an
interference event, since on this DUT the next transaction from the same controller is NACKed even
once the events read clear, and both instances are hard reset between injections. One injection
point per instance, not a sweep.

'''''


[[sec-230-smc_avsbus_interrupt_sources_test]]
===== 230 `smc_avsbus_interrupt_sources_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_interrupt_sources_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the AVSBus sdata pad held at the responding level by the bench

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Each AVSBus FIFO interrupt source raised, observed, cleared through the write-only clear register and observed gone.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` is write-only and single-pulse, so writing a bit is only worth anything with the matching source already raised: a write with nothing pending clears nothing and proves nothing. The retry sources are covered by `smc_avsbus_retry_exhaust_test`; this leaf raises the FIFO sources.
* The command FIFO is filled with the AVS clock gated off, so nothing drains it while it fills and the full condition does not depend on winning a race against the protocol engine.
* Both full flags follow their conditions rather than latching, so each is cleared only after its FIFO has drained; clearing while the condition holds leaves the flag set.
* The overflowing `AVS_CMD` write is refused on the bus as well as dropped, so the access itself is an observable of the full condition.
* FIFO depths come from the generated register header's reset values for the vacant-slot fields, not from the design.
* `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT` is not raised here. `architecture.adoc` lists it under Error Handling as "a response received when full is dropped", and says a full FIFO stops new launches but not the replies to commands already on the bus. `smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test` and `smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test` raise it, with a reply in flight meeting a full FIFO.
* Each source is read clear in `AVS_INTERRUPT` before its stimulus, so a source pending beforehand cannot pass as one the stimulus raised.
* The interrupt output is read as a DUT-produced observable. At reset every source is masked, so a raised source reaches nothing; the leaf opens the mask for the eight FIFO and protocol sources. Because a later source is raised while an earlier one is still pending, the output's level alone cannot say which source drives it, so each raised source is witnessed through the mask: with every mask bit closed the output must read 0 and with that source's bit alone open it must read 1. `AVS_SLAVE_ISSUED_INTERRUPT` stays masked: the slave-interrupt detector re-arms it from the idle level of the AVS serial data line, so it returns immediately after each clear and would hold the output high regardless of the sources under test. The entry state is established by clearing every source and reading the output low, not assumed.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_avsbus_interrupt_sources_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-CMD-FIFO-FULL-INT` |A full command FIFO reported `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS.CMD_FIFO_FULL` and raised `CMD_FIFO_FULL_INT`; once the clock was restored and the FIFO drained, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` removed the flag
|`CHK-AVS-CMD-FIFO-OVERFLOW-INT` |A further `AVS_CMD` write against the full FIFO was refused on the bus and dropped, leaving the occupancy unchanged, and raised `CMD_FIFO_OVERFLOW_INT`, which `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` removed
|`CHK-AVS-READBACK-FIFO-FULL-INT` |Responses filled the readback FIFO with `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS.READBACK_FIFO_FULL` set and raised `READBACK_FIFO_FULL_INT`; once the entries were read out, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` removed the flag
|`CHK-AVS-READBACK-HAS-DATA-INT` |Responses waiting in the readback FIFO raised `READBACK_HAS_DATA_INT`; once it was emptied, `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` removed the flag
|`CHK-AVS-READBACK-UNDERFLOW-INT` |Reading `AVS_READBACK` on an empty FIFO raised `READBACK_UNDERFLOW_INT`, which `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` removed
|`CHK-AVS-INTERRUPT-CLEAR-SOURCES` |All five sources above were each read clear before their stimulus, raised, observed in `AVS_INTERRUPT`, cleared through the write-only `AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR` and observed gone
|`CHK-AVS-IRQ-UNMASKED` |The block's interrupt output was low at entry with every source cleared; for each raised source it read 0 with every mask bit closed and 1 with that source's mask bit alone open; it returned low once every source had been cleared
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all seven checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The retry sources are left to `smc_avsbus_retry_exhaust_test`, and
`READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT` is not raised here but in `smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test` and
`smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test`. `AVS_SLAVE_ISSUED_INTERRUPT` stays masked and is not among the
sources under test, since its detector re-arms it from the idle level of the serial data line.

'''''


[[sec-231-smc_avsbus_clock_divider_test]]
===== 231 `smc_avsbus_clock_divider_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_clock_divider_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); observation on `tb_avs_clk_from_dut`, the AVS clock at the pad

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A written AVSBus clock divider setting must reach the clock the block drives.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CFG_1.AVS_CLOCK_SELECT` resets to a divided source, so the divider is already in the AVS clock path. Every other leaf leaves `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE` and `CLK_DIVIDER_DUTY_CYCLE_NUMERATOR` at their reset, and the divider only reloads when a written setting differs from the one it holds, so nothing shows that a written setting reaches the clock at all.
* The divisor and the numerator are compared separately, so each is changed on its own: two divisors, each double the last, then a numerator change at a held divisor.
* The minimum the RDL states for the divisor. Both fields reset to 0, which is below it, and the RDL explains the reset as a value chosen to match the divider's own reset copy so that no reload happens. Writing 0 deliberately is therefore not the same as leaving it: the divider takes the minimum of 2. The leaf measures that, and restores the clock by writing the hardware defaults the RDL names rather than the register's reset value.
* Expected periods come from the reset measurement scaled by the programmed divisors, and the expected high fraction from the numerator over 256 as the RDL defines it; no rate is taken from the design.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Require `AVS_CLOCK_SELECT` to be a divided source and `STOP_AVS_CLOCK_ON_IDLE` to be clear, then measure the period and high fraction at the reset setting.
. Write each divisor with the premux clocks gated around the change, as the register documentation prescribes, and measure again.
. Change only the numerator and measure the high fraction and the period.
. Error injection. Point: `CLK_DIVIDER_VALUE`. Kind: a written divisor of 0, below the minimum the RDL states. Expected response: the divider takes the minimum of 2, measured at the pad.
. Write the hardware defaults back and measure the reset rate again.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-CLKDIV-PERIOD` |Each written divisor scaled the measured AVS clock period against the reset measurement
|`CHK-AVS-CLKDIV-DUTY` |A numerator change on its own moved the high fraction to what the numerator asks for, at an unchanged period
|`CHK-AVS-CLKDIV-MINIMUM` |A written divisor of 0 was taken as the minimum of 2, not as the reset behaviour
|`CHK-AVS-CLKDIV-RESTORE` |The hardware-default divisor and numerator returned the clock to its reset period and high fraction
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-232-smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test]]
===== 232 `smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, which `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` puts in front of all three instances; observation on the resolved SCL net and on `ACQDATA`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A repeated START issued while the target's acquisition FIFO is full must hold the bus through the address phase until software drains it.

*Test Coverage*:

* The address phase, which `smc_i2c_target_acq_stretch_test` does not reach: that leaf fills the FIFO part-way through a transfer, so the target stretches at a data byte. Holding the address phase needs the FIFO to still be out of room when a new address arrives, which only a repeated START can arrange -- a STOP would end the transfer and let software drain at leisure.
* Both settings of `CTRL.NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT`, which `i2c.rdl` gives as ACK the address byte even if a stretch timeout occurs (`0`, for SMBus) or NACK it (`1`). The two settings take the target down different paths to the same hold, and in both the transfer has to complete once the FIFO is drained.
* A third leg where the repeated START asks the target to *transmit*. `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING` is not raised on this path and the leg does not look for it: `i2c_core.sv` gates the event on `event_read_cmd_received`, which `i2c_target_fsm.sv` emits from `ADDR_ACK_HOLD` only on the branch where the address phase did *not* stretch. The register's own contract is checked in `smc_i2c_target_nack_timeout_test`, on a read whose address phase was acknowledged normally. The target leaves the address-phase stretch into the transmit stretch rather than into byte acquisition, and stays there until software supplies a byte: the drain alone does not release it, and the leg requires that.
* One instance per entry. Filling an acquisition FIFO byte by byte is most of the leaf's time, so three of them in one simulation run past the time a single run is given; the instance is a parameter of the sequence and the package carries an entry for each, this one for I2C0 and cards 242 and 243 for I2C1 and I2C2. Only I2C0 has pads of its own on the bench bus, so the other two are reached through `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` with only the instance under test enabled.
* No stretch timeout is enabled in either leg, so a drain by software is the only thing that can release the hold. A leg that passed without the drain would be a different mechanism.
* `CTRL.ACQ_START_STOP_EN` is set, so the acquired stream carries its own framing and the repeated START arrives as an `ACQDATA.SIGNAL` of `RESTART` after every byte written before it. The STOP entry is matched on its signal alone, since the RDL defines no byte for it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target and require its acquisition FIFO to read empty and not full.
. Write bytes one at a time, checking `STATUS.ACQFULL` between them, and stop as soon as the target reports it is out of room.
. Issue a repeated START and the address again in the background, and measure the hold: only samples where the bus is low while the bench has released its own pull are counted.
. Require the bench's transfer to still be in flight, then drain `ACQDATA` until it completes.
. Compare the whole acquired stream against the bench's traffic and require every ACK bit to be low.
. Repeat with `CTRL.NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` set, and again with the repeated START asking for a read, where the release needs a byte in `TXDATA` as well as the drain.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH` |With `NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` clear, the repeated START was held on the bus, the drain released it, and the acquired stream carried the restart entry after every earlier byte and ended in a STOP
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH-NACK-MODE` |The same with `NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` set, which takes the target's other address-phase path to the same result
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH-READ` |When the held address phase belonged to a read, the target went on holding for a byte to send and was released only by a drain and a write into `TXDATA`, after which the bench read that byte back
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING` is not raised on the stretched-address read path and that
leg does not look for it; the register's own contract is checked in
`smc_i2c_target_nack_timeout_test`.

'''''

[[sec-233-smc_i2c_target_ack_ctrl_test]]
===== 233 `smc_i2c_target_ack_ctrl_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_ack_ctrl_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads; observation on the ACK bits the bench reads back and on `ACQDATA`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Software must be able to accept or refuse bytes through `TARGET_ACK_CTRL` while the target holds the bus for them.

*Test Coverage*:

* Both answers the register documentation gives software when `CTRL.ACK_CTRL_EN = 1` and the target stretches: reload `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES` to accept, or write `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK` to reject. No other leaf gives either answer to the block.
* The hold is the ACK counter's, not the acquisition FIFO's: `STATUS.ACQFULL` is required to be clear while `STATUS.ACK_CTRL_STRETCH` is set, so this cannot be read as the FIFO-full stretch that `smc_i2c_target_acq_stretch_test` covers.
* The count decrements per byte. `NBYTES` is reloaded with fewer bytes than remain, so the target has to stop again after exactly that many, and the leg requires exactly that number of holds -- no more, and none after the payload is covered.
* The write enable. `i2c_core.sv` gates `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES` writes on the same stretch condition, so a reload that reads back as 0 means the gate was shut when the documentation says it is open.
* The rejected byte is identifiable: the acquisition FIFO must carry a NACKed-data entry, not just a NACK on the wire.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target with `CTRL.ACK_CTRL_EN` and `CTRL.ACQ_START_STOP_EN`, and require `ACK_CTRL_STRETCH` clear before any transfer.
. Drive a multi-byte write from the bench in the background. `NBYTES` resets to 0, so the target holds at the first data byte.
. For each chunk: wait for `ACK_CTRL_STRETCH`, require `ACQFULL` clear, reload `NBYTES`, read it back, and wait for the hold to clear.
. Require the rest of the transfer to run out with no further hold, then compare the acquired stream and every ACK bit.
. Repeat with a second transfer, writing `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK` at the hold instead, and require the bench to see NACKs from that byte on.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ACK-CTRL-ACCEPT` |The target held once per reload of `NBYTES`, each reload released it for exactly that many bytes, and every byte was acknowledged and acquired in order
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ACK-CTRL-NACK` |Writing `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK` at the hold made the target refuse the transfer, which the bench saw as NACKs and software can attribute from the NACKed-data entry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-234-smc_avsbus_retry_suppressed_test]]
===== 234 `smc_avsbus_retry_suppressed_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_retry_suppressed_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the AVSBus sdata pad held at its idle level by the bench, so every reply reports the target as not responding

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A retry budget of 0 must answer an unanswered command without resending it. Extends `smc_avsbus_retry_exhaust_test` with the budget-0 cell, differing only in the budget.

*Test Coverage*:

* `AVS_CFG_0.MAX_RETRIES = 0`, which the design reads as programmed to suppress retries: the failing reply is pushed to the readback FIFO as it stands and the controller carries on. `smc_avsbus_retry_exhaust_test` covers the other side of the same register with a budget to spend; the two leaves differ only in the budget.
* The absences that define suppression -- no retry state on the FSM debug bus, `TOTAL_RETRIES` unmoved, `AVS_MASTER_IS_RETRYING` never set, `MAX_RETRIES_ATTEMPTED_INT` never raised -- together with the one presence that separates suppression from dropping the reply: the readback FIFO still holds it.
* A positive control on the same registers and the same probes. The same commands are then given a budget of 1, and the counter and the debug bus have to move; without it the absences above could all be dead probes.
* The retry failure sources are cleared and required to stay clear only before the first command. Once the bench has held sdata idle through a burst, the controller's own resync traffic meets the same failing reply, so a later clear cannot be required to hold.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Error injection. Point: the AVSBus sdata pad. Kind: the pad held at its idle level; every reply reports the target as not responding. Expected response: the queued commands are reported unresponsive and, with `MAX_RETRIES` at 0, answered without a resend. Save `AVS_CFG_0` and program `MAX_RETRIES` to 0.
. Clear both retry failure sources and require them clear, then read the retry counter.
. Queue two read commands and poll until the target is reported unresponsive, sampling the retrying flag on every poll.
. Require the counter, the flag, the debug bus and the budget-exhausted interrupt to show no retry, and the readback FIFO to hold the replies.
. Reprogram the budget to 1, queue the same commands, and require the counter and the debug bus to move.
. Restore `AVS_CFG_0`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-RETRY-SUPPRESSED` |With `MAX_RETRIES` at 0 the unanswered commands raised `SLAVE_UNRESPONSIVE_INT`, no retry was attempted by any of the four measures, and the failing replies still reached the readback FIFO
|`CHK-AVS-RETRY-SUPPRESSED-CONTROL` |The same commands with a budget of 1 moved `TOTAL_RETRIES` and put the retry states on the debug bus, so the suppressed leg is measuring live probes
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The retry failure sources are cleared and required to stay clear only before the
first command; once the bench has held sdata idle through a burst, the controller's own resync
traffic meets the same failing reply, so a later clear is not required to hold.

'''''

[[sec-235-smc_i2c_target_nack_timeout_test]]
===== 235 `smc_i2c_target_nack_timeout_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_nack_timeout_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads; observation on `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`, `ACQDATA` and the bus

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A stretch nobody releases must end in the target's own NACK, in both directions, on every instance.

*Test Coverage*:

* The expiry of `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL`, the cumulative limit on how long the target may stretch within one transaction. Every other stretch leaf is released by software first, so no other leaf reaches the limit.
* Both consequences the RDL names for it -- NACK an incoming data byte, release SDA for an outgoing one -- one leg each.
* ACK Control Mode is the way into the incoming hold, so the target stops at the first data byte instead of after a whole acquisition FIFO of them. It is the same hold `smc_i2c_target_ack_ctrl_test` answers; the difference is that nothing answers it here.
* An empty transmit FIFO is the way into the outgoing hold, and a released SDA line reads as all ones at the bench.
* `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` is the register witness. `i2c_core.sv` increments it on the edge where the target decides to NACK the transaction, and the field is read-to-clear, so each leg reads it clear beforehand and requires exactly one afterwards -- not merely non-zero.
* The acquisition stream must end with the NACK-stop entry, so software can see the transaction ended badly rather than inferring it from the missing data.
* One instance per entry. The hold relation needs a bus rate slow enough that it dominates the run, and three instances of that do not fit in the time one simulation is given; the instance is a parameter of the sequence and the package carries an entry for each, this one for I2C0 and cards 244 and 245 for I2C1 and I2C2. Only I2C0 has pads of its own on the bench bus, so the other two are reached through `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` with only the instance under test enabled.
* `VAL`, which holds the last sixteen oversampled levels of SCL and SDA, read with the bus idle on every instance: a released bus reads all ones in both halves.
* `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` at the top of its range. The field is writable, so it is preset to its top value and one more NACK is provoked; `i2c.rdl` gives the counter as "saturating at 255", so it has to hold there, and the read that returns it has to clear it.
* A repeated START inside a transaction, on I2C0. In a healthy transaction it is recorded as a restart entry. Inside one the target has already refused -- the stretch allowance ran out on its first data byte -- `CTRL.NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` decides the answer: clear, the target acknowledges every address but has already given up, so only the address is acknowledged; set, it refuses the address itself. Either way it is still one refused transaction, counted once, with no restart recorded.
* `TARGET_EVENTS` as a register rather than a flag. The outgoing leg sets `CTRL.TX_STRETCH_CTRL_EN`, so the target records the read it stretched for in `TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING`; a word of zeros and a word of ones that strobes only the top byte lane, so the lane carrying the bit is disabled while carrying a one, must both leave it set, and only a written one clears it. Each read is compared against the mask from the generated header.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target with a short `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL` allowance, and read `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` twice to clear it and prove it cleared.
. Error injection. Point: the target's ACK Control hold at the first data byte. Kind: an incoming write whose stretch nobody releases; the `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL` allowance runs out. Expected response: the target NACKs the byte. ACK Control Mode is enabled with its count at reset.
. Require a NACK on the wire, exactly one counted transaction, and a NACK-stop entry closing the stream.
. Error injection. Point: the target's transmit hold with the transmit FIFO empty. Kind: an outgoing read whose stretch nobody releases; the allowance runs out. Expected response: the target releases SDA.
. Require all ones at the bench, exactly one counted transaction, and a NACK-stop entry.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACK-TIMEOUT-RX` |The allowance ran out at a held incoming byte: the byte was NACKed, the transaction counted once, and the stream closed with a NACK-stop entry
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACK-TIMEOUT-TX` |The allowance ran out with nothing to transmit: SDA was released so the bench read all ones, the transaction counted once, and the stream closed with a NACK-stop entry
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-EVENTS-RETAIN` |`TARGET_EVENTS.TX_PENDING`, set by the target on the read it stretched for, survived a word of zeros and a word of ones that strobed only the top byte lane, so its own lane carried a one it was not enabled to take, and cleared only on a written one
|`CHK-I2C-VAL-IDLE` |`VAL` read all ones on every instance with the bus idle
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACK-COUNT-SATURATES` |A NACK taken with `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` preset to its top value left it there rather than wrapping, and the read that returned it cleared it
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-RESTART` |A repeated START in a healthy transaction was recorded as a restart entry; inside a transaction the target had already refused, the new address was acknowledged and nothing after it with `NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` clear, and refused with it set, with the transaction counted once and no restart recorded
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares on every instance, and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-236-smc_i2c0_target_fast_controller_test]]
===== 236 `smc_i2c0_target_fast_controller_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c0_target_fast_controller_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, with its bit rate changed part-way through a transfer; observation on the ACK bits, `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` and `ACQDATA`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A controller that releases SCL before the target's data hold time has elapsed must have its transaction abandoned.

*Test Coverage*:

* `TIMING3.THD_DAT`, the hold the target keeps with SCL low before driving an acknowledge. The threshold is a relation between that hold and the controller's SCL low period, so the leaf sets both: the target is given a hold far longer than any other leaf uses, and the bench is run at one rate well over it and one well under it.
* Both places the target makes the decision: the acknowledge of the address byte and the acknowledge of a data byte.
* The rate changes after the START in both fast legs, not before. The same hold governs both acknowledges, so at a single rate the address is always the first to go; and the bus monitor takes the same `THD_DAT` as its threshold for detecting a START (`i2c_bus_monitor.sv`), so a START clocked fast enough to violate the hold is not seen as a START at all, and the target never joins the transaction: no acknowledge, no count, nothing acquired.
* The hold is also kept below half the slow rate's low period, so the target always finishes driving an acknowledge before the clock rises again and the control transfers are clean.
* A transfer entirely at the slow rate runs before and after the two fast legs, so the abandons are the difference the rate makes rather than a target that never works.
* All three instances, reached through `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` with only the instance under test enabled.
* `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` is the register witness. It takes the edge on which the target decides to NACK the transaction and is read-to-clear, so each leg clears it and requires exactly its own -- one for each abandon, none for either control.
* What reaches the acquisition FIFO separates the two abandons: the address leg records nothing for the address and closes with the NACK-stop entry, the data leg keeps its start entry but records no data.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target with a long `TIMING3.THD_DAT`, read back the timing, and require the acquisition FIFO empty.
. Slow transfer: START, address, one data byte, STOP, all at the slow rate.
. Error injection. Point: the bench controller's SCL rate on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads. Kind: the address byte clocked under the target's `THD_DAT` hold, with the rate changed after a START at the slow rate. Expected response: no acknowledge, one count in `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`, and only the NACK-stop entry acquired.
. Error injection. Point: the same SCL rate. Kind: the data byte clocked under the hold, after START and address at the slow rate and a park until the target's hold on that acknowledge has finished. Expected response: no acknowledge, one count, and no data entry acquired.
. Slow transfer again.
. For each leg, drain the acquisition FIFO once its level has settled and read `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-FAST-CTRL-CONTROL` |Both slow transfers were acknowledged throughout, acquired in full and counted no NACK
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-FAST-CTRL-ADDR` |The address clocked under the hold time got no acknowledge, was counted once, and left only the NACK-stop entry
|`CHK-I2C0-TGT-FAST-CTRL-DATA` |With the address acknowledged at the slow rate, the data byte clocked under the hold time got no acknowledge, was counted once, and left no data entry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-237-smc_i2c_controller_stretch_test]]
===== 237 `smc_i2c_controller_stretch_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_stretch_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the target, a second bench pad driver as the device that holds the clock; observation on the transfer's own length and on what the target received

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The DUT's I2C controller must wait out a held clock and still deliver the transfer.

*Test Coverage*:

* The controller's wait for SCL to rise, which no other leaf takes: every controller leaf in the package talks to a device that never holds the clock.
* Six hold points across one transfer, so the wait is taken from the address byte, its acknowledge and the payload bytes rather than from one place in the bit loop. Each point is counted in SCL falling edges seen on the pads, not in nanoseconds from the queue: the write that queues the transfer does not complete at a fixed time, so delays measured from it put the hold in a different part of the bit loop from run to run.
* The hold starts after SCL has fallen, so the line is already low when it begins and the controller meets it when it tries to release -- a stretch, not a clock pulse cut short.
* The hold is a second driver on the open-drain bus, so the controller's own release cannot lift the line -- the same thing a stretching target does.
* No timeout is enabled. A controller that gave up instead of waiting would show as a byte the target never received, not as a timeout the leaf could read as success, and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` is required to stay clear on every leg.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads.
. Queue a three-entry write and time it with nothing holding the line.
. For each hold point: queue the same write to a fresh offset, hold SCL low for a fixed span starting that far into the transfer, then release.
. Require each held transfer to run at least three quarters of the hold longer than the clean one, to deliver the queued bytes, and to leave `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` clear.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-STRETCH-CLEAN` |The unheld transfer's length, which the held ones are measured against
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-STRETCH-HELD` |At every hold point the transfer ran longer by about the hold and still delivered every byte
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-238-smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test]]
===== 238 `smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the target, a second bench pad driver as the device that makes the edge; observation on `INTR_STATE.SDA_UNSTABLE`, `INTR_STATE.SDA_INTERFERENCE` and `STATUS.HOSTIDLE`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: An SDA edge inside an SCL high window is a START or a STOP; in a pulse the controller receives it must report `SDA_UNSTABLE`, in a pulse the controller drives high it must report `SDA_INTERFERENCE`, and the transfer is dropped.

*Test Coverage*:

* The expectations are the OpenTitan I2C theory of operation, which `hw/ip/i2c/doc/index.adoc` adopts: "the sda_unstable interrupt is asserted if, when receiving data or acknowledgement pulse, the value of the SDA signal does not remain constant over the duration of the SCL pulse, causing an unexpected START or STOP symbol", and "the sda_interference interrupt is raised whenever the Controller Module detects that another device is pulling SDA low while the Controller Module is trying to transmit logic high". `smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test` pulls SDA low at time offsets measured in bit periods, which lands the edge wherever it falls -- with this controller's timing usually while SCL is low. This leaf counts SCL rising edges from the START on the bus and pulls inside the high window of a chosen one, so the edge is a control symbol by construction and lands in a chosen pulse.
* The two pulses the controller receives, where the line is high because it is released: the acknowledge of an address nobody answers, and a one bit of a byte the target is returning. Each must raise `SDA_UNSTABLE`.
* The two pulses the controller drives high itself: the first address bit of a write, and the not-acknowledge the controller drives after the last byte of a read. Each must raise `SDA_INTERFERENCE`. The pull there is made a fixed 60 ns into the high window rather than at the rise, so the edge lies inside the high the controller is transmitting; no specification states a sampling requirement, the delay is a bench choice. Whether a driven pulse also reports `SDA_UNSTABLE`, or a received one `SDA_INTERFERENCE`, is not specified and not graded; the `INTR_STATE` word each pulse left is logged.
* The pull is released inside the same high window, because one that outlasts the pulse reaches the next one, where the line may belong to another device.
* The slot numbering is anchored on the START seen on the pads, not on a status read: a poll returns some cycles after the controller leaves idle, by which time bits have already been clocked.
* The read abandoned mid-byte runs last. The transfer the controller makes after it starts with the offset byte in place of the address, so no slot numbered from the START would be where it should be. Between legs the bus is clocked until the bench target lets SDA go and is given a STOP, since an abandoned transfer can leave the target part-way through a byte.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads, and run one uninterrupted write.
. Error injection. Point: the SDA line on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, inside the high window of a chosen SCL pulse counted from the START on the bus. Kind: SDA pulled low by the second bench driver -- at the rise for a received pulse, 60 ns after it for a driven one -- and released inside the same window. Expected response: `SDA_UNSTABLE` for the two received pulses (the acknowledge of an address nobody answers, a one bit of a byte the target returns), `SDA_INTERFERENCE` for the two driven pulses (the first address bit of a write, the not-acknowledge after the last byte of a read), and a return to idle. For each pulse: re-enable the controller from scratch, arm the injector, queue the transfer, wait for the START and count SCL rises.
. Require the interrupt the specification names for that pulse and a return to idle, then clear `CTRL`, clock the bus back to idle and give it a STOP.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-SYMBOL-CLEAN` |An uninterrupted write reached the target and left `SDA_UNSTABLE` and `SDA_INTERFERENCE` clear
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-SYMBOL-INTERFERENCE` |An edge made inside the high window of a pulse the controller drives high raised `SDA_INTERFERENCE` and returned the controller to idle, at both driven pulses
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-SYMBOL-UNSTABLE` |An edge made inside the high window of a pulse the controller receives raised `SDA_UNSTABLE` and returned the controller to idle, at both received pulses
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Nothing is asserted about the transfer after an injection: on this DUT the next transaction from the same controller is NACKed even once the events are cleared, so each leg re-enables the controller from scratch. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: Whether a driven pulse also reports `SDA_UNSTABLE`, or a received one
`SDA_INTERFERENCE`, is not specified and not graded; the `INTR_STATE` word each pulse left is
logged. The 60 ns delay into a driven high window is a bench choice, since no specification states a
sampling requirement. Nothing is asserted about the transfer after an injection.

'''''

[[sec-239-smc_uart_rbr_error_path_test]]
===== 239 `smc_uart_rbr_error_path_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_rbr_error_path_test`

*BFM / Model*: UART3's transmit pin crossed to UART0's receive pin (`+smc_uart_cross_3to0`); observation on `LSR` and `IIR`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; args `+smc_uart_cross_3to0`; tool Verilator
(cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A character that arrives broken while the receive FIFO is off must carry its flags through the receiver buffer register.

*Test Coverage*:

* The second of the two receive paths `uart_core.sv` selects with `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE`. Each path carries its own copy of the error flags. `smc_uart_error_conditions_test` breaks characters on the FIFO path and `smc_uart_core_mode_select_test` sends clean ones through the register path, so no other leaf sends a broken character down it.
* The two kinds two UARTs can disagree into existence: a parity disagreement, and a word length disagreement that makes the receiver sample its stop bit where a data bit still is.
* The framing character carries a one, so the frame is not the all-zero one a break is, and the leg requires `LSR.BI` to stay clear. A break sets the framing flag as well, so a break alone cannot separate the two.
* The framing character also carries a one in its eighth bit, beyond the five the receiver frames. A receiver framing five bits reads back only the low five, so the character read back is required to be exactly those: it shows the word length the receiver framed with rather than assuming it.
* `PE`, `FE` and `BI` are sticky copies of levels that hold while the character sits in the receiver buffer register, set a cycle after those levels and cleared by any read of LSR, while `ERROR_IN_RCVR_FIFO` follows the levels directly. The read that first sees `DR` can fall in that cycle and return `ERROR_IN_RCVR_FIFO` set with the specific flag not yet set. The character stays in the register until it is read out, so the leg reads LSR once more before reading the character, and the flag is set again by then.
* The receive trigger level, which `uart_core.sv` builds from `ECR.RCVR_TRIGGER_MS2B` and `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER` together and compares against the depth the FIFO was built with. Every other leaf programs a level the design supports; this one programs a level above the depth, where the watermark can never be reached.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. With both UARTs' FIFOs disabled and the two ends agreeing, send one character and require no error flag.
. Error injection. Point: the parity setting of the transmitter and the receiver. Kind: the transmitter at odd parity and the receiver at even; one character arrives with a parity disagreement. Expected response: `LSR.PE` set with `FE`, `BI` and `OE` clear.
. Error injection. Point: the word length of the transmitter and the receiver. Kind: the transmitter at eight bits and the receiver at five, with a character carrying a zero at the receiver's stop position and a one before it. Expected response: `LSR.FE` set with `PE`, `BI` and `OE` clear.
. Error injection. Point: the receive trigger level built from `ECR.RCVR_TRIGGER_MS2B` and `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER`. Kind: a level programmed above the FIFO depth, with the FIFOs on. Expected response: `LSR.DR` after one sent character, with no received-data-ready interrupt.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-RBR-CLEAN` |A character both ends agreed on reached the receiver buffer register with no error flag
|`CHK-UART-RBR-ERRORS` |A parity disagreement and a word length disagreement each reached the receiver buffer register with their own flag and no other: `PE` with `FE`, `BI` and `OE` clear, and `FE` with `PE`, `BI` and `OE` clear
|`CHK-UART-RXILVL-UNSUPPORTED` |With the trigger level above the FIFO depth a character still arrived and the received-data-ready interrupt stayed away
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-240-smc_i2c_controller_exits_test]]
===== 240 `smc_i2c_controller_exits_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_exits_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads for the first leg; an address no device answers for the second

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Two endings of a controller transaction no other leaf produces, and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` as a register rather than a flag.

*Test Coverage*:

* A read whose last byte carries no stop. The controller returns to the format FIFO for the entries queued behind it instead of stopping, which is the only way it leaves the read acknowledge into `POP_FMT_FIFO`. The target has to see a single stop for the whole sequence, not one per entry.
* A NACK left unhandled. `i2c.rdl` describes `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` as the limit on how long software may leave the controller halted on an unexpected NACK; past it `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` is raised beside the NACK. Every other leaf clears a NACK as soon as it sees one.
* A read split across two format entries, the first carrying `FDATA.RCONT`. The flag makes the controller acknowledge that entry's last byte rather than NACK it and carry on reading from the next entry, so the three bytes come back as one read with one start pair and one stop.
* A read count of zero. `i2c.rdl` gives `FBYTE` of zero with `READB` as a 256-byte read -- one more than any nonzero count can express, and four times the depth of the controller's receive FIFO, so software drains `RDATA` while it runs. The controller's bit period is shortened for this leg so the read costs a few hundred microseconds; the bench target samples on the SMC clock, far faster.
* `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` clears on a written one, so two writes that must *not* clear it are made first: a word of zeros over a set bit, and a word of ones that strobes only the top byte lane, so the lane carrying the bit is disabled while carrying a one. The bit is read back set after each, and only a written one clears it. Both set fields are checked this way.

The controller's third ending, the STOP it makes when `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` is cleared with a transaction still open, is driven by `smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test`.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads.
. Queue a write of an offset, a repeated start and a one-byte read *without* a stop, then a further write with a stop. Require the byte read back, the later write at the target, and one stop.
. Error injection. Point: the controller's format FIFO, with `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` armed. Kind: a write queued to an address no device answers, with the NACK left unhandled. Expected response: `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` and then `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` raised beside it.
. For each set field: write zeros, read it back set; write a word of ones with only the top byte lane strobed, read it back set; write a one, read it back clear.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-READ-CONTINUES` |A read whose last byte carried no stop returned to the format FIFO, the entry behind it reached the target, and the target saw a single stop
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NACK-TIMEOUT` |A NACK left unhandled past the programmed limit raised `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` beside it
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EVENTS-RETAIN` |Both set fields survived a word of zeros and a word of ones that strobed only the top byte lane, so their own lane carried a one it was not enabled to take, and cleared only on a written one
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-READ-RCONT` |A read split across two format entries, the first carrying `RCONT`, came back as one continuous read inside a single transaction
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-READ-256` |A read with a count of zero returned 256 bytes, the target's whole memory in order
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: The controller's third ending, the STOP it makes when `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` is cleared
with a transaction still open, is left to `smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test`.

'''''

[[sec-241-smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test]]
===== 241 `smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_frame_sequencing_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); the AVSBus sdata pad driven at its idle or responding level by the bench

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: How one AVSBus frame follows another, which the command mix decides.

*Test Coverage*:

* A command queued on its own. `architecture.adoc` describes a frame as a first subframe, as many middle subframes as there are further commands ready, and a last one, so with nothing behind it the first subframe is followed straight by the last. Every other leaf queues its commands in one burst, so no other leaf takes that path.
* A command queued while the bus is already running, spaced so that one of them arrives during a last subframe and starts a new frame from the end of it instead of letting the bus go idle.
* A command on its own, retried. With nothing queued behind it the frame is a first and a last subframe, so the retry is launched from the last subframe and transmits only; a transmit-and-receive retry would mean a second frame was on the wire.
* A command written while another frame's last subframe is on the wire, placed by watching the FSM debug bus for that subframe. The machine must go from the end of it straight into the next frame's first subframe, with no idle between.
* Retries suppressed with three commands queued, so the first frame has a middle subframe with more commands waiting behind it; every failing reply is kept, none retried.
* Retries suppressed with two commands written while a last subframe is on the wire. Its failing reply is kept, and the two commands have to go out once each and in order, as the mdata pad shows.
* The slave-issued interrupt cleared once nothing can raise it again. `avsbus_controller.sv` raises it while the bus is idle with sdata low and at the end of a first subframe whose reply opens with two zero bits, so with sdata at its responding level a clear is overtaken at once. With sdata released high neither can, and the clear has to hold until sdata is taken low again.
* The readback FIFO overflowing from the bus side. Each launch checks the room left for the reply of the frame it launches, but a frame launched while an earlier one is still retrying has its reply buffered and pushed later, after the earlier reply has taken the last slot. With one slot left before a retried pair, the second reply meets a full FIFO and raises `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT`: a reply to a command already launched is lost, as `architecture.adoc` allows. The pair is queued behind a full FIFO, which launches nothing, and one reply is then popped, so both commands are waiting when the first launch is decided and the second goes out as a middle subframe whatever the AVS clock rate.
* A command held back by the reply that takes the last readback slot. Three commands are queued behind a full readback FIFO and one reply is popped; the first two go out as one frame, the first reply takes the last slot at the end of the middle subframe with the third command still queued, and the third has to wait until a second pop and then go out on its own. `architecture.adoc` says nothing new is launched while the FIFO is full. The leg records `AVS_INTERRUPT`, which on this design shows `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT`: the second reply of that frame meets the full FIFO.
* A reply the master had to buffer. A frame retried while a later frame is already on the wire leaves that later reply pending; when the master returns to it, it either retries that one too or, if it is good, resynchronises the slave. The bench decides which by driving the pad: the retries are provoked at the idle level and the pad is then released to its responding level, so the buffered reply is a good one.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. With the pad at its responding level and the readback FIFO drained, queue one command and require a response, the last-subframe shift state on the debug bus and no middle-subframe state.
. Queue several commands one at a time with a short gap, and require a response for each.
. Error injection. Point: the AVSBus sdata pad. Kind: the pad held at its idle level with a retry budget programmed; two queued commands are answered as not responding. Expected response: `TOTAL_RETRIES` moves, and once the pad is released to its responding level the buffered reply takes the master to the slave-resynchronisation state on the debug bus. Queue the two commands, wait for `TOTAL_RETRIES` to move, then release the pad and require that state.
. With the readback FIFO filled, queue three commands, require all three still queued, pop one reply, and after the frame that refills the FIFO require one command still queued; pop again and require that command to go out and its reply to arrive.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-SINGLE-COMMAND` |A command with nothing behind it produced its response and took the machine through the last-subframe shift with no middle-subframe state on the debug bus; a middle subframe seen fails
|`CHK-AVS-LATE-COMMAND` |Commands written one at a time while the bus ran all produced responses
|`CHK-AVS-BUFFERED-REPLY` |After a retry with a second frame on the wire, a buffered reply that turned out good took the master to the slave resynchronisation rather than another retry
|`CHK-AVS-LONE-RETRY` |A command with nothing behind it, answered as not responding, was retried from its last subframe with a transmit-only retry
|`CHK-AVS-BACK-TO-BACK` |A command written while another frame's last subframe was on the wire started its first subframe straight from the end of it, and both replies arrived
|`CHK-AVS-SUPPRESSED-MID` |With `MAX_RETRIES` at 0 and three commands queued, every failing reply was kept without a retry, including one ended at a middle subframe with more commands waiting
|`CHK-AVS-SUPPRESSED-LAST` |With `MAX_RETRIES` at 0 and two commands queued while a last subframe was on the wire, its failing reply was kept and both commands went out once each, in order
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-INT-CLEAR` |The slave-issued interrupt, cleared with sdata released high, stayed clear until sdata was taken low again at idle
|`CHK-AVS-LAUNCH-GATE` |With three commands queued behind a full readback FIFO and one reply popped, the frame that refilled the FIFO left the third command queued until a second pop, after which it went out and answered
|`CHK-AVS-READBACK-OVERFLOW` |With one readback slot left before a retried pair, the second frame's buffered reply met a full FIFO and raised `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT`, which its clear removed
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: In the launch-gate leg `AVS_INTERRUPT` is recorded, not compared; on this design it
shows `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT` from the second reply of that frame meeting the full FIFO.

'''''

[[sec-264-smc_i2c1_target_addr_stretch_test]]
===== 264 `smc_i2c1_target_addr_stretch_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c1_target_addr_stretch_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, which `+smc_i2c_shared_bus` puts in front of all three instances; observation on the resolved SCL net and on `ACQDATA`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; args `+smc_i2c_shared_bus`; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The address-phase hold of card 232, on I2C1. Extends `smc_i2c0_target_addr_stretch_test` on I2C1.

*Test Coverage*:

* The same three legs the sequence drives for any instance -- `CTRL.NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` clear, set, and a repeated START that asks the target to transmit -- pointed at I2C1, with I2C0 and I2C2 disabled so only the instance under test can answer.
* A separate entry rather than a loop, because filling an acquisition FIFO byte by byte is most of the run and three of them do not fit in the time one simulation is given. Card 232 carries the mechanism in full.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i2c_target_addr_stretch_test_seq` with the instance set to 1. The steps are those of card 232.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C1-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH` |With `NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` clear, the repeated START was held on the bus, the drain released it, and the acquired stream carried the restart entry after every earlier byte and ended in a STOP
|`CHK-I2C1-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH-NACK-MODE` |The same with `NACK_ADDR_AFTER_TIMEOUT` set
|`CHK-I2C1-TGT-ADDR-STRETCH-READ` |The held address phase of a read was released only by a drain and a write into `TXDATA`, after which the bench read that byte back
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-246-smc_cpuif_handshake_test]]
===== 246 `smc_cpuif_handshake_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpuif_handshake_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` outstanding groups and `AxiTimingProfile` channel timing

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive every PeakRDL register block's AXI-Lite front end with pipelined, skewed and backpressured traffic.

*Test Coverage*:

* Each SMC register block sits behind the same generated AXI-Lite interface: it keeps up to two transactions in flight, alternates reads and writes, captures AW and W in separate registers, and holds a response until BREADY or RREADY. `smc_sep_in_axi_flow_control_test` drives that interface with outstanding and backpressured traffic, but only on the scratch registers, so no other leaf drives the parts below on any other block.
* **An accept in the same cycle a response is acknowledged.** The in-flight counter increments on an accept and decrements on an acknowledge; the cycle that does both needs a request already waiting as the previous response goes out, which serial traffic never has. Each block takes an outstanding group of interleaved reads and writes, deep enough that both the read-side and the write-side accept meet an acknowledge.
* **Write data ahead of its address.** An `AxiTimingProfile` with `aw_delay` set presents W before AW at SEP_IN for every block; `cpu_ctrl` and `zeroer_ctrl` also take a write with `w_delay` set. The skew does not survive the path. Every AXI-Lite demux in front of a block routes W only once it has forwarded that write's AW, and the AXI-to-AXI-Lite converter in front of `cpu_ctrl` and `zeroer_ctrl` does the same. So no block ever registers W with no AW, and on `cpu_ctrl` and `zeroer_ctrl` AW and W were seen to arrive in the same cycle under both skews. The front end's W-alone row is not claimed on any block, and its AW-alone row is not claimed on those two.
* **A response held against a low ready.** `b_ready_delay` and `r_ready_delay` hold BREADY and RREADY low on SEP_IN, but the interconnect in front of each block buffers responses and keeps the block's own ready high until that buffer is full. Each block therefore takes sixteen writes and then sixteen reads outstanding against a 32-cycle hold, which backs the responses up far enough to drop the block's ready. Behind `smc_misc_wrap` (chip_config, ndm_reset, scratch) and behind the straps window the path buffers more than that and the block's ready is never seen to drop; those blocks still take the traffic and are held to the same checks, but that row is not claimed for them.
* **Every access targets one probe register per block, and every write carries back the value it just read.** A probe is a plain read-write register, where a write of the value already held changes nothing, or a read-only one, which a write does not reach. The sequence checks each probe against the generated contract before issuing anything -- no field may carry a read action, a modified-write action or write-only access -- so a regenerated map cannot turn a probe into a trigger unnoticed. `FILTER_CONFIG` fails that check, since its write-once `locked` field is a modified write, so the filter block's probe is `START_ADDR`.
* The claim for each block is what a pipelined, skewed, backpressured manager is owed: every read in every group returns the value the block held, every write is answered, and the register still holds that value at the end. A front end that dropped, reordered or mis-paired an outstanding access returns the wrong word or loses the write.
* Three blocks need their own handling. `straps` sits in the mandatory region of the adopter external window; `memmap.adoc` places `STRAPS_LO` at BASE + 0x040_3000 and `straps.rdl` makes it `sw = r`, so it is a read-only probe reached by address. `uart_16550_dl` is decoded only while `LCR.DLAB` is set, so its leg sets DLAB, probes `DLL` and restores `LCR`. `uart_16550_main_wo` has no read side -- `uart_16550.sv` routes no read to it -- so it takes writes only, of `FCR = 0`, which at reset changes nothing, and `IIR.FIFOS_ENABLED` is read afterwards to show the FIFOs never turned on.

* **A read arriving on a held write.** The front end dispatches a waiting read ahead of a waiting write when the last access was a write. So a read that reaches the block in the cycle it registers AW and W holds that write for a cycle, and the next write's AW, if it is already behind, sees AWREADY low. Every block with a read side takes a pair of writes and a read with the read's arrival swept over twelve offsets. It also takes a single write and a read over the same offsets, which lines a read accept up with a write's acknowledge.
* **Mixed groups against a held response.** Eight writes and a read against a held BREADY, and eight reads and a write against a held RREADY, queue the opposite access behind two unacknowledged ones.
* **Where the held write cannot be seen.** A read holds a registered write for one cycle at most: the cycle after the read is dispatched goes to the write. A second in-flight access cannot hold it longer, because every demux in front of a block admits one write and one read at a time, and a write still waiting for its response keeps the next W out. So AWREADY is seen low only where the next AW reaches the block within one cycle of the previous W, which is where a single demux stage sits in front of it. Behind two stages -- `filter_ctrl`, `log_engine`, `uart_log_engine_ctrl` -- the next AW arrives two cycles after W, in the cycle the held write is dispatched and AWREADY is high again. Behind three -- `uart_16550_main`, `uart_16550_dl` -- it arrives four cycles after W. On `cpu_ctrl` and `zeroer_ctrl` the converter's burst splitter admits one write and one read at a time, since its per-ID counters are one bit wide for a depth of two or one. The next AW, AR or W reaches the block only in the cycle after the previous response, so no AW, AR or W is seen waiting on a low ready there. The row is not claimed for these seven blocks.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpuif_handshake_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPUIF-PIPELINED` |Every register block took an outstanding group of interleaved reads and writes on its probe deep enough that an accept met an acknowledge on both sides, and every read in every group returned the value the block held
|`CHK-CPUIF-WRITE-SKEW` |Every block took a write with W presented ahead of AW at SEP_IN, and cpu_ctrl and zeroer_ctrl also one with AW ahead of W; each carried back the held value and was answered, and the probe held it afterwards
|`CHK-CPUIF-READY-BACKPRESSURE` |Every block answered sixteen outstanding writes with BREADY held low and, where it has a read side, sixteen outstanding reads with RREADY held low; every read returned the held value and the probe read the same value before and after all three shapes
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CPUIF-PIPELINED`, `CHK-CPUIF-READY-BACKPRESSURE`, `CHK-CPUIF-WRITE-SKEW` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Three front-end rows are not claimed, because the path in front of the blocks never
presents them: the W-alone row on any block and the AW-alone row on `cpu_ctrl` and `zeroer_ctrl`,
since every demux and the AXI-to-AXI-Lite converter forward W only after that write's AW; the
ready-drop row behind `smc_misc_wrap` and the straps window, whose paths buffer more responses than
the hold backs up; and the held-write row on the seven blocks behind two or more demux stages or the
converter, where the next AW, AR or W never reaches the block within a cycle of the previous W.
Those blocks still take the traffic and are held to the same checks.

'''''

[[sec-247-smc_cpuif_external_stall_test]]
===== 247 `smc_cpuif_external_stall_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpuif_external_stall_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI), `SmcSysAxiGroupItem` outstanding groups

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Present requests to each register block while one of its external registers is still pending.

*Test Coverage*:

* Six SMC register blocks carry an external register: an access to it is handed to logic outside the generated block, and until that logic acknowledges, the block holds `external_pending` and stalls every further request. Serial traffic never presents a second request in that window, so no other leaf makes the stall hold a request back.
* Each block takes one outstanding group that opens with an access to its external register and follows it at once with a read and a write of the block's probe -- the same side-effect-free register `smc_cpuif_handshake_test` uses -- so both arrive while the external access is pending and both the read-side and the write-side stall hold a request back. A second external access closes the group.
