The claim is what a stalled manager is owed: every held-back request is answered once the stall lifts, the probe read returns the value the block held, each external read returns what its contract gives it, and the probe keeps its value.
* The external access is chosen so that it changes nothing. `AVS_CMD` and `FDATA` are write-only, so a read returns zero and pushes no command or format byte. `RESET_CTRL` holds the core resets and is only read. `CREDIT_EXPIRED` clears on a write, so it is only read. `RBR` pops the receiver on a read, but the receiver is empty at idle, so the read returns zero and `LSR.DR` is read afterwards and must still be clear. `SS_CONFIG` is plain read-write and is its own probe.
* The branch that raises `external_pending` is the witness that the stall happens: it is taken once for each `RESET_CTRL` read in `cpu_ctrl` and once for every access to `SS_CONFIG` in `reset_unit`, so the external acknowledge is not same-cycle and the probe requests queued behind it are presented while the block is pending.
* `uart_16550_main_wo` is left out: its only external register is `THR`, which transmits whatever is written to it, so no access to it leaves the block as it was.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpuif_external_stall_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPUIF-EXTERNAL-STALL` |On six register blocks an access to the external register was followed at once by a read and a write of the block's probe presented while the external access was pending; every held-back request was answered, the probe read returned the held value, each external read returned what its contract gives it, and the probe kept its value
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CPUIF-EXTERNAL-STALL` holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: `uart_16550_main_wo` is left out, since its only external register is `THR`, which
transmits whatever is written to it, so no access to it leaves the block as it was.

'''''

[[sec-248-smc_cpuif_wrong_direction_test]]
===== 248 `smc_cpuif_wrong_direction_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpuif_wrong_direction_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Access register blocks in the direction their contract does not define, and read the registers nobody reads.

*Test Coverage*:

* Each SMC register block decodes an address together with a direction: a read-only register's decode term is the address and a read, a write-only one's is the address and a write. The half of each term that pairs the address with the other direction -- a write at a read-only register, a read at a write-only one -- is driven by no other leaf, and neither is a read of the few registers no leaf reads at all.
* The expected answer comes from the generated block the RDL compiles to: a write to a read-only register is answered OKAY and takes no effect, and a read of a write-only register is answered OKAY and returns zero because the register has no readable field. Every write must be answered, and where the register holds still at idle and reading it has no side effect it must read the same value before and after a write of the complement of that value, so a write that reached any field would show in every bit; every write-only read must return zero; and around each block's accesses the block's probe register must read the same value, so no wrong-direction write aliased onto something writable.
* Registers that need care: `RDATA`, `ACQDATA` and `AVS_READBACK` pop a FIFO when read, so they are written but not read back and their block's FIFO level register is read either side instead. `TIMER_COUNT_LO` and `TIMER_COUNT_HI` run freely, so they rely on the probe guard. `LSR` and `MSR` clear their error bits and deltas on any read, so each is read once to settle those before the baseline. `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` clears when read but holds zero at idle, so the read clears nothing and must return zero. `TARGET_ACK_CTRL` takes a write of zero at idle, where hardware holds its `NBYTES` write enable off and a zero on the write-only `NACK` is no NACK; the write carries nothing the register could take, so it is answered but not counted among the writes shown to take no effect.
* Three UART rows are not driven because the UART's own demux never presents those accesses to the block they belong to: `uart_16550.sv` routes every write at the `THR` and `FCR` addresses to the write-only block, so the main block never sees a write at `RBR` or `IIR`, and it routes no read to the write-only block, so that block never sees a read at `FCR`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpuif_wrong_direction_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPUIF-WRITE-READ-ONLY` |Every write at a read-only register was answered and took no effect -- each register that holds still at idle read the same before and after a write of the complement of what it held, each FIFO whose data register pops on read kept its level -- and no block's probe register moved; the write of zero at `TARGET_ACK_CTRL` was answered and is not counted among them
|`CHK-CPUIF-READ-WRITE-ONLY` |Every read of a write-only register was answered and returned zero, and every register no leaf had read returned its RDL reset at idle
|===

*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-CPUIF-READ-WRITE-ONLY`, `CHK-CPUIF-WRITE-READ-ONLY` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Three UART rows are not driven, because the UART's own demux never presents a write
at `RBR` or `IIR` to the main block or a read at `FCR` to the write-only block. The write of zero at
`TARGET_ACK_CTRL` is answered but not counted among the writes shown to take no effect, since it
carries nothing the register could take.

'''''

[[sec-249-smc_i2c_target_read_abort_test]]
===== 249 `smc_i2c_target_read_abort_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_read_abort_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` bit-banging the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the controller, and a second bench pad driver as the other device on the bus; observation on `TARGET_EVENTS` and `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A target read ended by something other than the controller must raise the flag `i2c.rdl` gives it, and that flag must behave as a register.

*Test Coverage*:

* Arbitration loss as a target. `i2c_core.sv` detects it as the target transmitting while the SDA it released reads low with SCL high. The transmit FIFO holds all ones, so every bit the target sends is released, and a second driver pulls SDA low inside the SCL high window of the second data bit, counted in SCL rises from the START so the pull lands in the same bit every run. The SDA level just before the pull is required to be a one, so the conflict is measured rather than assumed.
* `TIMING3.THD_DAT` is raised to twenty core clocks for that leg. The pull is also an SDA edge with SCL high, which the bus monitor takes for a START once it has lasted `THD_DAT`, and the target's override block (`i2c_target_fsm.sv`) gives a START priority over arbitration loss. Twenty core clocks is still well inside the START the bench issues itself.
* A bus timeout while the target has a read to answer. `TIMEOUT_CTRL` is armed in bus mode, the target acknowledges its read address, and the bench holds SCL low for several times the limit. `i2c_target_fsm.sv` records it as a bus timeout on a read.
* Both flags are then checked as a register: a word of zeros over the set bit and a word of ones that strobes only the top byte lane of `TARGET_EVENTS`, so the lane carrying the bit is disabled while carrying a one, must both leave it set, and only a written one clears it. `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` is the second witness for arbitration loss, since the target refuses the transaction on the same edge and counts it once.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target with the raised data hold time, clear its events and its NACK count, and load `TXDATA` with all ones.
. Error injection. Point: the SDA line on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, inside the SCL high window of the second data bit counted from the START. Kind: the second bench driver pulls SDA low under a one the target is sending. Expected response: `ARBITRATION_LOST` raised and a NACK count of one. Read one byte with the bench controller and require a one just before the pull.
. Run the retain checks on `ARBITRATION_LOST`.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL line during a read whose address the target has acknowledged. Kind: SCL held low by the bench past the `TIMEOUT_CTRL` limit, armed in bus mode. Expected response: `BUS_TIMEOUT` raised. Bring the target up again with the bus timeout armed beforehand; run the retain checks on the flag afterwards.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-ARBITRATION-LOST` |SDA pulled low under a one the target was sending raised `ARBITRATION_LOST`, and the target refused the rest of the transaction, counting it once
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-READ-BUS-TIMEOUT` |SCL held low past the bus timeout during a read raised `BUS_TIMEOUT`
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-EVENTS-RETAIN-ABORT` |Both flags, set by the target itself, survived a word of zeros and a word of ones that strobed only the top byte lane, so their own lane carried a one it was not enabled to take, and cleared only on a written one
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-250-smc_i2c_controller_scl_events_test]]
===== 250 `smc_i2c_controller_scl_events_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_scl_events_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the target, and a second bench pad driver as another device on SCL and SDA; observation on `INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `STATUS` and the target's data

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Another device on SCL, at each point of a controller transfer where the controller has released it, must be answered the way `i2c_controller_fsm` specifies for that point.

*Test Coverage*:

* SCL pulled low while the controller holds a clock pulse high is clock synchronisation: `INTR_STATE.SCL_INTERFERENCE` is raised and the transfer carries on. Driven in the START hold, the acknowledge pulse, a read data pulse and the pulse of the acknowledge the controller drives itself.
* SCL falling while a repeated START or the STOP is being set up, or both lines low while the STOP is held, means the controller could not issue its control symbol before another device took the bus; the design reports it as arbitration loss through `ctrl_symbol_failed`. The STOP hold lasts only until the controller sees SDA rise, so that leg takes SDA on the STOP's setup rise and keeps it low when the controller releases it, then takes SCL as well once past the setup.
* SCL held low across a rise the controller expects is a stretch: in the setup of a first START, the setup of a repeated START, the pulse of its own acknowledge and the setup of the STOP. Each transfer then has to complete with the target's data intact and no event raised.
* SCL held low past `TIMEOUT_CTRL` in bus mode halts the controller with `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT`, which is then checked as a register: a word of zeros and a word of ones that strobes only the top byte lane, so its own lane carries a one it is not enabled to take, must both leave it set, and only a written one clears it.
* The controller disabled while held in the setup of a repeated START: the restart it was about to issue is still pending, and it must not reach the bus. The bench target has to see one START for the transfer, not two.
* Every point is placed by counting edges on the pads -- the START, the Nth SCL rise, or the fall after it -- so each lands in the same state on every run. Each leg re-enables the controller from scratch and returns the bus to idle afterwards, clocking the target out of any byte a halted transfer left it in.

SDA changing while the controller holds a pulse high is not driven here; `smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test` covers it, in the pulses the controller receives (`SDA_UNSTABLE`) and in those it drives (`SDA_INTERFERENCE`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL line on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads (and SDA as well in the STOP hold), at an edge counted from the START. Kind: a pull low by the second bench driver during a held-high pulse or in the setup of a repeated START or the STOP, or a hold across an expected rise. Expected response: `SCL_INTERFERENCE` for a pull during a held-high pulse, `ARBITRATION_LOST` for a pull in the setup of the repeated START or the STOP, and a completed transfer with the target's data intact for a hold across an expected rise. For each point: re-enable the controller, arm the injector, and queue the write or the write-restart-read.
. Require the response of that point; return the bus to idle.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL line, with `TIMEOUT_CTRL` armed in bus mode. Kind: SCL held low past the timeout. Expected response: `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.BUS_TIMEOUT` raised. Run the retain checks on it.
. Hold SCL in the setup of a repeated START, disable the controller during the hold, and require it to go idle with a single START seen by the target.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-SCL-INTERFERENCE` |SCL pulled low during each of the four held-high pulses raised `SCL_INTERFERENCE`
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-SYMBOL-FAILED` |SCL falling in the setup of a repeated START or of the STOP, and both lines low in the STOP hold, each raised `ARBITRATION_LOST`
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-STRETCH-POINTS` |SCL held across each of the four expected rises, and each transfer then completed with the target's data intact and no event
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-BUS-TIMEOUT` |SCL held past the bus timeout raised `BUS_TIMEOUT`, which survived zeros and a disabled lane and cleared only on a written one
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-PENDING-RESTART` |The controller disabled with a repeated START pending went idle without issuing it
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: SDA changing while the controller holds a pulse high is not driven here;
`smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test` covers it.

'''''

[[sec-251-smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test]]
===== 251 `smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_disable_stop_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the target and a pad watcher counting STOPs; observation on the pads, `INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `STATUS`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A controller that has started a transaction owns the bus until it gives a STOP; if software clears `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` with the transaction still open, the controller gives that STOP itself.

*Test Coverage*:

* The expectation is the OpenTitan I2C theory of operation, which `hw/ip/i2c/doc/index.adoc` adopts: software may "end the current transaction by setting CTRL.ENABLEHOST to 1'b0", and "if a NACK handling timeout occurs or CTRL.ENABLEHOST is cleared, then the FSM will halt again after the STOP condition is sent. The STOP condition terminates the transaction, leaving the FSM halted in the 'bus idle' state, with SDA and SCL released."
* The controller parked mid-transaction. When the format FIFO runs dry without a STOP, `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` sets, `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` stays clear and the controller holds SCL low. Clearing the enable there must put one STOP on the pads, raise `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE`, release both pads and return the controller to idle.
* The controller halted on a NACK, the case the theory of operation describes: the address nobody on the bench bus answers is NACKed, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` sets, `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` is raised, SCL is held low and the byte queued behind the address keeps `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` clear. Clearing the enable there must put one STOP on the pads, raise `CMD_COMPLETE` and release both pads; the controller returns to idle once the halt events are cleared.
* `INTR_STATE.CMD_COMPLETE` is raised only when the controller finishes a STOP or a repeated START (`i2c.rdl`), so it tells a STOP the controller made from any other edge on the pads, and the bench target must count exactly one STOP after each disable.
* The enable cleared between two format entries of a transfer in flight is not driven: no document states whether a STOP follows there, and the `CHK-I2C-CTRL-DISABLE-STOP-POP` token that graded it is withdrawn.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads.
. Queue a START and address and an offset byte with no STOP; wait for `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` and require SCL low and `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` clear. Clear `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and require a STOP on the pads, `CMD_COMPLETE`, one STOP at the target, both pads released and an idle controller.
. Error injection. Point: the controller's format FIFO. Kind: a START and an address no device on the bench bus answers, with an offset byte queued behind it. Expected response: `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK` set with `STATUS.HOSTIDLE` clear, `STATUS.FMTEMPTY` clear, `INTR_STATE.CONTROLLER_HALT` set and SCL low. Clear `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` and require a STOP on the pads, `CMD_COMPLETE`, one STOP at the target and both pads released; clear the controller events and the FIFOs and require an idle controller.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-DISABLE-STOP-HALTED` |Clearing the enable with the controller halted on a NACKed address made one STOP on the pads, raised `CMD_COMPLETE` and released both pads
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-DISABLE-STOP-IDLE` |Clearing the enable with the controller parked mid-transaction made one STOP on the pads, raised `CMD_COMPLETE`, released both pads and returned the controller to idle
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: The enable cleared between two format entries of a transfer in flight is not driven,
because no document states whether a STOP follows there; the token that graded it is withdrawn.

'''''

[[sec-252-smc_fw_narrow_store_lane_test]]
===== 252 `smc_fw_narrow_store_lane_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_fw_narrow_store_lane_test`

*BFM / Model*: the SMC C image `fw/tests/narrow_store_lane`, executed by hart 0 of the CPU cluster; verdict and target registers read over SEP_IN AXI

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fw.toml`; groups `all`, `fw`; not in `hosted` (needs
the RISC-V toolchain of the `c_compile` stage); `run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 3600; tags
`firmware`, `cpu`, `register`; seed 1; args `+smc_hold_cpu_boot`,
`+smc_scratch_ram_hex=narrow_store_lane.ecc.hex`; firmware image `narrow_store_lane`; tool Verilator
(cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: CPU word stores into one half of a 64-bit register word, which put the word on the other half's byte lanes with their strobes clear, leave the other half's fields unchanged.

*Test Coverage*:

* The register blocks with a 64-bit CPU interface (`smc_base_config`, `dfx_ctrl_status`, `cpu_ctrl`, `alias_remap`) write each field bit only where its byte strobe is set. The core replicates a 32-bit store across both halves of its 64-bit data bus and strobes only the addressed half, so a store of all ones to one half carries ones on every lane of the other half with its strobe clear. The bench's SEP_IN master zero-fills unstrobed lanes and cannot make this case; only a CPU store can.
* Six registers keep all their writable fields in the half the store does not address: `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`, `HANG_DET_SYS_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_SEP_AXI_CTRL`, `HANG_DET_DATA_ACCEL_CTRL`, `DEBUG_CTRL` and `RESET_TIMEOUT`. Each is stored to while every field holds its reset value, which differs from all ones, so a leak through a clear strobe would show on the read-back. In the first five, the stored half has no field and must still read 0. In `RESET_TIMEOUT` the stored half is read-only status. The boot contract leaves `timeout_mode` set before release, where a leak of ones would not show, so the image writes the reset value first and puts the boot value back afterwards.
* The four `CPU_CTRL` `MUTEX` registers are stored to in their upper half, first while free and then while held. The RDL makes any write a release, whichever half it selects, so each store must leave the mutex free, and a read must take it after each store.
* Alias-remap `region_attrs` region 0 is stored to in its lower half. That store takes `offset[31:12]`; `cacheable`, `valid` and `offset[55:32]` in the upper half carry ones on clear strobes and must stay 0. The region stays invalid, so the new offset remaps nothing, and the bench restores it.
* Three stores whose other half holds a field with an effect, each in a shape that writes that field harmlessly:
** `WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET` is 32 bits at `0x58`, with nothing declared at `0x5C`. A store to `0x5C` writes no field, and its singlepulse core-reset fields carry ones with their strobes clear.
** Outbound filter 14's `FILTER_CONFIG` keeps only `locked` (bit 63) in its upper half. An upper-half store with bit 31 clear writes 0 there, which `woset` ignores, while the lower lanes carry `read_allowed`, `write_allowed`, `entry_enabled`, `allow_ns` and `allow_burst` with their strobes clear. A lower-half store with only bit 31 set puts a one on `locked`'s lane with its strobe clear and writes the lower fields, `entry_enabled` included, to 0. The reset lower half is then written back, and the bench reads the reset word with `locked` clear after PASS.
** The zeroer starts on a `CTRL_STATUS` write only while `SIZE` is non-zero. An upper-half store with `SIZE` 0 puts a one on `INT_EN`'s lane with its strobe clear and starts nothing: the image requires `STATUS` idle, and the bench reads `CTRL_STATUS` 0 after PASS.
* CI: no hosted runner builds firmware, so this leaf runs on demand like the other `fw` leaves (<<smc-scheduled-holdouts>>). The image builds through `[c_build.default]` with the same path and post-process as `hello_world`, so the build needs nothing the other `fw` images do not.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Build `narrow_store_lane` through `[c_build.default]`, stage `narrow_store_lane.ecc.hex` beside the simulator, and hold `boot_stall` from t=0 (`+smc_hold_cpu_boot`).
. With the cores held, read every target over SEP_IN. The six registers must show their RDL reset word under their writable mask, each mutex must be taken by a read and then released, and `region_attrs` must read its reset word.
. Clear CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0, program the reset vector, and release the cores and `boot_stall`. The image reads each field half, stores all ones to the other half, fences, and reads the field half again, failing on any change or on a non-zero empty half. Each mutex must be free after its store while free and released by its store while held. The image then stores to `region_attrs` and requires `0xFFFFF000` in the lower half and the upper half unchanged. It prints each stage's result on the virtual console.
. Poll SCRATCH_0 for the PASS magic, failing on `TEST_FAIL`, on the `0xBAD0_xxxx` namespace, and on the bound expiring.
. Read every target over SEP_IN again, with `RESET_TIMEOUT` expected at the boot contract's value, then restore `region_attrs` and read the restore back.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FW-NARROW-STORE-BOOT` |The firmware's own PASS word is read back from CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0 after a cleared-and-verified start. The image posts it only when every target held across its store
|`CHK-FW-NARROW-STORE-HELD` |After PASS, over SEP_IN: the writable fields of five registers still hold their RDL reset word and `RESET_TIMEOUT` holds the boot contract's value, every mutex is still free, and `region_attrs` reads `offset[31:12]` all ones with the upper half at reset
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. No `ci` tag: the hosted runners have no RISC-V toolchain. Enrolled in: `all`, `fw`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-254-smc_i3c_dxt_table_test]]
===== 254 `smc_i3c_dxt_table_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_dxt_table_test`

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI driver (no external VIP)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Write and read back the Device Address Table, and read the Device Characteristic Table, of all six I3C instances through their CSR windows.

*Test Coverage*:

* The integration shell keeps each I3C instance's DAT and DCT in a single-port RAM, with a read-valid flop that a read reaching the RAM sets. No other leaf reads either table on any instance. The I3C CSR window maps both tables (`registers.rdl`: `external DAT` at `0x400`, `external DCT` at `0x800`), and `smc_addr.h` gives their per-instance bases and the instance count, six.
* **DAT.** `DAT_structure.rdl` makes every field of an entry `sw = rw`. The leaf reads entry 0 of every instance, writes each instance a pattern of its own over the fields the RDL declares, and then reads all six back after all six are written. A read answered without reaching the RAM, or from another instance's RAM, returns the wrong pattern. Each entry is then cleared and read back 0. Nothing writes the RAM before the leaf, so a four-state simulator reads the first read as X. That read only has to show that the entry does not already hold the pattern on every declared bit.
* **DCT.** `DCT_structure.rdl` makes every field `sw = r`. Only dynamic address assignment writes the table, and this bench does not run it, so its content is not specified: X under a four-state simulator, 0 under a two-state one. The leaf reads entry 0 of every instance twice, as four 32-bit words. Every read must complete with RRESP OKAY, and the two passes must agree on every bit known in both; an X matches anything. The read completing is what sets the RAM's read-valid flop.
* The SEP_IN master converts each read beat to an int and cannot hold X, so the reads of unwritten entries are taken from a tap on its R channel. The tap records each beat's RRESP and data as sampled and hands the master a copy with unresolvable data zeroed; the master's return value is not used for those reads.
* The I3C cores themselves are outside this plan's scope; the leaf credits the shell's table RAMs and the CSR-window path to them, not I3C protocol.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_i3c_dxt_table_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-DAT-TABLE-RW` |DAT entry 0 of each of the six instances read back its own pattern over the declared fields after all six were written, and each was cleared and read back 0
|`CHK-I3C-DCT-TABLE-READ` |DCT entry 0 of each of the six instances was read twice, every read completed with RRESP OKAY, and the two passes agreed on every bit known in both
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The I3C cores themselves are outside this plan's scope; the leaf credits the shell's
table RAMs and the CSR-window path, not I3C protocol. The DCT content is not specified, since only
dynamic address assignment writes it and this bench does not run it, so the two passes are required
only to agree on every bit known in both, and an X matches anything.

'''''

[[sec-259-smc_telemetry_buffer_overflow_test]]
===== 259 `smc_telemetry_buffer_overflow_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_telemetry_buffer_overflow_test`

*BFM / Model*: the bench ATB beat driver on telemetry receivers 0, 1 and 2 (`tb_telemetry0_*`, `tb_telemetry1_*`, `tb_telemetry2_*`), shared with `smc_telemetry_atb_capture_test`; observation on `STATUS`, `INTR_STATUS`, `CTRL`, the message registers and `peripheral_interrupts_o[10:9]`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Drive telemetry receiver 0 past each of its two bounded stores, the message buffer and the assembly buffer, and check what the register documentation says happens at each bound. Then run the queue overflow, push-against-pop, transmitter flush, `MISSING_LAST` and `INTR_TEST` legs on receivers 1 and 2.

*Test Coverage*:

* A message buffer filled past full. Messages with distinct probe IDs are sent without popping until `STATUS.BUFFER_FULL` sets, then two more. The depth is read off `STATUS.BUFFER_FULL` rather than assumed, because the IP documents give it as both 8 and 16. The drain must return exactly as many messages as the buffer held when it filled, as one unbroken run of the probe IDs sent, in the order sent. Which end of the run survived is recorded, not asserted, because no document states it.
* `CTRL.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` with its interrupt enabled. `telemetry_receiver.rdl` raises `INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` while more messages than the threshold are buffered. It is checked after every message on the way up and after every pop on the way down. `CTRL` carries the threshold beside `BUFFER_POP`, so every pop rewrites it.
* `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST`, raised when the maximum number of packets a message can have arrives without the last-packet flag. Packets without the flag are sent one at a time until it sets, which measures that maximum. It must then clear on a written one.
* A message of exactly that many packets, the last one flagged. It fills the assembly buffer exactly, must not raise `MISSING_LAST`, and must reach the message buffer.
* `CTRL.BUFFER_POP` written to an empty buffer, which the RDL says has no effect. The buffer must stay empty and not full, and the next message must read back its own probe ID.
* One beat short of the most a message can hold, an unfinished message must complete nothing and raise no `MISSING_LAST`. A flush written while a beat is presented on the ATB port, and a second flush, must leave the next message reading back its own probe ID.
* Receivers 1 and 2, queue full and overflow. Eight messages fill the `BUFFER_DEPTH` = 8 queue: `STATUS` reads 0x00 after each of the first seven and 0x10 after the eighth, with the first message in `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`. A ninth drops the oldest, the eight pops present the survivors in order, the empty queue reads `STATUS` = 0x01 and `PROBE_ID` = 0, and one more pop leaves both unchanged.
* Receivers 1 and 2, a push meeting a pop. With the queue full, `CTRL.BUFFER_POP` is written at each offset from -4 to +4 `clk_periph_i` cycles around the last beat of one more message. The drain must be every message after the oldest, or one fewer, in order; which one each offset gives is logged, because the documents do not decide it (SF-027).
* Receivers 1 and 2, `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` with three messages queued. The bench holds `afready_i` of these receivers high and does not publish their `afvalid_o`, so the flush runs with `afready_i` at that level: the request must self-clear within the poll bound, `STATUS` must read 0x00 with the first queued message in `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID`, and the three messages must drain in order. The handshake with `afready_i` low is not reachable on this bench (SF-044).
* Receivers 1 and 2, `MISSING_LAST`. Beats without the last-packet marker are sent one at a time until `INTR_STATUS.MISSING_LAST` sets, first with `INTR_ENABLE` = 0x00 and then 0x01. `peripheral_interrupts_o[8+r]` must stay 0 while disabled and rise while enabled, and a written one clears the status and the line. The next complete message must read back its own probe ID. The beat count is logged, not compared (SF-024).
* Receivers 1 and 2, `INTR_TEST.MISSING_LAST`. It must raise `peripheral_interrupts_o[8+r]` with the enable on and leave it 0 with the enable off. `INTR_STATUS` after the test write is logged (SF-025).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Ungate telemetry, flush, write a pop with the buffer empty, then send and read back one message.
. Error injection. Point: the ATB port of telemetry receiver 0, into the message buffer. Kind: messages with distinct probe IDs sent without popping until `STATUS.BUFFER_FULL` sets, then two more past full. Expected response: `BUFFER_FULL` set and staying set through the two extra messages, with the drain of step 3 returning exactly the depth's worth as an in-order run of the IDs sent. Set `CTRL.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` and enable its interrupt first, checking the threshold interrupt after each message.
. Pop everything, checking the threshold interrupt after each pop. Compare the probe IDs read back with the IDs sent.
. Error injection. Point: the ATB port, into the assembly buffer. Kind: packets without the last-packet flag sent one at a time past the maximum a message can have. Expected response: `MISSING_LAST` sets on the first packet past the maximum, not before, and clears on a written one. Flush first; clear the flag afterwards.
. Flush and send one message of that many packets with the last one flagged. Require no `MISSING_LAST` and a buffered message.
. Flush, send one beat fewer than the assembly buffer holds without the last-packet flag, then flush with a beat held valid, flush again and send one message.
. On receivers 1 and 2, flush and require `STATUS` = 0x01, `INTR_STATUS` = 0x00 and the interrupt line at 0.
. Send eight messages, then a ninth; pop nine times, reading `STATUS` and `TELEMETRY_PROBE_ID` around each pop.
. For each offset from -4 to +4, refill to full, send one more message with `CTRL.BUFFER_POP` written at that offset from its last beat, and drain.
. Queue three messages and write `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` with `afready_i` high; poll the bit until it clears and drain.
. With `INTR_ENABLE` off and then on, send beats without the last marker until `MISSING_LAST` sets, check the line and clear the status; send one complete message.
. Write `INTR_TEST.MISSING_LAST` with `INTR_ENABLE` on and off and check the line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-POP-EMPTY` |A pop on an empty buffer left it empty and not full, and the next message read back its own probe ID
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-THRESHOLD-INTR` |`INTR_STATUS.BUFFER_THRESHOLD` was set exactly while more messages than the threshold were buffered, filling and draining
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-BUFFER-OVERFLOW` |`BUFFER_FULL` set and stayed set through two more messages, and the drain returned exactly the depth's worth of messages as an in-order run of the IDs sent
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-MISSING-LAST` |`MISSING_LAST` set on the first packet past the maximum a message can have, not before, and cleared on a written one
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-FULL-MESSAGE` |A message of the maximum size with its last packet flagged reached the buffer without `MISSING_LAST`
|`CHK-TELEMETRY-PARTIAL-FLUSH` |A message one beat short completed nothing and raised nothing, and after a flush with a beat presented the next message read back intact
|`CHK-TELEM12-FULL` |On receivers 1 and 2, eight messages gave `STATUS` = 0x10 with the first probe ID visible, not before the eighth, and the first pop after the overflow gave `STATUS` = 0x00
|`CHK-TELEM12-OVERFLOW-ORDER` |On receivers 1 and 2, the ninth message dropped the oldest; the eight pops presented the survivors in order, then `STATUS` = 0x01 and `PROBE_ID` = 0, which an extra pop left unchanged
|`CHK-TELEM12-PUSH-POP-WINDOW` |On receivers 1 and 2, for every pop offset the drain was the no-drop or the one-drop run in order; which one is logged per offset (SF-027)
|`CHK-TELEM12-TX-FLUSH` |On receivers 1 and 2, with `afready_i` at its bench level (high), `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` self-cleared within the bound, `STATUS` read 0x00 with the first queued probe ID, and the three queued messages drained in order; the `afready_i`-low handshake is not reachable on this bench (SF-044)
|`CHK-TELEM12-MISSING-LAST` |On receivers 1 and 2, `MISSING_LAST` set with the line following `INTR_ENABLE`, a written one cleared status and line, and the next message read back intact; the beat count is logged (SF-024)
|`CHK-TELEM12-INTR-TEST` |On receivers 1 and 2, `INTR_TEST.MISSING_LAST` raised the line with the enable on and left it 0 with the enable off; `INTR_STATUS` after the write is logged (SF-025)
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |Every bounded wait of the receiver 1 and 2 legs is listed with its bound, its unit and the last state it saw
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The receiver 1 and 2 steps ran in order with strictly increasing time stamps, each checker line inside its own step
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all fourteen checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: Which end of the run of probe IDs survived the overflow is recorded, not asserted,
because no document states it. The buffer depth is read off `STATUS.BUFFER_FULL` rather than
assumed, because the IP documents give it as both 8 and 16.

'''''

[[sec-255-smc_i2c_controller_queue_shapes_test]]
===== 255 `smc_i2c_controller_queue_shapes_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_queue_shapes_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, and a pad watcher that counts SCL rises and STOPs; observation on `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `INTR_STATE`, `STATUS`, `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`, `RDATA` and the target's memory

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Six shapes of the controller's format queue that no other leaf writes. Every other controller leaf queues one transaction at a time, gives it a STOP, and drains the receive FIFO while the read runs.

*Test Coverage*:

* `FDATA.NAKOK` on an address nobody answers. `i2c.rdl` says the controller then does not halt, set `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.NACK`, or raise `CONTROLLER_HALT`. The transfer must run to its STOP with `CMD_COMPLETE`.
* Two transactions queued together, each with its own START and STOP. The controller leaves the first STOP for the format FIFO with the second transaction already waiting. The target must see two STARTs, two STOPs and both bytes.
* A transaction queued without its last entry, which runs dry and parks holding SCL low. The entry queued afterwards must finish it as one transaction.
** `CTRL.MULTI_CONTROLLER_MONITOR_EN` is set together with `ENABLEHOST`, as the RDL requires, so the controller sees the bus it parked on as busy and continues because it owns the open transaction.
** `HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL.VAL` gives the monitor its bus-free time.
** `TIMEOUT_CTRL` is in bus mode with `EN` clear across the park, and no `BUS_TIMEOUT` may result.
* A NACK left pending across a disable. `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` is armed, the controller is NACKed, and `CTRL.ENABLEHOST` is cleared before the timeout runs out.
** The controller closes the transaction with one STOP of its own.
** The handler timeout must not run while the controller is disabled.
** Re-enabled with the NACK still set, the timeout runs out, but with no transaction open nothing reaches the pads. Clearing `NACK` alone must then leave `UNHANDLED_NACK_TIMEOUT` set on its own, since each field clears only on its own written one. The disable waits a fixed settle after the NACK is seen, because the controller reaches IDLE only after the hold that follows the acknowledge.
* `CTRL.LLPBK` in controller mode, which `i2c.rdl` limits to the SMBus alert input. A transfer made with it set must reach the target unchanged.
* A read longer than the receive FIFO, with no `RDATA` reads until it ends.
** `INTR_STATE.RX_OVERFLOW` and `STATUS.RXFULL` must be raised.
** The FIFO, whose depth is read off `HOST_FIFO_STATUS.RXLVL`, must hold the first bytes read, in order.
** `RX_OVERFLOW` must clear on a written one.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target on the pads.
. For each shape, re-enable the controller, queue the entries, and check the result above.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NAKOK` |NACKs that `NAKOK` allowed left `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` at 0 and `CONTROLLER_HALT` clear, and the transfer ended in one STOP with `CMD_COMPLETE`
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-BACK-TO-BACK` |Two transactions queued together reached the target as two STARTs and two STOPs, with both bytes written
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-PARK-CONTINUE` |A parked transaction held SCL low with `HOSTIDLE` clear, raised no `BUS_TIMEOUT` with the timeout disabled, and the later entry finished it as one transaction
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-NACK-DISABLED` |A NACKed transaction closed with one STOP on disable, the handler timeout did not run while disabled, once re-enabled it ran out with nothing on the pads, and clearing NACK alone left the timeout flag set
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-LOOPBACK-HOST` |A write made with `LLPBK` set in controller mode reached the target unchanged, with no event
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-RX-OVERFLOW` |An undrained over-long read raised `RX_OVERFLOW` and `RXFULL`, the FIFO held the first bytes in order, and the interrupt cleared on a written one
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-256-smc_i2c_controller_edge_timing_test]]
===== 256 `smc_i2c_controller_edge_timing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_controller_edge_timing_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cEepromSlave` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, and a second bench pad driver that moves SCL and SDA together; observation on `INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `STATUS` and the target's data

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Test the controller's decisions that depend on how SCL and SDA move relative to each other. It samples the two lines through matching synchronisers, so some decisions arise only when both lines move on the same clock, or when SCL falls after the controller has already seen a stretch.

*Test Coverage*:

* SCL falling while SDA changes. Both lines are pulled low at the same instant, 60 ns into the high window of four pulses where SDA is high:
** a bit the controller transmits;
** the acknowledge of an address nobody answers;
** a one bit the target returns;
** the not-acknowledge the controller drives.
+
The fall is clock synchronisation and must raise `INTR_STATE.SCL_INTERFERENCE`.
* SCL rising while SDA changes, in the not-acknowledge pulse. Both lines are held low from the low phase before it, which stretches the pulse, and then released together. SDA rises with SCL, so the read must complete intact with no event.
* SCL falling after a stretch. SCL is held low for 5 us across the expected rise, released, and pulled low again 60 ns into the high window.
** In the same four pulses, the fall is clock synchronisation (`SCL_INTERFERENCE`).
** In the setup of a repeated START and in the setup of the STOP, the controller could not issue its control symbol (`CONTROLLER_EVENTS.ARBITRATION_LOST`). A word of zeros written over `CONTROLLER_EVENTS` must leave the flag set. `TSU_STA` or `TSU_STO` is lengthened so that the setup outlasts the pull's delay.
* SDA rising while SCL falls in the STOP hold. SDA is held low through the STOP's setup, then released at the moment SCL is pulled low. The controller sees SDA high and must finish its STOP with `CMD_COMPLETE` and no event.
* Another device in the setup of a first START. `TIMING2.TSU_STA` is lengthened so the setup can be hit from a time offset after the queue.
** SCL pulled low there means another device took the bus first. The transfer must still complete intact.
** SDA pulled low there must raise `INTR_STATE.SDA_INTERFERENCE`.
* Every point in a transfer is placed by counting edges on the pads from the START, as in `smc_i2c_controller_scl_events_test`. Each leg disables the controller, clears its events and returns the bus to idle afterwards.
* A repeated START set up too briefly. With `TIMING1.T_R` 0 and `TIMING2.TSU_STA` 1, the setup ends before the SCL the controller has just released is seen high, so the hold that follows starts with SCL still low. `TIMEOUT_CTRL` is set to stretch-timeout mode with `VAL` 0, so the setup ends with the stretch count past it. The controller must return to idle with no event; how many STARTs the bench target counts, and whether `INTR_STATE.STRETCH_TIMEOUT` is set, are recorded.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a host with the bench EEPROM target and the second pad driver on the pads.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL and SDA lines on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, at an edge counted from the START. Kind: both lines pulled low 60 ns into the high window of a transmitted bit, an unanswered acknowledge, a returned one bit or the controller's not-acknowledge; both held low through the not-acknowledge pulse and released together; SCL held 5 us across an expected rise and pulled low again, in the same four pulses and in the setup of a repeated START or the STOP; SDA held through the STOP setup and released as SCL is pulled low; SCL or SDA pulled low in the setup of a first START. Expected response: `SCL_INTERFERENCE` for the four synchronisation pulls; the read completed intact with no event for the held not-acknowledge; `SCL_INTERFERENCE` for the post-stretch pulls in the four pulses and `CONTROLLER_EVENTS.ARBITRATION_LOST` for those in the repeated START and STOP setups, the flag surviving a word of zeros; `CMD_COMPLETE` with no event for the STOP-hold release; the transfer completed intact for the SCL pull in the first START setup and `SDA_INTERFERENCE` for the SDA pull there. For each point: re-enable the controller, arm the edge, queue the transfer; then disable, clear and recover the bus.
. Error injection. Point: `TIMING1.T_R` and `TIMING2.TSU_STA`, with `TIMEOUT_CTRL` in stretch-timeout mode at `VAL` 0. Kind: a repeated START set up too briefly (`T_R` 0, `TSU_STA` 1) for the released SCL to be seen high. Expected response: the controller returns to idle with no event. Queue a write, repeated START and read, and wait for idle.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-FALL-CHANGE` |SCL and SDA pulled low together in each of the four pulses raised `SCL_INTERFERENCE`
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-RISE-CHANGE` |SCL and SDA released together into the not-acknowledge pulse left the read to complete intact with no event
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-STRETCH-FALL` |An SCL fall after a stretch raised `SCL_INTERFERENCE` in each pulse and `ARBITRATION_LOST` in each setup, and `ARBITRATION_LOST` survived a word of zeros
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-STOP-HOLD` |SDA released as SCL fell in the STOP hold let the STOP finish with `CMD_COMPLETE` and no event
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-FIRST-START` |SCL pulled in a first START's setup left the transfer to complete; SDA pulled there raised `SDA_INTERFERENCE`
|`CHK-I2C-CTRL-EDGE-SHORT-SETUP` |A repeated START set up too briefly for SCL to be seen high left the controller idle with no event
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all six checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: In the too-brief repeated START leg, how many STARTs the bench target counts and
whether `INTR_STATE.STRETCH_TIMEOUT` is set are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-257-smc_i2c_target_loopback_test]]
===== 257 `smc_i2c_target_loopback_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_target_loopback_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the external controller; observation on `STATUS`, `TARGET_FIFO_STATUS`, `ACQDATA` and the bytes read back. For the instance-1 legs, `+smc_i2c1_pads` makes the bench drive the resolved open-drain value onto the I2C1 pads, read back as `tb_i2c1_scl` / `tb_i2c1_sda`; on that pair an `SmcI2cEepromSlave` at 0x50 preset to 0x00..0xFF, a bench controller that samples SDA at the SCL high of every bit it drives, and a pad injector on `tb_i2c1_scl_ext_low` / `tb_i2c1_sda_ext_low`; ocah_axi_vip on SEP_IN writing and reading the I2C1 registers at the generated map's instance stride

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `CTRL.LLPBK` in target mode, which `i2c.rdl` describes as a target that "sends all received SDA data back out", driven against a transmit FIFO with one free entry; then the I2C1 core line controls on its own pads: `LLPBK`, `OVRD` / `VAL`, controller RX overflow and `RXRST`, `SCL_INTERFERENCE` and `SDA_UNSTABLE`.

*Test Coverage*:

* The transmit FIFO depth is measured by filling it through `TXDATA` until `STATUS.TXFULL` sets. The FIFO is then reset and loaded with one entry fewer.
* `LLPBK` is set with `ACQ_START_STOP_EN`, so the START and STOP are acquisition entries, and a two-byte write is made to the target.
** The first byte takes the free transmit entry.
** The second byte, and the STOP behind it, must wait in the acquisition FIFO.
** The START entry carries no payload and must not wait.
** `TARGET_FIFO_STATUS.ACQLVL` must show exactly two entries.
* A read cannot unblock this state. The target holds a read until the acquisition FIFO is empty, and the acquisition FIFO cannot empty into a full transmit FIFO. Software breaks the tie by reading `ACQDATA`, which must return the waiting byte as a data entry. The STOP entry must then leave on its own.
* A read of the whole transmit FIFO must return the bytes loaded through `TXDATA`, in order, followed by the first written byte looped back. It must leave the acquisition FIFO empty.
* I2C1 as a target at 0x26 with `ACQ_START_STOP_EN`: with `LLPBK=1` every SDA level sampled at the SCL high of each written data bit of 0x5A, 0xC3 must equal the driven bit; the acknowledge bits and acquisition entries are logged, not compared (SF-013). With `LLPBK=0` the acquisition FIFO must hold START with 0x26 << 1, 0x5A, 0xC3 and STOP.
* I2C1 with `OVRD.TXOVRDEN=1` and each (`SCLVAL`, `SDAVAL`) pair: the pads must read the values (0 low, 1 released) and `VAL` bit 0 and bit 16 must equal the pads, also while the bench pulls each line low with both released. After `TXOVRDEN=0` an ordinary write of 0x20, 0x5C must land with `HOSTIDLE=1`. The full `VAL` is logged (SF-014).
* A `READB` of 256 bytes with no `RDATA` pops must set `STATUS.RXFULL`; the bytes popped until `RXEMPTY=1` must be one in-order run of consecutive EEPROM bytes, and a written 0x8 must clear `RX_OVERFLOW`. Whether `RX_OVERFLOW` set, the level at full and the bytes retained are logged (SF-004). `FIFO_CTRL.RXRST` after a four-byte refill must leave `RXEMPTY=1` and `RXLVL=0`.
* A clean write must leave `SCL_INTERFERENCE` clear; SCL pulled low for 100 ns inside the controller-driven high of the address acknowledge pulse must set it, and a written 0x20 must clear it.
* A clean four-byte read must leave `SDA_UNSTABLE` clear; SDA pulled low inside the SCL high of a released read data bit must set it, and a written 0x100 must clear it.
* The controller-mode half of `LLPBK`, which masks `smbalert_ni`, is not exercised: with `+smc_i2c1_pads` the bench has no driver for the I2C1 alert pad (SF-043).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Bring up I2C0 as a target, measure the transmit FIFO depth, reset it and load one entry fewer.
. Set `LLPBK` and `ACQ_START_STOP_EN`, write two bytes from the external controller, and check `ACQLVL`.
. Read `ACQDATA`, check that the acquisition FIFO empties, then read the full depth back.
. Set `I2C_CTRL[1]` for target mode, select the I2C1 pads for LSIO, start the EEPROM, the bench controller and the injector on the I2C1 pads, wait for both pads high and program the I2C1 bring-up timing.
. Program `TARGET_ID` with 0x26, write 0x5A, 0xC3 with `LLPBK=1` sampling SDA per bit, wait for `TARGETIDLE` and drain `ACQDATA`; repeat with `LLPBK=0` and compare the four entries.
. Set `I2C_CTRL[1]` for controller mode, enable the host, write each `OVRD` pair and read `VAL` once the pads follow; with both released pull SCL, then SDA, low from the bench and read `VAL`; clear `OVRD` and write 0x20, 0x5C to the EEPROM.
. Program a fast timing set, queue a 256-byte read, poll `RXFULL`, read `HOST_FIFO_STATUS` and `INTR_STATE`, pop `RDATA` until `RXEMPTY`, wait for `HOSTIDLE`, write 0x8 to `INTR_STATE`; restore the bring-up timing, read four bytes, write `RXRST` and read `STATUS` and `HOST_FIFO_STATUS`.
. Write to the EEPROM cleanly, then again with the SCL pull; read `INTR_STATE`, write 0x20 and read it again.
. Read four bytes cleanly, then again with the SDA pull; read `INTR_STATE`, write 0x100 and read it again. Print the bounded waits.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-LOOPBACK-BLOCKED` |With one free transmit entry, the second written byte and its STOP waited in the acquisition FIFO, `ACQDATA` returned the byte as data, and the STOP then left
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-LOOPBACK-ECHO` |The read returned the `TXDATA` bytes in order and then the first written byte, and left the acquisition FIFO empty
|`CHK-I2C1-LLPBK-ECHO` |With I2C1 `LLPBK=1` each sampled SDA data bit equals the bit the bench drove, 16 of 16; the acquisition entries are logged (SF-013)
|`CHK-I2C1-LLPBK-OFF` |With `LLPBK=0` the acquisition FIFO holds START/0x26 << 1, 0x5A, 0xC3, STOP (`SIGNAL` 0x1, 0x0, 0x0, 0x2)
|`CHK-I2C1-OVRD-PADS` |For each (`SCLVAL`, `SDAVAL`) the pads read exactly those values; after `TXOVRDEN=0` the EEPROM receives 0x20, 0x5C and `STATUS.HOSTIDLE=1`
|`CHK-I2C1-OVRD-VAL` |`VAL` bit 0 (`SCL_RX`) and bit 16 (`SDA_RX`) equal the pads for every override and each bench-driven low; the full `VAL` is logged (SF-014)
|`CHK-I2C1-RX-OVERFLOW` |A 256-byte read without pops sets `RXFULL`, the popped bytes are one in-order run of consecutive EEPROM bytes ending with `RXEMPTY=1`, and a written 0x8 leaves `RX_OVERFLOW=0`; `RX_OVERFLOW`, the level at full and the retained bytes are logged (SF-004)
|`CHK-I2C1-RXRST` |After `FIFO_CTRL.RXRST=1` on a refilled FIFO `STATUS.RXEMPTY=1` and `HOST_FIFO_STATUS.RXLVL=0`
|`CHK-I2C1-SCL-INTERFERENCE` |A clean write leaves `SCL_INTERFERENCE=0`, the SCL pull inside a controller high sets it, and a written 0x20 clears it
|`CHK-I2C1-SDA-UNSTABLE` |A clean read leaves `SDA_UNSTABLE=0`, the SDA edge inside the SCL high of a read data bit sets it, and a written 0x100 clears it
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The ordered terms BRINGUP < I2C1_LLPBK_TGT < I2C1_OVRD < I2C1_RX_OVERFLOW < I2C1_SCL_INTERFERENCE < I2C1_SDA_UNSTABLE, after the I2C0 legs, each stamped after its own step and after its checker lines with increasing sim time
|`CHK-TIMEOUT-PATHS` |One entry per bounded wait of the leaf, each with its bound, fail-on-expiry path and the last state its expiry reports: the SEP_IN access bound, and from the I2C0 legs the LSIO-ready poll, the `TXFULL` fill and the VIP SCL-release bound (in `smc_i2c_protocol_vip`). The I2C1 legs add pad level, pad edge, target idle, acquisition drain and level, transfer completion, `RXFULL`, RX drain and idle, `INTR_STATE`, bus recovery and their own VIP SCL-release bound. The fixed waits of the I2C0 legs are listed as fixed waits with no expiry
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every checker holds after its compare and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-258-smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test]]
===== 258 `smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test`

*BFM / Model*: an in-sequence AVSBus slave responder on the sdata pad. It watches the master subframes on mdata over the DUT's AVS clock and, in the following subframe, shifts out a chosen 32-bit reply one bit per rising edge, holding sdata high between replies. Observation on `AVS_READBACK`, `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME`, `AVS_SLAVE_STATUS`, `AVS_NORMAL_STATUS`, `AVS_INTERRUPT` and the master subframes.

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the stimulus is the named frame, command or sequence the
specification states.

*Objective*: Give the controller the slave replies that a level held on sdata cannot give. A held level only ever produces all-zero or all-one replies.

*Test Coverage*:

* The reply format is transcribed from `interface.adoc` "AVSBus Slave Subframe". No document in this tree gives the CRC-3 polynomial, so each reply shape is sent once with each of the eight CRC codes.
** `architecture.adoc` says a reply that fails the check does not update `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME`.
** With `MAX_RETRIES` at 0, a failing reply is still delivered.
** So exactly one of the eight codes must update `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME`, and the other seven must reach `AVS_READBACK` without updating it. The accepted code is used for the legs that need a reply the controller believes.
* Reply shapes the responder produces:
** acknowledge 0 with status 0x10, 0x11 and data;
** acknowledge 1, resource unavailable;
** acknowledge 2, bad CRC;
** acknowledge 3, bad data;
** a frame-not-valid reply;
** the same shapes with each of the eight CRC codes.
* A good reply must reach `AVS_READBACK` and `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME` unchanged, and `AVS_SLAVE_STATUS` must show its acknowledge and status.
* Three acknowledge-1 replies against a budget of 2: the same command goes out three times, `TOTAL_RETRIES` rises by 2, and `MAX_RETRIES_ATTEMPTED_INT` is raised as the only unmasked source.
* An acknowledge-2 reply followed by a good one costs one retry and delivers the good reply.
* Acknowledge 3 is not a retry code. It is delivered at once and shown in `AVS_SLAVE_STATUS`.
* A frame-not-valid reply raises `SLAVE_UNRESPONSIVE_INT`, the only source unmasked.
* Two commands are sent back to back and the first is retried, so the second's reply waits.
** If the waiting reply is good, it is delivered after the retry's good reply.
** If it is acknowledge 1 and `MAX_RETRIES` is cleared while the retry is on the wire, it is delivered as it is, without a retry.
* The readback FIFO is filled by leaving every reply unread.
** The commands queued after it must wait with no subframe on the wire.
** A forced slave resync is requested while they wait.
** After one pop, every command must complete with its reply intact.
* sdata held low while the bus is idle raises `AVS_SLAVE_ISSUED_INTERRUPT` as the only unmasked source, and the clear register clears it.
* sdata is held low long enough to raise the slave interrupt, and a command queued while it is still low has to launch and read back its reply intact.
* The readback FIFO is filled to one slot short, and a pair of commands is sent with the first answered unavailable and a retry budget of 1. The retried command's good reply takes the last slot, and the second command's reply, which waited behind the retry, meets a full FIFO. `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT` must set. The interrupt line must be low with every source masked and high with only that source unmasked. The FIFO must drain the prefill and the retried reply, with the waiting reply the one dropped.
* The AVS clock duty-cycle numerator is changed on its own. Both divider fields reset to 0, a sentinel that leaves the divider on its hardware defaults (`interface.adoc`), so the defaults (divisor 4, numerator 0x80) are first written as real values. The numerator alone then goes to 0x40 and back. The clock at the pad must read 25% high and then 50% again. `smc_avsbus_clock_divider_test` changes the numerator with the divisor held, but its programming helper first writes back the saved reset `AVS_CFG_1`, divisor 0, under `TURN_OFF_ALL_PREMUX_CLOCKS`, so the divider sees the divisor drop to 0 and return together with the new numerator.
* Both FIFOs are filled and one `AVS_CMD` write more is made, which is refused. `READBACK_FIFO_FULL`, `CMD_FIFO_FULL` and `CMD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` must all be set. The AVSBus interrupt line, `tb_avsbus_irq`, must be low with every source masked and high with each of the three unmasked on its own, and every reply must then drain intact.
* A slave resync is forced while commands are still going out, with more queued behind it and the replies drained as they come. Every command must be answered intact. `AVS_READBACK` read with the FIFO empty must then be refused on the bus.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Mask every interrupt, start the responder, and set `MAX_RETRIES` to 0.
. Learn the accepted CRC code for each reply shape.
. Error injection. Point: the sdata responder's reply. Kind: acknowledge 1 against a budget of 2, acknowledge 2 followed by a good reply, acknowledge 3, a frame-not-valid reply, and a reply waiting behind a retry, with `MAX_RETRIES` and the interrupt mask set for each leg. Expected response: three identical subframes with `TOTAL_RETRIES` up by 2 and `MAX_RETRIES_ATTEMPTED_INT` for the acknowledge-1 leg; one retry then the good reply for the acknowledge-2 leg; delivery at once with `AVS_SLAVE_STATUS` showing the code for acknowledge 3; `SLAVE_UNRESPONSIVE_INT` for the frame-not-valid reply; and the buffered reply delivered after the retry's good reply. The good leg runs with them.
. Fill the readback FIFO, queue two more commands, force a resync, and drain.
. Hold sdata low with the bus idle, then clear the slave interrupt.
. Hold sdata low again and queue a command while it is low.
. Error injection. Point: `AVS_CMD`, with both FIFOs full. Kind: one command write more than the command FIFO holds. Expected response: the write is refused, with `READBACK_FIFO_FULL`, `CMD_FIFO_FULL` and `CMD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` set. Then unmask each FIFO interrupt on its own and drain.
. Error injection. Point: the readback FIFO, prefilled to one slot short, and the sdata responder. Kind: a pair of commands with the first answered unavailable under a retry budget of 1; the second's reply waits behind the retry and meets a full FIFO. Expected response: `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT` set, with the waiting reply the one dropped. Unmask the overflow interrupt on its own, and drain.
. Write the divider defaults as real values, then change only the duty-cycle numerator to a quarter and back, measuring the clock at the pad.
. Error injection. Point: `AVS_READBACK`. Kind: a read with the readback FIFO empty, after a resync forced mid-traffic. Expected response: the read is refused on the bus. Before it, queue four commands, force a slave resync, queue four more, and drain.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-CRC-ONE-GOOD` |For every reply shape exactly one CRC code was accepted, and the other seven were delivered without updating `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME`
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-READBACK` |A good reply reached `AVS_READBACK`, `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME` and `AVS_SLAVE_STATUS` unchanged
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-RETRY-CODES` |Acknowledge 1 exhausted a budget of 2 with three identical subframes and `MAX_RETRIES_ATTEMPTED_INT`; acknowledge 2 then good cost one retry
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-NO-RETRY` |Acknowledge 3 was delivered with no retry, and a frame-not-valid reply raised `SLAVE_UNRESPONSIVE_INT`
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-BUFFERED` |A reply that waited behind a retry was delivered after it: as good when good, and unretried once the budget was cleared
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-STALL` |A full readback FIFO held back further commands, and after a forced resync and a pop every command completed intact
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-INTERRUPT` |sdata low while idle raised `AVS_SLAVE_ISSUED_INTERRUPT` as the only unmasked source, and it cleared
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-RB-OVERFLOW` |A reply that waited behind a retry met a full readback FIFO and raised `READBACK_OVERFLOW_INT`; the line followed the mask for that source alone, and the waiting reply was the one dropped
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-NUMERATOR` |With only the duty-cycle numerator changing, the AVS clock went to 25% high and back to 50%
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-INTERRUPT-LAUNCH` |A command queued during a slave interrupt, with sdata still low, launched and read back its reply intact
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-MASKS` |With both FIFOs full and one command refused, three FIFO interrupts were set; the interrupt line followed the mask for each alone, and every reply drained
|`CHK-AVS-SLAVE-RESYNC-BUSY` |A resync forced mid-traffic left every command answered intact, and an empty readback read was refused
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all twelve checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: No document in this tree gives the CRC-3 polynomial, so each reply shape is sent once
with each of the eight CRC codes and exactly one of them must be accepted.

'''''

[[sec-260-smc_output_remap_window_test]]
===== 260 `smc_output_remap_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_output_remap_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN for the remap registers and JTAG ingress for the traffic); the SYS_OUT responder's memory

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Outbound words through the M-mode and hypervisor remap windows, at both their LOCAL_BASE and GLOBAL_BASE copies, land in SYS_OUT memory where the programmed entry puts them.

*Test Coverage*:

* The output fabric sends an outbound access in the M-mode or hypervisor window to that window's remap table and passes everything else through. Each window is decoded at `LOCAL_BASE` and at `GLOBAL_BASE` plus its offset. The offset is the generated `SMC_TOP_MMODE_REGION_BASE_ADDR` or `SMC_TOP_XVISOR_REGION_BASE_ADDR` less the register window base, and the size is `*_REGION_SIZE`. With the reset bases, the local copies sit just above the SMC's 16 MB aperture, so an inbound master that addresses them is sent out. No other leaf sends anything there: the remap-table leaves write the tables but run no traffic through them.
* `output_remap.rdl`: when an entry's `valid` bit is set, its `offset` replaces the upper bits of the address; the entry is selected by the access's 1 MB slot within its window, and the low 20 bits are kept. When `valid` is clear the address passes through unchanged. The leaf programs M-mode entries 0 and 1 and hypervisor entry 0 with distinct offsets in SYS_OUT memory and `valid` set, and M-mode entry 2 with an offset and `valid` clear, reading each entry's reset first.
* Seven words go out over the JTAG ingress: through the M-mode window's local copy in slots 0, 1 and 2 and its global copy, through the hypervisor window's local and global copies, and to one address just past the hypervisor window. Each must land in the responder's memory at the address the entry predicts, and the window address itself must keep its sentinel. The slot-2 word and the address past the window must land unremapped, and entry 2's offset target must keep its sentinel. Each word must read back through the same window. The entries are restored and read back.

* **Source-ID matching in the outbound filter.** `fabric.adoc` ("SMC Source ID by Traffic Path", and the output-fabric figure `assets/smc-output-fabric.svg`) has the M-mode output remap set the AxUSER source ID to `MMODE_ID` (0xC) and the Xvisor remap set it to `OTHER_ID` (0); the leaf carries both values as its own constants. `filter_ctrl.rdl` makes a `src_id` of 0 the wildcard, so only `MMODE_ID` can be matched.
** While the words go out, outbound filter entry 0 allows reads and writes to the M-mode targets for source `MMODE_ID`.
** Entry 1 covers the hypervisor target for the same source and allows nothing. The hypervisor words must still land, which they can only do if entry 1 does not match `OTHER_ID`.
** Entry 0 is then re-armed to deny the M-mode targets for `MMODE_ID` and one more M-mode word is written through the window: it must be refused with DECERR (`fabric.adoc`: a matching deny entry routes the transaction to an error slave that returns a decode error) and its SYS_OUT target must keep its sentinel, which only a path carrying exactly `MMODE_ID` does.
** Both entries are read at their RDL reset first and restored to it afterwards.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_output_remap_window_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OUTPUT-REMAP-WINDOWS` |All seven words landed in SYS_OUT memory at the predicted address and nowhere else, each read back through the window it was written through, and the M-mode word written once entry 0 denied source `MMODE_ID` was refused with DECERR and left its target untouched
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-280-smc_i2c_event_retain_test]]
===== 280 `smc_i2c_event_retain_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_event_retain_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the external controller for the target leg; observation on `INTR_STATE`, `TARGET_EVENTS`, `SMBUS_CTRL` and `TARGET_NACK_COUNT`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: I2C0 event and counter fields held to what `i2c.rdl` says a write may and may not do to them. Leaves that raise these events clear them at once, so for most of them no other leaf makes the write that must not clear a set bit.

*Test Coverage*:

* Six `INTR_STATE` event bits no other leaf holds across a write: `RX_OVERFLOW`, `SDA_UNSTABLE`, `UNEXP_STOP`, `SMBALERT`, `CONTROLLER_RX_FIFO_ERROR` and `TARGET_RX_FIFO_ERROR`. Each is forced through `INTR_TEST` (`sw = w`, `singlepulse`).
** A word of zeros written over `INTR_STATE` must leave the bit set.
** Its own written one must clear it, with every other bit unchanged.
* `TARGET_EVENTS.START_DETECT` and `STOP_DETECT`, set by a transfer to the enabled target. A word of zeros must leave both set, and each must clear on its own written one while the other stays.
* `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` (`hwclr`: "clears itself when the controller addresses this target"). A write of the bit over itself must leave it set, and it must read clear after the transfer that addresses the target.
* `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` (`sw = rw`, `rclr`). A written value must read back once and then read zero.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. For each of the six bits: force it through `INTR_TEST`, write zeros to `INTR_STATE`, then write its one.
. Write `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` and read it twice.
. Enable the target, set `SMBALERT` twice, write one byte from the external controller, then check `SMBALERT` and clear the start and stop flags one at a time.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-INTR-STATE-RETAIN` |Each of the six forced bits survived a word of zeros and cleared on its own written one, with every other bit unchanged
|`CHK-I2C-NACK-COUNT-WRITE` |`TARGET_NACK_COUNT` read the written value once and zero on the read after
|`CHK-I2C-TARGET-EVENTS-CLEAR` |The start and stop flags survived a word of zeros and each cleared on its own written one while the other stayed
|`CHK-I2C-SMBALERT-HWCLR` |`SMBALERT` stayed set when written over itself and cleared when the target was addressed
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-281-smc_uart_thr_paths_test]]
===== 281 `smc_uart_thr_paths_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_thr_paths_test`

*BFM / Model*: UART0 in `MCR.LOOP`, so each character comes back through its own receiver and no pad carries it; observation on `LSR`, `IIR` and `RBR`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: UART0 transmit-holding and receive paths that only unusual programming reaches. Every other UART leaf sets a non-zero divisor before writing `THR`, writes whole words, and uses a documented trigger level.

*Test Coverage*:

* A character written with the divisor latches at 0. The baud generator does not run, so the character must wait in `THR`, with `LSR.THRE` clear and nothing received.
** A second write while it waits finds `THR` occupied.
** Once the divisor is programmed, exactly one character must arrive. Which one is recorded, because no document says whether the second write replaces the first or is dropped; on this RTL the first is kept.
** The FIFOs are off for this leg, with `FCR.DMA_MODE_SELECT` set.
* A byte write that enables only the lane above `THR`'s character carries no character. Nothing may be transmitted, and a following whole write must be.
* A character left unread in `RBR` with the FIFOs off for four times the reception timeout. It must read back intact, and what `IIR` reports is recorded.
* Trigger code 0xC (`ECR.RCVR_TRIGGER_MS2B` = 3, `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER` = 0), past the last level `uart_16550_main.rdl` lists. It is programmed with the FIFOs on; a character must be received intact, and what `IIR` shows is recorded.
* The divisor is taken to 0 part-way through a character, which stops the baud generator under the transmitter. What `LSR` then shows and how much of the cut character arrives are recorded; once the divisor is restored, a following character must read back intact.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Error injection. Point: the UART0 divisor latches and `THR`. Kind: the divisor at 0 with the FIFOs off (the baud generator does not run), then two `THR` writes, the second finding `THR` occupied. Expected response: the character waits in `THR` with `LSR.THRE` clear and nothing received; once the divisor is set, exactly one character arrives. Loop UART0 back first.
. With the FIFOs on, write the lane above `THR`, then write `THR` whole.
. With the FIFOs off, receive a character and leave it unread before reading `IIR` and `RBR`.
. Error injection. Point: `ECR.RCVR_TRIGGER_MS2B` and `FCR.RCVR_TRIGGER`. Kind: trigger code 0xC, past the last level the register description lists, with the FIFOs on. Expected response: a character received intact, with what `IIR` shows recorded. Read `IIR` and `RBR`.
. Error injection. Point: the divisor latches, under a character in flight at a slow divisor. Kind: the divisor taken to 0 part-way through the character, stopping the baud generator under the transmitter, then restored. Expected response: after the restore and a drain, a following character reads back intact; what `LSR` showed and how much of the cut character arrived are recorded.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-THR-HOLD` |With the divisor at 0 the character waited in `THR`, nothing was received, and exactly one of the two written characters arrived once the divisor was set
|`CHK-UART-THR-LANE` |A write to the lane above `THR`'s character transmitted nothing, and the whole write after it arrived
|`CHK-UART-RBR-PARKED` |A character left unread with the FIFOs off, and one received with trigger code 0xC, both read back intact, with `IIR` recorded for each
|`CHK-UART-TX-CUT` |After a character was cut off by the divisor going to 0, the next character read back intact
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: Which of the two characters written with the divisor at 0 arrives is recorded,
because no document says whether the second write replaces the first or is dropped; on this RTL the
first is kept. What `IIR` reports for a character left unread with the FIFOs off and for one
received with trigger code 0xC is recorded, not compared. What `LSR` shows and how much of the cut
character arrives after the divisor goes to 0 are recorded.

'''''

[[sec-282-smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test]]
===== 282 `smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test`
