*BFM / Model*: output-fabric responder with `tb_output_axi_resp_hold` for the starved leg; the log engine on UART wrapper 0 fetches from an address inside the I2C0 instance's stride but past its `SIZE`, which the I2C wrapper refuses (the decode `smc_deadspace_decode_test` holds it to); observation on `INTR_STATUS` and `tb_uart_irq_combined[0]`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Make a log fetch come back with an error. The other log-engine leaves raise `LOG_FETCH_ERR` only through `INTR_TEST`.

*Test Coverage*:

* `LOG_REGION_ADDR` points at the refusing address and one `LOG_CTRL` element asks for a log. `INTR_STATUS.LOG_FETCH_ERR` must set and `LOG_WRITE_ERR` must not.
* `INTR_ENABLE.LOG_FETCH_ERR` is set. The wrapper's interrupt line must be low before the error and high after it. The status bit must then clear on its written one, and the line must drop. The line also carries the 16550's interrupt, so the UART is set up with its interrupts disabled.
* The error does not stop the engine: the fetched word is still handed to the write side and the log runs to its end, and only then does the engine clear the element's `LOG_CTRL` length, which retires its arbiter request. The leaf waits for that hardware clear, reads all eight bytes of the log back from the looped-back UART (`LSR.TEMT` reports the transmitter empty before the receiver has the last byte, so the drain runs on the count and then requires the transmitter idle), and only then disables the engine. Disabling the engine or zeroing the length first withdraws a request the arbiter has not granted, which the vendored `prim_arbiter_tree` forbids (`ReqStaysHighUntilGranted0_M` and `LockArbDecision_A`, `prim_arbiter_tree.sv`); a simulator that evaluates those assertions fails the run.
* A starved write side. The engine fetches one word at a time into a FIFO that runs ahead of the UART, so from local memory the next word is always waiting when a word's last byte leaves. A sixteen-byte log is placed in the output-fabric window, and the output responder's R channel is held once the first fetch has returned. The engine writes that word's eight bytes and then waits for a word its FIFO does not have. When all eight bytes have come back through the loopback, exactly one fetch may have returned. The hold is then released, and all sixteen bytes must arrive in order with no error status.
* `LOG_WRITE_ERR` has no bus to come from. The engine's write port reaches only its own wrapper's UART register blocks (`uart_log_engine_wrap.sv`), which answer every address without error. Its status is set instead through `INTR_TEST` (`sw = w`, `singlepulse`), with only `INTR_ENABLE.LOG_WRITE_ERR` set. The status must set alone, the interrupt line must rise, and the written one must clear the status and drop the line.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Set up UART0 as the transfer leaf does, and point the engine's region at the refusing address.
. Error injection. Point: the log engine's fetch port, with `LOG_REGION_ADDR` at the refusing address of step 1. Kind: one `LOG_CTRL` element asking for a log from an address the I2C wrapper refuses. Expected response: `INTR_STATUS.LOG_FETCH_ERR` set, `LOG_WRITE_ERR` not set, and the wrapper's interrupt line low before the error and high after it.
. Wait for `LOG_CTRL[0]` to clear, read the eight bytes back from the UART, stop the engine, and clear the status.
. Error injection. Point: the output-fabric responder's R channel (`tb_output_axi_resp_hold`). Kind: the R channel held once the first fetch of a sixteen-byte log from the output-fabric window has returned, starving the engine's write side. Expected response: the first word's eight bytes come back through the loopback with exactly one fetch returned, and after the release all sixteen bytes arrive in order with no error status. Open the outbound filter and preload two words in the window first; read eight bytes from the UART and check that one fetch returned, release the hold, read the other eight, and compare all sixteen.
. Error injection. Point: `INTR_TEST.LOG_WRITE_ERR`, with only `INTR_ENABLE.LOG_WRITE_ERR` set. Kind: the write-error status forced through `INTR_TEST`; the engine's write port has no bus that can refuse it. Expected response: the status sets alone, the line rises, and the written one clears the status and drops the line.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-FETCH-ERR` |A refused fetch set `LOG_FETCH_ERR` alone and raised the interrupt line with the interrupt enabled; the engine still finished the log, all eight bytes of the errored word reaching the looped-back UART, and cleared `LOG_CTRL[0]`, and the status cleared on its written one with the line dropping
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-STARVED-FETCH` |With the second fetch held until the first word's bytes had left, a sixteen-byte log from the output-fabric window still reached the UART complete and in order, with no error status
|`CHK-LOG-ENGINE-WRITE-ERR-TEST` |`INTR_TEST.LOG_WRITE_ERR` set the write status alone, which raised the line with only its interrupt enabled; its written one cleared it and the line dropped
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every checker holds after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: `LOG_WRITE_ERR` has no bus to come from, since the engine's write port reaches only
its own wrapper's UART register blocks, which answer every address without error; its status is set
through `INTR_TEST` instead.

'''''

[[sec-283-smc_octs_credit_expired_test]]
===== 283 `smc_octs_credit_expired_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_octs_credit_expired_test`

*BFM / Model*: the OCTS sync BFM on the sync and credit pads, with the chiplet strapped SECONDARY; observation on `CREDIT_EXPIRED` and `STATUS`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: `system_timer_octs.rdl` describes `CREDIT_EXPIRED.MAX_CYCLES_EXPIRED` as the largest number of cycles since a count credit was due, on a secondary. It says: "To reset the value of this register, write anything to it." No other leaf writes it.

*Test Coverage*:

* The timer is strapped SECONDARY and given a sync and two credits, as `smc_octs_dual_sync_test` does, then no more credits. `CREDIT_EXPIRED` must grow while the credits stay away.
* One late credit restarts the live count, and the register must keep its maximum.
* A write must then bring the register back below that maximum.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Strap SECONDARY, configure the timer, and inject a sync and two credits.
. Error injection. Point: the credit pad of the OCTS sync BFM. Kind: credits withheld after the sync and two credits. Expected response: `CREDIT_EXPIRED` grows between two reads with no credit in between.
. Inject one credit, read it again, write it, and read it once more.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCTS-CREDIT-EXPIRED` |`CREDIT_EXPIRED` grew while starved, held its maximum through a late credit, and dropped below it on a write
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-284-smc_efuse_guard_target_test]]
===== 284 `smc_efuse_guard_target_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_efuse_guard_target_test`

*BFM / Model*: `efuse_bank_model` answers the bank, loaded from the default eFuse image; observation on `EFUSE_READ_CTRL`, `EFUSE_READ_INTERFACE_READ_DATA`, `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL` and `EFUSE_INTERFACE_CTRL_STATUS`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/efuse.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `efuse`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The eFuse guard applying a field's hardware locks to the read and program interfaces. Every other leaf that uses those interfaces targets bit 0, which lies in `LOCKS` itself, a field whose locks the guard never applies. So no other leaf makes the guard look up a target and find a field.

*Test Coverage*:

* The default image leaves every SPARE word at zero, so a read of one could not tell a disclosed word from a withheld one. One bit of SPARE[6] is first set by an unlocked read-back program.
** The program must complete without error.
** A read of the word through the read interface must then return the asset word with that bit set.
* SPARE[6]'s read lock is set through `LOCKS`, which is write-1-to-set. The same read must complete with `READ_STATUS` set and `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` raised, and must not return the word.
* SPARE[7]'s write lock is set, and a read-back program of a bit the asset holds at 0 is issued.
** It must complete with `PROGRAM_STATUS` set and `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` raised.
** A read of the word afterwards must still return the asset value.
* A program of one SPARE[8] bit with `EFUSE_PROGRAM_CTRL.EFUSE_PROGRAM_READ_BACK` clear, a plain program. The leaf does not trust the command.
** The program must complete without error.
** A read of the word through the read interface must show the bit burnt.
** A read-back program of the same bit must find it set.
* The two locks hold until reset and are left set.
* With `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` still set, which "must be cleared by writing 1" (`efuse_interface_ctrl.rdl`), a read and a program of SPARE[9] must both be refused, and the program must not burn.
* Timeouts configured but not reached. A read-back program with the program timeout enabled at its reset length, and another with the timeout disabled and its length 0, must both complete. A program with no data bit must fail. A read with the read timeout disabled at length 0 must return exactly the two bits programmed.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Wait for sense, check that the two locks are clear, and clear `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR`.
. Error injection. Point: the read interface, with SPARE[6]'s read lock set through `LOCKS`. Kind: a read of a read-locked word. Expected response: the read completes with `READ_STATUS` set and `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` raised, and does not return the word. Before the lock: program one bit of SPARE[6] with read-back and read the word.
. Error injection. Point: the program interface, with SPARE[7]'s write lock set. Kind: a read-back program of a bit the asset holds at 0 in a write-locked field. Expected response: `PROGRAM_STATUS` set and `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` raised, and a read of the word afterwards still returns the asset value.
. Program one SPARE[8] bit without read-back, read the word, and program the same bit with read-back.
. Error injection. Point: both interfaces, with `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` still set from the locked read. Kind: a read and a program of SPARE[9] issued before the error is cleared. Expected response: both refused, and the program does not burn.
. Error injection. Point: the program interface. Kind: a program with no data bit. Expected response: the program fails. Also program two SPARE[9] bits under the two timeout settings, which must both complete, and read the word with the read timeout disabled at length 0.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|`CHK-EFUSE-PROGRAM-NO-READBACK` |A program without read-back completed, the read interface then showed the bit burnt, and a read-back program of the same bit found it set
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-EFUSE-GUARD-READ-TARGET` |An unlocked read of a SPARE word returned the value just programmed; with its read lock set the read failed with `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` and did not return it
|`CHK-EFUSE-GUARD-PROGRAM-TARGET` |A program of a write-locked SPARE field failed with `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR`, and the word still read its asset value
|`CHK-EFUSE-QUIET-TIMEOUTS` |Requests under `EFUSE_REQ_ERROR` were refused, programs completed under an enabled and a disabled timeout, a no-data program failed, and the word held exactly the two programmed bits
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-261-smc_regblock_partial_write_test]]
===== 261 `smc_regblock_partial_write_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_regblock_partial_write_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/register.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `register`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the cells are the stated reset values and access classes of
the register description.

*Objective*: Byte writes that must hold a set field on another lane, W1C events that must survive a write of zero, and writes of zero into a trigger and two status registers.

*Test Coverage*:

* A PeakRDL field updates as `(value & ~biten) | (data & biten)`, and a W1C field clears as `value & ~(data & biten)`. In these 32-bit blocks, the half of each term that keeps a set field is driven by no other leaf: a one held while a write strobes other lanes, or a W1C one held across a write that carries a zero. Every field and mask comes from the block's generated header.
* **Held across a byte write on another lane.** `I2C_CTRL.SMBUS_EN` on all three instances is set by a byte write to its own lane and must hold across a byte write to lane 0. I2C0 `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` must hold across a byte write to lane 1, which has no field. Each is read back after every step and restored.
* **W1C held across a zero, then cleared.** Six I2C0 `INTR_STATE` events (`RX_OVERFLOW`, `SDA_UNSTABLE`, `UNEXP_STOP`, `SMBALERT`, `CONTROLLER_RX_FIFO_ERROR`, `TARGET_RX_FIFO_ERROR`) and log-engine `INTR_STATUS.LOG_FETCH_ERR` are raised through `INTR_TEST`. Each must survive a full write of zero and clear on a write of one. Anything already latched, such as I2C0's `SMBALERT` event, which follows the SMBALERT output driven above, is cleared first.
* **Zero into a trigger or a status.** Full writes of zero to log-engine `INTR_TEST`, OCTS `TIMER_START` (`singlepulse`) and telemetry-receiver `INTR_STATUS` must leave each reading what it read before.
* **Writes whose only effect is documented.** OCTS `CREDIT_EXPIRED` is an external register that `system_timer_octs.rdl` resets on any write, so a write must leave it reading 0. I2C0 `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` is `rclr` and holds 0 at idle, so a read returns 0.
* **A flush held across a partial write.** Telemetry-receiver `CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH` is `hwclr` and clears on the ATB flush handshake, AFREADY with AFVALID. With receiver 0's AFREADY held low by the bench, the flush stays set, so a byte write to lane 0 must leave it set, and so must a full-word write of 1 to it. Raising AFREADY then clears it.
* **A byte write at FCR+1.** `uart_16550.sv` sends a write to the write-only block only when its address is exactly THR or FCR. A byte write at FCR+1 therefore reaches the main block, where it decodes at address 8, the read-only IIR word. `IIR` must read the same afterwards, with the FIFOs still off.
* **Rows left, and why.** A one on a lane whose strobe is off cannot come from SEP_IN, whose master zero-fills unstrobed lanes.
** It cannot come from the CPU into these 32-bit blocks either. A firmware byte store of `0xFF` into the empty top byte of I2C0 `INTR_STATE` reaches `i2c_reg` with only the strobed lane carrying data (`wdata 0xFF000000`, `wstrb 0x8`), so the path from the cluster zeroes the other lanes. The replication that reaches the 64-bit blocks (`smc_fw_narrow_store_lane_test`) does not reach the 32-bit ones. The `(data & biten)` "1 0" rows of `i2c_reg` (`INTR_STATE`, `CONTROLLER_EVENTS`, `TARGET_EVENTS`), `log_engine_reg` and `telemetry_receiver_reg` are therefore unreachable in this design.
** In the 64-bit blocks the firmware leaf takes the safe lanes. The rest carry a hazard:
** `WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET` (`singlepulse` core resets);
** `FILTER_CONFIG` (write-once `locked`, or a live window);
** zeroer `INT_EN` (any write starts a job);
** `TARGET_EVENTS.START_DETECT` and `STOP_DETECT` cleared while set, which need target bus traffic.
* **FILTER_CONFIG lock.** Each filter port holds the next write AW until the previous write's B is accepted, so a write queued behind the locking write is selected after `locked` is set. `smc_filter_lock_window_test` checks both banks.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_regblock_partial_write_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-DOCUMENTED-WRITE` |A write reset OCTS `CREDIT_EXPIRED` to 0; I2C0 `TARGET_NACK_COUNT` read 0 at idle; telemetry `TX_FLUSH` held across a lane-0 byte write and a full-word rewrite of 1 while AFREADY was low and cleared once it rose; a byte write at UART0 FCR+1 left `IIR` unchanged
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-PARTIAL-HOLD` |`SMBUS_EN` on the three `I2C_CTRL` instances and I2C0 `SMBUS_CTRL.SMBALERT` read back set after a byte write to another lane, and each was restored and read back
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-W1C-HOLD` |The six I2C0 events and `LOG_FETCH_ERR`, raised through `INTR_TEST`, read back set after a write of zero and clear after a write of one
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-ZERO-WRITE` |Writes of zero to log-engine `INTR_TEST`, OCTS `TIMER_START` and telemetry `INTR_STATUS` left each reading what it read before
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The `(data & biten)` "1 0" rows of the 32-bit blocks (`i2c_reg` `INTR_STATE`,
`CONTROLLER_EVENTS` and `TARGET_EVENTS`, `log_engine_reg`, `telemetry_receiver_reg`) are unreachable
in this design, because neither SEP_IN nor the CPU path puts a one on a lane whose strobe is off. In
the 64-bit blocks the firmware leaf takes the safe lanes and the hazardous rows are left:
`WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET`, `FILTER_CONFIG`, zeroer `INT_EN`, and `TARGET_EVENTS.START_DETECT` and
`STOP_DETECT` cleared while set. The `FILTER_CONFIG` lock is checked by
`smc_filter_lock_window_test`.

'''''

[[sec-262-smc_cpu_reset_pulse_test]]
===== 262 `smc_cpu_reset_pulse_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_reset_pulse_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: A SEP_IN core-reset pulse on core 1, timed at the cluster boundary and run with core 1's level reset held, and a withheld level reset whose timeout fires in give-up mode.

*Test Coverage*:

* **Pulse.** `cpu_ctrl.rdl` gives each core a `RESET_CTRL.coreN_reset_pulse_start` field: a one there starts a reset pulse whose length comes from `CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT`, and `core_resets_done` reads low for the core while its pulse runs. Outside this leaf the firmware boot contract is the only writer. From SEP_IN, core 1 is pulsed with every level-reset field high, so the pending pulse and then the running pulse are each the only reset request. Core 1's `core_resets_done` bit must fall and come back, and the other cores' bits must stay high. `RESET_TIMEOUT` is set to force mode for this leg, as the boot contract does, so the pulse is applied whether or not the cluster drains.
* **Pulse width.** `CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT` is set to `pre_reset_count` 2 and `post_reset_count` 3, and core 1 is pulsed with every level-reset field high. `post_reset_count` gives the cycles, minus one, that the pulse holds the core in reset, so core 1's bit of `tb_cpu_core_resets_n`, sampled at every `clk_smc_i` edge, must read low for exactly one run of 4 cycles.
* **Pulse with the level reset held.** `core1_reset_n_n0_scan` is written 0 and core 1's cluster reset must assert. Core 1 is then pulsed. A 0 in `core1_reset_n_n0_scan` holds the core in reset for the whole pulse, so core 1's bit of `tb_cpu_core_resets_n` must read 0 at every `clk_smc_i` sample from the pulse write until `core_resets_done` returns, including the cycle where the pulse hands back to the level reset. The level is then released and core 1's reset must deassert.
* **Give-up timeout.** Core 1's level reset is requested with `RESET_TIMEOUT` at `timeout_value` 1 and `timeout_mode` 0, and must read `reset_timeout` 1. It is then released, and both status bits must clear. `RESET_TIMEOUT` and `CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT` are restored and read back.
* **Mode 0 applies the reset once the drain completes.** `cpu_ctrl.rdl` describes `timeout_mode` 0 as "give up and report error (stay withheld, do not apply)", while `smc_cpu_ctrl_wrap.sv` computes `withhold = pending & ~force_apply` with `pending = sw_reset_req & ~drained_i`, so once the drain completes the request is applied in either mode and `reset_applied` reads 1 beside `reset_timeout`. The leaf reports `reset_applied` and does not grade it.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_cpu_reset_pulse_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPU-RST-GIVEUP` |Core 1's level reset under `timeout_mode` 0 and `timeout_value` 1 read `reset_timeout` 1, and both status bits cleared after the release
|`CHK-CPU-RST-PULSE` |Core 1's `core_resets_done` bit fell and returned after the pulse write, with the other cores' bits high throughout
|`CHK-CPU-RST-PULSE-HELD` |Core 1's cluster reset read 0 at every `clk_smc_i` sample of a pulse run with `core1_reset_n_n0_scan` held 0
|`CHK-CPU-RST-PULSE-WIDTH` |With `post_reset_count` 3, core 1's cluster reset read low for one run of exactly 4 `clk_smc_i` cycles
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all four checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `reset`.

*Scope limit*: `reset_applied` under `timeout_mode` 0 is reported and not graded: the register
description says the request stays withheld, while the wrapper applies it once the drain completes.

'''''

[[sec-285-smc_i2c_bus_corners_test]]
===== 285 `smc_i2c_bus_corners_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_bus_corners_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads as the external controller; observation on `INTR_STATE`, `STATUS`, `ACQDATA`, the bus response to an undecoded address, and `DATA_CTRL` of the I2C0 SCL pad

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Five edges around the I2C0 target that the target leaves never reach.

*Test Coverage*:

* A STOP where a NACK belongs. `i2c.rdl` raises `INTR_STATE.UNEXP_STOP` "when the controller sends this target a STOP before this target NACKs".
** A read from the target whose controller sends the STOP in the byte's acknowledge slot, where the controller rather than the target owns SDA, must raise it.
** The same read with `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` cleared before the STOP, and the controller enabled so the bus monitor still sees it, must not raise it.
* A NACK request that does not apply. `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK` takes effect "when `STATUS.ACK_CTRL_STRETCH = 1`". With ACK Control Mode off, the target is made to stretch on a full acquisition FIFO, and `NACK` is written during that stretch. Every byte of the write must still be acknowledged and read out in order.
* SCL taken during the bus-free time. `TIMING4.T_BUF` is lengthened and SCL is pulled low inside the wait after a STOP. The target must still answer the next write.
* An access inside the I2C wrapper's window, above its last instance stride and below its control registers, belongs to no register map. A read and a write there must both be refused on the bus. The window extent, the instance strides and the control register base come from the generated address map, and the probe is asserted to lie inside the window.
* LSIO ownership withdrawn. `gpio_intf.rdl` sets `lsio_enable` "while `lsio_interface_select_i` is asserted and `lsio_disable` is clear".
** With I2C0 enabled, its SCL pad (`DATA_CTRL[37]`, the "I2C[0] SCL" row of the integrator pad table `doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`) must report `lsio_enable`.
** With `lsio_disable` set, `lsio_enable` must read clear, also with `lsio_select` forced.
** Clearing `lsio_disable` must restore the register.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Error injection. Point: the acknowledge slot of a read byte on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads. Kind: a STOP sent by the external controller where a NACK belongs. Expected response: `UNEXP_STOP` raised; repeated with `CTRL.ENABLETARGET` cleared before the STOP and the controller enabled, it is not raised. Enable I2C0 as a target and read one byte first.
. Error injection. Point: `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NACK`. Kind: a NACK written during a FIFO-full stretch with ACK Control Mode off, where it does not apply. Expected response: every byte of the write still acknowledged and read out in order. Write more bytes than the acquisition FIFO holds, then drain.
. Error injection. Point: the SCL line inside the bus-free time after a STOP, with a long `TIMING4.T_BUF`. Kind: SCL pulled low by the external controller inside the wait. Expected response: the target still answers the next write. Write one byte before the pull and another after.
. Error injection. Point: the address between the I2C wrapper's last instance stride and its control registers, inside the window but in no register map. Kind: a read and a write there. Expected response: both refused on the bus.
. Enable the controller and toggle `lsio_disable` and `lsio_select` on the SCL pad.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-UNEXP-STOP` |A STOP in a read byte's acknowledge slot raised `UNEXP_STOP`; with the target disabled first it did not
|`CHK-I2C-TGT-NACK-IGNORED` |`NACK` written during a FIFO-full stretch with ACK Control Mode off left every byte acknowledged and read out in order
|`CHK-I2C-BUS-FREE-SCL` |SCL pulled inside the bus-free time left the target answering the next write
|`CHK-I2C-WRAP-PAST-CTRL` |A read and a write inside the wrapper window, between its instances and its control registers, were refused
|`CHK-I2C-PAD-LSIO-DISABLE` |`lsio_disable` cleared `lsio_enable` on the SCL pad, also with `lsio_select` forced, and clearing it restored the register
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-286-smc_octs_primary_start_test]]
===== 286 `smc_octs_primary_start_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_octs_primary_start_test`

*BFM / Model*: none; the bench strap stays at PRIMARY; observation on `STATUS` and `TIMER_COUNT`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/power.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Start a PRIMARY OCTS timer that has never run. Every other OCTS leaf starts the timer only after a secondary phase has already enabled it.

*Test Coverage*:

* `CTRL` is written while the timer is idle with the setting it runs on: `CREDIT_VAL` 0xFF and `PULSE_WIDTH` 0xF0, which keeps the RDL's rule that the credit value exceed the pulse width. `STATUS.RUNNING` must read clear.
* `TIMER_PRESET` is 0. After `TIMER_START`, `STATUS.RUNNING` must set and `TIMER_COUNT` must advance.
* `TIMER_START` "asserts the sync_load signal", a pulse `PULSE_WIDTH` cycles long. A second start written while that pulse is still out must reload the preset. The count read right after it must be below the count read twice after the first start.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check `STATUS` is PRIMARY and idle, program `CTRL` and the preset to 0.
. Write `TIMER_START`, read the count twice, write `TIMER_START` again, read it, wait, and read it again.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCTS-PRIMARY-START` |A never-run PRIMARY timer started from 0 with `RUNNING` set, and a second start during its sync pulse reloaded the count
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-287-smc_decode_hole_test]]
===== 287 `smc_decode_hole_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_decode_hole_test`

*BFM / Model*: none; system AXI accesses with their responses checked

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `decode`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Write and read the unmapped tail of three block apertures. The RDL address map reserves misc_wrap a 2 KiB aperture, the GPIO interfaces 4 KiB and the DMA controller 512 B (`ocah_aperture_size`), each with a smaller decoded extent. The crossbars decode each block to its extent, so an address in the tail reaches no block and the fabric's error slave answers it with the response the RDL gives an access past the decoded extent (`ocah_past_extent_resp`: a DECERR read for all three).

*Test Coverage*:

* Each probe is the word halfway between the end of the block's decoded extent (`SIZE` or `TOTAL_SIZE` from the generated `smc_addr.h`) and the end of its aperture (the generated memory map as data, `regs/gen/py/smc_memory_map.py`), and is checked to lie in no unit's decoded extent.
* Misc: 0xC000_2D04, past `NDM_RESET` ending at 0xC000_2A0C, inside the aperture ending 0xC000_3000. The live register is `SCRATCH_COLD` 0.
* GPIO: 0xC000_3A08, past the 65th GPIO interface ending at 0xC000_3410, inside the aperture ending 0xC000_4000. The live register is `DATA_CTRL` of GPIO 64.
* DMA: 0xC003_819C, past the DMA's 312 B decoded extent ending at 0xC003_8138, inside the aperture ending 0xC003_8200. The live register is the DMA's `DST_ADDRESS_LO`.
* For each, the live register is seeded and read back first, so a stray write can show. The unmapped read must answer DECERR and the unmapped write must be refused with an error response (the AXI-Lite peripheral and internal crossbars answer SLVERR to a write, the local crossbar DECERR); the write must leave the seed in place, and the read must not return it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. For each aperture: read the live register, seed it, and read the seed back.
. Error injection. Point: the unmapped word halfway between the block's decoded extent and the end of its aperture. Kind: a write of a payload there, then a read of it. Expected response: the read answers DECERR, the write is refused with an error response, the live register keeps its seed and the read does not return it.
. Require the unmapped read to answer DECERR and the write to be refused, the live register to still hold the seed and the unmapped read not to return it, then restore the live register.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DECODE-HOLE-MISC` |An unmapped write and read in the misc aperture's tail were refused (the read with DECERR), left `SCRATCH_COLD` 0 holding its seed and did not read it back
|`CHK-DECODE-HOLE-GPIO` |An unmapped write and read past the last GPIO interface were refused (the read with DECERR), left `DATA_CTRL` of GPIO 64 holding its seed and did not read it back
|`CHK-DECODE-HOLE-DATA_ACCEL` |An unmapped write and read past the DMA's decoded extent were refused (the read with DECERR), left the DMA's `DST_ADDRESS_LO` holding its seed and did not read it back
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-288-smc_zeroer_size_corners_test]]
===== 288 `smc_zeroer_size_corners_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_zeroer_size_corners_test`

*BFM / Model*: output-fabric responder and its memory model; observation on the responder's write-transaction counter and on readbacks through the JTAG AXI path

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `zeroer`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Run a zeroer job of zero bytes, and one that starts four bytes below a 4 KB boundary and ends mid-word. Every other zeroer leaf starts on a word, ends on a word and stays inside one page.

*Test Coverage*:

* `SIZE` is "Size in bytes of zeros to write". With `SIZE` at 0 the trigger write to `CTRL_STATUS` must write nothing: the poisoned word at `DEST_ADDR` keeps its poison, and across that trigger and an eight-byte job started after it the responder books exactly one write transaction.
* `DEST_ADDR` is a byte address, and `zeroer.adoc` lists unaligned starts and fragmentation at page boundaries. A sixteen-byte job from four bytes below a page boundary must zero the upper half of the word below the boundary, the word at it and the lower half of the word above, leave the other halves and the guard words on either side poisoned, and take at least two write transactions, since no AXI burst may cross a 4 KB boundary.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Open the output fabric filters and poison the destination words.
. Program `SIZE` 0, trigger, wait for `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` at 0, then run an eight-byte job at another poisoned word and count the responder's write transactions across both.
. Poison the three words around a page boundary and a guard word either side, run the sixteen-byte job from `page - 4`, and compare each word against its poison with the job's bytes cleared.
. Clear `SIZE` and `DEST_ADDR`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ZEROER-EMPTY-JOB` |A trigger with `SIZE` 0 left its destination poisoned, and the responder booked one write transaction across it and the eight-byte job after it
|`CHK-ZEROER-PAGE-CROSS` |A sixteen-byte job from four bytes below a page boundary zeroed exactly its bytes in at least two write transactions, with the guard words intact
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-289-smc_hang_detector_disable_test]]
===== 289 `smc_hang_detector_disable_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_hang_detector_disable_test`

*BFM / Model*: `tb_sep_axi_r_hold` holds a SEP_IN read at its R channel; the JTAG AXI master carries the control writes made during the stall; observation on `tb_axi_hang_irq_sep`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/irq.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `irq`, `hang`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Clear the SEP hang detector's `enable` while the detector has fired, and drive `irq_test` with `enable` clear. The other hang detector leaves clear `enable` only while the detector is quiet, and drive `irq_test` only with `enable` set.

*Test Coverage*:

* `HANG_DET_CTRL.enable`: "When 0, the counter reloads from the threshold and irq_o is forced low." With threshold 0x10 and a read held, the SEP interrupt fires. `enable` is then cleared with `irq_en` kept, and the interrupt has to read low at once and stay low for four thresholds while the read is still held.
* `irq_test` is "Gated by enable and irq_en". With `irq_en` and `irq_test` set and `enable` clear, the interrupt has to stay low for four thresholds. Setting `enable` as well has to raise it, and clearing the control has to drop it.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Disarm the SYS and DATA detectors. Program the SEP threshold to 0x10 and arm the detector.
. Error injection. Point: the R channel of a SEP_IN read (`tb_sep_axi_r_hold`). Kind: the read held past the SEP detector's threshold of 0x10. Expected response: the SEP interrupt fires; once `irq_en` alone is written through JTAG with the read still held, the interrupt reads low at once and stays low throughout the watch window. Read the control back, then release the read.
. Write `irq_en | irq_test` and require the interrupt low. Write `enable | irq_en | irq_test` and require it high, then clear the control and require it low.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-HANG-DISABLE-FIRED` |Clearing `enable` on a fired SEP detector, with the read still held, dropped its interrupt and kept it low
|`CHK-HANG-DISABLE-STATUS` |With `enable` cleared and the read still held, every `HANG_DET_*_CTRL.irq` reads 0
|`CHK-HANG-TEST-GATED` |`irq_test` with `enable` clear left the interrupt low, and setting `enable` raised it
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all three checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-290-smc_cpu_uncore_reset_test]]
===== 290 `smc_cpu_uncore_reset_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_cpu_uncore_reset_test`

*BFM / Model*: none; observation on `RESET_CTRL` and `RESET_TIMEOUT`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/reset.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`, `reset`;
`run_modes` `smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `reset`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Request the CPU cluster's uncore reset on its own with every core released. The other CPU reset leaves request core level resets and core pulses, never the uncore reset alone.

*Test Coverage*:

* `RESET_CTRL.uncore_reset_n_n0_scan` is the uncore's active-low reset. `RESET_TIMEOUT.reset_applied` is set once a software reset request "has been applied either after drain completes or after a force-mode timeout". With `RESET_TIMEOUT` in force mode after 32 cycles, writing the uncore reset low with every core field high has to set `reset_applied`.
* Writing the uncore reset high again removes the only request, so `reset_applied` has to clear and `reset_timeout` has to read clear.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Check that `RESET_CTRL` has the uncore and every core released and that no reset is applied.
. Program `RESET_TIMEOUT` to force mode after 32 cycles. Write the uncore reset low, read it back, and poll for `reset_applied`.
. Write the uncore reset high and poll for `reset_applied` clear. Restore `RESET_TIMEOUT` and read back both registers.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-CPU-UNCORE-RESET` |The uncore reset held alone set `reset_applied`, and releasing it cleared `reset_applied` and `reset_timeout`
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-291-smc_dma_backpressure_test]]
===== 291 `smc_dma_backpressure_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_dma_backpressure_test`

*BFM / Model*: output-fabric responder with `tb_output_axi_resp_hold` and its one-shot read-error injection; DMA sources in scratchpad memory

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/dma.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `dma`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Queue DMA descriptors behind a destination that stops answering, and read a burst the responder errors part-way through. The other DMA leaves launch one descriptor of at most eight bytes and wait for it, so the DMA never has more than one burst in flight, never reads more than one beat per burst, and never has a descriptor waiting behind another.

*Test Coverage*:

* Every destination is in the output-fabric window, and the responder's R and B channels are held before the first launch, so the DMA's writes go unanswered, it runs out of write credit, and later descriptors wait in the frontend's queue.
* The queue holds a 64-byte copy to a destination four bytes into a word (a multi-beat read and partial first and last write beats), a two-dimensional copy of forty eight-byte rows, a zero-length descriptor, a 64-byte copy whose source crosses a 4 KB boundary and whose destination does not, one whose destination crosses and whose source does not, and further 64-byte copies. The two page-crossing copies set `CONFIG.DECOUPLE_RW`, so each side is split at its own boundary rather than both at the nearer one.
* `dma_ctrl.rdl` gives `STATUS.BUSY[7:0]` as readiness to accept another command. Descriptors are launched until it reads clear, one more is launched, and the hold is released once that launch's read is accepted on SEP_IN.
* `NEXT_ID` must hand out consecutive ids starting one past `DONE`, `DONE` must reach the last one, and every destination must hold exactly its source bytes, with the four bytes either side keeping their poison.
* A 64-byte read from the output-fabric window is answered SLVERR on its third beat. The DMA has no error handling configured, so the transfer must still complete, exactly one SLVERR beat must be seen on SYS_OUT, and the beats answered OKAY must arrive intact. The errored beat's destination bytes are recorded.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Open the inbound and outbound filters. Fill every source span with a pattern and every destination span, plus a word either side, with poison.
. Error injection. Point: the output-fabric responder's R and B channels (`tb_output_axi_resp_hold`). Kind: both channels held before the first launch; the DMA's writes go unanswered and it runs out of write credit. Expected response: later descriptors wait in the frontend's queue until `STATUS.BUSY` reports no readiness. Program and launch descriptors, reading `STATUS` after each program, until it reports no readiness.
. Launch the refused descriptor, release the hold when its read is accepted on SEP_IN, wait for `DONE` to reach the last id, and compare every destination.
. Error injection. Point: the output-fabric responder's one-shot read-error injection, on the third beat of a 64-byte source read. Kind: SLVERR on that beat. Expected response: the transfer still completes with no error handling configured, exactly one SLVERR beat is seen on SYS_OUT, and the beats answered OKAY arrive intact. Copy the source to scratchpad memory and compare the other beats.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-DMA-BACKPRESSURE` |Descriptors queued behind held destination responses until `STATUS.BUSY` reported no readiness all completed with consecutive ids, and every destination held exactly its source bytes with its neighbours untouched
|`CHK-DMA-READ-ERROR-BEAT` |A 64-byte read answered SLVERR on its third beat completed, one SLVERR beat was seen on SYS_OUT, and the other beats arrived intact
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The errored beat's destination bytes are recorded, not compared.

'''''

[[sec-292-smc_i3c_private_write_test]]
===== 292 `smc_i3c_private_write_test`

*Phase*: 2

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i3c_private_write_test`

*BFM / Model*: none on the bus; the I3C0 pad model's DUT-drive observation (`tb_i3c0_sda_dut_low`); observation on the PIO response queue

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`, `i3c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, the stimulus is the named frame, command or sequence the
specification states.

*Objective*: Queue an I3C transfer on I3C0 and I3C1. The other single-build I3C leaves read the CSR window and set `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE`, but none queues a command, so those controllers never drive their buses.

*Test Coverage*:

* Each instance is brought up as the active controller the way the OCCP controller firmware does it: bus enabled in PIO mode, `STBY_CR_CONTROL.STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT` at the active-controller value, open-drain bus timing, queue thresholds, the PIO status enables and the PIO queues running. `T_IDLE` is shortened so the bus is available within the leg. DAT entry 0 is programmed with address 0x50 in its `STATIC_ADDRESS` and `DYNAMIC_ADDRESS` fields (`DAT_structure.rdl`) and read back, and cleared again afterwards.
* One HCI Immediate Data Transfer writes one byte to DAT entry 0, whose address nothing on the single build answers. The command descriptor is the sequence's own field table (`CMD_ATTR`, `TID`, `DEV_INDEX`, `DTT`, `WROC`, `TOC`; the DV OCCP controller driver's descriptor macros carry the same bit layout). The response descriptor's `ERR_STATUS` reports an address NACK as 0x5, and the response must carry that status and the command's `TID`.
* On I3C0 the controller has to drive SDA low at least once during the transfer.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. For I3C0, then I3C1: check `HC_CONTROL` at reset, bring the instance up as the active controller, program and read back DAT entry 0, and write the two command words.
. Poll `PIO_INTR_STATUS.RESP_READY`, read `RESPONSE_PORT` and compare its error status and TID.
. Clear DAT entry 0 and restore `PIO_CONTROL`, `HC_CONTROL` and `STBY_CR_CONTROL`.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I3C-PRIVATE-WRITE` |A private write to an unanswered address, queued on I3C0 and I3C1, returned NACK with its own TID on both, and the I3C0 controller drove SDA low during it
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-242-smc_jtag_axi_shape_test]]
===== 242 `smc_jtag_axi_shape_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_jtag_axi_shape_test`

*BFM / Model*: JTAG AXI driver (`ocah_axi_vip` AXI4 master on the JTAG2AXI input port), SEP_IN AXI driver for the filter arm

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: The third inbound manager of the input fabric carries the same burst and error-response shapes the SEP_IN and SYS_IN shape leaves establish.

*Test Coverage*:

* INCR bursts of 2, 8 and 32 full-width beats into the SPM, each read back as one burst of the same length, so a splitter that drops, repeats or reorders beats on the JTAG port is caught on the data.
* A read of the last unmapped page below `mmode_region`, must answer DECERR.
* GPIO0 ACCESS_FILTER is armed over SEP_IN with a privileged write; an unprivileged JTAG read of the register is refused with DECERR and the error-slave signature 0xBADCAB1E, as the Programmer's Guide GPIO section (`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc`, "Configuring Access Filtering") specifies, and an unprivileged JTAG write of the disarm value is refused with an error response whose code is reported, not asserted, since no document fixes how the fabric forwards a write-channel refusal; a privileged readback shows the refused write took no effect.
* A write to the unmapped page below `mmode_region` answers DECERR and a read of the empty inbound mailbox answers SLVERR, so both error codes are shown on both channels of this port.
* Three passes of outstanding writes and then of reads over the eight scratch registers under a 64-cycle BREADY/RREADY hold stall the port's response channels and, with that many addresses queued behind the register path, its address channels, measured per channel, and every read still returns the word its last write carried.
* The filter is restored to its generated reset and the access counts are measured: the sequence requires its own SEP_IN count and the scoreboard's JTAG AXI count to equal the expected numbers.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_jtag_axi_shape_test_seq` on the SEP_IN AXI sequencer; the JTAG legs go out through the JTAG AXI agent's sequencer as one-shot items. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.


*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-JTAG-AXI-BACKPRESSURE` |The BREADY/RREADY hold stalled the B and R channels for a non-zero number of cycles, measured by the sequence, and every read of the outstanding group is an exact scoreboard compare
|`CHK-JTAG-AXI-BURSTS` |Each burst readback is an exact scoreboard compare of every beat against the payload written; a dropped, repeated or misplaced beat fails
|`CHK-JTAG-AXI-ERRORS` |The unimplemented-region read and write and the refused filter read are compared against DECERR, the refused read against the error-slave signature and the empty-mailbox read against SLVERR by the sequence; the refused write must answer an error response and the privileged readback must still show the armed filter
|`CHK-JTAG-AXI-PORT` |Ledger line in the leaf: the completed JTAG AXI and SEP_IN access counts and the two reported response codes, logged after the sequence has recorded both error legs
|===


*Pass Criteria*: `CHK-JTAG-AXI-BACKPRESSURE`, `CHK-JTAG-AXI-BURSTS`, `CHK-JTAG-AXI-ERRORS` and `CHK-JTAG-AXI-PORT` hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`.

*Scope limit*: The error response code of the refused unprivileged JTAG write is reported, not
asserted, since no document fixes how the fabric forwards a write-channel refusal; the ledger line
logs the access counts and the two reported response codes.
'''''

[[sec-294-smc_i2c_window_landing_test]]
===== 294 `smc_i2c_window_landing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_i2c_window_landing_test`

*BFM / Model*: `SmcI2cMasterVip` on the `tb_i2c0_*` pads, its lines driven from chosen I2C clock edges; observation on `INTR_STATE`, `ACQDATA` and the controller's view of each acknowledge

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/i2c.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes` `smoke`;
`timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `i2c`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Place I2C0 `CTRL` writes, and a second timeout, on I2C clocks where a bus-monitor or target decision rests on a one- or two-clock condition. No other leaf times a register write to the I2C clock.

*Test Coverage*:

* The register path from SEP_IN to I2C0 crosses into the peripheral clock, so its length depends on the run's clock periods. It is measured first: `OVRD` with `TXOVRDEN` set and `SCLVAL` clear, in the same register block as `CTRL`, drives the SCL pad low on the clock it takes effect.
* The bench changes the bus from a clock edge it picks. A START or STOP is recognised `TIMING3.THD_DAT` clocks after that, plus the two-clock input synchroniser, so a `CTRL` write called that many clocks after the bus edge, less the measured path, takes effect on the recognising clock. Each placement is swept over two clocks either side.
* Monitor disabled as a START or STOP is recognised (`THD_DAT` 12). `CTRL` is cleared at each sweep point. After each point the target, enabled again, must acknowledge a write and deliver its byte.
* Target disabled as a read ends with a STOP. `CTRL` is written with `MULTI_CONTROLLER_MONITOR_EN` only, so the bus monitor keeps running while `ENABLETARGET` falls, at each point around the STOP in a read byte's acknowledge slot. `i2c.rdl` raises `UNEXP_STOP` "when the controller sends this target a STOP before this target NACKs". With the target disabled two clocks or more before the STOP it must stay clear, and with it disabled two clocks or more after, the target was enabled for the STOP and it must be raised. The two points between are recorded.
* A NACK timeout and a bus timeout on the same clock. With ACK Control Mode on, `TARGET_ACK_CTRL.NBYTES` 0 and `CTRL.ACQ_START_STOP_EN` set, the target stretches after the first data byte until `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL` (100 clocks) expires and then NACKs it. The bus monitor times the same low SCL from the controller's fall, eight clocks earlier, so the bus timeout is swept over 108 plus or minus two. At every point the address must be acknowledged, the data byte NACKed, and the ACQ FIFO must start with the START entry for the address. The rest of the ACQ FIFO is recorded per point.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Enable I2C0 as a target and measure the register path through `OVRD`.
. For each offset, pull SDA low, or release it after a START, from a chosen clock with `CTRL` cleared at the offset; then write to the target again.
. Error injection. Point: the acknowledge slot of a read byte, with `ENABLETARGET` cleared at a swept offset around the clock the STOP is recognised. Kind: SDA released in the acknowledge slot by the external controller, a STOP where a NACK belongs. Expected response: `UNEXP_STOP` clear when the target was disabled two clocks or more before the STOP, and raised when it was disabled two clocks or more after. For each offset, read a byte from the target and then read `INTR_STATE`.
. Error injection. Point: the target's ACK Control hold after the first data byte, with `TARGET_TIMEOUT_CTRL` at 100 clocks and the bus timeout swept over 108 plus or minus two. Kind: a stretch nobody releases; the NACK timeout and the bus timeout expire on or about the same clock. Expected response: at every point the address acknowledged, the data byte NACKed, and the START entry first in the ACQ FIFO. For each bus-timeout value, write an address and a data byte with ACK Control Mode on, then read the ACQ FIFO.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-I2C-MONITOR-DISABLE-AT-DETECT` |`CTRL` cleared around the clock a START or STOP is recognised left the target, enabled again, delivering a write at every point
|`CHK-I2C-TARGET-DISABLE-AT-STOP` |`ENABLETARGET` cleared around the clock a read's STOP is recognised left `UNEXP_STOP` clear when the target was disabled before the STOP and raised when it was disabled after
|`CHK-I2C-NACK-AND-BUS-TIMEOUT` |With a NACK timeout and bus timeouts around it, the address was acknowledged, the data byte NACKed and the START entry first in the ACQ FIFO at every point
|===

*Pass Criteria*: every checker holds after its compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `i2c`.

*Scope limit*: In the target-disable sweep the two points between the clear-before and raised-after
regions are recorded, not compared. In the timeout sweep the rest of the ACQ FIFO after the START
entry is recorded per point.

'''''

[[sec-295-smc_uart_window_landing_test]]
===== 295 `smc_uart_window_landing_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_uart_window_landing_test`

*BFM / Model*: the UART0 TX pad wired back to its RX pad by the bench for the transmit sweep, and the RX pad driven by the bench from chosen UART clock edges for the receive sweep; observation on `LSR` and `RBR`

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/uart.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `uart`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Place UART0 register writes on the clock the transmit FIFO empties and on the clock the receive timeout fires. No other leaf times a register write to the UART clock.

*Test Coverage*:

* The register path from SEP_IN to UART0 crosses into the UART clock, so its length depends on the run's clock periods. It is measured first: a write setting `LCR.SET_BREAK` drives the TX pad low one clock after it takes effect.
* THR write on the empty clock. With divisor 1 and 8N1, two bytes are queued and the transmit FIFO empties as the second moves to the transmitter, 288 clocks after the first byte's start bit reaches the TX pad. A third THR write is placed at each of two clocks either side of that clock. `uart_core.sv` clears the THR-empty interrupt's cleared flag on the empty clock and sets it on a THR write, so the on-clock write leaves a byte queued with the flag clear. With the TX pad wired back to RX, all three bytes of every point must arrive in order.
* FCR write on the timeout clock. The bench drives a byte on the RX pad, and the timeout count reaches its limit of 40 bit ticks 1589 clocks after the start bit begins. A write clearing `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` is placed at each of two clocks either side of that clock. After each point the FIFO is enabled again and a byte driven on RX must read back intact.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Enable UART0 without loopback at divisor 1, 8N1, FIFOs on, and measure the register path through `LCR.SET_BREAK`.
. For each offset, queue two bytes, call the third THR write at the offset from the first start bit, and read three bytes from the wired-back receiver.
. For each offset, drive a byte on RX with the FCR write called at the offset from its start bit, enable the FIFO again, drive another byte, and read it.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-UART-THR-ON-EMPTY` |A THR write placed around the clock the transmit FIFO empties delivered all three bytes of every point in order
|`CHK-UART-FCR-ON-TIMEOUT` |After an FCR write placed around the clock the receive timeout fires, a byte received with the FIFO enabled again read back intact at every point
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. Enrolled in: `all`, `hosted`, `uart`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.

'''''

[[sec-263-smc_filter_lock_window_test]]
===== 263 `smc_filter_lock_window_test`

*Phase*: 3

*Area*: FIRMWARE

*Source Module*: `smc_filter_lock_window_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN)

*Run mode*: one testlist entry in `testlists/fabric.toml`; groups `all`, `hosted`; `run_modes`
`smoke`; `timeout_sec` 1800; tags `ci`, `fabric`; seed 1; tool Verilator (cocotb).

*Randomization*: RAND-NONE: directed, every stimulus value is pinned by the entry and the sequence
draws nothing from the seed.

*Objective*: Writes queued right behind the write that locks a filter are refused and change nothing.

*Test Coverage*:

* `filter_ctrl.rdl` makes `FILTER_CONFIG.locked` (bit 63) `woset`: "Lock filter configurations. Write once register", and once it is set every later write to the entry's registers "is steered to the AXI error subordinate and terminates with a DECERR response; reads still return the locked configuration". No other field of the block carries a write enable, so the lock is enforced outside the register block by each filter's inner demux.
* The demux stores its port select with the AW. `locked` updates on the clock edge that arms B, so each filter port holds the next AW until that B is accepted and the select is sampled with `locked` already set.
* Arm leg: filter 15 of the outbound bank, then of the inbound bank, reads its reset word with `locked` and `entry_enabled` clear, and the locking write (reset word plus `locked`) is answered OKAY.
* Two `FILTER_CONFIG` writes queued in the same outstanding group directly behind the locking write, carrying `src_id` 5 and 6. Both must be answered DECERR, and `FILTER_CONFIG` must then read the reset word plus `locked`. The entry's address is registered with the SEP_IN monitor as the one place a DECERR is expected, so a DECERR anywhere else in the run fails the leaf; a DECERR on the locking write itself, which the monitor excuses at that address, fails through the scoreboard's OKAY expectation and the sequence's response assert. `entry_enabled` stays clear throughout, so filter 15 filters no traffic. Each bank emits `CHK-FILTER-LOCK-WINDOW`.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_filter_lock_window_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FILTER-LOCK-WINDOW` |Both writes queued behind the locking write were answered DECERR, the locking write OKAY, and `FILTER_CONFIG` read exactly the reset word plus `locked`
|===

*Pass Criteria*: both banks answer the two writes queued behind the locking write with DECERR, and each `FILTER_CONFIG` reads the reset word plus `locked`. Enrolled in `all` and `hosted` from `fabric.toml`.

*Scope limit*: None stated.
'''''

[[smc-formal-plan]]
[[smc-vplan-phase3]]
=== Phase 3 Tests

Phase 3 tests prove the residual contracts of each area
(<<smc-vplan-phase3-overview>>). Each Phase 3 test has a row in the
Scenario-Expanded Test Summary, marked "3" in the Phase column, and its entry in
the section of its area under Test Procedures, with `*Phase*: 3`. The rows are
for human readers and the entries are for tools and audits. The two name the
same tests. An entry follows the field rules of Test Procedures: `*Phase*`,
`*Area*`, `*Run mode*`, `*Randomization*`, `*Scope limit*`, and the
error-injection steps written as "Error injection. Point: ... Kind: ... Expected
response: ...". A Phase 3 test never overlaps a Phase 1 or Phase 2 test. An
entry that extends an open test names that test in its Objective. The Phase 3
contracts that no test can grade are in <<smc-vplan-phase3-lists>>. The
randomization class of every Phase 3 test is in <<smc-vplan-phase3-random>>. The
observation taps, the hooks and the PROPOSED drives of the Phase 3 tests are in
<<smc-vplan-phase3-proposed>>. The parked-test rule is in
<<smc-vplan-phase3-parked>>. The class words and bench terms are defined in
<<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-parked]]
==== Phase 3 Parked Tests

A parked test has no graded check that runs without a PROPOSED item or an
unstated value (<<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>). Its entry carries the field
`*Needs*:`, its summary row reads "3, parked", it takes no credit and it is not
in an executable total.

No Phase 3 entry carries a `*Needs*:` field, so every Phase 3 test is
executable: each is a member of `all` with a Checkers table whose tokens its
leaf requires (<<smc-vplan-evidence-gate>>), and at least one of its graded
checks is not blocked. The legs an entry leaves ungraded are named in its
`*Scope limit*` field; the ones a document leaves unstated are collected in
<<smc-vplan-phase3-lists>>. The cards the plan holds out of `all` are not parked
Phase 3 tests: the weekly `rtl_issue` reproducer
`smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test`, the two ROM hold-outs
`smc_occp_dual_unsecure_boot_test` and `smc_prod_rom_occp_ready_test`, and the
firmware hold-out `smc_fw_i3c5_csr_access_test` are held-out cards under
<<smc-held-out-testcases>> with their own closing conditions, and their summary
rows read "held out". The three `sanity` leaves of the dual elaboration are
Phase 1 cards held out of `all` for the elaboration reason that
<<smc-held-out-testcases>> states, not parked.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-random]]
==== Phase 3 Randomization

Every Phase 3 stimulus that has a legal matrix is a pure function of the run
seed, and `--seed N` replays the leaf. The stream is not a CSPRNG and no drawn
value is a key, a token or a nonce. No document quotes a per-seed value as
evidence. The class of a test is one of:

* `RAND-REP`: the seed draws points from a legal matrix, and every point has a stated outcome.
* `RANDCFG`: the seed draws a configuration, the test runs one scenario under it, and the expected outcome is a function of the configuration.
* `RAND-NONE`: the stimulus is directed, for the reason the entry states.

The drawn-cell contract and the fixed-cell exception are stated in
<<smc-vplan-drawn-cells>>. A row marked "fixed-cell variant" is a module of the
clock-cell or image-kind families that pins its cell by a class attribute and a
testlist entry. The Dimensions column repeats the draws or the reason of the
entry's `*Randomization*` field.
