[[smc-vplan-phase3-lists]]
==== Phase 3 Blocked Features, Observation Gaps and Scope

Each item is listed once. The area column names the area that the item concerns.
A blocked feature carries no Phase 3 credit. A feature with no observation point
has no check that can fail on it. An out of scope feature is graded by an open
Phase 1 or Phase 2 test, or has no stated pass or fail value, or belongs to
another plan. The observation taps, the hooks and the PROPOSED drives that the
tests use are in <<smc-vplan-phase3-proposed>>. A check that needs a PROPOSED
item is blocked (<<smc-credit-rules>>). A check that needs only observation taps
and added hooks is not blocked. A row names the document section or the register
that leaves the value unstated, what is unstated, and the enrolled tests that
log the value; where a test logs the value without grading it, the row names the
test and the log tag and does not report the value. A leg a test leaves ungraded
by its own design (a bench bound, an undriven leg, a measured-only sentence) is
stated in the entry's `*Scope limit*` field and is not listed here.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-blocked]]
===== Blocked features

A blocked feature has no check in Phase 3, because the specification or the
register description does not state the value that a check needs. The question
names what the specification must state before a check can fail on the feature.
Where a test uses part of a blocked feature, the note says what the test does.

[cols="2,5,6,5",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Feature |Open specification question |Note
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|The CLA action encoding: `integration/rdl/smc/dfd_cla.rdl` gives each of `Action0` to `Action3` a 6-bit "Select an Action" field, and `hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc` names `cpu_interrupts_o` bit 321 as the CLA interrupt.
|Blocked: the specification does not state which action code selects which action (the debug interrupt, the trace triggers, the counter controls). Source: `integration/rdl/smc/dfd_cla.rdl` (`Action0` to `Action3`); `hw/sys/smc/doc/dfd.adoc`; `hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc` (SMC CPU Interrupt Vector Map).
|The CLA entries (`smc_dfd_cla_node_eap_sweep_test`, `smc_dfd_cla_counter_edge_test`, `smc_dfd_cla_live_bus_test`, `smc_dfd_cla_snapshot_capture_test`, `smc_dfd_trace_accumulator_fill_test`) program the action index and grade the pair activation, the clear and the counters; the mapping of an action code to its effect is not graded, and the sweeps over the action values log the outcome of each.
|<<smc-vplan-area-mailbox,MAILBOX>>
|The mailbox clock gate closes during an idle gap while `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.mailbox_cg_en` is set.
|Blocked: the specification does not state whether the gate closes on an idle gap with the enable set, nor after how many idle cycles. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl` (`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.mailbox_cg_en`, "Clockgate enable for the mailbox"); `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` (Subsystem Controls and Clock Gating).
|`smc_mailbox_register_map_reset_test` sets the enable and grades that every aperture still answers, and logs the completion latency of the first write after the idle gap; `smc_mailbox_irq_ack_output_test` holds the gate enabled through its 512-cycle idle window. The bench has no gated-clock observation for the mailbox, so no entry grades the gate itself.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|The effect of `CTRL.UART_EN` = 0 on the UART0 transmit pad.
|Blocked: the specification does not state what the TX pad carries while `UART_EN` is clear (held idle, held at its last level, or released to the GPIO wrap). Source: `hw/ip/uart/uart_log_engine_wrap/regs/uart_log_engine_ctrl.rdl` (`CTRL.UART_EN`); no chapter states the pad level.
|`smc_uart_pad_mux_enable_test` grades the frame with `UART_EN` set, again after a clear and set, and logs the pad level and the decoded frames with `UART_EN` clear without grading them.
|===

[[smc-vplan-phase3-blocked-legs]]
====== Blocked legs of tested features

A tested feature can have a blocked leg. The test grades the rest of the
feature, and the note says how the test treats the blocked leg. The rows are
ordered by area.

[cols="2,5,6,5",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Item |Blocked leg and open question |Note
|<<smc-vplan-area-misc,MISC>>
|A write past the decoded extent of a register island answers the response `hw/sys/smc/regs/smc.rdl` declares for that island (`ocah_past_extent_resp`).
|Which code a past-extent write inside an island's aperture answers: `hw/sys/smc/regs/smc.rdl` declares `SLVERR` per island for the reset unit, the misc wrap, the GPIO interface, the base configuration, the alias remap, the eFuse map and the peripheral windows, and `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` (Address Space Organization) gives the decode responses of the fabric; the documents do not state which rule wins for a write. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/smc.rdl` (`ocah_past_extent_resp`); `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` (Address Space Organization); `hw/ip/i2c/regs/i2c_wrap.rdl` (`ocah_gap_resp`).
|`smc_reg_island_boundary_sweep_test` grades the read response and data on all 48 words and the write response on the nine `DECERR`-declared islands; on the fifteen `SLVERR`-declared islands it accepts `SLVERR` or `DECERR`, counts the answers per island and logs the count without grading the code. `smc_past_extent_slverr_units_test`, `smc_gap_decode_response_test` and `smc_i2c_window_decode_test` log the write response the same way.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|`DMA STATUS_0` bit 8 reports midend activity.
|When bit 8 reads 1, and for how long: during the copy, until retirement, or never once the midend has handed the transfer to the backend. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/dma.adoc` (Submission and Completion; "bit 8 indicates midend activity").
|`smc_dma_completion_status_test` grades `DONE_0` and `STATUS_0` at reset, idle, no-data and held, samples bit 8 on every poll and logs the samples without grading them; `smc_dma_backpressure_breadth_test` logs it under a held transfer.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The `NEXT_ID` and `DONE` reset values and the meaning of `DONE_0` after a command.
|`hw/sys/smc/doc/dma.adoc` and the register description `integration/rdl/smc/dma_ctrl.rdl` state different reset values for `NEXT_ID` and `DONE` and a different meaning for `DONE` (the last retired id versus a cumulative count); which one is normative. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/dma.adoc` (Stream and Register Ownership); `integration/rdl/smc/dma_ctrl.rdl` (`NEXT_ID`, `DONE`); GitHub issue tenstorrent/tt-oca-harness#2455.
|`smc_dma_invalid_descriptor_test` logs `NEXT_ID_0`, `DONE_0` and `STATUS_0[9:0]` for the `ENABLED_ND`-cleared and zero-length commands without comparing them until the issue is resolved; `smc_dma_completion_status_test` grades the values the chapter states.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A DMA row address that steps past 2^56 wraps within 56 bits.
|Whether the effective address wraps at bit 56, saturates or errors. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/dma.adoc` (Transfer Configuration; the register storage and effective field widths).
|`smc_dma_2d_copy_test` places the rows so that later rows lie beyond 2^56, requires the command to retire with AR and AW handshakes, and logs the addresses issued without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A zeroer job aimed at an unmapped local address or at a write-blocked outbound filter region.
|What such a job leaves in `CTRL_STATUS`, in the interrupt pulses, the AW handshakes, the B cycles and the SYS_OUT write count. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/zeroer.adoc` (Operation Details); `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc` (SRAM Initialization using Memory Zeroer).
|`smc_zeroer_sram_init_test` requires `STATUS` 0 twice and the denied region unchanged, and logs the other fields without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|Two ATB telemetry messages sent back to back are both queued.
|The spacing a receiver needs between the last packet of one message and the first packet of the next. `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc` (Assembly and Decode) states that a last-packet marker queues the message and that beats are accepted except during a receiver flush, and states no spacing. Source: the same chapter; `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/interface.adoc` (ATB Protocol Specifications, acceptance while `atready_o` is high).
|`smc_telemetry_tx_flush_test` sends its messages eight idle cycles apart, as the other telemetry entries do, and states that the documents do not state a spacing; the back-to-back case is not graded.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A receiver flush written while a message is in flight.
|Whether in-flight ATB beats are held or dropped when `CTRL.TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH` is written mid-message. Source: `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc` (Reset and Flush); `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/regs/telemetry_receiver.rdl` (`CTRL.TELEMETRY_RX_FLUSH`).
|`smc_telemetry_rx_flush_test` requires every beat to be accepted within 64 cycles and logs the accepted-beat and stalled-cycle counts and `STATUS` after 64 quiet cycles without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A full-word `CTRL` write that sets only `BUFFER_POP`.
|Whether such a write cancels a pending transmitter flush request (`CTRL.TELEMETRY_TX_FLUSH`). Source: `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc` (Telemetry Receiver, Buffer Management); `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/regs/telemetry_receiver.rdl` (`CTRL`).
|`smc_telemetry_ctrl_access_test` makes the write and logs the flush state without grading it.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A second AVSBus resync request while one is pending.
|Whether the second request gives one resync or two. Source: `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/architecture.adoc` (AVS Protocol Engine).
|`smc_avsbus_resync_force_test` requires one or two resync episodes and logs the count.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The AVSBus resync interval.
|Whether the residual between the programmed interval and the period is constant across `RESYNC_INTERVAL` values, and whether a rewrite of `RESYNC_INTERVAL` restarts or retargets the running interval. Source: `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/architecture.adoc` (AVS Protocol Engine); `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/interface.adoc` (Timing); `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/regs/avsbus_controller.rdl` (`RESYNC_INTERVAL`).
|`smc_avsbus_resync_timing_test` logs the periods and residuals and the times from the previous end, from the write and from the first resync's end without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The first OCTS count sample after `TIMER_START` with preset 0.
|When the first nonzero count sample appears; only an upper bound of 0x40 rises is stated by the entry. Source: `hw/ip/system_timer_octs/doc/architecture.adoc` (Counting and Synchronization).
|`smc_octs_primary_count_test` requires the first nonzero sample within the bound and logs the sample, its rise index and `RUNNING` at the first rise.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The watchdog `COUNT` register with both enables clear.
|Whether `COUNT` holds or counts while `CTRL.wdogenalways` and `CTRL.wdogcoreawake` are both clear. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` (`CTRL.wdogenalways`, `CTRL.wdogcoreawake`); `hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc` (Operation).
|`smc_wdt_count_feed_test` requires only that the later both-clear window matches the earlier one and logs the three reads and their increase; `smc_wdt_register_map_test` brackets `SCALED_COUNT` between two `COUNT` reads shifted by the scale, which holds for either behaviour.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The first `COUNT` read after a keyed write.
|Whether the read returns the written value or the written value plus one. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` (`COUNT`).
|`smc_wdt_count_feed_test` brackets the read between the written value and the written value plus twice the measured increase and logs the offset.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The watchdog lock between keyed writes.
|Whether a keyed `FEED` write of a non-feed word re-locks the watchdog, and whether `KEY` reads 1 between a second consecutive magic write and the following register write. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc` (Register Access); `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` (`KEY`, `FEED`).
|`smc_wdt_count_feed_test` logs `KEY` after the non-feed word and re-locks with a `CTRL` write if `KEY` reads set; `smc_wdt_key_relock_test` requires the following register write to be accepted and `KEY` to read 0 afterwards, and logs the `KEY` value in between.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The `wdogcoreawake` condition.
|Which reset defines the core-awake condition. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` (`CTRL.wdogcoreawake`); `hw/sys/smc/doc/cpu.adoc` (Watchdog Interface).
|`smc_wdt_count_feed_test` uses the core 1 level reset through `RESET_CTRL` and requires counting before and after it; no other reset is tried.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|A scaled watchdog value wider than `SCALED_COUNT.wdogs`.
|Whether a scaled value wider than the 16-bit field truncates or saturates. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` (`SCALED_COUNT.wdogs`).
|`smc_wdt_scale_zerocmp_test` logs `SCALED_COUNT` after `COUNT` 0x0001_2345 at scale 0 and 0x0002_4690 at scale 1 next to the shifted `COUNT` and compares nothing.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|A lock write to a filter entry that sets other fields together with `locked`.
|Whether the fields written together with the lock bit are applied. Source: `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/filter_ctrl.rdl` (`locked`); `hw/ip/axi_filter/doc/index.adoc` (Locking a Filter Entry).
|`smc_filter_lock_scope_test` requires the two `FILTER_CONFIG` reads to agree and bit 63 to be set exactly when the write answered `OKAY`, and logs the response and the two reads.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|An access through a clear (`valid` 0) output remap region.
|Which source ID the access carries. Source: `hw/ip/output_remap/regs/output_remap.rdl` (`REGION_ATTRS.valid`).
|`smc_outremap_prot_srcid_test` logs `awuser` and `aruser` of the region 4 access beside the direct and M-mode values without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|A write that hits overlapping alias regions 1 and 2.
|Which region wins. Source: `hw/ip/axi_alias_remap/regs/alias_remap.rdl` (`REGION`, `REGION_ATTRS.valid`).
|`smc_alias_remap_translate_test` requires one of the three possible landings and logs which, the response and the hit-probe level.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|The first address past the SHIM range of the external window.
|Which block answers it. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` (AXI-Lite External Window).
|`smc_ext_window_routing_test` requires the eFuse activity probe to stay low and logs the response, the data and whether an external request appeared.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|A read of a write-only register.
|What a read of a write-only or unreadable register returns. Source: `hw/ip/uart/log_engine/regs/log_engine.rdl` (`INTR_TEST`); `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/regs/avsbus_controller.rdl` (`AVS_INTERRUPT_CLEAR`).
|`smc_cpuif_ro_wo_edge_test` requires completion within the guard and the `SCRATCH_COLD` recovery read, and logs the response and data; `smc_uart_log_engine_reg_map_test` requires only that each `INTR_TEST` read answers, and logs the code and data at reset and after a write of 0x11.
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|`SS_CONFIG` is a read-write register.
|Whether `SS_CONFIG` stores a software write or reflects an external value: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/reset_unit/reset_unit.rdl` declares it `sw=rw`, and the write-side entry treats it as externally sourced. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/reset_unit/reset_unit.rdl` (`SS_CONFIG`).
|`smc_axil_write_side_test` writes the value `SS_CONFIG` already holds and grades the response and the unchanged read-back; neither reading is distinguished.
|<<smc-vplan-area-clock,CLOCK>>
|A write refused by a gated peripheral window.
|Whether a write that a gated window refuses with `SLVERR` may change peripheral state, and whether a write made under the gate lands or is dropped. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` (Subsystem Controls and Clock Gating); `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl` (`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`).
|`smc_periph_cg_window_extent_test` requires the `SLVERR` response and logs the register words before the write and after the enable is cleared; `smc_i2c_clock_gate_response_test` logs `HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT[0]` and `I2C_CTRL[2]` after the gated write; `smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test` logs DAT slot 15 word 0 of each instance after a gated write and the gate clear. None compares the word.
|<<smc-vplan-area-clock,CLOCK>>
|An access the peripheral has already accepted finishes when a clock gate sets, and an access issued while a core is held in reset answers `SLVERR`.
|What happens to a SEP_IN access accepted before `CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL` sets the peripheral gate, and to a read of a cluster watchdog register while its core is held in level reset: `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` says software quiesces first, `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` says a gated window answers `SLVERR` so software does not stall, and `hw/sys/smc/doc/cpu.adoc` says the cluster boundary stays isolated with `SLVERR` while a core is in reset; none states the fate of the in-flight access. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` (Subsystem Controls and Clock Gating); `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` (Access Control and Security); `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl` (`CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL`); `hw/sys/smc/doc/cpu.adoc` (CPU AXI Isolation).
|`smc_i2c_clock_gate_response_test` and `smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test` grade the gated and ungated responses, and `smc_i3c_clock_gate_window_test` logs the accesses in flight around the gate write; `smc_wdt_count_feed_test` grades the watchdog with the cores released and logs the accesses made while core 1 is held in level reset.
|<<smc-vplan-area-cpu,CPU>>
|The self-isolate release comes four cycles after SRAM initialisation completes and the cores are out of reset.
|Which clock edge starts the count of four. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/cpu.adoc` (CPU AXI Isolation, the self-isolate release on cold boot).
|`smc_cpu_boot_release_sequence_test` measures the release in `clk_smc_i` rises and grades the order of the boot terms; the count itself is logged.
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|A disabled trace sink that still receives trace.
|What the sink does with trace that arrives after its enable is cleared. Source: `integration/rdl/smc/dfd_dst.rdl` (`Trdstcontrol`).
|`smc_dfd_trace_accumulator_fill_test` logs the write pointer after the sink enable is cleared and does not hold it to a value.
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|The CLA edge-detect select.
|Which debug-bus signal each `CDbgSignalEdgeDetectCfg` select value names. Source: `integration/rdl/smc/dfd_cla.rdl` (`CDbgSignalEdgeDetectCfg`).
|`smc_dfd_cla_counter_edge_test` grades the configuration surface only; no detected edge is claimed.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|A CSR read of a read-locked shadow register.
|What the read returns: `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` fixes `0xbadcab1e` only for the JTAG lifecycle-demux error slave. Source: `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` (Access Permissions and Security; Hardware vs. Software Locks).
|`smc_efuse_locked_access_interrupt_test` grades the interrupt pulse and non-disclosure of the locked word and does not compare the returned word.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|A write to a write-locked eFuse field.
|Whether the guard refuses the write with an error response or ignores it. Source: `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` (Hardware vs. Software Locks); `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_efuse_map/smc_efuse_map.rdl` (`LOCKS`).
|`smc_efuse_lock_guard_test` grades that the write did not land and logs the response.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|`EFUSE_BANK_INIT_TIME` across a cold reset.
|Whether the field survives a cold reset, and so the release-to-first-command delay with the reset value and with 0x40. Source: `doc/integrator/src/smu-smc.adoc` (eFuse Interface; the SHIM control address window).
|`smc_efuse_bank_ctrl_window_test` logs the two delays, their difference and whether the value survived, without comparing them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|The shadow-register output port `shadow_regs_o`.
|What the port shows for a locked field, for a read-locked word and beyond the stored words. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc` (`shadow_regs_o`).
|`smc_efuse_map_lock_field_enforce_test` grades only the port's stability across rejected writes and hidden reads; `smc_efuse_map_sense_image_test` logs the read-locked words without comparing them; `smc_efuse_map_sep_write_test` compares the stored words only, word n at bits 32n to 32n+31.
|<<smc-vplan-area-gpio,GPIO>>
|A GPIO interrupt is one clock-cycle pulse per detected edge.
|Which clock the pulse is one cycle of: `hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc` states the pulse and no SMC chapter names the GPIO wrap clock. Source: `hw/ip/gpio/doc/architecture.adoc` (Interrupts); `hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` (Clock Architecture).
|`smc_gpio_irq_or_test` and `smc_gpio_rst_primary_test` compare the line width against the raw vector width and log the width in `clk_smc_i` cycles.
|<<smc-vplan-area-gpio,GPIO>>
|`DATA_CTRL.lsio_enable` reports the hardware LSIO request after the disable gate.
|Which wraps present a hardware LSIO request at reset: the pinned sources name a request only for the SPI pads and the permanently selected pads. Source: `hw/ip/gpio/regs/gpio_intf.rdl` (`DATA_CTRL.lsio_enable`); `doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv`.
|`smc_gpio_data_ctrl_ro_status_test` grades that software writes do not change the status bits and logs the per-wrap scan of `lsio_enable`; `smc_gpio_intf_regblock_sweep_test` accepts a reset word of 0 or the `lsio_enable` bit on every instance.
|<<smc-vplan-area-irq,IRQ>>
|The PLIC pending bit of the core 2 watchdog interrupt.
|Whether the pending bit is level or latched. Source: `hw/sys/smc/doc/interrupts.adoc` (Raw Vector and PLIC Numbering).
|`smc_wdt_irq_source_ids_test` logs core 2 `CTRL.wdogip0` and the pending level after the interrupt clear without grading them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-irq,IRQ>>
|A stall of exactly the programmed threshold.
|Whether a stall of exactly `HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD.value` rises fires the detector, and at which rise the interrupt first reads 1. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl` (`HANG_DET_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD`).

|<<smc-vplan-area-irq,IRQ>>
|The SEP detector interrupt after a late enable.
|How soon the interrupt returns after `irq_en` is set during a held read. Source: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/smc_base_config/smc_base_config.rdl` (`HANG_DET_CTRL`).

|`SMC_ATTRIBUTES` carries the interrupt and mailbox counts.

Source: `hw/ip/i2c/regs/i2c.rdl` (`FIFO_CTRL`, `INTR_STATE.BUS_TIMEOUT`, `CTRL.ENABLEHOST`); `hw/ip/i2c/doc/index.adoc`.

|<<smc-vplan-area-i2c,I2C>>
|A controller pulse that raises the other symbol interrupt.
|Whether a pulse the controller drives also reports `SDA_UNSTABLE`, or a pulse it receives also reports `SDA_INTERFERENCE`. Source: `hw/ip/i2c/doc/index.adoc` (the adopted theory of operation); `hw/ip/i2c/regs/i2c.rdl` (`INTR_STATE`).
|`smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test` grades the interrupt the theory of operation names for each pulse and logs the whole `INTR_STATE` word each pulse left.
|<<smc-vplan-area-i3c,I3C>>
|A write of bit n to a TTI `INTERRUPT_FORCE` register sets bit n of `INTERRUPT_STATUS`.

Source: `vendor/chipsalliance/i3c-core/upstream/src/rdl/target_transaction_interface.rdl` (`INTERRUPT_FORCE`, `INTERRUPT_STATUS`, `TARGET_ERR_INTR_FORCE`).
|`smc_i3c_csr_sweep_ext_test` grades the latch and the write-one-to-clear of every status its force sets, and logs per field whether the force set the status, without grading the fields the register description leaves open.
|<<smc-vplan-area-mailbox,MAILBOX>>

|What a write of 0x3 (`wflush` and `rflush` together) does: its response and which FIFOs drain. Source: `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/regs/axil_mailbox.rdl` (`CTRL`); `hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/interface.adoc` (Access Results).
|`smc_mailbox_flush_status_test` grades the single-bit flushes and logs the both-bits write (`CHK-CTRL-BOTH-BITS-OBSERVED`) without grading it.
|<<smc-vplan-area-mailbox,MAILBOX>>
|A word written in the same access group as a flush.

|<<smc-vplan-area-mailbox,MAILBOX>>

|The 32-entry receive FIFO and the overrun indication `LSR.OE`.

|`smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test` sends 33 characters with no read, grades that exactly the first 32 are readable in order and logs whether and when `OE` sets.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|A 33rd `THR` write with 32 characters queued, and a second `FCR.FIFO_ENABLE` write with characters held.
|Whether the 33rd write is accepted or refused, and whether the second enable write keeps or discards the four held characters. Source: `hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/doc/architecture.adoc` (FIFO Protection and Line Errors; Transmit and Receive Paths).
|`smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test` issues the 33rd write and logs its response, the later `LSR` and the readable count; for the enable write it accepts either none or exactly the four in order with `DR` clear after the last, and logs which.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|The receive trigger level fires at the programmed level.
|`doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc` says the receive interrupt fires when the FIFO holds "more than" the trigger amount, and its trigger table reads at the level; which reading is normative. Source: `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc` (UART, the receive trigger).
|`smc_uart_fifo_control_depth_test` logs the onset count for each trigger code and grades the ordering of the onsets, not the exact count.

|`IIR` with `IER.ETBEI` set on an already empty transmit buffer.

|`smc_uart_irq_thre_identify_test` requires `LSR.THRE` to read 1 and the up to 16 `IIR` reads to agree with one another, and logs them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>

|The CTS level at the SMC boundary is not stated, and the first `MSR` read after reset may report a modem-status delta with no transition. Source: `hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/regs/uart_16550_main.rdl` (`MSR`, reset 0x00; `DCTS` "changed since the last read"); `hw/sys/smc/doc/port_table.adoc` (the UART modem inputs).
|`smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test` grades that the delta bits clear on the second read (`CHK-UART-MSR-DELTA-CLEAR`) and logs the first read; `smc_uart_reg_reset_rw_test` logs the first `MSR` read on all four instances.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|`IER` bits 31:5.

|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|A second `THR` write with the divisor at 0.
|Whether the second write replaces the waiting character or is dropped. Source: `hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/regs/uart_16550_main.rdl` (`THR`, the divisor latches).
|`smc_uart_thr_paths_test` requires exactly one character to arrive once the divisor is set and logs which.
|<<smc-vplan-area-firmware,FIRMWARE>>
|The end of the probe-ID run that survives a telemetry buffer overflow.
|Which end of the run survives when the message buffer is filled past full. Source: `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/regs/telemetry_receiver.rdl` (`STATUS.BUFFER_FULL`); `hw/ip/telemetry_receiver/doc/architecture.adoc` (Message Queue and Readout).
|`smc_telemetry_buffer_overflow_test` requires the drain to return exactly the depth's worth as one in-order run and logs which end survived.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-unstated]]
====== Unstated cells that block no feature

Values that no document states and that no feature needs, which an entry records
without grading. Each bullet names the silent document section and the entry
that records the value.

<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>:

* The SRAM size the zeroer clears: `doc/programmer/src/smc-programming.adoc` states 128 KiB and the generated memory map (`hw/sys/smc/regs/gen/py/smc_memory_map.py`, `spm_memory`) spans 1 MiB. `smc_zeroer_sram_init_test` clears the 128 KiB the programming guide states and grades nothing past it.
* The AVSBus CRC-3 polynomial: no document in the tree states it; `hw/ip/avsbus_controller/doc/interface.adoc` (AVSBus Frame Format) gives the subframe layout only. `smc_avsbus_frame_transaction_test` excludes the CRC field from its `avs_mdata_o` compare; `smc_avsbus_slave_reply_test` sends each reply shape with each of the eight codes and requires that exactly one code updates `AVS_LATEST_SLAVE_SUBFRAME`.

<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>:

* A unit whose aperture crosses `BASE + REGION_SIZE`: `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` states that the inbound port reaches a unit only while its whole aperture lies below the boundary, and no enrolled test places the boundary inside an aperture. `smc_region_gated_units_decode_test` and `smc_region_zero_reset_recovery_test` grade units wholly below or wholly above it.
* The reset state of the sixteen inbound filter entries: `hw/sys/smc/doc/fabric.adoc` (Inbound Filtering) leaves the default to the chiplet integration and `hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/filter_ctrl.rdl` resets every entry disabled. `smc_sys_axi_in_port_test` issues its pre-admit SYS_IN read with the error response tolerated and logs the response.
* The write response of the window at `BASE + 0x001_7000` to `BASE + 0x001_7FFF` and of the gap past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block: `hw/sys/smc/doc/memmap.adoc` (Address Space Organization) states `SLVERR` for a write there and `hw/sys/smc/regs/smc.rdl` (`ocah_gap_resp`) declares `DECERR`. `smc_gap_decode_response_test` requires only that the code is the same across its six port and base combinations and logs it; `smc_cpuif_ro_wo_edge_test` logs the response and data at the first address past the `SCRATCH_COLD` block.

<<smc-vplan-area-i2c,I2C>>:

* `CTRL.LLPBK` in controller mode, which `hw/ip/i2c/regs/i2c.rdl` states makes the internal logic see `smbalert_ni` as deasserted: `smc_i2c_controller_queue_shapes_test` grades that a transfer made with the bit set reaches the target unchanged, and `smc_i2c_target_loopback_test` grades the target-mode loopback; no enrolled test drives the alert pad with the bit set in controller mode.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-noobs]]
===== Features with no observation point

A disposition says what is done about the missing observation. `ADD-PORT`: a
testbench port, drive or hook that the bench lacks would give the observation,
and the DUT does not change. `ACCEPT-PROBE`: a read-only probe, a `tb_*`
observation signal, a public-scope line or a hierarchical reference is the
observation. A probe that `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` does not list is
an observation tap the test adds to the signal list, and a check on it is
executable. `PERMANENT-HOLE`: no observation exists at the `smc_wrapper`
boundary on this bench, so no check can fail on the contract. A read-only tap is
not PROPOSED; a port, drive, inject or hook that `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`
has or that `hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` lists is not PROPOSED
(<<smc-vplan-blocked-taxonomy>>). The Why column names the tie-off, the bench
net or the register that the observation would need.

[cols="2,4,5,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Feature |Why there is no observation point |Disposition |Note
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The transmitter flush handshake of telemetry receivers 1 and 2 (`afvalid` / `afready`).
|`hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` exports `tb_telemetry0_afvalid` and drives `tb_telemetry0_afready` for receiver 0 only; the `afready` of every other receiver is held high and its `afvalid` is not exported.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_telemetry_receiver_isolation_test` grades the isolation on receiver 0's pins; `smc_telemetry_atb_capture_test` runs its transmitter-flush leg on receiver 0 only.
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|The write responses the zeroer receives from the output fabric.
|The signal list carries `tb_zeroer_bvalid` and no response code for the zeroer's B channel.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_zeroer_sram_init_test` logs the register-visible fields of the unmapped and denied jobs instead.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|`smc_region_size_o` on the `SMC_DUAL` elaboration.
|The port is left unconnected on both DUT instances of the dual bench in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`, so the pin-side effect of `REGION_SIZE` is not observable there.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_dual_base_addressing_test` grades the register and the decode and does not claim the port.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|A SYS_IN access whose AxUSER carries a non-zero source ID.
|Every SYS_IN master of the bench presents AxUSER 0, so a non-zero source ID matched against a wildcard `src_id` 0 entry is not reachable.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_infilt_attr_match_test` grades the other attribute matches and does not claim the source-ID match (`hw/ip/axi_filter/regs/filter_ctrl.rdl`, `src_id`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|The W, R and B channels of the external AXI-Lite port.
|The signal list taps the external port's AW and AR channels only (`tb_axil_external_awvalid`, `tb_axil_external_awaddr`, `tb_axil_external_arvalid`, `tb_axil_external_araddr`).
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_ext_window_routing_test` grades the response and data at SEP_IN together with the AR address match on the port; `smc_ext_window_aperture_test` grades the AW request and its address and does not claim the write data and strobes.
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|A SEP_IN request presented inside the primary-reset window.
|The SEP_IN AXI master of the bench takes `rst_primary_smc_clk_no` as its own reset and parks its request lines, so no request can be presented while the fabric is held.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_primary_reset_scope_test` claims the outbound filter register reverting for the fabric half and logs the four SEP_IN tallies without grading them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|`rst_primary_periph_clk_no`.
|The signal list carries no observation signal for the port.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_reset_sync_edge_test` grades the other sequenced resets and does not claim this one.
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|The automatic SRAM zeroing on cold boot.
|`smc_disable_sram_auto_init_i` is tied to 1 at both DUT instances in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`, so `smc_init_mem_done_o` rises as soon as the cluster reset releases.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_cold_boot_chain_order_test` records the SRAM-init step as not closed (`CHK-COLD-BOOT-NOT-CLOSED`); the zeroer leaves prove the software-triggered sweep.
|<<smc-vplan-area-clock,CLOCK>>
|Any all-zero reset value on a Verilator run.
|Verilator is a 2-state simulator: an unreset flop reads 0, so a compare of an all-zero reset value also passes on a flop that was never reset (Known Limitations).
|`PERMANENT-HOLE`
|Every all-zero reset compare of the plan carries this caveat; the entries that prove a clear from a programmed state (a non-zero write followed by the reset) are the ones that grade the reset.
|<<smc-vplan-area-clock,CLOCK>>
|A telemetry reset separate from the cold reset.
|`rst_telemetry_ni` is driven from the cold reset at both DUT instances in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_clock_domain_connectivity_test` records the telemetry reset cell as not closed (`CHK-CLOCK-DOMAIN-NOT-CLOSED`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-cpu,CPU>>
|The DFX done and pass inputs (`mem_repair_done_i`, `mem_repair_success_i`, `mbist_done_i`, `mbist_pass_i`).
|The four inputs are tied to 1 at the DUT instance in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`; only the two abort pins (`tb_mem_repair_abort`, `tb_mbist_abort`) are bench nets.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_dfx_status_abort_test`, `smc_dfx_status_smu_pulse_reset_test` and `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_noeffect_gate_test` take the register-description mask word as the idle expectation and exercise the two abort bits only; `smc_cold_boot_chain_order_test` records the repair step as not closed (`CHK-COLD-BOOT-NOT-CLOSED`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-cpu,CPU>>
|The boot strap word.
|The boot straps are tied to zero by the bench, so the captured strap word is a constant.
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_cpu_boot_regs_read_test` compares the word against the tied value and says so (`CHK-BOOT-STRAP-WORD`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|The CLA cross-trigger input and the timestamp capture of `CDbgClaTimestampConfig`.
|`xtrigger_ss_i` is tied to 0 at the DUT instance in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`, and the cross-trigger input is the only trigger of the capture bit (`integration/rdl/smc/dfd_cla.rdl`, `CDbgClaTimestampConfig`).
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_dfd_cla_mmr_sweep_test` sweeps the register and leaves the capture register and the capture bit unexercised.
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|The DFD clock gate (`DEBUG_CTRL.cg_en`, `force_clk_en`) and the cross-trigger outputs `xtrigger_ss_o`.
|No bench net observes the DFD clock, and `xtrigger_ss_o` is left unconnected in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv` (`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/dfx_ctrl_status/dfx_ctrl_status.rdl`, `DEBUG_CTRL`; `hw/sys/smc/doc/dfd.adoc`).
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_storage_test` grades the storage of the two fields only; `smc_dfx_debug_ctrl_noeffect_gate_test` grades the register accesses around the `cg_en` write and samples `tb_cla_clock_stop` and `tb_cla_halt_clock_global` with no positive control.
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|The trace accumulator's bank state, write offset and backpressure.
|No register of `integration/rdl/smc/dfd_dst.rdl` reports them; `Trdstempty` does not distinguish a stream draining into a RAM-mode sink.
|`PERMANENT-HOLE`
|`smc_dfd_trace_sink_concurrent_test` produces the boundary stimulus and claims the `Trdstempty` flag, not the bank state or the backpressure.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|`feat_ctrl` bit 37 `SMC_FUSE_TEST`.
|The bit is not consumed by SMC, so the lifecycle-gated JTAG eFuse matrix cannot observe it (Known Limitations).
|`PERMANENT-HOLE`
|`smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test` keeps the connection as a negative item.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|The eFuse sense bypass selected by `sep_security_disable_i`.
|The pin is tied to 0 on both `smc_wrapper` instances (<<smc-bench-tie-offs>>), so the bypass path of `hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc` (Security Disable Bypass Mechanism) is unreachable.
|`ADD-PORT`
|Every eFuse leaf proves the sensed path, which is the path a 0 selects; the tie-off row names the positive control that closes it.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|The raw OTP window and the eFuse macro.
|The raw OTP window has no responder on `smc_wrapper`, and an `efuse_bank_model` answers the sense (Verification Scope, Known Limitations).
|`PERMANENT-HOLE`
|No testcase exercises a permission check at the raw OTP window; `smc_efuse_bank_ctrl_window_test` grades the shim window handshake counts.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|`INTR_STATUS.LOG_WRITE_ERR`.
|The log-write AXI-Lite manager targets the wrapper's own `uart_16550` block, which ties write-error to 0 and answers every write OKAY, so no firmware-reachable stimulus raises the bit (Known Limitations).
|`PERMANENT-HOLE`
|`smc_fw_uart_log_engine_boundary_backpressure_test` logs the bit; `smc_log_engine_fetch_error_test` forces the status through `INTR_TEST` and grades the set, the interrupt line and the clear; `smc_fw_uart_log_engine_fetch_err_test` grades the fetch-error path, which has a stimulus.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|The modem-status inputs DSR, RI and DCD (`MSR` bits and their delta bits).
|`doc/integrator/meta/ocah_gpio_table.csv` pins no pad for them, so the bench has no drive and no stated level (`hw/ip/uart/uart_16550/regs/uart_16550_main.rdl`, `MSR`).
|`ADD-PORT`
|`smc_uart_spi_log_engine_test` masks every `MSR` compare to CTS and DCTS and logs the other bits; `smc_uart_reg_reset_rw_test` logs the first `MSR` read on all four instances.
|===

[[smc-vplan-phase3-proposed-drives]]
====== PROPOSED internal drives

A PROPOSED internal drive drives, forces or deposits into a net inside `smc` for
a purpose other than error injection, and it is not in
`hw/sys/smc/dv/docs/SMC_TB_ARCH.adoc` and not in `hw/sys/smc/dv/tb/tb_top.sv`. A
check that needs one is blocked. No Phase 3 entry of this plan needs one: every
force the suite uses is an error inject of <<smc-vplan-phase3-added-hooks>> (the
state-encoding and ECC injects), and the Verification Strategy admits no other
hierarchical write. The list is empty.

[[smc-vplan-phase3-oos]]
===== Out of scope

This section lists features outside Phase 3 credit. Each reason names the open
test that owns the feature, the plan that owns it, or states why no pass or fail
value exists, with the Verification Scope, Credit rules or Known Limitations
item it rests on.

[cols="2,5,8",options="header"]
|===
|Area |Feature |Reason
|<<smc-vplan-area-power,POWER>>
|OCTS pad-level protocol.
|`smc_octs_sanity_test` drives the AVSBus status CSR path and the sideband observability probe, a recorded substitute for a pad-level OCTS checker (Known Limitations); the OCTS register and count contracts are graded by `smc_octs_csr_access_test`, `smc_octs_primary_count_test` and the clock-rate cells.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|Everything behind the mandatory external AXI-Lite window (per-pad controls, the GPIO_CTRL window, the supplementary `gpio_extra_*` blocks, clock-observation and pad-bias blocks).
|Adopter implementation; this plan proves only the decode into the window (`smc_peripheral_instance_decode_test`, `smc_external_window_pad_ctrl_decode_test`, `smc_ext_window_routing_test`, `smc_gpio_ctrl_full_sweep_test`, `smc_gpio_ext_extra_decode_test`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|The DTP CSR window.
|No responder on `smc_wrapper`; the bench leaves the DTP CSR AXI-Lite response idle rather than answered by a placeholder (Verification Scope). `smc_axil_burst_idle_test` and `smc_axil_idle_test` report `dtp_csr_active` without a positive control, and `smc_peripheral_instance_decode_test` names the window as a cell not closed.
|<<smc-vplan-area-fabric,FABRIC>>
|The PLIC, CLINT and bus-error-unit windows at the reset `REGION_SIZE`.
|They lie outside the local and global apertures at the reset aperture and answer `DECERR` from the inbound port (`hw/sys/smc/doc/fabric.adoc`, Local and Remote Resource Access); `smc_region_size_plic_clint_beu_decode_test` reaches them after widening the aperture, and `smc_address_map_region_decode_test` and `smc_cluster_beu_test` take no credit for them.
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|The SMU integration of the SMC (`smu_wrapper` straps, the cool-reset pin at the SMU boundary, boundary I/O).
|The SMU plan (`hw/sys/smu/dv/docs/SMU_VPLAN.adoc`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|A warm-only reset (`rst_warm_ni` dropped without `rst_primary_ni`) and the registers it leaves intact.
|No enrolled test drops the warm reset alone (`hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`, Primary and Warm Reset); `smc_multi_reset_csr_persistence_test` states it as not claimed and leaves it to a testcase with a warm-only source (`SS_WARM_RESET_N` or the SEP watchdog pin).
|<<smc-vplan-area-reset,RESET>>
|The `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` byte-lane clear.
|An open RTL defect with a weekly `rtl_issue` reproducer (`smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test`, held out of `all`); a Known Limitations row, not a Phase 3 credit.
|<<smc-vplan-area-clock,CLOCK>>
|The adopter's PLL and PVT blocks.
|Placeholder RTL in this harness; there is no design behind the register interface (Verification Scope). The retired `smc_pll_*` and `smc_pvt_*` modules are listed in <<smc-deferred-disposition>>; `smc_temp_interrupt_test` proves the digital pin path only.
|<<smc-vplan-area-cpu,CPU>>
|The captured straps block.
|`smc_wrapper` declares no `captured_straps_i`, so there is no tap to drive; `smc_address_map_region_decode_test` reads the block and `smc_captured_straps_test` is retired (<<smc-deferred-disposition>>).
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|iJTAG (IEEE 1687) transactions.
|The bench has no iJTAG VIP; `smc_ijtag_basic_test` scans the CPU JTAG TAP and proves the surrounding CSR and AXI environment instead.
|<<smc-vplan-area-jtag,JTAG>>
|DFD fault injection from the DUT side.
|The retired `smc_dfd_dbs_fault_inject_test` latched a hardcoded capture token in TB glue; the plan takes no DFD fault-injection credit until a DUT-side observable exists (<<smc-deferred-disposition>>).
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|The eFuse macro, fuse programming and the SEP lifecycle policy behind `lc_state_i`.
|An `efuse_bank_model` answers the sense, so a storage change shows only that the controller's command reached the bank; the lifecycle policy is SEP-level verification and the bench drives the resolved state (Verification Scope). The image leaves (`smc_efuse_image_alt55_test`, `smc_efuse_image_altaa_test`, `smc_efuse_image_random_test`) and `smc_efuse_otp_burn_shadow_test` take transport and lock-enforcement credit only.
|<<smc-vplan-area-efuse,EFUSE>>
|The second lifecycle encodings 0x3 and 0x7 of RMA_SOP and RMA_CHIPLET.
|Not driven: `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test` asserts the matrix on 0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x6, 0x8 and the integrity-error row, one encoding per state (`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, Lifecycle State (LC_STATE) Effects).
|<<smc-vplan-area-irq,IRQ>>
|The cluster PLIC register file from the external port.
|The aperture accepts no writes from SEP_IN; PLIC programming is proven only by `smc_fw_plic_claim_test` on the CPU (Verification Scope, Known Limitations).
|<<smc-vplan-area-i2c,I2C>>
|The PMBus Linear11 data format.
|No document in this tree states it. `smc_smbus_pmbus_test` grades the encode and decode as a sequence self-check with no bus traffic, and `smc_smbus_pmbus_linear11_read_test` logs the decode of both words without comparing it.
|<<smc-vplan-area-i2c,I2C>>
|Recovery of a controller after an SDA interference event.
|Not claimed: `smc_i2c_controller_sda_interference_test` and `smc_i2c_controller_control_symbol_test` reset or re-enable both instances between injections and assert nothing about the transaction that follows an event (`hw/ip/i2c/doc/index.adoc`; `INTR_STATE.SDA_INTERFERENCE`).
|<<smc-vplan-area-i3c,I3C>>
|The I3C cores and the I3C protocol: CCC and IBI scenarios that need device-address-table state, the PIO and TTI queue ports and their action fields.
|No DAT/DCT RAM in `tb_top`; block-level I3C DV owns the protocol (Verification Scope). `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` is decode-only and takes no feature credit; `smc_i3c_dxt_table_test` credits the shell's table RAMs and the CSR-window path only; `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_core_test` and `smc_i3c_csr_sweep_ext_test` leave the queue ports and action fields at reset.
|<<smc-vplan-area-uart,UART>>
|UART protocol loopback and ROM firmware as feature credit.
|Credit rules: `smc_uart_loopback_test` and `smc_uart_char_loopback_test` are graded, and the ROM boot runs under `occp_rom` and <<smc-rom-dv-verification-plan>>, but neither is a feature-credit row of the Matrix.
|===


=== Formal Verification Plan

Formal property checking is not part of the SMC DV package. Every row of this plan is credited by simulation alone, and
`hw/sys/smc/dv/` carries no formal collateral: no `smc_formal_cfg.toml`
beside `smc_sim_cfg.toml`, no `testlists/formal.toml`, and no `formal/`
directory holding a property set, a bind file, a task file or a reset
environment. `python3 tools/dv/run_dv.py --validate-configs` lists no
`smc (formal)` view, `--list` shows no `fv` row for `smc`, and
`python3 tools/dv/run_dv.py --dut smc --mode formal` stops with
`formal config not found`. Hosted CI runs no formal job for any DUT
(`tools/dv/doc/run-dv.adoc`, Formal verification), so the PR gate and the
nightly and weekly tiers under Regression Groups are complete without one.
Formal verification is outside this package's scope and has no Known
Limitations row.

Adding a formal view follows `tools/dv/doc/run-dv.adoc` (Configuring a
formal view) and `hw/common/dv/docs/formal-property-style.adoc`;
`hw/sys/dtp/dv/` is the runner's reference implementation.

=== Regression Groups

[cols="1,3",options="header",]
|===
|Group |Meaning
|`smoke` |CI gate on every pull request and push (`sim.yml`): three toolchain-free bring-up leaves
|`all` |Every test this plan grades and the coverage set; `expected_count` is the membership gate. `hosted`, `fw` and `sanity` select by what a leaf builds and do not between them cover it
|`hosted` |Toolchain-free class of `all`, single-instance model; the nightly and weekly tiers on the hosted runners, one seed per leaf (`reseed: 1` in `regress.yml`)
|`fw` |Firmware class of `all`: the fifteen CPU-boot leaves whose image the `c_compile` stage builds with a picolibc-enabled RISC-V GCC or the toolchain container
|`sanity` |SMC_DUAL class of `all`: the three `target = "dual"` leaves, each loading a ROM or firmware image
|`axil`, `clock`, `combined`, `cpu`, `gpio`, `i2c`, `irq`, `reset`, `uart` |Feature subsets of `all` for a local run of one area; each lives in its feature testlist
|`occp_rom` |33 of the 34 BL0/SMC ROM cases (`smc_occp_ring_buffer_stress_test` is left out for runtime), including the hours-long dual-SMC unsecure boot; run on demand
|`occp_boot` |Runtime hold-out run on demand: the production ROM to its OCCP loop. Not in `all`
|`held_out` |Leaves waiting on an RTL fix or ruling, run on demand to re-measure. Not in `all`
|===

`README.md` owns the commands that run these groups (CI, nightly, hosted and
single-test forms). Non-ROM leaves outside `all` are defined in
`testlists/holdout.toml`; ROM/OCCP leaves are defined in
`testlists/smc_rom.toml`.


=== Signoff Package

The SMC signoff package is this book plus the tracker: the plans, contracts,
dispositions and scope exclusions below hold across candidates, and the
tracker's signoff item carries what belongs to one candidate (the commit, the
run trees it was qualified with, the open issues and their release dispositions).
Feature credit is the <<smc-scope-traceability-candidate,Scope and Traceability>> record above.

=== Release Qualification

A release candidate is qualified by regression evidence on the supported
framework and simulator pairs, graded by the runner's leaf rules and retained
with the run tree; a passing set of individual tests is not a qualification.
The runner's grading, record and CI contracts are in `tools/dv/doc/run-dv.adoc`.

[[smc-release-matrix]]
==== SMC release regression matrix

This chapter defines the mandatory qualification set: the *live* CI matrix on
Verilator — `smoke` per PR, `hosted` nightly and weekly. It is not narrowed
to a smaller tier. The leaves no tier
runs, and why, are recorded in <<smc-deferred-disposition>>.

`--dut smc` already instantiates `smc_wrapper`. There is no separate
`--dut smc_wrapper` job.

[[smc-release-combinations]]
===== Mandatory combinations

[cols="2,2,1,3",options="header",]
|===
|Tier |Command |Seeds |Blocks
|PR |`--dut smc --tool verilator --items smoke` |1 |PR merge (`sim.yml`)
|Nightly |`--dut smc --tool verilator --items hosted` |1 |Release qualification (`regress.yml`)
|Weekly |`--dut smc --tool verilator --items hosted` |1 |Dashboard (`dashboard.yml`); same group, no coverage (`coverage: false` in `regress.yml`)
|===

Group sizes are the `expected_count` guards: `all` and `hosted` in
`hw/sys/smc/dv/testlists/all.toml`.

No scheduled tier collects coverage: every SMC row of `regress.yml` carries
`coverage: false`. The coverage run of record is a developer or self-hosted
`run_dv --dut smc --items hosted fw --tool verilator --cov`, as
`SMC_FCOV.adoc` states.

[[smc-release-credit]]
===== Credit versus the CI group

`smoke` and `hosted` are debug breadth. Feature credit is the SCOPE YES rows,
not every leaf in the group. `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` is
HCI_VERSION decode (`proxy=True`) and is not in `smoke`.

The coverage gate is defined in `SMC_FCOV.adoc` (Coverage Policy); this chapter does
not absorb it.

=== Component Signoff

One subsection per signoff area. Each records the evidence contract its
scenarios meet, the negative-validation hooks that must fail a run, and the
disposition of every row whose realisation differs from its plan text.
