`allow_timeout=True` stays a reviewed exception: helpers in
`smc_csr_seq_utils.py` that set it score the timeout, and each live
call site keeps a rationale comment (README gate). Force / placeholder
paths receive no credit.

Depth groups `reset` / `clock` / `irq` remain debug breadth. They are
not an extra feature-credit set.

On Verilator and Xcelium the `ocah_prim` `prim_sync3` cell is replaced by the
behavioural stand-in in `tb/verilator_stubs/`; VCS drops it. Every leaf of
`reset.toml`, `clock.toml` and `irq.toml` has a row in the *Bench stand-ins*
section of <<smc-deferred-disposition>> stating which crossing sits on its
proof path, what its verdict reads, and its verdict on VCS with the product
cells. The PeakRDL external-ack assertions `assert_bad_ext_wr_ack` /
`assert_bad_ext_rd_ack` in `cpu_ctrl_reg`, `reset_unit_reg` and
`system_timer_octs_reg` fire once at time 0, before reset, while the ack
strobes are X; the cocotb verdicts do not depend on them, and
`smc_sim_cfg.toml` `[pass_fail]` waives that class at time 0 only.
`CheckMutualExclusionClk1` in `avsbus_controller.u_refclk_apbclk_mux`
(`prim_ag_clk_mux.sv`) fires under `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test` on VCS and
is not waived; Verilator compiles assertions out. The *Closes when* cell of the
`prim_sync2/3` control row in <<smc-deferred-disposition>> names what closes it.

The cool-reset OUT names (`smc_cool_reset_from_primary_chiplet_test`,
`smc_cool_reset_from_bmc_test`, `smc_cool_reset_x_cool_reset_test`) have rows
in <<smc-deferred-disposition>>.

[[smc-known-limitations]]
=== Known Limitations

[cols=",,",options="header",]
|===
|Limitation |Impact |Resolution Path
|At the `REGION_SIZE` reset (`0x0100_0000`) the cluster-local window `0xC800_xxxx` lies outside the local and global apertures, and an inbound SEP_IN access there answers DECERR |No access from this testbench at the reset aperture reaches a Bus Error Unit; `smc_cluster_beu_test` checks the DECERR, and `smc_region_size_plic_clint_beu_decode_test` reaches the BEUs after widening `REGION_SIZE` |By design: the SEP and SMU fabric decodes prevent such an address reaching the port. BEU behaviour needs a path that bypasses the mask
|Verilator is a 2-state simulator |Resolvability predicates (`is_resolvable`) cannot fail on a Verilator run, so X-propagation claims are not closed there |Retain a VCS or Xcelium run for the scenarios whose evidence depends on 4-state behaviour
|PLL and PVT are placeholder RTL in this harness |The PLL/PVT scenarios in the wider plan cannot be run: there is no design behind the register interface |Needs the adopter's PLL/PVT blocks integrated
|The I3C DAT/DCT RAM is not present in `tb_top` |CCC/IBI scenarios that need device-address-table state cannot run; `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` is decode-only |Add a DAT/DCT model, or drive the sequences from a full I3C host model
|The DTP CSR window has no responder |AXI-Lite accesses to it would wedge, so the boundary is left idle rather than answered by a placeholder |Connect the DTP CSR subordinate; SMU already connects the same port
|The cluster PLIC aperture (0xC400_0000) is not writable from SEP_IN AXI |No *cocotb* testcase can cover the PLIC register file from the external port: PRIORITY[1] accepts a write with OKAY and stores nothing, and the +2 MB context pages return non-OKAY. The measurement is recorded against `smc_cluster_plic_csr_test` in <<smc-deferred-disposition>>; the four register-level properties -- context independence across the eight threshold pages, source 0 and PENDING read-only, PENDING tracking a real interrupt -- need a write path. The PLIC's *function* is covered: `smc_fw_plic_claim_test` programs it from the CPU and claims through it |Expose a write path from SEP_IN, or extend the firmware image to read back what it programmed
|Verilator does not implement SV covergroups |The covergroups under `ifndef VERILATOR` in `cov/sv/` are the VCS `group` metric; on Verilator, functional coverage is the `cov/sv` cover properties in the `user` family |See `SMC_FCOV.adoc`
|`ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` clears its FLR-latched request on any write with a byte enable anywhere in the register, whatever the data (`smc_cool_reset_wrap.sv`), where `reset_unit.rdl` makes the request a `sw = rw` field at bit 0 |`smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test` shows it: a one-byte write of 0 at byte 1 clears the request. The leaf runs weekly in `rtl_issue` under `expect_fail` |Qualify the clear by bit 0's byte enable and a written 0; the leaf then moves to its feature testlist with the `ci` tag
|`smc_state_fault_inject_test` reaches the illegal eFuse and Zeroer state encodings only by forcing the state flops through the `tb_*_state_inject` hooks in `tb_top` |The stimulus is a testbench force, not a product-port access. The leaf runs in `all` and `hosted` and scores the DUT's reaction over the CSRs, so its PASS is evidence for the fail-closed behaviour and not for the reachability of an illegal encoding from any port |Reach an illegal encoding from a product port, or accept the force as the only stimulus for this property, recorded here
|The test modules the retired-module table in <<smc-deferred-disposition>> lists are out of the tree |Their blockers are outside the test: adopter placeholder PLL/PVT RTL, a wrapper pin that does not exist, an idle DTP boundary, a PLIC aperture SEP_IN cannot write, a CLINT window SEP_IN cannot reach, TB glue, or a pad-level VIP the bench lacks. The retired-module table in <<smc-deferred-disposition>> names the blocker per row |Clear the blocker named in the row; the module is restored from git history
|The raw OTP window has no responder on `smc_wrapper` |No testcase exercises a permission check at the raw OTP window -- the OTP bank itself, as distinct from the eFuse-shim CSR window `smc_efuse_chip_config_read_test_seq` reads over SEP_IN and the JTAG access-control path `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test` drives. `smc_efuse_permission_boundary_test` stays on the CSR side of the eFuse boundary and claims only the chip-config reads it makes. The permission semantics this bench can reach are covered elsewhere: `smc_efuse_jtag_lc_access_matrix_test` (lifecycle-gated JTAG-side access) and `smc_efuse_locked_access_interrupt_test` (locked-shadow access) |Add a raw-OTP responder to the bench, or assign the raw OTP permission path to the eFuse block-level TB
|`smc_octs_sanity_test` carries an OCTS name but drives the AVSBus status CSR path and the sideband observability probe |Its PASS is evidence for the AVS status window decode and the bench sideband probes, not for any OCTS register or pad; its protocol-VIP record is booked as a proxy. OCTS is covered by `smc_octs_dual_sync_test` (`dual`) and `smc_fw_octs_p0_primary_test` (`fw`) |Rename the leaf to what it drives, or give it OCTS stimulus and re-review the card
|`feat_ctrl` bit 37 `SMC_FUSE_TEST` is not consumed by SMC |The lifecycle-gated JTAG eFuse matrix cannot observe that bit; the connection stays a negative item |Cover the bit once SMC consumes it
|UART0 transmits two stop bits for a 5-bit word with `LCR.STB` set, where `uart_16550_main.rdl` describes 1.5 |`smc_uart_baud_word_parity_format_test` measures the frame length on the TX pad for every format; for the two 5-bit `STB = 1` formats it admits either 1.5 or 2 stop bits, records which one was measured, and so does not claim the RDL count for them (one stop bit still fails). Every other format is held to the RDL count |Fix the transmitter or the RDL description, then drop the admitted alternative so the two formats are held to one count
|`INTR_STATUS.LOG_WRITE_ERR` has no firmware-reachable stimulus in this wrap |The log-write AXI-Lite master targets the wrapper's own `uart_16550` block, which ties write-error to 0 and answers every write OKAY. `smc_fw_uart_log_engine_boundary_backpressure_test` covers length and TX backpressure only; `INTR_TEST.LOG_WRITE_ERR` proves the interrupt plumbing, not error detection |A bench-side fault injector on the log-write AXI-Lite B channel
|A force-mode CPU reset withdraws the R beat the CPU is presenting to the front-port demux without `ready` (`cocotb/seq_lib/README_cpu_isolate_flush.md`) |`smc_cpu_l2_read_wedge_test` reaches that state on purpose, and the front-port R arbiter's request-stability assertions (`rr_arb_tree` `req1` and `lock_req`) report the withdrawal on the reset cycle. The leaf passes `+smc_front_port_r_arb_assertoff` and `tb_top` holds off that one arbiter instance's assertions for that leaf only; every other leaf keeps them, and the leaf's five checkers are unchanged |A CPU reset cannot preserve a beat the fabric side has stopped accepting, and the design owner records this as a limitation of force mode rather than a defect. Re-arm the checks if force mode ever holds or flushes the beat under `ready`
|===

[[smc-held-out-testcases]]
==== Held-out testcases

Every leaf defined in `testlists/holdout.toml`, plus the hours-long
`smc_occp_dual_unsecure_boot_test` defined in `testlists/smc_rom.toml`.
None is a member of `all`; each card below states what a run of the leaf must
show and records no pass.

The `sanity` group is held out for a different reason, and keeps its cards
with the feature areas it exercises rather than below. Its three leaves --
`smc_dual_elaboration_test`, `smc_dual_axi_sram_probe_test` and
`smc_occp_sanity_test` -- elaborate `[targets.dual]`, while the rest of `all`
elaborates `[targets.default]`. A regression that collects coverage builds one
target per run, so a selection spanning both cannot be graded in one pass and
the dual leaves are measured by selecting `sanity`. They are not waiting on a
defect or a ruling: each passes on the dual bench. Issue #2479 tracks giving
the package regression both elaborations, and these three rejoin `all` when it
closes.

The reproducers are the `rtl_issue` group:

Tests whose job is to fail. Each holds the runnable evidence for one RTL
defect, so the defect has a measurement rather than a description alone. All
are enrolled through `rtl_issue` in `testlists/holdout.toml` -- no `ci` tag, not
in `smoke`, `hosted` or `all`. Every `[[tests]]` entry carries `expect_fail` naming the issue and
`expect_fail_match` pinned to the assertion it raises; the weekly tier runs
the group on its own `regress.yml` row and grades the recorded failure as
PASS, so the row goes red (`expected_fail_passed`) the week a defect is
fixed and the leaf moves to its feature testlist. The member is
`smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test` (the `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` byte-lane clear).

Every one carries an arm leg that must pass before its defect leg is scored.
Without that, a stuck-at field or a dead probe would satisfy the defect leg for
the wrong reason.

[[sec-293-smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test]]
===== 293 `smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test`

*BFM / Model*: `tb_cfg_flr_pf_active` raises the request; observation on `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG`

*Objective*: Writes to `ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG` that do not clear bit 0 must leave the FLR-latched request set.

*Test Coverage*:

* `reset_unit.rdl` makes `isolate_req_smc_reg` a single `sw = rw` field at bit 0, set by hardware when `cfg_flr_pf_active` rises and de-asserted by software. A write that does not select its byte lane cannot change it, and a write of 1 keeps it at 1.
* Arm leg: with the FLR counters at their reset value of 0, raising `cfg_flr_pf_active` sets the request without starting the cool-reset sequence, and bit 0 must read 1.
* Defect leg: a one-byte write of 0 at byte 1 must leave the request reading 1, and then a write of 1 to bit 0 must leave it reading 1.
* On this RTL the first write clears the request. `smc_cool_reset_wrap.sv` clears it on `isolate_req_smc_reg_wr_en && (|hwif_out.ISOLATE_REQ_SMC_REG.wr_biten)`, the byte enables of the whole external register, and ignores the write data.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_isolate_req_smc_lane_test_seq`. Each checker below is a named compare the DUT can fail; a token is emitted only after that compare holds.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-ISOLATE-REQ-SMC-LANE` |The FLR-latched request stayed set across a one-byte write of 0 at byte 1 and a write of 1 to bit 0
|===

*Pass Criteria*: fails on this RTL; enrolled in `rtl_issue` with `expect_fail`, not in `all`. The weekly tier grades the recorded failure as PASS and turns red the week the clear is qualified by bit 0's byte enable and a written 0.
'''''
[[sec-161-smc_occp_dual_unsecure_boot_test]]
===== 161 `smc_occp_dual_unsecure_boot_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_occp_dual_unsecure_boot_test`

*BFM / Model*: no model on either side -- `u_bfm` runs the `occp_unsecure_boot_test` DV ROM image against `u_dut` running the production boot ROM

*Objective*: OCCP unsecure boot end to end between two real SMCs over the shared I3C bus.

*Test Coverage*:

* Payload staging into the controller's scratch SRAM over its inbound AXI manager.
* The scratch 5-8 host protocol between testbench and controller firmware.
* ENTDAA, chunked OCCP `WRITE`s and the `JUMP`, firmware to firmware.
* Real traffic on the shared I3C bus, counted by the testbench rather than reported by firmware.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Hold the controller parked on its target-ready handshake so the staging window stays open.
. Draw the staging address and the transfer destination per run from the OCCP window, so honouring the WRITE address field and always writing from the bottom of the window are distinguishable.
. Stage the payload over AXI, seed scratch 5-8, and release both CPUs.
. Wait for the target ROM to reach its OCCP command loop, then let the controller drive the transfer and the JUMP.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-OCCP-TARGET-READY` |Target ROM is in its OCCP command loop, by POST code and trace
|`CHK-OCCP-PRECONDITION` |Target scratch 0 does not already hold the pass value before the transfer
|`CHK-OCCP-FW-SEED` |Controller RNG seeded from `RANDOM_SEED` and read back
|`CHK-OCCP-PAYLOAD-STAGED` |The payload reads back from the controller's SRAM exactly as staged
|`CHK-OCCP-HOST-PROTOCOL` |Controller scratch 5-8 reads back exactly as seeded
|`CHK-OCCP-TRANSFER-LANDED` |Target SRAM at the drawn destination holds the transferred image -- first and last word, read through the `smc_scratch_map_pkg` backdoor that `smc_dual_axi_sram_probe_test` holds against AXI. Raises on a mismatch
|`CHK-OCCP-BUS-ACTIVITY` |At least one I3C channel saw both an SCL fall and a START condition during the transfer, counted by the testbench rather than reported by firmware. Requiring the START rules out a clocking artefact moving `scl_falls` without a framed transfer
|`CHK-OCCP-CONTROLLER-NO-FAIL` |Controller scratch 0 is not `TEST_FAIL`
|`CHK-OCCP-JUMP-EXECUTED` |Target retired PC lands inside the transferred image
|`CHK-OCCP-PAYLOAD-EXECUTED` |Target scratch 0 holds `TEST_PASS`, written by the payload
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all ten checkers hold after their compares -- `CHK-OCCP-TARGET-READY`, `CHK-OCCP-PRECONDITION`, `CHK-OCCP-FW-SEED`, `CHK-OCCP-PAYLOAD-STAGED`, `CHK-OCCP-HOST-PROTOCOL`, `CHK-OCCP-TRANSFER-LANDED`, `CHK-OCCP-BUS-ACTIVITY`, `CHK-OCCP-CONTROLLER-NO-FAIL`, `CHK-OCCP-JUMP-EXECUTED`, `CHK-OCCP-PAYLOAD-EXECUTED`. The payload destination is whatever `pick_payload_addresses` draws for that seed; the landing check compares first and last word at that drawn address.

`CHK-OCCP-TRANSFER-LANDED` depends on `smc_scratch_map_pkg` decoding the drawn destination the same way `smc_dual_axi_sram_probe_test` holds against AXI. `pick_payload_addresses` draws from anywhere in the OCCP window, so the peek is almost never reading offset 0, and a decode right only for the first 256 bytes of the window would look in the wrong bank. The six-offset agreement in `smc_dual_axi_sram_probe_test` is what makes the checker able to raise.

Held out of `all` on runtime (hours of wall clock per run). Enrolled in: `occp_rom` only -- held out of `all` on runtime and run on demand as `occp_rom` (see <<smc-held-out-testcases>>). This card records what a run must show, not a pass.

'''''



[[sec-162-smc_prod_rom_occp_ready_test]]
===== 162 `smc_prod_rom_occp_ready_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_prod_rom_occp_ready_test`

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI); production boot ROM built with `I3C_CORE=chipsalliance`

*Objective*: Production boot ROM reaches its OCCP command processing loop.

*Test Coverage*:

* The real ROM from reset through strap and fuse read, security checks, interface map and OCCP init.
* No bus traffic and no controller: this is the single-instance precondition the OCCP boot tests build on.

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Run with `+rom_bin64=prod_rom.bin64` and `+smc_hold_cpu_boot`, holding `boot_stall` from t=0.
. Program `RESET_VECTOR` before any core fetches, then release.
. Read the ROM's POST code from scratch 1 and require boot phase `[31:28]` to reach `OCCP_PROC`.
. Cross-check against CPU ROM fetch activity, so the phase cannot be credited to anything but the ROM executing.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PROD-ROM-OCCP-PROC` |POST code reaches the OCCP command loop, corroborated by ROM fetch activity
|===

*Pass Criteria*: the POST code reaches `OCCP_PROC` and ROM fetch activity corroborates it. Real fuse sense is used -- no `+skip_fuse_sense` -- so the ROM reads straps and fuses itself. Enrolled in: `occp_boot` only -- held out of `all` on runtime and run on demand as `occp_boot` (see <<smc-held-out-testcases>>). This card records what a run must show, not a pass.

'''''

[[sec-325-smc_fw_i3c5_csr_access_test]]
===== 325 `smc_fw_i3c5_csr_access_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_fw_i3c5_csr_access_test`

*BFM / Model*: the SMC C image `fw/tests/i3c5_csr_access`, executed by hart 0 of the CPU cluster; verdict, published values and `HC_CONTROL` read over SEP_IN AXI; per-instance access counters on the I3C cores' CSR ports published by `tb_top`

*Objective*: The SMC CPU reads `HCI_VERSION` and `HC_CONTROL` in the CSR window of I3C instance 5 and sets and restores `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE`; the accesses are counted at the I3C cores' CSR ports.

*Test Coverage*:

* The CPU's path to the sixth I3C instance, at `SMC_TOP_OCA_I3C_WRAP_I3C_CSR_BASE_ADDR(5)` = `0xC003F000`. `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` reads the same registers on instance 0 from SEP_IN, and `smc_i3c_dxt_table_test` reaches the tables of all six instances from SEP_IN; neither starts from the cluster.
* Values: the image reads `HCI_VERSION`, `HC_CONTROL` at entry, `HC_CONTROL` after a store of `BUS_ENABLE`, and `HC_CONTROL` after a store of the entry word. It requires the reset words and the `BUS_ENABLE` mask that the generated `oca_i3c_wrap.h` field macros give, addresses each register through its generated `SMC_TOP_OCA_I3C_WRAP_I3C_CSR_I3CBASE_*_BASE_ADDR(5)` macro, and publishes each value in CPU_CTRL `SCRATCH_4`..`SCRATCH_7`. The bench compares the published values against the resets and the `BUS_ENABLE` field it parses from the vendor `base_registers.rdl` (`HCI_VERSION` `0x120`; `HC_CONTROL` `0x40`, `BUS_ENABLE` bit 31), not against the image's constants.
* Access count: `tb_i3c_csr_read_count` and `tb_i3c_csr_write_count` count R and B handshakes at each I3C core's AXI-Lite port, after the wrapper's instance decode. The bench issues no I3C access between release and PASS, so instance 5 must take exactly the image's four reads and two writes and the other five instances none. A wrong stride or base in the decode, or an access absorbed before the core, changes the count. Before release, one SEP_IN read of `HCI_VERSION` per instance must advance each instance's read counter by one, so the zeros on instances 0-4 come from counters shown to count. A SEP_IN read of `HC_CONTROL` after PASS must advance instance 5's read counter by one, which shows the counter counts.
* No I3C bus protocol claim: `BUS_ENABLE` is set and cleared with no transfer queued.
* Held out on this RTL. The CPU cluster's MMIO port address set (`chipyard.harness.TestHarness.OCAH4CORECluster.dts`, `mmio-port-axi4` ranges, and the matching decode in `OCAH4CORECluster_PMAChecker.sv`) covers `0xC0002000`-`0xC003EFFF` and resumes at `0xC0160000`, so `0xC003F000`-`0xC003FFFF` reaches neither the port nor the relocated error device. A CPU load from `HCI_VERSION` therefore takes a load access fault, the trap handler posts `TEST_FAIL`, and no access reaches any I3C core. SEP_IN reaches instance 5 (`smc_i3c_dxt_table_test`).

*Test Procedure*:

[arabic]
. Build `i3c5_csr_access` through `[c_build.default]`, stage `i3c5_csr_access.ecc.hex` beside the simulator, and hold `boot_stall` from t=0 (`+smc_hold_cpu_boot`).
. With the cores held, clear CPU_CTRL `SCRATCH_4`..`SCRATCH_7` and read each clear back. Read `HCI_VERSION` over SEP_IN once on each of the six instances against its RDL reset and require each instance's read counter to advance by exactly one and every write counter to stay put; log the per-instance deltas. Then sample the counters as the baseline for the firmware's accesses.
. Clear CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0, program the reset vector, and release the cores and `boot_stall`. The image reads `HCI_VERSION` and `HC_CONTROL`, stores `HC_CONTROL` with `BUS_ENABLE` set, fences and reads it back, stores the entry word, fences and reads it back, publishing each value read and failing on any mismatch.
. Poll SCRATCH_0 for the PASS magic, failing on `TEST_FAIL`, on the `0xBAD0_xxxx` namespace, and on the bound expiring.
. Sample the counters again and compare the per-instance deltas. Read `SCRATCH_4`..`SCRATCH_7` and compare them against the RDL. Read instance 5's `HC_CONTROL` over SEP_IN against its reset word and check that its read counter advanced by one.
. Whether the sequence passes or fails, log the per-instance access counts since the cores were released.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-FW-I3C5-CSR-COUNTER-PROBE` |Before release, one SEP_IN read of `HCI_VERSION` on each I3C instance advanced that instance's read counter by exactly one and no write counter, so all six counters count
|`CHK-FW-I3C5-CSR-BOOT` |The firmware's own PASS word is read back from CPU_CTRL SCRATCH_0 after a cleared-and-verified start. The image posts it only when every value it read matched
|`CHK-FW-I3C5-CSR-ACCESS-COUNT` |Between release and PASS the I3C cores' CSR ports completed four reads and two writes on instance 5 and none on instances 0 to 4
|`CHK-FW-I3C5-HCI-VERSION` |The `HCI_VERSION` value the CPU read and published equals the `base_registers.rdl` reset `0x120`
|`CHK-FW-I3C5-HC-CONTROL-BUS-ENABLE` |The `HC_CONTROL` values the CPU read at entry, after setting `BUS_ENABLE` and after the restore equal the RDL reset word, that word with `BUS_ENABLE` set, and the reset word; SEP_IN reads the reset word after PASS and instance 5's read counter advances by that one read
|===

*Pass Criteria*: all five checkers hold after their compares and every sequence assert holds. No `ci` tag: the hosted runners have no RISC-V toolchain. Enrolled in: `held_out` only -- out of `all` until the cluster's MMIO port covers the window (<<smc-scheduled-holdouts>>). This card records what a run must show, not a pass.

'''''

`smc_ref_clock_timer_rate_test` has an entry in `holdout.toml` and no card: it
fails the rate comparison it was written to make (`clk_rst.adoc` places the OCTS
system timer in the reference clock domain; `smc_peripherals.sv` clocks it from
`clk_smc_i`), and is re-measured on demand.

===== SV-UVM held-out scenarios

UVM-only leaves are enrolled in scope-named groups of `testlists/holdout.toml`
and run on demand with `--framework uvm --tool vcs`. They have no cocotb
realization.

[[sec-smc_regblock_sparse_strobe_test]]
====== `smc_regblock_sparse_strobe_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_regblock_sparse_strobe_test` (UVM-only independent scenario)

*BFM / Model*: ocah_axi_vip (AXI, SEP_IN); `smc_regblock_wide_ref_model`
predicts each read from accepted writes and generated RW masks, and predicts
an OKAY response for every catalogued read and write.

*Objective*: Single-byte, non-contiguous and null write strobes update exactly
the strobed RW bytes of selected 64-bit register-block words.

*Test Coverage*:

* Seven side-effect-free 64-bit words: Zeroer `DEST_ADDR` and `SIZE`, the three
  hang-detector timeout thresholds, and alias-remap region 0 `REGION_START`
  and `REGION_END`.
* Before any write, the Zeroer must be idle and the hang detectors and alias
  region disabled, so writes to catalogued words have no other effect.
* Per word: baseline read, full write, one single-byte write, fixed and seeded
  non-contiguous strobes, a null-strobe write and a restore, each followed by
  a predicted read. Passes 0 to 3 use all-ones, all-zeros, `0x55` and `0xAA`
  data; later passes use seeded data.
* Every SEP_IN byte lane is strobed at least once across the selected words.
* A passive Zeroer busy-sample count remains unchanged throughout the catalogued
  operations, including a clock-sampled busy pulse that ends before the final
  status read.

*Expectation Sources*: The catalogued words use the generated field masks and
defaults. The generated implementations of Zeroer, SMC base-config and
alias-remap drive `cpuif_wr_err = '0`, so writes reaching these register blocks
do not produce a register-block write error. This does not define the response
of an access rejected earlier in the fabric.
`zeroer_ctrl.rdl` defines DEST_ADDR and SIZE as the command address and byte count;
writing CTRL_STATUS triggers the command. The passive busy tap observes execution;
it is not a software-visible register interface.

*Test Procedure*:

Drive `smc_regblock_sparse_strobe_test_seq`. The safe-state reads run before
the first write. The sequence applies the full, single-byte, sparse, null and
restore operations to each catalogued word, requires no Zeroer busy or unknown
value sampled on a rising SMC clock edge from before the first catalogued
operation through the final status read, checks Zeroer state and lane
coverage, runs a real one-word Zeroer command to SPM after the no-start check
and requires the busy sample count to increase. It reads back DEST_ADDR and
SIZE after their control restore writes in every pass, waits with a bound
for all predicted comparisons, then checks scoreboard results and access
counts.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-BASELINE` |Each word reads its reset value before the first write
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-FULL-RW` |A full-strobe write updates exactly the RW bits
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-SINGLE-BYTE` |A single-byte write changes only the RW bits of that lane
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-SPARSE` |A non-contiguous strobe changes only the RW bits of the strobed lanes
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-NULL-STROBE` |A write with no strobed lane changes nothing
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-RESTORE` |Each word reads its reset value after the restore write
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-RESTORE-NONVAC` |At least one restore per pass changes an RW value
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-NO-ZEROER-START` |No rising SMC clock edge samples busy or X/Z during the catalogued operations; the busy tap and final `CTRL_STATUS.STATUS` are idle
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-ZEROER-BUSY-CONTROL` |A real one-word Zeroer START changes the known busy sample count in the same pass
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-LANE-COVERAGE` |All eight SEP_IN byte lanes were strobed
|`CHK-SB-REGBLOCK-WIDE` |Each catalogued read and write returns OKAY; each read also matches the passive model's predicted 64-bit value
|`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-SCOREBOARD` |Every predicted read and write was compared with no new mismatch
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The number of SEP_IN accesses equals the declared scenario
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY`, `CHK-MEM-RESP`, `CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |Scenario volume, frontdoor responses and bring-up completed as declared
|===

*Known Limitations*:

The claim covers the seven selected words under the safe-state preconditions.
The busy observation is clock-sampled; it does not grade sub-cycle glitches.
After the absence check, a bounded positive control uses the last aligned SPM
word as scratch. No CPU or other initiator may use that word during the pass.
It is left zero through a SEP_IN write that also updates the SPM model; its
initial SRAM contents are not read or restored. DEST_ADDR and SIZE return to
their reset values and are read back within the same pass. The control does
not grade the Zeroer's zeroed payload.
It excludes registers whose writes change decode, gating, reset, lock or other
operational state. `RESET_VECTOR_0` through `RESET_VECTOR_3` are excluded
because a later core reset that does not also assert warm reset can consume a
test pattern as a boot address. `DFX_CTRL.DEBUG_CTRL` is excluded because its
field behavior is outside this CSR byte-enable claim.
The scenario does not induce a non-OKAY response from the catalogued blocks.
The response negative proves the response comparison can fail, not how the model
handles a real error response; the error-read path has no directed run here.

*Pass Criteria*: all checks hold on every pass;
`+SMC_REGBLOCK_WIDE_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must fail `regblock_wide`
read comparisons: 59 read mismatches per pass, with writes unaffected.
`+SMC_REGBLOCK_WIDE_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` corrupts the sequence's
full-write, no-start and busy-control expectations and must fail seven
`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-FULL-RW` records and one
`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-NO-ZEROER-START` record and one
`CHK-REGBLOCK-WIDE-ZEROER-BUSY-CONTROL` record per pass (nine failures per pass),
while the scoreboard records no mismatch.
`+SMC_REGBLOCK_WIDE_RESPONSE_NEGATIVE`, used alone, changes only predicted
write responses to SLVERR and must fail every catalogued write comparison and
no read comparison: 54 write mismatches per pass (35 base writes, 15 fixed
sparse writes and four positive-control writes).
The positive run requires 113 comparisons per pass (59 reads and 54 writes).
With 16 passes, the sequence negative requires 144 checker failures and the
response negative requires 864 write mismatches; the scoreboard negative
requires 944 read mismatches. A separate local mutation
holding the busy tap or sample counter at zero must fail the busy-control
check even with the sequence negative disabled. Control completion and
safe-state prerequisites are outside the expectation-inverting negative.
The sequence and end-of-run scoreboard summary also report those mismatches.
Enrolled only in `csr_uvm_extended`, outside `all`, `hosted` and `ci`;
run on demand. This card records what a run must show, not a pass.

'''''

[[sec-smc_wdt_feed_zerocmp_test]]
====== `smc_wdt_feed_zerocmp_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_feed_zerocmp_test` (UVM-only independent scenario)

*BFM / Model*: `ocah_axi_vip` on SEP_IN. The passive
`smc_wdt_csr_ref_model` predicts CTRL (IP masked), KEY and CMP from observed
writes and predicts OKAY responses for in-scope reads and writes.
The sequence checks running-count behavior; timing bounds use the count rate
measured in the same pass.

*Objective*: Check keyed FEED clearing, rejection of the selected one-bit-invalid
FEED value, unlock consumption, scaled count, sampled compare rollover and software
clearing of the pending interrupt.

*Test Coverage*:

* Cores 0 through 3 rotate by pass; exercising all four requires four passes.
* Correct and one-bit-invalid FEED writes from a known COUNT, with KEY readbacks.
* SCALED_COUNT bracketed by COUNT readings with scale four and no 16-bit wrap.
* Eight COUNT samples spanning at least two compare periods with zerocmp enabled.
* Pending interrupt below CMP, above CMP, after clearing while elapsed remains
  asserted, preserved across FEED before software clearing, and cleared while
  elapsed is low.

*Expectation Sources*: `wdt.rdl` defines effective byte enables and unlock
consumption in its addrmap description. KEY defines the unlock magic and readback;
FEED defines the clearing magic, unlock requirement and preservation of pending IP.
CTRL.wdogscale and SCALED_COUNT define the count shift; CTRL.wdogzerocmp defines
COUNT reset when compare is reached. CTRL.wdogip0 defines hardware setting while
the compare condition holds and software clearing below compare. CMP defines the
comparison value. The passive model predicts CTRL, KEY and CMP under these rules;
register offsets, field masks and reset values come from generated collateral.
`hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc` describes the KEY/relock and byte-enable rules,
interrupt setting at or above CMP, and preservation of pending IP across FEED.

*Test Procedure*: Measure a positive running count rate. Exercise valid and invalid
FEED writes and their unlock consumption, bracket SCALED_COUNT, then sample COUNT
with zerocmp enabled. Disable zerocmp and bracket every interrupt observation with
COUNT readings on the intended side of CMP and below the 16-bit wrap limit.
Read CTRL after FEED and before each interrupt-clear phase to require that FEED
preserves pending IP, independently of the subsequent software clear.
Read CMP after each CMP write. Finally feed the watchdog, disable counting and
restore CMP. Wait with a bound for all predicted comparisons, then check exact
access and comparison counts with no new mismatch.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-RATE` |Calibration has increasing count and timestamps
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-CLEAR` |The FEED magic clears the known count within the measured time bound
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-REJECT` |The selected one-bit-invalid FEED does not decrease COUNT
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-SCALED` |Scaled count lies between shifted surrounding COUNT readings
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-ZEROCMP` |All samples are at or below CMP and an observed sample decreases
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-IP` |Interrupt observations match the compare condition, remain set after FEED and match the software-clear phases
|`CHK-WDT-FEED-WINDOW` |Scaling, sample span, deadline and eight COUNT brackets are valid
|`CHK-SB-WDT-CSR` |In-scope watchdog accesses return OKAY; CTRL (IP masked), KEY and CMP reads match the passive model
|`CHK-WDT-CSR-SCOREBOARD` |Each pass completes exactly the predicted comparisons with no new mismatch
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |Completed passes reach the minimum feature comparison count
|`CHK-NONVAC` |The sequence completes 85 fixed SEP_IN CSR accesses plus every compare-poll read; this checks stimulus accounting, not passive bus activity
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE`, `CHK-CSR-RESP` |Bring-up and frontdoor responses complete
|===

*Known Limitations*: Only one invalid FEED and one non-zero scale are checked.
Zerocmp is sampled, not checked on every clock; sampling phase can hide a rollover,
which is reported as a failure with timestamps rather than silently adjusting delay.
Locked FEED, watchdog reset outputs and CPU interrupt
delivery are outside this scenario.
Count-rate calibration does not independently grade clock frequency.
The feature assumes sequential WDT accesses and no writer other than SEP_IN.
Narrow or 64-bit reads are excluded. COUNT, COUNT_HI, SCALED_COUNT and FEED
read data are not graded; CTRL IP remains a sequence check. Locked writes,
incomplete strobes and mid-run warm reset are not exercised. Software uncore
reset and reset with outstanding WDT traffic are unsupported. Idle warm-reset
re-baselining is not validated.

*Pass Criteria*: Every checker passes on each pass.
`+SMC_WDT_FEED_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` changes expectations only and fails exactly one
record each of `CHK-WDT-FEED-CLEAR`,
`CHK-WDT-FEED-REJECT`, `CHK-WDT-FEED-SCALED`,
`CHK-WDT-FEED-ZEROCMP`, and three records of `CHK-WDT-FEED-IP` per pass:
seven failed records per pass in total.
The scoreboard records no mismatch in the sequence negative.
Used alone, `+SMC_WDT_CSR_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` corrupts predicted CTRL/KEY/CMP
read bit 0 and predicts SLVERR for writes: 61 feature mismatches per pass
(19 reads and 42 writes), plus one CHK-WDT-CSR-SCOREBOARD failure per pass.
The 24 fixed response-only reads and compare-poll reads still pass.
Positive runs complete 85 fixed comparisons plus poll reads per pass.
No directed run produces a real WDT error response; the negative validates
comparison sensitivity, not real error-response handling.
RATE and WINDOW remain unmodified in the negative run: they establish valid
measurement conditions, and a failed condition records FAIL then terminates
the pass with a fatal error.
The leaf runs on demand in `wdt_uvm_extended`, outside `all`, `hosted` and `ci`.

'''''

[[sec-smc_mailbox_cool_reset_recovery_test]]
====== `smc_mailbox_cool_reset_recovery_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_mailbox_cool_reset_recovery_test` (SV-UVM only)

*Objective*: A cool reset clears occupied mailbox FIFO state, sticky errors,
interrupt enables, thresholds and latched interrupt status; fresh traffic
recovers without returning a pre-reset word.

*BFM / Model*: Existing SEP_IN `ocah_axi_vip` and required `mailbox_fifo`
feature. The request-derived model predicts paired queues, ERROR, IRQEN,
thresholds, STATUS and read/write responses. IRQS data is checked by the
sequence at designated milestones, not predicted by the model.

*Test Coverage*: Two distinct mailbox pairs per pass, including pair 0 and
the last pair in fixed pass slots. A holds two forward words and one reverse
word; B holds one forward word. Overflow on A-out and underflow on B-in set
errors. IRQEN differs from reset on A-out/B-in and both thresholds differ
on A-out. IRQS on A-out is required non-zero. Other ports' default readbacks
are consistency checks, not discriminating reset evidence.

*Expectation Sources*: `axil_mailbox.rdl` supplies field masks, defaults,
read-clear ERROR, threshold clamping and write-one-clear IRQS.
`hw/ip/axi_lite_mailbox_unit/doc/architecture.adoc` defines paired FIFO
semantics, SLVERR on full writes/empty reads, and reset clearing queues,
thresholds, errors and interrupt state/enables. `clk_rst.adoc` defines
cool reset as a primary-reset source. Integration evidence for mailbox
primary reset is `smc_internal_regs.sv`, `u_smc_axil_mailbox.rst_ni`;
this reset-domain connection is taken from RTL, not independently specified
for the mailbox by name. Geometry comes from `smc_pkg` and generated addresses.

*Test Procedure*: Require the mailbox gate disabled and six-register default
baselines on both ports of both pairs. Fill A's forward queue, provoke the
overflow and underflow, and read ERROR as a positive control; recreate both
errors without reading ERROR again, then load A's reverse and B's forward
queues. Program/read back IRQEN and clamped thresholds; require populated
STATUS and non-zero IRQS. Drain comparisons, pulse cool reset and wait for
primary/warm release and fuse readiness. Read six default registers on all
four ports before three formerly occupied directions are probed empty.
Transfer four fresh words, check their identity and modeled full payload,
then flush, clear errors, restore IRQEN/thresholds, acknowledge IRQS and
read back all six registers. Bounds are bench limits, not device latency contracts.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-MBX-RST-PRE` |Default baseline, clock-gate scope and discriminating pre-reset DUT state hold; failures stop the run
|`CHK-MBX-RST-ASSERTED`, `CHK-MBX-RST-RELEASED` |Primary and warm reset reach both requested levels within bounds
|`CHK-MBX-RST-EPOCH` |One cool reset and no cold reset occur
|`CHK-MBX-RST-DEFAULTS` |Six generated defaults match on all four ports after reset
|`CHK-MBX-RST-EMPTY` |Three formerly occupied queues return one known SLVERR response without timeout
|`CHK-MBX-RST-RECOVERY` |Four fresh returned words carry the expected identity or payload
|`CHK-MBX-RST-CLEAN` |Six register defaults match on all four ports after cleanup
|`CHK-MBX-RST-SCOREBOARD` |No new mailbox comparison mismatch
|`CHK-SB-MAILBOX-FIFO` |Required feature has activity, no mismatch and no unpaired item
|`CHK-NONVAC` |141 mailbox memory accesses/comparisons and one clock-gate CSR read per pass
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY`, `CHK-MEM-RESP`, `CHK-CSR-RESP`, `CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |Prior-pass activity, access responses and bring-up complete
|===

*Known Limitations*: No AXI transaction remains outstanding through reset.
Only sequential aligned full-width/full-strobe accesses from SEP_IN are
supported; another mailbox accessor is excluded. Unsupported accesses in the
mailbox window stop the required feature. Mailbox clock gating, cold-only or
warm-only reset, FLR and interrupt wires are not exercised. IRQS exact bits
and timing before reset are not modeled; only non-zero pre-reset and default
post-reset/cleanup values are checked by the sequence. The last pre-reset
ERROR state is inferred from a repeated SLVERR access after its read-clear
positive control, not read directly. Thresholds and IRQEN are discriminating
only on the stated ports. FIFO occupancy evidence combines accepted pushes
and STATUS, which has no numeric level field. Data X/Z is checked through
the active read helper, not the passive model.
The cleanup flush acts on FIFOs that recovery has already drained. Its response
is checked, but its state-clearing effect and the model's flush behavior are
not independently validated by this scenario.

*Pass Criteria*: All required checks pass. Used alone,
`+SMC_MAILBOX_RESET_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` changes 24 DEFAULTS, three EMPTY and
four RECOVERY expectations per pass: 31 failures/pass or 496 for sixteen
passes, without model mismatch or UVM_FATAL. PRE, reset transitions/epoch,
CLEAN, NONVAC and response-validity prerequisites are not corrupted.
Used alone, `+SMC_MAILBOX_FIFO_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` corrupts every emitted
mailbox prediction's response (OKAY and SLVERR exchange), and defined
successful read data, without modifying shadow. It must produce 141
mismatches/pass, one scenario scoreboard failure/pass and one final
`CHK-SB-MAILBOX-FIFO` failure: 2273 errors for sixteen passes. The two
negative controls are mutually exclusive. Reset-shadow mutation is a local,
uncommitted validation experiment, not an enrolled test or persistent knob.
The leaf runs only on demand in `mailbox_uvm_extended`.

'''''

[[sec-smc_fabric_reg_clock_gate_test]]
====== `smc_fabric_reg_clock_gate_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_fabric_reg_clock_gate_test` (SV-UVM only)

*Objective*: Check enable-to-domain mapping and traffic-bearing CSR wake through
the filter/remapper register clock gates, independently of datapath wake.

*Test Coverage*: Six enables control eight observed domains while idle.
Five register domains each receive a write and a read starting with the gate
closed. Disabled controls, bounded closure with H programmed to 8 and 0,
register data, response and restore are graded. Closure latency and its
dependence on H are observed, not graded. Maximum hysteresis is observed only.

*BFM / Model*: Existing SEP_IN AXI master and passive monitor; scenario-local
activity watcher; required `fabric_reg` reference model and scoreboard.
The model predicts from completed monitor traffic, not sequence readbacks.
Every catalogued full-width single-beat read/write predicts OKAY, including
error observations. Only OKAY full-strobe writes update shadow.

*Expectation Sources*: `smc_base_config.rdl` CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL field descriptions;
`hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc` activity-based gate and bus-wake descriptions and
`smc-clock-distribution.svg` domain inventory. The address-remapper register
enable is interpreted to cover all three remapper register domains.
`filter_ctrl.rdl` defines START/END granule writeback; `alias_remap.rdl` and
`output_remap.rdl` define writable fields and reset values. Addresses, masks
and defaults come from generated collateral. RTL hierarchy is used for binding,
not as the expected result.

*Test Procedure*: Require disabled fabric gates, output remapping present,
inactive alias regions and unlocked/disabled last filter entries with the
8-byte granule and reset END. Read and verify the five catalogued reset words.
Check all-active disabled state, preload nominal hysteresis with enables clear,
then arm an epoch before each enable write and check both the final closed-domain
map and every domain observed closed during that epoch.
Enable all six controls and require all eight domains closed.

Visit five words in seeded order. Before each pattern write/read, arm an epoch
and observe the target closed; require actual busy and active samples and
bounded post-traffic closure. Check pattern and reset restore readbacks.
Exercise zero hysteresis on the outbound filter register port; log maximum
hysteresis without grading its closure. Restore and read CLOCK_GATE_CONTROL.
Drain passive comparisons before checking exact per-pass accounting.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-REG-CG-CONFIG` |Configuration and reset-baseline prerequisites and gate restore readback
|`CHK-REG-CG-OFF` |Disabled gates remain active and reopen within the test bound
|`CHK-REG-CG-MAP` |Final state and all sampled closures in each enable epoch match its domain group
|`CHK-REG-CG-CLOSE` |Bounded idle closure; no sampled busy domain has an inactive clock enable
|`CHK-REG-CG-WAKE` |Each cold pattern request produces observed busy and active samples
|`CHK-REG-CG-DATA` |Pattern and reset restore readbacks match defined register fields
|`CHK-REG-CG-SCOPE` |Resolved taps and bounded idle
|`CHK-REG-CG-SCOREBOARD` |27 new comparisons per pass with no new mismatch
|`CHK-SB-FABRIC-REG` |Catalogued accesses return OKAY; reads also match model data under RDL masks
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Eight domains observed closed, five observed waking, ten cold epochs; 39 CSR and 40 memory accesses
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE`, `CHK-CSR-RESP`, `CHK-MEM-RESP` |Bring-up and normal responses
|===

*Known Limitations*: Enable/activity taps do not check gated-clock edges,
sub-cycle glitches, scan/test override or reset during traffic. Datapath domains
are tested only while idle. The feature covers five sequential full-width,
full-strobe words with SEP_IN as the only writer. Filter CONFIG/END writes and
other access shapes stop the required feature rather than invent expectations.
Rejected-write shadow behavior and real error responses have no stimulus in
this scenario. Filter granule prerequisites restrict the scenario to 8 bytes.
The rounding branch is reached only with non-discriminating values: START=0
and END=7 already equal their rounded values. Reset-epoch recovery after
shadow changes is not exercised. These model branches are not independently
validated by this scenario.
The passive monitor does not retain data X/Z masks, so the feature does not
independently grade read-data X/Z. The scenario's full-width SEP_IN read helper
checks the active master result for missing data/mask beats and unknown bits.
Closure/reopen bounds are test completion limits, not exact timing guarantees.
Using the same closure bound at H=8 and H=0 does not prove that the programmed
hysteresis affects the latency; a gate ignoring H could satisfy this check.
`OBS-BLOCKED CHK-REG-CG-STICKY` asks whether maximum hysteresis must hold the
gate open; its closure result contributes no functional verdict.
No functional covergroup or coverage-closure claim is added.

*Pass Criteria*: Required records pass, no mismatch or unpaired item, exactly
27 passive comparisons per pass (17 reads and 10 writes).
Used alone, `+SMC_FABRIC_REG_CG_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` changes one CONFIG, OFF, MAP,
CLOSE, WAKE, DATA and SCOPE expectation per pass: seven failures per pass,
112 for sixteen passes, with no `fabric_reg` mismatch. The SCOPE negative
changes only the bounded-idle verdict after the outbound-filter cold pattern
write, not the closure wait or its control flow.
`+SMC_FABRIC_REG_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` corrupts the first outbound-filter START
read prediction after its first write per pass: one mismatch and one scenario
scoreboard failure per pass plus the final feature failure, 33 for sixteen
passes. Neither control changes DUT stimulus. Prerequisites, response checks,
NONVAC and watcher startup/stop are outside the negatives.
Enrolled only in `cg_uvm_extended`, outside `all`, `hosted` and scheduled tiers.

'''''

[[sec-smc_wdt_second_stage_reset_test]]
====== `smc_wdt_second_stage_reset_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_second_stage_reset_test` (SV-UVM only)

*Objective*: Check that servicing the selected core's second-stage watchdog
postpones expiry, stopping service allows expiry, and servicing another core
does not postpone the selected core's timeout and warm-reset recovery.

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN `ocah_axi_vip`; bounded sequence checks against live
per-core and aggregate timeout taps, WDT reset, warm reset and primary reset.
The required `wdt_csr` feature independently predicts CTRL (IP masked), KEY
and CMP readbacks and in-scope responses from passive SEP_IN traffic. COUNT
data is graded by the sequence, not by the model.

*Test Coverage*: All four cores rotate by pass. The timeout is programmed to
0x1800, distinct from reset. Correct-core service spans two configured
intervals; wrong-core pulses end before the expected reset window. Two warm
resets occur per pass. No CSR access overlaps reset. Non-reset CMP markers
on every core distinguish warm reset from retention. CTRL, COUNT and CMP
defaults are checked before explicit idle configuration after each reset.
The timeout is reprogrammed before the next leg and restored at the end.

*Expectation Sources*: `cpu_ctrl.rdl` defines WDT_TIMEOUT as the second-stage
cycle count and the four singlepulse WDT_TIMEOUT_RESET controls. `wdt.rdl`
defines rst-enable, always-count, compare and register reset values.
`hw/sys/smc/doc/clk_rst.adoc`, Primary and Warm Reset, defines second timeout
as a watchdog/warm-reset source and distinguishes it from primary reset.
The SMC owner has confirmed that warm reset resets the per-core watchdog
timers. `clk_rst.adoc` states that warm reset drives the CPU cluster's
interrupt and timer logic, and `hw/sys/smc/doc/watchdog.adoc` defers reset
effects to that section, but neither names the watchdogs; this check relies
on the owner's confirmation for reset scope and on `wdt.rdl` for register
defaults.
Addresses, masks and core count come from the existing generated collateral
and SMC types. Timing allowances below are bench measurement bounds, not new
software-visible register semantics.

*Test Procedure*: Require all cores released and WDTs in reset state. Save and
program WDT_TIMEOUT. Before each arm, read back COUNT=0 and CMP=0x800,
distinct from CMP reset, while counting is disabled. These are configuration
prerequisites, not a precise first-stage timing check. Program and read back
the same non-reset CMP marker on each other, disabled watchdog. Start the bounded
watcher before enabling the selected WDT and service it periodically. Require no expiry
during service, then stop CSR traffic and observe expiry and recovery. Re-arm
and service a different core, requiring expiry at the unserviced deadline.
Check reset scope. After each recovery, observe timeout retention without
grading it and check watchdog CTRL, COUNT and CMP defaults, then explicitly configure and
verify idle CTRL, COUNT and CMP readbacks on every core. Reprogram the timeout
before the wrong-core leg; restore the timeout and check exact CSR-access
accounting.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-CONFIG` |Explicitly programmed, rebaselined and restored CSR states match
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-FIRST` |The selected first timeout precedes second timeout and stays asserted until it
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-SERVICE` |Service duration, gaps and wrong-core pulse completion meet the stimulus bounds
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-HELD` |No second timeout or reset occurs during correct-core service
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-EXPIRES` |Second timeout falls within the configured interval and sampling allowance
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-WRONG-CORE` |A different core is serviced and cannot defer selected-core expiry
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-RECOVERY` |WDT/warm reset assert and release within bounds; fuse/warm readiness precedes further CSR access
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-SCOPE` |No primary reset, unknown observable or initially isolated core; timeout taps are idle and resets released after explicit rebaseline
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-WDT-RESET` |CTRL, COUNT and CMP match RDL defaults on every core after each warm reset, before reconfiguration
|`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-SCOREBOARD` |The pass adds no watchdog model mismatch
|`CHK-SB-WDT-CSR` |The required watchdog feature has comparisons, no mismatch and no unpaired item
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |Prior passes meet the passive watchdog comparison floor
|`CHK-NONVAC` |Two warm resets, 165 fixed CSR accesses plus service writes, and exactly 156 passive watchdog comparisons per pass
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE`, `CHK-CSR-RESP` |Bring-up and frontdoor responses complete
|===

*Known Limitations*: CPU execution and interrupt delivery are outside this
scenario. No core is held in software reset. Timeout taps are sampled on SMC
clock negedges; sub-cycle transitions are not graded. The unserviced timing
allowance is two cycles; the serviced allowance is two cycles after the last
write response. Recovery bounds of 4096 assertion and 16384 release cycles are
conservative bench limits, not latency guarantees. No CSR remains outstanding
across reset. CMP differs from reset on every core before each reset; CTRL
and COUNT differ only on the selected core. At least four passes are needed
to exercise the latter fields on all cores. The scenario does not validate
a general watchdog reference model or individual-core reset retention.
`CHK-WDT-STAGE2-TIMEOUT-RETAINED` is blocked by the undocumented CPU_CTRL
WDT_TIMEOUT retention across warm reset. It is logged as an observation,
excluded from the verdict, and replaced by explicit configuration before
subsequent stimulus.
Idle timeout taps after explicit rebaseline are a prerequisite for the next
measurement, not a claim about automatic warm-reset state clearing.

*Pass Criteria*: Every required checker passes. Used alone,
`+SMC_WDT_STAGE2_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` changes thirteen expectations per pass:
configured timeout, HELD, serviced EXPIRES, serviced RECOVERY and WRONG-CORE
expiry, plus eight post-warm watchdog-state records. It must produce thirteen
failures per pass (208 for sixteen passes) without UVM_FATAL and without model
mismatches. Used alone, `+SMC_WDT_CSR_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must produce 134
mismatches per pass (46 reads and 88 writes), one scenario scoreboard failure
per pass and one final `CHK-SB-WDT-CSR` failure: 2161 errors for sixteen passes.
The 22 COUNT comparisons per pass grade responses only and remain passing. Other
checks establish stimulus/observation validity and remain unchanged; invalid
conditions record failure and stop the run. Enrolled on demand in
`wdt_uvm_extended`, not the scheduled hosted tiers.

'''''

[[sec-smc_lock_pipelined_write_test]]
====== `smc_lock_pipelined_write_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_lock_pipelined_write_test` (SV-UVM-only scenario)

*Objective*: Grade keyed and bitwise lock semantics while successive writes
are outstanding on SEP_IN, with observed channel overlap as a prerequisite.

*Test Coverage*: Six WDT pipeline shapes on every core check one-write
unlock consumption, ineffective partial writes, writes before KEY, combined
FEED/KEY locking and backpressured responses. The final pass checks an
SS_CONFIG write queued after its bitwise lock. Each single-beat write uses
ID 0. The decisive pair must have both AW and W accepted before the prior
write's B handshake. Acceptance cycles, addresses, sizes, payloads, strobes
and IDs are observed on SEP_IN rather than inferred from sequence timing.

*Expectation Sources*: `wdt.rdl` byte-enable rules, KEY state, effective-write
relocking and simultaneous FEED/KEY semantics; generated register geometry
and reset values; `reset_unit.rdl` woset locks and the per-bit SS_CONFIG
write restriction. Sequence expectations are write-derived.
The passive lock-CSR model independently grades L1 readbacks.

*BFM / Model*: Existing SEP_IN master pipeline API and an AW/W/B watcher.
The required `lock_csr` feature independently grades six L1 readbacks.
The `wdt_csr` feature is not enabled: its documented scope is sequential
accesses, while WDT COUNT/KEY pipeline claims are sequence checks.

*Test Procedure*: Require WDT CTRL/CMP at reset, seed distinct COUNT values
whose low sixteen bits are below CMP, and observe the disabled counter.
Launch P1, P2A, P2B, P3, P4 and P5, retaining AW/W/B cycles for each operation
and checking final COUNT/KEY. P1/P5 require only the first effective COUNT
write to land. P2A ends after the partial write and checks COUNT unchanged
and KEY unlocked before a full write uses that unlock. P2B checks the full
write queued after the partial write. P3 checks a write preceding KEY is
refused. P4 requires FEED to clear COUNT to zero, the queued COUNT write to
be rejected and KEY to remain locked. P5 holds BREADY for sixteen cycles
after BVALID.
Restore each WDT. Require SS_CONFIG_LOCK clear before the final L1 pipeline.
L1 uses AxSIZE=2 at the LOCK and CONFIG CSR addresses, with WSTRB on their
respective byte lanes; WDT pipelines retain AxSIZE=3. Check the final
partially restored configuration and retained lock. Require six passive
lock-CSR comparisons with no new mismatch within a bounded wait.

*Known Limitations*: SEP_IN overlap does not prove concurrency inside WDT.
Only ID 0 and the declared byte-enable shapes are covered. In P4 the combined
FEED/KEY write follows a KEY unlock and is checked while counting is disabled;
the same write issued while locked is not exercised. WDT counting,
interrupts and CPU execution/reset are not exercised. L1 uses narrow CSR
writes, not a wide write spanning two CSRs. Locks persist after the last
pass. Background CPU SYS_OUT traffic is outside the claim. No strobe/ID
cross-coverage closure is claimed.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Description
|`CHK-PLOCK-SEED` |Control prerequisites and seeded baselines hold
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-ONE` |One unlock admits only the first effective write in P1/P5
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-INEFFECTIVE` |P2A preserves COUNT/unlock; P2A/P2B admit the subsequent full write
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-PREKEY` |P3 rejects COUNT written before KEY
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-FEEDKEY` |FEED clears COUNT and the queued COUNT write is rejected
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-STATE` |KEY reflects the expected lock state after each leg and cleanup
|`CHK-PLOCK-SSCFG` |L1 lock filters the queued write and reads back its mask
|`CHK-PLOCK-SSCFG-FINAL` |Partially restored SS_CONFIG and retained woset lock are correct
|`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-RESTORE` |COUNT, KEY and CTRL return to the prerequisite state
|`CHK-PLOCK-RESP` |Observed AW/W match issued ops and known OKAY responses echo ID 0
|`CHK-PLOCK-SCOREBOARD` |Six L1 reads are compared by the passive lock model without new mismatch
|`CHK-SB-LOCK-CSR` |The required lock feature has comparisons, no mismatch and no unpaired item
|`CHK-NONVAC` |All 24 WDT legs per pass and final L1 complete and overlap at their decisive pairs
|`CHK-CSR-RESP`, `CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE` |Mapped accesses and fuse bring-up complete
|===

*Pass Criteria*: All functional, completion, overlap and restoration checks
pass without timeout or protocol assertion. `+SMC_LOCK_PIPELINED_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE`
changes only the P1, P2A, P3 and P4 COUNT expectations on core 0, plus L1's config
expectation in the final pass. Exactly four checks fail per pass plus one
in the final pass: 65 failures for sixteen passes, with no fatal or unrelated
error and no lock-scoreboard mismatch. Used alone,
`+SMC_LOCK_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` must produce six L1 mismatches,
one `CHK-PLOCK-SCOREBOARD` failure and one `CHK-SB-LOCK-CSR` failure:
eight failures in total. These are expected signatures, not run results.
The CTRL/CMP reset-state and SS_CONFIG_LOCK-clear prerequisites under
`CHK-PLOCK-SEED` stop the run on failure and are outside both negative
controls. The sequence negative does not alter `CHK-PLOCK-WDT-STATE`,
`CHK-PLOCK-WDT-RESTORE`, `CHK-PLOCK-SSCFG-FINAL`, `CHK-PLOCK-RESP` or
`CHK-NONVAC` expectations.
Enrolled only in
`csr_uvm_extended`, outside `all`, `hosted` and `ci`.

'''''

[[sec-smc_wdt_core_awake_gate_test]]
====== `smc_wdt_core_awake_gate_test`

*Source Module*: `smc_wdt_core_awake_gate_test` (SV-UVM)

*BFM / Model*: SEP_IN AXI VIP and the passive `wdt_csr` feature.
The model grades in-scope responses and configuration readbacks; bounded
sequence checks grade count changes and endpoint COUNT/CMP state across
software core reset.

*Objective*: Check count suppression with wdogcoreawake and the priority
of wdogenalways across software core reset, with endpoint state-retention checks.

*Test Coverage*: All four cores rotate, one per pass. Measure the released
count rate, hold the selected core in reset with coreawake alone, and repeat
with always-count enabled. Scale and CMP keep the compare interrupt inactive.

*Expectation Sources*: `hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/wdt/wdt.rdl` defines coreawake
as counting only outside core reset and always-count as having priority.
`hw/sys/smc/regs/blocks/cpu_ctrl/cpu_ctrl.rdl` defines software reset control
and reset-applied status. Register masks come from generated collateral.
`hw/sys/smc/doc/cpu.adoc`, Cluster Boundary Isolation, states that the
boundary isolates while any core or the uncore is in reset and stalls
L2 frontend traffic. The live isolation tap controls safe CSR access.
The SMC owner confirms that individual core reset is a watchdog core-state
indicator, not a watchdog reset: COUNT and configuration are retained.

*Test Procedure*: Require the selected watchdog's disabled reset configuration
and save COUNT, CMP and reset control. Program CMP, coreawake and COUNT,
then calibrate a positive count rate. Apply reset and require reset-applied
and cluster isolation before the measurement interval. Release reset and wait
with a bound for isolation to clear before reading COUNT. Require calibrated
headroom below the COUNT limit, then require the final COUNT sample not to
be below the initial sample in the coreawake-only interval. Require the two
count bounds to differ by at least two integer count units before grading
HELD or ALWAYS. Repeat the interval with always-count enabled.
Read CMP after both intervals and require the programmed value. Restore the
disabled configuration and COUNT with readback, check reset control against
its baseline and require reset-applied to be clear, then restore CMP with
readback. Wait with a bound for passive comparisons.

*Checkers*:

[cols="1,2",options="header",]
|===
|Checker |Claim
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-CONFIG` |CTRL readbacks equal the programmed configuration and restored COUNT and CMP equal their saved values
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-CORE-RESET` |Reset status and cluster isolation reach their requested levels
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-RATE` |Released-core count and timestamps produce a positive rate
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-HELD` |Count growth excludes the held interval within the stated margin
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-ALWAYS` |Always-count includes the held interval within the stated margin
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-RETAINED` |COUNT after the coreawake-only interval is not below its initial sample; CMP after both reset intervals equals its programmed value
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-WINDOW` |HELD and ALWAYS bounds separate by at least two integer count units and calibrated advance leaves headroom below the 31-bit COUNT limit
|`CHK-WDT-AWAKE-SCOREBOARD` |No new passive watchdog mismatch occurs
|`CHK-SB-WDT-CSR` |In-scope responses and modeled readbacks match predictions
|`CHK-NONVAC` |35 CSR accesses and 35 passive watchdog comparisons complete per pass
|`CHK-SB-MIN-ACTIVITY` |Completed passes reach the passive comparison floor
|`CHK-FUSE-SENSE-DONE`, `CHK-CSR-RESP`, `CHK-MEM-RESP` |Bring-up and accesses complete
|===

*Known Limitations*: COUNT is sampled only at the two ends of each reset
interval. The mode-0 no-decrease check does not exclude a transient decrease.
The margin is one quarter of the held interval; exact stop/resume cycles and
absolute clock frequency are not graded. Four passes are required for all cores.
CPU execution, watchdog reset outputs and interrupt delivery are outside scope.
The scenario changes CPU_CTRL reset state and requires exclusive control.
The count measurement interval is stimulus, not a settling delay.
The shared wdt_csr assumptions and exclusions apply.
The ALWAYS lower bound uses the same endpoint samples, not a separate
retention check. CMP is read once after both reset intervals.
The no-wrap prerequisite uses the in-pass rate calibration; it does not
prove that wrap cannot occur under an incorrect count rate. The measured bounds
grade relative counting, not an independently specified absolute clock rate.

*Pass Criteria*: All checks pass. Used alone,
`+SMC_WDT_COREAWAKE_SEQUENCE_NEGATIVE` reverses one expectation each for
CONFIG, CORE-RESET, HELD and ALWAYS and both RETAINED expectations,
producing six failures per pass.
RATE remains a measurement prerequisite and terminates on invalid calibration.
WINDOW is also a measurement prerequisite and is not reversed by the negative.
`+SMC_WDT_CSR_SCOREBOARD_NEGATIVE` corrupts production model predictions;
the expected signature is 27 feature mismatches per pass: nine CTRL/CMP
read mismatches and 18 write-response mismatches. Eight COUNT read comparisons
still pass. CHK-WDT-AWAKE-SCOREBOARD fails once per pass; comparison-count
NONVAC records still pass.
The leaf runs on demand in `wdt_uvm_extended`, not in `all`, `hosted` or `ci`.

'''''

[[smc-deferred-disposition]]
==== SMC deferred and OUT disposition

This is the disposition of record for every test name the package catalogues
without a module under `hw/sys/smc/dv/cocotb/tests/`, and for every enrolled
leaf that no scheduled tier runs (<<smc-scheduled-holdouts>>). Nothing here is
enrolled PASS. Every `@pyuvm.test()` module under `cocotb/tests/` is in at
least one testlist (`smc_base_test` and `smc_dual_base_test` are base classes,
not tests); a catalogued name without a module is one of two kinds:

* A *retired test module* targets this bench and its blocker is
  outside the test: adopter placeholder RTL, a wrapper pin that does not
  exist, an idle boundary, an aperture or window SEP_IN cannot write or
  reach, TB glue, or a VIP the bench lacks. Its code, and
  the `seq_lib/<name>_seq.py` sequence where it had one, is in git history
  and is restored when the blocker named in its row clears.
* A *catalog-only name* never had a module here: a name from an external
  catalog whose intent a live enrolled name already proves, or a body that needs stimulus,
  RTL or a firmware image this bench does not have.

Buckets:

* `adopter-pending OUT` — waits on adopter IP, a product pin, firmware/ROM, or a TB terminator.
* `child-TB-owned` — protocol completeness belongs to a block-level TB (I3C, DTP).
* `waived` — fake BFM, TB-glue, or an alias already covered by a live name.

[[smc-idle-boundaries]]
===== Idle smc_wrapper boundaries (OUT)

These ports have no TB terminator on `--dut smc` / `smc_wrapper`
(`hw/sys/smc/dv/models/README.md`). They are OUT rather than terminated by a
placeholder responder. Block-level I3C and DTP signoff stay on those TBs;
do not count a wrapper terminator as that proof.

[cols="2,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|Boundary |Disposition |Reintroduction trigger
|I3C DAT/DCT |adopter-pending OUT |Real DAT/DCT macros on `smc_wrapper` / `smu_wrapper`. Protocol CCC/IBI remains I3C block DV. Do not credit `smc_i3c_to_fabric_test` as this proof.
|DTP CSR AXI-Lite |adopter-pending OUT |A real DTP CSR slave on `smc_wrapper`, or accept SMU-level DTP tests as the only wrapper-adjacent surface. SMU already wires DTP internally.
|===

[[smc-bench-tie-offs]]
===== Bench tie-offs

A tie-off is a constant on an `smc_wrapper` input port in `tb_top.sv` (the
single-instance `u_dut` and the `smc_dual_inst` wrapper instance). Every
`--dut smc` / `smc_wrapper` and SMC_DUAL leaf runs under it, on every tool.
Each row states the behaviour the constant keeps out of reach, the enrolled
claims that would change if the pin were driven, and the control that closes
the row.

[cols="2,1,5,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Tie-off |Value |Behaviour made unreachable |Tests whose claims would change |Control / closes when
|`sep_security_disable_i` (`tb_top.sv`, both `smc_wrapper` instances)
|`1'b0`
|The eFuse sense bypass (`hw/ip/efuse/doc/architecture.adoc`, "Security Disable Bypass Mechanism"). On the product the pin is the SEP `security_disable_o` token-match result (`sep.sv`, wired through `smu.sv`); inside SMC it reaches only `smc_efuse_wrapper` -> `efuse_interface_controller.security_disable_i`. SMC builds the controller with `HAS_LC_STATE=0` (`smc_efuse_wrapper.sv`), so the bypass takes the non-LC branch: the controller drives `shadow_regs_o` from the shadow registers whenever fuse sensing has finished or the pin is high, and drives all zeros otherwise (`efuse_interface_controller.sv`); its command mux routes the shadow-register sense FSM to the bank only while sensing is not done and the pin is low (`efuse_interface_controller.sv`). With the pin at 1 the FSM's reads are never routed, so `fuse_sense_done` never rises, the shadow registers keep their all-zero reset value and are exposed unsensed, and `fuse_reset_n` -- and with it `rst_warm` (`smc_reset_ctrl.sv`) -- never release: the warm domain never leaves reset. With the pin at 0 every run senses the bank, which is what the product does on a chip whose SEC_DIS token did not match.
|None of the enrolled claims: no leaf claims the bypass, and every eFuse leaf proves the sensed path, which is the path a 0 selects. Were the pin driven to 1 for a run, every sequence that calls `wait_fuse_sense_done` (40 sequence files under `cocotb/seq_lib/`; `smc_base_test_seq.py` defines the method and each leaf that needs the warm domain calls it itself) would time out on `tb_fuse_sense_done`, and every warm-domain CSR access would hang with no ready.
|Positive control: a leaf that drives the pin to 1 and requires `fuse_sense_done` to stay 0 while the shadow-register window still answers. It must stay in the cold domain: the eFuse controller sits under `rst_primary`, ahead of `rst_warm`, so its shadow reads through the eFuse CSR window -- over the OTP JTAG AXI-Lite port or the fabric path -- are the only thing that answers under bypass; nothing in the warm domain does. It needs a driven pin (a bench input in `smc_tb_signal_list.svh`, idle 0) in place of the constant. Closes when that leaf is enrolled, or when SEP-integrated signoff (SMU with SEP=1) is accepted as the only place the token-match path is exercised and that acceptance is recorded here.
|===

===== Retired test modules

Each row names the blocker whose clearing restores the module, and its sequence, from git history.

[cols="3,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Name |Bucket |Blocker and what restores the module
|smc_dfd_dbs_fault_inject_test
|waived
|TB-glue / not DUT RTL: the TB latches a hardcoded capture token, and the real DFD is `smc_dfd_wrap`. Must not be reported as feature PASS. Restore only with a DUT-side DFD fault-injection observable.
|smc_i3c_ccc_ibi_full_test
|child-TB-owned
|I3C CCC/IBI protocol is block-level I3C DV. Wrapper DAT/DCT macros are absent; see the idle-boundary table. Restore when real DAT/DCT macros reach `smc_wrapper`.
|smc_macro_axil_routing_test
|adopter-pending OUT
|DTP CSR port is idle on smc_wrapper (no TB terminator) and the PLL/PVT windows answer from OKAY+0 placeholder wraps. SMU already wires DTP; do not double-count DTP TB signoff. Restore when a DTP CSR subordinate and real PLL/PVT IP are on the wrapper.

[[smc-bench-standins]]
===== Bench stand-ins

A stand-in is DV-owned RTL that answers in place of a product cell or an
adopter block. Two sit on proof paths of this bench. Each has an inventory
row, a control row, and -- where the stand-in can supply a verdict -- one row
per enrolled leaf stating which crossing is on its proof path, what the
verdict reads, and the result of the control. `hw/sys/smc/dv/README.md`,
`tb/verilator_stubs/README.md` and `models/README.md` describe layout and
enrolment and point here; the dispositions live only here. The bench's one
assertion waiver answers in place of a product mechanism without being RTL,
so it takes its own record after the tables rather than a row in them.

Kinds used in the leaf tables:

* *reads the crossing* -- the verdict samples the stand-in's output itself
  (a CSR field or a `tb_top` tap wired to `q_o`). On Verilator that value has
  the stand-in as its author until the pipe has filled.
* *downstream* -- the verdict reads product state that the DUT derives from
  the crossing's output.
* *upstream* -- the verdict reads the near side; the crossing carries the
  value away and nothing behind it is read.
* *none* -- no `prim_sync3` is on the proof path. Every entry of
  `reset.toml`, `clock.toml` and `irq.toml` has a row, whether or not a
  stand-in is on its path.

[cols="2,3,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|Stand-in |Replaces |Enrolled by |Tools it reaches
|`tb/verilator_stubs/prim_sync3.sv`
|`hw/common/ocah_prim/rtl/prim_sync3.sv`: `prim_flop_3sync` behind `prim_cdc_rand_delay`. No DV build sets `+cdc_instrumentation_enabled=1`, so `prim_cdc_rand_delay` passes its input through and the product cell is also a plain flop pipe; the one behaviour the stand-in adds is `initial '0` on every stage, a defined `0` on the far side before the pipe has filled where the product cell shows X on a four-state simulator. Two-stage crossings are OpenTitan `prim_flop_2sync`, which has a reset port and no stand-in.
|`smc_sim_cfg.toml` `[build].stubs`, emitted ahead of the Bender filelist so Verilator's `-Wno-MODDUP` first-definition-wins picks them. The product cells stay in the same compile: the generated Bender filelist `build/smc_bender.f` (`[build].bender_filelist`).
|Verilator and Xcelium compile it; VCS does not. The runner (`tools/dv/runlib/stages.py`) filters `[build].stubs` only when `tool == "vcs"`: there it drops any stub whose basename the Bender graph supplies, so the VCS compile list carries no `prim_sync3` stub and the product cell elaborates. For every other tool in `smc_sim_cfg.toml` `tools` -- Verilator and Xcelium -- it keeps both files and emits them ahead of the Bender filelist, so their compile lists carry the stub and the product cell together. Verilator's `-Wno-MODDUP` first-definition-wins selects the stub; no Xcelium build of this bench is recorded, so which of the pair Xcelium elaborates is not established by this record.
|`models/axil_okay_slv.sv` (behind `models/pll_wrap.sv` and `pvt_wrap.sv`)
|Nothing in the product RTL. It terminates the adopter PLL and PVT AXI-Lite windows that a real integration fills with the adopter's CSRs, completing every access with `RESP_OKAY` and all-zero read data. pulp `axi_err_slv` cannot hold that place: it asserts at time zero on every simulator but Verilator.
|Bender `smc_wrapper` target: `hw/top/smc_ip_integration.sv` `u_pll_wrap` / `u_pvt_wrap`.
|Every tool.
|===

[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Stand-in |Control that keeps the claims honest |Closes when
|`prim_sync2/3`
|Height-3 control: the `reset`, `clock` and `irq` groups run on VCS with the product cells, `python3 tools/dv/run_dv.py --dut smc --items reset clock irq --tool vcs --regress`; the VCS compile list carries the product `prim_sync2.sv` / `prim_sync3.sv` from `smc_bender.f` and no stub. The PeakRDL immediate assertions `assert_bad_ext_wr_ack` / `assert_bad_ext_rd_ack` in `cpu_ctrl_reg`, `reset_unit_reg` and `system_timer_octs_reg` (six sites) each report once `at time 0 fs`, before any reset, while `arst_n` and the ack strobes are still X. That class is waived in `smc_sim_cfg.toml` `[pass_fail]` in the form SEP uses for `abr_reg`: an ignore pattern naming exactly these six assertions together with the `at time 0 fs` text, paired with a hard-fail pattern that turns a later firing of the same assertions into an error. One product assertion fires at a non-zero time and is not waived: `prim_ag_clk_mux.sv` `CheckMutualExclusionClk1` in `avsbus_controller.u_refclk_apbclk_mux` under `smc_cg_dft_reset_bringup_test`, the DFT `test_en_i` bypass leaf, on VCS; whether it fires depends on the seed. Verilator compiles assertions out. Neither observation depends on the synchroniser cells. The group selection excludes five entries of the three testlist files (named above the reset-group leaf table); `python3 tools/dv/run_dv.py --dut smc --items <the five names> --tool vcs --regress` covers those five on the same VCS build.
|Either the stand-ins leave the build, or the `CheckMutualExclusionClk1` firing in `avsbus_controller.u_refclk_apbclk_mux` under the DFT `test_en_i` bypass is resolved (a defect, or an assertion that must be disabled while `test_en_i` is high) and a repeat of this control is graded green by the runner.
|`axil_okay_slv`
|None beyond the live consumer's own positive control (below): the only enrolled claim behind it is reachability, which the DUT drives (`smc_external_req_o.ar_valid` observed high, then idle). No enrolled leaf compares a value the stand-in authors as evidence.
|Real PLL / PVT IP lands on the wrapper; the six retired consumers are then restored from git history per their rows above and re-graded against the real blocks.
|===

====== Bench-scope assertion waiver

The `[pass_fail]` pair of `smc_sim_cfg.toml` is the other thing that answers
in place of a product mechanism on this bench: it decides, for every leaf,
which assertion failure the runner reads as a failure. It is not DV-owned
RTL, so it takes its own record rather than a row in the inventory above, and
four fields: what is accepted with it in place, why the real path cannot be
used, the exact scope, and the command that re-confirms the entry against the
tree.

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Value
|Claim |A leaf graded PASS has had every assertion of the run read, apart from
the six PeakRDL external-ack assertions at time 0
|Why |`assert_bad_ext_wr_ack` and `assert_bad_ext_rd_ack` in `cpu_ctrl_reg`,
`reset_unit_reg` and `system_timer_octs_reg` are immediate assertions in the
post-reset branch of an `always_ff`. On a four-state simulator the first clock
edge sees `arst_n` and the ack strobes at X and each fires once at `0 fs`. The
blocks are generated, so the assertion cannot be gated in the tree, and
`$assertoff` races the time-0 evaluation
|Scope |One `extra_ignore_patterns` entry and one `extra_hard_fail_patterns`
entry of `smc_sim_cfg.toml` `[pass_fail]`, naming those six assertions and no
others. The ignore matches only the `at time 0 fs` text; the hard-fail matches
the companion timestamped line with a non-zero `failed at`, so a later firing
of the same assertions fails the run. No other assertion is touched:
`prim_ag_clk_mux` `CheckMutualExclusionClk1` still fails the leaf that fires
it, which the control above records
|Closes when |The generated blocks stop asserting on an X ack strobe, or the
bench drives `arst_n` and the ack strobes to a defined value before the first
clock edge. Either removes the pair
|===

Re-confirm: `grep -n 'assert_bad_ext' hw/sys/smc/dv/smc_sim_cfg.toml` prints
exactly two pattern lines, one under `extra_ignore_patterns` carrying
`at time 0 fs` and one under `extra_hard_fail_patterns` carrying
`failed at [1-9]`, and no third. A row that prints anything else is an entry
that has gone stale, and the entry is what needs the edit.

No eFuse leaf crosses one: the eFuse reset synchroniser is the vendored
